# Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita

*The great poem (mahakavya) of Kavi Karnapura in twenty sargas*

*Kavi Karnapura*

*Translated from the Sanskrit into English*

*Sanskrit text, transliteration, word for word, translation and notes*

---

## Translator's Note

The *Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita* is the Sanskrit *mahakavya* (great poem) of Kavi Karnapura (Paramananda Sena), the
youngest son of Shivananda Sena, who as a child received Mahaprabhu's mercy. The poem in twenty sargas was completed in
1464 Shaka (1542 CE), in the month of Ashadha (20.49); the author's main source, he says, was the notes of Murari Gupta
(20.42–43). It opens with the lament of the devotees after the Lord's disappearance and then tells His whole life, from
His appearance in Navadvipa to the last years in Puri, with special fullness for the Ratha-yatra and the festivals of Nilachala.

**Source.** The Sanskrit text follows the edition of Haridasa Shastri (Vrindavana), checked by hand against the scan; 1,912
verses by our count. Only Karnapura's text is translated; the translations and commentaries of the editions are not
included. Interpretation follows Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati.

## Sarga One — verses 1–29

**Metre:** verses 1–24 — *mandakranta* (17 syllables to the pada); verses 25–29 — *shikharini* (17 syllables).

**Contents of the passage:**
- 1–7 — mangalacharana, the auspicious invocation: Gauranga as Krishna who has become golden.
- 8–12 — the poet's self-abasement: why and how he undertakes to write.
- 13–29 — **the frame narrative:** Mahaprabhu has disappeared from the world, and the devotees lament their separation from Him. The poem opens not with His birth but with grief after His disappearance: the story is told from the point of loss.

### Verse 1

यः श्रीवृन्दावनभुवि पुरा सच्चिदानन्दसान्द्रो
गौराङ्गीभिः सदृशरुचिभिः श्यामधामा ननर्त ।
तासां शश्वद्दृढतरपरीरम्भसम्भेदतः किं
गौराङ्गः सन् जयति स नवद्वीपमालम्बमानः ॥१॥

*yaḥ śrī-vṛndāvana-bhuvi purā sac-cid-ānanda-sāndro*
*gaurāṅgībhiḥ sadṛśa-rucibhiḥ śyāma-dhāmā nanarta |*
*tāsāṁ śaśvad-dṛḍhatara-parīrambha-sambhedataḥ kiṁ*
*gaurāṅgaḥ san jayati sa navadvīpam ālambamānaḥ ||1||*

*Word for word:* *yaḥ* — who; *śrī* — of beautiful; *vṛndāvana* — of Vrindavana; *bhuvi* — on the land; *purā* — once; *sat* — with being; *cit* — with consciousness; *ānanda* — with bliss; *sāndraḥ* — dense; *gaurāṅgībhiḥ* — with golden-limbed [maidens]; *sadṛśa* — alike; *rucibhiḥ* — with [those having] radiance; *śyāma* — dark; *dhāmā* — in radiance; *nanarta* — danced; *tāsām* — of them; *śaśvat* — of constant; *dṛḍhatara* — ever firmer; *parīrambha* — of embraces; *sambhedataḥ* — from the union; *kim* — is it not that; *gaurāṅgaḥ* — golden-limbed; *san* — being; *jayati* — is victorious; *saḥ* — He; *navadvīpam* — Navadvipa; *ālambamānaḥ* — taking as His support.

**1.** He who once, on the land of beautiful Vrindavana, dense with being, consciousness and bliss, dark in His radiance, danced with golden-limbed maidens alike in their radiance — was it not from the union of their constant, ever firmer embraces that He Himself became golden? Glory to Him, to Gauranga, who has taken Navadvipa for His support!

*Note.* *Kim* is not a question of perplexity but a poetic conjecture (*utpreksha*): the poet offers an explanation of Chaitanya's golden colour. This is the principal theological image of the whole poem: Gauranga is Krishna, who has taken on the form and colour of His beloved gopis.

### Verse 2

यस्याङ्गश्रीमधुरिमपरीणाहपीयूषसेकै-
र्भास्वच्चामीकरजलमयैः शान्तनिःशेषतापै-
र्यस्य श्रीमत्पदजलरुहान्माकरन्दप्रवाहैः
साक्षात्प्रक्षालितमिव जगच्छश्वदानम्यतां सः ॥२॥

*yasyāṅga-śrī-madhurima-parīṇāha-pīyūṣa-sekair*
*bhāsvac-cāmīkara-jala-mayaiḥ śānta-niḥśeṣa-tāpair*
*yasya śrīmat-pada-jalaruhān mākaranda-pravāhaiḥ*
*sākṣāt prakṣālitam iva jagac chaśvad ānamyatāṁ saḥ ||2||*

*Word for word:* *yasya* — of whose; *aṅga* — of the body; *śrī* — of the beauty; *madhurima* — of the sweetness; *parīṇāha* — of the abundance; *pīyūṣa* — of nectar; *sekaiḥ* — with the sprinklings; *bhāsvat* — of shining; *cāmīkara* — gold; *jala* — of liquid; *mayaiḥ* — consisting; *śānta* — which have quenched; *niḥśeṣa* — without remainder; *tāpaiḥ* — the burning; *yasya* — of whose; *śrīmat* — beautiful; *pada* — of the feet; *jalaruhāt* — from the lotus; *mākaranda* — of honey; *pravāhaiḥ* — with the streams; *sākṣāt* — before one's eyes; *prakṣālitam* — washed; *iva* — as if; *jagat* — the world; *śaśvat* — always; *ānamyatām* — let [Him] be bowed to; *saḥ* — He.

**2.** By the sprinklings of the nectar of His bodily beauty, so abundant in sweetness — sprinklings that are like liquid shining gold and quench all burning without remainder — and by the streams of honey from the lotus of His beautiful feet, the world seems washed before one's very eyes. To Him let there ever be obeisance.

### Verse 3

जानुप्रान्तप्रसृमरभुजादण्डमुद्दण्डचण्ड-
द्योतश्रेणीपटुतरमहोमण्डलीमण्डिताङ्गम् ।
आकर्णान्तःस्खलितललितापाङ्गमत्यन्तरज्यद्-
गण्डाभोगं मृगपतिशताक्रीडमानं भजामः ॥३॥

*jānu-prānta-prasṛmara-bhujā-daṇḍam uddaṇḍa-caṇḍa-*
*dyota-śreṇī-paṭutara-maho-maṇḍalī-maṇḍitāṅgam |*
*ākarṇāntaḥ-skhalita-lalitāpāṅgam atyanta-rajyad-*
*gaṇḍābhogaṁ mṛgapati-śatākrīḍamānaṁ bhajāmaḥ ||3||*

*Word for word:* *jānu* — of the knees; *prānta* — to the edge; *prasṛmara* — extending; *bhujā* — arms; *daṇḍam* — [having] staffs; *uddaṇḍa* — of unrestrained; *caṇḍa* — fierce; *dyota* — of radiance; *śreṇī* — of rows; *paṭutara* — with most brilliant; *mahaḥ* — of light; *maṇḍalī* — with a circle; *maṇḍita* — adorned; *aṅgam* — [having] a body; *ā* — up to; *karṇa* — the ears; *antaḥ* — as far as; *skhalita* — slipping; *lalita* — playful; *apāṅgam* — [having] a sidelong glance; *atyanta* — deeply; *rajyat* — reddening; *gaṇḍa* — of the cheeks; *ābhogam* — [having] the breadth; *mṛgapati* — of lions; *śata* — a hundred; *ākrīḍamānam* — sporting [like]; *bhajāmaḥ* — we worship.

**3.** We worship Him whose arms, like staffs, reach to the edge of His knees; whose body is adorned with a most brilliant circle of light, rows of fierce, unrestrained radiance; whose playful sidelong glance slips all the way to His ears; whose broad cheeks flush a deep red; and who sports like a hundred lions.

### Verse 4

यस्य श्रीमन्नखमणिसुधारश्मिरम्यप्रकाशै-
स्त्रैलोक्यान्तर्जटितजडिमक्षालनायोन्मिषद्भिः ।
स्वीयप्रेमाम्बुधिलहरिकापूरपूरेण भूयो
जाड्यं चक्रे तमिह तदहो सेवतां जीवलोकः ॥४॥

*yasya śrīman-nakha-maṇi-sudhā-raśmi-ramya-prakāśais*
*trailokyāntar-jaṭita-jaḍima-kṣālanāyonmiṣadbhiḥ |*
*svīya-premāmbudhi-laharikā-pūra-pūreṇa bhūyo*
*jāḍyaṁ cakre tam iha tad aho sevatāṁ jīva-lokaḥ ||4||*

*Word for word:* *yasya* — of whose; *śrīmat* — beautiful; *nakha* — of the nails; *maṇi* — of the gems; *sudhā* — nectarean; *raśmi* — of rays; *ramya* — with the charming; *prakāśaiḥ* — light; *trailokya* — of the three worlds; *antaḥ* — within; *jaṭita* — ingrained; *jaḍima* — the dullness; *kṣālanāya* — for washing away; *unmiṣadbhiḥ* — flashing forth; *svīya* — of His own; *prema* — of love; *ambudhi* — of the ocean; *laharikā* — of the waves; *pūra* — of the flood; *pūreṇa* — by the inundation; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *jāḍyam* — stupor; *cakre* — produced; *tam* — Him; *iha* — here; *tat* — therefore; *aho* — oh, wonder; *sevatām* — let serve; *jīva* — of living beings; *lokaḥ* — the world.

**4.** The charming light of the gems of His beautiful nails, soft as nectar-rays, flashed forth to wash away the dullness ingrained within the three worlds; and then, with the inundation of the flooding waves of His own ocean of love, He again produced a stupor. Oh, wonder! Therefore let the world of living beings serve Him here.

*Note.* A play on words: *jaḍimā* is the dull inertness of the material world; *jāḍya* is the stupor of ecstasy, one of the eight *sattvika-bhavas* (immobility from an excess of feeling). The one is washed away by the light; the other comes with love.

### Verse 5

स्वीयैर्लीलाविलसितरसैः पादसेवाविलासै-
र्लास्योल्लासैर्यदयमकरोत्पूर्णपूर्णां त्रिलोकीम् ।
मन्ये भूयस्तदिह करुणा सैव नित्यं नवीना
भूयो भूयः प्रणमतुतरां तामिमां जीवलोकः ॥५॥

*svīyair līlā-vilasita-rasaiḥ pāda-sevā-vilāsair*
*lāsyollāsair yad ayam akarot pūrṇa-pūrṇāṁ trilokīm |*
*manye bhūyas tad iha karuṇā saiva nityaṁ navīnā*
*bhūyo bhūyaḥ praṇamatutarāṁ tām imāṁ jīva-lokaḥ ||5||*

*Word for word:* *svīyaiḥ* — with His own; *līlā* — of pastimes; *vilasita* — of the sports; *rasaiḥ* — with the tastes; *pāda* — to the feet; *sevā* — of service; *vilāsaiḥ* — with the joys; *lāsya* — of dance; *ullāsaiḥ* — with the raptures; *yat* — that; *ayam* — He; *akarot* — made; *pūrṇa-pūrṇām* — filled to overflowing; *trilokīm* — the three worlds; *manye* — I think; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *tat* — that; *iha* — here; *karuṇā* — mercy; *sā* — that; *eva* — very; *nityam* — eternally; *navīnā* — new; *bhūyaḥ bhūyaḥ* — again and again; *praṇamatu* — let bow; *tarām* — ever more; *tām* — to that; *imām* — to this; *jīva* — of living beings; *lokaḥ* — the world.

**5.** That He filled the three worlds to overflowing with the tastes of His own playful pastimes, with the joys of service to the feet, with the raptures of dance — this, I think, is that very mercy, eternally new, [shown] here once again. Let the world of living beings bow to it again and again, ever more deeply.

*Note.* *Pāda-sevā-vilāsa* can be understood both as "the play of service to the feet" (the devotees' service to Him) and as "the play of the feet" in dance.

### Verse 6

यत्र श्रीमन्मधुरिममयी कान्तिरेषा जगाम
व्याहारान्तं गुरुकरुणता पूर्णतामागतासीत् ।
वैदग्धीयं निखिलसुभगा हन्त निर्वाहमाप्ता
गौरांगस्य प्रणम तदिदं पादपाथोजयुग्मम् ॥६॥

*yatra śrīman-madhurima-mayī kāntir eṣā jagāma*
*vyāhārāntaṁ guru-karuṇatā pūrṇatām āgatāsīt |*
*vaidagdhīyaṁ nikhila-subhagā hanta nirvāham āptā*
*gaurāṅgasya praṇama tad idaṁ pāda-pāthoja-yugmam ||6||*

*Word for word:* *yatra* — in which; *śrīmat* — of beautiful; *madhurima* — sweetness; *mayī* — full; *kāntiḥ* — loveliness; *eṣā* — this; *jagāma* — reached; *vyāhāra* — of speech; *antam* — the limit; *guru* — weighty; *karuṇatā* — compassion; *pūrṇatām* — fullness; *āgatā* — having reached; *āsīt* — was; *vaidagdhī* — artfulness; *iyam* — this; *nikhila* — to all; *subhagā* — charming; *hanta* — ah; *nirvāham* — consummation; *āptā* — attained; *gaurāṅgasya* — of Gauranga; *praṇama* — bow; *tat* — to that; *idam* — to this; *pāda* — of the feet; *pāthoja* — of lotuses; *yugmam* — to the pair.

**6.** In them this loveliness, full of beautiful sweetness, went beyond the limit of speech; in them profound compassion reached its fullness; in them this artfulness, charming to all — ah! — attained its consummation. Bow down to that pair of lotus feet of Gauranga.

*Note.* *Vaidagdhī* is not merely "cleverness" but refinement in art, play and love. It is one of Krishna's qualities in Gaudiya aesthetics.

### Verse 7

चित्रं तावद्गुणजलनिधेस्तस्य लावण्यधाम्नो
वैदग्ध्यादेर्लवमपि सुधीर्भाषितुं कः समर्थः ।
स्वीयां शक्तिं द्विगुणगुणितां चेद्विधायैष वक्तुं
शक्तः शक्तः स्वयमपि नहि श्रीलगौरांगचन्द्रः ॥७॥

*citraṁ tāvad guṇa-jala-nidhes tasya lāvaṇya-dhāmno*
*vaidagdhyāder lavam api sudhīr bhāṣituṁ kaḥ samarthaḥ |*
*svīyāṁ śaktiṁ dviguṇa-guṇitāṁ ced vidhāyaiṣa vaktuṁ*
*śaktaḥ śaktaḥ svayam api na hi śrīla-gaurāṅga-candraḥ ||7||*

*Word for word:* *citram* — wonderful; *tāvat* — indeed; *guṇa* — of virtues; *jala* — of waters; *nidheḥ* — of the reservoir; *tasya* — of Him; *lāvaṇya* — of loveliness; *dhāmnaḥ* — of the abode; *vaidagdhya* — of artfulness; *ādeḥ* — and the rest; *lavam* — a particle; *api* — even; *sudhīḥ* — wise man; *bhāṣitum* — to express; *kaḥ* — who; *samarthaḥ* — is able; *svīyām* — His own; *śaktim* — power; *dvi* — two; *guṇa* — -fold; *guṇitām* — multiplied; *cet* — if; *vidhāya* — having made; *eṣaḥ* — He; *vaktum* — to tell; *śaktaḥ* — the Mighty One; *śaktaḥ* — able; *svayam* — Himself; *api* — even; *na hi* — not at all; *śrīla* — Srila; *gaurāṅga* — Gauranga; *candraḥ* — the moon.

**7.** Wonderful indeed! What wise man is able to express even a particle of the artfulness and other [virtues] of Him, the ocean of virtues, the abode of loveliness? Even if He, Srila Gaurangachandra, were to multiply His own power twofold in order to tell of it — even He Himself, the Mighty One, would not be able.

*Note.* The repetition *śaktaḥ śaktaḥ* rests on two meanings of the word: "mighty" (of Him) and "able" (to tell).

### Verse 8

अस्य श्रीमद्व्रजवरवधूप्राणनाथस्य लीला-
लावण्याढ्यं तरुणिमसुधासम्भृतं तं विलासम् ।
ये तत्पादाम्बुजमधुकरा वक्त्रतो हन्त तेषां
श्रुत्वा कोऽपि प्रचलहृदयश्चापलादेष वक्ति ॥८॥

*asya śrīmad-vraja-vara-vadhū-prāṇa-nāthasya līlā-*
*lāvaṇyāḍhyaṁ taruṇima-sudhā-sambhṛtaṁ taṁ vilāsam |*
*ye tat-pādāmbuja-madhukarā vaktrato hanta teṣāṁ*
*śrutvā ko 'pi pracala-hṛdayaś cāpalād eṣa vakti ||8||*

*Word for word:* *asya* — of this; *śrīmat* — of the beautiful; *vraja* — of Vraja; *vara* — of the best; *vadhū* — of the maidens; *prāṇa* — of the life; *nāthasya* — of the Lord; *līlā* — of pastimes; *lāvaṇya* — in loveliness; *āḍhyam* — rich; *taruṇima* — of youth; *sudhā* — with the nectar; *sambhṛtam* — filled; *tam* — that; *vilāsam* — play; *ye* — who; *tat* — of His; *pāda* — of the feet; *ambuja* — of the lotuses; *madhukarāḥ* — bees; *vaktrataḥ* — from the mouths; *hanta* — ah; *teṣām* — of them; *śrutvā* — having heard; *kaḥ* — some-; *api* — -one; *pracala* — with trembling; *hṛdayaḥ* — heart; *cāpalāt* — out of rashness; *eṣaḥ* — this; *vakti* — speaks.

**8.** He is the Lord of the life of the beautiful, best maidens of Vraja. Having heard of that play of His — rich in the loveliness of pastimes and filled with the nectar of youth — from the mouths of those who are bees at His lotus feet, ah, this someone, his heart trembling, speaks of it out of rashness.

*Note.* "This someone" (*ko 'pi eṣaḥ*) is the poet himself. In the edition the first word is printed with an old form of अ that resembles ग्र.

### Verse 9

क्वासौ तत्तद्विबुधनगरीचक्रचूडामणीनां
ब्रह्मादीनां मुकुटपदवीरत्ननीराजिताङ्घ्रिः ।
चापल्यैकप्रवणहृदयः क्वाहमत्यन्तमुग्ध-
स्तत्कारुण्यं महदिति कदाप्येष सद्भिर्न हेयः ॥९॥

*kvāsau tat-tad-vibudha-nagarī-cakra-cūḍāmaṇīnāṁ*
*brahmādīnāṁ mukuṭa-padavī-ratna-nīrājitāṅghriḥ |*
*cāpalyaika-pravaṇa-hṛdayaḥ kvāham atyanta-mugdhas*
*tat kāruṇyaṁ mahad iti kadāpy eṣa sadbhir na heyaḥ ||9||*

*Word for word:* *kva* — where; *asau* — He; *tat-tat* — of all those; *vibudha* — of the gods; *nagarī* — of the cities; *cakra* — of the circle; *cūḍāmaṇīnām* — of the crest-jewels; *brahma* — of Brahma; *ādīnām* — and the others; *mukuṭa* — of the crowns; *padavī* — in the settings; *ratna* — by the jewels; *nīrājita* — honoured with lamps; *aṅghriḥ* — [whose] feet; *cāpalya* — to frivolity; *eka* — solely; *pravaṇa* — inclined; *hṛdayaḥ* — with heart; *kva* — where; *aham* — I; *atyanta* — utterly; *mugdhaḥ* — foolish; *tat* — His; *kāruṇyam* — compassion; *mahat* — great; *iti* — therefore; *kadā* — ever; *api* — at all; *eṣaḥ* — this one; *sadbhiḥ* — by the virtuous; *na* — not; *heyaḥ* — to be rejected.

**9.** Where is He, whose feet are honoured, as with the lamps of *arati*, by the jewels set in the crowns of Brahma and the others, the crest-jewels of the circle of all the cities of the gods? And where am I, utterly foolish, my heart inclined to frivolity alone? His compassion is great — therefore let the virtuous never reject this one.

### Verse 10

यद्यद्दृष्टं श्रुतमपि च यत्तस्य लीलाविलासै-
स्तत्तत्प्राणैरतिशयमहामूढचित्ताय यन्मे ।
भूयो भूयः कथितमिति यद्यद्धृतं तत्र तत्र
क्षुद्रोऽयं तत्कथयति कियत्तत्कृपाया वशः सन् ॥१०॥

*yad yad dṛṣṭaṁ śrutam api ca yat tasya līlā-vilāsais*
*tat-tat-prāṇair atiśaya-mahā-mūḍha-cittāya yan me |*
*bhūyo bhūyaḥ kathitam iti yad yad dhṛtaṁ tatra tatra*
*kṣudro 'yaṁ tat kathayati kiyat tat-kṛpāyā vaśaḥ san ||10||*

*Word for word:* *yat yat* — whatever; *dṛṣṭam* — was seen; *śrutam* — heard; *api* — also; *ca* — and; *yat* — what; *tasya* — of Him; *līlā* — of pastimes; *vilāsaiḥ* — with the sports; *tat-tat* — with those very; *prāṇaiḥ* — [whose] life; *atiśaya* — exceedingly; *mahā* — greatly; *mūḍha* — foolish; *cittāya* — to [one] of mind; *yat* — what; *me* — to me; *bhūyaḥ bhūyaḥ* — again and again; *kathitam* — was told; *iti* — thus; *yat yat* — whatever; *dhṛtam* — retained; *tatra tatra* — here and there; *kṣudraḥ* — insignificant; *ayam* — this; *tat* — that; *kathayati* — tells; *kiyat* — a little; *tat* — of His; *kṛpāyāḥ* — of the mercy; *vaśaḥ* — under the sway; *san* — being.

**10.** Whatever I saw, and what I also heard; what was told again and again to me, so exceedingly foolish of mind, by those whose very life is the play of His pastimes; whatever [I] retained here and there — of that this insignificant one tells a little, being under the sway of His mercy.

*Note.* An important testimony to the sources of the poem: part of it the author saw himself (he was a child while Mahaprabhu was present in this world), part he heard from His close companions. *Līlā-vilāsais tat-tat-prāṇaiḥ* — the analysis is tentative: "by those whose life is these pastimes."

### Verse 11

संपूर्णोऽयं भवति यदि वा नोद्यमस्तेन किं मे
यावत्तावत्प्रभुविलसितोत्कीर्त्तने भूरि भाग्यम् ।
यद्वा शक्तेः सममनुवदन्नैव हास्याय सोऽयं
यस्मान्नैतच्चरितमखिलं ब्रह्मणोऽपि प्रमेयम् ॥११॥

*sampūrṇo 'yaṁ bhavati yadi vā nodyamas tena kiṁ me*
*yāvat tāvat prabhu-vilasitotkīrtane bhūri bhāgyam |*
*yad vā śakteḥ samam anuvadan naiva hāsyāya so 'yaṁ*
*yasmān naitac caritam akhilaṁ brahmaṇo 'pi prameyam ||11||*

*Word for word:* *sampūrṇaḥ* — complete; *ayam* — this; *bhavati* — becomes; *yadi* — if; *vā* — or; *na* — not; *udyamaḥ* — effort; *tena* — with that; *kim* — what; *me* — to me; *yāvat* — as much as; *tāvat* — so much; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *vilasita* — of the pastimes; *utkīrtane* — in the glorification; *bhūri* — great; *bhāgyam* — good fortune; *yat vā* — or else; *śakteḥ* — to [one's] power; *samam* — in proportion; *anuvadan* — retelling; *na* — not; *eva* — at all; *hāsyāya* — for laughter; *saḥ* — that; *ayam* — this [one]; *yasmāt* — because; *na* — not; *etat* — this; *caritam* — life-story; *akhilam* — in its entirety; *brahmaṇaḥ* — for Brahma; *api* — even; *prameyam* — measurable.

**11.** Whether this effort is completed or not — what is that to me? In glorifying the pastimes of the Lord, however much [is told], so much is great good fortune. Or else: one who retells them in proportion to his power is no cause for laughter at all, since this life-story in its entirety cannot be measured even by Brahma.

### Verse 12

यद्येतस्मिन्नहह भविता दूषणं न प्रमादात्
किञ्चित्तस्मिन्न खलु सुधियामाग्रहो जातु भावी ।
यत्ते श्रीमच्चरणकमलद्वन्द्वगाथानुमत्ता-
स्तस्मादेषु क्षणमपि न मे वर्त्तते काप्यपेक्षा ॥१२॥

*yady etasminn ahaha bhavitā dūṣaṇaṁ na pramādāt*
*kiñcit tasminn na khalu sudhiyām āgraho jātu bhāvī |*
*yat te śrīmac-caraṇa-kamala-dvandva-gāthānumattās*
*tasmād eṣu kṣaṇam api na me vartate kāpy apekṣā ||12||*

*Word for word:* *yadi* — if; *etasmin* — in this; *ahaha* — alas; *bhavitā* — there will be; *dūṣaṇam* — a flaw; *na* — not; *pramādāt* — from carelessness; *kiñcit* — some; *tasmin* — on it; *na* — not; *khalu* — surely; *sudhiyām* — of the wise; *āgrahaḥ* — insistence; *jātu* — ever; *bhāvī* — will be; *yat* — because; *te* — they; *śrīmat* — of the beautiful; *caraṇa* — feet; *kamala* — of the lotuses; *dvandva* — of the pair; *gāthā* — with the songs; *anumattāḥ* — intoxicated; *tasmāt* — therefore; *eṣu* — about them; *kṣaṇam* — for a moment; *api* — even; *na* — not; *me* — to me; *vartate* — is; *kā* — any; *api* — at all; *apekṣā* — concern.

**12.** If in this [work], alas, there should be some flaw — though not from carelessness — the wise will surely never dwell on it, for they are intoxicated with songs of the pair of [His] beautiful lotus feet. Therefore I have no concern about them even for a moment.

*Note.* *Na pramādāt* in the first line — so also in the Gosvami edition (GGM); the sense "though not from carelessness" is rendered literally.

### Verse 13

श्रीमद्वृन्दावनवरवधूप्राणनाथः समस्तं
विश्वं प्रेमामृतलहरिभिर्निर्भरं प्लावयित्वा ।
तल्लीलामृतमपि मुहुः स्वादयित्वा विशेषं
भूयस्तासां निकटमगमत्तद्वियोगाक्षमोऽसौ ॥१३॥

*śrīmad-vṛndāvana-vara-vadhū-prāṇa-nāthaḥ samastaṁ*
*viśvaṁ premāmṛta-laharibhir nirbharaṁ plāvayitvā |*
*tal-līlāmṛtam api muhuḥ svādayitvā viśeṣaṁ*
*bhūyas tāsāṁ nikaṭam agamat tad-viyogākṣamo 'sau ||13||*

*Word for word:* *śrīmat* — of beautiful; *vṛndāvana* — of Vrindavana; *vara* — of the best; *vadhū* — of the maidens; *prāṇa* — of the life; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *samastam* — the whole; *viśvam* — universe; *prema* — of love; *amṛta* — of the nectar; *laharibhiḥ* — with the waves; *nirbharam* — to the brim; *plāvayitvā* — having flooded; *tat* — of those; *līlā* — of pastimes; *amṛtam* — the nectar; *api* — also; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *svādayitvā* — having given to taste; *viśeṣam* — especially; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *tāsām* — of them; *nikaṭam* — to the nearness; *agamat* — went; *tat* — from them; *viyoga* — separation; *akṣamaḥ* — unable to bear; *asau* — He.

**13.** The Lord of the life of the beautiful, best maidens of Vrindavana flooded the whole universe to the brim with waves of the nectar of love; again and again He gave [all] a special taste of the nectar of those pastimes; and then, unable to bear separation from those maidens, He went back to be near them once more.

*Note.* Here the poet explains **Mahaprabhu's disappearance**: Krishna returned to the gopis, without whom He could not bear to be. The link with verse 14 ("He disappeared") supports this reading.

### Verse 14

इत्थं तत्तद्विलसितसुधापूरमास्वाद्य भूयः
शिक्षाव्याजात्प्रथितकरुणे हन्त हान्तर्दधाने ।
एतत्प्राणाः कथमपि इहा जीवनैः संविसृष्टाः
केचिद्भूमौ करुणकरुणाः सन्ति केचित्प्रयाताः ॥१४॥

*itthaṁ tat-tad-vilasita-sudhā-pūram āsvādya bhūyaḥ*
*śikṣā-vyājāt prathita-karuṇe hanta hāntardadhāne |*
*etat-prāṇāḥ katham api ihā jīvanaiḥ saṁvisṛṣṭāḥ*
*kecid bhūmau karuṇa-karuṇāḥ santi kecit prayātāḥ ||14||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *tat-tat* — of those; *vilasita* — of pastimes; *sudhā* — of nectar; *pūram* — the flood; *āsvādya* — having tasted; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *śikṣā* — of teaching; *vyājāt* — under the pretext; *prathita* — made manifest; *karuṇe* — [He whose] compassion; *hanta* — alas; *hā* — alas; *antardadhāne* — [when He] disappeared; *etat* — He; *prāṇāḥ* — [whose] life; *katham* — some-; *api* — -how; *ihā* — here; *jīvanaiḥ* — by life; *saṁvisṛṣṭāḥ* — abandoned; *kecit* — some; *bhūmau* — on the earth; *karuṇa-karuṇāḥ* — most pitiable; *santi* — remain; *kecit* — others; *prayātāḥ* — departed.

**14.** Thus, having once more tasted the flood of the nectar of those pastimes, He whose compassion had been made manifest under the pretext of teaching — alas, alas! — disappeared. Those whose life He was remain here somehow, as if abandoned by life itself: some, most pitiable, are on the earth; others have departed [after Him].

*Note.* *Ihā* — the vowel is lengthened for the metre (the *mandakranta* requires a long syllable at this point). *Śikṣā-vyāja*, "the pretext of teaching": Chaitanya's preaching is only the outward reason for His coming; the inner reason is the tasting of His own pastimes (verse 13).

### Verse 15

हा गौरांग प्रियतम हहा हा प्रभो दीनबन्धो
हा हा कष्टं निजधनजनप्राणजातिस्वरूप ।
इत्थं भूयः करुणकरुणः क्रन्दतां वाक्प्रबन्ध-
श्चित्तं भित्तीरपि च शतधा हन्त सद्यः करोति ॥१५॥

*hā gaurāṅga priyatama hahā hā prabho dīna-bandho*
*hā hā kaṣṭaṁ nija-dhana-jana-prāṇa-jāti-svarūpa |*
*itthaṁ bhūyaḥ karuṇa-karuṇaḥ krandatāṁ vāk-prabandhaś*
*cittaṁ bhittīr api ca śatadhā hanta sadyaḥ karoti ||15||*

*Word for word:* *hā* — O; *gaurāṅga* — Gauranga; *priyatama* — dearest; *hahā hā* — alas; *prabho* — O Lord; *dīna* — of the wretched; *bandho* — O friend; *hā hā* — oh; *kaṣṭam* — woe; *nija* — our own; *dhana* — of wealth; *jana* — of kin; *prāṇa* — of life; *jāti* — of lineage; *svarūpa* — O very embodiment; *ittham* — thus; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *karuṇa-karuṇaḥ* — most piteous; *krandatām* — of those weeping; *vāk* — of words; *prabandhaḥ* — the stream; *cittam* — the heart; *bhittīḥ* — walls; *api* — even; *ca* — and; *śatadhā* — into a hundred pieces; *hanta* — ah; *sadyaḥ* — at once; *karoti* — makes.

**15.** "O Gauranga, dearest! Alas, alas, O Lord, friend of the wretched! Oh, oh, woe — You who were the very embodiment of our wealth, our kin, our life and our lineage!" Thus, again and again, the most piteous stream of words of those who wept at once broke the heart, and even walls, into a hundred pieces — ah!

### Verse 16

केचित्केचिद्बहुविकलितास्तद्वियोगाग्नितापै-
र्दृष्ट्वा विश्वं प्रलयसमयप्रायशून्यातिशून्यम् ।
अन्तर्बाष्पव्रणशतकृतां वेदनां तैर्विलापै-
र्दूरीकर्त्तुं रुरुदुरसकृद्धाहहेत्युच्चनादैः ॥१६॥

*kecit kecid bahu-vikalitās tad-viyogāgni-tāpair*
*dṛṣṭvā viśvaṁ pralaya-samaya-prāya-śūnyātiśūnyam |*
*antar-bāṣpa-vraṇa-śata-kṛtāṁ vedanāṁ tair vilāpair*
*dūrīkartuṁ rurudur asakṛd dhā hahety ucca-nādaiḥ ||16||*

*Word for word:* *kecit kecit* — some; *bahu* — greatly; *vikalitāḥ* — weakened; *tat* — from Him; *viyoga* — of separation; *agni* — of the fire; *tāpaiḥ* — by the heat; *dṛṣṭvā* — seeing; *viśvam* — the world; *pralaya* — of the dissolution of the universe; *samaya* — at the time; *prāya* — as; *śūnya* — empty; *atiśūnyam* — utterly empty; *antar* — of inner; *bāṣpa* — tears; *vraṇa* — of wounds; *śata* — by a hundred; *kṛtām* — caused; *vedanām* — the pain; *taiḥ* — with those; *vilāpaiḥ* — laments; *dūrī* — away; *kartum* — to drive; *ruruduḥ* — wept; *asakṛt* — incessantly; *hā* — ah; *haha* — ah; *iti* — thus; *ucca* — with loud; *nādaiḥ* — cries.

**16.** Some, utterly weakened by the heat of the fire of separation from Him, saw the world as empty, utterly empty, as at the time of the dissolution of the universe; and to drive away with those laments the pain caused by a hundred wounds of inward tears, they wept incessantly with loud cries of "Ah! Ah!"

### Verse 17

हाहा लीना भवति सततं क्षोभशोकाग्निपूरे
हाहा प्राणप्रियतम भवद्विप्रयोगे धरित्री ।
पूर्वं यासौ तव चरणयोः स्निग्धमुग्धैर्विहारैः
स्निग्धैरासीत् सुकृतसुकृता धन्यधन्यातिपुण्या ॥१७॥

*hāhā līnā bhavati satataṁ kṣobha-śokāgni-pūre*
*hāhā prāṇa-priyatama bhavad-viprayoge dharitrī |*
*pūrvaṁ yāsau tava caraṇayoḥ snigdha-mugdhair vihāraiḥ*
*snigdhair āsīt sukṛta-sukṛtā dhanya-dhanyāti-puṇyā ||17||*

*Word for word:* *hāhā* — alas; *līnā* — sunk; *bhavati* — becomes; *satatam* — constantly; *kṣobha* — of agitation; *śoka* — of grief; *agni* — of the fire; *pūre* — in the flood; *hāhā* — alas; *prāṇa* — than life; *priyatama* — O dearer; *bhavat* — from You; *viprayoge* — in separation; *dharitrī* — the earth; *pūrvam* — formerly; *yā* — who; *asau* — she; *tava* — of Your; *caraṇayoḥ* — of the feet; *snigdha* — with tender; *mugdhaiḥ* — charming; *vihāraiḥ* — wanderings; *snigdhaiḥ* — tender; *āsīt* — was; *sukṛta-sukṛtā* — most blessed; *dhanya-dhanyā* — most fortunate; *ati* — exceedingly; *puṇyā* — holy.

**17.** "Alas, alas, O You who are dearer than life! In separation from You the earth is constantly sunk in a flood of the fire of agitation and grief — she who formerly, through the tender, charming, tender wanderings of Your feet, was most blessed, most fortunate, exceedingly holy."

### Verse 18

किं किं तस्मादहह सुकृतं दीर्घदीर्घं समन्ता-
च्चक्रे पृथ्वी तव पदरसैर्यत्प्रकृष्टा रसासीत् ।
हाहा संप्रत्यपि विरहिता हन्त सर्वंसहेति
स्वीयं नाम प्रकरणवशादन्वितार्थं चकार ॥१८॥

*kiṁ kiṁ tasmād ahaha sukṛtaṁ dīrgha-dīrghaṁ samantāc*
*cakre pṛthvī tava pada-rasair yat prakṛṣṭā rasāsīt |*
*hāhā sampraty api virahitā hanta sarvaṁsaheti*
*svīyaṁ nāma prakaraṇa-vaśād anvitārthaṁ cakāra ||18||*

*Word for word:* *kim kim* — what; *tasmāt* — before that; *ahaha* — ah; *sukṛtam* — pious deeds; *dīrgha-dīrgham* — long, long; *samantāt* — everywhere; *cakre* — performed; *pṛthvī* — the earth; *tava* — of Your; *pada* — of the feet; *rasaiḥ* — with the juices; *yat* — that; *prakṛṣṭā* — supreme; *rasā* — Rasa; *āsīt* — was; *hāhā* — alas; *samprati* — now; *api* — but; *virahitā* — separated; *hanta* — ah; *sarvaṁsahā* — "All-enduring"; *iti* — thus; *svīyam* — her own; *nāma* — name; *prakaraṇa* — of circumstance; *vaśāt* — by the force; *anvita* — conforming; *artham* — to the meaning; *cakāra* — made.

**18.** "Ah, what long, long pious deeds did the earth perform everywhere before, that through the juices of Your feet she was Rasa in the highest sense, 'full of taste'? Alas, now, separated [from You] — ah! — by force of circumstance she has made her other name, Sarvamsaha, 'All-enduring', true to its meaning."

*Note.* A play on two Sanskrit names of the Earth: *rasā* ("earth", but also "full of *rasa*, of taste") and *sarvaṁsahā* ("earth", literally "bearing everything").

### Verse 19

हाहा नाथ प्रियतम मनोनाथ कारुण्यसिन्धो
निःसीमागःशमन दयित प्रेष्ठ हाहा हताः स्मः ।
सर्वो लोकस्तव चरणयोर्विप्रयोगेऽतिदुर्गे
लीनो दीनः श्वसिति परमैर्दुष्कृतानां समूहैः ॥१९॥

*hāhā nātha priyatama mano-nātha kāruṇya-sindho*
*niḥsīmāgaḥ-śamana dayita preṣṭha hāhā hatāḥ smaḥ |*
*sarvo lokas tava caraṇayor viprayoge 'tidurge*
*līno dīnaḥ śvasiti paramair duṣkṛtānāṁ samūhaiḥ ||19||*

*Word for word:* *hāhā* — alas; *nātha* — O Lord; *priyatama* — O dearest; *manaḥ* — of the heart; *nātha* — O lord; *kāruṇya* — of compassion; *sindho* — O ocean; *niḥsīma* — of boundless; *āgaḥ* — offences; *śamana* — O extinguisher; *dayita* — O beloved; *preṣṭha* — O dearest of all; *hāhā* — alas; *hatāḥ* — lost; *smaḥ* — we are; *sarvaḥ* — the whole; *lokaḥ* — world; *tava* — of Your; *caraṇayoḥ* — of the feet; *viprayoge* — in separation; *ati* — most; *durge* — impassable; *līnaḥ* — sunk; *dīnaḥ* — wretched; *śvasiti* — sighs; *paramaiḥ* — with the greatest; *duṣkṛtānām* — of misdeeds; *samūhaiḥ* — with heaps.

**19.** "Alas, O Lord, O dearest, O lord of our hearts, O ocean of compassion, O extinguisher of boundless offences, O beloved, O dearest of all — alas, we are lost! In this most impassable separation from Your feet the whole world, sunk [in grief] and wretched, sighs under heaps of the greatest misdeeds."

### Verse 20

ये ये स्निग्धाः परमसुहृदस्ते त एव प्रयाता-
स्ते ते धन्याः प्रभुचरणयोः प्रेममात्रैकसाध्याः ।
हा धिक् कष्टं प्रभुमपि च तं तं संगं समेत्य
प्राणान्तस्तद्विरहविकलाः सन्ति हा धिक् कठोराः ॥२०॥

*ye ye snigdhāḥ parama-suhṛdas te ta eva prayātās*
*te te dhanyāḥ prabhu-caraṇayoḥ prema-mātraika-sādhyāḥ |*
*hā dhik kaṣṭaṁ prabhum api ca taṁ taṁ saṅgaṁ sametya*
*prāṇāntas tad-viraha-vikalāḥ santi hā dhik kaṭhorāḥ ||20||*

*Word for word:* *ye ye* — those who; *snigdhāḥ* — tender; *parama* — closest; *suhṛdaḥ* — friends; *te te* — they; *eva* — alone; *prayātāḥ* — departed; *te te* — they; *dhanyāḥ* — blessed; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *caraṇayoḥ* — for the feet; *prema* — love; *mātra* — only; *eka* — sole; *sādhyāḥ* — [whose] goal; *hā* — oh; *dhik* — shame; *kaṣṭam* — woe; *prabhum* — the Lord; *api* — and; *ca* — also; *tam tam* — that very; *saṅgam* — association; *sametya* — having attained; *prāṇāḥ* — the life-breaths; *antaḥ* — within; *tat* — from Him; *viraha* — by separation; *vikalāḥ* — tormented; *santi* — remain; *hā* — oh; *dhik* — shame; *kaṭhorāḥ* — hard.

**20.** "Those who were tender, His closest friends — they alone have departed. Blessed are they, whose sole goal was love alone for the feet of the Lord. Oh, shame and woe! We met the Lord Himself and had that very association with Him, and yet our life-breaths, tormented by separation from Him, remain within. Oh, shame — how hard they are!"

*Note.* *Prāṇāntas* is parsed as *prāṇāḥ antaḥ* ("the breath of life within"). Compare verse 26.

### Verse 21

ये तच्छ्रीमत्पदकमलयोः सौरभीं माधुरीं वा
तामासाद्य क्षणमपि न यत्सर्वमेव त्यजन्ति ।
ते वा कष्टं किमुत पशवः किं नु वृक्षा विरूढाः
किं ग्रावाणः शिव शिव न वा चेतनाभिर्विहीनाः ॥२१॥

*ye tac-chrīmat-pada-kamalayoḥ saurabhīṁ mādhurīṁ vā*
*tām āsādya kṣaṇam api na yat sarvam eva tyajanti |*
*te vā kaṣṭaṁ kim uta paśavaḥ kiṁ nu vṛkṣā virūḍhāḥ*
*kiṁ grāvāṇaḥ śiva śiva na vā cetanābhir vihīnāḥ ||21||*

*Word for word:* *ye* — who; *tat* — His; *śrīmat* — beautiful; *pada* — of the feet; *kamalayoḥ* — of the lotuses; *saurabhīm* — the fragrance; *mādhurīm* — the sweetness; *vā* — or; *tām* — that; *āsādya* — having obtained; *kṣaṇam* — for a moment; *api* — even; *na* — not; *yat* — so that; *sarvam* — everything; *eva* — at once; *tyajanti* — abandon; *te* — they; *vā* — then; *kaṣṭam* — alas; *kim uta* — are they; *paśavaḥ* — beasts; *kim nu* — or; *vṛkṣāḥ* — trees; *virūḍhāḥ* — rooted; *kim* — or; *grāvāṇaḥ* — stones; *śiva śiva* — Heaven forbid; *na vā* — are they not; *cetanābhiḥ* — of consciousness; *vihīnāḥ* — devoid.

**21.** "Those who, having known even for a moment that fragrance or sweetness of His beautiful lotus feet, do not at once abandon everything — alas, what are they then? Beasts? Or trees rooted [in the ground]? Or stones? Heaven forbid — are they not devoid of consciousness?"

*Note.* *Śiva śiva* is an exclamation of horror and aversion, like "Heaven forbid!" It occurs many times in this passage.

### Verse 22

यत्पादाम्भोरुहयुगरसास्वादनेनैव तृप्ता-
स्त्यक्त्वैकान्तं धनजनगृहं प्रेममात्रैकसाध्याः ।
दीनाः सन्तः परमकृतिनो हन्त सन्तः समन्तात्
कान्तारान्तर्गिरिषु विपिनेष्वेवमेवं चरन्ति ॥२२॥

*yat-pādāmbhoruha-yuga-rasāsvādanenaiva tṛptās*
*tyaktvaikāntaṁ dhana-jana-gṛhaṁ prema-mātraika-sādhyāḥ |*
*dīnāḥ santaḥ parama-kṛtino hanta santaḥ samantāt*
*kāntārāntar giriṣu vipineṣv evam evaṁ caranti ||22||*

*Word for word:* *yat* — whose; *pāda* — of the feet; *ambhoruha* — of the lotuses; *yuga* — of the pair; *rasa* — of the juice; *āsvādanena* — by the tasting; *eva* — alone; *tṛptāḥ* — satisfied; *tyaktvā* — having abandoned; *ekāntam* — utterly; *dhana* — wealth; *jana* — kin; *gṛham* — home; *prema* — love; *mātra* — only; *eka* — sole; *sādhyāḥ* — [whose] goal; *dīnāḥ* — poor; *santaḥ* — being; *parama* — supremely; *kṛtinaḥ* — accomplished; *hanta* — ah; *santaḥ* — saints; *samantāt* — everywhere; *kāntāra* — of the wilderness; *antaḥ* — within; *giriṣu* — on the mountains; *vipineṣu* — in the forests; *evam evam* — just so; *caranti* — wander.

**22.** "Satisfied by the mere tasting of the juice of the pair of His lotus feet, having utterly abandoned wealth, kin and home, their sole goal love alone, these saints, supremely accomplished — ah! — wander about like this everywhere, poor: in the depths of the wilderness, on the mountains, in the forests."

*Note.* A play on the two meanings of *santaḥ*: "being" (poor) and "saints".

### Verse 23

श्रीमत्पादाम्बुजयुगरसं चक्षुषापीय गन्धं
तस्याघ्राय प्रणयमधुरं प्रेमसीधुं च पीत्वा ।
आस्वाद्यैतद्वचनमधुरं हन्त को जीवलोक-
स्तद्विच्छेदं शिव शिव हहा हा कथं हन्त सोढा ॥२३॥

*śrīmat-pādāmbuja-yuga-rasaṁ cakṣuṣāpīya gandhaṁ*
*tasyāghrāya praṇaya-madhuraṁ prema-sīdhuṁ ca pītvā |*
*āsvādyaitad-vacana-madhuraṁ hanta ko jīva-lokas*
*tad-vicchedaṁ śiva śiva hahā hā kathaṁ hanta soḍhā ||23||*

*Word for word:* *śrīmat* — of beautiful; *pāda* — feet; *ambuja* — of the lotuses; *yuga* — of the pair; *rasam* — the juice; *cakṣuṣā* — with the eye; *āpīya* — having drunk; *gandham* — the fragrance; *tasya* — of it; *āghrāya* — having inhaled; *praṇaya* — with affection; *madhuram* — sweet; *prema* — of love; *sīdhum* — the wine; *ca* — and; *pītvā* — having drunk; *āsvādya* — having tasted; *etat* — His; *vacana* — of words; *madhuram* — the sweetness; *hanta* — ah; *kaḥ* — what; *jīva* — of the living; *lokaḥ* — person; *tat* — from Him; *vicchedam* — separation; *śiva śiva* — Heaven forbid; *hahā hā* — alas; *katham* — how; *hanta* — ah; *soḍhā* — will bear.

**23.** "Having drunk with the eyes the juice of the pair of His beautiful lotus feet, having inhaled their fragrance, having drunk the wine of love, sweet with affection, having tasted the sweetness of His words — ah, who among the living will bear separation from Him? Heaven forbid! Alas, alas — how, ah, will one bear it?"

*Note.* The verse lists all the senses: sight, smell, taste and hearing. The very fullness of that association makes the separation unbearable.

### Verse 24

अद्याप्येतच्चरणकमलद्वन्द्वगन्धेन सर्वे
त्यक्तासङ्गा निरवधिगलत्सर्वबन्धाः समन्तात् ।
स्वैरं स्वैरं नटनरभसैः कीर्त्तनैः सञ्चरन्तो
वर्त्तन्ते तद्विरहदहनं कः सहेतास्य तस्य ॥२४॥

*adyāpy etac-caraṇa-kamala-dvandva-gandhena sarve*
*tyaktāsaṅgā niravadhi-galat-sarva-bandhāḥ samantāt |*
*svairaṁ svairaṁ naṭana-rabhasaiḥ kīrtanaiḥ sañcaranto*
*vartante tad-viraha-dahanaṁ kaḥ sahetāsya tasya ||24||*

*Word for word:* *adya* — today; *api* — even; *etat* — His; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *kamala* — of the lotuses; *dvandva* — of the pair; *gandhena* — by the fragrance; *sarve* — all; *tyakta* — having given up; *āsaṅgāḥ* — attachments; *niravadhi* — endlessly; *galat* — falling away; *sarva* — all; *bandhāḥ* — [whose] bonds; *samantāt* — everywhere; *svairam svairam* — quite freely; *naṭana* — of dancing; *rabhasaiḥ* — with the raptures; *kīrtanaiḥ* — with kirtanas; *sañcarantaḥ* — wandering; *vartante* — continue; *tat* — from Him; *viraha* — of separation; *dahanam* — the fire; *kaḥ* — who; *saheta* — could bear; *asya* — of Him; *tasya* — of Him.

**24.** "Even today, by the fragrance of the pair of His lotus feet, all [people] everywhere give up their attachments; all their bonds fall away without end, and they go on wandering quite freely, in the raptures of dancing, with kirtanas. Who could bear the fire of separation from Him — from Him Himself?"

*Note.* "Even today" means the time when the poem was written, after Mahaprabhu's disappearance: the kirtana goes on.

### Verse 25

कथं वा दृष्टौ तौ परमकरुणौ हन्त चरणौ
कथं वा दम्भोलीप्रकरकठिनोऽयं बत जनः ।
कथं वा तत्प्रेम्णः पदमयमहो तिष्ठति च वा
कथं तद्विच्छेदे शिव शिव विधेर्वैशसमिदम् ॥२५॥

*kathaṁ vā dṛṣṭau tau parama-karuṇau hanta caraṇau*
*kathaṁ vā dambholī-prakara-kaṭhino 'yaṁ bata janaḥ |*
*kathaṁ vā tat-premṇaḥ padam ayam aho tiṣṭhati ca vā*
*kathaṁ tad-vicchede śiva śiva vidher vaiśasam idam ||25||*

*Word for word:* *katham* — how; *vā* — then; *dṛṣṭau* — were seen; *tau* — those; *parama* — with supreme; *karuṇau* — [full of] compassion; *hanta* — ah; *caraṇau* — feet; *katham* — how; *vā* — then; *dambholī* — of thunderbolts; *prakara* — a heap; *kaṭhinaḥ* — hard [as]; *ayam* — this; *bata* — alas; *janaḥ* — person; *katham* — how; *vā* — then; *tat* — for Him; *premṇaḥ* — of love; *padam* — the abode; *ayam* — he; *aho* — oh; *tiṣṭhati* — remains; *ca* — and; *vā* — then; *katham* — how; *tat* — from Him; *vicchede* — in separation; *śiva śiva* — Heaven forbid; *vidheḥ* — of fate; *vaiśasam* — slaughter; *idam* — this.

**25.** "How then were those supremely compassionate feet ever seen, ah? And how, alas, is this person as hard as a heap of thunderbolts? And how, oh, does he still remain an abode of love for Him? And how — Heaven forbid! — [has come] this slaughter wrought by fate, in separation from Him?"

*Note.* *Dambholi* is the vajra, Indra's thunderbolt weapon; in Sanskrit it is the standard of indestructible hardness (the same word is used of diamond). *Prakara* means "heap, multitude": the man is harder not than one vajra but than a whole heap of them. With this verse the metre changes to *shikharini*. The syntax of the verse is broken — a deliberate device: speech falters from grief.

### Verse 26

जगच्छून्यं मन्ये क्षितिरपि च दुःखाग्निनिवहे
विलीना लीयन्ते सकल मनुजास्तत्र विकलाः ।
तथाप्येते प्राणाः शिव शिव न गच्छन्ति विधुरा
अहो चित्रं शिव शिव विधिर्वामचरितः ॥२६॥

*jagac chūnyaṁ manye kṣitir api ca duḥkhāgni-nivahe*
*vilīnā līyante sakala-manujās tatra vikalāḥ |*
*tathāpy ete prāṇāḥ śiva śiva na gacchanti vidhurā*
*aho citraṁ śiva śiva vidhir vāma-caritaḥ ||26||*

*Word for word:* *jagat* — the world; *śūnyam* — empty; *manye* — I think; *kṣitiḥ* — the earth; *api* — also; *ca* — and; *duḥkha* — of grief; *agni* — of the fire; *nivahe* — in the mass; *vilīnā* — melted; *līyante* — melt; *sakala* — all; *manujāḥ* — people; *tatra* — there; *vikalāḥ* — exhausted; *tathā api* — and yet; *ete* — these; *prāṇāḥ* — life-breaths; *śiva śiva* — Heaven forbid; *na* — not; *gacchanti* — depart; *vidhurāḥ* — bereaved; *aho* — oh; *citram* — wonder; *śiva śiva* — Heaven forbid; *vidhiḥ* — fate; *vāma* — perverse; *caritaḥ* — in conduct.

**26.** "The world, I think, is empty; the earth too has melted in the mass of the fire of grief, and all people, exhausted, are melting there. And yet these bereaved life-breaths — Heaven forbid! — do not depart. Oh, what a wonder! Heaven forbid! How perverse are the ways of fate!"

*Note.* The last line is metrically incomplete: 15 syllables instead of 17. So also in the Gosvami edition (GGM); the lacuna apparently goes back to a common manuscript tradition (?).

### Verse 27

अहो अद्याप्यस्य प्रियगुणगणानां लवमपि
क्षणं संशृण्वन्तः कति कति न देहत्यज इह ।
सदा श्रुत्वा दृष्ट्वा सततमनुभूयापि च सुखं
विना तं जीवामः शिव शिव महद्दुष्कृतमिदम् ॥२७॥

*aho adyāpy asya priya-guṇa-gaṇānāṁ lavam api*
*kṣaṇaṁ saṁśṛṇvantaḥ kati kati na deha-tyaja iha |*
*sadā śrutvā dṛṣṭvā satatam anubhūyāpi ca sukhaṁ*
*vinā taṁ jīvāmaḥ śiva śiva mahad duṣkṛtam idam ||27||*

*Word for word:* *aho* — oh; *adya* — today; *api* — even; *asya* — of His; *priya* — dear; *guṇa* — of qualities; *gaṇānām* — of the multitude; *lavam* — a particle; *api* — even; *kṣaṇam* — for a moment; *saṁśṛṇvantaḥ* — hearing; *kati kati* — how many; *na* — not; *deha* — the body; *tyajaḥ* — [who have] given up; *iha* — here; *sadā* — always; *śrutvā* — having heard; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *satatam* — constantly; *anubhūya* — having experienced; *api* — also; *ca* — and; *sukham* — happiness; *vinā* — without; *tam* — Him; *jīvāmaḥ* — we live; *śiva śiva* — Heaven forbid; *mahat* — great; *duṣkṛtam* — sin; *idam* — this.

**27.** "Oh, even today how many here, hearing for a single moment even a particle of the multitude of His dear qualities, have given up the body! And we, who always heard [Him], saw [Him] and constantly experienced happiness, live without Him. Heaven forbid! This is a great sin."

*Note.* The sense: others give up the body out of love as soon as they hear of Him, while we, who saw Him, remain alive — and in this lies our guilt. The contrast in the second half of the verse and the link with verses 20 and 26 support this reading. A misprint in the edition: संश्रृण्वन्तः → संशृण्वन्तः.

### Verse 28

अहो धन्यैवेयं क्षितिरतितरां श्रीचरणयो-
रसैः पूर्णा नाम्ना गुणगणमहिम्ना च महता ।
तदेतद्विच्छेदानलविदलितेयं दलति नो
न जानीमः सीमां विधिविलसितस्य क्षणमपि ॥२८॥

*aho dhanyaiveyaṁ kṣitir atitarāṁ śrī-caraṇayo*
*rasaiḥ pūrṇā nāmnā guṇa-gaṇa-mahimnā ca mahatā |*
*tad etad-vicchedānala-vidaliteyaṁ dalati no*
*na jānīmaḥ sīmāṁ vidhi-vilasitasya kṣaṇam api ||28||*

*Word for word:* *aho* — oh; *dhanyā* — fortunate; *eva* — truly; *iyam* — this; *kṣitiḥ* — earth; *atitarām* — beyond measure; *śrī* — of beautiful; *caraṇayoḥ* — of the feet; *rasaiḥ* — with the juices; *pūrṇā* — full; *nāmnā* — with the Name; *guṇa* — of qualities; *gaṇa* — of the multitude; *mahimnā* — with the glory; *ca* — and; *mahatā* — great; *tat* — yet; *etat* — from Him; *viccheda* — of separation; *anala* — by the fire; *vidalitā* — torn apart; *iyam* — she; *dalati* — splits; *no* — not; *na* — not; *jānīmaḥ* — we know; *sīmām* — the limit; *vidhi* — of fate; *vilasitasya* — of the play; *kṣaṇam* — for a moment; *api* — even.

**28.** "Oh, truly fortunate beyond measure [was] this earth, full of the juices of His beautiful feet, of His Name, and of the great glory of the multitude of His qualities! Yet now, torn apart by the fire of separation from Him, she does not split asunder. We do not know, even for a moment, the limit of the play of fate."

*Note.* A paradox: the earth is "torn apart" (*vidalitā*) yet "does not split" (*dalati no*). It is the same thought as that of the life which does not depart (verses 20 and 26).

### Verse 29

इतीहोष्णं दीर्घं श्वसितमिदमुच्चैः प्रलपितं
वपुः क्षीणं क्षीणं नयनजलमत्यन्तबहुलम् ।
वहन्तोऽमी स्मृत्वा प्रियगुणगणं भूरि करुणं
रुदन्तोऽविश्रान्तं बत मुमुहुराश्चर्यमिति तत् ॥२९॥

*itīhoṣṇaṁ dīrghaṁ śvasitam idam uccaiḥ pralapitaṁ*
*vapuḥ kṣīṇaṁ kṣīṇaṁ nayana-jalam atyanta-bahulam |*
*vahanto 'mī smṛtvā priya-guṇa-gaṇaṁ bhūri karuṇaṁ*
*rudanto 'viśrāntaṁ bata mumuhur āścaryam iti tat ||29||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *iha* — here; *uṣṇam* — hot; *dīrgham* — long; *śvasitam* — breathing; *idam* — this; *uccaiḥ* — loud; *pralapitam* — lamentation; *vapuḥ* — body; *kṣīṇam kṣīṇam* — ever more wasted; *nayana* — of the eyes; *jalam* — water; *atyanta* — extremely; *bahulam* — abundant; *vahantaḥ* — bearing; *amī* — they; *smṛtvā* — having remembered; *priya* — dear; *guṇa* — of qualities; *gaṇam* — the multitude; *bhūri* — most; *karuṇam* — piteously; *rudantaḥ* — weeping; *aviśrāntam* — without rest; *bata* — alas; *mumuhuḥ* — swooned; *āścaryam* — a wonder; *iti* — thus; *tat* — that.

**29.** Thus, here, bearing these hot, long sighs and loud lamentations, a body wasting away more and more, and a most abundant water of the eyes, they remembered the multitude of His dear qualities, wept most piteously without rest, and — alas — swooned again and again. That was a wonder.

*Note.* The edition has *rudanto viśrāntam*; we read it with the omitted avagraha sign: *rudanto 'viśrāntam* ("without rest"). In the first word the anusvara is almost worn away in the print; *-ṣṇaṁ* is restored from the metre.

*Iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahākāvye prathamaḥ sargaḥ* — Thus ends the first sarga of the mahakavya "Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita".

---

## Sarga Two — verses 1–122

**Metre:** *vaṁśastha* (12 syllables per pada); verses 120–122 — *viyoginī*.
**Contents of the passage:**
- 1–8 — the glory of Navadvipa and the Ganga. Verses 5–8 form a *kalāpaka*: four verses, one sentence.
- 9–11 — the inhabitants of Navadvipa; Advaita.
- 12–18 — Srivasa, Jagannatha Mishra and Shachi; their eight daughters pass away.
- 19–21 — Vishvarupa.
- 22–24 — Shachi's pregnancy of thirteen months.
- 25–31 — spring comes before its time and adorns herself for the Lord's coming (27–31 are a *kulaka*).
- 32–37 — the full-moon night of Phalguna; the signs before the birth.
- 38–44 — the appearance of the Lord; the eclipse and the cries of "Hari!"; the horoscope.
- 45–55 — the beauty of the world serves each feature of His form.
- 56–59 — Nilambara Chakravarti; the birth rites.
- 60–62 — infancy; the name Vishvambhara.
- 63–67 — childhood play, dancing, first steps.
- 68–79 — Shachi binds Him; Nimai, seated on a heap of pots, teaches His mother non-duality; He throws a clod of earth.
- 80–85 — Shachi falls senseless; the wonder of the two coconuts.
- 86–89 — night: unseen guests, the jingling of anklets from bare feet.
- 90–100 — Vishvarupa takes sannyasa; the parents' grief; Nimai consoles them.
- 101–107 — play with His companions; Jagannatha Mishra's dream.
- 108–112 — Nimai teaches His mother to keep Ekadashi; "I am going" — He falls senseless.
- 113–116 — He comes to Himself; study in the teacher's house.
- 117–122 — Jagannatha Mishra's illness and passing on the bank of the Ganga; Shachi's lament.

### Verse 1

इयं मही भाग्यवती महीयसी
दिवोऽपि दिव्यादपि निर्मलैर्गुणैः ।
महान्ति रत्नानि यदा दधात्यतो
दधौ नवद्वीपमतीव दुर्लभम् ॥१॥

*iyaṁ mahī bhāgyavatī mahīyasī*
*divo 'pi divyād api nirmalair guṇaiḥ |*
*mahānti ratnāni yadā dadhāty ato*
*dadhau navadvīpam atīva durlabham ||1||*

*Word for word:* *iyam* — this; *mahī* — earth; *bhāgyavatī* — fortunate; *mahīyasī* — greatest; *divaḥ* — than heaven; *api* — even; *divyāt* — than the heavenly [world]; *api* — even; *nirmalaiḥ* — by pure; *guṇaiḥ* — by qualities; *mahānti* — great; *ratnāni* — jewels; *yadā* — since; *dadhāti* — bears; *ataḥ* — therefore; *dadhau* — bore; *navadvīpam* — Navadvipa; *atīva* — exceedingly; *durlabham* — rare.

**1.** This earth is fortunate: by the purity of her qualities she is greater than heaven, greater even than all that is heavenly. Since she is wont to bear great jewels, she therefore bore Navadvipa, a jewel exceedingly rare.

### Verse 2

अनेकधा सञ्चितभाग्यसञ्चयं
समस्तमेकत्र विधाय सर्वतः ।
महीरुहैरुत्पुलकेयमुत्सुका
दधौ नवद्वीप इति प्रथां किमु ॥२॥

*anekadhā sañcita-bhāgya-sañcayaṁ*
*samastam ekatra vidhāya sarvataḥ |*
*mahīruhair utpulakeyam utsukā*
*dadhau navadvīpa iti prathāṁ kimu ||2||*

*Word for word:* *anekadhā* — in many ways; *sañcita* — of accumulated; *bhāgya* — of good fortune; *sañcayam* — the store; *samastam* — entire; *ekatra* — in one place; *vidhāya* — having put; *sarvataḥ* — from everywhere; *mahīruhaiḥ* — with trees; *utpulakā* — with hair standing on end; *iyam* — she; *utsukā* — eager; *dadhau* — took; *navadvīpaḥ* — "Navadvipa"; *iti* — thus; *prathām* — the fame, the name; *kimu* — was it not…?

**2.** Was it not because this eager earth, her hair standing on end in the form of trees, gathered from everywhere into one place the whole store of good fortune she had amassed in many ways, that she won the renowned name "Navadvipa"?

*Note.* *Mahīruha*, "that which grows from the earth", is a tree. Trees as the *pulaka* (the hairs that stand on end in ecstasy) on the body of the Earth are a classical image of Sanskrit poetry.

### Verse 3

प्रभुः कदा वावतरिष्यतीत्यदो
विचिन्तयन्त्या मनसि प्रफुल्लया ।
मनोरथाक्रान्तिवशादनेकशः
सतां पदाब्जानुगतिर्यया दधे ॥३॥

*prabhuḥ kadā vāvatariṣyatīty ado*
*vicintayantyā manasi praphullayā |*
*manorathākrānti-vaśād anekaśaḥ*
*satāṁ padābjānugatir yayā dadhe ||3||*

*Word for word:* *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *kadā* — when; *vā* — indeed; *avatariṣyati* — will descend; *iti* — thus; *adaḥ* — this; *vicintayantyā* — by her who was pondering; *manasi* — in the mind; *praphullayā* — by her who was blossoming; *manoratha* — of desire; *ākrānti* — of the onset; *vaśāt* — by the force; *anekaśaḥ* — many times; *satām* — of the saintly; *pada* — of the feet; *abja* — of the lotuses; *anugatiḥ* — the following (the tread); *yayā* — by whom; *dadhe* — was borne.

**3.** "When indeed will the Lord descend?" — so she pondered, blossoming in her heart; and, carried away by the force of this longing, again and again she bore the tread of the lotus feet of the saintly.

*Note.* The earth, awaiting the Lord, "practises" on the saints in the meantime: she receives their steps as a foretaste of His.

### Verse 4

इयं नवद्वीपमिषेण मेदिनी
दधार भूयो मथुरामिवापराम् ।
वदेदमुष्याः सुकृतानि को नु वा
प्रभोः पदस्पर्शरसाकुलात्मनः ॥४॥

*iyaṁ navadvīpa-miṣeṇa medinī*
*dadhāra bhūyo mathurām ivāparām |*
*vaded amuṣyāḥ sukṛtāni ko nu vā*
*prabhoḥ pada-sparśa-rasākulātmanaḥ ||4||*

*Word for word:* *iyam* — this; *navadvīpa* — of Navadvipa; *miṣeṇa* — in the guise; *medinī* — earth; *dadhāra* — bore; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *mathurām* — Mathura; *iva* — as if; *aparām* — another; *vadet* — could tell; *amuṣyāḥ* — of her; *sukṛtāni* — the pious deeds; *kaḥ* — who; *nu vā* — indeed; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *pada* — of the feet; *sparśa* — of the touch; *rasa* — with the delight; *ākula* — overwhelmed; *ātmanaḥ* — [of her] whose soul.

**4.** In the guise of Navadvipa this earth bore once again, as it were, a second Mathura. Who indeed could tell the pious deeds of her whose soul is overwhelmed with the delight of the touch of the Lord's feet?

*Note.* Mathura is the birthplace of Krishna; Navadvipa, the birthplace of Gauranga, is a "second Mathura".

### Verse 5

आप्लाव्य या धूर्जटिसज्जटातटीं
कपालमालाच्छटया समन्विताम् ।
शशाङ्कलेखाप्रतिबिम्बरूपिणी-
मलब्धपूर्वां शफरीं समासदत् ॥५॥

*āplāvya yā dhūrjaṭi-saj-jaṭā-taṭīṁ*
*kapāla-mālā-cchaṭayā samanvitām |*
*śaśāṅka-lekhā-pratibimba-rūpiṇīm*
*alabdha-pūrvāṁ śapharīṁ samāsadat ||5||*

*Word for word:* *āplāvya* — having bathed; *yā* — who; *dhūrjaṭi* — of Dhurjati; *sat* — of the beautiful; *jaṭā* — of the matted locks; *taṭīm* — the slope; *kapāla* — of skulls; *mālā* — of the garland; *chaṭayā* — with the gleam; *samanvitām* — endowed; *śaśāṅka* — of the moon; *lekhā* — of the crescent; *pratibimba* — of the reflection; *rūpiṇīm* — having the form; *alabdha* — not obtained; *pūrvām* — before; *śapharīm* — a *śapharī* fish; *samāsadat* — obtained.

**5.** She bathed the slope of Shiva's beautiful matted locks, where the garland of skulls gleams, and there caught a little *shaphari* fish such as she had never caught before — the reflection of the crescent moon.

*Note.* *Dhūrjaṭi*, "he who wears heavy matted locks", is a name of Shiva. The Ganga, falling from heaven, passes through Shiva's hair; the crescent moon on his head is reflected in her water and looks like a silvery *śapharī* fish. The subject, "she" (the Ganga), is named outright only in verse 6: verses 5–8 are one sentence.

### Verse 6

प्रभोः पदाम्भोजयुगस्य पावनी
धारा मनोज्ञा मधुनो महीयसः ।
चकार यत्रास्पदमुत्सुका सती
समन्ततोऽसौ विमलाम्बुवाहिनी ॥६॥

*prabhoḥ padāmbhoja-yugasya pāvanī*
*dhārā manojñā madhuno mahīyasaḥ |*
*cakāra yatrāspadam utsukā satī*
*samantato 'sau vimalāmbu-vāhinī ||6||*

*Word for word:* *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *pada* — of the feet; *ambhoja* — of the lotuses; *yugasya* — of the pair; *pāvanī* — purifying; *dhārā* — stream; *manojñā* — charming; *madhunaḥ* — of honey; *mahīyasaḥ* — of great; *cakāra* — made; *yatra* — where; *āspadam* — an abode; *utsukā* — eager; *satī* — being; *samantataḥ* — on all sides; *asau* — she; *vimala* — pure; *ambu* — waters; *vāhinī* — carrying.

**6.** She is the purifying, charming stream of the great honey of the Lord's two lotus feet; and here [in Navadvipa], full of eagerness and carrying pure waters, she made her abode, [embracing it] on all sides.

*Note.* According to the Puranas, the Ganga flows from the foot of Vishnu; therefore her water is "the honey of His lotus feet".

### Verse 7

द्रवस्वरूपापि भवाब्धिशोषिणी
शुभ्रापि यासीद्धृतकृष्णविग्रहा ।
क्षित्याश्रितापि द्युनदीति विश्रुता
भ्रमापहापि भ्रमिविभ्रमावहा ॥७॥

*drava-svarūpāpi bhavābdhi-śoṣiṇī*
*śubhrāpi yāsīd dhṛta-kṛṣṇa-vigrahā |*
*kṣity-āśritāpi dyunadīti viśrutā*
*bhramāpahāpi bhrami-vibhramāvahā ||7||*

*Word for word:* *drava* — liquid; *svarūpā* — by nature; *api* — though; *bhava* — of worldly existence; *abdhi* — the ocean; *śoṣiṇī* — drying up; *śubhrā* — white; *api* — though; *yā* — who; *āsīt* — was; *dhṛta* — having assumed; *kṛṣṇa* — a dark; *vigrahā* — body; *kṣiti* — on the earth; *āśritā* — resting; *api* — though; *dyu* — heavenly; *nadī* — river; *iti* — thus; *viśrutā* — famed; *bhrama* — delusion; *apahā* — removing; *api* — though; *bhrami* — of whirlpools; *vibhrama* — the play; *āvahā* — bringing.

**7.** Though liquid by nature, she dries up the ocean of worldly existence; though white, she has assumed a dark body; though resting on the earth, she is famed as the heavenly river; though she dispels delusion, she brings the whirling play of eddies.

*Note.* The figure of *virodhābhāsa*, "apparent contradiction": each is resolved by a double meaning. *Kṛṣṇa-vigraha* is "a dark body", but also "the body of Krishna": the Ganga issues from the foot of Vishnu. *Bhrama* is "delusion", *bhrami* "whirling, an eddy".

### Verse 8

सेयं नवद्वीपभुवो महीयसीं
शोभामिवाधाय तदन्तवासिनी ।
प्रभोः पदाम्भोजयुगस्य सौरभ-
प्राप्त्यै बभूवोत्कलिकाकुलीकृता ॥८॥
(चतुर्भिः कलापकम्)

*seyaṁ navadvīpa-bhuvo mahīyasīṁ*
*śobhām ivādhāya tad-anta-vāsinī |*
*prabhoḥ padāmbhoja-yugasya saurabha-*
*prāptyai babhūvotkalikākulīkṛtā ||8||*

*Word for word:* *sā* — she; *iyam* — this; *navadvīpa* — of Navadvipa; *bhuvaḥ* — to the land; *mahīyasīm* — the greatest; *śobhām* — beauty; *iva* — as if; *ādhāya* — having imparted; *tat* — of it; *anta* — at the edge; *vāsinī* — dwelling; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *pada* — of the feet; *ambhoja* — of the lotuses; *yugasya* — of the pair; *saurabha* — of the fragrance; *prāptyai* — for the obtaining; *babhūva* — became; *utkalikā* — with waves (with longing); *ākulī-kṛtā* — agitated.

**8.** And she, dwelling at the edge of Navadvipa as if to impart the greatest beauty to that land, became all astir with waves of longing to obtain the fragrance of the Lord's two lotus feet.

*Note.* The edition prints «शोभामिवाधायत दन्तवासिनी», which makes no sense. We divide: *iva ādhāya tad-anta-vāsinī*, "as if imparting…, dwelling at its edge". A play on words: *utkalikā* is both "wave" and "longing". *Caturbhiḥ kalāpakam* — "a *kalāpaka* of four [verses]".

### Verse 9

वसन्ति यत्र क्षितिदेवसत्तमाः
सदा सदाचारपराः परायणाः ।
निरन्तरं वेदविधानकर्म्मसु
श्रुतिस्मृतीनां विधयः शरीरिणः ॥९॥

*vasanti yatra kṣiti-deva-sattamāḥ*
*sadā sad-ācāra-parāḥ parāyaṇāḥ |*
*nirantaraṁ veda-vidhāna-karmasu*
*śruti-smṛtīnāṁ vidhayaḥ śarīriṇaḥ ||9||*

*Word for word:* *vasanti* — live; *yatra* — where; *kṣiti* — of the earth; *deva* — gods; *sattamāḥ* — the best; *sadā* — always; *sat* — to good; *ācāra* — conduct; *parāḥ* — devoted; *parāyaṇāḥ* — given over to the Supreme; *nirantaram* — unceasingly; *veda* — by the Vedas; *vidhāna* — enjoined; *karmasu* — in rites; *śruti* — of shruti; *smṛtīnām* — and of smriti; *vidhayaḥ* — the injunctions; *śarīriṇaḥ* — embodied.

**9.** There live the best of the brahmanas, the "gods on earth". Ever devoted to righteous conduct, given over to the Supreme, unceasingly [engaged] in the rites enjoined by the Vedas, they are the injunctions of shruti and smriti in bodily form.

*Note.* *Kṣiti-deva* ("god of the earth") is a traditional designation of a brahmana.

### Verse 10

प्रभावभाजां भिषजां महत्तमाः
स्वधर्म्मनिष्ठाश्च विशां वराः परे ।
प्रतिष्ठया निःसहशुभ्रया सदा
समन्विता यत्र वसन्ति मानवाः ॥१०॥

*prabhāva-bhājāṁ bhiṣajāṁ mahattamāḥ*
*sva-dharma-niṣṭhāś ca viśāṁ varāḥ pare |*
*pratiṣṭhayā niḥsaha-śubhrayā sadā*
*samanvitā yatra vasanti mānavāḥ ||10||*

*Word for word:* *prabhāva* — power; *bhājām* — of those possessing; *bhiṣajām* — of physicians; *mahattamāḥ* — the greatest; *sva* — to their own; *dharma* — dharma; *niṣṭhāḥ* — faithful; *ca* — and; *viśām* — of the vaishyas; *varāḥ* — the best; *pare* — others; *pratiṣṭhayā* — with renown; *niḥsaha* — unsurpassed; *śubhrayā* — with bright; *sadā* — always; *samanvitāḥ* — endowed; *yatra* — where; *vasanti* — live; *mānavāḥ* — people.

**10.** There live the greatest of able physicians, the best of the vaishyas, faithful to their own dharma, and other people too — all ever endowed with bright, unsurpassed renown.

*Note.* *Niḥsaha*, "irresistible, unsurpassed": so in both editions (Goswami's, GGM, included), so no conjecture is needed. *Bhiṣaj* — physicians, the *vaidya* caste, to which Murari Gupta and Kavi Karnapura himself belonged.

### Verse 11

यमेतमद्वैतमहाशयः स्वयं
सतां महिम्ना महितो महीयसा ।
अलञ्चकारैतद् यदीयभावतः
प्रभुर्धरण्यां मनुजैर्विलोकितः ॥११॥

*yam etam advaita-mahāśayaḥ svayaṁ*
*satāṁ mahimnā mahito mahīyasā |*
*alañcakāraitad yadīya-bhāvataḥ*
*prabhur dharaṇyāṁ manujair vilokitaḥ ||11||*

*Word for word:* *yam* — which; *etam* — this; *advaita* — Advaita; *mahāśayaḥ* — the great-hearted; *svayam* — Himself; *satām* — by the saintly; *mahimnā* — for the greatness; *mahitaḥ* — honoured; *mahīyasā* — for the supreme; *alañcakāra* — adorned; *etat* — this; *yadīya* — whose; *bhāvataḥ* — through the love; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *dharaṇyām* — on earth; *manujaiḥ* — by people; *vilokitaḥ* — was beheld.

**11.** This [town] the great-hearted Advaita Himself adorned, He who is honoured by the saintly for His supreme greatness; and it was through His love that people beheld the Lord on earth.

*Note.* According to tradition, Mahaprabhu descended in answer to the prayers of Advaita Acharya (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 3). The syntax *yam etam … etad* is rough (so too in GGM): the masculine *yam etam* refers to Navadvipa.

### Verse 12

उवास यत्रानिशमत्युदारधी-
रधीतसर्वागमवेदकोविदः ।
सतां वरिष्ठः परमो महाशयः
श्रीवासनामा द्विजवंशचन्द्रमाः ॥१२॥

*uvāsa yatrāniśam atyudāra-dhīr*
*adhīta-sarvāgama-veda-kovidaḥ |*
*satāṁ variṣṭhaḥ paramo mahāśayaḥ*
*śrīvāsa-nāmā dvija-vaṁśa-candramāḥ ||12||*

*Word for word:* *uvāsa* — lived; *yatra* — where; *aniśam* — constantly; *ati* — very; *udāra* — generous; *dhīḥ* — [of] mind; *adhīta* — having studied; *sarva* — all; *āgama* — the agamas; *veda* — the Vedas; *kovidaḥ* — expert; *satām* — of the saintly; *variṣṭhaḥ* — the best; *paramaḥ* — supreme; *mahāśayaḥ* — great-souled; *śrīvāsa* — Srivasa; *nāmā* — by name; *dvija* — of the twice-born; *vaṁśa* — of the race; *candramāḥ* — the moon.

**12.** There constantly lived one named Srivasa — exceedingly generous of mind, expert, having studied all the agamas and Vedas, the best of the saintly, supremely great-souled, the moon of the race of the brahmanas.

### Verse 13

बभौ महावंशसमुद्भवः सुधी-
रनेकविद्याम्बुधिपारपण्डितः ।
द्विजातिवंशैकवतंसवद्यतः
श्रीमान् जगन्नाथ इतीह विश्रुतः ॥१३॥

*babhau mahā-vaṁśa-samudbhavaḥ sudhīr*
*aneka-vidyāmbudhi-pāra-paṇḍitaḥ |*
*dvijāti-vaṁśaika-vataṁsavad yataḥ*
*śrīmān jagannātha itīha viśrutaḥ ||13||*

*Word for word:* *babhau* — shone; *mahā* — of a great; *vaṁśa* — family; *samudbhavaḥ* — born; *sudhīḥ* — wise; *aneka* — of many; *vidyā* — branches of learning; *ambudhi* — of the oceans; *pāra* — [gone] to the far shore; *paṇḍitaḥ* — a scholar; *dvijāti* — of the twice-born; *vaṁśa* — of the race; *eka* — the one; *vataṁsa* — crest-ornament; *vat* — like; *yataḥ* — self-controlled; *śrīmān* — illustrious; *jagannāthaḥ* — Jagannatha; *iti* — thus; *iha* — here; *viśrutaḥ* — renowned.

**13.** There shone the illustrious one renowned in these parts as Jagannatha. Born of a great family, wise, a scholar who had crossed to the far shore of the oceans of many sciences, self-controlled, he was like the one crest-ornament of the race of the brahmanas.

### Verse 14

गुणैः समस्तैरयमेव शुद्धधी-
रधीतवेदो वरणीय एव हि ।
इतीह नीलाम्बरचक्रवर्त्तिना
वराय यस्मै सुधिया सुतार्पिता ॥१४॥

*guṇaiḥ samastair ayam eva śuddha-dhīr*
*adhīta-vedo varaṇīya eva hi |*
*itīha nīlāmbara-cakravartinā*
*varāya yasmai sudhiyā sutārpitā ||14||*

*Word for word:* *guṇaiḥ* — with qualities; *samastaiḥ* — with all; *ayam* — he; *eva* — alone; *śuddha* — of pure; *dhīḥ* — mind; *adhīta* — having studied; *vedaḥ* — the Vedas; *varaṇīyaḥ* — worthy to be chosen; *eva hi* — truly; *iti* — thus [judging]; *iha* — here; *nīlāmbara* — by Nilambara; *cakravartinā* — Chakravarti; *varāya* — to the bridegroom; *yasmai* — to whom; *sudhiyā* — by the wise; *sutā* — the daughter; *arpitā* — was given.

**14.** "He alone — with all virtues, pure of mind, learned in the Vedas — is truly worthy to be chosen": so judged the wise Nilambara Chakravarti, and gave him his daughter in marriage.

### Verse 15

शचीति नाम्नातिशुचेरचीक्लृपद्-
गुणेन सौशील्यरसेन तेऽनया ।
प्रतिष्ठया शुद्धतमां गरिष्ठतां
शची हि यां नाप पुरन्दरप्रिया ॥१५॥

*śacīti nāmnātiśucer acīkḷpad-*
*guṇena sauśīlya-rasena te 'nayā |*
*pratiṣṭhayā śuddhatamāṁ gariṣṭhatāṁ*
*śacī hi yāṁ nāpa purandara-priyā ||15||*

*Word for word:* *śacī* — Shachi; *iti* — thus; *nāmnā* — by name; *atiśuceḥ* — because of great purity; *acīkḷpat* — named; *guṇena* — by virtue; *sauśīlya* — of good nature; *rasena* — by the charm; *te* — (?); *anayā* — by her; *pratiṣṭhayā* — by renown; *śuddhatamām* — the purest; *gariṣṭhatām* — eminence; *śacī* — Shachi; *hi* — indeed; *yām* — which; *na* — not; *āpa* — attained; *purandara* — of Purandara; *priyā* — the beloved.

**15.** Because of her great purity she was given the name Shachi. By her virtue, by the charm of her good nature (?) and by her renown [she reached] the purest eminence — one that even Shachi, the beloved of Purandara, did not attain.

*Note.* (?) The first half of the verse is obscure; Goswami's edition (GGM) gives the same text. *Acīkḷpat* is the causative aorist of *kḷp*, "arranged, named"; cf. 2.62: *nāma acīkḷpat*, "gave a name". *Atiśuceḥ* is best taken as ablative, "because of her great purity", with a play on *śuci* ("pure") and *Śacī*. *Te 'nayā* remains unclear, and the text may be corrupt; the translation follows the general sense. The second half is clear. To be checked against another edition.

### Verse 16

उपेत्य तं मिश्रपुरन्दराह्वयं
निसर्गयोग्यं पदवीमुपाश्रितम् ।
बभौ शची चन्द्रकलेव नित्यशः
शची समासाद्य पुरन्दरं यथा ॥१६॥

*upetya taṁ miśra-purandarāhvayaṁ*
*nisarga-yogyaṁ padavīm upāśritam |*
*babhau śacī candra-kaleva nityaśaḥ*
*śacī samāsādya purandaraṁ yathā ||16||*

*Word for word:* *upetya* — having come to; *tam* — him; *miśra* — Mishra; *purandara* — Purandara; *āhvayam* — called; *nisarga* — by nature; *yogyam* — worthy; *padavīm* — the path; *upāśritam* — following; *babhau* — shone; *śacī* — Shachi; *candra* — of the moon; *kalā* — the crescent; *iva* — like; *nityaśaḥ* — day by day; *śacī* — Shachi; *samāsādya* — having obtained; *purandaram* — Purandara; *yathā* — as.

**16.** Having come [as wife] to him who was called Mishra Purandara — worthy by nature and walking the [righteous] path — Shachi shone day by day like the crescent of the moon, as Shachi shines on obtaining Purandara.

*Note.* A double play on names: *Purandara* is the second name of Jagannatha Mishra and a name of Indra; *Shachi* is the name of Gauranga's mother and of Indra's consort.

### Verse 17

तयोर्गृहे संवसतोः सतोः सदा
गृहस्थधर्म्मः सदुदारमासदत् ।
क्रमेण चाष्टौ तनुजाः पुरोऽभवं-
स्तथैव पञ्चत्वमुपाययुश्च ताः ॥१७॥

*tayor gṛhe saṁvasatoḥ satoḥ sadā*
*gṛhastha-dharmaḥ sad-udāram āsadat |*
*krameṇa cāṣṭau tanujāḥ puro 'bhavaṁs*
*tathaiva pañcatvam upāyayuś ca tāḥ ||17||*

*Word for word:* *tayoḥ* — of the two; *gṛhe* — in the house; *saṁvasatoḥ* — living together; *satoḥ* — righteous; *sadā* — always; *gṛhastha* — of householders; *dharmaḥ* — the duty; *sat* — well; *udāram* — generously; *āsadat* — was fulfilled; *krameṇa* — one after another; *ca* — and; *aṣṭau* — eight; *tanujāḥ* — daughters; *puraḥ* — first; *abhavan* — were born; *tathā* — in the same way; *eva* — indeed; *pañcatvam* — to the fivefold state; *upāyayuḥ* — went; *ca* — and; *tāḥ* — they.

**17.** As the righteous couple lived together, the duty of householders was always fulfilled in their home, well and generously. First eight daughters were born to them one after another — and in the same way, one after another, they went to the fivefold state.

*Note.* *Pañcatvam upāyayuḥ*, "they went to the fivefold state", that is, the body returned to the five elements: a euphemism for passing away. The eight daughters who passed away are mentioned also in the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Adi 13).

### Verse 18

ततश्च तौ सन्ततमेव दम्पती
बभूवतुर्दुःखितमौ महत्तमौ ।
प्रयत्नमाधाय सुतार्थमीयतुः
प्रभोः पदाब्जं शरणं कृपामयम् ॥१८॥

*tataś ca tau santatam eva dampatī*
*babhūvatur duḥkhitamau mahattamau |*
*prayatnam ādhāya sutārtham īyatuḥ*
*prabhoḥ padābjaṁ śaraṇaṁ kṛpāmayam ||18||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *ca* — and; *tau* — those two; *santatam* — constantly; *eva* — indeed; *dampatī* — husband and wife; *babhūvatuḥ* — became; *duḥkhitamau* — most unhappy; *mahattamau* — most noble; *prayatnam* — effort; *ādhāya* — having applied; *suta* — of a son; *artham* — for the sake; *īyatuḥ* — went; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *pada* — of the feet; *abjam* — to the lotus; *śaraṇam* — to the refuge; *kṛpā* — with mercy; *mayam* — filled.

**18.** And then that most noble couple became the most unhappy of people, their grief unceasing. With all their effort, for the sake of a son, they went for refuge to the merciful lotus feet of the Lord.

### Verse 19

ततोऽतिभाग्येन तयोरभूत्सुतः
स विश्वरूपः शुभरूपशोभितः ।
मुदं ययौ सा सुमुखी पिताप्यसौ
व्यडम्बयच्चाधनमात्तसद्वसुम् ॥१९॥

*tato 'tibhāgyena tayor abhūt sutaḥ*
*sa viśvarūpaḥ śubha-rūpa-śobhitaḥ |*
*mudaṁ yayau sā sumukhī pitāpy asau*
*vyaḍambayac cādhanam ātta-sad-vasum ||19||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *ati* — by great; *bhāgyena* — by good fortune; *tayoḥ* — to them; *abhūt* — was born; *sutaḥ* — a son; *saḥ* — he; *viśvarūpaḥ* — Vishvarupa; *śubha* — with a beautiful; *rūpa* — with form; *śobhitaḥ* — adorned; *mudam* — joy; *yayau* — attained; *sā* — she; *sumukhī* — fair-faced; *pitā* — the father; *api* — also; *asau* — he; *vyaḍambayat* — resembled; *ca* — and; *adhanam* — a poor man; *ātta* — who has obtained; *sat* — good; *vasum* — wealth.

**19.** Then, by great good fortune, a son was born to them — Vishvarupa, adorned with a beautiful form. The fair-faced [mother] rejoiced, and the father became like a poor man who has come into great wealth.

### Verse 20

स विश्वरूपः शुभरूपगर्वितां
तनुं वहंश्चन्द्र इव प्रकाशवान् ।
निपठ्य कालेन लघीयसाप्यसौ
समस्तविद्याम्बुधिपारमाययौ ॥२०॥

*sa viśvarūpaḥ śubha-rūpa-garvitāṁ*
*tanuṁ vahaṁś candra iva prakāśavān |*
*nipaṭhya kālena laghīyasāpy asau*
*samasta-vidyāmbudhi-pāram āyayau ||20||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — that; *viśvarūpaḥ* — Vishvarupa; *śubha* — of a beautiful; *rūpa* — of form; *garvitām* — proud; *tanum* — a body; *vahan* — bearing; *candraḥ* — the moon; *iva* — like; *prakāśavān* — shining; *nipaṭhya* — having studied; *kālena* — in a time; *laghīyasā* — very short; *api* — even; *asau* — he; *samasta* — of all; *vidyā* — learning; *ambudhi* — of the ocean; *pāram* — the far shore; *āyayau* — reached.

**20.** That Vishvarupa, bearing a body proud of its beautiful form, shone like the moon. Having studied for even a very short time, he reached the far shore of the ocean of all learning.

### Verse 21

शिशुः स आसीद्वयसा लघीयसा
सुधीरधीतागमवेदसञ्चयः ।
सरस्वतीयं रसनाग्रनर्त्तकी
बभूव वश्येव सदास्य निर्भरम् ॥२१॥

*śiśuḥ sa āsīd vayasā laghīyasā*
*sudhīr adhītāgama-veda-sañcayaḥ |*
*sarasvatīyaṁ rasanāgra-nartakī*
*babhūva vaśyeva sadāsya nirbharam ||21||*

*Word for word:* *śiśuḥ* — a child; *saḥ* — he; *āsīt* — was; *vayasā* — in age; *laghīyasā* — very young; *sudhīḥ* — wise; *adhīta* — having studied; *āgama* — of the agamas; *veda* — of the Vedas; *sañcayaḥ* — the collection; *sarasvatī* — Sarasvati; *iyam* — this; *rasanā* — of the tongue; *agra* — on the tip; *nartakī* — a dancer; *babhūva* — became; *vaśyā* — obedient; *iva* — as if; *sadā* — always; *asya* — his; *nirbharam* — wholly.

**21.** Though still a child in years, he was wise and had studied the whole body of the agamas and Vedas. Sarasvati, [goddess of speech], as if wholly at his command, became a dancer ever dancing on the tip of his tongue.

### Verse 22

ततश्च कालेन शुभेन सुन्दरी
शची विशेषं शुशुभे शुभेक्षणा ।
भविष्यदिन्दूदयशंसिनीं पुरः
पुरन्दराशां सदृशीं चकार सा ॥२२॥

*tataś ca kālena śubhena sundarī*
*śacī viśeṣaṁ śuśubhe śubhekṣaṇā |*
*bhaviṣyad-indūdaya-śaṁsinīṁ puraḥ*
*purandarāśāṁ sadṛśīṁ cakāra sā ||22||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *ca* — and; *kālena* — in time; *śubhena* — auspicious; *sundarī* — beautiful; *śacī* — Shachi; *viśeṣam* — especially; *śuśubhe* — shone; *śubha* — beautiful; *īkṣaṇā* — [having] eyes; *bhaviṣyat* — coming; *indu* — of the moon; *udaya* — the rising; *śaṁsinīm* — announcing; *puraḥ* — beforehand; *purandara* — of Purandara; *āśām* — the quarter; *sadṛśīm* — like; *cakāra* — made; *sā* — she.

**22.** Then, at an auspicious time, the lovely Shachi of beautiful eyes shone with a special radiance: she made [herself] like the quarter of Purandara [— the east —] which announces beforehand the coming rise of the moon.

*Note.* The east is the quarter of Indra-Purandara. Shachi is the wife of "Purandara" (Mishra), and her radiance before the birth of her son is compared to the eastern sky before moonrise: Gauranga is the "moon" (Gaurachandra).

### Verse 23

शची सती भाग्यमही महीयसी
सुकुक्षिपीयूषपयोनिधौ मुदा ।
मनोरमां दोहदलक्षणश्रियं
क्षपाकरस्येव नवां कलां दधौ ॥२३॥

*śacī satī bhāgya-mahī mahīyasī*
*su-kukṣi-pīyūṣa-payonidhau mudā |*
*manoramāṁ dohada-lakṣaṇa-śriyaṁ*
*kṣapākarasyeva navāṁ kalāṁ dadhau ||23||*

*Word for word:* *śacī* — Shachi; *satī* — virtuous; *bhāgya* — of good fortune; *mahī* — the earth; *mahīyasī* — greatest; *su* — of the beautiful; *kukṣi* — of the womb; *pīyūṣa* — of nectar; *payonidhau* — in the ocean; *mudā* — with joy; *manoramām* — charming; *dohada* — of pregnancy; *lakṣaṇa* — of the signs; *śriyam* — the beauty; *kṣapākarasya* — of the moon; *iva* — like; *navām* — a new; *kalām* — crescent; *dadhau* — bore.

**23.** The virtuous Shachi, great as the very earth of good fortune, joyfully bore in the nectar ocean of her lovely womb the charming beauty of the signs of pregnancy, like a new crescent of the moon.

*Note.* *Kṣapākara*, "maker of the night", is the moon. According to the Puranas the moon was born from the churning of the Milk Ocean. Here Shachi's womb is the "ocean of nectar", and the child within it the young crescent.

### Verse 24

क्रमेण मासा दश ते त्रयोऽधिकाः
समीयुरासन्नतराः समाप्तताम् ।
तपस्यमासश्चरमः सुमङ्गलो
बभूव तेषां जगतः सुखैकभूः ॥२४॥

*krameṇa māsā daśa te trayo 'dhikāḥ*
*samīyur āsannatarāḥ samāptatām |*
*tapasya-māsaś caramaḥ sumaṅgalo*
*babhūva teṣāṁ jagataḥ sukhaika-bhūḥ ||24||*

*Word for word:* *krameṇa* — gradually; *māsāḥ* — months; *daśa* — ten; *te* — those; *trayaḥ* — three; *adhikāḥ* — more; *samīyuḥ* — came; *āsannatarāḥ* — very near; *samāptatām* — to completion; *tapasya* — Tapasya; *māsaḥ* — month; *caramaḥ* — the last; *sumaṅgalaḥ* — most auspicious; *babhūva* — was; *teṣām* — of them; *jagataḥ* — of the world; *sukha* — of happiness; *eka* — the sole; *bhūḥ* — source.

**24.** Gradually those months — ten and three more — drew very near to their completion. The last of them was the most auspicious month of Tapasya, the sole source of happiness for the world.

*Note.* *Tapasya* is an old name of the month Phalguna (February–March): Gauranga appeared on the full moon of Phalguna. The thirteen months of pregnancy are a tradition, recorded also in the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Adi 13). The edition has *āsannatarā* without visarga before *s-*; we read *āsannatarāḥ*.

### Verse 25

असावृतूनां पतिरग्रतस्तदा
प्रभोः प्रकाशो भवितेति हर्षितः ।
स्वकालमुल्लङ्घ्य निजं पदं दधा-
वार्त्तिस्तथा तद्विषये हि शोभते ॥२५॥

*asāv ṛtūnāṁ patir agratas tadā*
*prabhoḥ prakāśo bhaviteti harṣitaḥ |*
*sva-kālam ullaṅghya nijaṁ padaṁ dadhāv*
*ārtis tathā tad-viṣaye hi śobhate ||25||*

*Word for word:* *asau* — that; *ṛtūnām* — of the seasons; *patiḥ* — lord; *agrataḥ* — ahead of time; *tadā* — then; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *prakāśaḥ* — the manifestation; *bhavitā* — will be; *iti* — thus [thinking]; *harṣitaḥ* — delighted; *sva* — his own; *kālam* — time; *ullaṅghya* — having overstepped; *nijam* — his own; *padam* — foot; *dadhau* — set; *ārtiḥ* — impatience; *tathā* — such; *tat* — in that; *viṣaye* — in matter; *hi* — indeed; *śobhate* — is becoming.

**25.** Then that lord of the seasons, [spring], delighted at the thought "The Lord will soon be manifest!", overstepped his own time and set his foot down ahead of it. In such a matter such impatience is indeed becoming.

*Note.* *Ārti* usually means "pain, distress"; here it is the aching impatience of expectation.

### Verse 26

उपैतुकामा सहकारनायकं
नवप्ररोहामवलम्ब्य वीरुधम् ।
क्वणद्भ्रमद्भृङ्गसमूहनूपुरं
वसन्तलक्ष्मीर्विपिने पदं दधौ ॥२६॥

*upaitu-kāmā sahakāra-nāyakaṁ*
*nava-prarohām avalambya vīrudham |*
*kvaṇad-bhramad-bhṛṅga-samūha-nūpuraṁ*
*vasanta-lakṣmīr vipine padaṁ dadhau ||26||*

*Word for word:* *upaitu* — to approach; *kāmā* — wishing; *sahakāra* — the mango; *nāyakam* — the lover; *nava* — new; *prarohām* — [having] shoots; *avalambya* — leaning on; *vīrudham* — a creeper; *kvaṇat* — humming; *bhramat* — whirling; *bhṛṅga* — of bees; *samūha* — a swarm; *nūpuram* — [having] as an anklet; *vasanta* — of spring; *lakṣmīḥ* — the beauty; *vipine* — in the forest; *padam* — foot; *dadhau* — set.

**26.** Wishing to approach her lover, the mango tree, the Beauty of Spring leaned on a creeper with fresh shoots and set foot in the forest; a humming, whirling swarm of bees was her anklet.

*Note.* *Sahakāra* is the fragrant mango. In Sanskrit poetry the mango is the "husband", and the flowering creeper that twines about it his "wife".

### Verse 27

स्ववेशविन्यासमिवाकरोदियं
प्रभोः प्रकाशो भवितेति सन्ततम् ।
वसन्तलक्ष्मीः सततोत्सुका सती
सतीव कान्तागमने शुचिस्मिता ॥२७॥

*sva-veśa-vinyāsam ivākarod iyaṁ*
*prabhoḥ prakāśo bhaviteti santatam |*
*vasanta-lakṣmīḥ satatotsukā satī*
*satīva kāntāgamane śuci-smitā ||27||*

*Word for word:* *sva* — her own; *veśa* — of attire; *vinyāsam* — the arrangement; *iva* — as if; *akarot* — made; *iyam* — she; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *prakāśaḥ* — the manifestation; *bhavitā* — will be; *iti* — thus [thinking]; *santatam* — constantly; *vasanta* — of spring; *lakṣmīḥ* — the beauty; *satata* — ever; *utsukā* — eager; *satī* — being; *satī* — a faithful wife; *iva* — like; *kānta* — of the beloved; *āgamane* — at the coming; *śuci* — with a bright; *smitā* — smile.

**27.** "The Lord will soon be manifest!" — so thinking, the Beauty of Spring, ever eager, kept arranging her attire, as it were, smiling brightly like a faithful wife at the coming of her beloved.

*Note.* Verses 27–31 form a *kulaka*: five verses, one sentence. Spring adorns herself for the Lord's coming: voice, smile, hair, ear-ornaments, unguents.

### Verse 28

स्वभावमाद्यत्कलकण्ठकाकली-
कलाविलासं दधती शुभस्वरम् ।
नवं समुद्यन्मधुपुष्पमाधुरी-
धुरीणमीषद्धसितं च कोमलम् ॥२८॥

*svabhāva-mādyat-kalakaṇṭha-kākalī-*
*kalā-vilāsaṁ dadhatī śubha-svaram |*
*navaṁ samudyan-madhu-puṣpa-mādhurī-*
*dhurīṇam īṣad-dhasitaṁ ca komalam ||28||*

*Word for word:* *svabhāva* — by nature; *mādyat* — of intoxicated; *kalakaṇṭha* — of cuckoos; *kākalī* — of the soft song; *kalā* — the artful; *vilāsam* — play; *dadhatī* — bearing; *śubha* — a beautiful; *svaram* — voice; *navam* — fresh; *samudyat* — of opening; *madhu* — of honey; *puṣpa* — of flowers; *mādhurī* — with the sweetness; *dhurīṇam* — laden; *īṣat* — a slight; *hasitam* — smile; *ca* — and; *komalam* — tender.

**28.** She bore a beautiful voice — the artful play of the soft song of cuckoos, intoxicated by their very nature — and a slight, tender smile, fresh and laden with the sweetness of opening honey-flowers.

*Note.* *Kalakaṇṭha*, "sweet-throated", is the kokila cuckoo. *Kākalī* is a low, soft strain.

### Verse 29

तमालमालादलमाधुरीमयं
बबन्ध धम्मिल्लभरं मनोहरम् ।
मधुव्रतालीमयचिल्लिवल्लरीं
प्रनर्त्तयामास सुखं मदालसाम् ॥२९॥

*tamāla-mālā-dala-mādhurī-mayaṁ*
*babandha dhammilla-bharaṁ manoharam |*
*madhuvratālī-maya-cilli-vallarīṁ*
*pranartayāmāsa sukhaṁ madālasām ||29||*

*Word for word:* *tamāla* — of tamala trees; *mālā* — of rows; *dala* — of the foliage; *mādhurī* — with the sweetness; *mayam* — filled; *babandha* — bound up; *dhammilla* — of braided hair; *bharam* — the mass; *manoharam* — captivating; *madhuvrata* — of bees; *ālī* — of lines; *maya* — consisting; *cilli* — of the brows; *vallarīm* — the creepers; *pranartayāmāsa* — made dance; *sukham* — happily; *mada* — with intoxication; *alasām* — languid.

**29.** She bound up the captivating mass of her braided hair, full of the sweetness of the foliage of rows of tamala trees, and happily made dance the creepers of her brows — lines of bees, languid with intoxication.

*Note.* The tamala is a tree with dark, almost black foliage; in Gaudiya poetry it is a constant image of Krishna's complexion. *Madhuvrata*, "one vowed to honey", is a bee.

### Verse 30

उन्मीलयामास च वामलोचनं
कृत्वावतंसं नवचारुपल्लवैः ।
लवङ्गपुष्पावलिहारहारिणी
दधार वासो नवमालिकामयम् ॥३०॥

*unmīlayāmāsa ca vāma-locanaṁ*
*kṛtvāvataṁsaṁ nava-cāru-pallavaiḥ |*
*lavaṅga-puṣpāvali-hāra-hāriṇī*
*dadhāra vāso nava-mālikā-mayam ||30||*

*Word for word:* *unmīlayāmāsa* — opened; *ca* — and; *vāma* — lovely; *locanam* — eyes; *kṛtvā* — having made; *avataṁsam* — ear-ornaments; *nava* — of new; *cāru* — of charming; *pallavaiḥ* — of shoots; *lavaṅga* — of clove; *puṣpa* — of flowers; *āvali* — of strings; *hāra* — with a necklace; *hāriṇī* — captivating; *dadhāra* — put on; *vāsaḥ* — a garment; *nava* — fresh; *mālikā* — jasmine (*navamālikā*); *mayam* — made of.

**30.** Having made ear-ornaments of new, charming shoots, she opened her lovely eyes; captivating with a necklace of strings of clove flowers, she put on a garment of navamalika blossoms.
