*Note.* "She opened her eyes" — the flowers opening. The edition reads *नवनालिका*, a misprint: Goswami's edition (GGM) reads *nava-mālikā* (navamalika, a kind of jasmine).

### Verse 31

अशोकमालादलकुङ्कुमद्रवैः
सदङ्गरागं विदधेऽतिहर्षिता ।
समाधुरीपुष्पपरागचन्दनै-
र्मनोहरे केशरकुड्मलस्तने ॥३१॥
(पञ्चभिः कुलकम्)

*aśoka-mālā-dala-kuṅkuma-dravaiḥ*
*sad-aṅga-rāgaṁ vidadhe 'tiharṣitā |*
*sa-mādhurī-puṣpa-parāga-candanair*
*manohare keśara-kuḍmala-stane ||31||*

*Word for word:* *aśoka* — of ashoka; *mālā* — of garlands; *dala* — of petals; *kuṅkuma* — of kunkuma; *dravaiḥ* — with liquids; *sat* — a fine; *aṅga* — body; *rāgam* — unguent; *vidadhe* — applied; *ati* — greatly; *harṣitā* — delighted; *sa* — with; *mādhurī* — sweetness; *puṣpa* — of flowers; *parāga* — of pollen; *candanaiḥ* — with sandal paste; *manohare* — on the charming; *keśara* — of keshara; *kuḍmala* — buds; *stane* — breast.

**31.** Overjoyed, she applied a fine body-unguent — the liquid kunkuma of the petals of ashoka garlands — and on her charming breast, the buds of keshara, sandal paste of sweet flower pollen.

*Note.* The ashoka is a tree with scarlet flowers; the keshara, a tree with fragrant buds (bakula or nagakeshara). *Pañcabhiḥ kulakam* — "a *kulaka* of five [verses]" (27–31). The edition misprints *कुट्नल* for *कुड्मल*.

### Verse 32

प्रसेदुराशा दश निर्मलं बभौ
नभो ववुः पुण्यतमाश्च मारुताः ।
मनांसि सर्वस्य जनस्य भेजिरे
प्रसन्नतां स्वच्छमभून्नदीजलम् ॥३२॥

*prasedur āśā daśa nirmalaṁ babhau*
*nabho vavuḥ puṇyatamāś ca mārutāḥ |*
*manāṁsi sarvasya janasya bhejire*
*prasannatāṁ svaccham abhūn nadī-jalam ||32||*

*Word for word:* *praseduḥ* — became clear; *āśāḥ* — the quarters; *daśa* — ten; *nirmalam* — spotless; *babhau* — shone; *nabhaḥ* — the sky; *vavuḥ* — blew; *puṇyatamāḥ* — most auspicious; *ca* — and; *mārutāḥ* — winds; *manāṁsi* — the minds; *sarvasya* — of every; *janasya* — of person; *bhejire* — attained; *prasannatām* — serenity; *svaccham* — clear; *abhūt* — became; *nadī* — of the river; *jalam* — the water.

**32.** The ten quarters grew clear, the sky shone spotless, most auspicious winds blew, the minds of all people grew serene, and the water of the river became clear.

### Verse 33

तदा शशाङ्कः परिपूर्णमण्डलः
स पौर्णमासीपरिरम्भहर्षितः ।
व्यरोचतातीव जगन्मनोरम-
श्चुम्बन्मुहुः पूर्वदिगङ्गनामुखम् ॥३३॥

*tadā śaśāṅkaḥ paripūrṇa-maṇḍalaḥ*
*sa paurṇamāsī-parirambha-harṣitaḥ |*
*vyarocatātīva jagan-manoramaś*
*cumban muhuḥ pūrva-dig-aṅganā-mukham ||33||*

*Word for word:* *tadā* — then; *śaśāṅkaḥ* — the moon; *paripūrṇa* — full; *maṇḍalaḥ* — [having] a disc; *saḥ* — he; *paurṇamāsī* — of the Full-moon Night; *parirambha* — by the embrace; *harṣitaḥ* — delighted; *vyarocata* — shone; *atīva* — exceedingly; *jagat* — of the world; *manoramaḥ* — the delight; *cumban* — kissing; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *pūrva* — of the eastern; *dik* — quarter; *aṅganā* — of the fair lady; *mukham* — the face.

**33.** Then the moon, his disc full, delighted by the embrace of the Full-moon Night, shone exceedingly, the delight of the world, kissing again and again the face of the fair lady of the East.

*Note.* In Sanskrit the moon (*śaśāṅka*, "hare-marked") is masculine and the full-moon night (*paurṇamāsī*) feminine; hence the image of lovers. To keep it, the moon is "he" in the translation.

### Verse 34

असावृतूनां पतिरग्रतोऽभव-
त्तथैव पक्षः सित एव सोऽभवत् ।
तथा तिथीनां प्रवरा च पूर्णिमा
गुणानुबन्धी खलु मङ्गलोदयः ॥३४॥

*asāv ṛtūnāṁ patir agrato 'bhavat*
*tathaiva pakṣaḥ sita eva so 'bhavat |*
*tathā tithīnāṁ pravarā ca pūrṇimā*
*guṇānubandhī khalu maṅgalodayaḥ ||34||*

*Word for word:* *asau* — that; *ṛtūnām* — of the seasons; *patiḥ* — lord; *agrataḥ* — in front; *abhavat* — was; *tathā eva* — likewise; *pakṣaḥ* — the fortnight; *sitaḥ* — bright; *eva* — indeed; *saḥ* — that; *abhavat* — was; *tathā* — likewise; *tithīnām* — of lunar days; *pravarā* — the best; *ca* — and; *pūrṇimā* — the full moon; *guṇa* — excellences; *anubandhī* — bringing in its train; *khalu* — truly; *maṅgala* — of the auspicious; *udayaḥ* — the rise.

**34.** The lord of the seasons, [spring], led the way; likewise the fortnight was the bright one; likewise [the day was] the best of lunar days, the full moon. Truly, the rise of the auspicious brings every excellence in its train.

### Verse 35

वनप्रियास्तत्समये मधून्मदा-
स्तदादि चक्रुः सकलं जयध्वनिम् ।
तदादि लास्यं विदधुर्मधुव्रताः
स दक्षिणस्तत्प्रथमं ववौ मरुत् ॥३५॥

*vanapriyās tat-samaye madhūnmadās*
*tadādi cakruḥ sakalaṁ jaya-dhvanim |*
*tadādi lāsyaṁ vidadhur madhuvratāḥ*
*sa dakṣiṇas tat prathamaṁ vavau marut ||35||*

*Word for word:* *vanapriyāḥ* — the cuckoos; *tat* — at that; *samaye* — time; *madhu* — by spring; *unmadāḥ* — intoxicated; *tadādi* — from then on; *cakruḥ* — raised; *sakalam* — universal; *jaya* — "Victory!"; *dhvanim* — the cry; *tadādi* — from then on; *lāsyam* — dance; *vidadhuḥ* — took up; *madhuvratāḥ* — the bees; *saḥ* — that; *dakṣiṇaḥ* — southern; *tat* — then; *prathamam* — for the first time; *vavau* — blew; *marut* — wind.

**35.** At that time the cuckoos, intoxicated by spring, from then on raised a universal cry of "Victory!"; from then on the bees took up their dance; and then for the first time the southern wind blew.

*Note.* *Vanapriya*, "darling of the forest", is the cuckoo. *Madhu* means both "spring" and "honey". The southern wind from the Malaya hills is a traditional sign of spring.

### Verse 36

स निर्भरस्तम्बभरेण मन्थरो
लतां लतां प्रत्युपगूहनैर्नवैः ।
पयोजमाध्वीकनिदाघवारिभृ-
द्ववौ मरुच्चन्दनशैलनन्दनः ॥३६॥

*sa nirbhara-stamba-bhareṇa mantharo*
*latāṁ latāṁ praty-upagūhanair navaiḥ |*
*payoja-mādhvīka-nidāgha-vāri-bhṛd*
*vavau marud candana-śaila-nandanaḥ ||36||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — that; *nirbhara* — heavy; *stamba* — of clusters; *bhareṇa* — by the burden; *mantharaḥ* — slowed; *latām latām* — each creeper; *prati* — in turn; *upagūhanaiḥ* — with embraces; *navaiḥ* — fresh; *payoja* — of lotuses; *mādhvīka* — the honeyed nectar; *nidāgha* — of heat; *vāri* — the drops; *bhṛt* — carrying; *vavau* — blew; *marut* — the wind; *candana* — of sandal; *śaila* — of the mountains; *nandanaḥ* — the son.

**36.** That wind, the son of the sandal mountains, blew slowly, weighed down by the burden of heavy flower clusters, with fresh embraces for each creeper in turn, carrying the honeyed nectar of lotuses as drops of sweat from the heat.

*Note.* "The son of the sandal mountains" is the wind from the Malaya hills in southern India, where sandalwood grows. *Nidāgha-vāri*, "the water of heat", is sweat: the wind is pictured as a lover, heated by the embraces of the creepers.

### Verse 37

ततो जगन्मङ्गलमङ्गलोदये
जगत्प्रसादः प्रबभूव निर्भरम् ।
अजस्रमेवाश्रमशून्यतां दधौ
तमिस्रमुच्छ्रायवता तदोजसा ॥३७॥

*tato jagan-maṅgala-maṅgalodaye*
*jagat-prasādaḥ prababhūva nirbharam |*
*ajasram evāśrama-śūnyatāṁ dadhau*
*tamisram ucchrāyavatā tad-ojasā ||37||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *jagat* — of the world; *maṅgala* — of the blessings; *maṅgala* — of the blessing; *udaye* — at the rise; *jagat* — of the world; *prasādaḥ* — serenity; *prababhūva* — arose; *nirbharam* — in fullness; *ajasram* — forever; *eva* — indeed; *āśrama* — of shelter; *śūnyatām* — the lack; *dadhau* — attained; *tamisram* — darkness; *ucchrāyavatā* — by the lofty; *tat* — His; *ojasā* — by the splendour.

**37.** Then, at the rising of the blessing of the world's blessings, the world was filled with serenity; and darkness, [overcome] by His lofty splendour, was left forever without shelter.

### Verse 38

ततः प्रभुर्भूमिगतो महौजसा
रराज सर्वाः ककुभः प्रकाशयन् ।
समं समुन्मील्य सुधांशुसञ्चयः
पपात भूमाविव विद्युतां चयैः ॥३८॥

*tataḥ prabhur bhūmi-gato mahaujasā*
*rarāja sarvāḥ kakubhaḥ prakāśayan |*
*samaṁ samunmīlya sudhāṁśu-sañcayaḥ*
*papāta bhūmāv iva vidyutāṁ cayaiḥ ||38||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *bhūmi* — to the earth; *gataḥ* — come; *mahā* — with great; *ojasā* — with splendour; *rarāja* — shone; *sarvāḥ* — all; *kakubhaḥ* — the quarters; *prakāśayan* — illuminating; *samam* — at once; *samunmīlya* — having flashed forth; *sudhāṁśu* — of moons; *sañcayaḥ* — a multitude; *papāta* — fell; *bhūmau* — on the earth; *iva* — as if; *vidyutām* — of lightnings; *cayaiḥ* — with masses.

**38.** Then the Lord, having come to the earth, shone with great splendour, illuminating all the quarters — as if a multitude of moons had flashed forth at once and fallen to the earth together with masses of lightning.

### Verse 39

तदोपरागः समभूत्तथा मुहु-
र्हरिं वदेति ध्वनिरुच्चकैर्नृणाम् ।
स्वनामसंकीर्त्तनमन्यथा नहि
प्रकाशमात्रेण भवेत्प्रकाशितम् ॥३९॥

*tadoparāgaḥ samabhūt tathā muhur*
*hariṁ vadeti dhvanir uccakair nṛṇām |*
*sva-nāma-saṅkīrtanam anyathā na hi*
*prakāśa-mātreṇa bhavet prakāśitam ||39||*

*Word for word:* *tadā* — then; *uparāgaḥ* — an eclipse; *samabhūt* — occurred; *tathā* — and; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *harim* — "Hari"; *vada* — say; *iti* — thus; *dhvaniḥ* — the cry; *uccakaiḥ* — loud; *nṛṇām* — of people; *sva* — of His own; *nāma* — of the name; *saṅkīrtanam* — the congregational chanting; *anyathā* — otherwise; *na hi* — not at all; *prakāśa* — by the appearance; *mātreṇa* — by mere; *bhavet* — would be; *prakāśitam* — made manifest.

**39.** Then an eclipse took place, and again and again rose the loud cry of the people: "Say 'Hari'!" For otherwise, by His mere appearance, the sankirtana of His own name would not have been made manifest.

*Note.* According to tradition, Mahaprabhu appeared during a lunar eclipse, when people, as was the custom, were bathing in the Ganga and chanting the name of Hari (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 13). *Hariṁ vada* is the Sanskrit form of the Bengali "Hari bol!" The poet's thought: the eclipse was needed so that the Lord's appearance would coincide with the kirtana of His name.

### Verse 40

सुधानिधिं तत्समये विधुन्तुद-
स्तुतोद सानन्दमरुन्तुदो भृशम् ।
अलं त्वया संप्रति शीतदीधितिः
समुद्गतोऽन्योऽस्ति भुवीति भावयन् ॥४०॥

*sudhā-nidhiṁ tat-samaye vidhuntudas*
*tutoda sānandam aruntudo bhṛśam |*
*alaṁ tvayā samprati śīta-dīdhitiḥ*
*samudgato 'nyo 'sti bhuvīti bhāvayan ||40||*

*Word for word:* *sudhā* — of nectar; *nidhim* — the treasury; *tat* — at that; *samaye* — time; *vidhuntudaḥ* — Rahu; *tutoda* — tormented; *sa-ānandam* — with joy; *aruntudaḥ* — cruel; *bhṛśam* — severely; *alam* — enough; *tvayā* — with you; *samprati* — now; *śīta* — cool; *dīdhitiḥ* — [having] rays; *samudgataḥ* — has risen; *anyaḥ* — another; *asti* — is; *bhuvi* — on the earth; *iti* — thus; *bhāvayan* — thinking.

**40.** At that time Rahu, the tormentor of the moon, cruelly and joyfully afflicted the treasury of nectar, thinking: "Enough of you! Now another, of cool rays, has risen on the earth."

*Note.* *Vidhuntuda*, "tormentor of the moon", is Rahu, the demon who, according to legend, swallows the moon at an eclipse. *Aruntuda* — "wounding to the quick". The "treasury of nectar" is the moon.

### Verse 41

प्रभुर्बुभूषुर्निजनामकीर्त्तने
निरन्तरप्रेमविलासलालसः ।
तदैव वीक्षध्वमथाकरोदसौ
जगत्स्वनामामृतपूरपूरितम् ॥४१॥

*prabhur bubhūṣur nija-nāma-kīrtane*
*nirantara-prema-vilāsa-lālasaḥ |*
*tadaiva vīkṣadhvam athākarod asau*
*jagat sva-nāmāmṛta-pūra-pūritam ||41||*

*Word for word:* *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *bubhūṣuḥ* — wishing to appear; *nija* — of His own; *nāma* — of the name; *kīrtane* — in the chanting; *nirantara* — of unceasing; *prema* — of love; *vilāsa* — for the pastimes; *lālasaḥ* — longing; *tadā* — then; *eva* — at that very [moment]; *vīkṣadhvam* — behold!; *atha* — and so; *akarot* — made; *asau* — He; *jagat* — the world; *sva* — of His own; *nāma* — of the name; *amṛta* — of the nectar; *pūra* — with the flood; *pūritam* — filled.

**41.** The Lord, longing for unceasing pastimes of love, wished to appear in the very chanting of His own name. Behold: at that very moment He filled the world with a flood of the nectar of His name!

### Verse 42

अथावलोक्य श्रिय एकविभ्रम-
प्रकाशविश्राममहीरुहाङ्कुरम् ।
पिता च माता च सुखाम्बुधौ मुहु-
र्बभूवतुर्मज्जनमात्रचेष्टितौ ॥४२॥

*athāvalokya śriya eka-vibhrama-*
*prakāśa-viśrāma-mahīruhāṅkuram |*
*pitā ca mātā ca sukhāmbudhau muhur*
*babhūvatur majjana-mātra-ceṣṭitau ||42||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *avalokya* — having seen; *śriyaḥ* — of beauty; *eka* — the sole; *vibhrama* — of the play; *prakāśa* — of the manifestation; *viśrāma* — the resting place; *mahīruha* — of the tree; *aṅkuram* — the sprout; *pitā* — the father; *ca* — and; *mātā* — the mother; *ca* — and; *sukha* — of happiness; *ambudhau* — in the ocean; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *babhūvatuḥ* — became; *majjana* — with plunging; *mātra* — only; *ceṣṭitau* — occupied.

**42.** Then, beholding this sprout of the tree that is the sole resting place where Beauty displays her play, the father and the mother plunged again and again into an ocean of happiness and could do nothing else.

*Note.* *Śrī* means both "beauty" and the goddess Lakshmi.

### Verse 43

ततः स मिश्रः कृतपुण्यसञ्चयैः
सुतं विलोक्यैव सुखैकभूरभूत् ।
इयत्तया वर्ज्जितमर्ज्जितं धनं
द्विजोच्चयेभ्यः समदात्तदैव हि ॥४३॥

*tataḥ sa miśraḥ kṛta-puṇya-sañcayaiḥ*
*sutaṁ vilokyaiva sukhaika-bhūr abhūt |*
*iyattayā varjitam arjitaṁ dhanaṁ*
*dvijoccayebhyaḥ samadāt tadaiva hi ||43||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *saḥ* — that; *miśraḥ* — Mishra; *kṛta* — performed; *puṇya* — of pious deeds; *sañcayaiḥ* — by the stores; *sutam* — the son; *vilokya* — having seen; *eva* — merely; *sukha* — of happiness; *eka* — the sole; *bhūḥ* — abode; *abhūt* — became; *iyattayā* — by measure; *varjitam* — unlimited; *arjitam* — earned; *dhanam* — wealth; *dvija* — of brahmanas; *uccayebhyaḥ* — to throngs; *samadāt* — gave away; *tadā* — then; *eva* — at that very [time]; *hi* — indeed.

**43.** Then Mishra, by virtue of the store of pious deeds he had performed, became, merely by seeing his son, the very abode of happiness; and at that very time he gave away to throngs of brahmanas the wealth he had earned, beyond all measure.

### Verse 44

प्रकाशमात्रेण सुदक्षिणा ग्रहा
बभूवुरस्य प्रथमं सुतुङ्गकाः ।
बभूव राशिः स तु सिंहसञ्ज्ञितो
नक्षत्रमुख्यापि च पूर्वफल्गुनी ॥४४॥

*prakāśa-mātreṇa sudakṣiṇā grahā*
*babhūvur asya prathamaṁ sutuṅgakāḥ |*
*babhūva rāśiḥ sa tu siṁha-sañjñito*
*nakṣatra-mukhyāpi ca pūrva-phalgunī ||44||*

*Word for word:* *prakāśa* — by the appearance; *mātreṇa* — by mere; *su* — very; *dakṣiṇāḥ* — favourable; *grahāḥ* — the planets; *babhūvuḥ* — became; *asya* — His; *prathamam* — at once; *su* — highly; *tuṅgakāḥ* — exalted; *babhūva* — was; *rāśiḥ* — the sign; *saḥ* — that; *tu* — and; *siṁha* — Simha (Leo); *sañjñitaḥ* — named; *nakṣatra* — of the nakshatras; *mukhyā* — the chief; *api ca* — and also; *pūrva-phalgunī* — Purva-phalguni.

**44.** By His mere appearance the planets at once became most favourable to Him and stood in high exaltation. The sign was the one called Simha (Leo), and the chief nakshatra was Purva-phalguni.

*Note.* *Tuṅga* in jyotisha is "exaltation", the position in which a planet has its greatest strength. The horoscope of Mahaprabhu is discussed in detail in the Chaitanya-bhagavata (Adi 3, "The Lord's horoscope") and the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Adi 13).

### Verse 45

मनोरमं वस्तु जगद्विराजि यत्
तदेव तस्मै यौतुकत्वमाययौ ।
तमन्तरेण क्षितिमण्डले न यन्
मनोज्ञतापात्रमिहास्ति कश्चन ॥४५॥

*manoramaṁ vastu jagad-virāji yat*
*tad eva tasmai yautukatvam āyayau |*
*tam antareṇa kṣiti-maṇḍale na yan*
*manojñatā-pātram ihāsti kaścana ||45||*

*Word for word:* *manoramam* — charming; *vastu* — thing; *jagat* — in the world; *virāji* — shining; *yat* — whatever; *tat* — that; *eva* — itself; *tasmai* — to Him; *yautukatvam* — the state of a gift; *āyayau* — attained; *tam* — Him; *antareṇa* — apart from; *kṣiti* — of the earth; *maṇḍale* — in the circle; *na* — not; *yat* — since; *manojñatā* — of charm; *pātram* — a vessel; *iha* — here; *asti* — is; *kaścana* — any.

**45.** Whatever charming thing shines in the world became of itself a festive gift to Him; for apart from Him there is here, in the whole circle of the earth, no vessel worthy of charm.

*Note.* The edition misprints *यतुकत्व*; we read *यौतुकत्व* (*yautuka*, a gift, a present made on a festive occasion). Verses 45–55 are "the service of beauty": each beautiful thing in the world becomes the servant of one feature of His form.

### Verse 46

समाधवः पार्वणशर्वरीपतिः
श्रियं समेत्य द्विगुणां मनोरमाम् ।
बभूव तस्याननचन्द्रसेवको
मनोरथो धावति दुर्लभे यतः ॥४६॥

*sa-mādhavaḥ pārvaṇa-śarvarī-patiḥ*
*śriyaṁ sametya dviguṇāṁ manoramām |*
*babhūva tasyānana-candra-sevako*
*manoratho dhāvati durlabhe yataḥ ||46||*

*Word for word:* *sa* — together with; *mādhavaḥ* — spring; *pārvaṇa* — of the full-moon; *śarvarī* — of the night; *patiḥ* — the lord; *śriyam* — beauty; *sametya* — having gained; *dviguṇām* — doubled; *manoramām* — charming; *babhūva* — became; *tasya* — His; *ānana* — of the face; *candra* — of the moon; *sevakaḥ* — the servant; *manorathaḥ* — desire; *dhāvati* — runs; *durlabhe* — towards what is hard to attain; *yataḥ* — for.

**46.** The lord of the full-moon night, together with spring, gained a doubled, charming beauty and became the servant of the moon of His face; for desire runs after what is hard to attain.

*Note.* *Mādhava* is a spring month (Vaishakha), here spring itself. "The lord of the night" is the moon.

च्छ्रुतिद्वयं नूतनपल्लवद्युतिः ॥४७॥

*Word for word:* *vinidra* — unsleeping; *śoṇa* — red; *amburuha* — lotuses; *āśrayāḥ* — dwelling in; *śriyaḥ* — the beauties; *vilocane* — the two eyes; *tasya* — His; *siṣevire* — served; *muhuḥ* — constantly; *bhruvau* — the two brows; *bhramat* — whirling; *bhṛṅga* — of bees; *vadhū* — of the wives; *gaṇaḥ* — the swarm; *abhajat* — served; *śruti* — of ears; *dvayam* — the pair; *nūtana* — of fresh; *pallava* — shoots; *dyutiḥ* — the lustre.

*Note.* *Vinidra*, "unsleeping", means opened (the lotus closes for the night).

*siṣevire darpaṇa-bimba-vibhramā*
*manoramaṁ gaṇḍa-yugasya maṇḍalam ||48||*

*Word for word:* *tila* — of sesame; *prasūnam* — the flower; *navam* — fresh; *āśu* — at once; *sevayā* — with service; *babhūva* — became [engaged]; *nāsā* — of the nose; *puṭam* — the nostrils; *unnata* — with lofty; *śriyā* — beauty [endowed]; *siṣevire* — served; *darpaṇa* — of a mirror; *bimba* — of the disc; *vibhramāḥ* — the charms; *manoramam* — charming; *gaṇḍa* — of cheeks; *yugasya* — of the pair; *maṇḍalam* — the round.

**48.** A fresh sesame flower at once took up the service of His nose, [graced] with lofty beauty; the charms of a round mirror served the charming round of His two cheeks.

*Note.* The sesame flower is a classical comparison for a beautiful nose. The syntax of the first half (*sevayā babhūva nāsā-puṭam*) is rough, so too in GGM; the translation follows the sense. In the third pada GGM reads *vibhramaṁ* (accusative) instead of *vibhramāḥ*.

*Word for word:* *navīna* — fresh; *bandhūka* — bandhuka flowers; *navīna* — fresh; *pallava* — shoots; *pravāla* — corals; *bimbāni* — bimba fruits; *nija* — with their own; *śriyā* — with beauty; *muhuḥ* — constantly; *jagat* — the world; *manojñam* — charming; *yugapat* — all at once; *siṣevire* — served; *nitāntam* — exceedingly; *oṣṭha* — the upper lip; *adharam* — the lower lip; *asya* — His; *komalam* — tender.

**49.** Fresh bandhuka flowers, fresh shoots, corals and bimba fruits, all at once and constantly, served with their beauty His lips — exceedingly tender, charming to the world.

*Note.* The bandhuka is a red flower; the bimba a red fruit. Both are standard comparisons for lips.

रदावलीसम्भवसम्पदुत्सुका
स्थिता परं संप्रति मौक्तिकद्युतिः ॥५०॥

*śaran-niśā-śobhā-sura-sāndra-candrikā*
*smitaṁ siṣeve 'sya jagan-manoramam |*
*radāvalī-sambhava-sampad-utsukā*
*sthitā paraṁ samprati mauktika-dyutiḥ ||50||*

*Word for word:* *śarat* — of autumn; *niśā* — of the night; *śobhā* — of the beauty; *(bhā)sura* — shining; *sāndra* — dense; *candrikā* — moonlight; *smitam* — the smile; *siṣeve* — served; *asya* — His; *jagat* — the world; *manoramam* — charming; *rada* — of teeth; *āvalī* — of the row; *sambhava* — of the appearance; *sampat* — for the riches; *utsukā* — eager; *sthitā* — stands; *param* — only; *samprati* — now; *mauktika* — of pearls; *dyutiḥ* — the lustre.

**50.** The dense, shining moonlight of a beautiful autumn night served His smile, which charms the world; while the lustre of pearls, eager for the riches [it will gain] when His row of teeth appears, for now only stands waiting.

*Note.* (?) The first pada is one syllable longer than the *vaṁśastha* metre allows — so too in Goswami's edition (GGM: *śobhāsura*); probably the correct reading is *śaran-niśā-bhāsura-sāndra-candrikā* ("the shining, dense moonlight of an autumn night"). The newborn has no teeth yet: hence the pearls, which will serve His teeth, "for now only stand waiting".

*Note.* A neck with three folds, "like a conch", is one of the marks of a great personality (*mahāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇa*).

*babhau pitur mānasa-haṁsa utsukaḥ ||61||*

*Word for word:* *kalasya* — of the sweet, lisping; *pīyūṣa* — of nectar; *payodhi* — of the ocean; *visphurat* — of the sparkling; *taraṅga* — of the waves; *vipruṭ* — of drops; *prakarasya* — [like] a spray; *komalaiḥ* — by tender; *vacaḥ* — of speech; *vilāsasya* — of the play; *kiyadbhiḥ* — by a few; *udgamaiḥ* — by the first stirrings; *babhau* — shone; *pituḥ* — of the father; *mānasa* — of the heart (of Manasa); *haṁsaḥ* — the swan; *utsukaḥ* — eager.

**61.** By a few tender first stirrings of His sweet, lisping play of speech — like a spray of drops from the sparkling waves of an ocean of nectar — the swan of His father's heart shone with eagerness.

*Note.* A play on words: *mānasa* is "heart, mind" and also Manasa, the Himalayan lake towards which, in poetic tradition, swans are drawn.

### Verse 62

भविष्यतीदं निजकीर्त्तनादिभि-
र्विलासलावण्यसुधामयैर्जगत् ।
इतीव विश्वम्भर इत्युदारधी-
रचीकॢपन्नाम मनोरमाशयः ॥६२॥

*bhaviṣyatīdaṁ nija-kīrtanādibhir*
*vilāsa-lāvaṇya-sudhāmayair jagat |*
*itīva viśvambhara ity udāra-dhīr*
*acīkḷpan nāma manoramāśayaḥ ||62||*

*Word for word:* *bhaviṣyati* — will be [filled]; *idam* — this; *nija* — with His own; *kīrtana* — with kirtana; *ādibhiḥ* — and the rest; *vilāsa* — of pastimes; *lāvaṇya* — of loveliness; *sudhā* — with nectar; *mayaiḥ* — full; *jagat* — world; *iti* — thus; *iva* — as if [thinking]; *viśvambharaḥ* — "Vishvambhara"; *iti* — thus; *udāra* — generous; *dhīḥ* — [whose] mind; *acīkḷpat* — gave; *nāma* — the name; *manorama* — lovely; *āśayaḥ* — [whose] intentions.

**62.** "This world will be [filled] with His kirtana and His other [pastimes], full of the nectar of playful loveliness" — as if thinking thus, [the father,] generous of mind and lovely in his intentions, gave Him the name Vishvambhara.

*Note.* *Viśvam-bhara* — "He who bears, sustains and fills the universe". The edition, like GGM, has *भविष्यति* ("will be"), and the phrase is elliptical. The reading *भरिष्यति* ("will fill") would explain the name directly, but the edition does not support it.

प्रतप्तकार्त्तस्वरशैलभासुर-

विलोलनीलालकभालमण्डलो
रराज राजन्मरुदंशुकोऽसकौ ॥६३॥

*pratapta-kārtasvara-śaila-bhāsura-*
*sphurat-tanuḥ smera-mukhendu-vibhramaḥ |*
*vilola-nīlālaka-bhāla-maṇḍalo*
*rarāja rājan-marud-aṁśuko 'sakau ||63||*

*Word for word:* *pratapta* — of molten; *kārtasvara* — gold; *śaila* — of a mountain; *bhāsura* — with the radiance; *sphurat* — flashing; *tanuḥ* — [whose] body; *smera* — of a smiling; *mukha* — of the face; *indu* — of the moon; *vibhramaḥ* — [having] the charm; *vilola* — with tossing; *nīla* — dark; *alaka* — curls; *bhāla* — of the forehead; *maṇḍalaḥ* — [having] the round; *rarāja* — shone; *rājat* — with gleaming; *marut* — wind; *aṁśukaḥ* — clad; *asakau* — this little one.

**63.** His body flashing with the radiance of a mountain of molten gold, with the charm of a smiling moon-face, His round forehead framed by tossing dark curls, this little one shone, clad in the gleaming wind.

*Note.* "Clad in the wind" means naked. *Asakau* is a diminutive of *asau* ("he"): an affectionate "this little one".

### Verse 64

अशेषमाधुर्य्यनिधेः समाहृतं

*Word for word:* *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *samāsādya* — having attained; *sa-śaiśavam* — childhood; *navam* — fresh; *nava* — the young; *indu* — moon; *vat* — like; *nitya* — ever; *navam* — new; *vyavardhata* — grew; *aśeṣa* — of all; *mādhurya* — sweetness; *nidheḥ* — from the treasury; *samāhṛtam* — drawn out; *mahā-mahā* — the greatest of great; *ratnam* — jewel; *iva* — like; *ati* — exceedingly; *harṣadam* — giving joy.

**64.** Having entered upon fresh childhood, the Lord grew like the young moon, ever new — like the greatest of great jewels, drawn out of the treasury of all sweetness and giving exceeding joy.

झणज्झणत्कारमनोज्ञकङ्कण-

*Word for word:* *jhaṇat-jhaṇat* — "jhan-jhan"; *kāra* — with the sound; *manojña* — of charming; *kaṅkaṇa* — bracelets; *pravāla* — of coral; *muktā* — of pearls; *maṇi* — of gems; *hāra* — of necklaces; *vibhramaiḥ* — with the charms; *nitamba* — of the hips; *bimba* — on the round; *eka* — alone; *vilambi* — hanging; *kiṅkiṇī* — of little bells; *raveṇa* — with the tinkling; *śaśvat* — continually; *kutukī* — playful; *nanarta* — danced; *saḥ* — He.

**65.** To the charming "jhan-jhan" of His bracelets, with the beauty of His necklaces of coral, pearls and gems, and to the tinkling of the little bells that alone hung upon the round of His hips, the playful child danced continually.

### Verse 66

अथैष कालेन शनैः शनैः क्षितौ
पदारविन्दं मधुमाधुरीमयम् ।
न्यस्यन्नमुष्याश्चिरविप्रयोगजं
जहार तापं करुणापयोनिधिः ॥६६॥

*athaiṣa kālena śanaiḥ śanaiḥ kṣitau*
*padāravindaṁ madhu-mādhurī-mayam |*
*nyasyann amuṣyāś cira-viprayoga-jaṁ*
*jahāra tāpaṁ karuṇā-payonidhiḥ ||66||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *eṣaḥ* — He; *kālena* — in time; *śanaiḥ śanaiḥ* — little by little; *kṣitau* — on the earth; *pada* — of the foot; *aravindam* — the lotus; *madhu* — of honey; *mādhurī* — with the sweetness; *mayam* — full; *nyasyan* — placing; *amuṣyāḥ* — her; *cira* — from long; *viprayoga* — separation; *jam* — born; *jahāra* — took away; *tāpam* — the burning distress; *karuṇā* — of mercy; *payonidhiḥ* — the ocean.

**66.** Then in time He, the ocean of mercy, placing little by little on the earth His lotus feet, full of honeyed sweetness, took away her burning distress, born of long separation.

*Note.* His first steps. Verse 60 described His crawling; now the earth receives not His knees but His feet.

### Verse 67

खेलाविलासेन वयस्यबालकै-

नवैर्नवैः पल्लवसञ्चयैरमून्
जघान तैस्तैर्मुदितैः स चाहतः ॥६७॥

*khelā-vilāsena vayasya-bālakair*

*navair navaiḥ pallava-sañcayair amūn*

*Word for word:* *khelā* — of games; *vilāsena* — in the sport; *vayasya* — of His own age; *bālakaiḥ* — with boys; *vihartu* — to play; *kāmaḥ* — wishing; *kamanīya* — lovely; *vigrahaḥ* — [whose] form; *navaiḥ navaiḥ* — with the freshest; *pallava* — of shoots; *sañcayaiḥ* — with bunches; *amūn* — them; *jaghāna* — struck; *taiḥ taiḥ* — by each of them; *muditaiḥ* — delighted; *saḥ* — He; *ca* — and; *āhataḥ* — [was] struck.

**67.** He of lovely form, wishing to sport in playful games with boys of His own age, struck them with bunches of the freshest shoots, and was struck in turn by each of them in their delight.

### Verse 68

तमेकदा तैः शिशुभिर्निरन्तरं
खेलन्तमेनं जननी विलोक्य सा ।
अभूद्विधर्त्तुं कृतकैतवं रुषा
समुद्यता तं क्षणमत्युदारधीः ॥६८॥

*tam ekadā taiḥ śiśubhir nirantaraṁ*
*khelantam enaṁ jananī vilokya sā |*

*Word for word:* *tam* — Him; *ekadā* — once; *taiḥ* — with those; *śiśubhiḥ* — children; *nirantaram* — ceaselessly; *khelantam* — playing; *enam* — Him; *jananī* — the mother; *vilokya* — having seen; *sā* — she; *abhūt* — became; *vidhartum* — to seize; *kṛta* — assumed; *kaitavam* — feignedly; *ruṣā* — with anger; *samudyatā* — ready; *tam* — Him; *kṣaṇam* — for a moment; *ati* — very; *udāra* — noble; *dhīḥ* — [whose] mind.

**68.** Once His mother saw Him playing ceaselessly with those children; and she, most noble-minded, with a show of feigned anger, for a moment made ready to seize Him.

### Verse 69

विलोक्य तामित्थमसौ रुषान्वितो
बभञ्ज भाण्डानि बहूनि सन्ततम् ।
तमीदृशं तत्र विलोक्य सा शची
बबन्ध भीता स्वयमप्यतिस्फुटम् ॥६९॥

*vilokya tām ittham asau ruṣānvito*
*babhañja bhāṇḍāni bahūni santatam |*
*tam īdṛśaṁ tatra vilokya sā śacī*
*babandha bhītā svayam apy atisphuṭam ||69||*

*Word for word:* *vilokya* — having seen; *tām* — her; *ittham* — thus; *asau* — He; *ruṣā* — with anger; *anvitaḥ* — filled; *babhañja* — broke; *bhāṇḍāni* — pots; *bahūni* — many; *santatam* — one after another; *tam* — Him; *īdṛśam* — such; *tatra* — there; *vilokya* — having seen; *sā* — she; *śacī* — Shachi; *babandha* — bound; *bhītā* — frightened; *svayam* — herself; *api* — even; *ati* — quite; *sphuṭam* — openly.

**69.** Seeing her thus, He was filled with anger and broke many pots one after another. Seeing Him like this, Shachi, frightened, bound Him herself, quite openly.

*Note.* A direct parallel to the *Damodara-lila*: Yashoda binds Krishna for a broken pot. Murari Gupta names this parallel outright: "in ancient times Yashoda likewise bound this child with ropes for cows".

### Verse 70

उपर्युपर्याहितभाण्डसंहतौ
सुगर्हितोच्छिष्टविसर्ज्जनस्थले ।
जगाम मातुः पुरतो महाप्रभुः
प्रकाशयन् ज्ञानपरां स विज्ञताम् ॥७०॥

*upary-upary-āhita-bhāṇḍa-saṁhatau*
*su-garhitocchiṣṭa-visarjana-sthale |*
*jagāma mātuḥ purato mahāprabhuḥ*
*prakāśayan jñāna-parāṁ sa vijñatām ||70||*

*Word for word:* *upari upari* — one upon another; *āhita* — piled; *bhāṇḍa* — of pots; *saṁhatau* — onto the heap; *su* — most; *garhita* — despised; *ucchiṣṭa* — of leftovers; *visarjana* — of throwing away; *sthale* — at the place; *jagāma* — went; *mātuḥ* — of the mother; *purataḥ* — before the eyes; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *prakāśayan* — displaying; *jñāna* — to knowledge; *parām* — devoted; *saḥ* — He; *vijñatām* — wisdom.

**70.** Before His mother's eyes Mahaprabhu went up onto a heap of pots piled one upon another, at the most despised place where leftover food is thrown away, displaying a wisdom wholly given to knowledge.

*Note.* A famous episode: Nimai sits on discarded pots in which food had been cooked (by the rules of purity they are unclean) and instructs His mother. It is found in the Chaitanya-bhagavata (Adi 7, the same chapter in which Vishvarupa takes sannyasa) and in Murari Gupta ("in the mood of Dattatreya").

जहीहि ताताशुचिदेशसंस्थितिं

**71.** Seeing her son gone to that exceedingly unclean place, Shachi spoke in words faltering with fear: "Child, do not stay in an unclean place! Make Yourself pure and come to my lap."

निशम्य मातुर्वचनं महाप्रभु-

*Word for word:* *niśamya* — having heard; *mātuḥ* — of the mother; *vacanam* — the words; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *nyarūpayat* — expounded; *sat* — of being; *cit* — of the conscious; *acit* — of the non-conscious; *svarūpatām* — the nature; *avehi* — understand; *mātaḥ* — O Mother; *vacanam* — word; *mama* — My; *īdṛśam* — such; *jahi* — give up; *bhramam* — delusion; *cetasi* — in the mind; *vibhrama* — by confusion; *ākule* — troubled.

**72.** Hearing His mother's words, Mahaprabhu expounded the nature of being — of the conscious and the non-conscious: "Mother, understand this word of Mine: give up the delusion in your mind, troubled as it is by confusion."

### Verse 73

इदं हि विश्वं सचराचरं तु य-
द्विलोक्यते तद्भ्रम एव केवलम् ।
पवित्रता वाप्यपवित्रतापि वा
कथं भवेदम्ब विचित्रमेव तत् ॥७३॥

*idaṁ hi viśvaṁ sa-carācaraṁ tu yad*
*vilokyate tad bhrama eva kevalam |*
*pavitratā vāpy apavitratāpi vā*
*kathaṁ bhaved amba vicitram eva tat ||73||*

*Word for word:* *idam* — this; *hi* — indeed; *viśvam* — universe; *sa* — with; *cara* — the moving; *acaram* — and the unmoving; *tu* — and; *yat* — what; *vilokyate* — is seen; *tat* — that; *bhramaḥ* — delusion; *eva* — merely; *kevalam* — only; *pavitratā* — purity; *vā api* — or; *apavitratā* — impurity; *api vā* — or else; *katham* — how; *bhavet* — can there be; *amba* — O Mother; *vicitram* — strange; *eva* — indeed; *tat* — that.

**73.** "This whole universe, with all that moves and does not move — whatever is seen — is delusion and nothing more. How then can there be purity, or impurity, Mother? That is strange indeed."

### Verse 74

यतो ह्यनानात्व इहैतदात्मनो
घटेत नैवेदमहं ममेत्यपि ।
स एक आत्मैव सदावशिष्यते
तदन्यदेतत्सकलं हि विभ्रमः ॥७४॥

*yato hy anānātva ihaitad-ātmano*
*ghaṭeta naivedam ahaṁ mamety api |*
*sa eka ātmaiva sadāvaśiṣyate*
*tad-anyad etat sakalaṁ hi vibhramaḥ ||74||*

*Word for word:* *yataḥ* — since; *hi* — indeed; *anānātve* — in the absence of multiplicity; *iha* — here; *etat* — of this; *ātmanaḥ* — of the Self; *ghaṭeta* — is fitting; *na eva* — not at all; *idam* — "this"; *aham* — "I"; *mama* — "mine"; *iti* — thus; *api* — even; *saḥ* — that; *ekaḥ* — one; *ātmā* — Self; *eva* — alone; *sadā* — always; *avaśiṣyate* — remains; *tat* — from it; *anyat* — other; *etat* — this; *sakalam* — all; *hi* — indeed; *vibhramaḥ* — delusion.

**74.** "For since there is no multiplicity here in this Self, there is no room at all even for 'this', 'I' and 'mine'. That one Self alone always remains; all this, which is other than it, is delusion."

*Note.* This is the teaching of Advaita Vedanta (absolute non-dualism). The Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition does not share it, and later Chaitanya Himself refutes it in His debates with the Mayavadis (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 6, 25). Here the child is playing the sage: the Chaitanya-bhagavata (Adi 7) and Murari state plainly that He taught "in the mood of Dattatreya". The comic side of the scene: a little boy sitting on scraps of leftover food lectures His mother that purity does not exist.

### Verse 75

इदं हि यद्वा सुरमर्त्त्यरक्षसां
तनूषु सर्व्वासु वसन्ति पञ्च ते ।
क्षितिर्जलं व्योम महो मरुत्तत-
स्तदात्मकं सर्व्वमभिन्नमेव हि ॥७५॥

*idaṁ hi yad vā sura-martya-rakṣasāṁ*
*tanūṣu sarvāsu vasanti pañca te |*
*kṣitir jalaṁ vyoma maho marut tatas*
*tad-ātmakaṁ sarvam abhinnam eva hi ||75||*

*Word for word:* *idam* — this; *hi* — indeed; *yat vā* — or else; *sura* — of gods; *martya* — of mortals; *rakṣasām* — of Rakshasas; *tanūṣu* — in the bodies; *sarvāsu* — in all; *vasanti* — dwell; *pañca* — five; *te* — those [elements]; *kṣitiḥ* — earth; *jalam* — water; *vyoma* — space; *mahaḥ* — light; *marut* — wind; *tataḥ* — therefore; *tat* — of them; *ātmakam* — consisting; *sarvam* — everything; *abhinnam* — undivided; *eva* — indeed; *hi* — surely.

**75.** "Or else, consider this: in all bodies — of gods, of mortals and of Rakshasas — dwell those five: earth, water, space, light and wind. Therefore everything, being made of them, is indeed undivided."

*Note.* *Mahas*, "light, radiance", here stands for the element of fire (*tejas*).

### Verse 76

अतः पवित्रं सकलं हि वस्तुतो
न चापवित्रं कियदप्यदो भुवि ।
इत्थं वदन्तं तमुदारधीः शची
दधार सा पाणियुगेन सत्वरा ॥७६॥

*ataḥ pavitraṁ sakalaṁ hi vastuto*
*na cāpavitraṁ kiyad apy ado bhuvi |*
*itthaṁ vadantaṁ tam udāra-dhīḥ śacī*
*dadhāra sā pāṇi-yugena satvarā ||76||*

*Word for word:* *ataḥ* — therefore; *pavitram* — pure; *sakalam* — everything; *hi* — indeed; *vastutaḥ* — in truth; *na* — not; *ca* — and; *apavitram* — impure; *kiyat api* — in the least; *adaḥ* — this; *bhuvi* — on earth; *ittham* — thus; *vadantam* — speaking; *tam* — Him; *udāra* — noble; *dhīḥ* — [whose] mind; *śacī* — Shachi; *dadhāra* — seized; *sā* — she; *pāṇi* — of hands; *yugena* — with the pair; *satvarā* — quickly.

**76.** "Therefore in truth everything is pure, and nothing here on earth is in the least impure." As He was speaking thus, noble-minded Shachi quickly seized Him with both hands.

### Verse 77

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *samānīya* — having brought; *surāpagā* — of the river of the gods; *jalam* — water; *sutam* — the son; *parisnāpya* — having bathed; *mudam* — joy; *parām* — the highest; *yayau* — attained; *tataḥ* — then; *ca* — and; *kālena* — after a time; *tathā eva* — just so; *tam* — Him; *śacī* — Shachi; *vilokya* — having seen; *tatra eva* — in that very place; *tatarja* — scolded; *bhāṣitaiḥ* — with words.

*Note.* *Surāpagā*, "the river of the gods", is the Ganga.

*Note.* The unseen guests are, according to tradition, demigods who come to see the Lord.

*Note.* *Tulākoṭi* is an anklet with little bells. The paradox — the sound grows as He moves away — is a sign of the miraculous; it continues in verse 88.

### Verse 88

*pitā ca mātā ca su-nūpura-svanaṁ*
*padābjayoḥ kevalayor manoramam |*
*akāla-saṁphulla-payoruhollasan-*
*madhuvratasyeva ravaṁ tad āśṛṇot ||88||*

*Word for word:* *pitā* — the father; *ca* — and; *mātā* — the mother; *ca* — and; *su* — beautiful; *nūpura* — of anklets; *svanam* — the jingling; *pada* — of the feet; *abjayoḥ* — of the lotuses; *kevalayoḥ* — of the bare; *manoramam* — charming; *akāla* — out of season; *saṁphulla* — in blossomed; *payoruha* — in a lotus; *ullasat* — rejoicing; *madhuvratasya* — of a bee; *iva* — like; *ravam* — the hum; *tadā* — then; *aśṛṇot* — heard.

**88.** Both father and mother then heard the beautiful, charming jingling of anklets from His bare lotus feet — like the hum of a bee rejoicing in a lotus that has blossomed out of season.

*Note.* *Kevala*, "alone, mere": the feet are bare, there are no anklets on them, yet the jingling is heard. A lotus opens by day; "out of season" means at night — this too is a sign of the miraculous. The singular verb with two subjects is a permissible licence; in the edition the end of the line is smudged (*tadāśṛṇo…*).

**91.** He was endowed with omniscience; his consciousness clung to the lotus feet of the Lord, and his mind was unattached to the world. Great of intellect, he had attained complete tranquillity and self-control.
