*sa citta-vṛttyā nitarāṁ vyamīmṛgat*
*kṣaṇena tāṁ tat-kalanāṁ viveda saḥ ||92||*

*Word for word:* *pitā* — the father; *vicintya* — having contemplated; *atha* — then; *vivāha* — of marriage; *maṅgalam* — the auspicious rite; *guṇasya* — to the virtues; *rūpasya* — to the beauty; *tadā* — then; *ucitām* — suitable; *vadhūm* — a bride; *saḥ* — he; *citta* — of the mind; *vṛttyā* — by the working; *nitarām* — earnestly; *vyamīmṛgat* — searched for; *kṣaṇena* — in a moment; *tām* — that; *tat* — his; *kalanām* — intention; *viveda* — knew; *saḥ* — he [the son].

**92.** Then the father, contemplating the auspicious rite of marriage, searched earnestly in his thoughts for a bride suited to [his son's] virtues and beauty; and [the son] in a moment knew that intention of his.

### Verse 93

स विश्वरूपः पितरं तथाविधै-
र्मनोरथैरुत्सुकमाकलय्य तम् ।
गृहं विहाय द्युनदीञ्च सन्तरन्
ययौ जिहासुः सकलं महाशयः ॥९३॥

*sa viśvarūpaḥ pitaraṁ tathā-vidhair*
*manorathair utsukam ākalayya tam |*
*gṛhaṁ vihāya dyunadīñ ca santaran*
*yayau jihāsuḥ sakalaṁ mahāśayaḥ ||93||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — that; *viśvarūpaḥ* — Vishvarupa; *pitaram* — the father; *tathāvidhaiḥ* — with such; *manorathaiḥ* — with desires; *utsukam* — eager; *ākalayya* — having perceived; *tam* — him; *gṛham* — home; *vihāya* — having left; *dyunadīm* — the heavenly river; *ca* — and; *santaran* — crossing; *yayau* — went away; *jihāsuḥ* — wishing to abandon; *sakalam* — everything; *mahāśayaḥ* — great-hearted.

**93.** Perceiving that his father was eager with such desires, the great-hearted Vishvarupa, wishing to abandon everything, left home, crossed the heavenly river [the Ganga] and went away.

### Verse 94

चकार सन्न्यासमदभ्रविभ्रमो
गुणाम्बुधिः सोऽभिसमापितक्रियः ।
न निःस्पृहाणां जगतीह निष्फले
महाधियां धावति चित्तविभ्रमः ॥९४॥

*cakāra sannyāsam adabhra-vibhramo*
*guṇāmbudhiḥ so 'bhisamāpita-kriyaḥ |*
*na niḥspṛhāṇāṁ jagatīha niṣphale*
*mahā-dhiyāṁ dhāvati citta-vibhramaḥ ||94||*

*Word for word:* *cakāra* — accepted; *sannyāsam* — sannyasa; *adabhra* — of no small; *vibhramaḥ* — [full of] splendour; *guṇa* — of virtues; *ambudhiḥ* — the ocean; *saḥ* — he; *abhisamāpita* — having completed; *kriyaḥ* — [whose] rites; *na* — not; *niḥspṛhāṇām* — of the desireless; *jagati* — toward the world; *iha* — here; *niṣphale* — fruitless; *mahā* — of great; *dhiyām* — of intellect; *dhāvati* — runs; *citta* — of the mind; *vibhramaḥ* — the restless wandering.

**94.** That ocean of virtues, full of no small splendour, completed the rites and accepted sannyasa. For the minds of the desireless, the great of intellect, do not wander restlessly toward this fruitless world.

*Note.* Vishvarupa's sannyasa is narrated in the Chaitanya-bhagavata, Adi 7, and the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 15. The word *vibhrama* is used twice: in the first line "splendour, grace", in the last "restless wandering" of the mind.

### Verse 95

तदैतदाश्रुत्य पिता प्रसूश्च सा
विलापमुच्चैरकरोन्मुमोह च ।
ततः समाश्वास्य हिताभिलाषुकौ
सदाशिषं तत्र सुते प्रचक्रतुः ॥९५॥

*tadaitad āśrutya pitā prasūś ca sā*
*vilāpam uccair akaron mumoha ca |*
*tataḥ samāśvāsya hitābhilāṣukau*
*sad-āśiṣaṁ tatra sute pracakratuḥ ||95||*

*Word for word:* *tadā* — then; *etat* — this; *āśrutya* — having heard; *pitā* — the father; *prasūḥ* — the mother; *ca* — and; *sā* — she; *vilāpam* — lament; *uccaiḥ* — loud; *akarot* — made; *mumoha* — swooned; *ca* — and; *tataḥ* — then; *samāśvāsya* — having recovered; *hita* — [his] welfare; *abhilāṣukau* — the two desiring; *sat* — good; *āśiṣam* — blessing; *tatra* — there; *sute* — on the son; *pracakratuḥ* — bestowed.

**95.** Then, hearing of this, the father and the mother lamented aloud and swooned. Then, recovering and desiring his welfare, they bestowed their good blessings on their son there.

*Note.* The verbs *akarot* and *mumoha* are singular with two subjects.

### Verse 96

अयं वयो नूतनमेव संश्रितो
बताधिशिश्राय यतित्वमेव यत् ।
तदा विधातः करुणा विधीयतां
सदात्र धर्म्मे निरतो भवेद्यथा ॥९६॥

*ayaṁ vayo nūtanam eva saṁśrito*
*batādhiśiśrāya yatitvam eva yat |*
*tadā vidhātaḥ karuṇā vidhīyatāṁ*
*sadātra dharme nirato bhaved yathā ||96||*

*Word for word:* *ayam* — he; *vayaḥ* — age; *nūtanam* — young; *eva* — only; *saṁśritaḥ* — has reached; *bata* — alas; *adhiśiśrāya* — has embraced; *yatitvam* — the life of a renunciant; *eva* — already; *yat* — since; *tadā* — therefore; *vidhātaḥ* — O Creator; *karuṇā* — mercy; *vidhīyatām* — let be shown; *sadā* — always; *atra* — in this; *dharme* — in dharma; *nirataḥ* — devoted; *bhavet* — may be; *yathā* — so that.

**96.** "He has only just reached youth — and, alas, he has already embraced the life of a renunciant! Therefore, O Creator, show mercy, so that he may always remain devoted to this dharma."

### Verse 97

इतीह भूयोऽतिविलप्य दुःखितौ
कनिष्ठमेतस्य मनोरमं सुतम् ।
ननन्दतुः क्रोडगतं विधाय तौ
सुनिर्वृतौ तत्तनुसङ्गशर्म्मभिः ॥९७॥

*itīha bhūyo 'tivilapya duḥkhitau*
*kaniṣṭham etasya manoramaṁ sutam |*
*nanandatuḥ kroḍa-gataṁ vidhāya tau*
*su-nirvṛtau tat-tanu-saṅga-śarmabhiḥ ||97||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *iha* — here; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *ati* — bitterly; *vilapya* — having lamented; *duḥkhitau* — the two grieving; *kaniṣṭham* — the younger [brother]; *etasya* — of him; *manoramam* — charming; *sutam* — son; *nanandatuḥ* — rejoiced; *kroḍa* — to the lap; *gatam* — brought; *vidhāya* — having made; *tau* — they; *su* — fully; *nirvṛtau* — comforted; *tat* — of His; *tanu* — of the body; *saṅga* — of the contact; *śarmabhiḥ* — by the delights.

**97.** Thus the grieving pair lamented bitterly again and again. Then they took his younger brother, their charming son, onto their lap and rejoiced, wholly comforted by the delight of contact with His body.

### Verse 98

उवाच वाचामृतपूरपूर्णया
मृतस्य जीवप्रदया दयाम्बुधिः ।
तदङ्गवल्लीमवगाह्य मातरं
तथैव तातञ्च सदा द्रवन्मनाः ॥९८॥

*uvāca vācāmṛta-pūra-pūrṇayā*
*mṛtasya jīva-pradayā dayāmbudhiḥ |*
*tad-aṅga-vallīm avagāhya mātaraṁ*
*tathaiva tātañ ca sadā dravan-manāḥ ||98||*

*Word for word:* *uvāca* — spoke; *vācā* — with speech; *amṛta* — of nectar; *pūra* — with a flood; *pūrṇayā* — full; *mṛtasya* — to the dead; *jīva* — life; *pradayā* — giving; *dayā* — of compassion; *ambudhiḥ* — the ocean; *tat* — her; *aṅga* — of the body; *vallīm* — the creeper; *avagāhya* — having embraced (lit. plunged into); *mātaram* — to the mother; *tathā eva* — likewise; *tātam* — to the father; *ca* — and; *sadā* — ever; *dravat* — melting; *manāḥ* — [with] heart.

**98.** And the ocean of compassion, His heart ever melting, embraced the creeper of His mother's body and spoke to His mother, and likewise to His father, with words full of a flood of nectar — words that would give life even to the dead:

### Verse 99

गतोऽग्रजो मे भवतीमुपेक्ष्य य-
त्तितिक्षयासौ पितरञ्च शान्तिमान् ।
मयैव कार्य्या जनकस्य तेऽपि च
क्षणात्सपर्य्या सकलैव नित्यशः ॥९९॥

*gato 'grajo me bhavatīm upekṣya yat*
*titikṣayāsau pitarañ ca śāntimān |*
*mayaiva kāryā janakasya te 'pi ca*
*kṣaṇāt saparyā sakalaiva nityaśaḥ ||99||*

*Word for word:* *gataḥ* — has gone; *agrajaḥ* — elder brother; *me* — My; *bhavatīm* — you; *upekṣya* — having left; *yat* — since; *titikṣayā* — with forbearance; *asau* — he; *pitaram* — the father; *ca* — and; *śāntimān* — peaceful; *mayā* — by Me; *eva* — alone; *kāryā* — will be rendered; *janakasya* — to the father; *te* — to you; *api ca* — and also; *kṣaṇāt* — from this moment; *saparyā* — service; *sakalā* — all; *eva* — entire; *nityaśaḥ* — constantly.

**99.** "Since My elder brother, peaceful as he is, has forbearingly left you and Father and gone away, from this moment I alone will render all service to Father and to you, constantly."

### Verse 100

तदा तदाकर्णयतोर्वचोऽमृतं
कलस्वरेणातिगभीरमर्थतः ।
तदैव पित्रोरभवत्परिप्लुतं
सुखैरनेकैर्वपुरुत्तनूरुहम् ॥१००॥

*tadā tad ākarṇayator vaco 'mṛtaṁ*
*kala-svareṇāti-gabhīram arthataḥ |*
*tadaiva pitror abhavat pariplutaṁ*
*sukhair anekair vapur ut-tanūruham ||100||*

*Word for word:* *tadā* — then; *tat* — that; *ākarṇayatoḥ* — of the two listening; *vacaḥ* — of speech; *amṛtam* — the nectar; *kala* — with sweet; *svareṇa* — with tone; *ati* — very; *gabhīram* — deep; *arthataḥ* — in meaning; *tadā eva* — at once; *pitroḥ* — of the parents; *abhavat* — became; *pariplutam* — bathed; *sukhaiḥ* — with joys; *anekaiḥ* — with many; *vapuḥ* — the body; *ut* — erect; *tanūruham* — [with] hairs.

**100.** Then, as the parents listened to that nectar of His speech — sweet in tone and very deep in meaning — their bodies were at once bathed in many joys, and their hair stood on end.

### Verse 101

तदङ्गसङ्गामृतधारया तया
मनस्तयोराप्लुतमेव निश्चितम् ।
असंवृतान्तः परिवाहितेव सा
यदीक्षणद्वन्द्वपथेन निर्गता ॥१०१॥

*tad-aṅga-saṅgāmṛta-dhārayā tayā*
*manas tayor āplutam eva niścitam |*
*asaṁvṛtāntaḥ parivāhiteva sā*
*yad īkṣaṇa-dvandva-pathena nirgatā ||101||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — of His; *aṅga* — of the body; *saṅga* — of the contact; *amṛta* — of nectar; *dhārayā* — with the stream; *tayā* — with that; *manaḥ* — the heart; *tayoḥ* — of the two; *āplutam* — flooded; *eva* — indeed; *niścitam* — surely; *asaṁvṛta* — not contained; *antaḥ* — within; *parivāhitā* — overflowing; *iva* — as if; *sā* — it [the stream]; *yat* — since; *īkṣaṇa* — of the eyes; *dvandva* — of the pair; *pathena* — by the path; *nirgatā* — came out.

**101.** Their hearts were surely flooded by that stream of nectar of contact with His body: for, not contained within, it overflowed, as it were, and came out by way of their two eyes.

*Note.* That is, as tears of joy. The edition's *अक्षिण* is a misprint: the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *yad-īkṣaṇa-dvandva-pathena* ("by the path of the pair of eyes"; at the end GGM has *nirgataḥ*).

### Verse 102

पठन् सपर्य्यापर एव सर्व्वदा
तयोर्महाकारुणिकः सुखावहः ।
वयस्यभावेन वयस्यबालकै-
र्निरन्तरं खेलति खेलयत्यपि ॥१०२॥

*paṭhan saparyā-para eva sarvadā*
*tayor mahā-kāruṇikaḥ sukhāvahaḥ |*
*vayasya-bhāvena vayasya-bālakair*
*nirantaraṁ khelati khelayaty api ||102||*

*Word for word:* *paṭhan* — studying; *saparyā* — to service; *paraḥ* — devoted; *eva* — indeed; *sarvadā* — always; *tayoḥ* — to the two; *mahā* — greatly; *kāruṇikaḥ* — compassionate; *sukha* — joy; *āvahaḥ* — bringing; *vayasya* — of a friend; *bhāvena* — with the feeling; *vayasya* — of the same age; *bālakaiḥ* — with boys; *nirantaram* — constantly; *khelati* — plays; *khelayati* — makes [others] play; *api* — also.

**102.** Most compassionate, He studied and was always devoted to serving His parents, bringing them joy. And with the boys of His own age, as their friend, He played without end and got up games for them.

### Verse 103

स्वतन्त्रमालोक्य कदाचिदात्मजं
पिता वचोभिर्निरभर्त्सयन्मुहुः ।
ततो रजन्यां शयितोऽतिशुद्धधी-
र्ददर्श संस्वप्नमदभ्रभाग्यवान् ॥१०३॥

*svatantram ālokya kadācid ātmajaṁ*
*pitā vacobhir nirabhartsayan muhuḥ |*
*tato rajanyāṁ śayito 'ti-śuddha-dhīr*
*dadarśa saṁsvapnam adabhra-bhāgyavān ||103||*

*Word for word:* *svatantram* — self-willed; *ālokya* — seeing; *kadācit* — once; *ātmajam* — the son; *pitā* — the father; *vacobhiḥ* — with words; *nirabhartsayat* — scolded; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *tataḥ* — then; *rajanyām* — at night; *śayitaḥ* — lying asleep; *ati* — utterly; *śuddha* — pure; *dhīḥ* — [of] mind; *dadarśa* — saw; *saṁsvapnam* — a dream; *adabhra* — no small; *bhāgyavān* — possessing good fortune.

**103.** Once, seeing that his son was self-willed, the father scolded Him again and again. Then at night, as he slept, that man of utterly pure mind, possessed of no small good fortune, saw a dream.

### Verse 104

सुतः स्वतन्त्रो मम किं सदा भवे-
दतीवखेलाकुललोलमानसः ।
इतीव कृत्वा बहुमन्यते भवान्
न चैवमाविष्कृतगौरविग्रहम् ॥१०४॥

*sutaḥ svatantro mama kiṁ sadā bhaved*
*atīva-khelākula-lola-mānasaḥ |*
*itīva kṛtvā bahu-manyate bhavān*
*na caivam āviṣkṛta-gaura-vigraham ||104||*

*Word for word:* *sutaḥ* — son; *svatantraḥ* — self-willed; *mama* — my; *kim* — whether; *sadā* — always; *bhavet* — will be; *atīva* — excessively; *khelā* — with play; *ākula* — absorbed; *lola* — restless; *mānasaḥ* — [with] mind; *iti* — thus; *iva* — as it were; *kṛtvā* — having considered; *bahu-manyate* — hold in high esteem; *bhavān* — you; *na* — not; *ca* — and; *evam* — thus; *āviṣkṛta* — who has revealed; *gaura* — golden; *vigraham* — form.

**104.** [A brahmana said in the dream:] "Thinking, as it were, 'Will my son always be so self-willed, His mind restless and wholly absorbed in play?' — you do not hold in due esteem Him who has thus revealed a golden form."

*Note.* Who is speaking becomes clear from verse 106. This dream of Jagannatha Mishra is also told in the Chaitanya-bhagavata, Adi.

### Verse 105

पशुर्यथा स्पर्शसुखं महामणे-
र्भजन्नपीमं परिलोकयन्नपि ।
न वेत्ति तत्तत्सदसद्विवेचनां
स्वभावमुग्धस्य विवेचना कुतः ॥१०५॥

*paśur yathā sparśa-sukhaṁ mahā-maṇer*
*bhajann apīmaṁ parilokayann api |*
*na vetti tat-tat-sad-asad-vivecanāṁ*
*svabhāva-mugdhasya vivecanā kutaḥ ||105||*

*Word for word:* *paśuḥ* — an animal; *yathā* — as; *sparśa* — of the touch; *sukham* — the pleasure; *mahā* — of a great; *maṇeḥ* — of a gem; *bhajan* — enjoying; *api* — though; *imam* — it; *parilokayan* — looking it over; *api* — even; *na* — not; *vetti* — knows; *tat-tat* — of each thing; *sat* — of the valuable; *asat* — and the worthless; *vivecanām* — the discernment; *svabhāva* — by nature; *mugdhasya* — of one foolish; *vivecanā* — discernment; *kutaḥ* — whence.

**105.** "As an animal, though it enjoys the pleasant touch of a great gem and even looks it over, cannot discern the valuable from the worthless — for whence can discernment come to one who is foolish by nature?"

### Verse 106

इत्थं वचोभिर्बत भर्त्सयन्नमुं
द्विजो जगादातिरुषारुणेक्षणः ।
प्रबुद्ध आसीत्तत एव सन्मनाः
सुविस्मितस्तत्सकलं जगाद च ॥१०६॥

*itthaṁ vacobhir bata bhartsayann amuṁ*
*dvijo jagādāti-ruṣāruṇekṣaṇaḥ |*
*prabuddha āsīt tata eva sanmanāḥ*
*su-vismitas tat sakalaṁ jagāda ca ||106||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *vacobhiḥ* — with words; *bata* — ah; *bhartsayan* — scolding; *amum* — him; *dvijaḥ* — the brahmana; *jagāda* — spoke; *ati* — with great; *ruṣā* — with anger; *aruṇa* — red; *īkṣaṇaḥ* — [with] eyes; *prabuddhaḥ* — awake; *āsīt* — became; *tataḥ eva* — at once; *sat* — good; *manāḥ* — [with] heart; *su* — greatly; *vismitaḥ* — astonished; *tat* — that; *sakalam* — all; *jagāda* — told; *ca* — and.

**106.** Thus, scolding him with these words, the brahmana spoke, his eyes red with great anger. Then at once [Mishra] awoke, good-hearted [as he was], and, greatly astonished, told it all.

### Verse 107

निशम्य तं स्वप्नमतीव विस्मिता
बभूवुरुत्साहपराश्च मानवाः ।
मनोवचोभिः पुरुषर्षभं प्रभुं
महाशयोऽसाविति साधु मेनिरे ॥१०७॥

*niśamya taṁ svapnam atīva vismitā*
*babhūvur utsāha-parāś ca mānavāḥ |*
*mano-vacobhiḥ puruṣarṣabhaṁ prabhuṁ*
*mahāśayo 'sāv iti sādhu menire ||107||*

*Word for word:* *niśamya* — having heard; *tam* — that; *svapnam* — dream; *atīva* — greatly; *vismitāḥ* — astonished; *babhūvuḥ* — became; *utsāha* — to enthusiasm; *parāḥ* — given; *ca* — and; *mānavāḥ* — the people; *manaḥ* — with mind; *vacobhiḥ* — and with words; *puruṣa* — among men; *ṛṣabham* — the bull; *prabhum* — the Lord; *mahāśayaḥ* — a great soul; *asau* — He; *iti* — thus; *sādhu* — rightly; *menire* — deemed.

**107.** Hearing of that dream, the people were greatly astonished and filled with enthusiasm. In mind and in words they rightly deemed the Lord, the bull among men: "He is a great soul."

*Note.* *Puruṣarṣabha*, "bull among men", that is, the best of men — a common epic epithet.

### Verse 108

ततः कदाचिन्निवसन् स्वमन्दिरे
समुद्यदादित्यमहोमहोज्ज्वलः ।
स्वतेजसाध्वस्ततमिस्रसञ्चयो
जगाद देवो जननीं पुरःस्थिताम् ॥१०८॥

*tataḥ kadācin nivasan sva-mandire*
*samudyad-āditya-maho-mahojjvalaḥ |*
*sva-tejasā dhvasta-tamisra-sañcayo*
*jagāda devo jananīṁ puraḥ-sthitām ||108||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *kadācit* — once; *nivasan* — staying; *sva* — in His own; *mandire* — in the house; *samudyat* — of the rising; *āditya* — of the sun; *mahaḥ* — with the splendour; *mahā* — greatly; *ujjvalaḥ* — blazing; *sva* — with His own; *tejasā* — with radiance; *dhvasta* — [by whom] dispelled; *tamisra* — of darkness; *sañcayaḥ* — the masses; *jagāda* — said; *devaḥ* — the Lord; *jananīm* — to the mother; *puraḥ* — in front; *sthitām* — standing.

**108.** Then once, while He was staying in His own house, the Lord — blazing with the splendour of the rising sun, the masses of darkness dispelled by His own radiance — said to His mother, who stood before Him:

### Verse 109

संश्रूयतां मातरिदं वदामि य-
त्तथेति तस्योदितमाददे शची ।
यदुच्यते तात समस्तमेव तत्
करिष्यते तद्वद तात भाषितम् ॥१०९॥

*saṁśrūyatāṁ mātar idaṁ vadāmi yat*
*tatheti tasyoditam ādade śacī |*
*yad ucyate tāta samastam eva tat*
*kariṣyate tad vada tāta bhāṣitam ||109||*

*Word for word:* *saṁśrūyatām* — let it be heard; *mātaḥ* — O Mother; *idam* — this; *vadāmi* — I say; *yat* — what; *tathā* — very well; *iti* — thus; *tasya* — His; *uditam* — words; *ādade* — accepted; *śacī* — Shachi; *yat* — what; *ucyate* — is said; *tāta* — O dear child; *samastam* — all; *eva* — indeed; *tat* — that; *kariṣyate* — will be done; *tat* — that; *vada* — speak; *tāta* — O dear child; *bhāṣitam* — what is to be said.

**109.** "Mother, listen to what I am going to say." "Very well," — Shachi accepted His words. "Whatever is said, dear child, all of it will be done. Speak, dear child, what You would say."

*Note.* The edition has *yam ucyate*; we read *yad ucyate*.

### Verse 110

कदापि मातर्हरिवासरे त्वया
न कार्य्यमेवादनमित्यसौ पुनः ।
जगाद पश्चात्तनुजोदितं शची
समाददे निर्भरभाग्यभूषिता ॥११०॥

*kadāpi mātar hari-vāsare tvayā*
*na kāryam evādanam ity asau punaḥ |*
*jagāda paścāt tanujoditaṁ śacī*
*samādade nirbhara-bhāgya-bhūṣitā ||110||*

*Word for word:* *kadā api* — ever; *mātaḥ* — O Mother; *hari* — of Hari; *vāsare* — on the day; *tvayā* — by you; *na* — not; *kāryam* — is to be done; *eva* — at all; *adanam* — eating; *iti* — thus; *asau* — He; *punaḥ* — then; *jagāda* — said; *paścāt* — afterwards; *tanuja* — by the son; *uditam* — what was said; *śacī* — Shachi; *samādade* — accepted; *nirbhara* — with full; *bhāgya* — with good fortune; *bhūṣitā* — adorned.

**110.** "Mother, never take food on the day of Hari," He then said. And Shachi, adorned with the fullness of good fortune, accepted what her son had said.

*Note.* *Hari-vāsara*, "the day of Hari", is Ekadashi, the eleventh lunar day, on which Vaishnavas fast. The boy teaches His mother to keep Ekadashi.

### Verse 111

पुनश्च ताम्बूलफलादि शुद्धिम-
न्निवेदितं यत्तदपास्य मातरम् ।
जगाद मातः परिपालयात्मनः
सुतस्य देहं चलितोऽहमञ्जसा ॥१११॥

*punaś ca tāmbūla-phalādi śuddhiman*
*niveditaṁ yat tad apāsya mātaram |*
*jagāda mātaḥ paripālayātmanaḥ*
*sutasya dehaṁ calito 'ham añjasā ||111||*

*Word for word:* *punaḥ* — then; *ca* — and; *tāmbūla* — betel; *phala* — fruits; *ādi* — and so on; *śuddhimat* — pure; *niveditam* — offered; *yat* — what; *tat* — that; *apāsya* — having cast aside; *mātaram* — to the mother; *jagāda* — said; *mātaḥ* — O Mother; *paripālaya* — protect; *ātmanaḥ* — of your own; *sutasya* — of the son; *deham* — the body; *calitaḥ* — departing; *aham* — I; *añjasā* — at once.

**111.** Then, casting aside the pure betel, fruits and other things that had been offered [to Him], He said to His mother: "Mother, take care of the body of your son. I am going away at once."

*Note.* The text has *calitaḥ*: "I am going" (literally, "I have set out").

### Verse 112

स इत्थमुत्थाय महाप्रभुः क्षितौ
पपात शम्पायुतकोटिकोटिवत् ।
इतीममालोक्य विसंज्ञमाकुला
सिषेच गङ्गासलिलैः शची चिरम् ॥११२॥

*sa ittham utthāya mahāprabhuḥ kṣitau*
*papāta śampāyuta-koṭi-koṭivat |*
*itīmam ālokya visaṁjñam ākulā*
*siṣeca gaṅgā-salilaiḥ śacī ciram ||112||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — He; *ittham* — thus [having spoken]; *utthāya* — having risen; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *kṣitau* — to the ground; *papāta* — fell; *śampā* — of lightning flashes; *ayuta* — of myriads; *koṭi-koṭi* — of millions upon millions; *vat* — like; *iti* — thus; *imam* — Him; *ālokya* — having seen; *visaṁjñam* — unconscious; *ākulā* — alarmed; *siṣeca* — sprinkled; *gaṅgā* — of the Ganga; *salilaiḥ* — with waters; *śacī* — Shachi; *ciram* — for a long time.

**112.** Having said this, Mahaprabhu rose up — and fell to the ground like millions upon millions of myriads of lightning flashes. Seeing Him thus unconscious, Shachi in alarm sprinkled Him with Ganga water for a long time.

### Verse 113

ततः प्रबोधस्थिरया धिया समं
नवप्रबोधाम्बुजराजदीक्षणः ।
समुत्थितोऽसौ महसा निसर्गिणा
समावृतः शारदचन्द्रवद्बभौ ॥११३॥

*tataḥ prabodha-sthirayā dhiyā samaṁ*
*nava-prabodhāmbuja-rājad-īkṣaṇaḥ |*
*samutthito 'sau mahasā naisargiṇā*
*samāvṛtaḥ śārada-candravad babhau ||113||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *prabodha* — by awakening; *sthirayā* — steadied; *dhiyā* — with mind; *samam* — together with; *nava* — newly; *prabodha* — opened; *ambuja* — like lotuses; *rājat* — shining; *īkṣaṇaḥ* — [with] eyes; *samutthitaḥ* — having risen; *asau* — He; *mahasā* — with splendour; *nisargiṇā* — with natural; *samāvṛtaḥ* — enveloped; *śārada* — the autumn; *candra* — moon; *vat* — like; *babhau* — shone.

**113.** Then, His mind steadied by awakening, His eyes shining like newly opened lotuses, He rose up, enveloped in His natural splendour, and shone like the autumn moon.

*Note.* *Prabodha* is used twice: the "awakening" of the mind and the "opening" of the lotus.

### Verse 114

तदा तदाश्रुत्य पितापि तादृशं
जगाम भूयः सह विस्मयं स्वयम् ।
उवाच वाचश्च सदर्थवाचिकाः
किमेतदेतत्किमितीतिरीतितः ॥११४॥

*tadā tad āśrutya pitāpi tādṛśaṁ*
*jagāma bhūyaḥ saha vismayaṁ svayam |*
*uvāca vācaś ca sad-artha-vācikāḥ*
*kim etad etat kim itīti rītitaḥ ||114||*

*Word for word:* *tadā* — then; *tat* — that; *āśrutya* — having heard; *pitā* — the father; *api* — too; *tādṛśam* — such; *jagāma* — came; *bhūyaḥ* — then; *saha* — with; *vismayam* — astonishment; *svayam* — himself; *uvāca* — spoke; *vācaḥ* — words; *ca* — and; *sat* — true; *artha* — meaning; *vācikāḥ* — expressing; *kim* — what; *etat* — this; *etat* — this; *kim* — what; *iti iti* — thus, thus; *rītitaḥ* — after the manner.

**114.** Then, hearing of such a thing, the father too came in person, full of astonishment, and spoke words that expressed his true meaning, after this manner: "What is this? This — what is it?"

*Note.* The last pada, with its repetitions (so also in GGM), conveys bewildered speech. *Rītitaḥ*, "after the manner [of]", is taken here as describing how the father spoke.

### Verse 115

तदाशयं तच्चरितं तदिङ्गितं
विदन्ति तद्विभ्रममत्र के जनाः ।
न हि स्वयम्भूः श्रुतयश्च ताः स्वयं
भवोऽपि तावत् प्रभवो भविष्णवः ॥११५॥

*tad-āśayaṁ tac-caritaṁ tad-iṅgitaṁ*
*vidanti tad-vibhramam atra ke janāḥ |*
*na hi svayambhūḥ śrutayaś ca tāḥ svayaṁ*
*bhavo 'pi tāvat prabhavo bhaviṣṇavaḥ ||115||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — His; *āśayam* — intention; *tat* — His; *caritam* — conduct; *tat* — His; *iṅgitam* — hints; *vidanti* — know; *tat* — His; *vibhramam* — play; *atra* — here; *ke* — what; *janāḥ* — people; *na hi* — for not; *svayambhūḥ* — the Self-born; *śrutayaḥ* — the Vedas; *ca* — and; *tāḥ* — those; *svayam* — themselves; *bhavaḥ* — Bhava (Shiva); *api* — even; *tāvat* — likewise; *prabhavaḥ* — lords; *bhaviṣṇavaḥ* — mighty.

**115.** What people here can know His intentions, His conduct, His hints, His play? For [they are known] neither to the Self-born [Brahma], nor to the Vedas themselves, nor even to Bhava and the other mighty lords.

*Note.* The last pada is corrupt in the edition ("भवोऽपित वत् प्रभोवो भविष्णवः"); the Gosvami edition (GGM) gives *bhavo 'pi tāvat prabhavo bhaviṣṇavaḥ*, and the same can be made out in the corrupt setting — so we read it. In the first pada GGM has *tad-āśrayaṁ* ("His shelter") instead of *tad-āśayaṁ*.

### Verse 116

गुरोर्गृहे सम्वसता महाधिया
समस्तविद्याः सकृतार्थताः कृताः ।
क्षणेन तस्मिन् विविशुश्च ताः स्वयं
पयोनिधौ नद्य इवोत्सुका भृशम् ॥११६॥

*guror gṛhe saṁvasatā mahā-dhiyā*
*samasta-vidyāḥ sa-kṛtārthatāḥ kṛtāḥ |*
*kṣaṇena tasmin viviśuś ca tāḥ svayaṁ*
*payonidhau nadya ivotsukā bhṛśam ||116||*

*Word for word:* *guroḥ* — of the teacher; *gṛhe* — in the house; *saṁvasatā* — by [Him] living; *mahā* — of great; *dhiyā* — [by Him] of intellect; *samasta* — all; *vidyāḥ* — branches of learning; *sa* — with; *kṛtārthatāḥ* — fulfilment of purpose; *kṛtāḥ* — were made; *kṣaṇena* — in a moment; *tasmin* — into Him; *viviśuḥ* — entered; *ca* — and; *tāḥ* — they; *svayam* — of themselves; *payonidhau* — into the ocean; *nadyaḥ* — rivers; *iva* — like; *utsukāḥ* — eager; *bhṛśam* — greatly.

**116.** Living in His teacher's house, He of great intellect brought all branches of learning to the fulfilment of their purpose; and of themselves they entered Him in a moment, like rivers eagerly rushing into the ocean.

### Verse 117

ततः पिता तस्य निवृत्तयौवनो
जरां स भेजे ज्वरितोऽतिदुर्बलः ।
तथाविधं तं परिलक्ष्य स प्रभु-
र्निनाय गङ्गातटभूमिमाकुलः ॥११७॥

*tataḥ pitā tasya nivṛtta-yauvano*
*jarāṁ sa bheje jvarito 'ti-durbalaḥ |*
*tathā-vidhaṁ taṁ parilakṣya sa prabhur*
*nināya gaṅgā-taṭa-bhūmim ākulaḥ ||117||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *pitā* — the father; *tasya* — His; *nivṛtta* — passed; *yauvanaḥ* — [whose] youth; *jarām* — old age; *saḥ* — he; *bheje* — reached; *jvaritaḥ* — feverish; *ati* — extremely; *durbalaḥ* — weak; *tathāvidham* — in such a state; *tam* — him; *parilakṣya* — having seen; *saḥ* — that; *prabhuḥ* — Lord; *nināya* — brought; *gaṅgā* — of the Ganga; *taṭa* — of the bank; *bhūmim* — to the ground; *ākulaḥ* — distressed.

**117.** Then His father, his youth gone by, reached old age; stricken with fever, he grew extremely weak. Seeing him in such a state, the Lord in distress brought him to the bank of the Ganga.

*Note.* By custom, one whose end is near is brought to the bank of the Ganga.

### Verse 118

पितुः पदं वक्षसि दुःखितात्मना
निधाय तेपे नितरां कृपावता ।
पितः क्व मां प्रोज्झ्य सुदीनमेककं
शिशुं कथं हन्त भवान् गमिष्यति ॥११८॥

*pituḥ padaṁ vakṣasi duḥkhitātmanā*
*nidhāya tepe nitarāṁ kṛpāvatā |*
*pitaḥ kva māṁ projjhya su-dīnam ekakaṁ*
*śiśuṁ kathaṁ hanta bhavān gamiṣyati ||118||*

*Word for word:* *pituḥ* — of the father; *padam* — the foot; *vakṣasi* — on the chest; *duḥkhita* — grieving; *ātmanā* — by [Him] of heart; *nidhāya* — having placed; *tepe* — grieved (lit. burned); *nitarām* — intensely; *kṛpāvatā* — by the compassionate one; *pitaḥ* — O Father; *kva* — where; *mām* — Me; *projjhya* — abandoning; *su* — utterly; *dīnam* — wretched; *ekakam* — lonely; *śiśum* — a child; *katham* — how; *hanta* — alas; *bhavān* — you; *gamiṣyati* — will go.

**118.** With a grieving heart the compassionate [Lord] placed His father's foot on His chest and lamented bitterly: "Father, where are you going? Alas, how can you go, abandoning Me — an utterly wretched, lonely child?"

### Verse 119

निशम्य वाक्यामृतमस्य हर्षदं
ततोऽन्तकाले द्विजपुङ्गवोऽसकौ ।
समर्पणं ते रघुनाथपादयोः
कृतं सुखी स्यामिति पुत्रमब्रवीत् ॥११९॥

*niśamya vākyāmṛtam asya harṣadaṁ*
*tato 'nta-kāle dvija-puṅgavo 'sakau |*
*samarpaṇaṁ te raghunātha-pādayoḥ*
*kṛtaṁ sukhī syām iti putram abravīt ||119||*

*Word for word:* *niśamya* — having heard; *vākya* — of the words; *amṛtam* — the nectar; *asya* — His; *harṣadam* — joy-giving; *tataḥ* — then; *anta* — of the end; *kāle* — at the time; *dvija* — of brahmanas; *puṅgavaḥ* — the best; *asakau* — this; *samarpaṇam* — the entrusting; *te* — of You; *raghunātha* — of Raghunatha; *pādayoḥ* — to the feet; *kṛtam* — has been made; *sukhī* — happy; *syām* — may I be; *iti* — thus; *putram* — to the son; *abravīt* — said.

**119.** Hearing the joy-giving nectar of His words, this best of brahmanas, at the hour of his end, said to his son: "I have entrusted You to the feet of Raghunatha; [now] may I be at peace."

*Note.* Raghunatha is Rama. *Syām* is first person: "may I be happy".

### Verse 120

अथ सा पतिपादपङ्कज-
द्वयमालिङ्ग्य सगद्गदस्वरम् ।
परिदेवनयानया मुहु-
र्बहुधा नेत्रजलैरसेचयत् ॥१२०॥

*atha sā pati-pāda-paṅkaja-*
*dvayam āliṅgya sa-gadgada-svaram |*
*paridevanayānayā muhur*
*bahudhā netra-jalair asecayat ||120||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *sā* — she; *pati* — of the husband; *pāda* — of the feet; *paṅkaja* — of the lotuses; *dvayam* — the pair; *āliṅgya* — having embraced; *sa* — with; *gadgada* — faltering; *svaram* — [with] voice; *paridevanayā* — with lament; *anayā* — with this; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *bahudhā* — abundantly; *netra* — of the eyes; *jalaiḥ* — with the waters; *asecayat* — bathed.

**120.** Then she [Shachi] embraced her husband's two lotus feet and, in a faltering voice, with this lament, again and again bathed them abundantly with the water of her eyes:

*Note.* From verse 120 the metre changes to *viyoginī*: by the custom of the mahakavya, the closing verses of a sarga are written in a different metre.

### Verse 121

अपि मां परिहाय दुःखिता-
मतिदीनां कुररीमिव प्रभो ।
क्व नु सम्प्रति यासि नीयतां
निजदासी बहुदुःखकर्षिता ॥१२१॥

*api māṁ parihāya duḥkhitām*
*ati-dīnāṁ kurarīm iva prabho |*
*kva nu samprati yāsi nīyatāṁ*
*nija-dāsī bahu-duḥkha-karṣitā ||121||*

*Word for word:* *api* — can it be that; *mām* — me; *parihāya* — leaving; *duḥkhitām* — grieving; *ati* — utterly; *dīnām* — forlorn; *kurarīm* — an osprey; *iva* — like; *prabho* — O lord; *kva* — where; *nu* — then; *samprati* — now; *yāsi* — are you going; *nīyatām* — let be taken; *nija* — your own; *dāsī* — maidservant; *bahu* — by many; *duḥkha* — sorrows; *karṣitā* — worn down.

**121.** "O my lord, will you really leave me — grieving, utterly forlorn, like a *kurari* bird? Where are you going now? Take with you your own maidservant, worn down by many sorrows."

*Note.* *Kurarī* is a bird of prey (the osprey); in Sanskrit poetry it is the symbol of a plaintive, lonely cry.

### Verse 122

दिवि देवगणे निरन्तरं
सुमनोवर्षिणि भूरिशः सुखात् ।
भुवि कीर्त्तनतत्परे जने
द्युनदीमध्यगतः स निर्ववौ ॥१२२॥

*divi deva-gaṇe nirantaraṁ*
*sumano-varṣiṇi bhūriśaḥ sukhāt |*
*bhuvi kīrtana-tatpare jane*
*dyunadī-madhya-gataḥ sa nirvavau ||122||*

*Word for word:* *divi* — in the sky; *deva* — of gods; *gaṇe* — the host [being]; *nirantaram* — unceasingly; *sumanaḥ* — flowers; *varṣiṇi* — raining; *bhūriśaḥ* — abundantly; *sukhāt* — from joy; *bhuvi* — on the earth; *kīrtana* — to kirtana; *tatpare* — devoted; *jane* — the people [being]; *dyunadī* — of the heavenly river; *madhya* — in the midst; *gataḥ* — situated; *saḥ* — he; *nirvavau* — passed away (lit. was extinguished).

**122.** While in the sky the hosts of gods, out of joy, rained down flowers abundantly and unceasingly, and on earth the people were absorbed in kirtana, he, standing in the midst of the heavenly river, passed away.

*Note.* *Nir-vā*, "to go out, to be extinguished", that is, to pass away. To leave the body in the waters of the Ganga amid kirtana is held to be a blessed end; hence the gods' rain of flowers.

*Iti śrī-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahākāvye dvitīyaḥ sargaḥ* — Thus ends the second sarga of the mahakavya "Sri Chaitanya-charitamrita".

---

## Sarga Three — verses 1–144

**Metre:** *upajāti* (11 syllables per pada) and *vaṁśastha* (12 syllables) in alternation; verses 143–144 — *praharṣiṇī*.

**Contents of the passage:**
- 1–4 — Gauranga's youth; His teachers.
- 5–11 — the meeting with Lakshmipriya on the way to the Ganga.
- 12–24 — the match: Shachi keeps silent, Nimai reproaches His mother, Vanamali obtains her consent.
- 25–39 — Vanamali at the house of Vallabhacharya; the praise of the bridegroom; the consent of the bride's father.
- 40–49 — the preparations: the fixing of the date, the *adhivasa*, the *nandimukha-shraddha*, music and the cries of "ulu-ulu".
- 50–58 — Shachi, being a widow, cannot perform the rites; Nimai weeps for His father and consoles His mother.
- 59–62 — the bride is adorned; the procession with the palanquin to Vallabha's house.
- 63–70 — the wedding rite: the *varana*, the exchange of flowers and the first glance, the giving away of the bride, *arghya* and *madhuparka*.
- 71–74 — the return home; Shachi welcomes the newly-weds.
- 75–81 — married life; a description of Lakshmipriya's beauty (*nakha-śikha*, "from the toenails to the crown of the head").
- 82–95 — the journey to East Bengal: the people are enchanted by Him; the river Padmavati; He teaches there for several months.
- 96–101 — at home Lakshmipriya serves Shachi and pines for her husband; the snakebite.
- 102–105 — the physicians are powerless; on the bank of the Ganga she leaves her body.
- 106–118 — Shachi's lament over her daughter-in-law; the funeral rites.
- 119–125 — Nimai returns and consoles His mother: "She was not merely a human being."
- 126–144 — the second marriage: the matchmaking of Kashinatha, the consent of Sanatana Mishra, Vishnupriya; the *adhivasa*, the procession, the rite.

### Verse 1

नवीनलावण्यसुधाम्बुधारा-
भृता नवीनेन सदङ्गकेन ।
तं यौवराज्ये सकलस्य यूनः
प्रसूनचापोऽभिषिषेच भूयः ॥१॥

*navīna-lāvaṇya-sudhāmbu-dhārā-*
*bhṛtā navīnena sad-aṅgakena |*
*taṁ yauvarājye sakalasya yūnaḥ*
*prasūna-cāpo 'bhiṣiṣeca bhūyaḥ ||1||*

*Word for word:* *navīna* — of fresh; *lāvaṇya* — of loveliness; *sudhā* — of nectar; *ambu* — of the water; *dhārā* — with streams; *bhṛtā* — filled; *navīnena* — with youthful; *sat* — beautiful; *aṅgakena* — with the body; *tam* — Him; *yauvarājye* — to the rank of crown prince (to the kingdom of youth); *sakalasya* — of all; *yūnaḥ* — of young men; *prasūna* — of flowers; *cāpaḥ* — [he whose] bow [is]; *abhiṣiṣeca* — anointed; *bhūyaḥ* — again.

**1.** With His youthful and beautiful body, filled with streams of the nectar-water of fresh loveliness, the god of the flower bow anointed Him once more as crown prince — sovereign of youth over all young men.

*Note.* "The god of the flower bow" is Kama, the god of love. A play on words: *yauvarājya* is "the rank of heir to the throne", but also "the kingdom of youth" (*yuvan*, a young man). The body full of streams of loveliness is itself, as it were, the vessel of the anointing.

### Verse 2

पपाठ सत्पण्डितविष्णुनाम्नः
सुदर्शनादप्यतिहर्षभाजः ।
गुरुत्वमाकल्प्य महानुकम्पां
चकार हर्षादनयोः किमेषः ॥२॥

*papāṭha sat-paṇḍita-viṣṇu-nāmnaḥ*
*sudarśanād apy ati-harṣa-bhājaḥ |*
*gurutvam ākalpya mahānukampāṁ*
*cakāra harṣād anayoḥ kim eṣaḥ ||2||*

*Word for word:* *papāṭha* — studied; *sat* — of the worthy; *paṇḍita* — of the pandita; *viṣṇu* — Vishnu; *nāmnaḥ* — by name; *sudarśanāt* — from Sudarshana; *api* — also; *ati* — of great; *harṣa* — joy; *bhājaḥ* — [from him] partaking; *gurutvam* — the position of teacher; *ākalpya* — having conferred; *mahā* — great; *anukampām* — kindness; *cakāra* — did; *harṣāt* — out of joy; *anayoḥ* — to these two; *kim* — was it not that; *eṣaḥ* — He.

**2.** He studied under the worthy pandita named Vishnu and also under Sudarshana, who was filled with great joy. Was it not out of joy that He did these two a great kindness, granting them the position of His teachers?

*Note.* There are two teachers here, Vishnu and Sudarshana.

### Verse 3

ततश्च वैयाकरणात्स गङ्गा-
दासादभूत्प्रत्यनुभूतविद्यः ।
यदेष विद्यामददाद्द्विजेभ्य-
स्तेनैव पुण्येन पपाठ सोऽत्र ॥३॥

*tataś ca vaiyākaraṇāt sa gaṅgā-*
*dāsād abhūt pratyanubhūta-vidyaḥ |*
*yad eṣa vidyām adadād dvijebhyas*
*tenaiva puṇyena papāṭha so 'tra ||3||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *ca* — and; *vaiyākaraṇāt* — from the grammarian; *saḥ* — He; *gaṅgādāsāt* — from Gangadasa; *abhūt* — became; *pratyanubhūta* — [one by whom] was fully realized; *vidyaḥ* — learning; *yat* — because; *eṣaḥ* — that [teacher]; *vidyām* — knowledge; *adadāt* — used to give; *dvijebhyaḥ* — to the brahmanas; *tena* — by that; *eva* — very; *puṇyena* — by the merit; *papāṭha* — studied; *saḥ* — He; *atra* — here (with him).

**3.** Then He mastered learning under the grammarian Gangadasa. Because that teacher used to give knowledge to the brahmanas, it was by that very merit [of his] that the Lord studied with him.

*Note.* Gangadasa Pandita was Nimai's principal teacher of grammar; all the biographies mention him.

### Verse 4

सतीर्थवृन्दैः परिहासवद्भि-
र्हसन् विशेषं सवदावदेन ।
ततान लीलाप्रतिभानवार्त्ता-
मुर्वीसदुर्वीसुरवंशरत्नम् ॥४॥

*satīrtha-vṛndaiḥ parihāsavadbhir*
*hasan viśeṣaṁ sa-vadāvadena |*
*tatāna līlā-pratibhāna-vārttām*
*urvī-sad-urvīsura-vaṁśa-ratnam ||4||*

*Word for word:* *satīrtha* — of fellow students; *vṛndaiḥ* — with throngs; *parihāsavadbhiḥ* — with jesting; *hasan* — laughing; *viśeṣam* — especially; *sa* — with; *vadāvadena* — eloquence; *tatāna* — spread; *līlā* — of playful; *pratibhāna* — wit; *vārttām* — talk; *urvī* — on the earth; *sat* — dwelling; *urvīsura* — of the brahmanas; *vaṁśa* — of the line; *ratnam* — the jewel.

**4.** Laughing with throngs of jesting fellow students, and with especial eloquence, He — the jewel of the line of the brahmanas who dwell on the earth — spread talk full of playful wit.

*Note.* *Urvī-sura*, "god of the earth", is a brahmana (cf. *kṣiti-deva*, 2.9).

### Verse 5

कदाचनासौ वनमालिनाम्नो
गृहे सदाचार्यवरस्य नाथः ।
जगाम सम्भाषरसेन हर्षा-
द्यदृच्छया श्रीमयगौरदेहः ॥५॥

*kadācanāsau vanamāli-nāmno*
*gṛhe sad-ācārya-varasya nāthaḥ |*
*jagāma sambhāṣa-rasena harṣād*
*yadṛcchayā śrī-maya-gaura-dehaḥ ||5||*

*Word for word:* *kadācana* — once; *asau* — He; *vanamāli* — Vanamali; *nāmnaḥ* — by name; *gṛhe* — to the house; *sat* — of the worthy; *ācārya* — of the acharya; *varasya* — of the excellent; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *jagāma* — went; *sambhāṣa* — of conversation; *rasena* — for the relish; *harṣāt* — with joy; *yadṛcchayā* — by chance; *śrī* — beauty; *maya* — full of; *gaura* — golden; *dehaḥ* — [whose] body.

**5.** Once the Lord, whose golden body was full of beauty, went by chance, joyfully, to the house of the worthy and excellent acharya named Vanamali, for the relish of conversation.

### Verse 6

निवर्त्तमानेन ततः सुखेन
संभाष्य तं वर्त्मनि तेन तत्र ।
अकारि पीयूषमिव क्षरन्ती
नेत्रातिथिः काचनहेमवल्ली ॥६॥

*nivartamānena tataḥ sukhena*
*saṁbhāṣya taṁ vartmani tena tatra |*
*akāri pīyūṣam iva kṣarantī*
*netrātithiḥ kācana hema-vallī ||6||*

*Word for word:* *nivartamānena* — by [Him] returning; *tataḥ* — then; *sukhena* — happily; *saṁbhāṣya* — having conversed; *tam* — with him; *vartmani* — on the road; *tena* — by Him; *tatra* — there; *akāri* — was made; *pīyūṣam* — nectar; *iva* — as if; *kṣarantī* — pouring forth; *netra* — of the eyes; *atithiḥ* — the guest; *kā cana* — a certain; *hema* — golden; *vallī* — creeper.

**6.** Having conversed with him, He was returning happily, and there on the road He made a certain golden creeper, pouring forth nectar, as it were, the guest of His eyes.

### Verse 7

सा वल्लभाचार्यसुता चलन्ती
स्नातुं सखीभिः सुरदीर्घिकायाम् ।
लक्ष्मीरनेनैव सहावतीर्णा
प्रभोर्ययौ लोचनवर्त्म तत्र ॥७॥

*sā vallabhācārya-sutā calantī*
*snātuṁ sakhībhiḥ sura-dīrghikāyām |*
*lakṣmīr anenaiva sahāvatīrṇā*
*prabhor yayau locana-vartma tatra ||7||*

*Word for word:* *sā* — she; *vallabha* — of Vallabha; *ācārya* — of the acharya; *sutā* — the daughter; *calantī* — going; *snātum* — to bathe; *sakhībhiḥ* — with her friends; *sura* — of the gods; *dīrghikāyām* — in the pond; *lakṣmīḥ* — Lakshmi; *anena* — with Him; *eva* — indeed; *saha* — together; *avatīrṇā* — descended; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *yayau* — came; *locana* — of the eyes; *vartma* — into the path; *tatra* — there.

**7.** She was the daughter of Vallabhacharya — Lakshmi herself, who had descended together with Him. Going with her friends to bathe in the river of the gods, she there came into the path of the Lord's eyes.

*Note.* *Sura-dīrghikā*, "the pond of the gods", is the Ganga. This scene of the meeting by the river is found also in the Chaitanya-bhagavata, Adi 10.

### Verse 8

विलोक्य स प्राक्तनवल्लभां तां
सुखाम्बुधौ मज्जनमाततान ।
नैसर्गिकं प्रेम यथावकाशं
प्रसह्य नामोदयतीह कं वा ॥८॥

*vilokya sa prāktana-vallabhāṁ tāṁ*
*sukhāmbudhau majjanam ātatāna |*
*naisargikaṁ prema yathāvakāśaṁ*
*prasahya nāmodayatīha kaṁ vā ||8||*

*Word for word:* *vilokya* — having seen; *saḥ* — He; *prāktana* — of old; *vallabhām* — beloved; *tām* — her; *sukha* — of happiness; *ambudhau* — in the ocean; *majjanam* — immersion; *ātatāna* — performed; *naisargikam* — natural; *prema* — love; *yathāvakāśam* — as occasion offers; *prasahya* — forcibly; *na* — not; *āmodayati* — delights; *iha* — here; *kam* — whom; *vā* — indeed.

**8.** Seeing her, His beloved of old, He plunged into the ocean of happiness. Whom indeed in this world does natural love not overpower with delight when the occasion offers?

*Note.* *Prāktana*, "former, of old": Lakshmipriya is the eternal consort of the Lord, Lakshmi.

### Verse 9

तथाविधां तामवलोक्य रामां
मनस्यभूदुल्लसितः कृपाब्धिः ।
मणिं विना दुर्लभमाभिराम्यं
न हैमनी हारलता प्रयाति ॥९॥

*tathā-vidhāṁ tām avalokya rāmāṁ*
*manasy abhūd ullasitaḥ kṛpābdhiḥ |*
*maṇiṁ vinā durlabham ābhirāmyaṁ*
*na haimanī hāra-latā prayāti ||9||*

*Word for word:* *tathāvidhām* — such; *tām* — her; *avalokya* — having seen; *rāmām* — lovely woman; *manasi* — in the heart; *abhūt* — became; *ullasitaḥ* — joyful; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *abdhiḥ* — the ocean; *maṇim* — a gem; *vinā* — without; *durlabham* — rare; *ābhirāmyam* — charm; *na* — not; *haimanī* — golden; *hāra* — of a necklace; *latā* — the strand; *prayāti* — attains.

**9.** Seeing such a lovely woman, the ocean of mercy rejoiced in His heart. Without a gem, a golden necklace strand does not attain a rare charm.

### Verse 10

सा शैशवादेकपदेन बाला
समागता यौवनसीम्नि किञ्चित् ।
परित्रुटच्चापलजायमान-
त्रपा तमालोक्य ननन्द शश्वत् ॥१०॥

*sā śaiśavād eka-padena bālā*
*samāgatā yauvana-sīmni kiñcit |*
*parituṭac-cāpala-jāyamāna-*
*trapā tam ālokya nananda śaśvat ||10||*

*Word for word:* *sā* — she; *śaiśavāt* — from childhood; *eka* — with one; *padena* — with a step; *bālā* — the girl; *samāgatā* — having come; *yauvana* — of youth; *sīmni* — to the border; *kiñcit* — a little; *paritruṭat* — breaking off; *cāpala* — [whose] restlessness; *jāyamāna* — being born; *trapā* — [whose] shyness; *tam* — Him; *ālokya* — having seen; *nananda* — rejoiced; *śaśvat* — continually.

**10.** The girl had come with a single step from childhood a little way over the border of youth: her childish restlessness was breaking off and shyness was being born. Seeing Him, she rejoiced continually.

### Verse 11

अथाजगामैष निरीक्ष्य कान्तां
तैस्तैर्वयस्यैर्विहरंस्तथैव ।
पठन्सदोद्ग्राहपरः परेशो
रराज गूढस्थिररम्यलीलः ॥११॥

*athājagāmaiṣa nirīkṣya kāntāṁ*
*tais tair vayasyair viharaṁs tathaiva |*
*paṭhan sadodgrāha-paraḥ pareśo*
*rarāja gūḍha-sthira-ramya-līlaḥ ||11||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *ājagāma* — returned; *eṣaḥ* — He; *nirīkṣya* — having gazed at; *kāntām* — the beloved; *taiḥ taiḥ* — with those [same]; *vayasyaiḥ* — with friends; *viharan* — sporting; *tathā eva* — just as before; *paṭhan* — studying; *sadā* — always; *udgrāha* — on going over [lessons]; *paraḥ* — intent; *pareśaḥ* — the Supreme Lord; *rarāja* — shone; *gūḍha* — hidden; *sthira* — steady; *ramya* — charming; *līlaḥ* — [whose] play.

**11.** Having gazed at His beloved, He returned, sporting just as before with those friends of His. Studying, ever intent on going over His lessons, the Supreme Lord shone, His charming play hidden and steady.

### Verse 12

अथापरेद्युर्वनमालिनामा
प्रभोः य आचार्य उपेत्य वेश्म ।
नमश्चकार प्रणतो महात्मा
शचीं शुचिः संकथयन्विधिज्ञः ॥१२॥

*athāparedyur vanamāli-nāmā*
*prabhoḥ ya ācārya upetya veśma |*
*namaś cakāra praṇato mahātmā*
*śacīṁ śuciḥ saṅkathayan vidhi-jñaḥ ||12||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *aparedyuḥ* — on the next day; *vanamāli* — Vanamali; *nāmā* — by name; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *yaḥ* — who; *ācāryaḥ* — the acharya; *upetya* — having come to; *veśma* — the house; *namaḥ cakāra* — paid homage; *praṇataḥ* — bowing down; *mahātmā* — the great soul; *śacīm* — to Shachi; *śuciḥ* — pure; *saṅkathayan* — conversing; *vidhi* — the proper rules; *jñaḥ* — knowing.

**12.** Then on the next day the acharya named Vanamali — a great soul, pure and versed in the proper rules of conduct — came to the Lord's house, bowed low and paid homage to Shachi, and entered into conversation [with her].

*Note.* Vanamali Acharya acts as the matchmaker (*ghaṭaka*), as in the Chaitanya-bhagavata, Adi 10.

### Verse 13

सुताय ते देवि वृतास्ति काचित्
कन्यातिधन्या गुणरूपशीलैः ।
सा वल्लभाचार्यसुता वराङ्गी
मूर्त्तेव लक्ष्मीः क्षितितोऽवतीर्णा ॥१३॥

*sutāya te devi vṛtāsti kācit*
*kanyāti-dhanyā guṇa-rūpa-śīlaiḥ |*
*sā vallabhācārya-sutā varāṅgī*
*mūrteva lakṣmīḥ kṣitito 'vatīrṇā ||13||*

*Word for word:* *sutāya* — for the son; *te* — your; *devi* — O lady; *vṛtā* — chosen; *asti* — there is; *kācit* — a certain; *kanyā* — maiden; *ati* — very; *dhanyā* — blessed; *guṇa* — with qualities; *rūpa* — with beauty; *śīlaiḥ* — and with character; *sā* — she; *vallabha* — of Vallabha; *ācārya* — of the acharya; *sutā* — the daughter; *varāṅgī* — fair of form; *mūrtā* — embodied; *iva* — like; *lakṣmīḥ* — Lakshmi; *kṣititaḥ* — to the earth (?); *avatīrṇā* — descended.

**13.** "O lady, for your son a certain maiden has been chosen, most blessed in qualities, beauty and character: that fair daughter of Vallabhacharya, like Lakshmi embodied, descended to the earth."

*Note.* *Vṛtā* ("chosen") can be understood in two ways: "chosen [as a bride] for your son", or "[the maiden] who has chosen your son". (?) *Kṣititaḥ* is an ablative ("from the earth"); the sense requires *kṣitau* ("on, to the earth"). The text is the same in Goswami's edition (GGM).

### Verse 14

विधीयतां तत्र लघुप्रयत्न-
स्तनूजरत्नस्य विवाहकार्य्ये ।
यदीच्छसि श्रीमति तां सदङ्गां
श्रियं वधूरत्नमनिन्द्यशीलाम् ॥१४॥

*vidhīyatāṁ tatra laghu-prayatnas*
*tanūja-ratnasya vivāha-kārye |*
*yadīcchasi śrīmati tāṁ sad-aṅgāṁ*
*śriyaṁ vadhū-ratnam anindya-śīlām ||14||*

*Word for word:* *vidhīyatām* — let be made; *tatra* — in that; *laghu* — slight; *prayatnaḥ* — effort; *tanūja* — of the son; *ratnasya* — of the jewel; *vivāha* — of the marriage; *kārye* — in the matter; *yadi* — if; *icchasi* — you desire; *śrīmati* — O glorious lady; *tām* — her; *sat* — beautiful; *aṅgām* — [whose] limbs; *śriyam* — Lakshmi; *vadhū* — of a bride; *ratnam* — a jewel; *anindya* — blameless; *śīlām* — [whose] character.

**14.** "If you desire, O glorious lady, that Lakshmi of lovely limbs, a jewel of a bride of blameless character, then let but a slight effort be made in the matter of the marriage of your jewel of a son."

### Verse 15

इत्यस्य संश्रुत्य वचोऽमृतं सा
तूष्णीमभून्नैव किमप्युवाच ।
अश्रद्दधाना वचनेऽस्य तस्मिन्
सुतेऽपि तल्लक्षणलक्षणार्था ॥१५॥

*ity asya saṁśrutya vaco 'mṛtaṁ sā*
*tūṣṇīm abhūn naiva kim apy uvāca |*
*aśraddadhānā vacane 'sya tasmin*
*sute 'pi tal-lakṣaṇa-lakṣaṇārthā ||15||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *asya* — his; *saṁśrutya* — having heard; *vacaḥ* — the words; *amṛtam* — nectar; *sā* — she; *tūṣṇīm* — silent; *abhūt* — became; *na eva* — not at all; *kim api* — anything; *uvāca* — said; *aśraddadhānā* — not trusting; *vacane* — in the word; *asya* — his; *tasmin* — in that; *sute* — in the son; *api* — also; *tat* — of that; *lakṣaṇa* — the signs; *lakṣaṇa* — of noting; *arthā* — desirous.

**15.** Having heard the nectar of his words, she fell silent and said nothing at all. She did not [fully] trust his word, and wished to note the signs of the same [desire] in her son as well.

### Verse 16

नैवाकलय्याशु वचांसि शच्या
ययौ स आचार्यवरोऽतिदुःखी ।
विलोकयामास मनःकथाभिः
कषायितास्योऽथ महाप्रभुं तम् ॥१६॥

*naivākalayyāśu vacāṁsi śacyā*
*yayau sa ācārya-varo 'ti-duḥkhī |*
*vilokayāmāsa manaḥ-kathābhiḥ*
*kaṣāyitāsyo 'tha mahāprabhuṁ tam ||16||*

*Word for word:* *na eva* — not at all; *ākalayya* — having heard; *āśu* — at once; *vacāṁsi* — words; *śacyāḥ* — of Shachi; *yayau* — went away; *saḥ* — that; *ācārya* — acharya; *varaḥ* — excellent; *ati* — very; *duḥkhī* — sad; *vilokayāmāsa* — saw; *manaḥ* — of the mind; *kathābhiḥ* — by the musings; *kaṣāyita* — clouded; *āsyaḥ* — [whose] face; *atha* — then; *mahāprabhum* — Mahaprabhu; *tam* — Him.

**16.** Hearing no word at all from Shachi straight away, that excellent acharya went away very sad. Then, his face clouded by the musings of his mind, he saw Mahaprabhu.

### Verse 17

असौ नवद्वीपकिशोरचन्द्र-
श्चन्द्राननश्चन्द्रसहस्रकान्तः ।
आचार्यमालोक्य ननाम हृष्टो
दृढं परिष्वज्य च धीरमूचे ॥१७॥

*asau navadvīpa-kiśora-candraś*
*candrānanaś candra-sahasra-kāntaḥ |*
*ācāryam ālokya nanāma hṛṣṭo*
*dṛḍhaṁ pariṣvajya ca dhīram ūce ||17||*

*Word for word:* *asau* — He; *navadvīpa* — of Navadvipa; *kiśora* — young; *candraḥ* — moon; *candra* — moon-like; *ānanaḥ* — [whose] face; *candra* — of moons; *sahasra* — a thousand; *kāntaḥ* — lovely [as]; *ācāryam* — the acharya; *ālokya* — having seen; *nanāma* — bowed; *hṛṣṭaḥ* — joyful; *dṛḍham* — firmly; *pariṣvajya* — having embraced; *ca* — and; *dhīram* — calmly; *ūce* — spoke.

**17.** He — the young moon of Navadvipa, moon-faced, lovely as a thousand moons — seeing the acharya, joyfully bowed to him, embraced him firmly and calmly said:

### Verse 18

आसीः क्व गन्ता त्वमये महात्मन्
कथं नु वा त्वं विमनाः प्रयासि ।
स आह मातुश्चरणौ तवैव
द्रष्टुं गतः सम्प्रति यामि दुःखी ॥१८॥

*āsīḥ kva gantā tvam aye mahātman*
*kathaṁ nu vā tvaṁ vimanāḥ prayāsi |*
*sa āha mātuś caraṇau tavaiva*
*draṣṭuṁ gataḥ samprati yāmi duḥkhī ||18||*

*Word for word:* *āsīḥ* — were; *kva* — where; *gantā* — gone; *tvam* — you; *aye* — O; *mahātman* — O great soul; *katham* — why; *nu vā* — then; *tvam* — you; *vimanāḥ* — downcast; *prayāsi* — go; *saḥ* — he; *āha* — said; *mātuḥ* — of the mother; *caraṇau* — the feet; *tava* — your; *eva* — indeed; *draṣṭum* — to see; *gataḥ* — gone; *samprati* — now; *yāmi* — I go; *duḥkhī* — sad.

**18.** "Where had you gone, O great soul? And why do you go [along] so downcast?" He said: "I had gone to see the feet of your mother; now I go [away] sad."

### Verse 19

न किञ्चिदूचे तमिदं स शृण्वन्
स्वमेव गेहं प्रययौ कृपाब्धिः ।
तदीयया तद्विमनस्तयासीत्
स्वयं दयावारिनिधिः सुदुःखी ॥१९॥

*na kiñcid ūce tam idaṁ sa śṛṇvan*
*svam eva gehaṁ prayayau kṛpābdhiḥ |*
*tadīyayā tad-vimanastayāsīt*
*svayaṁ dayā-vārinidhiḥ su-duḥkhī ||19||*

*Word for word:* *na* — not; *kiñcit* — anything; *ūce* — said; *tam* — to him; *idam* — this; *saḥ* — He; *śṛṇvan* — hearing; *svam* — own; *eva* — indeed; *geham* — to the house; *prayayau* — went; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *abdhiḥ* — the ocean; *tadīyayā* — by his; *tat* — that; *vimanastayā* — by the dejection; *āsīt* — became; *svayam* — Himself; *dayā* — of compassion; *vārinidhiḥ* — the ocean; *su* — very; *duḥkhī* — sad.

**19.** Hearing this, the ocean of mercy said nothing to him and went to His own house. But that dejection of his made the ocean of compassion Himself very sad.

### Verse 20

आगत्य गेहं जननीं ततोऽसौ
पप्रच्छ नाथः स्तनयित्नुधीरम् ।
किमुक्तमाचार्यवराय मात-
स्त्वया यतोऽसौ विमनाः प्रयाति ॥२०॥

*āgatya gehaṁ jananīṁ tato 'sau*
*papraccha nāthaḥ stanayitnu-dhīram |*
*kim uktam ācārya-varāya mātas*
*tvayā yato 'sau vimanāḥ prayāti ||20||*

*Word for word:* *āgatya* — having come; *geham* — home; *jananīm* — the mother; *tataḥ* — then; *asau* — He; *papraccha* — asked; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *stanayitnu* — like thunder; *dhīram* — deeply; *kim* — what; *uktam* — [was] said; *ācārya* — to the acharya; *varāya* — to the excellent; *mātaḥ* — O mother; *tvayā* — by you; *yataḥ* — that, because of which; *asau* — he; *vimanāḥ* — downcast; *prayāti* — goes away.

**20.** Then, having come home, the Lord asked His mother in a voice deep as thunder: "Mother, what did you say to the excellent acharya, that he goes away so downcast?"

### Verse 21

कथं न तस्यानुमतौ मतिस्ते
बभूव नामोदितमुक्तमस्य ।
प्रीतिर्यथा स्यात्सुजनस्य साधो-
स्तथैव कर्त्तुं सुजनः प्रमाणम् ॥२१॥

*kathaṁ na tasyānumatau matis te*
*babhūva nāmoditam uktam asya |*
*prītir yathā syāt sujanasya sādhos*
*tathaiva kartuṁ sujanaḥ pramāṇam ||21||*

*Word for word:* *katham* — why; *na* — not; *tasya* — with him; *anumatau* — towards agreement; *matiḥ* — the mind; *te* — your; *babhūva* — was [inclined]; *na* — not; *āmoditam* — approved; *uktam* — what was said; *asya* — by him; *prītiḥ* — pleasure; *yathā* — so that; *syāt* — there may be; *sujanasya* — of a good man; *sādhoḥ* — of a saintly; *tathā eva* — just so; *kartum* — to act; *sujanaḥ* — a good man; *pramāṇam* — the standard.

**21.** "Why was your mind not inclined to agree with him? Why was what he said not approved? To act just so that a good and saintly man is pleased — in this a good man is the standard."

*Note.* Mahaprabhu indirectly reveals His own wish.

### Verse 22

विज्ञाय पुत्रानुमतिं मुदासौ
प्रस्थापयामास तदात्मलोकम् ।
आचार्यवर्यानयनाय शीघ्रं
निष्पाद्यते किं न तदीच्छया यत् ॥२२॥

*vijñāya putrānumatiṁ mudāsau*
*prasthāpayāmāsa tadātma-lokam |*
*ācārya-varyānayanāya śīghraṁ*
*niṣpādyate kiṁ na tad-icchayā yat ||22||*

*Word for word:* *vijñāya* — having understood; *putra* — of the son; *anumatim* — the consent; *mudā* — with joy; *asau* — she; *prasthāpayāmāsa* — sent; *tadā* — then; *ātma* — her own; *lokam* — people; *ācārya* — the acharya; *varya* — excellent; *ānayanāya* — to bring; *śīghram* — quickly; *niṣpādyate* — is accomplished; *kim* — what; *na* — not; *tat* — His; *icchayā* — by the wish; *yat* — for.

**22.** Understanding that her son consented, she joyfully sent her own people at once to bring the excellent acharya quickly. For what is not accomplished by His wish?

### Verse 23

द्रुतं स आगत्य शचीं प्रणम्या-
वदत्किमाज्ञापयतीश्वरी मे ।
विधीयतेऽसौ शिरसा नियोगो
नियुज्यतां तत्तव किङ्करोऽस्मि ॥२३॥

*drutaṁ sa āgatya śacīṁ praṇamyā-*
*vadat kim ājñāpayatīśvarī me |*
*vidhīyate 'sau śirasā niyogo*
*niyujyatāṁ tat tava kiṅkaro 'smi ||23||*

*Word for word:* *drutam* — quickly; *saḥ* — he; *āgatya* — having come; *śacīm* — to Shachi; *praṇamya* — having bowed; *avadat* — said; *kim* — what; *ājñāpayati* — commands; *īśvarī* — the mistress; *me* — me; *vidhīyate* — is carried out; *asau* — this; *śirasā* — with the head; *niyogaḥ* — charge; *niyujyatām* — let it be enjoined; *tat* — therefore; *tava* — your; *kiṅkaraḥ* — servant; *asmi* — I am.

**23.** He came quickly, bowed to Shachi and said: "What does my mistress command me? Any charge is carried out [by me] with bowed head. So let it be enjoined: I am your servant."

### Verse 24

विज्ञापितं योऽस्ति यदत्र तात
तदेव कर्त्तुं त्वमिह प्रमाणम् ।
त्वं वत्सलोऽतीव सुहृत्कुटुम्बं
स्निग्धः स्वयं चेत्यथ सा जगाद ॥२४॥

*vijñāpitaṁ yo 'sti yad atra tāta*
*tad eva kartuṁ tvam iha pramāṇam |*
*tvaṁ vatsalo 'tīva suhṛt kuṭumbaṁ*
*snigdhaḥ svayaṁ cety atha sā jagāda ||24||*

*Word for word:* *vijñāpitam* — proposed; *yaḥ* — which (?); *asti* — is; *yat* — what; *atra* — here; *tāta* — O dear son; *tat* — that; *eva* — very [thing]; *kartum* — to carry out; *tvam* — you; *iha* — here; *pramāṇam* — the authority; *tvam* — you; *vatsalaḥ* — affectionate; *atīva* — very; *suhṛt* — a friend; *kuṭumbam* — kin; *snigdhaḥ* — dear; *svayam* — yourself; *ca* — and; *iti* — thus; *atha* — then; *sā* — she; *jagāda* — said.

**24.** Then she said: "Dear son, what has been proposed here — you yourself are the authority to carry out that very thing. You are most affectionate, a friend, our kin, and dear to us yourself."

*Note.* (?) *Yo 'sti* is grammatically unclear (masculine beside the neuter *vijñāpitam*); the sense is clear from the context. *Tāta* is an affectionate address of an elder to a younger person. The text is the same in Goswami's edition (GGM).

### Verse 25

शचीं नमस्कृत्य शुचिर्जगाम
विधित्सुरेतस्य विवाहकार्य्यम् ॥२५॥

*tataḥ samākarṇya vacaḥ sa dhīraḥ*
*sv-adhīta-sarvāgama eva tūrṇam |*
*śacīṁ namaskṛtya śucir jagāma*
*vidhitsur etasya vivāha-kāryam ||25||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *samākarṇya* — having heard; *vacaḥ* — the words; *saḥ* — he; *dhīraḥ* — the steady one; *su* — well; *adhīta* — [by whom] were studied; *sarva* — all; *āgamaḥ* — the scriptures (agamas); *eva* — indeed; *tūrṇam* — at once; *śacīm* — to Shachi; *namaskṛtya* — having bowed; *śuciḥ* — pure; *jagāma* — set out; *vidhitsuḥ* — wishing to arrange; *etasya* — His; *vivāha* — of the marriage; *kāryam* — the business.

**25.** Then, having heard her words, that steady and pure man, who had thoroughly studied all the scriptures, bowed to Shachi and set out at once, wishing to arrange the business of His marriage.

### Verse 26

स वल्लभाचार्यगृहेऽतिहर्षा-

प्रत्युद्गमोऽग्रार्चनमेव साधोः ॥२६॥

*sa vallabhācārya-gṛhe 'ti-harṣāj*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — he; *vallabha* — of Vallabha; *ācārya* — of the acharya; *gṛhe* — to the house; *ati* — great; *harṣāt* — from joy; *jagāma* — went; *kautūhala* — with eager excitement; *pūrṇa* — full; *cetāḥ* — [whose] heart; *tūrṇam* — at once; *vilokya* — having seen; *enam* — him; *asau* — the other; *udasthāt* — rose; *pratyudgamaḥ* — going out to meet; *agra* — the foremost; *arcanam* — honour; *eva* — indeed; *sādhoḥ* — of a saintly man.

**26.** In great joy, his heart full of eager excitement, he went to the house of Vallabhacharya. Seeing him, the other at once rose: going out to meet [a guest] is indeed the foremost honour paid by a saintly man.

### Verse 27

स वल्लभो भूमिसुरैकरत्नं

सदैव धीरो विनयेन भाति ॥२७॥

*sa vallabho bhūmi-suraika-ratnaṁ*
*dideśa tasmai varam āsanaṁ tat |*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — that; *vallabhaḥ* — Vallabha; *bhūmi* — of the earth; *sura* — of the gods; *eka* — the one; *ratnam* — jewel; *dideśa* — showed; *tasmai* — to him; *varam* — an excellent; *āsanam* — seat; *tat* — that; *papraccha* — asked; *paścāt* — afterwards; *ca* — and; *vinīta* — humble; *ceṣṭaḥ* — [whose] conduct; *sadā* — always; *eva* — indeed; *dhīraḥ* — a steady man; *vinayena* — with humility; *bhāti* — shines.

**27.** Vallabha showed that unique jewel among the gods of the earth to an excellent seat, and afterwards, humble in his bearing, he inquired. A steady man always shines with humility.

### Verse 28

अनुग्रहोऽयं मयि ते बभूव
स्फुटं यदत्रागमनं त्वदीयम् ।
कार्य्यं कियद्वाप्यवशिष्यते त-
द्वक्तुं महाधीस्त्वमिह प्रमाणम् ॥२८॥

*anugraho 'yaṁ mayi te babhūva*
*sphuṭaṁ yad atrāgamanaṁ tvadīyam |*
*kāryaṁ kiyad vāpy avaśiṣyate tad*
*vaktuṁ mahā-dhīs tvam iha pramāṇam ||28||*

*Word for word:* *anugrahaḥ* — favour; *ayam* — this; *mayi* — to me; *te* — your; *babhūva* — has been; *sphuṭam* — clearly; *yat* — that; *atra* — here; *āgamanam* — coming; *tvadīyam* — your; *kāryam* — business; *kiyat* — what; *vā api* — then; *avaśiṣyate* — remains; *tat* — that; *vaktum* — to tell; *mahā* — great; *dhīḥ* — [of] intelligence; *tvam* — you; *iha* — here; *pramāṇam* — the authority.

**28.** "Your coming here is clearly a favour you have shown me. What business, then, remains [for me to do]? It is for you, O wise one, to tell it."

### Verse 29

इत्थं निशम्याशु महानुभावः
प्रभोर्विवाहे घटनां विधित्सुः ।
उवाच हर्षोद्गतरोमवृन्दः
शुभस्वरां वाचमनिन्दितात्मा ॥२९॥

*itthaṁ niśamyāśu mahānubhāvaḥ*
*prabhor vivāhe ghaṭanāṁ vidhitsuḥ |*
*uvāca harṣodgata-roma-vṛndaḥ*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *niśamya* — having heard; *āśu* — at once; *mahānubhāvaḥ* — the noble one; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *vivāhe* — in the marriage; *ghaṭanām* — the arranging; *vidhitsuḥ* — wishing to accomplish; *uvāca* — spoke; *harṣa* — from joy; *udgata* — standing on end; *roma* — of hairs; *vṛndaḥ* — [whose] multitude; *śubha* — auspicious; *svarām* — [of] tone; *vācam* — speech; *anindita* — blameless; *ātmā* — [whose] soul.

**29.** Hearing this, the noble one, blameless in soul, eager to bring about the arrangement of the Lord's marriage, at once spoke words of auspicious tone, the hairs of his body standing on end with joy:

### Verse 30

गुणैर्वरो मिश्रपुरन्दरात्मजः
शरीरवत्तामतनुः किमाश्रितः ।
य एष सौन्दर्य्यमयीं तनूमिमां
जगत्त्रयीलोकविमोहिनीं श्रितः ॥३०॥

*guṇair varo miśra-purandarātmajaḥ*
*śarīravattām atanuḥ kim āśritaḥ |*
*ya eṣa saundarya-mayīṁ tanūm imāṁ*
*jagat-trayī-loka-vimohinīṁ śritaḥ ||30||*

*Word for word:* *guṇaiḥ* — in qualities; *varaḥ* — excellent; *miśra-purandara* — of Mishra Purandara; *ātmajaḥ* — the son; *śarīravattām* — embodiment; *atanuḥ* — the Bodiless One; *kim* — has not…?; *āśritaḥ* — taken on; *yaḥ* — who; *eṣaḥ* — he; *saundarya* — beauty; *mayīm* — made of; *tanūm* — body; *imām* — this; *jagat* — of the worlds; *trayī* — of the three; *loka* — the people; *vimohinīm* — enchanting; *śritaḥ* — has assumed.

**30.** "The son of Mishra Purandara is excellent in qualities. Has not the Bodiless One himself taken on a body? For He has assumed this body made of beauty, which enchants the people of the three worlds."

*Note.* *Atanu*, "the Bodiless One", is Kama: according to the legend, Shiva burnt him with his glance, and since then the god of love has had no body. From verse 30 the metre is *vaṁśastha*.

### Verse 31

य एष निष्णाततया तथा विधे-
र्विधानदक्षस्य विधानकर्म्मणि ।
विधाय सौन्दर्य्यसमूहमग्रतः
सुधामयः कोऽप्यतनुर्विनिर्ममे ॥३१॥

*ya eṣa niṣṇātatayā tathā vidher*
*vidhāna-dakṣasya vidhāna-karmaṇi |*
*vidhāya saundarya-samūham agrataḥ*
*sudhā-mayaḥ ko 'py atanur vinirmame ||31||*

*Word for word:* *yaḥ* — who; *eṣaḥ* — he; *niṣṇātatayā* — with expertise; *tathā* — such; *vidheḥ* — of the Creator; *vidhāna* — in creating; *dakṣasya* — of the skilled; *vidhāna* — of creation; *karmaṇi* — in the work; *vidhāya* — having made, having gathered; *saundarya* — of beauty; *samūham* — the whole mass; *agrataḥ* — first; *sudhā* — nectar; *mayaḥ* — made of; *kaḥ api* — some; *atanuḥ* — god of love; *vinirmame* — was fashioned.

**31.** "He is one whom the Creator, skilled in creating, first gathering together the whole store of beauty, fashioned with such mastery in the work of creation — some god of love made of nectar."

*Note.* The Creator (*vidhi*) is Brahma.

### Verse 32

यदास्यचन्द्रं विधिना विधाय तं
चिराय भूयिष्ठमिवात्मसौष्ठवम् ।
विदाम्बभूवे गदता प्रतिक्षणं
चतुर्भिरास्यैरपि साधु साध्विति ॥३२॥

*yad-āsya-candraṁ vidhinā vidhāya taṁ*
*cirāya bhūyiṣṭham ivātma-sauṣṭhavam |*
*vidāmbabhūve gadatā pratikṣaṇaṁ*
*caturbhir āsyair api sādhu sādhv iti ||32||*

*Word for word:* *yat* — whose; *āsya* — of the face; *candram* — the moon; *vidhinā* — by the Creator; *vidhāya* — having made; *tam* — it; *cirāya* — for all time; *bhūyiṣṭham* — the greatest; *iva* — as it were; *ātma* — of his own; *sauṣṭhavam* — masterpiece; *vidāmbabhūve* — was recognized; *gadatā* — by [him] saying; *pratikṣaṇam* — every moment; *caturbhiḥ* — with four; *āsyaiḥ* — with mouths; *api* — even; *sādhu sādhu* — "excellent, excellent"; *iti* — thus.

**32.** "Having fashioned the moon of His face, the Creator recognized it as, it seems, the greatest masterpiece of his own of all time; and every moment, even with all four mouths, he exclaims: 'Excellent! Excellent!'"

*Note.* The Creator, Brahma, has four faces.

### Verse 33

अतः सुतायास्तव योग्यविभ्रमः
स कल्पवल्ल्या इव कल्पभूरुहः ।
योगोऽस्तु मुक्तामणिवर्य्ययोरिव
प्रियाकरः सर्व्वजगज्जनस्य सः ॥३३॥

*ataḥ sutāyās tava yogya-vibhramaḥ*
*sa kalpa-vallyā iva kalpa-bhūruhaḥ |*
*yogo 'stu muktā-maṇi-varyayor iva*
*priyākaraḥ sarva-jagaj-janasya saḥ ||33||*

*Word for word:* *ataḥ* — therefore; *sutāyāḥ* — for the daughter; *tava* — your; *yogya* — fitting; *vibhramaḥ* — [whose] grace; *saḥ* — he; *kalpa* — of wishes; *vallyāḥ* — for the creeper; *iva* — like; *kalpa* — of wishes; *bhūruhaḥ* — the tree; *yogaḥ* — the union; *astu* — let there be; *muktā* — of the pearl; *maṇi* — of the gem; *varyayoḥ* — of the best; *iva* — as; *priya* — of delight; *ākaraḥ* — a mine; *sarva* — of all; *jagat* — of the world; *janasya* — for the people; *saḥ* — that [union].

**33.** "Therefore His grace is fitting for your daughter, as a wish-fulfilling tree is for a wish-fulfilling creeper. Let there be a union, as of the finest pearl and the finest gem — a mine of delight for all the people of the world."

### Verse 34

निशम्य सौम्योऽथ स वल्लभद्विजो
द्विजैकरत्नं तमुवाच हर्षतः ।
विचिन्त्य भूयो मनसा शुभंयुना
सख्येन विख्यातयशःसमुच्चयः ॥३४॥

*niśamya saumyo 'tha sa vallabha-dvijo*
*dvijaika-ratnaṁ tam uvāca harṣataḥ |*
*vicintya bhūyo manasā śubhaṁyunā*
*sakhyena vikhyāta-yaśaḥ-samuccayaḥ ||34||*

*Word for word:* *niśamya* — having heard; *saumyaḥ* — gentle; *atha* — then; *saḥ* — that; *vallabha* — Vallabha; *dvijaḥ* — the brahmana; *dvija* — of the twice-born; *eka* — the one; *ratnam* — jewel; *tam* — to that; *uvāca* — said; *harṣataḥ* — joyfully; *vicintya* — having reflected; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *manasā* — with a mind; *śubhaṁyunā* — with an auspicious; *sakhyena* — in friendship; *vikhyāta* — widely renowned; *yaśaḥ* — of fame; *samuccayaḥ* — [who is] a store.

**34.** Having heard this, the gentle brahmana Vallabha, a store of widely renowned fame, reflected once more with an auspicious mind and then joyfully, in friendship, said to that unique jewel of the twice-born:

### Verse 35

भाग्यातिभाग्येन महानुभाव मे
योगेन तत्संप्रति तेन भूयते ।
तथाविधस्यास्य समं तथाविधै-
र्यथातथं स्याद्घटना मनोरमा ॥३५॥

*bhāgyātibhāgyena mahānubhāva me*
*yogena tat samprati tena bhūyate |*
*tathā-vidhasyāsya samaṁ tathā-vidhair*
*yathā-tathaṁ syād ghaṭanā manoramā ||35||*

*Word for word:* *bhāgya* — of fortune; *atibhāgyena* — by the surpassing fortune; *mahānubhāva* — O noble one; *me* — my; *yogena* — by the conjunction; *tat* — that; *samprati* — now; *tena* — by that; *bhūyate* — comes to be; *tathāvidhasya* — of such; *asya* — of him; *samam* — together; *tathāvidhaiḥ* — with such; *yathātatham* — as is fitting; *syāt* — let be; *ghaṭanā* — the joining; *manoramā* — charming.

**35.** "O noble one, if this now comes to be, it is through the conjunction of my fortune of fortunes. May the joining of such a one as He with such [a bride] be charming, as is fitting."

*Note.* (?) The syntax of the verse is uneven; the sense is given from the general course of the speech. The text is the same in Goswami's edition (GGM).

### Verse 36

यदीश्वरः स्यान्मयि सुप्रसादभाक्
भाग्योदयो वा यदि मे महान् भवेत् ।
यदस्ति पुत्र्याः सुकृतं महत्तरं
तदीदृशस्तत्पतिरेव निश्चयः ॥३६॥

*yadīśvaraḥ syān mayi suprasāda-bhāk*
*bhāgyodayo vā yadi me mahān bhavet |*
*yad asti putryāḥ sukṛtaṁ mahattaraṁ*
*tad īdṛśas tat-patir eva niścayaḥ ||36||*

*Word for word:* *yadi* — if; *īśvaraḥ* — the Lord; *syāt* — should be; *mayi* — towards me; *su* — great; *prasāda* — of grace; *bhāk* — partaking; *bhāgya* — of fortune; *udayaḥ* — the dawning; *vā* — or; *yadi* — if; *me* — my; *mahān* — great; *bhavet* — should be; *yat* — if; *asti* — there is; *putryāḥ* — of the daughter; *sukṛtam* — merit; *mahattaram* — very great; *tat* — then; *īdṛśaḥ* — such a one; *tat* — her; *patiḥ* — husband; *eva* — indeed; *niścayaḥ* — certain.

**36.** "If the Lord be very gracious to me, or if a great dawning of fortune be mine, if my daughter has some very great merit — then such a one will surely be her husband; that is certain."

### Verse 37

यथा गुणैः काञ्चनहारवल्ली
रत्नेन सन्नायकतां गतेन ।
निष्पन्नतां याति तथा त्वदीयै-
र्गुणैस्तयोः संघटना घटेत ॥३७॥

*yathā guṇaiḥ kāñcana-hāra-vallī*
*ratnena san-nāyakatāṁ gatena |*
*niṣpannatāṁ yāti tathā tvadīyair*
*guṇais tayoḥ saṅghaṭanā ghaṭeta ||37||*

*Word for word:* *yathā* — as; *guṇaiḥ* — by threads; *kāñcana* — of gold; *hāra* — of a necklace; *vallī* — the strand; *ratnena* — by a gem; *sat* — fine; *nāyakatām* — the place of the central stone; *gatena* — having taken; *niṣpannatām* — completeness; *yāti* — attains; *tathā* — so; *tvadīyaiḥ* — by your; *guṇaiḥ* — by virtues; *tayoḥ* — of the two; *saṅghaṭanā* — the union; *ghaṭeta* — may come about.

**37.** "As the strand of a golden necklace attains completeness through its threads, with a fine gem set in the place of the central stone, so by your virtues may the union of these two come about."

*Note.* A play on words: *guṇa* is both "thread" and "virtue"; *nāyaka* is both "the central, principal stone of a necklace" and "the hero, the bridegroom". From verse 37 the metre is again *upajāti* (verse 38 is *vaṁśastha*).

### Verse 38

इत्यूचिवांस्तां विनयोक्तिवत्तया
तया महाप्रीत इमं जगाद सः ।
तवेदृशा सद्विनयेन सत्वरं
संपत्स्यते सर्व्वमशेषमङ्गलम् ॥३८॥

*ity ūcivāṁs tāṁ vinayokti-vattayā*
*tayā mahā-prīta imaṁ jagāda saḥ |*
*tavedṛśā sad-vinayena satvaraṁ*
*sampatsyate sarvam aśeṣa-maṅgalam ||38||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *ūcivān* — having spoken; *tām* — with that; *vinaya* — modest; *ukti* — of speech; *vattayā* — by the quality; *tayā* — by that; *mahā* — greatly; *prītaḥ* — pleased; *imam* — to him; *jagāda* — said; *saḥ* — he; *tava* — your; *īdṛśā* — by such; *sat* — true; *vinayena* — by humility; *satvaram* — quickly; *sampatsyate* — will come to pass; *sarvam* — all; *aśeṣa* — complete; *maṅgalam* — auspiciousness.

**38.** Greatly pleased by that modesty of speech in the one who had spoken thus, Vanamali said to him: "Through such true humility of yours everything will quickly come to pass with complete auspiciousness."

*Note.* The nominative *ūcivān* ("having spoken") agrees grammatically with *saḥ*, but in sense it refers to Vallabha, who has just spoken; the translation follows the sense.

### Verse 39

इत्थं स संभाष्य मिथो द्विजाग्र्यो
जगाद भूयो निलयेषु शच्याः ।
न्यवेदयत्सर्व्वमदभ्रभाग्यो
विवाहकौतूहललोलचित्तः ॥३९॥

*itthaṁ sa saṁbhāṣya mitho dvijāgryo*
*jagāda bhūyo nilayeṣu śacyāḥ |*
*nyavedayat sarvam adabhra-bhāgyo*
*vivāha-kautūhala-lola-cittaḥ ||39||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *saḥ* — he; *saṁbhāṣya* — having conversed; *mithaḥ* — with each other; *dvija* — of the twice-born; *agryaḥ* — the foremost; *jagāda* — came (lit. said); *bhūyaḥ* — again; *nilayeṣu* — to the abode; *śacyāḥ* — of Shachi; *nyavedayat* — related; *sarvam* — everything; *adabhra* — of no small; *bhāgyaḥ* — [whose] fortune; *vivāha* — of the wedding; *kautūhala* — with the excitement; *lola* — trembling; *cittaḥ* — [whose] heart.

**39.** Having thus conversed with one another, that foremost of the twice-born came again to Shachi's abode. Of no small fortune, his heart trembling with the excitement of the wedding, he related everything.

*Note.* The edition has *jagāda* ("said"); with the locative *nilayeṣu* one would expect *jagāma* ("went"). The text is the same in Goswami's edition (GGM). The translation follows the sense: "came".

### Verse 40

शची तथा तत्सकलं विदित्वा
हर्षेण पूर्णामविदत्तनूं स्वाम् ।
विचिन्त्य मूर्त्तिं निजभाग्यराशिं
तनूजरत्नं निभृतं जगाद ॥४०॥

*śacī tathā tat sakalaṁ viditvā*
*harṣeṇa pūrṇām avidat tanūṁ svām |*
*vicintya mūrtiṁ nija-bhāgya-rāśiṁ*
*tanūja-ratnaṁ nibhṛtaṁ jagāda ||40||*

*Word for word:* *śacī* — Shachi; *tathā* — thus; *tat* — that; *sakalam* — all; *viditvā* — having learned; *harṣeṇa* — with joy; *pūrṇām* — full; *avidat* — felt; *tanūm* — body; *svām* — her own; *vicintya* — having considered [Him]; *mūrtim* — embodied; *nija* — of her own; *bhāgya* — of fortune; *rāśim* — the heap; *tanūja* — to the son; *ratnam* — jewel; *nibhṛtam* — privately; *jagāda* — said.

**40.** Having thus learned all that, Shachi felt her own body full of joy. Considering Him the embodied heap of her own good fortune, she spoke privately to her jewel of a son:

### Verse 41

विवाहमाङ्गल्यविशेषदक्षिणो
विधीयतां तत्समयः सुखावहः ।
तदा तदाकर्ण्य स चित्तवृत्तिभि-
श्चकार नाथः कलनां कलानिधिः ॥४१॥

*vivāha-māṅgalya-viśeṣa-dakṣiṇo*
*vidhīyatāṁ tat-samayaḥ sukhāvahaḥ |*
*tadā tad ākarṇya sa citta-vṛttibhiś*
*cakāra nāthaḥ kalanāṁ kalā-nidhiḥ ||41||*

*Word for word:* *vivāha* — of the wedding; *māṅgalya* — in auspiciousness; *viśeṣa* — special; *dakṣiṇaḥ* — rich; *vidhīyatām* — let it be fixed; *tat* — its; *samayaḥ* — time; *sukha* — joy; *āvahaḥ* — bringing; *tadā* — then; *tat* — that; *ākarṇya* — having heard; *saḥ* — He; *citta* — of the mind; *vṛttibhiḥ* — by the movements; *cakāra* — made; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *kalanām* — the reckoning; *kalā* — of arts; *nidhiḥ* — the treasure-house.

**41.** "Let the time for it be fixed — one rich in the special auspiciousness of a wedding and bringing joy." Then, having heard this, the Lord, the treasure-house of all arts, made the reckoning in His mind.

*Note.* *Kalā-nidhi* — "treasure-house of arts", but also "treasure-house of digits [of the moon]", an epithet of the moon.

### Verse 42

द्रव्याण्यदभ्राणि मनोज्ञविभ्रमो
मातुर्निदेशादहरत्तदा रहः ।
चकार कालं शुभलग्नभूषितं
सोऽयं तदा किं स्वमेव भूषितः ॥४२॥

*dravyāṇy adabhrāṇi manojña-vibhramo*
*mātur nideśād aharat tadā rahaḥ |*
*cakāra kālaṁ śubha-lagna-bhūṣitaṁ*
*so 'yaṁ tadā kiṁ svayam eva bhūṣitaḥ ||42||*

*Word for word:* *dravyāṇi* — provisions; *adabhrāṇi* — abundant; *manojña* — of captivating; *vibhramaḥ* — [full] of charm; *mātuḥ* — of the mother; *nideśāt* — by the bidding; *aharat* — gathered; *tadā* — then; *rahaḥ* — in private; *cakāra* — made; *kālam* — the time; *śubha* — by an auspicious; *lagna* — ascendant; *bhūṣitam* — adorned; *saḥ* — He; *ayam* — this; *tadā* — then; *kim* — was not…?; *svayam* — Himself; *eva* — indeed; *bhūṣitaḥ* — adorned.

**42.** At His mother's bidding He, full of captivating charm, then quietly gathered abundant provisions, and He fixed a time adorned with an auspicious ascendant. Was it not He Himself who was then adorned?

*Note.* In the last pada we read, with the Gosvami edition (GGM), *svayam eva* ("He Himself"), which gives the full metre (our text has *svam eva*, a syllable short). The sense: the auspicious time adorned Him, or rather He Himself was its ornament. *Lagna* — the ascendant sign of the zodiac at the moment of the rite.

### Verse 43

मृदङ्गचारुध्वनिभङ्गिसङ्गी
सङ्गीतकोलाहल उच्छ्रितोऽभूत् ।
तथैव तत्रातिशयो गरीया-
न्नृत्योद्गमो हर्षितनर्त्तकानाम् ॥४३॥

*mṛdaṅga-cāru-dhvani-bhaṅgi-saṅgī*
*saṅgīta-kolāhala ucchrito 'bhūt |*
*tathaiva tatrātiśayo garīyān*
*nṛtyodgamo harṣita-nartakānām ||43||*

*Word for word:* *mṛdaṅga* — of the mridanga; *cāru* — of the lovely; *dhvani* — of the sound; *bhaṅgi* — by the cadences; *saṅgī* — accompanied; *saṅgīta* — of music; *kolāhalaḥ* — the tumult; *ucchritaḥ* — risen; *abhūt* — was; *tathā eva* — likewise; *tatra* — there; *atiśayaḥ* — unbounded; *garīyān* — great; *nṛtya* — of dance; *udgamaḥ* — the upsurge; *harṣita* — of joyful; *nartakānām* — of dancers.

**43.** A tumult of music arose, accompanied by the lovely cadences of the mridanga; and likewise there arose there a great, unbounded surge of dance among the joyful dancers.

### Verse 44

भूदेववेदध्वनिभिः समन्ता-
न्मृदङ्गनादैर्जयनादमिश्रैः ।
सचन्दनैरागुरवैः प्रधूपै-
रौशीरवद्भिः स रराज कालः ॥४४॥

*bhūdeva-veda-dhvanibhiḥ samantān*
*mṛdaṅga-nādair jaya-nāda-miśraiḥ |*
*sa-candanair āguravaiḥ pradhūpair*
*auśīravadbhiḥ sa rarāja kālaḥ ||44||*

*Word for word:* *bhūdeva* — of the brahmanas; *veda* — of the Vedas; *dhvanibhiḥ* — with the sounds; *samantāt* — on every side; *mṛdaṅga* — of mridangas; *nādaiḥ* — with the sounds; *jaya* — of "jaya"; *nāda* — with cries; *miśraiḥ* — mingled; *sa* — with; *candanaiḥ* — sandal; *āguravaiḥ* — of aguru; *pradhūpaiḥ* — with incense; *auśīravadbhiḥ* — with ushira; *saḥ* — that; *rarāja* — shone; *kālaḥ* — time.

**44.** With the sound of the Vedas [chanted] by the brahmanas on every side, with the sound of mridangas mingled with cries of "Jaya!", with incense of sandal, aguru and ushira — that time shone.

*Note.* *Aguru* — the fragrant aloe-wood; *uśīra* — vetiver, a fragrant root.

### Verse 45

उर्व्वीसदुर्व्वीसुररत्नदत्तां
जाज्वल्यमानामधिवासलक्ष्मीम् ।
आसाद्य भाति स्म सरोहिणीको
यथा सुधारश्मिरथैष नाथः ॥४५॥

*urvī-sad-urvīsura-ratna-dattāṁ*
*jājvalyamānām adhivāsa-lakṣmīm |*
*āsādya bhāti sma sa-rohiṇīko*
*yathā sudhā-raśmir athaiṣa nāthaḥ ||45||*

*Word for word:* *urvī* — on the earth; *sat* — dwelling; *urvīsura* — of the brahmanas; *ratna* — by the jewels; *dattām* — conferred; *jājvalyamānām* — blazing; *adhivāsa* — of the adhivasa; *lakṣmīm* — the splendour; *āsādya* — having obtained; *bhāti sma* — shone; *sa* — with; *rohiṇīkaḥ* — Rohini; *yathā* — as; *sudhā* — of nectar; *raśmiḥ* — [the lord of] rays; *atha* — then; *eṣaḥ* — this; *nāthaḥ* — Lord.

**45.** Having obtained the blazing splendour of the adhivasa, conferred by the jewels among the brahmanas dwelling on earth, the Lord then shone like the nectar-rayed moon beside Rohini.

*Note.* *Adhivāsa* — the rite on the eve of the wedding: consecration, anointing, the offering of gifts. Rohini — the nakshatra, the Moon's favourite wife.

### Verse 46

ततो द्विजेभ्यः प्रददुः प्रकामं
ताम्बूलमाल्यान्यपि चन्दनानि ।
रेजुस्तदा ते सकला महान्तः
स्मेराननाः हर्षसमुद्रमग्नाः ॥४६॥

*tato dvijebhyaḥ pradaduḥ prakāmaṁ*
*tāmbūla-mālyāny api candanāni |*
*rejus tadā te sakalā mahāntaḥ*
*smerānanā harṣa-samudra-magnāḥ ||46||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *dvijebhyaḥ* — to the brahmanas; *pradaduḥ* — they gave; *prakāmam* — abundantly; *tāmbūla* — betel; *mālyāni* — garlands; *api* — and; *candanāni* — sandal; *rejuḥ* — shone; *tadā* — then; *te* — they; *sakalāḥ* — all; *mahāntaḥ* — the venerable; *smera* — smiling; *ānanāḥ* — [with] faces; *harṣa* — of joy; *samudra* — in the ocean; *magnāḥ* — immersed.

**46.** Then they gave the brahmanas betel, garlands and sandal in abundance, and all those venerable men shone with smiling faces, immersed in an ocean of joy.

### Verse 47

स वल्लभोऽभ्येत्य तदा सदुर्व्वी-
गीर्व्वाणरत्नैर्द्विजसुन्दरीभिः ।
महाप्रभोर्गन्धसुगन्धिमाल्यैः
शुभाधिवासं विदधे विधिज्ञः ॥४७॥

*sa vallabho 'bhyetya tadā sad-urvī-*
*gīrvāṇa-ratnair dvija-sundarībhiḥ |*
*mahāprabhor gandha-sugandhi-mālyaiḥ*
*śubhādhivāsaṁ vidadhe vidhi-jñaḥ ||47||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — that; *vallabhaḥ* — Vallabha; *abhyetya* — having come; *tadā* — then; *sat* — worthy; *urvī* — of the earth; *gīrvāṇa* — of the gods; *ratnaiḥ* — with the jewels; *dvija* — of the brahmanas; *sundarībhiḥ* — with the beautiful wives; *mahāprabhoḥ* — of Mahaprabhu; *gandha* — with fragrances; *sugandhi* — sweet-scented; *mālyaiḥ* — with garlands; *śubha* — the auspicious; *adhivāsam* — adhivasa; *vidadhe* — performed; *vidhi* — rites; *jñaḥ* — knowing.

**47.** Then Vallabha, the knower of rites, came with the jewels among the worthy gods of the earth and with the beautiful wives of the brahmanas, and performed the auspicious adhivasa of Mahaprabhu with fragrances and sweet-scented garlands.

*Note.* *Gīrvāṇa* ("god"), like *urvīsura*, here means a brahmana.

### Verse 48

अथ प्रभाते विमलार्कभूषिते
स्वयं कृतस्नानविधिर्यथाविधि ।
प्रभुः पितॄनर्च्चयितुं यथा तथा
नान्दीमुखश्राद्धमथाकरोदसौ ॥४८॥

*atha prabhāte vimalārka-bhūṣite*
*svayaṁ kṛta-snāna-vidhir yathā-vidhi |*
*prabhuḥ pitṝn arcayituṁ yathā tathā*
*nāndīmukha-śrāddham athākarod asau ||48||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *prabhāte* — in the morning; *vimala* — by the spotless; *arka* — sun; *bhūṣite* — adorned; *svayam* — Himself; *kṛta* — having performed; *snāna* — of bathing; *vidhiḥ* — the rite; *yathāvidhi* — according to the rules; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *pitṝn* — the forefathers; *arcayitum* — to honour; *yathā tathā* — as is fitting; *nāndīmukha* — the nandimukha; *śrāddham* — shraddha; *atha* — then; *akarot* — performed; *asau* — He.

**48.** Then, in the morning adorned by the spotless sun, the Lord Himself performed His bath according to the rules, and then, to honour the forefathers as is fitting, He performed the nandimukha shraddha.

*Note.* *Nāndīmukha-śrāddha* — a rite in honour of the forefathers performed before a joyful occasion, a wedding among others.

### Verse 49

ततो द्विजातिश्रुतिपाठनादै-
र्मृदङ्गनादैः पणवस्वनैश्च ।
वराङ्गनावक्त्रविनिर्गतैस्तै-
रुलूलशब्दैस्तुमुलो महोऽभूत् ॥४९॥

*tato dvijāti-śruti-pāṭha-nādair*
*mṛdaṅga-nādaiḥ paṇava-svanaiś ca |*
*varāṅganā-vaktra-vinirgatais tair*
*ulūla-śabdais tumulo maho 'bhūt ||49||*
