*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *dvijāti* — of the brahmanas; *śruti* — of the Vedas; *pāṭha* — of the recitation; *nādaiḥ* — with the sounds; *mṛdaṅga* — of mridangas; *nādaiḥ* — with the sounds; *paṇava* — of panava drums; *svanaiḥ* — with the roar; *ca* — and; *vara* — of lovely; *aṅganā* — women; *vaktra* — from the mouths; *vinirgataiḥ* — issuing; *taiḥ* — with those; *ulūla* — of "ulu-ulu"; *śabdaiḥ* — with the sounds; *tumulaḥ* — tumultuous; *mahaḥ* — festival; *abhūt* — there was.

**49.** Then there was a tumultuous festival: with the sound of the brahmanas reciting the Vedas, with the sound of mridangas and the roar of panava drums, and with those cries of "ulu-ulu" issuing from the mouths of lovely women.

*Note.* *Ulūla* — the jubilant cry of women (*ulu-dhvani*), without which no Bengali wedding takes place to this day.

### Verse 50

शची द्विजानां महिला यथायथं
तत्तत्सपर्य्याग्रहिलास्तदावदत् ।
अलं मया भर्त्तृपदाब्जहीनया
कर्त्तव्यमेतद्भवतीभिरेव हि ॥५०॥

*śacī dvijānāṁ mahilā yathā-yathaṁ*
*tat-tat-saparyā-grahilās tadāvadat |*
*alaṁ mayā bhartṛ-padābja-hīnayā*
*kartavyam etad bhavatībhir eva hi ||50||*

*Word for word:* *śacī* — Shachi; *dvijānām* — of the brahmanas; *mahilāḥ* — to the wives; *yathāyatham* — each in her turn; *tat-tat* — for those various; *saparyā* — rites of worship; *grahilāḥ* — eager; *tadā* — then; *avadat* — said; *alam* — enough; *mayā* — with me; *bhartṛ* — of the husband; *pada* — of the feet; *abja* — of the lotuses; *hīnayā* — bereft; *kartavyam* — to be done; *etat* — this; *bhavatībhiḥ* — by you; *eva* — yourselves; *hi* — indeed.

**50.** Then Shachi said to the wives of the brahmanas, each of whom was eager to perform those various rites of worship: "It is not for me, bereft of my husband's lotus feet. This must be done by you yourselves."

*Note.* By custom a widow takes no part in the auspicious wedding rites. A bitter detail amid the festivity: at her son's wedding Shachi stands aside. From verse 50 the metre is *vaṁśastha*.

### Verse 51

स मातुरित्थं करुणोदितं प्रभु-
र्निशम्य तातस्मृतिदुःखविह्वलः ।
मुक्ताफलस्थूलविलोचनाम्भसां
बिन्दूनुवाह प्रवरोरुवक्षसि ॥५१॥

*sa mātur itthaṁ karuṇoditaṁ prabhur*
*niśamya tāta-smṛti-duḥkha-vihvalaḥ |*
*muktāphala-sthūla-vilocanāmbhasāṁ*
*bindūn uvāha pravaroru-vakṣasi ||51||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — that; *mātuḥ* — of the mother; *ittham* — thus; *karuṇa* — piteously; *uditam* — spoken; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *niśamya* — having heard; *tāta* — of the father; *smṛti* — at the memory; *duḥkha* — with grief; *vihvalaḥ* — overwhelmed; *muktāphala* — [like] pearls; *sthūla* — large; *vilocana* — of the eyes; *ambhasām* — of the water; *bindūn* — drops; *uvāha* — bore; *pravara* — splendid; *uru* — broad; *vakṣasi* — on the chest.

**51.** Hearing these piteous words of His mother, the Lord, overwhelmed with grief at the memory of His father, wept: tears as large as pearls ran down His broad and splendid chest.

### Verse 52

तथाविधं तत्समये विलोक्य सा
सुतं सुदीनाह सहाङ्गनागणैः ।
पितः कथं मङ्गलकर्म्म कुर्वता
विमुच्यते वारि दृशोरमङ्गलम् ॥५२॥

*tathā-vidhaṁ tat-samaye vilokya sā*
*sutaṁ su-dīnāha sahāṅganā-gaṇaiḥ |*
*pitaḥ kathaṁ maṅgala-karma kurvatā*
*vimucyate vāri dṛśor amaṅgalam ||52||*

*Word for word:* *tathāvidham* — such; *tat* — at that; *samaye* — time; *vilokya* — having seen; *sā* — she; *sutam* — the son; *su* — very; *dīnā* — sad; *āha* — said; *saha* — together with; *aṅganā* — of women; *gaṇaiḥ* — with the crowd; *pitaḥ* — O father (i.e. dear son); *katham* — how; *maṅgala* — an auspicious; *karma* — rite; *kurvatā* — by one performing; *vimucyate* — is shed; *vāri* — water; *dṛśoḥ* — from the eyes; *amaṅgalam* — inauspicious.

**52.** Seeing her son like this at that time, [Shachi,] very sad herself, said, together with the crowd of women: "Dear son, how can You, while performing an auspicious rite, shed tears from Your eyes? It is inauspicious!"

*Note.* *Pitaḥ*, literally "O father": the affectionate address of a Bengali mother to her son (Beng. *bābā*, "daddy").

### Verse 53

स मातुरित्थं वचनेन नाथो
द्राघीयसा निश्वसितेन तेन ।
म्लानोरुवक्षाः करुणं बभाषे
प्रभातचन्द्रप्रतिमास्यचन्द्रः ॥५३॥

*sa mātur itthaṁ vacanena nātho*
*drāghīyasā niśvasitena tena |*
*mlānoru-vakṣāḥ karuṇaṁ babhāṣe*
*prabhāta-candra-pratimāsya-candraḥ ||53||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — that; *mātuḥ* — of the mother; *ittham* — thus; *vacanena* — by the word; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *drāghīyasā* — with a long; *niśvasitena* — with a sigh; *tena* — with that; *mlāna* — drooping; *uru* — broad; *vakṣāḥ* — [with] chest; *karuṇam* — piteously; *babhāṣe* — spoke; *prabhāta* — of dawn; *candra* — to the moon; *pratima* — like; *āsya* — of the face; *candraḥ* — [with] the moon.

**53.** At these words of His mother the Lord heaved a long, deep sigh; His broad chest drooped, and the moon of His face grew pale like the moon at dawn. Then He spoke piteously:

### Verse 54

धनानि किम्वा मनुजा न सन्ति मे
येनेदृशं मातरुदीरितं वचः ।
त्वयाद्य दैन्येन पराश्रयाग्रहो
विधीयते किं वद दुःखतप्तया ॥५४॥

*dhanāni kiṁ vā manujā na santi me*
*yenedṛśaṁ mātar udīritaṁ vacaḥ |*
*tvayādya dainyena parāśrayāgraho*
*vidhīyate kiṁ vada duḥkha-taptayā ||54||*

*Word for word:* *dhanāni* — riches; *kim vā* — or what?; *manujāḥ* — men; *na* — not; *santi* — are; *me* — of Me; *yena* — by which; *īdṛśam* — such; *mātaḥ* — O Mother; *udīritam* — spoken; *vacaḥ* — word; *tvayā* — by you; *adya* — today; *dainyena* — in dejection; *para* — on others; *āśraya* — of reliance; *āgrahaḥ* — insistence; *vidhīyate* — is made; *kim* — why; *vada* — tell; *duḥkha* — by grief; *taptayā* — by [you,] scorched.

**54.** "O Mother, have I no riches or people, that you speak such words? Tell Me, why today, scorched by grief, do you in dejection insist on leaning on others?

### Verse 55

त्वयैव दृष्टं द्विजसज्जनेभ्यः
प्रकाममृक्थं रभसाद्विकीर्णम् ।
ताम्बूलमाल्यानि च गन्धवन्ति
प्रकर्षतोऽलङ्करणांशुकानि ॥५५॥

*tvayaiva dṛṣṭaṁ dvija-saj-janebhyaḥ*
*prakāmam ṛkthaṁ rabhasād vikīrṇam |*
*tāmbūla-mālyāni ca gandhavanti*
*prakarṣato 'laṅkaraṇāṁśukāni ||55||*

*Word for word:* *tvayā* — by you; *eva* — yourself; *dṛṣṭam* — seen; *dvija* — to the brahmanas; *sat* — to good; *janebhyaḥ* — to people; *prakāmam* — abundantly; *ṛktham* — wealth; *rabhasāt* — eagerly; *vikīrṇam* — scattered; *tāmbūla* — betel; *mālyāni* — garlands; *ca* — and; *gandhavanti* — fragrant; *prakarṣataḥ* — in profusion; *alaṅkaraṇa* — ornaments; *aṁśukāni* — garments.

**55.** "You yourself have seen how wealth was scattered eagerly and abundantly to the brahmanas and good people — betel and fragrant garlands, ornaments and garments in profusion.

*Note.* The metre here is again *upajāti*: in this sarga Kavi Karnapura freely alternates *vaṁśastha* and *upajāti*.

### Verse 56

पित्रापि हीनोऽहमकुण्ठशक्तिः
किं मातरित्थं पुरतो ममोक्तम् ।
अमर्त्यकार्य्येषु सदैव शक्ता-
स्तथापि यल्लौकिकमेव कुर्म्मः ॥५६॥

*pitrāpi hīno 'ham akuṇṭha-śaktiḥ*
*kiṁ mātar itthaṁ purato mamoktam |*
*amartya-kāryeṣu sadaiva śaktās*
*tathāpi yal laukikam eva kurmaḥ ||56||*

*Word for word:* *pitrā* — of the father; *api* — though; *hīnaḥ* — bereft; *aham* — I; *akuṇṭha* — unimpaired; *śaktiḥ* — [with] power; *kim* — why; *mātaḥ* — O Mother; *ittham* — thus; *purataḥ* — before; *mama* — Me; *uktam* — spoken; *amartya* — of immortals; *kāryeṣu* — in the deeds; *sadā* — always; *eva* — indeed; *śaktāḥ* — capable; *tathā api* — yet; *yat* — that which; *laukikam* — worldly; *eva* — only; *kurmaḥ* — We do.

**56.** "Though I am bereft of My father, My power is unimpaired. Why, O Mother, do you speak thus before Me? We are always capable even of the deeds of immortals — and yet We do only what is customary in the world."

*Note.* The Lord half-reveals His divinity: "We are capable of the deeds of immortals." The plural is the majestic "We".

### Verse 57

इतीरितं तस्य निशम्य माता
तं सान्त्वयित्वा मधुरैर्वचोभिः ।
सचन्दनैरागुरवानुलेपै-
र्लिलेप वक्षःस्थलमात्मजस्य ॥५७॥

*itīritaṁ tasya niśamya mātā*
*taṁ sāntvayitvā madhurair vacobhiḥ |*
*sa-candanair āgurava-anulepair*
*lilepa vakṣaḥ-sthalam ātmajasya ||57||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *īritam* — spoken; *tasya* — His; *niśamya* — having heard; *mātā* — the mother; *tam* — Him; *sāntvayitvā* — having comforted; *madhuraiḥ* — with sweet; *vacobhiḥ* — with words; *sa* — with; *candanaiḥ* — sandal; *āgurava* — of aguru; *anulepaiḥ* — with unguents; *lilepa* — anointed; *vakṣaḥ* — of the chest; *sthalam* — the expanse; *ātmajasya* — of the son.

**57.** Having heard what He said, His mother comforted Him with sweet words and anointed her son's chest with unguents of sandal and aguru.

*Note.* The edition prints *sāntvayitā*; we read *sāntvayitvā*.

### Verse 58

त्रैलोक्यमाधुर्य्यमयार्य्यकान्तिः
प्रसूनमाल्याभरणानुलेपैः ।
विभूषितः स्मेरमुखो विरेजे
सौन्दर्य्यलक्ष्म्येव वृतः स्वयं सः ॥५८॥

*trailokya-mādhurya-mayārya-kāntiḥ*
*prasūna-mālyābharaṇānulepaiḥ |*
*vibhūṣitaḥ smera-mukho vireje*
*saundarya-lakṣmyeva vṛtaḥ svayaṁ saḥ ||58||*

*Word for word:* *trailokya* — of the three worlds; *mādhurya* — with the sweetness; *maya* — full; *ārya* — noble; *kāntiḥ* — [with] lustre; *prasūna* — of flowers; *mālya* — with garlands; *ābharaṇa* — with ornaments; *anulepaiḥ* — with unguents; *vibhūṣitaḥ* — adorned; *smera* — smiling; *mukhaḥ* — [with] face; *vireje* — shone; *saundarya* — of beauty; *lakṣmyā* — by the goddess; *iva* — as if; *vṛtaḥ* — chosen; *svayam* — herself; *saḥ* — He.

**58.** Adorned with garlands of flowers, with ornaments and unguents, His face smiling, His noble lustre full of the sweetness of the three worlds, He shone as if chosen [as husband] by the goddess of beauty herself.

*Note.* *Vṛta* — "chosen" as husband, as at a *svayaṁvara*, the rite at which a bride chooses her bridegroom.

### Verse 59

तस्मिन्क्षणे वल्लभभूमिदेवः
समाप्य कार्य्यं पितृदेवतानाम् ।
विभूषयामास विभूषिताङ्गीं
सुतामलङ्कारकुलैर्महार्घ्यैः ॥५९॥

*tasmin kṣaṇe vallabha-bhūmidevaḥ*
*samāpya kāryaṁ pitṛ-devatānām |*
*vibhūṣayāmāsa vibhūṣitāṅgīṁ*
*sutām alaṅkāra-kulair mahārghyaiḥ ||59||*

*Word for word:* *tasmin* — at that; *kṣaṇe* — moment; *vallabha* — Vallabha; *bhūmidevaḥ* — the brahmana; *samāpya* — having completed; *kāryam* — the rite; *pitṛ* — for the forefathers; *devatānām* — and for the gods; *vibhūṣayāmāsa* — adorned; *vibhūṣita* — [already] adorned; *aṅgīm* — whose limbs; *sutām* — the daughter; *alaṅkāra* — of ornaments; *kulaiḥ* — with multitudes; *mahā* — very; *arghyaiḥ* — precious.

**59.** At that very moment the brahmana Vallabha, having completed the rites for the forefathers and the gods, adorned his daughter, whose limbs were [already] adorned [by beauty], with a multitude of very precious ornaments.

### Verse 60

वरस्य सौन्दर्य्यभृतां वरस्य
द्विजास्ततोऽस्यानयनाय जग्मुः ।
संप्रेषितास्तेन ततस्तदैव
शुभस्वरां वाचममन्दमूचुः ॥६०॥

*varasya saundarya-bhṛtāṁ varasya*
*dvijās tato 'syānayanāya jagmuḥ |*
*sampreṣitās tena tatas tadaiva*
*śubha-svarāṁ vācam amandam ūcuḥ ||60||*

*Word for word:* *varasya* — of the best; *saundarya* — beauty; *bhṛtām* — among those possessing; *varasya* — of the bridegroom; *dvijāḥ* — the brahmanas; *tataḥ* — then; *asya* — His; *ānayanāya* — for the bringing; *jagmuḥ* — went; *sampreṣitāḥ* — sent; *tena* — by him; *tataḥ* — then; *tadā eva* — at once; *śubha* — auspicious; *svarām* — in tone; *vācam* — speech; *amandam* — loudly; *ūcuḥ* — spoke.

**60.** Then the brahmanas, sent by him, went to bring the bridegroom, the best of all who possess beauty, and at once they spoke loudly, in auspicious tones:

*Note.* A play on words: *vara* is both "best" and "bridegroom".

### Verse 61

विधीयतां संप्रति वत्स यात्रा
पन्थान एते शुभदा भवन्तु ।
अथैष बन्धुद्विजसज्जनाद्यै-
र्दोलामधिश्रित्य ययौ प्रसन्नः ॥६१॥

*vidhīyatāṁ samprati vatsa yātrā*
*panthāna ete śubhadā bhavantu |*
*athaiṣa bandhu-dvija-saj-janādyair*
*dolām adhiśritya yayau prasannaḥ ||61||*

*Word for word:* *vidhīyatām* — let it be made; *samprati* — now; *vatsa* — O child; *yātrā* — the journey; *panthānaḥ* — roads; *ete* — these; *śubhadāḥ* — auspicious; *bhavantu* — may be; *atha* — then; *eṣaḥ* — He; *bandhu* — with relatives; *dvija* — brahmanas; *sat* — good; *jana* — people; *ādyaiḥ* — and others; *dolām* — the palanquin; *adhiśritya* — having mounted; *yayau* — set out; *prasannaḥ* — joyful.

**61.** "O child, let the journey be made now. May these roads be auspicious!" Then He, joyful, mounted the palanquin and set out with relatives, brahmanas, good people and others.

### Verse 62

प्रदीप्तदीपावलिभिर्विशिष्टं
तस्याविशत्सद्भवनं मनोज्ञम् ।
ततोऽभिगम्यालयमध्यमेनं
निनाय विप्रो निजभाग्यराशिम् ॥६२॥

*pradīpta-dīpāvalibhir viśiṣṭaṁ*
*tasyāviśat sad-bhavanaṁ manojñam |*
*tato 'bhigamyālaya-madhyam enaṁ*
*nināya vipro nija-bhāgya-rāśim ||62||*

*Word for word:* *pradīpta* — of blazing; *dīpa* — of lamps; *āvalibhiḥ* — by rows; *viśiṣṭam* — distinguished; *tasya* — his; *aviśat* — entered; *sat* — beautiful; *bhavanam* — house; *manojñam* — charming; *tataḥ* — then; *abhigamya* — having come forward to meet; *ālaya* — of the house; *madhyam* — into the middle; *enam* — Him; *nināya* — led; *vipraḥ* — the brahmana; *nija* — of his own; *bhāgya* — of good fortune; *rāśim* — the treasure.

**62.** He entered [Vallabha's] beautiful, charming house, distinguished by rows of blazing lamps. Then the brahmana came forward to meet Him and led Him into the midst of the house — Him, the whole treasure of his own good fortune.

### Verse 63

पाद्यादिना तं वरयाम्बभूव स
द्विजो नवद्वीपमहौषधीश्वरम् ।
बभौ वृतस्तेन महाप्रभुस्तदा
त्रैलोक्यलक्ष्मीललितां तनुं श्रितः ॥६३॥

*pādyādinā taṁ varayāmbabhūva sa*
*dvijo navadvīpa-mahauṣadhīśvaram |*
*babhau vṛtas tena mahāprabhus tadā*
*trailokya-lakṣmī-lalitāṁ tanuṁ śritaḥ ||63||*

*Word for word:* *pādya* — with water for the feet; *ādinā* — and the rest; *tam* — Him; *varayāmbabhūva* — chose [as bridegroom]; *saḥ* — that; *dvijaḥ* — brahmana; *navadvīpa* — of Navadvipa; *mahā* — the great; *oṣadhī* — of herbs; *īśvaram* — lord; *babhau* — shone; *vṛtaḥ* — chosen; *tena* — by him; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *tadā* — then; *trailokya* — of the three worlds; *lakṣmī* — with the beauty; *lalitām* — lovely; *tanum* — a body; *śritaḥ* — having assumed.

**63.** With water for the feet and the other offerings, the brahmana chose Him as bridegroom — Him, the great lord of herbs [the moon] of Navadvipa. And Mahaprabhu, chosen by him, then shone, having assumed a body lovely with the beauty of the three worlds.

*Note.* *Oṣadhīśvara*, "lord of healing herbs", is the moon: in Indian belief the moon nourishes plants. *Varaṇa* — the rite in which the bride's father "chooses" the bridegroom.

### Verse 64

स गौरचन्द्रः कनकाङ्गदादिभि-
र्विराजमानोरुभुजान्तरः स्वयम् ।
कल्पद्रुमश्रीरुचिरस्य विभ्रमं
जहार हारी तपनीयभूभृतः ॥६४॥

*sa gauracandraḥ kanakāṅgadādibhir*
*virājamānoru-bhujāntaraḥ svayam |*
*kalpadruma-śrī-rucirasya vibhramaṁ*
*jahāra hārī tapanīya-bhūbhṛtaḥ ||64||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — that; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra; *kanaka* — with golden; *aṅgada* — armlets; *ādibhiḥ* — and the rest; *virājamāna* — shining; *uru* — broad; *bhujāntaraḥ* — [with] chest; *svayam* — Himself; *kalpadruma* — of wish-fulfilling trees; *śrī* — with the beauty; *rucirasya* — lovely; *vibhramam* — the splendour; *jahāra* — stole; *hārī* — wearing a necklace; *tapanīya* — golden; *bhūbhṛtaḥ* — of the mountain.

**64.** Gaurachandra Himself, His broad chest shining with golden armlets and other ornaments, wearing a necklace, stole the splendour of the golden mountain made lovely by the beauty of wish-fulfilling trees.

*Note.* A play on words: *hārī* is "wearing a necklace" and also "captivating, stealing". The golden mountain is Meru, where the wish-fulfilling trees grow.

### Verse 65

सुतां समानीय शरन्निशापते-
र्ज्योत्स्नामिव स्नापितदिग्वधूगणाम् ।
प्रभावनिध्वस्ततमिस्रसञ्चयां
स्वलङ्कृतां तां प्रभवे ददौ द्विजः ॥६५॥

*sutāṁ samānīya śaran-niśāpater*
*jyotsnām iva snāpita-dig-vadhū-gaṇām |*
*prabhāva-nidhvasta-tamisra-sañcayāṁ*
*sv-alaṅkṛtāṁ tāṁ prabhave dadau dvijaḥ ||65||*

*Word for word:* *sutām* — the daughter; *samānīya* — having brought; *śarat* — of the autumn; *niśāpateḥ* — of the moon; *jyotsnām* — the light; *iva* — like; *snāpita* — who has bathed; *dik* — of the quarters; *vadhū* — of the maidens; *gaṇām* — the host; *prabhāva* — by her radiance; *nidhvasta* — who has dispelled; *tamisra* — of darkness; *sañcayām* — the masses; *su* — beautifully; *alaṅkṛtām* — adorned; *tām* — her; *prabhave* — to the Lord; *dadau* — gave; *dvijaḥ* — the brahmana.

**65.** The brahmana brought his beautifully adorned daughter — like the light of the autumn moon, which bathes the host of maidens of the quarters and by its radiance dispels the masses of darkness — and gave her to the Lord.

### Verse 66

चिराय सा लब्धफलं मनोरथं
विलोक्य बाला चरणाम्बुजं प्रभोः ।
समाश्रिता दीप्तिमुवाह भूयसीं
सौन्दर्य्यलक्ष्मीरिव सा स्वयंवरा ॥६६॥

*cirāya sā labdha-phalaṁ manorathaṁ*
*vilokya bālā caraṇāmbujaṁ prabhoḥ |*
*samāśritā dīptim uvāha bhūyasīṁ*
*saundarya-lakṣmīr iva sā svayaṁvarā ||66||*

*Word for word:* *cirāya* — long-cherished; *sā* — she; *labdha* — having obtained; *phalam* — fruit; *manoratham* — the desire; *vilokya* — having seen; *bālā* — the girl; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *ambujam* — the lotus; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *samāśritā* — having taken shelter; *dīptim* — radiance; *uvāha* — bore; *bhūyasīm* — surpassing; *saundarya* — of beauty; *lakṣmīḥ* — the goddess; *iva* — like; *sā* — she; *svayaṁvarā* — choosing her husband herself.

**66.** Beholding the lotus feet of the Lord — her long-cherished desire, now come to fruit — the girl took shelter of them and bore a surpassing radiance, like the goddess of beauty herself choosing her own husband.

### Verse 67

परस्परं तौ सुमनःसमूहौ
विचक्रतुः प्रेमरसेन सार्द्धम् ।
तयोरभिक्षा सममाविरासी-
त्तदैव चित्रा शशिनोरिवासौ ॥६७॥

*parasparaṁ tau sumanaḥ-samūhau*
*vicakratuḥ prema-rasena sārdham |*
*tayor abhīkṣā samam āvirāsīt*
*tadaiva citrā śaśinor ivāsau ||67||*

*Word for word:* *parasparam* — at each other; *tau* — the two; *sumanaḥ* — of flowers; *samūhau* — handfuls; *vicakratuḥ* — cast; *prema* — of love; *rasena* — with the rapture; *sārdham* — together with; *tayoḥ* — their; *abhīkṣā* — glance; *samam* — at once; *āvirāsīt* — appeared; *tadā eva* — at that very moment; *citrā* — Chitra; *śaśinoḥ* — of the moon (?); *iva* — as; *asau* — that.

**67.** With the rapture of love the two cast handfuls of flowers at each other — and at that very moment their glances appeared together, as [the meeting] of Chitra and the moon.

*Note.* The exchange of flowers and the first glance of bride and groom (Beng. *śubha-dṛṣṭi*, "the auspicious glance") are rites of the Bengali wedding. (?) The edition has *abhikṣā*; we read *abhīkṣā* ("glance"). The dual *śaśinoḥ* is unclear; the text is the same in the Gosvami edition (GGM). Possibly: "that [glance] of the two moons", i.e. bride and groom are two moons, and the wondrous (*citrā*) glance between them is like the bright star Chitra.

### Verse 68

अथोपविश्य प्रभवे प्रदातुं
सुतां द्विजोऽसौ विधिना विधिज्ञः ।
वराय पाद्यं विनिवेद्य हृद्यं
हृदिस्थितं प्रेमविलोचनाभ्याम् ॥६८॥

*athopaviśya prabhave pradātuṁ*
*sutāṁ dvijo 'sau vidhinā vidhi-jñaḥ |*
*varāya pādyaṁ vinivedya hṛdyaṁ*
*hṛdi-sthitaṁ prema-vilocanābhyām ||68||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *upaviśya* — having sat down; *prabhave* — to the Lord; *pradātum* — to give; *sutām* — the daughter; *dvijaḥ* — the brahmana; *asau* — that; *vidhinā* — according to the rule; *vidhi* — of the rite; *jñaḥ* — the knower; *varāya* — to the bridegroom; *pādyam* — water for the feet; *vinivedya* — having offered; *hṛdyam* — heartfelt; *hṛdi* — in the heart; *sthitam* — held; *prema* — of love; *vilocanābhyām* — with the two eyes.

**68.** Then the brahmana, the knower of the rite, sat down to give his daughter to the Lord according to the rule, and with his two eyes full of love he offered the bridegroom water for His feet — heartfelt, welling up from within his heart.

*Note.* That is, the tears of love became the water for the feet.

### Verse 69

तमर्घ्यमर्घ्यं मधुपर्कभूषितं
सविष्टरं सुन्दरमासनं ततः ।
क्रमेण तस्मै महनीयमूर्त्तये
ददौ वरस्य प्रवराय शुद्धधीः ॥६९॥

*tam arghyam arghyaṁ madhuparka-bhūṣitaṁ*
*sa-viṣṭaraṁ sundaram āsanaṁ tataḥ |*
*krameṇa tasmai mahanīya-mūrtaye*
*dadau varasya pravarāya śuddha-dhīḥ ||69||*

*Word for word:* *tam* — that; *arghyam* — worthy; *arghyam* — arghya offering; *madhuparka* — with madhuparka; *bhūṣitam* — adorned; *sa* — with; *viṣṭaram* — a grass mat; *sundaram* — a beautiful; *āsanam* — seat; *tataḥ* — then; *krameṇa* — in due order; *tasmai* — to Him; *mahanīya* — worthy of worship; *mūrtaye* — whose form; *dadau* — gave; *varasya* — of bridegrooms; *pravarāya* — to the best; *śuddha* — pure; *dhīḥ* — [whose] mind.

**69.** Then the pure-minded [brahmana] offered in due order to Him, the best of bridegrooms, whose form is worthy of worship, that worthy arghya adorned with madhuparka, and a beautiful seat with a grass mat.

*Note.* *Arghya* — the respectful offering of water; *madhuparka* — a mixture of honey, curd and ghee offered to an honoured guest and to the bridegroom; *viṣṭara* — a mat of kusha grass.

### Verse 70

दत्त्वा तनूजां महिताय तस्मै
बभार हर्षं सदृशं समुत्सुकः ।
इमानि चासौ मनसि प्रकामं
बहिर्विभेदाथ तनूरुहेषु ॥७०॥

*dattvā tanūjāṁ mahitāya tasmai*
*babhāra harṣaṁ sadṛśaṁ samutsukaḥ |*
*imāni cāsau manasi prakāmaṁ*
*bahir vibhedātha tanūruheṣu ||70||*

*Word for word:* *dattvā* — having given; *tanūjām* — the daughter; *mahitāya* — to the honoured; *tasmai* — to Him; *babhāra* — felt; *harṣam* — joy; *sadṛśam* — befitting; *samutsukaḥ* — deeply moved; *imāni* — these [joys]; *ca* — and; *asau* — he; *manasi* — in the mind; *prakāmam* — abundantly; *bahiḥ* — outward; *vibheda* — burst; *atha* — then; *tanūruheṣu* — in the hairs of the body.

**70.** Having given his daughter to Him, the honoured one, the brahmana, deeply moved, felt a joy befitting [the occasion]. And these joys, abundant in his mind, then burst outward — in the hairs of his body [standing on end].

### Verse 71

ततो निवृत्ते महिते महोत्सवे
प्रियां समादाय कृपामहाम्बुधिः ।
रराज राजन्मुखपद्मविभ्रमो
यथा शशी चन्द्रिकया समन्वितः ॥७१॥

*tato nivṛtte mahite mahotsave*
*priyāṁ samādāya kṛpā-mahāmbudhiḥ |*
*rarāja rājan-mukha-padma-vibhramo*
*yathā śaśī candrikayā samanvitaḥ ||71||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *nivṛtte* — [when] concluded; *mahite* — the glorious; *mahā* — great; *utsave* — festival; *priyām* — the beloved; *samādāya* — having taken; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *mahā* — the great; *ambudhiḥ* — ocean; *rarāja* — shone; *rājat* — radiant; *mukha* — of the face; *padma* — of the lotus; *vibhramaḥ* — [with] the charm; *yathā* — as; *śaśī* — the moon; *candrikayā* — with its moonlight; *samanvitaḥ* — united.

**71.** Then, when the glorious great festival had concluded, the great ocean of mercy took His beloved with Him and shone, the charm of His lotus face radiant, like the moon united with its moonlight.

### Verse 72

विश्वम्भरो विश्वजनाय कौतुकं
विकीर्य्य विश्वार्त्तिभरैर्महाप्रभुः ।
लक्ष्मीं समादाय शरीरिणीं श्रियं
सौन्दर्य्यसारस्य जगाम वेश्मनि ॥७२॥

*viśvambharo viśva-janāya kautukaṁ*
*vikīrya viśvārti-bharair mahāprabhuḥ |*
*lakṣmīṁ samādāya śarīriṇīṁ śriyaṁ*
*saundarya-sārasya jagāma veśmani ||72||*

*Word for word:* *viśvambharaḥ* — Vishvambhara; *viśva* — to all; *janāya* — to the people; *kautukam* — delight; *vikīrya* — having scattered; *viśva* — of the world; *ārti* — of the sorrows; *bharaiḥ* — (?) (read *haraiḥ* — with [the acts] removing); *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *lakṣmīm* — Lakshmi; *samādāya* — having taken; *śarīriṇīm* — embodied; *śriyam* — the beauty; *saundarya* — of loveliness; *sārasya* — of the essence; *jagāma* — went; *veśmani* — home.

**72.** Vishvambhara Mahaprabhu, having scattered delight to all the people and relieved the sorrows of the world, took Lakshmi — the embodied beauty of the very essence of loveliness — and went home.

*Note.* (?) *Viśvārti-bharaiḥ* ("with loads of the world's sorrows") does not fit the sense; probably *viśvārti-haraiḥ* ("removing the world's sorrows"), and the translation follows this reading. The text is the same in the Gosvami edition (GGM).

### Verse 73

द्विजाङ्गनानामथ सञ्चयैः सा
शची सुतोद्वाहसुखैरनेकैः ।
अस्फूर्त्तिमत्तां धियमेत्य गेहे
प्रवेशयामास वधूं सुतञ्च ॥७३॥

*dvijāṅganānām atha sañcayaiḥ sā*
*śacī sutodvāha-sukhair anekaiḥ |*
*asphūrtimattāṁ dhiyam etya gehe*
*praveśayāmāsa vadhūṁ sutañ ca ||73||*

*Word for word:* *dvija* — of the brahmanas; *aṅganānām* — of the wives; *atha* — then; *sañcayaiḥ* — with the throngs; *sā* — that; *śacī* — Shachi; *suta* — of the son; *udvāha* — of the wedding; *sukhaiḥ* — by the joys; *anekaiḥ* — many; *asphūrtimattām* — to a state of being overwhelmed; *dhiyam* — mind; *etya* — having come; *gehe* — into the house; *praveśayāmāsa* — led; *vadhūm* — the bride; *sutam* — the son; *ca* — and.

**73.** Then Shachi, with throngs of brahmana wives, her mind overwhelmed by the many joys of her son's wedding, led the bride and her son into the house.

*Note.* *Asphūrtimattā*, literally "a state without manifestation": the mind is so full that it cannot act.

### Verse 74

दत्त्वा द्विजेभ्यो बहुधैव हर्षिता
वसूनि वासांसि च चन्दनानि ।
लेभे तदा निर्वृतिमुत्तमां शची
समाप्तकृत्या हि महाजनोद्यमाः ॥७४॥

*dattvā dvijebhyo bahudhaiva harṣitā*
*vasūni vāsāṁsi ca candanāni |*
*lebhe tadā nirvṛtim uttamāṁ śacī*
*samāpta-kṛtyā hi mahājanodyamāḥ ||74||*

*Word for word:* *dattvā* — having given; *dvijebhyaḥ* — to the brahmanas; *bahudhā* — in many ways; *eva* — indeed; *harṣitā* — delighted; *vasūni* — wealth; *vāsāṁsi* — clothes; *ca* — and; *candanāni* — sandal; *lebhe* — obtained; *tadā* — then; *nirvṛtim* — peace; *uttamām* — the highest; *śacī* — Shachi; *samāpta* — completed; *kṛtyāḥ* — [whose] tasks; *hi* — for; *mahājana* — of great people; *udyamāḥ* — the undertakings.

**74.** Delighted, Shachi gave the brahmanas wealth, clothes and sandal in many ways, and then found the highest peace: for the undertakings of great people reach their completion.

### Verse 75

वसन्स इत्थं निजमन्दिरे प्रभु-
र्मुमोद लक्ष्म्या सह कान्तया तया ।
सदा जनन्या परिचिन्तितक्रियो
गृहस्थधर्म्मं सदुदारमावहन् ॥७५॥

*vasan sa itthaṁ nija-mandire prabhur*
*mumoda lakṣmyā saha kāntayā tayā |*
*sadā jananyā paricintita-kriyo*
*gṛhastha-dharmaṁ sad-udāram āvahan ||75||*

*Word for word:* *vasan* — living; *saḥ* — He; *ittham* — thus; *nija* — in His own; *mandire* — in the home; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *mumoda* — rejoiced; *lakṣmyā* — with Lakshmi; *saha* — together; *kāntayā* — with the beloved; *tayā* — with her; *sadā* — always; *jananyā* — by the mother; *paricintita* — planned; *kriyaḥ* — [whose] acts; *gṛhastha* — of a householder; *dharmam* — the duty; *sat* — nobly; *udāram* — generously; *āvahan* — carrying out.

**75.** Living thus in His own home, the Lord rejoiced with His beloved Lakshmi. Always doing what His mother planned, He carried out the duties of a householder nobly and generously.

### Verse 76

कान्ताङ्गसङ्गामृतधारया तया-
भिषेचयन्ती हृदयेशयद्रुमम् ।
मनोभिलाषस्तवकोच्चयं सुख-
प्रसूनवृन्दं विरराज सा भृशम् ॥७६॥

*kāntāṅga-saṅgāmṛta-dhārayā tayā-*
*bhiṣecayantī hṛdayeśaya-drumam |*
*mano-'bhilāṣa-stavakoccayaṁ sukha-*
*prasūna-vṛndaṁ virarāja sā bhṛśam ||76||*

*Word for word:* *kānta* — of the beloved; *aṅga* — of the body; *saṅga* — of the touch; *amṛta* — of nectar; *dhārayā* — with the stream; *tayā* — with that; *abhiṣecayantī* — watering; *hṛdayeśaya* — abiding in the heart; *drumam* — the tree; *manaḥ* — of the heart; *abhilāṣa* — of desires; *stavaka* — of clusters; *uccayam* — [bearing] a mass; *sukha* — of happiness; *prasūna* — of flowers; *vṛndam* — [bearing] a multitude; *virarāja* — shone; *sā* — she; *bhṛśam* — exceedingly.

**76.** With that stream of nectar — the touch of her beloved's body — she watered the tree abiding in her heart, laden with clusters of her heart's desires and with a multitude of flowers of happiness; and she shone exceedingly.

*Note.* *Hṛdayeśaya* is read as *hṛdaye-śaya*, "abiding in the heart" (cf. *hṛc-chaya*, love): the tree of love in her heart. It may also be taken as "[the tree] of the lord of the heart": then the husband is the wish-fulfilling tree and the wife the stream that waters it.

### Verse 77

उरस्तडागस्य किमब्जकोरकौ
मनोहरे हारलताफले किमु ।
लावण्यसिन्धोः किमु कोकशावकौ
मनोजदन्तावलकुम्भकौ किमु ॥७७॥

*uras-taḍāgasya kim abja-korakau*
*manohare hāra-latā-phale kimu |*
*lāvaṇya-sindhoḥ kimu koka-śāvakau*
*manoja-dantāvala-kumbhakau kimu ||77||*

*Word for word:* *uraḥ* — of the bosom; *taḍāgasya* — of the pond; *kim* — are they?; *abja* — of the lotus; *korakau* — two buds; *manohare* — charming; *hāra* — of the necklace; *latā* — of the creeper; *phale* — two fruits; *kimu* — or; *lāvaṇya* — of loveliness; *sindhoḥ* — of the ocean; *kimu* — or; *koka* — of the chakravaka; *śāvakau* — two chicks; *manoja* — of the god of love; *dantāvala* — of the elephant; *kumbhakau* — the two frontal globes; *kimu* — or.

**77.** [Her young breasts —] are they two lotus buds in the pond of her bosom? Or two charming fruits on the creeper of her necklace? Or two chakravaka chicks in the ocean of loveliness? Or the two frontal globes of the elephant of the god of love?

*Note.* Verses 77–80 are the description of the heroine's beauty (*nakha-śikha*) traditional in a mahakavya; all the comparisons are conventional images of Sanskrit poetry. *Koka* — the chakravaka, the ruddy shelduck; a pair of these birds is the emblem of conjugal love.

### Verse 78

विधेर्निजं सौष्ठवमुन्निनीषतो
निर्म्माणरम्ये किमु हेमकुम्भकौ ।
स्तनौ नवारब्धसमुद्गकौ प्रभोः
संबिभ्रती हर्षभरं बभास सा ॥७८॥
(युग्मकम्)

*vidher nijaṁ sauṣṭhavam unninīṣato*
*nirmāṇa-ramye kimu hema-kumbhakau |*
*stanau navārabdha-samudgakau prabhoḥ*
*saṁbibhratī harṣa-bharaṁ babhāsa sā ||78||*

*Word for word:* *vidheḥ* — of the Creator; *nijam* — his own; *sauṣṭhavam* — skill; *unninīṣataḥ* — wishing to display; *nirmāṇa* — in workmanship; *ramye* — lovely; *kimu* — or; *hema* — golden; *kumbhakau* — two little pitchers; *stanau* — the breasts; *nava* — newly; *ārabdha* — begun; *samudgakau* — two caskets; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *saṁbibhratī* — bearing; *harṣa* — of joy; *bharam* — the fullness; *babhāsa* — shone; *sā* — she.

**78.** Or are they two little golden pitchers, lovely in workmanship, [fashioned] by the Creator wishing to display his own skill? Bearing her breasts — two newly begun caskets [holding] the fullness of the Lord's joy — she shone.

*Note.* *Yugmakam* — "a pair": verses 77–78 form a single sentence.

### Verse 79

मुखेन मन्दाक्षविनम्रचक्षुषा
स्मितानुपृक्तेन सदोष्ठरोचिषा ।
स्मेरेण गण्डेन मधूकपाण्डुना
मनोधिराजस्य मनो जहार सा ॥७९॥

*mukhena mandākṣa-vinamra-cakṣuṣā*
*smitānupṛktena sad-oṣṭha-rociṣā |*
*smereṇa gaṇḍena madhūka-pāṇḍunā*
*mano-'dhirājasya mano jahāra sā ||79||*

*Word for word:* *mukhena* — with the face; *mandākṣa* — from modesty; *vinamra* — lowered; *cakṣuṣā* — [with] eyes; *smita* — by a smile; *anupṛktena* — touched; *sat* — of lovely; *oṣṭha* — lips; *rociṣā* — [with] the lustre; *smereṇa* — smiling; *gaṇḍena* — with the cheek; *madhūka* — [like] the madhuka flower; *pāṇḍunā* — pale; *manaḥ* — of hearts; *adhirājasya* — of the sovereign; *manaḥ* — the heart; *jahāra* — stole; *sā* — she.

**79.** With her face — its eyes lowered in modesty, touched by a smile, with the lustre of her lovely lips — and with her smiling cheek, pale as a madhuka flower, she stole the heart of the very sovereign of hearts.

*Note.* *Madhūka* — a tree with pale cream-coloured flowers.

### Verse 80

सुसीमभाजा स्तनकोरकेण सा
बलद्वलीकेन कृशोदरेण च ।
नितम्बिना सज्जघनेन सुन्दरी
सदा मनोनाथमनः समाददे ॥८०॥

*susīma-bhājā stana-korakeṇa sā*
*balad-valīkena kṛśodareṇa ca |*
*nitambinā saj-jaghanena sundarī*
*sadā mano-nātha-manaḥ samādade ||80||*

*Word for word:* *susīma* — lovely contour; *bhājā* — possessing; *stana* — of the breast; *korakeṇa* — with the bud; *sā* — she; *balat* — showing; *valīkena* — [with] folds; *kṛśa* — with slender; *udareṇa* — with the waist; *ca* — and; *nitambinā* — rounded; *sat* — with lovely; *jaghanena* — with the hips; *sundarī* — the beauty; *sadā* — always; *manaḥ* — of the heart; *nātha* — of the lord; *manaḥ* — the heart; *samādade* — captivated.

**80.** With the bud of her breast of lovely contour, with her slender waist showing its folds, and with her lovely rounded hips, the beauty always captivated the heart of the lord of her heart.

*Note.* *Balad-valīka* — probably the *trivalī*, the three folds on the abdomen, a mark of feminine beauty.

### Verse 81

तदङ्गसंसर्गसुधाम्बुराशेः
प्रवाहसंगाहनशीतलस्य ।
लावण्यमत्यन्तनितान्तकान्तं
बभूव गौराङ्गमहाप्रभोस्ततः ॥८१॥

*tad-aṅga-saṁsarga-sudhāmbu-rāśeḥ*
*pravāha-saṁgāhana-śītalasya |*
*lāvaṇyam atyanta-nitānta-kāntaṁ*
*babhūva gaurāṅga-mahāprabhos tataḥ ||81||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — of her; *aṅga* — of the body; *saṁsarga* — of the contact; *sudhā* — of nectar; *amburāśeḥ* — of the ocean; *pravāha* — in the current; *saṁgāhana* — by bathing; *śītalasya* — of [Him who was] cooled; *lāvaṇyam* — the loveliness; *atyanta* — exceedingly; *nitānta* — utterly; *kāntam* — charming; *babhūva* — became; *gaurāṅga* — of Gauranga; *mahāprabhoḥ* — of Mahaprabhu; *tataḥ* — then.

**81.** Then the loveliness of Gauranga Mahaprabhu, refreshed by bathing in the current of the nectar-ocean of contact with her body, became exceedingly, utterly charming.

### Verse 82

इत्थं कियन्त्यत्र दिनानि नाथो
नीत्वा कृपार्थं करुणैकसिन्धुः ।
ययौ मघोनो दिशि सज्जनौघैः
सार्द्धं समृद्धैर्निजसत्कृपाभिः ॥८२॥

*itthaṁ kiyanty atra dināni nātho*
*nītvā kṛpārthaṁ karuṇaika-sindhuḥ |*
*yayau maghono diśi saj-janaughaiḥ*
*sārdhaṁ samṛddhair nija-sat-kṛpābhiḥ ||82||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *kiyanti* — some; *atra* — here; *dināni* — days; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *nītvā* — having spent; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *artham* — for the sake; *karuṇā* — of compassion; *eka* — the only; *sindhuḥ* — ocean; *yayau* — went; *maghonaḥ* — of Maghavan; *diśi* — in the direction; *sat* — of good; *jana* — of people; *oghaiḥ* — with throngs; *sārdham* — together; *samṛddhaiḥ* — with [those] enriched; *nija* — by His own; *sat* — true; *kṛpābhiḥ* — by mercies.

**82.** Having thus spent some days here, the Lord, the one ocean of compassion, went for the sake of [showing] mercy in the direction of Maghavan [— to the east], together with throngs of good people enriched by His own true mercy.

*Note.* *Maghavan* is Indra, the lord of the east. This is Nimai's journey to East Bengal (Chaitanya-bhagavata, Adi 14, "The Lord visits East Bengal"; Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 16).

### Verse 83

स यत्र यत्र प्रभुरुद्गतोऽभू-
दभूतपूर्व्वः शतचन्द्रतुल्यः ।
विलोक्य नाथं खलु तत्र तत्र
रूपामृतेनापि मुमोह लोकः ॥८३॥

*sa yatra yatra prabhur udgato 'bhūd*
*abhūta-pūrvaḥ śata-candra-tulyaḥ |*
*vilokya nāthaṁ khalu tatra tatra*
*rūpāmṛtenāpi mumoha lokaḥ ||83||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — that; *yatra yatra* — wherever; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *udgataḥ* — appeared; *abhūt* — was; *abhūta* — not having been; *pūrvaḥ* — before (unprecedented); *śata* — a hundred; *candra* — moons; *tulyaḥ* — like; *vilokya* — having seen; *nātham* — the Lord; *khalu* — indeed; *tatra tatra* — there; *rūpa* — of beauty; *amṛtena* — by the nectar; *api* — even; *mumoha* — was enchanted; *lokaḥ* — the people.

**83.** Wherever the Lord appeared — unprecedented, like a hundred moons — there the people, seeing the Lord, were enchanted by the very nectar of His beauty.

### Verse 84

लावण्यपीयूषनिधौ मनुष्या
विलोक्य वक्त्रेन्दुमदृष्टपूर्व्वम् ।
विलोचनाभ्यां सततं पिबन्त-
स्तृष्णाविकारस्य न पारमीयुः ॥८४॥

*lāvaṇya-pīyūṣa-nidhau manuṣyā*
*vilokya vaktrendum adṛṣṭa-pūrvam |*
*vilocanābhyāṁ satataṁ pibantas*
*tṛṣṇā-vikārasya na pāram īyuḥ ||84||*

*Word for word:* *lāvaṇya* — of loveliness; *pīyūṣa* — of the nectar; *nidhau* — in the treasure-house (ocean); *manuṣyāḥ* — the people; *vilokya* — having seen; *vaktra* — of the face; *indum* — the moon; *adṛṣṭa* — not seen; *pūrvam* — before; *vilocanābhyām* — with their eyes; *satatam* — continually; *pibantaḥ* — drinking; *tṛṣṇā* — of thirst; *vikārasya* — of the agitation; *na* — not; *pāram* — the end; *īyuḥ* — reached.

**84.** Seeing the moon of His face, never seen before, in that treasure-ocean of the nectar of loveliness, the people drank it continually with their eyes, yet never reached the end of the agitation of their thirst.

### Verse 85

परस्परं ते कथयाम्बभूवुः
क एष कस्यैष महानुभावः ।
पुण्येन वा केन दधार गर्भे
सुनिर्वृता का सुकुमारमेनम् ॥८५॥

*parasparaṁ te kathayāmbabhūvuḥ*
*ka eṣa kasyaiṣa mahānubhāvaḥ |*
*puṇyena vā kena dadhāra garbhe*
*su-nirvṛtā kā su-kumāram enam ||85||*

*Word for word:* *parasparam* — to one another; *te* — they; *kathayāmbabhūvuḥ* — said; *kaḥ* — who; *eṣaḥ* — this; *kasya* — whose; *eṣaḥ* — this; *mahānubhāvaḥ* — noble one; *puṇyena* — by merit; *vā* — and; *kena* — by what; *dadhāra* — bore; *garbhe* — in the womb; *su* — supremely; *nirvṛtā* — blessed; *kā* — what [woman]; *su* — very; *kumāram* — tender youth; *enam* — this.

**85.** They said to one another: "Who is He? Whose [son] is this noble one? And by what merit did some supremely blessed woman bear this very tender youth in her womb?"

### Verse 86

अनङ्ग एवायमभूच्छरीरी
विधाय लक्ष्मीं द्विगुणां स्वकीयाम् ।
अस्माकमक्ष्णोः श्रवणद्वयस्य
न गोचरः कुत्रचिदेवमेषः ॥८६॥

*anaṅga evāyam abhūc charīrī*
*vidhāya lakṣmīṁ dviguṇāṁ svakīyām |*
*asmākam akṣṇoḥ śravaṇa-dvayasya*
*na gocaraḥ kutracid evam eṣaḥ ||86||*

*Word for word:* *anaṅgaḥ* — the Bodiless One; *eva* — himself; *ayam* — this; *abhūt* — has become; *śarīrī* — embodied; *vidhāya* — having made; *lakṣmīm* — beauty; *dviguṇām* — twofold; *svakīyām* — his own; *asmākam* — of our; *akṣṇoḥ* — of the eyes; *śravaṇa* — of ears; *dvayasya* — of the pair; *na* — not; *gocaraḥ* — within the range; *kutracit* — anywhere; *evam* — such; *eṣaḥ* — this.

**86.** "This is the Bodiless One himself, who has taken on a body, making his own beauty twofold! Never anywhere has such a one come within the range of our eyes or of our ears."

*Note.* The Bodiless One (*Anaṅga*) is Kama, the god of love (cf. *Atanu*, 3.30).

### Verse 87

स्त्रियस्तथोचुर्नयनोत्पलाभ्यां
तदास्यपीयूषरसं पिबन्त्यः ।
क एष कन्दर्पसमस्तदर्पं
तिरस्करोत्यङ्गरुचैव शश्वत् ॥८७॥

*striyas tathocur nayanotpalābhyāṁ*
*tad-āsya-pīyūṣa-rasaṁ pibantyaḥ |*
*ka eṣa kandarpa-samasta-darpaṁ*
*tiraskaroty aṅga-rucaiva śaśvat ||87||*

*Word for word:* *striyaḥ* — the women; *tathā* — likewise; *ūcuḥ* — said; *nayana* — of the eyes; *utpalābhyām* — with the [two] lotuses; *tat* — His; *āsya* — of the face; *pīyūṣa* — of the nectar; *rasam* — the taste; *pibantyaḥ* — drinking; *kaḥ* — who; *eṣaḥ* — this; *kandarpa* — of Kandarpa; *samasta* — all; *darpam* — the pride; *tiraskaroti* — puts to shame; *aṅga* — of the body; *rucā* — by the lustre; *eva* — alone; *śaśvat* — constantly.

**87.** Likewise the women, drinking the taste of the nectar of His face with the lotuses of their eyes, said: "Who is this, who by the lustre of His body alone constantly puts to shame all the pride of Kandarpa?"

*Note.* *Kandarpa* is Kama, the god of love.

### Verse 88

सौभाग्यराशेः कतरेव वल्ली
लीलावतोऽस्यानुपमैव लीला ।
रतिं विधायात्र रतिं न का वा
तिरस्करोत्यद्भुत एष सर्गः ॥८८॥

*saubhāgya-rāśeḥ katareva vallī*
*līlāvato 'syānupamaiva līlā |*
*ratiṁ vidhāyātra ratiṁ na kā vā*
*tiraskaroty adbhuta eṣa sargaḥ ||88||*

*Word for word:* *saubhāgya* — of good fortune; *rāśeḥ* — of the heap; *katarā* — which [woman]; *iva* — like; *vallī* — the creeper; *līlāvataḥ* — of the playful one; *asya* — of this; *anupamā* — incomparable; *eva* — indeed; *līlā* — the play; *ratim* — love; *vidhāya* — having conceived; *atra* — for him; *ratim* — Rati; *na* — not; *kā* — which [woman]; *vā* — indeed; *tiraskaroti* — puts to shame; *adbhutaḥ* — wondrous; *eṣaḥ* — this; *sargaḥ* — creation.

**88.** "Which woman is the creeper [clinging] to this heap of good fortune? Incomparable indeed is the play of this playful one! What woman, having conceived love (*rati*) for Him, would not put Rati to shame? Wondrous is this creation!"

*Note.* A play on words: *rati* is "attraction, love", and Rati, the consort of the god of love. The first pada admits more than one reading; the text is the same in Goswami's edition (GGM).

### Verse 89

शृण्वन्नसौ मुग्धवधूजनेरिता
वाचो नवद्वीपकिशोरचन्द्रमाः ।
लावण्यलक्ष्मीस्तिमितेन रज्यता
कटाक्षपातेन ददर्श ताः प्रभुः ॥८९॥

*śṛṇvann asau mugdha-vadhū-janeritā*
*vāco navadvīpa-kiśora-candramāḥ |*
*lāvaṇya-lakṣmī-stimitena rajyatā*
*kaṭākṣa-pātena dadarśa tāḥ prabhuḥ ||89||*

*Word for word:* *śṛṇvan* — hearing; *asau* — He; *mugdha* — by innocent; *vadhū* — of young women; *jana* — by the folk; *īritāḥ* — uttered; *vācaḥ* — the words; *navadvīpa* — of Navadvipa; *kiśora* — the youthful; *candramāḥ* — moon; *lāvaṇya* — of loveliness; *lakṣmī* — with the splendour; *stimitena* — with steeped; *rajyatā* — with affectionate; *kaṭākṣa* — of a sidelong glance; *pātena* — with the casting; *dadarśa* — looked; *tāḥ* — at them; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord.

**89.** Hearing the words uttered by the innocent young women, the Lord, the youthful moon of Navadvipa, looked at them with an affectionate sidelong glance, steeped in the splendour of loveliness.

### Verse 90

यन्नाममात्रश्रवणेन देहिन-
स्तरन्ति संसारसमुद्रमुल्वणम् ।
सोऽपि स्वयं लोचनवर्त्मसंश्रित-
स्तद्वर्ण्यतां केन कृपा महाप्रभोः ॥९०॥

*yan-nāma-mātra-śravaṇena dehinas*
*taranti saṁsāra-samudram ulvaṇam |*
*so 'pi svayaṁ locana-vartma-saṁśritas*
*tad varṇyatāṁ kena kṛpā mahāprabhoḥ ||90||*

*Word for word:* *yat* — whose; *nāma* — of the name; *mātra* — merely; *śravaṇena* — by the hearing; *dehinaḥ* — embodied beings; *taranti* — cross; *saṁsāra* — of worldly existence; *samudram* — the ocean; *ulvaṇam* — dreadful; *saḥ* — He; *api* — even; *svayam* — Himself; *locana* — of the eyes; *vartma* — the path; *saṁśritaḥ* — entered; *tat* — therefore; *varṇyatām* — can be described; *kena* — by whom; *kṛpā* — the mercy; *mahāprabhoḥ* — of Mahaprabhu.

**90.** He by merely hearing whose name embodied beings cross the dreadful ocean of worldly existence — He Himself came into the path of their eyes. Who, then, can describe the mercy of Mahaprabhu?

### Verse 91

पद्मावतीं द्वीपवतीं कृपावान्
स्नानेन सौभाग्यवतीं चकार ।
तस्यास्तटं साधुभिरर्हितोऽसौ
महाप्रभुः सद्गृहमध्यवात्सीत् ॥९१॥

*padmāvatīṁ dvīpavatīṁ kṛpāvān*
*snānena saubhāgyavatīṁ cakāra |*
*tasyās taṭaṁ sādhubhir arhito 'sau*
*mahāprabhuḥ sad-gṛham adhyavātsīt ||91||*

*Word for word:* *padmāvatīm* — the Padmavati; *dvīpavatīm* — the river (having islands); *kṛpāvān* — the merciful one; *snānena* — by bathing; *saubhāgyavatīm* — fortunate; *cakāra* — made; *tasyāḥ* — its; *taṭam* — bank; *sādhubhiḥ* — by the saintly; *arhitaḥ* — honoured; *asau* — He; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *sat* — a good; *gṛham* — house; *adhyavātsīt* — dwelt in.

**91.** By bathing in it, the merciful Lord made the river Padmavati fortunate. Honoured by the saintly, Mahaprabhu dwelt in a good house on its bank.

*Note.* The Padmavati is the Padma, the main channel of the Ganga in East Bengal (now Bangladesh). *Dvīpavatī*, "having islands", means a river. This episode is also in the Chaitanya-bhagavata, Adi 14.

### Verse 92

महद्भिरुच्चैः पुलिनैः सुशोभै-
स्तरस्विना दीप्तिमती जवेन ।
तदङ्गसङ्गामृतपूरपूर्णा
सैषा तदा स्वस्तटिनीसमाभूत् ॥९२॥

*mahadbhir uccaiḥ pulinaiḥ suśobhais*
*tarasvinā dīptimatī javena |*
*tad-aṅga-saṅgāmṛta-pūra-pūrṇā*
*saiṣā tadā svas-taṭinī-samābhūt ||92||*

*Word for word:* *mahadbhiḥ* — with great; *uccaiḥ* — with high; *pulinaiḥ* — with sandbanks; *suśobhaiḥ* — with beautiful; *tarasvinā* — with swift; *dīptimatī* — sparkling; *javena* — with current; *tat* — His; *aṅga* — of the body; *saṅga* — of the contact; *amṛta* — of nectar; *pūra* — with the flood; *pūrṇā* — filled; *sā* — that; *eṣā* — this [river]; *tadā* — then; *svaḥ* — of heaven; *taṭinī* — to the river; *samā* — equal; *abhūt* — became.

**92.** With its great, high and beautiful sandbanks, sparkling with its swift current, and filled with the flood of nectar of contact with His body, that river then became equal to the river of heaven.

*Note.* The river of heaven is the Ganga.

### Verse 93

तरङ्गहस्तैः शफरीविलोचनै-
र्नितम्बरूपैः पुलिनैर्विसारिभिः ।
पद्मावती तुल्यगुणा मृगीदृशां
चकार कौतूहलमस्य शाश्वतम् ॥९३॥

*taraṅga-hastaiḥ śapharī-vilocanair*
*nitamba-rūpaiḥ pulinair visāribhiḥ |*
*padmāvatī tulya-guṇā mṛgī-dṛśāṁ*
*cakāra kautūhalam asya śāśvatam ||93||*

*Word for word:* *taraṅga* — with waves; *hastaiḥ* — [as] with hands; *śapharī* — with *śapharī* fish; *vilocanaiḥ* — [as] with eyes; *nitamba* — of hips; *rūpaiḥ* — in the form; *pulinaiḥ* — with sandbanks; *visāribhiḥ* — with broad; *padmāvatī* — the Padmavati; *tulya* — equal; *guṇā* — in qualities; *mṛgī* — of a doe; *dṛśām* — to [women] with the eyes; *cakāra* — gave; *kautūhalam* — delight; *asya* — to Him; *śāśvatam* — unceasing.

**93.** With its waves for hands, its *śapharī* fish for eyes and its broad sandbanks for hips, the Padmavati, equal in qualities to doe-eyed maidens, gave Him unceasing delight.

*Note.* *Śapharī* — a small, quick, glittering fish, a classical comparison for the darting eyes of a woman.

### Verse 94

महात्मनां पुण्यसमूहभाजां
कुर्व्वन् सुखं नेत्रमहोत्पलस्य ।
ममाद माद्यत्करिराजगामी
जगन्मनोहारिविहारलोलः ॥९४॥

*mahātmanāṁ puṇya-samūha-bhājāṁ*
*kurvan sukhaṁ netra-mahotpalasya |*
*mamāda mādyat-kari-rāja-gāmī*
*jagan-mano-hāri-vihāra-lolaḥ ||94||*

*Word for word:* *mahātmanām* — of the great souls; *puṇya* — of merits; *samūha* — a multitude; *bhājām* — of [those] possessing; *kurvan* — giving; *sukham* — joy; *netra* — of the eyes; *mahā* — to the great; *utpalasya* — to the lotus; *mamāda* — rejoiced; *mādyat* — of an intoxicated; *karirāja* — of the king of elephants; *gāmī* — having the gait; *jagat* — of the world; *manaḥ* — the heart; *hāri* — captivating; *vihāra* — with strolls; *lolaḥ* — absorbed.

**94.** Giving joy to the great lotuses of the eyes of the great souls possessed of a multitude of merits, He rejoiced, moving with the gait of an intoxicated king of elephants, absorbed in strolls that captivated the heart of the world.

*Note.* "An elephant's gait" is a classical comparison for a majestic, unhurried step.

### Verse 95

तत्रैव नाथः कियतः स मासा-
नध्यापयन्कोमलचित्तवृत्तिः ।
जगज्जनाह्लादकरास्यचन्द्रो
निनाय कोटीन्दुसमानकान्तिः ॥९५॥

*tatraiva nāthaḥ kiyataḥ sa māsān*
*adhyāpayan komala-citta-vṛttiḥ |*
*jagaj-janāhlāda-karāsya-candro*
*nināya koṭīndu-samāna-kāntiḥ ||95||*

*Word for word:* *tatra eva* — right there; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *kiyataḥ* — some; *saḥ* — He; *māsān* — months; *adhyāpayan* — teaching; *komala* — of tender; *citta* — of heart; *vṛttiḥ* — [whose] disposition; *jagat* — of the world; *jana* — to the people; *āhlāda* — delight; *kara* — giving; *āsya* — of the face; *candraḥ* — [whose] moon; *nināya* — spent; *koṭi* — to millions; *indu* — of moons; *samāna* — equal; *kāntiḥ* — [whose] radiance.

**95.** Right there the Lord — tender of heart, the moon of whose face gave delight to the people of the world, whose radiance equalled that of millions of moons — spent some months teaching.

### Verse 96

अथात्र लक्ष्मीर्निजमन्दिरे सा
प्राणाधिनाथस्मृतिमात्रचेष्टा ।
पदाब्जसंवाहनमार्ज्जनाद्यैः
श्वश्रूसपर्य्यानिरता बभूव ॥९६॥

*athātra lakṣmīr nija-mandire sā*
*prāṇādhinātha-smṛti-mātra-ceṣṭā |*
*padābja-saṁvāhana-mārjanādyaiḥ*
*śvaśrū-saparyā-niratā babhūva ||96||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — meanwhile; *atra* — here; *lakṣmīḥ* — Lakshmi; *nija* — her own; *mandire* — in the house; *sā* — she; *prāṇa* — of her life; *adhinātha* — of the lord; *smṛti* — remembrance; *mātra* — only; *ceṣṭā* — [whose] activity; *pada* — of the feet; *abja* — of the lotuses; *saṁvāhana* — by the massaging; *mārjana* — by cleaning; *ādyaiḥ* — and so on; *śvaśrū* — of her mother-in-law; *saparyā* — to the service; *niratā* — devoted; *babhūva* — was.

**96.** Meanwhile here, in her own house, Lakshmi, whose only activity was remembrance of the lord of her life, was devoted to the service of her mother-in-law — massaging her lotus feet, cleaning and so on.

### Verse 97

निरन्तरं प्राणपतेः समागमं
विचिन्तयन्ती चिरमुत्सुकात्मना ।
सम्मार्ज्जनस्वस्तिकलेपनादिभि-
श्चकार सा देवगृहेऽभिषेवणम् ॥९७॥

*nirantaraṁ prāṇa-pateḥ samāgamaṁ*
*vicintayantī ciram utsukātmanā |*
*sammārjana-svastika-lepanādibhiś*
*cakāra sā deva-gṛhe 'bhiṣevaṇam ||97||*

*Word for word:* *nirantaram* — incessantly; *prāṇa* — of her life; *pateḥ* — of the lord; *samāgamam* — the reunion; *vicintayantī* — thinking of; *ciram* — long; *utsuka* — with eager; *ātmanā* — with heart; *sammārjana* — by sweeping; *svastika* — by [drawing] *svastika* signs; *lepana* — by smearing; *ādibhiḥ* — and so on; *cakāra* — performed; *sā* — she; *deva* — of God; *gṛhe* — in the house; *abhiṣevaṇam* — service.

**97.** Incessantly, long and with an eager heart thinking of reunion with the lord of her life, she performed service in the house of God, sweeping, drawing *svastika* signs, smearing [the floor] and so on.

*Note.* The *svastika* is an ancient Indian auspicious sign (from *su-asti*, "may it be well"), drawn on the floor and at the threshold. Smearing the floor (with clay and cow dung) is a traditional purification. The "house of God" is the household shrine.

### Verse 98

सुशीतलाभिः शुचिशीलताभि-
र्गिरा सुधापूरितयातिमृद्व्या ।
मेने शची मूर्त्तिमतीं श्रियं तां
तनूमिवान्यां तनुजस्य तस्य ॥९८॥

*suśītalābhiḥ śuci-śīlatābhir*
*girā sudhā-pūritayāti-mṛdvyā |*
*mene śacī mūrtimatīṁ śriyaṁ tāṁ*
*tanūm ivānyāṁ tanujasya tasya ||98||*

*Word for word:* *su* — very; *śītalābhiḥ* — by gentle; *śuci* — by pure; *śīlatābhiḥ* — by ways of conduct; *girā* — by speech; *sudhā* — with nectar; *pūritayā* — by filled; *ati* — very; *mṛdvyā* — by soft; *mene* — considered; *śacī* — Shachi; *mūrtimatīm* — embodied; *śriyam* — Shri (Lakshmi); *tām* — her; *tanūm* — a body; *iva* — as if; *anyām* — another; *tanujasya* — of the son; *tasya* — of that.

**98.** Because of her very gentle and pure ways and her very soft speech filled with nectar, Shachi considered her Shri [Lakshmi] embodied — as if another body of her son.

### Verse 99

इत्थं गृहे तत्र वधूद्वितीया
विचिन्तयन्ती तनुजागमं सा ।
निनाय कालं चिरमासजन्ती
वध्वां सुतस्नेहमतिप्रवृद्धम् ॥९९॥

*itthaṁ gṛhe tatra vadhū-dvitīyā*
*vicintayantī tanujāgamaṁ sā |*
*nināya kālaṁ ciram āsajantī*
*vadhvāṁ suta-sneham ati-pravṛddham ||99||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *gṛhe* — in the house; *tatra* — there; *vadhū* — [with] the daughter-in-law; *dvitīyā* — as [her only] companion; *vicintayantī* — thinking of; *tanuja* — of the son; *āgamam* — the return; *sā* — she; *nināya* — passed; *kālam* — the time; *ciram* — long; *āsajantī* — fixing; *vadhvām* — on the daughter-in-law; *suta* — for the son; *sneham* — affection; *ati* — greatly; *pravṛddham* — increased.

**99.** Thus, in the house there, with her daughter-in-law as her only companion, thinking of her son's return, she passed the time for long, fixing on her daughter-in-law her greatly increased affection for her son.

### Verse 100

विज्ञाय कालादयथाविहारिणः
प्रभोर्मतं सा निजचित्तवृत्तिभिः ।
तामेव विच्छेदरुजं बताश्रिता
तदातिरोधात्तमिहाकरोन्मनः ॥१००॥

*vijñāya kālād ayathā-vihāriṇaḥ*
*prabhor mataṁ sā nija-citta-vṛttibhiḥ |*
*tām eva viccheda-rujaṁ batāśritā*
*tadātirodhāt tam ihākaron manaḥ ||100||*

*Word for word:* *vijñāya* — having understood; *kālāt* — in time; *ayathā* — not as [known]; *vihāriṇaḥ* — of [Him who was] roaming; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *matam* — the intention; *sā* — she; *nija* — of her own; *citta* — of heart; *vṛttibhiḥ* — by the movements; *tām* — that; *eva* — very; *viccheda* — of separation; *rujam* — pain; *bata* — alas; *āśritā* — having taken on; *tadā* — then; *atirodhāt* — with great restraint (?); *tam* — on Him; *iha* — here; *akarot* — fixed; *manaḥ* — [her] mind.

**100.** Understanding in time, by the movements of her own heart, the intention of the Lord, who was roaming she knew not where, she — alas! — took on that very pain of separation, and then, with great restraint, fixed her mind on Him here.

*Note.* (?) The verse is obscure. *Tam* (masculine) is taken here as "on Him" (the Lord), with *manaḥ akarot*, "set her mind"; one may also read *tadā tirodhāt*, "for the sake of disappearance [from the world]" — cf. the snakebite in the next verse. This prepares her departure (v. 101). The text is the same in Goswami's edition (GGM).

### Verse 101

दैवादथो मन्दिरमध्यमागत-
श्चक्षुःश्रवाः क्रूरतरः सुपामरः ।
वध्वाः पदं शारदपद्मसौरभं
भेजे कठोरैर्दशनैः कठोरधीः ॥१०१॥

*daivād atho mandira-madhyam āgataś*
*cakṣuḥ-śravāḥ krūrataraḥ su-pāmaraḥ |*
*vadhvāḥ padaṁ śārada-padma-saurabhaṁ*
*bheje kaṭhorair daśanaiḥ kaṭhora-dhīḥ ||101||*

*Word for word:* *daivāt* — by fate; *atho* — and then; *mandira* — of the house; *madhyam* — into the interior; *āgataḥ* — having come; *cakṣuḥ* — with the eyes; *śravāḥ* — hearing (a serpent); *krūrataraḥ* — most cruel; *su* — utterly; *pāmaraḥ* — vile; *vadhvāḥ* — of the daughter-in-law; *padam* — the foot; *śārada* — of an autumn; *padma* — of a lotus; *saurabham* — having the fragrance; *bheje* — seized; *kaṭhoraiḥ* — with hard; *daśanaiḥ* — with fangs; *kaṭhora* — hard; *dhīḥ* — [whose] mind.

**101.** And then, by fate, a serpent — most cruel, utterly vile and hard of heart — came into the house and seized with its hard fangs the foot of the daughter-in-law, fragrant as an autumn lotus.

*Note.* *Cakṣuḥ-śravas*, "hearing with the eyes", is a serpent: according to Indian belief, snakes have no ears and hear with their eyes. Lakshmipriya's departure through a snakebite is also described in the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 16.20–21, where the snake is called "the serpent of separation" (*viraha-sarpa*).

### Verse 102

तथाविधां तामवलोक्य दुःखिता
शची चकाराथ विषप्रमार्ज्जनम् ।
तथा प्रसङ्गोत्तमसञ्चयानसौ
यत्नं समानीय चिरं वधूप्रिया ॥१०२॥

*tathā-vidhāṁ tām avalokya duḥkhitā*
*śacī cakārātha viṣa-pramārjanam |*
*tathā prasaṅgottama-sañcayān asau*
*yatnaṁ samānīya ciraṁ vadhū-priyā ||102||*

*Word for word:* *tathāvidhām* — in such a state; *tām* — her; *avalokya* — having seen; *duḥkhitā* — grieved; *śacī* — Shachi; *cakāra* — performed; *atha* — then; *viṣa* — of the poison; *pramārjanam* — the removal; *tathā* — also; *prasaṅga* — in this matter; *uttama* — of the best [experts]; *sañcayān* — numbers; *asau* — she; *yatnam* — with effort; *samānīya* — having summoned; *ciram* — long; *vadhū* — to her daughter-in-law; *priyā* — loving.

**102.** Seeing her in such a state, the grieving Shachi, who loved her daughter-in-law, then set about removing the poison; and with long effort she also summoned a great number of the best experts in this matter.

*Note.* *Prasaṅgottama* is unclear; it is understood here as "the best [experts] in this matter", i.e. healers of snakebite. The text is the same in Goswami's edition (GGM).

### Verse 103

अनेकधा तैर्विहिताः प्रकारा
विषस्य दूरीकरणाय नैव ।
शेकुस्तदा दैवकृतं विदित्वा
मोहं समीयुर्विकलाश्च सर्व्वे ॥१०३॥

*anekadhā tair vihitāḥ prakārā*
*viṣasya dūrīkaraṇāya naiva |*
*śekus tadā daiva-kṛtaṁ viditvā*
*mohaṁ samīyur vikalāś ca sarve ||103||*

*Word for word:* *anekadhā* — of many kinds; *taiḥ* — by them; *vihitāḥ* — applied; *prakārāḥ* — the means; *viṣasya* — of the poison; *dūrīkaraṇāya* — for the removal; *na eva* — not at all; *śekuḥ* — were able; *tadā* — then; *daiva* — by fate; *kṛtam* — done; *viditvā* — having understood; *moham* — bewilderment; *samīyuḥ* — fell into; *vikalāḥ* — helpless; *ca* — and; *sarve* — all.

**103.** They applied means of many kinds for removing the poison, but they could do nothing at all. Then, understanding it to be the doing of fate, they all fell into bewilderment, helpless.

### Verse 104

तदीश्वरेणेरितमेव मत्वा
वधूं वधूस्नेहकृशा कृशाङ्गीम् ।
गङ्गातटेऽन्यामिव तत्र गङ्गां
निनाय धन्यामतिदुःखदग्धा ॥१०४॥

*tad īśvareṇeritam eva matvā*
*vadhūṁ vadhū-sneha-kṛśā kṛśāṅgīm |*
*gaṅgā-taṭe 'nyām iva tatra gaṅgāṁ*
*nināya dhanyām ati-duḥkha-dagdhā ||104||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — that; *īśvareṇa* — by the Lord; *īritam* — ordained; *eva* — indeed; *matvā* — having considered; *vadhūm* — the daughter-in-law; *vadhū* — for the daughter-in-law; *sneha* — by affection; *kṛśā* — worn; *kṛśa* — wasted; *aṅgīm* — in body; *gaṅgā* — of the Ganga; *taṭe* — to the bank; *anyām* — another; *iva* — like; *tatra* — there; *gaṅgām* — Ganga; *nināya* — carried; *dhanyām* — blessed; *ati* — extremely; *duḥkha* — by grief; *dagdhā* — burnt.

**104.** Considering it to be ordained by the Lord, [Shachi,] worn by affection for her daughter-in-law and burnt by extreme grief, carried the blessed daughter-in-law, wasted in body, to the bank of the Ganga — as if [carrying] another Ganga there.

*Note.* As with Jagannatha Mishra (2.117), one who is about to leave the body is by custom carried to the bank of the Ganga.

### Verse 105

ततो विमाने दिवि राजमाने
प्रसूनवर्षैर्दिविषद्भिराप्तैः ।
पत्युः पदाब्जं हृदि गाढमेषा
ततः परिष्वज्य जहौ तनुं स्वाम् ॥१०५॥

*tato vimāne divi rājamāne*
*prasūna-varṣair diviṣadbhir āptaiḥ |*
*patyuḥ padābjaṁ hṛdi gāḍham eṣā*
*tataḥ pariṣvajya jahau tanuṁ svām ||105||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *vimāne* — [when] a celestial chariot; *divi* — in the sky; *rājamāne* — was shining; *prasūna* — of flowers; *varṣaiḥ* — with showers; *diviṣadbhiḥ* — [when] the dwellers of heaven; *āptaiḥ* — had arrived; *patyuḥ* — of her husband; *pada* — of the feet; *abjam* — the lotus; *hṛdi* — in her heart; *gāḍham* — tightly; *eṣā* — she; *tataḥ* — then; *pariṣvajya* — having embraced; *jahau* — left; *tanum* — body; *svām* — her own.

**105.** Then, when a celestial chariot shone in the sky and the dwellers of heaven had arrived with showers of flowers, she embraced tightly in her heart the lotus feet of her husband, and then left her body.

### Verse 106

ततोऽङ्कमारोप्य सुदुःखिता शची
वधूं विमुग्धा रुदती विलापिनी ।
जगाद कृच्छ्राद्वचसा गरीयसा
क्षोभेण शोकेन च गद्गदस्वरम् ॥१०६॥

*tato 'ṅkam āropya su-duḥkhitā śacī*
*vadhūṁ vimugdhā rudatī vilāpinī |*
*jagāda kṛcchrād vacasā garīyasā*
*kṣobheṇa śokena ca gadgada-svaram ||106||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *aṅkam* — onto her lap; *āropya* — having placed; *su* — extremely; *duḥkhitā* — unhappy; *śacī* — Shachi; *vadhūm* — the daughter-in-law; *vimugdhā* — bewildered; *rudatī* — weeping; *vilāpinī* — lamenting; *jagāda* — spoke; *kṛcchrāt* — with difficulty; *vacasā* — with words; *garīyasā* — with heavy; *kṣobheṇa* — from agitation; *śokena* — from sorrow; *ca* — and; *gadgada* — faltering; *svaram* — [in] a voice.

**106.** Then the most unhappy Shachi, bewildered, placed her daughter-in-law on her lap and, weeping and lamenting, spoke with difficulty in heavy words, her voice faltering from agitation and sorrow:

### Verse 107

गतः सुतो मे भवतीं समर्प्य
प्रियस्तवासौ मयि दुःखभाजि ।
हीना त्वया तस्य मुखं कथं वा
द्रक्ष्यामि दुःखैकनिवासभूमिः ॥१०७॥

*gataḥ suto me bhavatīṁ samarpya*
*priyas tavāsau mayi duḥkha-bhāji |*
*hīnā tvayā tasya mukhaṁ kathaṁ vā*
*drakṣyāmi duḥkhaika-nivāsa-bhūmiḥ ||107||*

*Word for word:* *gataḥ* — has gone; *sutaḥ* — son; *me* — my; *bhavatīm* — you; *samarpya* — having entrusted; *priyaḥ* — beloved; *tava* — your; *asau* — he; *mayi* — to me; *duḥkha* — sorrow; *bhāji* — to [one] who has; *hīnā* — deprived; *tvayā* — of you; *tasya* — his; *mukham* — face; *katham* — how; *vā* — then; *drakṣyāmi* — shall I see; *duḥkha* — of sorrow; *eka* — sole; *nivāsa* — of dwelling; *bhūmiḥ* — the place.

**107.** "My son, your beloved, went away having entrusted you to me, the sorrowful one. How, then, deprived of you, shall I see His face — I, now the dwelling-place of sorrow alone?"

### Verse 108

त्वया कृता प्रीतिरतीव गौरवं
निरन्तरं यत्र विशेषभक्त्या ।
कथं त्विदानीं परिदेवनान्वितो
विलोक्यते न क्षणमप्ययं जनः ॥१०८॥

*tvayā kṛtā prītir atīva gauravaṁ*
*nirantaraṁ yatra viśeṣa-bhaktyā |*
*kathaṁ tv idānīṁ paridevanānvito*
*vilokyate na kṣaṇam apy ayaṁ janaḥ ||108||*

*Word for word:* *tvayā* — by you; *kṛtā* — was shown; *prītiḥ* — love; *atīva* — great; *gauravam* — respect; *nirantaram* — constantly; *yatra* — to whom; *viśeṣa* — with special; *bhaktyā* — with devotion; *katham* — how; *tu* — then; *idānīm* — now; *paridevana* — with lamentation; *anvitaḥ* — overcome; *vilokyate* — is looked at; *na* — not; *kṣaṇam* — for a moment; *api* — even; *ayam* — this; *janaḥ* — person.

**108.** "You constantly showed love and great respect, with special devotion, to this person. How, then, is she now, overcome with lamentation, not looked at [by you] even for a moment?"

*Note.* *Ayaṁ janaḥ* ("this person") — Shachi speaks of herself, with humility.

### Verse 109

आहूतमात्रैव मया ददासि
प्रहर्षभीतिस्मितभक्तिलज्जम् ।
प्रत्युत्तरं हन्त कथं त्विदानीं
न भाषसे मां रुदतीं सशोकाम् ॥१०९॥

*āhūta-mātraiva mayā dadāsi*
*praharṣa-bhīti-smita-bhakti-lajjam |*
*pratyuttaraṁ hanta kathaṁ tv idānīṁ*
*na bhāṣase māṁ rudatīṁ sa-śokām ||109||*

*Word for word:* *āhūta* — called; *mātrā* — merely; *eva* — as soon as; *mayā* — by me; *dadāsi* — you would give; *praharṣa* — with joy; *bhīti* — with timidity; *smita* — with a smile; *bhakti* — with devotion; *lajjam* — with modesty [full of]; *pratyuttaram* — an answer; *hanta* — alas; *katham* — how; *tu* — then; *idānīm* — now; *na* — not; *bhāṣase* — you speak; *mām* — to me; *rudatīm* — weeping; *sa* — with; *śokām* — grief.

**109.** "As soon as I merely called you, you would give an answer full of joy, timidity, smiles, devotion and modesty. Alas, how is it, then, that now you do not speak to me as I weep in grief?"

### Verse 110

यद्वा मयि प्रीतिलवोऽपि नास्ति ते
बभूव दैवेन यदीदृशी गतिः ।
अमुं तव प्राणपतिं ममात्मजं
न वीक्ष्य किं वा व्रजसि प्रियंवदे ॥११०॥

*yad vā mayi prīti-lavo 'pi nāsti te*
*babhūva daivena yad īdṛśī gatiḥ |*
*amuṁ tava prāṇa-patiṁ mamātmajaṁ*
*na vīkṣya kiṁ vā vrajasi priyaṁvade ||110||*

*Word for word:* *yat vā* — or is it that; *mayi* — for me; *prīti* — of love; *lavaḥ* — a drop; *api* — even; *na asti* — there is not; *te* — in you; *babhūva* — has come about; *daivena* — by fate; *yat* — that; *īdṛśī* — such; *gatiḥ* — a fate; *amum* — him; *tava* — your; *prāṇa* — of life; *patim* — the lord; *mama* — my; *ātmajam* — son; *na* — not; *vīkṣya* — having seen; *kim vā* — can it be that; *vrajasi* — you go; *priyaṁvade* — O sweet-spoken one.

**110.** "Or is it that there is not even a drop of love for me in you, that by fate such a lot has befallen you? But can it be, O sweet-spoken one, that you are going without seeing Him — the lord of your life, my son?"

### Verse 111

असौ तव प्राणपतिः प्रियङ्करो
निरन्तरं प्रेमनवप्रकाशिनि ।
अमुं प्रति प्रीतिलवोऽपि नास्ति ते
किं मातरित्थं क्रियते यतस्त्वया ॥१११॥

*asau tava prāṇa-patiḥ priyaṅkaro*
*nirantaraṁ prema-nava-prakāśini |*
*amuṁ prati prīti-lavo 'pi nāsti te*
*kiṁ mātar itthaṁ kriyate yatas tvayā ||111||*

*Word for word:* *asau* — he; *tava* — your; *prāṇa* — of life; *patiḥ* — the lord; *priyaṅkaraḥ* — giving joy; *nirantaram* — always; *prema* — love; *nava* — new; *prakāśini* — O you who revealed; *amum* — him; *prati* — towards; *prīti* — of love; *lavaḥ* — a drop; *api* — even; *na asti* — there is not; *te* — in you; *kim* — is it that; *mātaḥ* — O mother (i.e. dear child); *ittham* — thus; *kriyate* — is done; *yataḥ* — since; *tvayā* — by you.

**111.** "He, the lord of your life, always gave you joy, O you who ever revealed new love [to Him]. Is it that there is not even a drop of love in you for Him, O dear child, since you act thus?"

*Note.* *Mātaḥ* ("O mother") is an affectionate Bengali form of address from an elder to a younger; cf. *pitaḥ* to a son (3.52).

### Verse 112

निरन्तरं या गमनाय पत्यु-
र्विचिन्तयन्ती त्वमुदश्रु सुभ्रु ।
विलोक्य मां साध्वसपूर्वमासीः
सलज्जमश्रूण्यपसारयन्ती ॥११२॥

*nirantaraṁ yā gamanāya patyur*
*vicintayantī tvam udaśru subhru |*
*vilokya māṁ sādhvasa-pūrvam āsīḥ*
*sa-lajjam aśrūṇy apasārayantī ||112||*

*Word for word:* *nirantaram* — incessantly; *yā* — who; *gamanāya* — about the return; *patyuḥ* — of your husband; *vicintayantī* — thinking; *tvam* — you; *udaśru* — in tears; *subhru* — O fair-browed one; *vilokya* — having seen; *mām* — me; *sādhvasa* — with timidity; *pūrvam* — accompanied by; *āsīḥ* — used to be; *sa* — with; *lajjam* — shame; *aśrūṇi* — tears; *apasārayantī* — wiping away.

**112.** "O fair-browed one, you who were always thinking of your husband's return and were in tears — on seeing me, you would timidly and bashfully wipe away your tears."

### Verse 113

या त्वं त्रपायै मयि साध्वसाय
स्वजीवितेशस्य वियोगदुःखम् ।
दत्त्वा बहिश्चेतसि तप्यमाना
लज्जावती प्रत्यहमेवमासीः ॥११३॥

*yā tvaṁ trapāyai mayi sādhvasāya*
*sva-jīviteśasya viyoga-duḥkham |*
*dattvā bahiś cetasi tapyamānā*
*lajjāvatī pratyaham evam āsīḥ ||113||*

*Word for word:* *yā* — who; *tvam* — you; *trapāyai* — to shyness; *mayi* — before me; *sādhvasāya* — to timidity; *sva* — of your own; *jīvita* — of life; *īśasya* — of the lord; *viyoga* — of separation; *duḥkham* — the grief; *dattvā* — having given over; *bahiḥ* — outwardly; *cetasi* — in the heart; *tapyamānā* — tormented; *lajjāvatī* — modest; *pratyaham* — every day; *evam* — thus; *āsīḥ* — lived.

**113.** "You, who gave over the grief of separation from the lord of your life to shyness and to timidity before me — modest outwardly, tormented in your heart — lived thus every day."

*Note.* (?) The syntax with the datives *trapāyai*, *sādhvasāya* is unusual. The sense: she hid her grief from her mother-in-law. The text is the same in Goswami's edition (GGM).

### Verse 114

सा त्वं तदीयास्यसुधामयूखं
तवैव चेतःकुमुदैककान्तम् ।
कठोरचित्ते तमवीक्ष्य साक्षात्
कथं कुतो वा व्रजसि प्रसह्य ॥११४॥

*sā tvaṁ tadīyāsya-sudhā-mayūkhaṁ*
*tavaiva cetaḥ-kumudaika-kāntam |*
*kaṭhora-citte tam avīkṣya sākṣāt*
*kathaṁ kuto vā vrajasi prasahya ||114||*

*Word for word:* *sā* — that one; *tvam* — you; *tadīya* — his; *āsya* — of the face; *sudhā* — of nectar; *mayūkham* — [the moon] with rays; *tava* — of your; *eva* — own; *cetaḥ* — of the heart; *kumuda* — of the night-lily; *eka* — the only; *kāntam* — beloved; *kaṭhora* — hard; *citte* — O you whose heart [is]; *tam* — him; *avīkṣya* — without seeing; *sākṣāt* — face to face; *katham* — how; *kutaḥ* — whither; *vā* — and; *vrajasi* — are you going; *prasahya* — forcibly (suddenly).

**114.** "O hard-hearted one, how can you, such as you were, go away so suddenly, and whither, without seeing face to face that nectar-rayed moon of His face — the only beloved of the night-lily of your own heart?"

*Note.* The night-lily (*kumuda*) opens only under the moon — a constant image of the loving heart. In the edition lines 2 and 3 are in reverse order; the order has been restored according to the metre.

### Verse 115

कथं महाक्रूरमते विहाय मां
स्वभावमृद्वी भवता वधूरियम् ।
अदंशि सर्प क्षणमप्यसौ दया
त्वामेव पस्पर्श न साम्प्रतं ननु ॥११५॥

*kathaṁ mahā-krūra-mate vihāya māṁ*
*svabhāva-mṛdvī bhavatā vadhūr iyam |*
*adaṁśi sarpa kṣaṇam apy asau dayā*
*tvām eva pasparśa na sāmprataṁ nanu ||115||*

*Word for word:* *katham* — how; *mahā* — most; *krūra* — cruel; *mate* — O you whose mind [is]; *vihāya* — having passed over; *mām* — me; *svabhāva* — by nature; *mṛdvī* — gentle; *bhavatā* — by you; *vadhūḥ* — daughter-in-law; *iyam* — this; *adaṁśi* — was bitten; *sarpa* — O serpent; *kṣaṇam* — for a moment; *api* — even; *asau* — that; *dayā* — pity; *tvām* — you; *eva* — even; *pasparśa* — touched; *na* — not; *sāmpratam* — fitting; *nanu* — surely.

**115.** "O serpent, most cruel of mind! How could you pass over me and bite this daughter-in-law, gentle by nature? Did pity not touch you even for a moment? Surely this was not fitting!"

*Note.* Shachi would rather the serpent had bitten her instead.

### Verse 116

यदङ्गमेतत्कुसुमैः सुदूयते
बाष्पोष्मणा चापि शिरीषकोमलम् ।
कथं नु वा तेऽसहतातिदुःसहं
विषाग्नितेजस्तदिदं हतास्मि तत् ॥११६॥

*yad aṅgam etat kusumaiḥ sudūyate*
*bāṣpoṣmaṇā cāpi śirīṣa-komalam |*
*kathaṁ nu vā te 'sahatāti-duḥsahaṁ*
*viṣāgni-tejas tad idaṁ hatāsmi tat ||116||*

*Word for word:* *yat* — which; *aṅgam* — body; *etat* — this; *kusumaiḥ* — by flowers; *sudūyate* — is hurt; *bāṣpa* — of breath; *ūṣmaṇā* — by the warmth; *ca api* — and even; *śirīṣa* — [like the flower of] the *śirīṣa*; *komalam* — tender; *katham* — how; *nu vā* — then; *te* — your; *asahata* — endured; *ati* — utterly; *duḥsaham* — unbearable; *viṣa* — of poison; *agni* — of the fire; *tejaḥ* — the heat; *tat* — that; *idam* — this; *hatā* — struck down; *asmi* — I am; *tat* — therefore.

**116.** "This body, tender as a *śirīṣa* flower, which was hurt even by flowers and by the warmth of breath — how, then, did it endure the utterly unbearable heat of the fire of your poison? I am struck down!"

*Note.* The *śirīṣa* (*Albizia lebbeck*) is a tree with the finest, downy flowers — the standard of tenderness in Sanskrit poetry.

### Verse 117

इत्थं सुदीना विलपन्त्यनुक्षणं
विलोचनद्वन्द्वजलेन भूयसा ।
चकार सा क्षालितमेव सन्ततं
स्नेहेन वध्वा वदनेन्दुमण्डलम् ॥११७॥

*itthaṁ su-dīnā vilapanty anukṣaṇaṁ*
*vilocana-dvandva-jalena bhūyasā |*
*cakāra sā kṣālitam eva santataṁ*
*snehena vadhvā vadanendu-maṇḍalam ||117||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *su* — utterly; *dīnā* — wretched; *vilapantī* — lamenting; *anukṣaṇam* — every moment; *vilocana* — of eyes; *dvandva* — of the pair; *jalena* — with the water; *bhūyasā* — with abundant; *cakāra* — made; *sā* — she; *kṣālitam* — bathed; *eva* — indeed; *santatam* — continually; *snehena* — with affection; *vadhvāḥ* — of the daughter-in-law; *vadana* — of the face; *indu* — of the moon; *maṇḍalam* — the disc.

**117.** Thus, utterly wretched, lamenting every moment, she continually bathed with affection the moon-disc of her daughter-in-law's face in the abundant water of her two eyes.

### Verse 118

समाप्य कृच्छ्रेण चितोचिताः क्रियाः
गृहं ययौ रोदनमेव कुर्वती ।
कथं वधूशून्यमवेक्ष्यते गृहं
तनूजरत्नश्च तथेति दुःखिता ॥११८॥

*samāpya kṛcchreṇa citocitāḥ kriyāḥ*
*gṛhaṁ yayau rodanam eva kurvatī |*
*kathaṁ vadhū-śūnyam avekṣyate gṛhaṁ*
*tanūja-ratnaś ca tatheti duḥkhitā ||118||*

*Word for word:* *samāpya* — having completed; *kṛcchreṇa* — with difficulty; *cita* — to the pyre; *ucitāḥ* — befitting; *kriyāḥ* — the rites; *gṛham* — home; *yayau* — went; *rodanam* — weeping; *eva* — only; *kurvatī* — doing; *katham* — how; *vadhū* — of the daughter-in-law; *śūnyam* — empty; *avekṣyate* — will look upon; *gṛham* — the house; *tanūja* — son; *ratnaḥ* — [my] jewel of a; *ca* — and; *tathā* — so; *iti* — thus [thinking]; *duḥkhitā* — grieving.

**118.** Having completed with difficulty the rites befitting the pyre, she went home, doing nothing but weep. "How will my jewel of a son look upon the house thus empty of His wife?" — so she grieved.

### Verse 119

अथागतो गौरसुधामयूखः
कियद्दिनान्तरमेव गेहे ।
निस्तार्य्य तत्रत्यजनानजस्रं
स्वमातृदुःखान्यपहर्त्तुकामः ॥११९॥

*athāgato gaura-sudhā-mayūkhaḥ*
*kiyad-dinān-taram eva gehe |*
*nistārya tatratya-janān ajasraṁ*
*sva-mātṛ-duḥkhāny apahartu-kāmaḥ ||119||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *āgataḥ* — returned; *gaura* — the golden; *sudhā* — of nectar; *mayūkhaḥ* — [moon] with rays; *kiyat* — some; *dina* — days; *antaram* — after; *eva* — just; *gehe* — home; *nistārya* — having delivered; *tatratya* — of that place; *janān* — the people; *ajasram* — tirelessly; *sva* — of His own; *mātṛ* — of the mother; *duḥkhāni* — the sorrows; *apahartu* — to remove; *kāmaḥ* — desiring.

**119.** Then, just a few days later, the golden moon with nectar rays returned home. Having tirelessly delivered the people of that land, He now desired to remove His own mother's sorrows.

### Verse 120

विलोक्य हर्षं न तथाविधं सा
सुतं चिरं प्रोषितमप्यगच्छत् ।
वधूवियोगेन सुदुःसहेन
तदा यदाधिक्यमनेन भेजे ॥१२०॥

*vilokya harṣaṁ na tathā-vidhaṁ sā*
*sutaṁ ciraṁ proṣitam apy agacchat |*
*vadhū-viyogena su-duḥsahena*
*tadā yad ādhikyam anena bheje ||120||*

*Word for word:* *vilokya* — having seen; *harṣam* — joy; *na* — not; *tathāvidham* — such; *sā* — she; *sutam* — son; *ciram* — long; *proṣitam* — absent; *api* — though; *agacchat* — attained; *vadhū* — from the daughter-in-law; *viyogena* — by the separation; *su* — extremely; *duḥsahena* — by unbearable; *tadā* — then; *yat* — because; *ādhikyam* — intensification; *anena* — through Him; *bheje* — obtained.

**120.** Though she saw her son, so long absent, she did not feel such joy [as before]; for the most unbearable separation from her daughter-in-law then grew more intense through Him.

### Verse 121

विधाय भूयो भुवि दण्डवन्नतिं
रजः समादाय पदद्वयस्य ।
तथाविधां तामवलोक्य दुःखितां
प्रपच्छ नाथो मनसा विदन्नपि ॥१२१॥

*vidhāya bhūyo bhuvi daṇḍavan-natiṁ*
*rajaḥ samādāya pada-dvayasya |*
*tathā-vidhāṁ tām avalokya duḥkhitāṁ*
*papraccha nātho manasā vidann api ||121||*

*Word for word:* *vidhāya* — having made; *bhūyaḥ* — again and again; *bhuvi* — on the ground; *daṇḍavat* — like a stick; *natim* — obeisance; *rajaḥ* — the dust; *samādāya* — having taken; *pada* — of the feet; *dvayasya* — of the pair; *tathāvidhām* — in such a state; *tām* — her; *avalokya* — seeing; *duḥkhitām* — grieved; *papraccha* — asked; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *manasā* — in mind; *vidan* — knowing; *api* — although.

**121.** Again and again He made obeisance on the ground like a stick and took the dust of her two feet; and seeing her so grieved, the Lord questioned her, although in His mind He knew.

*Note.* *Daṇḍavat*, "like a stick": the full obeisance, in which one lies stretched full length on the ground. To take the dust from the feet of elders is a sign of respect.

### Verse 122

स्वकीयवाणीसुधयावगाहय-
न्नयं जनन्याः सकलां तनूं ततः ।
जगाद मातर्मलिनेव लक्ष्यसे
कथं त्वमेवं ननु कथ्यतामिति ॥१२२॥

*svakīya-vāṇī-sudhayāvagāhayann*
*ayaṁ jananyāḥ sakalāṁ tanūṁ tataḥ |*
*jagāda mātar malineva lakṣyase*
*kathaṁ tvam evaṁ nanu kathyatām iti ||122||*

*Word for word:* *svakīya* — of His own; *vāṇī* — of speech; *sudhayā* — with the nectar; *avagāhayan* — bathing; *ayam* — He; *jananyāḥ* — of the mother; *sakalām* — the whole; *tanūm* — body; *tataḥ* — then; *jagāda* — said; *mātaḥ* — O Mother; *malinā* — dimmed; *iva* — as if; *lakṣyase* — you appear; *katham* — why; *tvam* — you; *evam* — thus; *nanu* — pray; *kathyatām* — let it be told; *iti* — thus.

**122.** Then, bathing His mother's whole body in the nectar of His own speech, He said: "Mother, you seem as if dimmed. Why are you so? Pray, tell Me."

### Verse 123

इत्थं समस्तं बुबुधे महाप्रभु-
स्तदप्यनुक्तं सहसा हसन्मुहुः ।
तदीयनेत्रद्वयनिर्भरोद्गतैः
पयोभिराख्यातमिव साक्षात् ॥१२३॥

*itthaṁ samastaṁ bubudhe mahāprabhus*
*tad apy anuktaṁ sahasā hasan muhuḥ |*
*tadīya-netra-dvaya-nirbharodgataiḥ*
*payobhir ākhyātam iva sākṣāt ||123||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *samastam* — everything; *bubudhe* — understood; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *tat* — that; *api* — although; *anuktam* — unspoken; *sahasā* — at once; *hasan* — smiling; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *tadīya* — her; *netra* — of eyes; *dvaya* — of the pair; *nirbhara* — abundantly; *udgataiḥ* — welling up; *payobhiḥ* — by the waters; *ākhyātam* — told; *iva* — as if; *sākṣāt* — plainly.

**123.** Thus Mahaprabhu, smiling again and again, understood everything at once, though it was left unspoken: it was as if the waters welling up abundantly from her two eyes had told it plainly.

*Note.* Mahaprabhu's smile here is not indifference but knowledge: for Him Lakshmipriya's departure is no loss (vv. 124–125). (?) In the edition the last pada is a syllable short of the metre; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *ākhyānitam eva*, which also does not give the full metre.

### Verse 124

वधूस्तवासौ परलोकमागता
मातस्तदत्रास्ति महद्धि कारणम् ।
इयं कदाचिन्नहि मानुषी भवेत्
कस्यापि हेतोः पृथिवीं समागता ॥१२४॥

*vadhūs tavāsau para-lokam āgatā*
*mātas tad atrāsti mahad dhi kāraṇam |*
*iyaṁ kadācin nahi mānuṣī bhavet*
*kasyāpi hetoḥ pṛthivīṁ samāgatā ||124||*

*Word for word:* *vadhūḥ* — daughter-in-law; *tava* — your; *asau* — she; *para* — the other; *lokam* — world; *āgatā* — gone to; *mātaḥ* — O Mother; *tat* — of that; *atra* — in this; *asti* — there is; *mahat* — a great; *hi* — indeed; *kāraṇam* — cause; *iyam* — she; *kadācit* — ever; *na hi* — by no means; *mānuṣī* — a human being; *bhavet* — could be; *kasya api* — of some; *hetoḥ* — for the sake of a purpose; *pṛthivīm* — to the earth; *samāgatā* — came.

**124.** "Mother, this daughter-in-law of yours has gone to the other world, and there is indeed a great cause for it. She could never have been a mere human being: she came to the earth for some purpose."

*Note.* The edition has *mānuṣo* (masculine); the sense requires *mānuṣī*.

### Verse 125

अहं हि जानामि तदेतदस्या
यं कारणं भूमिमुपागतायाः ।
तथागतायाश्च समस्तमेव
तत्त्यज्यतां मातरिह प्रमोहः ॥१२५॥

*ahaṁ hi jānāmi tad etad asyā*
*yaṁ kāraṇaṁ bhūmim upāgatāyāḥ |*
*tathā-gatāyāś ca samastam eva*
*tat tyajyatāṁ mātar iha pramohaḥ ||125||*

*Word for word:* *aham* — I; *hi* — indeed; *jānāmi* — know; *tat* — that; *etat* — this; *asyāḥ* — of her; *yam* — which; *kāraṇam* — cause; *bhūmim* — to the earth; *upāgatāyāḥ* — [of her] who came; *tathā* — thus; *gatāyāḥ* — [of her] who departed; *ca* — and; *samastam* — all; *eva* — indeed; *tat* — therefore; *tyajyatām* — let it be given up; *mātaḥ* — O Mother; *iha* — in this; *pramohaḥ* — bewilderment.

**125.** "I indeed know all of it — the cause for which she came to the earth and [for which] she departed thus. Therefore, Mother, give up your bewilderment in this matter."

### Verse 126

इत्थं निशम्याशु वचः सुतस्य
शची ययौ निर्वृतिमुत्तमां सा ।
ननन्द पुत्रेण समं तथान्यैः
स्वबन्धुभिः स्वैर्विभवैः शचीव ॥१२६॥

*itthaṁ niśamyāśu vacaḥ sutasya*
*śacī yayau nirvṛtim uttamāṁ sā |*
*nananda putreṇa samaṁ tathānyaiḥ*
*sva-bandhubhiḥ svair vibhavaiḥ śacīva ||126||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *niśamya* — having heard; *āśu* — quickly; *vacaḥ* — the words; *sutasya* — of the son; *śacī* — Shachi; *yayau* — attained; *nirvṛtim* — peace; *uttamām* — supreme; *sā* — she; *nananda* — rejoiced; *putreṇa* — with the son; *samam* — together; *tathā* — likewise; *anyaiḥ* — with other; *sva* — her own; *bandhubhiḥ* — with kinsfolk; *svaiḥ* — with her own; *vibhavaiḥ* — with riches; *śacī* — Shachi [the consort of Indra]; *iva* — like.

**126.** Having thus heard her son's words, Shachi quickly attained supreme peace. Together with her son, and likewise with her other kinsfolk and her own riches, she rejoiced like Shachi, the consort of Indra.

*Note.* A play on the name: Shachi, the Lord's mother, and Shachi, the wife of Indra, the queen of heaven.

### Verse 127

ततोऽतिवेलं मनसा विचिन्त्य
तनूजरत्नस्य विवाहकार्य्यम् ।
समानयामास तदैव काशी-
नाथं द्विजश्रेष्ठमदीनसत्त्वा ॥१२७॥

*tato 'tivelaṁ manasā vicintya*
*tanūja-ratnasya vivāha-kāryam |*
*samānayāmāsa tadaiva kāśī-*
*nāthaṁ dvija-śreṣṭham adīna-sattvā ||127||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *ativelam* — at length; *manasā* — in mind; *vicintya* — having pondered; *tanūja* — of the son; *ratnasya* — of the jewel; *vivāha* — of the marriage; *kāryam* — the matter; *samānayāmāsa* — summoned; *tadā eva* — at once; *kāśīnātham* — Kashinatha; *dvija* — of brahmanas; *śreṣṭham* — the best; *adīna* — undaunted; *sattvā* — [she] of spirit.

**127.** Then, having long pondered in her mind the matter of the marriage of her jewel of a son, she, undaunted in spirit, at once summoned Kashinatha, the best of brahmanas.

*Note.* Kashinatha (Kashinatha Pandita) is the brahmana go-between at Mahaprabhu's second marriage, to Vishnupriya (Chaitanya-bhagavata, Adi 15, "The marriage to Vishnupriya").

### Verse 128

आनीय तं क्षिप्रमुवाच विप्रं
तदात्मजोद्वाहविधिं विवित्सुः ।
समुच्यतां मत्तनुजाय कन्यां
सनातनो विप्रवरः प्रदातुम् ॥१२८॥

*ānīya taṁ kṣipram uvāca vipraṁ*
*tad-ātmajodvāha-vidhiṁ vivitsuḥ |*
