*samucyatāṁ mat-tanujāya kanyāṁ*
*sanātano vipra-varaḥ pradātum ||128||*

*Word for word:* *ānīya* — having brought; *tam* — that; *kṣipram* — quickly; *uvāca* — said; *vipram* — to the brahmana; *tat* — her; *ātmaja* — of the son; *udvāha* — of the marriage; *vidhim* — the arrangement; *vivitsuḥ* — wishing to find (?); *samucyatām* — let it be told; *mat* — to my; *tanujāya* — to son; *kanyām* — daughter; *sanātanaḥ* — Sanatana; *vipra* — of brahmanas; *varaḥ* — the best; *pradātum* — to give.

**128.** Having brought the brahmana, she, wishing to find a way to arrange her son's marriage, quickly said to him: "Let Sanatana, the best of brahmanas, be asked to give his daughter to my son."

*Note.* Sanatana Mishra is the raja-pandita of Navadvipa, the father of Vishnupriya (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 16). (?) *Vivitsuḥ* (desiderative of *vid*, "to find": "wishing to find") is masculine, though the subject is Shachi — an irregularity of the edition. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 129

इत्थं निशम्यैव वचांसि विप्रः
क्षिप्रं प्रमोदेन सनातनाय ।
न्यवेदयन्माङ्गलिकं विधित्सु-
र्वैवाहिकं तत्सकलं विधिज्ञः ॥१२९॥

*itthaṁ niśamyaiva vacāṁsi vipraḥ*
*kṣipraṁ pramodena sanātanāya |*
*nyavedayan māṅgalikaṁ vidhitsur*
*vaivāhikaṁ tat sakalaṁ vidhi-jñaḥ ||129||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *niśamya* — having heard; *eva* — just; *vacāṁsi* — the words; *vipraḥ* — the brahmana; *kṣipram* — quickly; *pramodena* — with joy; *sanātanāya* — to Sanatana; *nyavedayat* — conveyed; *māṅgalikam* — auspicious; *vidhitsuḥ* — wishing to arrange; *vaivāhikam* — concerning the wedding; *tat* — that; *sakalam* — all; *vidhi* — the rules; *jñaḥ* — knowing.

**129.** As soon as he had heard these words, the brahmana, who knew the rules, wishing to arrange [the match], quickly and joyfully conveyed to Sanatana all that auspicious matter of the wedding.

### Verse 130

तदा तदाकर्ण्य वचो विमृश्य
स्वैर्बन्धुभिः कार्य्यमवश्यमेतत् ।
इत्थं विचिन्त्याथ जगाद हृष्टो
निर्णीयतां काल इदं विधेयम् ॥१३०॥

*tadā tad ākarṇya vaco vimṛśya*
*svair bandhubhiḥ kāryam avaśyam etat |*
*itthaṁ vicintyātha jagāda hṛṣṭo*
*nirṇīyatāṁ kāla idaṁ vidheyam ||130||*

*Word for word:* *tadā* — then; *tat* — that; *ākarṇya* — having heard; *vacaḥ* — word; *vimṛśya* — having deliberated; *svaiḥ* — with his own; *bandhubhiḥ* — kinsmen; *kāryam* — to be done; *avaśyam* — certainly; *etat* — this; *ittham* — thus; *vicintya* — having reflected; *atha* — then; *jagāda* — said; *hṛṣṭaḥ* — joyful; *nirṇīyatām* — let it be fixed; *kālaḥ* — the time; *idam* — this; *vidheyam* — is to be done.

**130.** Then, having heard those words and deliberated with his kinsmen, [Sanatana] reflected thus: "This must certainly be done." And then he joyfully said: "Let the time be fixed; this is to be done."

### Verse 131

निशम्य सर्व्वं वचनं स विप्रः
सुखेन शीघ्रं समुपेत्य शच्यै ।
न्यवेदयत्तत्परिकर्ण्य साऽपि
तुतोष सानन्दममन्दभाग्या ॥१३१॥

*niśamya sarvaṁ vacanaṁ sa vipraḥ*
*sukhena śīghraṁ samupetya śacyai |*
*nyavedayat tat parikarṇya sāpi*
*tutoṣa sānandam amanda-bhāgyā ||131||*

*Word for word:* *niśamya* — having heard; *sarvam* — all; *vacanam* — the word; *saḥ* — that; *vipraḥ* — brahmana; *sukhena* — joyfully; *śīghram* — swiftly; *samupetya* — having come; *śacyai* — to Shachi; *nyavedayat* — reported; *tat* — that; *parikarṇya* — having heard; *sā* — she; *api* — too; *tutoṣa* — was delighted; *sa-ānandam* — with bliss; *amanda* — not small; *bhāgyā* — [she whose] fortune [was].

**131.** Having heard all that was said, the brahmana joyfully and swiftly went to Shachi and reported it to her. Hearing it, she too, whose good fortune was by no means small, was delighted and filled with bliss.

### Verse 132

सनातनेन प्रहितोऽथ कश्चित्
समेत्य तां तत्र जगाद नत्वा ।
गुणेन रूपेण वरां वराङ्गीं
स याचते ते तनयाय दातुम् ॥१३२॥

*sanātanena prahito 'tha kaścit*
*sametya tāṁ tatra jagāda natvā |*
*guṇena rūpeṇa varāṁ varāṅgīṁ*
*sa yācate te tanayāya dātum ||132||*

*Word for word:* *sanātanena* — by Sanatana; *prahitaḥ* — sent; *atha* — then; *kaścit* — someone; *sametya* — having come; *tām* — to her; *tatra* — there; *jagāda* — said; *natvā* — having bowed; *guṇena* — in virtue; *rūpeṇa* — in beauty; *varām* — excellent; *varāṅgīm* — lovely of form; *saḥ* — he; *yācate* — begs; *te* — your; *tanayāya* — to son; *dātum* — to give.

**132.** Then a messenger sent by Sanatana came to her there, bowed and said: "He begs [leave] to give to your son [his daughter], lovely of form and excellent in virtue and beauty."

### Verse 133

विष्णुप्रियां प्राप्य तवात्मजः प्रियां
यथार्थसंज्ञामिव तां करोतु सः ।
वृत्ते विवाहे भवतां सुनिर्वृता-
वुमामहेशाविव तौ परस्परम् ॥१३३॥

*viṣṇupriyāṁ prāpya tavātmajaḥ priyāṁ*
*yathārtha-saṁjñām iva tāṁ karotu saḥ |*
*vṛtte vivāhe bhavatāṁ su-nirvṛtāv*
*umā-maheśāv iva tau parasparam ||133||*

*Word for word:* *viṣṇupriyām* — Vishnupriya; *prāpya* — having obtained; *tava* — your; *ātmajaḥ* — son; *priyām* — dear; *yathārtha* — true to its meaning; *saṁjñām* — [her] with a name; *iva* — as it were; *tām* — her; *karotu* — let him make; *saḥ* — he; *vṛtte* — [when] has taken place; *vivāhe* — the wedding; *bhavatām* — may [the two] be; *su* — perfectly; *nirvṛtau* — happy; *umā* — Uma; *maheśau* — and Mahesha; *iva* — like; *tau* — the two; *parasparam* — with each other.

**133.** "Having obtained the dear Vishnupriya, let your son make her, as it were, one whose name is true to its meaning. When the wedding has taken place, may the two be perfectly happy with each other, like Uma and Mahesha."

*Note.* *Viṣṇu-priyā* means "beloved of Vishnu": by becoming the wife of Gauranga (Vishnu), she will make her name come true. Uma and Mahesha are Parvati and Shiva, the model of conjugal happiness.

### Verse 134

गत्वा स सर्व्वं द्विजपुङ्गवाय
न्यवेदयत्तत्कथितं समस्तम् ।
सत्पण्डितः सोऽपि सनातनस्तैः
सनातनैर्हर्षभरैरुदासे ॥१३४॥

*gatvā sa sarvaṁ dvija-puṅgavāya*
*nyavedayat tat kathitaṁ samastam |*
*sat-paṇḍitaḥ so 'pi sanātanas taiḥ*
*sanātanair harṣa-bharair udāse ||134||*

*Word for word:* *gatvā* — having gone [back]; *saḥ* — he; *sarvam* — everything; *dvija* — of brahmanas; *puṅgavāya* — to the foremost; *nyavedayat* — reported; *tat* — that; *kathitam* — said; *samastam* — all; *sat* — the worthy; *paṇḍitaḥ* — pandita; *saḥ* — he; *api* — too; *sanātanaḥ* — Sanatana; *taiḥ* — with those; *sanātanaiḥ* — everlasting; *harṣa* — of joy; *bharaiḥ* — with floods; *udāse* — (?) rejoiced.

**134.** Having gone back, he reported to that foremost of brahmanas all that had been said. And the worthy pandita Sanatana too (?) rejoiced with those everlasting — "sanatana" — floods of joy.

*Note.* A play on words: *Sanātana* (the name) and *sanātana*, "eternal, everlasting". (?) *Udāse* is the reading of the edition; the sense "rejoiced greatly" is conjectural (the verb *ud-ās* usually means "to sit up" or "to remain indifferent", which does not fit; the text is perhaps corrupt). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 135

द्रव्याणि भद्राणि स शुद्धकीर्त्तिः
समाहरत्कौतुकलोलचेताः ।
निर्णीय कालं तरसाधिवासं
विधातुकामो मुमुदे सुतायाः ॥१३५॥

*dravyāṇi bhadrāṇi sa śuddha-kīrtiḥ*
*samāharat kautuka-lola-cetāḥ |*
*nirṇīya kālaṁ tarasādhivāsaṁ*
*vidhātu-kāmo mumude sutāyāḥ ||135||*

*Word for word:* *dravyāṇi* — provisions; *bhadrāṇi* — auspicious; *saḥ* — he; *śuddha* — of pure; *kīrtiḥ* — [he] of fame; *samāharat* — gathered; *kautuka* — with eagerness; *lola* — trembling; *cetāḥ* — [with] a heart; *nirṇīya* — having fixed; *kālam* — the time; *tarasā* — speedily; *adhivāsam* — the adhivasa; *vidhātu* — to perform; *kāmaḥ* — wishing; *mumude* — rejoiced; *sutāyāḥ* — of the daughter.

**135.** He of spotless fame, his heart trembling with eagerness, gathered auspicious provisions; and having fixed the time, wishing speedily to perform his daughter's adhivasa, he rejoiced.

### Verse 136

शुभेन लग्नेन विभूषिते ततः
प्रकाशमाने समये समन्ततः ।
शुभाधिवासं विदधे महामति-
र्महाधियामाप्तफला मनोरथाः ॥१३६॥

*śubhena lagnena vibhūṣite tataḥ*
*prakāśamāne samaye samantataḥ |*
*śubhādhivāsaṁ vidadhe mahāmatir*
*mahā-dhiyām āpta-phalā manorathāḥ ||136||*

*Word for word:* *śubhena* — with an auspicious; *lagnena* — ascendant; *vibhūṣite* — adorned; *tataḥ* — then; *prakāśamāne* — shining; *samaye* — at the time; *samantataḥ* — on every side; *śubha* — the auspicious; *adhivāsam* — adhivasa; *vidadhe* — performed; *mahā* — of great; *matiḥ* — [he] of mind; *mahā* — of the great; *dhiyām* — of minds; *āpta* — having obtained; *phalāḥ* — fruit; *manorathāḥ* — desires.

**136.** Then, at the [appointed] time, adorned with an auspicious ascendant and shining on every side, the high-minded [Sanatana] performed the auspicious adhivasa: the desires of the great-minded attain their fruit.

### Verse 137

ततो ददौ भूसुरपुङ्गवेभ्य-
स्ताम्बूलमाल्यानि सचन्दनानि ।
संप्रेषितैस्तैरपि कारयित्वा
जामातुरग्रे मुदितोऽधिवासम् ॥१३७॥

*tato dadau bhūsura-puṅgavebhyas*
*tāmbūla-mālyāni sa-candanāni |*
*sampreṣitais tair api kārayitvā*
*jāmātur agre mudito 'dhivāsam ||137||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *dadau* — gave; *bhūsura* — to the brahmanas; *puṅgavebhyaḥ* — to the foremost; *tāmbūla* — betel; *mālyāni* — garlands; *sa* — with; *candanāni* — sandal; *sampreṣitaiḥ* — sent; *taiḥ* — by them; *api* — also; *kārayitvā* — having had performed; *jāmātuḥ* — of the son-in-law; *agre* — before; *muditaḥ* — joyful; *adhivāsam* — the adhivasa.

**137.** Then he gave betel, garlands and sandal to the foremost brahmanas; and, joyful, he had them, sent [by him], perform the adhivasa before the son-in-law.

*Note.* *Jāmātur agre* can mean both "in the presence of the son-in-law" (the brahmanas sent by the bride's father perform the adhivasa at the bridegroom's house) and "first of all, the son-in-law's adhivasa".

### Verse 138

अथ प्रभाते प्रभुराह्निकीं क्रियां
स्नात्वा चकार द्युनदीपयःसु सः ।
कियद्विलम्बेन च तं महीसुरा
हर्षादलंचक्रुरलं प्रसाधनैः ॥१३८॥

*atha prabhāte prabhur āhnikīṁ kriyāṁ*
*snātvā cakāra dyunadī-payaḥsu saḥ |*
*kiyad-vilambena ca taṁ mahīsurā*
*harṣād alaṁcakrur alaṁ prasādhanaiḥ ||138||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *prabhāte* — at daybreak; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *āhnikīm* — daily; *kriyām* — rite; *snātvā* — having bathed; *cakāra* — performed; *dyunadī* — of the heavenly river; *payaḥsu* — in the waters; *saḥ* — He; *kiyat* — a little; *vilambena* — after a delay; *ca* — and; *tam* — Him; *mahīsurāḥ* — the brahmanas; *harṣāt* — joyfully; *alaṁcakruḥ* — adorned; *alam* — amply; *prasādhanaiḥ* — with finery.

**138.** Then at daybreak the Lord bathed in the waters of the heavenly river and performed His daily rites; and after a little while the brahmanas joyfully adorned Him amply with finery.

*Note.* The heavenly river is the Ganga. A play of sounds: *alaṁcakrur alam*.

### Verse 139

ऊचुश्च साधो विजयस्व साधु
साधुर्विवाहस्य बभूव कालः ।
इत्थं निशम्यारचयत्कृपालु-
र्यात्रां समारुह्य मनोज्ञदोलाम् ॥१३९॥

*ūcuś ca sādho vijayasva sādhu*
*sādhur vivāhasya babhūva kālaḥ |*
*itthaṁ niśamyāracayat kṛpālur*
*yātrāṁ samāruhya manojña-dolām ||139||*

*Word for word:* *ūcuḥ* — said; *ca* — and; *sādho* — O virtuous One; *vijayasva* — be victorious; *sādhu* — well; *sādhuḥ* — auspicious; *vivāhasya* — of the wedding; *babhūva* — has come; *kālaḥ* — the time; *ittham* — thus; *niśamya* — having heard; *aracayat* — made; *kṛpāluḥ* — the merciful one; *yātrām* — the procession; *samāruhya* — having mounted; *manojña* — a charming; *dolām* — palanquin.

**139.** And they said: "O virtuous One, may You be victorious! It is well: the auspicious time for the wedding has come." Hearing this, the merciful Lord mounted a charming palanquin and set out in procession.

### Verse 140

सन्तप्तचामीकरगौरदेहो
दोलामुपेतः शरदभ्रशुभ्राम् ।
दुग्धाम्बुराशेरुपरि प्ररूढं
शृङ्गं सुमेरोः स जिगाय सद्यः ॥१४०॥

*santapta-cāmīkara-gaura-deho*
*dolām upetaḥ śarad-abhra-śubhrām |*
*dugdhāmbu-rāśer upari prarūḍhaṁ*
*śṛṅgaṁ sumeroḥ sa jigāya sadyaḥ ||140||*

*Word for word:* *santapta* — of heated; *cāmīkara* — gold; *gaura* — golden; *dehaḥ* — [He whose] body [was]; *dolām* — the palanquin; *upetaḥ* — having taken; *śarat* — of autumn; *abhra* — [like] a cloud; *śubhrām* — white; *dugdha* — of milk; *amburāśeḥ* — of the ocean; *upari* — above; *prarūḍham* — risen; *śṛṅgam* — the peak; *sumeroḥ* — of Sumeru; *saḥ* — He; *jigāya* — surpassed; *sadyaḥ* — at once.

**140.** His body golden as molten gold, seated in a palanquin white as an autumn cloud, He at once surpassed the peak of Sumeru rising above the Milk Ocean.

*Note.* The image: Gauranga's golden body in the white palanquin is like the golden mountain Sumeru above the white Milk Ocean.

### Verse 141

जामातरं वीक्ष्य समीपमागतं
प्रोद्गम्य हर्षेण तनूरुहैः समम् ।
पाद्यासनाद्यैर्वरयाम्बभूव
क्षणेन कन्याञ्च ददौ स कूकुदः ॥१४१॥

*jāmātaraṁ vīkṣya samīpam āgataṁ*
*prodgamya harṣeṇa tanūruhaiḥ samam |*
*pādyāsanādyair varayāmbabhūva*
*kṣaṇena kanyāñ ca dadau sa kūkudaḥ ||141||*

*Word for word:* *jāmātaram* — the son-in-law; *vīkṣya* — seeing; *samīpam* — near; *āgatam* — arrived; *prodgamya* — having risen to meet; *harṣeṇa* — with joy; *tanūruhaiḥ* — with the hairs of the body; *samam* — together; *pādya* — with water for the feet; *āsana* — with a seat; *ādyaiḥ* — and the rest; *varayāmbabhūva* — chose [as bridegroom]; *kṣaṇena* — in a moment; *kanyām* — the daughter; *ca* — and; *dadau* — gave; *saḥ* — he; *kūkudaḥ* — the giver of the daughter.

**141.** Seeing the son-in-law arrive near, he joyfully rose to meet Him — and the hairs of his body rose together with him; with water for the feet, a seat and the rest he performed the choosing of the bridegroom, and in a moment the giver of the bride gave away his daughter.

*Note.* *Prodgamya* is a play on words: Sanatana "rose" to meet the bridegroom, and his hairs "rose" from joy. The choosing of the bridegroom is the *varaṇa*. *Kūkuda* is a rare word: "one who gives an adorned daughter in marriage".

### Verse 142

द्विजस्त्रियः स्वस्तिकधूपदीपै-
रमुष्य निर्मञ्छनमादरेण ।
चक्रुः समानीय ततः स कन्यां
प्रादाद्द्विजस्तस्य पदाम्बुजेभ्यः ॥१४२॥

*dvija-striyaḥ svastika-dhūpa-dīpair*
*amuṣya nirmañchanam ādareṇa |*
*cakruḥ samānīya tataḥ sa kanyāṁ*
*prādād dvijas tasya padāmbujebhyaḥ ||142||*

*Word for word:* *dvija* — of the brahmanas; *striyaḥ* — the wives; *svastika* — with svastika signs; *dhūpa* — with incense; *dīpaiḥ* — with lamps; *amuṣya* — for Him; *nirmañchanam* — the rite of protection; *ādareṇa* — with reverence; *cakruḥ* — performed; *samānīya* — having brought; *tataḥ* — then; *saḥ* — that; *kanyām* — daughter; *prādāt* — gave; *dvijaḥ* — brahmana; *tasya* — His; *pada* — of the feet; *ambujebhyaḥ* — to the lotuses.

**142.** The wives of the brahmanas reverently performed for Him the rite of protection with svastika signs, incense and lamps; then the brahmana brought his daughter and gave her to His lotus feet.

*Note.* *Nirmañchana* is the rite in which lamps and incense are waved around the bridegroom to ward off the evil eye.

### Verse 143

उन्मीलत्पटुपटहप्रकृष्टढक्का-
निस्वानैः स्फुटरटितैश्च मर्द्दलानाम् ।
श्रीमद्भिर्जयनिनदैः प्रसूनवृष्ट्या
रेजाते स्मितसुमुखौ परस्परं तौ ॥१४३॥

*unmīlat-paṭu-paṭaha-prakṛṣṭa-ḍhakkā-*
*nisvānaiḥ sphuṭa-raṭitaiś ca mardalānām |*
*śrīmadbhir jaya-ninadaiḥ prasūna-vṛṣṭyā*
*rejāte smita-sumukhau parasparaṁ tau ||143||*

*Word for word:* *unmīlat* — breaking forth; *paṭu* — of clear-toned; *paṭaha* — of pataha drums; *prakṛṣṭa* — of mighty; *ḍhakkā* — of dhakka drums; *nisvānaiḥ* — with the roar; *sphuṭa* — with distinct; *raṭitaiḥ* — with the beating; *ca* — and; *mardalānām* — of mardalas; *śrīmadbhiḥ* — with splendid; *jaya* — of "Jaya!"; *ninadaiḥ* — with cries; *prasūna* — of flowers; *vṛṣṭyā* — with a rain; *rejāte* — shone; *smita* — smiling; *sumukhau* — [both] with lovely faces; *parasparam* — at each other; *tau* — the two.

**143.** Amid the roar, breaking forth, of clear-toned pataha drums and mighty dhakkas, the distinct beating of the mardalas, splendid cries of "Jaya!" and a rain of flowers, the two shone, smiling at each other with lovely faces.

*Note.* The metre changes to *praharṣiṇī* (13 syllables) for the closing verses of the sarga. Pataha, dhakka and mardala are kinds of Bengali drums.

### Verse 144

इत्येवं गृहमनयद्वधूं महद्भि-
र्वादित्रध्वनिसहितैर्जयध्वनैश्च ।
सा हृष्टा सपदि निवेशयाञ्चकार
स्त्रीरत्नं मुदितमनाः शची स्वगेहम् ॥१४४॥

*ity evaṁ gṛham anayad vadhūṁ mahadbhir*
*vāditra-dhvani-sahitair jaya-dhvanaiś ca |*
*sā hṛṣṭā sapadi niveśayāñcakāra*
*strī-ratnaṁ mudita-manāḥ śacī sva-geham ||144||*

*Word for word:* *iti evam* — thus; *gṛham* — home; *anayat* — brought; *vadhūm* — the bride; *mahadbhiḥ* — loud; *vāditra* — of instruments; *dhvani* — sounds; *sahitaiḥ* — accompanied by; *jaya* — of "Jaya!"; *dhvanaiḥ* — with cries; *ca* — and; *sā* — she; *hṛṣṭā* — joyful; *sapadi* — at once; *niveśayāñcakāra* — led in; *strī* — among women; *ratnam* — the jewel; *mudita* — delighted; *manāḥ* — [with] a heart; *śacī* — Shachi; *sva* — her own; *geham* — into the house.

**144.** Thus, with cries of "Jaya!" accompanied by the loud sounds of instruments, He brought the bride home; and Shachi, joyful, her heart delighted, at once led that jewel among women into her house.

*Iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahākāvye tṛtīyaḥ sargaḥ samāptaḥ* — Thus ends the third sarga of the mahakavya "Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita".

---

## Sarga Four — verses 1–77

**Metre:** *drutavilambita* (12 syllables per pada); verses 73–74 — *toṭaka*; verse 76 — *śikhariṇī*; verse 77 — *vaṁśastha*.
**Parallels:** Chaitanya-bhagavata, Adi 12–13 (Nimai the teacher; the victory over Keshava Kashmiri); Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 16.

**Contents of the passage:**
- 1–4 — married life with Vishnupriya; the beauty of Gauranga.
- 5–20 — Gauranga as a teacher among His students (the verses are built on *yamaka*, the repetition of syllables; many passages are obscure).
- 21–24 — the journey to Gaya with Chandrashekhara Acharya.
- 25–49 — a poetic interlude: a lotus pond, sunset, night, morning, mountains and deer along the way (the story stands still; continuous *yamaka*).
- 50–55 — the river Chora: the fever, the cure with the water from the brahmanas' feet; Rajagiri (Rajagriha); the entry into Gaya.
- 56–61 — **the meeting with Ishvara Puri; the initiation**.
- 62–65 — the shraddha at Gaya (the Phalgu, Pretashila, Manasa); at the footprint of Vishnu — the first ecstasy.
- 66–68 — the impulse to go to Madhuvana (Vraja); a voice from the sky bids Him return.
- 69–75 — the return home, music; Shachi distributes gifts.
- 76–77 — the beginning of kirtana (the month of Magha).

### Verse 1

अथ कृपारसवारिनिधीन्दुना
स्वजनमानसकैरवबन्धुना ।
दयितया सह तत्र विराजिता
निजगृहे जगृहे गृहमेधिता ॥१॥

*atha kṛpā-rasa-vārinidhīndunā*
*sva-jana-mānasa-kairava-bandhunā |*
*dayitayā saha tatra virājitā*
*nija-gṛhe jagṛhe gṛhamedhitā ||1||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *rasa* — of the liquid; *vārinidhi* — of the ocean; *indunā* — by the moon; *sva* — of His own; *jana* — people; *mānasa* — of the hearts; *kairava* — of the white lilies; *bandhunā* — by the friend; *dayitayā* — the beloved; *saha* — with; *tatra* — there; *virājitā* — splendid; *nija* — in His own; *gṛhe* — in the house; *jagṛhe* — was accepted; *gṛhamedhitā* — the householder's life.

**1.** Then, there in His own house, together with His beloved, He — the moon risen from the ocean of the nectar of mercy, the friend of the white lilies of His own people's hearts — accepted the splendid life of a householder.

*Note.* The moon rose from the churned Milk Ocean; the white lily (*kairava*) opens under the moon. A play of sounds: *gṛhe jagṛhe gṛhamedhitā*.

### Verse 2

द्रुतसुवर्णसुवर्णरुचः शुचे-
र्मधुरकोमलशीतलविभ्रमः ।
श्रियमसौ मधुरामतिसुन्दरी-
मवपुषो वपुषोऽनुरुचाहरत् ॥२॥

*druta-suvarṇa-suvarṇa-rucaḥ śucer*
*madhura-komala-śītala-vibhramaḥ |*
*śriyam asau madhurām ati-sundarīm*
*avapuṣo vapuṣo 'nurucāharat ||2||*

*Word for word:* *druta* — of molten; *suvarṇa* — gold; *su* — of beautiful; *varṇa* — colour; *rucaḥ* — [of the body] having the lustre; *śuceḥ* — of the pure; *madhura* — of sweet; *komala* — tender; *śītala* — cooling; *vibhramaḥ* — [He] of charm; *śriyam* — the beauty; *asau* — He; *madhurām* — sweet; *ati* — exceedingly; *sundarīm* — lovely; *avapuṣaḥ* — from the Bodiless One; *vapuṣaḥ* — of the body; *anurucā* — by the radiance; *aharat* — stole.

**2.** He, full of sweet, tender and cooling charm, by the radiance of His pure body, which had the lustre of the beautiful colour of molten gold, stole the sweet and exceedingly lovely beauty of the Bodiless One.

*Note.* A play on words: *avapuṣo vapuṣo*, "from the Bodiless One … of the body". The Bodiless One is Kama, the god of love (cf. 3.30).

### Verse 3

अमूमवेक्ष्य हृदा हृदयेशयः
सपदि निश्चितमित्थममन्यत ।
इममृते मम मन्मथता जनै-
रनुकथं नु कथं न हसिष्यते ॥३॥

*amūm avekṣya hṛdā hṛdayeśayaḥ*
*sapadi niścitam ittham amanyata |*
*imam ṛte mama manmathatā janair*
*anukathaṁ nu kathaṁ na hasiṣyate ||3||*

*Word for word:* *amūm* — Him; *avekṣya* — having seen; *hṛdā* — with the heart; *hṛdayeśayaḥ* — "he who lies in the heart", the god of love; *sapadi* — at once; *niścitam* — firmly; *ittham* — thus; *amanyata* — thought; *imam* — Him; *ṛte* — beside; *mama* — my; *manmathatā* — fame as "the churner of minds"; *janaiḥ* — by people; *anukatham* — at every telling; *nu* — indeed; *katham* — how; *na* — not; *hasiṣyate* — will be laughed at.

**3.** The god of love, seeing Him with his heart, at once firmly concluded: "Beside Him, how will my fame as 'the churner of minds' not be laughed at by people whenever it is spoken of?"

*Note.* *Hṛdayeśaya*, "he who lies in the heart", and *manmatha*, "churner of the mind", are both names of Kamadeva. The edition has *amūm* (feminine); the sense requires *amum* (masculine, "Him"). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 4

निजपदाब्जरसैरतिशीतलै-
र्जगदपूरयदात्तकृपारसः ।
य इह तत्कथने विरमन्त्यहो
तनुधरा नु धरासु वसन्ति ते ॥४॥

*nija-padābja-rasair ati-śītalair*
*jagad apūrayad ātta-kṛpā-rasaḥ |*
*ya iha tat-kathane viramanty aho*
*tanu-dharā nu dharāsu vasanti te ||4||*

*Word for word:* *nija* — of His own; *pada* — of the feet; *abja* — of the lotuses; *rasaiḥ* — with the juices; *ati* — very; *śītalaiḥ* — cooling; *jagat* — the world; *apūrayat* — filled; *ātta* — having taken up; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *rasaḥ* — the taste; *ye* — who; *iha* — here; *tat* — about Him; *kathane* — from speaking; *viramanti* — cease; *aho* — ah; *tanu* — bodies; *dharāḥ* — bearing; *nu* — whether; *dharāsu* — on the earth; *vasanti* — live; *te* — they.

**4.** Filled with the taste of mercy, He filled the world with the very cooling juices of His lotus feet. Ah, those here who cease from speaking of Him — do they [truly] live on the earth? They are mere bearers of bodies.

*Note.* A play on words: *tanu-dharā*, "body-bearers" — *dharāsu*, "on the earth".

### Verse 5

अथ गुरुत्वमुपेत्य विकस्वरा-
म्बुजविलोलविलोचनखेलनैः ।
द्विजगणं समपाठयदेष य-
त्प्रतिभयातिभयाकुलितो गुरुः ॥५॥

*atha gurutvam upetya vikasvarā-*
*mbuja-vilola-vilocana-khelanaiḥ |*
*dvija-gaṇaṁ samapāṭhayad eṣa yat*
*pratibhayāti-bhayākulito guruḥ ||5||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *gurutvam* — the position of teacher; *upetya* — having assumed; *vikasvara* — of blossoming; *ambuja* — [like] lotuses; *vilola* — of restless; *vilocana* — of the eyes; *khelanaiḥ* — with the play; *dvija* — of brahmanas; *gaṇam* — the throng; *samapāṭhayat* — taught; *eṣaḥ* — He; *yat* — so that; *pratibhayā* — by [His] genius; *ati* — with great; *bhaya* — fear; *ākulitaḥ* — confounded; *guruḥ* — Guru [Brihaspati].

**5.** Then, having become a teacher, He taught the throng of brahmanas with the play of His restless eyes, like blossoming lotuses — so that Guru himself, [the teacher of the gods,] was confounded by His genius, in great fear.

*Note.* A pun: *pratibhayāti-bhaya*, "by genius — great fear". *Guru* is both "teacher" and Brihaspati, the preceptor of the gods and the standard of learning.

### Verse 6

विविधशिष्यसदस्यपि राजतः
कनकगौरतनोर्मधुरद्युतेः ।
सुखवतः परिपाठयतोऽस्य सा
सुरुचिरा रुचिरास सुधारसम् ॥६॥

*vividha-śiṣya-sadasy api rājataḥ*
*kanaka-gaura-tanor madhura-dyuteḥ |*
*sukhavataḥ paripāṭhayato 'sya sā*
*su-rucirā rucir āsa sudhā-rasam ||6||*

*Word for word:* *vividha* — of various; *śiṣya* — of students; *sadasi* — in the assembly; *api* — even; *rājataḥ* — [of Him] shining; *kanaka* — [like] gold; *gaura* — golden; *tanoḥ* — [of Him] whose body [is]; *madhura* — sweet; *dyuteḥ* — [of Him] whose effulgence [is]; *sukhavataḥ* — joyful; *paripāṭhayataḥ* — teaching; *asya* — of Him; *sā* — that; *su* — most; *rucirā* — lovely; *ruciḥ* — lustre; *āsa* — cast forth; *sudhā* — of nectar; *rasam* — the juice.

**6.** As He — His body golden as gold, His effulgence sweet — shone even in the assembly of His various students and joyfully taught them, that most lovely lustre of His cast forth the juice of nectar.

*Note.* A play of sounds: *su-rucirā rucir āsa*. *Āsa* is taken as the perfect of *as*, "to throw, to cast forth", not as "was".

### Verse 7

दशनरश्मिभिरच्छरदच्छदौ
स्नपयता सततं वदनेन्दुना ।
स्मितसुधामधुरेण महाप्रभु-
र्घनरुचा नवचारुरुचिर्बभौ ॥७॥

*daśana-raśmibhir accha-radacchadau*
*snapayatā satataṁ vadanendunā |*
*smita-sudhā-madhureṇa mahāprabhur*
*ghana-rucā nava-cāru-rucir babhau ||7||*

*Word for word:* *daśana* — of the teeth; *raśmibhiḥ* — with the rays; *accha* — clear; *radacchadau* — the two lips; *snapayatā* — bathing; *satatam* — constantly; *vadana* — of the face; *indunā* — with the moon; *smita* — of the smile; *sudhā* — with the nectar; *madhureṇa* — sweet; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *ghana* — with dense; *rucā* — lustre; *nava* — fresh; *cāru* — lovely; *ruciḥ* — [He] of radiance; *babhau* — shone.

**7.** With the moon of His face, sweet with the nectar of His smile, constantly bathing His clear lips in the rays of His teeth, Mahaprabhu shone with dense lustre, His radiance fresh and lovely.

*Note.* The edition has *घनरुधा*; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *ghana-rucā*, "with dense lustre", and we read so.

### Verse 8

सकलशिष्यमुखानि महाप्रभोः
कलयतः ककुभः सततारुणाः ।
विदधिरे बहुविभ्रमयावलत्-
करुणयारुणया नयनश्रिया ॥८॥

*sakala-śiṣya-mukhāni mahāprabhoḥ*
*kalayataḥ kakubhaḥ satatāruṇāḥ |*
*vidadhire bahu-vibhramayā valat-*
*karuṇayāruṇayā nayana-śriyā ||8||*

*Word for word:* *sakala* — of all; *śiṣya* — the students; *mukhāni* — the faces; *mahāprabhoḥ* — of Mahaprabhu; *kalayataḥ* — [of Him] looking upon; *kakubhaḥ* — the quarters; *satata* — ever; *aruṇāḥ* — red; *vidadhire* — were made; *bahu* — of much; *vibhramayā* — [full] of playfulness; *valat* — surging; *karuṇayā* — with compassion; *aruṇayā* — reddish; *nayana* — of the eyes; *śriyā* — by the beauty.

**8.** As Mahaprabhu looked upon the faces of all His students, the quarters were made ever red by the reddish beauty of His eyes, full of playfulness and surging with compassion.

*Note.* A play of sounds: *karuṇayā aruṇayā*.

### Verse 9

करतलेन गिरां गुरुविभ्रमै-
र्भ्रमवता स बभौ परितः स्फुरन् ।
कनकशैल इवोद्गतगैरिको-
दयलता लयताण्डवखेलनाम् ॥९॥

*kara-talena girāṁ guru-vibhramair*
*bhramavatā sa babhau paritaḥ sphuran |*
*kanaka-śaila ivodgata-gairikodaya-latā-*
*laya-tāṇḍava-khelanām ||9||*

*Word for word:* *kara* — of the hand; *talena* — with the palm; *girām* — of speech; *guru* — with great; *vibhramaiḥ* — graces; *bhramavatā* — moving in circles; *saḥ* — He; *babhau* — shone; *paritaḥ* — all around; *sphuran* — flashing; *kanaka* — a golden; *śailaḥ* — mountain; *iva* — like; *udgata* — risen; *gairika* — of red ochre; *udaya* — emerging; *latā* — of the veins; *laya* — rhythmic; *tāṇḍava* — of the tandava dance; *khelanām* — [displaying] the play.

**9.** With the palm of His hand moving in circles with the great graces of His speech, He shone, flashing all around, like a golden mountain [displaying] the play of a rhythmic tandava dance of risen, emerging veins of red ochre.

*Note.* The red palm against the golden body is like veins of red ochre (*gairika*) on a golden mountain. *Tāṇḍava* is a vigorous, rhythmic dance (the dance of Shiva). (?) The end of the verse is syntactically obscure; it is rendered according to the sense. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 10

अयमयं नु किमस्य कमस्य वा
किमयमर्थ उतस्विदयं त्विति ।
कलकलोऽस्य बभूव सुखाय स
त्रिचतुरैश्चतुरैः परितः कृतः ॥१०॥

*ayam ayaṁ nu kim asya kam asya vā*
*kim ayam artha utasvid ayaṁ tv iti |*
*kala-kalo 'sya babhūva sukhāya sa*
*tri-caturaiś caturaiḥ paritaḥ kṛtaḥ ||10||*

*Word for word:* *ayam* — this; *ayam* — this; *nu* — is it; *kim* — what; *asya* — of this; *kam* — which; *asya* — of this; *vā* — or; *kim* — is it; *ayam* — this; *arthaḥ* — sense; *utasvit* — or perhaps; *ayam* — this; *tu* — indeed; *iti* — thus; *kala-kalaḥ* — the clamour; *asya* — to Him; *babhūva* — was; *sukhāya* — for delight; *saḥ* — that; *tri* — three; *caturaiḥ* — or four; *caturaiḥ* — by clever [students]; *paritaḥ* — all around; *kṛtaḥ* — raised.

**10.** "Is it this? Or this? What is [the meaning] of this? Or which [word] of this? Is this the sense — or perhaps this?" — the clamour that three or four clever [students] raised all around Him was His delight.

*Note.* A lively scene: the students vie with one another over an interpretation. A play of sounds: *tri-caturaiś caturaiḥ*, "by three or four clever ones".

### Verse 11

प्रभुमुखे युगपत्पतयालुभि-
र्विसृमरैरलिभिर्विदधे मुहुः ।
विततपक्षविधूननसक्षणै-
र्दिगबलागवलावलिविभ्रमा ॥११॥

*prabhu-mukhe yugapat patayālubhir*
*visṛmarair alibhir vidadhe muhuḥ |*
*vitata-pakṣa-vidhūnana-sakṣaṇair*
*dig-abalā-gavalāvali-vibhramā ||11||*

*Word for word:* *prabhu* — of the Lord; *mukhe* — on the face; *yugapat* — all at once; *patayālubhiḥ* — alighting; *visṛmaraiḥ* — scattering; *alibhiḥ* — by bees; *vidadhe* — was produced; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *vitata* — of outspread; *pakṣa* — wings; *vidhūnana* — in the fluttering; *sa-kṣaṇaiḥ* — exultant; *dik* — of the quarters; *abalā* — for the maidens; *gavala* — of buffalo horn; *āvali* — of rows; *vibhramā* — the charm.

**11.** Again and again the bees, now alighting all at once on the Lord's face, now scattering, exultant in the fluttering of their outspread wings, lent the maidens of the quarters the charm of rows of [ornaments black as] buffalo horn.

*Note.* The bees take the Lord's face for a lotus (cf. v. 12). In the edition the last pada reads *dig-abalā abalāvali-vibhramāḥ*; we read with the Gosvami edition (GGM) *dig-abalā-gavalāvali-vibhramā*: *gavala* is the horn of the wild buffalo, a byword for blackness.

### Verse 12

किसलयं सलयं किमु वारुणं
सकमलं कमलं किमु वेत्यलिः ।
इह तदा हतदाक्ष्य इव प्रभोः
करदलं रदलङ्घनयाभजत् ॥१२॥

*kisalayaṁ salayaṁ kimu vāruṇaṁ*
*sa-kamalaṁ kamalaṁ kimu vety aliḥ |*
*iha tadā hata-dākṣya iva prabhoḥ*
*kara-dalaṁ rada-laṅghanayābhajat ||12||*

*Word for word:* *kisalayam* — a young shoot; *salayam* — swaying; *kimu* — is it; *vāruṇam* — or red; *sa* — with; *kamalam* — water; *kamalam* — a lotus; *kimu* — is it; *vā* — or; *iti* — thus [wondering]; *aliḥ* — the bee; *iha* — here; *tadā* — then; *hata* — lost; *dākṣyaḥ* — [having] its cleverness; *iva* — as if; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *kara* — of the hand; *dalam* — the petal; *rada* — of the teeth; *laṅghanayā* — with the touch (?); *abhajat* — resorted to.

**12.** "Is it a swaying, red young shoot? Or is it a lotus in its water?" — so wondering, the bee, as if it had lost its wits, then fell upon the petal of the Lord's hand (?) with a touch of its teeth.

*Note.* A play of sounds: *kisalayaṁ salayaṁ*, *sa-kamalaṁ kamalam* (*kam* — "water"); *vāruṇam* is *vā aruṇam*, "or red". (?) *Rada-laṅghanayā* is obscure (literally "by the overstepping of the teeth"). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 13

नखसुधांशुसुधां शुचिमुक्षता
सुरुचिरेण चिरेण मधुव्रतः ।
करदलेन दलेन रुचाप्यभू-
द्धवलता वलता सुचिरोषितः ॥१३॥

*nakha-sudhāṁśu-sudhāṁ śucim ukṣatā*
*su-rucireṇa cireṇa madhuvrataḥ |*
*kara-dalena dalena rucāpy abhūd*
*dhavalatā-valatā su-ciroṣitaḥ ||13||*

*Word for word:* *nakha* — of the nails; *sudhāṁśu* — of the moons; *sudhām* — the nectar; *śucim* — pure; *ukṣatā* — sprinkling; *su* — most; *rucireṇa* — lovely; *cireṇa* — long; *madhuvrataḥ* — the bee; *kara* — of the hand; *dalena* — by the petal; *dalena* — by the petal; *rucā* — by the lustre; *api* — also; *abhūt* — became; *dhavala* — from the white; *latā* — creepers; *valatā* — turned away; *su* — very; *cira* — long; *uṣitaḥ* — having dwelt.

**13.** Because of the most lovely petal of His hand, which long sprinkled the pure nectar of the moons of His nails, and because of its lustre, the bee, which had long dwelt on the white creepers, turned away from them.

*Note.* The verse is built on *yamaka*, the repetition of identical syllables with different meanings: *rucireṇa cireṇa*, *kara-dalena dalena*, *dhavalatā valatā*. The translation follows the sense; many words in such verses cannot be analysed unambiguously. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 14

स परितः परिलक्ष्य धुरीणतां
मधुरिमा धुरि मानवतां श्रियाम् ।
भुवि हितं विहितं रचयन्सता-
मगमदागमदाक्ष्यममुष्य किम् ॥१४॥

*sa paritaḥ parilakṣya dhurīṇatāṁ*
*madhurimā dhuri mānavatāṁ śriyām |*
*bhuvi hitaṁ vihitaṁ racayan satām*
*agamad āgama-dākṣyam amuṣya kim ||14||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — that; *paritaḥ* — on every side; *parilakṣya* — having perceived; *dhurīṇatām* — pre-eminence; *madhurimā* — sweetness; *dhuri* — at the head; *mānavatām* — of human beings; *śriyām* — of the beauties; *bhuvi* — on the earth; *hitam* — the good; *vihitam* — prescribed; *racayan* — arranging; *satām* — for the virtuous; *agamat* — came to know; *āgama* — in the scriptures; *dākṣyam* — the skill; *amuṣya* — His; *kim* — did not…? (?).

**14.** (?) Sweetness, perceiving on every side His pre-eminence at the head of the beauties of human beings — did it not also come to know His skill in the scriptures, as He arranged on earth the prescribed good for the virtuous?

*Note.* (?) The verse is very obscure (*yamaka*: *dhurīṇatāṁ … dhuri*, *agamad āgama*). The translation is conjectural. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 15

प्रभुमुखेन्दुगलद्वचनामृतं
मृतजनस्य च जीवितदायि तत् ।
श्रुतिपथेन निपीय चिरेण ते
मुदमिता दमिताखिलकल्मषाः ॥१५॥

*prabhu-mukhendu-galad-vacanāmṛtaṁ*
*mṛta-janasya ca jīvita-dāyi tat |*
*śruti-pathena nipīya cireṇa te*
*mudam itā damitākhila-kalmaṣāḥ ||15||*

*Word for word:* *prabhu* — of the Lord; *mukha* — of the face; *indu* — from the moon; *galat* — flowing; *vacana* — of words; *amṛtam* — the nectar; *mṛta* — to a dead; *janasya* — person; *ca* — even; *jīvita* — life; *dāyi* — giving; *tat* — that; *śruti* — of hearing; *pathena* — by the path; *nipīya* — having drunk; *cireṇa* — long; *te* — they; *mudam* — joy; *itāḥ* — attained; *damita* — subdued; *akhila* — all; *kalmaṣāḥ* — [they whose] sins [were].

**15.** Having long drunk through the path of their ears the nectar of words flowing from the moon of the Lord's face — a nectar that gives life even to the dead — they, all their sins subdued, attained joy.

*Note.* A play of sounds: *mudam itā damitā*.

### Verse 16

धवलपक्षसपक्षरुगंशुकः
शुकचञ्चुरुचं चुलुकीकृताम् ।
मधुरयोर्नु दधेऽधरयोरसौ
मधुरयोर्यदयं परिजृम्भते ॥१६॥

*dhavala-pakṣa-sapakṣa-rug-aṁśukaḥ*
*śuka-cañcu-rucaṁ culukī-kṛtām |*
*madhurayor nu dadhe 'dharayor asau*
*madhurayor yad ayaṁ parijṛmbhate ||16||*

*Word for word:* *dhavala* — of the bright; *pakṣa* — fortnight; *sapakṣa* — like; *ruk* — [whose] lustre [is]; *aṁśukaḥ* — [He whose] garment [is]; *śuka* — of the parrot; *cañcu* — of the beak; *rucam* — the beauty; *culukī* — a mouthful; *kṛtām* — made into; *madhurayoḥ* — in the sweet; *nu* — did not…?; *dadhe* — held; *adharayoḥ* — in the lips; *asau* — He; *madhurayoḥ* — over the sweet [lips]; *yat* — since; *ayam* — it; *parijṛmbhate* — spreads.

**16.** His garment had the lustre of the bright fortnight of the moon. Did He not take the beauty of the parrot's beak in a single sip and hold it in His sweet lips? — for it spreads over those sweet [lips].

*Note.* The edition gives *nudadhe* and *madhu-rayo* ("a stream of honey"); we read with the Gosvami edition (GGM) *nu dadhe* and *madhurayor*: the Lord's lips are red like a parrot's beak.

### Verse 17

नवविकस्वरपङ्कजभास्वरं
स्मितमधुद्रवविश्वविलोभनम् ।
जहसुरस्य मुखेन्दुमवेक्ष्य ते
रसमयं समयन्तमशोणताम् ॥१७॥

*nava-vikasvara-paṅkaja-bhāsvaraṁ*
*smita-madhu-drava-viśva-vilobhanam |*
*jahasur asya mukhendum avekṣya te*
*rasamayaṁ samayantam aśoṇatām ||17||*

*Word for word:* *nava* — freshly; *vikasvara* — blossomed; *paṅkaja* — [like] a lotus; *bhāsvaram* — resplendent; *smita* — of the smile; *madhu* — of honey; *drava* — with the liquid; *viśva* — the world; *vilobhanam* — enchanting; *jahasuḥ* — laughed; *asya* — His; *mukha* — of the face; *indum* — the moon; *avekṣya* — having beheld; *te* — they; *rasa* — of rasa; *mayam* — full; *samayantam* — bringing to; *aśoṇatām* — paleness.

**17.** Beholding the moon of His face — resplendent as a freshly blossomed lotus, enchanting the world with the honeyed liquid of its smile, full of rasa, bringing [red lotuses] to paleness — they laughed for joy.

*Note.* *Samayantam aśoṇatām*, literally "bringing to un-redness": beside His face the red lotus loses its colour.

### Verse 18

विधुरसौष्ठवतां लभतां मुहु-
र्विधुरसौ वलता वदनांशुना ।
मधुरसान्वितपुष्पमनोरमो
मधुरसाधुरसावभिवर्त्तताम् ॥१८॥

*vidhur asauṣṭhavatāṁ labhatāṁ muhur*
*vidhur asau valatā vadanāṁśunā |*
*madhu-rasānvita-puṣpa-manoramo*
*madhur asādhu-rasāv abhivartatām ||18||*

*Word for word:* *vidhuḥ* — the moon; *asauṣṭhavatām* — unloveliness; *labhatām* — let it obtain; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *vidhuḥ* — the moon; *asau* — this; *valatā* — turning [towards it]; *vadana* — of the face; *aṁśunā* — by the ray; *madhu* — of honey; *rasa* — with the juice; *anvita* — filled; *puṣpa* — with flowers; *manoramaḥ* — charming; *madhuḥ* — spring; *asādhu* — of poor; *rasau* — taste (?); *abhivartatām* — let it become.

**18.** Let this moon, [touched] by the ray of His face turned towards it, again and again lose its loveliness; and let spring, charming with flowers filled with the juice of honey, become insipid.

*Note.* Again a *yamaka*: *vidhur asauṣṭhavatāṁ … vidhur asau*, *madhu-rasānvita … madhur asādhu-rasau*. (?) The form *rasau* is unclear. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 19

इति जनः परिपाठयति प्रभौ
प्रभवता प्रतिभानरसाब्धिना ।
मधुरिमाणमवेक्ष्य समुज्जगौ
नवसुधा वसुधामिव किं श्रिता ॥१९॥

*iti janaḥ paripāṭhayati prabhau*
*prabhavatā pratibhāna-rasābdhinā |*
*madhurimāṇam avekṣya samujjagau*
*nava-sudhā vasudhām iva kiṁ śritā ||19||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *janaḥ* — the people; *paripāṭhayati* — [when] was teaching; *prabhau* — the Lord; *prabhavatā* — with mighty; *pratibhāna* — of inspired insight; *rasa* — of rasa; *abdhinā* — with the ocean; *madhurimāṇam* — the sweetness; *avekṣya* — beholding; *samujjagau* — cried aloud; *nava* — a new; *sudhā* — nectar; *vasudhām* — to the earth; *iva* — as it were; *kim* — has not…?; *śritā* — come.

**19.** When the Lord was teaching thus with His mighty ocean of the rasa of inspired insight, the people, beholding His sweetness, cried aloud: "Has not a new nectar, as it were, come down to the earth?"

*Note.* A play of sounds: *nava-sudhā vasudhām*.

### Verse 20

इति कियन्ति दिनानि महाप्रभुः
समनयत्परिपाठ्य कृपानिधिः ।
निजतनोर्महसा स दिनन्दिनं
प्रभवता भवतापचयानपि ॥२०॥

*iti kiyanti dināni mahāprabhuḥ*
*samanayat paripāṭhya kṛpā-nidhiḥ |*
*nija-tanor mahasā sa dinandinaṁ*
*prabhavatā bhava-tāpa-cayān api ||20||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *kiyanti* — a number of; *dināni* — days; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *samanayat* — spent / quelled; *paripāṭhya* — teaching; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *nidhiḥ* — the treasure-house; *nija* — of His own; *tanoḥ* — of the body; *mahasā* — by the splendour; *saḥ* — He; *dinandinam* — day by day; *prabhavatā* — mighty; *bhava* — of worldly existence; *tāpa* — of the torments; *cayān* — the heaps; *api* — also.

**20.** Thus Mahaprabhu, the treasure-house of mercy, spent a number of days teaching; and day by day, by the mighty splendour of His own body, He also quelled the heaps of the torments of worldly existence.

*Note.* The verb *samanayat* works twice: "spent [the days]" and, echoing *śamanayat*, "quelled [the torments]".

### Verse 21

स जननीभगिनीपतिना गयां
सममुपैतुमनास्तदनन्तरम् ।
निजमनोरमचेष्टितविभ्रमैः
सुमनसां मनसां मुदमावहत् ॥२१॥

*sa jananī-bhaginī-patinā gayāṁ*
*samam upaitu-manās tad-anantaram |*
*nija-manorama-ceṣṭita-vibhramaiḥ*
*sumanasāṁ manasāṁ mudam āvahat ||21||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — He; *jananī* — of the mother; *bhaginī* — of the sister; *patinā* — with the husband; *gayām* — to Gaya; *samam* — together; *upaitu* — to go; *manāḥ* — minded (wishing); *tat* — that; *anantaram* — after; *nija* — by His own; *manorama* — charming; *ceṣṭita* — of movements; *vibhramaiḥ* — by the graces; *sumanasām* — of good people; *manasām* — to the hearts; *mudam* — joy; *āvahat* — brought.

**21.** After that, wishing to go to Gaya together with the husband of His mother's sister, He brought joy to the hearts of good people by the graces of His own charming movements.

*Note.* The edition reads *nija-yato raya-* (obscure); we read *nija-manorama-* with the Gosvami edition (GGM). The husband of Shachi's sister is Chandrashekhara Acharya (Acharyaratna). The pilgrimage to Gaya is a turning point: there Nimai meets Ishvara Puri and receives initiation (Chaitanya-bhagavata, Adi 17; Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 17).

### Verse 22

प्रथममुल्लसितो विजयोद्यमे
परिसमाप्तविधिर्महितो मुहुः ।
द्विजगणेन सुखैर्ववृधे जय-
स्वनवता नवतामरसेक्षणः ॥२२॥

*prathamam ullasito vijayodyame*
*parisamāpta-vidhir mahito muhuḥ |*
*dvija-gaṇena sukhair vavṛdhe jaya-*
*svanavatā nava-tāmarasekṣaṇaḥ ||22||*

*Word for word:* *prathamam* — first; *ullasitaḥ* — exultant; *vijaya* — of setting out; *udyame* — in the undertaking; *parisamāpta* — having completed; *vidhiḥ* — the rites; *mahitaḥ* — honoured; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *dvija* — of brahmanas; *gaṇena* — by the crowd; *sukhaiḥ* — with joys; *vavṛdhe* — grew; *jaya* — of "Jaya!"; *svanavatā* — by [the crowd] resounding with cries; *nava* — fresh; *tāmarasa* — [like] lotuses; *īkṣaṇaḥ* — [He whose] eyes.

**22.** First, exultant at the undertaking of setting out, He completed the rites; and, honoured again and again by the crowd of brahmanas resounding with cries of "Jaya!", He whose eyes were like fresh lotuses grew ever fuller of joy.

*Note.* Nimai went to Gaya to perform the shraddha rites for His father. A play of sounds: *jaya-svanavatā nava-tāmarasa*.

### Verse 23

द्विजगणैर्भगणैरिव संक्षरन्
द्युतिसुधा वसुधासु शशीव सः ।
सुकथितैः पथि तैर्विलसन्प्रभू
रसमयं समयं तममन्यत ॥२३॥

*dvija-gaṇair bha-gaṇair iva saṅkṣaran*
*dyuti-sudhā vasudhāsu śaśīva saḥ |*
*sukathitaiḥ pathi tair vilasan prabhū*
*rasamayaṁ samayaṁ tam amanyata ||23||*

*Word for word:* *dvija* — of brahmanas; *gaṇaiḥ* — with the throngs; *bha* — of stars; *gaṇaiḥ* — with the hosts; *iva* — as; *saṅkṣaran* — pouring forth; *dyuti* — of radiance; *sudhāḥ* — the nectars; *vasudhāsu* — upon the lands; *śaśī* — the moon; *iva* — like; *saḥ* — He; *sukathitaiḥ* — with good conversations; *pathi* — on the way; *taiḥ* — with them; *vilasan* — delighting; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *rasa* — with sweetness; *mayam* — filled; *samayam* — time; *tam* — that; *amanyata* — considered.

**23.** With the throngs of brahmanas as the moon with the hosts of stars, pouring forth the nectar of His radiance upon the lands like the moon, and delighting on the way in good conversation with them, the Lord considered that time filled with sweetness.

### Verse 24

क्वचन वीक्ष्य मनोज्ञतमां स्थलीं
स्थलपयोरुहपादपयोरुहाम् ।
उपतरङ्गिणि तेन विशद्विभ्रमे
न मधुपा मधु पातुमनुत्सुकाः ॥२४॥

*kvacana vīkṣya manojñatamāṁ sthalīṁ*
*sthala-payoruha-pāda-payoruhām |*
*upataraṅgiṇi tena viśad-vibhrame*
*na madhupā madhu pātum anutsukāḥ ||24||*

*Word for word:* *kvacana* — somewhere; *vīkṣya* — having seen; *manojñatamām* — most charming; *sthalīm* — a spot; *sthala* — land; *payoruha* — lotuses; *pāda* — of the feet; *payoruhām* — of the lotuses; *upataraṅgiṇi* — near a river; *tena* — by Him; *viśat* — being entered (sat in); *vibhrame* — in grace; *na* — not; *madhupāḥ* — the bees; *madhu* — the honey; *pātum* — to drink; *anutsukāḥ* — unwilling.

**24.** Somewhere near a river He saw a most charming spot, and when He in His grace sat down there, the bees were far from unwilling to drink the honey of His lotus feet, [taking them for] land lotuses.

*Note.* *Na anutsukāḥ*, "not unwilling", that is, greedily eager: a double negative. *Sthala-padma*, the "land lotus", is the hibiscus.

### Verse 25

निभृतनीलमधुव्रतलोचनै-
र्ललितकेशरदन्तविकस्वरैः ।
विकसिताम्बुरुहाननमण्डलै-
र्मधुरसाधुरसा मधुशालिनी ॥२५॥

*nibhṛta-nīla-madhuvrata-locanair*
*lalita-keśara-danta-vikasvaraiḥ |*
*vikasitāmburuhānana-maṇḍalair*
*madhura-sādhu-rasā madhu-śālinī ||25||*

*Word for word:* *nibhṛta* — quiet; *nīla* — dark; *madhuvrata* — bees; *locanaiḥ* — [as] eyes; *lalita* — lovely; *keśara* — filaments; *danta* — [as] teeth; *vikasvaraiḥ* — with gleaming; *vikasita* — of opened; *amburuha* — lotuses; *ānana* — [as] faces; *maṇḍalaiḥ* — with the circles; *madhura* — of sweet; *sādhu* — excellent; *rasā* — [full of] juice; *madhu* — with honey; *śālinī* — rich.

**25.** [The row of lotuses in the pond] — with quiet dark bees for eyes, gleaming with lovely filaments for teeth, with the circles of opened lotuses for faces, full of sweet and excellent juice, rich in honey…

*Note.* Verses 25–26 are a *yugmaka*, one sentence. The subject is *kamalinī-tati* (v. 26), "the row of lotuses" in the pond, described as a beautiful woman.

### Verse 26

मदनमन्थरहंसवधूगति-
प्रतिपदोल्लसिता मधुराकृतिः ।
कमलिनीततिरस्य मुदं दधे
सरसि को रसिको विलसेन्न हि ॥२६॥
(युग्मकम्)

*madana-manthara-haṁsa-vadhū-gati-*
*pratipadollasitā madhurākṛtiḥ |*
*kamalinī-tatir asya mudaṁ dadhe*
*sarasi ko rasiko vilasen na hi ||26||*

*Word for word:* *madana* — with love; *manthara* — slow; *haṁsa* — of swans; *vadhū* — of the females; *gati* — by the gait; *pratipada* — at every step; *ullasitā* — enlivened; *madhura* — lovely; *ākṛtiḥ* — [whose] form; *kamalinī* — of lotuses; *tatiḥ* — the row; *asya* — to Him; *mudam* — joy; *dadhe* — gave; *sarasi* — at a lake; *kaḥ* — what; *rasikaḥ* — connoisseur; *vilaset* — would delight; *na hi* — not.

**26.** …enlivened at every step by the gait of the female swans, slow with love, and lovely in form — this row of lotuses gave Him joy. For what connoisseur of beauty would not delight at a lake?

*Note.* Here begins the descriptive insertion traditional in a mahakavya: the lake, the sunset and the night (descriptions of forest and twilight). The story stands still; this is a poetic exercise. Verses 25–40 are saturated with *yamaka* (repetition of syllables) and are deliberately ambiguous.

### Verse 27

मधुकरा मधुपानमदोन्मदाः
किमिदमेव गदन्ति मुहुर्मुहुः ।
स्फुटसरोजवनीष्ववनीतले
कलभतां लभतां रसिको जनः ॥२७॥

*madhukarā madhu-pāna-madonmadāḥ*
*kim idam eva gadanti muhur muhuḥ |*
*sphuṭa-saroja-vanīṣv avanī-tale*
*kalabhatāṁ labhatāṁ rasiko janaḥ ||27||*

*Word for word:* *madhukarāḥ* — the bees; *madhu* — of honey; *pāna* — from the drinking; *mada* — by the intoxication; *unmadāḥ* — maddened; *kim* — is it not; *idam* — this; *eva* — just; *gadanti* — say; *muhuḥ muhuḥ* — again and again; *sphuṭa* — of opened; *saroja* — lotuses; *vanīṣu* — in the groves; *avanī* — of the earth; *tale* — on the surface; *kalabhatām* — the state of a young elephant; *labhatām* — let him attain; *rasikaḥ* — connoisseur; *janaḥ* — the man.

**27.** Is it not just this that the bees, maddened by the intoxication of drinking honey, say again and again: "Let the connoisseur on the face of the earth become a young elephant in the groves of opened lotuses"?

*Note.* The humming of the bees is presented as their speech. A young elephant in a lotus pond is an image of carefree enjoyment. A play of sounds: *kalabhatāṁ labhatām*.

### Verse 28

सरसि का रसिको विरतो भवे-
दुरसि को रसिकोऽधृततत्कुचः ।
ननु कथन्नु कथञ्चन तौ मतौ
कमलकोमलकोरकवन्नयौ ॥२८॥

*sarasi kā rasiko virato bhaved*
*urasi ko rasiko 'dhṛta-tat-kucaḥ |*
*nanu kathan nu kathañcana tau matau*
*kamala-komala-korakavan nayau ||28||*

*Word for word:* *sarasi* — at a lake; *kaḥ* — what; *rasikaḥ* — connoisseur; *virataḥ* — indifferent; *bhavet* — would be; *urasi* — to the chest; *kaḥ* — what; *rasikaḥ* — connoisseur; *adhṛta* — not having pressed; *tat* — her; *kucaḥ* — breasts; *nanu* — surely; *katham nu* — how then; *kathañcana* — in any way; *tau* — those two; *matau* — [not] esteemed; *kamala* — of the lotus; *komala* — tender; *korakavat* — like buds; *nayau* — (?).

**28.** (?) "What connoisseur would remain indifferent at a lake? What connoisseur would not press her breasts [— the lotus buds —] to his chest? How then could those two, tender as lotus buds, in any way not be esteemed?"

*Note.* (?) The verse is obscure and erotically coloured (lotus buds are the stock comparison for a woman's breasts); it continues the speech of the bees, and "she" is the row of lotuses of vv. 25–26. The translation is tentative; *nayau* is unclear (perhaps to be divided *na yau*, "which… not"). The text is the same in the Gosvami edition (GGM).

### Verse 29

इह दृशां सुदृशां सुषमां समां
तुलयितुं लयितुं च मुहुर्मुहुः ।
कुवलयं वलयं पवनैर्वनै-
रकति वा कति का मधुरा धुराः ॥२९॥

*iha dṛśāṁ sudṛśāṁ suṣamāṁ samāṁ*
*tulayituṁ layituṁ ca muhur muhuḥ |*
*kuvalayaṁ valayaṁ pavanair vanair*
*akati vā kati kā madhurā dhurāḥ ||29||*

*Word for word:* *iha* — here; *dṛśām* — of the eyes; *sudṛśām* — of fair-eyed women; *suṣamām* — the beauty; *samām* — equal; *tulayitum* — to rival; *layitum* — to merge (?); *ca* — and; *muhuḥ muhuḥ* — again and again; *kuvalayam* — the blue lotuses; *valayam* — [in] a ring; *pavanaiḥ* — by the winds; *vanaiḥ* — by the waters (?); *akati* — swayed (?); *vā* — or; *kati* — how many; *kā* — what; *madhurāḥ* — sweet; *dhurāḥ* — (?).

**29.** (?) Here the blue lotuses, swaying in a ring with the winds and the waters, again and again [strove] to rival and to merge with the equal beauty of the eyes of fair-eyed women — how many, and what sweet (?)…

*Note.* (?) The verse is almost pure *yamaka* (*dṛśāṁ sudṛśām*, *tulayituṁ layitum*, *kuvalayaṁ valayam*, *pavanair vanair*, *kati vā kati*) and cannot be analysed with certainty. The translation is tentative. The text is the same in the Gosvami edition (GGM).

### Verse 30

तनुतरङ्गतरङ्गमवीक्ष्य सा-
ऽतनुतरङ्गगतं प्रियमाकुला ।
तनुतरङ्गमयन्त्यखिलं पयो-
ऽतनुतरङ्गममुष्य सितच्छदी ॥३०॥

*tanu-taraṅga-taraṅgam avīkṣya sā-*
*'tanu-taraṅga-gataṁ priyam ākulā |*
*tanu-taraṅgam ayanty akhilaṁ payo-*
*'tanu-taraṅgam amuṣya sitacchadī ||30||*

*Word for word:* *tanu* — of fine; *taraṅga* — ripples; *taraṅgam* — amid the wave; *avīkṣya* — not seeing; *sā* — she; *atanu* — by a great; *taraṅga* — wave; *gatam* — carried off; *priyam* — the beloved; *ākulā* — agitated; *tanu* — the fine; *taraṅgam* — ripples; *ayantī* — going over; *akhilam* — all; *payaḥ* — the water; *atanu* — greatly; *taraṅgam* — billowing (?); *amuṣya* — of him (towards him); *sitacchadī* — the female swan ("white-winged").

**30.** The white-winged [swan], not seeing amid the fine ripples her beloved, who had been carried off by a great wave, went in agitation over the fine ripples [towards] him, making all the water billow greatly (?).

*Note.* The whole verse is built on the repetition *tanu-taraṅga / atanu-taraṅga* ("fine ripples / great wave"). *Atanu*, "the Bodiless One", is also a name of Kama, so *atanu-taraṅga* can be heard as "a wave of love". The translation follows the sense.

### Verse 31

कलरुता गरुतामवधूननं

र्मदकलोदकलोलितचक्रिका ॥३१॥

*kala-rutā garutām avadhūnanaṁ*
*vidadhatī dadhatī praṇayaṁ priye |*
*akṛtakā kṛtakāpi mudaṁ vibhor*
*mada-kalodaka-lolita-cakrikā ||31||*

*Word for word:* *kala* — sweet; *rutā* — [with] cry; *garutām* — of the wings; *avadhūnanam* — fluttering; *vidadhatī* — making; *dadhatī* — cherishing; *praṇayam* — affection; *priye* — for the beloved; *akṛtakā* — unfeigned; *kṛtakā* — having produced; *api* — also; *mudam* — joy; *vibhoḥ* — for the all-pervading Lord; *mada* — with intoxication; *kala* — sweet; *udaka* — the water; *lolita* — stirring; *cakrikā* — [in] circles (?).

**31.** Crying sweetly, fluttering her wings, cherishing an unfeigned affection for her beloved, stirring the water in circles, sweet with intoxication, she also produced joy for the all-pervading Lord.

*Note.* (?) A play of sounds: *akṛtakā kṛtakā*, *mada-kalodaka-lolita*. *Cakrikā* is unclear (whirlpools? or the *cakravāka* bird?). The text is the same in the Gosvami edition (GGM).

### Verse 32

तनुतरङ्गजवेन तरङ्गितं

सुरुचिरे रुचिरेव हि कामिनः ॥३२॥

*tanu-taraṅga-javena taraṅgitaṁ*
*nikaṭa-gaṁ sarasaḥ sarasaṁ taṭam |*
*parivilokya yayau mudam uttamāṁ*
*su-rucire rucir eva hi kāminaḥ ||32||*

*Word for word:* *tanu* — of small; *taraṅga* — waves; *javena* — by the rush; *taraṅgitam* — rippled; *nikaṭa* — near; *gam* — lying; *sarasaḥ* — of the pond; *sarasam* — lush; *taṭam* — the bank; *parivilokya* — having looked around at; *yayau* — attained; *mudam* — joy; *uttamām* — the highest; *su* — very; *rucire* — in the beautiful; *ruciḥ* — delight; *eva* — truly; *hi* — for; *kāminaḥ* — of one who loves.

**32.** Looking around at the lush bank of the pond close by, rippled by the rush of small waves, He attained the highest joy: for one who loves truly delights in what is very beautiful.

*Note.* A play of sounds: *sarasaḥ sarasam* ("of the pond" — "lush"), *su-rucire ruciḥ*.

अमलशीकरशीतलमेदुरः

श्रमहतीर्महतीर्विदधे मरुत् ॥३३॥

*kuvalayaṁ kalayan valayākṛti |*
*balaya-sādhvasa-sādhv-ati-mantharaḥ*
*śrama-hatīr mahatīr vidadhe marut ||33||*

*Word for word:* *amala* — of pure; *śīkara* — spray; *śītala* — with the coolness; *meduraḥ* — laden; *kuvalayam* — the blue lotuses; *kalayan* — swaying; *valaya* — of rings; *ākṛti* — in the shape; *balaya* — (?); *sādhvasa* — of timidity; *sādhu* — gently; *ati* — very; *mantharaḥ* — slow; *śrama* — fatigue; *hatīḥ* — removals; *mahatīḥ* — great; *vidadhe* — brought about; *marut* — the breeze.

**33.** The breeze, laden with the coolness of pure spray, swaying the blue lotuses in the shape of rings, gently and very slowly (?), brought about a great removal of [His] fatigue.

*Note.* (?) *Balaya-sādhvasa* is unclear; the general sense of the verse is clear: a cool breeze with spray blew slowly and removed the great fatigue of the road. The text is the same in the Gosvami edition (GGM).

### Verse 34

अथ पथि प्रथितातिसुखोद्गमं

*atha pathi prathitāti-sukhodgamaṁ*
*laghu calantam alantam avekṣya saḥ |*
*kim anurāga-rasair ati-lohito*
*dinapatir na patiṣyati vihvalaḥ ||34||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *pathi* — on the way; *prathita* — displaying; *ati* — a great; *sukha* — of happiness; *udgamam* — upsurge; *laghu* — lightly; *calantam* — walking; *alantam* — (?); *avekṣya* — having seen; *saḥ* — he; *kim* — will not; *anurāga* — of love (redness); *rasaiḥ* — with the juices; *ati* — deeply; *lohitaḥ* — reddened; *dinapatiḥ* — the lord of the day; *na* — not; *patiṣyati* — will fall; *vihvalaḥ* — overwhelmed.

**34.** Then, seeing Him walking lightly on the way (?), displaying a great upsurge of happiness, will not the lord of the day, deeply reddened by the juices of love, fall, overwhelmed?

*Note.* The description of the sunset begins: the sun reddens and "falls" below the horizon. *Anurāga* means both "love" and "reddening". (?) *Alantam* is unclear. The text is the same in the Gosvami edition (GGM).

*atha vilokya gatañ carama-acale*
*pipatiṣuṁ paripakva-phalākṛtim |*
*dinakaraṁ bhramaraiḥ saha niḥsṛtair*
*gata-rasā tarasā bhavad abjinī ||35||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *vilokya* — having seen; *gatam* — gone; *carama* — to the western; *acale* — to the mountain; *pipatiṣum* — about to fall; *paripakva* — of a ripe; *phala* — fruit; *ākṛtim* — [having] the form; *dinakaram* — the sun; *bhramaraiḥ* — with the bees; *saha* — together; *niḥsṛtaiḥ* — that flew out; *gata* — lost; *rasā* — [whose] sap; *tarasā* — at once; *abhavat* — became; *abjinī* — the lotus pond.

**35.** Then, seeing the sun gone to the Western Mountain, about to fall, like a ripe fruit in form, the lotus pond, together with the bees that flew out [of it], at once lost its sap.

*Note.* Day lotuses close at sunset, and the bees leave them. A play of sounds: *gata-rasā tarasā*.

### Verse 36

अपतता क्वचनापि च निर्यता

कुमुदिनी मुदिनी रजनी तदा ॥३६॥

*apatatā kvacanāpi ca niryatā*
*mada-kalāli-kulena samantataḥ |*
*sahaja-vairavatīva babhūva sā*
*kumudinī mudinī rajanī tadā ||36||*

*Word for word:* *apatatā* — by [the swarm] not alighting; *kvacana api* — anywhere; *ca* — and; *niryatā* — flying out; *mada* — with intoxication; *kala* — sweetly [humming]; *ali* — of bees; *kulena* — by the swarm; *samantataḥ* — on all sides; *sahaja* — inborn; *vaira* — enmity; *vatī* — possessing; *iva* — as if; *babhūva* — became; *sā* — that; *kumudinī* — with night-lilies; *mudinī* — joyful; *rajanī* — night; *tadā* — then.

**36.** As the swarm of bees, sweetly humming in their intoxication, flew out on all sides and alighted nowhere, that night, with its night-lilies, then became joyful, as if possessed of an inborn enmity [towards the day lotuses].

*Note.* Night and day are "enemies": the night-lilies (*kumuda*) open when the day lotuses close. A play of sounds: *kumudinī mudinī*.

### Verse 37

नवविकाशपरापि कुमुद्वती

*madhukaraiḥ sutarāṁ paribodhitā |*

*priyatamā-yata-māna-virāmataḥ ||37||*

*Word for word:* *nava* — for a new; *vikāśa* — blossoming; *parā* — intent; *api* — though; *kumudvatī* — the pond of night-lilies; *madhukaraiḥ* — by the bees; *sutarām* — thoroughly; *paribodhitā* — was awakened; *balavatā* — by an ardent; *dayitena* — by a lover; *yathā* — as; *bhavet* — happens; *priyatamā* — of the beloved; *āyata* — long; *māna* — of the sulking; *virāmataḥ* — upon the end.

**37.** The pond of night-lilies, though already intent on a new blossoming, was thoroughly awakened by the bees — as happens to a beloved [awakened] by her ardent lover when her long sulking has come to an end.

*Note.* *Māna*, the "sulking" or jealous estrangement of the beloved, is an important notion in the aesthetics of love.

### Verse 38

अविरतं नलिनीमधुमाधुरी-

कुमुदिनीमभजन्निरतस्पृहा
नवरसा वरसाधुजनाः खलु ॥३८॥

*aviratam nalinī-madhu-mādhurī-*
*mada-madā api puṣpa-liho muhuḥ |*
*kumudinīm abhajan nirata-spṛhā*
*nava-rasā vara-sādhu-janāḥ khalu ||38||*

*Word for word:* *aviratam* — ceaselessly; *nalinī* — of the day lotuses; *madhu* — of the honey; *mādhurī* — by the sweetness; *mada* — with intoxication; *madāḥ* — intoxicated; *api* — though; *puṣpa* — of flowers; *lihaḥ* — the lickers (bees); *muhuḥ* — again; *kumudinīm* — to the night-lilies; *abhajan* — resorted; *nirata* — with unceasing; *spṛhāḥ* — [having] desire; *nava* — new; *rasāḥ* — [seeking] taste; *vara* — the best; *sādhu* — good; *janāḥ* — people; *khalu* — indeed.

**38.** Though ceaselessly intoxicated by the sweetness of the honey of the day lotuses, the bees, the lickers of flowers, again resorted to the night-lilies with unceasing desire: indeed, the best of good people [ever seek] a new taste.

*Note.* *Nava-rasa*, "new taste", can also be heard as "the nine rasas" of poetics. A play of sounds: *nava-rasā vara-sādhu*.

*'para-dine laghu vāti nabhasvati |*
*ruciratāṁ karuṇā-maya-vāridher*
*hṛdayam uddharam utsukatā yayau ||40||*

*Word for word:* *dina* — of the day; *mukhasya* — of the beginning; *vilokayataḥ* — of [Him] gazing at; *tataḥ* — then; *apara* — on the next; *dine* — day; *laghu* — lightly; *vāti* — while blowing; *nabhasvati* — the wind; *ruciratām* — the loveliness; *karuṇā* — compassion; *maya* — of [Him] full; *vāridheḥ* — of the ocean; *hṛdayam* — the heart; *uddharam* — lofty; *utsukatā* — eager delight; *yayau* — came to.

**40.** Then, on the next day, as a light wind was blowing, eager delight came to the lofty heart of the ocean full of compassion as He gazed at the loveliness of the dawn.

### Verse 41

सपदि सङ्कुचता दलता नवं
दलचयेन ततः समविभ्रमा ।
उदयताविशतालिकुलेन च
प्रवसतावसता रजसाऽपि च ॥४१॥

*sapadi saṅkucatā dalatā navaṁ*
*dala-cayena tataḥ sama-vibhramā |*
*udayatāviśatāli-kulena ca*
*pravasatā-vasatā rajasāpi ca ||41||*

*Word for word:* *sapadi* — at once; *saṅkucatā* — contracting; *dalatā* — opening; *navam* — anew; *dala* — of petals; *cayena* — by the mass; *tataḥ* — then; *sama* — equal; *vibhramā* — [having] charm; *udayatā* — rising; *viśatā* — entering; *ali* — of bees; *kulena* — by the swarm; *ca* — and; *pravasatā* — flying away; *vasatā* — settling; *rajasā* — by the pollen; *api ca* — and also.

**41.** At once, by the mass of petals — some contracting, others opening anew — [all] of equal charm; then by the swarm of bees rising and entering; and by the pollen, too, flying away and settling…

*Note.* Verses 41–42 are a *yugmaka*. The verse is built on pairs of opposites (contracting / opening, rising / entering, flying away / settling): at dawn the night-lilies close and the day lotuses open. The edition reads *samadi*; we read *sapadi* ("at once") with the Gosvami edition (GGM).

(युग्मकम्)

*dina-mukhe 'sya tatāna mahāprabhor*
*mudam anekatamāṁ pathi gacchataḥ |*
*kumudinī nalinī ca samantato*
*vidhi-kṛte 'dhikṛteva vicitratā ||42||*

*Word for word:* *dina* — of the day; *mukhe* — at the beginning; *asya* — to Him; *tatāna* — gave; *mahāprabhoḥ* — to Mahaprabhu; *mudam* — joy; *anekatamām* — most manifold; *pathi* — on the way; *gacchataḥ* — going; *kumudinī* — the night-lily; *nalinī* — the day lotus; *ca* — and; *samantataḥ* — on all sides; *vidhi* — by the Creator; *kṛte* — in [what was] made; *adhikṛtā* — appointed; *iva* — as if; *vicitratā* — variety.

**42.** …at daybreak the night-lily and the day lotus on all sides gave the most manifold joy to Him, Mahaprabhu, as He went on His way — as if they were Variety herself, appointed over the Creator's handiwork.

### Verse 43

स हृदये हृदयेप्सितमीक्षणा-

र्दिविरता विरता विततीर्दधे ॥४३॥

*akṛtako 'kṛtako na hi vibhramaḥ |*
*smaraṇato raṇato 'pi mudaṁ prabhor*
*divi-ratā viratā vitatīr dadhe ||43||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — that; *hṛdaye* — in the heart; *hṛdaya* — by the heart; *īpsitam* — desired; *īkṣaṇāt* — from the sight; *akṛtakaḥ* — unfeigned; *akṛtakaḥ* — not made (?); *na hi* — not indeed; *vibhramaḥ* — charm; *smaraṇataḥ* — from remembering; *raṇataḥ* — from the sounding; *api* — also; *mudam* — joy; *prabhoḥ* — to the Lord; *divi* — in the sky; *ratāḥ* — delighting [to fly]; *viratāḥ* — [birds] (?); *vitatīḥ* — flocks; *dadhe* — brought.

**43.** (?) The flocks of birds that delight in the sky — their unfeigned, artless charm, desired by the heart — brought joy to the Lord in His heart by their sight, by remembrance and by their singing.

*Note.* (?) The verse almost defies analysis: it is unbroken *yamaka* (*hṛdaye hṛdaye*, *akṛtako 'kṛtako*, *smaraṇato raṇato*, *divi-ratā viratā*). The translation follows only the general sense. The text is the same in the Gosvami edition (GGM).

### Verse 44

चिरमिव प्रतिबोधमुपागता
गिरिभुवो विभुलोचनवर्त्मगाः ।
विविधपत्त्रिरवेण जयध्वनिं
सपदि सम्पदि सन्ततमादधुः ॥४४॥

*ciram iva pratibodham upāgatā*
*giri-bhuvo vibhu-locana-vartma-gāḥ |*
*vividha-pattri-raveṇa jaya-dhvaniṁ*
*sapadi sampadi santatam ādadhuḥ ||44||*

*Word for word:* *ciram* — after a long [sleep]; *iva* — as if; *pratibodham* — awakening; *upāgatāḥ* — having reached; *giri* — mountain; *bhuvaḥ* — the lands; *vibhu* — of the all-pervading Lord; *locana* — of the eyes; *vartma* — the path; *gāḥ* — entering; *vividha* — of various; *pattri* — birds; *raveṇa* — with the calls; *jaya* — of "Jaya!"; *dhvanim* — the cry; *sapadi* — at once; *sampadi* — in celebration; *santatam* — continuous; *ādadhuḥ* — raised.

**44.** The mountain lands, entering the path of the all-pervading Lord's eyes, as if awakened after a long [sleep], at once raised in celebration a continuous cry of "Jaya!" with the calls of various birds.

*Note.* The road to Gaya passes through hilly country (in present-day Bihar). A play of sounds: *sapadi sampadi*.

### Verse 45

सुहरिता हरितालरुचां चयैः
क्वचन काञ्चनकान्तरुचिः क्वचित् ।
घनसमानसमा स्वरुचासिता
क्वच सिता च सिताच्छशिलाचयैः ॥४५॥

*su-haritā haritāla-rucāṁ cayaiḥ*
*kvacana kāñcana-kānta-ruciḥ kvacit |*
*ghana-samāna-samā sva-rucāsitā*
*kvaca sitā ca sitāccha-śilā-cayaiḥ ||45||*

*Word for word:* *su* — brightly; *haritā* — green; *haritāla* — of orpiment; *rucām* — of lustres; *cayaiḥ* — with masses; *kvacana* — somewhere; *kāñcana* — of gold; *kānta* — lovely; *ruciḥ* — [having] radiance; *kvacit* — somewhere; *ghana* — a raincloud; *samāna* — like; *samā* — a plain (?); *sva* — by its own; *rucā* — colour; *asitā* — dark; *kvaca* — somewhere; *sitā* — white; *ca* — and; *sita* — of white; *accha* — clear; *śilā* — stones; *cayaiḥ* — with masses.

**45.** [The mountain land] — bright green, [and] with masses of the lustre of orpiment; somewhere having the lovely radiance of gold; somewhere a plain (?) dark in its own colour, like a raincloud; and somewhere white with masses of clear white stones…

*Note.* Verses 45–46 are a *yugmaka*. The edition reads *rucāñcayaiḥ*; we read *rucāṁ cayaiḥ* ("with masses of lustre") with the Gosvami edition (GGM). *Haritāla* is orpiment, a yellow mineral; *harita* itself can mean both "green" and "yellowish".

### Verse 46

विकसितैः कसितैः कुसुमोच्चयै-
रिव दरी वदरी विधुरायिता ।
विहसतीह सतीक्षणगे प्रभा-
वधरभूधरभूरतिसुन्दरी ॥४६॥
(युग्मकम्)

*vikasitaiḥ kasitaiḥ kusumoccayair*
*iva darī vadarī vidhurāyitā |*
*vihasatīha satīkṣaṇa-ge prabhāv*
*adhara-bhūdhara-bhūr ati-sundarī ||46||*

*Word for word:* *vikasitaiḥ* — with blossoming; *kasitaiḥ* — (?); *kusuma* — of flowers; *uccayaiḥ* — with masses; *iva* — as if; *darī* — the cave; *vadarī* — (?); *vidhurāyitā* — (?) (shone like the moon?); *vihasatī* — smiling; *iha* — here; *sati* — [when] the good; *īkṣaṇa* — the range of sight; *ge* — entering; *prabhau* — the Lord; *adhara* — lower; *bhūdhara* — of the mountain; *bhūḥ* — the land; *ati* — exceedingly; *sundarī* — beautiful.

**46.** (?) …when the good Lord came within her sight, that exceedingly beautiful land at the foot of the mountains, smiling here as if with masses of blossoming flowers, [her] caves (?)…, shone.

*Note.* (?) The second pada (*darī vadarī vidhurāyitā*) cannot be analysed with confidence, and the translation follows the general sense. The text is the same in the Gosvami edition (GGM).

### Verse 47

अगवयैर्गवयैः शरणीकृतं
विसृमरैः सृमरैरुपशोभितम् ।
वृततरं ततरङ्कुभिरीश्वरः
स्थलमलोलमलोकयदध्वनि ॥४७॥

*aga-vayair gavayaiḥ śaraṇī-kṛtaṁ*
*visṛmaraiḥ sṛmarair upaśobhitam |*
*vṛtataraṁ tata-raṅkubhir īśvaraḥ*
*sthalam alolam alokayad adhvani ||47||*

*Word for word:* *aga* — of the mountains; *vayaiḥ* — (?); *gavayaiḥ* — by gayals; *śaraṇī* — a shelter; *kṛtam* — made; *visṛmaraiḥ* — by roaming; *sṛmaraiḥ* — by *sṛmara* deer; *upaśobhitam* — adorned; *vṛtataram* — thickly filled; *tata* — with numerous; *raṅkubhiḥ* — with *raṅku* deer; *īśvaraḥ* — the Lord; *sthalam* — a spot; *alolam* — quiet; *alokayat* — saw; *adhvani* — on the way.

**47.** On the way the Lord saw a quiet spot made a shelter by the gayals of the mountains (?), adorned by roaming *sṛmara* deer and thickly filled with numerous *raṅku* deer.

*Note.* The *gavaya* is the gayal, a forest ox; the *sṛmara* and the *raṅku* are kinds of deer.

### Verse 48

अनृजुलोचनलोचनविभ्रमै-
रनुपदं नु पदं नटयन्त्यसौ ।
द्रुततमं ततमञ्जुरसं न तं
वशयिता शयिता मृगसन्ततिः ॥४८॥

*anṛju-locana-locana-vibhramair*
*anupadaṁ nu padaṁ naṭayanty asau |*
*drutatamaṁ tata-mañju-rasaṁ na taṁ*
*vaśayitā śayitā mṛga-santatiḥ ||48||*

*Word for word:* *anṛju* — of slanting; *locana* — eyes; *locana* — of the glances; *vibhramaiḥ* — by the charms; *anupadam* — at every step; *nu* — indeed; *padam* — the step; *naṭayantī* — making dance; *asau* — that; *drutatamam* — most swiftly; *tata* — widespread; *mañju* — lovely; *rasam* — [full of] rasa; *na* — not; *tam* — Him; *vaśayitā* — will captivate (?); *śayitā* — lying; *mṛga* — of deer; *santatiḥ* — the herd.

**48.** (?) That herd of deer, lying [at rest], yet at every step making its feet dance most swiftly — would it not, by the charms of the glances of its slanting eyes, captivate Him, full of widespread lovely rasa?

*Note.* (?) The verse is obscure; the translation follows the sense. The text is the same in the Gosvami edition (GGM).

### Verse 49

इति स वर्त्मनि गौरसुधानिधि-
र्विविधकौतुकवीक्षणकौतुकी ।
विरुरुचे सुखमग्नमना व्रजन्
विविधसद्विधसत्परिपालितः ॥४९॥

*iti sa vartmani gaura-sudhā-nidhir*
*vividha-kautuka-vīkṣaṇa-kautukī |*
*viruruce sukha-magna-manā vrajan*
*vividha-sad-vidha-sat-paripālitaḥ ||49||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *saḥ* — He; *vartmani* — on the way; *gaura* — golden; *sudhā* — of nectar; *nidhiḥ* — the treasure-house; *vividha* — various; *kautuka* — wonders; *vīkṣaṇa* — to see; *kautukī* — eager; *viruruce* — shone; *sukha* — in happiness; *magna* — immersed; *manāḥ* — [whose] heart; *vrajan* — going; *vividha* — of various; *sat* — good; *vidha* — kinds; *sat* — by the virtuous; *paripālitaḥ* — protected.

**49.** Thus He, the golden treasure-house of nectar, eager to see the various wonders on the way, went on, His heart immersed in happiness, protected by the virtuous of many good kinds — and He shone.

*Note.* *Vividha-sad-vidha* probably means "of various stations" (householders and renunciants).

### Verse 50

पथि स चोरनदे प्रभुरातनो-
त्प्लवनतर्पणपूजनमुत्सुकः ।
ज्वरितमस्य वपुः समभूत्ततो
न चरितं चरितं भवति प्रभोः ॥५०॥

*pathi sa cora-nade prabhur ātanot*
*plavana-tarpaṇa-pūjanam utsukaḥ |*
*jvaritam asya vapuḥ samabhūt tato*
*na caritaṁ caritaṁ bhavati prabhoḥ ||50||*

*Word for word:* *pathi* — on the way; *saḥ* — that; *cora* — Chora; *nade* — in the river; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *ātanot* — performed; *plavana* — bathing; *tarpaṇa* — the offering of water to the forefathers; *pūjanam* — worship; *utsukaḥ* — eager; *jvaritam* — feverish; *asya* — His; *vapuḥ* — body; *samabhūt* — became; *tataḥ* — then; *na* — not; *caritam* — penetrated (understood); *caritam* — the conduct; *bhavati* — is; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord.

**50.** On the way, in the river Chora, the Lord eagerly performed bathing, the offering of water to the forefathers and worship. Then His body became feverish. The conduct of the Lord is not to be fathomed.

*Note.* The episode of the fever on the way to Gaya is also in the Chaitanya-bhagavata, Adi 17: Nimai is cured by drinking water that has washed the feet of brahmanas (v. 52 ff.). The Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *cīra-nade* ("in the river Chira"); we keep *cora-nade* of our edition: in Murari (1.15.8) this is the river Chorandhayaka. A play of sounds: *na caritaṁ caritam*.

### Verse 51

पथि शरीरगतेयमसुस्थता
कथमभूत्प्रतिकूलकरी मम ।
इति विचिन्तयता द्विजसञ्चयो
निजगदे जगदेककृपालुना ॥५१॥

*pathi śarīra-gateyam asusthatā*
*katham abhūt pratikūla-karī mama |*
*iti vicintayatā dvija-sañcayo*
*nijagade jagad-eka-kṛpālunā ||51||*

*Word for word:* *pathi* — on the way; *śarīra* — in the body; *gatā* — arisen; *iyam* — this; *asusthatā* — illness; *katham* — how; *abhūt* — has come about; *pratikūla* — hindrance; *karī* — causing; *mama* — to Me; *iti* — thus; *vicintayatā* — by [Him] reflecting; *dvija* — of brahmanas; *sañcayaḥ* — the assembly; *nijagade* — was addressed; *jagat* — of the world; *eka* — by the one; *kṛpālunā* — merciful.

**51.** "How has this illness come about in My body on the way, causing Me hindrance?" Reflecting thus, the one merciful [friend] of the world addressed the assembly of brahmanas.

*Note.* A play of sounds: *nijagade jagad-eka*.

### Verse 52

अथ विचिन्त्य भृशं मनसात्मनो
ज्वरशमाय महाप्रभुरौषधम् ।
क्षितिसुराङ्घ्रिपयो न्यदिशत्स्वयं
नहि कृपां हि कृपाम्बुधिरुज्झति ॥५२॥

*atha vicintya bhṛśaṁ manasātmano*
*jvara-śamāya mahāprabhur auṣadham |*
*kṣitisurāṅghri-payo nyadiśat svayaṁ*
*nahi kṛpāṁ hi kṛpāmbudhir ujjhati ||52||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *vicintya* — having pondered; *bhṛśam* — deeply; *manasā* — in mind; *ātmanaḥ* — His own; *jvara* — of the fever; *śamāya* — for the allaying; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *auṣadham* — as the remedy; *kṣitisura* — of the gods on earth (brahmanas); *aṅghri* — of the feet; *payaḥ* — the water; *nyadiśat* — prescribed; *svayam* — Himself; *na hi* — never; *kṛpām* — mercy; *hi* — for; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *ambudhiḥ* — the ocean; *ujjhati* — abandons.

**52.** Then, having pondered deeply in His mind, Mahaprabhu Himself prescribed as the remedy for allaying His own fever the water [that had washed] the feet of the brahmanas, the gods on earth. For the ocean of mercy never abandons mercy.

*Note.* Cf. the Chaitanya-bhagavata, Adi 17: the Lord drinks *vipra-pādodaka*, the water from the feet of brahmanas, to show the glory of the brahmanas.

### Verse 53

ज्वरशमोऽथ बभूव महाप्रभोः
सपदि तेन तदीयपदाम्बुना ।
जगति तच्चरितानि विदन्तु के
सुनिभृता निभृतानि जगत्त्रये ॥५३॥

*jvara-śamo 'tha babhūva mahāprabhoḥ*
*sapadi tena tadīya-padāmbunā |*
*jagati tac-caritāni vidantu ke*
*su-nibhṛtā nibhṛtāni jagat-traye ||53||*

*Word for word:* *jvara* — of the fever; *śamaḥ* — the subsiding; *atha* — and then; *babhūva* — came; *mahāprabhoḥ* — of Mahaprabhu; *sapadi* — at once; *tena* — by that; *tadīya* — their; *pada* — of the feet; *ambunā* — by the water; *jagati* — in the world; *tat* — His; *caritāni* — deeds; *vidantu* — may know; *ke* — who; *su* — deeply; *nibhṛtāḥ* — hidden; *nibhṛtāni* — concealed; *jagat* — of worlds; *traye* — in the three.

**53.** And then, by that water from their feet, Mahaprabhu's fever at once subsided. Who in the world may know His deeds, deeply hidden, concealed in the three worlds?

### Verse 54

अथ समेत्य स राजगिरिं प्रभु-
र्द्विजगणेन मुदा व्यतनोत्तदा ।
पितृसमर्हणमुत्तममादरा-
दुपरमे परमेष्ठिसरस्यपि ॥५४॥

*atha sametya sa rājagiriṁ prabhur*
*dvija-gaṇena mudā vyatanot tadā |*
*pitṛ-samarhaṇam uttamam ādarād*
*uparame parameṣṭhi-sarasy api ||54||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *sametya* — having come to; *saḥ* — that; *rājagirim* — Rajagiri; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *dvija* — of brahmanas; *gaṇena* — with the company; *mudā* — joyfully; *vyatanot* — performed; *tadā* — then; *pitṛ* — of the forefathers; *samarhaṇam* — the worship; *uttamam* — excellent; *ādarāt* — with devotion; *uparame* — at the conclusion (?); *parameṣṭhi* — of Brahma; *sarasi* — at the lake; *api* — also.

**54.** Then the Lord, having come with the company of brahmanas to Rajagiri, joyfully and with devotion performed there the excellent worship of the forefathers; and at the conclusion (?) also at the lake of Brahma.

*Note.* Rajagiri (Rajagriha, present-day Rajgir) and the lake of Brahma, the Brahma-kunda, are sacred places of pilgrimage near Gaya where the shraddha is performed. (?) *Uparame*, "at the conclusion", is uncertain.

### Verse 55

अखिलतीर्थवरेषु पितृक्रियाः
स कृतसद्विधि तत्र समापयन् ।
अथ गयां सह भूसुरसञ्चयै-
रविशदाविशदात्मभिरुत्सुकैः ॥५५॥

*akhila-tīrtha-vareṣu pitṛ-kriyāḥ*
*sa kṛta-sad-vidhi tatra samāpayan |*
*atha gayāṁ saha bhūsura-sañcayair*
*aviśad āviśad-ātmabhir utsukaiḥ ||55||*

*Word for word:* *akhila* — in all; *tīrtha* — holy places; *vareṣu* — in the best; *pitṛ* — for the forefathers; *kriyāḥ* — the rites; *saḥ* — He; *kṛta* — done; *sat* — in proper; *vidhi* — order; *tatra* — there; *samāpayan* — completing; *atha* — then; *gayām* — Gaya; *saha* — together; *bhūsura* — of brahmanas; *sañcayaiḥ* — with the throngs; *aviśat* — entered; *āviśat* — possessed; *ātmabhiḥ* — with [whose] souls; *utsukaiḥ* — eager.

**55.** Having completed there, in proper order, the rites for the forefathers at all the best holy places, He then entered Gaya together with throngs of brahmanas, eager, their souls possessed [by fervour].

*Note.* A play of sounds: *aviśad āviśad*.

### Verse 56

अथ स गौरकिशोरसुधाकरः
प्रथितमीश्वरपूर्वपुरीति तम् ।
सपदि वीक्ष्य मुदं निरपायिनीं
हृदि तदादितदापि ययौ प्रभुः ॥५६॥

*atha sa gaura-kiśora-sudhākaraḥ*
*prathitam īśvara-pūrva-purīti tam |*
*sapadi vīkṣya mudaṁ nirapāyinīṁ*
*hṛdi tadādi tadāpi yayau prabhuḥ ||56||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *saḥ* — that; *gaura* — golden; *kiśora* — youthful; *sudhākaraḥ* — moon; *prathitam* — renowned; *īśvara* — Ishvara; *pūrva* — preceded by; *purī* — Puri; *iti* — thus [named]; *tam* — him; *sapadi* — at once; *vīkṣya* — having seen; *mudam* — joy; *nirapāyinīm* — unfailing; *hṛdi* — in the heart; *tadādi* — from that moment on; *tadā api* — and then too; *yayau* — attained; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord.

**56.** Then that golden youthful moon, the Lord, at once seeing him who was renowned as "Puri" preceded by "Ishvara", attained in His heart, then and from that moment on, an unfailing joy.

*Note.* **The meeting with Ishvara Puri** is a key moment in Mahaprabhu's life: in Gaya He receives initiation from him (Chaitanya-bhagavata, Adi 17; Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 17). Ishvara Puri is a disciple of Madhavendra Puri, who is important also in the story of Nityananda.

### Verse 57

तमवनम्य निपत्य च भूतले
बहुलहर्षपरिप्लुतमानसः ।
अथ जगाद गभीरघनस्वरां
विनयतो नयतोषकरीं गिरम् ॥५७॥

*tam avanamya nipatya ca bhūtale*
*bahula-harṣa-pariplutamānasaḥ |*
*atha jagāda gabhīra-ghana-svarāṁ*
*vinayato naya-toṣa-karīṁ giram ||57||*

*Word for word:* *tam* — to him; *avanamya* — having bowed; *nipatya* — having fallen; *ca* — and; *bhūtale* — to the ground; *bahula* — with abundant; *harṣa* — joy; *paripluta* — flooded; *mānasaḥ* — [whose] heart; *atha* — then; *jagāda* — spoke; *gabhīra* — deep; *ghana* — like a thundercloud; *svarām* — [whose] tone; *vinayataḥ* — with humility; *naya* — by propriety; *toṣa* — delight; *karīm* — giving; *giram* — words.

**57.** Bowing to him and falling to the ground, His heart flooded with abundant joy, He then spoke with humility words deep in tone like a thundercloud, delightful in their propriety:

### Verse 58

तव पदाम्बुजयुग्ममिदं प्रभो
बहुलभाग्यभरेण विलोकितम् ।
वद यथा हरिभक्तिगुणाद्भवेत्
प्रभवतो भवतोयधिशोषणम् ॥५८॥

*tava padāmbuja-yugmam idaṁ prabho*
*bahula-bhāgya-bhareṇa vilokitam |*
*vada yathā hari-bhakti-guṇād bhavet*
*prabhavato bhava-toyadhi-śoṣaṇam ||58||*

*Word for word:* *tava* — of your; *pada* — of the feet; *ambuja* — of the lotuses; *yugmam* — the pair; *idam* — this; *prabho* — O master; *bahula* — of great; *bhāgya* — of good fortune; *bhareṇa* — by the abundance; *vilokitam* — has been seen; *vada* — tell; *yathā* — how; *hari* — to Hari; *bhakti* — of devotion; *guṇāt* — by the power; *bhavet* — may come about; *prabhavataḥ* — mighty; *bhava* — of worldly existence; *toyadhi* — of the ocean; *śoṣaṇam* — the drying up.

**58.** "O master, by an abundance of great good fortune I have beheld this pair of your lotus feet. Tell [Me] how, by the mighty power of devotion to Hari, the ocean of worldly existence may be dried up."

*Note.* *Prabhavataḥ* is taken as an ablative agreeing with *guṇāt*: "by the mighty power". A play of sounds: *prabhavato bhava-toyadhi*.

### Verse 59

इति निशम्य महाप्रभुभाषितं
मुदमवाप्य यतिः स महाशयः ।
मनुमदात्प्रभवे करुणानिधिः
कृतदयं तदयं तममन्यत ॥५९॥

*iti niśamya mahāprabhu-bhāṣitaṁ*
*mudam avāpya yatiḥ sa mahāśayaḥ |*
*manum adāt prabhave karuṇā-nidhiḥ*
*kṛta-dayaṁ tad ayaṁ tam amanyata ||59||*
