*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *niśamya* — having heard; *mahāprabhu* — of Mahaprabhu; *bhāṣitam* — the speech; *mudam* — joy; *avāpya* — having attained; *yatiḥ* — the ascetic; *saḥ* — that; *mahāśayaḥ* — great-souled; *manum* — the mantra; *adāt* — gave; *prabhave* — to the Lord; *karuṇā* — of compassion; *nidhiḥ* — the treasure-house; *kṛta* — [as one who had] shown; *dayam* — mercy; *tat* — therefore; *ayam* — He; *tam* — him; *amanyata* — considered.

**59.** Hearing these words of Mahaprabhu, that great-souled ascetic rejoiced and, a treasure-house of compassion, gave the mantra to the Lord; and therefore the Lord considered him one who had shown Him mercy.

*Note.* *Manu* here is the mantra of initiation. According to the Chaitanya-bhagavata (Adi 17), Ishvara Puri gave Nimai the ten-syllable mantra (*daśākṣara*). A play of sounds: *kṛta-dayaṁ tad ayaṁ*.

### Verse 60

अमुमवाप्य मनुं व्रजभाविनी-
जनपतेः पुलकाङ्कुरशोभिना ।
विगलदश्रुभृता विनयादयं
निजगदे जगदेककृपावता ॥६०॥

*amum avāpya manuṁ vraja-bhāvinī-*
*jana-pateḥ pulakāṅkura-śobhinā |*
*vigalad-aśru-bhṛtā vinayād ayaṁ*
*nijagade jagad-eka-kṛpāvatā ||60||*

*Word for word:* *amum* — this; *avāpya* — having received; *manum* — mantra; *vraja* — of Vraja; *bhāvinī* — of the lovely; *jana* — women; *pateḥ* — of the Lord; *pulaka* — of hairs standing on end; *aṅkura* — with the sprouts; *śobhinā* — adorned; *vigalat* — streaming; *aśru* — tears; *bhṛtā* — bearing; *vinayāt* — with humility; *ayam* — this; *nijagade* — was spoken; *jagat* — of the world; *eka* — by the one; *kṛpāvatā* — merciful [friend].

**60.** Having received this mantra of the Lord of the lovely women of Vraja, He, the one merciful [friend] of the world — adorned with the sprouts of hairs standing on end and shedding streaming tears — humbly spoke these [words]:

*Note.* "The mantra of the Lord of the women of Vraja" is the mantra of Krishna (the Gopala mantra). These signs of ecstasy are the first in the poem: from this moment Nimai the scholar becomes Gauranga the devotee. A play of sounds: *nijagade jagad-eka*.

### Verse 61

यतिपते भवतः पदसङ्गमा-
त्सुमहतीह बभूव कृतार्थता ।
स्वगुरुभक्तिरिति प्रतिगृह्णता
विचकरे च करे पदजं रजः ॥६१॥

*yati-pate bhavataḥ pada-saṅgamāt*
*su-mahatīha babhūva kṛtārthatā |*
*sva-guru-bhaktir iti pratigṛhṇatā*
*vicakare ca kare padajaṁ rajaḥ ||61||*

*Word for word:* *yati* — of ascetics; *pate* — O lord; *bhavataḥ* — your; *pada* — with the feet; *saṅgamāt* — from the meeting; *su* — very; *mahatī* — great; *iha* — here; *babhūva* — has come about; *kṛtārthatā* — the fulfilment of [My] purpose; *sva* — to one's own; *guru* — guru; *bhaktiḥ* — devotion; *iti* — thus [showing]; *pratigṛhṇatā* — by [Him] receiving; *vicakare* — was strewn; *ca* — and; *kare* — on the hand; *padajam* — from the feet; *rajaḥ* — the dust.

**61.** "O lord of ascetics, through meeting your feet the purpose [of My life] has here been very greatly fulfilled." And, [showing] thus devotion to one's own guru, He received the dust of his feet and strewed it on His hand.

*Note.* Literally, "the dust from [his] feet was strewn on the hand by Him who received [it]"; the sense is that the Lord took up the dust of His guru's feet [to place it on His head]. A play of sounds: *vicakare ca kare*.

### Verse 62

अथ स फल्गुनदीप्लवने यथा-
विधि विधाय पितॄन्समतर्पयत् ।
शवमहीभृति पिण्डमदादथो
करुणतोऽरुणतोऽप्यरुणेक्षणः ॥६२॥

*atha sa phalgu-nadī-plavane yathā-*
*vidhi vidhāya pitṝn samatarpayat |*
*śava-mahībhṛti piṇḍam adād atho*
*karuṇato 'ruṇato 'py aruṇekṣaṇaḥ ||62||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *saḥ* — He; *phalgu* — of the Phalgu; *nadī* — river; *plavane* — the bathing [in]; *yathāvidhi* — according to rule; *vidhāya* — having performed; *pitṝn* — the forefathers; *samatarpayat* — satisfied with libations; *śava* — of the dead (Pretashila); *mahībhṛti* — on the mountain; *piṇḍam* — the pinda; *adāt* — offered; *atho* — then; *karuṇataḥ* — from compassion; *aruṇataḥ* — than the dawn; *api* — even; *aruṇa* — red; *īkṣaṇaḥ* — [He] with eyes.

**62.** Then, having bathed according to rule in the river Phalgu, He satisfied the forefathers with libations; and then, on the Mountain of the Dead, He offered the pinda — His eyes red with compassion, redder even than the dawn.

*Note.* The Phalgu is the river at Gaya, the chief place of the shraddha. The *piṇḍa* is a ball of rice offered to the forefathers. The edition has *śva-mahībhṛt*; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *śava-mahībhṛt*, "the mountain of the dead", that is, Pretashila near Gaya. A play of sounds: *karuṇato 'ruṇato 'py aruṇekṣaṇaḥ*.

### Verse 63

समवतीर्य्य ततो व्यतनोत्क्रियाः
पितृगणस्य स दक्षिणमानसे ।
द्विजगणैश्च तथोत्तरमानसे
सहृदयैर्हृदयैकसुधाकरः ॥६३॥

*samavatīrya tato vyatanot kriyāḥ*
*pitṛ-gaṇasya sa dakṣiṇa-mānase |*
*dvija-gaṇaiś ca tathottara-mānase*
*sahṛdayair hṛdayaika-sudhākaraḥ ||63||*

*Word for word:* *samavatīrya* — having come down; *tataḥ* — then; *vyatanot* — performed; *kriyāḥ* — the rites; *pitṛ* — of forefathers; *gaṇasya* — for the host; *saḥ* — He; *dakṣiṇa-mānase* — at Dakshina-manasa; *dvija* — of brahmanas; *gaṇaiḥ* — with the throngs; *ca* — and; *tathā* — likewise; *uttara-mānase* — at Uttara-manasa; *sahṛdayaiḥ* — with sensitive-hearted; *hṛdaya* — of hearts; *eka* — the one; *sudhākaraḥ* — moon.

**63.** Then, having come down, He — the one moon of hearts — performed the rites for the host of forefathers at Dakshina-manasa, and likewise at Uttara-manasa, together with throngs of sensitive-hearted brahmanas.

*Note.* Dakshina-manasa and Uttara-manasa are sacred ponds at Gaya, places of the shraddha. A play of sounds: *sahṛdayair hṛdayaika*.

### Verse 64

पितृगणस्य गयाशिरसि क्रिया
अथ विधाय हरेः पदपद्धतिम् ।
प्रभुरवेक्ष्य मुदं हृदि निर्भरां
स सहसा सह साधुजनैर्ययौ ॥६४॥

*pitṛ-gaṇasya gayā-śirasi kriyā*
*atha vidhāya hareḥ pada-paddhatim |*
*prabhur avekṣya mudaṁ hṛdi nirbharāṁ*
*sa sahasā saha sādhu-janair yayau ||64||*

*Word for word:* *pitṛ* — of forefathers; *gaṇasya* — for the host; *gayā* — of Gaya; *śirasi* — on the head; *kriyāḥ* — the rites; *atha* — then; *vidhāya* — having performed; *hareḥ* — of Hari; *pada* — of the feet; *paddhatim* — the print; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *avekṣya* — beholding; *mudam* — joy; *hṛdi* — in the heart; *nirbharām* — full; *saḥ* — He; *sahasā* — at once; *saha* — together with; *sādhu* — saintly; *janaiḥ* — with the people; *yayau* — went to.

**64.** Then, having performed the rites for the host of forefathers on the Gaya-shiras, the Lord, beholding the print of Hari's feet, at once — together with the saintly people — attained a joy that filled His heart.

*Note.* *Gayā-śiras*, "the head of Gaya" (by tradition, the head of the demon Gayasura). The Vishnupada is the temple at Gaya with the footprint of Vishnu in stone. According to all the biographies (Chaitanya-bhagavata, Adi 17), it is at Gaya that Nimai is first seized by the ecstasy of love; in Karnapura — at the sight of the print of Hari's feet. A play of sounds: *sahasā saha*.

### Verse 65

कथमभून्न हरेः पदपद्धतिं
समवलोकयतो मृदुतैव सः ।
इति विचिन्तयतोऽस्य दृशोर्झरो
विपुलकः पुलकश्च तदाभवत् ॥६५॥

*katham abhūn na hareḥ pada-paddhatiṁ*
*samavalokayato mṛdutaiva saḥ |*
*iti vicintayato 'sya dṛśor jharo*
*vipulakaḥ pulakaś ca tadābhavat ||65||*

*Word for word:* *katham* — how; *abhūt* — has become; *na* — not; *hareḥ* — of Hari; *pada* — of the feet; *paddhatim* — the print; *samavalokayataḥ* — while gazing on; *mṛdutā* — softness; *eva* — itself; *saḥ* — he [i.e. I]; *iti* — thus; *vicintayataḥ* — as [He] was thinking; *asya* — His; *dṛśoḥ* — from the eyes; *jharaḥ* — a torrent; *vipulakaḥ* — abundant; *pulakaḥ* — the bristling of the hairs; *ca* — and; *tadā* — then; *abhavat* — arose.

**65.** "How is it that I, gazing on the print of Hari's feet, have not become softness itself?" As He thought thus, a torrent poured from His eyes, and an abundant bristling of His hairs arose.

*Note.* The paradox: His self-reproach for "hardness of heart" is itself the first outburst of love. *Saḥ*, "he", is taken as the subject: the Lord speaks of Himself in the third person, and *mṛdutā eva*, "softness itself", is the predicate. A play of sounds: *vipulakaḥ pulakaḥ*.

### Verse 66

इति तथाविधया निजचेष्टया
सपदि मुक्तसमस्तजनप्रभुः ।
अभवदुल्लसितश्चलितुं तदा
मधुवने धुवनेन चलत्तनुः ॥६६॥

*iti tathā-vidhayā nija-ceṣṭayā*
*sapadi mukta-samasta-jana-prabhuḥ |*
*abhavad ullasitaś calituṁ tadā*
*madhu-vane dhuvanena calat-tanuḥ ||66||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *tathāvidhayā* — by such; *nija* — His own; *ceṣṭayā* — by the impulse; *sapadi* — at once; *mukta* — having left; *samasta* — all; *jana* — people; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *abhavat* — became; *ullasitaḥ* — jubilant; *calitum* — to go; *tadā* — then; *madhuvane* — to Madhuvana; *dhuvanena* — with trembling; *calat* — shaking; *tanuḥ* — [He] with a body.

**66.** Thus, by such an impulse of His own, the Lord at once left all people and became jubilant [and eager] to go then to Madhuvana, His body shaking with trembling.

*Note.* Madhuvana is one of the twelve forests of Vraja (Mathura). Nimai's impulse to go to Vrindavana after His initiation is also found in the Chaitanya-bhagavata and the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Adi 17). A play of sounds: *madhu-vane dhuvanena*.

### Verse 67

अथ दिवः समभूदशरीरिणी
सपदि गीर्नवमेघवराकृतिः ।
पुनरुपैष्यति तत्र महाप्रभुः
स्वभवनं भव नन्दयितुं पुनः ॥६७॥

*atha divaḥ samabhūd aśarīriṇī*
*sapadi gīr nava-megha-varākṛtiḥ |*
*punar upaiṣyati tatra mahāprabhuḥ*
*sva-bhavanaṁ bhava nandayituṁ punaḥ ||67||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *divaḥ* — from the sky; *samabhūt* — arose; *aśarīriṇī* — bodiless; *sapadi* — at once; *gīḥ* — a voice; *nava* — of a new; *megha* — cloud; *vara* — excellent; *ākṛtiḥ* — having the form (?); *punaḥ* — again; *upaiṣyati* — will come; *tatra* — there; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *sva* — Your own; *bhavanam* — home; *bhava* — be [there now] (?); *nandayitum* — to gladden; *punaḥ* — again.

**67.** Then at once there arose from the sky a bodiless voice, having the excellent form of a new cloud: "Mahaprabhu will come there again. [Now] be [at] Your own home, to gladden it once more."

*Note.* (?) The syntax of the voice is uneven: the third person "will come" stands beside the imperative *bhava*, "be". The "form of a new cloud" is probably the deep rumble of a rain-cloud. Mahaprabhu will indeed go to Vrindavana later, already a sannyasi (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 17). The text is the same in the Gosvami edition (GGM).

### Verse 68

इति निशम्य दिवो गिरमुत्तमां
प्रमुदितेन महाप्रभुना ततः ।
निजगृहे चलितुं महिताशयैः
प्रववृतेऽववृतेन महीसुरैः ॥६८॥

*iti niśamya divo giram uttamāṁ*
*pramuditena mahāprabhunā tataḥ |*
*nija-gṛhe calituṁ mahitāśayaiḥ*
*pravavṛte 'vavṛtena mahīsuraiḥ ||68||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *niśamya* — having heard; *divaḥ* — from the sky; *giram* — the voice; *uttamām* — supreme; *pramuditena* — by the delighted; *mahāprabhunā* — by Mahaprabhu; *tataḥ* — then; *nija* — His own; *gṛhe* — to the home; *calitum* — to go; *mahita* — of noble; *āśayaiḥ* — [with] minds; *pravavṛte* — was set out; *avavṛtena* — surrounded; *mahīsuraiḥ* — by the brahmanas.

**68.** Hearing that supreme voice from the sky, Mahaprabhu, delighted, then set out to go to His own home, surrounded by brahmanas of noble mind.

### Verse 69

अथ कियद्दिनमात्रविलम्बतो
निकटमागत आत्मज इत्यसौ ।
निजगृहान्समपूरयदुत्सवैः
सुमहतामहता हि मनोरथाः ॥६९॥

*atha kiyad-dina-mātra-vilambato*
*nikaṭam āgata ātmaja ity asau |*
*nija-gṛhān samapūrayad utsavaiḥ*
*su-mahatām ahatā hi manorathāḥ ||69||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *kiyat* — a few; *dina* — days; *mātra* — only; *vilambataḥ* — after the delay of; *nikaṭam* — near; *āgataḥ* — has come; *ātmajaḥ* — the son; *iti* — thus [learning]; *asau* — she; *nija* — her own; *gṛhān* — house; *samapūrayat* — filled; *utsavaiḥ* — with festivities; *su* — very; *mahatām* — of the great; *ahatāḥ* — unobstructed; *hi* — for; *manorathāḥ* — the desires.

**69.** Then, after a delay of only a few days, learning that her son had come near, she [Shachi] filled her house with festivities — for the desires of the very great are unobstructed.

*Note.* The edition has *sumahatāṁ mahatā* ("in the very great — by a great [desire]"); the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *sumahatām ahatā*, "the desires of the very great meet no obstacle", and so we read.

### Verse 70

मृदुमृदङ्गयशःपटहोल्लस-
त्पणवकाहलकांस्यसुमर्द्दलैः ।
युगपदेव भृशं परिताडना-
द्ध्वनिरभून्निरभूत इवोच्छ्रितः ॥७०॥

*mṛdu-mṛdaṅga-yaśaḥ-paṭaholl­asat-*
*paṇava-kāhala-kāṁsya-su-mardalaiḥ |*
*yugapad eva bhṛśaṁ paritāḍanād*
*dhvanir abhūn nirabhūta ivocchritaḥ ||70||*

*Word for word:* *mṛdu* — of soft; *mṛdaṅga* — mridangas; *yaśaḥ* — yashas (?); *paṭaha* — patahas; *ullasat* — ringing; *paṇava* — panavas; *kāhala* — kahalas; *kāṁsya* — cymbals; *su* — fine; *mardalaiḥ* — with mardalas; *yugapat* — simultaneously; *eva* — indeed; *bhṛśam* — mightily; *paritāḍanāt* — from the beating; *dhvaniḥ* — a sound; *abhūt* — arose; *nirabhūtaḥ* — unprecedented; *iva* — as if; *ucchritaḥ* — towering up.

**70.** From the mighty, simultaneous beating of soft mridangas, yashas (?), patahas, ringing panavas, kahalas, bronze cymbals and fine mardalas there arose a sound — unprecedented, as if towering up [to the sky].

*Note.* The list of instruments: *mṛdaṅga*, *paṭaha*, *paṇava* and *mardala* are drums; *kāhala* is a large horn; *kāṁsya*, bronze cymbals. (?) *Yaśaḥ* in the list is obscure: perhaps the name of an instrument, or else an epithet of the patahas ("of renown"). The text is the same in the Gosvami edition (GGM). A play of sounds: *abhūn nirabhūta*.

### Verse 71

अतिसुखेन परिप्लुतमानसा
सुरुचिरेण चिरेण तनूभुवा ।
गृहमुपेत्य ततो ददृशे मुदा
स्वजननी जननीतिषु कोविदा ॥७१॥

*ati-sukhena pariplutamānasā*
*su-rucireṇa cireṇa tanūbhuvā |*
*gṛham upetya tato dadṛśe mudā*
*sva-jananī jana-nītiṣu kovidā ||71||*

*Word for word:* *ati* — with great; *sukhena* — happiness; *paripluta* — flooded; *mānasā* — [she] with a heart; *su* — very; *rucireṇa* — by the handsome; *cireṇa* — after a long time; *tanūbhuvā* — by the son; *gṛham* — the home; *upetya* — having reached; *tataḥ* — then; *dadṛśe* — was seen; *mudā* — with joy; *sva* — His own; *jananī* — mother; *jana* — of people; *nītiṣu* — in the ways; *kovidā* — skilled.

**71.** Then, after a long time, the very handsome son reached home and joyfully beheld His mother, skilled in the ways of the world, her heart flooded with great happiness.

*Note.* Plays of sounds: *su-rucireṇa cireṇa*, *sva-jananī jana-nītiṣu*.

### Verse 72

प्रभुरथो जननीपदजं रजः
करतलेन शिरस्यदधान्मुहुः ।
अथ पपात स दण्डवदुत्सुको
भुवि नयं विनयं विदधन्मुहुः ॥७२॥

*prabhur atho jananī-padajaṁ rajaḥ*
*kara-talena śirasy adadhān muhuḥ |*
*atha papāta sa daṇḍavad utsuko*
*bhuvi nayaṁ vinayaṁ vidadhan muhuḥ ||72||*

*Word for word:* *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *atho* — then; *jananī* — of the mother; *padajam* — from the feet; *rajaḥ* — the dust; *karatalena* — with the palm; *śirasi* — on the head; *adadhāt* — placed; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *atha* — then; *papāta* — fell; *saḥ* — He; *daṇḍavat* — like a rod; *utsukaḥ* — eager; *bhuvi* — on the ground; *nayam* — propriety; *vinayam* — humility; *vidadhat* — showing; *muhuḥ* — again and again.

**72.** Then the Lord again and again took with His palm the dust from His mother's feet and placed it on His head; then, eager, He fell on the ground like a rod, again and again showing propriety and humility.

### Verse 73

सुघनं सुततं सुघनं सुततं
सहसा शुषिरैः सहसा शुषिरैः ।
अथ वाद्यमभूदथ वाद्यमभू-
द्रभसोद्यमभू रभसोद्यमभूः ॥७३॥

*sughanaṁ sutataṁ sughanaṁ sutataṁ*
*sahasā śuṣiraiḥ sahasā śuṣiraiḥ |*
*atha vādyam abhūd atha vādyam abhūr*
*rabhasodyama-bhū rabhasodyama-bhūḥ ||73||*

*Word for word:* *su* — well; *ghanam* — "solid" [instruments] (struck instruments of metal); *su* — well; *tatam* — "stretched" [instruments] (stringed); *su* — well; *ghanam* — solid; *su* — well; *tatam* — stretched; *sahasā* — all at once; *śuṣiraiḥ* — with "hollow" [instruments] (wind); *sahasā* — all at once; *śuṣiraiḥ* — with hollow; *atha* — and then; *vādyam* — music; *abhūt* — arose; *atha* — and then; *vādyam* — music; *abhūt* — arose; *rabhasa* — of impetuous; *udyama* — ardour; *bhūḥ* — the source; *rabhasa-udyama-bhūḥ* — the source of impetuous ardour.

**73.** All at once the music rang out — of fine metal instruments and fine stringed instruments, together with the wind instruments; music arose, music arose — the source of impetuous ardour, the source of impetuous ardour!

*Note.* The verse is sound-painting: each pada is repeated twice, like the echo of an orchestra. *Ghana* (solid, i.e. metal), *tata* (stretched, i.e. stringed) and *śuṣira* (hollow, i.e. wind) are classes of instruments in Indian musical theory; the fourth class is *avanaddha*, drums covered with skin (v. 70). *Sughanam sutatam* may also be heard adverbially: "densely, unbrokenly". The end of the verse is read according to the Gosvami edition (GGM): *abhūd rabhasodyama-bhū rabhasodyama-bhūḥ* (our edition has *abhūr abhasodyama-*). In the edition the verse is wrongly numbered 74.

### Verse 74

अथ काञ्चनकाञ्चननव्यलतां
मृदुलां मृदुलाञ्चितशुभ्रपटाम् ।
मुदितामुदितामथ वीक्ष्य तनुं
वसु तस्य सुतस्य ससर्ज शची ॥७४॥

*atha kāñcana-kāñcana-navya-latāṁ*
*mṛdulāṁ mṛdulāñcita-śubhra-paṭām |*
*muditām uditām atha vīkṣya tanuṁ*
*vasu tasya sutasya sasarja śacī ||74||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *kāñcana* — some (?); *kāñcana* — golden; *navya* — new; *latām* — [like] a creeper; *mṛdulām* — tender; *mṛdula* — with soft; *añcita* — adorned; *śubhra* — white; *paṭām* — with cloth; *muditām* — joyful; *uditām* — radiant; *atha* — and; *vīkṣya* — seeing; *tanum* — the body; *vasu* — wealth; *tasya* — of that; *sutasya* — of the son; *sasarja* — gave away [for the sake]; *śacī* — Shachi.

**74.** Then, seeing the body of her son — like some new golden creeper, tender, adorned with soft white cloth, joyful and radiant — Shachi gave away wealth for His sake.

*Note.* Again *yamaka*: *kāñcana-kāñcana*, *mṛdulāṁ mṛdula-*, *muditām uditām*. The first *kāñcana* is probably *kāṁcana*, "some, a certain", agreeing with *latām*.

### Verse 75

द्विजगणाय सनर्त्तकवादक-
प्रभृतयेऽपि च भिक्षुगणाय सा ।
निजसुतागमनोल्लसिता ददौ
निभृतसंभृतसम्पदिजं वसु ॥७५॥

*dvija-gaṇāya sa-nartaka-vādaka-*
*prabhṛtaye 'pi ca bhikṣu-gaṇāya sā |*
*nija-sutāgamanollasitā dadau*
*nibhṛta-saṁbhṛta-sampadijaṁ vasu ||75||*

*Word for word:* *dvija* — of brahmanas; *gaṇāya* — to the throng; *sa* — together with; *nartaka* — dancers; *vādaka* — musicians; *prabhṛtaye* — and others; *api ca* — and also; *bhikṣu* — of mendicants; *gaṇāya* — to the throng; *sā* — she; *nija* — of her own; *suta* — son; *āgamana* — by the arrival; *ullasitā* — gladdened; *dadau* — gave; *nibhṛta* — secretly; *saṁbhṛta* — stored up; *sampat* — of [her] means; *ijam* — born from; *vasu* — the wealth.

**75.** Gladdened by her son's arrival, she gave to the throng of brahmanas, together with the dancers, musicians and others, and also to the throng of mendicants, the wealth she had secretly stored up from her means.

### Verse 76

गयाया इत्येवं स्वगृहमगमद्भूरिकरुण-
प्रभुः पौषस्यान्ते सकलतनुभृत्तापशमनः ।
ततो माघस्यादौ निरवधि निजैः कीर्त्तनरसैः
प्रकाशं चावेशं भुवि विकिरति स्मानुदिवसम् ॥७६॥

*gayāyā ity evaṁ sva-gṛham agamad bhūri-karuṇa-*
*prabhuḥ pauṣasyānte sakala-tanu-bhṛt-tāpa-śamanaḥ |*
*tato māghasyādau niravadhi nijaiḥ kīrtana-rasaiḥ*
*prakāśaṁ cāveśaṁ bhuvi vikirati smānudivasam ||76||*

*Word for word:* *gayāyāḥ* — from Gaya; *iti evam* — thus; *sva* — His own; *gṛham* — home; *agamat* — returned to; *bhūri* — of abundant; *karuṇa* — compassion; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *pauṣasya* — of the month of Pausha; *ante* — at the end; *sakala* — of all; *tanubhṛt* — embodied beings; *tāpa* — the torments; *śamanaḥ* — who soothes; *tataḥ* — then; *māghasya* — of the month of Magha; *ādau* — at the beginning; *niravadhi* — without limit; *nijaiḥ* — with His own; *kīrtana* — of kirtana; *rasaiḥ* — with the rasas; *prakāśam* — the manifestation [of His divinity]; *ca* — and; *āveśam* — the inspired ecstasy; *bhuvi* — over the earth; *vikirati sma* — scattered; *anudivasam* — day after day.

**76.** Thus the Lord of abundant compassion, who soothes the torments of all embodied beings, returned home from Gaya at the end of the month of Pausha. Then, from the beginning of the month of Magha, day after day, without limit, He scattered over the earth, with the rasas of His own kirtana, the manifestation [of His divinity] and inspired ecstasy.

*Note.* The metre changes to *śikhariṇī* — the close of the sarga. Pausha is December–January, Magha January–February. **The beginning of kirtana** in Navadvipa is the opening of the Madhya-lila (Chaitanya-bhagavata, Madhya 1).

### Verse 77

इति क्षणोत्क्षिप्तसमस्तचेष्टितः
प्रतिक्षणं गायति निर्भरं मुहुः ।
पदे पदे रोदिति रोमहर्षणै-
र्विमुक्तकण्ठं करुणापयोनिधिः ॥७७॥

*iti kṣaṇotkṣipta-samasta-ceṣṭitaḥ*
*pratikṣaṇaṁ gāyati nirbharaṁ muhuḥ |*
*pade pade roditi roma-harṣaṇair*
*vimukta-kaṇṭhaṁ karuṇā-payonidhiḥ ||77||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *kṣaṇa* — in a moment; *utkṣipta* — cast off; *samasta* — all; *ceṣṭitaḥ* — [He] with activities; *pratikṣaṇam* — at every moment; *gāyati* — sings; *nirbharam* — fully; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *pade pade* — at every step; *roditi* — weeps; *roma* — of the hairs; *harṣaṇaiḥ* — with the bristling; *vimukta* — with unrestrained; *kaṇṭham* — voice; *karuṇā* — of compassion; *payonidhiḥ* — the ocean.

**77.** Thus the ocean of compassion, having in a moment cast off all [other] activities, sings at every moment, again and again, with all His heart; at every step He weeps with unrestrained voice, the hairs of His body bristling.

*Note.* The metre of the last verse is *vaṁśastha*.

*Iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahākāvye caturthaḥ sargaḥ samāptaḥ* — Thus ends the fourth sarga of the mahakavya "Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita".

---

## Sarga Five — verses 1–129

**Metre:** *praharṣiṇī* (13 syllables per pada); verse 126 — *śikhariṇī*; verse 127 — *śārdūla-vikrīḍita*; verses 128–129 — *drutavilambita*.
**Parallels:** Chaitanya-bhagavata, Madhya 1–2 ("The beginning of sankirtana").

**Contents of the passage:**
- 1–9 — after Gaya: Nimai weeps with love; Shachi asks her son for *prema*; the blessing of the brahmanas.
- 10–14 — He loses the sense of time; at the sound of the Name He falls to the ground; four months of kirtana and teaching.
- 15–21 — **the manifestation of Varaha in the house of Murari Gupta**.
- 22–31 — at Srivasa's: "Do you see Shiva, Skanda and Brahma?"; Advaita comes, and the Lord reveals Himself to Him just as He had resolved; straw between the teeth.
- 32–37 — summer comes; Gaura, radiant, goes to Srivasa.
- 38–50 — the **mahabhisheka** in the house of Srivasa: the bathing with the waters of the Ganga; the Lord sits on the throne of the Deities; light breaks through the chinks.
- 51–52 — all recognise in Him the Lord of the three worlds; a flute sounds.
- 53–60 — the Lord passes into the living quarters; the brothers adorn the house, Gadadhara prepares the bed; the town shines brighter than Ilavrita; a festival for all.
- 61–68 — Gadadhara weaves flower ornaments, dresses and anoints the Lord.
- 69–80 — the wives of the brahmanas are admitted to the Lord: "Always think of Me"; gifts; the Lord gives away cloth, chews betel, accepts offerings.
- 81–90 — Advaita's dance; **Shachi** before the Lord: "He is not your son!"; the touch of His foot, her ecstasy.
- 91–99 — a night of pastimes; the round of the houses of the four brothers; "I am leaving" — the devotees' threat; the Lord falls senseless.
- 100–110 — dawn, a long swoon; kirtana brings Him back; the effulgence withdrawn: "the summer sun has become the autumn moon".
- 111–118 — "I remember nothing"; Srivasa's jest about maya; eleven watches without sleep or food.
- 119–124 — the bath, worship in the house of Srivasa, the return to His mother.
- 125–127 — eight months (from Jyaishtha to Pausha) of dancing in the house of Srivasa.
- 128–129 — Gadadhara is constantly at the Lord's side.

### Verse 1

आगत्य स्वगृहमथ स्वकीर्त्तनाद्यैः
संरेजे निरवधि रोदनैर्विभिन्नः ।
दृष्ट्वैवंविधमनिशं सविस्मयासी-
दित्येतत्किमिति किमित्यथ प्रसूः सा ॥१॥

*āgatya sva-gṛham atha sva-kīrtanādyaiḥ*
*saṁreje niravadhi rodanair vibhinnaḥ |*
*dṛṣṭvaivaṁ-vidham aniśaṁ sa-vismayāsīd*
*ity etat kim iti kim ity atha prasūḥ sā ||1||*

*Word for word:* *āgatya* — having come; *sva* — His own; *gṛham* — to the home; *atha* — then; *sva* — with His own; *kīrtana* — kirtana; *ādyaiḥ* — and the like; *saṁreje* — shone; *niravadhi* — without limit; *rodanaiḥ* — by sobs; *vibhinnaḥ* — shaken; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *evaṁvidham* — such; *aniśam* — constantly; *sa* — with; *vismayā* — wonder; *āsīt* — was; *iti* — thus; *etat* — this; *kim* — what; *iti* — thus; *kim* — what; *iti* — thus; *atha* — and; *prasūḥ* — the mother; *sā* — she.

**1.** Having then come to His home, He shone without limit with His kirtana and the like, shaken by sobs. Seeing Him constantly so, His mother was filled with wonder: "What is this? What is it?"

### Verse 2

यामिन्यां शयितवतः शची कदाचित्
पुत्रस्य प्रथममवेक्ष्य रोदनं सा ।
ब्रूहीत्थं किमहह तात रोदिषि त्वं
साशङ्कं तमिति जगाद भूरिभाग्या ॥२॥

*yāminyāṁ śayitavataḥ śacī kadācit*
*putrasya prathamam avekṣya rodanaṁ sā |*
*brūhītthaṁ kim ahaha tāta rodiṣi tvaṁ*
*sāśaṅkaṁ tam iti jagāda bhūri-bhāgyā ||2||*

*Word for word:* *yāminyām* — at night; *śayitavataḥ* — who was lying [in bed]; *śacī* — Shachi; *kadācit* — once; *putrasya* — of the son; *prathamam* — for the first time; *avekṣya* — having seen; *rodanam* — the weeping; *sā* — she; *brūhi* — tell; *ittham* — so; *kim* — why; *ahaha* — ah; *tāta* — O dear child; *rodiṣi* — weep; *tvam* — You; *sa* — with; *āśaṅkam* — anxiety; *tam* — to Him; *iti* — thus; *jagāda* — said; *bhūri* — of great; *bhāgyā* — [she] of fortune.

**2.** Once at night Shachi, rich in great fortune, seeing for the first time the weeping of her son as He lay [in bed], said to Him anxiously: "Ah, O dear child, tell me — why do You weep so?"

### Verse 3

तच्छ्रुत्वा न किमपि चेदुवाच नाथः
प्रेमार्द्रो नयनजलाभिषिक्तसर्व्वगात्रः ।
सात्यन्तं निरवधि चिन्तिता तदासी-
त्प्रेमेत्येतदपि विवेद दैवयोगात् ॥३॥

*tac chrutvā na kim api ced uvāca nāthaḥ*
*premārdro nayana-jalābhiṣikta-sarva-gātraḥ |*
*sātyantaṁ niravadhi cintitā tadāsīt*
*premety etad api viveda daiva-yogāt ||3||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — that; *śrutvā* — having heard; *na* — not; *kim api* — anything; *cet* — when; *uvāca* — answered; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *prema* — by love; *ārdraḥ* — softened; *nayana* — of the eyes; *jala* — by the water; *abhiṣikta* — bathed; *sarva* — [with] the whole; *gātraḥ* — body; *sā* — she; *atyantam* — extremely; *niravadhi* — boundlessly; *cintitā* — anxious; *tadā* — then; *āsīt* — was; *prema* — "[it is] prema"; *iti* — thus; *etat* — this; *api* — too; *viveda* — understood; *daiva* — of providence; *yogāt* — by the dispensation.

**3.** When, hearing that, the Lord answered nothing — softened by love, His whole body bathed in the water of His eyes — she became extremely, boundlessly anxious; and then, by the dispensation of providence, she understood this too: "It is *prema*, love."

### Verse 4

ज्ञात्वैतद्विमलमनाः शची तनूजं
सार्द्राक्षी विनयपरा भृशं ययाचे ।
मह्यं यद्धनमखिलं प्रयच्छसि त्वं
प्रेमाख्यं किमु न ददासि साम्प्रतं तत् ॥४॥

*jñātvaitad vimala-manāḥ śacī tanūjaṁ*
*sārdrākṣī vinaya-parā bhṛśaṁ yayāce |*
*mahyaṁ yad dhanam akhilaṁ prayacchasi tvaṁ*
*premākhyaṁ kimu na dadāsi sāmprataṁ tat ||4||*

*Word for word:* *jñātvā* — having understood; *etat* — this; *vimala* — [with] a pure; *manāḥ* — heart; *śacī* — Shachi; *tanūjam* — the son; *sa* — with; *ārdra* — moist; *akṣī* — [she] with eyes; *vinaya* — to humility; *parā* — devoted; *bhṛśam* — earnestly; *yayāce* — begged; *mahyam* — to me; *yat* — which; *dhanam* — wealth; *akhilam* — all; *prayacchasi* — give; *tvam* — You; *prema* — prema; *ākhyam* — called; *kimu* — why; *na* — not; *dadāsi* — give; *sāmpratam* — now; *tat* — that.

**4.** Understanding this, pure-hearted Shachi, her eyes moist, humbly and earnestly begged her son: "You give me all the wealth [You have] — why then do You not now give [me] that [wealth] called *prema*?"

### Verse 5

देवानामविदितमेतदत्यलभ्यं
प्रेमेदं यदवगतं त्वया गयायाम् ।
दीनायै तदिह हि मे प्रयच्छ तात
स्नेहस्ते यदि मयि तिष्ठति क्षणञ्च ॥५॥

*devānām aviditam etad aty-alabhyaṁ*
*premedaṁ yad avagataṁ tvayā gayāyām |*
*dīnāyai tad iha hi me prayaccha tāta*
*snehas te yadi mayi tiṣṭhati kṣaṇañ ca ||5||*

*Word for word:* *devānām* — to the gods; *aviditam* — unknown; *etat* — this; *ati* — exceedingly; *alabhyam* — hard to attain; *prema* — love; *idam* — this; *yat* — which; *avagatam* — obtained; *tvayā* — by You; *gayāyām* — at Gaya; *dīnāyai* — to the wretched; *tat* — that; *iha* — here; *hi* — indeed; *me* — to me; *prayaccha* — give; *tāta* — O dear child; *snehaḥ* — affection; *te* — Your; *yadi* — if; *mayi* — for me; *tiṣṭhati* — remains; *kṣaṇam* — for a moment; *ca* — even.

**5.** "This love which You obtained at Gaya — unknown to the gods, exceedingly hard to attain — give it here to me, a wretched woman, O dear child, if Your affection for me remains even for a moment."

### Verse 6

इत्यस्या गिरमधिगम्य गौरचन्द्रः
स्नेहार्द्रः प्रतिवचनं ददौ जनन्यै ।
तन्मातस्तव भविता चिरेण नूनं
यत्ते स्याद्गुरुतरवैष्णवानुकम्पा ॥६॥

*ity asyā giram adhigamya gauracandraḥ*
*snehārdraḥ prativacanaṁ dadau jananyai |*
*tan mātas tava bhavitā cireṇa nūnaṁ*
*yat te syād gurutara-vaiṣṇavānukampā ||6||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *asyāḥ* — her; *giram* — speech; *adhigamya* — having heard; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra; *sneha* — by affection; *ārdraḥ* — softened; *prativacanam* — a reply; *dadau* — gave; *jananyai* — to the mother; *tat* — that; *mātaḥ* — O Mother; *tava* — yours; *bhavitā* — will be; *cireṇa* — in time; *nūnam* — surely; *yat* — when; *te* — to you; *syāt* — there will be; *gurutara* — very great; *vaiṣṇava* — of the Vaishnavas; *anukampā* — the mercy.

**6.** Hearing her words thus, Gaurachandra, softened by affection, gave His mother a reply: "O Mother, it will surely be yours in time, when the very great mercy of the Vaishnavas comes to you."

*Note.* An important theological motif: even the mother of God receives prema not from Him directly but by the mercy of His devotees. Cf. Chaitanya-bhagavata, Madhya 22 ("The forgiveness of Shachidevi"): Shachi receives forgiveness for her offence against Advaita.

### Verse 7

तच्छ्रुत्वा मुदमधिकां ययौ ततः सा
तन्नूनं मम भवितेति हृष्टचित्ता ।
गौराङ्गोऽपि तदधिगम्य मातृचित्तं
विप्रेन्द्रान् विनयपरो जगाद भूयः ॥७॥

*tac chrutvā mudam adhikāṁ yayau tataḥ sā*
*tan nūnaṁ mama bhaviteti hṛṣṭa-cittā |*
*gaurāṅgo 'pi tad adhigamya mātṛ-cittaṁ*
*viprendrān vinaya-paro jagāda bhūyaḥ ||7||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — that; *śrutvā* — having heard; *mudam* — joy; *adhikām* — great; *yayau* — attained; *tataḥ* — then; *sā* — she; *tat* — that; *nūnam* — surely; *mama* — mine; *bhavitā* — will be; *iti* — thus [thinking]; *hṛṣṭa* — [with] a delighted; *cittā* — heart; *gaurāṅgaḥ* — Gauranga; *api* — and; *tat* — that; *adhigamya* — perceiving; *mātṛ* — of the mother; *cittam* — the heart; *vipra* — of brahmanas; *indrān* — to the best; *vinaya* — to humility; *paraḥ* — devoted; *jagāda* — spoke; *bhūyaḥ* — further.

**7.** Hearing that, she attained great joy, her heart delighted: "Then it will surely be mine!" And Gauranga, perceiving His mother's heart, humbly spoke further to the best of the brahmanas:

### Verse 8

प्रेमायं निरवधि मृग्यते जनन्या
भक्तिश्च प्रभुचरणे गरीयसीयम् ।
ते स्यातां सपदि यथाशिषो भवद्भि-
र्युज्यन्तां तदनु तथोचुरेवमेते ॥८॥

*premāyaṁ niravadhi mṛgyate jananyā*
*bhaktiś ca prabhu-caraṇe garīyasīyam |*
*te syātāṁ sapadi yathāśiṣo bhavadbhir*
*yujyantāṁ tad anu tathocur evam ete ||8||*

*Word for word:* *premā* — love; *ayam* — this; *niravadhi* — boundlessly; *mṛgyate* — is sought; *jananyā* — by [My] mother; *bhaktiḥ* — devotion; *ca* — and; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *caraṇe* — to the feet; *garīyasī* — most weighty; *iyam* — this; *te* — these two; *syātām* — may be; *sapadi* — soon; *yathā* — so that; *āśiṣaḥ* — blessings; *bhavadbhiḥ* — by you; *yujyantām* — let be bestowed; *tat anu* — after that; *tathā* — accordingly; *ūcuḥ* — spoke; *evam* — thus; *ete* — they.

**8.** "My mother seeks this love boundlessly, and this most weighty devotion to the feet of the Lord. Let blessings be bestowed by you, so that both may soon be hers." And thereupon they spoke accordingly.

### Verse 9

इत्येवं क्वचन रुदन्विलोचनाभ्यां
धाराणां शतशतमादधात्युरःसु ।
श्लेष्माणं क्षिपति मुहुर्मुहुः स्थविष्ठं
नासाभ्यां भुवि विलुठन्क्वचित्स नाथः ॥९॥

*ity evaṁ kvacana rudan vilocanābhyāṁ*
*dhārāṇāṁ śata-śatam ādadhāty uraḥsu |*
*śleṣmāṇaṁ kṣipati muhur muhuḥ sthaviṣṭhaṁ*
*nāsābhyāṁ bhuvi viluṭhan kvacit sa nāthaḥ ||9||*

*Word for word:* *iti evam* — thus; *kvacana* — sometimes; *rudan* — weeping; *vilocanābhyām* — from the eyes; *dhārāṇām* — of streams; *śata-śatam* — hundreds upon hundreds; *ādadhāti* — pours; *uraḥsu* — on the breast; *śleṣmāṇam* — mucus; *kṣipati* — expels; *muhuḥ muhuḥ* — again and again; *sthaviṣṭham* — copious; *nāsābhyām* — from the nose; *bhuvi* — on the ground; *viluṭhan* — rolling; *kvacit* — sometimes; *saḥ* — He; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord.

**9.** Thus the Lord, sometimes weeping, would pour from His eyes hundreds upon hundreds of streams on His breast; sometimes, rolling on the ground, He would again and again expel copious mucus from His nose.

*Note.* Kavi Karnapura is not afraid of the "unlovely" bodily details of ecstasy — tears, mucus from the nose, rolling on the ground. This is deliberate realism: the Chaitanya-bhagavata and the Chaitanya-charitamrita write in the same way. *Uraḥsu* is plural, literally "on the breasts" — a poetic plural, or "on the breasts [of those beside Him]".

### Verse 10

प्रत्यूषप्रभृति दिनं समस्तमेव
प्रेमाश्रुप्रचुररवै रुदन्विनीय ।
यामिन्या भवति सति प्रभुः प्रबोधे
वैकल्याद्दिनमिति तर्कयाम्बभूव ॥१०॥

*pratyūṣa-prabhṛti dinaṁ samastam eva*
*premāśru-pracura-ravai rudan vinīya |*
*yāminyā bhavati sati prabhuḥ prabodhe*
*vaikalyād dinam iti tarkayāmbabhūva ||10||*

*Word for word:* *pratyūṣa* — from dawn; *prabhṛti* — onward; *dinam* — the day; *samastam* — whole; *eva* — indeed; *prema* — of love; *aśru* — with tears; *pracura* — abundant; *ravaiḥ* — with cries; *rudan* — weeping; *vinīya* — having passed; *yāminyā* — night (?); *bhavati sati* — [when] it had come; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *prabodhe* — on awakening; *vaikalyāt* — from agitation; *dinam* — day; *iti* — thus; *tarkayāmbabhūva* — supposed.

**10.** Having passed the whole day from dawn onward weeping, with loud cries and abundant tears of love, the Lord, when night had come and He awoke [to outer consciousness], in His agitation supposed that it was day.

*Note.* *Yāminyā bhavati sati* is irregular; the sense of a locative absolute is required: "when night had come".

### Verse 11

सन्ध्यायां किमपि रुदन्विमुक्तकण्ठः
प्रातः स्यात्कथमपि चेद्बहिःप्रबोधः ।
तन्नक्तं व्रजति कियत्कदेति गौरो
वैकल्याद्वदति न तस्य कालभेदः ॥११॥

*sandhyāyāṁ kim api rudan vimukta-kaṇṭhaḥ*
*prātaḥ syāt katham api ced bahiḥ-prabodhaḥ |*
*tan naktaṁ vrajati kiyat kadeti gauro*
*vaikalyād vadati na tasya kāla-bhedaḥ ||11||*

*Word for word:* *sandhyāyām* — at twilight; *kim api* — somehow; *rudan* — weeping; *vimukta* — [with] unrestrained; *kaṇṭhaḥ* — voice; *prātaḥ* — in the morning; *syāt* — there should be; *katham api* — somehow; *cet* — if; *bahiḥ* — outer; *prabodhaḥ* — consciousness; *tat* — then; *naktam* — the night; *vrajati* — is passing; *kiyat* — how much; *kadā* — when; *iti* — thus; *gauraḥ* — Gaura; *vaikalyāt* — from agitation; *vadati* — says; *na* — not; *tasya* — for Him; *kāla* — of time; *bhedaḥ* — distinction.

**11.** At twilight He wept somehow with unrestrained voice; and if in the morning outer consciousness somehow returned to Him, Gaura in His agitation would ask: "So the night is passing? How much [is left]? When [will it end]?" For Him there was no distinction of time.

*Note.* In the edition the first pada is a syllable short of the metre; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *kim api rudan vimukta-kaṇṭhaḥ* ("somehow weeping with unrestrained voice"), and the missing *rudan* is restored.

### Verse 12

नामैकं श्रवणपथं यदैव गच्छे-
त्तत्सोऽयं भुवि विलुठन्बलप्रकामम् ।
द्राघिष्ठैः श्वसनसमीरणैः सकम्पै-
र्नेत्रान्तप्रसृमरधारया च रेजे ॥१२॥

*nāmaikaṁ śravaṇa-pathaṁ yadaiva gacchet*
*tat so 'yaṁ bhuvi viluṭhan bala-prakāmam |*
*drāghiṣṭhaiḥ śvasana-samīraṇaiḥ sa-kampair*
*netrānta-prasṛmara-dhārayā ca reje ||12||*

*Word for word:* *nāma* — Name; *ekam* — a single; *śravaṇa* — of hearing; *patham* — the path; *yadā eva* — as soon as; *gacchet* — entered; *tat* — then; *saḥ* — He; *ayam* — this; *bhuvi* — on the ground; *viluṭhan* — rolling; *bala* — of strength; *prakāmam* — to the full; *drāghiṣṭhaiḥ* — with very long; *śvasana* — of breath; *samīraṇaiḥ* — with the blasts; *sa* — with; *kampaiḥ* — trembling; *netra* — of the eyes; *anta* — from the corners; *prasṛmara* — flowing forth; *dhārayā* — with a stream; *ca* — and; *reje* — shone.

**12.** As soon as a single Name entered the path of His hearing, He would roll on the ground with all His strength, and shone with long, trembling sighs and with a stream flowing from the corners of His eyes.

### Verse 13

सोत्कण्ठं निरवधि कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्णे-
त्याजल्पन्क्वचन विभिन्नसन्नकण्ठः ।
हर्षोद्भवैस्तनुरुहसञ्चयैर्विभाति
प्रायोऽयं प्रतिदिनमेवमेव भूत्वा ॥१३॥

*sotkaṇṭhaṁ niravadhi kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇety*
*ājalpan kvacana vibhinna-sanna-kaṇṭhaḥ |*
*harṣodbhavais tanuruha-sañcayair vibhāti*
*prāyo 'yaṁ pratidinam evam eva bhūtvā ||13||*

*Word for word:* *sa* — with; *utkaṇṭham* — longing; *niravadhi* — without end; *kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa* — "Krishna, Krishna, Krishna"; *iti* — thus; *ājalpan* — murmuring; *kvacana* — sometimes; *vibhinna* — [with] broken; *sanna* — choked; *kaṇṭhaḥ* — voice; *harṣa* — from joy; *udbhavaiḥ* — risen; *tanuruha* — of the hairs of the body; *sañcayaiḥ* — with the masses; *vibhāti* — shines; *prāyaḥ* — almost; *ayam* — He; *pratidinam* — every day; *evam eva* — just so; *bhūtvā* — being.

**13.** Murmuring with longing, without end, "Krishna, Krishna, Krishna!", sometimes with a broken and choked voice, He shone with the hairs of His body standing on end in masses from joy. Such He was almost every day.

### Verse 14

स स्नात्वा दिवसमुखे करोति पूजा-
मश्नाति प्रतिदिवसं मुदा निवेद्य ।
सद्विप्रानपि परिपाठयन्नुदारान्
माघाद्यानिति चतुरो निनाय मासान् ॥१४॥

*sa snātvā divasa-mukhe karoti pūjām*
*aśnāti pratidivasaṁ mudā nivedya |*
*sad-viprān api paripāṭhayann udārān*
*māghādyān iti caturo nināya māsān ||14||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — He; *snātvā* — having bathed; *divasa* — of the day; *mukhe* — at the beginning; *karoti* — performs; *pūjām* — worship; *aśnāti* — eats; *pratidivasam* — every day; *mudā* — with joy; *nivedya* — having offered [to God]; *sat* — worthy; *viprān* — brahmanas; *api* — also; *paripāṭhayan* — teaching; *udārān* — noble; *māgha* — with Magha; *ādyān* — beginning; *iti* — thus; *caturaḥ* — four; *nināya* — spent; *māsān* — months.

**14.** Bathing at the beginning of the day, He performed worship; every day He ate with joy what had been offered [to God]; and teaching also the noble and worthy brahmanas, He thus spent four months, beginning with Magha.

*Note.* The four months are Magha, Phalguna, Chaitra and Vaishakha (January–May).

### Verse 15

प्रेमार्द्रः सपुलकमेकदा मुरारे-
र्वैद्यस्यालयमगमत्कृपासमुद्रः ।
तत्रासौ सपदि निवेश्य देवगेहे
संभिन्नो नयनजलैः समध्यवात्सीत् ॥१५॥

*premārdraḥ sa-pulakam ekadā murārer*
*vaidyasyālayam agamat kṛpā-samudraḥ |*
*tatrāsau sapadi niveśya deva-gehe*
*saṁbhinno nayana-jalaiḥ samadhyavātsīt ||15||*

*Word for word:* *prema* — by love; *ārdraḥ* — softened; *sa* — with; *pulakam* — hairs standing on end; *ekadā* — once; *murāreḥ* — of Murari; *vaidyasya* — of the physician; *ālayam* — to the house; *agamat* — went; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *samudraḥ* — the ocean; *tatra* — there; *asau* — He; *sapadi* — at once; *niveśya* — having entered; *deva* — of God; *gehe* — in the house; *saṁbhinnaḥ* — convulsed; *nayana* — of the eyes; *jalaiḥ* — with the waters; *samadhyavātsīt* — settled.

**15.** Once the ocean of mercy, softened by love, His hairs standing on end, went to the house of Murari the physician. There He at once entered the shrine of the house and settled there, convulsed with tears.

*Note.* Murari Gupta is a physician (*vaidya*), Nimai's boyhood friend and the author of the earliest biography (the Kadacha). The episode of Varaha's manifestation in Murari's house is found in the Chaitanya-bhagavata (Madhya 3) and in Murari Gupta himself.

### Verse 16

आश्चर्यं दशनयुगेन गां बलीया-
न्वाराहं वपुरिदमावहन्क एषः ।
मर्म्मस्पृक्तुदति महामहीध्रतुल्यो
भूयोऽसाविति निगदन्ससर्प पश्चात् ॥१६॥

*āścaryaṁ daśana-yugena gāṁ balīyān*
*vārāhaṁ vapur idam āvahan ka eṣaḥ |*
*marma-spṛk tudati mahā-mahīdhra-tulyo*
*bhūyo 'sāv iti nigadan sasarpa paścāt ||16||*

*Word for word:* *āścaryam* — a wonder; *daśana* — of tusks; *yugena* — with the pair; *gām* — the earth; *balīyān* — mighty; *vārāham* — of a boar; *vapuḥ* — the body; *idam* — this; *āvahan* — bearing; *kaḥ* — who; *eṣaḥ* — this; *marma* — the vitals; *spṛk* — reaching; *tudati* — pierces; *mahā* — a great; *mahīdhra* — mountain; *tulyaḥ* — like; *bhūyaḥ* — ever more; *asau* — He; *iti* — thus; *nigadan* — saying; *sasarpa* — crept; *paścāt* — backwards.

**16.** "What a wonder! Who is this mighty One who bears this boar's body, [holding up] the earth on a pair of tusks? Like a great mountain, He pierces [Me] ever more, reaching to the very vitals!" Saying this, He crept backwards.

*Note.* **The manifestation of Varaha:** Mahaprabhu takes on the mood of Varaha, the boar avatara who raised the Earth from the waters on His tusks. The edition has *bhūye*; we read *bhūyo* ("ever more, again") with the Gosvami edition (GGM).

### Verse 17

इत्युक्त्वा सपदि तथा तदीयभावं
संगृह्णन्भुवि भुजजानुभिर्व्रजन्सः ।
घूर्णाभिस्तरलतरेण दृग्युगेन
द्राघिष्ठामपि विदधे च हूंकृतिं ताम् ॥१७॥

*ity uktvā sapadi tathā tadīya-bhāvaṁ*
*saṅgṛhṇan bhuvi bhuja-jānubhir vrajan saḥ |*
*ghūrṇābhis taralatareṇa dṛg-yugena*
*drāghiṣṭhām api vidadhe ca hūṅkṛtiṁ tām ||17||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *uktvā* — having said; *sapadi* — at once; *tathā* — so; *tadīya* — His [Varaha's]; *bhāvam* — mood; *saṅgṛhṇan* — taking on; *bhuvi* — on the ground; *bhuja* — on the arms; *jānubhiḥ* — and knees; *vrajan* — moving; *saḥ* — He; *ghūrṇābhiḥ* — with rollings; *taralatareṇa* — very restless; *dṛk* — of eyes; *yugena* — with the pair; *drāghiṣṭhām* — very long; *api* — also; *vidadhe* — made; *ca* — and; *hūṅkṛtim* — the roar "hum"; *tām* — that.

**17.** Having said this, He at once took on His mood: moving over the ground on His arms and knees, His very restless eyes rolling, He also let out that long roar, "Hum!"

### Verse 18

दन्ताग्रैः सपदि स पैत्तलाम्बुपात्रं
धृत्वासौ बहुभयमुन्मुखोऽतिदूरे ।
संक्षिप्यंस्तदनु मुरारिगुप्तमूचे
रूपं मे सहजमुदीरयेति शश्वत् ॥१८॥

*dantāgraiḥ sapadi sa paittalāmbu-pātraṁ*
*dhṛtvāsau bahu-bhayam unmukho 'ti-dūre |*
*saṅkṣipyaṁs tad-anu murāri-guptam ūce*
*rūpaṁ me sahajam udīrayeti śaśvat ||18||*

*Word for word:* *danta* — of the teeth; *agraiḥ* — with the tips; *sapadi* — at once; *saḥ* — He; *paittala* — brass; *ambu* — for water; *pātram* — a vessel; *dhṛtvā* — having seized; *asau* — He; *bahu* — great; *bhayam* — fear [inspiring]; *unmukhaḥ* — raising His head; *ati* — very; *dūre* — far; *saṅkṣipyan* — flinging; *tat anu* — after that; *murāri-guptam* — to Murari Gupta; *ūce* — said; *rūpam* — the form; *me* — My; *sahajam* — natural; *udīraya* — describe; *iti* — thus; *śaśvat* — insistently.

**18.** At once He seized a brass water-vessel with the tips of His teeth and, inspiring great fear, raised His head and flung it far away. After that He said insistently to Murari Gupta: "Describe My natural form!"

*Note.* The vessel lifted with the teeth is the image of Varaha raising the Earth on His tusks.

### Verse 19

तच्छ्रुत्वा भुवि निपतन्स भीतभीतो
नो विद्मो वयमिह ते स्वरूपमेतत् ।
आत्मानं स्वयमेवमात्मनैव वेत्थे-
त्यूचेऽसौ प्रतिवचनैश्च गीतयोक्तैः ॥१९॥

*tac chrutvā bhuvi nipatan sa bhīta-bhīto*
*no vidmo vayam iha te svarūpam etat |*
*ātmānaṁ svayam evam ātmanaiva vettha*
*ity ūce 'sau prativacanaiś ca gītayoktaiḥ ||19||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — that; *śrutvā* — having heard; *bhuvi* — on the ground; *nipatan* — falling; *saḥ* — he; *bhīta-bhītaḥ* — terror-stricken; *na u* — not; *vidmaḥ* — know; *vayam* — we; *iha* — here; *te* — Your; *svarūpam* — own form; *etat* — this; *ātmānam* — Yourself; *svayam* — Yourself; *evam* — thus; *ātmanā* — by Yourself; *eva* — alone; *vettha* — know; *iti* — thus; *ūce* — said; *asau* — he; *prativacanaiḥ* — with a reply; *ca* — and; *gītayā* — by the Gita; *uktaiḥ* — spoken.

**19.** Hearing that, Murari fell to the ground, terror-stricken: "We do not know this own form of Yours. You Yourself know Yourself thus, by Yourself alone." So he answered, with words spoken in the Gita.

*Note.* Murari quotes the Bhagavad-gita (10.15): *svayam evātmanātmānaṁ vettha tvaṁ puruṣottama* — "You Yourself know Yourself by Yourself, O Supreme Person."

### Verse 20

भूयोऽसौ स हसितवन्मधुद्रवैस्तैः
प्रत्यूचे प्रतिवचनैः प्रभुस्तमेनम् ।
वेदोऽयं ननु किमु वेत्त्ययं विमुग्ध-
संमोहादवचिनुतेऽन्धवत्स नित्यम् ॥२०॥

*bhūyo 'sau sa hasitavan madhu-dravais taiḥ*
*pratyūce prativacanaiḥ prabhus tam enam |*
*vedo 'yaṁ nanu kimu vetty ayaṁ vimugdha-*
*saṁmohād avacinute 'ndhavat sa nityam ||20||*

*Word for word:* *bhūyaḥ* — again; *asau* — He; *saḥ* — that; *hasitavat* — smiling; *madhu* — of honey; *dravaiḥ* — moist; *taiḥ* — with those; *pratyūce* — replied; *prativacanaiḥ* — with words; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *tam enam* — to him; *vedaḥ* — the Veda; *ayam* — this; *nanu* — indeed; *kimu* — what; *vetti* — knows; *ayam* — it; *vimugdha* — of the bewildered; *saṁmohāt* — out of confusion; *avacinute* — gropes; *andhavat* — like a blind man; *saḥ* — it; *nityam* — eternally.

**20.** Then the Lord, smiling, replied to him in words moist with honey: "What, indeed, does this Veda know? Out of bewildered confusion it eternally gropes [for Me] like a blind man."

### Verse 21

इत्युक्त्वा श्रुतिगदितं निपठ्य भूयः
सोत्प्रासं स परिहसन्नुवाच नाथः ।
वेदानामिह खलु नास्ति शक्तिरेषा
ज्ञातुं मामिति निगदन्ययौ स्वगेहम् ॥२१॥

*ity uktvā śruti-gaditaṁ nipaṭhya bhūyaḥ*
*sotprāsaṁ sa parihasann uvāca nāthaḥ |*
*vedānām iha khalu nāsti śaktir eṣā*
*jñātuṁ mām iti nigadan yayau sva-geham ||21||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *uktvā* — having spoken; *śruti* — by the Shruti; *gaditam* — what is declared; *nipaṭhya* — having recited; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *sa* — with; *utprāsam* — mockery; *saḥ* — He; *parihasan* — laughing; *uvāca* — said; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *vedānām* — of the Vedas; *iha* — here; *khalu* — truly; *na asti* — there is not; *śaktiḥ* — power; *eṣā* — this; *jñātum* — to know; *mām* — Me; *iti* — thus; *nigadan* — saying; *yayau* — went; *sva* — to His own; *geham* — home.

**21.** Having spoken thus and recited once more what the Shruti declares, the Lord, laughing, said with mockery: "Truly, the Vedas have no such power to know Me." And saying this, He went to His own home.

*Note.* Which text of the Shruti is meant is not specified. A probable parallel is Taittiriya Upanishad 2.4: *yato vāco nivartante aprāpya manasā saha* ("from which words turn back, together with the mind, without reaching it").

### Verse 22

अन्येद्युः स्वगृहमभि क्षपेशकोटि-
श्रीयुक्तः परपरभागभाक्प्रतीकः ।
श्रीवासं निजपुरतः स्थितं महस्वा-
नभ्यूचे सह बलहुङ्कृतैर्वचोभिः ॥२२॥

*anyedyuḥ sva-gṛham abhi kṣapeśa-koṭi-*
*śrī-yuktaḥ para-para-bhāga-bhāk pratīkaḥ |*
*śrīvāsaṁ nija-purataḥ sthitaṁ mahasvān*
*abhyūce saha bala-huṅkṛtair vacobhiḥ ||22||*

*Word for word:* *anyedyuḥ* — on the next day; *sva* — His own; *gṛham abhi* — at the house; *kṣapeśa* — of moons; *koṭi* — of millions; *śrī* — with the beauty; *yuktaḥ* — endowed; *para-para* — the very highest; *bhāga* — excellence; *bhāk* — possessing; *pratīkaḥ* — [with] a form; *śrīvāsam* — to Srivasa; *nija* — Himself; *purataḥ* — before; *sthitam* — standing; *mahasvān* — radiant; *abhyūce* — spoke; *saha* — with; *bala* — mighty; *huṅkṛtaiḥ* — with roars; *vacobhiḥ* — with words.

**22.** The next day, at His own house, He — endowed with the beauty of millions of moons, His form possessing the very highest excellence, all radiant — spoke to Srivasa, who stood before Him, in words accompanied by mighty roars:

*Note.* *Kṣapeśa*, "lord of the night", is the moon.

### Verse 23

त्वं भोः पश्यसि न किमत्र पञ्चवक्त्रान्
षड्वक्त्रानपि च चतुर्मुखान्समेतान् ।
सोऽप्यूचे न खलु विलोक्यते मयासौ
षड्वक्त्रप्रभृतिजनः समागतोऽयम् ॥२३॥

*tvaṁ bhoḥ paśyasi na kim atra pañca-vaktrān*
*ṣaḍ-vaktrān api ca catur-mukhān sametān |*
*so 'py ūce na khalu vilokyate mayāsau*
*ṣaḍ-vaktra-prabhṛti-janaḥ samāgato 'yam ||23||*

*Word for word:* *tvam* — you; *bhoḥ* — O [friend] (hey); *paśyasi* — see; *na kim* — do not; *atra* — here; *pañca* — five; *vaktrān* — the faced ones; *ṣaṭ* — six; *vaktrān* — the faced ones; *api ca* — and also; *catuḥ* — four; *mukhān* — the faced ones; *sametān* — assembled; *saḥ* — he; *api* — for his part; *ūce* — said; *na khalu* — not at all; *vilokyate* — is seen; *mayā* — by me; *asau* — this; *ṣaṭ* — six; *vaktra* — faced; *prabhṛti* — and the rest; *janaḥ* — company; *samāgataḥ* — assembled; *ayam* — this.

**23.** "Hey, do you not see the five-faced, the six-faced and the four-faced assembled here?" And he replied: "No, I do not see this company assembled here — the six-faced and the rest."

*Note.* The five-faced is Shiva, the six-faced Kartikeya (Skanda), the four-faced Brahma: the gods have come to see the Lord. Compare 2.86, where the invisible guests in the house are seen by Shachi alone.

### Verse 24

इत्युक्ते सति तदनूपतस्थिवांसं
नाम्ना श्रीपतिमनुजं ददर्श विप्रः ।
सोऽभ्येत्य श्रुतिनिकटेषु धीरमूचे-
ऽद्वैतस्यागमनकथां प्रभुं दिदृक्षोः ॥२४॥

*ity ukte sati tad-anūpatasthivāṁsaṁ*
*nāmnā śrīpatim anujaṁ dadarśa vipraḥ |*
*so 'bhyetya śruti-nikaṭeṣu dhīram ūce*
*'dvaitasyāgamana-kathāṁ prabhuṁ didṛkṣoḥ ||24||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *ukte sati* — when it had been said; *tat* — behind him; *anūpatasthivāṁsam* — standing; *nāmnā* — by name; *śrīpatim* — Shripati; *anujam* — the younger brother; *dadarśa* — saw; *vipraḥ* — the brahmana; *saḥ* — he; *abhyetya* — having approached; *śruti* — to the ears; *nikaṭeṣu* — close; *dhīram* — softly; *ūce* — told; *advaitasya* — of Advaita; *āgamana* — of the arrival; *kathām* — the news; *prabhum* — the Lord; *didṛkṣoḥ* — wishing to see.

**24.** When this had been said, the brahmana saw his younger brother, Shripati by name, standing behind him. Shripati came up and softly, close to his ear, told him the news that Advaita had arrived, wishing to see the Lord.

*Note.* Shripati is one of Srivasa's brothers (Srivasa, Sri Rama, Shripati, Shrinidhi). The arrival of Advaita: Chaitanya-bhagavata, Madhya 6 ("The meeting with Sri Advaita").

### Verse 25

आचार्यः किमिह समागतोऽस्ति तस्यै
तज्ज्ञात्वा सपदि समुत्थितोऽजिरेषु ।
आगत्य प्रतिपदहूंकृतां स वाणीं
प्रत्यूचे महितमहामहःसमूहः ॥२५॥

*ācāryaḥ kim iha samāgato 'sti tasyai*
*taj jñātvā sapadi samutthito 'jireṣu |*
*āgatya pratipada-hūṅkṛtāṁ sa vāṇīṁ*
*pratyūce mahita-mahā-mahaḥ-samūhaḥ ||25||*

*Word for word:* *ācāryaḥ* — the Acharya; *kim* — whether; *iha* — here; *samāgataḥ* — come; *asti* — has; *tasyai* — (?); *tat* — that; *jñātvā* — having learned; *sapadi* — at once; *samutthitaḥ* — risen; *ajireṣu* — into the courtyard; *āgatya* — having come; *pratipada* — at every word; *hūṅkṛtām* — with roars; *saḥ* — He; *vāṇīm* — speech; *pratyūce* — spoke in reply; *mahita* — of glorious; *mahā* — great; *mahaḥ* — effulgence; *samūhaḥ* — a mass.

**25.** "Has the Acharya come here?" Learning that it was so, He at once rose, came out into the courtyard and — a mass of glorious, great effulgence — made reply in words broken by a roar at every one:

*Note.* (?) *Tasyai* (dative feminine) is unclear; perhaps it stands for *tasmai*, "to him". The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text. Grammatically *samutthitaḥ*, *āgatya* and *pratyūce* share one subject, *saḥ … mahita-mahā-mahaḥ-samūhaḥ*, that is, the Lord; the reply follows in verse 26.

### Verse 26

ते ज्ञास्यन्त्यहह सपद्यमुत्र ये ये
यास्यन्ति क्ष्मामधुनाधिकारहीनाः ।
इत्युक्त्वा गुरुतरहूंकृतैर्विभिन्नः
श्रीवासालयमगमद्द्रुतं प्रभुः सः ॥२६॥

*te jñāsyanty ahaha sapady amutra ye ye*
*yāsyanti kṣmām adhunādhikāra-hīnāḥ |*
*ity uktvā gurutara-hūṅkṛtair vibhinnaḥ*
*śrīvāsālayam agamad drutaṁ prabhuḥ saḥ ||26||*

*Word for word:* *te* — they; *jñāsyanti* — will know; *ahaha* — ah; *sapadi* — soon; *amutra* — there (in the next world); *ye ye* — all who; *yāsyanti* — will go; *kṣmām* — to the earth; *adhunā* — now; *adhikāra* — of qualification; *hīnāḥ* — devoid; *iti* — thus; *uktvā* — having said; *gurutara* — with heavy; *hūṅkṛtaiḥ* — with roars; *vibhinnaḥ* — shaken; *śrīvāsa* — of Srivasa; *ālayam* — to the house; *agamat* — went; *drutam* — swiftly; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *saḥ* — He.

**26.** (?) "Ah, soon they will know there — all those who, now devoid of qualification, will go to the earth…" Having said this, the Lord, shaken by heavy roars, went swiftly to the house of Srivasa.

*Note.* (?) The sense of the first half is obscure. Perhaps it refers to those who are not yet worthy to see His divinity. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 27

तत्रैव द्रुतमधिगत्य गाढबन्धं
सम्बध्यार्गलमवरद्वये विकुर्वन् ।
बह्वाविष्कृतसहजप्रकाशभास्वा-
नावासे रहसि रराज गौरचन्द्रः ॥२७॥

*tatraiva drutam adhigatya gāḍha-bandhaṁ*
*sambadhyārgalam avara-dvaye vikurvan |*
*bahv-āviṣkṛta-sahaja-prakāśa-bhāsvān*
*āvāse rahasi rarāja gauracandraḥ ||27||*

*Word for word:* *tatra eva* — there itself; *drutam* — swiftly; *adhigatya* — having entered; *gāḍha* — firmly; *bandham* — fastened; *sambadhya* — having shot; *argalam* — the bolt; *avara* — of the door; *dvaye* — on both leaves; *vikurvan* — transforming (?); *bahu* — abundantly; *āviṣkṛta* — revealed; *sahaja* — with His innate; *prakāśa* — radiance; *bhāsvān* — shining; *āvāse* — in the chamber; *rahasi* — secluded; *rarāja* — shone forth; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra.

**27.** Swiftly entering there, He shot the bolt firmly across both leaves of the door; and, transforming (?), brilliant with His innate radiance abundantly revealed, Gaurachandra shone forth in the secluded chamber.

*Note.* (?) *Vikurvan*, literally "transforming, undergoing change", may refer to the ecstatic transformations of His body or to the manifestation of His own form; the meaning is uncertain.

### Verse 28

अद्वैतो निजनिलयात्समागतोऽसौ
सम्प्रादुष्कृतसहजो विलोकितव्यः ।
इत्येवं मनसि विधाय सत्प्रतिज्ञां
तत्काले वहिरुदभूत्कवाटयोस्तत् ॥२८॥

*advaito nija-nilayāt samāgato 'sau*
*samprāduṣkṛta-sahajo vilokitavyaḥ |*
*ity evaṁ manasi vidhāya sat-pratijñāṁ*
*tat-kāle bahir udabhūt kavāṭayos tat ||28||*

*Word for word:* *advaitaḥ* — Advaita; *nija* — from His own; *nilayāt* — home; *samāgataḥ* — come; *asau* — He; *samprāduṣkṛta* — having manifested; *sahajaḥ* — [His] innate [form]; *vilokitavyaḥ* — is to be seen; *iti evam* — thus; *manasi* — in the mind; *vidhāya* — having made; *sat* — firm; *pratijñām* — a vow; *tat* — at that; *kāle* — time; *bahiḥ* — outside; *udabhūt* — appeared; *kavāṭayoḥ* — at the two leaves of the door; *tat* — then.

**28.** Advaita, who had come from his own home, made a firm vow in His mind: "He must be seen [by me] with His innate [form] fully manifest." And at that very time He appeared outside, at the leaves of the door.

*Note.* The motif of a test: Advaita wants the Lord Himself to reveal to Him His divine form. In the Chaitanya-bhagavata (Madhya 6) Advaita sees the Lord in the form for which He had prayed.

### Verse 29

श्रीवासद्विजकुलचन्द्रमः कनीया-
नेषः श्रीपतिरथ तत्समागमं तम् ।
साशङ्कं सपदि निवेदयाञ्चकार
ज्ञात्वैवैतत्स्वयममुचत्प्रभुः कवाटम् ॥२९॥

*śrīvāsa-dvija-kula-candramaḥ kanīyān*
*eṣaḥ śrīpatir atha tat-samāgamaṁ tam |*
*sāśaṅkaṁ sapadi nivedayāñcakāra*
*jñātvaivaitat svayam amucat prabhuḥ kavāṭam ||29||*

*Word for word:* *śrīvāsa* — of Srivasa; *dvija* — of brahmanas; *kula* — of the race; *candramaḥ* — the moon; *kanīyān* — the younger [brother]; *eṣaḥ* — this; *śrīpatiḥ* — Shripati; *atha* — then; *tat* — his; *samāgamam* — arrival; *tam* — that; *sa* — with; *āśaṅkam* — timidity; *sapadi* — at once; *nivedayāñcakāra* — announced; *jñātvā* — having learned; *eva* — just; *etat* — this; *svayam* — Himself; *amucat* — opened; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *kavāṭam* — the door.

**29.** Then Shripati, the younger brother of Srivasa, the moon of the brahmana race, timidly announced his arrival at once; and, just on learning this, the Lord Himself unbolted the door.

### Verse 30

सङ्कल्पो मनसि कृतो यथैव तेन
श्रीभाजं प्रभुमवलोक्य तं तथैव ।
अद्वैतस्तृणनिचयं रदैर्गृहीत्वा
सुस्निग्धो भुवि निपपात दण्डवत्सः ॥३०॥

*saṅkalpo manasi kṛto yathaiva tena*
*śrī-bhājaṁ prabhum avalokya taṁ tathaiva |*
*advaitas tṛṇa-nicayaṁ radair gṛhītvā*
*susnigdho bhuvi nipapāta daṇḍavat saḥ ||30||*

*Word for word:* *saṅkalpaḥ* — the resolve; *manasi* — in the mind; *kṛtaḥ* — made; *yathā eva* — just as; *tena* — by Him; *śrī* — splendour; *bhājam* — possessing; *prabhum* — the Lord; *avalokya* — having beheld; *tam* — Him; *tathā eva* — exactly so; *advaitaḥ* — Advaita; *tṛṇa* — of straw; *nicayam* — a bunch; *radaiḥ* — with the teeth; *gṛhītvā* — having taken; *su* — deeply; *snigdhaḥ* — loving; *bhuvi* — on the ground; *nipapāta* — fell; *daṇḍavat* — like a rod; *saḥ* — he.

**30.** Beholding the Lord in His splendour exactly as He had resolved in His mind, the deeply loving Advaita took a bunch of straw between His teeth and fell on the ground like a rod.

*Note.* Straw between the teeth is an ancient Indian sign of complete submission: "I am like a cow, your beast". Rupa Gosvami does the same on meeting Mahaprabhu (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 1).

### Verse 31

तं दृष्ट्वा प्रभुरपि दोर्द्वयेन शीघ्रं
श्रीभाजं स्वयमिव मुन्निनाय पश्चात् ।
हर्षेणाशिथिलितमाश्लिषद्विशेषं
प्रेमाश्रुस्रवणझरैः सिषेच भूयः ॥३१॥

*taṁ dṛṣṭvā prabhur api dor-dvayena śīghraṁ*
*śrī-bhājaṁ svayam iva munninnāya paścāt |*
*harṣeṇāśithilitam āśliṣad viśeṣaṁ*
*premāśru-sravaṇa-jharaiḥ siṣeca bhūyaḥ ||31||*

*Word for word:* *tam* — him; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *api* — too; *doḥ* — of arms; *dvayena* — with the pair; *śīghram* — swiftly; *śrī-bhājam* — the glorious one; *svayam* — [His] own self; *iva* — as if; *unninnāya* — raised up; *paścāt* — then; *harṣeṇa* — with joy; *aśithilitam* — without loosening; *āśliṣat* — embraced; *viśeṣam* — especially; *prema* — of love; *aśru* — of tears; *sravaṇa* — of the flowing; *jharaiḥ* — with torrents; *siṣeca* — bathed; *bhūyaḥ* — again and again.

**31.** Seeing Him, the Lord too swiftly raised the glorious [Advaita] up with both His arms, as if [He were] His own self; then, in His joy, He embraced Him with special closeness, never loosening His hold, and bathed Him again and again with torrents of flowing tears of love.

*Note.* The edition reads *svayam iva munninnāya*, the Gosvami edition (GGM) *svayam iva munnināya*: in both cases the *m* is a linking sound before *unni-* ("raised up"), so the sense is clear.

### Verse 32

इत्येवंविधविविधोल्लसद्विहारै-
र्विश्रान्तोऽभवदृतुनायकोऽवसन्तः ।
अत्रान्ते प्रभुनटनावलोकहृष्टः
किं ग्रीष्मः प्रहसति मल्लिकाविकासैः ॥३२॥

*ity evaṁ-vidha-vividhollasad-vihārair*
*viśrānto 'bhavad ṛtu-nāyako vasantaḥ |*
*atrānte prabhu-naṭanāvaloka-hṛṣṭaḥ*
*kiṁ grīṣmaḥ prahasati mallikā-vikāsaiḥ ||32||*

*Word for word:* *iti evaṁvidha* — of such kinds; *vividha* — various; *ullasat* — exultant; *vihāraiḥ* — by the pastimes; *viśrāntaḥ* — wearied; *abhavat* — became; *ṛtu* — of the seasons; *nāyakaḥ* — the leader; *vasantaḥ* — spring; *atra* — here; *ante* — at the end; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *naṭana* — the dancing; *avaloka* — at seeing; *hṛṣṭaḥ* — delighted; *kim* — is it not that; *grīṣmaḥ* — summer; *prahasati* — laughs; *mallikā* — of jasmine; *vikāsaiḥ* — with the blossoming.

**32.** By such various, exultant pastimes spring, the leader of the seasons, was wearied. And now, at its end, does not summer, delighted at seeing the Lord's dancing, laugh with the blossoming of jasmine?

*Note.* The change of seasons marks the passage of time: spring gives way to summer (*grīṣma*, the hot season, May–June). The blossoming of jasmine as "laughter" is a classical image.

### Verse 33

विच्छेदादिव सुरभेर्दिनान्यमूनि
प्रत्यग्रादतिविधुराणि संश्रयन्ते ।
उद्दीप्यद्दिनकरजातवेदसः किं
ज्वालाभिर्निरवधि देहदाहवर्त्म ॥३३॥

*vicchedād iva surabher dināny amūni*
*pratyagrād ati-vidhurāṇi saṁśrayante |*
*uddīpyad-dinakara-jāta-vedasaḥ kiṁ*
*jvālābhir niravadhi deha-dāha-vartma ||33||*

*Word for word:* *vicchedāt* — from the separation; *iva* — as if; *surabheḥ* — from spring; *dināni* — the days; *amūni* — these; *pratyagrāt* — from the fresh; *ati* — utterly; *vidhurāṇi* — bereaved; *saṁśrayante* — take to; *uddīpyat* — of the blazing; *dinakara* — of the sun; *jātavedasaḥ* — of the fire; *kim* — is it not that; *jvālābhiḥ* — with the flames; *niravadhi* — without end; *deha* — of the body; *dāha* — of burning; *vartma* — the path.

**33.** These days, utterly bereaved, as it were, by their fresh separation from spring — do they not take, without end, the path of burning their bodies in the flames of the blazing fire that is the sun?

*Note.* *Surabhi*, "the fragrant one", is spring. *Jātavedas* is Agni, fire. The image is of a bereaved wife who enters the fire after her husband.

### Verse 34

उद्दामद्युमणिरुचो मुहुर्ज्वलन्त्यो
यद्यप्याश्रयमयमम्बु शोषयन्ति ।
पद्मिन्यास्तदपि दधात्यतीव सौख्यं
दुःखञ्च प्रियविहितं प्रियं तनोति ॥३४॥

*uddāma-dyumaṇi-ruco muhur jvalantyo*
*yady apy āśraya-mayam ambu śoṣayanti |*
*padminyās tad api dadhāty atīva saukhyaṁ*
*duḥkhañ ca priya-vihitaṁ priyaṁ tanoti ||34||*

*Word for word:* *uddāma* — unrestrained; *dyumaṇi* — of the sun; *rucaḥ* — the rays; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *jvalantyaḥ* — blazing; *yadi api* — although; *āśraya* — the support; *mayam* — forming; *ambu* — the water; *śoṣayanti* — dry up; *padminyāḥ* — to the lotus; *tat api* — even so; *dadhāti* — gives; *atīva* — very great; *saukhyam* — happiness; *duḥkham* — pain; *ca* — and; *priya* — by the beloved; *vihitam* — caused; *priyam* — dear; *tanoti* — becomes.

**34.** Although the unrestrained rays of the sun, blazing again and again, dry up the water that is the lotus's support, even so [the sun] gives the lotus very great happiness: for pain too, when caused by the beloved, becomes dear.

*Note.* The sun is the "beloved" of the day-lotus. A thought important for Gaudiya aesthetics: pain from the beloved is sweet (compare Shikshashtaka 8).

### Verse 35

नैदाघं निजमहसा निदाघरश्मिं
न्यक्कुर्वन्सततं नवनवेन गौरः ।
अन्येद्युर्द्विजतनुजान्विपाठयन्स
प्रोद्भिन्नप्रकटनिजप्रकाश आसीत् ॥३५॥

*naidāghaṁ nija-mahasā nidāgha-raśmiṁ*
*nyakkurvan satataṁ nava-navena gauraḥ |*
*anyedyur dvija-tanujān vipāṭhayan sa*
*prodbhinna-prakaṭa-nija-prakāśa āsīt ||35||*

*Word for word:* *naidāgham* — of summer; *nija* — with His own; *mahasā* — radiance; *nidāgha* — of heat; *raśmim* — the [one with] rays (the sun); *nyakkurvan* — putting to shame; *satatam* — constantly; *nava-navena* — ever new; *gauraḥ* — Gaura; *anyedyuḥ* — on the next day; *dvija* — of brahmanas; *tanujān* — the sons; *vipāṭhayan* — teaching; *saḥ* — He; *prodbhinna* — burst forth; *prakaṭa* — manifest; *nija* — His own; *prakāśaḥ* — [with] radiance; *āsīt* — was.

**35.** Constantly putting to shame the hot-rayed summer sun with His own ever-new radiance, Gaura, on the next day, while teaching the sons of brahmanas, had His own radiance burst forth and become manifest.

### Verse 36

इत्येतद्विधसहजप्रकाशभास्वा-
न्निर्भिन्नः सदरुणसर्व्वगात्रयष्टिः ।
प्रत्यग्रोन्मिषदरुणोत्पलाङ्घ्रियुग्मः
श्रीवासालयमगमद्विमुक्तसङ्गः ॥३६॥

*ity etad-vidha-sahaja-prakāśa-bhāsvān*
*nirbhinnaḥ sad-aruṇa-sarva-gātra-yaṣṭiḥ |*
*pratyagronmiṣad-aruṇotpalāṅghri-yugmaḥ*
*śrīvāsālayam agamad vimukta-saṅgaḥ ||36||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *etat-vidha* — with such; *sahaja* — innate; *prakāśa* — radiance; *bhāsvān* — shining; *nirbhinnaḥ* — overwhelmed; *sat* — beautifully; *aruṇa* — rosy; *sarva* — whole; *gātra* — of the body; *yaṣṭiḥ* — [whose] slender stem; *pratyagra* — fresh; *unmiṣat* — opening; *aruṇa* — red; *utpala* — [like] lotuses; *aṅghri* — of feet; *yugmaḥ* — [whose] pair; *śrīvāsa* — of Srivasa; *ālayam* — to the house; *agamat* — went; *vimukta* — having left; *saṅgaḥ* — company.

**36.** Thus, shining with such innate radiance, overwhelmed, the slender stem of His whole body a beautiful rosy hue, His two feet like fresh, opening red lotuses, He left all company and went to the house of Srivasa.

### Verse 37

उन्मीलद्द्युमणिगणप्रकाशभाजं
प्रत्यग्रस्फुटतरशोणसारसाक्षम् ।
गच्छन्तं द्रुतमरुणाङ्घ्रिपद्मयोस्तै-
र्विन्यासैः पथि ददृशुर्जनाः सचित्रम् ॥३७॥

*unmīlad-dyumaṇi-gaṇa-prakāśa-bhājaṁ*
*pratyagra-sphuṭatara-śoṇa-sārasākṣam |*
*gacchantaṁ drutam aruṇāṅghri-padmayos tair*
*vinyāsaiḥ pathi dadṛśur janāḥ sa-citram ||37||*

*Word for word:* *unmīlat* — of rising; *dyumaṇi* — of suns; *gaṇa* — of a host; *prakāśa* — the radiance; *bhājam* — possessing; *pratyagra* — fresh; *sphuṭatara* — fully opened; *śoṇa* — red; *sārasa* — [like] lotuses; *akṣam* — [whose] eyes; *gacchantam* — going; *drutam* — swiftly; *aruṇa* — red; *aṅghri* — of feet; *padmayoḥ* — of the lotuses; *taiḥ* — with those; *vinyāsaiḥ* — with the steps; *pathi* — on the road; *dadṛśuḥ* — saw; *janāḥ* — the people; *sa* — with; *citram* — wonder.

**37.** The people on the road watched with wonder as He went swiftly with the steps of His red lotus feet — possessing the radiance of a host of rising suns, His eyes like fresh, fully opened red lotuses.

### Verse 38

तत्पुर्य्यां सपदि निवेश्य देवगेह-
स्यालिन्दोपरि परितस्थिवान्परेशः ।
ध्यायन्तं गृहमधि निर्भरैकतानं
श्रीवासं प्रकटप्रकाशमाजुहाव ॥३८॥

*tat-puryāṁ sapadi niveśya deva-gehasy-*
*ālindopari paritasthivān pareśaḥ |*
*dhyāyantaṁ gṛham adhi nirbharaika-tānaṁ*
*śrīvāsaṁ prakaṭa-prakāśam ājuhāva ||38||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — his; *puryām* — into the house; *sapadi* — at once; *niveśya* — having entered; *deva* — of God; *gehasya* — of the shrine; *alinda* — the veranda; *upari* — upon; *paritasthivān* — took His place; *pareśaḥ* — the Supreme Lord; *dhyāyantam* — meditating; *gṛham adhi* — within the house; *nirbhara* — wholly; *eka* — on one [object]; *tānam* — fixed; *śrīvāsam* — Srivasa; *prakaṭa* — manifest; *prakāśam* — [He with] radiance; *ājuhāva* — called.

**38.** At once entering his house, the Supreme Lord took His place upon the veranda of the shrine and, with His radiance manifest, called Srivasa, who was within the house, meditating, wholly fixed on one object.

### Verse 39

तच्छ्रुत्वा सपदि गृहाद्बहिर्बभूव
ध्यानादि प्रकटमपोह्य विप्रमुख्यः ।
उन्मीलन्गुरुमहसं महायताङ्गं
सोऽद्राक्षीन्निजपुरतः स्थितं परेशम् ॥३९॥

*tac chrutvā sapadi gṛhād bahir babhūva*
*dhyānādi prakaṭam apohya vipra-mukhyaḥ |*
*unmīlan guru-mahasaṁ mahāyatāṅgaṁ*
*so 'drākṣīn nija-purataḥ sthitaṁ pareśam ||39||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — that; *śrutvā* — having heard; *sapadi* — at once; *gṛhāt* — from the house; *bahiḥ* — outside; *babhūva* — came; *dhyāna* — meditation; *ādi* — and the rest; *prakaṭam* — openly; *apohya* — having set aside; *vipra* — of brahmanas; *mukhyaḥ* — the foremost; *unmīlan* — opening [his eyes]; *guru* — [with] mighty; *mahasam* — effulgence; *mahā* — majestic; *āyata* — tall; *aṅgam* — [with] a body; *saḥ* — he; *adrākṣīt* — saw; *nija* — himself; *purataḥ* — before; *sthitam* — standing; *pareśam* — the Supreme Lord.

**39.** Hearing that, the foremost of brahmanas at once openly set aside his meditation and the rest and came out of the house. Opening his eyes, he saw standing before him the Supreme Lord, of mighty effulgence, His body tall and majestic.

### Verse 40

उद्भ्रान्तः प्रकटनिजप्रकाशवेगै-
रज्यद्भिर्महिततनूर्नवैर्महोभिः ।
पाथोभिः सुरसरितो ममाभिषेकं
शीघ्रं कुर्व्विति निजगाद गौरचन्द्रः ॥४०॥

*udbhrāntaḥ prakaṭa-nija-prakāśa-vegai-*
*rajyadbhir mahita-tanur navair mahobhiḥ |*
*pāthobhiḥ sura-sarito mamābhiṣekaṁ*
*śīghraṁ kurv iti nijagāda gauracandraḥ ||40||*

*Word for word:* *udbhrāntaḥ* — agitated; *prakaṭa* — of the manifest; *nija* — of His own; *prakāśa* — radiance; *vegaiḥ* — by the surges; *rajyadbhiḥ* — with reddening; *mahita* — glorious; *tanuḥ* — [whose] body; *navaiḥ* — with fresh; *mahobhiḥ* — with rays; *pāthobhiḥ* — with the waters; *sura* — of the gods; *saritaḥ* — of the river; *mama* — My; *abhiṣekam* — ceremonial bathing; *śīghram* — quickly; *kuru* — perform; *iti* — thus; *nijagāda* — declared; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra.

**40.** Agitated by the surges of His own manifest radiance, His glorious body [aglow] with fresh, reddening rays, Gaurachandra declared: "Quickly perform My ceremonial bathing with the waters of the river of the gods!"

*Note.* The **mahabhisheka** is the royal bathing of the Lord in the house of Srivasa, the beginning of the *maha-prakasha* (Chaitanya-bhagavata, Madhya 9–10, "The completion of the maha-prakasha-lila").

### Verse 41

तच्छ्रुत्वा सपदि सहोदरैरमुष्य
श्रीरामप्रभृतिभिरुत्सुकैर्महद्भिः ।
तच्चेष्टासुखविवशैस्तदाह्रियन्त
द्रव्याणि स्वयमिव जग्मुराहृतत्वम् ॥४१॥

*tac chrutvā sapadi sahodarair amuṣya*
*śrīrāma-prabhṛtibhir utsukair mahadbhiḥ |*
*tac-ceṣṭā-sukha-vivaśais tadāhriyanta*
*dravyāṇi svayam iva jagmur āhṛtatvam ||41||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — that; *śrutvā* — having heard; *sapadi* — at once; *sahodaraiḥ* — by the brothers; *amuṣya* — his; *śrīrāma* — by Sri Rama; *prabhṛtibhiḥ* — and the others; *utsukaiḥ* — eager; *mahadbhiḥ* — noble; *tat* — His; *ceṣṭā* — of the acts; *sukha* — by the joy; *vivaśaiḥ* — overpowered; *tadā* — then; *āhriyanta* — were brought; *dravyāṇi* — the articles; *svayam* — of themselves; *iva* — as if; *jagmuḥ* — went; *āhṛtatvam* — to the state of being brought.

**41.** Hearing that, his noble brothers — Sri Rama and the others — eager and overpowered by the joy of His acts, at once brought the articles; and the articles seemed to come into the state of being brought of their own accord.

### Verse 42

तत्कैश्चिन्नवकलसीशतं समन्ता-
दाजह्रे झटिति तथा जलैः पुपूरे ।
सर्व्वाभिः सविधगताभिरङ्गनाभिः
स्वर्वापीजलहरणाय शीघ्रमीये ॥४२॥

*tat kaiścin nava-kalasī-śataṁ samantād*
*ājahre jhaṭiti tathā jalaiḥ pupūre |*
*sarvābhiḥ savidha-gatābhir aṅganābhiḥ*
*svar-vāpī-jala-haraṇāya śīghram īye ||42||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — then; *kaiścit* — by some; *nava* — of new; *kalasī* — pitchers; *śatam* — a hundred; *samantāt* — from all sides; *ājahre* — was brought; *jhaṭiti* — in an instant; *tathā* — and likewise; *jalaiḥ* — with water; *pupūre* — was filled; *sarvābhiḥ* — by all; *savidha* — nearby; *gatābhiḥ* — who were; *aṅganābhiḥ* — by the women; *svaḥ* — of heaven; *vāpī* — of the stream; *jala* — water; *haraṇāya* — for fetching; *śīghram* — quickly; *īye* — it was gone.

**42.** Then in an instant some brought a hundred new pitchers from all sides and likewise filled them with water: all the women who were nearby quickly went to fetch water from the heavenly stream, [the Ganga].

### Verse 43

गम्भारीविरचितपीठमध्यराजी
श्रीगौरः स्नवनचिकीर्षयाजिरान्तः ।
दुग्धाब्धेरुपरिगतस्य मेरुशृङ्ग-
स्याभिक्षां सपदि विडम्बयाम्बभूव ॥४३॥

*gambhārī-viracita-pīṭha-madhya-rājī*
*śrī-gauraḥ snavana-cikīrṣayājirāntaḥ |*
*dugdhābdher upari-gatasya meru-śṛṅgasy-*
*ābhikṣāṁ sapadi viḍambayāmbabhūva ||43||*

*Word for word:* *gambhārī* — of gambhari wood; *viracita* — made; *pīṭha* — of a seat; *madhya* — in the middle; *rājī* — shining; *śrī-gauraḥ* — Sri Gaura; *snavana* — the bath; *cikīrṣayā* — with the wish to undergo; *ajira* — of the courtyard; *antaḥ* — in the midst; *dugdha* — of milk; *abdheḥ* — the ocean; *upari* — above; *gatasya* — risen; *meru* — of Meru; *śṛṅgasya* — of a peak; *ābhikṣām* — the beauty (?) (so also in the Gosvami edition (GGM), which there reads *plavana-* for *snavana-*); *sapadi* — at once; *viḍambayāmbabhūva* — imitated.

**43.** Wishing to receive the bath, Sri Gaura sat shining in the midst of the courtyard on a seat made of gambhari wood, and at once took on the beauty of a peak of Meru risen above the Ocean of Milk.

*Note.* (?) *Ābhikṣā* is not a known word; perhaps it stands for *abhikhyā*, "splendour, beauty".

### Verse 44

आनीतैरति लघु जह्नुकन्यकायाः
पाथोभिः सुरभिसुवासितैः प्रकामम् ।
कर्पूरागुरुगुरुगन्धसारवद्भिः
श्रीवासस्तमभिषिषेच हृष्टचित्तः ॥४४॥

*ānītair ati laghu jahnu-kanyakāyāḥ*
*pāthobhiḥ surabhi-suvāsitaiḥ prakāmam |*
*karpūrāguru-guru-gandha-sāravadbhiḥ*
*śrīvāsas tam abhiṣiṣeca hṛṣṭa-cittaḥ ||44||*

*Word for word:* *ānītaiḥ* — brought; *ati* — very; *laghu* — quickly; *jahnu* — of Jahnu; *kanyakāyāḥ* — of the daughter; *pāthobhiḥ* — with the waters; *surabhi* — with fragrances; *suvāsitaiḥ* — well scented; *prakāmam* — to his heart's content; *karpūra* — camphor; *aguru* — aguru; *guru* — heavy; *gandhasāra* — sandalwood; *vadbhiḥ* — containing; *śrīvāsaḥ* — Srivasa; *tam* — Him; *abhiṣiṣeca* — bathed; *hṛṣṭa* — joyful; *cittaḥ* — [with] a heart.

**44.** With the waters of the daughter of Jahnu, brought very quickly and well scented with fragrances — with camphor, aguru and heavy sandalwood — Srivasa, his heart joyful, bathed Him to his heart's content.

*Note.* The "daughter of Jahnu" (Jahnavi) is the Ganga.

### Verse 45

द्राघिष्ठैर्निरवधि-शश्वदुन्मिषद्भि-
स्तेजोभिः कणकनिकाशराजिगौरैः ।
अत्यच्छा वपुषि पतन्त्यमुष्य धारा
गौराङ्गीक्रियत इवाभिषेकवाराम् ॥४५॥

*drāghiṣṭhair niravadhi-śaśvad-unmiṣadbhis*
*tejobhiḥ kanaka-nikāśa-rāji-gauraiḥ |*
*aty-acchā vapuṣi patanty amuṣya dhārā*
*gaurāṅgī kriyata ivābhiṣeka-vārām ||45||*

*Word for word:* *drāghiṣṭhaiḥ* — far-reaching; *niravadhi* — boundlessly; *śaśvat* — continually; *unmiṣadbhiḥ* — flashing; *tejobhiḥ* — by the rays; *kanaka* — of gold; *nikāśa* — on a touchstone; *rāji* — [like] a streak; *gauraiḥ* — golden; *ati* — very; *acchāḥ* — clear; *vapuṣi* — on the body; *patanti* — fall; *amuṣya* — His; *dhārāḥ* — the streams; *gaurāṅgī kriyate* — is made golden-limbed; *iva* — as if; *abhiṣeka* — of the bathing; *vārām* — of the waters.

**45.** The very clear streams fall on His body; and, by His rays — far-reaching, boundless, continually flashing, golden like a streak of gold on a touchstone — [the stream] of the bathing waters is, as it were, made golden-limbed.

*Note.* *Gaurāṅgī kriyate*, "is made *gaurāṅga*, golden-limbed": the waters, as it were, take on the Lord's own name.

### Verse 46

गङ्गानां कलसशतेन सज्जलानां
सेकोऽयं झटिति पटीवदङ्गभाजम् ।
निर्व्यूढोऽभवदनुभूय तज्जलं भू-
रुच्छ्वासैः सुबहु कृतार्थतां जगाम ॥४६॥

*gaṅgānāṁ kalasa-śatena saj-jalānāṁ*
*seko 'yaṁ jhaṭiti paṭīvad aṅga-bhājam |*
*nirvyūḍho 'bhavad anubhūya taj jalaṁ bhūr*
*ucchvāsaiḥ su-bahu kṛtārthatāṁ jagāma ||46||*

*Word for word:* *gaṅgānām* — of the Ganga; *kalasa* — of pitchers; *śatena* — with a hundred; *sat* — pure; *jalānām* — of waters; *sekaḥ* — sprinkling; *ayam* — this; *jhaṭiti* — in an instant; *paṭīvat* — like a cloth; *aṅga* — the body; *bhājam* — clothing; *nirvyūḍhaḥ* — accomplished; *abhavat* — was; *anubhūya* — having tasted; *tat* — that; *jalam* — water; *bhūḥ* — the earth; *ucchvāsaiḥ* — with sighs [of joy]; *su* — very; *bahu* — greatly; *kṛtārthatām* — the fulfilment of its purpose; *jagāma* — attained.

**46.** This bathing with a hundred pitchers of the pure waters of the Ganga, clothing His body in an instant like a cloth, was accomplished; and the earth, tasting that water, with sighs [of joy], attained in full measure the fulfilment of its purpose.

### Verse 47

स्नानान्ते वरवसनेन सारयित्वा
गात्राम्भः करयुगलेन तस्य पश्चात् ।
श्रीवासस्तनुतरशुभ्रशुद्धवासो-
द्वन्द्वेन प्रसरवता सुखेन भेजे ॥४७॥

*snānānte vara-vasanena sārayitvā*
*gātrāmbhaḥ kara-yugalena tasya paścāt |*
*śrīvāsas tanutara-śubhra-śuddha-vāso-*
*dvandvena prasaravatā sukhena bheje ||47||*

*Word for word:* *snāna* — of the bath; *ante* — at the end; *vara* — with an excellent; *vasanena* — cloth; *sārayitvā* — having wiped away; *gātra* — from the limbs; *ambhaḥ* — the water; *kara* — of hands; *yugalena* — with the pair; *tasya* — His; *paścāt* — afterwards; *śrīvāsaḥ* — Srivasa; *tanutara* — very fine; *śubhra* — white; *śuddha* — pure; *vāsaḥ* — of garments; *dvandvena* — with a pair; *prasaravatā* — overflowing; *sukhena* — with joy; *bheje* — served [Him].

**47.** At the end of the bath Srivasa wiped the water from His limbs with an excellent cloth, using both hands, and afterwards, with overflowing joy, served Him with a pair of very fine, white, pure garments.

*Note.* The pair of garments is the lower (*dhoti*) and the upper (*uttariya*).

### Verse 48

श्रीगौरस्तनुवसनद्वयं गृहीत्वा
नीहारप्रचयसुपृक्तमेरुशोभाम् ।
जग्राहोद्भटमहसा महीयसासौ
संभिन्नो द्रुतमविशच्च देववेश्म ॥४८॥

*śrī-gauras tanu-vasana-dvayaṁ gṛhītvā*
*nīhāra-pracaya-supṛkta-meru-śobhām |*
*jagrāhodbhaṭa-mahasā mahīyasāsau*
*saṁbhinno drutam aviśac ca deva-veśma ||48||*

*Word for word:* *śrī-gauraḥ* — Sri Gaura; *tanu* — of fine; *vasana* — garments; *dvayam* — the pair; *gṛhītvā* — having taken; *nīhāra* — of mist; *pracaya* — with a veil; *supṛkta* — joined; *meru* — of Meru; *śobhām* — the beauty; *jagrāha* — took on; *udbhaṭa* — with mighty; *mahasā* — effulgence; *mahīyasā* — with supreme; *asau* — He; *saṁbhinnaḥ* — overwhelmed; *drutam* — swiftly; *aviśat* — entered; *ca* — and; *deva* — of God; *veśma* — the shrine.

**48.** Taking the pair of fine garments, Sri Gaura took on the beauty of Meru wrapped in a veil of mist; and, overwhelmed by His mighty, supreme effulgence, He swiftly entered the shrine.

### Verse 49

तस्यान्तः सपदि निविश्य गौरचन्द्रः
पर्य्यङ्के ललितरुचौ महामहस्वान् ।
देवानां प्रतिकृतिसञ्चयं समन्ता-
दाक्षिप्य स्वयमकरोत्सुखोपवेशम् ॥४९॥

*tasyāntaḥ sapadi niviśya gauracandraḥ*
*paryaṅke lalita-rucau mahā-mahasvān |*
*devānāṁ pratikṛti-sañcayaṁ samantād*
*ākṣipya svayam akarot sukhopaveśam ||49||*

*Word for word:* *tasya* — of it; *antaḥ* — inside; *sapadi* — at once; *niviśya* — having entered; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra; *paryaṅke* — on the couch; *lalita* — of charming; *rucau* — lustre; *mahā* — with great; *mahasvān* — effulgence [filled]; *devānām* — of the gods; *pratikṛti* — of the Deity forms; *sañcayam* — the gathering; *samantāt* — on all sides; *ākṣipya* — having pushed aside; *svayam* — Himself; *akarot* — made; *sukha* — comfortable; *upaveśam* — sitting.

**49.** At once entering within it, Gaurachandra, filled with great effulgence, pushed aside on all sides the gathering of the Deity forms of the gods and Himself sat down at ease upon the couch of charming lustre.

*Note.* The Lord Himself sits on the throne of the Deities — a sign of the *maha-prakasha*, the manifestation of His divinity (Chaitanya-bhagavata, Madhya 9: "The Lord sat on the throne of Vishnu").

### Verse 50

अप्राप्यावसरममुष्य वेश्ममध्ये
तेजोभिर्बहिरपि सन्धिभिर्व्यभेदि ।
तत्काले जननिचयस्य हर्षराशिः
स्वान्तान्तः पुलकभरैर्बहिर्बभूव ॥५०॥

*aprāpyāvasaram amuṣya veśma-madhye*
*tejobhir bahir api sandhibhir vyabhedi |*
*tat-kāle jana-nicayasya harṣa-rāśiḥ*
*svāntāntaḥ pulaka-bharair bahir babhūva ||50||*
