*Word for word:* *aprāpya* — not finding; *avasaram* — room; *amuṣya* — of it; *veśma* — of the house; *madhye* — inside; *tejobhiḥ* — by the rays; *bahiḥ* — outward; *api* — even; *sandhibhiḥ* — through the chinks; *vyabhedi* — a way was broken; *tat* — at that; *kāle* — time; *jana* — of people; *nicayasya* — of the crowd; *harṣa* — of joy; *rāśiḥ* — the heap; *svānta* — the heart; *antaḥ* — from within; *pulaka* — of bristling hair; *bharaiḥ* — with the abundance; *bahiḥ* — outside; *babhūva* — came.

**50.** Finding no room inside the house, His rays broke their way out through the chinks; and at that time the heaped-up joy of the crowd of people came out from within their hearts in an abundance of bristling hair.

*Note.* A parallel: light from within breaks out through the chinks — joy from within breaks out through the bristling hair on the skin.

### Verse 51

सर्व्वे तत्समयमवाप्य हर्षमग्ना
गौराङ्गं परिविविदुस्त्रिलोकनाथम् ।
श्रीवंशीध्वनिमथ शुश्रुवुश्च सर्व्वे
रम्यं तन्मुखकमलोद्गतं चिराय ॥५१॥

*sarve tat-samayam avāpya harṣa-magnā*
*gaurāṅgaṁ parivividus tri-loka-nātham |*
*śrī-vaṁśī-dhvanim atha śuśruvuś ca sarve*
*ramyaṁ tan-mukha-kamalodgataṁ cirāya ||51||*

*Word for word:* *sarve* — all; *tat* — that; *samayam* — moment; *avāpya* — having reached; *harṣa* — in joy; *magnāḥ* — immersed; *gaurāṅgam* — Gauranga; *parivividuḥ* — recognised [as]; *tri* — of the three; *loka* — worlds; *nātham* — the Lord; *śrī* — beautiful; *vaṁśī* — of the flute; *dhvanim* — the sound; *atha* — then; *śuśruvuḥ* — heard; *ca* — and; *sarve* — all; *ramyam* — enchanting; *tat* — His; *mukha* — of the mouth; *kamala* — from the lotus; *udgatam* — issuing; *cirāya* — for long.

**51.** At that moment all, immersed in joy, recognised Gauranga as the Lord of the three worlds; and then all of them heard for a long time the enchanting sound of the beautiful flute issuing from the lotus of His mouth.

*Note.* The sound of the flute is the sign of Krishna: those present recognise Him in Gaura.

### Verse 52

तत्तापे सुखमतुलं समस्तलोकै-
रासेदे पुलककुलैरशोभदङ्गम् ।
संभेजे नयनजलैः स रोमहर्षः
श्रीगौरे जयति तथाविधे तदानीम् ॥५२॥

*tat-tāpe sukham atulaṁ samasta-lokair*
*āsede pulaka-kulair aśobhad aṅgam |*
*saṁbheje nayana-jalaiḥ sa roma-harṣaḥ*
*śrī-gaure jayati tathā-vidhe tadānīm ||52||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — in that; *tāpe* — heat (?); *sukham* — happiness; *atulam* — incomparable; *samasta* — by all; *lokaiḥ* — by the people; *āsede* — was attained; *pulaka* — of bristling hair; *kulaiḥ* — with masses; *aśobhat* — shone (?); *aṅgam* — the body; *saṁbheje* — was joined; *nayana* — of the eyes; *jalaiḥ* — with the waters; *saḥ* — that; *roma* — of the hair; *harṣaḥ* — thrill; *śrī-gaure* — when Sri Gaura; *jayati* — was triumphant; *tathā* — such; *vidhe* — [manifest]; *tadānīm* — then.

**52.** In that heat all the people attained incomparable happiness; their bodies shone with masses of bristling hair, and that thrill was joined with the waters of their eyes — while Sri Gaura, manifest in such a form, was triumphant then.

*Note.* The second line is printed unclearly in the edition; the reading *aśobhad aṅgam* ("the body shone") is chosen by the metre (⏑ — ⏑ — —) and the sense. *Tat-tāpe*, "in that heat" (the summer of verses 32–37, or the heat of His radiance); a misprint for *tat-kāle*, as in verse 50, is not excluded (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *athoñcad-aṅgam* in the second line, which is also unclear.

### Verse 53

गौराङ्गोऽवददथ भूसुरैकरत्नं
श्रीवासं परममहामहोविभिन्नः ।
एतस्माद्भवनवराद्भवद्गृहान्त-
र्यास्यामीत्यथ सततप्रकाशरम्यः ॥५३॥

*gaurāṅgo 'vadad atha bhūsuraika-ratnaṁ*
*śrīvāsaṁ parama-mahā-maho-vibhinnaḥ |*
*etasmād bhavana-varād bhavad-gṛhāntar*
*yāsyāmīty atha satata-prakāśa-ramyaḥ ||53||*

*Word for word:* *gaurāṅgaḥ* — Gauranga; *avadat* — said; *atha* — then; *bhūsura* — of brahmanas; *eka* — the one; *ratnam* — to the jewel; *śrīvāsam* — to Srivasa; *parama* — with supreme; *mahā* — great; *mahaḥ* — effulgence; *vibhinnaḥ* — bursting forth; *etasmāt* — from this; *bhavana* — chamber; *varāt* — excellent; *bhavat* — your; *gṛha* — of the house; *antaḥ* — inside; *yāsyāmi* — I shall go; *iti* — thus; *atha* — and; *satata* — with unceasing; *prakāśa* — radiance; *ramyaḥ* — beautiful.

**53.** Then Gauranga, bursting forth with supreme, great effulgence, beautiful with unceasing radiance, said to Srivasa, the one jewel among brahmanas: "From this excellent chamber I shall go into the inner part of your house."

*Note.* *Bhūsura*, "a god on earth", is a brahmana. "This chamber" is the shrine (*deva-veśma*, verse 48); "your house" is Srivasa's living quarters.

### Verse 54

तच्छ्रुत्वा झटिति सहोदरैः समस्तै-
स्तद्गेहं सुखविवशैः समस्कृतोच्चैः ।
मध्यद्वारि च बहुवेष्टनैस्तथा तै-
रावव्रे भवति सुगोपितं यथा तत् ॥५४॥

*tac chrutvā jhaṭiti sahodaraiḥ samastais*
*tad-gehaṁ sukha-vivaśaiḥ samaskṛtoccaiḥ |*
*madhya-dvāri ca bahu-veṣṭanais tathā tair*
*āvavre bhavati sugopitaṁ yathā tat ||54||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — that; *śrutvā* — having heard; *jhaṭiti* — in an instant; *sahodaraiḥ* — by the brothers; *samastaiḥ* — by all; *tat* — his; *geham* — house; *sukha* — by joy; *vivaśaiḥ* — overpowered; *samaskṛta* — was adorned; *uccaiḥ* — lavishly; *madhya* — middle; *dvāri* — at the door; *ca* — and; *bahu* — with many; *veṣṭanaiḥ* — with hangings; *tathā* — so; *taiḥ* — by them; *āvavre* — it was screened; *bhavati* — becomes; *sugopitam* — well concealed; *yathā* — so that; *tat* — it.

**54.** Hearing that, all [Srivasa's] brothers, overpowered by joy, in an instant lavishly adorned his house, and they screened the middle door with many hangings so that it was well concealed.

*Note.* Srivasa's brothers are Sri Rama, Shripati and Shrinidhi. *Samaskṛta* (not *saṁskṛta*) is used for the metre, in the sense "adorned".

### Verse 55

श्रीवासस्तदनु गदाधरं बभाषे
खट्वाद्यं सकलममुत्र नीयतां तत् ।
इत्युक्तः स च सकलं निनाय तत्र
प्रेमार्द्रो निरवधि विस्मृतात्मचेष्टः ॥५५॥

*śrīvāsas tad-anu gadādharaṁ babhāṣe*
*khaṭvādyaṁ sakalam amutra nīyatāṁ tat |*
*ity uktaḥ sa ca sakalaṁ nināya tatra*
*premārdro niravadhi vismṛtātma-ceṣṭaḥ ||55||*

*Word for word:* *śrīvāsaḥ* — Srivasa; *tat* — that; *anu* — after; *gadādharam* — to Gadadhara; *babhāṣe* — said; *khaṭvā* — the couch; *ādyam* — and so on; *sakalam* — all; *amutra* — there; *nīyatām* — let be carried; *tat* — that; *iti* — thus; *uktaḥ* — addressed; *saḥ* — he; *ca* — and; *sakalam* — all; *nināya* — carried; *tatra* — there; *prema* — with love; *ārdraḥ* — melted; *niravadhi* — boundlessly; *vismṛta* — having forgotten; *ātma* — his own; *ceṣṭaḥ* — actions.

**55.** After that Srivasa said to Gadadhara: "Let the couch and everything else be carried there." Thus addressed, Gadadhara, boundlessly melted with love and forgetful of what he himself was doing, carried everything there.

### Verse 56

सच्चन्द्रातपमुपरि प्रतत्य तूर्णं
तस्यान्ते सुरुचिरचामराणि तेने ।
पर्य्यङ्कोपरि कशिपूत्तमं निपात्य
श्रीमद्भिर्वरवसनैरथानुवव्रे ॥५६॥

*sac-candrātapam upari pratatya tūrṇaṁ*
*tasyānte su-rucira-cāmarāṇi tene |*
*paryaṅkopari kaśipūttamaṁ nipātya*
*śrīmadbhir vara-vasanair athānuvavre ||56||*

*Word for word:* *sat* — a fine; *candrātapam* — canopy; *upari* — above; *pratatya* — having spread; *tūrṇam* — quickly; *tasya* — of it; *ante* — along the edge; *su* — very; *rucira* — beautiful; *cāmarāṇi* — chamaras; *tene* — hung; *paryaṅka* — the couch; *upari* — upon; *kaśipu* — a mattress; *uttamam* — the best; *nipātya* — having laid; *śrīmadbhiḥ* — with splendid; *vara* — excellent; *vasanaiḥ* — with cloths; *atha* — then; *anuvavre* — covered.

**56.** Quickly spreading a fine canopy above, he hung very beautiful chamaras along its edge; laying the best of mattresses upon the couch, he then covered it with splendid, excellent cloths.

*Note.* *Candrātapa* (literally "moonlight") is an awning, a canopy over a throne or couch. A *chamara* is a whisk of yak tail, a royal insignia.

### Verse 57

गौराङ्गस्तदथ गृहं व्रजन् विरेजे
तेजोभिर्लघु तिरयन् विवस्वदोजः ।
शम्पानां शतशतकोटिकोटिवत् स
प्रोन्मील्य क्षितिमिव संश्रितश्चकास्ति ॥५७॥

*gaurāṅgas tad atha gṛhaṁ vrajan vireje*
*tejobhir laghu tirayan vivasvad-ojaḥ |*
*śampānāṁ śata-śata-koṭi-koṭivat sa*
*pronmīlya kṣitim iva saṁśritaś cakāsti ||57||*

*Word for word:* *gaurāṅgaḥ* — Gauranga; *tat* — that; *atha* — then; *gṛham* — house; *vrajan* — going to; *vireje* — shone; *tejobhiḥ* — with rays; *laghu* — easily; *tirayan* — eclipsing; *vivasvat* — of the sun; *ojaḥ* — the might; *śampānām* — of lightning flashes; *śata* — hundreds; *śata* — of hundreds; *koṭi* — of crores; *koṭivat* — like crores; *saḥ* — He; *pronmīlya* — having burst open; *kṣitim* — upon the earth; *iva* — as if; *saṁśritaḥ* — come to rest; *cakāsti* — shines.

**57.** Then Gauranga, going to that house, shone, easily eclipsing with His rays the might of the sun. He shines like hundreds upon hundreds of crores upon crores of lightning flashes that have burst open and, as it were, come to rest upon the earth.

*Note.* A crore (*koṭi*) is ten million.

### Verse 58

पादाम्भोरुहयुगलं विलासपूर्व्वं
विन्यस्य क्षितिषु चलन्महामहस्वान् ।
पर्य्यङ्कं परममनोहरं स भेजे
मेरोः सच्छिखर इवान्यशैलपृष्ठम् ॥५८॥

*pādāmbhoruha-yugalaṁ vilāsa-pūrvaṁ*
*vinyasya kṣitiṣu calan mahā-mahasvān |*
*paryaṅkaṁ parama-manoharaṁ sa bheje*
*meroḥ sac-chikhara ivānya-śaila-pṛṣṭham ||58||*

*Word for word:* *pāda* — of feet; *ambhoruha* — of lotuses; *yugalam* — the pair; *vilāsa* — with playful grace; *pūrvam* — accompanied; *vinyasya* — setting down; *kṣitiṣu* — on the ground; *calan* — walking; *mahā* — with great; *mahasvān* — effulgence [filled]; *paryaṅkam* — the couch; *parama* — supremely; *manoharam* — captivating; *saḥ* — He; *bheje* — took; *meroḥ* — of Meru; *sat* — a fine; *śikharaḥ* — peak; *iva* — like; *anya* — of another; *śaila* — mountain; *pṛṣṭham* — the summit.

**58.** Setting down His pair of lotus feet on the ground with playful grace as He walked, He, filled with great effulgence, took His place on the supremely captivating couch — like a fine peak of Meru upon the summit of another mountain.

### Verse 59

सद्गौरैः परममहोभिरुन्मिषद्भिः
सर्व्वा पूः परिमिलिता तदा तदीयैः ।
बभ्राज प्रमथमिव प्रजेशसृष्टां
न्यक्कुर्व्वन्त्यनिशमिलावृतस्य शोभाम् ॥५९॥

*sad-gauraiḥ parama-mahobhir unmiṣadbhiḥ*
*sarvā pūḥ parimilitā tadā tadīyaiḥ |*
*babhrāja pramatham iva prajeśa-sṛṣṭāṁ*
*nyak-kurvanty aniśam ilāvṛtasya śobhām ||59||*

*Word for word:* *sat* — pure; *gauraiḥ* — golden; *parama* — supreme; *mahobhiḥ* — with rays; *unmiṣadbhiḥ* — flashing; *sarvā* — the whole; *pūḥ* — city; *parimilitā* — suffused; *tadā* — then; *tadīyaiḥ* — with His; *babhrāja* — shone; *pramatham* — crushingly; *iva* — as if; *prajeśa* — by the Lord of creatures; *sṛṣṭām* — created; *nyak* — to nothing; *kurvantī* — reducing; *aniśam* — unceasingly; *ilāvṛtasya* — of Ilavrita; *śobhām* — the beauty.

**59.** Then the whole city, suffused with His pure, golden, supreme, flashing rays, shone as if crushingly and unceasingly reducing to nothing the beauty of Ilavrita, created by the Lord of creatures.

*Note.* Ilavrita is the central region (*varsha*) of Jambudvipa, around the golden mountain Meru; the Lord of creatures (*Prajesha*, Prajapati) is Brahma. The edition (and the Gosvami edition) reads *pramatham*, "crushingly"; an earlier conjecture *prathamam* ("for the first time") is unnecessary. The edition also has *पुः*, corrected to *पूः* (nominative of *pur*, "city"). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 60

कैश्चिद्वा परिपिपिषे न गन्धसार-
स्ताम्बूलं न हि कति सज्जितं प्रचक्रे ।
आजह्रे कुसुमशतं तदा न कैश्चि-
त्पूर्णा भूः किमिव महोत्सवैस्तदानीम् ॥६०॥

*kaiś cid vā paripipiṣe na gandha-sāras*
*tāmbūlaṁ na hi kati sajjitaṁ pracakre |*
*ājahre kusuma-śataṁ tadā na kaiścit*
*pūrṇā bhūḥ kim iva mahotsavais tadānīm ||60||*

*Word for word:* *kaiḥ cit* — by whom; *vā* — then; *paripipiṣe* — was ground; *na* — not; *gandha* — fragrant; *sāraḥ* — essence (sandalwood); *tāmbūlam* — betel; *na* — not; *hi* — indeed; *kati* — how many; *sajjitam* — prepared; *pracakre* — made; *ājahre* — was brought; *kusuma* — of flowers; *śatam* — a hundred; *tadā* — then; *na* — not; *kaiścit* — by whom; *pūrṇā* — filled; *bhūḥ* — the earth; *kim iva* — with what [not]; *mahā* — great; *utsavaiḥ* — with festivities; *tadānīm* — then.

**60.** By whom was sandalwood not ground then? How many did not prepare betel? By whom were hundreds of flowers not brought then? With what great festivities was the earth not filled at that time!

*Note.* *Gandha-sāra* is sandalwood.

### Verse 61

कर्पूरैर्मरिचसिताभिरप्यखण्डा-
नन्दस्यानुभवसहोदरं समन्तात् ।
कैर्नो वा सपदि पयोविभावनादि-
व्यापारै रस इव सम्मदात् प्रसस्रे ॥६१॥

*karpūrair marica-sitābhir apy akhaṇḍā-*
*nandasyānubhava-sahodaraṁ samantāt |*
*kair no vā sapadi payo-vibhāvanādi-*
*vyāpārai rasa iva sammadāt prasasre ||61||*

*Word for word:* *karpūraiḥ* — with camphor; *marica* — with pepper; *sitābhiḥ* — with sugar; *api* — and; *akhaṇḍa* — of unbroken; *ānandasya* — of bliss; *anubhava* — to the experience; *sahodaram* — own brother (akin); *samantāt* — all around; *kaiḥ* — by whom; *no* — not; *vā* — indeed; *sapadi* — at once; *payaḥ* — of milk; *vibhāvana* — the preparation; *ādi* — and the like; *vyāpāraiḥ* — by the activities; *rasaḥ* — rasa; *iva* — as it were; *sammadāt* — out of joy; *prasasre* — was made to flow.

**61.** By whom, out of joy, was a *rasa* not at once set flowing all around — own brother, as it were, to the experience of unbroken bliss — through the work of preparing milk and the like, with camphor, pepper and sugar?

*Note.* The syllable *-nu-* in the second line is poorly printed in the edition; *anubhava* is restored by metre and sense. A play on words from the theory of *rasa*: *vibhāvana* ("preparation", but also *vibhāva*, the cause of an emotion), *anubhava* (echoing *anubhāva*, its outward expression), and *rasa* itself — both "drink, juice" and "aesthetic relish". Camphor and pepper are the usual spices for sweetened milk in Bengal.

### Verse 62

सोत्कण्ठं सपदि गदाधरेण पुष्पैः
सामोदैरतिरुचिरैः स्वयं तदानीम् ।
माल्यौघः प्रवणतरेण सौष्ठवेन
स्वस्वान्तैरिव स मनोरथैर्जगुम्फे ॥६२॥

*sotkaṇṭhaṁ sapadi gadādhareṇa puṣpaiḥ*
*sāmodair ati-ruciraiḥ svayaṁ tadānīm |*
*mālyaughaḥ pravaṇatareṇa sauṣṭhavena*
*sva-svāntair iva sa manorathair jagumphe ||62||*

*Word for word:* *sa* — with; *utkaṇṭham* — eagerness; *sapadi* — at once; *gadādhareṇa* — by Gadadhara; *puṣpaiḥ* — from flowers; *sa* — with; *āmodaiḥ* — fragrance (joy); *ati* — very; *ruciraiḥ* — lovely (pleasing); *svayam* — himself; *tadānīm* — then; *mālya* — of garlands; *oghaḥ* — a multitude; *pravaṇatareṇa* — most devoted; *sauṣṭhavena* — with skill; *sva* — of his own; *svāntaiḥ* — heart; *iva* — as if; *saḥ* — that; *manorathaiḥ* — from the desires; *jagumphe* — was woven.

**62.** Then Gadadhara himself, at once and eagerly, with most devoted skill, wove a multitude of garlands from fragrant, exceedingly lovely flowers — as if he were weaving them from the desires of his own heart.

*Note.* The epithets are double: *sāmoda* is "fragrant" and "joyful", *atirucira* "very lovely" and "much desired"; they fit both the flowers and Gadadhara's desires.

### Verse 63

उत्तंसं कुटिलकचोचितं वतंसौ
सश्रीकश्रुतियुगलोचितौ तथैव ।
नैपुण्याद्विरचितपुष्पबन्धरम्यं
ग्रैवेयं तदनु ललाटिकाञ्च कान्ताम् ॥६३॥

*uttaṁsaṁ kuṭila-kacocitaṁ vataṁsau*
*saśrīka-śruti-yugalocitau tathaiva |*
*naipuṇyād viracita-puṣpa-bandha-ramyaṁ*
*graiveyaṁ tad-anu lalāṭikāñ ca kāntām ||63||*

*Word for word:* *uttaṁsam* — a crown [of flowers] for the head; *kuṭila* — for the curling; *kaca* — locks; *ucitam* — suited; *vataṁsau* — a pair of ear ornaments; *saśrīka* — for the beautiful; *śruti* — of ears; *yugala* — pair; *ucitau* — suited; *tathā eva* — likewise; *naipuṇyāt* — skilfully; *viracita* — fashioned; *puṣpa* — of flowers; *bandha* — with knots; *ramyam* — charming; *graiveyam* — a necklace; *tat* — that; *anu* — after; *lalāṭikām* — an ornament for the forehead; *ca* — and; *kāntām* — lovely.

**63.** [He made] a crown suited to the curling locks, and likewise a pair of ear ornaments suited to the pair of beautiful ears; then a necklace, charming with skilfully fashioned knots of flowers, and a lovely ornament for the forehead.

*Note.* All the ornaments in verses 63–65 are made of flowers. *Vataṁsa* is the same as *avataṁsa*, an ear ornament.

### Verse 64

हारञ्च ग्रथनसुकौशलातिमुग्धं
केयूरे वलययुगञ्च कङ्कणे च ।
सर्व्वासामपि विदधे तदङ्गुलीनां
सच्छोभाचितरुचिरोर्म्मिकासमूहम् ॥६४॥

*hārañ ca grathana-su-kauśalāti-mugdhaṁ*
*keyūre valaya-yugañ ca kaṅkaṇe ca |*
*sarvāsām api vidadhe tad-aṅgulīnāṁ*
*sac-chobhācita-ruciormikā-samūham ||64||*

*Word for word:* *hāram* — a string [for the chest]; *ca* — and; *grathana* — of weaving; *su* — by great; *kauśala* — skill; *ati* — exceedingly; *mugdham* — charming; *keyūre* — a pair of armlets; *valaya* — of bangles; *yugam* — a pair; *ca* — and; *kaṅkaṇe* — a pair of bracelets; *ca* — and; *sarvāsām* — for all; *api* — even; *vidadhe* — he made; *tat* — His; *aṅgulīnām* — of the fingers; *sat* — with true; *śobhā* — beauty; *ācita* — filled; *rucira* — of lovely; *ūrmikā* — rings; *samūham* — a set.

**64.** He also made a string [for the chest], exceedingly charming through great skill in weaving, a pair of armlets, a pair of bangles and a pair of bracelets, and for all His fingers a set of lovely rings filled with true beauty.

*Note.* *Keyūra* is an armlet worn on the upper arm; *valaya* and *kaṅkaṇa* are two kinds of bracelet worn on the wrist.

### Verse 65

रम्यं सारसनमपि क्रमात् पदाब्जे
मञ्जीरं तदनु तदङ्गुलीविभूषाम् ।
निर्म्माय क्षणत इतः स गौरदेहे
सोत्कण्ठं चिरमुपयोजयाम्बभूव ॥६५॥

*ramyaṁ sārasanam api kramāt padābje*
*mañjīraṁ tad-anu tad-aṅgulī-vibhūṣām |*
*nirmāya kṣaṇata itaḥ sa gaura-dehe*
*sotkaṇṭhaṁ ciram upayojayām babhūva ||65||*

*Word for word:* *ramyam* — a lovely; *sārasanam* — girdle; *api* — and; *kramāt* — in due order; *pada* — the feet; *abje* — for the lotuses; *mañjīram* — anklet; *tat* — that; *anu* — after; *tat* — their; *aṅgulī* — of the toes; *vibhūṣām* — ornament; *nirmāya* — having made; *kṣaṇataḥ* — in a moment; *itaḥ* — thereupon; *saḥ* — he; *gaura* — of Gaura; *dehe* — on the body; *sa* — with; *utkaṇṭham* — longing; *ciram* — for a long time; *upayojayām babhūva* — put [them] on.

**65.** In due order, in a moment, he made a lovely girdle, anklets for the lotus feet and, after that, ornaments for their toes; and thereupon, full of longing, he spent a long time putting them on Gaura's body.

### Verse 66

आपादाङ्गुलि वरभालपट्टदेशं
श्रीखण्डागुरुघनसारकुङ्कुमानाम् ।
सत्पङ्कैर्वपुरलिपत्तदीयमेतत्
सोत्कण्ठं निविडमनन्तभाग्यराशिः ॥६६॥

*ā-pādāṅguli vara-bhāla-paṭṭa-deśaṁ*
*śrīkhaṇḍāguru-ghanasāra-kuṅkumānām |*
*sat-paṅkair vapur alipat tadīyam etat*
*sotkaṇṭhaṁ niviḍam ananta-bhāgya-rāśiḥ ||66||*

*Word for word:* *ā* — from; *pāda* — of the feet; *aṅguli* — the toes; *vara* — to the beautiful; *bhāla* — of the forehead; *paṭṭa* — expanse; *deśam* — region; *śrīkhaṇḍa* — of sandalwood; *aguru* — of aguru; *ghanasāra* — of camphor; *kuṅkumānām* — of kunkuma; *sat* — with fine; *paṅkaiḥ* — pastes; *vapuḥ* — body; *alipat* — anointed; *tadīyam* — His; *etat* — this; *sa* — with; *utkaṇṭham* — eagerness; *niviḍam* — thickly; *ananta* — of endless; *bhāgya* — good fortune; *rāśiḥ* — a heap.

**66.** And he [Gadadhara], a heap of endless good fortune, eagerly and thickly anointed this body of His — from the toes to the beautiful expanse of the forehead — with fine pastes of sandalwood, aguru, camphor and kunkuma.

*Note.* *Kunkuma* is a saffron (red-yellow) paste.

### Verse 67

लिप्तस्यापि च वपुषो घनं सुपङ्कैः
श्रीखण्डागुरुरचितै रतिप्रमोदैः ।
तेजोभिः परितिरयद्भिरेतदुच्चै-
रुद्द्योतैः कनकनिकायचारुगौरैः ॥६७॥

*liptasyāpi ca vapuṣo ghanaṁ su-paṅkaiḥ*
*śrīkhaṇḍāguru-racitai rati-pramodaiḥ |*
*tejobhiḥ paritirayadbhir etad uccair*
*uddyotaiḥ kanaka-nikāya-cāru-gauraiḥ ||67||*

*Word for word:* *liptasya* — anointed; *api* — though; *ca* — and; *vapuṣaḥ* — of the body; *ghanam* — thickly; *su* — with fine; *paṅkaiḥ* — pastes; *śrīkhaṇḍa* — of sandalwood; *aguru* — and aguru; *racitaiḥ* — made; *rati* — delight; *pramodaiḥ* — [giving] joy; *tejobhiḥ* — with rays; *paritirayadbhiḥ* — covering over; *etat* — this; *uccaiḥ* — powerfully; *uddyotaiḥ* — with radiances; *kanaka* — of gold; *nikāya* — like a heap; *cāru* — beautifully; *gauraiḥ* — golden.

**67.** His body was thickly anointed with fine, delightful pastes made of sandalwood and aguru; yet its rays powerfully overspread this [anointing] — radiances beautifully golden like a heap of gold…

*Note.* Verses 67–68 form one sentence: the genitive *vapuṣaḥ* and the instrumentals *tejobhiḥ… uddyotaiḥ* continue in verse 68 (*tejobhir nija-vapuṣo… saṁbhinnaḥ*).

### Verse 68

तैरेतैः कुसुमविभूषणैः समस्तै-
स्तैरेतैर्मलयजकुङ्कुमस्य पङ्कैः ।
तेजोभिर्निजवपुषो निसर्गगौरैः
संभिन्नः क इव बभूव गौरचन्द्रः ॥६८॥

*tair etaiḥ kusuma-vibhūṣaṇaiḥ samastais*
*tair etair malayaja-kuṅkumasya paṅkaiḥ |*
*tejobhir nija-vapuṣo nisarga-gauraiḥ*
*saṁbhinnaḥ ka iva babhūva gauracandraḥ ||68||*

*Word for word:* *taiḥ etaiḥ* — with these very; *kusuma* — flower; *vibhūṣaṇaiḥ* — ornaments; *samastaiḥ* — all; *taiḥ etaiḥ* — with these very; *malayaja* — of sandalwood; *kuṅkumasya* — and of kunkuma; *paṅkaiḥ* — with the pastes; *tejobhiḥ* — with the rays; *nija* — of His own; *vapuṣaḥ* — body; *nisarga* — by nature; *gauraiḥ* — golden; *saṁbhinnaḥ* — commingled; *kaḥ* — whom; *iva* — like; *babhūva* — became; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra.

**68.** …with all these flower ornaments, with these pastes of sandalwood and kunkuma, and with the naturally golden rays of His own body — commingled with all these, whom did Gaurachandra come to resemble?

*Note.* *Malayaja* ("born on Malaya") is sandalwood from the Malaya hills. The rhetorical question "whom did He resemble?" means: no one.

### Verse 69

द्वाराग्रेऽजिरभुवि वेष्टनानि दृष्ट्वा
नास्माभिः प्रभुरवलोकितव्य एव ।
इत्येवं मनसि विभाव्य तेपुरुच्चैः
श्रीवासप्रभृतिसगर्भ्यसर्व्वपत्न्यः ॥६९॥

*dvārāgre 'jira-bhuvi veṣṭanāni dṛṣṭvā*
*nāsmābhiḥ prabhur avalokitavya eva |*
*ity evaṁ manasi vibhāvya tepur uccaiḥ*
*śrīvāsa-prabhṛti-sagarbhya-sarva-patnyaḥ ||69||*

*Word for word:* *dvāra* — the door; *agre* — before; *ajira* — of the courtyard; *bhuvi* — on the ground; *veṣṭanāni* — the hangings; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *na* — not; *asmābhiḥ* — by us; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *avalokitavyaḥ* — will be seen; *eva* — at all; *iti evam* — thus; *manasi* — in the mind; *vibhāvya* — having concluded; *tepuḥ* — were tormented; *uccaiḥ* — sorely; *śrīvāsa* — of Srivasa; *prabhṛti* — and the others; *sagarbhya* — of the uterine brothers; *sarva* — all; *patnyaḥ* — the wives.

**69.** Seeing the hangings before the door, in the courtyard, the wives of Srivasa and of all his brothers thought in their minds: "We shall not see the Lord at all!" — and they were sorely distressed.

*Note.* The hangings on the middle door — verse 54.

### Verse 70

गौराङ्गः सपदि तथाविधा विदित्वा
ताः सर्व्वाः कृतसुकृता द्विजातिपत्नीः ।
एताः किं गृहमधि नो विशन्ति सर्व्वा
आगच्छन्त्विति निदिदेश तत्र पश्चात् ॥७०॥

*gaurāṅgaḥ sapadi tathā-vidhā viditvā*
*tāḥ sarvāḥ kṛta-sukṛtā dvijāti-patnīḥ |*
*etāḥ kiṁ gṛham adhi no viśanti sarvā*
*āgacchantv iti nidideśa tatra paścāt ||70||*

*Word for word:* *gaurāṅgaḥ* — Gauranga; *sapadi* — at once; *tathā* — such; *vidhāḥ* — [in] a state; *viditvā* — having understood; *tāḥ* — those; *sarvāḥ* — all; *kṛta* — who had performed; *sukṛtāḥ* — pious deeds; *dvijāti* — of the twice-born; *patnīḥ* — the wives; *etāḥ* — these; *kim* — why; *gṛham* — the house; *adhi* — into; *no* — not; *viśanti* — enter; *sarvāḥ* — all; *āgacchantu* — let them come; *iti* — thus; *nidideśa* — commanded; *tatra* — then; *paścāt* — afterwards.

**70.** Gauranga at once understood that all those virtuous wives of the brahmanas were in such a state, and then gave the command: "Why do they not come into the house? Let them all come!"

### Verse 71

श्रीवासस्तदनु निदेशमेतदीयं
ज्ञात्वा ताः सपदि समाजुहाव हर्षात् ।
ताः सर्व्वा अपि विविशुः सहर्षलज्जं
वैकल्याद्गृहमवलोकनाय तस्य ॥७१॥

*śrīvāsas tad-anu nideśam etadīyaṁ*
*jñātvā tāḥ sapadi samājuhāva harṣāt |*
*tāḥ sarvā api viviśuḥ sa-harṣa-lajjaṁ*
*vaikalyād gṛham avalokanāya tasya ||71||*

*Word for word:* *śrīvāsaḥ* — Srivasa; *tat* — that; *anu* — after; *nideśam* — the command; *etadīyam* — His; *jñātvā* — having learned; *tāḥ* — them; *sapadi* — at once; *samājuhāva* — called; *harṣāt* — out of joy; *tāḥ* — they; *sarvāḥ* — all; *api* — and; *viviśuḥ* — entered; *sa* — with; *harṣa* — joy; *lajjam* — and shyness; *vaikalyāt* — in agitation; *gṛham* — the house; *avalokanāya* — in order to see; *tasya* — Him.

**71.** Learning this command of His, Srivasa joyfully called them at once; and all of them, in agitation, joyful and shy, entered the house to see Him.

### Verse 72

आविश्य प्रकटितसत्प्रकाशरम्यं
तं दृष्ट्वा मुदमतुलामभूतपूर्व्वाम् ।
संप्रापुर्भुवि च निपेतुरात्ततोषा-
स्तत्पादाम्बुजमपि निर्भरं प्रपन्नाः ॥७२॥

*āviśya prakaṭita-sat-prakāśa-ramyaṁ*
*taṁ dṛṣṭvā mudam atulām abhūta-pūrvām |*
*samprāpur bhuvi ca nipetur ātta-toṣās*
*tat-pādāmbujam api nirbharaṁ prapannāḥ ||72||*

*Word for word:* *āviśya* — having entered; *prakaṭita* — with manifest; *sat* — true; *prakāśa* — radiance; *ramyam* — beautiful; *tam* — Him; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *mudam* — joy; *atulām* — incomparable; *abhūta* — not having been; *pūrvām* — before; *samprāpuḥ* — attained; *bhuvi* — to the ground; *ca* — and; *nipetuḥ* — fell; *ātta* — having obtained; *toṣāḥ* — contentment; *tat* — His; *pāda* — of the feet; *ambujam* — to the lotus; *api* — and; *nirbharam* — wholly; *prapannāḥ* — surrendered.

**72.** Entering and seeing Him, beautiful with His true radiance manifest, they attained an incomparable joy such as they had never known before; and, filled with contentment, they fell to the ground, wholly surrendered to His lotus feet.

### Verse 73

मच्चित्ता भवत सदेत्यभीक्ष्णमुक्त्वा
सर्व्वासां शिरसि पदारविन्दयुग्मम् ।
कारुण्यामृतरससेचनातिसार्द्रः
श्रीगौरः परमगुणाम्बुधिर्व्यधत्त ॥७३॥

*mac-cittā bhavata sadety abhīkṣṇam uktvā*
*sarvāsāṁ śirasi padāravinda-yugmam |*
*kāruṇyāmṛta-rasa-secanāti-sārdraḥ*
*śrī-gauraḥ parama-guṇāmbudhir vyadhatta ||73||*

*Word for word:* *mat* — on Me; *cittāḥ* — with minds fixed; *bhavata* — be; *sadā* — always; *iti* — thus; *abhīkṣṇam* — again and again; *uktvā* — having said; *sarvāsām* — of all; *śirasi* — on the head; *pada* — of the feet; *aravinda* — of the lotuses; *yugmam* — the pair; *kāruṇya* — of compassion; *amṛta* — of the nectar; *rasa* — with the juice; *secana* — by the sprinkling; *ati* — deeply; *sa-ārdraḥ* — moistened; *śrī-gauraḥ* — Sri Gaura; *parama* — of supreme; *guṇa* — virtues; *ambudhiḥ* — the ocean; *vyadhatta* — placed.

**73.** Saying again and again, "Be always with your minds fixed on Me!", Sri Gaura, an ocean of supreme virtues, deeply moistened by the sprinkling of the nectar-juice of compassion, placed His pair of lotus feet on the head of each one of them.

*Note.* *Mac-cittā bhavata* echoes the Gita: *mac-cittaḥ* (18.57–58), *man-manā bhava* (9.34, 18.65).

### Verse 74

तैरेतैरतिमहतां सतां महद्भिः
श्रीवासप्रभृतिभिरेव सत्प्रकाशः ।
पश्यद्भिर्निजनिजचित्तहर्षराशि-
र्देहीव प्रथममलं तदा व्यतर्कि ॥७४॥

*tair etair ati-mahatāṁ satāṁ mahadbhiḥ*
*śrīvāsa-prabhṛtibhir eva sat-prakāśaḥ |*
*paśyadbhir nija-nija-citta-harṣa-rāśir*
*dehīva prathamam alaṁ tadā vyatarki ||74||*

*Word for word:* *taiḥ etaiḥ* — by these very; *ati* — very; *mahatām* — of the great; *satām* — among the saints; *mahadbhiḥ* — by the great; *śrīvāsa* — by Srivasa; *prabhṛtibhiḥ* — and the others; *eva* — indeed; *sat* — of true; *prakāśaḥ* — radiance [full]; *paśyadbhiḥ* — looking on; *nija-nija* — of each one's own; *citta* — heart; *harṣa* — of joy; *rāśiḥ* — the heap; *dehī* — embodied; *iva* — as if; *prathamam* — at first; *alam* — fully; *tadā* — then; *vyatarki* — was taken to be.

**74.** And Srivasa and the others, great among the very greatest saints, looking on Him, full of true radiance, at first fully took Him then to be the very joy of each one's own heart, embodied, as it were.

### Verse 75

सर्व्वे तच्चरणसरोरुहां समीपम्
स्वर्णाढ्यं सकलमिह प्रचिक्षिपुस्ते ।
तैरेतैरथ समभूत्तदैव खट्टा
सत्कल्पव्रततिरिवातिरत्नसूः सा ॥७५॥

*sarve tac-caraṇa-saroruhāṁ samīpaṁ*
*svarṇāḍhyaṁ sakalam iha pracikṣipus te |*
*tair etair atha samabhūt tadaiva khaṭṭā*
*sat-kalpa-vratatir ivāti-ratna-sūḥ sā ||75||*

*Word for word:* *sarve* — all; *tat* — His; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *saroruhām* — of the lotuses; *samīpam* — near; *svarṇa* — in gold; *āḍhyam* — rich; *sakalam* — everything; *iha* — here; *pracikṣipuḥ* — laid down; *te* — they; *taiḥ etaiḥ* — by these very [gifts]; *atha* — and; *samabhūt* — became; *tadā eva* — at once; *khaṭṭā* — the couch; *sat* — a fine; *kalpa* — wish-fulfilling; *vratatiḥ* — creeper; *iva* — like; *ati* — in abundance; *ratna* — jewels; *sūḥ* — bringing forth; *sā* — that.

**75.** They all laid here at His lotus feet everything they had that was rich in gold; and with these [gifts] the couch at once became like a fine wish-fulfilling creeper that brings forth jewels in abundance.

*Note.* *Khaṭṭā* — so in the edition (compare *khaṭvā* in verse 55); it is the Bengali form of the same word. The *kalpa-latā* is the heavenly wish-fulfilling creeper.

### Verse 76

कार्पासं वसनयुगं जहौ निवीय
क्षौमं श्रीयुतमथ हेमगौरदेहः ।
तद्वस्त्रं द्विजवनिताभ्य आत्मनैव
स्नेहेन न्यदिशदसौ कृपासमुद्रः ॥७६॥

*kārpāsaṁ vasana-yugaṁ jahau nivīya*
*kṣaumaṁ śrī-yutam atha hema-gaura-dehaḥ |*
*tad-vastraṁ dvija-vanitābhya ātmanaiva*
*snehena nyadiśad asau kṛpā-samudraḥ ||76||*

*Word for word:* *kārpāsam* — of cotton; *vasana* — of garments; *yugam* — the pair; *jahau* — cast off; *nivīya* — having put on; *kṣaumam* — silk; *śrī* — with splendour; *yutam* — endowed; *atha* — then; *hema* — like gold; *gaura* — golden; *dehaḥ* — [He] whose body; *tat* — that; *vastram* — cloth; *dvija* — of the brahmanas; *vanitābhyaḥ* — to the wives; *ātmanā* — Himself; *eva* — indeed; *snehena* — with love; *nyadiśat* — bestowed; *asau* — He; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *samudraḥ* — the ocean.

**76.** Then, putting on splendid silk, He whose body is golden like gold cast off the pair of cotton garments; and that cloth He, the ocean of mercy, Himself lovingly bestowed on the wives of the brahmanas.

*Note.* *Kṣauma* is cloth of linen or silk.

### Verse 77

भूयोऽन्यच्छुचि वसनं ददौ प्रसन्नः
प्रासाद्यं निजपरमप्रियेभ्य एभ्यः ।
पर्य्यङ्कोपरि परितस्थिवान् विलासी
संरेजे सुविलासितानि तानि कुर्व्वन् ॥७७॥

*bhūyo 'nyac chuci vasanaṁ dadau prasannaḥ*
*prāsādyaṁ nija-parama-priyebhya ebhyaḥ |*
*paryaṅkopari paritasthivān vilāsī*
*saṁreje su-vilāsitāni tāni kurvan ||77||*

*Word for word:* *bhūyaḥ* — again; *anyat* — other; *śuci* — pure; *vasanam* — cloth; *dadau* — gave; *prasannaḥ* — pleased; *prāsādyam* — as prasada; *nija* — His own; *parama* — most; *priyebhyaḥ* — to the dear; *ebhyaḥ* — to these; *paryaṅka* — the couch; *upari* — upon; *paritasthivān* — seated; *vilāsī* — playful; *saṁreje* — shone; *su* — beautifully; *vilāsitāni* — enlivened with play; *tāni* — them; *kurvan* — making.

**77.** Pleased, He again gave other pure cloth as *prasada* to these, His dearest ones; and, seated upon the couch, playful, He shone, making all those [things] beautifully alive with His play.

*Note.* *Prāsādya* is "what is given as grace", that is, as *prasada*. The end of the verse is unclear: *tāni* (neuter) may refer to the garments or to all the gifts. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 78

उत्सार्य क्षणमनुलिप्तमेव भूयः
संधत्ते मलयजपङ्कमिष्टगन्धि ।
माल्यानि क्षणनिहितानि तानि हित्वा
भूयोऽसौ रहसि दधाति पुष्पमालाः ॥७८॥

*utsārya kṣaṇam anuliptam eva bhūyaḥ*
*saṁdhatte malayaja-paṅkam iṣṭa-gandhi |*
*mālyāni kṣaṇa-nihitāni tāni hitvā*
*bhūyo 'sau rahasi dadhāti puṣpa-mālāḥ ||78||*

*Word for word:* *utsārya* — having wiped off; *kṣaṇam* — for a moment; *anuliptam* — applied; *eva* — only; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *saṁdhatte* — puts on; *malayaja* — of sandalwood; *paṅkam* — paste; *iṣṭa* — of favourite; *gandhi* — fragrance; *mālyāni* — the garlands; *kṣaṇa* — for a moment; *nihitāni* — put on; *tāni* — those; *hitvā* — having cast off; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *asau* — He; *rahasi* — in seclusion; *dadhāti* — puts on; *puṣpa* — of flowers; *mālāḥ* — garlands.

**78.** Wiping off [the paste] applied only a moment before, He again puts on a paste of sandalwood of His favourite fragrance; casting off the garlands put on only a moment before, He again, in seclusion, puts on garlands of flowers.

### Verse 79

ताम्बूलं सततमुपाश्नतोऽस्य भूय-
स्त्यक्तेनाप्यतिवहलेन चर्व्वितेन ।
पूर्णः स्यात् सपदि पतद्ग्रहस्तदेनं
बारंबारमपनयन्ति विप्रपत्न्यः ॥७९॥

*tāmbūlaṁ satatam upāśnato 'sya bhūyas*
*tyaktenāpy ati-vahalena carvitena |*
*pūrṇaḥ syāt sapadi patadgrahas tad enaṁ*
*bāraṁ-bāram apanayanti vipra-patnyaḥ ||79||*

*Word for word:* *tāmbūlam* — betel; *satatam* — constantly; *upāśnataḥ* — chewing; *asya* — of Him; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *tyaktena* — discarded; *api* — and; *ati* — very; *vahalena* — copious; *carvitena* — with the chewed [betel]; *pūrṇaḥ* — filled; *syāt* — would be; *sapadi* — at once; *patadgrahaḥ* — the spittoon; *tat* — therefore; *enam* — it; *bāram-bāram* — again and again; *apanayanti* — carry away; *vipra* — of the brahmanas; *patnyaḥ* — the wives.

**79.** As He constantly chewed betel, the spittoon would at once be filled again with the very copious chewed [betel] He discarded; and so the wives of the brahmanas carried it away again and again.

*Note.* *Vahala* = *bahala*, "thick, copious" (*b* and *v* are often interchanged in Bengali orthography; compare *bāraṁ-bāram* for *vāraṁ vāram*).

### Verse 80

आघ्रेयं सपदि विजिघ्रति स्म नाथो
भोग्यञ्च प्रतिबुभुजे कृपासमुद्रः ।
आदेयं यदपि दधार सर्व्वमेवं
गौराङ्गः सविलसितं चकार भूयः ॥८०॥

*āghreyaṁ sapadi vijighrati sma nātho*
*bhogyañ ca pratibubhuje kṛpā-samudraḥ |*
*ādeyaṁ yad api dadhāra sarvam evaṁ*
*gaurāṅgaḥ sa-vilasitaṁ cakāra bhūyaḥ ||80||*

*Word for word:* *āghreyam* — what is to be smelled; *sapadi* — at once; *vijighrati sma* — smelled; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *bhogyam* — what is to be enjoyed; *ca* — and; *pratibubhuje* — partook of; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *samudraḥ* — the ocean; *ādeyam* — what is to be taken; *yat* — whatever; *api* — and; *dadhāra* — accepted; *sarvam* — everything; *evam* — thus; *gaurāṅgaḥ* — Gauranga; *sa* — with; *vilasitam* — play; *cakāra* — did; *bhūyaḥ* — again [and again].

**80.** The Lord at once smelled whatever was to be smelled; the ocean of mercy partook of whatever was to be enjoyed and accepted whatever was to be taken — thus Gauranga did everything, again and again, playfully.

### Verse 81

यूयं नृत्यथ झटितीत्यथो कृपावा-
नद्वैतप्रभुवरमादिदेश धीरम् ।
तच्छ्रुत्वा मुदितमनाः समं महद्भि-
र्गायद्भिः सुखविवशैरसौ ननर्त ॥८१॥

*yūyaṁ nṛtyatha jhaṭitīty atho kṛpāvān*
*advaita-prabhu-varam ādideśa dhīram |*
*tac chrutvā mudita-manāḥ samaṁ mahadbhir*
*gāyadbhiḥ sukha-vivaśair asau nanarta ||81||*

*Word for word:* *yūyam* — you; *nṛtyatha* — dance; *jhaṭiti* — at once; *iti* — thus; *atho* — then; *kṛpāvān* — the merciful [Lord]; *advaita* — Advaita; *prabhu* — of masters; *varam* — the best; *ādideśa* — commanded; *dhīram* — wise; *tat* — that; *śrutvā* — having heard; *mudita* — rejoicing; *manāḥ* — [with] a heart; *samam* — together with; *mahadbhiḥ* — the great [Vaishnavas]; *gāyadbhiḥ* — singing; *sukha* — by happiness; *vivaśaiḥ* — overwhelmed; *asau* — he; *nanarta* — danced.

**81.** Then the merciful [Lord] commanded the wise Advaita, the best of masters: "Dance, at once!" Hearing that, He, His heart rejoicing, danced together with the great [Vaishnavas], who sang, overwhelmed with happiness.

### Verse 82

श्रीवासोदितसमुपागता सकम्पं
सा देवी सकलजगज्जनस्य माता ।
मातेति प्रथितवती महाप्रभोर्या
तत्काले प्रभुपुरतो बभूव भीता ॥८२॥

*śrīvāsodita-samupāgatā sa-kampaṁ*
*sā devī sakala-jagaj-janasya mātā |*
*māteti prathitavatī mahāprabhor yā*
*tat-kāle prabhu-purato babhūva bhītā ||82||*

*Word for word:* *śrīvāsa* — of Srivasa; *udita* — at the word; *samupāgatā* — having come; *sa* — with; *kampam* — trembling; *sā* — that; *devī* — lady; *sakala* — of all; *jagat* — the world; *janasya* — of the people; *mātā* — the mother; *mātā* — the mother; *iti* — as; *prathitavatī* — known; *mahāprabhoḥ* — of Mahaprabhu; *yā* — who; *tat* — at that; *kāle* — time; *prabhu* — the Lord; *purataḥ* — before; *babhūva* — became; *bhītā* — afraid.

**82.** At Srivasa's word there came, trembling, that lady, the mother of all the people of the world, who was known as the mother of Mahaprabhu; and at that time, standing before the Lord, she was afraid.

*Note.* This is Shachidevi.

### Verse 83

तां दृष्ट्वा सपदि महाप्रभुर्मुखाब्जं
तत्तिर्य्यक् सचकितमेव सामि चक्रे ।
तद्दृष्ट्वा हृदि समवाप्य दुःखमेष
श्रीवासः सभयमुवाच गौरचन्द्रम् ॥८३॥

*tāṁ dṛṣṭvā sapadi mahāprabhur mukhābjaṁ*
*tat tiryak sa-cakitam eva sāmi cakre |*
*tad dṛṣṭvā hṛdi samavāpya duḥkham eṣa*
*śrīvāsaḥ sa-bhayam uvāca gauracandram ||83||*

*Word for word:* *tām* — her; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *sapadi* — at once; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *mukha* — of the face; *abjam* — the lotus; *tat* — that; *tiryak* — to the side; *sa* — with; *cakitam* — alarm; *eva* — as it were; *sāmi* — half; *cakre* — made (turned away); *tat* — this; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *hṛdi* — in the heart; *samavāpya* — having felt; *duḥkham* — pain; *eṣaḥ* — this; *śrīvāsaḥ* — Srivasa; *sa* — with; *bhayam* — fear; *uvāca* — said; *gauracandram* — to Gaurachandra.

**83.** Seeing her, Mahaprabhu at once, as if startled, turned His lotus face half away to the side. Seeing this, Srivasa, pained at heart, said fearfully to Gaurachandra:

### Verse 84

नैवेदं परमदयस्य ते कृपालो-
र्योग्यञ्चेद्वयमपि कुत्र ते भवामः ।
नैतत्ते प्रभुवर युज्यते प्रभुत्वं
तत्पश्चात् त्वरितमुवाच ताञ्च विप्रः ॥८४॥

*naivedaṁ parama-dayasya te kṛpālor*
*yogyaṁ ced vayam api kutra te bhavāmaḥ |*
*naitat te prabhu-vara yujyate prabhutvaṁ*
*tat paścāt tvaritam uvāca tāñ ca vipraḥ ||84||*

*Word for word:* *na* — not; *eva* — at all; *idam* — this; *parama* — supremely; *dayasya* — of the compassionate; *te* — of You; *kṛpāloḥ* — of the merciful; *yogyam* — worthy; *cet* — if; *vayam* — we; *api* — too; *kutra* — where; *te* — Yours; *bhavāmaḥ* — shall be; *na* — not; *etat* — this; *te* — for You; *prabhu* — of lords; *vara* — O best; *yujyate* — befits; *prabhutvam* — lordliness; *tat* — that; *paścāt* — after; *tvaritam* — quickly; *uvāca* — said; *tām* — to her; *ca* — and; *vipraḥ* — the brahmana.

**84.** "This is not at all worthy of You, who are supremely compassionate and merciful! And if it is worthy, then where do we, too, stand as Yours? This lordliness does not befit You, O best of lords!" And after that the brahmana quickly said to her:

*Note.* In the second line the edition has *योग्यञ्चे द्वयमपि*; we read *yogyaṁ ced vayam api*. Literally, "where shall we be Yours?" The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 85

आगच्छ प्रणम निपत्य भूमिपृष्ठे
श्रुत्वैवं पुनरपि तां विलम्बमानाम् ।
नायं ते सुत इति नम्यतां निपत्य
क्ष्मापृष्ठे त्वरितमिति प्रियं जगाद ॥८५॥

*āgaccha praṇama nipatya bhūmi-pṛṣṭhe*
*śrutvaivaṁ punar api tāṁ vilambamānām |*
*nāyaṁ te suta iti namyatāṁ nipatya*
*kṣmā-pṛṣṭhe tvaritam iti priyaṁ jagāda ||85||*

*Word for word:* *āgaccha* — come; *praṇama* — bow down; *nipatya* — having fallen; *bhūmi* — of the earth; *pṛṣṭhe* — on the surface; *śrutvā* — having heard; *evam* — thus; *punaḥ api* — still; *tām* — to her; *vilambamānām* — hesitating; *na* — not; *ayam* — He; *te* — your; *sutaḥ* — son; *iti* — thus; *namyatām* — let [Him] be bowed to; *nipatya* — having fallen; *kṣmā* — of the earth; *pṛṣṭhe* — on the surface; *tvaritam* — quickly; *iti* — thus; *priyam* — kindly; *jagāda* — said.

**85.** "Come, fall on the ground and bow down!" And when, having heard this, she still hesitated, he said to her kindly: "He is not your son! Quickly fall to the ground and bow down [to Him]!"

### Verse 86

इत्येवं परिकलयन्त्यसौ निपत्य
क्ष्मापृष्ठे प्रभुमनमत्तदैव देवी ।
श्रीवासस्तदवसरे जगाद नाथं
साशङ्कं द्रुतहृदयो भयेन धीरः ॥८६॥

*ity evaṁ parikalayanty asau nipatya*
*kṣmā-pṛṣṭhe prabhum anamat tadaiva devī |*
*śrīvāsas tad-avasare jagāda nāthaṁ*
*sāśaṅkaṁ druta-hṛdayo bhayena dhīraḥ ||86||*

*Word for word:* *iti evam* — thus; *parikalayantī* — reflecting; *asau* — she; *nipatya* — having fallen; *kṣmā* — of the earth; *pṛṣṭhe* — on the surface; *prabhum* — to the Lord; *anamat* — bowed down; *tadā eva* — at once; *devī* — the lady; *śrīvāsaḥ* — Srivasa; *tat* — at that; *avasare* — moment; *jagāda* — said; *nātham* — to the Lord; *sa* — with; *āśaṅkam* — apprehension; *druta* — melting; *hṛdayaḥ* — [with] a heart; *bhayena* — from fear; *dhīraḥ* — the wise.

**86.** Reflecting thus, the lady at once fell to the ground and bowed down to the Lord. At that moment the wise Srivasa, his heart melting with fear, said apprehensively to the Lord:

### Verse 87

कारुण्यं कुरु भगवन् प्रभो तदस्यै
येनेयं त्वयि न करोति पुत्रभावम् ।
येनेयं तव चरणे भवेत् प्रपन्ना
तेनैव प्रभवति निर्वृतिर्ममापि ॥८७॥

*kāruṇyaṁ kuru bhagavan prabho tad asyai*
*yeneyaṁ tvayi na karoti putra-bhāvam |*
*yeneyaṁ tava caraṇe bhavet prapannā*
*tenaiva prabhavati nirvṛtir mamāpi ||87||*

*Word for word:* *kāruṇyam* — mercy; *kuru* — show; *bhagavan* — O Bhagavan; *prabho* — O Lord; *tat* — therefore; *asyai* — to her; *yena* — so that; *iyam* — she; *tvayi* — towards You; *na* — not; *karoti* — has; *putra* — of [a mother to] a son; *bhāvam* — the feeling; *yena* — so that; *iyam* — she; *tava* — at Your; *caraṇe* — feet; *bhavet* — may become; *prapannā* — surrendered; *tena* — by that; *eva* — alone; *prabhavati* — comes about; *nirvṛtiḥ* — peace; *mama* — my; *api* — too.

**87.** "Show mercy to her, then, O Bhagavan, O Lord, so that she may not regard You as a son, so that she may surrender at Your feet. Only by that shall I too find peace."

*Note.* In Karnapura Srivasa asks the Lord to replace Shachi's maternal feeling with reverence. The later Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition, by contrast, sees maternal love (*vatsalya*) as one of the highest expressions of love; here we have an episode of the *maha-prakasha*, when the Lord revealed His majesty.

### Verse 88

इत्युक्ते सति सहसा महाशयोऽस्या
मूर्द्धनि श्रीयुतपदपङ्कजं स नाथः ।
आधाय प्रथितकृपस्तथैव तस्यै
कारुण्यं परिकलयन्नुवाच हृष्टः ॥८८॥

*ity ukte sati sahasā mahāśayo 'syā*
*mūrdhani śrī-yuta-pada-paṅkajaṁ sa nāthaḥ |*
*ādhāya prathita-kṛpas tathaiva tasyai*
*kāruṇyaṁ parikalayann uvāca hṛṣṭaḥ ||88||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *ukte sati* — when it had been said; *sahasā* — at once; *mahā* — great; *āśayaḥ* — [of] heart; *asyāḥ* — her; *mūrdhani* — on the head; *śrī* — with beauty; *yuta* — endowed; *pada* — of the foot; *paṅkajam* — the lotus; *saḥ* — that; *nāthaḥ* — Lord; *ādhāya* — having placed; *prathita* — renowned; *kṛpaḥ* — [for] mercy; *tathā eva* — just so; *tasyai* — to her; *kāruṇyam* — mercy; *parikalayan* — bestowing; *uvāca* — said; *hṛṣṭaḥ* — joyful.

**88.** When this had been said, that great-hearted Lord, renowned for His mercy, at once placed His beautiful lotus foot on her head and, bestowing mercy on her just so, joyfully said ["So be it"].

*Note.* The Lord's words are not in the text: *uvāca* has no direct speech; the words in brackets are our supplement. (?) Perhaps *tathaiva* ("just so") itself is His reply. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 89

स्पृष्टे तत्पदकमले तदैव चित्रं
नेत्राभ्यामभिदधती जलं गरीयः ।
विभ्रान्ता पुलकितदेहयष्टिरासीत्
सोद्दामं नटनपरा हतत्रपैव ॥८९॥

*spṛṣṭe tat-pada-kamale tadaiva citraṁ*
*netrābhyām abhidadhatī jalaṁ garīyaḥ |*
*vibhrāntā pulakita-deha-yaṣṭir āsīt*
*soddāmaṁ naṭana-parā hata-trapaiva ||89||*

*Word for word:* *spṛṣṭe* — when touched; *tat* — His; *pada* — of the foot; *kamale* — the lotus; *tadā eva* — at once; *citram* — what a wonder; *netrābhyām* — from the eyes; *abhidadhatī* — shedding; *jalam* — water; *garīyaḥ* — copious; *vibhrāntā* — bewildered; *pulakita* — thrilled with hairs on end; *deha* — of the body; *yaṣṭiḥ* — [her] slender stalk; *āsīt* — became; *sa* — with; *uddāmam* — without restraint; *naṭana* — to dancing; *parā* — given up; *hata* — having lost; *trapā* — shame; *eva* — utterly.

**89.** The moment His lotus foot touched [her] — what a wonder! — she, shedding copious tears from her eyes, became bewildered, her slender body thrilled with hairs standing on end; and, all shame utterly lost, she gave herself up to unrestrained dancing.

*Note.* The edition has *स्पृष्टै* and *देहषष्टि* — misprints; we read *spṛṣṭe* (locative absolute) and *deha-yaṣṭi* ("body-stalk", of a slender figure).

### Verse 90

एतैः सा बहुविधचेष्टया प्रसह्य
व्यावृत्ता सुचिरमिवाप चित्तधैर्य्यम् ।
क्रन्दन्ती नयनजलेन धौतदेहा
संभिन्ना सभयमसौ जगाम गेहम् ॥९०॥

*etaiḥ sā bahu-vidha-ceṣṭayā prasahya*
*vyāvṛttā suciram ivāpa citta-dhairyam |*
*krandantī nayana-jalena dhauta-dehā*
*saṁbhinnā sa-bhayam asau jagāma geham ||90||*

*Word for word:* *etaiḥ* — by these [devotees]; *sā* — she; *bahu* — of many; *vidha* — kinds; *ceṣṭayā* — by effort; *prasahya* — forcibly; *vyāvṛttā* — brought back; *suciram* — after a very long time; *iva* — as it were; *āpa* — regained; *citta* — of mind; *dhairyam* — composure; *krandantī* — weeping; *nayana* — of the eyes; *jalena* — by the water; *dhauta* — washed; *dehā* — [with] a body; *saṁbhinnā* — shaken; *sa* — with; *bhayam* — fear; *asau* — she; *jagāma* — went; *geham* — home.

**90.** With many kinds of effort they forcibly brought her back [to her senses], and only after a very long time, as it were, did she regain her composure. Weeping, her body washed with the water of her eyes, shaken, she went home in fear.

### Verse 91

उन्निद्रप्रथमसरोजपत्रनेत्रो
गौराङ्गः परमविलासवान् कृपावान् ।
यामिन्या विगतकृशद्वियामवत्या-
स्तद्यामद्वयमनयत्तथा विहारैः ॥९१॥

*unnidra-prathama-saroja-patra-netro*
*gaurāṅgaḥ parama-vilāsavān kṛpāvān |*
*yāminyā vigata-kṛśa-dviyāmavatyās*
*tad-yāma-dvayam anayat tathā vihāraiḥ ||91||*

*Word for word:* *unnidra* — opened; *prathama* — for the first time; *saroja* — of a lotus; *patra* — [like] the petals; *netraḥ* — [He] whose eyes; *gaurāṅgaḥ* — Gauranga; *parama* — supreme; *vilāsavān* — full of playfulness; *kṛpāvān* — merciful; *yāminyāḥ* — of the night; *vigata* — gone; *kṛśa* — short; *dvi* — two; *yāmavatyāḥ* — having watches; *tat* — its; *yāma* — of watches; *dvayam* — the pair; *anayat* — spent; *tathā* — thus; *vihāraiḥ* — in pastimes.

**91.** Two short watches of the night had already passed; and Gauranga — His eyes like the petals of a lotus just opened for the first time, full of supreme playfulness, merciful — spent its [remaining] two watches thus, in pastimes.

*Note.* A *yāma* (*prahara*) is a watch, a quarter of the night, about three hours. The watches are "short" because these are summer nights (verses 32–37).

### Verse 92

आश्लेषैः कति च तथैष कांश्चिदन्या-
नाचुम्बैस्तदनु च चर्व्वितैस्तथान्यान् ।
इत्येवं परमकृपानिधिः सुतृप्तान्
चक्रे सद्विलसितलीलया महत्या ॥९२॥

*āśleṣaiḥ kati ca tathaiṣa kāṁścid anyān*
*ācumbais tad-anu ca carvitais tathānyān |*
*ity evaṁ parama-kṛpā-nidhiḥ sutṛptān*
*cakre sad-vilasita-līlayā mahatyā ||92||*

*Word for word:* *āśleṣaiḥ* — with embraces; *kati ca* — some; *tathā* — so; *eṣaḥ* — He; *kāṁścit* — some; *anyān* — others; *ācumbaiḥ* — with kisses; *tat* — that; *anu* — after; *ca* — and; *carvitaiḥ* — with the chewed [betel]; *tathā* — so; *anyān* — others; *iti evam* — thus; *parama* — of supreme; *kṛpā* — mercy; *nidhiḥ* — the treasure-house; *sutṛptān* — fully satisfied; *cakre* — made; *sat* — beautiful; *vilasita* — of play; *līlayā* — by the pastime; *mahatyā* — great.

**92.** Some He [satisfied] with embraces, others with kisses, and others again with chewed [betel]; thus the treasure-house of supreme mercy fully satisfied [them all] by His great and beautiful playful pastime.

*Note.* *Carvita* is betel chewed by the Lord — the greatest *prasada*.

### Verse 93

इत्येवं पुनरपि देवतालयेऽसौ
संगत्य क्षणमवतस्थिवान् विरेजे ।
तत्पश्चादतिकरुणः क्रमाच्चतुर्णां
भ्रातॄणामपि चतुरो गृहान् जगाम ॥९३॥

*ity evaṁ punar api devatālaye 'sau*
*saṁgatya kṣaṇam avatasthivān vireje |*
*tat paścād ati-karuṇaḥ kramāc caturṇāṁ*
*bhrātṝṇām api caturo gṛhān jagāma ||93||*

*Word for word:* *iti evam* — thus; *punaḥ api* — once more; *devatā* — of the Deity; *ālaye* — to the abode; *asau* — He; *saṁgatya* — having come; *kṣaṇam* — for a while; *avatasthivān* — having stayed; *vireje* — shone; *tat* — that; *paścāt* — after; *ati* — exceedingly; *karuṇaḥ* — compassionate; *kramāt* — in turn; *caturṇām* — of the four; *bhrātṝṇām* — brothers; *api* — and; *caturaḥ* — to the four; *gṛhān* — houses; *jagāma* — went.

**93.** Thus He came once more to the shrine and, staying there a little while, shone; after that, exceedingly compassionate, He went in turn to the four houses of the four brothers.

*Note.* The four brothers are Srivasa, Sri Rama, Shripati and Shrinidhi; each had his own house around a common courtyard.

### Verse 94

इत्येवं बहु विलसत्कृतप्रकाशो
भूयोऽपि प्रभुरधिगम्य देवगेहम् ।
तान् सर्व्वानवददलं विलम्बितैस्तद्
गच्छामीत्यतिकमनीयगौरदेहः ॥९४॥

*ity evaṁ bahu vilasat-kṛta-prakāśo*
*bhūyo 'pi prabhur adhigamya deva-geham |*
*tān sarvān avadad alaṁ vilambitais tad*
*gacchāmīty ati-kamanīya-gaura-dehaḥ ||94||*

*Word for word:* *iti evam* — thus; *bahu* — in many ways; *vilasat* — playing; *kṛta* — [He who had] made; *prakāśaḥ* — [His] radiance [manifest]; *bhūyaḥ api* — once more; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *adhigamya* — having come to; *deva* — of God; *geham* — the house; *tān* — to them; *sarvān* — all; *avadat* — said; *alam* — enough; *vilambitaiḥ* — of delays; *tat* — so; *gacchāmi* — I am going; *iti* — thus; *ati* — exceedingly; *kamanīya* — lovely; *gaura* — golden; *dehaḥ* — [He] whose body.

**94.** Having thus manifested His radiance, playing in many ways, the Lord, whose golden body was exceedingly lovely, came once more to the shrine and said to them all: "Enough of delays — so I am going."

*Note.* (?) "I am going" — in the light of verse 95: leaving this manifestation (or this body). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 95

तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनममुष्य ते समस्ता
अद्वैतप्रभृतय एवमेवमूचुः ।
एवं चेद्वयमपि तद्गले कृपाणं
बद्ध्वैतत् सपदि शरीरमाजहीमः ॥९५॥

*tac chrutvā vacanam amuṣya te samastā*
*advaita-prabhṛtaya evam evam ūcuḥ |*
*evaṁ ced vayam api tad gale kṛpāṇaṁ*
*baddhvaitat sapadi śarīram ājahīmaḥ ||95||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — those; *śrutvā* — having heard; *vacanam* — words; *amuṣya* — His; *te* — they; *samastāḥ* — all; *advaita* — Advaita; *prabhṛtayaḥ* — and the others; *evam evam* — just so; *ūcuḥ* — said; *evam* — so; *cet* — if; *vayam* — we; *api* — too; *tat* — then; *gale* — to the neck; *kṛpāṇam* — a sword; *baddhvā* — having tied; *etat* — this; *sapadi* — at once; *śarīram* — body; *ājahīmaḥ* — shall abandon.

**95.** Hearing these words of His, Advaita and all the others spoke just so: "If that is so, then we too shall at once tie a sword to our necks and abandon this body!"

*Note.* The edition has *बद्धैतत्*, a misprint for *बद्ध्वैतत्* (*baddhvā etat*). *Evam evam ūcuḥ* — so for the metre (the edition runs it together as *एवमेव मूचुः*).

### Verse 96

गौराङ्गोऽप्यथ हसितं विधाय सद्रा-
गित्येतत् किमिति किमात्थ वाक्यमेतत् ।
उक्त्वैवं क्षणमवतस्थिवान् धरण्यां
हुङ्कारैः सह निपपात चित्रमेतत् ॥९६॥

*gaurāṅgo 'py atha hasitaṁ vidhāya sadrāg*
*ity etat kim iti kim āttha vākyam etat |*
*uktvaivaṁ kṣaṇam avatasthivān dharaṇyāṁ*
*huṅkāraiḥ saha nipapāta citram etat ||96||*

*Word for word:* *gaurāṅgaḥ* — Gauranga; *api* — and; *atha* — then; *hasitam* — a laugh; *vidhāya* — having given; *sadrāk* — at once; *iti* — thus; *etat* — this; *kim* — what; *iti* — thus; *kim* — what; *āttha* — you say; *vākyam* — word; *etat* — this; *uktvā* — having said; *evam* — thus; *kṣaṇam* — for a moment; *avatasthivān* — having stood still; *dharaṇyām* — to the ground; *huṅkāraiḥ* — roars; *saha* — with; *nipapāta* — fell; *citram* — a wonder; *etat* — this.

**96.** Then Gauranga laughed and at once said: "What is this? What is this word you are saying?" Having said this, He stood still for a moment — and then, with roars, fell to the ground. What a wonder!

*Note.* A *hunkara* is a thunderous cry of "hum!", a sign of ecstasy; compare Advaita's hunkaras.

### Verse 97

इत्येवं भुवि सुचिरं विलुठ्य नाथो
निश्चेष्टः समजनि हेमगौरदेहः ।
तत्कालच्युतमिव काञ्चनाचलस्य
क्ष्मापृष्ठे ज्वलदनिशं मनोज्ञशृङ्गम् ॥९७॥

*ity evaṁ bhuvi suciraṁ viluṭhya nātho*
*niśceṣṭaḥ samajani hema-gaura-dehaḥ |*
*tat-kāla-cyutam iva kāñcanācalasya*
*kṣmā-pṛṣṭhe jvalad aniśaṁ manojña-śṛṅgam ||97||*

*Word for word:* *iti evam* — thus; *bhuvi* — on the ground; *suciram* — for a long time; *viluṭhya* — having rolled; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *niśceṣṭaḥ* — motionless; *samajani* — became; *hema* — like gold; *gaura* — golden; *dehaḥ* — [He] whose body; *tat* — at that; *kāla* — moment; *cyutam* — fallen; *iva* — like; *kāñcana* — of the golden; *acalasya* — mountain; *kṣmā* — of the earth; *pṛṣṭhe* — on the surface; *jvalat* — blazing; *aniśam* — ceaselessly; *manojña* — lovely; *śṛṅgam* — a peak.

**97.** Thus, having rolled on the ground for a long time, the Lord, His body golden like gold, became motionless — like a lovely peak of the golden mountain that has just fallen to the earth and blazes ceaselessly.

*Note.* The golden mountain is Meru.

### Verse 98

भूयोऽयं मृदि च विलुठ्य चत्वरान्तः
संमूर्च्छन्निव विरराम रम्यमूर्त्तिः ।
चेष्टाद्यं न किमपि नोत्तरञ्च किञ्चि-
न्नस्पन्दः श्वसितसमीरणश्च नैव ॥९८॥

*bhūyo 'yaṁ mṛdi ca viluṭhya catvarāntaḥ*
*saṁmūrcchann iva virarāma ramya-mūrtiḥ |*
*ceṣṭādyaṁ na kim api nottarañ ca kiñcin*
*na spandaḥ śvasita-samīraṇaś ca naiva ||98||*

*Word for word:* *bhūyaḥ* — again; *ayam* — He; *mṛdi* — in the dust; *ca* — and; *viluṭhya* — having rolled; *catvara* — of the courtyard; *antaḥ* — in the middle; *saṁmūrcchan* — swooning; *iva* — as if; *virarāma* — fell still; *ramya* — of lovely; *mūrtiḥ* — form; *ceṣṭā* — movement; *ādyam* — and the like; *na* — not; *kim api* — any; *na* — not; *uttaram* — answer; *ca* — and; *kiñcit* — any; *na* — not; *spandaḥ* — a tremor; *śvasita* — of breath; *samīraṇaḥ* — the stirring; *ca* — and; *na eva* — not at all.

**98.** And again, having rolled in the dust in the middle of the courtyard, He of the lovely form fell still, as if swooning: no movement or the like, no answer whatever, no tremor — and no stirring of breath at all.

### Verse 99

चिक्षेप क्षितिषु यथा भुजौ तथा तौ
तादृक्षाविव किल तस्थतुश्चिराय ।
तस्थौ श्रीपदयुगलं तथा यथासौ
चिक्षेप क्षणमनु विस्मृताङ्गचेष्टः ॥९९॥

*cikṣepa kṣitiṣu yathā bhujau tathā tau*
*tādṛkṣāv iva kila tasthatuś cirāya |*
*tasthau śrī-pada-yugalaṁ tathā yathāsau*
*cikṣepa kṣaṇam anu vismṛtāṅga-ceṣṭaḥ ||99||*

*Word for word:* *cikṣepa* — flung; *kṣitiṣu* — on the ground; *yathā* — as; *bhujau* — the arms; *tathā* — so; *tau* — they; *tādṛkṣau* — just the same; *iva* — as it were; *kila* — indeed; *tasthatuḥ* — remained; *cirāya* — for a long time; *tasthau* — remained; *śrī* — of beautiful; *pada* — feet; *yugalam* — the pair; *tathā* — so; *yathā* — as; *asau* — He; *cikṣepa* — had cast; *kṣaṇam* — a moment; *anu* — before; *vismṛta* — [He] who had forgotten; *aṅga* — of the body; *ceṣṭaḥ* — the movements.

**99.** As He had flung His arms upon the ground, so they remained, just the same, for a long time; and His beautiful pair of feet stayed just as He had cast them down a moment before, forgetful of the movements of His body.

### Verse 100

इत्येवं भवति सति क्षपाव्यपाये
पर्य्यासीत् सपदि रविः समुद्गतोऽभूत् ।
मूर्च्छाभिर्गतसकलक्रियः प्रकामं
नैवायं प्रकृतिमवाप गौरचन्द्रः ॥१००॥

*ity evaṁ bhavati sati kṣapā-vyapāye*
*paryāsīt sapadi raviḥ samudgato 'bhūt |*
*mūrcchābhir gata-sakala-kriyaḥ prakāmaṁ*
*naivāyaṁ prakṛtim avāpa gauracandraḥ ||100||*

*Word for word:* *iti evam* — thus; *bhavati sati* — while it was happening; *kṣapā* — of the night; *vyapāye* — at the departure; *paryāsīt* — [it] was over; *sapadi* — at once; *raviḥ* — the sun; *samudgataḥ* — risen; *abhūt* — was; *mūrcchābhiḥ* — through swoons; *gata* — [He] who had lost; *sakala* — all; *kriyaḥ* — activity; *prakāmam* — entirely; *na eva* — not at all; *ayam* — He; *prakṛtim* — natural state; *avāpa* — regained; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra.

**100.** While things were thus, the night passed away, and at once the sun had risen. But Gaurachandra, who through His swoons had entirely lost all activity, did not regain His natural state at all.

*Note.* *Paryāsīt* is from *pari-√as* ("to be over, come to an end").

### Verse 101

ते सर्व्वे परमपरं सहस्रभारै-
र्दुःखानां किमिति किमित्युदीरयन्तः ।
निश्चेष्टं प्रभुमवलोक्य भूमिपृष्ठे
स्विन्नाङ्गाः परिमुमुहुर्द्रुतं समन्तात् ॥१०१॥

*te sarve param aparaṁ sahasra-bhārair*
*duḥkhānāṁ kim iti kim ity udīrayantaḥ |*
*niśceṣṭaṁ prabhum avalokya bhūmi-pṛṣṭhe*
*svinnāṅgāḥ parimumuhur drutaṁ samantāt ||101||*

*Word for word:* *te* — they; *sarve* — all; *param* — one; *aparam* — to another; *sahasra* — by thousands; *bhāraiḥ* — of burdens; *duḥkhānām* — of sorrows; *kim* — what; *iti* — thus; *kim* — what; *iti* — thus; *udīrayantaḥ* — saying; *niśceṣṭam* — motionless; *prabhum* — the Lord; *avalokya* — having seen; *bhūmi* — of the ground; *pṛṣṭhe* — on the surface; *svinna* — bathed in sweat; *aṅgāḥ* — [with] bodies; *parimumuhuḥ* — swooned; *drutam* — swiftly; *samantāt* — on every side.

**101.** Weighed down by thousands of burdens of sorrow, they all kept saying to one another, "What is this? What is it?" — and, seeing the Lord lying motionless on the ground, their bodies bathed in sweat, they swiftly swooned on every side.

### Verse 102

यातैषा सपदि निशा समुद्गतोऽर्कः
सम्पन्नोऽपि च घटिकार्द्ध एष सोऽपि ।
यामार्द्धस्तदनु च याम एष भूतो
हा हा किं तदपि बुबोध नैव नाथः ॥१०२॥

*yātaiṣā sapadi niśā samudgato 'rkaḥ*
*sampanno 'pi ca ghaṭikārdha eṣa so 'pi |*
*yāmārdhas tad-anu ca yāma eṣa bhūto*
*hā hā kiṁ tad api bubodha naiva nāthaḥ ||102||*

*Word for word:* *yātā* — has gone; *eṣā* — this; *sapadi* — in a moment; *niśā* — night; *samudgataḥ* — has risen; *arkaḥ* — the sun; *sampannaḥ* — has passed; *api ca* — and now; *ghaṭikā* — of a ghatika; *ardhaḥ* — the half; *eṣaḥ* — this; *saḥ api* — and that too; *yāma* — of a watch; *ardhaḥ* — the half; *tat* — that; *anu* — after; *ca* — and; *yāmaḥ* — a watch; *eṣaḥ* — this; *bhūtaḥ* — has passed; *hā hā* — alas, alas; *kim* — why; *tat api* — even so; *bubodha* — has awoken; *na eva* — not at all; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord.

**102.** "This night has passed in a moment, the sun has risen; now half a ghatika has gone — and that too is past; then half a watch, and after it this whole watch has gone by. Alas, alas! Why, even so, has the Lord not awoken?"

*Note.* A *ghaṭikā* is 24 minutes; a *yāma* (watch) is about three hours.

### Verse 103

इत्येतत् सततमुदीरयन्त एते
दुःखार्त्ताश्चलित इति प्रतेपुरुच्चैः ।
संरुद्धे परमदृढे कवाटबन्धे
तत्पुर्य्यां तमभिनिवेश्य ते निषेदुः ॥१०३॥

*ity etat satatam udīrayanta ete*
*duḥkhārtāś calita iti pratepur uccaiḥ |*
*saṁruddhe parama-dṛḍhe kavāṭa-bandhe*
*tat-puryāṁ tam abhiniveśya te niṣeduḥ ||103||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *etat* — this; *satatam* — constantly; *udīrayantaḥ* — repeating; *ete* — they; *duḥkha* — by sorrow; *ārtāḥ* — afflicted; *calitaḥ* — [He] has gone; *iti* — [thinking] thus; *pratepuḥ* — were tormented; *uccaiḥ* — intensely; *saṁruddhe* — being fastened; *parama* — very; *dṛḍhe* — firm; *kavāṭa* — of the door; *bandhe* — the bolt; *tat* — in that; *puryām* — dwelling; *tam* — Him; *abhiniveśya* — having laid down; *te* — they; *niṣeduḥ* — sat down.

**103.** Constantly repeating this, afflicted with sorrow, they were intensely tormented, thinking, "He has gone!" Having laid Him down in that dwelling and fastened the door with a very firm bolt, they sat down [around Him].

*Note.* *Calitaḥ*, "has gone": in their fear, that He had departed from this world (cf. vv. 94–95). *Pur* here means "dwelling".

### Verse 104

अद्वैतस्त्वथ शतहुङ्कृतैः करेण
क्षिप्ताम्भो वदनममुष्य संसिषेच ।
गौराङ्गस्तदपि न बोधतामवाप
स्पन्दं निःश्वसितसमीरणं न चापि ॥१०४॥

*advaitas tv atha śata-huṅkṛtaiḥ kareṇa*
*kṣiptāmbho vadanam amuṣya saṁsiṣeca |*
*gaurāṅgas tad api na bodhatām avāpa*
*spandaṁ niḥśvasita-samīraṇaṁ na cāpi ||104||*

*Word for word:* *advaitaḥ* — Advaita; *tu* — but; *atha* — then; *śata* — with a hundred; *huṅkṛtaiḥ* — roars; *kareṇa* — with the hand; *kṣipta* — flung; *ambhaḥ* — [with] water; *vadanam* — the face; *amuṣya* — His; *saṁsiṣeca* — sprinkled; *gaurāṅgaḥ* — Gauranga; *tat api* — even so; *na* — not; *bodhatām* — consciousness; *avāpa* — regained; *spandam* — a quiver; *niḥśvasita* — of breathing; *samīraṇam* — the breeze; *na* — not; *ca api* — and even.

**104.** Then Advaita, with a hundred roars, sprinkled His face with water flung from His hand; yet Gauranga did not regain consciousness — there was no quiver, not even the breeze of breath.

### Verse 105

चिन्ताभिर्मनसि विभाव्य कीर्त्तनं त-
च्चक्रुस्ते मधुमधुरं सुधीरधीरम् ।
तच्छ्रुत्वा स तु चिरकालमेव नाथो
नह्येव प्रकृतिमियाय गौरचन्द्रः ॥१०५॥

*cintābhir manasi vibhāvya kīrtanaṁ tac*
*cakrus te madhu-madhuraṁ sudhīra-dhīram |*
*tac chrutvā sa tu cira-kālam eva nātho*
*nahy eva prakṛtim iyāya gauracandraḥ ||105||*

*Word for word:* *cintābhiḥ* — by reflections; *manasi* — in the mind; *vibhāvya* — having resolved; *kīrtanam* — kirtana; *tat* — that; *cakruḥ* — performed; *te* — they; *madhu* — than honey; *madhuram* — sweeter; *sudhīra* — most; *dhīram* — deep; *tat* — that; *śrutvā* — having heard; *saḥ* — He; *tu* — however; *cira* — for a long; *kālam* — time; *eva* — indeed; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *nahi eva* — not at all; *prakṛtim* — to His natural state; *iyāya* — returned; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra.

**105.** Having reflected and resolved in their minds, they performed that kirtana, sweeter than honey, deep and most solemn. Yet, though hearing it, the Lord Gaurachandra for a long time did not return to His natural state.

### Verse 106

अश्रान्तं श्रवणपथैः प्रविश्य चेत-
स्तस्यैतत् सुमधुरकीर्त्तनामृतेन ।
तैः सार्द्धं सुखितमनोभिरत्र भूयः
सन्तेने सपदि तनूरुहेषु हर्षः ॥१०६॥

*aśrāntaṁ śravaṇa-pathaiḥ praviśya cetas*
*tasyaitat su-madhura-kīrtanāmṛtena |*
*taiḥ sārdhaṁ sukhita-manobhir atra bhūyaḥ*
*santene sapadi tanūruheṣu harṣaḥ ||106||*

*Word for word:* *aśrāntam* — unceasingly; *śravaṇa* — of hearing; *pathaiḥ* — by the paths; *praviśya* — having entered; *cetaḥ* — the heart; *tasya* — His; *etat* — this; *su* — very; *madhura* — sweet; *kīrtana* — of the kirtana; *amṛtena* — by the nectar; *taiḥ* — them; *sārdham* — together with; *sukhita* — gladdened; *manobhiḥ* — [with] hearts; *atra* — here; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *santene* — spread; *sapadi* — at once; *tanūruheṣu* — over the hairs of the body; *harṣaḥ* — the thrill.

**106.** When, through the paths of hearing, the nectar of this very sweet kirtana had unceasingly entered His heart, at once the thrill [of joy] spread again over the hairs of His body — and together with it [joy spread] among them, their hearts gladdened.

*Note.* *Harṣa* means both "joy" and "the bristling of the hairs".

### Verse 107

यद्धर्षैः सममुदभूत् स रोमहर्षो
गौरस्य प्रकृतिमुपेयुषः समन्तात् ।
तद्दुःखैः सममपि निर्भरैर्विवृत्तिं
पार्श्वस्य प्रभुरकरोत् क्रमेण तत्र ॥१०७॥

*yad dharṣaiḥ samam udabhūt sa roma-harṣo*
*gaurasya prakṛtim upeyuṣaḥ samantāt |*
*tad duḥkhaiḥ samam api nirbharair vivṛttiṁ*
*pārśvasya prabhur akarot krameṇa tatra ||107||*

*Word for word:* *yat* — as; *harṣaiḥ* — with [their] joys; *samam* — together; *udabhūt* — arose; *saḥ* — that; *roma* — of the hairs; *harṣaḥ* — the bristling; *gaurasya* — of Gaura; *prakṛtim* — to His natural state; *upeyuṣaḥ* — returning; *samantāt* — all over; *tat* — so then; *duḥkhaiḥ* — with [their] sorrows; *samam* — together; *api* — also; *nirbharaiḥ* — heavy; *vivṛttim* — a turning; *pārśvasya* — of the side; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *akarot* — made; *krameṇa* — gradually; *tatra* — there.

**107.** Just as the bristling of the hairs arose all over Gaura, who was returning to His natural state, together with their joys, so then the Lord there slowly turned onto His side — and together with that their heavy sorrows turned away.

*Note.* A play on *vivṛtti*: "turning [of the body onto its side]" and "turning back, cessation". The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 108

गौराङ्गश्चिरमनुभूय कीर्त्तनं तत्
प्रव्यक्तं दृढशयितः शनैरुदस्थात् ।
तैर्भूयस्त्यजति सति प्रभौ प्रकाशा-
विष्कारं व्यघटि तदास्य वेशभूषा ॥१०८॥

*gaurāṅgaś ciram anubhūya kīrtanaṁ tat*
*pravyaktaṁ dṛḍha-śayitaḥ śanair udasthāt |*
*tair bhūyas tyajati sati prabhau prakāśā-*
*viṣkāraṁ vyaghaṭi tadāsya veśa-bhūṣā ||108||*

*Word for word:* *gaurāṅgaḥ* — Gauranga; *ciram* — long; *anubhūya* — having relished; *kīrtanam* — kirtana; *tat* — that; *pravyaktam* — clearly; *dṛḍha* — fast; *śayitaḥ* — [who had] lain; *śanaiḥ* — slowly; *udasthāt* — rose; *taiḥ* — by them; *bhūyaḥ* — in turn; *tyajati sati* — when giving up; *prabhau* — the Lord; *prakāśa* — of the effulgence; *āviṣkāram* — the manifestation; *vyaghaṭi* — was undone; *tadā* — then; *asya* — His; *veśa* — attire; *bhūṣā* — and ornaments.

**108.** Having long and now clearly relished that kirtana, Gauranga, who had lain motionless, slowly rose. And when the Lord in turn gave up the manifestation of His effulgence, His attire and ornaments were then taken off by them.

*Note.* *Vyaghaṭi* is the passive aorist of *vi-ghaṭ*, "to come apart, to be undone": together with the withdrawal of the effulgence the festive attire of the great bathing (vv. 61–68) is removed. One may also understand that they dressed Him again in His ordinary clothes.

### Verse 109

उत्थाय प्रभुरथ देवगेहभित्तिं
संहृत्य प्रकटनिजप्रकाशतेजः ।
भूयोऽसौ मृदुमधुरां दधार लक्ष्मीं
नैदाघो रविरिव शारदेन्दुरासीत् ॥१०९॥

*utthāya prabhur atha deva-geha-bhittiṁ*
*saṁhṛtya prakaṭa-nija-prakāśa-tejaḥ |*
*bhūyo 'sau mṛdu-madhurāṁ dadhāra lakṣmīṁ*
*naidāgho ravir iva śāradendur āsīt ||109||*

*Word for word:* *utthāya* — having risen; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *atha* — then; *deva* — of God; *geha* — of the house; *bhittim* — to the wall; *saṁhṛtya* — having withdrawn; *prakaṭa* — manifest; *nija* — His own; *prakāśa* — of effulgence; *tejaḥ* — the fire; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *asau* — He; *mṛdu* — soft; *madhurām* — sweet; *dadhāra* — assumed; *lakṣmīm* — beauty; *naidāghaḥ* — the summer; *raviḥ* — sun; *iva* — as if; *śārada* — the autumn; *induḥ* — moon; *āsīt* — had become.

**109.** Having risen, the Lord then [went] to the wall of the shrine and withdrew the manifest fire of His effulgence. Once more He assumed a soft, sweet beauty — as if the summer sun had become the autumn moon.

*Note.* *Deva-geha-bhittim* (accusative) stands without a verb of motion; the text may be corrupt. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 110

आश्वस्य क्षणमथ दन्तसत्प्रसून-
द्योतैस्तैरधरदले विभेदयन् सः ।
प्रत्यूचे चिरशयितो यथा प्रबुद्धे
निद्रान्ते किमपि कथञ्चनाप्यजानन् ॥११०॥

*āśvasya kṣaṇam atha danta-sat-prasūna-*
*dyotais tair adhara-dale vibhedayan saḥ |*
*pratyūce cira-śayito yathā prabuddhe*
*nidrānte kim api kathañcanāpy ajānan ||110||*

*Word for word:* *āśvasya* — having recovered His breath; *kṣaṇam* — for a moment; *atha* — then; *danta* — of the teeth; *sat* — beautiful; *prasūna* — of the flowers; *dyotaiḥ* — with the gleam; *taiḥ* — with that; *adhara* — of the lips; *dale* — the petals; *vibhedayan* — parting; *saḥ* — He; *pratyūce* — replied; *cira* — long; *śayitaḥ* — one who has slept; *yathā* — as; *prabuddhe* — on awakening; *nidrā* — of sleep; *ante* — at the end; *kim api* — anything; *kathañcana api* — at all; *ajānan* — not knowing.

**110.** Then, recovering His breath for a moment, He parted the petals of His lips with the gleam of the beautiful flowers of His teeth and replied — like one who has slept long and, waking at the end of sleep, knows nothing at all:

### Verse 111

एतावान् किमु समयः सुषुप्तिभाजा
निद्रायामतिगमितो मया चिराय ।
प्रत्यूषे यदहमपाठयं द्विजाती-
नाश्चर्य्यं किमिति तदेव संस्मरामि ॥१११॥

*etāvān kim u samayaḥ suṣupti-bhājā*
*nidrāyām atigamito mayā cirāya |*
*pratyūṣe yad aham apāṭhayaṁ dvijātīn*
*āścaryaṁ kim iti tad eva saṁsmarāmi ||111||*

*Word for word:* *etāvān* — so much; *kim u* — can it be that; *samayaḥ* — time; *suṣupti* — deep sleep; *bhājā* — sunk in; *nidrāyām* — in sleep; *atigamitaḥ* — was spent; *mayā* — by Me; *cirāya* — for long; *pratyūṣe* — at dawn; *yat* — that; *aham* — I; *apāṭhayam* — taught; *dvijātīn* — the twice-born; *āścaryam* — a wonder; *kim iti* — how is it; *tat* — that; *eva* — only; *saṁsmarāmi* — I remember.

**111.** "Can it be that I, sunk in deep sleep, have spent so much time sleeping, for so long? I remember only that at dawn I was teaching the twice-born. How strange this is!"

*Note.* At this time Gaura is still teaching grammar (vv. 10–14: "four months of kirtana and teaching").

### Verse 112

सोत्प्रासं तदनु जगाद गौरचन्द्रं
श्रीवासो विमलमना मनाग्विहस्य ।
नेदानीं प्रभवितुमर्हति त्वदीया
मायेयं विदिततमा बभूव भूयः ॥११२॥

*sotprāsaṁ tad-anu jagāda gauracandraṁ*
*śrīvāso vimala-manā manāg vihasya |*
*nedānīṁ prabhavitum arhati tvadīyā*
*māyeyaṁ viditatamā babhūva bhūyaḥ ||112||*

*Word for word:* *sa* — with; *utprāsam* — mockery; *tat* — that; *anu* — after; *jagāda* — said; *gauracandram* — to Gaurachandra; *śrīvāsaḥ* — Srivasa; *vimala* — pure; *manāḥ* — [with] a heart; *manāk* — slightly; *vihasya* — having smiled; *na* — not; *idānīm* — now; *prabhavitum* — to prevail; *arhati* — is able; *tvadīyā* — Your; *māyā* — maya; *iyam* — this; *viditatamā* — thoroughly known; *babhūva* — has become; *bhūyaḥ* — now.

**112.** Then Srivasa, pure in heart, smiling slightly, said to Gaurachandra in jest: "This maya of Yours can no longer prevail now: it has become thoroughly known!"

*Note.* In the edition the second line reads *श्रीवासो विमल मनाग्विहस्य* — 11 syllables instead of 13. We restore *vimala-manā manāg* (one of two adjacent *manā* having dropped out), which gives the correct metre (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *vimalaṁ manāg*, with the same missing syllable.

### Verse 113

तच्छ्रुत्वा किमिति किमात्थ किं नु वा मा-
मित्येवं परिहससि प्रकाममेव ।
नो जाने क्षणमपि किञ्चिदेतदेतत्
प्रत्यूचे सचकितमेव गौरचन्द्रः ॥११३॥

*tac chrutvā kim iti kim āttha kiṁ nu vā mām*
*ity evaṁ parihasasi prakāmam eva |*
*no jāne kṣaṇam api kiñcid etad etat*
*pratyūce sa-cakitam eva gauracandraḥ ||113||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — that; *śrutvā* — having heard; *kim* — what; *iti* — thus; *kim* — what; *āttha* — do you say; *kim* — why; *nu* — then; *vā* — or; *mām* — at Me; *iti evam* — thus; *parihasasi* — do you laugh; *prakāmam* — freely; *eva* — indeed; *na u* — not; *jāne* — I know; *kṣaṇam api* — even for a moment; *kiñcit* — anything; *etat etat* — of all this; *pratyūce* — replied; *sa* — with; *cakitam* — astonishment; *eva* — indeed; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra.

**113.** Hearing that, Gaurachandra replied in astonishment: "What? What are you saying? Why do you laugh at Me so freely? I know nothing of all this — not for a moment!"

### Verse 114

यामानां त्रयमिति सम्बभूव तत्रा-
तीतैरष्टभिरपि सार्द्धमत्र यामैः ।
न स्नानं न च गृहकर्म नान्यचेष्टा
नो निद्रा न च शयनं तदा जनस्य ॥११४॥

*yāmānāṁ trayam iti sambabhūva tatrā-*
*tītair aṣṭabhir api sārdham atra yāmaiḥ |*
*na snānaṁ na ca gṛha-karma nānya-ceṣṭā*
*no nidrā na ca śayanaṁ tadā janasya ||114||*

*Word for word:* *yāmānām* — of watches; *trayam* — three; *iti* — thus; *sambabhūva* — passed; *tatra* — there; *atītaiḥ* — elapsed; *aṣṭabhiḥ* — eight; *api* — also; *sārdham* — together with; *atra* — here; *yāmaiḥ* — watches; *na* — neither; *snānam* — bathing; *na ca* — nor; *gṛha* — household; *karma* — work; *na* — nor; *anya* — other; *ceṣṭā* — activity; *na u* — nor; *nidrā* — sleep; *na ca* — nor; *śayanam* — lying down; *tadā* — then; *janasya* — for the people.

**114.** Thus three watches passed there, in addition to the eight watches that had elapsed here before. And all that time the people had no bath, no household work, no other activity, no sleep — they did not even lie down.

*Note.* Eight watches make a day and a night; together with the three, eleven watches — about 33 hours.

### Verse 115

इत्येकाधिकदशभिः सुदीर्घदीर्घै-
र्यामैस्तैर्निमिष इवाभवत् स कालः ।
एतेषु क्षणमपि पक्ष्मणां विवृत्ति-
र्नैवासीत् सुखमहतां तदा जनानाम् ॥११५॥

*ity ekādhika-daśabhiḥ sudīrgha-dīrghair*
*yāmais tair nimiṣa ivābhavat sa kālaḥ |*
*eteṣu kṣaṇam api pakṣmaṇāṁ vivṛttir*
*naivāsīt sukha-mahatāṁ tadā janānām ||115||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *eka* — by one; *adhika* — exceeding; *daśabhiḥ* — by ten; *sudīrgha* — very long; *dīrghaiḥ* — long; *yāmaiḥ* — by watches; *taiḥ* — by those; *nimiṣaḥ* — a blink; *iva* — like; *abhavat* — became; *saḥ* — that; *kālaḥ* — time; *eteṣu* — in them; *kṣaṇam api* — even for a moment; *pakṣmaṇām* — of the eyelashes; *vivṛttiḥ* — movement; *na eva* — not at all; *āsīt* — was; *sukha* — with happiness; *mahatām* — great; *tadā* — then; *janānām* — of the people.

**115.** Thus that time — those eleven long, very long watches — became like a single blink of the eye; and during them not even for a moment did the eyelashes of the people, great in their happiness, move.

*Note.* *Vivṛtti*, "turning, movement" — here, of blinking. Eleven watches passed "like a blink" (*nimiṣa*), and yet no one blinked.

### Verse 116

नेत्राभ्यां चिरमुपवाससस्पृहाभ्यां
श्रोत्राभ्यां बधिरतया विवर्ज्जिताभ्याम् ।
स्वान्तेन प्रथमसमुद्गतेन लोका
निस्पन्दा इव सततं बभूवुरेते ॥११६॥

*netrābhyāṁ ciram upavāsa-saspṛhābhyāṁ*
*śrotrābhyāṁ badhiratayā vivarjitābhyām |*
*svāntena prathama-samudgatena lokā*
*nispandā iva satataṁ babhūvur ete ||116||*

*Word for word:* *netrābhyām* — with eyes; *ciram* — long; *upavāsa* — by fasting; *sa* — with; *spṛhābhyām* — [as if] eager; *śrotrābhyām* — with ears; *badhiratayā* — by deafness; *vivarjitābhyām* — abandoned; *svāntena* — with a heart; *prathama* — for the first time; *samudgatena* — arisen; *lokāḥ* — the people; *nispandāḥ* — motionless; *iva* — as if; *satatam* — all the while; *babhūvuḥ* — were; *ete* — these.

**116.** With eyes eager as after a long fast, with ears freed from deafness, with hearts as if newly born, these people remained all the while as though motionless.

### Verse 117

अश्रान्तं गतनिमिषं विलोकयन्त्यो
गौराङ्गाहितपरमप्रसादमुग्धाः ।
देहादि क्षणमपि नैव सस्मरुस्ता
बाह्यान्तःप्रमदभरेण विप्रपत्न्यः ॥११७॥

*aśrāntaṁ gata-nimiṣaṁ vilokayantyo*
*gaurāṅgāhita-parama-prasāda-mugdhāḥ |*
*dehādi kṣaṇam api naiva sasmarus tā*
*bāhyāntaḥ-pramada-bhareṇa vipra-patnyaḥ ||117||*

*Word for word:* *aśrāntam* — unwearied; *gata* — without; *nimiṣam* — blinking; *vilokayantyaḥ* — gazing; *gaurāṅga* — by Gauranga; *āhita* — bestowed; *parama* — by the supreme; *prasāda* — grace; *mugdhāḥ* — enchanted; *deha* — the body; *ādi* — and so on; *kṣaṇam api* — even for a moment; *na eva* — not at all; *sasmaruḥ* — remembered; *tāḥ* — they; *bāhya* — outer; *antaḥ* — and inner; *pramada* — of joy; *bhareṇa* — from the abundance; *vipra* — of the brahmanas; *patnyaḥ* — the wives.

**117.** The wives of the brahmanas, enchanted by the supreme grace bestowed by Gauranga, gazed [at Him] unwearied, without blinking, and from the abundance of joy, outer and inner, did not remember for even a moment their bodies or anything else.

### Verse 118

इत्येवं परमरहस्यमीक्षमाणाः
क्षुत्तृष्णापरिभवमेव नापुरेते ।
किञ्चैतत् क्षणमिव चेद्दिनद्वयं स्या-
त्तत् किं क्षुत्प्रभृतिभिरत्र देहधर्मैः ॥११८॥

*ity evaṁ parama-rahasyam īkṣamāṇāḥ*
*kṣut-tṛṣṇā-paribhavam eva nāpur ete |*
*kiñcaitat kṣaṇam iva ced dina-dvayaṁ syāt*
*tat kiṁ kṣut-prabhṛtibhir atra deha-dharmaiḥ ||118||*

*Word for word:* *iti evam* — thus; *parama* — the supreme; *rahasyam* — secret; *īkṣamāṇāḥ* — beholding; *kṣut* — of hunger; *tṛṣṇā* — and thirst; *paribhavam* — the dominion; *eva* — at all; *na* — not; *āpuḥ* — experienced; *ete* — they; *kiñca* — moreover; *etat* — this; *kṣaṇam* — a moment; *iva* — like; *cet* — if; *dina* — of days; *dvayam* — a pair; *syāt* — was; *tat* — then; *kim* — what [place]; *kṣut* — with hunger; *prabhṛtibhiḥ* — and the rest; *atra* — here; *deha* — of the body; *dharmaiḥ* — with the properties.

**118.** Beholding thus the supreme secret, they did not feel the dominion of hunger and thirst at all. And moreover, if two days were like a moment, what place was there here for hunger and the other properties of the body?

### Verse 119

अत्रान्ते परमसुखेन सज्जयित्वा
गात्रोद्वर्त्तनपरवस्तुदत्तचित्तैः ।
स्नानाय प्रति विदधे तथोद्यमं तै-
र्गौराङ्गः परमकृपारसाम्बुराशिः ॥११९॥

*atrānte parama-sukhena sajjayitvā*
*gātrodvartana-para-vastu-datta-cittaiḥ |*
*snānāya prati vidadhe tathodyamaṁ tair*
*gaurāṅgaḥ parama-kṛpā-rasāmbu-rāśiḥ ||119||*

*Word for word:* *atra* — of this; *ante* — at the end; *parama* — with supreme; *sukhena* — joy; *sajjayitvā* — having made ready; *gātra* — of the body; *udvartana* — for rubbing; *para* — the finest; *vastu* — substances; *datta* — given; *cittaiḥ* — [by those] whose hearts; *snānāya* — for bathing; *prati* — towards; *vidadhe* — made; *tathā* — thus; *udyamam* — an effort; *taiḥ* — together with them; *gaurāṅgaḥ* — Gauranga; *parama* — of supreme; *kṛpā* — mercy; *rasa* — of the rasa; *ambu-rāśiḥ* — the ocean.

**119.** When all this had ended, [the devotees], with supreme joy and with their hearts wholly given to it, made ready the finest substances for rubbing the body; and Gauranga, the ocean of the rasa of supreme mercy, set about bathing together with them.

*Note.* *Udvartana* — rubbing the body with fragrant pastes before bathing.

### Verse 120

स्नानान्ते निजनिजवेश्म जग्मुरेते
गौराङ्गः पुनरपि तस्य वेश्म गत्वा ।
श्रीरामप्रभृतिसहोदरैश्चतुर्भि-
स्तत्पत्नीभिरपि समर्हितो रराज ॥१२०॥

*snānānte nija-nija-veśma jagmur ete*
*gaurāṅgaḥ punar api tasya veśma gatvā |*
*śrīrāma-prabhṛti-sahodaraiś caturbhis*
*tat-patnībhir api samarhito rarāja ||120||*

*Word for word:* *snāna* — of the bath; *ante* — at the end; *nija-nija* — each his own; *veśma* — to the house; *jagmuḥ* — went; *ete* — they; *gaurāṅgaḥ* — Gauranga; *punaḥ api* — again; *tasya* — his (Srivasa's); *veśma* — to the house; *gatvā* — having gone; *śrīrāma* — by Sri Rama; *prabhṛti* — headed by; *sahodaraiḥ* — by the brothers; *caturbhiḥ* — four; *tat* — their; *patnībhiḥ* — by the wives; *api* — and; *samarhitaḥ* — honoured; *rarāja* — shone.

**120.** After the bath they all went each to his own house; and Gauranga, going again to his [Srivasa's] house, shone there, honoured by the four brothers headed by Sri Rama and by their wives.

### Verse 121

र्गौराङ्गः सुखमतुलं जगाम भूयः ॥१२१॥

*srag-gandhair vara-vasanaiś ca bhūṣaṇaiś ca*
*śrīkhaṇḍa-drava-sahitaiś ca dhīra-paṅkaiḥ |*
*snehena prati-dina-nūtanena dattair*
*gaurāṅgaḥ sukham atulaṁ jagāma bhūyaḥ ||121||*

*Word for word:* *srak* — with garlands; *gandhaiḥ* — with fragrances; *vara* — with fine; *vasanaiḥ* — garments; *ca* — and; *bhūṣaṇaiḥ* — with ornaments; *ca* — and; *śrīkhaṇḍa* — of sandal; *drava* — with the liquid; *sahitaiḥ* — mixed; *ca* — and; *dhīra* — thick (?); *paṅkaiḥ* — with pastes; *snehena* — with love; *prati* — every; *dina* — day; *nūtanena* — new; *dattaiḥ* — offered; *gaurāṅgaḥ* — Gauranga; *sukham* — happiness; *atulam* — incomparable; *jagāma* — attained; *bhūyaḥ* — again.

**121.** With garlands and fragrances, with fine garments and ornaments, and with thick pastes mixed with liquid sandal — all offered with a love that was new every day — Gauranga again attained incomparable happiness.

*Note.* *Dhīra-paṅka* — literally "firm, dense paste".

### Verse 122

प्रत्यङ्गं तनुमनुलिप्य चन्दनेन

यद्योग्यं तदपि सुखेन भोजयित्वा ॥१२२॥

*praty-aṅgaṁ tanum anulipya candanena*
