ब्रह्मेति किं नु भवतात्र निरूप्यते त-
दित्थं निगद्य च पपाठ पुनः स्वयं सः ॥३५॥

*atrāntare sva-purataḥ sthitam aty-udāraṁ*
*proce mahā-karuṇa eṣa mukunda-dattam |*
*brahmeti kiṁ nu bhavatātra nirūpyate tad*
*itthaṁ nigadya ca papāṭha punaḥ svayaṁ saḥ ||35||*

*Word for word:* *atra* — at this; *antare* — time; *sva* — Him; *purataḥ* — before; *sthitam* — standing; *ati* — most; *udāram* — noble; *proce* — said; *mahā* — greatly; *karuṇaḥ* — merciful; *eṣaḥ* — He; *mukunda-dattam* — to Mukunda Datta; *brahma* — Brahman; *iti* — as; *kim* — what; *nu* — then; *bhavatā* — by you; *atra* — here; *nirūpyate* — is understood; *tat* — that; *ittham* — thus; *nigadya* — having said; *ca* — and; *papāṭha* — recited; *punaḥ* — then; *svayam* — Himself; *saḥ* — He.

**35.** At this time the greatly merciful [Lord] said to the most noble Mukunda Datta, who stood before Him: "What, then, do you understand here by 'Brahman'?" And having said this, He Himself then recited [a verse]:

*Note.* Mukunda Datta was a singer, an associate of Gaura.

### Verse 36

रमन्ते योगिनोऽनन्ते सत्यानन्दे चिदात्मनि ।
इति रामपदेनासौ परं ब्रह्माभिधीयते ॥३६॥

*ramante yogino 'nante satyānande cid-ātmani |*
*iti rāma-padenāsau paraṁ brahmābhidhīyate ||36||*

*Word for word:* *ramante* — take delight; *yoginaḥ* — yogis; *anante* — in the infinite; *satya* — true; *ānande* — in bliss; *cit* — spiritual; *ātmani* — in the Self; *iti* — therefore; *rāma* — "Rama"; *padena* — by the word; *asau* — this; *param* — supreme; *brahma* — Brahman; *abhidhīyate* — is called.

**36.** "Yogis take delight in the infinite, truly blissful, spiritual Self; therefore the Supreme Brahman is called by the word 'Rama'."

*Note.* The metre is *anuṣṭubh*. A verse from the Padma Purana (the "Rama-sahasranama"), quoted in the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 9.29. The verb *ram*, "to delight", yields the name *Rāma*: the Supreme Brahman is the one in whom [yogis] delight.

### Verse 37

भूयोऽपि तं समनुशिष्य जगाद नाथः
किञ्चित् क्रुधाधरदलद्वयकम्पितेन ।
रूपं चतुर्भुजमतीववरं ततोऽन्य-
न्न्यूनं कियद्द्विभुजमित्ययि किं मतं ते ॥३७॥

*bhūyo 'pi taṁ samanuśiṣya jagāda nāthaḥ*
*kiñcit krudhādhara-dala-dvaya-kampitena |*
*rūpaṁ catur-bhujam atīva-varaṁ tato 'nyan*
*nyūnaṁ kiyad dvi-bhujam ity ayi kiṁ mataṁ te ||37||*

*Word for word:* *bhūyaḥ api* — again; *tam* — him; *samanuśiṣya* — instructing; *jagāda* — said; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *kiñcit* — slightly; *krudhā* — with anger; *adhara* — of the lips; *dala* — of the petals; *dvaya* — of the pair; *kampitena* — with a trembling; *rūpam* — the form; *catuḥ* — four; *bhujam* — armed; *atīva* — exceedingly; *varam* — excellent; *tataḥ* — than it; *anyat* — the other; *nyūnam* — inferior; *kiyat* — somewhat; *dvi* — two; *bhujam* — armed; *iti* — thus; *ayi* — hey; *kim* — is it; *matam* — the opinion; *te* — of you.

**37.** And again, instructing him, the Lord spoke, the two petals of His lips trembling slightly with anger: "Hey! Is it your opinion that the four-armed form is exceedingly excellent, and that the other, the two-armed, is somewhat inferior to it?"

*Note.* The edition has *न्नूनं* (*nūnam*, "surely"); we read *nyūnam* ("inferior"), as the sense requires (*kiyat*, "somewhat"). The two-armed form is Krishna, the four-armed Vishnu-Narayana.

### Verse 38

यद्यात्मनो हितमवैषि तदा परस्मा-
त्तद्द्वैभुजं वरमिति प्रतिकीर्त्तय त्वम् ।
श्रुत्वैष तन्निगदितं करुणाविलासि
भूमौ निपत्य निजगाद सहर्षशङ्कम् ॥३८॥

*yady ātmano hitam avaiṣi tadā parasmāt*
*tad dvaibhujaṁ varam iti pratikīrtaya tvam |*
*śrutvaiṣa tan nigaditaṁ karuṇā-vilāsi*
*bhūmau nipatya nijagāda sa-harṣa-śaṅkam ||38||*

*Word for word:* *yadi* — if; *ātmanaḥ* — your own; *hitam* — good; *avaiṣi* — you understand; *tadā* — then; *parasmāt* — than the other; *tat* — that; *dvaibhujam* — two-armed [form]; *varam* — better; *iti* — thus; *pratikīrtaya* — proclaim; *tvam* — you; *śrutvā* — having heard; *eṣaḥ* — he; *tat* — those; *nigaditam* — words; *karuṇā* — with mercy; *vilāsi* — playing; *bhūmau* — on the ground; *nipatya* — having fallen; *nijagāda* — said; *sa* — with; *harṣa* — joy; *śaṅkam* — and fear.

**38.** "If you understand your own good, proclaim: 'That two-armed form is better than the other!'" Hearing those words of His, in which mercy played, [Mukunda] fell on the ground and said with joy and fear:

### Verse 39

स्नातं मया सुरनदीपयसि प्रकामं
श्रीवैष्णवाङ्घ्रिरजसाङ्गमलङ्कृतञ्च ।
श्रीमंस्त्वदीयपदपद्मयुगातपत्रं
मूर्द्धनि प्रयच्छ कुरु दास्यपदेऽभिषेकम् ॥३९॥

*snātaṁ mayā sura-nadī-payasi prakāmaṁ*
*śrī-vaiṣṇavāṅghri-rajasāṅgam alaṅkṛtañ ca |*
*śrīmaṁs tvadīya-pada-padma-yugātapatraṁ*
*mūrdhani prayaccha kuru dāsya-pade 'bhiṣekam ||39||*

*Word for word:* *snātam* — it has been bathed; *mayā* — by me; *sura* — of the gods; *nadī* — of the river; *payasi* — in the waters; *prakāmam* — to my heart's content; *śrī-vaiṣṇava* — of the holy Vaishnavas; *aṅghri* — of the feet; *rajasā* — with the dust; *aṅgam* — body; *alaṅkṛtam* — adorned; *ca* — and; *śrīman* — O beautiful One; *tvadīya* — of Your; *pada* — feet; *padma* — of the lotus; *yuga* — of the pair; *ātapatram* — the parasol; *mūrdhani* — over [my] head; *prayaccha* — give; *kuru* — perform; *dāsya* — of a servant; *pade* — to the office; *abhiṣekam* — consecration.

**39.** "I have bathed to my heart's content in the waters of the river of the gods, and my body is adorned with the dust of the feet of the holy Vaishnavas. O beautiful One, give me the parasol of Your two lotus feet over my head, and perform my consecration to the office of a servant!"

*Note.* The image is that of a royal consecration (*abhiṣeka*): the bath (in the Ganga), the anointing (with the dust of the Vaishnavas), the royal parasol (*ātapatra*) — the feet of the Lord; but Mukunda's "kingdom" is service. The edition has *प्रयेच्छ*, a misprint.

### Verse 40

एवं निशम्य करुणारसपूर्णचेता-
स्तद्वाक्सुधाप्रमुदितेन ततः परेशः ।
श्रीमत्पदाम्बुजयुगं निजलोकनाथ-
मस्यादधाच्छिरसि पूततमे प्रसन्नः ॥४०॥

*evaṁ niśamya karuṇā-rasa-pūrṇa-cetās*
*tad-vāk-sudhā-pramuditena tataḥ pareśaḥ |*
*śrīmat-padāmbuja-yugaṁ nija-loka-nātham*
*asyādadhāc chirasi pūtatame prasannaḥ ||40||*

*Word for word:* *evam* — this; *niśamya* — having heard; *karuṇā* — of mercy; *rasa* — with the nectar; *pūrṇa* — full; *cetāḥ* — [with] a heart; *tat* — his; *vāk* — of the words; *sudhā* — by the nectar; *pramuditena* — gladdened; *tataḥ* — then; *para* — the Supreme; *īśaḥ* — Lord; *śrīmat* — beautiful; *pada* — of feet; *ambuja* — of lotus; *yugam* — the pair; *nija* — of His own; *loka* — people; *nātham* — the sovereign; *asya* — his; *adadhāt* — placed; *śirasi* — on the head; *pūtatame* — most pure; *prasannaḥ* — pleased.

**40.** Hearing this, the Supreme Lord, His heart full of the nectar of mercy and gladdened by the nectar of his words, was pleased and then placed on his most pure head His two beautiful lotus feet — the sovereign of His own people.

### Verse 41

रोमाञ्चसञ्चयसमञ्चितदेहयष्टि-
र्निर्यद्विलोचनपयोझरवृन्दधौतः ।
तत्पादपङ्कजयुगस्य तदैव लब्ध्वा
स्पर्शं बभूव क इवातिशयोत्सुकात्मा ॥४१॥

*romāñca-sañcaya-samañcita-deha-yaṣṭir*
*niryad-vilocana-payo-jhara-vṛnda-dhautaḥ |*
*tat-pāda-paṅkaja-yugasya tadaiva labdhvā*
*sparśaṁ babhūva ka ivātiśayotsukātmā ||41||*

*Word for word:* *romāñca* — of bristling hairs; *sañcaya* — with a mass; *samañcita* — covered; *deha* — of the body; *yaṣṭiḥ* — [with] the slender stem; *niryat* — pouring; *vilocana* — from the eyes; *payaḥ* — of water; *jhara* — of streams; *vṛnda* — by a multitude; *dhautaḥ* — washed; *tat* — His; *pāda* — of feet; *paṅkaja* — of lotus; *yugasya* — of the pair; *tadā eva* — at once; *labdhvā* — having obtained; *sparśam* — the touch; *babhūva* — became; *kaḥ iva* — like whom [else]; *atiśaya* — boundlessly; *utsuka* — longing; *ātmā* — [with] a soul.

**41.** Having at once received the touch of His two lotus feet, [Mukunda] — his slender frame covered with masses of bristling hair, washed by streams of water pouring from his eyes — became boundlessly filled with longing: who else could be like him?

*Note.* In the edition a syllable is missing from the fourth line (*babhūva ivātiśaya-*: the metre is broken and there is a hiatus); the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *babhūva ka ivātiśayotsukātmā*, and so we read.

### Verse 42

भूयो जगाद करुणैकनिधिर्मुरारिं
श्रीगौरचन्द्र इदमुद्भटभावरम्यः ।
आध्यात्मिकं किमु कृतं नु तवास्ति गीतं
सत्यं वदाशु तदिदं यदि वा कृतं भोः ॥४२॥

*bhūyo jagāda karuṇaika-nidhir murāriṁ*
*śrī-gauracandra idam udbhaṭa-bhāva-ramyaḥ |*
*ādhyātmikaṁ kim u kṛtaṁ nu tavāsti gītaṁ*
*satyaṁ vadāśu tad idaṁ yadi vā kṛtaṁ bhoḥ ||42||*

*Word for word:* *bhūyaḥ* — then; *jagāda* — said; *karuṇā* — of mercy; *eka* — the sole; *nidhiḥ* — treasure-house; *murārim* — to Murari; *śrī-gauracandraḥ* — Sri Gaurachandra; *idam* — this; *udbhaṭa* — in an intense; *bhāva* — mood; *ramyaḥ* — charming; *ādhyātmikam* — "spiritual"; *kim u* — whether; *kṛtam* — composed; *nu* — then; *tava* — of you; *asti* — there is; *gītam* — a song; *satyam* — the truth; *vada* — tell; *āśu* — quickly; *tat idam* — this; *yadi vā* — whether or not; *kṛtam* — composed; *bhoḥ* — O [Murari] (hey).

**42.** Then Sri Gaurachandra, the sole treasure-house of mercy, charming in an intense mood, said this to Murari: "Hey, is there then some 'spiritual' song composed by you? Tell the truth quickly: have you composed one or not?"

*Note.* Murari Gupta is a physician from Shrihatta, a friend of Nimai's and the future author of the "Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita" (the *Kadacha*). *Ādhyātmika* ("concerning the higher Self") probably carries a note of reproach for a leaning towards speculation. The Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *kim u kṛtaṁ na tavāsti gītaṁ* ("have you not composed a song about the higher Self?").

### Verse 43

वाञ्छास्ति चेत्तव तु जीवितमेव किम्वा
प्रेमोदयेषु तदिदं चपलं विहाय ।
श्रीमत्कृपारसपरिप्लुतपादपद्म-
माहात्म्यरूपगुणवर्णनमातनुष्व ॥४३॥

*vāñchāsti cet tava tu jīvitam eva kiṁ vā*
*premodayeṣu tad idaṁ capalaṁ vihāya |*
*śrīmat-kṛpā-rasa-paripluta-pāda-padma-*
*māhātmya-rūpa-guṇa-varṇanam ātanuṣva ||43||*

*Word for word:* *vāñchā* — a desire; *asti* — there is; *cet* — if; *tava* — of you; *tu* — but; *jīvitam* — life; *eva* — itself; *kim vā* — or rather; *prema* — of love; *udayeṣu* — for the dawnings; *tat idam* — this; *capalam* — frivolity; *vihāya* — having given up; *śrīmat* — of beautiful; *kṛpā* — mercy; *rasa* — with the nectar; *paripluta* — bathed; *pāda* — of the feet; *padma* — of the lotus; *māhātmya* — of the greatness; *rūpa* — of the form; *guṇa* — and of the qualities; *varṇanam* — a description; *ātanuṣva* — compose.

**43.** "But if you desire life itself — or rather the dawnings of love — then give up this frivolity and compose a description of the greatness, form and qualities of the lotus feet [of the Lord], bathed in the nectar of beautiful mercy."

*Note.* The edition has *jīvitam ena*, a misprint; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *jīvitam eva* (without *tu*).

### Verse 44

श्रुत्वा महाप्रभुवचो मधुरं ततोऽसौ
नारायणोऽवददमुं प्रति वैद्यमुख्यः ।
कारुण्यमीश्वर विधेहि मुरारिगुप्ते
वक्तुं यथार्हति तवैव चरित्रमेषः ॥४४॥

*śrutvā mahāprabhu-vaco madhuraṁ tato 'sau*
*nārāyaṇo 'vadad amuṁ prati vaidya-mukhyaḥ |*
*kāruṇyam īśvara vidhehi murāri-gupte*
*vaktuṁ yathārhati tavaiva caritram eṣaḥ ||44||*

*Word for word:* *śrutvā* — having heard; *mahāprabhu* — of Mahaprabhu; *vacaḥ* — the words; *madhuram* — sweet; *tataḥ* — then; *asau* — this; *nārāyaṇaḥ* — Narayana; *avadat* — said; *amum prati* — to Him; *vaidya* — of physicians; *mukhyaḥ* — the foremost; *kāruṇyam* — mercy; *īśvara* — O Lord; *vidhehi* — show; *murāri-gupte* — to Murari Gupta; *vaktum* — to describe; *yathā* — so that; *arhati* — may be able; *tava* — Your; *eva* — own; *caritram* — deeds; *eṣaḥ* — he.

**44.** Hearing the sweet words of Mahaprabhu, Narayana, the foremost of physicians, then said to Him: "O Lord, show mercy to Murari Gupta, so that he may be able to describe Your own deeds."

*Note.* The edition prints the name in quotation marks: *«नारायणो»*. Who this Narayana the physician is remains unclear; *amam* in the edition is a misprint (the Gosvami edition (GGM) has *amum*). An important episode: here Murari receives the blessing to describe the life of Gaura — which was fulfilled in his *Kadacha*, on which Karnapura relies.

### Verse 45

श्रुत्वाथ तं प्रति तदा परमप्रहृष्ट-
स्तत्प्रार्थनां स निजगाद कृपासमुद्रः ।
यद्यद्वदिष्यति तदेव समस्तमेव
शुद्धं भविष्यति भविष्यति शक्तिरुग्रा ॥४५॥

*śrutvātha taṁ prati tadā parama-prahṛṣṭas*
*tat-prārthanāṁ sa nijagāda kṛpā-samudraḥ |*
*yad yad vadiṣyati tad eva samastam eva*
*śuddhaṁ bhaviṣyati bhaviṣyati śaktir ugrā ||45||*

*Word for word:* *śrutvā* — having heard; *atha* — then; *tam prati* — to him; *tadā* — then; *parama* — supremely; *prahṛṣṭaḥ* — delighted; *tat* — his; *prārthanām* — request; *saḥ* — He; *nijagāda* — said; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *samudraḥ* — the ocean; *yat yat* — whatever; *vadiṣyati* — he will say; *tat* — that; *eva* — very; *samastam* — all; *eva* — surely; *śuddham* — faultless; *bhaviṣyati* — will be; *bhaviṣyati* — there will be; *śaktiḥ* — power; *ugrā* — mighty.

**45.** Then, having heard his request, the ocean of mercy, supremely delighted, said to him: "Whatever he says, all of it will surely be faultless, and there will be mighty power [in his words]."

*Note.* The edition has *तत् प्रार्थना*; we read *tat-prārthanām* (accusative).

### Verse 46

शृण्वन्नसौ तदुदितं सुमनाः प्रहृष्टः
प्रोत्फुल्लरोमनिचयो मुमुदे मुरारिः ।
पीयूषसिन्धुषु निमग्नमिवातिवेल-
मात्मानमुद्भटसुखैकवशो विवेद ॥४६॥

*śṛṇvann asau tad-uditaṁ sumanāḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ*
*protphulla-roma-nicayo mumude murāriḥ |*
*pīyūṣa-sindhuṣu nimagnam ivātivelam*
*ātmānam udbhaṭa-sukhaika-vaśo viveda ||46||*

*Word for word:* *śṛṇvan* — hearing; *asau* — he; *tat* — His; *uditam* — words; *sumanāḥ* — good-hearted; *prahṛṣṭaḥ* — delighted; *protphulla* — standing erect; *roma* — of hairs; *nicayaḥ* — [with] a mass; *mumude* — rejoiced; *murāriḥ* — Murari; *pīyūṣa* — of nectar; *sindhuṣu* — in oceans; *nimagnam* — immersed; *iva* — as if; *ativelam* — beyond measure; *ātmānam* — himself; *udbhaṭa* — of intense; *sukha* — happiness; *eka* — solely; *vaśaḥ* — under the sway; *viveda* — felt.

**46.** Hearing His words, the good-hearted Murari was delighted and rejoiced, the hairs of his body standing erect. Wholly under the sway of an intense happiness, he felt himself immersed beyond measure, as it were, in oceans of nectar.

*Note.* A variant noted in the edition: *sukhaika-rasaḥ* instead of *sukhaika-vaśaḥ*.

### Verse 47

श्रीवासपण्डितमहामतिरत्युदार-
शीलः स्वभावहरिभक्तिरतोऽतिधीरः ।
शुद्धः स्वधर्मनिरतो बहुशान्तदान्त-
स्तत्सेवनेन मुमुदेऽनुदिनं महात्मा ॥४७॥

*śrīvāsa-paṇḍita-mahāmatir aty-udāra-*
*śīlaḥ svabhāva-hari-bhakti-rato 'ti-dhīraḥ |*
*śuddhaḥ sva-dharma-nirato bahu-śānta-dāntas*
*tat-sevanena mumude 'nudinaṁ mahātmā ||47||*

*Word for word:* *śrīvāsa-paṇḍita* — Srivasa Pandita; *mahāmatiḥ* — great-minded; *ati* — very; *udāra* — noble; *śīlaḥ* — [of] character; *svabhāva* — by nature; *hari* — to Hari; *bhakti* — in devotion; *rataḥ* — delighting; *ati* — very; *dhīraḥ* — steadfast; *śuddhaḥ* — pure; *sva* — to his own; *dharma* — duty; *nirataḥ* — devoted; *bahu* — deeply; *śānta* — peaceful; *dāntaḥ* — self-controlled; *tat* — to Him; *sevanena* — in service; *mumude* — rejoiced; *anudinam* — day after day; *mahātmā* — the great soul.

**47.** The great-minded Srivasa Pandita — very noble in character, by nature delighting in devotion to Hari, very steadfast, pure, devoted to his own duty, deeply peaceful and self-controlled — that great soul rejoiced day after day in service to Him.

### Verse 48

एवं निरन्तरमुपासनया च नृत्यैः
सङ्कीर्त्तनैरपि तथा विविधैश्च भावैः ।
श्रीवासपण्डितमहाशय एव नित्यं
तत्सङ्गतोऽतिविलसन् मुमुदे महात्मा ॥४८॥

*evaṁ nirantaram upāsanayā ca nṛtyaiḥ*
*saṅkīrtanair api tathā vividhaiś ca bhāvaiḥ |*
*śrīvāsa-paṇḍita-mahāśaya eva nityaṁ*
*tat-saṅgato 'ti-vilasan mumude mahātmā ||48||*

*Word for word:* *evam* — thus; *nirantaram* — unceasingly; *upāsanayā* — with worship; *ca* — and; *nṛtyaiḥ* — with dances; *saṅkīrtanaiḥ* — with sankirtanas; *api* — also; *tathā* — likewise; *vividhaiḥ* — with various; *ca* — and; *bhāvaiḥ* — feelings; *śrīvāsa-paṇḍita* — Srivasa Pandita; *mahāśayaḥ* — the large-hearted; *eva* — indeed; *nityam* — always; *tat* — with Him; *saṅgataḥ* — in company; *ati* — greatly; *vilasan* — sporting; *mumude* — rejoiced; *mahātmā* — the great soul.

**48.** Thus, unceasingly — with worship, with dances and sankirtanas, and likewise with feelings of various kinds — the large-hearted Srivasa Pandita, that great soul, always rejoiced, sporting freely in His company.

### Verse 49

अध्यापयन् द्विजसुतानपरेद्युरीशः
शश्वत् स्वनामगुणकीर्त्तनमाततान ।
दैवादुवाच पुरतो द्विजसूनुरेको
नाथं न किञ्चिदपि जातु विदंस्तदन्ते ॥४९॥

*adhyāpayan dvija-sutān aparedyur īśaḥ*
*śaśvat sva-nāma-guṇa-kīrtanam ātatāna |*
*daivād uvāca purato dvija-sūnur eko*
*nāthaṁ na kiñcid api jātu vidaṁs tad-ante ||49||*

*Word for word:* *adhyāpayan* — teaching; *dvija* — of brahmanas; *sutān* — the sons; *aparedyuḥ* — on another day; *īśaḥ* — the Lord; *śaśvat* — continually; *sva* — of His own; *nāma* — Name; *guṇa* — and of qualities; *kīrtanam* — the glorification; *ātatāna* — spread; *daivāt* — as fate would have it; *uvāca* — said; *purataḥ* — before [Him]; *dvija* — of a brahmana; *sūnuḥ* — son; *ekaḥ* — one; *nātham* — to the Lord; *na* — not; *kiñcit api* — anything; *jātu* — at all; *vidan* — understanding; *tat* — of that; *ante* — at the end.

**49.** On another day the Lord, while teaching the sons of brahmanas, continually spread the glorification of His own Name and qualities. And as fate would have it, one brahmana's son, understanding nothing whatsoever, spoke before the Lord at the end of it:

*Note.* Cf. Chaitanya-bhagavata, Madhya 1.252–289: after Gaya, Nimai explains every word to His students as Krishna instead of teaching grammar. The episode with the student itself (verses 49–52) — Murari 2.4.33–34; Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 17.72–74.

### Verse 50

नाम्नो य एष महिमा खलु सोऽर्थवादः
इत्थं खलस्य वचनं परिकर्ण्य सर्व्वम् ।
कर्णौ पिधाय सह तेन पुरःसरेण
गङ्गातटं समगमद्घृणया महत्या ॥५०॥

*nāmno ya eṣa mahimā khalu so 'rthavādaḥ*
*itthaṁ khalasya vacanaṁ parikarṇya sarvam |*
*karṇau pidhāya saha tena puraḥsareṇa*
*gaṅgā-taṭaṁ samagamad ghṛṇayā mahatyā ||50||*

*Word for word:* *nāmnaḥ* — of the Name; *yaḥ* — which; *eṣaḥ* — this; *mahimā* — greatness; *khalu* — surely; *saḥ* — it; *arthavādaḥ* — mere praise; *ittham* — such; *khalasya* — of the scoundrel; *vacanam* — words; *parikarṇya* — having heard out; *sarvam* — all; *karṇau* — the ears; *pidhāya* — having stopped; *saha* — together with; *tena* — him; *puraḥsareṇa* — going ahead; *gaṅgā* — of the Ganga; *taṭam* — to the bank; *samagamat* — went; *ghṛṇayā* — with revulsion; *mahatyā* — great.

**50.** "This greatness of the Name — surely it is mere *arthavāda*!" Having heard out all such words of the scoundrel, [the Lord] stopped His ears and with great revulsion went to the bank of the Ganga, with him going ahead.

*Note.* *Arthavāda* (a term of Mimamsa) is a laudatory statement that has no direct force of injunction; to call the glory of the Name *arthavāda* is one of the ten offences against the Name.

### Verse 51

स्नात्वा सचेल उदगात् सह चेलवृन्दैः
शुद्धैः शुचिर्निजगृहं मुदितो जगाम ।
यः कीर्त्तयत्यनुदिनं य इदं शृणोति
स प्रेम्णि नाम्नि नितरां भवति प्रलीनः ॥५१॥

*snātvā sa-cela udagāt saha cela-vṛndaiḥ*
*śuddhaiḥ śucir nija-gṛhaṁ mudito jagāma |*
*yaḥ kīrtayaty anudinaṁ ya idaṁ śṛṇoti*
*sa premṇi nāmni nitarāṁ bhavati pralīnaḥ ||51||*

*Word for word:* *snātvā* — having bathed; *sa* — with; *celaḥ* — [His] clothes; *udagāt* — came out; *saha* — with; *cela* — of clothes; *vṛndaiḥ* — sets (many); *śuddhaiḥ* — clean; *śuciḥ* — purified; *nija* — to His own; *gṛham* — home; *muditaḥ* — joyful; *jagāma* — went; *yaḥ* — who; *kīrtayati* — recounts; *anudinam* — every day; *yaḥ* — who; *idam* — this; *śṛṇoti* — hears; *saḥ* — he; *premṇi* — in love; *nāmni* — in the Name; *nitarām* — wholly; *bhavati* — becomes; *pralīnaḥ* — absorbed.

**51.** Having bathed in His clothes, He came out [of the water] and, purified, in clean clothes, joyfully went to His own home. Whoever recounts this every day, whoever hears it, becomes wholly absorbed in love and in the Name.

*Note.* Bathing in one's clothes (*sacela-snāna*) is purification after contact with defilement — here, after the words of an offender. *Cela-vṛndaiḥ* — literally "with a multitude of clothes" (?). The edition has *प्रेम्नि*, a Bengali spelling. The text is the same in the Gosvami edition (GGM).

### Verse 52

इत्थं स्वनाममहिमा प्रथमं प्रकामं
प्रख्यापितः क्रमत एव शनैस्तथैव ।
आध्यात्मिकं पदमपासितमात्मपाद-
पद्मोपसेवनरसेन परमेश्वरेण ॥५२॥

*itthaṁ sva-nāma-mahimā prathamaṁ prakāmaṁ*
*prakhyāpitaḥ kramata eva śanais tathaiva |*
*ādhyātmikaṁ padam apāsitam ātma-pāda-*
*padmopasevana-rasena parameśvareṇa ||52||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *sva* — of His own; *nāma* — Name; *mahimā* — the greatness; *prathamam* — first; *prakāmam* — fully; *prakhyāpitaḥ* — was proclaimed; *kramataḥ* — step by step; *eva* — indeed; *śanaiḥ* — gradually; *tathā eva* — likewise; *ādhyātmikam* — "spiritual" [speculative]; *padam* — position; *apāsitam* — was set aside; *ātma* — of His own; *pāda* — feet; *padma* — of the lotus; *upasevana* — of the service; *rasena* — by the rapture; *parama* — by the Supreme; *īśvareṇa* — Lord.

**52.** Thus the Supreme Lord first proclaimed in full the greatness of His own Name; and then, gradually and step by step, He likewise set aside the "spiritual" position through the rapture of service to His own lotus feet.

*Note.* *Ādhyātmika* is the same word as in the reproach to Murari (verse 42): speculative "spirituality" without *bhakti*.

### Verse 53

नाथः कदाचिदथ तैर्निजपादभक्तैः
श्रीवासपण्डितमुखैः सुखसागरः सः ।
अद्वैतचन्द्रमवलोकितुमस्य गेहे
श्रीमाननङ्ग इव विग्रहवान् प्रतस्थे ॥५३॥

*nāthaḥ kadācid atha tair nija-pāda-bhaktaiḥ*
*śrīvāsa-paṇḍita-mukhaiḥ sukha-sāgaraḥ saḥ |*
*advaitacandram avalokitum asya gehe*
*śrīmān anaṅga iva vigrahavān pratasthe ||53||*

*Word for word:* *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *kadācit* — once; *atha* — then; *taiḥ* — with those; *nija* — of His own; *pāda* — feet; *bhaktaiḥ* — devotees; *śrīvāsa-paṇḍita* — Srivasa Pandita; *mukhaiḥ* — headed by; *sukha* — of happiness; *sāgaraḥ* — the ocean; *saḥ* — He; *advaitacandram* — Advaitachandra; *avalokitum* — to see; *asya* — His; *gehe* — at the house; *śrīmān* — beautiful; *anaṅgaḥ* — Ananga; *iva* — like; *vigrahavān* — possessing a body; *pratasthe* — set out.

**53.** Then once the Lord, the ocean of happiness, beautiful like Ananga, the bodiless, having taken a body, set out with those devotees of His feet headed by Srivasa Pandita to see Advaitachandra at His house.

*Note.* Ananga ("the bodiless") is Kamadeva, the god of love. Advaita's house is in Shantipura. The second half of the verse repeats verse 16.

### Verse 54

गच्छन् पथि प्रथितनर्त्तनकीर्त्तनाद्यै-
र्गायन्नटन्नपि जगाम तदस्य वेश्म ।
अद्वैतचन्द्रमधिभूमिषु दण्डवत् स
भूयः पपात निजभक्तमहत्त्ववेदी ॥५४॥

*gacchan pathi prathita-nartana-kīrtanādyair*
*gāyan naṭann api jagāma tad asya veśma |*
*advaitacandram adhi bhūmiṣu daṇḍavat sa*
*bhūyaḥ papāta nija-bhakta-mahattva-vedī ||54||*

*Word for word:* *gacchan* — going; *pathi* — on the road; *prathita* — with famous; *nartana* — dances; *kīrtana* — kirtanas; *ādyaiḥ* — and the like; *gāyan* — singing; *naṭan* — dancing; *api* — and; *jagāma* — came; *tat* — to that; *asya* — His; *veśma* — house; *advaitacandram* — Advaitachandra; *adhi* — before; *bhūmiṣu* — on the ground; *daṇḍavat* — like a rod; *saḥ* — He; *bhūyaḥ* — in His turn; *papāta* — fell; *nija* — of His own; *bhakta* — devotees; *mahattva* — the greatness; *vedī* — knowing.

**54.** Going along the road with famous dances, kirtanas and the like, singing and dancing, He came to His house. And He who knows the greatness of His own devotees in His turn fell on the ground like a rod before Advaitachandra.

*Note.* *Bhūyaḥ*, "in His turn": that is, after Advaita had fallen before Him. The edition has *भुयः*.

### Verse 55

आलिङ्गनान्यथ परस्परमुत्सुकाङ्गौ
तौ चक्रतुः परमकारुणिकौ जगत्सु ।
अद्वैत एव किमु किं नु स गौरचन्द्र
इत्यूहितौ जनचयेन बभूवतुश्च ॥५५॥

*āliṅganāny atha parasparam utsukāṅgau*
*tau cakratuḥ parama-kāruṇikau jagatsu |*
*advaita eva kim u kiṁ nu sa gauracandra*
*ity ūhitau jana-cayena babhūvatuś ca ||55||*

*Word for word:* *āliṅganāni* — embraces; *atha* — then; *parasparam* — mutual; *utsuka* — [with] longing; *aṅgau* — bodies; *tau* — the two; *cakratuḥ* — made; *parama* — supremely; *kāruṇikau* — merciful; *jagatsu* — in the worlds; *advaitaḥ* — Advaita; *eva* — indeed; *kim u* — is it; *kim nu* — or is it; *saḥ* — He; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra; *iti* — thus; *ūhitau* — wondered about; *jana* — of people; *cayena* — by the crowd; *babhūvatuḥ* — They became; *ca* — and.

**55.** Then the two, supremely merciful in all the worlds, Their bodies full of longing, embraced each other; and the crowd of people wondered about Them: "Is this Advaita? Or is it He, Gaurachandra?"

*Note.* A play on the name *Advaita*, "non-dual": in the embrace the two became indistinguishable.

### Verse 56

शुद्धासने समुपविश्य स गौरचन्द्रः
स्वच्छां कथामकथयत् करुणैकराशिः ।
आविष्कृतस्वपदभक्तिविलासलोलो
नानाविधेन निजभक्तिनिरूपणेन ॥५६॥

*śuddhāsane samupaviśya sa gauracandraḥ*
*svacchāṁ kathām akathayat karuṇaika-rāśiḥ |*
*āviṣkṛta-sva-pada-bhakti-vilāsa-lolo*
*nānā-vidhena nija-bhakti-nirūpaṇena ||56||*

*Word for word:* *śuddha* — on a clean; *āsane* — seat; *samupaviśya* — having sat down; *saḥ* — He; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra; *svacchām* — lucid; *kathām* — discourse; *akathayat* — spoke; *karuṇā* — of mercy; *eka* — the sole; *rāśiḥ* — store; *āviṣkṛta* — revealed; *sva* — to His own; *pada* — feet; *bhakti* — of devotion; *vilāsa* — in the play; *lolaḥ* — absorbed; *nānā* — of many; *vidhena* — kinds; *nija* — of His own; *bhakti* — devotion; *nirūpaṇena* — with the explanation.

**56.** Seated on a clean seat, Gaurachandra, the sole store of mercy, absorbed in the play of the devotion to His own feet that He had revealed, held a lucid discourse, explaining devotion to Himself in many ways.

### Verse 57

अद्वैत एष निजगाद ततो महात्मा
भक्तिः कलौ न खलु वर्त्तत एव मूढाः ।
ये संवदन्ति कुधियः सकलास्त एते
पश्यन्तु तत्तदशृणोत् स्वयमेव नाथः ॥५७॥

*advaita eṣa nijagāda tato mahātmā*
*bhaktiḥ kalau na khalu vartata eva mūḍhāḥ |*
*ye saṁvadanti kudhiyaḥ sakalās ta ete*
*paśyantu tat tad aśṛṇot svayam eva nāthaḥ ||57||*

*Word for word:* *advaitaḥ* — Advaita; *eṣaḥ* — this; *nijagāda* — said; *tataḥ* — then; *mahātmā* — the great soul; *bhaktiḥ* — bhakti; *kalau* — in Kali; *na* — not; *khalu* — surely; *vartate* — exists; *eva* — at all; *mūḍhāḥ* — fools; *ye* — who; *saṁvadanti* — keep saying; *kudhiyaḥ* — dull-witted; *sakalāḥ* — all; *te ete* — those; *paśyantu* — let them look; *tat* — that; *tat* — that; *aśṛṇot* — heard; *svayam* — Himself; *eva* — indeed; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord.

**57.** Then the great-souled Advaita said: "Let all those dull-witted fools who keep saying, 'In Kali there is no bhakti at all,' look [at this]!" And the Lord Himself heard it.

### Verse 58

नास्तीति यो वदति तस्य गतिर्हि नास्ति
तस्यैव जन्म विफलं खलु सोऽतिपापी ।
भक्तिर्हि राजति कलौ सततं तदाति-
क्रोधारुणाक्षियुगलो भगवान् जगाद ॥५८॥

*nāstīti yo vadati tasya gatir hi nāsti*
*tasyaiva janma viphalaṁ khalu so 'ti-pāpī |*
*bhaktir hi rājati kalau satataṁ tadāti-*
*krodhāruṇākṣi-yugalo bhagavān jagāda ||58||*

*Word for word:* *na asti* — there is none; *iti* — thus; *yaḥ* — who; *vadati* — says; *tasya* — of him; *gatiḥ* — path; *hi* — truly; *na asti* — there is not; *tasya* — of him; *eva* — very; *janma* — birth; *viphalam* — fruitless; *khalu* — surely; *saḥ* — he; *ati* — a great; *pāpī* — sinner; *bhaktiḥ* — bhakti; *hi* — for; *rājati* — reigns; *kalau* — in Kali; *satatam* — always; *tadā* — then; *ati* — with intense; *krodha* — anger; *aruṇa* — reddened; *akṣi* — of eyes; *yugalaḥ* — [with] a pair; *bhagavān* — Bhagavan; *jagāda* — said.

**58.** Then Bhagavan, His two eyes reddened with intense anger, said: "He who says 'There is none' truly has no path; his very birth is fruitless; surely he is a great sinner! For bhakti reigns in Kali always."

*Note.* The edition has *तस्यै जन्म*; the metre requires *tasyaiva*. The edition gives *tad ādi* (obscure); the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *tadāti-krodhāruṇākṣi-yugalaḥ* ("then, with eyes reddened by intense anger"), and so we read.

### Verse 59

श्रीवास एष तदनन्तरमित्थमूचे
दृष्ट्वा ततो द्विजमवैष्णवमेकमुग्रम् ।
विघ्नो बभूव नितरामयमत्र नूनं
सङ्कीर्त्तने कथमितो बहिरेष याति ॥५९॥

*śrīvāsa eṣa tad-anantaram ittham ūce*
*dṛṣṭvā tato dvijam avaiṣṇavam ekam ugram |*
*vighno babhūva nitarām ayam atra nūnaṁ*
*saṅkīrtane katham ito bahir eṣa yāti ||59||*

*Word for word:* *śrīvāsaḥ* — Srivasa; *eṣaḥ* — this; *tat* — that; *anantaram* — after; *ittham* — thus; *ūce* — said; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *tataḥ* — there; *dvijam* — a brahmana; *avaiṣṇavam* — not a Vaishnava; *ekam* — one; *ugram* — fierce; *vighnaḥ* — an obstacle; *babhūva* — has become; *nitarām* — great; *ayam* — he; *atra* — here; *nūnam* — surely; *saṅkīrtane* — to the sankirtana; *katham* — how; *itaḥ* — from here; *bahiḥ* — away; *eṣaḥ* — he; *yāti* — goes.

**59.** After that Srivasa, seeing there a fierce brahmana who was not a Vaishnava, said thus: "Surely he will be a great obstacle to the sankirtana here. How can he be got away from here?"

### Verse 60

त्वच्चिन्तयालमलमत्र न चैष विप्र
आयास्यतीत्यवितथं निजगाद नाथः ।
नैवागमत् स च तदीयमनोनिदेशै-
रत्रान्तरे मुदमियाय स भूमिदेवः ॥६०॥

*tvac-cintayālam alam atra na caiṣa vipra*
*āyāsyatīty avitathaṁ nijagāda nāthaḥ |*
*naivāgamat sa ca tadīya-mano-nideśair*
*atrāntare mudam iyāya sa bhūmi-devaḥ ||60||*

*Word for word:* *tvat* — of your; *cintayā* — with worry; *alam alam* — enough, enough; *atra* — here; *na* — not; *ca* — and; *eṣaḥ* — this; *vipraḥ* — brahmana; *āyāsyati* — will come; *iti* — thus; *avitatham* — unfailingly; *nijagāda* — said; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *na eva* — not at all; *agamat* — came; *saḥ* — he; *ca* — and; *tadīya* — His; *manaḥ* — mental; *nideśaiḥ* — by the commands; *atra antare* — meanwhile; *mudam* — joy; *iyāya* — attained; *saḥ* — that; *bhūmi-devaḥ* — god on earth (brahmana).

**60.** "Enough, enough of your worry here: this brahmana will not come," the Lord said unfailingly. And by His mental commands he did not come at all; and meanwhile that god on earth [Srivasa] rejoiced.

*Note.* In the edition the first line (*त्वच्चिन्तयालमत्र*) lacks two syllables; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *tvac-cintayālam alam atra*, and so we read. In the third line the edition has *नैवागम*; we read *naivāgamat* (for the metre). *Bhūmi-deva*, "god on earth", is a brahmana; here, evidently, Srivasa himself.

### Verse 61

श्रीवासविप्रतिलकांसतटे स दक्षं
विन्यस्य बाहुमितरञ्च गदाधरांसे ।
श्रीरामपण्डितवराङ्गतटे पदाब्जं
दत्त्वा रराज स सुधांशुसमूहकान्तः ॥६१॥

*śrīvāsa-vipra-tilakāṁsa-taṭe sa dakṣaṁ*
*vinyasya bāhum itarañ ca gadādharāṁse |*
*śrīrāma-paṇḍita-varāṅga-taṭe padābjaṁ*
*dattvā rarāja sa sudhāṁśu-samūha-kāntaḥ ||61||*

*Word for word:* *śrīvāsa* — of Srivasa; *vipra* — of the brahmanas; *tilaka* — of the ornament; *aṁsa* — of the shoulder; *taṭe* — on the slope; *saḥ* — He; *dakṣam* — the right; *vinyasya* — having placed; *bāhum* — arm; *itaram* — the other; *ca* — and; *gadādhara* — of Gadadhara; *aṁse* — on the shoulder; *śrīrāma-paṇḍita* — of Sri Rama Pandita; *vara-aṅga* — of the head; *taṭe* — on the surface; *pada* — of the foot; *abjam* — the lotus; *dattvā* — having set; *rarāja* — shone; *saḥ* — He; *sudhāṁśu* — of moons; *samūha* — than a multitude; *kāntaḥ* — lovelier.

**61.** Placing His right arm on the shoulder of Srivasa, the ornament of the brahmanas, and the other on the shoulder of Gadadhara, and setting His lotus foot on the head of Sri Rama Pandita, He shone, lovelier than a multitude of moons.

*Note.* *Varāṅga* ("the best limb") is the head.

### Verse 62

क्रीडापरोऽस्य निलये स महेश्वरस्य
राजीवलोचनयुगः कलधौतगौरः ।
स्मेराननः सपदि दर्पकदर्पहारी
रेजे निजैर्जनचयै रचयन् विहारम् ॥६२॥

*krīḍā-paro 'sya nilaye sa maheśvarasya*
*rājīva-locana-yugaḥ kaladhauta-gauraḥ |*
*smerānanaḥ sapadi darpaka-darpa-hārī*
*reje nijair jana-cayai racayan vihāram ||62||*

*Word for word:* *krīḍā* — to play; *paraḥ* — given; *asya* — of this; *nilaye* — in the abode; *saḥ* — He; *mahā* — great; *īśvarasya* — of the Lord; *rājīva* — of lotuses; *locana* — of eyes; *yugaḥ* — [with] a pair; *kaladhauta* — like gold; *gauraḥ* — golden; *smera* — smiling; *ānanaḥ* — [with] a face; *sapadi* — at once; *darpaka* — of Kandarpa; *darpa* — the pride; *hārī* — stealing; *reje* — shone; *nijaiḥ* — with His own; *jana* — of people; *cayaiḥ* — with the crowds; *racayan* — arranging; *vihāram* — pastimes.

**62.** Given to play in the abode of this great Lord [Advaita], He — with a pair of lotus eyes, golden as pure gold, His face smiling, at once stealing the pride of Kandarpa — shone, arranging pastimes with the crowds of His own people.

*Note.* *Maheśvara*, "the great Lord": Advaita is held to be an incarnation of Mahavishnu and Sadashiva. *Darpaka* (Kandarpa) is the god of love.

### Verse 63

अध्यात्मतत्त्वमभि गौरमहाप्रभुः स
व्याख्यां चकार बहुदुर्गमबोधमन्यैः ।
एकोऽवशिष्यत इहाविरतं स आत्मा
सृष्टौ स एव पुनरेकक एव भाति ॥६३॥

*adhyātma-tattvam abhi gaura-mahāprabhuḥ sa*
*vyākhyāṁ cakāra bahu-durgama-bodham anyaiḥ |*
*eko 'vaśiṣyata ihāvirataṁ sa ātmā*
*sṛṣṭau sa eva punar ekaka eva bhāti ||63||*

*Word for word:* *adhyātma* — of the higher Self; *tattvam* — the truth; *abhi* — concerning; *gaura-mahāprabhuḥ* — Gaura Mahaprabhu; *saḥ* — He; *vyākhyām* — an explanation; *cakāra* — gave; *bahu* — very; *durgama* — difficult; *bodham* — to understand; *anyaiḥ* — for others; *ekaḥ* — one; *avaśiṣyate* — remains; *iha* — here; *aviratam* — unceasingly; *saḥ* — that; *ātmā* — Atma; *sṛṣṭau* — in creation; *saḥ* — it; *eva* — the same; *punaḥ* — again; *ekakaḥ* — alone; *eva* — indeed; *bhāti* — shines.

**63.** Gaura Mahaprabhu gave an explanation concerning the truth of the higher Self, very difficult for others to understand: "Here the one Atma alone unceasingly remains; and in creation it is the very same [Atma] that again shines, alone."

*Note.* Cf. Srimad-Bhagavatam 2.9.32 (*aham evāsam evāgre… paścād ahaṁ yad etac ca yo 'vaśiṣyeta so 'smy aham*). Verses 63–68 are the "difficult knowledge" (*jñāna*) that the Lord sets out in Advaita's house; cf. Murari 2.5.20–33 (the Lord expounds the path of knowledge and proclaims the highest — bhakti) and Chaitanya-bhagavata, Madhya 19.20 ff., where Advaita deliberately expounds the Yoga-vasishtha. The translation of the philosophical lines of verses 63–67 is provisional.

### Verse 64

इत्थं प्रसार्य्य स्वकरौ करुणासमुद्रो
मुष्टीचकार च पुनर्द्रुतमेव नृत्यन् ।
सच्चित्स्वरूपमथ तत्त्वनिरूपणं त-
द्भूयो जगाद जगदेकगतिः प्रकामम् ॥६४॥

*itthaṁ prasārya sva-karau karuṇā-samudro*
*muṣṭī-cakāra ca punar drutam eva nṛtyan |*
*sac-cit-svarūpam atha tattva-nirūpaṇaṁ tad*
*bhūyo jagāda jagad-eka-gatiḥ prakāmam ||64||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *prasārya* — having opened; *sva* — His own; *karau* — hands; *karuṇā* — of mercy; *samudraḥ* — the ocean; *muṣṭī-cakāra* — clenched into fists; *ca* — and; *punaḥ* — again; *drutam* — quickly; *eva* — indeed; *nṛtyan* — dancing; *sat* — of being; *cit* — of consciousness; *svarūpam* — [having] the nature; *atha* — then; *tattva* — of the truth; *nirūpaṇam* — the exposition; *tat* — that; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *jagāda* — set forth; *jagat* — of the world; *eka* — the only; *gatiḥ* — refuge; *prakāmam* — at length.

**64.** Thus [speaking], the ocean of mercy, dancing, opened His hands and at once clenched them again into fists. Then He, the only refuge of the world, again set forth at length that exposition of the truth whose nature is being and consciousness.

*Note.* The gesture apparently depicts the unfolding and folding up of the world (creation and dissolution) (?). The edition has *जयदेकगतिः*; we read *jagad-eka-gatiḥ*. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 65

भावोऽपि निश्चितमनर्थक एव तस्य
सद्रूपमेव सुधियामवधारणीयम् ।
यद्ब्रह्मणो भवति नैव कदापि मुक्ति-
रेकत्वमेतदवबोधमृते हि सा स्यात् ॥६५॥

*bhāvo 'pi niścitam anarthaka eva tasya*
*sad-rūpam eva sudhiyām avadhāraṇīyam |*
*yad brahmaṇo bhavati naiva kadāpi muktir*
*ekatvam etad-avabodham ṛte hi sā syāt ||65||*

*Word for word:* *bhāvaḥ* — becoming (being that has arisen); *api* — too; *niścitam* — certainly; *anarthakaḥ* — meaningless; *eva* — indeed; *tasya* — its; *sat* — true; *rūpam* — nature; *eva* — alone; *sudhiyām* — by the wise; *avadhāraṇīyam* — is to be ascertained; *yat* — for; *brahmaṇaḥ* — with Brahman; *bhavati* — comes about; *na eva* — not; *kadāpi* — ever; *muktiḥ* — liberation; *ekatvam* — oneness; *etat* — of this; *avabodham* — the understanding; *ṛte* — without; *hi* — indeed; *sā* — it; *syāt* — could be.

**65.** "Becoming, too, is certainly meaningless; the wise should ascertain only its true nature. For without the understanding of this, liberation — oneness with Brahman — never comes about at all."

*Note.* The syntax of the second half is unclear (*hi sā syāt*, "for it would be", hangs loose); we translate by the sense. *Etat* may also be taken as referring to the oneness: "without understanding this oneness with Brahman there is never liberation". The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 66

पश्याङ्गुली करगते पुनरेककस्य
सैकोऽमृतेन निचितां परिलोचिताञ्च ।
अन्यां व्रणेन गलतातितरामवद्यां
नो पश्यति क्षणमपि प्रकटं घृणार्त्तः ॥६६॥

*paśyāṅgulī kara-gate punar ekakasya*
*sa eko 'mṛtena nicitāṁ parilocitāñ ca |*
*anyāṁ vraṇena galatātitarām avadyāṁ*
*no paśyati kṣaṇam api prakaṭaṁ ghṛṇārtaḥ ||66||*

*Word for word:* *paśya* — look; *aṅgulī* — two fingers; *kara* — on the hand; *gate* — situated; *punaḥ* — now; *ekakasya* — of one [person]; *saḥ* — he; *ekaḥ* — one and the same; *amṛtena* — with nectar; *nicitām* — anointed; *parilocitām* — gazed upon [fondly]; *ca* — and; *anyām* — the other; *vraṇena* — with a sore; *galatā* — oozing; *atitarām* — utterly; *avadyām* — loathsome; *na u* — not; *paśyati* — looks at; *kṣaṇam api* — even for a moment; *prakaṭam* — openly; *ghṛṇā* — by disgust; *ārtaḥ* — tormented.

**66.** "Look: here are two fingers on the hand of a single person. The one anointed with nectar he, one and the same, gazes upon [fondly]; at the other, utterly loathsome with an oozing sore, he, tormented by disgust, will not look openly for even a moment."

*Note.* The point of the parable within the chain of verses 65–67 is unclear (?): perhaps the one Atma relates differently to its *upādhis* (coverings). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 67

इत्थं स एक इह शेषपदं ह्यनादि-
रात्मा सदैव परिशिष्यत एवमेषः ।
सोपाधिरेव भवति प्रकटादुपाधे-
र्मुक्तोऽन्यथा स खलु कश्चिदपीह जीवः ॥६७॥

*itthaṁ sa eka iha śeṣa-padaṁ hy anādir*
*ātmā sadaiva pariśiṣyata evam eṣaḥ |*
*sopādhir eva bhavati prakaṭād upādher*
*mukto 'nyathā sa khalu kaścid apīha jīvaḥ ||67||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *saḥ* — that; *ekaḥ* — one; *iha* — here; *śeṣa* — of "the remainder"; *padam* — [the bearer of] the word; *hi* — indeed; *anādiḥ* — beginningless; *ātmā* — Atma; *sadā eva* — always; *pariśiṣyate* — remains; *evam* — thus; *eṣaḥ* — this; *sa-upādhiḥ* — with a covering; *eva* — indeed; *bhavati* — becomes; *prakaṭāt* — from the manifest; *upādheḥ* — covering; *muktaḥ* — freed; *anyathā* — otherwise; *saḥ* — it; *khalu* — indeed; *kaścit api* — some; *iha* — here; *jīvaḥ* — jiva.

**67.** "Thus here that one beginningless Atma — what is called 'the remainder' — always remains. This same [Atma] does become possessed of a covering; freed from the manifest covering, [it is the Atma]; otherwise it is indeed just some jiva here."

*Note.* The edition has *भवती* and *उपाधे मुक्तो*; we read *bhavati*, *upādher muktaḥ*. *Śeṣa* — "remainder" (cf. *avaśiṣyate* in verse 63). The translation is provisional. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 68

इत्थं प्रभुर्बहु निरूप्य निसर्गदुर्गं
ज्ञानं तथा लघुतया स्वजनान् विबोध्य ।
विश्रम्य तत्र गलदश्रुझरप्लुताक्षो
रोमाञ्चसञ्चययुतो मधुरं जगाद ॥६८॥

*itthaṁ prabhur bahu nirūpya nisarga-durgaṁ*
*jñānaṁ tathā laghutayā sva-janān vibodhya |*
*viśramya tatra galad-aśru-jhara-plutākṣo*
*romāñca-sañcaya-yuto madhuraṁ jagāda ||68||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *bahu* — at length; *nirūpya* — having expounded; *nisarga* — by nature; *durgam* — hard of access; *jñānam* — knowledge; *tathā* — thus; *laghutayā* — simply; *sva* — His own; *janān* — people; *vibodhya* — having made understand; *viśramya* — having paused; *tatra* — then; *galat* — of falling; *aśru* — tears; *jhara* — by a stream; *pluta* — flooded; *akṣaḥ* — [with] eyes; *romāñca* — of bristling hairs; *sañcaya* — with masses; *yutaḥ* — covered; *madhuram* — sweetly; *jagāda* — said.

**68.** Having thus expounded at length knowledge that is by nature hard of access, and having thus made His own people understand it simply, the Lord fell silent; then, His eyes flooded with a stream of falling tears, covered with masses of bristling hairs, He sweetly said:

*Note.* *Laghutayā* — "lightly, simply", or "by showing its insignificance". The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 69

स्निह्यन्मनाः पुलकितो विरुदन् हसंश्च
प्रेमासवेन जडवद्गतदेहधर्मा ।
गायन्नटन्नपि समस्तमिदं त्रिलोकं
मद्भक्त एव परिपाति पुनाति नित्यम् ॥६९॥

*snihyan-manāḥ pulakito virudan hasaṁś ca*
*premāsavena jaḍavad gata-deha-dharmā |*
*gāyan naṭann api samastam idaṁ tri-lokaṁ*
*mad-bhakta eva paripāti punāti nityam ||69||*

*Word for word:* *snihyat* — melting with love; *manāḥ* — [with] a heart; *pulakitaḥ* — with bristling hairs; *virudan* — weeping; *hasan* — laughing; *ca* — and; *prema* — of love; *āsavena* — by the intoxicating drink; *jaḍavat* — like one insensible; *gata* — [for whom] gone; *deha* — of the body; *dharmā* — the properties; *gāyan* — singing; *naṭan* — dancing; *api* — and; *samastam* — entire; *idam* — this; *tri* — threefold; *lokam* — world; *mat* — My; *bhaktaḥ* — devotee; *eva* — it is; *paripāti* — protects; *punāti* — purifies; *nityam* — always.

**69.** "With a heart melting with love, the hairs of his body bristling, now weeping and now laughing, having lost, like one insensible, the properties of the body through the intoxicating drink of love, singing and dancing — it is My devotee who always protects and purifies this entire threefold world.

वाग्गद्गदा द्रवते यस्य चित्तं
रुदत्यभीक्ष्णं हसति क्वचिच्च ।
विलज्ज उद्गायति नृत्यते च
मद्भक्तियुक्तो भुवनं पुनाति ॥

*vāg gadgadā dravate yasya cittaṁ*
*rudaty abhīkṣṇaṁ hasati kvacic ca |*
*vilajja udgāyati nṛtyate ca*
*mad-bhakti-yukto bhuvanaṁ punāti ||*

*Word for word:* *vāk* — speech; *gadgadā* — faltering; *dravate* — melts; *yasya* — whose; *cittam* — heart; *rudati* — weeps; *abhīkṣṇam* — again and again; *hasati* — laughs; *kvacit* — sometimes; *ca* — and; *vilajjaḥ* — without shame; *udgāyati* — sings aloud; *nṛtyate* — dances; *ca* — and; *mat* — to Me; *bhakti* — with devotion; *yuktaḥ* — endowed; *bhuvanam* — the world; *punāti* — purifies.

'He whose speech falters, whose heart melts, who weeps again and again and sometimes laughs, who without shame sings aloud and dances — he, endowed with devotion to Me, purifies the world.'"

*Note.* The metre is *upajāti*. Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.14.24 (Krishna's words to Uddhava). In the edition the verse stands in quotation marks and without a number; the next verse of the edition is 70.

### Verse 70

इत्युक्तवान्निजजनैः करुणैकसिन्धुः

नृत्योद्यतः स्वयमसौ जगतीतले यत्
प्रेम प्रकाशयति तत्करुणैव सैषा ॥७०॥

*ity uktavān nija-janaiḥ karuṇaika-sindhuḥ*
*smerānanaḥ pramudito madhuraṁ nanarta |*
*nṛtyodyataḥ svayam asau jagatī-tale yat*
*prema prakāśayati tat karuṇaiva saiṣā ||70||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *uktavān* — having spoken; *nija* — His own; *janaiḥ* — with the people; *karuṇā* — of mercy; *eka* — the sole; *sindhuḥ* — ocean; *smera* — smiling; *ānanaḥ* — [with] a face; *pramuditaḥ* — joyful; *madhuram* — sweetly; *nanarta* — danced; *nṛtya* — to dance; *udyataḥ* — setting about; *svayam* — Himself; *asau* — He; *jagatī* — of the earth; *tale* — on the surface; *yat* — that; *prema* — love; *prakāśayati* — reveals; *tat* — that; *karuṇā* — the mercy; *eva* — precisely; *sā eṣā* — this.

**70.** Having spoken thus, the sole ocean of mercy, His face smiling, joyfully and sweetly danced with His own people. That He Himself, setting about to dance, reveals love on the surface of the earth — that is precisely this mercy [of His].

*Note.* The edition has *प्रेमप्रकाशयति* written as one word; we read *prema prakāśayati*.

श्रीवासगेहमगमत् प्रभुरेष तावत् ॥७१॥

*tatrāparedyur amala-dyumaṇi-prakāśo*
*'dvaitaḥ sametya karuṇā-nidhi-darśanāya |*
*snātvārcanañ ca viracayya sameti yāvat*
*śrīvāsa-geham agamat prabhur eṣa tāvat ||71||*

*Word for word:* *tatra* — there; *aparedyuḥ* — on the next day; *amala* — of the spotless; *dyumaṇi* — sun; *prakāśaḥ* — [with] the radiance; *advaitaḥ* — Advaita; *sametya* — having arrived; *karuṇā* — of mercy; *nidhi* — the treasure-house; *darśanāya* — to see; *snātvā* — having bathed; *arcanam* — worship; *ca* — and; *viracayya* — having performed; *sameti* — was coming; *yāvat* — while; *śrīvāsa* — of Srivasa; *geham* — to the house; *agamat* — went; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *eṣaḥ* — this; *tāvat* — meanwhile.

**71.** On the next day Advaita, radiant as the spotless sun, arrived there to see the treasure-house of mercy. While He, having bathed and performed His worship, was about to come, the Lord in the meantime went to the house of Srivasa.

### Verse 72

शान्त्यर्थमित्थमवदत् कमलायताक्षः ॥७२॥

*gatvātha tatra sa manāg ghasitaṁ vidhāya*
*daṇḍe prasūnam upayojya ca huṅkṛtena |*
*etad gadārcanam aho kṛtam asti duṣṭa-*
*śānty-artham ittham avadat kamalāyatākṣaḥ ||72||*

*Word for word:* *gatvā* — having gone; *atha* — then; *tatra* — there; *saḥ* — He; *manāk* — slight; *hasitam* — a smile; *vidhāya* — having made; *daṇḍe* — on a staff; *prasūnam* — a flower; *upayojya* — having placed; *ca* — and; *huṅkṛtena* — with a roar; *etat* — this; *gadā* — of the club; *arcanam* — worship; *aho* — aho; *kṛtam asti* — has been performed; *duṣṭa* — of the wicked; *śānti* — of the subduing; *artham* — for the sake; *ittham* — thus; *avadat* — said; *kamala* — like lotuses; *āyata* — long; *akṣaḥ* — [He whose] eyes.

**72.** Having gone there, He smiled slightly, placed a flower on a staff and, with a roar, He whose eyes were long like lotuses said thus: "Aho! This worship of the club has been performed for the subduing of the wicked!"

*Note.* The edition has *मनाग्धसितं*; we read *manāg ghasitam* (*manāk* + *hasitam*). The club (*gadā*) is the weapon of Vishnu and of Balarama.

### Verse 73

एकोऽस्ति दुष्टतम एव मदीयभक्त-
द्वेषी गलद्व्रणतनुर्बहुकुष्ठरोगैः ।
भूयोऽपि तं परमनारकिनं विधास्ये
तच्छिष्यकानपि तथा श्वशृगालभक्ष्यान् ॥७३॥

*eko 'sti duṣṭatama eva madīya-bhakta-*
*dveṣī galad-vraṇa-tanur bahu-kuṣṭha-rogaiḥ |*
*bhūyo 'pi taṁ parama-nārakinaṁ vidhāsye*
*tac-chiṣyakān api tathā śva-śṛgāla-bhakṣyān ||73||*

*Word for word:* *ekaḥ* — one; *asti* — there is; *duṣṭatamaḥ* — most wicked; *eva* — indeed; *madīya* — of My; *bhakta* — devotees; *dveṣī* — a hater; *galat* — oozing; *vraṇa* — with sores; *tanuḥ* — [whose] body; *bahu* — by many; *kuṣṭha* — of leprosy; *rogaiḥ* — by the diseases; *bhūyaḥ api* — moreover; *tam* — him; *parama* — utter; *nārakinam* — a denizen of hell; *vidhāsye* — I shall make; *tat* — his; *śiṣyakān* — wretched disciples; *api* — also; *tathā* — likewise; *śva* — of dogs; *śṛgāla* — and of jackals; *bhakṣyān* — food.

**73.** "There is one most wicked hater of My devotees, his body oozing with sores from many kinds of leprosy. I shall, moreover, make him an utter denizen of hell, and likewise his wretched disciples food for dogs and jackals!"

*Note.* Probably Gopala Chapala, who offended Srivasa and was struck with leprosy (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 17.37–59; Murari 2.13).

इच्छामि गन्तुमटवीमित एव सा भू-

*Word for word:* *icchāmi* — I wish; *gantum* — to go; *aṭavīm* — into the forest; *itaḥ* — from here; *eva* — indeed; *sā* — this; *bhūḥ* — land; *vyāghrasya* — to a tiger; *ke api* — some; *sadṛśāḥ* — similar; *harayaḥ* — monkeys; *tathā* — likewise; *anye* — others; *kecit* — some; *tathā* — likewise; *tṛṇa* — grass; *nibhāḥ* — resembling; *taravaḥ* — trees; *ca* — and; *kecit* — some; *tena* — therefore; *idam* — this; *eva* — very; *su* — very; *mahat* — great; *vipinam* — forest; *sudurgam* — impassable.

**74.** "I wish to go from here into the forest! [But] this very land [is a forest]: some here are like tigers, others likewise are monkeys, some likewise are like grass, and some are trees. Therefore this very [place] is a vast, impassable forest!"

*Note.* The first hint of the future sannyasa. *Hari* can also mean "lion".

सोऽयं निपत्य सभयं प्रणनाम भूयः ॥७५॥

*advaita āgata iti śrutam asti kiṁ tan*

*Word for word:* *advaitaḥ* — Advaita; *āgataḥ* — has come; *iti* — that; *śrutam asti* — it is heard; *kim* — why; *tat* — then; *na* — not; *āyāti* — comes; *asau* — He; *ciram* — for so long; *ataḥ* — therefore; *nanu* — surely; *tatra* — there; *yāmi* — I shall go; *ittham* — thus; *vicintayataḥ* — while [He] was reflecting; *eva* — just; *puraḥ* — before; *asya* — Him; *bhūmau* — on the ground; *saḥ ayam* — He (Advaita); *nipatya* — having fallen; *sa* — with; *bhayam* — awe; *praṇanāma* — bowed down; *bhūyaḥ* — again and again.

**75.** "It is heard that Advaita has come — why then does He not come for so long? So I shall surely go to Him there." Just as He was reflecting thus, Advaita fell to the ground before Him and in awe bowed down again and again.

**76.** Then He quickly raised Advaita, took Him by the hand and said: "Surely it is for your sake that I have come here." Having spoken thus, the ever-merciful [Lord] sat down together with Him on a couch and thereupon shone openly.

*Note.* The edition has *तन्तु* = *taṁ tu*. "I have come for your sake": Advaita called Gaura down to earth by His prayers (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 3).

**77.** Then, at His command, the great soul Advaita danced wildly, the workings of His mind overwhelmed by an excess of happiness. Seeing all this, the Lord, the moon of the ocean of rasa, joyfully said to Him, filling His heart with rasa:

एते भवन्ति खलु पात्रममुष्य सत्यम् ॥७८॥

*kṣauṇyāṁ tvad-artham iha nūnam upāgato 'smi ||79||*

*Word for word:* *jyotsnāvatīṣu* — moonlit; *rajanīṣu* — on nights; *tathā* — thus; *upaviṣṭaḥ* — seated; *taiḥ* — them; *sārdham* — with; *udyat* — of the rising; *akhara* — mild-rayed [moon]; *dyuti* — with the radiance; *dīpyamānaḥ* — shining; *advaitam* — to Advaita; *eva* — in particular; *nijagāda* — said; *bhavān* — you; *hi* — indeed; *bhaktaḥ* — a devotee; *kṣauṇyām* — to the earth; *tvat* — of you; *artham* — for the sake; *iha* — here; *nūnam* — surely; *upāgataḥ asmi* — I have come.

**79.** Thus, seated with them on moonlit nights, shining with a radiance like that of the rising mild-rayed [moon], He said to Advaita in particular: "It is you indeed who are a devotee; surely it is for your sake that I have come here to the earth."

*Note.* *Akhara-dyuti*, "whose rays are not harsh", is the moon.

श्रीवासभूसुरवरेण भवत्कृपैषा
भक्तः क एष यदिदं स्वयमीश ऊचे ॥८०॥

*tac chṛṇvatātha jagade madhurair vacobhir*

*bhaktaḥ ka eṣa yad idaṁ svayam īśa ūce ||80||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — that; *śṛṇvatā* — by [him] hearing; *atha* — then; *jagade* — was addressed; *madhuraiḥ* — with sweet; *vacobhiḥ* — words; *bhītyā* — with fear; *ca* — and; *bhūri* — boundlessly; *karuṇaḥ* — merciful; *jagatī* — of the earth; *patiḥ* — the Lord; *saḥ* — that; *śrīvāsa* — by Srivasa; *bhūsura* — of the gods on earth (brahmanas); *vareṇa* — by the best; *bhavat* — Your; *kṛpā* — mercy; *eṣā* — this; *bhaktaḥ* — devotee; *kaḥ* — who; *eṣaḥ* — this; *yat* — that; *idam* — this; *svayam* — Himself; *īśaḥ* — the Lord; *ūce* — has said.

**80.** Hearing this, Srivasa, the best of brahmanas, then addressed that boundlessly merciful Lord of the earth with sweet words and with fear: "This is Your mercy! Who is this devotee, that the Lord Himself has said this [of him]?"

*Note.* Srivasa's remark is double-edged; it can also be understood as "Who is a devotee [by himself]? It is only Your mercy." *Īśa ūce* stands for *īśaḥ ūce*: the hiatus shows the nominative, "the Lord Himself has said", not the vocative *īśa* (which would give *īśoce*). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 81

रोषेण कम्पदशनच्छदनद्वयस्तं
श्रीवासपण्डितमुवाच दृढैर्वचोभिः ।
भक्तः किमुद्धव इहैनमृते मदीयः
किम्वा शुकस्तव यदेवमभून्मनीषा ॥८१॥

*roṣeṇa kampa-daśana-cchadana-dvayas taṁ*
*śrīvāsa-paṇḍitam uvāca dṛḍhair vacobhiḥ |*
*bhaktaḥ kim uddhava ihainam ṛte madīyaḥ*
*kiṁ vā śukas tava yad evam abhūn manīṣā ||81||*

*Word for word:* *roṣeṇa* — with anger; *kampa* — trembling; *daśana-cchadana* — of lips; *dvayaḥ* — [with] a pair; *tam* — to that; *śrīvāsa-paṇḍitam* — Srivasa Pandita; *uvāca* — said; *dṛḍhaiḥ* — with harsh; *vacobhiḥ* — words; *bhaktaḥ* — a devotee; *kim* — is there; *uddhavaḥ* — Uddhava; *iha* — here; *enam* — Him; *ṛte* — apart from; *madīyaḥ* — of Mine; *kim vā* — or; *śukaḥ* — Shuka; *tava* — your; *yat* — that; *evam* — such; *abhūt* — has arisen; *manīṣā* — opinion.

**81.** His two lips trembling with anger, He said to Srivasa Pandita in harsh words: "Is there here, apart from Him, any devotee of Mine — an Uddhava, or a Shuka — that you should have come to such an opinion?"

*Note.* The sense: Advaita is to the Lord what Uddhava and Shukadeva are; there is no other such here. *Daśana-cchada*, "the covering of the teeth", is the lip.

### Verse 82

अस्यां हि भारतभुवि प्रकटं किमन्यो-
ऽद्वैतं विनास्ति सकलामरसङ्घवन्द्यम् ।
मत्तुल्य एव तदयं ह्यवधारणीयो
नैवास्य कोऽपि भुवने सदृशोऽस्ति जातु ॥८२॥

*asyāṁ hi bhārata-bhuvi prakaṭaṁ kim anyo*
*'dvaitaṁ vināsti sakalāmara-saṅgha-vandyam |*
*mat-tulya eva tad ayaṁ hy avadhāraṇīyo*
*naivāsya ko 'pi bhuvane sadṛśo 'sti jātu ||82||*

*Word for word:* *asyām* — in this; *hi* — indeed; *bhārata* — of Bharata; *bhuvi* — in the land; *prakaṭam* — manifest; *kim* — is there; *anyaḥ* — another; *advaitam* — Advaita; *vinā* — apart from; *asti* — is; *sakala* — by all; *amara* — of the immortals; *saṅgha* — by the hosts; *vandyam* — worthy of homage; *mat* — to Me; *tulyaḥ* — equal; *eva* — indeed; *tat* — therefore; *ayam* — He; *hi* — indeed; *avadhāraṇīyaḥ* — must be regarded; *na eva* — not at all; *asya* — to Him; *kaḥ api* — anyone; *bhuvane* — in the world; *sadṛśaḥ* — similar; *asti* — is; *jātu* — ever.

**82.** "In this land of Bharata, is there manifest anyone apart from Advaita who is worthy of the homage of all the hosts of the immortals? Therefore He must be regarded as equal to Me; nowhere in the world is there ever anyone like Him."

### Verse 83

तूष्णीं बभूव तदयं वचनं निशम्य
तत्तत्तदा पुनरुवाच तथा कृपालुः ।
अध्यात्ममत्र न कदापि भवद्विधेन
जिह्वाग्रतोऽपि करणीयमिदं क्षणञ्च ॥८३॥

*tūṣṇīṁ babhūva tad ayaṁ vacanaṁ niśamya*
*tat tat tadā punar uvāca tathā kṛpāluḥ |*
*adhyātmam atra na kadāpi bhavad-vidhena*
*jihvāgrato 'pi karaṇīyam idaṁ kṣaṇañ ca ||83||*

*Word for word:* *tūṣṇīm* — silent; *babhūva* — became; *tat* — those; *ayam* — he; *vacanam* — words; *niśamya* — having heard; *tat tat* — this and that; *tadā* — then; *punaḥ* — again; *uvāca* — said; *tathā* — thus; *kṛpāluḥ* — the merciful; *adhyātmam* — "spiritual" [speculation]; *atra* — here; *na* — not; *kadāpi* — ever; *bhavat* — you; *vidhena* — by [one] like; *jihvā* — of the tongue; *agrataḥ* — with the tip; *api* — even; *karaṇīyam* — should be done; *idam* — this; *kṣaṇam* — for a moment; *ca* — and.

**83.** Hearing those words, he [Srivasa] fell silent. Then the merciful [Lord] again said this and that: "Here those like you must never, not even for a moment, engage in this 'spiritual' [speculation], even with the tip of the tongue.

### Verse 84

यद्युच्यते क्षणमपि प्रकटं कदापि
नो दास्यते परमदुर्लभभक्तियोगः ।
इत्युक्तवत्यथ विभौ मम विस्मृतिः स्या-
त्तस्मिंस्तथा कुरु तथेत्यवदन्महान्तः ॥८४॥

*yady ucyate kṣaṇam api prakaṭaṁ kadāpi*
*no dāsyate parama-durlabha-bhakti-yogaḥ |*
*ity uktavaty atha vibhau mama vismṛtiḥ syāt*
*tasmiṁs tathā kuru tathety avadan mahāntaḥ ||84||*

*Word for word:* *yadi* — if; *ucyate* — is uttered; *kṣaṇam api* — even for a moment; *prakaṭam* — aloud; *kadāpi* — ever; *na u* — not; *dāsyate* — will be granted; *parama* — supremely; *durlabha* — rare; *bhakti* — of devotion; *yogaḥ* — the yoga; *iti* — thus; *uktavati* — when [He] had spoken; *atha* — then; *vibhau* — the Almighty; *mama* — in me; *vismṛtiḥ* — forgetfulness; *syāt* — let there be; *tasmin* — of it; *tathā* — so; *kuru* — make; *tathā* — so; *iti* — thus; *avadan* — said; *mahāntaḥ* — the great [souls].

**84.** If it is ever uttered aloud even for a moment, the supremely rare bhakti-yoga will not be granted." When the Almighty had spoken thus, the great souls said: "Let me forget it — make it so, make it so!"

*Note.* *Mama vismṛtiḥ* — literally "let there be forgetfulness in me": each of them says it.

### Verse 85

ऊचे मुरारिरिदमीश्वर वेद्मि नैवा-
ध्यात्मं कदापि भगवन् करुणां विधेहि ।
जानासि तच्छ्रुतमिहास्ति मया पुरस्ता-
दित्येव तं पथि जगाद महाप्रभुः सः ॥८५॥

*ūce murārir idam īśvara vedmi naivā-*
*dhyātmaṁ kadāpi bhagavan karuṇāṁ vidhehi |*
*jānāsi tac chrutam ihāsti mayā purastād*
*ity eva taṁ pathi jagāda mahāprabhuḥ saḥ ||85||*

*Word for word:* *ūce* — said; *murāriḥ* — Murari; *idam* — this; *īśvara* — O Lord; *vedmi* — I know; *na eva* — not at all; *adhyātmam* — speculation on the higher Self; *kadāpi* — ever; *bhagavan* — O Bhagavan; *karuṇām* — mercy; *vidhehi* — show; *jānāsi* — you know; *tat* — that; *śrutam* — heard; *iha* — here; *asti* — has been; *mayā* — by Me; *purastāt* — before; *iti* — thus; *eva* — indeed; *tam* — to him; *pathi* — on the road; *jagāda* — said; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *saḥ* — He.

**85.** Murari said: "O Lord, I have never known any speculation on the higher Self at all! O Bhagavan, show mercy!" And Mahaprabhu said to him on the road: "You know it: I have heard it here before."

*Note.* The edition has *tat pathi*; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *taṁ pathi* ("to him on the road"), and so we read. Cf. verses 42–43, where the Lord rebukes Murari for his song on the higher Self.

### Verse 86

इत्थं निदाघसमयः स तदीयनृत्य-

शैत्यं स्वभावमवलम्ब्य चकार भूयः
स्निग्धं विचित्रमिदमत्र मनस्तडागम् ॥८६॥

*itthaṁ nidāgha-samayaḥ sa tadīya-nṛtya-*
*gītāmṛtena satataṁ sakale nṛ-loke |*
*śaityaṁ svabhāvam avalambya cakāra bhūyaḥ*
*snigdhaṁ vicitram idam atra manas-taḍāgam ||86||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *nidāgha* — summer; *samayaḥ* — season; *saḥ* — that; *tadīya* — His; *nṛtya* — of dancing; *gīta* — and of singing; *amṛtena* — by the nectar; *satatam* — constantly; *sakale* — in the whole; *nṛ* — of men; *loke* — in the world; *śaityam* — coolness; *svabhāvam* — as its nature; *avalambya* — having taken on; *cakāra* — made; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *snigdham* — full; *vicitram* — a wonder; *idam* — this; *atra* — here; *manaḥ* — of the mind; *taḍāgam* — the pond.

**86.** Thus, through the nectar of His dancing and singing, that summer season constantly took on coolness as its nature throughout the whole world of men and again made the pond of the mind full — a wonder, this!

*Note.* A paradox: the summer, which dries up ponds, here fills them.

*Word for word:* *sūkṣmeṇa* — with fine; *śubhra* — white; *vasanena* — cloth; *sukha* — comfort; *āvahena* — bringing; *kṛtvā* — having made; *śirasi* — on the head; *anupamām* — a peerless; *madhurām* — charming; *vibhūṣām* — ornament; *udyat* — gleaming; *su* — beautiful; *vidruma* — of corals; *manohara* — [with] a captivating; *hāra* — string; *kaṇṭhaḥ* — [whose] neck; *nṛtya* — of the dance; *udyame* — at the outset; *vijayate* — is victorious; *kanaka* — of gold; *adri* — as the mountain; *gauraḥ* — golden.

**87.** Having made on His head a peerless, charming ornament of fine, white, comfortable cloth, a captivating string of gleaming, beautiful corals on His neck, He, golden as the mountain of gold, is victorious as He sets about the dance.

*Note.* The ornament of cloth on the head is a turban. The mountain of gold is Meru.

**88.** With armlets, wristlets, gleaming bangles and the rest, which share in the special play of His two unrestrained arms, His spread fingers gleaming with golden rings, He, the bewilderer of Manmatha, is victorious as He sets about the dance.

*Word for word:* *pratyagra* — freshly; *phulla* — blossomed; *sarasīruha* — [like] lotuses; *ramya* — lovely; *pāṇiḥ* — [whose] hands; *kānti* — of radiance; *chaṭā* — of streams; *sravaṇa* — by the outpouring; *dīpita* — lighting up; *dik* — of the quarters; *samūhaḥ* — all; *vakṣaḥ-sthala* — of the chest; *dyuti* — by the splendour; *vinirjita* — surpassed; *meru* — of Meru; *śṛṅgaḥ* — [by whom] the peak; *nṛtyati* — dances; *asau* — He; *aviratam* — without pause; *madhura* — sweet; *adhara-oṣṭhaḥ* — [whose] lips.

*Word for word:* *cañcat* — swaying; *manorama* — charming; *dhaṭī* — of a loincloth; *paridhāna* — with the garment; *ramyaḥ* — beautiful; *tat-tat* — it; *bahiḥ* — over; *vilasatā* — with gleaming; *rasanena* — with the girdle; *kamraḥ* — lovely; *uddāma* — unrestrained; *nartaka* — of dancers; *ghaṭā* — of the host; *mukuṭa* — of the crown; *argha* — precious; *ratnam* — jewel; *lāsye* — in the dance; *vilāsa* — of play; *rasikaḥ* — a connoisseur; *madhuram* — sweetly; *cakāsti* — shines.

*Note.* *Dhaṭī* is a strip of cloth, a loincloth.

*śrīman-nitamba-paribimba-vilambi-rājad-*

*Word for word:* *śrīmat* — of the splendid; *nitamba* — of the hips; *paribimba* — over the round; *vilambi* — hanging down; *rājat* — gleaming; *uddāma* — freely swinging; *sārasana* — of the girdle; *vibhrama* — by the play; *citta* — hearts; *hārī* — stealing; *ūru* — of the thighs; *dvaya* — of the two; *uru* — broad; *pariṇāha* — of the round; *miṣeṇa* — under the guise; *cāru* — lovely; *sat* — well; *vṛtta* — rounded; *rāma-kadalī* — of *rāma-kadalī* banana trunks; *dvayam* — a pair; *eva* — as it were; *bibhrat* — bearing.

**91.** He steals hearts with the play of His gleaming, freely swinging girdle hanging down over the round of His splendid hips; and under the guise of the broad round of His two thighs He bears, as it were, a pair of lovely, well-rounded *rāma-kadalī* banana trunks.

*Note.* *Rāma-kadalī* is a variety of banana; the smooth banana trunk is the canonical image of the thigh in Indian poetry.

### Verse 92

*śrīmat-padāmbuja-yugaṁ vara-haṁsakādyair*

*Word for word:* *śrīmat* — splendid; *pada* — of the feet; *ambuja* — of the lotuses; *yugam* — the pair; *vara* — with excellent; *haṁsaka* — anklets; *ādyaiḥ* — and the rest; *udyat* — shining; *nakha* — of the nails; *indu-maṇi* — of the moonstones; *dīdhitibhiḥ* — with the rays; *praphullam* — blossoming; *bibhrat* — bearing; *vilāsa* — to play; *param* — given; *aṅka-talam* — lap; *ca* — and; *ramyam* — lovely; *nṛtya* — of the dance; *utsave* — at the festival; *vijayate* — is victorious; *druta* — molten; *hema* — as gold; *gauraḥ* — golden.

**92.** Bearing the pair of His splendid lotus feet, blossoming with excellent anklets and the rest and with the rays of His shining nails — moonstones — and a lovely lap given to play, He, golden as molten gold, is victorious at the festival of the dance.

*Note.* *Indu-maṇi* (moonstone) — the Lord's toenails. In the edition *परमङ्कतलं* is understood as *param aṅka-talam*.

### Verse 93

उद्यत्प्रवालरुचिरञ्जितपादमूलो

**93.** The soles of His feet tinged with the lustre of gleaming coral, moving over the earth with charming and sweet placing [of His steps], His radiance sweet, tender and lovely, He shone as He set about the dance, like beautiful Ananga, the bodiless, having taken a body.

### Verse 94

उद्यन्मृदङ्गकरतालकमन्दिराद्यै-

विप्राङ्गनागणमुखाम्बुरुहोद्गतेन
प्रोच्चैरुलूलुनिनदेन महान्महोऽभूत् ॥९४॥

*udyan-mṛdaṅga-kara-tālaka-mandirādyair*
*uccaiś carat-svara-puraḥsara-ramya-gītaiḥ |*
*viprāṅganā-gaṇa-mukhāmburuhodgatena*
*proccair ulūlu-ninadena mahān maho 'bhūt ||94||*

*Word for word:* *udyat* — resounding; *mṛdaṅga* — with mridangas; *kara-tālaka* — karatalas; *mandirā* — mandiras; *ādyaiḥ* — and the rest; *uccaiḥ* — loudly; *carat* — flowing; *svara* — by melodies; *puraḥsara* — led; *ramya* — with lovely; *gītaiḥ* — songs; *vipra* — of the brahmanas; *aṅganā* — of the wives; *gaṇa* — of the host; *mukha* — of the faces; *amburuha* — from the lotuses; *udgatena* — rising; *pra-uccaiḥ* — very loud; *ulūlu* — "ulu-ulu"; *ninadena* — with the cry; *mahān* — a great; *mahaḥ* — festival; *abhūt* — there was.

**94.** With resounding mridangas, karatalas, mandiras and the rest, with lovely songs led by loudly flowing melodies, with the very loud cry of "ulu-ulu" rising from the lotus faces of the host of brahmanas' wives, there was a great festival.

*Note.* The *mridanga* is the clay drum of kirtana; *karatalas* are hand cymbals.

### Verse 95

पुंस्कोकिलस्वरमनोहरकण्ठनादाः
सन्मन्दिरायुगविभूषितपाणिपद्माः ।
उच्चैर्जगुः सपदि नृत्यमवेक्ष्य तस्य
हृष्टाः प्रमोदमधुरं पुलकाकुलाङ्गाः ॥९५॥

*puṁs-kokila-svara-manohara-kaṇṭha-nādāḥ*
*san-mandirā-yuga-vibhūṣita-pāṇi-padmāḥ |*
*uccair jaguḥ sapadi nṛtyam avekṣya tasya*
*hṛṣṭāḥ pramoda-madhuraṁ pulakākulāṅgāḥ ||95||*

*Word for word:* *puṁs* — male; *kokila* — of the cuckoo; *svara* — [like] the voice; *manohara* — captivating; *kaṇṭha* — of the throat; *nādāḥ* — [whose] sounds; *sat* — fine; *mandirā* — of mandiras; *yuga* — with pairs; *vibhūṣita* — adorned; *pāṇi* — of the hands; *padmāḥ* — [whose] lotuses; *uccaiḥ* — loudly; *jaguḥ* — sang; *sapadi* — at once; *nṛtyam* — the dance; *avekṣya* — seeing; *tasya* — His; *hṛṣṭāḥ* — joyful; *pramoda* — with delight; *madhuram* — sweetly; *pulaka* — with bristling hairs; *ākula* — covered; *aṅgāḥ* — [whose] bodies.

**95.** With voices as captivating as the call of the male cuckoo, their lotus hands adorned with pairs of fine mandiras, they [the brahmanas' wives], seeing His dance, at once joyfully sang aloud, sweet with delight, their bodies covered with bristling hairs.

*Note.* The subject is the brahmanas' wives of verse 94. The *kokila* is the Indian cuckoo, whose voice is an image of sweet singing.

### Verse 96

रोमाञ्चसञ्चिततनुर्गलदश्रुधारा-
धौतः श्रमाम्बुलहरीपरिमिश्रिताङ्गः ।
भावैरथाष्टभिरशेषरसेन नाथः
प्रोद्दामनर्त्तनघटामुकुटार्घरत्नम् ॥९६॥

*romāñca-sañcita-tanur galad-aśru-dhārā-*
*dhautaḥ śramāmbu-laharī-parimiśritāṅgaḥ |*
*bhāvair athāṣṭabhir aśeṣa-rasena nāthaḥ*
*proddāma-nartana-ghaṭā-mukuṭārgha-ratnam ||96||*

*Word for word:* *romāñca* — with bristling hairs; *sañcita* — covered; *tanuḥ* — [whose] body; *galat* — of falling; *aśru* — tears; *dhārā* — by streams; *dhautaḥ* — washed; *śrama* — of fatigue; *ambu* — of the water (sweat); *laharī* — with waves; *parimiśrita* — drenched; *aṅgaḥ* — [whose] limbs; *bhāvaiḥ* — with the states of ecstasy; *atha* — and; *aṣṭabhiḥ* — eight; *aśeṣa* — complete; *rasena* — with rapture; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *pra-uddāma* — unrestrained; *nartana* — of dance[rs]; *ghaṭā* — of the host; *mukuṭa* — of the crown; *argha* — precious; *ratnam* — jewel.

**96.** His body covered with bristling hairs, washed by streams of falling tears, His limbs drenched with waves of sweat, with the eight states of ecstasy and with complete rapture, the Lord — the precious jewel in the crown of the host of unrestrained dancers —

*Note.* Verses 96–97 are a *yugmaka* (marked as a pair in the edition). The eight states are the *aṣṭa-sāttvika-bhāvas*: stupefaction, perspiration, bristling of the hairs, faltering of the voice, trembling, change of colour, tears and fainting. The text has *nartana* ("dance") where verse 90 has *nartaka* ("dancer"); we translate as in verse 90.

### Verse 97

उद्दामनिश्वसितमारुतवेपमान-
रक्ताधरद्वितयपल्लवकान्तिकम्रः ।
दन्तांशुधौतदशनच्छदभिन्नकान्ति-
कान्तो रराज नटनेन विलासभाजा ॥९७॥

*uddāma-niśvasita-māruta-vepamāna-*
*raktādhara-dvitaya-pallava-kānti-kamraḥ |*
*dantāṁśu-dhauta-daśana-cchada-bhinna-kānti-*
*kānto rarāja naṭanena vilāsa-bhājā ||97||*

*Word for word:* *uddāma* — vehement; *niśvasita* — of breathing; *māruta* — by the wind; *vepamāna* — trembling; *rakta* — red; *adhara* — of lips; *dvitaya* — of the pair; *pallava* — of the young shoots; *kānti* — with the lustre; *kamraḥ* — lovely; *danta* — of the teeth; *aṁśu* — by the rays; *dhauta* — washed; *daśana-cchada* — of the lips; *bhinna* — varied; *kānti* — by the lustre; *kāntaḥ* — charming; *rarāja* — shone; *naṭanena* — with a dance; *vilāsa* — of play; *bhājā* — full.

**97.** — lovely with the lustre of the pair of His red lips, like young shoots trembling in the wind of His vehement breathing, charming with the varied lustre of His lips washed by the rays of His teeth — shone with a dance full of play.

### Verse 98

इत्थं विधाय नटनं नवकम्बलेन
रम्ये वरासनतले पटुविभ्रमाढ्यः ।
तत्रोपविश्य विशदे मधुरं जगाद
श्रीवासपण्डितमतीव सुभागधेयम् ॥९८॥

*itthaṁ vidhāya naṭanaṁ nava-kambalena*
*ramye varāsana-tale paṭu-vibhramāḍhyaḥ |*
*tatropaviśya viśade madhuraṁ jagāda*
*śrīvāsa-paṇḍitam atīva su-bhāgadheyam ||98||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *vidhāya* — having performed; *naṭanam* — the dance; *nava* — with a new; *kambalena* — blanket; *ramye* — lovely; *vara* — excellent; *āsana* — of a seat; *tale* — on the surface; *paṭu* — skilful; *vibhrama* — in playfulness; *āḍhyaḥ* — rich; *tatra* — there; *upaviśya* — having sat down; *viśade* — on a clean; *madhuram* — sweetly; *jagāda* — spoke; *śrīvāsa-paṇḍitam* — to Srivasa Pandita; *atīva* — exceedingly; *su* — good; *bhāgadheyam* — [endowed with] fortune.

**98.** Having danced thus, He, rich in skilful playfulness, sat down there on a clean, excellent seat made lovely by a new blanket, and sweetly spoke to the exceedingly fortunate Srivasa Pandita:

### Verse 99

श्रीर्विष्णुभक्तिरियमेव भवानमुष्या
वासः स्थितिस्त्वयि विराजति विष्णुभक्तिः ।
श्रीवास इत्यधिकृतो मधुरेण नाम्ना
पश्चान्मुरारिमवदत् कवितां पठेति ॥९९॥

*śrīr viṣṇu-bhaktir iyam eva bhavān amuṣyā*
*vāsaḥ sthitis tvayi virājati viṣṇu-bhaktiḥ |*
*śrīvāsa ity adhikṛto madhureṇa nāmnā*
*paścān murārim avadat kavitāṁ paṭheti ||99||*

*Word for word:* *śrīḥ* — Sri; *viṣṇu* — to Vishnu; *bhaktiḥ* — devotion; *iyam* — this; *eva* — just; *bhavān* — you; *amuṣyāḥ* — of it; *vāsaḥ* — the abode; *sthitiḥ* — the dwelling; *tvayi* — in you; *virājati* — shines; *viṣṇu* — to Vishnu; *bhaktiḥ* — devotion; *śrīvāsaḥ* — Srivasa; *iti* — thus; *adhikṛtaḥ* — invested; *madhureṇa* — with the sweet; *nāmnā* — name; *paścāt* — afterwards; *murārim* — to Murari; *avadat* — He said; *kavitām* — poetry; *paṭha* — recite; *iti* — thus.

**99.** "'Sri' is just this — devotion to Vishnu; and you are its abode (*vāsa*), its dwelling: devotion to Vishnu shines in you. [So] you are invested with the sweet name 'Srivasa'." Afterwards He said to Murari: "Recite [your] poetry!"

*Note.* The etymology of the name: *śrī* (here *viṣṇu-bhakti*) + *vāsa* ("abode").

### Verse 100

सोऽयं पपाठ कवितां स्वकृतामनेकां
श्रीराघवेन्द्रगुणरूपविलासगाथाम् ।
इत्थं निशम्य रघुनन्दनराजसिंह-
श्लोकाष्टकं पदमधात्तदमुष्य मूर्द्धनि ॥१००॥

*so 'yaṁ papāṭha kavitāṁ sva-kṛtām anekāṁ*
*śrī-rāghavendra-guṇa-rūpa-vilāsa-gāthām |*
*itthaṁ niśamya raghunandana-rāja-siṁha-*
*ślokāṣṭakaṁ padam adhāt tad amuṣya mūrdhani ||100||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ ayam* — he; *papāṭha* — recited; *kavitām* — poetry; *sva* — by himself; *kṛtām* — composed; *anekām* — many; *śrī-rāghava-indra* — of Sri Raghavendra, the lord of the Raghus; *guṇa* — the qualities; *rūpa* — form; *vilāsa* — pastimes; *gāthām* — singing of; *ittham* — thus; *niśamya* — having heard; *raghunandana* — on Raghunandana; *rāja-siṁha* — the lion among kings; *śloka* — of verses; *aṣṭakam* — the set of eight; *padam* — [His] foot; *adhāt* — placed; *tat* — then; *amuṣya* — his; *mūrdhani* — on the head.

**100.** And he recited many poems of his own composition, singing of the qualities, form and pastimes of Sri Raghavendra. Having thus heard the eight verses on Raghunandana, the lion among kings, [the Lord] then placed His foot on his head.

*Note.* Murari Gupta is a devotee of Rama (cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 15.137–157). He himself described his "Ramashtaka" and this blessing in the *Kadacha* (Murari 2.7.6–18); according to the Chaitanya-charitamrita, the Lord called him "Ramadasa". The fourth line has a syllable too many: the metre requires *mūrdhni* (*मूर्द्ध्नि*) for *मूर्द्धनि* (?).

### Verse 101

त्वं 'रामदास' इति भो भव मत्प्रसादा-
द्भाले लिलेख चतुरक्षरमेतदेव ।
पश्चात् पपाठ मधुरं मधुराकृतिः स
श्लोकं महाप्रभुरतीव कृपासमुद्रः ॥१०१॥

*tvaṁ 'rāmadāsa' iti bho bhava mat-prasādād*
*bhāle lilekha catur-akṣaram etad eva |*
*paścāt papāṭha madhuraṁ madhurākṛtiḥ sa*
*ślokaṁ mahāprabhur atīva kṛpā-samudraḥ ||101||*

*Word for word:* *tvam* — you; *rāmadāsaḥ* — Ramadasa; *iti* — thus; *bhoḥ* — O [Murari]; *bhava* — be; *mat* — My; *prasādāt* — by the grace; *bhāle* — on the forehead; *lilekha* — He wrote; *catuḥ* — of four; *akṣaram* — syllables [the word]; *etat* — this; *eva* — very; *paścāt* — then; *papāṭha* — recited; *madhuram* — sweetly; *madhura* — charming; *ākṛtiḥ* — in form; *saḥ* — He; *ślokam* — a verse; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *atīva* — boundless; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *samudraḥ* — the ocean.

**101.** "O [Murari], by My grace be you 'Ramadasa'!" — and He wrote on his forehead this very word of four syllables. Then Mahaprabhu, charming in form, the boundless ocean of mercy, sweetly recited a verse:

*Note.* *Rā-ma-dā-sa* — four syllables; "Ramadasa" means "servant of Rama". Murari is a devotee of Rama (cf. verse 100).

न साधयति मां योगो न सांख्यं धर्म उद्धव ।
न स्वाध्यायस्तपस्त्यागो यथा भक्तिर्ममोर्जिता ॥

*na sādhayati māṁ yogo na sāṅkhyaṁ dharma uddhava |*
*na svādhyāyas tapas tyāgo yathā bhaktir mamorjitā ||*

*Word for word:* *na* — not; *sādhayati* — wins over; *mām* — Me; *yogaḥ* — yoga; *na* — not; *sāṅkhyam* — Sankhya; *dharmaḥ* — dharma; *uddhava* — O Uddhava; *na* — not; *svādhyāyaḥ* — study of the Vedas; *tapaḥ* — austerity; *tyāgaḥ* — renunciation; *yathā* — as; *bhaktiḥ* — devotion; *mama* — to Me; *ūrjitā* — grown strong.

"Neither yoga nor Sankhya nor dharma, O Uddhava, neither study of the Vedas nor austerity nor renunciation wins Me over as does devotion to Me that has grown strong."

*Note.* The metre is *anuṣṭubh*. Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.14.20. Unnumbered in the edition.

### Verse 102

इत्थं पपाठ मधुरं तत आगतांस्ता-

श्रीवास एव वदतीह यदा यथा वै
कर्त्तव्यमेतदधुना नियतं भवद्भिः ॥१०२॥

*itthaṁ papāṭha madhuraṁ tata āgatāṁs tān*
*ūce dvijān dvija-mayūkha-samāplutoṣṭhaḥ |*
*śrīvāsa eva vadatīha yadā yathā vai*
*kartavyam etad adhunā niyataṁ bhavadbhiḥ ||102||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *papāṭha* — having recited; *madhuram* — sweetly; *tataḥ* — then; *āgatān* — who had come; *tān* — to those; *ūce* — said; *dvijān* — to the brahmanas; *dvija* — of the teeth; *mayūkha* — by the rays; *samāpluta* — bathed; *oṣṭhaḥ* — [He] whose lips; *śrīvāsaḥ* — Srivasa; *eva* — just; *vadati* — says; *iha* — here; *yadā* — when; *yathā* — how; *vai* — indeed; *kartavyam* — must be done; *etat* — that; *adhunā* — from now on; *niyatam* — strictly; *bhavadbhiḥ* — by you.

**102.** Having thus sweetly recited [the verse], He, His lips bathed in the rays of His teeth, then said to the brahmanas who had come: "Whatever Srivasa says here — when and how he says it — that from now on you must strictly do."

*Note.* A play on words: *dvija* is "twice-born" (a brahmana) and "tooth" (which is born twice).

### Verse 103

श्रीरामपण्डितमथाह सदैव कार्य्यं

*itthaṁ vadan sa ruruce rucirānanenduḥ ||103||*

*Word for word:* *śrīrāma-paṇḍitam* — to Sri Rama Pandita; *atha* — then; *āha* — said; *sadā eva* — always; *kāryam* — should be done; *jyeṣṭhasya* — to the elder [brother]; *sevanam* — service; *idam* — this; *hi* — for; *mama* — to Me; *eva* — itself; *sevā* — service; *etena* — by this; *te* — for you; *sakalam* — everything; *eva* — indeed; *śivāya* — for good; *bhūyāt* — may be; *ittham* — thus; *vadan* — speaking; *saḥ* — He; *ruruce* — shone; *rucira* — beautiful; *ānana* — of [His] face; *induḥ* — [with] the moon.

**103.** Then He said to Sri Rama Pandita: "Always render this service to your elder brother, for it is service to Me Myself. By this may everything turn out for your good." Speaking thus, He shone, the moon of His face beautiful.

*śrīvāsa-paṇḍita-samarpita-dugdha-pūga-*
