*Word for word:* *śrīvāsa-paṇḍita* — by Srivasa Pandita; *samarpita* — offered; *dugdha* — the milk; *pūga* — the betel nuts; *mālyāni* — the garlands; *tatra* — there; *saḥ* — He; *niṣevya* — having partaken of; *tataḥ* — then; *avaśeṣam* — the remnants; *tebhyaḥ* — to those; *prasāda* — with grace; *sumukhaḥ* — gracious of face; *nija* — of His own; *pāda* — feet; *padma* — lotus; *bhaktebhyaḥ* — to the devotees; *eva* — indeed; *bhagavān* — Bhagavan; *pradadau* — gave; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *abdhiḥ* — the ocean.

**104.** Having partaken there of the milk, betel nuts and garlands offered by Srivasa Pandita, Bhagavan, the ocean of mercy, His face gracious with kindness, then gave the remnants to those devotees of His lotus feet.

### Verse 105

इत्थं निनाय सकलां स निशां निशेश-
कोटिप्रकाशमधुराननचन्द्रबिम्बः ।
उद्याति तिग्मकिरणेऽथ महाप्रभुं तं
संनम्य वेश्मनि यथातथमीयुरेते ॥१०५॥

*itthaṁ nināya sakalāṁ sa niśāṁ niśeśa-*
*koṭi-prakāśa-madhurānana-candra-bimbaḥ |*
*udyāti tigma-kiraṇe 'tha mahāprabhuṁ taṁ*
*saṁnamya veśmani yathā-tatham īyur ete ||105||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *nināya* — spent; *sakalām* — the whole; *saḥ* — He; *niśām* — night; *niśā-īśa* — of moons; *koṭi* — of millions; *prakāśa* — with the radiance; *madhura* — of [His] sweet; *ānana* — face; *candra* — of the moon; *bimbaḥ* — [He whose] disc; *udyāti* — as [it] rose; *tigma* — the hot-; *kiraṇe* — rayed [sun]; *atha* — then; *mahāprabhum* — to Mahaprabhu; *tam* — to Him; *saṁnamya* — having bowed; *veśmani* — home; *yathā-tatham* — each to his own; *īyuḥ* — went; *ete* — they.

**105.** Thus He spent the whole night — He, the moon-disc of whose sweet face shines with the radiance of millions of moons. And when the hot-rayed [sun] rose, they bowed to Mahaprabhu and went home, each to his own.

### Verse 106

भूयश्च देवतटिनीप्लवनेन मुग्धाः
संपूज्य देवसदनाच्च यथायथं ते ।
आजग्मुरस्य पदपङ्कजदर्शनार्थं
तन्मात्रजीवनमहौषधयो महान्तः ॥१०६॥

*bhūyaś ca deva-taṭinī-plavanena mugdhāḥ*
*saṁpūjya deva-sadanāc ca yathā-yathaṁ te |*
*ājagmur asya pada-paṅkaja-darśanārthaṁ*
*tan-mātra-jīvana-mahauṣadhayo mahāntaḥ ||106||*

*Word for word:* *bhūyaḥ* — again; *ca* — and; *deva* — divine; *taṭinī* — in the river; *plavanena* — by bathing; *mugdhāḥ* — made lovely; *saṁpūjya* — having worshipped; *deva* — of the Deity; *sadanāt* — from the shrine; *ca* — and; *yathā-yatham* — each in his turn; *te* — they; *ājagmuḥ* — came; *asya* — His; *pada* — feet; *paṅkaja* — lotus; *darśana* — of seeing; *artham* — for the sake; *tat* — He; *mātra* — alone; *jīvana* — of life; *mahā* — the great; *auṣadhayaḥ* — [for whom is] remedy; *mahāntaḥ* — the great souls.

**106.** And then those great souls, for whom He alone is the great remedy of life, made lovely by bathing in the divine river and having performed worship, came each in his turn from the shrine of the Deity, again to see His lotus feet.

*Note.* The divine river is the Ganga.

### Verse 107

दृष्ट्वा महाप्रभुरथैष समागतांस्ता-
नूचे पयोधरगभीररवः सुधीरम् ।
अत्रागतोऽस्ति मतिमानवधूतनित्या-
नन्दः श्रुतं कथममुष्य विलोकनं स्यात् ॥१०७॥

*dṛṣṭvā mahāprabhur athaiṣa samāgatāṁs tān*
*ūce payodhara-gabhīra-ravaḥ sudhīram |*
*atrāgato 'sti matimān avadhūta-nityā-*
*nandaḥ śrutaṁ katham amuṣya vilokanaṁ syāt ||107||*

*Word for word:* *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *atha* — then; *eṣaḥ* — He; *samāgatān* — assembled; *tān* — them; *ūce* — said; *payodhara* — like a cloud's; *gabhīra* — deep; *ravaḥ* — [with] a voice; *sudhīram* — very steadily; *atra* — here; *āgataḥ asti* — has come; *matimān* — the wise; *avadhūta* — avadhuta; *nityānandaḥ* — Nityananda; *śrutam* — [have you] heard; *katham* — how; *amuṣya* — of Him; *vilokanam* — a sight; *syāt* — could be.

**107.** Then Mahaprabhu, seeing them assembled, said very steadily, in a voice deep as a cloud's: "The wise avadhuta Nityananda has come here. Have you heard? How could we see Him?"

*Note.* An *avadhūta* is a wandering ascetic who has "shaken off" all conventions. The beginning of the episode of the meeting with Nityananda (Chaitanya-bhagavata, Madhya 3–4; Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 17.11).

### Verse 108

हे रामपण्डित मुकुन्द मुरारिगुप्त
नारायण द्रुतमितस्त्वरितं प्रयात ।
अत्रास्ति स प्रचुरभाग्यभरो महात्मा
गत्वा समानयत तं महितानुभावम् ॥१०८॥

*he rāma-paṇḍita mukunda murāri-gupta*
*nārāyaṇa drutam itas tvaritaṁ prayāta |*
*atrāsti sa pracura-bhāgya-bharo mahātmā*
*gatvā samānayata taṁ mahitānubhāvam ||108||*

*Word for word:* *he* — O; *rāma-paṇḍita* — Rama Pandita; *mukunda* — O Mukunda; *murāri-gupta* — O Murari Gupta; *nārāyaṇa* — O Narayana; *drutam* — quickly; *itaḥ* — from here; *tvaritam* — in haste; *prayāta* — set out; *atra* — here; *asti* — is; *saḥ* — that; *pracura* — of abundant; *bhāgya* — fortune; *bharaḥ* — full; *mahātmā* — great soul; *gatvā* — having gone; *samānayata* — bring; *tam* — Him; *mahita* — glorious; *anubhāvam* — in majesty.

**108.** "O Rama Pandita, Mukunda, Murari Gupta, Narayana! Quickly, set out from here in haste: that great soul, full of abundant fortune, is here. Go and bring Him, glorious in His majesty!"

*Note.* Narayana is probably the same "foremost of physicians" as in verse 44.

### Verse 109

आज्ञापिता इति महाप्रभुना ततस्ते
गत्वा भृशं पथि विचार्य न तं विलोक्य ।
भूयः समेत्य च विलोकित एष नैव
कुत्रापि किं बत विधेयमितीदमूचुः ॥१०९॥

*ājñāpitā iti mahāprabhunā tatas te*
*gatvā bhṛśaṁ pathi vicārya na taṁ vilokya |*
*bhūyaḥ sametya ca vilokita eṣa naiva*
*kutrāpi kiṁ bata vidheyam itīdam ūcuḥ ||109||*

*Word for word:* *ājñāpitāḥ* — commanded; *iti* — thus; *mahāprabhunā* — by Mahaprabhu; *tataḥ* — then; *te* — they; *gatvā* — having gone; *bhṛśam* — thoroughly; *pathi* — along the roads; *vicārya* — having searched; *na* — not; *tam* — Him; *vilokya* — seeing; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *sametya* — having come together; *ca* — and; *vilokitaḥ* — seen; *eṣaḥ* — He; *na eva* — not at all; *kutra api* — anywhere; *kim* — what; *bata* — alas; *vidheyam* — is to be done; *iti* — thus; *idam* — this; *ūcuḥ* — they said.

**109.** Thus commanded by Mahaprabhu, they went and searched the roads thoroughly, but did not see Him. Coming back together, they said: "He is not to be seen anywhere at all. Alas, what is to be done?"

### Verse 110

भूयस्तथाह भगवानधुना न दृश्यः
सोऽयं भवद्भिरिह सायमवेक्षितव्यः ।
स्वान् स्वान् गृहान् सपदि गच्छत तत्तदानी-
मत्रागमिष्यथ तथेति ययुर्गृहं ते ॥११०॥

*bhūyas tathāha bhagavān adhunā na dṛśyaḥ*
*so 'yaṁ bhavadbhir iha sāyam avekṣitavyaḥ |*
*svān svān gṛhān sapadi gacchata tat tadānīm*
*atrāgamiṣyatha tatheti yayur gṛhaṁ te ||110||*

*Word for word:* *bhūyaḥ* — again; *tathā* — thus; *āha* — said; *bhagavān* — Bhagavan; *adhunā* — now; *na* — not; *dṛśyaḥ* — to be seen; *saḥ ayam* — He; *bhavadbhiḥ* — by you; *iha* — here; *sāyam* — in the evening; *avekṣitavyaḥ* — will be seen; *svān svān* — each to his own; *gṛhān* — homes; *sapadi* — now; *gacchata* — go; *tat* — therefore; *tadānīm* — then; *atra* — here; *āgamiṣyatha* — you will come; *tathā* — very well; *iti* — thus; *yayuḥ* — went; *gṛham* — home; *te* — they.

**110.** Then Bhagavan said again: "Now He is not to be seen; you will see Him here in the evening. So go now each to your own home, and then come here." "Very well," [they said,] and went home.

### Verse 111

सायं ततः पथि चलन् सह तैः कृपालु-
र्वैद्यं मुरारिमवलोक्य जगाद धीरम् ।
आचार्य्यनन्दनगृहेऽस्ति हि सोऽवधूत-
स्तत्र प्रयाहि चपलं तमिहानयेति ॥१११॥

*sāyaṁ tataḥ pathi calan saha taiḥ kṛpālur*
*vaidyaṁ murārim avalokya jagāda dhīram |*
*ācārya-nandana-gṛhe 'sti hi so 'vadhūtas*
*tatra prayāhi capalaṁ tam ihānayeti ||111||*

*Word for word:* *sāyam* — in the evening; *tataḥ* — then; *pathi* — along the road; *calan* — walking; *saha* — with; *taiḥ* — them; *kṛpāluḥ* — the merciful [Lord]; *vaidyam* — the physician; *murārim* — Murari; *avalokya* — seeing; *jagāda* — said; *dhīram* — calmly; *ācārya-nandana* — of Nandana Acharya; *gṛhe* — in the house; *asti* — is; *hi* — indeed; *saḥ* — that; *avadhūtaḥ* — avadhuta; *tatra* — there; *prayāhi* — go; *capalam* — quickly; *tam* — Him; *iha* — here; *ānaya* — bring; *iti* — thus.

**111.** Then in the evening, walking along the road with them, the merciful [Lord] saw the physician Murari and calmly said: "That avadhuta is in the house of Nandana Acharya. Go there quickly and bring Him here."

*Note.* In the Chaitanya-bhagavata (Madhya 3), Nityananda, on arriving in Navadvipa, stayed in the house of Nandana Acharya.

### Verse 112

इत्थं स तत्र समुपेत्य ददर्श नित्या-
नन्दं प्रभुं च समलोकयदेष साक्षात् ।
आनम्य तं मधुरमाह सुधांशुकम्रः
काक्वा नयेन विनयेन कृपारसाब्धिः ॥११२॥

*itthaṁ sa tatra samupetya dadarśa nityā-*
*nandaṁ prabhuṁ ca samalokayad eṣa sākṣāt |*
*ānamya taṁ madhuram āha sudhāṁśu-kamraḥ*
*kākvā nayena vinayena kṛpā-rasābdhiḥ ||112||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *saḥ* — He; *tatra* — there; *samupetya* — having come; *dadarśa* — saw; *nityānandam* — Nityananda; *prabhum* — the Lord; *ca* — and; *samalokayat* — beheld; *eṣaḥ* — He [Nityananda]; *sākṣāt* — face to face; *ānamya* — having bowed; *tam* — to Him; *madhuram* — sweetly; *āha* — said; *sudhāṁśu* — than the moon; *kamraḥ* — lovelier; *kākvā* — with a modulated voice; *nayena* — courteously; *vinayena* — with humility; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *rasa* — of the nectar; *abdhiḥ* — the ocean.

**112.** Thus He came there and saw Nityananda, and Nityananda beheld the Lord face to face. And, bowing to Him, [the Lord] — lovelier than the moon, the ocean of the nectar of mercy — spoke sweetly, courteously and humbly, His voice modulated with feeling:

*Note.* After the second line the edition gives a variant in parentheses, *(पश्चात्)* — probably for *sākṣāt*. *Kāku* is a modulation of the voice that expresses feeling.

### Verse 113

त्वं भूतलेऽतुलमहामहिमार्णवोऽसि
संसारसागरविशोषणमातनोषि ।
निःशेषदेहिकुलनन्दथुमेव कुर्व्वन्
पाषण्डिनां हृदयमाकुलयस्यशेषम् ॥११३॥

*tvaṁ bhūtale 'tula-mahā-mahimārṇavo 'si*
*saṁsāra-sāgara-viśoṣaṇam ātanoṣi |*
*niḥśeṣa-dehi-kula-nandathum eva kurvan*
*pāṣaṇḍināṁ hṛdayam ākulayasy aśeṣam ||113||*

*Word for word:* *tvam* — You; *bhū-tale* — on earth; *atula* — of incomparable; *mahā* — great; *mahima* — glory; *arṇavaḥ* — an ocean; *asi* — are; *saṁsāra* — of samsara; *sāgara* — of the ocean; *viśoṣaṇam* — the drying up; *ātanoṣi* — You accomplish; *niḥśeṣa* — of all; *dehi* — embodied beings; *kula* — of the races; *nandathum* — joy; *eva* — indeed; *kurvan* — bringing about; *pāṣaṇḍinām* — of the godless; *hṛdayam* — the heart; *ākulayasi* — You throw into turmoil; *aśeṣam* — utterly.

**113.** "On earth You are an ocean of incomparable, great glory — [and yet] You dry up the ocean of samsara. Bringing joy to all the races of embodied beings, You utterly throw into turmoil the hearts of the godless.

*Note.* A paradox: an ocean that dries up an ocean.

### Verse 114

त्वं त्यक्तलोकनिचयोऽपि समस्तलोक-
सम्यक्श्रिताङ्घ्रिकमलद्वय एव नित्यम् ।
वैराग्यमाश्रयसि सन्ततमेव लोके
रागो महान् प्रविरतः खलु लक्ष्यतेऽसौ ॥११४॥

*tvaṁ tyakta-loka-nicayo 'pi samasta-loka-*
*samyak-śritāṅghri-kamala-dvaya eva nityam |*
*vairāgyam āśrayasi santatam eva loke*
*rāgo mahān pravirataḥ khalu lakṣyate 'sau ||114||*

*Word for word:* *tvam* — You; *tyakta* — who have abandoned; *loka* — of people; *nicayaḥ* — the multitude; *api* — although; *samasta* — by all; *loka* — people; *samyak* — wholly; *śrita* — resorted to; *aṅghri* — of feet; *kamala* — lotus; *dvayaḥ* — [You] whose pair; *eva* — indeed; *nityam* — always; *vairāgyam* — detachment; *āśrayasi* — You take refuge in; *santatam* — constantly; *eva* — indeed; *loke* — in the world; *rāgaḥ* — passion (love); *mahān* — great; *pravirataḥ* — unceasing (lit. "ceased"); *khalu* — yet; *lakṣyate* — is seen; *asau* — this.

**114.** "Though You have abandoned the multitude of people, the pair of Your lotus feet is always wholly the refuge of all people. In this world You constantly take refuge in detachment — and yet a great, unceasing love is seen [in You]."

*Note.* The figure *virodhābhāsa* ("apparent contradiction"): *vairāgya* is "detachment", literally "absence of *rāga*", and at the same time a great *rāga* (love for Krishna) is seen. *Pravirata* (literally "ceased") is unclear here; perhaps another play on words. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 115

इत्यूचिवान् सह निजाङ्घ्रिसरोजभक्तैः
सङ्कीर्त्तनं समकरोन्नटनञ्च भूयः ।
तत्रावधूतपदधूलिभिरात्मलोक-
शीर्षं चकार परिपूततमं परं सः ॥११५॥

*ity ūcivān saha nijāṅghri-saroja-bhaktaiḥ*
*saṅkīrtanaṁ samakaron naṭanañ ca bhūyaḥ |*
*tatrāvadhūta-pada-dhūlibhir ātma-loka-*
*śīrṣaṁ cakāra paripūtatamaṁ paraṁ saḥ ||115||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *ūcivān* — having spoken; *saha* — together with; *nija* — His own; *aṅghri* — feet; *saroja* — lotus; *bhaktaiḥ* — with the devotees; *saṅkīrtanam* — sankirtana; *samakarot* — performed; *naṭanam* — dancing; *ca* — and; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *tatra* — there; *avadhūta* — of the avadhuta; *pada* — feet; *dhūlibhiḥ* — with the dust; *ātma* — of His own; *loka* — people; *śīrṣam* — the heads; *cakāra* — made; *paripūtatamam* — most purified; *param* — utterly; *saḥ* — He.

**115.** Having spoken thus, He again performed sankirtana and dancing together with the devotees of His lotus feet; and there, with the dust of the avadhuta's feet, He made the heads of His own people utterly, supremely pure.

### Verse 116

इत्थं व्रजन् पथि शचीतनयः स तैस्तै-
स्तस्यावधूतपरमस्य कथां जगाद ।
ज्ञानं पुरो भवति भक्तिरथो विरक्ति-
रित्थं वदत्ययमतः परमोऽयमेव ॥११६॥

*itthaṁ vrajan pathi śacī-tanayaḥ sa tais tais*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *vrajan* — going; *pathi* — along the road; *śacī* — of Shachi; *tanayaḥ* — the son; *saḥ* — He; *taiḥ taiḥ* — with those [devotees]; *tasya* — about that; *avadhūta* — avadhuta; *paramasya* — supreme; *kathām* — a talk; *jagāda* — spoke; *jñānam* — knowledge; *puraḥ* — first; *bhavati* — is; *bhaktiḥ* — devotion; *atho* — then; *viraktiḥ* — detachment; *ittham* — thus; *vadati* — declares; *ayam* — He; *ataḥ* — therefore; *paramaḥ* — supreme; *ayam* — He; *eva* — indeed.

**116.** Going thus along the road with those [devotees], the son of Shachi spoke about that supreme avadhuta: "First comes knowledge, then devotion, then detachment — so He [Himself, by His life,] declares. Therefore He indeed is supreme."

*Note.* The sense of the second half is unclear. Cf. Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.2.42: *bhaktiḥ pareśānubhavo viraktiḥ*. In the edition this verse is mistakenly numbered "117" (the next one is also numbered 117). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 117

इत्थं विचिन्त्य करुणाब्धिरथापरेद्यु-

सद्भोजितं तदनु चन्दनकुङ्कुमाद्यैः
प्रत्यङ्गमेवमनुलिप्य ननन्द नाथः ॥११७॥

*itthaṁ vicintya karuṇābdhir athāparedyur*
*bhikṣārtham asya niyataṁ nirato babhūva |*
*sad-bhojitaṁ tad-anu candana-kuṅkumādyaiḥ*
*praty-aṅgam evam anulipya nananda nāthaḥ ||117||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *vicintya* — having reflected; *karuṇā* — of compassion; *abdhiḥ* — the ocean; *atha* — then; *aparedyuḥ* — on the next day; *bhikṣā* — of a meal; *artham* — for the sake; *asya* — His; *niyatam* — diligently; *nirataḥ* — engaged; *babhūva* — was; *sat* — well; *bhojitam* — fed; *tat* — that; *anu* — after; *candana* — with sandal; *kuṅkuma* — with kunkuma; *ādyaiḥ* — and the rest; *prati* — each; *aṅgam* — limb; *evam* — thus; *anulipya* — having anointed; *nananda* — rejoiced; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord.

**117.** Having reflected thus, the ocean of compassion on the next day diligently busied Himself with a meal for Him [Nityananda]. When He had been well fed, the Lord then anointed each of His limbs with sandal, kunkuma and the rest, and rejoiced.

*Note.* *Bhikṣā* — alms; a meal offered to a sannyasi or an avadhuta.

### Verse 118

अन्येद्युरेष भगवानवधूतवेशः

आमन्त्र्य सोऽनुमुमुदे धरणीसुराग्र्यो
भिक्षां ददौ तदनु चन्दनकैर्लिलेप ॥११८॥

*anyedyur eṣa bhagavān avadhūta-veśaḥ*
*śrīvāsa-geham agamat kṣudhitaḥ prakāmam |*
*āmantrya so 'numumude dharaṇī-surāgryo*
*bhikṣāṁ dadau tad-anu candanakair lilepa ||118||*

*Word for word:* *anyedyuḥ* — on another day; *eṣaḥ* — this; *bhagavān* — divine one; *avadhūta* — of an avadhuta; *veśaḥ* — in the attire; *śrīvāsa* — of Srivasa; *geham* — to the house; *agamat* — came; *kṣudhitaḥ* — hungry; *prakāmam* — very; *āmantrya* — having invited; *saḥ* — he; *anumumude* — rejoiced; *dharaṇī-sura* — of the gods on earth (brahmanas); *agryaḥ* — the foremost; *bhikṣām* — a meal; *dadau* — gave; *tat* — that; *anu* — after; *candanakaiḥ* — with sandal; *lilepa* — anointed.

**118.** On another day this divine one, in the attire of an avadhuta, came to the house of Srivasa, very hungry. The foremost of brahmanas [Srivasa] rejoiced, invited Him, gave Him a meal, and afterwards anointed Him with sandal.

*Note.* *Bhagavān* here refers to Nityananda.

### Verse 119

विश्राममत्र स चकार तथैव भुक्त्वा
तत्रैव सोऽपि करुणानिधिरुद्गतोऽभूत् ।
आगत्य देवनिलये वरकम्बलेन
रम्यं वरासनमुपेत्य रराज नाथः ॥११९॥

*viśrāmam atra sa cakāra tathaiva bhuktvā*
*tatraiva so 'pi karuṇā-nidhir udgato 'bhūt |*
*āgatya deva-nilaye vara-kambalena*
*ramyaṁ varāsanam upetya rarāja nāthaḥ ||119||*

*Word for word:* *viśrāmam* — rest; *atra* — here; *saḥ* — He; *cakāra* — took; *tathā eva* — likewise; *bhuktvā* — having eaten; *tatra eva* — there too; *saḥ api* — He also; *karuṇā* — of compassion; *nidhiḥ* — the treasury; *udgataḥ abhūt* — appeared; *āgatya* — having come; *deva* — of God; *nilaye* — into the abode; *vara* — with a fine; *kambalena* — blanket; *ramyam* — made charming; *vara* — excellent; *āsanam* — a seat; *upetya* — having taken; *rarāja* — shone; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord.

**119.** Having eaten, He [Nityananda] rested there. And there too appeared the treasury of compassion: coming into the shrine, the Lord took an excellent seat, made charming by a fine blanket, and shone.

### Verse 120

ऊचेऽवधूतमथ गौरसुधाकरोऽसौ
मां पश्य पश्य कृतवानसि यच्छ्रमं त्वम् ।
इत्युक्त एष नहि किञ्चन तस्य देहे
प्रैक्षिष्ट नैव तदबुद्ध महानुभावः ॥१२०॥

*ūce 'vadhūtam atha gaura-sudhākaro 'sau*
*māṁ paśya paśya kṛtavān asi yac chramaṁ tvam |*
*ity ukta eṣa nahi kiñcana tasya dehe*
*praikṣiṣṭa naiva tad abuddha mahānubhāvaḥ ||120||*

*Word for word:* *ūce* — said; *avadhūtam* — to the avadhuta; *atha* — then; *gaura* — Gaura; *sudhākaraḥ* — the moon; *asau* — this; *mām* — at Me; *paśya paśya* — look, look; *kṛtavān asi* — You have taken; *yat* — since; *śramam* — trouble; *tvam* — You; *iti* — thus; *uktaḥ* — addressed; *eṣaḥ* — He; *nahi* — not; *kiñcana* — anything; *tasya* — His; *dehe* — in the body; *praikṣiṣṭa* — saw; *na eva* — not at all; *tat* — that; *abuddha* — understood; *mahānubhāvaḥ* — the great soul.

**120.** Then that moon, Gaura, said to the avadhuta: "Look, look at Me, since You have taken the trouble [to come]!" Thus addressed, He saw nothing [special] in His [the Lord's] body: the great soul did not understand it at all.

*Note.* The division of *naiva tad abuddha* is unclear. We take *na eva* with *abuddha* and the great soul (*mahānubhāvaḥ*) as Nityananda: "did not understand it at all"; then *jñātvā* in verse 121 refers to the Lord, who "understood this". One may also take *mahānubhāvaḥ* as the Lord, who "understood this" already here. The verse prepares verses 121–122.

### Verse 121

ज्ञात्वा स इत्थमतिकारुणिकस्ततस्ता-
नूचे बहिर्व्रजत शीघ्रमितो भवन्तः ।
गच्छत्सु तेषु स च तत्र ददर्श तस्य
देहे दिनेशशतकोटिमहो महीयः ॥१२१॥

*jñātvā sa ittham ati-kāruṇikas tatas tān*
*ūce bahir vrajata śīghram ito bhavantaḥ |*
*gacchatsu teṣu sa ca tatra dadarśa tasya*
*dehe dineśa-śata-koṭi-maho mahīyaḥ ||121||*

*Word for word:* *jñātvā* — having understood; *saḥ* — He; *ittham* — thus; *ati* — very; *kāruṇikaḥ* — compassionate; *tataḥ* — then; *tān* — to them; *ūce* — said; *bahiḥ* — outside; *vrajata* — go; *śīghram* — quickly; *itaḥ* — from here; *bhavantaḥ* — you; *gacchatsu teṣu* — when they had gone; *saḥ* — He; *ca* — and; *tatra* — then; *dadarśa* — saw; *tasya* — His; *dehe* — in the body; *dina-īśa* — of suns; *śata* — of hundreds; *koṭi* — of crores; *mahaḥ* — a radiance; *mahīyaḥ* — most mighty.

**121.** Understanding this, the most compassionate [Lord] then said to those [present]: "Go outside quickly, all of you." And when they had gone, He [Nityananda] then saw in His [the Lord's] body a most mighty radiance, [like that] of hundreds of crores of suns.

### Verse 122

पुरः षड्भिर्दोर्भिः परमरुचिरं तत्र च पुन-
श्चतुर्णां बाहूनां परमललितत्वेन मधुरम् ।
तदीयं तद्रूपं सपदि परिलोच्याशु सहसा
तदाश्चर्य्यं भूयो द्विभुजमथ भूयोऽप्यकलयत् ॥१२२॥

*puraḥ ṣaḍbhir dorbhiḥ parama-ruciraṁ tatra ca punaś*
*caturṇāṁ bāhūnāṁ parama-lalitatvena madhuram |*
*tadīyaṁ tad-rūpaṁ sapadi parilocyāśu sahasā*
*tad āścaryaṁ bhūyo dvi-bhujam atha bhūyo 'py akalayat ||122||*

*Word for word:* *puraḥ* — first; *ṣaḍbhiḥ* — with six; *dorbhiḥ* — arms; *parama* — supremely; *ruciram* — beautiful; *tatra* — there; *ca* — and; *punaḥ* — then; *caturṇām* — of four; *bāhūnām* — arms; *parama* — with the supreme; *lalitatvena* — grace; *madhuram* — sweet; *tadīyam* — His; *tat* — that; *rūpam* — form; *sapadi* — at once; *parilocya* — having beheld; *āśu* — swiftly; *sahasā* — suddenly; *tat* — that; *āścaryam* — wondrous; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *dvi* — two-; *bhujam* — armed [form]; *atha* — then; *bhūyaḥ api* — again and again; *akalayat* — contemplated.

**122.** Having at once beheld that form of His — first supremely beautiful with six arms, and then sweet with the supreme grace of four arms — He swiftly, suddenly [beheld] again that wondrous two-armed [form], and then contemplated it again and again.

*Note.* The metre is *śikhariṇī* (17 syllables). The revelation of the *ṣaḍ-bhuja* (the six-armed form) to Nityananda — Chaitanya-bhagavata, Madhya 5.92–94: in the hands are the conch, disc, mace, lotus, plough and pestle (the form of Vishnu and Balarama); Nityananda loses consciousness. The iconography of "the arms of Rama, Krishna and Gaura" is not given by the Chaitanya-bhagavata here. In Karnapura the six-armed form is followed by the four-armed and the two-armed forms.

### Verse 123

विलोक्येत्थं तत्तत् परमरमणीयं सुमधुरं
कृपासिन्धो रूपामृतमिदममन्दं प्रमुदितः ।
जहासोच्चैर्नृत्यन्नतिशयसुखास्फालनपरो
भृशं नित्यानन्दः सुखजलधिसंप्लाविततनुः ॥१२३॥

इति श्रीकृष्णचैतन्यचरितामृते महाकाव्ये भक्तसम्मेलनं नाम षष्ठः सर्गः ॥

*vilokyetthaṁ tat tat parama-ramaṇīyaṁ su-madhuraṁ*
*kṛpā-sindho rūpāmṛtam idam amandaṁ pramuditaḥ |*
*jahāsoccair nṛtyann atiśaya-sukhāsphālana-paro*
*bhṛśaṁ nityānandaḥ sukha-jaladhi-saṁplāvita-tanuḥ ||123||*

*iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahā-kāvye bhakta-sammelanaṁ nāma ṣaṣṭhaḥ sargaḥ ||*

*Word for word:* *vilokya* — having beheld; *ittham* — thus; *tat tat* — all this; *parama* — supremely; *ramaṇīyam* — enchanting; *su* — very; *madhuram* — sweet; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *sindhoḥ* — of the ocean; *rūpa* — of the form; *amṛtam* — nectar; *idam* — this; *amandam* — immensely; *pramuditaḥ* — delighted; *jahāsa* — laughed; *uccaiḥ* — loudly; *nṛtyan* — dancing; *atiśaya* — from excess; *sukha* — of happiness; *āsphālana* — to clapping [His hands]; *paraḥ* — given; *bhṛśam* — wildly; *nityānandaḥ* — Nityananda; *sukha* — of happiness; *jaladhi* — by the ocean; *saṁplāvita* — flooded; *tanuḥ* — [with] a body.

**123.** Having thus beheld all this — this supremely enchanting, very sweet nectar of the form of the ocean of mercy — Nityananda, immensely delighted, His body flooded by an ocean of happiness, danced wildly, given to clapping His hands from excess of happiness, and laughed loudly.

*Note.* The metre is *śikhariṇī*. The edition has *संप्लावितनुः*; we read *saṁplāvita-tanuḥ*.

Thus ends the sixth sarga, named "The Gathering of the Devotees", in the mahakavya "Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita".

---

## Sarga Seven — verses 1–107

**Title of the sarga:** none — the colophon of the edition gives no title for this sarga.
**Metre:** *pramitākṣarā* (12 syllables per pada: ⏑⏑— ⏑—⏑ ⏑⏑— ⏑⏑—); verse 98 — *śārdūla-vikrīḍita*; verses 99 and 102 — *upajāti*; verse 100 — *praharṣiṇī*; verse 101 — *vasanta-tilakā*; verses 103–106 — *śālinī*; verse 107 — *sragdharā*.
**Total verses:** 107 (plus an unnumbered quotation after verse 100).

**Contents of the passage:**
- 1–2 — at night Gaura weeps in His sleep; Shachi asks: "Why are You weeping?" — "I have seen the Sweet One."
- 3–12 — a description of Krishna as seen in the dream, from the peacock feathers to the hem of His garment; Shachi's joy.
- 13–20 — some days later, in the house of "the best of brahmanas" (cf. 6.118–123), Gaura reveals to Nityananda the six-armed form (conch, disc, club; flute, lotus, bow), then the four-armed and the two-armed; Nityananda showers Him with flowers and dances.
- 21–24 — Nityananda's dance; He is Balarama.
- 25–29 — the Lord sends the devotees with Nityananda to Kamalaksha (Advaita, "Rudra"); Advaita exults on hearing of the six-armed form.
- 30–33 — Advaita comes and roars like a lion; the Lord reveals His splendour in the shrine of Srivasa ("Narada"); worship, the distribution of gifts.
- 34–37 — liberation is insignificant for the devotees; a night of dancing, the morning bath.
- 38–40 — the beginning of the rains: the clouds cover the moon and the sun, put to shame by Gaura.
- 41–47 — pictures of the rains: the clouds weep for joy, the lotuses hide, the clouds are a parasol over the dancing Gaura, the earth grows soft and turns red from His feet.
- 48–49 — Haridasa comes; the Lord embraces him and bids that he be given a seat of honour.
- 50–52 — Haridasa sits on the ground; the Lord anoints and feeds him; Haridasa dances in the Lord's house.
- 53–56 — Advaita is sent home; Nityananda receives garments as *prasāda* and distributes them among the devotees.
- 57–62 — the evening kirtana; Nityananda whirls "like a wheel", rolls on the ground and disappears together with Srivasa; the search.
- 63–69 — Gaura appears saddened; dancing; play with the devotees' garments; Nityananda dances — the Lord bids [them] drink the water from His feet.
- 70–75 — the joy of the gods; Haridasa's dance; the Lord performs *pūjā* to Advaita and gives Him mahaprasada.
- 76–78 — a wandering mendicant with his son sees Gaura dancing and falls unconscious.
- 79–82 — **Nrisimha**: after the *śrāddha* Srivasa recites the "Thousand Names"; Gaura, club in hand, runs to him; the people flee.
- 83–85 — the Lord calms down: "Have I wronged the people?" — "This is only the greatness of Your mercy."
- 86–90 — a singer of songs about Shiva; Gaura dances on his shoulders like Shiva; Srivasa and Mukunda recite hymns to Shiva.
- 91–93 — a brahmana woman takes the dust of His feet — Gaura throws Himself into the Ganga; Nityananda pulls Him out.
- 94–97 — the lament of the devotees; the night at a brahmana's house; in the morning, the crossing of the Ganga; He is brought home.
- 98–102 — "If I leave My mother…"; Murari: "No one will blame [You]"; Murari recites the verse of Sudama (Srimad-Bhagavatam 10.81.16); the Lord reveals His majesty: "This body is *sac-cid-ānanda*."
- 103–106 — Gaura is bathed again with the waters of the Ganga; He Himself sheds tears; kirtana.
- 107 — Gaura with the devotees cleanses the world of false knowledge and sweeps the temples.

### Verse 1

अपरेद्युरेष निशि सुप्तिमितो
विरुरोद निर्भरमतिप्रकटम् ।
तनयं तथाविधमवेक्ष्य शची
सभयं जगाद जगदेकपतिम् ॥१॥

*aparedyur eṣa niśi suptim ito*
*viruroda nirbharam ati-prakaṭam |*
*tanayaṁ tathā-vidham avekṣya śacī*
*sa-bhayaṁ jagāda jagad-eka-patim ||1||*

*Word for word:* *aparedyuḥ* — on another day; *eṣaḥ* — He; *niśi* — at night; *suptim* — sleep; *itaḥ* — having entered; *viruroda* — wept; *nirbharam* — unrestrainedly; *ati* — very; *prakaṭam* — loudly; *tanayam* — the son; *tathā* — such; *vidham* — [being] of a kind; *avekṣya* — having seen; *śacī* — Shachi; *sa* — with; *bhayam* — fear; *jagāda* — said; *jagat* — of the world; *eka* — to the sole; *patim* — Lord.

**1.** On another day, at night, as He lay asleep, He wept unrestrainedly and very loudly. Seeing her son in such a state, Shachi in fear spoke to the sole Lord of the world:

*Note.* Cf. the beginning of Sarga Five (verse 2): the same motif of weeping at night, now with the cause explained.

### Verse 2

किमु तात रोदिति भवानवदत्
स तथेति मातरमुवाच ततः ।
अयि निद्रया विकलितेन मया
स विलोकितोऽस्ति मधुरो मधुरः ॥२॥

*kim u tāta roditi bhavān avadat*
*sa tatheti mātaram uvāca tataḥ |*
*ayi nidrayā vikalitena mayā*
*sa vilokito 'sti madhuro madhuraḥ ||2||*

*Word for word:* *kim u* — why then; *tāta* — dear child; *roditi* — weep; *bhavān* — You; *avadat* — she said; *saḥ* — He; *tathā* — thus; *iti* — so; *mātaram* — to the mother; *uvāca* — said; *tataḥ* — then; *ayi* — O [Mother]; *nidrayā* — by sleep; *vikalitena* — overwhelmed; *mayā* — by Me; *saḥ* — He; *vilokitaḥ asti* — has been seen; *madhuraḥ madhuraḥ* — the Sweet, the Sweet One.

**2.** "Why then are You weeping, dear child?" she said. And He then answered His mother thus: "O Mother, overwhelmed by sleep, I have seen Him — the Sweet One, the Sweet One!"

### Verse 3

नवनीलनीरदसमूहरुचि-
र्नवनीलकण्ठदलमण्डनकः ।
घनमेदुरातिकुटिलप्रसृत-
कचसञ्चयप्रसृतभालतलः ॥३॥

*nava-nīla-nīrada-samūha-rucir*
*nava-nīlakaṇṭha-dala-maṇḍanakaḥ |*
*ghana-medurāti-kuṭila-prasṛta-*
*kaca-sañcaya-prasṛta-bhāla-talaḥ ||3||*

*Word for word:* *nava* — of fresh; *nīla* — dark-blue; *nīrada* — clouds; *samūha* — of a bank; *ruciḥ* — [with] the lustre; *nava* — with fresh; *nīlakaṇṭha* — peacock; *dala* — feathers; *maṇḍanakaḥ* — adorned; *ghana* — thick; *medura* — lush; *ati* — very; *kuṭila* — curling; *prasṛta* — spreading; *kaca* — of locks; *sañcaya* — [with] a mass; *prasṛta* — overspread; *bhāla* — of the forehead; *talaḥ* — [with] the expanse.

**3.** "[He had] the lustre of a bank of fresh dark-blue clouds and was adorned with fresh peacock feathers; a mass of thick, lush, very curling, spreading locks overspread His forehead;

*Note.* Verses 3–10 are a portrait of Krishna "from head to foot" (*keśādi-pādānta*), all one sentence in the nominative ("He was…"). *Nīlakaṇṭha* ("blue-throated") is the peacock. The edition has *प्रसरत-*; the metre requires *prasṛta*.

### Verse 4

सुरसूनसञ्चयवतंसरस-
प्रमदभ्रमद्भ्रमरविभ्रमभृत् ।
अलसोल्लसन्मधुरचिल्लिलतः
श्रवणान्तसञ्चरितनेत्रयुगः ॥४॥

*sura-sūna-sañcaya-vataṁsa-rasa-*
*pramada-bhramad-bhramara-vibhrama-bhṛt |*
*alasollasan-madhura-cilli-lataḥ*
*śravaṇānta-sañcarita-netra-yugaḥ ||4||*

*Word for word:* *sura* — celestial; *sūna* — of flowers; *sañcaya* — of a cluster; *vataṁsa* — of the crest-garland; *rasa* — by the nectar; *pramada* — intoxicated; *bhramat* — circling; *bhramara* — of bees; *vibhrama* — the charm; *bhṛt* — bearing; *alasa* — languidly; *ullasat* — playing; *madhura* — sweet; *cilli* — of eyebrows; *lataḥ* — [with] the creepers; *śravaṇa* — of the ears; *anta* — to the edges; *sañcarita* — extending; *netra* — of eyes; *yugaḥ* — [with] a pair.

**4.** He bore the charm of the bees circling about, intoxicated by the nectar of His crest-garland of clustered celestial flowers; the creepers of His sweet eyebrows played languidly, and His pair of eyes extended to His very ears;

*Note.* The edition has *सुरसुन*; the metre requires *sura-sūna* ("celestial flowers"). *Cilli* — eyebrow (late Sanskrit).

### Verse 5

अरुणारुणाक्षिकमलः प्रमदो
घनसान्द्रदृष्टिलहरीमधुरः ।
सदपाङ्गभङ्गिमजगन्मदनः
स्मितगण्डमण्डललसन्मुकुरः ॥५॥

*aruṇāruṇākṣi-kamalaḥ pramado*
*ghana-sāndra-dṛṣṭi-laharī-madhuraḥ |*
*sad-apāṅga-bhaṅgima-jagan-madanaḥ*
*smita-gaṇḍa-maṇḍala-lasan-mukuraḥ ||5||*

*Word for word:* *aruṇa* — like the dawn; *aruṇa* — red; *akṣi* — of eyes; *kamalaḥ* — [with] the lotuses; *pramadaḥ* — joyful; *ghana* — of dense; *sāndra* — deep; *dṛṣṭi* — of glances; *laharī* — with the waves; *madhuraḥ* — sweet; *sat* — of lovely; *apāṅga* — sidelong glances; *bhaṅgima* — by the curves; *jagat* — of the world; *madanaḥ* — the intoxicator (Madana); *smita* — with a smile; *gaṇḍa* — of cheeks; *maṇḍala* — [with] the circles; *lasat* — gleaming; *mukuraḥ* — [like] mirrors.

**5.** His lotus eyes were red as the dawn; joyful, He was sweet with dense, deep waves of glances; by the curves of His lovely sidelong glances He was Madana to the whole world; the circles of His cheeks, touched by a smile, gleamed like mirrors;

*Note.* *Madana* is Kamadeva, the god of love; *jagan-madana*, "intoxicating the world", i.e. Madana-mohana. The edition has *प्रमदो*; possibly *pramada* is part of the next word (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 6

तपनीयकुण्डलविलासलस-
च्छ्रवणद्वयीहृतजगद्धृदयः ।
नवविद्रुमद्रुमकडम्बलस-
न्मधुराधरद्युतिसुधामधुरः ॥६॥

*tapanīya-kuṇḍala-vilāsa-lasac-*
*chravaṇa-dvayī-hṛta-jagad-dhṛdayaḥ |*
*nava-vidruma-druma-kaḍamba-lasan-*
*madhurādhara-dyuti-sudhā-madhuraḥ ||6||*

*Word for word:* *tapanīya* — of golden; *kuṇḍala* — earrings; *vilāsa* — with the play; *lasat* — gleaming; *śravaṇa* — of ears; *dvayī* — by the pair; *hṛta* — stealing; *jagat* — of the world; *hṛdayaḥ* — the heart; *nava* — of fresh; *vidruma* — coral; *druma* — of the tree; *kaḍamba* — [like] a shoot; *lasat* — shining; *madhura* — of sweet; *adhara* — lips; *dyuti* — of the lustre; *sudhā* — with the nectar; *madhuraḥ* — sweet.

**6.** with His pair of ears, gleaming with the play of golden earrings, He stole the heart of the world; He was sweet with the nectar of the lustre of His sweet lips, which shone like a shoot of a fresh coral tree;

*Note.* *Kaḍamba* — "shoot, stalk".

### Verse 7

दशनप्रसूनरुचिमञ्जरिका-
धरपल्लवारुणिमकम्रमुखः ।
मधुमाधुरीमधुरसच्चिबुकः
शुचिकम्बुकण्ठतटहारधरः ॥७॥

*daśana-prasūna-ruci-mañjarikā-*
*dhara-pallavāruṇima-kamra-mukhaḥ |*
*madhu-mādhurī-madhura-sac-cibukaḥ*
*śuci-kambu-kaṇṭha-taṭa-hāra-dharaḥ ||7||*

*Word for word:* *daśana* — of teeth; *prasūna* — of flowers; *ruci* — of lustre; *mañjarikā* — with the cluster of blossoms; *adhara* — of lips; *pallava* — of shoots; *aruṇima* — with the redness; *kamra* — lovely; *mukhaḥ* — [with] a face; *madhu* — of honey; *mādhurī* — with the sweetness; *madhura* — sweet; *sat* — lovely; *cibukaḥ* — [with] a chin; *śuci* — pure; *kambu* — [like] a conch; *kaṇṭha* — of the neck; *taṭa* — on the slope; *hāra* — a necklace; *dharaḥ* — wearing.

**7.** His face was lovely with the blossom-cluster of the lustre of His flower-like teeth and with the redness of His shoot-like lips; His lovely chin was sweet with the sweetness of honey; on the slope of His neck, pure as a conch, He wore a necklace;

*Note.* A neck "like a conch" — with three folds, a mark of beauty.

### Verse 8

नवमौक्तिकप्रकरहारलता-
विलसद्गलो विलसदंसतटः ।
तपनीयसूत्रपरिकॢप्तलस-
द्वरकौस्तुभस्फुरदुरःसरणिः ॥८॥

*nava-mauktika-prakara-hāra-latā-*
*vilasad-galo vilasad-aṁsa-taṭaḥ |*
*tapanīya-sūtra-parikḷpta-lasad-*
*vara-kaustubha-sphurad-uraḥ-saraṇiḥ ||8||*

*Word for word:* *nava* — of fresh; *mauktika* — pearls; *prakara* — of a multitude; *hāra* — of a necklace; *latā* — with the creeper; *vilasat* — gleaming; *galaḥ* — [with] a neck; *vilasat* — gleaming; *aṁsa* — of the shoulders; *taṭaḥ* — [with] the slopes; *tapanīya* — golden; *sūtra* — on a thread; *parikḷpta* — fastened; *lasat* — shining; *vara* — by the excellent; *kaustubha* — Kaustubha; *sphurat* — glittering; *uraḥ* — of the chest; *saraṇiḥ* — [with] the expanse.

**8.** His neck gleamed with the creeper of a necklace of many fresh pearls, the slopes of His shoulders gleamed; the expanse of His chest glittered with the shining, excellent Kaustubha fastened on a golden thread;

*Note.* The *Kaustubha* is the jewel on the chest of Vishnu/Krishna, obtained at the churning of the ocean. The edition has *परिकलृप्त*; we read *parikḷpta*.

अमरप्रसूननवमाल्यकला-

विलसद्वराङ्गदसुकङ्कणकः ॥९॥

*amara-prasūna-nava-mālya-kalā-*

*vara-jānu-lambi-mṛdu-pīna-bhujā-*
*vilasad-varāṅgada-su-kaṅkaṇakaḥ ||9||*

*Word for word:* *amara* — celestial; *prasūna* — of flowers; *nava* — of a fresh; *mālya* — garland; *kalā* — by the elegance; *lalita* — charming; *uru* — broad; *pīna* — full; *sat* — lovely; *uraḥ* — [with] a chest; *madhuraḥ* — sweet; *vara* — fine; *jānu* — the knees; *lambi* — reaching; *mṛdu* — tender; *pīna* — mighty; *bhujā* — on the arms; *vilasat* — gleaming; *vara* — with excellent; *aṅgada* — armlets; *su* — with lovely; *kaṅkaṇakaḥ* — wrist-bracelets.

*Note.* Arms reaching the knees (*ājānu-bāhu*) are a sign of a great man.

*Note.* An "undulating" belly — with three folds (*trivali*), a canon of beauty. The golden cloth is the *pītāmbara*, Krishna's yellow garment.

### Verse 11

स्मितदीधितिस्नपितदिग्वलयः

सुखसञ्चयैर्मम सुविह्वलता ॥११॥

*smita-dīdhiti-snapita-dig-valayaḥ*
*karuṇā-kaṭākṣa-madhuraḥ kamalaḥ |*
*iti taṁ vilokya sahasāvirabhūt*
*sukha-sañcayair mama su-vihvalatā ||11||*

*Word for word:* *smita* — of the smile; *dīdhiti* — with the rays; *snapita* — bathing; *dik* — of the directions; *valayaḥ* — the circle; *karuṇā* — compassionate; *kaṭākṣa* — with sidelong glances; *madhuraḥ* — sweet; *kamalaḥ* — [tender as a] lotus; *iti* — such; *tam* — Him; *vilokya* — having seen; *sahasā* — suddenly; *āvirabhūt* — arose; *sukha* — of happiness; *sañcayaiḥ* — from the abundance; *mama* — in Me; *su* — complete; *vihvalatā* — bewilderment.

**11.** with the rays of His smile He bathed the whole circle of the directions; sweet with compassionate sidelong glances, [tender as a] lotus. Seeing Him so, I was suddenly overcome by complete bewilderment from the abundance of happiness.

*Note.* *Kamalaḥ* (masculine, "lotus") as an attribute is unusual; perhaps *komalaḥ* ("tender") should be read. As an adjective *kamala* also means "rose-coloured, lotus-hued" (cf. verse 18). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

तनयोदितान्यथ निशम्य शची
सहसाभवत् सपुलकं मुदिता ॥१२॥

*atha rodimi prati-muhur vikalaḥ*
*sukha-sāgare 'smi kṛta-saṁplavanaḥ |*
*tanayoditāny atha niśamya śacī*
*sahasābhavat sa-pulakaṁ muditā ||12||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — and now; *rodimi* — I weep; *prati-muhuḥ* — again and again; *vikalaḥ* — overwhelmed; *sukha* — of happiness; *sāgare* — in the ocean; *asmi* — I am; *kṛta* — having made; *saṁplavanaḥ* — immersion; *tanaya* — of the son; *uditāni* — the words; *atha* — then; *niśamya* — having heard; *śacī* — Shachi; *sahasā* — at once; *abhavat* — became; *sa* — with; *pulakam* — hair standing on end; *muditā* — joyful.

**12.** And now, overwhelmed, I weep again and again: I have plunged into an ocean of happiness." Hearing her son's words, Shachi at once rejoiced, the hair on her body standing on end.

### Verse 13

प्रभुरप्यसौ नयनवारिझरै-
र्जलधिद्वयं किमदधादुरसि ।
कियता दिनेन समुपेत्य बभौ
द्विजपुङ्गवालयवरं तदिदम् ॥१३॥

*prabhur apy asau nayana-vāri-jharair*
*jaladhi-dvayaṁ kim adadhād urasi |*
*kiyatā dinena samupetya babhau*
*dvija-puṅgavālaya-varaṁ tad idam ||13||*

*Word for word:* *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *api* — and; *asau* — He; *nayana* — of the eyes; *vāri* — of water; *jharaiḥ* — with the torrents; *jaladhi* — of oceans; *dvayam* — a pair; *kim* — as if; *adadhāt* — bore; *urasi* — on the chest; *kiyatā* — after some; *dinena* — days; *samupetya* — having come to; *babhau* — shone; *dvija* — of brahmanas; *puṅgava* — of the best; *ālaya* — the house; *varam* — excellent; *tat idam* — that very.

**13.** And the Lord, with the torrents of tears from His eyes, seemed to bear two oceans on His chest. After some days He came to that excellent house of the best of brahmanas and shone [there].

*Note.* No subject is named in the second half; we take it, as the grammar suggests, to be the Lord (*prabhuḥ* of the first half), with *tad idam* (neuter accusative) going with the house. One may also understand Nityananda, who in verse 14 is "there" (*tatra*); Nityananda's name is not in the verse. "The best of brahmanas" is not named either; in 6.118 Srivasa is called "the foremost of brahmanas", and the revelation of 6.119–122 takes place in his house. Verses 14–22 evidently repeat and expand the episode at the end of Sarga Six (6.120–123): the revelation of the six-armed form to Nityananda. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

महनीयमूर्त्तिरवधूतविभुः

*Note.* The sentence continues in verse 15.

*Word for word:* *apibat* — drank; *vilocana* — of the eyes; *puṭena* — with the cup; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *na* — not; *tṛṣaḥ* — of the thirst; *asya* — His; *pāram* — the end; *agamat* — reached; *vibhavaḥ* — the abundance [of beauty]; *vara* — beautiful; *ṣaṭ* — six-; *bhujam* — armed; *tam* — Him; *atha* — then; *dakṣiṇataḥ* — on the right; *dara* — a conch; *cakra* — a disc; *nirmala* — a gleaming; *gadā* — club; *astra* — weapons; *dharam* — holding.

*Note.* *Dara* — the conch (*śaṅkha*).

*muralī-varāmburuha-śārṅga-dharaṁ*
*rucirair athāpara-bhuja-tritayaiḥ |*
*druta-śātakumbha-maya-bhūmiruhas*
*taruṇāṅkuraṁ karuṇayāruṇitam ||16||*

*Word for word:* *muralī* — a flute; *vara* — a fine; *amburuha* — lotus; *śārṅga* — the Sharnga bow; *dharam* — holding; *ruciraiḥ* — with beautiful; *atha* — and; *apara* — other; *bhuja* — of arms; *tritayaiḥ* — with the three; *druta* — of molten; *śātakumbha* — gold; *maya* — made; *bhūmiruhaḥ* — of a tree; *taruṇa* — a young; *aṅkuram* — shoot; *karuṇayā* — with compassion; *aruṇitam* — reddened.

*Note.* The set of attributes differs from the later tradition (Chaitanya-bhagavata, Chaitanya-charitamrita: the bow and arrow of Rama, the flute of Krishna, the staff and waterpot of a sannyasi): in Karnapura they are the weapons of Vishnu (conch, disc, club, lotus, the Sharnga bow) and the flute of Krishna.

*Word for word:* *avalokya* — having seen; *vismita* — astonished; *manāḥ* — in mind; *sumanāḥ* — the good-hearted; *sumanaḥ* — of flowers; *cayam* — a heap; *rahasi* — in private; *tam* — Him; *vyakirat* — showered; *tat* — that; *anantaram* — after; *ca* — and; *bahu* — great; *harṣa* — of joy; *bharaiḥ* — from the weight; *vidalat* — bursting; *manāḥ* — [with] a heart; *naṭitum* — to dance; *ārabhata* — began.

*Note.* A play on *sumanāḥ* ("good-hearted") and *sumanas* ("flower"). Verses 19–20 are one sentence (*avalokya* governs both forms).
