*manujaiḥ kṣitau parimitiḥ kriyatām ||23||*

*Word for word:* *vividhām* — varied; *śriyam* — fortune; *sapadi* — at once; *yat* — of whom; *kṛpayā* — by the mercy; *labhate* — obtain; *sadā* — always; *bhuvi* — on earth; *samasta* — all; *janaḥ* — people; *kim u* — how [could]; *tasya* — of Him; *bhūri* — of immense; *mahima* — greatness; *ambunidheḥ* — of the ocean; *manujaiḥ* — by human beings; *kṣitau* — on earth; *parimitiḥ* — a measuring; *kriyatām* — be made.

**23.** He by whose mercy all people on earth always obtain varied fortune at once — how could human beings on earth take the measure of Him, the ocean of immense greatness?

*Note.* Verses 23–24 might be taken as Gaura's words; but by the construction (*atha… nijagāda* in 24cd) they are rather the author's, and Gaura's speech is verse 25.

### Verse 24

बलराम इत्यवनिमध्यमधि
प्रथितो य एष महनीयगुणः ।
अथ गौरशीतकिरणः स्वजना-
न्निजगाद भूरिकरुणः कमनः ॥२४॥

*balarāma ity avani-madhyam adhi*
*prathito ya eṣa mahanīya-guṇaḥ |*
*atha gaura-śīta-kiraṇaḥ sva-janān*
*nijagāda bhūri-karuṇaḥ kamanaḥ ||24||*

*Word for word:* *balarāmaḥ* — Balarama; *iti* — as; *avani* — of the earth; *madhyam adhi* — throughout; *prathitaḥ* — renowned; *yaḥ eṣaḥ* — He who; *mahanīya* — worthy of honour; *guṇaḥ* — [with] qualities; *atha* — and then; *gaura* — Gaura; *śīta-kiraṇaḥ* — the cool-rayed (the moon); *sva* — to His own; *janān* — people; *nijagāda* — said; *bhūri* — immensely; *karuṇaḥ* — merciful; *kamanaḥ* — charming.

**24.** — He who, with qualities worthy of honour, is renowned throughout the earth as Balarama. And then Gaura, the cool-rayed moon, immensely merciful and charming, said to His own people:

*Note.* Nityananda is Balarama, the elder brother of Krishna.

### Verse 25

अवधूत एष परिभोगगतः
कमलाक्षदेवभवने झटिति ।
अमुना समं व्रजत तस्य पुरो-
ऽस्य च सन्महत्त्वमुपकीर्त्तयत ॥२५॥

*avadhūta eṣa paribhoga-gataḥ*
*kamalākṣa-deva-bhavane jhaṭiti |*
*amunā samaṁ vrajata tasya puro*
*'sya ca san-mahattvam upakīrtayata ||25||*

*Word for word:* *avadhūtaḥ* — avadhuta; *eṣaḥ* — this; *paribhoga* — for a meal; *gataḥ* — going; *kamalākṣa-deva* — of Kamalaksha Deva; *bhavane* — to the house; *jhaṭiti* — now; *amunā* — Him; *samam* — together with; *vrajata* — go; *tasya* — of him (Kamalaksha); *puraḥ* — before; *asya* — of this one (the avadhuta); *ca* — and; *sat* — the true; *mahattvam* — greatness; *upakīrtayata* — proclaim.

**25.** "This avadhuta is now going to the house of Kamalaksha Deva for a meal. Go together with Him, and before Him [Kamalaksha] proclaim the true greatness of this one [the avadhuta]."

*Note.* Kamalaksha is the worldly name of Advaita Acharya (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 13.62 and elsewhere).

### Verse 26

तमुपेत्य ते सममनेन मुहु-
र्भुवि दण्डवन्नतिततिं विदधुः ।
भुवि रुद्र इत्यधिगतोऽस्ति हि यः
कमलाक्षसंज्ञ इह विप्रकुले ॥२६॥

*tam upetya te samam anena muhur*
*bhuvi daṇḍavan-nati-tatiṁ vidadhuḥ |*
*bhuvi rudra ity adhigato 'sti hi yaḥ*
*kamalākṣa-saṁjña iha vipra-kule ||26||*

*Word for word:* *tam* — to Him; *upetya* — having come; *te* — they; *samam* — together; *anena* — with Him; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *bhuvi* — on the ground; *daṇḍavat* — like rods; *nati* — of obeisances; *tatim* — a series; *vidadhuḥ* — made; *bhuvi* — on earth; *rudraḥ* — Rudra; *iti* — as; *adhigataḥ asti* — is known; *hi* — indeed; *yaḥ* — who; *kamalākṣa* — Kamalaksha; *saṁjñaḥ* — by name; *iha* — here; *vipra* — of brahmanas; *kule* — in a family.

**26.** Coming together with Him [Nityananda] to Him who is known on earth as Rudra, and here, in a family of brahmanas, bears the name Kamalaksha, they made obeisances again and again, falling on the ground like rods.

*Note.* Advaita is an incarnation of Sadashiva (Rudra) and of Mahavishnu (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 6).

### Verse 27

अवतीर्णतामुपगतं तममी
परिलोक्य नाथगदितं जगदुः ।
स निशम्य षड्भुजचतुर्भुजता-
मवनीतले विहितगौरतनोः ॥२७॥

*avatīrṇatām upagataṁ tam amī*
*parilokya nātha-gaditaṁ jagaduḥ |*
*sa niśamya ṣaḍ-bhuja-catur-bhujatām*
*avanī-tale vihita-gaura-tanoḥ ||27||*

*Word for word:* *avatīrṇatām* — the state of one descended; *upagatam* — who had attained; *tam* — Him; *amī* — they; *parilokya* — having seen; *nātha* — by the Lord; *gaditam* — what was said; *jagaduḥ* — related; *saḥ* — He; *niśamya* — having heard; *ṣaṭ* — six; *bhuja* — -armed; *catuḥ* — four; *bhujatām* — -armedness; *avanī* — of the earth; *tale* — on the surface; *vihita* — who had assumed; *gaura* — a golden; *tanoḥ* — of Him [with] a body.

**27.** Seeing Him, who had come down [to earth], they related to Him what the Lord had said. And He [Advaita], having heard of the six-armed and four-armed forms of Him who had assumed a golden body on the surface of the earth —

*Note.* Verses 27–28 form one sentence: *karuṇālayasya* ("of the abode of mercy", 28) goes with *vihita-gaura-tanoḥ*.

### Verse 28

करुणालयस्य मुमुदे सुभृशं
सुखसागरे विहितसंप्लवनः ।
अथ तन्निवेदनवचोमुदिता
विनिवेद्य ते ह्युपनता अनमन् ॥२८॥

*karuṇālayasya mumude subhṛśaṁ*
*sukha-sāgare vihita-saṁplavanaḥ |*
*atha tan-nivedana-vaco-muditā*
*vinivedya te hy upanatā anaman ||28||*

*Word for word:* *karuṇā* — of mercy; *ālayasya* — of the abode; *mumude* — rejoiced; *subhṛśam* — immensely; *sukha* — of happiness; *sāgare* — in the ocean; *vihita* — having made; *saṁplavanaḥ* — a plunge; *atha* — then; *tat* — that; *nivedana* — of the report; *vacaḥ* — by the words; *muditāḥ* — gladdened; *vinivedya* — having made known; *te* — they; *hi* — indeed; *upanatāḥ* — drawing near; *anaman* — bowed down.

**28.** — [of Him], the abode of mercy, plunged into an ocean of happiness and rejoiced immensely. Then they, gladdened by the words of that report, having made [everything] known, drew near and bowed down.

*Note.* *Tan-nivedana-vacaḥ* may also be understood as His (Advaita's) words in reply to the report.

### Verse 29

करुणालयस्य चरणाब्जरजः
परिगृह्य तत्पदयुगानुगताः ।
अपरेद्युरप्ययममन्दगुणः
कमलाक्षदेव उदियाय ततः ॥२९॥

*karuṇālayasya caraṇābja-rajaḥ*
*parigṛhya tat-pada-yugānugatāḥ |*
*aparedyur apy ayam amanda-guṇaḥ*
*kamalākṣa-deva udiyāya tataḥ ||29||*

*Word for word:* *karuṇā* — of mercy; *ālayasya* — of the abode; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *abja* — of the lotus; *rajaḥ* — the dust; *parigṛhya* — having taken; *tat* — His; *pada* — of feet; *yuga* — the pair; *anugatāḥ* — following; *aparedyuḥ* — on the next day; *api* — and; *ayam* — this; *amanda* — not slight; *guṇaḥ* — [whose] virtues; *kamalākṣa-devaḥ* — Kamalaksha Deva; *udiyāya* — came; *tataḥ* — then.

**29.** Taking the dust of the lotus feet of that abode of mercy, they followed His pair of feet. And on the next day this Kamalaksha Deva, whose virtues are not slight, came [to the Lord].

*Note.* The "abode of mercy" here is evidently Kamalaksha himself (in verse 28 the same epithet refers to Gaura). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 30

अवलोक्य गौरशशिनं च तदा
मदसिंहनादरुचिरः समभूत् ।
समुपागतेऽत्र महनीयगुणे
गिरिशप्रभौ प्रभुरसौ जगताम् ॥३०॥

*avalokya gaura-śaśinaṁ ca tadā*
*mada-siṁha-nāda-ruciraḥ samabhūt |*
*samupāgate 'tra mahanīya-guṇe*
*giriśa-prabhau prabhur asau jagatām ||30||*

*Word for word:* *avalokya* — having seen; *gaura* — Gaura; *śaśinam* — the moon; *ca* — and; *tadā* — then; *mada* — of an intoxicated; *siṁha* — lion; *nāda* — with the roar; *ruciraḥ* — splendid; *samabhūt* — became; *samupāgate* — when [He] had arrived; *atra* — here; *mahanīya* — worthy of honour; *guṇe* — [with] qualities; *giriśa* — Girisha; *prabhau* — the master; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *asau* — He; *jagatām* — of the worlds.

**30.** And then, seeing Gaura, the moon, He [Advaita] became splendid with a roar like that of an intoxicated lion. And when He, the master Girisha, of qualities worthy of honour, had arrived here, the Lord of the worlds —

*Note.* *Girisha* ("lord of the mountain") is Shiva: Advaita as Shiva. The roar is Advaita's *huṅkāra*.

### Verse 31

सहसाविरातनुत भूरिदयः
प्रकटप्रकाशमथ गौडशशी ।
भुवि नारदोऽयमिति यः प्रथितो
भवनेषु तस्य स तु देवगृहे ॥३१॥

*sahasāvir ātanuta bhūri-dayaḥ*
*prakaṭa-prakāśam atha gauḍa-śaśī |*
*bhuvi nārado 'yam iti yaḥ prathito*
*bhavaneṣu tasya sa tu deva-gṛhe ||31||*

*Word for word:* *sahasā* — at once; *āviḥ ātanuta* — revealed; *bhūri* — immensely; *dayaḥ* — kind; *prakaṭa* — manifest; *prakāśam* — splendour; *atha* — then; *gauḍa* — of Gauda; *śaśī* — the moon; *bhuvi* — on earth; *nāradaḥ* — Narada; *ayam* — this; *iti* — as; *yaḥ* — who; *prathitaḥ* — is renowned; *bhavaneṣu* — among the dwellings; *tasya* — of him; *saḥ* — He; *tu* — and; *deva-gṛhe* — in the shrine.

**31.** — the immensely kind moon of Gauda then at once revealed a manifest splendour in the shrine among the dwellings of him who is renowned on earth as Narada.

*Note.* Srivasa is an incarnation of Narada (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 10.8; *Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika*). Gauda is Bengal.

### Verse 32

प्रकटप्रकाशमवदर्श्य तदा
सुखमस्य भूरिकरुणोऽतनुत ।
अथ तं तथाविधमवेक्ष्य भृशं
ननृतुर्जगुर्मुमुदिरे बहु ते ।
परिपूज्य पुष्पफलपूगधनै-
र्भुवि दण्डवद्बहुसुखैरनमन् ॥३२॥

*prakaṭa-prakāśam avadarśya tadā*
*sukham asya bhūri-karuṇo 'tanuta |*
*atha taṁ tathā-vidham avekṣya bhṛśaṁ*
*nanṛtur jagur mumudire bahu te |*
*paripūjya puṣpa-phala-pūga-dhanair*
*bhuvi daṇḍavad bahu-sukhair anaman ||32||*

*Word for word:* *prakaṭa* — manifest; *prakāśam* — splendour; *avadarśya* — having shown; *tadā* — then; *sukham* — happiness; *asya* — on him; *bhūri* — immensely; *karuṇaḥ* — merciful; *atanuta* — bestowed; *atha* — and; *tam* — Him; *tathā* — such; *vidham* — in form; *avekṣya* — having seen; *bhṛśam* — intensely; *nanṛtuḥ* — danced; *jaguḥ* — sang; *mumudire* — rejoiced; *bahu* — much; *te* — they; *paripūjya* — having worshipped; *puṣpa* — with flowers; *phala* — fruits; *pūga* — betel nuts; *dhanaiḥ* — and riches; *bhuvi* — on the ground; *daṇḍavat* — like rods; *bahu* — with great; *sukhaiḥ* — happiness; *anaman* — bowed down.

**32.** Having then shown him the manifest splendour, the immensely merciful one bestowed happiness on him. And they, seeing Him in such a form, danced intensely, sang and rejoiced much; having worshipped Him with flowers, fruits, betel nuts and riches, with great happiness they bowed down on the ground like rods.

*Note.* The verse has six padas (so in the edition).

### Verse 33

परितस्तदर्च्चनमसौ कृपया
परिगृह्य तेभ्य इदमेव ददौ ।
वसनं प्रसूनमपि कारुणिकः
करुणालयस्य करुणा महती ॥३३॥

*paritas tad-arcanam asau kṛpayā*
*parigṛhya tebhya idam eva dadau |*
*vasanaṁ prasūnam api kāruṇikaḥ*
*karuṇālayasya karuṇā mahatī ||33||*

*Word for word:* *paritaḥ* — from all sides; *tat* — their; *arcanam* — offerings; *asau* — He; *kṛpayā* — mercifully; *parigṛhya* — having accepted; *tebhyaḥ* — to them; *idam eva* — these very [things]; *dadau* — gave; *vasanam* — cloths; *prasūnam* — flowers; *api* — and; *kāruṇikaḥ* — the compassionate one; *karuṇā* — of mercy; *ālayasya* — of the abode; *karuṇā* — the mercy; *mahatī* — [is] great.

**33.** Having mercifully accepted their offerings from all sides, the compassionate [Lord] gave these very things — cloths and flowers — to them. Great is the mercy of the abode of mercy!

### Verse 34

जगतीत्रयस्य जनताभिरति-
प्रतिमृग्यमत्यसुलभं बहुधा ।
अपवर्गमप्यतिलघुं सहसा
सुखतन्मया विदधुरित्थममी ॥३४॥

*jagatī-trayasya janatābhir ati-*
*pratimṛgyam aty-asulabhaṁ bahudhā |*
*apavargam apy ati-laghuṁ sahasā*
*sukha-tanmayā vidadhur ittham amī ||34||*

*Word for word:* *jagatī* — of worlds; *trayasya* — of the three; *janatābhiḥ* — by the peoples; *ati* — eagerly; *pratimṛgyam* — sought; *ati* — very; *asulabham* — hard to attain; *bahudhā* — in many ways; *apavargam* — liberation; *api* — even; *ati* — very; *laghum* — trifling; *sahasā* — at once; *sukha* — in happiness; *tanmayāḥ* — absorbed; *vidadhuḥ* — deemed; *ittham* — thus; *amī* — they.

**34.** Thus they, absorbed in happiness, at once deemed very trifling even liberation, which the peoples of the three worlds eagerly seek in many ways and which is so hard to attain.

*Note.* *Apavarga* is liberation (moksha); cf. Srimad-Bhagavatam 3.29.13: pure devotees do not accept even liberation.

### Verse 35

न दिनं न रात्रिमथ तेऽथ विदु-
र्न सुखं न दुःखमपि ते परमाः ।
किमनीप्सितापि सतनूनभज-
ज्जडतामिषेण भुवि मुक्तिरमून् ॥३५॥

*na dinaṁ na rātrim atha te 'tha vidur*
*na sukhaṁ na duḥkham api te paramāḥ |*
*kim anīpsitāpi sa-tanūn abhajaj*
*jaḍatā-miṣeṇa bhuvi muktir amūn ||35||*

*Word for word:* *na* — neither; *dinam* — day; *na* — nor; *rātrim* — night; *atha* — and; *te* — they; *atha* — and; *viduḥ* — knew; *na* — neither; *sukham* — happiness; *na* — nor; *duḥkham* — sorrow; *api* — even; *te* — they; *paramāḥ* — the supreme; *kim* — did not?; *anīpsitā* — unwanted; *api* — though; *sa* — with; *tanūn* — bodies; *abhajat* — serve; *jaḍatā* — of stupor; *miṣeṇa* — in the guise; *bhuvi* — on earth; *muktiḥ* — liberation; *amūn* — them.

**35.** Those supreme [souls] knew neither day nor night, nor even happiness or sorrow. Did not liberation itself, though unwanted, serve them on earth, while they were still in their bodies, in the guise of their stupor?

*Note.* Stupor (*jaḍatā*, *stambha*) is one of the ecstatic symptoms; the poet compares it with the insensibility of one liberated in this life (*jīvan-mukta*).

### Verse 36

अभिभास्वदुद्गमनमित्थममी
ननृतुर्जगुर्मुमुदिरे बहु ते ।
रजनीं विनीय सकलाञ्च पुन-
र्दिवसादिमेत्य विवशा अभवन् ॥३६॥

*abhi-bhāsvad-udgamanam ittham amī*
*nanṛtur jagur mumudire bahu te |*
*rajanīṁ vinīya sakalāñ ca punar*
*divasādim etya vivaśā abhavan ||36||*

*Word for word:* *abhi* — until; *bhāsvat* — of the sun; *udgamanam* — the rising; *ittham* — thus; *amī* — they; *nanṛtuḥ* — danced; *jaguḥ* — sang; *mumudire* — rejoiced; *bahu* — much; *te* — they; *rajanīm* — the night; *vinīya* — having spent; *sakalām* — whole; *ca* — and; *punaḥ* — then; *divasa* — of the day; *ādim* — the beginning; *etya* — having reached; *vivaśāḥ* — overcome; *abhavan* — became.

**36.** Thus they danced, sang and rejoiced much until the rising of the sun; and having spent the whole night [so], at the beginning of the day they were overcome.

### Verse 37

द्युनदीजलं समवगाह्य ततः
प्रथमं दिनस्य मुदितास्त इमे ।
असुधारणैकपरमौषधिव-
च्चरणं प्रभोर्मृदुतरं ददृशुः ॥३७॥

*dyu-nadī-jalaṁ samavagāhya tataḥ*
*prathamaṁ dinasya muditās ta ime |*
*asu-dhāraṇaika-paramauṣadhi-vac*
*caraṇaṁ prabhor mṛdutaraṁ dadṛśuḥ ||37||*

*Word for word:* *dyu* — of the heavenly; *nadī* — river; *jalam* — in the water; *samavagāhya* — having bathed; *tataḥ* — then; *prathamam* — at the beginning; *dinasya* — of the day; *muditāḥ* — joyful; *te ime* — they; *asu* — life; *dhāraṇa* — for sustaining; *eka* — the one; *parama* — supreme; *auṣadhi* — a medicine; *vat* — like; *caraṇam* — the feet; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *mṛdutaram* — most tender; *dadṛśuḥ* — beheld.

**37.** Then, at the beginning of the day, having bathed in the water of the heavenly river, they joyfully beheld the most tender feet of the Lord, the one supreme medicine for sustaining their life.

*Note.* The heavenly river is the Ganga.

### Verse 38

अथ तस्य नर्त्तनविलासमिमं
परिलोकितुं सरभसं मुदितः ।
मुदिरः शनैर्नभसि किं विदधौ
सहसोद्गमं मधुरमेदुररुक् ॥३८॥

*atha tasya nartana-vilāsam imaṁ*
*parilokituṁ sa-rabhasaṁ muditaḥ |*
*mudiraḥ śanair nabhasi kiṁ vidadhau*
*sahasodgamaṁ madhura-medura-ruk ||38||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — and then; *tasya* — His; *nartana* — of dancing; *vilāsam* — play; *imam* — this; *parilokitum* — to behold; *sa* — with; *rabhasam* — eagerness; *muditaḥ* — joyful; *mudiraḥ* — the cloud; *śanaiḥ* — slowly; *nabhasi* — in the sky; *kim* — did not?; *vidadhau* — make; *sahasā* — suddenly; *udgamam* — a rising; *madhura* — sweet; *medura* — dense; *ruk* — [full of] lustre.

**38.** And then, to behold this play of His dancing, did not the joyful cloud, full of a sweet, dense lustre, eagerly rise in the sky — suddenly, yet slowly?

*Note.* A play on *mudita* ("joyful") and *mudira* ("cloud"). Verses 38–40 are *utprekṣā* (poetic fancy): nature responds to Gaura. The rainy season begins.

### Verse 39

भुवि भाति गौरहिमरश्मिरयं
मधुरद्युतिः किमधुना भवता ।
इति भूरिशो नभसि चन्द्रमसं
जलदोद्गमः सपदि किं पिदधे ॥३९॥

*bhuvi bhāti gaura-hima-raśmir ayaṁ*
*madhura-dyutiḥ kim adhunā bhavatā |*
*iti bhūriśo nabhasi candramasaṁ*
*jaladodgamaḥ sapadi kiṁ pidadhe ||39||*

*Word for word:* *bhuvi* — on earth; *bhāti* — shines; *gaura* — Gaura; *hima-raśmiḥ* — the cool-rayed (the moon); *ayam* — this; *madhura* — sweet; *dyutiḥ* — [whose] radiance; *kim* — what [use]; *adhunā* — now; *bhavatā* — of you; *iti* — [thinking] thus; *bhūriśaḥ* — wholly; *nabhasi* — in the sky; *candramasam* — the moon; *jalada* — of clouds; *udgamaḥ* — the rising; *sapadi* — at once; *kim* — did not?; *pidadhe* — cover.

**39.** "This moon, Gaura, sweet in radiance, shines on earth — what use is there of you now?" Was it [thinking] thus that the rising clouds at once wholly covered the moon in the sky?

### Verse 40

इह गौरचन्द्रमहसा महता
परिनिर्जितो दिनपतिर्नभसि ।
त्रपयैव किं विनिविवेश भृशं
जलदावलीष्वविरलासु ततः ॥४०॥

*iha gauracandra-mahasā mahatā*
*parinirjito dinapatir nabhasi |*
*trapayaiva kiṁ vinivivesa bhṛśaṁ*
*jaladāvalīṣv aviralāsu tataḥ ||40||*

*Word for word:* *iha* — here; *gauracandra* — of Gaurachandra; *mahasā* — by the splendour; *mahatā* — great; *parinirjitaḥ* — vanquished; *dinapatiḥ* — the lord of the day (the sun); *nabhasi* — in the sky; *trapayā* — from shame; *eva* — indeed; *kim* — did not?; *viniviveśa* — enter; *bhṛśam* — deep; *jalada* — of clouds; *āvalīṣu* — into the rows; *aviralāsu* — dense; *tataḥ* — then.

**40.** Was it not from shame that the lord of the day, vanquished here by the great splendour of Gaurachandra, then sank deep into the dense rows of clouds in the sky?

### Verse 41

विकसत्कदम्बनवगन्धरसै-
रतिचारुवासितवतीः ककुभः ।
परिरभ्य हर्षभवमश्रुभरं
जलदोद्गमः क्षणवशादमुचत् ॥४१॥

*vikasat-kadamba-nava-gandha-rasair*
*ati-cāru-vāsitavatīḥ kakubhaḥ |*
*parirabhya harṣa-bhavam aśru-bharaṁ*
*jaladodgamaḥ kṣaṇa-vaśād amucat ||41||*

*Word for word:* *vikasat* — of blossoming; *kadamba* — kadambas; *nava* — with the fresh; *gandha* — fragrance; *rasaiḥ* — and sap; *ati* — very; *cāru* — charmingly; *vāsitavatīḥ* — perfumed; *kakubhaḥ* — the quarters; *parirabhya* — having embraced; *harṣa* — from joy; *bhavam* — born; *aśru* — of tears; *bharam* — a flood; *jalada* — of clouds; *udgamaḥ* — the rising; *kṣaṇa* — of the moment; *vaśāt* — by force; *amucat* — shed.

**41.** The rising clouds embraced the quarters, very charmingly perfumed with the fresh fragrance and sap of blossoming kadambas, and in that very moment shed a flood of tears born of joy.

*Note.* The edition has *वासिनवतीः*; we read *vāsitavatīḥ* ("perfumed"), as the sense requires (?). The kadamba blooms in the rainy season; the quarters (*kakubh*, feminine) are the beloveds of the clouds. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 42

करुणासवेन मधुरे मधुरे
चरणाम्बुजेऽस्य भुवि राजति किम् ।
इह मादृशैरिति ममज्ज तदा
सरसीरुहां ततिरियं सरसि ॥४२॥

*karuṇāsavena madhure madhure*
*caraṇāmbuje 'sya bhuvi rājati kim |*
*iha mādṛśair iti mamajja tadā*
*sarasīruhāṁ tatir iyaṁ sarasi ||42||*

*Word for word:* *karuṇā* — of mercy; *āsavena* — with the wine; *madhure madhure* — sweetest; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *ambuje* — when the lotus; *asya* — His; *bhuvi* — on earth; *rājati* — shines; *kim* — what [use]; *iha* — here; *mādṛśaiḥ* — of such as we; *iti* — [thinking] thus; *mamajja* — sank; *tadā* — then; *sarasīruhām* — of lotuses; *tatiḥ* — the row; *iyam* — this; *sarasi* — in the lake.

**42.** "When the lotus of His feet, sweetest with the wine of mercy, shines on earth, what use is there here of such as we?" — [thinking] thus, this row of lotuses then sank in the lake.

*Note.* In the rainy season lotuses go under the water.

### Verse 43

हरिणीदृशां कुटिलमेदुरस-
त्कचपाशभासुररुचो जलदाः ।
चपलाचयैर्मधुरतां दधिरे
स्फुटकेतकाङ्कितमालतरोः ॥४३॥

*hariṇī-dṛśāṁ kuṭila-medura-sat-*
*kaca-pāśa-bhāsura-ruco jaladāḥ |*
*capalā-cayair madhuratāṁ dadhire*
*sphuṭa-ketakāṅkita-tamāla-taroḥ ||43||*

*Word for word:* *hariṇī* — of a doe; *dṛśām* — of [women with] eyes; *kuṭila* — curling; *medura* — thick; *sat* — lovely; *kaca* — of hair; *pāśa* — the tresses; *bhāsura* — gleaming; *rucaḥ* — [with] lustre [like]; *jaladāḥ* — the clouds; *capalā* — of lightning; *cayaiḥ* — with swarms; *madhuratām* — the charm; *dadhire* — took on; *sphuṭa* — blossoming; *ketaka* — with ketakas; *aṅkita* — marked; *tamāla* — tamala; *taroḥ* — of a tree.

**43.** The clouds, with a gleaming lustre like the curling, thick, lovely tresses of doe-eyed women, took on with their swarms of lightning the charm of a tamala tree marked with blossoming ketakas.

*Note.* The tamala is a tree with dark bark (an image of Krishna); the ketaka is a fragrant flower with golden-white petals (the lightning on the cloud). The edition has *केतकाङ्कित तमालतरोः* as two words; we read them as a compound.

### Verse 44

लघु नृत्यतोऽस्य चरणाम्बुरुहं
क्षितिसङ्गमो व्यथयते बहुशः ।
इति चिन्तया जलमुचः सलिलै-
र्मृदुलां सदैव धरणीं विदधुः ॥४४॥

*laghu nṛtyato 'sya caraṇāmburuhaṁ*
*kṣiti-saṅgamo vyathayate bahuśaḥ |*
*iti cintayā jala-mucaḥ salilair*
*mṛdulāṁ sadaiva dharaṇīṁ vidadhuḥ ||44||*

*Word for word:* *laghu* — lightly; *nṛtyataḥ* — of [Him] dancing; *asya* — His; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *amburuham* — the lotus; *kṣiti* — with the earth; *saṅgamaḥ* — contact; *vyathayate* — pains; *bahuśaḥ* — greatly; *iti* — thus; *cintayā* — with the thought; *jala-mucaḥ* — the clouds; *salilaiḥ* — with waters; *mṛdulām* — soft; *sadā eva* — always; *dharaṇīm* — the earth; *vidadhuḥ* — made.

**44.** "When He dances lightly, contact with the earth greatly pains the lotus of His feet" — with this thought the clouds always made the earth soft with their waters.

### Verse 45

स यदा सुखेन तनुते नटनं
विलसत्पदाम्बुजविलासरसः ।
जलदास्तदैव करुणैकनिधे-
र्ललितातपत्रसुषमां दधति ॥४५॥

*sa yadā sukhena tanute naṭanaṁ*
*vilasat-padāmbuja-vilāsa-rasaḥ |*
*jaladās tadaiva karuṇaika-nidher*
*lalitātapatra-suṣamāṁ dadhati ||45||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — He; *yadā* — when; *sukhena* — joyfully; *tanute* — performs; *naṭanam* — the dance; *vilasat* — shining; *pada* — of the feet; *ambuja* — of the lotuses; *vilāsa* — of the play; *rasaḥ* — [savouring] the delight; *jaladāḥ* — the clouds; *tadā eva* — at that very moment; *karuṇā* — of mercy; *eka* — of the one; *nidheḥ* — of the treasury; *lalita* — of a charming; *ātapatra* — parasol; *suṣamām* — the beauty; *dadhati* — take on.

**45.** When He, savouring the delight of the play of His shining lotus feet, joyfully performs His dance, at that very moment the clouds take on the beauty of a charming parasol over the one treasury of mercy.

*Note.* The parasol (*ātapatra*) is an emblem of royalty.

### Verse 46

नवविद्रुमद्रुमकदम्बरुचा
पदपल्लवस्य मधुरच्छटया ।
धरणीं चकार करुणाब्धिरसा-
वरुणायितामरुणपाणितलः ॥४६॥

*nava-vidruma-druma-kadamba-rucā*
*pada-pallavasya madhura-cchaṭayā |*
*dharaṇīṁ cakāra karuṇābdhir asāv*
*aruṇāyitām aruṇa-pāṇi-talaḥ ||46||*

*Word for word:* *nava* — of fresh; *vidruma* — coral; *druma* — trees; *kadamba* — of a grove; *rucā* — with the lustre; *pada* — of the feet; *pallavasya* — of the sprouts; *madhura* — with the sweet; *chaṭayā* — radiance; *dharaṇīm* — the earth; *cakāra* — made; *karuṇā* — of mercy; *abdhiḥ* — the ocean; *asau* — He; *aruṇāyitām* — reddened; *aruṇa* — reddish; *pāṇi* — of the hands; *talaḥ* — [with] the palms.

**46.** With the sweet radiance of His sprout-like feet, lustrous as a grove of fresh coral trees, He, the ocean of mercy, whose palms are reddish, made the earth red.

*Note.* Here *kadamba* means "multitude, grove" (cf. verse 6, where the edition has *कड़म्ब*).

### Verse 47

तपनीयगौरवपुषो महसा
नटतोऽस्य वारिदबलवत्तिमिराः ।
ककुभो विभिन्नरुचयो मिलितां
मृगनाभिकुङ्कुमरुचं विदधुः ॥४७॥

*tapanīya-gaura-vapuṣo mahasā*
*naṭato 'sya vārida-balavat-timirāḥ |*
*kakubho vibhinna-rucayo militāṁ*
*mṛganābhi-kuṅkuma-rucaṁ vidadhuḥ ||47||*

*Word for word:* *tapanīya* — as refined gold; *gaura* — golden; *vapuṣaḥ* — of [Him with] a body; *mahasā* — by the splendour; *naṭataḥ* — dancing; *asya* — of Him; *vārida* — of the clouds; *bala* — by the might; *vat* — possessing; *timirāḥ* — darkness; *kakubhaḥ* — the quarters; *vibhinna* — mixed; *rucayaḥ* — [with] lustre; *militām* — blended; *mṛganābhi* — of musk; *kuṅkuma* — and kunkuma; *rucam* — the lustre; *vidadhuḥ* — took on.

**47.** By the splendour of Him dancing, His body golden as refined gold, the quarters, dark with the might of the clouds, their lustre mixed [with His], took on the blended lustre of musk and kunkuma.

*Note.* Musk is dark, kunkuma golden-red: the darkness of the clouds and the gold of Gaura. *Vārida-balavat-timirāḥ* is understood as "with darkness from the might of the clouds" (*balavat-timira* may also be simply "deep darkness"). The Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *militāḥ* ("blended", of the quarters).

### Verse 48

तत आगतश्च हरिदासमहा-
महिताशयं सुमहनीयगुणम् ।
निजपादपङ्कजमधून्मदस-
द्भ्रमरं विलोक्य मुमुदे स विभुः ॥४८॥

*tata āgataś ca haridāsa-mahā-*
*mahitāśayaṁ su-mahanīya-guṇam |*
*nija-pāda-paṅkaja-madhūnmada-sad-*
*bhramaraṁ vilokya mumude sa vibhuḥ ||48||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *āgataḥ* — having come; *ca* — and; *haridāsa* — Haridasa; *mahā* — very; *mahita* — exalted; *āśayam* — [of] heart; *su* — most; *mahanīya* — worthy of honour; *guṇam* — [with] qualities; *nija* — of His own; *pāda* — of the feet; *paṅkaja* — of the lotus; *madhu* — by the honey; *unmada* — maddened; *sat* — fine; *bhramaram* — a bee; *vilokya* — having seen; *mumude* — rejoiced; *saḥ* — that; *vibhuḥ* — all-pervading Lord.

**48.** Then, having come, the all-pervading Lord saw Haridasa — of a most exalted heart, with qualities most worthy of honour, a fine bee maddened by the honey of His own lotus feet — and rejoiced.

*Note.* Haridasa Thakura, the "namacharya" (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Antya 3, 11). *Āgataś ca* formally refers to the Lord; by the sense it may also be understood: "seeing that Haridasa had come".

### Verse 49

परिरभ्य निर्भरममुं सहसा
स्वपदाब्जभक्तमनुरक्ततमम् ।
वरमासनं करुणया स्वजनै-
र्नयनश्रियानयदनेककृपः ॥४९॥

*parirabhya nirbharam amuṁ sahasā*
*sva-padābja-bhaktam anuraktatamam |*
*varam āsanaṁ karuṇayā sva-janair*
*nayana-śriyānayad aneka-kṛpaḥ ||49||*

*Word for word:* *parirabhya* — having embraced; *nirbharam* — tightly; *amum* — him; *sahasā* — at once; *sva* — of His own; *pada* — of the feet; *abja* — of the lotus; *bhaktam* — the devotee; *anuraktatamam* — most devoted; *varam* — an excellent; *āsanam* — seat; *karuṇayā* — mercifully; *sva* — by His own; *janaiḥ* — people; *nayana* — of the eyes; *śriyā* — by the grace; *anayat* — had brought; *aneka* — of manifold; *kṛpaḥ* — [the Lord] of mercy.

**49.** At once tightly embracing him, the most devoted servant of His own lotus feet, the Lord of manifold mercy, by the grace of His eyes, mercifully had His own people bring an excellent seat.

*Note.* "By the grace of His eyes": by a sign of His glance.

### Verse 50

अभिवाद्य तत्तु शिरसा प्रणतो
वरमासनं भुवि चकार पदम् ।
प्रभुपादपङ्कजपरागचयं
परिगृह्य भक्तिपरया सधिया ॥५०॥

*abhivādya tat tu śirasā praṇato*
*varam āsanaṁ bhuvi cakāra padam |*
*prabhu-pāda-paṅkaja-parāga-cayaṁ*
*parigṛhya bhakti-parayā sa-dhiyā ||50||*

*Word for word:* *abhivādya* — having saluted; *tat* — that (seat); *tu* — but; *śirasā* — with his head; *praṇataḥ* — bowing; *varam* — an excellent; *āsanam* — seat; *bhuvi* — on the ground; *cakāra* — made; *padam* — [his] place; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *pāda* — of the feet; *paṅkaja* — of the lotus; *parāga* — of pollen; *cayam* — a heap; *parigṛhya* — having taken; *bhakti* — on devotion; *parayā* — intent; *sa-dhiyā* — with a mind.

**50.** But he, bowing, saluted that seat with his head and made his place on the bare ground his excellent seat, having taken, with a mind intent on devotion, a heap of pollen from the lotus feet of the Lord.

*Note.* Haridasa's humility: a Muslim by birth, he does not sit on the seat of honour (cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Antya 11).

### Verse 51

तनुमस्य चन्दनरसेन तदा
परिलिप्य माल्यमवयोज्य हृदि ।
स चतुर्विधं मधुरमन्नमतः
परिभोज्य भूरिकरुणो मुमुदे ॥५१॥

*tanum asya candana-rasena tadā*
*parilipya mālyam avayojya hṛdi |*
*sa catur-vidhaṁ madhuram annam ataḥ*
*paribhojya bhūri-karuṇo mumude ||51||*

*Word for word:* *tanum* — the body; *asya* — his; *candana* — of sandal; *rasena* — with the paste; *tadā* — then; *parilipya* — having anointed; *mālyam* — a garland; *avayojya* — having placed; *hṛdi* — on the chest; *saḥ* — He; *catuḥ* — of four; *vidham* — kinds; *madhuram* — sweet; *annam* — food; *ataḥ* — then; *paribhojya* — having fed; *bhūri* — immensely; *karuṇaḥ* — merciful; *mumude* — rejoiced.

**51.** Then the immensely merciful [Lord] anointed his body with sandal paste, placed a garland on his chest, and then fed him sweet food of four kinds — and rejoiced.

*Note.* The four kinds of food are those that are chewed, sucked, licked and drunk (*carvya*, *coṣya*, *lehya*, *peya*).

### Verse 52

अनुनृत्य सोऽपि हरिकीर्त्तनतः
सततं प्रभोर्निलय एव बभौ ।
अवलोक्य तञ्च निजपादयुग-
प्रियमाननन्द स तु गौरशशी ॥५२॥

*anunṛtya so 'pi hari-kīrtanataḥ*
*satataṁ prabhor nilaya eva babhau |*
*avalokya tañ ca nija-pāda-yuga-*
*priyam ānananda sa tu gaura-śaśī ||52||*

*Word for word:* *anunṛtya* — dancing after; *saḥ* — he; *api* — too; *hari* — of Hari; *kīrtanataḥ* — to the kirtana; *satatam* — constantly; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *nilaye* — in the house; *eva* — very; *babhau* — shone; *avalokya* — seeing; *tam* — him; *ca* — and; *nija* — His own; *pāda* — of feet; *yuga* — the pair; *priyam* — loving; *ānananda* — rejoiced; *saḥ* — He; *tu* — and; *gaura* — Gaura; *śaśī* — the moon.

**52.** And he too, dancing after [the Lord] to the kirtana of Hari, constantly shone in the very house of the Lord; and Gaura, the moon, rejoiced, seeing him, the lover of His pair of feet.

*Note.* The edition has *निलयएव* as one word.

### Verse 53

अथ तत्र तेन सह देवघटा-
मुकुटार्घ्यरत्नरुचिराजिपदः ।
गमनाय गेहमभितः सहसा
गतवन्तमाह गिरिशं स विभुः ॥५३॥

*atha tatra tena saha deva-ghaṭā-*
*mukuṭārghya-ratna-ruci-rāji-padaḥ |*
*gamanāya geham abhitaḥ sahasā*
*gatavantam āha giriśaṁ sa vibhuḥ ||53||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *tatra* — there; *tena* — him; *saha* — with; *deva* — of gods; *ghaṭā* — of the host; *mukuṭa* — of the crowns; *arghya* — precious; *ratna* — of the gems; *ruci* — of lustre; *rāji* — [lit by] a line; *padaḥ* — [whose] feet; *gamanāya* — to go; *geham abhitaḥ* — home; *sahasā* — at once; *gatavantam* — who had come; *āha* — told; *giriśam* — Girisha; *saḥ* — that; *vibhuḥ* — all-pervading Lord.

**53.** Then the all-pervading Lord, whose feet [are lit by] a line of lustre from the precious gems in the crowns of the host of gods, told Girisha, who had come there together with him [Haridasa], to go home at once.

*Note.* Girisha is Advaita (verse 30). The gods touch the Lord's feet with their crowns as they bow.

### Verse 54

स तथेति तस्य वचनाद्गिरिशः
पृथिवीतलेषु कमलाक्ष इति ।
प्रथितो य एष भवनं मुदितः
स ययौ जगत्प्रभुगिरा परया ॥५४॥

*sa tatheti tasya vacanād giriśaḥ*
*pṛthivī-taleṣu kamalākṣa iti |*
*prathito ya eṣa bhavanaṁ muditaḥ*
*sa yayau jagat-prabhu-girā parayā ||54||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — He; *tathā iti* — "so be it"; *tasya* — His; *vacanāt* — at the word; *giriśaḥ* — Girisha; *pṛthivī* — of the earth; *taleṣu* — on the surfaces; *kamalākṣaḥ* — Kamalaksha; *iti* — as; *prathitaḥ* — renowned; *yaḥ eṣaḥ* — He who; *bhavanam* — home; *muditaḥ* — joyful; *saḥ* — He; *yayau* — went; *jagat* — of the world; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *girā* — by the word; *parayā* — supreme.

**54.** "So be it," [said] Girisha, He who is renowned on the face of the earth as Kamalaksha; and at the Lord's word He joyfully went home, [led] by the supreme word of the Lord of the world.

### Verse 55

अवधूतमीश्वरमथो विनया-
न्निजगाद तं जिगमिषुं यमिनम् ।
समनुव्रजन्निति विधेहि विभो
सुमहाप्रसादममलं वसनम् ॥५५॥

*avadhūtam īśvaram atho vinayān*
*nijagāda taṁ jigamiṣuṁ yaminam |*
*samanuvrajann iti vidhehi vibho*
*su-mahā-prasādam amalaṁ vasanam ||55||*

*Word for word:* *avadhūtam* — to the avadhuta; *īśvaram* — to the master; *atho* — then; *vinayāt* — humbly; *nijagāda* — said; *tam* — to Him; *jigamiṣum* — wishing to go; *yaminam* — to the ascetic; *samanuvrajan* — accompanying; *iti* — thus; *vidhehi* — accept; *vibho* — O mighty one; *su* — most; *mahā* — great; *prasādam* — prasada; *amalam* — spotless; *vasanam* — cloth.

**55.** Then, accompanying the avadhuta — the master, the ascetic who wished to depart — [the Lord] humbly said to Him: "O mighty one, accept this most great prasada, a spotless cloth."

### Verse 56

इति तद्बहिर्वसनमेकमसौ
परिगृह्य कारुणिकतां रचयन् ।
निजपादजीवनधनेभ्य ऋते
कमलाक्षदेवमददात् करुणः ॥५६॥

*iti tad-bahir-vasanam ekam asau*
*parigṛhya kāruṇikatāṁ racayan |*
*nija-pāda-jīvana-dhanebhya ṛte*
*kamalākṣa-devam adadāt karuṇaḥ ||56||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *tat* — of them; *bahiḥ* — outer; *vasanam* — garment; *ekam* — one; *asau* — He; *parigṛhya* — having taken; *kāruṇikatām* — compassion; *racayan* — showing; *nija* — His own; *pāda* — feet; *jīvana* — of life; *dhanebhyaḥ* — to [those whose] treasure; *ṛte* — except; *kamalākṣa-devam* — Kamalaksha Deva; *adadāt* — gave; *karuṇaḥ* — compassionate.

**56.** Thus [addressed], He took one outer garment of them, and, showing compassion, the compassionate [Nityananda] gave [the rest] to those whose life's treasure is His feet — except Kamalaksha Deva.

*Note.* The edition reads *nijagāda* ("said"), which does not fit; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *nija-pāda-jīvana-dhanebhyaḥ*, "to those whose life's treasure is His feet", and so we read. Why Advaita is excepted is unclear (He has already gone home, verse 54).

### Verse 57

अभिवाद्य तत्तु शिरसा त इमे
प्रभुणा समं स्वगृहमेव ययुः ।
द्युनदीजलेषु विहिताप्लवनाः
कृतपूजना अपि यथाविधि ते ॥५७॥

*abhivādya tat tu śirasā ta ime*
*prabhuṇā samaṁ sva-gṛham eva yayuḥ |*
*dyu-nadī-jaleṣu vihitāplavanāḥ*
*kṛta-pūjanā api yathā-vidhi te ||57||*

*Word for word:* *abhivādya* — having saluted; *tat* — that; *tu* — and; *śirasā* — with the head; *te ime* — they; *prabhuṇā* — the master (Nityananda); *samam* — with; *sva* — to their own; *gṛham* — homes; *eva* — indeed; *yayuḥ* — went; *dyu* — of the heavenly; *nadī* — river; *jaleṣu* — in the waters; *vihita* — having made; *āplavanāḥ* — a bath; *kṛta* — having performed; *pūjanāḥ* — worship; *api* — and; *yathā-vidhi* — according to the rules; *te* — they.

**57.** Saluting that [gift] with their heads, they went with the master [Nityananda] to their own homes; they bathed in the waters of the heavenly river and performed worship according to the rules.

### Verse 58

अनुसन्ध्यमाययुरथो निलये
परमेश्वरस्य परमोल्लसिताः ।
स उपागतः सहृदयैः परमै-
र्जगतां प्रभुः प्रभवता महसा ॥५८॥

*anusandhyam āyayur atho nilaye*
*parameśvarasya paramollasitāḥ |*
*sa upāgataḥ sahṛdayaiḥ paramair*
*jagatāṁ prabhuḥ prabhavatā mahasā ||58||*

*Word for word:* *anusandhyam* — towards evening; *āyayuḥ* — came; *atho* — then; *nilaye* — to the abode; *parama* — of the Supreme; *īśvarasya* — Lord; *parama* — exceedingly; *ullasitāḥ* — jubilant; *saḥ* — that; *upāgataḥ* — came; *sahṛdayaiḥ* — with intimate [friends]; *paramaiḥ* — the best; *jagatām* — of the worlds; *prabhuḥ* — master; *prabhavatā* — with a powerful; *mahasā* — splendour.

**58.** Then, towards evening, exceedingly jubilant, they came to the abode of the Supreme Lord. That master of the worlds [Nityananda] also came, with the best of His intimate friends, with a powerful splendour.

### Verse 59

महता महेन महनीयतनु-
र्निजकीर्त्तनं नटनमप्यकरोत् ।
स तु चक्रवद्भ्रमणविभ्रमसं-
प्रसरन्महःसमुदयेन तदा ।
तिरयन्निलावृतविलासरुचं
रुचिराननो रुचिरवागमृतः ॥५९॥

*mahatā mahena mahanīya-tanur*
*nija-kīrtanaṁ naṭanam apy akarot |*
*sa tu cakravad-bhramaṇa-vibhrama-saṁ-*
*prasaran-mahaḥ-samudayena tadā |*
*tirayann ilāvṛta-vilāsa-rucaṁ*
*rucirānano rucira-vāg-amṛtaḥ ||59||*

*Word for word:* *mahatā* — with great; *mahena* — splendour; *mahanīya* — worthy of honour; *tanuḥ* — [with] a body; *nija* — His own; *kīrtanam* — kirtana; *naṭanam* — dance; *api* — and; *akarot* — performed; *saḥ* — He; *tu* — and; *cakravat* — like a wheel; *bhramaṇa* — of whirling; *vibhrama* — from the play; *saṁprasarat* — spreading; *mahaḥ* — of splendour; *samudayena* — by the mass; *tadā* — then; *tirayan* — eclipsing; *ilāvṛta* — of Ilavrita; *vilāsa* — of the delights; *rucam* — the lustre; *rucira* — lovely; *ānanaḥ* — [with] a face; *rucira* — lovely; *vāk* — of words; *amṛtaḥ* — [with] the nectar.

**59.** He, whose body is worthy of honour, performed with great splendour His own kirtana and dance. And then, whirling like a wheel, by the mass of splendour spreading from the play of His whirling He eclipsed the lustre of the delights of Ilavrita — He of the lovely face and the lovely nectar of words.

*Note.* The verse has six padas. On Ilavrita cf. 5.59. *Nija-kīrtana*, "His own kirtana", i.e. the kirtana of Nityananda. *Mahena* (from *maha*) may also be taken as "with a great festival".

### Verse 60

नटनान्तरे निजजनान् परितः
परिरभ्य निर्भरमथो सह तैः ।
विलुठन् करणाम्बुजयुगेन मुदं
प्रहसन्मृगेन्द्र इव संप्रबभौ ॥६०॥

*naṭanāntare nija-janān paritaḥ*
*parirabhya nirbharam atho saha taiḥ |*
*viluṭhan karaṇāmbuja-yugena mudaṁ*
*prahasan mṛgendra iva saṁprababhau ||60||*

*Word for word:* *naṭana* — of dancing; *antare* — in the intervals; *nija* — His own; *janān* — people; *paritaḥ* — on all sides; *parirabhya* — having embraced; *nirbharam* — tightly; *atho* — then; *saha* — together; *taiḥ* — with them; *viluṭhan* — rolling; *kara* — of hands; *ambuja* — of lotuses; *yugena* — with the pair (?); *mudam* — with joy; *prahasan* — laughing aloud; *mṛga-indraḥ* — the king of beasts (a lion); *iva* — like; *saṁprababhau* — shone forth.

**60.** In the intervals of dancing He tightly embraced His own people on all sides, and then, rolling [on the ground] together with them, [with] His pair of lotus hands [outspread], laughing aloud with joy, He shone forth like a lion.

*Note.* The edition has *करणाम्बुज-*, a syllable too many for the metre; we read *karāmbuja-* ("lotus hands") (?). The verse might be referred to the Lord, but verse 61 shows that it concerns Nityananda.

### Verse 61

चिरमेवमेव धरणीषु विभुः
परिलुठ्य भक्तनिचयान्तरतः ।
भुवि नारदो य इह विप्रवरः
परिगृह्य तं प्रभुवरोऽन्तरधात् ॥६१॥

*ciram evam eva dharaṇīṣu vibhuḥ*
*pariluṭhya bhakta-nicayāntarataḥ |*
*bhuvi nārado ya iha vipra-varaḥ*
*parigṛhya taṁ prabhu-varo 'ntaradhāt ||61||*

*Word for word:* *ciram* — for a long time; *evam eva* — thus; *dharaṇīṣu* — on the ground; *vibhuḥ* — the lord; *pariluṭhya* — having rolled about; *bhakta* — of devotees; *nicaya* — the crowd; *antarataḥ* — in the midst of; *bhuvi* — on earth; *nāradaḥ* — Narada; *yaḥ* — who; *iha* — here; *vipra* — of brahmanas; *varaḥ* — the best; *parigṛhya* — having taken; *tam* — him; *prabhu* — of lords; *varaḥ* — the best; *antaradhāt* — disappeared.

**61.** Having rolled about thus on the ground for a long time in the midst of the crowd of devotees, the best of lords took with Him that best of brahmanas who here on earth is Narada [Srivasa] and disappeared.

*Note.* That is, Nityananda disappeared together with Srivasa. The epithets *vibhuḥ* and *prabhu-varaḥ* could also denote the Lord; possibly it is the Lord Himself who disappears with Srivasa, as in Murari (2.10.12–13); cf. verse 63, where Gaura appears before the grieving devotees.

### Verse 62

न समीक्ष्यतेऽथ भृशमाकुलिता-
स्तमितस्ततः समनुसन्दधिरे ।
त इतस्ततोऽथ न समीक्ष्य भृशं
विकला बभूवुरतिदुःखभरैः ॥६२॥

*na samīkṣyate 'tha bhṛśam ākulitās*
*tam itas tataḥ samanusandadhire |*
*ta itas tato 'tha na samīkṣya bhṛśaṁ*
*vikalā babhūvur ati-duḥkha-bharaiḥ ||62||*

*Word for word:* *na* — not; *samīkṣyate* — is seen; *atha* — then; *bhṛśam* — greatly; *ākulitāḥ* — alarmed; *tam* — for Him; *itaḥ tataḥ* — here and there; *samanusandadhire* — searched; *te* — they; *itaḥ tataḥ* — here and there; *atha* — and; *na* — not; *samīkṣya* — having found; *bhṛśam* — utterly; *vikalāḥ* — bewildered; *babhūvuḥ* — became; *ati* — of great; *duḥkha* — sorrow; *bharaiḥ* — by the weight.

**62.** "He is not to be seen!" — and, greatly alarmed, they searched for Him here and there. Not finding Him anywhere, they became utterly bewildered under the weight of great sorrow.

### Verse 63

अथ तांस्तथाविधहृदः करुणा-
नधिगम्य भूरिकरुणो मधुरः ।
विकिरन्मनोज्ञतमदृष्टिसुधां
स तु गौरचन्द्र उदियाय ततः ॥६३॥

*atha tāṁs tathā-vidha-hṛdaḥ karuṇān*
*adhigamya bhūri-karuṇo madhuraḥ |*
*vikiran manojñatama-dṛṣṭi-sudhāṁ*
*sa tu gauracandra udiyāya tataḥ ||63||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *tān* — them; *tathā* — such; *vidha* — [being] of a kind; *hṛdaḥ* — whose hearts; *karuṇān* — piteous; *adhigamya* — having understood; *bhūri* — boundlessly; *karuṇaḥ* — compassionate; *madhuraḥ* — sweet; *vikiran* — scattering; *manojñatama* — most enchanting; *dṛṣṭi* — of the glance; *sudhām* — the nectar; *saḥ* — He; *tu* — and; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra; *udiyāya* — rose; *tataḥ* — then.

**63.** Then the boundlessly compassionate, sweet Gaurachandra, understanding them to be piteous, their hearts in such a state, rose [before them like the moon], scattering the nectar of His most enchanting glance.

### Verse 64

अभितोऽभितस्तमभिगौररुचं
कमलाननं करुणया परया ।
परिलोकयन्तमतिसान्द्रमुदं
नयनैर्नितान्तमपिबन्निव ते ॥६४॥

*abhito 'bhitas tam abhi-gaura-rucaṁ*
*kamalānanaṁ karuṇayā parayā |*
*parilokayantam ati-sāndra-mudaṁ*
*nayanair nitāntam apibann iva te ||64||*

*Word for word:* *abhitaḥ abhitaḥ* — from all sides; *tam* — Him; *abhi* — all around; *gaura* — golden; *rucam* — [with] a lustre; *kamala* — lotus-; *ānanam* — faced; *karuṇayā* — with mercy; *parayā* — supreme; *parilokayantam* — looking around; *ati* — very; *sāndra* — deep; *mudam* — [with] joy; *nayanaiḥ* — with their eyes; *nitāntam* — insatiably; *apiban* — drank; *iva* — as if; *te* — they.

**64.** And from all sides they, as it were, insatiably drank with their eyes Him — the lotus-faced One, surrounded by a golden lustre, full of very deep joy, looking around at all with supreme mercy.

### Verse 65

तदनन्तरञ्च रभसाकुलितैः
सह तैः स्वपादयुगमात्रधनैः ।
निजकीर्त्तनामृतरसेन मुहु-
र्नटनं चकार रससिन्धुशशी ॥६५॥

*tad-anantarañ ca rabhasākulitaiḥ*
*saha taiḥ sva-pāda-yuga-mātra-dhanaiḥ |*
*nija-kīrtanāmṛta-rasena muhur*
*naṭanaṁ cakāra rasa-sindhu-śaśī ||65||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — that; *anantaram* — after; *ca* — and; *rabhasa* — by fervour; *ākulitaiḥ* — overwhelmed; *saha* — together; *taiḥ* — with them; *sva* — His; *pāda* — of feet; *yuga* — the pair; *mātra* — the only; *dhanaiḥ* — [whose] wealth; *nija* — of His own; *kīrtana* — of the kirtana; *amṛta* — of the nectar; *rasena* — with the rapture; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *naṭanam* — dancing; *cakāra* — performed; *rasa* — of rasa; *sindhu* — of the ocean; *śaśī* — the moon.

**65.** And after that the moon of the ocean of rasa danced again and again, in the rapture of the nectar of His own kirtana, together with them — overwhelmed by fervour, whose only wealth is the pair of His feet.

### Verse 66

अथ कर्हिचिद्बहुविलासनिधी
रजनीमुखे सुखमयाम्बुनिधिः ।
अवकृष्य भक्तजनवस्त्रचयं
परितो विलस्य पुनरेव ददौ ॥६६॥

*atha karhicid bahu-vilāsa-nidhī*
*rajanī-mukhe sukha-mayāmbunidhiḥ |*
*avakṛṣya bhakta-jana-vastra-cayaṁ*
*parito vilasya punar eva dadau ||66||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *karhicit* — once; *bahu* — of many; *vilāsa* — pastimes; *nidhiḥ* — the treasury; *rajanī* — of the night; *mukhe* — at the beginning; *sukha* — of happiness; *maya* — consisting; *ambunidhiḥ* — the ocean; *avakṛṣya* — having pulled off; *bhakta* — of the devotees; *jana* — of the people; *vastra* — garments; *cayam* — all; *paritaḥ* — all around; *vilasya* — having frolicked; *punaḥ eva* — again; *dadau* — gave back.

**66.** Then once, at the beginning of the night, the treasury of many pastimes, the ocean of happiness, pulled off all the garments of the devotees, frolicked [with them] all around, and gave them back again.

*Note.* An echo of Krishna's *vastra-haraṇa-līlā* (the stealing of the gopis' garments). The edition's *निधी* stands for *nidhiḥ* before *r* (sandhi).

### Verse 67

तदनन्तरं पुनरतीवसुखा-
दवधूत ईश्वर उपेत्य ततः ।
अवलोक्य गौरमतिसान्द्ररुचं
मधुरं जगौ नटनमप्यकरोत् ॥६७॥

*tad-anantaraṁ punar atīva-sukhād*
*avadhūta īśvara upetya tataḥ |*
*avalokya gauram ati-sāndra-rucaṁ*
*madhuraṁ jagau naṭanam apy akarot ||67||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — that; *anantaram* — after; *punaḥ* — again; *atīva* — from great; *sukhāt* — happiness; *avadhūtaḥ* — the avadhuta; *īśvaraḥ* — the master; *upetya* — having come; *tataḥ* — there; *avalokya* — having seen; *gauram* — Gaura; *ati* — very; *sāndra* — dense; *rucam* — [with] radiance; *madhuram* — sweetly; *jagau* — sang; *naṭanam* — dancing; *api* — also; *akarot* — performed.

**67.** After that the avadhuta, the master, came there again and, seeing Gaura in His dense radiance, from great happiness sang sweetly and danced.

### Verse 68

नटनान्तरे तु भगवान् जगतां
प्रभुरादिदेश निजभक्तजनान् ।
अवधूतपादकमलस्य शुभा-
न्यवनेजनानि पिबत क्रमतः ॥६८॥

*naṭanāntare tu bhagavān jagatāṁ*
*prabhur ādideśa nija-bhakta-janān |*
*avadhūta-pāda-kamalasya śubhāny*
*avanejanāni pibata kramataḥ ||68||*

*Word for word:* *naṭana* — of the dancing; *antare* — in an interval; *tu* — and; *bhagavān* — Bhagavan; *jagatām* — of the worlds; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *ādideśa* — commanded; *nija* — His own; *bhakta* — devotees; *janān* — the people; *avadhūta* — of the avadhuta; *pāda* — of the feet; *kamalasya* — of the lotus; *śubhāni* — auspicious; *avanejanāni* — the washings [the water]; *pibata* — drink; *kramataḥ* — in turn.

**68.** And in an interval of the dancing Bhagavan, the Lord of the worlds, commanded His devotees: "Drink in turn the auspicious water that has washed the lotus feet of the avadhuta."

*Note.* *Pādodaka*, *caraṇāmṛta* — the water that has washed the feet of a saint.

### Verse 69

त इदं निशम्य वचनं शिरसा
प्रणतेन तत्पदपयांसि दधुः ।
उपजीविनश्चरणपङ्करुहो
वचने भवन्ति सततं निरताः ॥६९॥

*ta idaṁ niśamya vacanaṁ śirasā*
*praṇatena tat-pada-payāṁsi dadhuḥ |*
*upajīvinaś caraṇa-paṅkaruho*
*vacane bhavanti satataṁ niratāḥ ||69||*

*Word for word:* *te* — they; *idam* — this; *niśamya* — having heard; *vacanam* — word; *śirasā* — with the head; *praṇatena* — bowed; *tat* — His; *pada* — of the feet; *payāṁsi* — the waters; *dadhuḥ* — accepted; *upajīvinaḥ* — those who live [by the mercy]; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *paṅkaruhaḥ* — of the lotus; *vacane* — to the word; *bhavanti* — are; *satatam* — always; *niratāḥ* — devoted.

**69.** Having heard this word, they bowed their heads and accepted the water of His feet. Those who live [by the mercy] of the lotus feet [of the Lord] are always devoted to His word.

### Verse 70

वचसा विलासगमनेन कृपा-
मृदुना विलोकितरसेन ततः ।
हसितेन सान्द्रमधुरेण सुखं
विदधे जनस्य जगतां करुणः ॥७०॥

*vacasā vilāsa-gamanena kṛpā-*
*mṛdunā vilokita-rasena tataḥ |*
*hasitena sāndra-madhureṇa sukhaṁ*
*vidadhe janasya jagatāṁ karuṇaḥ ||70||*

*Word for word:* *vacasā* — with speech; *vilāsa* — playful; *gamanena* — with gait; *kṛpā* — by mercy; *mṛdunā* — softened; *vilokita* — of the glance; *rasena* — with the sweetness; *tataḥ* — then; *hasitena* — with laughter; *sāndra* — deep; *madhureṇa* — sweet; *sukham* — happiness; *vidadhe* — bestowed; *janasya* — on the people; *jagatām* — of the worlds; *karuṇaḥ* — the compassionate.

**70.** Then with His speech, His playful gait, the sweetness of His glance softened by mercy, and His deep, sweet laughter, the compassionate [Lord] bestowed happiness on the people of the worlds.

### Verse 71

विहरन्तमित्थमवलोक्य सदा
परमं प्रभुं नभसि देवगणाः ।
दयिताकुलैः प्रमदमत्तधियो
दिवसं निशाञ्च गमयन्ति मुदा ॥७१॥

*viharantam ittham avalokya sadā*
*paramaṁ prabhuṁ nabhasi deva-gaṇāḥ |*
*dayitā-kulaiḥ pramada-matta-dhiyo*
*divasaṁ niśāñ ca gamayanti mudā ||71||*

*Word for word:* *viharantam* — sporting; *ittham* — thus; *avalokya* — beholding; *sadā* — always; *paramam* — the Supreme; *prabhum* — Lord; *nabhasi* — in the sky; *deva* — of gods; *gaṇāḥ* — the hosts; *dayitā* — of beloveds; *kulaiḥ* — with the throngs; *pramada* — with rapture; *matta* — intoxicated; *dhiyaḥ* — [with] minds; *divasam* — the day; *niśām* — the night; *ca* — and; *gamayanti* — pass; *mudā* — joyfully.

**71.** Beholding the Supreme Lord always sporting thus, the hosts of the gods in the sky, together with the throngs of their beloveds, their minds intoxicated with rapture, joyfully pass their days and nights.

### Verse 72

हरिदास ईश्वर इति प्रथितः
परमो जनो दयितगौरपदः ।
पुनरेत्य नूपुरमनोज्ञपद-
द्वितयो ननर्त्त परमेशपुरः ॥७२॥

*haridāsa īśvara iti prathitaḥ*
*paramo jano dayita-gaura-padaḥ |*
*punar etya nūpura-manojña-pada-*
*dvitayo nanarta parameśa-puraḥ ||72||*

*Word for word:* *haridāsaḥ* — Haridasa; *īśvaraḥ* — a lord; *iti* — as; *prathitaḥ* — renowned; *paramaḥ* — supreme; *janaḥ* — person; *dayita* — who holds dear; *gaura* — of Gaura; *padaḥ* — the feet; *punaḥ* — again; *etya* — having come; *nūpura* — by ankle-bells; *manojña* — made charming; *pada* — of feet; *dvitayaḥ* — [with] the pair; *nanarta* — danced; *parama* — of the Supreme; *īśa* — Lord; *puraḥ* — before.

**72.** Haridasa, renowned as a lord, a supreme soul who holds dear the feet of Gaura, came again and danced before the Supreme Lord, the pair of his feet made charming by ankle-bells.

*Note.* *Īśvara* of Haridasa is an honorific "lord"; in the tradition he is an incarnation of Brahma and Prahlada (Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika 93–94). *Nūpura* — ankle-bracelets with little bells.

### Verse 73

पुनरागतः स कमलाक्षविभुः
प्रभुपादपङ्कजयुगं मृदुलम् ।
परिलोक्य हर्षविभराप्लुतधीः
सुभृशं ननन्द जगतीसुखदः ॥७३॥

*punar āgataḥ sa kamalākṣa-vibhuḥ*
*prabhu-pāda-paṅkaja-yugaṁ mṛdulam |*
*parilokya harṣa-vibharāpluta-dhīḥ*
*su-bhṛśaṁ nananda jagatī-sukhadaḥ ||73||*

*Word for word:* *punaḥ* — again; *āgataḥ* — having come; *saḥ* — that; *kamalākṣa* — Kamalaksha; *vibhuḥ* — the lord; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *pāda* — of the feet; *paṅkaja* — of lotuses; *yugam* — the pair; *mṛdulam* — tender; *parilokya* — having beheld; *harṣa* — of joy; *vibhara* — with the excess; *āpluta* — flooded; *dhīḥ* — [with] a mind; *su-bhṛśam* — immeasurably; *nananda* — rejoiced; *jagatī* — on the world; *sukha* — happiness; *daḥ* — bestowing.

**73.** The lord Kamalaksha, who bestows happiness on the world, came again and, beholding the tender pair of the Lord's lotus feet, His mind flooded with an excess of joy, rejoiced immeasurably.

### Verse 74

ललितेन पाद्यसलिलेन ततः
सह दूर्व्वयाक्षतचयैश्च ततः ।
सुमनश्चयैर्मलयजन्मरसैः
परिपूज्य तं प्रभुवरोऽन्नमदात् ॥७४॥

*lalitena pādya-salilena tataḥ*
*saha dūrvayākṣata-cayaiś ca tataḥ |*
*sumanaś-cayair malaya-janma-rasaiḥ*
*paripūjya taṁ prabhu-varo 'nnam adāt ||74||*

*Word for word:* *lalitena* — charming; *pādya* — for washing the feet; *salilena* — with water; *tataḥ* — then; *saha* — together with; *dūrvayā* — dūrvā grass; *akṣata* — of unbroken rice; *cayaiḥ* — with handfuls; *ca* — and; *tataḥ* — then; *sumanaḥ* — of flowers; *cayaiḥ* — with heaps; *malaya* — on Malaya; *janma* — born (sandalwood); *rasaiḥ* — with the juices; *paripūjya* — having worshipped; *tam* — Him; *prabhu* — of lords; *varaḥ* — the best; *annam* — food; *adāt* — gave.

**74.** Then the best of lords worshipped Him [Advaita] with charming water for washing the feet, with dūrvā grass and handfuls of unbroken rice, with heaps of flowers and with sandalwood paste — and gave Him food.

*Note.* Thus Gaura worships Advaita according to the rite (*pūjā*): *pādya*, *dūrvā* and *akṣata* (unbroken rice), flowers, sandalwood. The food is the *mahā-prasāda* of verse 75.

### Verse 75

अतिसाध्वसादररसेन ततः

हरिकीर्त्तनामृतसुखाम्बुनिधौ ॥७५॥

*ati-sādhvasādara-rasena tataḥ*

*prabhunā samaṁ pari nanarta bhṛśaṁ*
*hari-kīrtanāmṛta-sukhāmbunidhau ||75||*

*Word for word:* *ati* — with great; *sādhvasa* — awe; *ādara* — and reverence; *rasena* — with the feeling; *tataḥ* — then; *saḥ* — He; *mahā-prasādam* — the mahaprasada; *avagṛhya* — having accepted; *mudā* — joyfully; *prabhunā* — with the Lord; *samam* — together; *pari nanarta* — danced; *bhṛśam* — wildly; *hari* — of Hari; *kīrtana* — of the kirtana; *amṛta* — of the nectar; *sukha* — of happiness; *ambunidhau* — in the ocean.

**75.** Having joyfully accepted the mahaprasada with great awe and reverence, He then danced wildly together with the Lord in the ocean of happiness that is the nectar of Hari's kirtana.

### Verse 76

अथ कश्चनातिशयदीनमना-
स्तनयेन भिक्षुरनुसङ्गतया ।
नटतोऽस्य गौरशशिनः परमं
किमपीह वीक्ष्य विमुमोह ततः ॥७६॥

*atha kaścanātiśaya-dīna-manās*
*tanayena bhikṣur anusaṅgatayā |*
*naṭato 'sya gaura-śaśinaḥ paramaṁ*
*kim apīha vīkṣya vimumoha tataḥ ||76||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *kaścana* — a certain; *atiśaya* — exceedingly; *dīna* — dejected; *manāḥ* — [with] a heart; *tanayena* — by a son; *bhikṣuḥ* — mendicant; *anusaṅgatayā* — accompanied; *naṭataḥ* — dancing; *asya* — of this; *gaura* — of Gaura; *śaśinaḥ* — of the moon; *paramam* — supreme; *kim api* — something; *iha* — here; *vīkṣya* — having beheld; *vimumoha* — swooned; *tataḥ* — then.

**76.** Then a certain mendicant [wanderer] with an exceedingly dejected heart, accompanied by his son, beheld here something supreme in the dancing moon, Gaura, and swooned.

*Note.* The edition has *भिक्षुरेणुसङ्गतया*, against the metre; we read *bhikṣur anusaṅgatayā* ("accompanied [by his son]") (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

चिरमुत्थितस्तु स जगाद तदा

समकीर्त्तयल्ललितगीतकलाम् ॥७७॥

*ciram utthitas tu sa jagāda tadā*
*kim aho vilokitam aho kim iti |*

*samakīrtayal lalita-gīta-kalām ||77||*

*Word for word:* *ciram* — after a long time; *utthitaḥ* — having risen; *tu* — and; *saḥ* — he; *jagāda* — said; *tadā* — then; *kim* — what; *aho* — oh; *vilokitam* — has been seen; *aho* — oh; *kim* — what; *iti* — thus; *tat* — that; *anantaram* — after; *ca* — and; *saha* — together; *taiḥ* — with them; *muditaḥ* — joyful; *samakīrtayat* — sang; *lalita* — charming; *gīta* — of song; *kalām* — the art.

**77.** Rising after a long time, he then said: "Oh, what have I seen? Oh, what [was it]?" And after that, joyful, he sang together with them with the charming art of song.

र्द्विगुणीभवत्तनुरतीवसुखी ।
नयनाम्बुभिः सततधौततनू
रससागरे परिममज्ज भृशम् ॥७८॥

*iti bhikṣur eṣa vipulaiḥ pulakair*
*dviguṇī-bhavat-tanur atīva-sukhī |*

*rasa-sāgare parimamajja bhṛśam ||78||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *bhikṣuḥ* — mendicant; *eṣaḥ* — this; *vipulaiḥ* — abundant; *pulakaiḥ* — with hairs standing on end; *dviguṇī* — twofold; *bhavat* — becoming; *tanuḥ* — [with] a body; *atīva* — immensely; *sukhī* — happy; *nayana* — of the eyes; *ambubhiḥ* — with the waters; *satata* — constantly; *dhauta* — washed; *tanūḥ* — [with] a body; *rasa* — of rasa; *sāgare* — in the ocean; *parimamajja* — plunged; *bhṛśam* — wholly.

**78.** Thus this mendicant, immensely happy — his body seeming to double in size with the abundance of hairs standing on end, and constantly washed by the waters of his eyes — plunged wholly into the ocean of rasa.

### Verse 79

अथ कर्हिचिद्द्विजकुलैकशशी

अपठद्बृहत्पदयुतं प्रथमं
सहस्रनामकृतपैत्रकृतिः ॥७९॥

*atha karhicid dvija-kulaika-śaśī*
*bhuvi yas tu nārada iti prathitaḥ |*
*apaṭhad bṛhat-pada-yutaṁ prathamaṁ*
*sahasra-nāma kṛta-paitra-kṛtiḥ ||79||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *karhicit* — once; *dvija* — of the twice-born; *kula* — of the race; *eka* — the one; *śaśī* — moon; *bhuvi* — on earth; *yaḥ* — who; *tu* — and; *nāradaḥ* — Narada; *iti* — as; *prathitaḥ* — renowned; *apaṭhat* — recited; *bṛhat* — the "great"; *pada* — word [name]; *yutam* — containing (?); *prathamam* — first; *sahasra* — of the thousand; *nāma* — names [the hymn]; *kṛta* — who had performed; *paitra* — for the ancestors; *kṛtiḥ* — the rite.

**79.** Then once the one moon of the race of brahmanas, he who on earth is renowned as Narada, having performed the rite for the ancestors, recited the "Thousand Names" [of Vishnu], containing the great name.

*Note.* The last pada in the edition is a syllable short of the norm (11 instead of 12): the text is corrupt (?). *Paitra-kṛti* is the *śrāddha*, the memorial rite for the father. "The great name" (*bṛhat-pada*) — judging by verse 80, the name of Nrisimha (?). The episode: Chaitanya-bhagavata, Madhya 2 — hearing the name of Nrisimha in the "Vishnu-sahasra-nama", Gaura enters the mood of Nrisimha. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 80

पुरुषर्षभोऽगमदमुष्य गृहम् ॥८०॥

*narasiṁha-bhāvam adhigatya tataḥ*
*puruṣarṣabho 'gamad amuṣya gṛham ||80||*

*Word for word:* *sva* — in His own; *gṛhe* — house; *sthitaḥ* — staying; *saḥ* — He; *bhagavān* — Bhagavan; *nṛhareḥ* — of Nrihari; *abhidhām* — the name; *niśamya* — having heard; *mahitaḥ* — magnified; *mahasā* — by radiance; *narasiṁha* — of Narasimha; *bhāvam* — the mood; *adhigatya* — having assumed; *tataḥ* — then; *puruṣa* — of men; *ṛṣabhaḥ* — the bull (the best); *agamat* — went; *amuṣya* — his; *gṛham* — to the house.

**80.** While staying in His own house, Bhagavan heard the name of Nrihari and, magnified by radiance, assumed the mood of Narasimha; and then the best of men went to his house.

*Note.* Nrihari, Narasimha — Vishnu in the form of the Man-lion. The house of Gaura and the house of Srivasa are close to each other.

महतीं गदां करपयोरुहयोः

*Word for word:* *mahatīm* — a huge; *gadām* — club; *kara* — of the hands; *payoruhayoḥ* — in the lotuses; *parigṛhya* — having taken; *duḥsaham* — unbearable; *upetya* — having assumed; *mahaḥ* — radiance; *abhidhāvati sma* — ran; *pathi* — along the road; *bhūmi* — of the earth; *talam* — the surface; *dalayan* — shaking; *pada* — of the feet; *ambuja* — of the lotuses; *valat* — moving; *dalanaiḥ* — with the blows.

**81.** Taking a huge club in His lotus hands and assuming an unbearable radiance, He ran along the road, shaking the surface of the earth with the blows of His moving lotus feet.

*Note.* The edition has *पदाम्बुजबलद्दलनैः*; we read *valad-* ("moving"; *b* and *v* are often confused) (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

परिदुद्रुवुर्द्रुतमतिप्रचलाः ॥८२॥

*paridudruvur drutam ati-pracalāḥ ||82||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *tam* — Him; *tathā* — such; *vidham* — [being] of a kind; *avekṣya* — having seen; *janāḥ* — the people; *pathi* — along the road; *dhāvanena* — by running; *paridīpta* — blazing; *javam* — [with] swiftness; *abhitaḥ abhitaḥ* — in all directions; *bhayam* — fear; *upetya* — having felt; *bhṛśam* — intense; *paridudruvuḥ* — fled; *drutam* — hastily; *ati* — extremely; *pracalāḥ* — agitated.

**82.** Then, seeing Him in such a state — running along the road with blazing swiftness — the people, feeling intense fear and extremely agitated, hastily fled in all directions.

**83.** But seeing those people given to flight, He therefore regained His composure here, put aside that huge club, and then went slowly to his house.

**84.** Having arrived there, the Lord, His heart softened from having seen the flight of the people, then said: "Am I then forever an offender toward those people?"

**85.** "O Bhagavan, there can by no means be any offence anywhere on the part of You, the Lord, the remover of all offences! This [seeming] offence is truly only the greatness of Your compassion," His own people said.

### Verse 86

**86.** And on another day, before this ocean of compassion, a certain fine singer sang with the highest joy a song about Shiva, in the hope of the mercy of this compassionate Lord.

*Note.* The episode: Chaitanya-bhagavata, Madhya 8 — Gaura climbs onto the shoulders of a singer singing about Shiva and dances in the mood of Shiva.

### Verse 87

*naṭanaṁ cakāra sa ca dhūrjaṭivat ||87||*

*Word for word:* *niśamayya* — having heard; *gītam* — the song; *ati* — very; *dhīra* — steady; *padam* — [with] words (steps); *lalitam* — charming; *babhūva* — became; *bhagavān* — Bhagavan; *muditaḥ* — delighted; *adhiruhya* — having climbed onto; *tasya* — his; *lasat* — gleaming; *aṁsa* — of the shoulder; *taṭam* — the slope; *naṭanam* — dancing; *cakāra* — performed; *saḥ* — He; *ca* — and; *dhūrjaṭi* — Dhurjati; *vat* — like.

**87.** Having heard the charming song, with its words of very steady tread, Bhagavan was delighted; and, climbing onto the gleaming slope of his shoulders, He danced like Dhurjati.

*Note.* *Dhūrjaṭi* ("having heavy matted locks") is Shiva. *Pada* means both "word" and "step".

### Verse 88

मदघूर्णिताक्षियुगलो विपुलैः
पुलकैरतीवरुचिरो रुचिमान् ।
स तदंसमूलमधिरुह्य तदा
शिववन्ननर्त्त करुणाम्बुनिधिः ॥८८॥

*mada-ghūrṇitākṣi-yugalo vipulaiḥ*
*pulakair atīva-ruciro rucimān |*
*sa tad-aṁsa-mūlam adhiruhya tadā*
*śivavan nanarta karuṇāmbunidhiḥ ||88||*

*Word for word:* *mada* — from intoxication; *ghūrṇita* — rolling; *akṣi* — of eyes; *yugalaḥ* — [with] a pair; *vipulaiḥ* — abundant; *pulakaiḥ* — with hairs standing on end; *atīva* — exceedingly; *ruciraḥ* — beautiful; *rucimān* — radiant; *saḥ* — He; *tat* — his; *aṁsa* — of the shoulder; *mūlam* — the base; *adhiruhya* — having climbed onto; *tadā* — then; *śiva* — Shiva; *vat* — like; *nanarta* — danced; *karuṇā* — of compassion; *ambunidhiḥ* — the ocean.

**88.** His eyes rolling from intoxication, exceedingly beautiful with abundant hairs standing on end, radiant, the ocean of compassion then climbed onto his shoulders and danced like Shiva.

### Verse 89

भुवि यस्तु नारद इति प्रथितः
स पपाठ तत्र गिरिशस्तवनम् ।
अतिसुस्वरः स तु मुकुन्दभिष-
क्स्तवनं महिम्न इह हन्त जगौ ॥८९॥

*bhuvi yas tu nārada iti prathitaḥ*
*sa papāṭha tatra giriśa-stavanam |*
*ati-susvaraḥ sa tu mukunda-bhiṣak-*
*stavanaṁ mahimna iha hanta jagau ||89||*

*Word for word:* *bhuvi* — on earth; *yaḥ* — who; *tu* — and; *nāradaḥ* — Narada; *iti* — as; *prathitaḥ* — renowned; *saḥ* — he; *papāṭha* — recited; *tatra* — there; *giriśa* — to Girisha; *stavanam* — a hymn of praise; *ati* — very; *susvaraḥ* — sweet-voiced; *saḥ* — that; *tu* — and; *mukunda* — Mukunda; *bhiṣak* — the physician; *stavanam* — the hymn of praise; *mahimnaḥ* — "Mahimna"; *iha* — here; *hanta* — lo; *jagau* — sang.

**89.** He who on earth is renowned as Narada recited there a hymn of praise to Girisha, and lo, the very sweet-voiced physician Mukunda sang here the hymn of praise "Mahimna".

*Note.* The "Shiva-mahimna-stotra" (of Pushpadanta) is a famous hymn to Shiva. Mukunda Datta was by caste a *vaidya* (physician). *Giriśa* ("lord of the mountain") is Shiva.

### Verse 90

तदनन्तरं स तु तदंसभुवं

वरमासनं निजजनान् सततं
परिहर्षयन् कुमुदबान्धववत् ॥९०॥

*tad-anantaraṁ sa tu tad-aṁsa-bhuvaṁ*
*parimucya tatra rabhasād abhajat |*
*varam āsanaṁ nija-janān satataṁ*
*pariharṣayan kumuda-bāndhava-vat ||90||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — that; *anantaram* — after; *saḥ* — He; *tu* — and; *tat* — his; *aṁsa* — of the shoulder; *bhuvam* — the place; *parimucya* — having left; *tatra* — there; *rabhasāt* — swiftly; *abhajat* — took; *varam* — the best; *āsanam* — seat; *nija* — His own; *janān* — people; *satatam* — constantly; *pariharṣayan* — delighting; *kumuda* — of the night lotuses; *bāndhava* — the friend (the moon); *vat* — like.

**90.** After that He left the place on his shoulders and swiftly took the best seat there, constantly delighting His own people like the moon, the friend of the night lotuses.

*Note.* *Kumuda* — white night lotuses, which open in the moonlight.

### Verse 91

नटनावसानसमयेऽन्यदिने
पुरतः समेत्य विनिपत्य भुवि ।
भृशमग्रहीत् पदपयोजरजां-
स्यथ काचन द्विजवधूप्रवरा ॥९१॥

*naṭanāvasāna-samaye 'nya-dine*
*purataḥ sametya vinipatya bhuvi |*
*bhṛśam agrahīt pada-payoja-rajāṁsy*
*atha kācana dvija-vadhū-pravarā ||91||*

*Word for word:* *naṭana* — of the dancing; *avasāna* — of the end; *samaye* — at the time; *anya* — on another; *dine* — day; *purataḥ* — before [Him]; *sametya* — having approached; *vinipatya* — having fallen; *bhuvi* — on the ground; *bhṛśam* — eagerly; *agrahīt* — took; *pada* — of the feet; *payoja* — of the lotus; *rajāṁsi* — the dust; *atha* — then; *kācana* — a certain; *dvija* — of brahmanas; *vadhū* — among the wives; *pravarā* — most excellent.

**91.** Then on another day, when the dancing had ended, a certain most excellent brahmana's wife approached, fell on the ground before [Him], and eagerly took the dust of His lotus feet.

*Note.* The episode — Murari 2.11.19–25 (the same: a brahmana woman takes the dust from the feet of the Lord as He lies [on the ground], and He throws Himself into the Ganga). In the Chaitanya-bhagavata (Madhya 17.30–47) the Lord throws Himself into the Ganga for another reason — lamenting that He is deprived of prema (because of Advaita's "trick"); Nityananda and Haridasa pull Him out, and He spends the night in the house of Nandana Acharya.

### Verse 92

चपलं प्रसृत्य बहुधा विकलः ॥९२॥

*tad idaṁ vilokya sahasaiva tayā*
*vihitaṁ babhāra bahu-duḥkha-bharam |*
*dyu-nadī-jale 'tha nipapāta tadā*

*Word for word:* *tat idam* — this; *vilokya* — having seen; *sahasā eva* — at once; *tayā* — by her; *vihitam* — done; *babhāra* — bore; *bahu* — great; *duḥkha* — of sorrow; *bharam* — the weight; *dyu* — of the heavenly; *nadī* — river; *jale* — into the water; *atha* — and; *nipapāta* — threw Himself; *tadā* — then; *capalam* — swiftly; *prasṛtya* — having run out; *bahudhā* — extremely; *vikalaḥ* — distraught.

**92.** Seeing what she had done, He at once bore the weight of great sorrow; and then, extremely distraught, He swiftly ran out and threw Himself into the waters of the heavenly river.

*Note.* The edition has *बहुःदुखभरम्*, a misprint.

### Verse 93

तममुं तथाविधमवेक्ष्य बली

गुरुदोर्द्वयेन सहसा विकलः ॥९३॥

*tam amuṁ tathā-vidham avekṣya balī*
*samam uddadhāra payaso 'tibalāt |*
*avadhūta-deva iha gaura-vibhuṁ*
*guru-dor-dvayena sahasā vikalaḥ ||93||*

*Word for word:* *tam amum* — Him; *tathā* — such; *vidham* — [being] of a kind; *avekṣya* — having seen; *balī* — the mighty; *samam* — all at once; *uddadhāra* — pulled out; *payasaḥ* — from the water; *ati* — with great; *balāt* — strength; *avadhūta-devaḥ* — the divine avadhuta; *iha* — here; *gaura* — Gaura; *vibhum* — the Lord; *guru* — mighty; *doḥ* — of arms; *dvayena* — with the pair; *sahasā* — at once; *vikalaḥ* — distraught.

**93.** Seeing Him in such a state, the mighty divine avadhuta, distraught, at once pulled Gaura, the Lord, out of the water with great strength, with His pair of mighty arms.

*Note.* The second pada in the edition (*सममुद्धार परसोऽतिबलात्*) breaks the metre; *paraso* is probably a misprint for *payaso* ("from the water"); the verbal form is corrupt: the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *samam uddadhāra*, and so we read.

### Verse 95

स मुरारिगुप्तनिलयं सह तै-
रुपगत्य भूरिकरुणः प्रबभौ ।

रजनीञ्च तत्र करुणोऽगमयत् ॥९५॥

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — He; *murāri-gupta* — of Murari Gupta; *nilayam* — to the house; *saha* — together; *taiḥ* — with them; *upagatya* — having come; *bhūri* — boundlessly; *karuṇaḥ* — compassionate; *prababhau* — shone; *punaḥ api* — then again; *agāt* — went; *dvija* — of a brahmana; *geham* — to the house; *atho* — and; *rajanīm* — the night; *ca* — and; *tatra* — there; *karuṇaḥ* — the compassionate; *agamayat* — spent.

**95.** The boundlessly compassionate [Lord] came together with them to the house of Murari Gupta and shone [there]; then He went on again to the house of a brahmana, and there the compassionate [Lord] spent the night.

*Note.* Which brahmana is meant is not specified; the Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text. In the Chaitanya-bhagavata (see the note to verse 91) the Lord spends the night in the house of Nandana Acharya.

*Note.* *Uttara* means "opposite" or "northern".

### Verse 97

अथ ते भयेन महता विनयैः

*parisāntvanaṁ kila vidhāya muhuḥ |*

श्रीवासस्य गृहं समेत्य स पुनः प्रोवाच धीराक्षरं

त्यक्त्वाहं जननीं व्रजामि किल चेत् कुत्रापि तस्माज्जनः
सर्व्वोऽयं कृतवान् विरुद्धमसकौ नूनं वदिष्यत्यदः ॥९८॥

*śrīvāsasya gṛhaṁ sametya sa punaḥ provāca dhīrākṣaraṁ*
*sarveṣām avaśṛṇvatāṁ hi purataḥ śrī-gauracandraḥ prabhuḥ |*
*tyaktvāhaṁ jananīṁ vrajāmi kila cet kutrāpi tasmāj janaḥ*
*sarvo 'yaṁ kṛtavān viruddham asakau nūnaṁ vadiṣyaty adaḥ ||98||*

*Word for word:* *śrīvāsasya* — of Srivasa; *gṛham* — to the house; *sametya* — having come; *saḥ* — He; *punaḥ* — again; *provāca* — spoke; *dhīra* — firm; *akṣaram* — [in] words; *sarveṣām* — of all; *avaśṛṇvatām* — listening; *hi* — indeed; *purataḥ* — before; *śrī-gauracandraḥ* — Sri Gaurachandra; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *tyaktvā* — having left; *aham* — I; *jananīm* — mother; *vrajāmi* — go away; *kila* — indeed; *cet* — if; *kutra api* — somewhere; *tasmāt* — then; *janaḥ* — the people; *sarvaḥ* — all; *ayam* — these; *kṛtavān* — has done; *viruddham* — what is wrong; *asakau* — this wretch; *nūnam* — surely; *vadiṣyati* — will say; *adaḥ* — that.

### Verse 99

मुरारिगुप्तोऽथ जगाद वाक्यं

न कोऽपि नाथेह भवत्सु तत्त-
द्वदिष्यति प्रेमदपादपद्मः ॥९९॥

*murāri-gupto 'tha jagāda vākyaṁ*
*śrutvā tadīyaṁ sudhayaiva siktam |*
*na ko 'pi nātheha bhavatsu tat tad*
*vadiṣyati prema-da-pāda-padmaḥ ||99||*

*Word for word:* *murāri-guptaḥ* — Murari Gupta; *atha* — then; *jagāda* — spoke; *vākyam* — the speech; *śrutvā* — having heard; *tadīyam* — His; *sudhayā* — with nectar; *eva* — as if; *siktam* — sprinkled; *na* — not; *kaḥ api* — anyone; *nātha* — O Lord; *iha* — here; *bhavatsu* — about You; *tat tat* — such things; *vadiṣyati* — will say; *prema* — love; *da* — bestowing; *pāda* — of the feet; *padmaḥ* — [You whose] lotuses.

### Verse 100

श्रुत्वेत्थं वचनमसौ कृपासमुद्रः
