सोऽप्येवं पुलकघटाविभिन्नदेहः
श्लोकैकं मुदितमनाः पपाठ दैन्यात् ॥१००॥

*śrutvetthaṁ vacanam asau kṛpā-samudraḥ*
*saṁhṛṣṭaḥ parama-sukhas tam āliliṅga |*
*so 'py evaṁ pulaka-ghaṭā-vibhinna-dehaḥ*
*ślokaikaṁ mudita-manāḥ papāṭha dainyāt ||100||*

*Word for word:* *śrutvā* — having heard; *ittham* — such; *vacanam* — words; *asau* — He; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *samudraḥ* — the ocean; *saṁhṛṣṭaḥ* — delighted; *parama* — with supreme; *sukhaḥ* — happiness [filled]; *tam* — him; *āliliṅga* — embraced; *saḥ* — he; *api* — and; *evam* — thus; *pulaka* — of hairs standing on end; *ghaṭā* — by a multitude; *vibhinna* — pierced; *dehaḥ* — [with] a body; *śloka* — verse; *ekam* — one; *mudita* — joyful; *manāḥ* — [with] a heart; *papāṭha* — recited; *dainyāt* — in humility.

**100.** Having heard such words, the ocean of mercy, delighted and filled with supreme happiness, embraced him. And he, his body thus pierced by a multitude of hairs standing on end, his heart joyful, recited in humility a verse:

*Note.* The metre is *praharṣiṇī*.

क्वाहं दरिद्रः पापीयानित्यादि ।

*kvāhaṁ daridraḥ pāpīyān ity-ādi |*

*Word for word:* *kva* — where [am]; *aham* — I; *daridraḥ* — poor; *pāpīyān* — a great sinner; *iti-ādi* — and so on.

"Where am I, a poor sinner…" and so on.

*Note.* The edition gives only the beginning. This is Srimad-Bhagavatam 10.81.16 (the words of Sudama): *kvāhaṁ daridraḥ pāpīyān kva kṛṣṇaḥ śrī-niketanaḥ / brahma-bandhur iti smāhaṁ bāhubhyāṁ parirambhitaḥ* — "Where am I, a poor sinner, and where is Krishna, the abode of Sri! And yet He embraced me with His arms, [seeing in me] a brahmana, though only by birth."

### Verse 101

श्रुत्वा स इत्थमुदितं भगवांस्तदैव
स्वैश्वर्य्यमुत्तममुपेत्य रराज नाथः ।
रम्यासनोपरि परिष्ठित उद्भटेन
तेजश्चयेन दिननाथसहस्रतुल्यः ॥१०१॥

*śrutvā sa ittham uditaṁ bhagavāṁs tadaiva*
*svaiśvaryam uttamam upetya rarāja nāthaḥ |*
*ramyāsanopari pariṣṭhita udbhaṭena*
*tejaś-cayena dina-nātha-sahasra-tulyaḥ ||101||*

*Word for word:* *śrutvā* — having heard; *saḥ* — He; *ittham* — thus; *uditam* — what was said; *bhagavān* — Bhagavan; *tadā eva* — at once; *sva* — His own; *aiśvaryam* — majesty; *uttamam* — supreme; *upetya* — having assumed; *rarāja* — shone; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *ramya* — of a charming; *āsana* — seat; *upari* — upon; *pariṣṭhitaḥ* — seated; *udbhaṭena* — with a mighty; *tejaḥ* — of effulgence; *cayena* — mass; *dina-nātha* — of suns; *sahasra* — to a thousand; *tulyaḥ* — equal.

**101.** Having heard what was thus said, Bhagavan, the Lord, at once assumed His own supreme majesty and, seated upon a charming seat, shone with a mighty mass of effulgence, equal to a thousand suns.

*Note.* The metre is *vasanta-tilakā*.

### Verse 102

इदं शरीरं परमं मनोज्ञं
सच्चिद्घनानन्दमयं ममैव ।
जानीत यूयं नहि किञ्चिदन्य-
द्विनास्ति भूमौ स इतीदमूचे ॥१०२॥

*idaṁ śarīraṁ paramaṁ manojñaṁ*
*sac-cid-ghanānanda-mayaṁ mamaiva |*
*jānīta yūyaṁ nahi kiñcid anyad*
*vināsti bhūmau sa itīdam ūce ||102||*

*Word for word:* *idam* — this; *śarīram* — body; *paramam* — supreme; *manojñam* — enchanting; *sat* — of being; *cit* — of consciousness; *ghana* — concentrated; *ānanda* — of bliss; *mayam* — consisting; *mama* — Mine; *eva* — indeed; *jānīta* — know; *yūyam* — you; *nahi* — not; *kiñcit* — anything; *anyat* — else; *vinā* — apart from [it]; *asti* — is; *bhūmau* — on earth; *saḥ* — He; *iti* — thus; *idam* — this; *ūce* — said.

**102.** "Know that this body of Mine is supreme, enchanting, made of concentrated being, consciousness and bliss; apart from it there is nothing else on earth," He said.

*Note.* The metre is *upajāti*. *Sac-cid-ānanda-ghana* is the formula of the divine body (cf. Brahma-samhita 5.1: *sac-cid-ānanda-vigrahaḥ*).

### Verse 103

हृष्टास्तत्तन्नाथवाक्यं निशम्य
प्रोद्यद्रोमाञ्चाञ्चिताङ्गाः समन्तात् ।
श्रीवासाद्या नेत्रवारिप्रवाहैः
सम्यक् स्नातास्तत्र तत्रैवमासन् ॥१०३॥

*hṛṣṭās tat tan nātha-vākyaṁ niśamya*
*prodyad-romāñcāñcitāṅgāḥ samantāt |*
*śrīvāsādyā netra-vāri-pravāhaiḥ*
*samyak snātās tatra tatraivam āsan ||103||*

*Word for word:* *hṛṣṭāḥ* — delighted; *tat tat* — these; *nātha* — of the Lord; *vākyam* — words; *niśamya* — having heard; *prodyat* — rising; *romāñca* — with bristling hairs; *añcita* — covered; *aṅgāḥ* — [with] limbs; *samantāt* — all over; *śrīvāsa* — Srivasa; *ādyāḥ* — and the others; *netra* — of the eyes; *vāri* — of water; *pravāhaiḥ* — by streams; *samyak* — thoroughly; *snātāḥ* — bathed; *tatra tatra* — right there; *evam* — thus; *āsan* — remained.

**103.** Having heard these words of the Lord, Srivasa and the others were delighted; their limbs all over were covered with rising, bristling hairs, and, thoroughly bathed by streams of tears, they remained thus right where they were.

*Note.* The metre is *śālinī* (11 syllables), up to verse 106 inclusive.

### Verse 104

श्रीवासोऽसौ पूर्व्ववद्गाङ्गतोयैः
स्वच्छस्वच्छैः स्नापयामास भूयः ।
श्रीगौराङ्गं तत्पदैकावलम्बः
प्रेमाम्भोभिर्धौतसर्व्वाङ्गरम्यम् ॥१०४॥

*śrīvāso 'sau pūrvavad gāṅga-toyaiḥ*
*svaccha-svacchaiḥ snāpayām āsa bhūyaḥ |*
*śrī-gaurāṅgaṁ tat-padaikāvalambaḥ*
*premāmbhobhir dhauta-sarvāṅga-ramyam ||104||*

*Word for word:* *śrīvāsaḥ* — Srivasa; *asau* — this; *pūrvavat* — as before; *gāṅga* — of the Ganga; *toyaiḥ* — with the waters; *svaccha-svacchaiḥ* — most pure; *snāpayām āsa* — bathed; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *śrī-gaurāṅgam* — Sri Gauranga; *tat* — His; *pada* — feet; *eka* — the sole; *avalambaḥ* — [whose] support; *prema* — of love; *ambhobhiḥ* — with the waters; *dhauta* — washed; *sarva* — in all; *aṅga* — limbs; *ramyam* — beautiful.

**104.** And Srivasa, whose sole support is His feet, again, as before, bathed with the most pure waters of the Ganga Sri Gauranga, beautiful in all His limbs, washed by the waters of love.

*Note.* "As before" — the *mahābhiṣeka* in Sarga Five (verses 38–46).

### Verse 105

यावत् कुम्भैर्गौरचन्द्राङ्गयष्टौ
गङ्गातोयैर्भूसुरोऽयं सिषेच ।
तावत् स्वाङ्गे नेत्रपाथोरुहाभ्यां
प्रेम्णा निर्यत्तोयमुद्गीर्णवान् सः ॥१०५॥

*yāvat kumbhair gauracandrāṅga-yaṣṭau*
*gaṅgā-toyair bhūsuro 'yaṁ siṣeca |*
*tāvat svāṅge netra-pāthoruhābhyāṁ*
*premṇā niryat-toyam udgīrṇavān saḥ ||105||*

*Word for word:* *yāvat* — as much as; *kumbhaiḥ* — from jars; *gauracandra* — of Gaurachandra; *aṅga* — of the body; *yaṣṭau* — on the stem; *gaṅgā* — of the Ganga; *toyaiḥ* — with the waters; *bhūsuraḥ* — brahmana; *ayam* — this; *siṣeca* — poured; *tāvat* — so much; *sva* — on His own; *aṅge* — body; *netra* — of the eyes; *pāthoruhābhyām* — from the lotuses; *premṇā* — from love; *niryat* — flowing forth; *toyam* — water; *udgīrṇavān* — poured out; *saḥ* — He.

**105.** As much of the waters of the Ganga as this brahmana poured from jars on the slender stem of Gaurachandra's body, so much water, flowing forth from love, did He pour out from the lotuses of His eyes on His own body.

*Note.* *Bhūsura* ("a god on earth") is a brahmana, here Srivasa. *Aṅga-yaṣṭi* ("the stem of the body") — a slender, graceful figure.

### Verse 106

एवं भूयः कौतुकं ते विलोक्य
प्रेमोद्भ्रान्ताः कीर्त्तनं नर्त्तनञ्च ।
उच्चैरुच्चैश्चक्रुरुन्मत्तचित्ताः
श्रीगौराङ्गप्रेममात्रावलम्बाः ॥१०६॥

*evaṁ bhūyaḥ kautukaṁ te vilokya*
*premodbhrāntāḥ kīrtanaṁ nartanañ ca |*
*uccair uccaiś cakrur unmatta-cittāḥ*
*śrī-gaurāṅga-prema-mātrāvalambāḥ ||106||*

*Word for word:* *evam* — thus; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *kautukam* — wonder; *te* — they; *vilokya* — having seen; *prema* — from love; *udbhrāntāḥ* — maddened; *kīrtanam* — kirtana; *nartanam* — dancing; *ca* — and; *uccaiḥ uccaiḥ* — louder and louder; *cakruḥ* — performed; *unmatta* — intoxicated; *cittāḥ* — [with] hearts; *śrī-gaurāṅga* — for Sri Gauranga; *prema* — love; *mātra* — the only; *avalambāḥ* — [whose] support.

**106.** Seeing such a wonder again, they — maddened by love, their hearts intoxicated, they whose only support is love for Sri Gauranga — performed kirtana and dancing louder and louder.

### Verse 107

अन्येद्युर्गौरचन्द्रो निजजनसहितो भक्तिशिक्षां वितन्व-
न्नत्यन्ताश्चर्य्यचेष्टः कमलभवभवाद्यैर्भृशं भावनीयः ।
कुज्ञानाद्यैः समन्तात् सकलमनुपुरं देवतानां निकेतं
सन्मार्जन्या च चक्रे जगति सुविदितो मार्ज्जितं शश्वदेव ॥१०७॥

इति श्रीकृष्णचैतन्यचरितामृते महाकाव्ये सप्तमः सर्गः ॥

*anyedyur gauracandro nija-jana-sahito bhakti-śikṣāṁ vitanvann*
*atyantāścarya-ceṣṭaḥ kamala-bhava-bhavādyair bhṛśaṁ bhāvanīyaḥ |*
*kujñānādyaiḥ samantāt sakalam anupuraṁ devatānāṁ niketaṁ*
*sanmārjanyā ca cakre jagati suvidito mārjitaṁ śaśvad eva ||107||*

*iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahā-kāvye saptamaḥ sargaḥ ||*

*Word for word:* *anyedyuḥ* — on another day; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra; *nija* — His own; *jana* — people; *sahitaḥ* — together with; *bhakti* — of devotion; *śikṣām* — the teaching; *vitanvan* — spreading; *atyanta* — extremely; *āścarya* — wondrous; *ceṣṭaḥ* — [whose] deeds; *kamala-bhava* — by Brahma (born from the lotus); *bhava* — by Shiva; *ādyaiḥ* — and the others; *bhṛśam* — incessantly; *bhāvanīyaḥ* — to be contemplated; *kujñāna* — of false knowledge; *ādyaiḥ* — [from] and the rest; *samantāt* — everywhere; *sakalam* — everything; *anupuram* — in every town; *devatānām* — of the deities; *niketam* — the abodes; *sanmārjanyā* — with a good broom; *ca* — and; *cakre* — made; *jagati* — in the world; *suviditaḥ* — renowned; *mārjitam* — cleansed; *śaśvat eva* — constantly.

**107.** On another day Gaurachandra, whose deeds are extremely wondrous, who is incessantly contemplated by Brahma, Shiva and the others, spreading the teaching of devotion together with His own people, cleansed everything everywhere of false knowledge and the rest — and with a good broom He constantly swept clean the abodes of the deities in every town, becoming renowned for this in the world.

*Note.* The metre is *sragdharā* (21 syllables). A twofold cleansing: of the world from false knowledge (*kujñāna*), and of the temples with a broom; cf. the later cleansing of the Gundicha temple (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 12), where the broom is an image of the cleansing of the heart. The syntax of *kujñānādyaiḥ* (instrumental instead of ablative) is not entirely clear (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

*Note.* The colophon of the edition gives no title for the sarga.

Thus ends the seventh sarga in the mahakavya "Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita".

## Sarga Eight — verses 1–63

**Title of the sarga:** *Śrī-vṛndāvana-vihāra-varṇana*, "The Description of the Pastimes in Vrindavana" (from the colophon).
**Metre:** *anuṣṭubh* (*śloka*); verse 61 — *śikhariṇī*; verses 62–63 — *vasanta-tilakā*.
**Total verses:** 63.

**Contents of the passage:**
- 1–9 — a leper begs to be healed; the Lord refuses: "You hated Srivasa"; the Vaishnavas are His life-airs moving outside [the body].
- 10–16 — a brahmana who was not admitted to the kirtana breaks his sacred thread and curses Gaura: "May Your samsara be cut off!"; the Lord rejoices at the curse as at a blessing.
- 17–26 — Gaura in the mood of **Balarama**: "Give [Me] honey!"; He turns white like a mountain of silver; with a plough, in a blue garment; in the house of Murari Gupta.
- 27–36 — He hurls away a strong brahmana; the days of absorption; "I have seen a man with a plough, like a mountain of silver"; Chandrashekhara Acharya sees Balarama in Gaura.
- 37–46 — the dance in the mood of Balarama; an intoxicating fragrance, swarms of bees; Sri Rama [Pandita] sees Balarama's associates descended from the sky; Vanamali sees a golden plough as large as a mountain.
- 47–55 — a rain of flowers from the gods; dawn; bathing and water-play in the Ganga.
- 56–60 — "Give Me the flute!" — "The gopis are guarding it"; the Lord in bliss: "Speak, speak!" — Srivasa tells of the pastimes in Vrindavana and on the Yamuna.
- 61–63 — Srivasa's speech on Krishna's ever-new pastimes in Vrindavana; "Speak more!"

### Verse 1

कदाचिदथ तं प्रीत्या गच्छन्तं परमं प्रभुम् ।
प्रणम्य विनयात् कश्चित् प्रोवाच मधुराक्षरम् ॥१॥

*kadācid atha taṁ prītyā gacchantaṁ paramaṁ prabhum |*
*praṇamya vinayāt kaścit provāca madhurākṣaram ||1||*

*Word for word:* *kadācit* — once; *atha* — then; *tam* — to Him; *prītyā* — with affection; *gacchantam* — walking; *paramam* — to the Supreme; *prabhum* — Lord; *praṇamya* — having bowed down; *vinayāt* — humbly; *kaścit* — someone; *provāca* — spoke; *madhura* — sweet; *akṣaram* — with words.

**1.** Then once, as the Supreme Lord was walking [along the road], someone humbly bowed down to Him with affection and spoke to Him in sweet words:

### Verse 2

सर्व्वे त्वां देवदेवेशं सच्चिद्घनशरीरिणम् ।
पुरुषं परमं प्राहुस्तन्नोद्धरसि किं नु माम् ॥२॥

*sarve tvāṁ deva-deveśaṁ sac-cid-ghana-śarīriṇam |*
*puruṣaṁ paramaṁ prāhus tan noddharasi kiṁ nu mām ||2||*

*Word for word:* *sarve* — all; *tvām* — You; *deva* — of the gods; *deva* — of the gods; *īśam* — the Lord; *sat* — of being; *cit* — of consciousness; *ghana* — concentrated; *śarīriṇam* — possessing a body; *puruṣam* — the Person; *paramam* — Supreme; *prāhuḥ* — call; *tat* — so; *na* — not; *uddharasi* — You deliver; *kim nu* — why then; *mām* — me.

**2.** "All call You the Lord of the gods of gods, the Supreme Person whose body is concentrated being and consciousness. Why then do You not deliver me?

### Verse 3

त्राहि मां सर्व्व सर्व्वेश कुष्ठात् परमगर्हितात् ।
दोधूयमानहृदयं कृपां कुरु कृपानिधे ॥३॥

*trāhi māṁ sarva sarveśa kuṣṭhāt parama-garhitāt |*
*dodhūyamāna-hṛdayaṁ kṛpāṁ kuru kṛpā-nidhe ||3||*

*Word for word:* *trāhi* — save; *mām* — me; *sarva* — O All; *sarva* — of all; *īśa* — O Lord; *kuṣṭhāt* — from leprosy; *parama* — utterly; *garhitāt* — loathsome; *dodhūyamāna* — tormented; *hṛdayam* — [me,] whose heart; *kṛpām* — mercy; *kuru* — show; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *nidhe* — O treasure-house.

**3.** O All, O Lord of all, save me from this utterly loathsome leprosy! My heart is tormented — show mercy, O treasure-house of mercy!"

*Note.* This is the same leper, a hater of Srivasa, as in Sarga Six, verse 73 (by tradition, Gopala Chapala; Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 17.37–58).

### Verse 4

श्रुत्वेदं तद्वचः श्रीमान् क्रोधारुणितलोचनः ।
जगाद वदनव्याजाद्द्विजराजेन शोभितः ॥४॥

*śrutvedaṁ tad-vacaḥ śrīmān krodhāruṇita-locanaḥ |*
*jagāda vadana-vyājād dvija-rājena śobhitaḥ ||4||*

*Word for word:* *śrutvā* — having heard; *idam* — these; *tat* — his; *vacaḥ* — words; *śrīmān* — the beautiful one; *krodha* — with anger; *aruṇita* — reddened; *locanaḥ* — whose eyes; *jagāda* — spoke; *vadana* — of the face; *vyājāt* — in the guise; *dvija-rājena* — by the king of the twice-born (the moon); *śobhitaḥ* — adorned.

**4.** Having heard these words of his, the beautiful [Lord], adorned with the king of the twice-born (the moon) in the guise of His face, spoke, His eyes reddened with anger:

*Note.* *Dvija-rāja*, "king of the twice-born", is both the moon (which is "born twice", rising anew) and the best of brahmanas. Gaura's face is the moon.

### Verse 5

आः पापात्मन् दुराचार मद्भक्तद्वेषकारक ।
त्वामुद्धरिष्ये चेन्नाहमुद्धरिष्यामि कं ततः ॥५॥

*āḥ pāpātman durācāra mad-bhakta-dveṣa-kāraka |*
*tvām uddhariṣye cen nāham uddhariṣyāmi kaṁ tataḥ ||5||*

*Word for word:* *āḥ* — ah; *pāpa* — sinful; *ātman* — O soul; *durācāra* — O evil-doer; *mat* — of My; *bhakta* — devotees; *dveṣa* — hatred; *kāraka* — O you who harbour; *tvām* — you; *uddhariṣye* — I shall deliver; *cet* — if; *na* — not; *aham* — I; *uddhariṣyāmi* — shall deliver; *kam* — whom; *tataḥ* — then.

**5.** "Ah, O sinful soul, O evil-doer who harbour hatred for My devotees! If I were to deliver you, then whom would I not deliver?

*Note.* The edition has *kiṁ tataḥ* ("what of it?"), and the line is obscure; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *kaṁ tataḥ*, "whom then [would I not deliver]", and so we read.

### Verse 6

श्रीवासस्य सदा द्वेषं यतस्त्वं कृतवानसि ।
अतएव प्रतिभवं कुष्ठी खलु भविष्यसि ॥६॥

*śrīvāsasya sadā dveṣaṁ yatas tvaṁ kṛtavān asi |*
*ata eva prati-bhavaṁ kuṣṭhī khalu bhaviṣyasi ||6||*

*Word for word:* *śrīvāsasya* — towards Srivasa; *sadā* — always; *dveṣam* — hatred; *yataḥ* — since; *tvam* — you; *kṛtavān asi* — have harboured; *ataḥ eva* — therefore; *prati* — in every; *bhavam* — birth; *kuṣṭhī* — a leper; *khalu* — certainly; *bhaviṣyasi* — you will be.

**6.** Since you have always harboured hatred towards Srivasa, you will therefore certainly be a leper in every birth.

### Verse 7

अस्मिन् देहे तु ये प्राणास्ते न लक्ष्याः कदाचन ।
बहिश्चरा इव प्राणा वैष्णवा इति विद्धि मे ॥७॥

*asmin dehe tu ye prāṇās te na lakṣyāḥ kadācana |*
*bahiś-carā iva prāṇā vaiṣṇavā iti viddhi me ||7||*

*Word for word:* *asmin* — in this; *dehe* — body; *tu* — but; *ye* — which; *prāṇāḥ* — life-airs; *te* — they; *na* — not; *lakṣyāḥ* — visible; *kadācana* — ever; *bahiḥ* — outside; *carāḥ* — moving; *iva* — as if; *prāṇāḥ* — life-airs; *vaiṣṇavāḥ* — the Vaishnavas; *iti* — thus; *viddhi* — know; *me* — My.

**7.** The life-airs that are in this body are never visible; but know that the Vaishnavas are My life-airs, moving, as it were, outside [the body].

*Note.* *Bahiś-cara prāṇa*, "life moving outside the body": the devotees are the very life of the Lord (cf. Srimad-Bhagavatam 9.4.68: *sādhavo hṛdayaṁ mahyam*). The edition has *लक्ष्या* without the visarga.

### Verse 8

ये ये येन प्रकारेण तान् द्विषन्ति मम प्रियान् ।
तेषां तेषां प्रतिभवं नरके पतनं भवेत् ॥८॥

*ye ye yena prakāreṇa tān dviṣanti mama priyān |*
*teṣāṁ teṣāṁ prati-bhavaṁ narake patanaṁ bhavet ||8||*

*Word for word:* *ye ye* — whoever; *yena* — in whatever; *prakāreṇa* — way; *tān* — those; *dviṣanti* — hate; *mama* — My; *priyān* — dear ones; *teṣām teṣām* — of each of them; *prati* — in every; *bhavam* — birth; *narake* — into hell; *patanam* — a fall; *bhavet* — there will be.

**8.** Whoever, in whatever way, hates those dear ones of Mine — each of them will fall into hell in every birth.

### Verse 9

वैष्णवेभ्यो नता ये च ये तदाज्ञापरायणाः ।
ते त एव तरिष्यन्ति संसारार्णवमुत्कटम् ॥९॥

*vaiṣṇavebhyo natā ye ca ye tad-ājñā-parāyaṇāḥ |*
*te ta eva tariṣyanti saṁsārārṇavam utkaṭam ||9||*

*Word for word:* *vaiṣṇavebhyaḥ* — before the Vaishnavas; *natāḥ* — bow down; *ye* — who; *ca* — and; *ye* — who; *tat* — to their; *ājñā* — commands; *parāyaṇāḥ* — devoted; *te te* — they; *eva* — alone; *tariṣyanti* — will cross; *saṁsāra* — of samsara; *arṇavam* — the ocean; *utkaṭam* — fearsome.

**9.** Those who bow down before the Vaishnavas and are devoted to their commands — they alone will cross the fearsome ocean of samsara."

### Verse 10

इत्युक्त्वा गेहमगमत् श्रीवासस्य महाप्रभुः ।
तेन सार्द्धं तदा रेमे भगवान् भक्तभक्तिमान् ॥१०॥

*ity uktvā geham agamat śrīvāsasya mahāprabhuḥ |*
*tena sārdhaṁ tadā reme bhagavān bhakta-bhaktimān ||10||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *uktvā* — having spoken; *geham* — to the house; *agamat* — went; *śrīvāsasya* — of Srivasa; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *tena* — with him; *sārdham* — together; *tadā* — then; *reme* — took delight; *bhagavān* — Bhagavan; *bhakta* — to the devotees; *bhaktimān* — devoted.

**10.** Having spoken thus, Mahaprabhu went to the house of Srivasa, and there Bhagavan, who is devoted to His devotees, took delight together with him.

### Verse 11

एकदा नृत्यसमये द्रष्टुं गौराङ्गसुन्दरम् ।
चलितो द्वारपालेन वारितो धरणीसुरः ॥११॥

*ekadā nṛtya-samaye draṣṭuṁ gaurāṅga-sundaram |*
*calito dvāra-pālena vārito dharaṇī-suraḥ ||11||*

*Word for word:* *ekadā* — once; *nṛtya* — of the dancing; *samaye* — at the time; *draṣṭum* — to see; *gaurāṅga* — Gauranga; *sundaram* — the beautiful; *calitaḥ* — having set out; *dvāra* — of the door; *pālena* — by the keeper; *vāritaḥ* — was stopped; *dharaṇī-suraḥ* — a brahmana (lit. "a god on earth").

**11.** Once, at the time of the dancing, a brahmana set out to see the beautiful Gauranga, but was stopped by the doorkeeper.

*Note.* The kirtanas in Srivasa's house were held behind closed doors (Chaitanya-bhagavata, Madhya 8 and 26; Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 17.41).

### Verse 12

क्रुद्धोऽपरदिने सोऽयं गङ्गायास्तटसन्निधौ ।
दृष्ट्वा जगत्प्रभुं तत्र दुर्मुखो रोषलोहितः ॥१२॥

*kruddho 'para-dine so 'yaṁ gaṅgāyās taṭa-sannidhau |*
*dṛṣṭvā jagat-prabhuṁ tatra durmukho roṣa-lohitaḥ ||12||*

*Word for word:* *kruddhaḥ* — angry; *apara* — on another; *dine* — day; *saḥ ayam* — this man; *gaṅgāyāḥ* — of the Ganga; *taṭa* — the bank; *sannidhau* — near; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *jagat* — of the world; *prabhum* — the Lord; *tatra* — there; *durmukhaḥ* — foul-mouthed; *roṣa* — with fury; *lohitaḥ* — red.

**12.** On another day this foul-mouthed [brahmana], [still] angry, saw the Lord of the world there, near the bank of the Ganga, and turned red with fury.

### Verse 13

उपवीतं द्विधा छित्त्वा शापं दास्यन्निदं जगौ ।
त्वां नृत्यसमये द्रष्टुं गतवानहमेकदा ॥१३॥

*upavītaṁ dvidhā chittvā śāpaṁ dāsyann idaṁ jagau |*
*tvāṁ nṛtya-samaye draṣṭuṁ gatavān aham ekadā ||13||*

*Word for word:* *upavītam* — the sacred thread; *dvidhā* — in two; *chittvā* — having broken; *śāpam* — a curse; *dāsyan* — about to pronounce; *idam* — this; *jagau* — said; *tvām* — You; *nṛtya* — of the dancing; *samaye* — at the time; *draṣṭum* — to see; *gatavān* — went; *aham* — I; *ekadā* — once.

**13.** Breaking his sacred thread in two, about to pronounce a curse, he said this: "Once I went to see You at the time of the dancing,

*Note.* Breaking the sacred thread (*upavīta*) is the gesture of a brahmana's curse (cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 17.33–35: "May Your worldly life be destroyed!").

### Verse 14

तवैव द्वारपालेन वारितस्तेन दुःखितः ।
शापं ददामि तत्तुभ्यं संसारच्छित्तिरस्तु ते ॥१४॥

*tavaiva dvāra-pālena vāritas tena duḥkhitaḥ |*
*śāpaṁ dadāmi tat tubhyaṁ saṁsāra-cchittir astu te ||14||*

*Word for word:* *tava* — by Your; *eva* — own; *dvāra* — of the door; *pālena* — by the keeper; *vāritaḥ* — stopped; *tena* — by that; *duḥkhitaḥ* — grieved; *śāpam* — a curse; *dadāmi* — I give; *tat* — therefore; *tubhyam* — to You; *saṁsāra* — of samsara; *chittiḥ* — a cutting off; *astu* — let there be; *te* — for You.

**14.** and, stopped by Your very own doorkeeper, I was grieved by it. Therefore I give You a curse: let Your samsara be cut off!"

*Note.* A double meaning: "may Your worldly (household) life be ruined" — and "may Your round of rebirth cease" (liberation). Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 17.34.

### Verse 15

तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवान्नाथो ननन्द मनसा मुहुः ।
रुष्टस्य शापो विप्रस्य वरोऽभूदिति हर्षितः ॥१५॥

*tac chrutvā bhagavān nātho nananda manasā muhuḥ |*
*ruṣṭasya śāpo viprasya varo 'bhūd iti harṣitaḥ ||15||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — that; *śrutvā* — having heard; *bhagavān* — Bhagavan; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *nananda* — rejoiced; *manasā* — in His heart; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *ruṣṭasya* — of the angry; *śāpaḥ* — the curse; *viprasya* — of the brahmana; *varaḥ* — a blessing; *abhūt* — has become; *iti* — [thinking] thus; *harṣitaḥ* — delighted.

**15.** Hearing that, the Lord, Bhagavan, rejoiced in His heart again and again, delighted [at the thought]: "The curse of the angry brahmana has become a blessing!"

*Note.* A foreshadowing of *sannyāsa*: the "cutting off of samsara" is the leaving of home.

### Verse 16

इति श्रुत्वा हरौ शापं ब्रह्मशापाद्विमुच्यते ।
तदिदं श्रद्धया लोकैः श्रोतव्यं शुद्धबुद्धिभिः ॥१६॥

*iti śrutvā harau śāpaṁ brahma-śāpād vimucyate |*
*tad idaṁ śraddhayā lokaiḥ śrotavyaṁ śuddha-buddhibhiḥ ||16||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *śrutvā* — having heard; *harau* — on Hari; *śāpam* — of the curse; *brahma* — of a brahmana; *śāpāt* — from the curse; *vimucyate* — is freed; *tat idam* — this; *śraddhayā* — with faith; *lokaiḥ* — by people; *śrotavyam* — should be heard; *śuddha* — pure; *buddhibhiḥ* — whose intelligence.

**16.** Whoever hears thus of the curse [laid] on Hari is freed from a brahmana's curse. Therefore this should be heard with faith by people of pure intelligence.

*Note.* A *phala-śruti*, "the fruit of hearing".

### Verse 17

अन्येद्युः पद्मिनीं मुद्रां करेणार्कोऽपसारयन् ।
उदयाद्रेः समुत्तस्थौ विलासी शयनादिव ॥१७॥

*anyedyuḥ padminīṁ mudrāṁ kareṇārko 'pasārayan |*
*udayādreḥ samuttasthau vilāsī śayanād iva ||17||*

*Word for word:* *anyedyuḥ* — on the next day; *padminīm* — of the lotuses; *mudrām* — the seal; *kareṇa* — with its ray (hand); *arkaḥ* — the sun; *apasārayan* — removing; *udaya* — of sunrise; *adreḥ* — from the mountain; *samuttasthau* — rose; *vilāsī* — a lover; *śayanāt* — from his bed; *iva* — like.

**17.** On the next day the sun, removing with its ray-hand the seal from the lotuses, rose from the mountain of sunrise like a lover from his bed.

*Note.* At night the lotuses are closed, as if sealed; *kara* means both "ray" and "hand". *Padminī* is both "a lotus pond" and a type of beautiful woman.

### Verse 18

ततो गौराङ्गचन्द्रोऽपि ब्राह्मणान् सज्जनान् बहून् ।
पाठयन् पूर्णपीयूषरश्मिवत् स व्यरोचत ॥१८॥

*tato gaurāṅga-candro 'pi brāhmaṇān saj-janān bahūn |*
*pāṭhayan pūrṇa-pīyūṣa-raśmivat sa vyarocata ||18||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *gaurāṅga-candraḥ* — Gaurangachandra; *api* — too; *brāhmaṇān* — brahmanas; *sat-janān* — virtuous people; *bahūn* — many; *pāṭhayan* — teaching; *pūrṇa* — full; *pīyūṣa-raśmi* — the nectar-rayed (moon); *vat* — like; *saḥ* — He; *vyarocata* — shone.

**18.** Then Gaurangachandra too, teaching many virtuous brahmanas, shone like the full nectar-rayed moon.

### Verse 19

क्षणाद्वैह्वल्यसम्भिन्नः स्खलत्सर्व्वतनुः प्रभुः ।
मधूनि देहि देहीति बभाषे मधुराननः ॥१९॥

*kṣaṇād vaihvalya-sambhinnaḥ skhalat-sarva-tanuḥ prabhuḥ |*
*madhūni dehi dehīti babhāṣe madhurānanaḥ ||19||*

*Word for word:* *kṣaṇāt* — suddenly; *vaihvalya* — by agitation; *sambhinnaḥ* — overcome; *skhalat* — staggering; *sarva* — whole; *tanuḥ* — whose body; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *madhūni* — honey (an intoxicating drink); *dehi dehi* — give, give; *iti* — thus; *babhāṣe* — said; *madhura* — sweet; *ānanaḥ* — whose face.

**19.** Suddenly the Lord, overcome by agitation, His whole body staggering, His face sweet, began to say: "Give [Me] honey, give!"

*Note.* *Madhu* is honey and also an intoxicating drink (*vāruṇī*), beloved of Balarama. The episode: Murari 2.14; Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 17.115–120 ("Give Me honey!" — Nityananda brings Ganga water; Chandrashekhara, *ācārya-śekhara*, sees Balarama in the Lord; Vanamali sees the golden plough). In the Chaitanya-bhagavata there are similar scenes — Madhya 3.145–162 and 5.37–50 ("Bring wine!"; the Lord asks Nityananda for the plough and the club) — but not in the house of Murari.

### Verse 20

आश्चर्य्यमाश्चर्य्यमिदं चरितं परमात्मनः ।
हाटकाचलगौरोऽयं रौप्याचल इवाभवत् ॥२०॥

*āścaryam āścaryam idaṁ caritaṁ paramātmanaḥ |*
*hāṭakācala-gauro 'yaṁ raupyācala ivābhavat ||20||*

*Word for word:* *āścaryam āścaryam* — wonderful, wonderful; *idam* — this; *caritam* — deed; *parama* — of the Supreme; *ātmanaḥ* — Soul; *hāṭaka* — of gold; *acala* — [like] a mountain; *gauraḥ* — golden; *ayam* — He; *raupya* — of silver; *acalaḥ* — a mountain; *iva* — like; *abhavat* — became.

**20.** Wonderful, wonderful is this deed of the Supreme Soul: He, golden as a mountain of gold, became like a mountain of silver!

*Note.* Balarama is white; Gaura "turns white", taking on His mood. The edition has *रोप्याचल*; we read *raupya-*.

### Verse 21

सीरपाणिं नीलवासःसमलङ्कृतविग्रहम् ।
घूर्णापूर्णाक्षियुगलं मदमत्तविचेष्टितम् ॥२१॥

*sīra-pāṇiṁ nīla-vāsaḥ-samalaṅkṛta-vigraham |*
*ghūrṇā-pūrṇākṣi-yugalaṁ mada-matta-viceṣṭitam ||21||*

*Word for word:* *sīra* — a plough; *pāṇim* — [Him] in whose hand; *nīla* — blue; *vāsaḥ* — with a garment; *samalaṅkṛta* — adorned; *vigraham* — whose body; *ghūrṇā* — with rolling; *pūrṇa* — filled; *akṣi* — of eyes; *yugalam* — whose pair; *mada* — by intoxication; *matta* — of one inebriated; *viceṣṭitam* — whose movements.

**21.** [They saw Him] with a plough in His hand, His body adorned with a blue garment, His eyes rolling, His movements those of one inebriated with intoxication —

*Note.* The plough (*sīra*, *hala*) and the blue garment are attributes of Balarama (*Haladhara*, *Nīlāmbara*). Verses 21–22 form one sentence.

### Verse 22

एवं तत्तत्क्षणे सर्व्वे ददृशुस्ते मुदान्विताः ।
रोहिण्यङ्गभुवो भावं दधानं परमेश्वरम् ॥२२॥

*evaṁ tat-tat-kṣaṇe sarve dadṛśus te mudānvitāḥ |*
*rohiṇy-aṅga-bhuvo bhāvaṁ dadhānaṁ parameśvaram ||22||*

*Word for word:* *evam* — thus; *tat-tat* — at that very; *kṣaṇe* — moment; *sarve* — all; *dadṛśuḥ* — saw; *te* — they; *mudā* — with joy; *anvitāḥ* — filled; *rohiṇī* — of Rohini; *aṅga* — from the body; *bhuvaḥ* — of the one born (the son); *bhāvam* — the mood; *dadhānam* — assuming; *parama* — the Supreme; *īśvaram* — Lord.

**22.** — thus at that very moment they all, filled with joy, saw the Supreme Lord assuming the mood of the son of Rohini.

*Note.* The son of Rohini is Balarama. The edition has *दधानां*; we read *dadhānam*.

### Verse 23

कीर्त्तयद्भिस्ततः सर्व्वैर्जनैः सह महाप्रभुः ।
मुरारिगुप्तनिलये जगाम परमोत्सुकः ॥२३॥

*kīrtayadbhis tataḥ sarvair janaiḥ saha mahāprabhuḥ |*
*murāri-gupta-nilaye jagāma paramotsukaḥ ||23||*

*Word for word:* *kīrtayadbhiḥ* — chanting; *tataḥ* — then; *sarvaiḥ* — all; *janaiḥ* — the people; *saha* — together with; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *murāri-gupta* — of Murari Gupta; *nilaye* — to the house; *jagāma* — went; *parama* — extremely; *utsukaḥ* — eager.

**23.** Then Mahaprabhu, extremely eager, went together with all the chanting people to the house of Murari Gupta.

### Verse 24

मधूनि देहि देहीति तत्रापि मधुराक्षरम् ।
उक्त्वाम्बुपात्रं हस्तेन धृत्वाम्बूनि भृशं पपौ ॥२४॥

*madhūni dehi dehīti tatrāpi madhurākṣaram |*
*uktvāmbu-pātraṁ hastena dhṛtvāmbūni bhṛśaṁ papau ||24||*

*Word for word:* *madhūni* — honey; *dehi dehi* — give, give; *iti* — thus; *tatra api* — there too; *madhura* — sweet; *akṣaram* — in words; *uktvā* — having said; *ambu* — of water; *pātram* — a vessel; *hastena* — with His hand; *dhṛtvā* — having taken; *ambūni* — the water; *bhṛśam* — eagerly; *papau* — drank.

**24.** There too He said in sweet words, "Give [Me] honey, give!" — and, taking a vessel of water in His hand, He drank the water eagerly.

*Note.* The edition has *उक्ताम्बुपात्रं*; we read *uktvāmbu-pātram* (the sandhi of *uktvā* + *ambu*).

### Verse 25

मदघूर्णितलोलाक्षः क्षणदानाथसुन्दरः ।
शुक्लैर्महोभिर्गेहस्य शैत्यं कुर्व्वन्ननर्त्त सः ॥२५॥

*mada-ghūrṇita-lolākṣaḥ kṣaṇadā-nātha-sundaraḥ |*
*śuklair mahobhir gehasya śaityaṁ kurvan nanarta saḥ ||25||*

*Word for word:* *mada* — from intoxication; *ghūrṇita* — rolling; *lola* — restless; *akṣaḥ* — whose eyes; *kṣaṇadā* — of the night; *nātha* — [like] the lord (the moon); *sundaraḥ* — beautiful; *śuklaiḥ* — with white; *mahobhiḥ* — rays; *gehasya* — of the house; *śaityam* — coolness; *kurvan* — making; *nanarta* — danced; *saḥ* — He.

**25.** His restless eyes rolling from intoxication, beautiful as the lord of the night, He danced, bringing coolness to the house with white rays [like the moon].

*Note.* The edition has *घूर्न्नित* and *शैत्यं* ("coolness"); the Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same — therefore we keep *śaityam* (rather than *śauklyam*, "whiteness"): the Lord, like the moon, gives coolness.

### Verse 26

नाहं स कृष्णो वचसा योऽसौ शीघ्रं सुखी भवेत् ।
तदानयानय भृशं मधून्यद्य समर्पय ॥२६॥

*nāhaṁ sa kṛṣṇo vacasā yo 'sau śīghraṁ sukhī bhavet |*
*tad ānayānaya bhṛśaṁ madhūny adya samarpaya ||26||*

*Word for word:* *na* — not; *aham* — I; *saḥ* — that; *kṛṣṇaḥ* — Krishna; *vacasā* — by words; *yaḥ asau* — who; *śīghram* — quickly; *sukhī* — satisfied; *bhavet* — becomes; *tat* — therefore; *ānaya ānaya* — bring, bring; *bhṛśam* — plentifully; *madhūni* — honey; *adya* — now; *samarpaya* — offer.

**26.** "I am not that Krishna who is quickly satisfied by words. So bring, bring — offer [Me] plenty of honey now!"

*Note.* The sense is unclear (?). Probably Gaura, as Balarama, says: "I am not Krishna, for whom it is enough to be glorified — I want the intoxicating drink." The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 27

इत्युक्त्वैकेन हस्तेन द्विजैकं प्राक्षिपत् प्रभुः ।
आरादेव पपातासौ मल्लोऽपि बलवत्तरः ॥२७॥

*ity uktvaikena hastena dvijaikaṁ prākṣipat prabhuḥ |*
*ārād eva papātāsau mallo 'pi balavattaraḥ ||27||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *uktvā* — having said; *ekena* — with one; *hastena* — hand; *dvija* — brahmana; *ekam* — a certain; *prākṣipat* — hurled away; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *ārāt eva* — far off; *papāta* — fell; *asau* — he; *mallaḥ* — a wrestler; *api* — though; *balavattaraḥ* — very strong.

**27.** Having said this, the Lord hurled away a certain brahmana with one hand, and he fell far off, though he was a very strong wrestler.

*Note.* The edition has *इत्युनक्त्वैकेन*, a misprint.

### Verse 28

प्रातरेव बलावेशविवशो रजनीमुखे ।
प्रबुद्धः स्यात्तदा स्नानं करोति कमलेक्षणः ॥२८॥

*prātar eva balāveśa-vivaśo rajanī-mukhe |*
*prabuddhaḥ syāt tadā snānaṁ karoti kamalekṣaṇaḥ ||28||*

*Word for word:* *prātaḥ* — from the morning; *eva* — indeed; *bala* — of Balarama; *āveśa* — by the absorption; *vivaśaḥ* — overpowered; *rajanī* — of the night; *mukhe* — at the beginning; *prabuddhaḥ* — come to Himself; *syāt* — would be; *tadā* — then; *snānam* — a bath; *karoti* — takes; *kamala* — lotus; *īkṣaṇaḥ* — eyed.

**28.** Overpowered from the very morning by His absorption in Balarama, the lotus-eyed [Lord] would come to Himself only at nightfall — and then He would take His bath.

*Note.* *Āveśa*, literally "entering", is the state in which another form of the Lord manifests in Gaura.

### Verse 29

अपरेद्युर्दीप्यमानस्तेजोभिरतिदुःसहैः ।
मुहुर्मुमोह भगवान् विकीर्णकचसञ्चयः ॥२९॥

*aparedyur dīpyamānas tejobhir ati-duḥsahaiḥ |*
*muhur mumoha bhagavān vikīrṇa-kaca-sañcayaḥ ||29||*

*Word for word:* *aparedyuḥ* — on another day; *dīpyamānaḥ* — blazing; *tejobhiḥ* — with effulgence; *ati* — utterly; *duḥsahaiḥ* — unbearable; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *mumoha* — swooned; *bhagavān* — Bhagavan; *vikīrṇa* — dishevelled; *kaca* — of hair; *sañcayaḥ* — whose mass.

**29.** On another day Bhagavan, blazing with an utterly unbearable effulgence, His mass of hair dishevelled, swooned again and again.

### Verse 30

बलदेवावेशरम्यं मत्तद्विरदगामिनम् ।
मत्तसिंहसमोल्लासं मदघूर्णितलोचनम् ॥३०॥

*baladevāveśa-ramyaṁ matta-dvirada-gāminam |*
*matta-siṁha-samollāsaṁ mada-ghūrṇita-locanam ||30||*

*Word for word:* *baladeva* — in Baladeva; *āveśa* — by the absorption; *ramyam* — beautiful; *matta* — of a maddened; *dvirada* — elephant; *gāminam* — having the gait; *matta* — a maddened; *siṁha* — lion; *sama* — like; *ullāsam* — whose exultation; *mada* — from intoxication; *ghūrṇita* — rolling; *locanam* — whose eyes.

**30.** Him — beautiful in His absorption in Baladeva, moving with the gait of a maddened elephant, exulting like a maddened lion, His eyes rolling from intoxication,

*Note.* Verses 30–32 form one sentence.

### Verse 31

रज्यद्गण्डस्थलं चण्डरश्मिकोटिसमप्रभम् ।
वैह्वल्यनुन्नहृदयं दृष्ट्वेत्थं ते तदावदन् ॥३१॥

*rajyad-gaṇḍa-sthalaṁ caṇḍa-raśmi-koṭi-sama-prabham |*
*vaihvalya-nunna-hṛdayaṁ dṛṣṭvetthaṁ te tadāvadan ||31||*

*Word for word:* *rajyat* — reddening; *gaṇḍa-sthalam* — whose cheeks; *caṇḍa-raśmi* — of hot-rayed (suns); *koṭi* — millions; *sama* — equal to; *prabham* — whose radiance; *vaihvalya* — by agitation; *nunna* — stirred; *hṛdayam* — whose heart; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *ittham* — thus; *te* — they; *tadā* — then; *avadan* — said.

**31.** His cheeks reddening, His radiance equal to that of millions of hot-rayed suns, His heart stirred by agitation — seeing Him thus, they then said:

### Verse 32

किमिदं नाथ को वायं वेशः किम्वा परं महः ।
किमत्र कारणं ब्रूहि भगवान् सर्वभावनः ॥३२॥

*kim idaṁ nātha ko vāyaṁ veśaḥ kiṁ vā paraṁ mahaḥ |*
*kim atra kāraṇaṁ brūhi bhagavān sarva-bhāvanaḥ ||32||*

*Word for word:* *kim* — what; *idam* — this; *nātha* — O Lord; *kaḥ* — what; *vā* — or; *ayam* — this; *veśaḥ* — guise; *kim vā* — or what; *param* — supreme; *mahaḥ* — splendour; *kim* — what; *atra* — here; *kāraṇam* — the cause; *brūhi* — tell; *bhagavān* — [You are] Bhagavan; *sarva* — of all; *bhāvanaḥ* — the creator.

**32.** "What is this, O Lord? What is this guise, what this supreme splendour? Tell [us] what the cause of it is — for You are Bhagavan, the creator of all!"

*Note.* The edition writes *कोवायं* as one word. *Bhagavān* is nominative where the vocative *bhagavan* would be expected; the metre is the same either way. We take it as "[You are] Bhagavan"; it may also be understood as an address. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 33

एवं बलावेशलीलाललितो ललितास्पदम् ।
उवाच स्खलितं शश्वद्वचनं मदघूर्णितः ॥३३॥

*evaṁ balāveśa-līlā-lalito lalitāspadam |*
*uvāca skhalitaṁ śaśvad vacanaṁ mada-ghūrṇitaḥ ||33||*

*Word for word:* *evam* — thus; *bala* — in Balarama; *āveśa* — of absorption; *līlā* — by the play; *lalitaḥ* — charming; *lalita* — of charm; *āspadam* — the abode; *uvāca* — spoke; *skhalitam* — faltering; *śaśvat* — again and again; *vacanam* — speech; *mada* — by intoxication; *ghūrṇitaḥ* — reeling.

**33.** Thus He, charming in the play of His absorption in Balarama, reeling with intoxication, spoke words that were an abode of charm, faltering again and again:

*Note.* *Lalitāspadam* (neuter) may be taken with *vacanam*, "words that were an abode of charm", or, as a noun in apposition, with the Lord: "He, the abode of charm".

### Verse 34

दृष्टो मया सीरपाणिर्नीलाम्बरधरः पुमान् ।
रौप्याचल इव श्रीमान् कोऽप्यसौ मादृशैरिह ॥३४॥

*dṛṣṭo mayā sīra-pāṇir nīlāmbara-dharaḥ pumān |*
*raupyācala iva śrīmān ko 'py asau mādṛśair iha ||34||*

*Word for word:* *dṛṣṭaḥ* — has been seen; *mayā* — by Me; *sīra* — a plough; *pāṇiḥ* — in whose hand; *nīla* — blue; *ambara* — a garment; *dharaḥ* — wearing; *pumān* — a man; *raupya* — of silver; *acalaḥ* — a mountain; *iva* — like; *śrīmān* — splendid; *kaḥ api* — someone; *asau* — that; *mādṛśaiḥ* — by such as Me; *iha* — here.

**34.** "I have seen a man with a plough in His hand, wearing a blue garment, splendid like a mountain of silver — someone [wondrous], [seen] here [only] by such as Me."

*Note.* The end of the verse (*mādṛśair iha*) is unclear; the translation is tentative. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 35

श्रीचन्द्रशेखराचार्यरत्नं तत्र जगाद तम् ।
यस्त्वया नाथ दृष्टोऽसौ कुत्रास्ते बलिनां वरः ॥३५॥

*śrī-candraśekharācārya-ratnaṁ tatra jagāda tam |*
*yas tvayā nātha dṛṣṭo 'sau kutrāste balināṁ varaḥ ||35||*

*Word for word:* *śrī-candraśekhara* — Sri Chandrashekhara; *ācārya-ratnam* — Acharyaratna (the jewel among acharyas); *tatra* — then; *jagāda* — said; *tam* — to Him; *yaḥ* — who; *tvayā* — by You; *nātha* — O Lord; *dṛṣṭaḥ* — has been seen; *asau* — that one; *kutra* — where; *āste* — is; *balinām* — of the strong; *varaḥ* — the best.

**35.** Then Sri Chandrashekhara Acharyaratna said to Him: "O Lord, where is that best of the strong whom You have seen?"

*Note.* Chandrashekhara Acharya (Acharyaratna) is Gaura's maternal uncle. The cases in the first line look confused: *ratnam* and *tam* are both accusative in form, and *ratnaḥ … tam* would be expected. Since *ratna* is a neuter noun, however, *-ratnam* may also be the nominative ("Chandrashekhara, the jewel among acharyas"), with *tam*, "to Him", as the object of *jagāda*. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 36

एवं वदन् ददर्शासौ तमेव हलिनः प्रभोः ।
आवेशावेशविन्यासं बिभ्रतं गौरसुन्दरम् ॥३६॥

*evaṁ vadan dadarśāsau tam eva halinaḥ prabhoḥ |*
*āveśāveśa-vinyāsaṁ bibhrataṁ gaura-sundaram ||36||*

*Word for word:* *evam* — thus; *vadan* — speaking; *dadarśa* — saw; *asau* — he; *tam eva* — Him indeed; *halinaḥ* — of the Plough-bearer; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *āveśa-āveśa* — of absorption upon absorption; *vinyāsam* — the appearance; *bibhratam* — bearing; *gaura* — Gaura; *sundaram* — beautiful.

**36.** Even as he spoke thus, he saw that very [one] — beautiful Gaura, bearing the appearance of the Lord, the Plough-bearer, in absorption upon absorption.

*Note.* *Āveśāveśa* is probably a dittography (a misprint). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 37

ततस्तद्भावमापन्नः श्रीमान् कोटीन्दुसुन्दरः ।
गौराङ्गो नर्त्तनं चक्रे तैः सर्व्वैर्मुदितात्मभिः ॥३७॥

*tatas tad-bhāvam āpannaḥ śrīmān koṭīndu-sundaraḥ |*
*gaurāṅgo nartanaṁ cakre taiḥ sarvair muditātmabhiḥ ||37||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *tat* — His (Balarama's); *bhāvam* — the mood; *āpannaḥ* — having assumed; *śrīmān* — splendid; *koṭi* — than millions; *indu* — of moons; *sundaraḥ* — more beautiful; *gaurāṅgaḥ* — Gauranga; *nartanam* — dancing; *cakre* — performed; *taiḥ* — with them; *sarvaiḥ* — with all; *mudita* — joyful; *ātmabhiḥ* — whose hearts.

**37.** Then splendid Gauranga, more beautiful than millions of moons, having assumed that mood, danced together with all of them, their hearts full of joy.

### Verse 38

नृत्यतस्तस्य पीयूषद्रवसिक्तैः पदे पदे ।
जल्पितैस्ते स्वर्गसुखमधरीचक्रुरञ्जसा ॥३८॥

*nṛtyatas tasya pīyūṣa-drava-siktaiḥ pade pade |*
*jalpitais te svarga-sukham adharī-cakrur añjasā ||38||*

*Word for word:* *nṛtyataḥ* — of the dancing; *tasya* — of Him; *pīyūṣa* — of nectar; *drava* — with the juice; *siktaiḥ* — sprinkled; *pade pade* — at every step; *jalpitaiḥ* — by the words; *te* — they; *svarga* — of heaven; *sukham* — the happiness; *adharī-cakruḥ* — placed beneath; *añjasā* — easily.

**38.** By the words of the dancing [Lord], sprinkled at every step with the juice of nectar, they easily placed the happiness of heaven beneath [their own].

### Verse 39

एवं दिनं स नृत्येन निनाय परमप्रभुः ।
कीर्त्तनामृतवापीषु स्नातैस्तैः स्वजनैः सह ॥३९॥

*evaṁ dinaṁ sa nṛtyena nināya parama-prabhuḥ |*
*kīrtanāmṛta-vāpīṣu snātais taiḥ sva-janaiḥ saha ||39||*

*Word for word:* *evam* — thus; *dinam* — the day; *saḥ* — He; *nṛtyena* — in dancing; *nināya* — spent; *parama* — the Supreme; *prabhuḥ* — Lord; *kīrtana* — of kirtana; *amṛta* — of the nectar; *vāpīṣu* — in the ponds; *snātaiḥ* — who had bathed; *taiḥ* — with those; *sva* — His own; *janaiḥ* — people; *saha* — together.

**39.** Thus the Supreme Lord spent the day in dancing together with His own people, who had bathed in the ponds of the nectar of kirtana.

### Verse 40

ततोऽपराह्णे भूयोऽस्मिन् नृत्यति श्रीयुते मरुत् ।
मदगन्धैर्दिशः सर्व्वाः समन्तात् समपूजयत् ॥४०॥

*tato 'parāhṇe bhūyo 'smin nṛtyati śrī-yute marut |*
*mada-gandhair diśaḥ sarvāḥ samantāt samapūjayat ||40||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *aparāhṇe* — in the afternoon; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *asmin* — when He; *nṛtyati* — was dancing; *śrī-yute* — splendid; *marut* — the wind; *mada* — intoxicating (of musk); *gandhaiḥ* — with fragrances; *diśaḥ* — the quarters; *sarvāḥ* — all; *samantāt* — all around; *samapūjayat* — honoured.

**40.** Then in the afternoon, when the splendid [Lord] was dancing again, the wind honoured all the quarters all around with intoxicating fragrances.

*Note.* The edition has *श्रीयते* and *समपूजयत्*; we read *śrī-yute* (as the edition itself prints in verse 50); *samapūjayat* ("honoured") is confirmed by the Gosvami edition (GGM) as well, so it is kept. *Mada-gandha* is the fragrance of musk, or of *vāruṇī*, the intoxicating drink beloved of Balarama (cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 17.112–118: the scent of *vāruṇī* in the house of Srivasa).

### Verse 41

तं तं गन्धं समाघ्राय मदोत्कटमतिस्फुटम् ।
आकस्मिकैरिव घनैर्भ्रमरैः पिदधे नभः ॥४१॥

*taṁ taṁ gandhaṁ samāghrāya madotkaṭam ati-sphuṭam |*
*ākasmikair iva ghanair bhramaraiḥ pidadhe nabhaḥ ||41||*

*Word for word:* *tam tam* — that; *gandham* — fragrance; *samāghrāya* — having smelt; *mada* — with intoxication; *utkaṭam* — laden; *ati* — very; *sphuṭam* — distinct; *ākasmikaiḥ* — sudden; *iva* — like; *ghanaiḥ* — clouds; *bhramaraiḥ* — by bees; *pidadhe* — was covered; *nabhaḥ* — the sky.

**41.** Having smelt that very distinct fragrance, laden with intoxication, the bees covered the sky like sudden clouds.

### Verse 42

श्रीरामनामा विप्राग्र्यो ददर्शाकाशमण्डलात् ।
समागतान् महाकान्तीन् महादीप्तीन् महाजनान् ॥४२॥

*śrīrāma-nāmā viprāgryo dadarśākāśa-maṇḍalāt |*
*samāgatān mahā-kāntīn mahā-dīptīn mahā-janān ||42||*

*Word for word:* *śrīrāma* — Sri Rama; *nāmā* — by name; *vipra* — of brahmanas; *agryaḥ* — the foremost; *dadarśa* — saw; *ākāśa* — of the sky; *maṇḍalāt* — from the vault; *samāgatān* — come down; *mahā* — of great; *kāntīn* — beauty; *mahā* — of great; *dīptīn* — radiance; *mahā-janān* — great beings.

**42.** The foremost of brahmanas, Sri Rama by name, saw great beings who had come down from the vault of the sky — of great beauty, of great radiance,

*Note.* Sri Rama [Pandita] is Srivasa's brother (6.6). Verses 42–44 form one sentence.

### Verse 43

दिव्यगन्धानुलिप्ताङ्गान् दिव्याभरणभूषितान् ।
दिव्यस्रग्वसनान् दिव्यान् दिव्यरूपगुणाश्रयान् ॥४३॥

*divya-gandhānuliptāṅgān divyābharaṇa-bhūṣitān |*
*divya-srag-vasanān divyān divya-rūpa-guṇāśrayān ||43||*

*Word for word:* *divya* — with heavenly; *gandha* — fragrances; *anulipta* — anointed; *aṅgān* — whose bodies; *divya* — with heavenly; *ābharaṇa* — ornaments; *bhūṣitān* — adorned; *divya* — heavenly; *srak* — garlands; *vasanān* — [wearing] and garments; *divyān* — heavenly; *divya* — of heavenly; *rūpa* — beauty; *guṇa* — and qualities; *āśrayān* — abodes.

**43.** their bodies anointed with heavenly fragrances, adorned with heavenly ornaments, wearing heavenly garlands and garments — heavenly [beings], abodes of heavenly beauty and qualities,

### Verse 44

एककर्णधृताम्भोजकर्णपूरमनोहरान् ।
उष्णीषपट्टसंश्लिष्टमस्तकान् हृष्टमानसान् ॥४४॥

*eka-karṇa-dhṛtāmbhoja-karṇa-pūra-manoharān |*
*uṣṇīṣa-paṭṭa-saṁśliṣṭa-mastakān hṛṣṭa-mānasān ||44||*

*Word for word:* *eka* — in one; *karṇa* — ear; *dhṛta* — worn; *ambhoja* — of lotus; *karṇa-pūra* — by an earring; *manoharān* — captivating; *uṣṇīṣa* — with turbans; *paṭṭa* — silken; *saṁśliṣṭa* — wrapped; *mastakān* — whose heads; *hṛṣṭa* — joyful; *mānasān* — whose hearts.

**44.** captivating with a lotus earring worn in one ear, their heads wrapped in silken turbans, their hearts joyful.

*Note.* An earring in one ear is a mark of Balarama (*eka-kuṇḍala*); these are evidently His associates.

### Verse 45

अन्ये तस्य मुखाच्छ्रुत्वा ननृतुर्जगुरञ्जसा ।
कीर्त्तनेन हरेर्नाम्नामाम्नायसुधियो भृशम् ॥४५॥

*anye tasya mukhāc chrutvā nanṛtur jagur añjasā |*
*kīrtanena harer nāmnām āmnāya-sudhiyo bhṛśam ||45||*

*Word for word:* *anye* — others; *tasya* — his; *mukhāt* — from the mouth; *śrutvā* — having heard; *nanṛtuḥ* — danced; *jaguḥ* — sang; *añjasā* — at once; *kīrtanena* — with the kirtana; *hareḥ* — of Hari; *nāmnām* — of the names; *āmnāya* — in the Vedas; *sudhiyaḥ* — learned; *bhṛśam* — ardently.

**45.** Others, learned in the Vedas, hearing this from his mouth, at once danced and sang ardently, with the kirtana of the names of Hari.

### Verse 46

तत्रैव कश्चिद्विप्राग्र्यो वनमाली महाशयः ।
अपश्यत् पर्वताकारं हलं काञ्चननिर्मितम् ॥४६॥

*tatraiva kaścid viprāgryo vanamālī mahāśayaḥ |*
*apaśyat parvatākāraṁ halaṁ kāñcana-nirmitam ||46||*

*Word for word:* *tatra eva* — right there; *kaścit* — a certain; *vipra* — of brahmanas; *agryaḥ* — the foremost; *vanamālī* — Vanamali; *mahā* — great; *āśayaḥ* — [whose] soul; *apaśyat* — saw; *parvata* — of a mountain; *ākāram* — of the size; *halam* — a plough; *kāñcana* — of gold; *nirmitam* — made.

**46.** Right there a certain high-souled foremost of brahmanas, Vanamali, saw a plough made of gold, the size of a mountain.

*Note.* Vanamali Acharya; cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 17.119: "Vanamali Acharya saw a golden plough in the hand of Balarama." Probably the same Vanamali who arranged the marriage with Lakshmipriya (Murari 1.9); the father of Gadadhara is Madhava Mishra, not Vanamali.

### Verse 47

दृष्ट्वा सविस्मयो भूत्वा लोचनाश्रुझराकुलः ।
पुलकौघपरीताङ्गो न सस्मार तदा तनुम् ॥४७॥

*dṛṣṭvā sa-vismayo bhūtvā locanāśru-jharākulaḥ |*
*pulakaugha-parītāṅgo na sasmāra tadā tanum ||47||*

*Word for word:* *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *sa* — with; *vismayaḥ* — wonder; *bhūtvā* — having become; *locana* — from the eyes; *aśru* — of tears; *jhara* — by streams; *ākulaḥ* — overwhelmed; *pulaka* — of hairs standing on end; *ogha* — with a flood; *parīta* — covered; *aṅgaḥ* — whose body; *na* — not; *sasmāra* — remembered; *tadā* — then; *tanum* — the body.

**47.** Seeing this, he was filled with wonder; overwhelmed by streams of tears from his eyes, his body covered with a flood of hairs standing on end, he then forgot his body.

### Verse 48

ततो ननर्त्त तैः सार्द्धं निजकीर्त्तनमङ्गलैः ।
हलायुधावेशरम्यो रम्यगौराङ्गसुन्दरः ॥४८॥

*tato nanarta taiḥ sārdhaṁ nija-kīrtana-maṅgalaiḥ |*
*halāyudhāveśa-ramyo ramya-gaurāṅga-sundaraḥ ||48||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *nanarta* — danced; *taiḥ* — with them; *sārdham* — together; *nija* — of His own; *kīrtana* — of the kirtana; *maṅgalaiḥ* — auspicious; *halāyudha* — of Halayudha (Balarama); *āveśa* — by the absorption; *ramyaḥ* — charming; *ramya* — charming; *gaurāṅga* — Gauranga; *sundaraḥ* — beautiful.

**48.** Then charming, beautiful Gauranga, charming in His absorption in Halayudha, danced together with them — the auspicious [singers] of His own kirtana.

*Note.* *Halāyudha*, "He whose weapon is the plough", is Balarama.

### Verse 49

दिवि देवगणाः सर्वे समहेन्द्राः सपद्मजाः ।
प्रणेमुः कुसुमस्तोमं वर्षन्तो नतकन्धराः ॥४९॥

*divi deva-gaṇāḥ sarve sa-mahendrāḥ sa-padmajāḥ |*
*praṇemuḥ kusuma-stomaṁ varṣanto nata-kandharāḥ ||49||*

*Word for word:* *divi* — in the sky; *deva* — of gods; *gaṇāḥ* — the hosts; *sarve* — all; *sa* — with; *mahā-indrāḥ* — Mahendra; *sa* — with; *padma-jāḥ* — the Lotus-born; *praṇemuḥ* — bowed down; *kusuma* — of flowers; *stomam* — a multitude; *varṣantaḥ* — showering; *nata* — bent; *kandharāḥ* — whose necks.

**49.** In the sky all the hosts of the gods, with Mahendra and the Lotus-born, bowed down with bent necks, showering a multitude of flowers.

*Note.* Mahendra is Indra; the Lotus-born is Brahma.

### Verse 50

एवं निशावशेषोऽभून्नृत्यति श्रीयुते प्रभौ ।
चन्द्रश्चरमशैलान्तं चुचुम्ब शनकैरिव ॥५०॥

*evaṁ niśāvaśeṣo 'bhūn nṛtyati śrī-yute prabhau |*
*candraś carama-śailāntaṁ cucumba śanakair iva ||50||*

*Word for word:* *evam* — thus; *niśā* — of the night; *avaśeṣaḥ* — the end; *abhūt* — came; *nṛtyati* — while dancing; *śrī-yute* — splendid; *prabhau* — the Lord; *candraḥ* — the moon; *carama* — of the last (western); *śaila* — mountain; *antam* — the edge; *cucumba* — kissed; *śanakaiḥ* — softly; *iva* — as if.

**50.** Thus, while the splendid Lord was dancing, the night drew to its end, and the moon, as it were, softly kissed the edge of the western mountain.

*Note.* *Carama-śaila* is the mountain of sunset.

### Verse 51

नृत्यतस्तस्य नटनदर्शनार्थमियं किमु ।
पुरन्दराशा तरुणी बभूवात्यनुरागिणी ॥५१॥

*nṛtyatas tasya naṭana-darśanārtham iyaṁ kim u |*
*purandarāśā taruṇī babhūvāty-anurāgiṇī ||51||*

*Word for word:* *nṛtyataḥ* — of the dancing; *tasya* — of Him; *naṭana* — the dance; *darśana* — to see; *artham* — in order; *iyam* — this; *kim u* — was it not?; *purandara* — of Purandara; *āśā* — the quarter (the east); *taruṇī* — a young [maiden]; *babhūva* — became; *ati* — exceedingly; *anurāgiṇī* — enamoured (crimson).

**51.** Was it not in order to see the dance of the dancing [Lord] that this young [maiden], the quarter of Purandara, became so enamoured and crimson?

*Note.* The quarter of Purandara (Indra) is the east. *Anurāga* means both "love" and "redness" (the dawn).

### Verse 52

मन्दगन्धवहः शश्वज्ज्योत्स्नयाभ्युपगूहितः ।
कुमुदानि समाधुन्वन् गौराङ्घ्रिमभजत्ततः ॥५२॥

*manda-gandhavahaḥ śaśvaj jyotsnayābhyupagūhitaḥ |*
*kumudāni samādhunvan gaurāṅghrim abhajat tataḥ ||52||*

*Word for word:* *manda* — gentle; *gandhavahaḥ* — the wind (bearer of fragrance); *śaśvat* — constantly; *jyotsnayā* — by the moonlight; *abhyupagūhitaḥ* — embraced; *kumudāni* — the night lotuses; *samādhunvan* — stirring; *gaura* — of Gaura; *aṅghrim* — the feet; *abhajat* — served; *tataḥ* — then.

**52.** Then the gentle wind, constantly embraced by the moonlight, stirring the night lotuses, served the feet of Gaura.

*Note.* The edition has *सनाधुन्वन्*; we read *samādhunvan*.

### Verse 53

ततस्तैः स्वजनैः सार्द्धं स्वर्णद्यां जगतां प्रभुः ।
उपेयिवान् बभौ नाथो यथा मेरुः सहाद्रिभिः ॥५३॥

*tatas taiḥ sva-janaiḥ sārdhaṁ svar-ṇadyāṁ jagatāṁ prabhuḥ |*
*upeyivān babhau nātho yathā meruḥ sahādribhiḥ ||53||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *taiḥ* — with those; *sva* — His own; *janaiḥ* — people; *sārdham* — together; *svaḥ* — heavenly; *nadyām* — to the river; *jagatām* — of the worlds; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *upeyivān* — having come; *babhau* — shone; *nāthaḥ* — the Master; *yathā* — as; *meruḥ* — Meru; *saha* — with; *adribhiḥ* — the mountains.

**53.** Then the Lord of the worlds, the Master, having come with His own people to the heavenly river, shone like Meru among the mountains.

*Note.* The edition has *उपोथिवान्*; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *upeyivān* ("having come", the perfect participle of *upa-√i*), and so we read. The heavenly river is the Ganga.

### Verse 54

अवगाह्य ततो गङ्गां गाङ्गेयाचलसुन्दरः ।
करवारिभिरन्योन्यं चकार जलखेलनम् ॥५४॥

*avagāhya tato gaṅgāṁ gāṅgeyācala-sundaraḥ |*
*kara-vāribhir anyonyaṁ cakāra jala-khelanam ||54||*

*Word for word:* *avagāhya* — having plunged into; *tataḥ* — then; *gaṅgām* — the Ganga; *gāṅgeya* — golden; *acala* — than a mountain; *sundaraḥ* — more beautiful; *kara* — of the hands; *vāribhiḥ* — with the water; *anyonyam* — one another; *cakāra* — made; *jala* — water; *khelanam* — play.

**54.** Then, having plunged into the Ganga, He who is more beautiful than a golden mountain made water-play, [all] splashing one another with water from their hands.

*Note.* *Gāṅgeya*, "born of the Ganga", is gold (from the myth of Kartikeya). A play on *gaṅgā* and *gāṅgeya*.

### Verse 55

एवं नानाप्रकाराणि क्रीडितानि समापयन् ।
ययौ गेहं निजं गौरो यथेन्दुरुदयाचलम् ॥५५॥

*evaṁ nānā-prakārāṇi krīḍitāni samāpayan |*
*yayau gehaṁ nijaṁ gauro yathendur udayācalam ||55||*

*Word for word:* *evam* — thus; *nānā* — of various; *prakārāṇi* — kinds; *krīḍitāni* — pastimes; *samāpayan* — concluding; *yayau* — went; *geham* — to the house; *nijam* — His own; *gauraḥ* — Gaura; *yathā* — as; *induḥ* — the moon; *udaya* — of rising; *acalam* — to the mountain.

**55.** Thus concluding pastimes of various kinds, Gaura went to His own house, as the moon [goes] to the mountain of rising.

*Note.* The text has *udayācala*, the mountain of rising (in the east), not the mountain of setting.

### Verse 56

हसन्नसौ सुमधुरं श्रीवासमवदत् प्रभुः ।
वेणुं प्रयच्छ मे शीघ्रं क्व सोऽस्ति न तु दृश्यते ॥५६॥

*hasann asau sumadhuraṁ śrīvāsam avadat prabhuḥ |*
*veṇuṁ prayaccha me śīghraṁ kva so 'sti na tu dṛśyate ||56||*

*Word for word:* *hasan* — laughing; *asau* — He; *sumadhuram* — very sweetly; *śrīvāsam* — to Srivasa; *avadat* — said; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *veṇum* — the flute; *prayaccha* — give; *me* — to Me; *śīghram* — quickly; *kva* — where; *saḥ* — it; *asti* — is; *na* — not; *tu* — but; *dṛśyate* — is seen.

**56.** Laughing very sweetly, the Lord said to Srivasa: "Give Me the flute, quickly! Where is it? It is nowhere to be seen."

*Note.* From the mood of Balarama — to the mood of Krishna.

### Verse 57

ततोऽयं विप्रप्रवरो हसन्निदमभाषत ।
वेणुस्तवास्ति गोपीभिः परितः परिरक्षितः ॥५७॥

*tato 'yaṁ vipra-pravaro hasann idam abhāṣata |*
*veṇus tavāsti gopībhiḥ paritaḥ parirakṣitaḥ ||57||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *ayam* — this; *vipra* — of brahmanas; *pravaraḥ* — the best; *hasan* — laughing; *idam* — this; *abhāṣata* — said; *veṇuḥ* — the flute; *tava* — Your; *asti* — is; *gopībhiḥ* — by the gopis; *paritaḥ* — on all sides; *parirakṣitaḥ* — guarded (hidden).

**57.** Then this best of brahmanas, laughing, said: "Your flute is guarded on all sides by the gopis."

*Note.* An echo of the *vaṁśī-caurya* — the stealing of Krishna's flute by Radha and the gopis.

### Verse 58

वृन्दावनक्रीडितानि स्मृत्वा स्मृत्वा कृपानिधिः ।
सान्द्रानन्दैकसन्दोहमग्नस्तूष्णीमभूत् क्षणम् ॥५८॥

*vṛndāvana-krīḍitāni smṛtvā smṛtvā kṛpā-nidhiḥ |*
*sāndrānandaika-sandoha-magnas tūṣṇīm abhūt kṣaṇam ||58||*

*Word for word:* *vṛndāvana* — in Vrindavana; *krīḍitāni* — the pastimes; *smṛtvā smṛtvā* — remembering again and again; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *nidhiḥ* — the treasury; *sāndra* — of deep; *ānanda* — bliss; *eka* — unbroken; *sandoha* — in the flood; *magnaḥ* — immersed; *tūṣṇīm* — silent; *abhūt* — became; *kṣaṇam* — for a moment.

**58.** Remembering again and again the pastimes in Vrindavana, the treasury of mercy, immersed in an unbroken flood of deep bliss, fell silent for a moment.

### Verse 59

ततश्चातिशयाविष्टो हृष्टरोमा महाप्रभुः ।
ब्रूहि ब्रूहीति सततमुच्चैस्तं निजगाद सः ॥५९॥

*tataś cātiśayāviṣṭo hṛṣṭa-romā mahāprabhuḥ |*
*brūhi brūhīti satatam uccais taṁ nijagāda saḥ ||59||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *ca* — and; *atiśaya* — exceedingly; *āviṣṭaḥ* — absorbed; *hṛṣṭa* — standing on end; *romā* — whose hairs; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *brūhi brūhi* — speak, speak; *iti* — thus; *satatam* — incessantly; *uccaiḥ* — loudly; *tam* — to him; *nijagāda* — said; *saḥ* — He.

**59.** And then Mahaprabhu, exceedingly absorbed, His hairs standing on end, loudly and incessantly said to him: "Speak, speak!"

### Verse 60

वृन्दावनक्रीडनञ्च यमुनाक्रीडनं तथा ।
सर्वं ततोऽसौ श्रीवासो वर्णयामास भूरिशः ॥६०॥

*vṛndāvana-krīḍanañ ca yamunā-krīḍanaṁ tathā |*
*sarvaṁ tato 'sau śrīvāso varṇayām āsa bhūriśaḥ ||60||*

*Word for word:* *vṛndāvana* — in Vrindavana; *krīḍanam* — the play; *ca* — and; *yamunā* — on the Yamuna; *krīḍanam* — the play; *tathā* — also; *sarvam* — all; *tataḥ* — then; *asau* — this; *śrīvāsaḥ* — Srivasa; *varṇayām āsa* — described; *bhūriśaḥ* — at length.

**60.** Then this Srivasa described everything at length — the play in Vrindavana and also the play on the Yamuna.

### Verse 61

पुरा वृन्दारण्ये तरुणहरिणाक्षीभिरनिशं
त्वयि प्रेमाविष्टे विलसति य आसीत् स विभवः ।
त्वयैवातृप्तेनाजनि न यदि तन्नाथ रभसः
कथङ्कारं नित्यं नव नव इवायं समभवत् ॥६१॥

*purā vṛndāraṇye taruṇa-hariṇākṣībhir aniśaṁ*
*tvayi premāviṣṭe vilasati ya āsīt sa vibhavaḥ |*
*tvayaivātṛptenājani na yadi tan nātha rabhasaḥ*
*kathaṅkāraṁ nityaṁ nava nava ivāyaṁ samabhavat ||61||*

*Word for word:* *purā* — once; *vṛndā-araṇye* — in the forest of Vrinda; *taruṇa* — young; *hariṇa* — of does; *akṣībhiḥ* — with [maidens] with the eyes; *aniśam* — incessantly; *tvayi* — when You; *prema* — by love; *āviṣṭe* — absorbed; *vilasati* — sported; *yaḥ* — which; *āsīt* — there was; *saḥ* — that; *vibhavaḥ* — splendour; *tvayā* — by You; *eva* — Yourself; *atṛptena* — never satiated; *ajani* — was born; *na* — not; *yadi* — if; *tat* — that; *nātha* — O Lord; *rabhasaḥ* — rapture; *katham-kāram* — how; *nityam* — eternally; *nava nava* — new and new; *iva* — as if; *ayam* — this; *samabhavat* — would have become.

**61.** "Once, in the forest of Vrinda, when You, absorbed in love, sported incessantly with young doe-eyed [maidens], there was a splendour. If that had not been born of You Yourself, O Lord, who are never satiated, how could this rapture have become eternally new, as if ever new and new?"

*Note.* The metre is *śikhariṇī*. The thought: it is the insatiability of Krishna Himself that makes His pastimes eternally new. The syntax of *ajani* in the third line is not entirely clear (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 62

आमञ्जुगुञ्जदलिपुञ्जनिकुञ्जरम्यं
वृन्दावनं निरुपमं स पुरा प्रविश्य ।
क्रीडां चकर्थ रसकौतुककामतन्त्र-
मन्त्रस्वरूप इव यत्त्वमतिप्रियं तत् ॥६२॥

*ā-mañju-guñjad-ali-puñja-nikuñja-ramyaṁ*
*vṛndāvanaṁ nirupamaṁ sa purā praviśya |*
*krīḍāṁ cakartha rasa-kautuka-kāma-tantra-*
*mantra-svarūpa iva yat tvam ati-priyaṁ tat ||62||*

*Word for word:* *ā* — exceedingly; *mañju* — sweetly; *guñjat* — humming; *ali* — of bees; *puñja* — with swarms; *nikuñja* — with bowers; *ramyam* — charming; *vṛndāvanam* — Vrindavana; *nirupamam* — incomparable; *saḥ* — that [same One]; *purā* — once; *praviśya* — having entered; *krīḍām* — play; *cakartha* — You performed; *rasa* — of rasa; *kautuka* — of delight; *kāma* — of love; *tantra* — of the science; *mantra* — of the mantra; *svarūpaḥ* — the embodiment; *iva* — as if; *yat* — which; *tvam* — You; *ati* — exceedingly; *priyam* — dear; *tat* — that.

**62.** "Once You entered incomparable Vrindavana, charming with its bowers where swarms of bees hum very sweetly, and played there as if You were the very embodiment of the mantra of the science of love, delight and rasa. That is what is dearest to You!"

*Note.* The metre is *vasanta-tilakā*.

### Verse 63

एवं निशम्य मदमत्तमृगेन्द्रनादं
भूयो वदेति मधुरं निजगाद नाथः ।
अत्रान्तरे द्विजवरः स च तत्कृपाभिः
सर्वं तदीयचरितं प्रकटं जगाद ॥६३॥

इति श्रीकृष्णचैतन्यचरितामृते महाकाव्ये श्रीवृन्दावनविहारवर्णनं नाम अष्टमः सर्गः ॥

*evaṁ niśamya mada-matta-mṛgendra-nādaṁ*
*bhūyo vadeti madhuraṁ nijagāda nāthaḥ |*
*atrāntare dvija-varaḥ sa ca tat-kṛpābhiḥ*
*sarvaṁ tadīya-caritaṁ prakaṭaṁ jagāda ||63||*

*iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahā-kāvye śrī-vṛndāvana-vihāra-varṇanaṁ nāma aṣṭamaḥ sargaḥ ||*

*Word for word:* *evam* — this; *niśamya* — having heard; *mada* — with intoxication; *matta* — maddened; *mṛga-indra* — of a lion; *nādam* — [with] a roar; *bhūyaḥ* — more; *vada* — speak; *iti* — thus; *madhuram* — sweetly; *nijagāda* — said; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *atra antare* — thereupon; *dvija* — of the twice-born; *varaḥ* — the best; *saḥ* — he; *ca* — and; *tat* — His; *kṛpābhiḥ* — by the mercy; *sarvam* — all; *tadīya* — His; *caritam* — deeds; *prakaṭam* — clearly; *jagāda* — recounted.

**63.** Hearing this, the Lord, with a roar like that of a lion maddened by intoxication, sweetly said: "Speak more!" And thereupon that best of the twice-born, by His mercy, clearly recounted all His deeds.

*Note.* The metre is *vasanta-tilakā*.

Thus ends the eighth sarga, named "The Description of the Pastimes in Vrindavana", in the mahakavya "Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita".

---

## Sarga Nine — verses 1–95

**Title of the sarga:** none — the colophon of the edition gives no title for this sarga.
**Metre:** *svāgatā* (11 syllables per pada: —⏑— ⏑⏑⏑ —⏑⏑ ——); verse 94 — *praharṣiṇī*; verse 95 — *mandākrāntā*.
**Total verses:** 95.

**Contents of the passage:** Srivasa's account of Krishna's pastimes with the gopis — the walk in the forest, the bathing in the Yamuna, the entry into the jewelled pavilion.
- 1 — Srivasa begins his account (continuing 8.60–63).
- 2–20 — the gopis enter the forest with Krishna: lightning beside a cloud; their first shyness yields to Manmatha; gestures and gaits; bees alight on the creepers of their bodies; the gopis walk embracing Krishna.
- 21–31 — the Lakshmi of the forest brings gifts; the friends tease a proud one (*kulaka* 22–26: the *mādhavī* and the jasmine tormented by bees); a gopi embraces a creeper as a friend; "the cuckoo calls 'kuhū' — it is darkness you desire".
- 32–47 — gathering flowers: Krishna is adorned with a flower, lifts the gopis to the high branches, calls Radha lotus-faced (34); a bee on Krishna; reproaches to the "bee" (*kulaka* 37–39); "there is a bower!"; balls of flowers; coaxing the proud one.
- 48–50 — Krishna turns to another; the gopis are bathed in perspiration from the forest play.
- 51–78 — the bathing in the Yamuna: splashing, the "water drum", the *śapharī* fish, lotuses and stalks hold back the garments; the washed-off colours and ornaments are gifts to the Yamuna; wet braids and garments.
- 79–93 — a *kulaka* of fifteen verses: the jewelled pavilion (walls like mirrors, moonstones and sunstones, emerald "grass", ruby "pomegranates", a crystal pond).
- 94–95 — the singing of the birds; the wish-fulfilling creepers perform *nīrājana* over the gopis with cries of "Victory!"

### Verse 1

इत्थमुद्भटसुखाम्बुधिमग्नं
गौरचन्द्रमथ यथा सोऽभिजगाद ।
श्रूयतां प्रभुवर स्वविहारं
प्राक्कृतं स्वयमहं कथयामि ॥१॥

*ittham udbhaṭa-sukhāmbudhi-magnaṁ*
*gauracandram atha yathā so 'bhijagāda |*
*śrūyatāṁ prabhu-vara sva-vihāraṁ*
*prāk-kṛtaṁ svayam ahaṁ kathayāmi ||1||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *udbhaṭa* — of mighty; *sukha* — happiness; *ambudhi* — in the ocean; *magnam* — immersed; *gauracandram* — to Gaurachandra; *atha* — then; *yathā* (?) — (as); *saḥ* — he (Srivasa); *abhijagāda* — said; *śrūyatām* — let it be heard; *prabhu* — of lords; *vara* — O best; *sva* — Your own; *vihāram* — pastime; *prāk* — formerly; *kṛtam* — performed; *svayam* — myself; *aham* — I; *kathayāmi* — shall tell.

**1.** Then he said to Gaurachandra, thus immersed in an ocean of mighty happiness: "Listen, O best of lords: I myself shall tell [You] of Your own pastimes, performed of old."

*Note.* The second pada in the edition (*गौरचन्द्रमथ यथा सोऽभिजगाद*) has 13 syllables instead of 11; without *yathā* (*gauracandram atha so 'bhijagāda*) the *svāgatā* metre is restored exactly, so *yathā* is probably an interpolation or a misprint (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 2

वीक्ष्य तद्वदनमनिर्वचनीयं
रम्यरम्यमपि वल्गुमनोभिः ।
श्रेयसा सह विलासवतीभिः
स्वाङ्गवल्लिभिरकारि विचित्रम् ॥२॥

*vīkṣya tad-vadanam anirvacanīyaṁ*
*ramya-ramyam api valgu-manobhiḥ |*
*śreyasā [preyasā] saha vilāsavatībhiḥ*
*svāṅga-vallibhir akāri vicitram ||2||*

*Word for word:* *vīkṣya* — having seen; *tat* — His; *vadanam* — face; *anirvacanīyam* — indescribable; *ramya-ramyam* — the most charming of the charming; *api* — and; *valgu* — tender; *manobhiḥ* — with hearts; *preyasā* — with the beloved; *saha* — together; *vilāsavatībhiḥ* — by the playful [maidens]; *sva* — of their own; *aṅga* — limbs; *vallibhiḥ* — with the creepers; *akāri* — was made; *vicitram* — a wonder.

**2.** Seeing His indescribable face, the most charming of all that is charming, the playful [maidens], tender-hearted, wrought wonders with the creepers of their limbs together with their beloved.

*Note.* The edition has *श्रेयसा* ("with the good"); cf. *preyasā* in verse 3: we read *preyasā* (?). The first pada has 12 syllables instead of 11; with *tan-mukham* in place of *tad-vadanam* the *svāgatā* metre is exact — perhaps a gloss has displaced the original word (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 3

प्रेयसा सह नवीनतमाल-
श्यामलेन विपिनं प्रविशन्तः ।
तत्पुरो नवघनेन विलासं
विद्युतां दधुरमूर्व्रजवध्वः ॥३॥

*preyasā saha navīna-tamāla-*
*śyāmalena vipinaṁ praviśantaḥ [praviśantyaḥ] |*
*tat-puro nava-ghanena vilāsaṁ*
*vidyutāṁ dadhur amūr vraja-vadhvaḥ ||3||*

*Word for word:* *preyasā* — with the beloved; *saha* — together; *navīna* — young; *tamāla* — [as] a tamala tree; *śyāmalena* — dark; *vipinam* — the forest; *praviśantyaḥ* — entering; *tat* — Him; *puraḥ* — before; *nava* — new; *ghanena* — with a cloud; *vilāsam* — the play; *vidyutām* — of lightnings; *dadhuḥ* — displayed; *amūḥ* — these; *vraja* — of Vraja; *vadhvaḥ* — the young women.

**3.** Entering the forest together with their beloved, dark as a young tamala tree, these young women of Vraja displayed before Him the play of lightnings with a new rain cloud.

*Note.* The edition has *praviśantaḥ*, a masculine form with a feminine subject; the sense requires *praviśantyaḥ* (the metre is unchanged) (?). The golden gopis before Krishna, dark as a cloud, are like lightning on a cloud. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 4

रामणीयकमवेक्ष्य रमण्यो
मानसेन मनसिजेन लसन्त्यः ।
चेष्टया रुचिरयालसभाजो
भाविताः समभवन्नधिनाथम् ॥४॥

*rāmaṇīyakam avekṣya ramaṇyo*
*mānasena manasijena lasantyaḥ |*
*ceṣṭayā rucirayālasa-bhājo*
*bhāvitāḥ samabhavann adhinātham ||4||*

*Word for word:* *rāmaṇīyakam* — the loveliness; *avekṣya* — having beheld; *ramaṇyaḥ* — the beautiful women; *mānasena* — heartfelt; *manasijena* — with love; *lasantyaḥ* — shining; *ceṣṭayā* — with movement; *rucirayā* — charming; *ālasa* — languor; *bhājaḥ* — possessing; *bhāvitāḥ* — filled with feeling; *samabhavan* — became; *adhinātham* — towards their master.

**4.** Beholding His loveliness, the beautiful women shone with love born in the heart; charming in their movements, full of languor, they became wholly filled with feeling for their master.

*Note.* *Rucirayālasa-* = *rucirayā* (agreeing with *ceṣṭayā*) + *ālasa*. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 5

साभिलासमथ भाववतीनां
कृष्णचन्द्रमभिमुग्धवधूनाम् ।
साध्वसं प्रथमजं तिरयित्वा
मन्मथेन हृदये समुदासे ॥५॥

*sābhilāṣam atha bhāvavatīnāṁ*
*kṛṣṇacandram abhi mugdha-vadhūnām |*
*sādhvasaṁ prathamajaṁ tirayitvā*
*manmathena hṛdaye samudāse ||5||*

*Word for word:* *sa* — with; *abhilāṣam* — longing; *atha* — then; *bhāvavatīnām* — full of feeling; *kṛṣṇacandram* — Krishnachandra; *abhi* — towards; *mugdha* — innocent; *vadhūnām* — of the young women; *sādhvasam* — shyness; *prathama* — of the first [meeting]; *jam* — born; *tirayitvā* — having dispelled; *manmathena* — by Manmatha; *hṛdaye* — in the heart; *samudāse* — it was risen (he arose).

**5.** Then, in the hearts of the innocent young women, full of feeling and longing for Krishnachandra, Manmatha arose, dispelling the shyness born of the first [meeting].

*Note.* The edition has *साभिलास* for the usual *sābhilāṣa*. *Samudāse* is an impersonal passive perfect (*bhāve prayoga*): "it was risen by Manmatha", that is, Manmatha arose.

### Verse 6

अंशुकं शिथिलितं द्रढयित्वा
बिभ्रती सचकितत्रपमेका ।
सस्मितप्रियसखीजनपार्श्वे
लीलया लघु चलन्त्यभिरेजे ॥६॥

*aṁśukaṁ śithilitaṁ draḍhayitvā*
*bibhratī sa-cakita-trapam ekā |*
*sa-smita-priya-sakhī-jana-pārśve*
*līlayā laghu calanty abhireje ||6||*

*Word for word:* *aṁśukam* — the garment; *śithilitam* — loosened; *draḍhayitvā* — having tightened; *bibhratī* — holding; *sa* — with; *cakita* — alarm; *trapam* — [and] shame; *ekā* — one; *sa* — with; *smita* — smiles; *priya* — of dear; *sakhī* — friends; *jana* — of the company; *pārśve* — to the side; *līlayā* — playfully; *laghu* — lightly; *calantī* — moving; *abhireje* — shone.

**6.** One, startled and abashed, tightened her loosened garment and, holding it, moved lightly and playfully to the side of her dear, smiling friends — and she shone.

### Verse 7

कापि मन्दमयता परिवृत्ते
मारुतेन कुचयुग्मकचेले ।
सम्भ्रमात् प्रियसखीजनमुच्चै-
रालिलिङ्ग परिपश्यति कृष्णे ॥७॥

*kāpi mandam ayatā parivṛtte*
*mārutena kuca-yugma-kacele |*
*sambhramāt priya-sakhī-janam uccair*
*āliliṅga paripaśyati kṛṣṇe ||7||*

*Word for word:* *kā api* — a certain [maiden]; *mandam* — gently; *ayatā* — blowing; *parivṛtte* — when [it] was turned aside; *mārutena* — by the breeze; *kuca* — of the breasts; *yugma* — of the pair; *kacele* — the covering; *sambhramāt* — in confusion; *priya* — dear; *sakhī* — friend; *janam* — from the circle; *uccaiḥ* — tightly; *āliliṅga* — embraced; *paripaśyati* — while looking on; *kṛṣṇe* — Krishna.

**7.** When the gently blowing breeze turned aside the covering of another's bosom while Krishna looked on, she in confusion tightly embraced a dear friend.

*Note.* *Kacela* is a rare word, apparently a covering for the bosom or a bodice; possibly a corruption. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 8

उन्नमय्य भुजयुग्ममथान्या
पीवरस्तनयुगोन्नमनेन ।
साङ्गभङ्गमलसेन लसन्ती
जृम्भतेस्म पुरतो दयितस्य ॥८॥

*unnamayya bhuja-yugmam athānyā*
*pīvara-stana-yugonnamanena |*
*sāṅga-bhaṅgam alasena lasantī*
*jṛmbhate sma purato dayitasya ||8||*

*Word for word:* *unnamayya* — having raised; *bhuja* — of arms; *yugmam* — the pair; *atha* — and; *anyā* — another; *pīvara* — full; *stana* — of breasts; *yuga* — of the pair; *unnamanena* — with the lifting; *sa* — with; *aṅga* — of the body; *bhaṅgam* — a bending; *alasena* — languidly; *lasantī* — shining; *jṛmbhate sma* — stretched with a yawn; *purataḥ* — before; *dayitasya* — the beloved.

**8.** And another, raising both her arms, so that her full bosom was lifted, and languidly bending her whole body, stretched with a yawn before her beloved, radiant.

### Verse 9

पीवरोरसिजकुड्मलकान्तां
पाणिधूतनवपल्लवकान्तिम् ।
प्रोज्झ्य काननलतां वरनारी-
देहवल्लिमभजन्मधुपौघः ॥९॥

*pīvarorasija-kuḍmala-kāntāṁ*
*pāṇi-dhūta-nava-pallava-kāntim |*
*projjhya kānana-latāṁ vara-nārī-*
*deha-vallim abhajan madhupaughaḥ ||9||*

*Word for word:* *pīvara* — full; *urasija* — of breasts; *kuḍmala* — with the buds; *kāntām* — lovely; *pāṇi* — by the hands; *dhūta* — put to shame; *nava* — of young; *pallava* — shoots; *kāntim* — [whose] beauty; *projjhya* — having abandoned; *kānana* — of the forest; *latām* — the creeper; *vara* — of a beautiful; *nārī* — woman; *deha* — of the body; *vallim* — the creeper; *abhajat* — resorted to; *madhupa* — of bees; *oghaḥ* — a swarm.

**9.** Abandoning the forest creeper, a swarm of bees resorted to the creeper of the body of a beautiful maiden — lovely with the buds of her full bosom, her hands putting to shame the beauty of young shoots.

*Note.* In the edition the lines are wrongly divided (*प्रोज्झ्य काननलतां — / वरनारी देहवल्लि…*): by the metre, *vara-nārī* belongs to the third pada.

### Verse 10

सुभ्रुवां तनुलतासु लतानां
श्रीरियं सपरितोषमभूत् किम् ।
सर्वतः सपदि तासु यदेतन्-
मञ्जुगुञ्जदलिनां कुलमासीत् ॥१०॥

*subhruvāṁ tanu-latāsu latānāṁ*
*śrīr iyaṁ sa-paritoṣam abhūt kim |*
*sarvataḥ sapadi tāsu yad etan*
*mañju-guñjad-alināṁ kulam āsīt ||10||*

*Word for word:* *subhruvām* — of the fair-browed; *tanu* — of the bodies; *latāsu* — into the creepers; *latānām* — of the creepers; *śrīḥ* — beauty; *iyam* — this; *sa* — with; *paritoṣam* — delight; *abhūt* — passed (came to dwell); *kim* — did not?; *sarvataḥ* — from all sides; *sapadi* — at once; *tāsu* — around them; *yat* — since; *etat* — this; *mañju* — sweetly; *guñjat* — humming; *alinām* — of bees; *kulam* — swarm; *āsīt* — appeared.

**10.** Had not the beauty of the creepers joyfully passed into the creepers of the bodies of the fair-browed [maidens]? For at once, on all sides, this swarm of sweetly humming bees appeared around them.

### Verse 11

एकयौष्ठपतनेऽमृतपत्वं
प्रेप्सुरुन्मदतरो मधुपायी ।
ओष्ठदंशनरतस्य सतोषं
प्रेयसः स्मरणतो न निरासे ॥११॥

*ekayauṣṭha-patane 'mṛta-pa-tvaṁ*
*prepsur unmadataro madhu-pāyī |*
*oṣṭha-daṁśana-ratasya satoṣaṁ*
*preyasaḥ smaraṇato na nirāse ||11||*

*Word for word:* *ekayā* — by one; *oṣṭha* — on the lip; *patane* — on falling; *amṛta* — of nectar; *pa* — of a drinker; *tvam* — the state; *prepsuḥ* — desiring to obtain; *unmadataraḥ* — greatly intoxicated; *madhu* — honey; *pāyī* — drinking (the bee); *oṣṭha* — the lips; *daṁśana* — to biting; *ratasya* — given; *satoṣam* — gladly; *preyasaḥ* — of the beloved; *smaraṇataḥ* — from remembrance; *na* — not; *nirāse* — was driven away.

**11.** A greatly intoxicated honey-drinking bee, longing to become a drinker of nectar, fell on the lip of one [maiden]; and she gladly did not drive it away, remembering her beloved, who is given to biting the lips.

*Note.* *Amṛta-pa-tvam* — "the state of a drinker of nectar" (*amṛta-pa* + *-tva*). *Nirāse* is an impersonal passive: "by one [maiden] there was no driving away".

### Verse 12

मन्थरं मदनविह्वलहंसी-
लास्यशंसि मधुरक्रमरम्यम् ।
आदधुश्चरणपङ्कजरम्यं
सुभ्रुवोऽथ लघु तत्र विहर्तुम् ॥१२॥

*mantharaṁ madana-vihvala-haṁsī-*
*lāsya-śaṁsi madhura-krama-ramyam |*
*ādadhuś caraṇa-paṅkaja-ramyaṁ*
*subhruvo 'tha laghu tatra vihartum ||12||*

*Word for word:* *mantharam* — slow; *madana* — by love; *vihvala* — overwhelmed; *haṁsī* — of a female swan; *lāsya* — the dance; *śaṁsi* — recalling; *madhura* — with sweet; *krama* — steps; *ramyam* — charming; *ādadhuḥ* — displayed; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *paṅkaja* — of the lotuses; *ramyam* — the loveliness; *subhruvaḥ* — the fair-browed; *atha* — then; *laghu* — lightly; *tatra* — there; *vihartum* — in order to play.

**12.** Then, in order to play there, the fair-browed [maidens] displayed the loveliness of their lotus feet — a light, unhurried [gait], charming with its sweet steps, recalling the dance of a female swan overwhelmed by love.

*Note.* The syntax is unclear: the attributes *mantharam … madhura-krama-ramyam* imply "gait" (*gatim*), while the second *ramyam* is probably a noun, "loveliness". The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 13

उल्लसन्मदनमन्थरपाद-
न्यासभाजि गमने रमणीनाम् ।
श्रोणिबिम्बकुचयोः परिणाहः
खेदयन्नपि बभूव सुखाय ॥१३॥

*ullasan-madana-manthara-pāda-*
*nyāsa-bhāji gamane ramaṇīnām |*
*śroṇi-bimba-kucayoḥ pariṇāhaḥ*
*khedayann api babhūva sukhāya ||13||*

*Word for word:* *ullasat* — swelling; *madana* — by love; *manthara* — slowed; *pāda* — of the feet; *nyāsa* — placing; *bhāji* — having; *gamane* — in the gait; *ramaṇīnām* — of the beautiful women; *śroṇi* — of the hips; *bimba* — rounded; *kucayoḥ* — [and] of the breasts; *pariṇāhaḥ* — the fullness; *khedayan* — wearying; *api* — though; *babhūva* — became; *sukhāya* — for happiness.

**13.** As the beautiful women walked, their steps slowed by swelling love, the fullness of their rounded hips and bosoms, though it wearied them, became a source of happiness.

*Note.* In the edition the lines are wrongly divided (*…पादन्यास / भाजि…*): the boundary of the padas falls inside the word *pāda-nyāsa*.

### Verse 14

वीचिभङ्ग इव काञ्चनकाञ्ची-
कामडिण्डिमरवेण नितम्बः ।
सुभ्रुवां गमनविभ्रमभूषो
मन्दमन्दमलसेन ननर्त ॥१४॥

*vīci-bhaṅga iva kāñcana-kāñcī-*
*kāma-ḍiṇḍima-raveṇa nitambaḥ |*
*subhruvāṁ gamana-vibhrama-bhūṣo*
*manda-mandam alasena nanarta ||14||*

*Word for word:* *vīci* — of a wave; *bhaṅgaḥ* — the curve; *iva* — like; *kāñcana* — golden; *kāñcī* — of the girdle; *kāma* — of Kama; *ḍiṇḍima* — of the drum; *raveṇa* — to the sound; *nitambaḥ* — the hips; *subhruvām* — of the fair-browed; *gamana* — of the gait; *vibhrama* — with the grace; *bhūṣaḥ* — adorned; *manda-mandam* — very slowly; *alasena* — languidly; *nanarta* — danced.

**14.** To the sound of the golden girdle — the drum of Kama — the hips of the fair-browed [maidens], adorned with the grace of their gait, danced very slowly and languidly, like the curve of a wave.

### Verse 15

कोमलं चरणपद्ममशक्तं
मास्म गा द्रुततरं मदिराक्षि ।
इत्यतीव विवशौ रुदतः किं
नूपुरौ प्रणयतो रमणीनाम् ॥१५॥

*komalaṁ caraṇa-padmam aśaktaṁ*
*mā sma gā drutataraṁ madirākṣi |*
*ity atīva vivaśau rudataḥ kiṁ*
*nūpurau praṇayato ramaṇīnām ||15||*

*Word for word:* *komalam* — tender; *caraṇa* — of the foot; *padmam* — the lotus; *aśaktam* — without strength; *mā sma gāḥ* — do not go; *drutataram* — too quickly; *madirā* — intoxicating; *akṣi* — O [maiden] with eyes; *iti* — thus; *atīva* — utterly; *vivaśau* — helpless; *rudataḥ* — cry; *kim* — do [they] not?; *nūpurau* — the two anklets; *praṇayataḥ* — out of love; *ramaṇīnām* — of the beautiful women.

**15.** "Tender is the lotus of your foot, it has no strength — do not go so quickly, O maiden with intoxicating eyes!" — is it not this that the anklets of the beautiful women, utterly helpless, cry out of love?

### Verse 16

तत्तदङ्घ्रिकमलस्य विलासे
सस्पृहं कथयतीव महान्तम् ।
स्वानुरागमनुरागवतीनां
यावकैररुणिता वनभूमिः ॥१६॥

*tat-tad-aṅghri-kamalasya vilāse*
*sa-spṛhaṁ kathayatīva mahāntam |*
*svānurāgam anurāgavatīnāṁ*
*yāvakair aruṇitā vana-bhūmiḥ ||16||*

*Word for word:* *tat-tat* — of each of them; *aṅghri* — of the feet; *kamalasya* — of the lotus; *vilāse* — for the play; *sa* — with; *spṛham* — longing; *kathayati* — tells; *iva* — as if; *mahāntam* — great; *sva* — its own; *anurāgam* — love (redness); *anurāgavatīnām* — of the loving [maidens]; *yāvakaiḥ* — with lac; *aruṇitā* — reddened; *vana* — of the forest; *bhūmiḥ* — the ground.

**16.** Reddened with the lac from the feet of the loving [maidens], the forest ground seemed to tell longingly of its own great love for the play of the lotus feet of each of them.

*Note.* A play on words: *anurāga* means both "love" and "redness". The earth, reddened by *yāvaka* (the red lac for the feet), seems to confess its love.

### Verse 17

कृष्णपृष्ठतटलग्नकुचाग्रा
तत्तदंसविलसद्भुजमूला ।
साचितद्वदनचुम्बितवक्त्रा
कापि तत्र रुरुचेऽनुचलन्ती ॥१७॥

*kṛṣṇa-pṛṣṭha-taṭa-lagna-kucāgrā*
*tat-tad-aṁsa-vilasad-bhuja-mūlā |*
*sāci-tad-vadana-cumbita-vaktrā*
*kāpi tatra ruruce 'nucalantī ||17||*
