*Word for word:* *kṛṣṇa* — of Krishna; *pṛṣṭha* — of the back; *taṭa* — to the slope; *lagna* — pressed; *kuca* — of the breasts; *agrā* — [whose] tips; *tat-tat* — now on one, now on the other of His; *aṁsa* — shoulders; *vilasat* — resting; *bhuja* — of the arms; *mūlā* — [whose] upper parts; *sāci* — turned sideways; *tat* — by His; *vadana* — face; *cumbita* — kissed; *vaktrā* — [whose] face; *kā api* — a certain [maiden]; *tatra* — there; *ruruce* — shone; *anucalantī* — following.

**17.** There one [maiden] shone as she followed [Him], her bosom pressed to Krishna's back, her arms resting now on one, now on the other of His shoulders, her face kissed by His face as He turned it sideways.

*Note.* The compound *sāci-tad-vadana-cumbita-vaktrā* admits two readings: either Krishna, turning His face sideways, kisses her, or she, turning her face, kisses Him.

### Verse 18

पृष्ठतः प्रियतमेन भुजाभ्यां
श्लिष्टवक्षसिरुहाम्बुरुहाक्षी ।
इन्द्रनीलमणिहारमिवास्याः
कण्ठसीम्नि दधती चलितासीत् ॥१८॥

*pṛṣṭhataḥ priyatamena bhujābhyāṁ*
*śliṣṭa-vakṣasiruhāmburuhākṣī |*
*indranīla-maṇi-hāram ivāsyāḥ*
*kaṇṭha-sīmni dadhatī calitāsīt ||18||*

*Word for word:* *pṛṣṭhataḥ* — from behind; *priyatamena* — by the dearest one; *bhujābhyām* — with both arms; *śliṣṭa* — embraced; *vakṣasi-ruha* — [whose] breasts ("growing on the chest"); *amburuha* — lotus-; *akṣī* — eyed; *indranīla* — of sapphire; *maṇi* — of gems; *hāram* — a necklace; *iva* — like; *asyāḥ* — her; *kaṇṭha* — of the throat; *sīmni* — at the border; *dadhatī* — bearing; *calitā āsīt* — walked.

**18.** Another, lotus-eyed, whose bosom her dearest one embraced from behind with both arms, walked on bearing them at her throat like a necklace of sapphires.

*Note.* Krishna's dark arms at the gopi's throat are compared to a necklace of *indranīla* (sapphire). The edition has *इवास्या* without the visarga — a misprint.

### Verse 19

केशवांसतटराजिभुजाया
मन्थरालसगतेः सह यान्त्याः ।
तन्नितम्बभुवि लग्नविलग्नो
वीचिवत् किल रराज नितम्बः ॥१९॥

*keśavāṁsa-taṭa-rāji-bhujāyā*
*mantharālasa-gateḥ saha yāntyāḥ |*
*tan-nitamba-bhuvi lagna-vilagno*
*vīcivat kila rarāja nitambaḥ ||19||*

*Word for word:* *keśava* — of Keshava; *aṁsa* — of the shoulder; *taṭa* — on the slope; *rāji* — shining; *bhujāyāḥ* — [of her] whose arm; *manthara* — slow; *alasa* — languid; *gateḥ* — whose gait; *saha* — together; *yāntyāḥ* — walking; *tat* — His; *nitamba* — of the hip; *bhuvi* — on the region; *lagna* — touching; *vilagnaḥ* — [and] parting; *vīcivat* — like a wave; *kila* — indeed; *rarāja* — shone; *nitambaḥ* — the hip.

**19.** And of her who walked beside Him with a slow, languid gait, her arm shining on Keshava's shoulder, the hip, now touching His hip and now parting from it, shone indeed like a wave.

### Verse 20

प्राणनाथमधि कापि सखिभि-
र्बिभ्रती गतिमनङ्गविभङ्गा ।
साङ्गभङ्गमनुगांसतटेऽधाद्
बाहुमूलमुदयत्कुचमूलम् ॥२०॥

*prāṇa-nātham adhi kāpi sakhibhir [sakhībhir]*
*bibhratī gatim anaṅga-vibhaṅgā |*
*sāṅga-bhaṅgam anugāṁsa-taṭe 'dhād*
*bāhu-mūlam udayat-kuca-mūlam ||20||*

*Word for word:* *prāṇa* — of life; *nātham* — the lord; *adhi* — towards; *kā api* — a certain [maiden]; *sakhībhiḥ* — with friends; *bibhratī* — having; *gatim* — a gait; *anaṅga* — by Ananga (love); *vibhaṅgā* — [whose] curves; *sa* — with; *aṅga* — of the body; *bhaṅgam* — a bending; *anugā* — of the [friend] following; *aṁsa* — of the shoulder; *taṭe* — on the slope; *adhāt* — placed; *bāhu* — of the arm; *mūlam* — the root; *udayat* — rising; *kuca* — of the bosom; *mūlam* — [where is] the base.

**20.** One, walking with her friends towards the lord of her life, her gait curved by Ananga, bending her body, laid her arm on the shoulder of the friend who followed her — and near the root of her arm her bosom rose.

*Note.* The edition has *सखिभिः*; the metre requires *sakhībhiḥ* (the tenth syllable is long).

### Verse 21

तत्क्षणे क्षणत एव वधूनां
मन्मथेन बहुधा विवशानाम् ।
आययौ सपदि काननलक्ष्मीः
सा यथेप्सितमुपायनभारम् ॥२१॥

*tat-kṣaṇe kṣaṇata eva vadhūnāṁ*
*manmathena bahudhā vivaśānām |*
*āyayau sapadi kānana-lakṣmīḥ*
*sā yathepsitam upāyana-bhāram ||21||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — at that; *kṣaṇe* — moment; *kṣaṇataḥ* — in an instant; *eva* — very; *vadhūnām* — to the young women; *manmathena* — by Manmatha; *bahudhā* — in many ways; *vivaśānām* — rendered helpless; *āyayau* — came; *sapadi* — at once; *kānana* — of the forest; *lakṣmīḥ* — the Lakshmi (the beauty); *sā* — she; *yathā* — as; *īpsitam* — [they] desired; *upāyana* — of gifts; *bhāram* — [with] a load.

**21.** At that very moment, in an instant, the Lakshmi of the forest herself at once came to the young women, whom Manmatha had rendered helpless in many ways, bringing a load of gifts — all that they desired.

*Note.* The "Lakshmi of the forest" is its beauty personified. Verses 22–26 that follow (a *kulaka*) are the teasing speech of one of the gopis.

### Verse 22

मास्म मानिनि कृथाः श्रममुच्चै-
स्त्यज्यतां विवशतां सरसाक्षि ।
हेमगौरि गरिमाणमुपेतो
मान एष भवितैव चरिष्णुः ॥२२॥

*mā sma mānini kṛthāḥ śramam uccais*
*tyajyatāṁ vivaśatāṁ sarasākṣi |*
*hema-gauri garimāṇam upeto*
*māna eṣa bhavitaiva cariṣṇuḥ ||22||*

*Word for word:* *mā sma kṛthāḥ* — do not make; *mānini* — O proud one; *śramam* — effort; *uccaiḥ* — great; *tyajyatām* — let [it] be given up; *vivaśatām* — helplessness; *sarasa* — moist; *akṣi* — O [maiden] with eyes; *hema* — like gold; *gauri* — O fair one; *garimāṇam* — heaviness; *upetaḥ* — having attained; *mānaḥ* — pique; *eṣaḥ* — this; *bhavitā* — will become; *eva* — certainly; *cariṣṇuḥ* — fleeting.

**22.** "Do not torment yourself so greatly, O proud one; give up this helplessness, O moist-eyed one! O you who are fair as gold, heavy as this pique of yours has grown, it will certainly prove fleeting.

*Note.* *Māna* is the loving pique, the jealous anger of the beloved — one of the moods of the pastimes of love.

### Verse 23

पश्य मत्तहरिणाक्षि धुनाना
पल्लवं तव करस्य समानम् ।
माधवी कुसुमयौवनरम्या
बाध्यते मधुकरैरतिलुब्धैः ॥२३॥

*paśya matta-hariṇākṣi dhunānā*
*pallavaṁ tava karasya samānam |*
*mādhavī kusuma-yauvana-ramyā*
*bādhyate madhukarair ati-lubdhaiḥ ||23||*

*Word for word:* *paśya* — look; *matta* — of an intoxicated; *hariṇa* — doe; *akṣi* — O [maiden] with the eyes; *dhunānā* — waving; *pallavam* — a shoot; *tava* — to your; *karasya* — hand; *samānam* — similar; *mādhavī* — the *mādhavī* creeper; *kusuma* — of blossoms; *yauvana* — by the youth; *ramyā* — lovely; *bādhyate* — is tormented; *madhukaraiḥ* — by bees; *ati* — exceedingly; *lubdhaiḥ* — greedy.

**23.** Look, O you whose eyes are like an intoxicated doe's: the *mādhavī* creeper, lovely with the youth of her blossoms, waves a shoot like your hand — and the exceedingly greedy bees torment her.

*Note.* The edition has माधुरी ("sweetness"); we read *mādhavī*, the *mādhavī* creeper (the metre is unchanged), as the image requires (cf. the jasmine creeper in verse 24). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 24

धर्षितापि मधुपैरिह मल्ली-
वल्लिरुल्लसितकुड्मलरम्या ।
पाणिवत् किशलयं विधुनाना
किं शशाक परिमर्दशमाय ॥२४॥

*dharṣitāpi madhupair iha mallī-*
*vallir ullasita-kuḍmala-ramyā |*
*pāṇivat kiśalayaṁ vidhunānā*
*kiṁ śaśāka parimarda-śamāya ||24||*

*Word for word:* *dharṣitā* — assailed; *api* — though; *madhupaiḥ* — by bees; *iha* — here; *mallī* — of jasmine; *valliḥ* — the creeper; *ullasita* — opening; *kuḍmala* — with buds; *ramyā* — lovely; *pāṇivat* — like a hand; *kiśalayam* — a young shoot; *vidhunānā* — waving; *kim* — whether; *śaśāka* — was able; *parimarda* — the onslaught; *śamāya* — to quell.

**24.** And here is the jasmine creeper, lovely with her opening buds: assailed by the bees, she waves a young shoot like a hand — but could she ever quell their onslaught?

### Verse 25

पश्य भृङ्गलुलिता दलकम्पै-
रेवमेव परिवक्ति लतेयम् ।
नैव नैव मदभाजि विरंसौ
सुभ्रुवो मनसि तिष्ठति मानः ॥२५॥

*paśya bhṛṅga-lulitā dala-kampair*
*evam eva parivakti lateyam |*
*naiva naiva mada-bhāji viraṁsau*
*subhruvo manasi tiṣṭhati mānaḥ ||25||*

*Word for word:* *paśya* — look; *bhṛṅga* — by bumblebees; *lulitā* — ruffled; *dala* — of the leaves; *kampaiḥ* — by the trembling; *evam eva* — just this; *parivakti* — proclaims; *latā* — creeper; *iyam* — this; *na eva na eva* — by no means, by no means; *mada* — intoxication; *bhāji* — experiencing; *viraṁsau* — longing to sport; *subhruvaḥ* — of a fair-browed girl; *manasi* — in the heart; *tiṣṭhati* — remains; *mānaḥ* — pique.

**25.** Look: this creeper, ruffled by the bumblebees, proclaims just this by the trembling of her leaves: in the heart of a fair-browed girl, intoxicated and longing for the play [of love], pique by no means, by no means remains.

### Verse 26

आश्रवं तमिमाश्लिष कान्तं
मुञ्च मुञ्च सखि मानमसन्तम् ।
कापि भावचतुरा परिहासैः
प्राणनाथमभि काञ्चिदवादीत् ॥२६॥ (कुलकम्)

*āśravaṁ tam imam āśliṣa kāntaṁ*
*muñca muñca sakhi mānam asantam |*
*kāpi bhāva-caturā parihāsaiḥ*
*prāṇa-nātham abhi kāñcid avādīt ||26|| (kulakam)*

*Word for word:* *āśravam* — obedient; *tam imam* — this very; *āśliṣa* — embrace; *kāntam* — beloved; *muñca muñca* — give up, give up; *sakhi* — O friend; *mānam* — pique; *asantam* — empty; *kā api* — a certain [gopi]; *bhāva* — in the moods [of love]; *caturā* — expert; *parihāsaiḥ* — with jests; *prāṇa-nātham abhi* — in the presence of the lord of [her] life; *kāñcit* — to a certain [proud girl]; *avādīt* — spoke.

**26.** Here is your obedient beloved — embrace Him! Give up, O friend, give up this empty pique!" So, in the presence of the lord of her life, a certain [maiden], expert in the moods [of love], spoke jestingly to a certain [proud girl].

*Note.* *Kulaka*: verses 22–26 form a single sentence. In the edition the first pada (*आश्रवं तमिमाश्लिष कान्तं*) has 10 syllables instead of 11 — one short syllable is missing; the transliteration *tam imam āśliṣa* restores it, and the *svāgatā* metre is then exact (the syllable *ma* was probably lost before *mā*) (?). *Āśliṣa* is an irregular imperative of *ā-śliṣ* (the regular form is *āśliṣya*); the poet uses it again in verse 28, where the metre confirms it. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 27

किं बलप्रियबलोत्तरमध्ये
स्वैरमाचरसि नो ललितानि ।
यत्र चूतलतिकाः करलभ्या
निर्भरं मुकुलिता विलसन्ति ॥२७॥

*kiṁ bala-priya-balottara-madhye*
*svairam ācarasi no lalitāni |*
*yatra cūta-latikāḥ kara-labhyā*
*nirbharaṁ mukulitā vilasanti ||27||*

*Word for word:* *kim* — why; *bala-priya* — of the Beloved of Balarama (Krishna); *bala* (*vana*?) — [of the grove]; *uttara* — excellent; *madhye* — in the midst; *svairam* — freely; *ācarasi* — do you perform; *no* — not; *lalitāni* — pastimes; *yatra* — where; *cūta* — mango; *latikāḥ* — young branches; *kara* — by the hand; *labhyāḥ* — reachable; *nirbharam* — thickly; *mukulitāḥ* — budding; *vilasanti* — shine forth.

**27.** "Why do you not sport freely in the midst of the excellent [grove] of the Beloved of Balarama, where the young mango branches, thickly covered in buds, shine within reach of the hand?"

*Note.* *Balottara* is obscure; perhaps *vanottara*, "excellent forest", should be read (?). It is not clear who is addressing whom. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 28

स्वागतं सखि चिरादसि दृष्टा
माश्लिषेति विकसत्कुचमूलम् ।
कापि भावविवशा रभसाभि-
स्तत्र कामपि लतां परिरेभे ॥२८॥

*svāgataṁ sakhi cirād asi dṛṣṭā*
*mā[m] āśliṣeti vikasat-kuca-mūlam |*
*kāpi bhāva-vivaśā rabhasābhis*
*tatra kām api latāṁ parirebhe ||28||*

*Word for word:* *svāgatam* — welcome; *sakhi* — O friend; *cirāt* — after a long time; *asi* — you are; *dṛṣṭā* — seen; *mām* — me; *āśliṣa* — embrace; *iti* — thus [saying]; *vikasat* — rising; *kuca* — of the breasts; *mūlam* — [so that] the base; *kā api* — a certain [gopi]; *bhāva* — by emotion; *vivaśā* — overpowered; *rabhasābhiḥ* — impetuously; *tatra* — there; *kām api* — some; *latām* — creeper; *parirebhe* — embraced.

**28.** "Welcome, O friend! At last I see you after so long — embrace me!" And with these words a certain [maiden], overpowered by emotion, impetuously embraced some creeper there, her bosom rising [as she opened her arms].

*Note.* The form रभसाभिः is unclear (one would expect *rabhasā* or *rabhasāt*); the sense is "impetuously". Intoxicated with love, the gopi takes the creeper for a friend. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 29

सुभ्रु वल्लिविटपेन विकृष्टं
वक्षसोऽञ्चलमलङ्कुरु मुग्धे ।
मा पतेदिह सरोरुहकोष-
भ्रान्तितो मधुकरः सखि मुग्धः ॥२९॥

*subhru valli-viṭapena vikṛṣṭaṁ*
*vakṣaso 'ñcalam alaṅkuru mugdhe |*
*mā pated iha saroruha-kośa-*
*bhrāntito madhukaraḥ sakhi mugdhaḥ ||29||*

*Word for word:* *subhru* — O fair-browed one; *valli* — of a creeper; *viṭapena* — by a branch; *vikṛṣṭam* — pulled away; *vakṣasaḥ* — from the breast; *añcalam* — the edge of the garment; *alaṅkuru* — set right; *mugdhe* — O artless one; *mā patet* — may not alight; *iha* — here; *saroruha* — of a lotus; *kośa* — for the bud; *bhrāntitaḥ* — by mistake; *madhukaraḥ* — a bee; *sakhi* — O friend; *mugdhaḥ* — foolish.

**29.** "O fair-browed, artless girl, put right the edge of your garment, which the branch of a creeper has pulled from your bosom — lest, O friend, some foolish bee, mistaking it for the bud of a lotus, should alight here!"

*Note.* *Mugdha* is said of both: the "artless" girl and the "foolish" bee.

### Verse 30

चन्द्रिकाः किमिह तेन हि रम्या
वाञ्छितं तिमिरमेव भवत्योः ।
यत् कुहूरिति मुहुर्निगदन्तं
कोकिलं कलयसीह सतृष्णम् ॥३०॥

*candrikāḥ kim iha te na hi ramyāḥ*
*vāñchitaṁ timiram eva bhavatyoḥ |*
*yat kuhūr iti muhur nigadantaṁ*
*kokilaṁ kalayasīha satṛṣṇam ||30||*

*Word for word:* *candrikāḥ* — the moonlight; *kim* — is it that; *iha* — here; *te* — to you; *na hi* — not indeed; *ramyāḥ* — pleasing; *vāñchitam* — desired; *timiram* — darkness; *eva* — only; *bhavatyoḥ* — by you two; *yat* — since; *kuhūḥ* — "kuhu" (the new moon); *iti* — thus; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *nigadantam* — calling; *kokilam* — the cuckoo; *kalayasi* — you listen to; *iha* — here; *sa* — with; *tṛṣṇam* — thirst.

**30.** "Is the moonlight here not pleasing to you? It is darkness alone that you two desire — for here you listen so thirstily to the cuckoo that keeps calling 'Kuhū!'"

*Note.* A pun: *kuhū* is both the call of the cuckoo (*kokila*) and the moonless night of the new moon, favourable for meetings. The edition (like the Gosvami edition) has *tena hi*, which is syntactically obscure; we read *te na hi*, "not … to you".

### Verse 31

तद्व्रजाम इत एव विदूरं
तिष्ठ साम्प्रतमभिप्रियमेका ।
इत्यलीकवचनारचनाभि-
र्गन्तुमिष्टमतनिष्ट ततोऽन्या ॥३१॥

*tad vrajāma ita eva vidūraṁ*
*tiṣṭha sāmpratam abhipriyam ekā |*
*ity alīka-vacanā-racanābhir*
*gantum iṣṭam atanisṭa tato 'nyā ||31||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — so; *vrajāmaḥ* — let us go; *itaḥ* — from here; *eva* — indeed; *vidūram* — far away; *tiṣṭha* — stay; *sāmpratam* — now; *abhi* — with; *priyam* — the beloved; *ekā* — alone; *iti* — thus; *alīka* — feigned; *vacanā* — of words; *racanābhiḥ* — by contrivances; *gantum* — to go; *iṣṭam* — the wish; *ataniṣṭa* — made known; *tataḥ* — then; *anyā* — another.

**31.** "So let us go far away from here, and you stay now alone with your beloved." With such contrivances of feigned words another [friend] then made known her wish to leave.

*Note.* The edition has तिष्ट, a misprint for तिष्ठ.

### Verse 32

एतदेव कुसुमं तव रम्यं
कर्णयोरिति समुन्नतबाहुः ।
कृष्णवक्षसि मिलत्कुचकुम्भा
काचनामुमभिभूषयति स्म ॥३२॥

*etad eva kusumaṁ tava ramyaṁ*
*karṇayor iti samunnata-bāhuḥ |*
*kṛṣṇa-vakṣasi milat-kuca-kumbhā*
*kācanāmum abhibhūṣayati sma ||32||*

*Word for word:* *etat* — this; *eva* — very; *kusumam* — flower; *tava* — on You; *ramyam* — beautiful; *karṇayoḥ* — over the ears; *iti* — thus [saying]; *samunnata* — raised; *bāhuḥ* — [with] arms; *kṛṣṇa* — of Krishna; *vakṣasi* — the chest; *milat* — touching; *kuca* — of the breasts; *kumbhā* — [with] the pitchers; *kācana* — a certain [gopi]; *amum* — Him; *abhibhūṣayati sma* — adorned.

**32.** "This very flower looks beautiful on You — over Your ears!" And so saying, a certain [maiden], raising her arms, adorned Him, the pitchers of her bosom touching Krishna's chest.

### Verse 33

ऊरुमूलमभिबध्य भुजाभ्या-
मुच्चकैः सुमनसोऽवचिचीषुः ।
काप्युरःस्थलविलग्ननितम्बा
माधवेन कृतहर्षमुदासे ॥३३॥

*ūru-mūlam abhibadhya bhujābhyām*
*uccakaiḥ sumanaso 'vacicīṣuḥ |*
*kāpy uraḥ-sthala-vilagna-nitambā*
*mādhavena kṛta-harṣam udāse ||33||*

*Word for word:* *ūru* — of the thighs; *mūlam* — the upper part; *abhibadhya* — having clasped; *bhujābhyām* — with both arms; *uccakaiḥ* — [growing] high up; *sumanasaḥ* — flowers; *avacicīṣuḥ* — wishing to pick; *kā api* — a certain [gopi]; *uraḥ-sthala* — to the chest; *vilagna* — pressed; *nitambā* — [whose] hips; *mādhavena* — by Madhava; *kṛta* — with shown; *harṣam* — delight; *udāse* — was lifted up.

**33.** A certain [maiden] wished to pick flowers growing high up, and Madhava, delighted, clasped her with both arms below the hips and lifted her up, her hips pressed to His chest.

*Note.* *Udāse* is the passive perfect of *ud-as*, "to lift up"; cf. *samudāse* in verse 5.

### Verse 34

अम्बुजं मुखमिदं तव राधे
कुन्ददामवदना कुसुमैः किम् ।
इत्थमुन्नयता चिबुकाग्रं
प्रेयसी प्रियतमेन चुचुम्बे ॥३४॥

*ambujaṁ mukham idaṁ tava rādhe*
*kunda-dāma-vadanā [-radanā] kusumaiḥ kim |*
*ittham unnayatā cibukāgraṁ*
*preyasī priyatamena cucumbe ||34||*

*Word for word:* *ambujam* — a lotus; *mukham* — face; *idam* — this; *tava* — Your; *rādhe* — O Radha; *kunda* — of kunda (jasmine); *dāma* — [with] a garland; *radanā* — [You, whose] teeth; *kusumaiḥ* — with flowers; *kim* — what [need]; *ittham* — thus [saying]; *unnayatā* — lifting; *cibuka* — of the chin; *agram* — the tip; *preyasī* — the darling; *priyatamena* — by the most beloved; *cucumbe* — was kissed.

**34.** "This face of Yours is a lotus, O Radha, and Your teeth a garland of *kunda* jasmine — what need have You of flowers?" Saying this, the most beloved lifted the tip of His darling's chin and kissed Her.

*Note.* Here Radha is named in the sarga for the first time. The edition has *°vadanā* ("with a face"); we read *°radanā*, "with teeth": a garland of white kunda flowers is the standard image for teeth. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 35

आनता कुचभरैर्मुहुरुच्चैः
पुष्पसंग्रहपरा विकलापि ।
उत्करादगलदुरःस्थलचेला
कापि कृष्णहृदये विजहार ॥३५॥

*ānatā kuca-bharair muhur uccaiḥ*
*puṣpa-saṅgraha-parā vikalāpi |*
*ut-karād galad-uraḥ-sthala-celā*
*kāpi kṛṣṇa-hṛdaye vijahāra ||35||*

*Word for word:* *ānatā* — bowed down; *kuca* — of the breasts; *bharaiḥ* — by the weight; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *uccaiḥ* — up high; *puṣpa* — flowers; *saṅgraha* — on gathering; *parā* — intent; *vikalā* — flustered; *api* — though; *ut* — raised; *karāt* — because of the hand; *galat* — slipping; *uraḥ-sthala* — from the bosom; *celā* — [whose] cloth; *kā api* — a certain [gopi]; *kṛṣṇa* — of Krishna; *hṛdaye* — on the heart; *vijahāra* — sported.

**35.** Another, though bowed down by the weight of her bosom and flustered, again and again reached up, intent on gathering flowers; and as the cloth slipped from her bosom because her hand was raised, she sported upon Krishna's heart.

*Note.* The edition has उत्करा द्गलद्, a wrong division of words; we read *utkarād galad-*.

### Verse 36

लीनमप्यलिमवेक्ष्य हरन्ती
केशवं कररुहैरथ वीक्ष्य ।
संभ्रमभ्रमिवशादवशाङ्गी
निर्ममज्ज दयितोरसि काचित् ॥३६॥

*līnam apy alim avekṣya harantī*
*keśavaṁ kara-ruhair atha vīkṣya |*
*sambhrama-bhrami-vaśād avaśāṅgī*
*nirmamajja dayitorasi kācit ||36||*

*Word for word:* *līnam* — nestled (merged); *api* — even; *alim* — a bee; *avekṣya* — having noticed; *harantī* — removing; *keśavam* — Keshava; *kara-ruhaiḥ* — with her fingernails; *atha* — then; *vīkṣya* — having seen; *sambhrama* — of confusion; *bhrami* — of the giddiness; *vaśāt* — under the sway; *avaśa* — helpless; *aṅgī* — [whose] limbs; *nirmamajja* — sank; *dayita* — of the beloved; *urasi* — on the chest; *kācit* — a certain [gopi].

**36.** A certain [maiden] noticed a bee nestled [on Krishna] and went to remove it with her fingernails — and then saw [that she was touching] Keshava. In the whirl of her confusion her limbs grew helpless, and she sank upon her beloved's chest.

*Note.* The bee, dark like Krishna, merges with Him, and in removing it the gopi touches Keshava Himself with her nails.

### Verse 37

प्रोज्झ्य फुल्लकुसुमावलिमेतां
कुड्मलेषु निपतिष्यति मुग्धः ।
भृङ्गरागपरवानसि तत्त्वं
रज्यतां मनसि को हि विवेकः ॥३७॥

*projjhya phulla-kusumāvalim etāṁ*
*kuḍmaleṣu nipatiṣyati mugdhaḥ |*
*bhṛṅga-rāga-paravān asi tat tvaṁ*
*rajyatāṁ manasi ko hi vivekaḥ ||37||*

*Word for word:* *projjhya* — having abandoned; *phulla* — of full-blown; *kusuma* — flowers; *āvalim* — the row; *etām* — this; *kuḍmaleṣu* — on the buds; *nipatiṣyati* — will alight; *mugdhaḥ* — the fool; *bhṛṅga* — of a bee; *rāga* — by the ardour (colour); *paravān* — enslaved; *asi* — are; *tat* — therefore; *tvam* — you; *rajyatām* — of those who are dyed [with ardour]; *manasi* — in the mind; *kaḥ* — what; *hi* — indeed; *vivekaḥ* — discernment.

**37.** "Abandoning this row of full-blown flowers, the fool will alight on the buds! You are enslaved by a bee's *rāga* — and what discernment, indeed, is there in the minds of those who are dyed [with it]?

*Note.* The beginning of a *kulaka* (37–39): the gopi addresses the bee but aims at Krishna. A pun: *rāga* means both "ardour" and "colour"; *bhṛṅga-rāga* is both "a bee's ardour" and "blackness". The syntax of *tat tvaṁ rajyatām* is unclear; we take *rajyatām* as the genitive plural of the participle, "of those who are dyed" (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 38

श्यामलोऽसि सततं मधुमत्तः
पद्मिनीषु निरतश्चपलोऽसि ।
चञ्चरीकसदृशोऽसि ततस्त्वं
कस्यचिन्ननु समस्तगुणेन ॥३८॥

*śyāmalo 'si satataṁ madhu-mattaḥ*
*padminīṣu nirataś capalo 'si |*
*cañcarīka-sadṛśo 'si tatas tvaṁ*
*kasyacin nanu samasta-guṇena ||38||*

*Word for word:* *śyāmalaḥ* — dark; *asi* — you are; *satatam* — always; *madhu* — with honey (wine, spring); *mattaḥ* — intoxicated; *padminīṣu* — to lotus plants (to *padminīs*); *nirataḥ* — attached; *capalaḥ* — fickle; *asi* — you are; *cañcarīka* — O bee; *sadṛśaḥ* — similar; *asi* — you are; *tataḥ* — therefore; *tvam* — you; *kasyacit* — to a certain someone; *nanu* — surely; *samasta* — in every; *guṇena* — quality.

**38.** You are dark, ever drunk with honey, attached to lotuses, fickle — so surely, O bee, you resemble a certain someone in every quality!

*Note.* *Padminī* is both "lotus plant" and a *padminī*, the highest of the types of women in the classical typology.

### Verse 39

संविमर्दनसहासहतां नो
वेत्सि मुग्धतम रागपरोऽसि ।
इत्थमात्तकुतुकं कृतरोषा
कापि कृष्णमपदिश्य जगाद ॥३९॥ (कुलकम्)

*saṁvimardana-sahāsahatāṁ no*
*vetsi mugdhatama rāga-paro 'si |*
*ittham ātta-kutukaṁ kṛta-roṣā*
*kāpi kṛṣṇam apadiśya jagāda ||39|| (kulakam)*

*Word for word:* *saṁvimardana* — the crushing onslaught; *saha* — the ability to bear; *asahatām* — [and] the inability; *no* — not (or *naḥ* — our); *vetsi* — you know; *mugdhatama* — O most foolish one; *rāga* — to ardour; *paraḥ* — given; *asi* — you are; *ittham* — thus; *ātta* — having assumed; *kutukam* — playfulness; *kṛta* — feigning; *roṣā* — anger; *kā api* — a certain [gopi]; *kṛṣṇam* — at Krishna; *apadiśya* — hinting; *jagāda* — spoke.

**39.** You do not know whether we can bear your onslaught or not, O most foolish one — you are given to ardour alone!" So, playfully feigning anger, a certain [maiden] spoke, hinting at Krishna.

*Note.* *No* may be taken as *na u*, "not", or as *naḥ*, "our"; in the latter case the line is a reproachful question: "Do you know what we can bear and what we cannot?"

### Verse 40

घ्रातुमागतमवेक्ष्य मुखाब्जं
चञ्चरीकमपरा रभसेन ।
श्रोतुमेव न निरास कराभ्यां
माधवस्य परिहासवचांसि ॥४०॥

*ghrātum āgatam avekṣya mukhābjaṁ*
*cañcarīkam aparā rabhasena |*
*śrotum eva na nirāsa karābhyāṁ*
*mādhavasya parihāsa-vacāṁsi ||40||*

*Word for word:* *ghrātum* — to smell; *āgatam* — come; *avekṣya* — having seen; *mukha* — of the face; *abjam* — the lotus; *cañcarīkam* — a bee; *aparā* — another; *rabhasena* — eagerly (on purpose); *śrotum* — to hear; *eva* — only; *na* — not; *nirāsa* — drove away; *karābhyām* — with her hands; *mādhavasya* — of Madhava; *parihāsa* — teasing; *vacāṁsi* — words.

**40.** Another, seeing a bee that had come to smell the lotus of her face, on purpose did not drive it away with her hands — only so as to hear Madhava's teasing words.

### Verse 41

मन्थरा तव गतिः सहजैषा
तत्र चेत् प्रतिपदं रमणेन ।
प्रस्थिता तदिह किं चलितव्यं
पश्य सुन्दरि तदत्र निकुञ्जम् ॥४१॥

*mantharā tava gatiḥ sahajaiṣā*
*tatra cet pratipadaṁ ramaṇena |*
*prasthitā tad iha kiṁ calitavyaṁ*
*paśya sundari tad atra nikuñjam ||41||*

*Word for word:* *mantharā* — slow; *tava* — your; *gatiḥ* — gait; *sahajā* — natural; *eṣā* — this; *tatra* — moreover; *cet* — if; *prati-padam* — at every step; *ramaṇena* — with the beloved; *prasthitā* — [you] have set out; *tat* — then; *iha* — here; *kim* — why; *calitavyam* — [should one] go on; *paśya* — look; *sundari* — O beautiful one; *tat* — that; *atra* — here; *nikuñjam* — bower.

**41.** "Your gait is slow by nature; and if, besides, you have set out with your beloved, [lingering] at every step, why go any further? Look, O beautiful one: there is a bower right here!

*Note.* Verses 41–42 form a single speech.

### Verse 42

यः श्रुतौ लपति ते भ्रमरोऽयं
श्यामलोत्पलदलान्तरितः सन् ।
नावगच्छसि किमेतदितीदं
कापि काञ्चिदिति सस्मितमूचे ॥४२॥

*yaḥ śrutau lapati te bhramaro 'yaṁ*
*śyāmalotpala-dalāntaritaḥ san |*
*nāvagacchasi kim etad itīdaṁ*
*kāpi kāñcid iti sasmitam ūce ||42||*

*Word for word:* *yaḥ* — which; *śrutau* — at the ear; *lapati* — whispers; *te* — your; *bhramaraḥ* — bee; *ayam* — this; *śyāmala* — of the dark; *utpala* — lotus; *dala* — by the petal; *antaritaḥ* — hidden; *san* — being; *na* — not; *avagacchasi* — do you understand; *kim* — what; *etat* — this; *iti* — thus; *idam* — this; *kā api* — a certain [gopi]; *kāñcit* — to another; *iti* — thus; *sa* — with; *smitam* — a smile; *ūce* — said.

**42.** This bee, hiding behind the petal of the dark lotus at your ear and whispering into it — do you not understand what it is saying?" So, with a smile, one [maiden] said to another.

*Note.* The dark lotus is an ornament worn over the ear. *Ava-gam* means both "to understand" and "to go"; the question may also be heard as "why do you not go?"

### Verse 43

कीदृशीं स्रजमहं रचयेयं
कम्बुकण्ठि तव कण्ठतटाय ।
इत्यसौ सकुतुकं दयिताया
वक्षसो वसनमाशु जहार ॥४३॥

*kīdṛśīṁ srajam ahaṁ racayeyaṁ*
*kambu-kaṇṭhi tava kaṇṭha-taṭāya |*
*ity asau sa-kutukaṁ dayitāyā*
*vakṣaso vasanam āśu jahāra ||43||*

*Word for word:* *kīdṛśīm* — what kind of; *srajam* — garland; *aham* — I; *racayeyam* — should weave; *kambu* — [like] a conch; *kaṇṭhi* — O [maiden] whose neck; *tava* — your; *kaṇṭha* — of the neck; *taṭāya* — for the slope; *iti* — thus [saying]; *asau* — He; *sa* — with; *kutukam* — mischief; *dayitāyāḥ* — of the beloved; *vakṣasaḥ* — from the bosom; *vasanam* — the cloth; *āśu* — swiftly; *jahāra* — took away.

**43.** "What kind of garland should I weave for the slope of your neck, O you whose neck is like a conch?" Saying this, He mischievously, in an instant, took away the cloth from His beloved's bosom.

*Note.* A neck "like a conch" has three folds, a mark of beauty.

### Verse 44

कापि पुष्पमयकन्दुकवृन्दं
प्राहिणोदघरिपुं परि शश्वत् ।
चन्द्रमोभिरिव तन्मधुरिम्णा-
मौपहारिकममन्दमकार्षीत् ॥४४॥

*kāpi puṣpamaya-kanduka-vṛndaṁ*
*prāhiṇod agha-ripuṁ pari śaśvat |*
*candramobhir iva tan-madhurimṇām*
*aupahārikam amandam akārṣīt ||44||*

*Word for word:* *kā api* — a certain [gopi]; *puṣpa-maya* — made of flowers; *kanduka* — of balls; *vṛndam* — a multitude; *prāhiṇot* — threw; *agha* — of Agha; *ripum* — at the Enemy; *pari* — all around; *śaśvat* — incessantly; *candramobhiḥ* — with moons; *iva* — as if; *tat* — His; *madhurimṇām* — to the sweetnesses; *aupahārikam* — an offering; *amandam* — abundant; *akārṣīt* — made.

**44.** A certain [maiden] incessantly threw a multitude of flower-balls all around the Enemy of Agha, as though making an abundant offering of moons to His sweetness.

*Note.* The edition has अघदिपुं, a misprint for अघरिपुं. The white flower-balls are compared to moons. The sense of the second half is rendered approximately. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 45

फुल्लचूतलतिकापरिरम्भैः
पिञ्जरः पिकयुवा मधुमत्तः ।
मन्मथं कलयतीव विशेषं
मन्मनो विकलमेव बभूव ॥४५॥

*phulla-cūta-latikā-parirambhaiḥ*
*piñjaraḥ pika-yuvā madhu-mattaḥ |*
*manmathaṁ kalayatīva viśeṣaṁ*
*man-mano vikalam eva babhūva ||45||*

*Word for word:* *phulla* — of blossoming; *cūta* — mango; *latikā* — branches; *parirambhaiḥ* — by the embraces; *piñjaraḥ* — turned yellow; *pika* — cuckoo; *yuvā* — young; *madhu* — with spring (with honey); *mattaḥ* — intoxicated; *manmatham* — Manmatha; *kalayati* — summons; *iva* — as if; *viśeṣam* — especially; *mat* — my; *manaḥ* — heart; *vikalam* — distraught; *eva* — utterly; *babhūva* — has become.

**45.** "The young cuckoo, intoxicated with spring and turned golden-yellow by the embraces of the blossoming mango branches, seems to be summoning Manmatha in earnest — and my heart has become utterly distraught.

*Note.* With this verse there seems to begin the speech of one of the gopis to the proud girl (45–47). The speaker is not named, however: the *iti* of verse 48, whose subject is Krishna, may also point to Krishna Himself as the speaker, "the beloved" and "the lord" (46–47) then being His words about Himself (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 46

मा कृथाः कथमपि प्रथयानं
मानमानय मधूनि ददस्व ।
मानयोऽयमभिनाथमजस्रं
मानिनि प्रकटमानवशत्वम् ॥४६॥

*mā kṛthāḥ katham api prathayānaṁ*
*mānam ānaya madhūni dadasva |*
*mā[a]nayo 'yam abhinātham ajasraṁ*
*mānini prakaṭa-māna-vaśatvam ||46||*

*Word for word:* *mā kṛthāḥ* — do not make; *katham api* — in any way; *prathayānam* (*prathamānam*?) — growing; *mānam* — pique; *ānaya* — bring; *madhūni* — honey (sweet drink); *dadasva* — give; *anayaḥ* — bad policy; *ayam* — this; *abhi-nātham* — towards the lord; *ajasram* — constant; *mānini* — O proud one; *prakaṭa* — open; *māna* — to pique; *vaśatvam* — subjection.

**46.** Do not in any way let your pique grow, O proud one; bring honey and offer it [to Him]! To be constantly and openly in the power of pique towards your lord is bad policy.

*Note.* The verse plays on the sounds of *māna*: *mānam ānaya*, *mānayo*, *mānini*, *māna-*. The beginning of the third pada can also be understood as *mā* + *anayaḥ*, "let there not be this folly". *Prathayānam* is an irregular form; one would expect *prathamānam*. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 47

पाययस्व मधुराधरसीधुं
जीवय प्रियतमं दयनीयम् ।
नूनमत्र भवती हृदयेशा
कातरं नु हृदयं न हि वेत्सि ॥४७॥

*pāyayasva madhurādhara-sīdhuṁ*
*jīvaya priyatamaṁ dayanīyam |*
*nūnam atra bhavatī hṛdayeśā*
*kātaraṁ nu hṛdayaṁ na hi vetsi ||47||*

*Word for word:* *pāyayasva* — give to drink; *madhura* — of the sweet; *adhara* — lips; *sīdhum* — the nectar (liquor); *jīvaya* — revive; *priyatamam* — the beloved; *dayanīyam* — pitiable; *nūnam* — surely; *atra* — here; *bhavatī* — you; *hṛdaya* — of the heart; *īśā* — mistress; *kātaram* — distressed; *nu* — really; *hṛdayam* — heart; *na hi vetsi* — do you not know.

**47.** Give [Him] to drink the nectar of your sweet lips; revive your pitiable beloved! Surely you are the mistress of His heart here — do you really not know how distressed that heart is?"

### Verse 48

इत्यतीव मृदुलः स्मरमत्तः
श्यामलोऽपि सततं गुरुरागः ।
प्रेयसो गुणवशीकृतचित्तां
चित्तनाथ इतरामभजिष्ट ॥४८॥

*ity atīva mṛdulaḥ smara-mattaḥ*
*śyāmalo 'pi satataṁ guru-rāgaḥ |*
*preyaso guṇa-vaśīkṛta-cittāṁ*
*citta-nātha itarām abhajiṣṭa ||48||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *atīva* — exceedingly; *mṛdulaḥ* — tender; *smara* — with love; *mattaḥ* — intoxicated; *śyāmalaḥ* — dark; *api* — though; *satatam* — always; *guru* — deeply; *rāgaḥ* — coloured (full of love); *preyasaḥ* — of the beloved; *guṇa* — by the qualities; *vaśīkṛta* — won over; *cittām* — [her whose] heart; *citta* — of hearts; *nāthaḥ* — the lord; *itarām* — to another; *abhajiṣṭa* — turned.

**48.** Thus the lord of hearts — exceedingly tender, intoxicated with love, dark yet always deeply crimson — turned to another, whose heart had been won over by the qualities of her beloved.

*Note.* An apparent contradiction (*virodhābhāsa*): He is "dark" (*śyāmala*) and yet always "deeply coloured, crimson" (*guru-rāga*, that is, full of ardent love).

### Verse 49

भूषितं सुमनसा वपुरासां
काननश्रियमिमां यदहार्षीत् ।
तेन तेन शुशुभेऽतितरां तत्
सद्गृहीतमुपयाति गुणाय ॥४९॥

*bhūṣitaṁ sumanasā vapur āsāṁ*
*kānana-śriyam imāṁ yad ahārṣīt |*
*tena tena śuśubhe 'titarāṁ tat*
*sad-gṛhītam upayāti guṇāya ||49||*

*Word for word:* *bhūṣitam* — adorned; *sumanasā* — with flowers (by the good-minded); *vapuḥ* — the body; *āsām* — their; *kānana* — of the forest; *śriyam* — beauty; *imām* — this; *yat* — since; *ahārṣīt* — stole; *tena tena* — by that very [deed]; *śuśubhe* — shone; *atitarām* — all the more; *tat* — for; *sat* — by the good; *gṛhītam* — what is taken; *upayāti* — goes; *guṇāya* — to virtue (onto the string).

**49.** Adorned with flowers, their bodies stole this beauty of the forest, and by that very [deed] they shone all the more: for what is taken by the good turns to virtue.

*Note.* A pun: *sumanas* is both "a flower" and "a good-minded person"; *sat*, "good"; *guṇa*, both "virtue" and "string" (of a garland): flowers taken up go onto the string of a garland.

### Verse 50

या द्रवन्ति सुरतश्रमभाजः
सौकुमार्यपरभागसदङ्ग्यः ।
ताश्चिरं वनविहारजखेदात्
स्वेदसिन्धुषु तथैवममज्जुः ॥५०॥

*yā dravanti surata-śrama-bhājaḥ*
*saukumārya-para-bhāga-sad-aṅgyaḥ |*
*tāś ciraṁ vana-vihāraja-khedāt*
*sveda-sindhuṣu tathaivam amajjuḥ ||50||*

*Word for word:* *yāḥ* — who; *dravanti* — melt; *surata* — of love's play; *śrama* — the fatigue; *bhājaḥ* — experiencing; *saukumārya* — of delicacy; *para-bhāga* — at the height; *sat* — beautiful; *aṅgyaḥ* — [whose] limbs; *tāḥ* — they; *ciram* — long; *vana* — in the forest; *vihāra* — from the pastimes; *ja* — born; *khedāt* — from the weariness; *sveda* — of perspiration; *sindhuṣu* — in oceans; *tathā evam* — in just the same way; *amajjuḥ* — sank.

**50.** They whose beautiful limbs are the very height of delicacy, who melt even at the fatigue of love's play, now, from the weariness born of their long pastimes in the forest, sank in just the same way into oceans of perspiration.

### Verse 51

नीलनीरधरकान्त्यमृताढ्यां
विस्फुटाम्बुजमनोरमनेत्राम् ।
भेजिरेऽथ यमुनामलसाङ्ग्यः
प्रेयसस्तनुमिव श्रमभाजः ॥५१॥

*nīla-nīradhara-kānty-amṛtāḍhyāṁ*
*visphuṭāmbuja-manorama-netrām |*
*bhejire 'tha yamunām alasāṅgyaḥ*
*preyasas tanum iva śrama-bhājaḥ ||51||*

*Word for word:* *nīla* — of a dark; *nīradhara* — rain-cloud; *kānti* — of the lustre; *amṛta* — with the nectar; *āḍhyām* — rich; *visphuṭa* — open; *ambuja* — lotuses; *manorama* — lovely; *netrām* — [whose] eyes; *bhejire* — entered; *atha* — then; *yamunām* — the Yamuna; *alasa* — languid; *aṅgyaḥ* — [whose] limbs; *preyasaḥ* — of the beloved; *tanum* — the body; *iva* — as if; *śrama* — fatigue; *bhājaḥ* — experiencing.

**51.** Then, wearied, their limbs languid, they entered the Yamuna — rich in the nectar of the lustre of a dark rain-cloud, her lovely eyes the open lotuses — as though [entering] the very body of their beloved.

*Note.* The edition has प्रेयसन्तनुम्; we read *preyasas tanum*. The dark Yamuna with her lotus eyes is like Krishna's own body.

### Verse 52

स्निग्धसान्द्रघननीलतरङ्गै-
रुल्लसत्पृषतपुष्पसमूहैः ।
आससाद सहसा रविपुत्री
केशपाशललितं रमणीनाम् ॥५२॥

*snigdha-sāndra-ghana-nīla-taraṅgair*
*ullasat-pṛṣata-puṣpa-samūhaiḥ |*
*āsasāda sahasā ravi-putrī*
*keśa-pāśa-lalitaṁ ramaṇīnām ||52||*

*Word for word:* *snigdha* — glossy; *sāndra* — dense; *ghana* — [like] a cloud; *nīla* — dark; *taraṅgaiḥ* — with waves; *ullasat* — leaping; *pṛṣata* — of spray; *puṣpa* — of flowers; *samūhaiḥ* — with clusters; *āsasāda* — attained; *sahasā* — suddenly; *ravi* — of the Sun; *putrī* — the daughter; *keśa* — of hair; *pāśa* — of the braids; *lalitam* — the charm; *ramaṇīnām* — of the beautiful women.

**52.** With her glossy, dense waves, dark as a cloud, and the clusters of flowers of her leaping spray, the daughter of the Sun suddenly attained the charm of the braided hair of the beautiful women.

*Note.* The Yamuna is the daughter of Surya. Her dark waves with their white spray are like black braids adorned with flowers.

### Verse 53

ईषदप्यहमुपेतुमशक्तः
सुभ्रु तत्तव तनुमवलम्बे ।
इत्यसावलसमूर्तिरथैका-
माश्लिषन्नुपययौ यमुनायाम् ॥५३॥

*īṣad apy aham upetum aśaktaḥ*
*subhru tat tava tanum avalambe |*
*ity asāv alasa-mūrtir athaikām*
*āśliṣann upayayau yamunāyām ||53||*

*Word for word:* *īṣat* — a little; *api* — even; *aham* — I; *upetum* — to go; *aśaktaḥ* — unable; *subhru* — O fair-browed one; *tat* — therefore; *tava* — on your; *tanum* — body; *avalambe* — I shall lean; *iti* — thus [saying]; *asau* — He; *alasa* — languid; *mūrtiḥ* — [whose] form; *atha* — then; *ekām* — one; *āśliṣan* — embracing; *upayayau* — went down; *yamunāyām* — into the Yamuna.

**53.** "O fair-browed one, I cannot go even a little way; so I shall lean on you." Saying this, He, languid in form, embraced one of them and went down into the Yamuna.

### Verse 54

चुम्बितानि नखदन्तनिपातान्
प्रायशः सरभसं विलपय्य ।
तौ परस्परजयोत्सुकचित्तौ
सिञ्चतः करजलैर्हृदयेशौ ॥५४॥

*cumbitāni nakha-danta-nipātān*
*prāyaśaḥ sarabhasaṁ vilapayya |*
*tau paraspara-jayotsuka-cittau*
*siñcataḥ kara-jalair hṛdayeśau ||54||*

*Word for word:* *cumbitāni* — kisses; *nakha* — of nails; *danta* — [and] of teeth; *nipātān* — the marks; *prāyaśaḥ* — almost all; *sa* — with; *rabhasam* — eagerness; *vilapayya* — having washed away (?); *tau* — the two; *paraspara* — over each other; *jaya* — for victory; *utsuka* — eager; *cittau* — [whose] hearts; *siñcataḥ* — splash; *kara* — of the hands; *jalaiḥ* — with the water; *hṛdaya* — of hearts; *īśau* — the two lords.

**54.** Eagerly washing away almost all [the traces of] kisses and the marks of nails and teeth, the two lords of each other's hearts, each eager for victory over the other, splashed one another with handfuls of water.

*Note.* The edition (like the Gosvami edition) has *vilapayya*. We take it as a gerund of the causative of *vi-lī*, "to dissolve, wash away" (*vilāpayati*): in the water the traces of the pastimes are washed off (?). A conjectural reading *vipalāya*, "having fled [from each other]", is also possible.

### Verse 55

वारि वारिततमा करनीरैः
प्रेयसा किमपि नित्यनवीना ।
वारिभिर्मिलति सूक्ष्मदुकूले
कूलमुज्जिगमिषुः किमुदस्थात् ॥५५॥

*vāri vāritatamā kara-nīraiḥ*
*preyasā kim api nitya-navīnā |*
*vāribhir milati sūkṣma-dukūle*
*kūlam ujjigamiṣuḥ kim udasthāt ||55||*

*Word for word:* *vāri* — in the water; *vāritatamā* — utterly repulsed; *kara* — of the hands; *nīraiḥ* — by the water; *preyasā* — by the beloved; *kim api* — a certain [gopi]; *nitya* — ever; *navīnā* — youthful; *vāribhiḥ* — with the water; *milati* — having merged; *sūkṣma* — fine; *dukūle* — the silk; *kūlam* — to the bank; *ujjigamiṣuḥ* — wishing to go up; *kim* — was it [because]; *udasthāt* — rose.

**55.** A certain ever-youthful [maiden], utterly repulsed in the water by the handfuls of water [thrown by] her beloved, rose up wishing to go up onto the bank — was it because her fine silk had merged with the water?

*Note.* Alliteration: *vāri vāritatamā … vāribhiḥ*, *dukūle* — *kūlam*. The wet silk has become transparent, and the gopi hastens to the bank.

### Verse 56

सुभ्रुवोऽधियमुनं श्लथनीव्याः
श्लिष्यता प्रियतमेन सलीलम् ।
स्रोतसापहृतमंशुकमच्छे
वारि गोपितुमिवाङ्गमभाजि ॥५६॥

*subhruvo 'dhiyamunaṁ ślatha-nīvyāḥ*
*śliṣyatā priyatamena salīlam |*
*srotasāpahṛtam aṁśukam acche*
*vāri gopitum ivāṅgam abhāji ||56||*

*Word for word:* *subhruvaḥ* — of a fair-browed [gopi]; *adhi-yamunam* — in the Yamuna; *ślatha* — loosened; *nīvyāḥ* — [whose] waistband knot; *śliṣyatā* — embracing; *priyatamena* — by the most beloved; *salīlam* — playfully; *srotasā* — by the current; *apahṛtam* — carried off; *aṁśukam* — [her] garment; *acche* — in the clear; *vāri* — water; *gopitum* — to hide; *iva* — as if; *aṅgam* — the body; *abhāji* — was taken [into His arms].

**56.** In the Yamuna a fair-browed [maiden's] waistband came loose, and the current carried off her garment; her most beloved, playfully embracing her, took her body into His arms, as though to hide it in the clear water.

*Note.* *Abhāji* we take as the passive aorist of *bhaj*: "[her] body was taken" — Krishna's embrace covers her in the transparent water. It may also be from *bhañj*, "to bend": "[His] body was bent, as though to hide in the clear water the garment carried off by the current."

### Verse 57

हावहारि जलमण्डुकलीलां
खेलया मधुरिपौ विदधत्याः ।
लोलशङ्खनिनदैरपरस्य
नृत्यतीव विपुलं कुचयुग्मम् ॥५७॥

*hāva-hāri jala-maṇḍuka-līlāṁ*
*khelayā madhu-ripau vidadhatyāḥ |*
*lola-śaṅkha-ninadair aparasya [aparasyāḥ]*
*nṛtyatīva vipulaṁ kuca-yugmam ||57||*

*Word for word:* *hāva* — by coquetry; *hāri* — captivating; *jala* — of the water; *maṇḍuka* — drum; *līlām* — the game; *khelayā* — in fun; *madhu* — of Madhu; *ripau* — before the Enemy; *vidadhatyāḥ* — of [her who was] playing; *lola* — jingling; *śaṅkha* — of conch-shell [bangles]; *ninadaiḥ* — to the sound; *aparasyāḥ* — of another; *nṛtyati* — dances; *iva* — as if; *vipulam* — ample; *kuca* — of breasts; *yugmam* — the pair.

**57.** As another, in fun, played before the Enemy of Madhu the coquettish, captivating game of the "water drum", her ample bosom seemed to dance to the jingling of her conch-shell bangles.

*Note.* *Jala-maṇḍuka* is a water game: striking the water with the palms so that it sounds like a drum. The edition has अपरस्य (masculine); the sense requires *aparasyāḥ* (the metre is unchanged) (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 58

पीवरस्तननितम्बनिवेशे
वीचिभिर्विघटनैर्घटनैश्च ।

सुभ्रुवामथ ययुः सलिलानि ॥५८॥

*pīvara-stana-nitamba-niveśe*
*vīcibhir vighaṭanair ghaṭanaiś ca |*
*gaṇḍa-śaila-pada-viskhalitatvaṁ*
*subhruvām atha yayuḥ salilāni ||58||*

*Word for word:* *pīvara* — of full; *stana* — breasts; *nitamba* — [and] hips; *niveśe* — at the place; *vīcibhiḥ* — in waves; *vighaṭanaiḥ* — by separating; *ghaṭanaiḥ* — by colliding; *ca* — and; *gaṇḍa-śaila* — of boulders; *pada* — at the foot; *viskhalitatvam* — stumbling; *subhruvām* — of the fair-browed [gopis]; *atha* — then; *yayuḥ* — attained; *salilāni* — the waters.

**58.** Then at the full bosoms and hips of the fair-browed [maidens] the waters, now parting, now colliding in waves, took on the stumbling of a stream at the foot of boulders.

### Verse 59

कापि कान्तममृताञ्जलिपूरै-
र्लोलशङ्खवलया स्नपयन्तम् ।
धारयन्त्यपि ददौ करकम्पैः
पारितोषिकमुरोरुहनृत्यम् ॥५९॥

*kāpi kāntam amṛtāñjali-pūrair*
*lola-śaṅkha-valayā snapayantam |*
*dhārayanty api dadau kara-kampaiḥ*
*pāritoṣikam uroruha-nṛtyam ||59||*

*Word for word:* *kā api* — a certain [gopi]; *kāntam* — the beloved; *amṛta* — of nectar[-like water]; *añjali* — with handfuls; *pūraiḥ* — full; *lola* — jingling; *śaṅkha* — conch-shell; *valayā* — [whose] bangles; *snapayantam* — drenching; *dhārayantī* — holding; *api* — even while; *dadau* — gave; *kara* — of the hands; *kampaiḥ* — by the trembling; *pāritoṣikam* — as a reward; *uroruha* — of the breasts; *nṛtyam* — the dance.

**59.** A certain [maiden] with jingling conch-shell bangles caught hold of her beloved as He was drenching her with full handfuls of nectar-like water, and by the trembling of her hands gave Him as a reward the dance of her bosom.

### Verse 60

कापि मुग्धरमणी प्रियवक्षः
प्रेप्सुरच्छसलिलेऽप्यगभीरे ।
धुन्वति करदले बहुशङ्खे
प्रेयसः कनकहारलतासीत् ॥६०॥

*kāpi mugdha-ramaṇī priya-vakṣaḥ*
*prepsur accha-salile 'py agabhīre |*
*dhunvati kara-dale bahu-śaṅkhe*
*preyasaḥ kanaka-hāra-latāsīt ||60||*

*Word for word:* *kā api* — a certain; *mugdha* — artless; *ramaṇī* — beauty; *priya* — of the dear one; *vakṣaḥ* — the chest; *prepsuḥ* — longing to reach; *accha* — clear; *salile* — in the water; *api* — though; *agabhīre* — shallow; *dhunvati* — as [she] shook; *kara* — the hand; *dale* — petal-like; *bahu* — with many; *śaṅkhe* — conch-shell [bangles]; *preyasaḥ* — of the beloved; *kanaka* — golden; *hāra* — of a necklace; *latā* — the creeper; *āsīt* — became.

**60.** A certain artless beauty longed to reach her dear one's chest; and as, in the clear water, shallow though it was, she shook her petal-like hand laden with many conch-shell bangles, she became the golden creeper of a necklace on her beloved.

*Note.* The golden-complexioned gopi on Krishna's dark chest is like a golden necklace.

### Verse 61

ऊरुरोधसि चलच्छफरीणां
वृत्तिभिः सभयकौतुकगर्वम् (हर्षं वा) ।
चारुशीत्कृतिलसद्दशनाभिः
पाणिकम्पनमकारि वधूभिः ॥६१॥

*ūru-rodhasi calac-chapharīṇāṁ*
*vṛttibhiḥ sa-bhaya-kautuka-garvam (harṣaṁ vā) |*
*cāru-śītkṛti-lasad-daśanābhiḥ*
*pāṇi-kampanam akāri vadhūbhiḥ ||61||*

*Word for word:* *ūru* — of the thighs; *rodhasi* — on the bank; *calat* — darting; *śapharīṇām* — of the *śapharī* fish; *vṛttibhiḥ* — by the movements; *sa* — with; *bhaya* — fear; *kautuka* — curiosity; *garvam* — [and] pride; (*harṣam vā* — or: joy); *cāru* — charming; *śītkṛti* — with the hiss "śīt"; *lasat* — flashing; *daśanābhiḥ* — [with] teeth; *pāṇi* — of the hands; *kampanam* — a shaking; *akāri* — was made; *vadhūbhiḥ* — by the young women.

**61.** At the movements of the *śapharī* fish darting about the banks of their thighs, the young women shook their hands with fear, curiosity and pride, their teeth flashing as they charmingly hissed "sh-sh!"

*Note.* The edition gives a variant: *garvam* or *harṣam* ("joy"). *Śītkāra* — drawing in the breath through the teeth — is a conventional sign in kavya of the thrill of love.

सर्वतः करदलाहतिरोह-

आससाद सलिलं घनघर्मान्
स्नापयच्छ्रमविनोदपटीयः ॥६२॥

*sarvataḥ kara-dalāhati-rohad-*
*vīci vakṣasiruhān atha tāsām |*
*āsasāda salilaṁ ghana-gharmān*
*snāpayac chrama-vinoda-paṭīyaḥ ||62||*

*Word for word:* *sarvataḥ* — on all sides; *kara* — of the hands; *dala* — of the petals; *āhati* — from the blows; *rohat* — rising; *vīci* — [with] waves; *vakṣasiruhān* — the breasts ("growing on the chest"); *atha* — then; *tāsām* — their; *āsasāda* — reached; *salilam* — the water; *ghana* — heavily; *gharmān* — perspiring; *snāpayat* — bathing; *śrama* — weariness; *vinoda* — in dispelling; *paṭīyaḥ* — most skilful.

**62.** Then the water — most skilful at dispelling weariness — its waves rising on all sides from the blows of their petal-like hands, reached their bosoms, heavy with perspiration, and bathed them.

### Verse 63

सम्पदेव हि सतामुपमापि ॥६३॥

*tatra padma-vadaneti vadhūnām*
*ākalayya ramaṇād abhidhānam |*

*Word for word:* *tatra* — there; *padma* — lotus-; *vadanā* — faced; *iti* — thus; *vadhūnām* — of the young women; *ākalayya* — having heard; *ramaṇāt* — from the dear one; *abhidhānam* — the name; *ānanarta* — danced; *nu* — as it were; *taraṅga* — on the waves; *gam* — moving; *abjam* — the lotus; *sampad* — good fortune; *eva* — indeed; *hi* — for; *satām* — for the worthy; *upamā* — [being] a comparison; *api* — even.

**63.** There, hearing the young women called "lotus-faced" by their dear one, the lotus riding on the waves danced, as it were: for to the worthy even to serve as a comparison is good fortune indeed.

### Verse 64

कापि काञ्चनरुचिर्यमुनायाः

कृष्णमप्यनिकटस्थममंस्त ॥६४॥

*Word for word:* *kā api* — a certain [maiden]; *kāñcana* — golden; *ruciḥ* — in lustre; *yamunāyāḥ* — of the Yamuna; *śyāmale* — in the dark; *payasi* — water; *bhāva* — of feeling; *vaśa* — in the power; *aṅgī* — [whose] body; *sarvam* — whole; *aṅgam* — [whose] body; *abhisambhṛta* — filled; *nīlam* — with blue; *kṛṣṇam* — Krishna; *api* — even; *anikaṭa* — not near; *stham* — standing; *amaṁsta* — thought.

**64.** A certain golden-hued [maiden], her body in the power of feeling, thought even Krishna, His whole body steeped in blue, to be far away in the dark water of the Yamuna.

*Note.* *Sarvam aṅgam abhisambhṛta-nīlam* qualifies Krishna ("whose whole body is steeped in blue"): the dark Krishna has merged with the dark water, and the gopi thinks He is not beside her.

### Verse 65

ओष्ठपल्लवमयावकमक्षि

वीतरागविलसन्नखरेखौ

*Word for word:* *oṣṭha* — of the lips; *pallavam* — the shoot; *a-yāvakam* — without lac; *akṣi* — the eye; *kṣīṇa* — with faded; *kajjalam* — collyrium; *uroruha* — of the breasts; *kumbhau* — the two jars; *vīta* — bereft; *rāga* — of colour; *vilasat* — gleaming; *nakha* — of nails; *rekhau* — [with] the marks; *preyasā* — by the beloved; *nidhuvana* — of love's play; *antam* — the end; *iva* — as if; *aikṣi* — was seen.

*Note.* The water has washed away the cosmetics, and the gopis look as they do at the close of love's play. *Vīta-rāga* — "bereft of colour (kunkuma)" and, by double meaning, "free of passion".

### Verse 67

*Note.* The bees fly up to the lotus of her face.

### Verse 68

काञ्चिदत्र कमलानि जिहीर्षुं
पद्मिनीसमुदये मिलिताङ्गीम् ।
निर्भरं वलयिता बिसवल्ली
श्रोणिरोधसि रुरोध रुषेव ॥६८॥

*kāñcid atra kamalāni jihīrṣuṁ*
*padminī-samudaye militāṅgīm |*
*nirbharaṁ valayitā bisa-vallī*
*śroṇi-rodhasi rurodha ruṣeva ||68||*

*Word for word:* *kāñcit* — a certain [maiden]; *atra* — here; *kamalāni* — lotuses; *jihīrṣum* — wishing to pluck; *padminī* — of lotus plants; *samudaye* — in the throng; *milita* — mingled; *aṅgīm* — [whose] limbs; *nirbharam* — tightly; *valayitā* — coiling round; *bisa* — of lotus stalk; *vallī* — the creeper; *śroṇi* — of the hips; *rodhasi* — on the bank; *rurodha* — held back; *ruṣā* — with anger; *iva* — as if.

**68.** Here one [maiden], wishing to pluck lotuses, made her way deep into the throng of lotus plants — and a creeper of lotus stalk, coiling tightly round the bank of her hips, held her back, as if in anger.

### Verse 69

प्राक् प्रति प्रियतमं श्लथनीव्याः

तत्क्षणेन सुदृशो बिसवल्ल्या
पद्मिनी प्रियसखीव रुरोध ॥६९॥

*prāk prati priyatamaṁ ślatha-nīvyāḥ*
*srotasā śithilitaṁ tanu-celam |*
*tat-kṣaṇena sudṛśo bisa-vallyā*
*padminī priya-sakhīva rurodha ||69||*

*Word for word:* *prāk* — already before; *prati* — towards; *priyatamam* — the dearest one; *ślatha* — loosened; *nīvyāḥ* — of [her] whose knot; *srotasā* — by the current; *śithilitam* — loosened; *tanu* — thin; *celam* — the garment; *tat-kṣaṇena* — at that very moment; *sudṛśaḥ* — of the fair-eyed one; *bisa* — of the stalk; *vallyā* — with the creeper; *padminī* — the lotus plant; *priya* — dear; *sakhī* — a friend; *iva* — like; *rurodha* — held back.

**69.** The thin garment of a fair-eyed [maiden], whose knot had already loosened before for her dearest one, was loosened by the current — but at that very moment the lotus plant, like a dear friend, held it back with the creeper of its stalk.

*Note.* The edition has *श्रोतसा*, a misprint for *स्रोतसा*.

वारिभिर्द्विगुणमाकुलितासीत् ॥७०॥

*kāpi niḥsaha-tanuḥ pratikūlaṁ*
*nihnutā samudayanty alasena |*
*preyasā saha sakhībhir amandaṁ*
*vāribhir dviguṇam ākulitāsīt ||70||*

*Word for word:* *kā api* — a certain [maiden]; *niḥsaha* — exhausted; *tanuḥ* — [whose] body; *pratikūlam* — in defiance; *nihnutā* — hidden; *samudayantī* — rising up; *alasena* — languidly; *preyasā* — by the beloved; *saha* — together; *sakhībhiḥ* — with [her] friends; *amandam* — relentlessly; *vāribhiḥ* — with water; *dviguṇam* — doubly; *ākulitā* — flustered; *āsīt* — was.

**70.** One [maiden], her body exhausted, hid herself in defiance; and as she languidly rose up [from the water], she was doubly flustered, relentlessly [splashed] with water by her beloved together with her friends.

### Verse 71

काप्युदेतुमसकृद्यतमाना

त्रासिता तमपराधयति स्म ॥७१॥

*kāpy udetum asakṛd yatamānā*
*kānta-pāṇi-dala-saṁyamitāpi |*
*ūru-lagna-śapharī-parivṛtti-*

*Word for word:* *kā api* — a certain [maiden]; *udetum* — to get out; *asakṛt* — repeatedly; *yatamānā* — trying; *kānta* — of the beloved; *pāṇi* — of the hand; *dala* — by the petal; *saṁyamitā* — held back; *api* — though; *ūru* — to the thigh; *lagna* — clinging; *śapharī* — of a *śapharī* fish; *parivṛtti* — by the turning; *trāsitā* — frightened; *tam* — Him; *aparādhayati sma* — blamed.

**71.** One [maiden] tried again and again to get out, though held back by the petal of her beloved's hand; and when a *śapharī* fish clinging to her thigh turned over and frightened her, she blamed Him.

### Verse 72

सूक्ष्मसार्द्रवसनेन तटान्तं
प्राप्तया कुचयुगं पिदधत्या ।
तादृशं तदपि वीक्ष्य कयाचिद्
व्रीडयाभिरमणं समहासि ॥७२॥

*sūkṣma-sārdra-vasanena taṭāntaṁ*
*prāptayā kuca-yugaṁ pidadhatyā |*
*tādṛśaṁ tad api vīkṣya kayācid*
*vrīḍayābhiramaṇaṁ samahāsi ||72||*

*Word for word:* *sūkṣma* — fine; *sa-ārdra* — wet; *vasanena* — with the garment; *taṭa* — of the bank; *antam* — the edge; *prāptayā* — by [her] who had reached; *kuca* — of breasts; *yugam* — the pair; *pidadhatyā* — covering; *tādṛśam* — such (showing through); *tat* — it; *api* — still; *vīkṣya* — having seen; *kayācit* — by a certain [maiden]; *vrīḍayā* — from shyness; *abhi-ramaṇam* — before the dear one; *samahāsi* — there was laughing.

**72.** One [maiden], reaching the edge of the bank and covering her bosom with her fine wet garment, saw that it still showed through just the same — and laughed in shyness before her dear one.

### Verse 73

सुभ्रुवोऽथ विषमक्रमभूषा
वस्त्रमात्रकृतयत्नविशेषाः ।
स्नेहनुन्नमलसे रविपुत्र्यै
सत्प्रसादमिव तत्तदकार्षुः ॥७३॥

*subhruvo 'tha viṣama-krama-bhūṣā*
*vastra-mātra-kṛta-yatna-viśeṣāḥ |*
*sneha-nunnam alase ravi-putryai*
*sat-prasādam iva tat tad akārṣuḥ ||73||*

*Word for word:* *subhruvaḥ* — the fair-browed; *atha* — then; *viṣama* — disordered; *krama* — in arrangement; *bhūṣāḥ* — [with] ornaments; *vastra* — for the garment; *mātra* — only; *kṛta* — having taken; *yatna* — care; *viśeṣāḥ* — special; *sneha* — by affection; *nunnam* — prompted; *alase* — in languor; *ravi* — of the Sun; *putryai* — to the daughter; *sat* — a fine; *prasādam* — gracious gift; *iva* — as it were; *tat tat* — this and that; *akārṣuḥ* — made.

**73.** Then the fair-browed [maidens], their ornaments all awry, taking particular care only of their garments, in their languor made this and that, as it were, a fine gracious gift, prompted by affection, to the daughter of the Sun.

*Note.* Many of the ornaments fell into the Yamuna. The form *alase* is unclear; it is taken here as "languid" (of the gopis). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

केशपाशकुसुमैर्मणिहारै-

सत्सखीव यमुनापि रराज ॥७४॥

*keśa-pāśa-kusumair maṇi-hārair*
*niḥsṛtaiś ca valayai rasanābhiḥ |*
*majjanād vigalitair anulepaiḥ*
*sat-sakhīva yamunāpi rarāja ||74||*

*Word for word:* *keśa* — of hair; *pāśa* — from the braids; *kusumaiḥ* — with the flowers; *maṇi* — jewelled; *hāraiḥ* — with necklaces; *niḥsṛtaiḥ* — slipped off; *ca* — and; *valayaiḥ* — with bracelets; *rasanābhiḥ* — with girdles; *majjanāt* — from bathing; *vigalitaiḥ* — washed away; *anulepaiḥ* — with unguents; *sat* — a true; *sakhī* — friend; *iva* — like; *yamunā* — the Yamuna; *api* — too; *rarāja* — shone.

**74.** With the flowers from their braids, with jewelled necklaces, with bracelets and girdles that had slipped off, with unguents washed away in the bathing — with all this the Yamuna too shone, like a true friend.

*Note.* The unguents are aguru, musk and the like.

*Word for word:* *nirbharam* — abundantly; *ghana* — of dense; *taraṅga* — waves; *vibhaṅgāt* — from the breaking; *saṁgalat* — trickling; *jala* — of water; *lavaḥ* — [with] drops; *kaca* — of hair; *pāśaḥ* — the braid; *tāraka* — of stars; *udgamana* — by the rising; *ramyatara* — lovelier; *ābhaḥ* — [whose] appearance; *dhvānta* — of darkness; *rāśiḥ* — a mass; *iva* — like; *tatra* — there; *rarāja* — shone.

**75.** Their braids, from which drops of water trickled abundantly as the dense waves broke, shone there like a mass of darkness made lovelier by the rising of the stars.

### Verse 76

आनितम्बपतितै रमणीनां

*ādadhe ramaṇayoḥ kim ihaikyaṁ*
*prema-rāśim itayoḥ kaca-pāśaiḥ ||76||*

*Word for word:* *ā* — right down to; *nitamba* — the hips; *patitaiḥ* — falling; *ramaṇīnām* — of the beautiful women; *nīla* — dark; *nīradhara* — of rain clouds; *sāndratama* — most dense; *ābhaiḥ* — [with] the appearance; *ādadhe* — was displayed; *ramaṇayoḥ* — of the two lovers; *kim* — was it not; *iha* — here; *aikyam* — oneness; *prema* — of love; *rāśim* — a mass; *itayoḥ* — [of the two] who had attained; *kaca* — of hair; *pāśaiḥ* — by the braids.

**76.** Did not the braids of the beautiful women, falling right down to their hips, dense as dark rain clouds, here display the oneness of the two lovers, who had attained a very mass of love?

*Note.* The dark braids of the gopis are of the same colour as Krishna, and seem to bear witness to the oneness of the lovers.

### Verse 77

निर्भरं मिलितमङ्गलतायां

प्रोच्छलत्तदिदमुद्वमतीव ॥७७॥

*rūpa-rūpam amṛtaṁ bahu-pītam |*
*syandad-ambu vasanaṁ mṛdu-sūkṣmaṁ*
*procchalat tad idam udvamatīva ||77||*

*Word for word:* *nirbharam* — closely; *militam* — clinging; *aṅga* — of the body; *latāyām* — to the creeper; *rūpa-rūpam* — the beauty of beauties; *amṛtam* — the nectar; *bahu* — abundantly; *pītam* — drunk; *syandat* — streaming; *ambu* — [with] water; *vasanam* — the garment; *mṛdu* — soft; *sūkṣmam* — fine; *procchalat* — overflowing; *tat idam* — that very [nectar]; *udvamati* — pours back; *iva* — as if.

**77.** The soft, fine garment, clinging closely to the creeper of the body and streaming with water, seemed to pour back, overflowing, that very nectar of the beauty of beauties which it had drunk so abundantly.

### Verse 78

कापि शीत्कृतिपरा भुजवल्या
स्वस्तिकेन पिदधे कुचयुग्मम् ।
अन्वहं विरहिणौ न भवेता-
मित्यरुद्ध लतया किल कोकौ ॥७८॥

*kāpi śītkṛti-parā bhuja-vallyā*
*svastikena pidadhe kuca-yugmam |*
*anvahaṁ virahiṇau na bhavetām*
*ity aruddha latayā kila kokau ||78||*

*Word for word:* *kā api* — a certain [maiden]; *śītkṛti* — on hissing "śīt"; *parā* — intent; *bhuja* — of the arms; *vallyā* — with the creeper; *svastikena* — crosswise; *pidadhe* — covered; *kuca* — of breasts; *yugmam* — the pair; *anu-aham* — day after day; *virahiṇau* — separated; *na bhavetām* — may they not be; *iti* — thus [thinking]; *aruddha* — held back; *latayā* — with a creeper; *kila* — as it were; *kokau* — the pair of chakravakas.

**78.** One [maiden], shivering and hissing "śīt", covered her bosom with the creeper of her arms crossed over it — as if she had held back a pair of chakravaka birds with a creeper, so that they might not be parted day after day.

*Note.* In kavya the bosom is traditionally compared to a pair of chakravaka birds (*koka*), which, according to popular belief, are parted every night.

### Verse 79

रत्नभित्तिषु निजप्रतिबिम्बै-
र्भूयसीं तनुरुचिं कलयन्त्यः ।
यत्र विस्मयवशं रभसेषु
प्राप्नुवन्ति चकितैणदृशस्ताः ॥७९॥

*ratna-bhittiṣu nija-pratibimbair*
*bhūyasīṁ tanu-ruciṁ kalayantyaḥ |*
*yatra vismaya-vaśaṁ rabhaseṣu*
*prāpnuvanti cakitaiṇa-dṛśas tāḥ ||79||*

*Word for word:* *ratna* — jewelled; *bhittiṣu* — on the walls; *nija* — by their own; *pratibimbaiḥ* — reflections; *bhūyasīm* — multiplied; *tanu* — of [their] bodies; *rucim* — the radiance; *kalayantyaḥ* — perceiving; *yatra* — where; *vismaya* — of wonder; *vaśam* — into the power; *rabhaseṣu* — in [their] eagerness; *prāpnuvanti* — come; *cakita* — of a startled; *eṇa* — doe; *dṛśaḥ* — [with] the eyes; *tāḥ* — they.

**79.** There, perceiving on the jewelled walls the radiance of their bodies multiplied by their own reflections, they, with eyes like a startled doe's, in their eagerness fell under the sway of wonder.

*Note.* With this verse begins the description (through *yatra*, "where") of the jewelled pavilion which the gopis enter after bathing in order to adorn themselves. The word to which all these "where"s refer is *ālayam* ("pavilion") in verse 93, which concludes the *kulaka* (79–93).

### Verse 80

प्रेयसा परिहृते तनुचेले
दीप इत्यभिनिरीक्ष्य पिधित्सुः ।

सत्रपाजनि चिरं प्रतिबिम्बैः ॥८०॥

*preyasā parihṛte tanu-cele*
*dīpa ity abhinirīkṣya pidhitsuḥ |*
*yatra ratna-kiraṇān prati bālā*
*satrapājani ciraṁ pratibimbaiḥ ||80||*

*Word for word:* *preyasā* — by the beloved; *parihṛte* — when [it] was drawn away; *tanu* — thin; *cele* — the garment; *dīpaḥ* — a lamp; *iti* — thus [thinking]; *abhinirīkṣya* — having looked; *pidhitsuḥ* — wishing to cover; *yatra* — where; *ratna* — of the gems; *kiraṇān prati* — the rays; *bālā* — a young maiden; *sa* — with; *trapā* — shame; *ajani* — became; *ciram* — for long; *pratibimbaiḥ* — because of the reflections.

**80.** There a young maiden, when her beloved drew away her thin garment, looked at the rays of the gems, took them for a lamp and wished to cover them — and for a long time was abashed by her reflections.

*Note.* A familiar motif of kavya: the shy heroine tries to put out or cover the gems, taking them for a lamp.

### Verse 81

सुस्मितैर्हिममयूखमयूखैः

*susmitair hima-mayūkha-mayūkhaiḥ*

*vedir aikṣi kila yatra payobhiḥ*
*sphāṭikair viracitā iti vadhūbhiḥ ||81||*

*Word for word:* *su-smitaiḥ* — smiling; *hima* — cool-; *mayūkha* — rayed [moon]; *mayūkhaiḥ* — by the rays; *saṁsravantī* — oozing; *aniśam* — ceaselessly; *indu* — moon-; *maṇīnām* — of stones; *vediḥ* — the dais; *aikṣi* — was seen; *kila* — as it were; *yatra* — where; *payobhiḥ* — of waters; *sphāṭikaiḥ* — crystal; *viracitā* — built; *iti* — thus; *vadhūbhiḥ* — by the young women.

**81.** There a dais of moonstones, ceaselessly oozing [moisture] under the smiling rays of the cool-rayed [moon], seemed to the young women to be built of crystal waters.

*Note.* The *candrakānta* (moonstone) is believed to exude moisture in moonlight. The edition has *संश्रवन्ति*; we read *saṁsravantī*.

### Verse 82

सुभ्रुवां चरणपल्लवपातै-

शोणरत्नसमलङ्कृतगर्भा
दृश्यते स्फटिकभूरपि यत्र ॥८२॥

*bimbavaty anavagāham agādhāt (?) |*
*śoṇa-ratna-samalaṅkṛta-garbhā*
*dṛśyate sphaṭika-bhūr api yatra ||82||*

*Word for word:* *subhruvām* — of the fair-browed; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *pallava* — of the shoots; *pātaiḥ* — by the treading; *bimbavatī* — reflecting; *anavagāham* — so as not to be entered; *agādhāt* — from fathomlessness (?); *śoṇa* — with red; *ratna* — gems; *samalaṅkṛta* — adorned; *garbhā* — [whose] interior; *dṛśyate* — appears; *sphaṭika* — crystal; *bhūḥ* — floor; *api* — even; *yatra* — where

**82.** There even the crystal floor, reflecting the shoot-like feet of the fair-browed [maidens] as they trod upon it, seemed so fathomless that one could not step onto it, its depths adorned, as it seemed, with red gems.

*Note.* The end of the second pada (*°m agādhāt*) is grammatically unclear (?). The red gems in the depths are the reflections of the reddened feet. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

**83.** There, with the parrots, cuckoos, peacocks and pigeons painted on the jewelled wall as if alive, the other [birds] dwelling in the house — the very same kinds — merrily chattered.

### Verse 84

यत्र चित्रपरपुष्टवधूनां
