बालचूततरुमञ्जरिकालि-
र्गृह्यतामिति मुहुः प्रलपन्ति ॥८४॥

*yatra citra-parapuṣṭa-vadhūnāṁ*
*cāru-cañcu-puṭam anv ati-mugdhāḥ |*
*bāla-cūta-taru-mañjarikālir*
*gṛhyatām iti muhuḥ pralapanti ||84||*

*Word for word:* *yatra* — where; *citra* — painted; *parapuṣṭa* — of cuckoos; *vadhūnām* — of the females; *cāru* — charming; *cañcu* — of the beaks; *puṭam anu* — towards the tips; *ati* — very; *mugdhāḥ* — innocent [maidens]; *bāla* — of a young; *cūta* — mango; *taru* — tree; *mañjarikā* — of blossoms; *āliḥ* — a cluster; *gṛhyatām* — take; *iti* — thus; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *pralapanti* — say.

**84.** There the most innocent [maidens], holding out a cluster of blossoms of a young mango tree to the charming beaks of painted hen-cuckoos, kept saying again and again: "Take it!"

*Note.* *Parapuṣṭa* ("nourished by others") is the cuckoo, which lays its eggs in other birds' nests.

### Verse 85

उन्मिषद्विविधरत्नमयूखै-
र्यत्र नित्यमितरेतरपृक्तैः ।
चारुनिर्मिति मनोज्ञमयत्न-
स्वस्तिकादि परिकर्म विभाति ॥८५॥

*unmiṣad-vividha-ratna-mayūkhair*
*yatra nityam itaretara-pṛktaiḥ |*
*cāru-nirmiti manojñam ayatna-*
*svastikādi parikarma vibhāti ||85||*

*Word for word:* *unmiṣat* — flashing forth; *vividha* — of various; *ratna* — gems; *mayūkhaiḥ* — by the rays; *yatra* — where; *nityam* — ever; *itaretara* — with one another; *pṛktaiḥ* — mingled; *cāru* — beautifully; *nirmiti* — wrought; *manojñam* — charming; *ayatna* — effortless; *svastika* — svastikas; *ādi* — and the like; *parikarma* — ornamentation; *vibhāti* — shines.

**85.** There, by the rays of various gems flashing forth and ever mingling with one another, an ornamentation of svastikas and other [auspicious figures] shines forth — charming, beautifully wrought, and arising without any effort.

### Verse 86

उल्लसन्मरकताश्ममणीनां
राजिषु प्रतिपदं व्रजबालाः ।
अङ्कतः शिशुमृगीं मृदुदोर्भ्यां
प्रेरयन्ति किल यत्र सुखेन ॥८६॥

*ullasan-marakatāśma-maṇīnāṁ*
*rājiṣu pratipadaṁ vraja-bālāḥ |*
*aṅkataḥ śiśu-mṛgīṁ mṛdu-dorbhyāṁ*
*prerayanti kila yatra sukhena ||86||*

*Word for word:* *ullasat* — gleaming; *marakata-aśma* — emerald; *maṇīnām* — of stones; *rājiṣu* — towards the rows; *pratipadam* — at every step; *vraja* — of Vraja; *bālāḥ* — the girls; *aṅkataḥ* — from [their] laps; *śiśu* — young; *mṛgīm* — doe; *mṛdu* — with soft; *dorbhyām* — arms; *prerayanti* — urge on; *kila* — indeed; *yatra* — where; *sukhena* — joyfully.

**86.** There at every step the girls of Vraja joyfully let a little fawn down from their laps and with their soft arms urged it on towards the rows of gleaming emerald stones.

*Note.* The girls take the emeralds for grass.

### Verse 87

शोणरत्नमयवीथिषु काश्चि-
द्भूषणाय मुदिताः स्वमभीक्ष्य ।
यत्र कुङ्कुमरसेन कदाचि-
न्नाङ्गरागमनुरागत ईषुः ॥८७॥

*śoṇa-ratnamaya-vīthiṣu kāścid*
*bhūṣaṇāya muditāḥ svam abhīkṣya |*
*yatra kuṅkuma-rasena kadācin*
*nāṅga-rāgam anurāgata īṣuḥ ||87||*

*Word for word:* *śoṇa* — red; *ratna* — gems; *maya* — made of; *vīthiṣu* — in the galleries; *kāścit* — some; *bhūṣaṇāya* — for adornment; *muditāḥ* — delighted; *svam* — themselves; *abhīkṣya* — having seen; *yatra* — where; *kuṅkuma* — of kunkuma; *rasena* — with the liquid; *kadācit* — ever; *na* — not; *aṅga* — of the body; *rāgam* — the colouring; *anurāgataḥ* — from the redness (from love); *īṣuḥ* — wished.

**87.** There some, about to adorn themselves in the galleries made of red gems, saw themselves [already reddened] and, delighted, out of that redness no longer wished to colour their bodies with kunkuma liquid.

*Note.* A play on words: *anurāgataḥ* — "from the redness" (the glow of the rubies) and "from love".

### Verse 88

यत्र कल्पतरवो विविधानां
ज्योतिषां व्यतिकरैः सुमणीनाम् ।
उच्चकैर्ज्वलदमन्दशिखाग्रै-
र्मण्डिता इव बभुर्वरदीपैः ॥८८॥

*yatra kalpa-taravo vividhānāṁ*
*jyotiṣāṁ vyatikaraiḥ sumaṇīnām |*
*uccakair jvalad-amanda-śikhāgrair*
*maṇḍitā iva babhur vara-dīpaiḥ ||88||*

*Word for word:* *yatra* — where; *kalpa* — wish-fulfilling; *taravaḥ* — trees; *vividhānām* — of various; *jyotiṣām* — lustres; *vyatikaraiḥ* — by the intermingling; *su-maṇīnām* — of excellent gems; *uccakaiḥ* — high; *jvalat* — blazing; *amanda* — bright; *śikhā* — of flame; *agraiḥ* — [with] tongues; *maṇḍitāḥ* — adorned; *iva* — as if; *babhuḥ* — shone; *vara* — with fine; *dīpaiḥ* — lamps.

**88.** There the wish-fulfilling trees, through the intermingling of the various lustres of excellent gems, shone as if adorned with fine lamps whose bright tongues of flame blazed high.

### Verse 89

पक्वदाडिमधिया शुकशावा-
स्तेषु शोणमणिषूपचरन्तः ।
नानुभूय चरणाहतिभिर्नो
चञ्चुमादधति यत्र कदापि ॥८९॥

*pakva-dāḍima-dhiyā śuka-śāvās*
*teṣu śoṇa-maṇiṣūpacarantaḥ |*
*nānubhūya caraṇāhatibhir no*
*cañcum ādadhati yatra kadāpi ||89||*

*Word for word:* *pakva* — ripe; *dāḍima* — pomegranates; *dhiyā* — taking [them] for; *śuka* — of parrots; *śāvāḥ* — the young; *teṣu* — to those; *śoṇa* — red; *maṇiṣu* — gems; *upacarantaḥ* — approaching; *na* — not; *anubhūya* — having felt [softness]; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *āhatibhiḥ* — by the strikes; *no* — not; *cañcum* — the beak; *ādadhati* — apply; *yatra* — where; *kadā api* — ever.

**89.** There the young parrots, taking those red gems for ripe pomegranates, came up to them; but, feeling no [softness] under the strikes of their feet, never once applied their beaks.

*Note.* The double negative in the third and fourth padas admits different interpretations (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 90

पुष्पमिच्छति न हीरकबुद्ध्या
हीरकं श्रयति पुष्पधियैषः ।
यत्र दैववशतो मधुपत्वं
गच्छति स्म मधुपः खलु मौग्ध्यात् ॥९०॥

*puṣpam icchati na hīraka-buddhyā*
*hīrakaṁ śrayati puṣpa-dhiyaiṣaḥ |*
*yatra daiva-vaśato madhupatvaṁ*
*gacchati sma madhupaḥ khalu maugdhyāt ||90||*

*Word for word:* *puṣpam* — a flower; *icchati* — wants; *na* — not; *hīraka* — for a diamond; *buddhyā* — taking [it]; *hīrakam* — to a diamond; *śrayati* — clings; *puṣpa* — for a flower; *dhiyā* — taking [it]; *eṣaḥ* — this [bee]; *yatra* — where; *daiva* — of fate; *vaśataḥ* — by the power; *madhupa* — of "honey-drinker"; *tvam* — the state; *gacchati sma* — attained; *madhupaḥ* — the bee; *khalu* — indeed; *maugdhyāt* — from folly.

**90.** There the bee, in its folly, does not want a flower, taking it for a diamond, and clings to a diamond, taking it for a flower; so it was only by the will of fate that the bee ever attained the state of a "honey-drinker".

### Verse 91

एकतः स्फटिकपाटलगौरै-
रन्यतो मरकतद्युतिभिन्नैः ।
चन्द्रिकातिमिरयोरिव वीथी
यत्र चारुसलिलैः किल वापी ॥९१॥

*ekataḥ sphaṭika-pāṭala-gaurair*
*anyato marakata-dyuti-bhinnaiḥ |*
*candrikā-timirayor iva vīthī*
*yatra cāru-salilaiḥ kila vāpī ||91||*

*Word for word:* *ekataḥ* — on one side; *sphaṭika* — from crystal; *pāṭala* — pinkish; *gauraiḥ* — [and] white; *anyataḥ* — on the other; *marakata* — of emeralds; *dyuti* — by the lustre; *bhinnaiḥ* — shot through; *candrikā* — of moonlight; *timirayoḥ* — [and] of darkness; *iva* — like; *vīthī* — a strip; *yatra* — where; *cāru* — with lovely; *salilaiḥ* — waters; *kila* — indeed; *vāpī* — a pond.

**91.** There a pond with lovely waters — on one side pinkish-white from the crystal, on the other shot through with the lustre of emeralds — was like a strip where moonlight and darkness meet.

### Verse 92

स्फाटिकं तटमभि प्रतिमग्नः
प्रोत्थितो द्युपतिरत्नतटान्ते ।
निर्भरं विलपति प्रतिकान्तां
यत्र चारुसरसीमभि कोकः ॥९२॥

*sphāṭikaṁ taṭam abhi pratimagnaḥ*
*protthito dyupati-ratna-taṭānte |*
*nirbharaṁ vilapati pratikāntāṁ*
*yatra cāru-sarasīm abhi kokaḥ ||92||*

*Word for word:* *sphāṭikam* — crystal; *taṭam abhi* — at the bank; *pratimagnaḥ* — having dived; *protthitaḥ* — having emerged; *dyu-pati* — of the lord of the sky (the sun); *ratna* — of the gem; *taṭa* — of the bank; *ante* — at the edge; *nirbharam* — bitterly; *vilapati* — laments; *prati* — for; *kāntām* — [his] mate; *yatra* — where; *cāru* — lovely; *sarasīm abhi* — towards the lake; *kokaḥ* — the chakravaka.

**92.** There a chakravaka, having dived at the crystal bank and emerged at the edge of the bank of sunstone, bitterly laments for his mate, turned towards the lovely lake.

*Note.* *Dyupati-ratna* ("the gem of the lord of the sky") is the sunstone (*sūryakānta*). The edition has *prothito*; the Gosvami edition (GGM) has *protthito* ("having emerged"), and so we read.

### Verse 93

भूषणाय विविशुर्लघुखेलं
तं मनोरमविशालविचित्रम् ।
आलयं कुवलयामलनेत्रा-
श्चन्द्रिका इव सुधामयसिन्धौ ॥९३॥
पञ्चदशभिः कुलकम् ॥

*bhūṣaṇāya viviśur laghu-khelaṁ*
*taṁ manorama-viśāla-vicitram |*
*ālayaṁ kuvalayāmala-netrāś*
*candrikā iva sudhāmaya-sindhau ||93||*
*pañcadaśabhiḥ kulakam ||*

*Word for word:* *bhūṣaṇāya* — to adorn themselves; *viviśuḥ* — entered; *laghu* — lightly; *khelam* — playfully; *tam* — that; *manorama* — captivating; *viśāla* — spacious; *vicitram* — wondrous; *ālayam* — pavilion; *kuvalaya* — as blue lotuses; *amala* — pure; *netrāḥ* — [maidens with] eyes; *candrikāḥ* — moonlight; *iva* — like; *sudhā* — nectar; *maya* — consisting of; *sindhau* — into the ocean; *pañcadaśabhiḥ* — of fifteen [verses]; *kulakam* — a *kulaka*.

**93.** And the [maidens] with eyes pure as blue lotuses lightly, playfully entered that captivating, spacious, wondrous pavilion to adorn themselves, as moonlight [enters] an ocean of nectar. *(A kulaka of fifteen verses.)*

*Note.* Verses 79–93 form a *kulaka*, a single sentence: all the subordinate clauses with "where" (*yatra*) refer to the word *ālayam* ("pavilion").

### Verse 94

श्रीमद्भिः परभृतबर्हिकीरहंसैः
सत्पारावतमधुपावलीकपोतैः ।
अन्योन्यस्वपरिवर्धतोऽप्यपूर्वं
संभेजे श्रवणरसायनत्वमुच्चैः ॥९४॥

*śrīmadbhiḥ parabhṛta-barhi-kīra-haṁsaiḥ*
*sat-pārāvata-madhupāvalī-kapotaiḥ |*
*anyonya-sva-parivardhato 'py apūrvaṁ*
*sambheje śravaṇa-rasāyanatvam uccaiḥ ||94||*

*Word for word:* *śrīmadbhiḥ* — by splendid; *parabhṛta* — cuckoos; *barhi* — peacocks; *kīra* — parrots; *haṁsaiḥ* — [and] swans; *sat* — by fine; *pārāvata* — turtle-doves; *madhupa* — of bees; *āvalī* — swarms; *kapotaiḥ* — [and] pigeons; *anyonya* — mutually; *sva* — their own [voices]; *parivardhataḥ* — from increasing; *api* — and; *apūrvam* — unprecedented; *sambheje* — attained; *śravaṇa* — for the ears; *rasāyanatvam* — the quality of an elixir; *uccaiḥ* — in the highest degree.

**94.** Through the splendid cuckoos, peacocks, parrots and swans, the fine turtle-doves, the swarms of bees and the pigeons, each raising its own voice above the others', [the pavilion] became in the highest degree an unprecedented elixir for the ears.

*Note.* The metre is *praharṣiṇī*. The subject of *sambheje* is not named; by the sense it is the "pavilion" of verse 93 (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 95

उद्गच्छन्तीष्वथ वरवधूष्वालयान्तेषु जाता
नानापुष्पैः सुरभिमधुरैः कल्पवल्ल्यः समन्तात् ।
चक्रुर्नीराजनमिव मुहुः कूजितैः कोकिलानां
संकुर्वत्यो जय जय जयेत्युच्चकैर्हर्षनादम् ॥९५॥

*udgacchantīṣv atha vara-vadhūṣv ālayānteṣu jātā*
*nānā-puṣpaiḥ surabhi-madhuraiḥ kalpa-vallyaḥ samantāt |*
*cakrur nīrājanam iva muhuḥ kūjitaiḥ kokilānāṁ*
*saṅkurvatyo jaya jaya jayety uccakair harṣa-nādam ||95||*

*Word for word:* *udgacchantīṣu* — as [they] went up; *atha* — then; *vara* — lovely; *vadhūṣu* — the young women; *ālaya* — of the pavilion; *anteṣu* — within; *jātāḥ* — grown; *nānā* — with various; *puṣpaiḥ* — flowers; *surabhi* — fragrant; *madhuraiḥ* — sweet; *kalpa* — wish-fulfilling; *vallyaḥ* — creepers; *samantāt* — on every side; *cakruḥ* — performed; *nīrājanam* — the rite of *nīrājana*; *iva* — as it were; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *kūjitaiḥ* — with the singing; *kokilānām* — of cuckoos; *saṅkurvatyaḥ* — raising; *jaya jaya jaya* — victory, victory, victory; *iti* — thus; *uccakaiḥ* — loudly; *harṣa* — of joy; *nādam* — a cry.

**95.** Then, as the lovely young women went up [into the pavilion], the wish-fulfilling creepers grown within it on every side performed, as it were, *nīrājana* over them with various fragrant, sweet flowers, and with the singing of the cuckoos again and again loudly raised a joyful cry: "Victory, victory, victory!"

*Note.* The metre is *mandākrāntā*. *Nīrājana* is a rite of welcome: a lamp, flowers and the like are waved before one who is honoured.

**Colophon:** *iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahākāvye navamaḥ sargaḥ* — "Thus [ends] the ninth sarga in the mahakavya 'Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita'." (The colophon gives no title for the sarga.)

---

## Sarga Ten — verses 1–80

**Title of the sarga:** none — the colophon of the edition gives no title for this sarga.
**Metre:** *svāgatā* (11 syllables per pada: —⏑— ⏑⏑⏑ —⏑⏑ ——); verses 74–80 — *mālinī*.
**Total verses:** 80.

**Contents of the passage:** the continuation of Srivasa's account — the night of Radha, Krishna and the gopis in the jewelled pavilion (classical themes of the mahakavya: sunset, moonrise, adornment, the drinking party, love's play, daybreak).
- 1–3 — the gopis prepare a couch of *mālatī* flowers and perfume the pavilion with incense; the sun sets so as not to stand in their way.
- 4–9 — sunset: the sun draws in its rays; the West holds the sun like red-hot iron (an ordeal); the darkness is the smoke of the serpents' breath; the elephants and the winged mountains of the quarters.
- 10–15 — the darkness deepens; Night lifts her veil; the swan of the moon emerges from the eastern lake; the moon is a silver casket.
- 16–27 — adornment: garments, unguents, coiffures, mirrors; some refuse ornaments ("the body is the ornament of ornaments"); Krishna gazes at His own attire.
- 28–45 — moonlight and the drinking party: the circling cup, tipsy speech and movements, kisses and bites, the "relish" (*vidaṁśa*).
- 46–73 — love's play (after the manner of the *kāma-śāstra*); 65–66 — Kama makes Radha and Krishna exchange roles.
- 74–80 (*mālinī*) — fulfilment and sleep; the lamp shakes its head: "there is nothing like this anywhere"; the sun puts out the night-lamp; the friends' morning jests ("the lake", "the bee and the lotus").

### Verse 1

मालतीकुसुमतल्पमनल्पं
सोपबर्हमभिसंभृतवाञ्छाः ।
मण्डनार्थमथ मन्दिरमध्यं
मण्डितं व्यरचयन्मदिराक्ष्यः ॥१॥

*mālatī-kusuma-talpam analpaṁ*
*sopabarham abhisambhṛta-vāñchāḥ |*
*maṇḍanārtham atha mandira-madhyaṁ*
*maṇḍitaṁ vyaracayan madirākṣyaḥ ||1||*

*Word for word:* *mālatī* — of *mālatī* (jasmine); *kusuma* — of flowers; *talpam* — a couch; *analpam* — spacious; *sa* — with; *upabarham* — a pillow; *abhisambhṛta* — filled; *vāñchāḥ* — [whose] longings; *maṇḍana* — of adornment; *artham* — for the sake; *atha* — then; *mandira* — of the pavilion; *madhyam* — the interior; *maṇḍitam* — adorned; *vyaracayan* — made; *madira* — intoxicating; *akṣyaḥ* — [maidens with] eyes.

**1.** Then the maidens with intoxicating eyes, full of longing, made a spacious couch of *mālatī* flowers with a pillow, and for the sake of [their] adornment made the interior of the pavilion beautifully adorned.

### Verse 2

सौरभोद्यदसितागुरुधूपै-
र्धूपितं निरवकाशविकाशैः ।
सञ्चरत्तरशशित्रसरेणु-
व्याप्तमाप्तगुरुगौरवगन्धम् ॥२॥

*saurabhodyad-asitāguru-dhūpair*
*dhūpitaṁ niravakāśa-vikāśaiḥ |*
*sañcarat-tara-śaśi-trasareṇu-*
*vyāptam āpta-guru-gaurava-gandham ||2||*

*Word for word:* *saurabha* — with fragrance; *udyat* — rising; *asita* — of black; *aguru* — aloe-wood; *dhūpaiḥ* — with incense; *dhūpitam* — perfumed; *niravakāśa* — leaving no gap; *vikāśaiḥ* — spreading; *sañcarat-tara* — darting to and fro; *śaśi* — of the moon[light]; *trasareṇu* — with motes; *vyāptam* — filled; *āpta* — having acquired; *guru* — heavy; *gaurava* — majestic; *gandham* — fragrance.

**2.** [They] perfumed it with incense of black aloe-wood, whose clouds rose fragrantly and spread, leaving no gap; it was filled with motes darting to and fro in the moonbeams, and acquired a heavy, majestic fragrance.

*Note.* *trasareṇu* — a mote of dust visible in a beam of light.

### Verse 3

इत्थमुत्थितवती रतिभूमौ
वीक्ष्य गोकुलवधूर्दिननाथः ।
वर्धतां निधुवनोन्नतिरासा-
मित्यपास्तपटिमास्तमियाय ॥३॥

*ittham utthitavatī rati-bhūmau*
*vīkṣya gokula-vadhūr dina-nāthaḥ |*
*vardhatāṁ nidhuvanonnatir āsām*
*ity apāsta-paṭimāstam iyāya ||3||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *utthitavatīḥ* — risen up; *rati* — of love; *bhūmau* — on the ground (place); *vīkṣya* — seeing; *gokula* — of Gokula; *vadhūḥ* — the young women; *dina* — of the day; *nāthaḥ* — the lord; *vardhatām* — let it increase; *nidhuvana* — of love's play; *unnatiḥ* — the rising; *āsām* — their; *iti* — thus [thinking]; *apāsta* — having laid aside; *paṭimā* — his strength; *astam* — to his setting; *iyāya* — went.

**3.** Seeing the young women of Gokula thus risen up [ready] in the place of love, the lord of the day thought, "Let their love's play rise ever higher!" — and, laying aside his might, went to his setting.

### Verse 4

सर्वतः प्रसृमरास्तपतो मे
निर्भरं य इह ते यदि हेयाः ।
कीदृशैरहह तद्भवितव्यं
कर्षतीति किरणान्नु पतङ्गः ॥४॥

*sarvataḥ prasṛmarās tapato me*
*nirbharaṁ ya iha te yadi heyāḥ |*
*kīdṛśair ahaha tad bhavitavyaṁ*
*karṣatīti kiraṇān nu pataṅgaḥ ||4||*

*Word for word:* *sarvataḥ* — in all directions; *prasṛmarāḥ* — spreading; *tapataḥ* — blazing; *me* — from me; *nirbharam* — abundantly; *ye* — which; *iha* — here; *te* — they; *yadi* — if; *heyāḥ* — are to be abandoned; *kīdṛśaiḥ* — of what kind; *ahaha* — alas; *tat* — then; *bhavitavyam* — [they] will have to become; *karṣati* — draws in; *iti* — thus [thinking]; *kiraṇān* — the rays; *nu* — is it not; *pataṅgaḥ* — the sun.

**4.** "The rays that spread abundantly in all directions from me as I blaze — if they are to be abandoned here, alas, what will become of them?" Is it not with this thought that the sun draws in its rays?

*Note.* The syntax of *kīdṛśair … bhavitavyam* is rendered according to the sense (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 5

चन्द्रमाः स्वपिति तारकगेहे
कीदृशी त्वमिति वादशमाय ।
वारुणीदिगबलारुणमर्कं
लोहपिण्डमिव तप्तमधत्त ॥५॥

*candramāḥ svapiti tāraka-gehe*
*kīdṛśī tvam iti vāda-śamāya |*
*vāruṇī-dig-abalāruṇam arkaṁ*
*loha-piṇḍam iva taptam adhatta ||5||*

*Word for word:* *candramāḥ* — the moon; *svapiti* — sleeps; *tāraka* — of the stars; *gehe* — in the house; *kīdṛśī* — what sort [of wife]; *tvam* — you; *iti* — such; *vāda* — talk; *śamāya* — to silence; *vāruṇī* — of Varuna; *dik* — the quarter (the west); *abalā* — the woman; *aruṇam* — red; *arkam* — the sun; *loha* — of iron; *piṇḍam* — a ball; *iva* — like; *taptam* — red-hot; *adhatta* — took up.

**5.** "The moon sleeps in the house of the stars — what sort of wife are you?" To silence such talk, the woman West, the quarter of Varuna, took up the red sun like a red-hot ball of iron.

*Note.* An allusion to the ordeal (*divya*): a woman accused of infidelity proves her innocence by holding red-hot iron.

### Verse 6

द्योतितानि विरचय्य तथान्य-
द्वीपवर्तिनि दिवाकररत्ने ।
अभ्यपूरि जगदुच्चतमिस्रं
श्वासधूमपटलैर्भुजगानाम् ॥६॥

*dyotitāni viracayya tathānya-*
*dvīpa-vartini divākara-ratne |*
*abhyapūri jagad ucca-tamisraṁ*
*śvāsa-dhūma-paṭalair bhujagānām ||6||*

*Word for word:* *dyotitāni* — illumined; *viracayya* — having made; *tathā* — so; *anya* — on another; *dvīpa* — continent; *vartini* — when [it] abode; *divākara* — of the sun; *ratne* — the jewel; *abhyapūri* — was filled; *jagat* — the world; *ucca* — deeply; *tamisram* — darkened; *śvāsa* — of the breath; *dhūma* — of smoke; *paṭalaiḥ* — with clouds; *bhujagānām* — of the serpents.

**6.** When the jewel of the sun, having made [those lands] bright, had gone to abide on another continent, the world, plunged in deep darkness, was filled [as it were] with clouds of the smoky breath of the serpents.

*Note.* *dvīpa* — a continent of Puranic cosmology. The darkness is compared to the venomous, smoky breath of the Nagas of the nether world.

### Verse 7

दिग्गजाः किमु परस्परयुक्ताः
किं पुनर्दिगचलाश्चलपक्षाः ।
इत्थमूहितविकारविशेषं
ध्वान्तमत्र न ममौ जगदण्डे ॥७॥

*dig-gajāḥ kim u paraspara-yuktāḥ*
*kiṁ punar dig-acalāś cala-pakṣāḥ |*
*ittham ūhita-vikāra-viśeṣaṁ*
*dhvāntam atra na mamau jagad-aṇḍe ||7||*

*Word for word:* *dik* — of the quarters; *gajāḥ* — the elephants; *kim u* — have …?; *paraspara* — with one another; *yuktāḥ* — come together; *kim punaḥ* — or else; *dik* — of the quarters; *acalāḥ* — the mountains; *cala* — moving; *pakṣāḥ* — [with] wings; *ittham* — thus; *ūhita* — conjectured; *vikāra* — transformation; *viśeṣam* — [whose] particular; *dhvāntam* — the darkness; *atra* — here; *na* — not; *mamau* — was contained; *jagat* — of the universe; *aṇḍe* — in the egg.

**7.** "Have the elephants of the quarters come together with one another? Or have the mountains of the quarters set their wings in motion?" So [people] conjectured about its strange transformation; the darkness could no longer be contained here in the egg of the universe.

*Note.* According to the myth, the mountains once had wings, until Indra cut them off with his thunderbolt (*vajra*).

### Verse 8

किं तमालतरुभिर्जगदेत-
न्निर्मितं ननु किमञ्जनपुञ्जैः ।
रञ्जितं नु हरकण्ठमयूखैः
किं न्वभूदिह दिगन्तरलोपः ॥८॥

*kiṁ tamāla-tarubhir jagad etan*
*nirmitaṁ nanu kim añjana-puñjaiḥ |*
*rañjitaṁ nu hara-kaṇṭha-mayūkhaiḥ*
*kiṁ nv abhūd iha dig-antara-lopaḥ ||8||*

*Word for word:* *kim* — whether; *tamāla* — *tamāla*; *tarubhiḥ* — from trees; *jagat* — world; *etat* — this; *nirmitam* — fashioned; *nanu kim* — or else; *añjana* — of collyrium; *puñjaiḥ* — from heaps; *rañjitam* — dyed; *nu* — whether; *hara* — of Hara (Shiva); *kaṇṭha* — of the throat; *mayūkhaiḥ* — by the rays; *kim nu* — or; *abhūt* — has come about; *iha* — here; *dik* — of the quarters; *antara* — of the intervals; *lopaḥ* — the vanishing.

**8.** Has this world been fashioned from *tamāla* trees? Or from heaps of collyrium? Has it been dyed by the rays of Hara's [blue] throat? Or have the intervals between the quarters vanished here?

*Note.* Shiva's throat turned blue from the *hālāhala* poison that he drank.

### Verse 9

पद्मिनीजनवियोगसुतप्तो
निर्ममज्ज जलधौ दिननाथः ।
सान्द्रधूमपटलैरिव तस्मा-
दुद्गतैर्जगदपूरि तमोभिः ॥९॥

*padminī-jana-viyoga-sutapto*
*nirmamajja jaladhau dina-nāthaḥ |*
*sāndra-dhūma-paṭalair iva tasmād*
*udgatair jagad apūri tamobhiḥ ||9||*

*Word for word:* *padminī* — lotus; *jana* — from [his] beloved ones; *viyoga* — by separation; *sutaptaḥ* — intensely heated; *nirmamajja* — plunged; *jaladhau* — into the ocean; *dina* — of the day; *nāthaḥ* — the lord; *sāndra* — dense; *dhūma* — of smoke; *paṭalaiḥ* — with clouds; *iva* — as if; *tasmāt* — from there; *udgataiḥ* — rising; *jagat* — the world; *apūri* — was filled; *tamobhiḥ* — with darkness.

**9.** Scorched by separation from his beloved lotuses, the lord of the day plunged into the ocean — and the world was filled with darkness rising from there like dense clouds of smoke.

*Note.* A red-hot body plunged into water gives off steam and smoke.

### Verse 10

पतिताः किमु दिशो गगनं वा
भ्रंशितं किमु समुद्गमिता भूः ।
लोपितं किमथ वा खलु विश्वं
स्निग्धसान्द्ररुचिरैस्तिमिरौघैः ॥१०॥

*patitāḥ kim u diśo gaganaṁ vā*
*bhraṁśitaṁ kim u samudgamitā bhūḥ |*
*lopitaṁ kim atha vā khalu viśvaṁ*
*snigdha-sāndra-rucirais timiraughaiḥ ||10||*

*Word for word:* *patitāḥ* — fallen; *kim u* — have …?; *diśaḥ* — the quarters; *gaganam* — the sky; *vā* — or; *bhraṁśitam* — toppled; *kim u* — has …?; *samudgamitā* — heaved up; *bhūḥ* — the earth; *lopitam* — blotted out; *kim* — has …?; *atha vā* — or else; *khalu* — indeed; *viśvam* — the universe; *snigdha* — by glossy; *sāndra* — dense; *ruciraiḥ* — beautiful; *timira* — of darkness; *oghaiḥ* — floods.

**10.** Have the quarters fallen? Or has the sky been toppled? Has the earth been heaved up? Or else has the universe indeed been blotted out by glossy, dense, beautiful floods of darkness?

### Verse 11

सम्मदादिव परस्परमाशा-
योषितो मृगमदोत्करचूर्णैः ।
मन्मथोन्मथितमुग्धवधूनां
रञ्जयन्ति पुरकेलिवनान्तम् ॥११॥

*sammadād iva parasparam āśā-*
*yoṣito mṛgamadotkara-cūrṇaiḥ |*
*manmathonmathita-mugdha-vadhūnāṁ*
*rañjayanti pura-keli-vanāntam ||11||*

*Word for word:* *sammadāt* — out of merriment; *iva* — as if; *parasparam* — one another; *āśā* — of the quarters; *yoṣitaḥ* — the women; *mṛgamada* — of musk; *utkara* — with heaps; *cūrṇaiḥ* — of powder; *manmatha* — by Manmatha; *unmathita* — agitated; *mugdha* — artless; *vadhūnām* — of the young women; *rañjayanti* — colour; *pura* — before (?); *keli* — of play; *vana* — of the grove; *antam* — the depths.

**11.** As though out of merriment [pelting] one another with heaps of musk powder, the women of the quarters colour [with darkness] the depths of the pleasure grove before the artless young women agitated by Manmatha.

*Note.* The darkness is compared to the dark musk powder that people throw at one another at a festival. *pura-* may be understood as *puraḥ* ("in front"); possibly "the pleasure grove of the town" (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 12

आगतः किमु न वेत्यथ पत्यु-
र्वीक्षणोत्कमनसा रभसेन ।
पूर्वदिक्तटमुखात् स्मितमुग्धा-
च्छ्यामया तिमिरचेलमुदासे ॥१२॥

*āgataḥ kim u na vety atha patyur*
*vīkṣaṇotka-manasā rabhasena |*
*pūrva-dik-taṭa-mukhāt smita-mugdhāc*
*chyāmayā timira-celam udāse ||12||*

*Word for word:* *āgataḥ* — has come; *kim u* — whether; *na vā* — or not; *iti* — thus [thinking]; *atha* — then; *patyuḥ* — the husband; *vīkṣaṇa* — to see; *utka* — eager; *manasā* — [with] heart; *rabhasena* — hastily; *pūrva* — of the eastern; *dik* — quarter; *taṭa* — of the edge; *mukhāt* — from the face; *smita* — with a smile; *mugdhāt* — lovely; *śyāmayā* — by Night; *timira* — of darkness; *celam* — the veil; *udāse* — was lifted.

**12.** "Has he come or not?" So thinking, Night, her heart eager to see her husband, hastily lifted the veil of darkness from the face of the eastern horizon, lovely with a smile.

*Note.* Night's husband is the moon; before moonrise the east grows pale. *śyāmā* — "the dark one", an epithet of the night.

### Verse 13

आश्लिषन्नतितरां तुहिनांशुः
प्रांशुना सुललितेन करेण ।
यामिनीमृगदृशः सुपिनद्धं
ध्वान्तनीलवसनं समुदासे ॥१३॥

*āśliṣann atitarāṁ tuhināṁśuḥ*
*prāṁśunā sulalitena kareṇa |*
*yāminī-mṛga-dṛśaḥ supinaddhaṁ*
*dhvānta-nīla-vasanaṁ samudāse ||13||*

*Word for word:* *āśliṣan* — embracing; *atitarām* — tightly; *tuhina* — cool; *aṁśuḥ* — rayed (the moon); *prāṁśunā* — with long; *sulalitena* — graceful; *kareṇa* — with the hand (ray); *yāminī* — of Night; *mṛga* — of a doe; *dṛśaḥ* — [with] the eyes; *supinaddham* — tightly fastened; *dhvānta* — of darkness; *nīla* — blue; *vasanam* — the garment; *samudāse* — drew off.

**13.** The cool-rayed moon, embracing doe-eyed Night tightly with his long, graceful hand, drew off her tightly fastened blue garment of darkness.

*Note.* *kara* means both "hand" and "ray".

### Verse 14

अङ्कशैवलविभूषितपृष्ठो
बिभ्रदल्पतरभानुमृणालम् ।
पूर्वदिक्तटसरोवरमध्या-
दुन्ममज्ज शनकैः शशिहंसः ॥१४॥

*aṅka-śaivala-vibhūṣita-pṛṣṭho*
*bibhrad alpatara-bhānu-mṛṇālam |*
*pūrva-dik-taṭa-sarovara-madhyād*
*unmamajja śanakaiḥ śaśi-haṁsaḥ ||14||*

*Word for word:* *aṅka* — of the mark (the moon's spot); *śaivala* — with the waterweed; *vibhūṣita* — adorned; *pṛṣṭhaḥ* — [with] back; *bibhrat* — bearing; *alpatara* — slender; *bhānu* — of rays; *mṛṇālam* — the lotus-stalk; *pūrva* — of the eastern; *dik* — quarter; *taṭa* — of the edge; *sarovara* — of the lake; *madhyāt* — from the middle; *unmamajja* — emerged; *śanakaiḥ* — slowly; *śaśi* — the moon; *haṁsaḥ* — swan.

**14.** The swan of the moon, its back adorned with the waterweed of its mark, bearing [in its beak] the slender lotus-stalk of its rays, slowly emerged from the middle of the lake of the eastern horizon.

*Note.* Swans are believed to feed on lotus stalks.

### Verse 15

रौप्यसम्पुट इवेन्दुरमन्दो
दिग्वधूनिचयमण्डनहेतुः ।
मण्डनार्थमथ मुग्धवधूना-
मुत्ससर्प विकिरन्नमृतौघम् ॥१५॥

*raupya-sampuṭa ivendur amando*
*dig-vadhū-nicaya-maṇḍana-hetuḥ |*
*maṇḍanārtham atha mugdha-vadhūnām*
*utsasarpa vikirann amṛtaugham ||15||*

*Word for word:* *raupya* — silver; *sampuṭaḥ* — casket; *iva* — like; *induḥ* — the moon; *amandaḥ* — full; *dik* — of the quarters; *vadhū* — of the wives; *nicaya* — of the host; *maṇḍana* — of the adornment; *hetuḥ* — the means; *maṇḍana* — of adornment; *artham* — for the sake; *atha* — then; *mugdha* — of the artless; *vadhūnām* — young women; *utsasarpa* — rose; *vikiran* — scattering; *amṛta* — of nectar; *ogham* — a flood.

**15.** Like a silver casket [of cosmetics] for adorning the host of the wives of the quarters, the full moon then rose, scattering a flood of nectar, to adorn the artless young women.

### Verse 16

वासितानि पटवासविमर्दै-
र्निर्भरं तनुसुखानि तनूनि ।
अंशुकानि दधिरे मदिराक्ष्यो
मान्मथानि किमु शुद्धयशांसि ॥१६॥

*vāsitāni paṭavāsa-vimardair*
*nirbharaṁ tanu-sukhāni tanūni |*
*aṁśukāni dadhire madirākṣyo*
*mānmathāni kim u śuddha-yaśāṁsi ||16||*

*Word for word:* *vāsitāni* — perfumed; *paṭavāsa* — of scented powder; *vimardaiḥ* — by rubbing; *nirbharam* — richly; *tanu* — to the body; *sukhāni* — pleasant; *tanūni* — fine; *aṁśukāni* — garments; *dadhire* — put on; *madira* — intoxicating; *akṣyaḥ* — [maidens with] eyes; *mānmathāni* — of Manmatha; *kim u* — or was it; *śuddha* — pure; *yaśāṁsi* — the fame.

**16.** The maidens with intoxicating eyes put on fine garments, pleasant to the body and richly perfumed by rubbing with scented powder — or was it the pure fame of Manmatha [that they put on]?

*Note.* In kavya fame (*yaśas*) is imagined as white; the white garments are the embodied fame of the god of love.

### Verse 17

अंशुकाञ्चललसन्निबिडोरुः
सुभ्रुवां कनकसौभगकम्रः ।
मन्मथस्य नगरीसपताक-
स्तम्भदम्भमहरत् सविशेषम् ॥१७॥

*aṁśukāñcala-lasan-nibiḍoruḥ*
*subhruvāṁ kanaka-saubhaga-kamraḥ |*
*manmathasya nagarī-sapatāka-*
*stambha-dambham aharat saviśeṣam ||17||*

*Word for word:* *aṁśuka* — of the garment; *añcala* — beneath the edge; *lasat* — gleaming; *nibiḍa* — firm; *ūruḥ* — thigh; *subhruvām* — of the fair-browed; *kanaka* — golden; *saubhaga* — with loveliness; *kamraḥ* — charming; *manmathasya* — of Manmatha; *nagarī* — of the city; *sa* — with; *patāka* — flags; *stambha* — of the pillars; *dambham* — the pretension; *aharat* — took away; *saviśeṣam* — far surpassing.

**17.** The firm thighs of the fair-browed [maidens], gleaming beneath the edges of their garments and charming with a golden loveliness, far surpassed the pretensions of the flag-decked pillars of Manmatha's city.

*Note.* The thighs are golden pillars; the edges of the garments are the flags upon them.

### Verse 18

गन्धवासितसितांशुकखण्डै-
र्मार्जनाय समलङ्कृतगर्भः ।
राजति स्म सुदृशां कचपाशः
कौमुदीमिव पिबंस्तिमिरौघः ॥१८॥

*gandha-vāsita-sitāṁśuka-khaṇḍair*
*mārjanāya samalaṅkṛta-garbhaḥ |*
*rājati sma sudṛśāṁ kaca-pāśaḥ*
*kaumudīm iva pibaṁs timiraughaḥ ||18||*

*Word for word:* *gandha* — with fragrances; *vāsita* — perfumed; *sita* — white; *aṁśuka* — of cloth; *khaṇḍaiḥ* — with strips; *mārjanāya* — for drying; *samalaṅkṛta* — adorned; *garbhaḥ* — [whose] interior; *rājati sma* — shone; *sudṛśām* — of the fair-eyed; *kaca* — of hair; *pāśaḥ* — the braid (mass); *kaumudīm* — the moonlight; *iva* — like; *piban* — drinking; *timira* — of darkness; *oghaḥ* — a flood.

**18.** The braided hair of the fair-eyed [maidens], within which strips of white cloth perfumed with fragrances had been set for drying it, shone like a flood of darkness drinking the moonlight.

*Note.* The edition has *कचपासः* — a misprint for *कचपाशः*.

### Verse 19

मृष्टमुक्तचिकुरा वलयन्ती
चारुवामकरजैरलकाग्रम् ।
दर्पणार्पितविलोचनलक्ष्मीः
कापि कामनगरीव रराज ॥१९॥

*mṛṣṭa-mukta-cikurā valayantī*
*cāru-vāma-karajair alakāgram |*
*darpaṇārpita-vilocana-lakṣmīḥ*
*kāpi kāma-nagarīva rarāja ||19||*

*Word for word:* *mṛṣṭa* — dried; *mukta* — let loose; *cikurā* — [with] hair; *valayantī* — curling; *cāru* — with lovely; *vāma* — of the left hand; *karajaiḥ* — with the nails; *alaka* — of a lock; *agram* — the tip; *darpaṇa* — on the mirror; *arpita* — fixed; *vilocana* — of [whose] eyes; *lakṣmīḥ* — the beauty; *kā api* — a certain [maiden]; *kāma* — of Kama; *nagarī* — the city; *iva* — like; *rarāja* — shone.

**19.** One, her hair dried and let loose, curling the tip of a lock with the lovely nails of her left hand, the beauty of her eyes fixed upon a mirror, shone like the city of Kama.

*Note.* The comparison with "the city of Kama" is not wholly transparent (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 20

सत्प्रसाधनिकया लघुहेलं
मृष्टमुक्तचिकुरा वरनारी ।
अन्वलिप्त वपुरुत्तमसान्द्रैः
कुङ्कुमच्छिदुरचन्दनपङ्कैः ॥२०॥

*sat-prasādhanikayā laghu-helaṁ*
*mṛṣṭa-mukta-cikurā vara-nārī |*
*anvalipta vapur uttama-sāndraiḥ*
*kuṅkuma-cchidura-candana-paṅkaiḥ ||20||*

*Word for word:* *sat* — with a skilled; *prasādhanikayā* — tiring-maid; *laghu* — lightly; *helam* — playfully; *mṛṣṭa* — dried; *mukta* — let loose; *cikurā* — [with] hair; *vara* — lovely; *nārī* — woman; *anvalipta* — anointed; *vapuḥ* — the body; *uttama* — with excellent; *sāndraiḥ* — thick; *kuṅkuma* — with *kuṅkuma*; *chidura* — streaked; *candana* — of sandalwood; *paṅkaiḥ* — with pastes.

**20.** Another lovely woman, her hair dried and let loose, with the help of a skilled tiring-maid lightly and playfully anointed her body with excellent thick pastes of sandalwood streaked with *kuṅkuma*.

### Verse 21

सान्द्रचन्द्रमृगनाभिविभिन्नः
कौङ्कुमेन च रसेन विमुग्धः ।
आदधे वपुषि मुग्धवधूभि-
श्चन्द्रपङ्क इव चन्दनपङ्कः ॥२१॥

*sāndra-candra-mṛganābhi-vibhinnaḥ*
*kauṅkumena ca rasena vimugdhaḥ |*
*ādadhe vapuṣi mugdha-vadhūbhiś*
*candra-paṅka iva candana-paṅkaḥ ||21||*

*Word for word:* *sāndra* — with thick; *candra* — camphor; *mṛganābhi* — [and] musk; *vibhinnaḥ* — mixed; *kauṅkumena* — of *kuṅkuma*; *ca* — and; *rasena* — with the juice; *vimugdhaḥ* — blended; *ādadhe* — was applied; *vapuṣi* — on the body; *mugdha* — by the artless; *vadhūbhiḥ* — young women; *candra* — of the moon; *paṅkaḥ* — a paste; *iva* — like; *candana* — of sandalwood; *paṅkaḥ* — paste.

**21.** The artless young women applied to their bodies sandal paste mixed with thick camphor and musk and blended with the juice of *kuṅkuma* — like a paste made of the moon.

*Note.* *candra* here means "camphor" (*karpūra*), with a play on its meaning "moon".

### Verse 22

भूषणस्य च विभूषणमङ्गं
तत् किमेभिरिति कापि वराङ्गी ।
नाभजत् किमपि किन्त्वनुभेजे
केवले सदनुलेपनचेले ॥२२॥

*bhūṣaṇasya ca vibhūṣaṇam aṅgaṁ*
*tat kim ebhir iti kāpi varāṅgī |*
*nābhajat kim api kintv anubheje*
*kevale sad-anulepana-cele ||22||*

*Word for word:* *bhūṣaṇasya* — of ornament; *ca* — indeed; *vibhūṣaṇam* — the ornament; *aṅgam* — the body; *tat* — so; *kim* — what [need]; *ebhiḥ* — of these; *iti* — thus [thinking]; *kā api* — a certain; *vara* — beautiful; *aṅgī* — of limb; *na* — not; *abhajat* — put on; *kim api* — anything; *kintu* — but; *anubheje* — accepted; *kevale* — only; *sat* — fine; *anulepana* — unguent; *cele* — [and] a garment.

**22.** "[My] body is itself the ornament of ornaments — so what need have I of these?" Thinking thus, one [maiden], beautiful of limb, put on nothing at all, but accepted only fine unguent and a garment.

### Verse 23

स्पर्शनव्यवधिरेव किमन्य-
न्मा कृथाः सुतनु तत्तनुबाधाम् ।
इत्यदः प्रियसखीवचनान्ते
नानुलेपमपि काचिदियेष ॥२३॥

*sparśana-vyavadhir eva kim anyan*
*mā kṛthāḥ sutanu tat tanu-bādhām |*
*ity adaḥ priya-sakhī-vacanānte*
*nānulepam api kācid iyeṣa ||23||*

*Word for word:* *sparśana* — to touch; *vyavadhiḥ* — a barrier; *eva* — only; *kim* — what; *anyat* — else; *mā kṛthāḥ* — do not cause; *sutanu* — O you of lovely body; *tat* — therefore; *tanu* — to the body; *bādhām* — burden; *iti* — thus; *adaḥ* — these; *priya* — of a dear; *sakhī* — friend; *vacana* — of the words; *ante* — at the end; *na* — not; *anulepam* — unguent; *api* — even; *kācit* — a certain [maiden]; *iyeṣa* — wanted.

**23.** "Unguent is only a barrier to touch — what else is it? So do not burden your body, O lovely one!" When her dear friend had said these words, one did not want even unguent.

### Verse 24

लोचनद्वयरुचैव समीपं
प्राप्तया श्रवणयोरतिशोभा ।
जायते किममुनेति कयाचि-
न्नादधे कुवलयस्य वतंसम् ॥२४॥

*locana-dvaya-rucaiva samīpaṁ*
*prāptayā śravaṇayor atiśobhā |*
*jāyate kim amuneti kayācin*
*nādadhe kuvala[ya]sya vataṁsam ||24||*

*Word for word:* *locana* — of eyes; *dvaya* — of the pair; *rucā* — by the lustre; *eva* — already; *samīpam* — near; *prāptayā* — which has reached; *śravaṇayoḥ* — of the ears; *atiśobhā* — exceeding beauty; *jāyate* — arises; *kim* — what [use]; *amunā* — of this; *iti* — thus [thinking]; *kayācit* — by a certain [maiden]; *na* — not; *ādadhe* — was put on; *kuvalayasya* — of a blue lotus; *vataṁsam* — the ear-ornament.

**24.** "By the very lustre of my two eyes, which reaches close to them, my ears already gain exceeding beauty — what use is this?" Thinking so, one did not put on an ear-ornament of blue lotus.

*Note.* Eyes that "reach to the ears" are a mark of beauty. The edition has *कुवलस्य*, but the metre requires *kuvalayasya* (a syllable has dropped out).

### Verse 25

मुक्तमुक्तमपि कैशिकमेत-
च्छोभते यदपि मुग्धसखीभिः ।
स्वीयशिल्पकलनादिव युक्त्या
बन्धनं तदपि चारु वितेने ॥२५॥

*mukta-muktam api kaiśikam etac*
*chobhate yad api mugdha-sakhībhiḥ |*
*svīya-śilpa-kalanād iva yuktyā*
*bandhanaṁ tad api cāru vitene ||25||*

*Word for word:* *mukta-muktam* — let quite loose; *api* — even; *kaiśikam* — hair; *etat* — this; *śobhate* — is beautiful; *yat api* — although; *mugdha* — by charming; *sakhībhiḥ* — friends; *svīya* — their own; *śilpa* — skill; *kalanāt* — to display; *iva* — as if; *yuktyā* — deftly; *bandhanam* — a coiffure; *tat api* — nevertheless; *cāru* — lovely; *vitene* — was made.

**25.** Although this hair was beautiful even when let quite loose, [her] charming friends, as if to display their own skill, nevertheless deftly arranged it in a lovely coiffure.

### Verse 26

दर्पणस्य खलु दर्पणमेत-
ल्लोच्यतां कथमिति प्रवराङ्गी ।
अङ्गमैक्षत सविभ्रममङ्गे
स्वच्छमच्छतरहाटकगौरे ॥२६॥

*darpaṇasya khalu darpaṇam etal*
*locyatāṁ katham iti pravarāṅgī |*
*aṅgam aikṣata savibhramam aṅge*
*svaccham acchatara-hāṭaka-gaure ||26||*

*Word for word:* *darpaṇasya* — of the mirror; *khalu* — indeed; *darpaṇam* — the mirror; *etat* — this [body]; *locyatām* — is to be looked into; *katham* — how; *iti* — thus [thinking]; *pravara* — most beautiful; *aṅgī* — of limb; *aṅgam* — a limb; *aikṣata* — gazed at; *sa* — with; *vibhramam* — playful grace; *aṅge* — in [another] limb; *svaccham* — clear; *acchatara* — of the purest; *hāṭaka* — gold; *gaure* — fair as.

**26.** "This [body] is indeed the mirror of the mirror — how then is it to be looked into?" Thinking so, one most beautiful of limb playfully gazed at one clear limb [reflected] in another, fair as the purest gold.

### Verse 27

घूर्णितारुणविलोचनभङ्ग्या
सादरं पुलकितो हृदयेशः ।
प्रेयसीविहितवेशविलासं
शश्वदैक्षत निजं सकलाङ्गम् ॥२७॥

*ghūrṇitāruṇa-vilocana-bhaṅgyā*
*sādaraṁ pulakito hṛdayeśaḥ |*
*preyasī-vihita-veśa-vilāsaṁ*
*śaśvad aikṣata nijaṁ sakalāṅgam ||27||*

*Word for word:* *ghūrṇita* — of rolling; *aruṇa* — reddish; *vilocana* — eyes; *bhaṅgyā* — with the play; *sa* — with; *ādaram* — tender care; *pulakitaḥ* — thrilling with joy; *hṛdaya* — of hearts; *īśaḥ* — the lord; *preyasī* — by His beloveds; *vihita* — arranged; *veśa* — of attire; *vilāsam* — [with] the grace; *śaśvat* — again and again; *aikṣata* — gazed at; *nijam* — His own; *sakala* — whole; *aṅgam* — body.

**27.** And the lord of their hearts, thrilling with joy, tenderly, with the play of His rolling, reddish eyes, gazed again and again at His whole body, gracefully attired by His beloveds.

### Verse 28

इत्थमात्तवसनाः कृतभूषा-
स्ता विभूषयितुमासत भूयः ।
चन्द्रमा मधुमदः कुसुमेषुः
के भवन्ति महतां न सहायाः ॥२८॥

*ittham ātta-vasanāḥ kṛta-bhūṣās*
*tā vibhūṣayitum āsata bhūyaḥ |*
*candramā madhu-madaḥ kusumeṣuḥ*
*ke bhavanti mahatāṁ na sahāyāḥ ||28||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *ātta* — having put on; *vasanāḥ* — garments; *kṛta* — having made; *bhūṣāḥ* — adornment; *tāḥ* — them; *vibhūṣayitum* — to adorn; *āsata* — set about; *bhūyaḥ* — still more; *candramāḥ* — the moon; *madhu* — of wine; *madaḥ* — the intoxication; *kusuma* — flower-; *iṣuḥ* — arrowed (Kama); *ke* — who; *bhavanti* — become; *mahatām* — of the great; *na* — not; *sahāyāḥ* — helpers.

**28.** When they had thus put on their garments and adorned themselves, the moon, the intoxication of wine and the Flower-arrowed [god] set about adorning them still more. Who does not become a helper of the great?

### Verse 29

निर्भरः शशिमयूखसमूहो
लोपितद्रुमपुरादिविभागः ।
तूर्णमाविरभवत् कमनीयो
मान्मथः किमपि राजतसर्गः ॥२९॥

*nirbharaḥ śaśi-mayūkha-samūho*
*lopita-druma-purādi-vibhāgaḥ |*
*tūrṇam āvirabhavat kamanīyo*
*mānmathaḥ kim api rājata-sargaḥ ||29||*

*Word for word:* *nirbharaḥ* — dense; *śaśi* — of the moon; *mayūkha* — of rays; *samūhaḥ* — the mass; *lopita* — having blotted out; *druma* — of trees; *pura* — of settlements; *ādi* — and the rest; *vibhāgaḥ* — [whose] boundaries; *tūrṇam* — swiftly; *āvirabhavat* — appeared; *kamanīyaḥ* — charming; *mānmathaḥ* — of Manmatha; *kim api* — some; *rājata* — silver; *sargaḥ* — creation.

**29.** A dense flood of moonbeams, blotting out the boundaries between trees, settlements and all else, swiftly appeared — some charming silver creation of Manmatha.

### Verse 30

चित्तनिर्वृतिकरीः शशिभासो
भासुराः सपदि वीक्ष्य वधूभिः ।
आदधे मनसि मन्मथलक्ष्मी-
रासवेन तदनन्तरमाभिः ॥३०॥

*citta-nirvṛti-karīḥ śaśi-bhāso*
*bhāsurāḥ sapadi vīkṣya vadhūbhiḥ |*
*ādadhe manasi manmatha-lakṣmīr*
*āsavena tad-anantaram ābhiḥ ||30||*

*Word for word:* *citta* — to the heart; *nirvṛti* — delight; *karīḥ* — bringing; *śaśi* — of the moon; *bhāsaḥ* — the beams; *bhāsurāḥ* — bright; *sapadi* — at once; *vīkṣya* — having seen; *vadhūbhiḥ* — by the young women; *ādadhe* — was received; *manasi* — into the heart; *manmatha* — of Manmatha; *lakṣmīḥ* — the splendour; *āsavena* — by wine; *tat-anantaram* — right after that; *ābhiḥ* — by them.

**30.** The young women at once beheld the bright moonbeams that bring delight to the heart, and right after that, through wine, they received the splendour of Manmatha into their hearts.

*Note.* Here begins the scene of the drinking party (*pāna-goṣṭhī*), customary in a mahakavya.

### Verse 31

साधुरीतिरियमेव वधूनां
माधुरीति मधुरो मधुवारः ।
तां पुनः प्रथयति स्म विशेषं
मान्मथैर्नवविकारविभङ्गैः ॥३१॥

*sādhu-rītir iyam eva vadhūnāṁ*
*mādhurīti madhuro madhu-vāraḥ |*
*tāṁ punaḥ prathayati sma viśeṣaṁ*
*mānmathair nava-vikāra-vibhaṅgaiḥ ||31||*

*Word for word:* *sādhu* — finest; *rītiḥ* — quality (manner); *iyam* — this; *eva* — very; *vadhūnām* — of young women; *mādhurī* — sweetness; *iti* — thus [reasoning]; *madhuraḥ* — sweet; *madhu* — of wine; *vāraḥ* — the round (circling cup); *tām* — it; *punaḥ* — moreover; *prathayati sma* — increased; *viśeṣam* — especially; *mānmathaiḥ* — born of Manmatha; *nava* — with new; *vikāra* — changes; *vibhaṅgaiḥ* — [and] graceful turns.

**31.** "This very sweetness is the finest quality of young women!" — [so reasoning], the sweet round of wine increased it all the more with new changes and graceful turns born of Manmatha.

*Note.* The syntax of *iti* and the play on *sādhu-rīti* / *mādhurī* are rendered according to the sense (?). *madhu-vāra* — a round of drinking, the cup passed in turn at a feast. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 32

लोहितोत्पलदलं प्रति खेल-
च्चञ्चरीकघटयेव चिराय ।
अन्वरञ्जि नयनाञ्जनलक्ष्म्या
सुभ्रुवां प्रियमनः स्मरकेण ॥३२॥

*lohitotpala-dalaṁ prati khelac-*
*cañcarīka-ghaṭayeva cirāya |*
*anvarañji nayanāñjana-lakṣmyā*
*subhruvāṁ priya-manaḥ smarakeṇa (?) ||32||*

*Word for word:* *lohita* — of a red; *utpala* — lotus; *dalam prati* — over the petal; *khelat* — playing; *cañcarīka* — of bees; *ghaṭayā* — by a swarm; *iva* — as if; *cirāya* — for long; *anvarañji* — was captivated (coloured); *nayana* — of the eyes; *añjana* — of the collyrium; *lakṣmyā* — by the beauty; *subhruvām* — of the fair-browed; *priya* — of the beloved; *manaḥ* — the heart; *smarakeṇa* (?) — by love.

**32.** The heart of their beloved was long held captive — by love (?) — by the beauty of the collyrium in the eyes of the fair-browed [maidens], as though by a swarm of bees playing over the petal of a red lotus.

*Note.* The eyes, reddened by wine, are the red lotus; the dark pupils and collyrium are the bees. The form *smarakeṇa* is unclear (?); it may perhaps refer to the maidens, "stricken by Smara". The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 33

क्लान्तकान्तरमणीमुखबिम्बैः
पद्मवासित इवासव एषः ।
पातुमाहितरसस्य दृशाभूत्
प्रेयसोऽरुणरुचापि च पीतः ॥३३॥

*klānta-kānta-ramaṇī-mukha-bimbaiḥ*
*padma-vāsita ivāsava eṣaḥ |*
*pātum āhita-rasasya dṛśābhūt*
*preyaso 'ruṇa-rucāpi ca pītaḥ ||33||*

*Word for word:* *klānta* — of the languid; *kānta* — lovely; *ramaṇī* — beauties; *mukha* — of the faces; *bimbaiḥ* — by the reflections; *padma* — with lotuses; *vāsitaḥ* — perfumed; *iva* — as if; *āsavaḥ* — wine; *eṣaḥ* — this; *pātum* — to drink; *āhita* — who had conceived; *rasasya* — a relish; *dṛśā* — by the eye; *abhūt* — was; *preyasaḥ* — of the beloved; *aruṇa* — red; *rucā* — [whose] lustre; *api ca* — even; *pītaḥ* — drunk.

**33.** This wine, [mirroring] the faces of the lovely, languid beauties, was as if perfumed with lotuses. The beloved, who had conceived a relish for drinking it, drank it even with His eye, ruddy in its lustre.

### Verse 34

आययुः किमु परस्परयोगा-
त्सुभ्रुवोऽधरमधूनि मधूनि ।
स्वादुमिष्टमधिकं यदमादी-
त्तन्मुखात् परिपिबन् हृदयेशः ॥३४॥

*āyayuḥ kim u paraspara-yogāt*
*subhruvo 'dhara-madhūni madhūni |*
*svādum iṣṭam adhikaṁ yad amādīt*
*tan-mukhāt paripiban hṛdayeśaḥ ||34||*

*Word for word:* *āyayuḥ* — became; *kim u* — have …?; *paraspara* — mutual; *yogāt* — from contact; *subhruvaḥ* — of the fair-browed one; *adhara* — of the lips; *madhūni* — the honey; *madhūni* — the wines; *svādum* — sweet; *iṣṭam* — cherished; *adhikam* — the more; *yat* — for; *amādīt* — became intoxicated; *tat* — her; *mukhāt* — from the mouth; *paripiban* — drinking deeply; *hṛdaya* — of hearts; *īśaḥ* — the lord.

**34.** Had the wines, through mutual contact, become the honey of the fair-browed one's lips? For the lord of hearts, drinking deeply from her lips the sweet, cherished [draught], became all the more intoxicated.

### Verse 35

यद्वचः श्रवणवर्त्म न यातं
प्रेयसः सपदि सापि नवीना ।
वारुणीमदवशादवदंशं
तत्तदोष्ठमतनिष्ट निकामम् ॥३५॥

*yad vacaḥ śravaṇa-vartma na yātaṁ*
*preyasaḥ sapadi sāpi navīnā |*
*vāruṇī-mada-vaśād avadaṁśaṁ*
*tat tad oṣṭham ataniṣṭa nikāmam ||35||*

*Word for word:* *yat* — what; *vacaḥ* — [in] speech; *śravaṇa* — of hearing; *vartma* — the path; *na* — not; *yātam* — reached; *preyasaḥ* — of the beloved; *sapadi* — at once; *sā* — she; *api* — even; *navīnā* — young; *vāruṇī* — of wine; *mada* — of the intoxication; *vaśāt* — under the sway; *avadaṁśam* — a bite (a relish); *tat tat* — again and again; *oṣṭham* — the lip; *ataniṣṭa* — made; *nikāmam* — to her heart's content.

**35.** What had never reached the path of hearing even in speech, that the young maiden at once did, under the sway of the intoxication of wine: to her heart's content she made her beloved's lip, again and again, a morsel to bite.

*Note.* The edition has *श्रवणवर्त्मनि* ("on the path of hearing"); the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *śravaṇa-vartma na yātam* ("which has not reached the ear", that is, unheard of). We accept the reading with the negative (the metre is unchanged). *avadaṁśa* means "a bite" and also "a relish taken with drink" (cf. *vidaṁśa*, verse 38).

### Verse 36

या शिरीषकुसुमादपि मृद्वी
सौरभं सुखमुवाह सदैव ।
दुःखवन्मदवशादवसादः
कीदृगित्यपि न वेद चिरं सा ॥३६॥

*yā śirīṣa-kusumād api mṛdvī*
*saurabhaṁ [sauratam?] sukham uvāha sadaiva |*
*duḥkhavan mada-vaśād avasādaḥ*
*kīdṛg ity api na veda ciraṁ sā ||36||*

*Word for word:* *yā* — she who; *śirīṣa* — of the *śirīṣa*; *kusumāt* — than the flower; *api* — even; *mṛdvī* — more delicate; *saurabham* — fragrance (or *sauratam* — [the bliss] of love's play?); *sukham* — happiness; *uvāha* — bore; *sadā eva* — always; *duḥkhavat* — painful; *mada* — of intoxication; *vaśāt* — from the sway; *avasādaḥ* — exhaustion; *kīdṛk* — what kind; *iti* — this; *api* — even; *na* — not; *veda* — knew; *ciram* — for long; *sā* — she.

**36.** She who is more delicate even than a *śirīṣa* flower, and who had always known only fragrance and happiness, for long did not even know what the painful exhaustion that comes under the sway of intoxication is like.

*Note.* Perhaps *sauratam* ("[the happiness] of love's play") should be read in place of *saurabham* (?). The *śirīṣa* flower is the standard of delicacy. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 37

वारुणीमभिगतो द्रवभावं
मन्मथः प्रविशतीव वधूषु ।
अङ्गमङ्गमभितः किल सर्व-
ग्रन्थयः शिथिलतां यदुपेयुः ॥३७॥

*vāruṇīm abhigato drava-bhāvaṁ*
*manmathaḥ praviśatīva vadhūṣu |*
*aṅgam aṅgam abhitaḥ kila sarva-*
*granthayaḥ śithilatāṁ yad upeyuḥ ||37||*

*Word for word:* *vāruṇīm* — [as] wine; *abhigataḥ* — having assumed; *drava* — liquid; *bhāvam* — form; *manmathaḥ* — Manmatha; *praviśati* — enters; *iva* — as if; *vadhūṣu* — into the young women; *aṅgam aṅgam abhitaḥ* — in every limb; *kila* — indeed; *sarva* — all; *granthayaḥ* — the knots (joints); *śithilatām* — slackness; *yat* — since; *upeyuḥ* — attained.

**37.** Manmatha, assuming the liquid form of wine, seemed himself to enter into the young women: for in every limb all the knots grew slack.

*Note.* *granthi* means both "joint" and "knot" (of a girdle or garment).

### Verse 38

दत्तमात्ममुखतो मधु भूयः
किं जिघृक्षुरभिपीड्य रदाग्रैः ।
भर्तुरोष्ठदलदंशपरापि
प्रेयसी रचयतीव विदंशम् ॥३८॥

*dattam ātma-mukhato madhu bhūyaḥ*
*kiṁ jighṛkṣur abhipīḍya radāgraiḥ |*
*bhartur oṣṭha-dala-daṁśa-parāpi*
*preyasī racayatīva vidaṁśam ||38||*

*Word for word:* *dattam* — given; *ātma* — her own; *mukhataḥ* — from the mouth; *madhu* — wine; *bhūyaḥ* — back; *kim* — as if; *jighṛkṣuḥ* — wishing to take; *abhipīḍya* — pressing; *rada* — of the teeth; *agraiḥ* — with the tips; *bhartuḥ* — of her lord; *oṣṭha* — of the lip; *dala* — the petal; *daṁśa* — on biting; *parā* — intent; *api* — and; *preyasī* — the beloved; *racayati* — prepares; *iva* — as if; *vidaṁśam* — a relish (a bite).

**38.** The beloved, as though wishing to take back the wine she had given from her own mouth, pressed the petal of her lord's lip with the tips of her teeth; intent on biting it, she seemed to be preparing a relish [to go with the wine].

*Note.* A pun: *vidaṁśa* is both "a relish taken with wine" and "a bite".

### Verse 39

वारुणीमदवशादवशाङ्गी
भ्रश्यदप्यभिविवेद न वासः ।
पाणिरेव तदरुद्ध नितान्त-
न्यासतः किल तदेव विचित्रम् ॥३९॥

*vāruṇī-mada-vaśād avaśāṅgī*
*bhraśyad apy abhiviveda na vāsaḥ |*
*pāṇir eva tad aruddha nitānta-*
*nyāsataḥ kila tad eva vicitram ||39||*

*Word for word:* *vāruṇī* — of wine; *mada* — of the intoxication; *vaśāt* — from the sway; *avaśa* — powerless; *aṅgī* — [with] limbs; *bhraśyat* — slipping; *api* — even; *abhiviveda* — noticed; *na* — not; *vāsaḥ* — the garment; *pāṇiḥ* — the hand; *eva* — by itself; *tat* — it; *aruddha* — held back; *nitānta* — constant; *nyāsataḥ* — from practice; *kila* — truly; *tat eva* — that very thing; *vicitram* — the wonder.

**39.** One [maiden], her limbs powerless from the intoxication of wine, did not even notice her garment slipping; her hand held it back by itself, from long habit — that indeed was the wonder!

### Verse 40

एकमस्ति मनसीतरदुक्तं
तत्र च प्रतिपदं स्खलनं हि ।
ईहितं किमपि वाञ्छितमन्य-
त्किं प्रमाद इव भाति मदोऽयम् ॥४०॥

*ekam asti manasītarad uktaṁ*
*tatra ca pratipadaṁ skhalanaṁ hi |*
*īhitaṁ kim api vāñchitam anyat*
*kiṁ pramāda iva bhāti mado 'yam ||40||*

*Word for word:* *ekam* — one thing; *asti* — is; *manasi* — in the mind; *itarat* — another; *uktam* — is said; *tatra* — in it; *ca* — and; *pratipadam* — at every word; *skhalanam* — a stumbling; *hi* — indeed; *īhitam* — is undertaken; *kim api* — one thing; *vāñchitam* — is desired; *anyat* — another; *kim* — does not …?; *pramādaḥ* — madness; *iva* — like; *bhāti* — appear; *madaḥ* — intoxication; *ayam* — this.

**40.** One thing is in the mind, another is said, and at every word there is a stumbling; one thing is undertaken, another is desired — does not this intoxication seem like madness?

### Verse 41

अर्धमर्धमिव भाषितमासा-
मर्धमर्धमिव चेष्टितमस्य ।
सुभ्रुवां हृदयलोपविधाने
मन्मथः किमसृजन्मधुवारम् ॥४१॥

*ardham ardham iva bhāṣitam āsām*
*ardham ardham iva ceṣṭitam asya |*
*subhruvāṁ hṛdaya-lopa-vidhāne*
*manmathaḥ kim asṛjan madhu-vāram ||41||*

*Word for word:* *ardham ardham* — half and half; *iva* — as it were; *bhāṣitam* — the speech; *āsām* — their; *ardham ardham* — half and half; *iva* — as it were; *ceṣṭitam* — the movements; *asya* — His; *subhruvām* — of the fair-browed; *hṛdaya* — of the hearts; *lopa* — the stealing; *vidhāne* — for accomplishing; *manmathaḥ* — Manmatha; *kim* — whether; *asṛjat* — created; *madhu* — of wine; *vāram* — the round.

**41.** Their speech came as if in halves and halves; His movements came as if in halves and halves. Was it to steal the hearts of the fair-browed [maidens] that Manmatha created the round of wine?

### Verse 42

उज्जगाम हृदयादनुरागो
लोचने मधुमदारुणशोभे ।
सुभ्रुवः किमिह यद्भरभारा-
द्घूर्णया भ्रमति खञ्जमिवैतत् ॥४२॥

*ujjagāma hṛdayād anurāgo*
*locane madhu-madāruṇa-śobhe |*
*subhruvaḥ kim iha yad-bhara-bhārād*
*ghūrṇayā bhramati khañjam ivaitat ||42||*

*Word for word:* *ujjagāma* — rose; *hṛdayāt* — from the heart; *anurāgaḥ* — love (redness); *locane* — into the eyes; *madhu* — of wine; *mada* — from the intoxication; *aruṇa* — red; *śobhe* — [with] beauty; *subhruvaḥ* — of the fair-browed one; *kim* — whether; *iha* — here; *yat* — of which; *bhara* — of the weight; *bhārāt* — from the burden; *ghūrṇayā* — with giddiness; *bhramati* — roam; *khañjam iva* — like wagtails; *etat* — they.

**42.** Did love rise from the heart of the fair-browed one into her eyes, beautiful with the redness of wine's intoxication? For under the burden of its weight they roam about here giddily, like wagtails.

*Note.* *Anurāga* means both "love" and "redness". *Khañja* usually means "lame"; *khañjam* here is evidently a shortened *khañjana*, the wagtail, a usual comparison for restless eyes. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 43

दष्टवत्यभिमते दयितोष्ठं
रञ्जितत्वमगमन् दशनान्ताः ।
स्वच्छतामवकलय्य नु गच्छन्
यावकः स्थितिमियेष तदेषु ॥४३॥

*daṣṭavaty abhimate dayitoṣṭhaṁ*
*rañjitatvam agaman daśanāntāḥ |*
*svacchatām avakalayya nu gacchan*
*yāvakaḥ sthitim iyeṣa tad eṣu ||43||*

*Word for word:* *daṣṭavati* — when [she] had bitten; *abhimate* — the beloved [maiden]; *dayita* — of the dear one; *oṣṭham* — the lip; *rañjitatvam* — colour; *agaman* — took on; *daśana* — of the teeth; *antāḥ* — the tips; *svacchatām* — the purity; *avakalayya* — having perceived; *nu* — as it seems; *gacchan* — departing; *yāvakaḥ* — the lac; *sthitim* — a dwelling; *iyeṣa* — desired; *tat* — therefore; *eṣu* — in them.

**43.** When the beloved [maiden] bit her dear one's lip, the tips of her teeth took on colour. Was it, it seems, that the lac, as it departed [from the lip], perceived their purity and therefore desired to dwell in them?

### Verse 44

चुम्बति प्रियतमेऽक्षि मृगाक्ष्याः
पानपाटलितमञ्जनहीनम् ।
तत्तदोष्ठरुचिभिर्घनघूर्णा
पक्ष्मराजिमनुरञ्जयतीव ॥४४॥

*cumbati priyatame 'kṣi mṛgākṣyāḥ*
*pāna-pāṭalitam añjana-hīnam |*
*tat-tad-oṣṭha-rucibhir ghana-ghūrṇā*
*pakṣma-rājim anurañjayatīva ||44||*

*Word for word:* *cumbati* — when [He] kissed; *priyatame* — the dearest one; *akṣi* — the eye; *mṛga* — like a doe's; *akṣyāḥ* — of [the maiden with] eyes; *pāna* — from drinking; *pāṭalitam* — rosy; *añjana* — of collyrium; *hīnam* — bereft; *tat-tat* — of His; *oṣṭha* — of the lips; *rucibhiḥ* — with the lustre; *ghana* — deeply; *ghūrṇā* — reeling; *pakṣma* — of the lashes; *rājim* — the row; *anurañjayati* — colours; *iva* — as it were.

**44.** When the dearest one kissed the doe-eyed [maiden's] eye, rosy from drinking and bereft of collyrium, she, deeply reeling, as it were coloured the row of her lashes with the lustre of His lips.

*Note.* The agreement of *ghana-ghūrṇā* (feminine) is unclear; we refer it to the gopi. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 45

दष्टवत्यतितरां दशनाग्रै-
र्वल्लभे मधुमदादधरौष्ठम् ।
मन्दकण्ठनिनदैः कलकण्ठ्यः
कोमलं करुणमेव चुकूजुः ॥४५॥

*daṣṭavaty atitarāṁ daśanāgrair*
*vallabhe madhu-madād adharauṣṭham |*
*manda-kaṇṭha-ninadaiḥ kala-kaṇṭhyaḥ*
*komalaṁ karuṇam eva cukūjuḥ ||45||*

*Word for word:* *daṣṭavati* — when [He] had bitten; *atitarām* — hard; *daśana* — of the teeth; *agraiḥ* — with the tips; *vallabhe* — the dear one; *madhu* — of wine; *madāt* — from the intoxication; *adhara-oṣṭham* — the lower lip; *manda* — with low; *kaṇṭha* — of the throat; *ninadaiḥ* — sounds; *kala* — sweet-; *kaṇṭhyaḥ* — voiced [maidens]; *komalam* — softly; *karuṇam* — plaintively; *eva* — indeed; *cukūjuḥ* — cooed.

**45.** When the dear one, from the intoxication of wine, bit their lower lips hard with the tips of His teeth, the sweet-voiced [maidens] cooed softly and plaintively indeed, with low sounds of the throat.

*Note.* Cf. the description of the sounds of love (*maṇita*) in the *kāma-śāstra*.

### Verse 46

ओष्ठपल्लवपुटं दयिताया
दष्टवत्यतितरां मधुमर्दे ।
पाणिपल्लवमपि प्रचकम्पे
सख्यमेकसुखदुःखगमेव ॥४६॥

*oṣṭha-pallava-puṭaṁ dayitāyā*
*daṣṭavaty atitarāṁ madhu-marde |*
*pāṇi-pallavam api pracakampe*
*sakhyam eka-sukha-duḥkha-gam eva ||46||*

*Word for word:* *oṣṭha* — of the lips; *pallava* — of the shoot; *puṭam* — the cup; *dayitāyāḥ* — of the beloved; *daṣṭavati* — when [He] had bitten; *atitarām* — hard; *madhu* — of Madhu; *marde* — the Crusher; *pāṇi* — of the hand; *pallavam* — the shoot; *api* — too; *pracakampe* — trembled; *sakhyam* — friendship; *eka* — one [and the same]; *sukha* — joy; *duḥkha* — [and] sorrow; *gam* — sharing; *eva* — indeed.

**46.** When the Crusher of Madhu bit hard the cup of His beloved's shoot-like lips, the shoot of her hand trembled too: for friendship indeed shares one joy and one sorrow.

*Note.* Lips and hands are both "shoots" (*pallava*), and hence "friends".

### Verse 47

धुन्वती करदले स्मितभाषा
शीत्कृतैरविरतोत्सवमेका ।
लोलशङ्खवलयध्वनिलक्ष्यं
मन्दमन्दमिव शङ्खमपूरि ॥४७॥

*dhunvatī kara-dale smita-bhāṣā*
*śītkṛtair avirata-utsavam ekā |*
*lola-śaṅkha-valaya-dhvani-lakṣyaṁ*
*manda-mandam iva śaṅkham apūri ||47||*

*Word for word:* *dhunvatī* — shaking; *kara* — of the hands; *dale* — the petals; *smita* — with a smile; *bhāṣā* — speaking; *śītkṛtaiḥ* — with hisses of "śīt"; *avirata* — unceasing; *utsavam* — a festival; *ekā* — one [maiden]; *lola* — swaying; *śaṅkha* — of conch-shell; *valaya* — of the bangles; *dhvani* — by the sound; *lakṣyam* — marked; *manda-mandam* — very softly; *iva* — as it were; *śaṅkham* — a conch; *apūri* — was filled (was sounded).

**47.** One [maiden], shaking the petals of her hands, speaking with a smile, made of her hissing breaths an unceasing festival; and in the sound of her swaying conch-shell bangles it was as if a conch were being sounded very softly.

*Note.* The sound of the conch (*śaṅkha*) accompanies festivals and rites.

### Verse 48

गण्डयुग्ममलिकं किमु किंवा
लोचने किमधरः किमु वान्यत् ।
चुम्बनेन रमणो रमणीनां
भिन्नभिन्नरसपूर्णमबुद्ध ॥४८॥

*gaṇḍa-yugmam alikaṁ kim u kiṁ vā*
*locane kim adharaḥ kim u vānyat |*
*cumbanena ramaṇo ramaṇīnāṁ*
*bhinna-bhinna-rasa-pūrṇam abuddha ||48||*

*Word for word:* *gaṇḍa* — of the cheeks; *yugmam* — the pair; *alikam* — the forehead; *kim u kiṁ vā* — or else; *locane* — the eyes; *kim* — or; *adharaḥ* — the lip; *kim u vā* — or; *anyat* — something else; *cumbanena* — by kissing; *ramaṇaḥ* — the dear one; *ramaṇīnām* — of the lovely women; *bhinna-bhinna* — each different; *rasa* — with taste; *pūrṇam* — full; *abuddha* — found.

**48.** The cheeks, the forehead, or the eyes, or the lip, or whatever else of the lovely women — kissing them, the dear one found each full of a different taste.

### Verse 49

केशपाशवलनादवतीर्णः
सङ्गतः स्तनमतङ्गजकुम्भे ।
घूर्णया मदजया प्रियपाणि-
र्निर्ममज्ज तदुरःसरसीषु ॥४९॥

*keśa-pāśa-valanād avatīrṇaḥ*
*saṅgataḥ stana-mataṅgaja-kumbhe |*
*ghūrṇayā madajayā priya-pāṇir*
*nirmamajja tad-uraḥ-sarasīṣu ||49||*

*Word for word:* *keśa* — of hair; *pāśa* — from the braids; *valanāt* — from twining; *avatīrṇaḥ* — having descended; *saṅgataḥ* — having met; *stana* — of the breasts; *mataṅgaja* — of the elephant; *kumbhe* — with the frontal globe; *ghūrṇayā* — with a giddiness; *madajayā* — born of intoxication (of an elephant's must); *priya* — of the dear one; *pāṇiḥ* — the hand; *nirmamajja* — plunged; *tat* — their; *uraḥ* — of the bosoms; *sarasīṣu* — into the lakes.

**49.** The dear one's hand, descending from twining their braided hair, met the elephant's frontal globes — their bosoms — and, reeling with a giddiness born of intoxication, plunged into the lakes of their bosoms.

*Note.* An image of the elephant: the bosom is likened to the frontal globes on an elephant's forehead, and *mada* means both "intoxication" and an elephant's must. An elephant in must plunges into a lake.

### Verse 50

अन्तरीयमवकृष्य किमु स्वं
भावमाशु विदधे वसनं सः ।
लोहितौ कुचघटावनुरक्तौ
यच्चकार हृदयेशय एषः ॥५०॥

*antarīyam avakṛṣya kim u svaṁ*
*bhāvam āśu vidadhe vasanaṁ saḥ |*
*lohitau kuca-ghaṭāv anuraktau*
*yac cakāra hṛdayeśaya eṣaḥ ||50||*

*Word for word:* *antarīyam* — the covering garment; *avakṛṣya* — having drawn away; *kim u* — whether; *svam* — His own; *bhāvam* — feeling; *āśu* — at once; *vidadhe* — made; *vasanam* — the garment; *saḥ* — He; *lohitau* — red; *kuca* — of the breasts; *ghaṭau* — the jars; *anuraktau* — loving (reddened); *yat* — since; *cakāra* — made; *hṛdaye-śayaḥ* — He who lies in the heart; *eṣaḥ* — this.

**50.** Having drawn away the covering garment, did He at once make His own feeling [their] garment? For He who lies in the heart made the red jars of their bosoms glow with love.

*Note.* *Hṛdayeśaya* ("lying in the heart") is an epithet of Kama, here applied to Krishna. *Anurakta* means both "loving" and "reddened".

### Verse 51

अर्धमिलितमथार्धनिमग्नं
भाषितं ननननेति वदन्त्या ।
मुग्धया बत गुरो रतशिक्षा-
दक्षिणेव विदधे करकम्पः ॥५१॥

*ardha-militam athārdha-nimagnaṁ*
*bhāṣitaṁ na-na-na-neti vadantyā |*
*mugdhayā bata guro rata-śikṣā-*
*dakṣiṇeva vidadhe kara-kampaḥ ||51||*

*Word for word:* *ardha* — half; *militam* — uttered; *atha* — and; *ardha* — half; *nimagnam* — swallowed; *bhāṣitam* — speech; *na-na-na-na* — "no-no-no-no"; *iti* — thus; *vadantyā* — saying; *mugdhayā* — by the artless [maiden]; *bata* — ah; *guroḥ* — to the teacher; *rata* — of love; *śikṣā* — for the instruction; *dakṣiṇā* — the fee; *iva* — as if; *vidadhe* — was made; *kara* — of the hands; *kampaḥ* — a trembling.

**51.** An artless [maiden], saying "No-no-no-no…" in speech half uttered and half swallowed, trembled with her hands — ah, as if paying her teacher the fee for lessons in love.

*Note.* *Dakṣiṇā* is the fee given to the teacher at the end of study. The edition prints *गुरोरतशिक्षा*; we read *guro rata-śikṣā-*.

### Verse 52

माधवस्य करपल्लवसङ्गा-
दाससाद पुलकं कुचयुग्मम् ।
कन्दुकीकृतममन्दकदम्ब-
द्वन्द्वमुत्क्षिपति किं कुसुमेषुः ॥५२॥

*mādhavasya kara-pallava-saṅgād*
*āsasāda pulakaṁ kuca-yugmam |*
*kandukīkṛtam amanda-kadamba-*
*dvandvam utkṣipati kiṁ kusumeṣuḥ ||52||*

*Word for word:* *mādhavasya* — of Madhava; *kara* — of the hand; *pallava* — of the shoot; *saṅgāt* — from the touch; *āsasāda* — attained; *pulakam* — a thrill (bristling of the hair); *kuca* — of the breasts; *yugmam* — the pair; *kandukīkṛtam* — made into balls; *amanda* — full; *kadamba* — of kadamba flowers; *dvandvam* — a pair; *utkṣipati* — tosses up; *kim* — whether; *kusuma* — flower-; *iṣuḥ* — arrowed (Kama).

**52.** At the touch of Madhava's shoot-like hand her bosom thrilled, its hair standing on end: was the Flower-arrowed [god] tossing up a pair of full kadamba blossoms as balls?

*Note.* The round kadamba flower, covered with bristling filaments, is a usual comparison for a body on which the hair stands on end (*pulaka*).

### Verse 53

नैव नैतदरविन्दयुगं त-
त्किं विमुग्ध नखमत्र ददासि ।
इत्यमुं त्रुटितमौक्तिकहार-
द्योतितं कुचयुगं हसतीव ॥५३॥

*naiva naitad aravinda-yugaṁ tat*
*kiṁ vimugdha nakham atra dadāsi |*
*ity amuṁ truṭita-mauktika-hāra-*
*dyotitaṁ kuca-yugaṁ hasatīva ||53||*

*Word for word:* *na eva na* — not at all; *etat* — this; *aravinda* — of lotuses; *yugam* — a pair; *tat* — so; *kim* — why; *vimugdha* — O bewildered One; *nakham* — a nail; *atra* — here; *dadāsi* — You set; *iti* — thus; *amum* — at Him; *truṭita* — of a broken; *mauktika* — pearl; *hāra* — of the necklace; *dyotitam* — lit up; *kuca* — of the breasts; *yugam* — the pair; *hasati* — laughs; *iva* — as it were.

**53.** "This is not, not at all, a pair of lotuses — so why, O bewildered One, do You set Your nail here?" — thus, lit up by the pearls of a broken necklace, her bosom, as it were, laughed at Him.

*Note.* In kavya laughter is conceived as white; hence the pearls are its laughter.

### Verse 54

सौरतोत्सवविधेः कुसुमेषो-
र्मुख्यतः फलकरीव किमर्चा ।
मङ्गलं कनककुम्भमभीशो
यत्तमेवमभिवाहयति स्म ॥५४॥

*saurata-utsava-vidheḥ kusumeṣor*
*mukhyataḥ phala-karīva kim arcā |*
*maṅgalaṁ kanaka-kumbham abhīśo*
*yat tam evam abhivāhayati sma ||54||*

*Word for word:* *saurata* — of love's play; *utsava* — of the festival; *vidheḥ* — of the rite; *kusumeṣoḥ* — of the Flower-arrowed [god] (Kama); *mukhyataḥ* — first of all; *phala* — fruit; *karī* — bringing; *iva* — as it were; *kim* — whether; *arcā* — worship; *maṅgalam* — auspicious; *kanaka* — golden; *kumbham* — jar; *abhīśaḥ* — the Lord; *yat* — since; *tam* — it; *evam* — thus; *abhivāhayati sma* — had brought.

**54.** Is this not, as it were, the worship that first of all bears fruit in the festive rite of love's play of the Flower-arrowed [god]? For thus the Lord had the auspicious golden jar brought [to Him].

*Note.* A full golden jar (*maṅgala-kalaśa*) is an indispensable article of a rite; here it is the gopi's bosom. The sense of the verse is rendered approximately (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 55

साधु साधुरयमेव जिताः स्मो
निश्चितं शशिमुखि प्रतिजाने ।
इत्यसौ किमलिखज्जयलेखां
प्रेयसीकुचयुगे स्वकरेण ॥५५॥

*sādhu sādhur ayam eva jitāḥ smo*
*niścitaṁ śaśi-mukhi pratijāne |*
*ity asau kim alikhaj jaya-lekhāṁ*
*preyasī-kuca-yuge sva-kareṇa ||55||*

*Word for word:* *sādhu sādhuḥ* — well done, well done; *ayam eva* — this is it; *jitāḥ smaḥ* — We are defeated; *niścitam* — surely; *śaśi* — moon-; *mukhi* — O faced one; *pratijāne* — I admit; *iti* — thus [saying]; *asau* — He; *kim* — whether; *alikhat* — wrote; *jaya* — of victory; *lekhām* — a charter; *preyasī* — of the beloved; *kuca* — of the breasts; *yuge* — on the pair; *sva* — with His own; *kareṇa* — hand.

**55.** "Well done, well done! This is it — We are defeated, O moon-faced one; I surely admit it!" Was it thus [saying] that He wrote with His own hand a charter of victory on His beloved's bosom?

*Note.* The marks of the nails are the letters of the charter. *Jitāḥ smaḥ* means "we are defeated".

### Verse 56

कान्तवक्षसि निविष्टमुरोज-
द्वन्द्वमेव सुदृशः परिरम्भे ।
यद्द्रुतं हृदयमीक्षणरन्ध्रै-
रुच्छलद्बहिरभूत् सह घर्मैः ॥५६॥

*kānta-vakṣasi niviṣṭam uroja-*
*dvandvam eva sudṛśaḥ parirambhe |*
*yad drutaṁ hṛdayam īkṣaṇa-randhrair*
*ucchalad bahir abhūt saha gharmaiḥ ||56||*

*Word for word:* *kānta* — of the beloved; *vakṣasi* — into the chest; *niviṣṭam* — entered; *uroja* — of the breasts; *dvandvam* — the pair; *eva* — only; *sudṛśaḥ* — of the fair-eyed one; *parirambhe* — in the embrace; *yat* — for; *drutam* — melted; *hṛdayam* — the heart; *īkṣaṇa* — of the eyes; *randhraiḥ* — through the windows; *ucchalat* — welling up; *bahiḥ* — outside; *abhūt* — came; *saha* — together; *gharmaiḥ* — with perspiration.

**56.** In the embrace, only the fair-eyed one's bosom entered her beloved's chest: for her heart, melted, came welling out through the windows of her eyes together with perspiration.

### Verse 57

ऊरुमूलमभितः कृतवासा
श्लिष्यति प्रियतमे मदिराक्ष्याः ।
अंशुकेन सह विश्लथबन्धा
निर्ययौ स्वयमथो किमु लज्जा ॥५७॥

*ūru-mūlam abhitaḥ kṛta-vāsā*
*śliṣyati priyatame madirākṣyāḥ |*
*aṁśukena saha viślatha-bandhā*
*niryayau svayam atho kim u lajjā ||57||*

*Word for word:* *ūru* — of the thighs; *mūlam abhitaḥ* — about the base; *kṛta* — who had made; *vāsā* — [its] dwelling; *śliṣyati* — when [He] embraced; *priyatame* — the dearest one; *madira* — intoxicating; *akṣyāḥ* — of [the maiden with] eyes; *aṁśukena* — the garment; *saha* — together with; *viślatha* — loosened; *bandhā* — [whose] knot; *niryayau* — departed; *svayam* — of itself; *atho* — then; *kim u* — whether; *lajjā* — Shame.

**57.** When the dearest one embraced the [maiden] with intoxicating eyes, did Shame, who had made its dwelling about the base of her thighs, then depart of its own accord, together with the garment whose knot had loosened?

### Verse 58

मन्मथद्विरदपुङ्गवसङ्ग-
स्तत्समाकलनशृङ्खलयेव ।
अंशुके वियति तत्र नितम्बः
केवलं रसनयैव रराज ॥५८॥

*manmatha-dvirada-puṅgava-saṅgas*
*tat-samākalana-śṛṅkhalayeva |*
*aṁśuke viyati tatra nitambaḥ*
*kevalaṁ rasanayaiva rarāja ||58||*

*Word for word:* *manmatha* — of Manmatha; *dvirada* — of the elephant; *puṅgava* — of the lordly; *saṅgaḥ* — the meeting-place; *tat* — of it; *samākalana* — for the capture; *śṛṅkhalayā* — with a chain; *iva* — as if; *aṁśuke* — when the garment; *viyati* — was going away; *tatra* — there; *nitambaḥ* — the hips; *kevalam* — only; *rasanayā* — with the girdle; *eva* — alone; *rarāja* — shone.

**58.** As the garment slipped away, her hips — the meeting-place of Manmatha's lordly elephant — shone there with the girdle alone, as if with a chain for capturing it.

### Verse 59

प्रस्खलन् कुचघटाद्वलिवीचि-
विभ्रमैरित इतः परिभूतः ।
नाभिकूपमभिनिर्भरमग्नो
निर्वृतः कथमभूत् प्रियपाणिः ॥५९॥

*praskhalan kuca-ghaṭād vali-vīci-*
*vibhramair ita itaḥ paribhūtaḥ |*
*nābhi-kūpam abhinirbhara-magno*
*nirvṛtaḥ katham abhūt priya-pāṇiḥ ||59||*

*Word for word:* *praskhalan* — slipping; *kuca* — of the breasts; *ghaṭāt* — from the jar; *vali* — of the folds; *vīci* — of the waves; *vibhramaiḥ* — by the play; *itaḥ itaḥ* — this way and that; *paribhūtaḥ* — tossed; *nābhi* — of the navel; *kūpam abhi* — into the well; *nirbhara* — deeply; *magnaḥ* — sunk; *nirvṛtaḥ* — at rest; *katham* — how; *abhūt* — could be; *priya* — of the dear one; *pāṇiḥ* — the hand.

**59.** Slipping from the jars of her bosom, tossed this way and that by the play of the waves of her folds, sunk deep into the well of her navel — how could the dear one's hand be at rest?

*Note.* *Vali* — the three folds of the waist (*trivali*), a mark of beauty.

### Verse 60

अन्तरीयविगमादलसाङ्गी
लोचने झटिति सा निमिमील ।
मन्यते निरसनेन गता ह्री-
र्लोचने बहुरुषेव रुरोध ॥६०॥

*antarīya-vigamād alasāṅgī*
*locane jhaṭiti sā nimimīla |*
*manyate nirasanena gatā hrīr*
*locane bahu-ruṣeva rurodha ||60||*

*Word for word:* *antarīya* — of the covering garment; *vigamāt* — from the departure; *alasa* — languid; *aṅgī* — in body; *locane* — the eyes; *jhaṭiti* — at once; *sā* — she; *nimimīla* — closed; *manyate* — it seems; *nirasanena* — by being driven out; *gatā* — departed; *hrīḥ* — Shame; *locane* — the eyes; *bahu* — in great; *ruṣā* — anger; *iva* — as if; *rurodha* — blocked.

**60.** When the covering garment fell away, the languid [maiden] at once closed her eyes. It seems that Shame, driven out and departed, blocked her eyes as if in great anger.

### Verse 61

मुष्टिना यदवलग्नमधासी-

आमृशन्नित इतः सनितम्बं
निर्जगाम न पुनः प्रियपाणिः ॥६१॥

*muṣṭinā yad avalagnam adhāsīt*
*tena yo 'tra suciraṁ prajagalbhe |*
*āmṛśann ita itaḥ sanitambaṁ*
*nirjagāma na punaḥ priya-pāṇiḥ ||61||*

*Word for word:* *muṣṭinā* — in the fist; *yat* — since; *avalagnam* — the waist; *adhāsīt* — [it] held; *tena* — therefore; *yaḥ* — which; *atra* — here; *suciram* — for a long time; *prajagalbhe* — grew bold; *āmṛśan* — caressing; *itaḥ itaḥ* — here and there; *sa* — together with; *nitambam* — the hips; *nirjagāma* — departed; *na* — not; *punaḥ* — again; *priya* — of the dear one; *pāṇiḥ* — the hand.

**61.** Because the dear one's hand had held her waist in its fist, it grew bold there for a long time; caressing [it] here and there, together with her hips, it did not leave again.

*Note.* A waist that can be encircled by the fist is a mark of beauty.

### Verse 62

उन्नमय्य चिबुकं मधुरोष्ठीं

सा बबन्ध तमथो भुजपाशैः
किं रुजा किमु रुषा नु मुदा किम् ॥६२॥

*unnamayya cibukaṁ madhuroṣṭhīṁ*
*nirbharaṁ dhayati gokula-nāthe |*
*sā babandha tam atho bhuja-pāśaiḥ*
*kiṁ rujā kim u ruṣā nu mudā kim ||62||*

*Word for word:* *unnamayya* — having raised; *cibukam* — the chin; *madhura* — sweet-; *oṣṭhīm* — lipped [maiden]; *nirbharam* — deeply; *dhayati* — when [He] drank; *gokula* — of Gokula; *nāthe* — the Lord; *sā* — she; *babandha* — bound; *tam* — Him; *atho* — then; *bhuja* — of the arms; *pāśaiḥ* — with the nooses; *kim* — whether; *rujā* — from pain; *kim u* — or; *ruṣā* — from anger; *nu* — or; *mudā* — from joy; *kim* — whether.

**62.** When the Lord of Gokula, raising the chin of the sweet-lipped [maiden], drank deeply [of her lips], she then bound Him with the nooses of her arms — from pain? or from anger? or from joy?

### Verse 63

कोमलस्य कुसुमादपि दोष्णः
पीडनं दृढमिदं च सुखाय ।
हन्त ही तदपि चक्षुरुदस्रं
वाम एव मदनः सुरतेऽपि ॥६३॥

*komalasya kusumād api doṣṇaḥ*
*pīḍanaṁ dṛḍham idaṁ ca sukhāya |*

*Word for word:* *komalasya* — tender; *kusumāt* — than a flower; *api* — even; *doṣṇaḥ* — of the arm; *pīḍanam* — the pressing; *dṛḍham* — firm; *idam* — this; *ca* — and; *sukhāya* — for joy; *hanta hī* — ah, alas; *tat api* — even so; *cakṣuḥ* — the eye; *udasram* — full of tears; *vāmaḥ* — wayward; *eva* — indeed; *madanaḥ* — Madana; *surate* — in love's play; *api* — even.

**63.** This firm pressing of an arm more tender even than a flower is also for joy; and yet — ah, alas! — her eyes are full of tears: Madana is wayward indeed, even in love's play!

### Verse 64

निर्भरं रतमदो व्रजनाथो

आश्रयाश्रयवतोः किमु साम्या-
ज्जातमत्र रसनैव रसज्ञा ॥६४॥

*nirbharaṁ rata-mado vraja-nātho*
*yat papāta sahasaiva nitambāt |*
*āśrayāśrayavatoḥ kim u sāmyāj*
*jātam atra rasanaiva rasajñā ||64||*

*Word for word:* *nirbharam* — deeply; *rata* — with love; *madaḥ* — intoxicated; *vraja* — of Vraja; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *yat* — when; *papāta* — fell; *sahasā* — suddenly; *eva* — indeed; *nitambāt* — from the hips; *āśraya* — of the support; *āśrayavatoḥ* — [and] of the supported; *kim u* — whether; *sāmyāt* — from the sameness; *jātam* — became; *atra* — here; *rasanā* — the girdle; *eva* — itself; *rasajñā* — a tongue (a knower of taste).

**64.** When the Lord of Vraja, deeply intoxicated with love, suddenly slipped from her hips, the girdle there itself became a "tongue" — was it from the sameness of the support and the supported?

*Note.* A play on words: *rasanā* is both "girdle" and "tongue", and *rasajñā* is "tongue" (literally "knower of taste"). The girdle jingled, as if it had begun to speak. The sense of "the sameness of the support and the supported" (the hips and Krishna, or the hips and the girdle) is unclear (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 65

बाधिते निधुवने प्रमदानां

*Word for word:* *bādhite* — when hindered [by weariness]; *nidhuvane* — love's play; *pramadānām* — of the young women; *kāmaḥ* — Kama; *eva* — himself; *khalu* — truly; *kāma-daḥ* — a granter of desires; *eṣaḥ* — this; *vyatyayam* — an exchange [of roles]; *yat* — that; *akarot* — made; *atha* — then; *rādhā-kṛṣṇayoḥ* — of Radha and Krishna; *ati* — most; *vicitram* — wondrous; *idam tat* — this.

**65.** When the love's play of the young women was hindered [by weariness], Kama himself truly proved a granter of desires: that he then exchanged the roles of Radha and Krishna — this was most wondrous!

*Note.* This refers to *viparīta-rata*, love's play with the roles reversed, known from the *kāma-śāstra*.

*Word for word:* *kā api* — a certain; *mugdha* — artless; *ramaṇī* — beauty; *viparīte* — in the reversed; *mādhavena* — with Madhava; *surate* — love's play; *tanu* — to [His] body; *lagnā* — clinging; *cumbitā* — kissed; *kati* — how many times; *na* — not; *cumbati* — kisses; *śaśvat* — ceaselessly; *su-smitam* — with a sweet smile; *laghu* — furtively; *vilokya vilokya* — glancing again and again.

**67.** A certain artless beauty, clinging to His body in love's play with Madhava with the roles reversed, once kissed [by Him] — how many times did she not kiss [Him] in return, ceaselessly, with a sweet smile, furtively glancing [at Him] again and again!

### Verse 71
