निःसहः स हरिणीनयनायाः ।
अर्पयन्निव सुधारसपूरः
पर्यपूरि निखिलेप्सितमेव ॥७१॥

*mādhavasya mṛdulorasi deho*
*niḥsahaḥ sa hariṇī-nayanāyāḥ |*
*arpayann iva sudhā-rasa-pūraḥ*
*paryapūri nikhilepsitam eva ||71||*

*Word for word:* *mādhavasya* — of Madhava; *mṛdula* — on the soft; *urasi* — chest; *dehaḥ* — the body; *niḥsahaḥ* — exhausted; *saḥ* — that; *hariṇī* — like a doe's; *nayanāyāḥ* — of [the maiden with] eyes; *arpayan* — offering; *iva* — as if; *sudhā* — of nectar; *rasa* — of the juice; *pūraḥ* — a flood; *paryapūri* — was fulfilled; *nikhila* — all; *īpsitam* — that was desired; *eva* — indeed.

**71.** That exhausted body of the doe-eyed [maiden] on Madhava's soft chest was as if offering [Him] a flood of nectar-juice, and all that [He] desired was fulfilled.

### Verse 72

प्रेयसीचरितसाधुसुधाभि-
स्तृप्तचित्तमधुपो मधुघाती ।
विभ्रमद्भ्रमरसम्मदमत्तः
सद्द्वितीयसुरते प्रबभूव ॥७२॥

*preyasī-carita-sādhu-sudhābhis*
*tṛpta-citta-madhupo madhu-ghātī |*
*vibhramad-bhramara-sammada-mattaḥ*
*sad-dvitīya-surate prababhūva ||72||*

*Word for word:* *preyasī* — of the beloved; *carita* — of the doings; *sādhu* — with the excellent; *sudhābhiḥ* — nectar; *tṛpta* — sated; *citta* — of the heart; *madhupaḥ* — [whose] bee; *madhu* — of Madhu; *ghātī* — the Slayer; *vibhramat* — circling; *bhramara* — of a bee; *sammada* — with the rapture; *mattaḥ* — intoxicated; *sat* — excellent; *dvitīya* — second; *surate* — for love's play; *prababhūva* — became ready.

**72.** The Slayer of Madhu, the bee of His heart sated with the excellent nectar of His beloved's doings, intoxicated with the rapture of a circling bee, became ready for a second, excellent love's play.

*Note.* The edition prints *°सम्पदमत्तः* ("not intoxicated with wealth"?); we read *°sammada-mattaḥ*, "intoxicated with rapture", as in the Gosvami edition (GGM). *Sad-dvitīya-surate* may perhaps also be understood as "in love's play with an excellent companion" (*dvitīyā* — "companion") (?).

### Verse 73

ओषधिः समधुराधरसीधु-
स्तद्वचो मनुवरः कुचकुम्भौ ।
तौ मणी व्रजवधूरिह कृष्णं
किं न मोहयतु जीवयताद्वा ॥७३॥

*oṣadhiḥ sa-madhurādhara-sīdhus*
*tad-vaco manu-varaḥ kuca-kumbhau |*
*tau maṇī vraja-vadhūr iha kṛṣṇaṁ*
*kiṁ na mohayatu jīvayatād vā ||73||*

*Word for word:* *oṣadhiḥ* — the [healing] herb; *saḥ* — that; *madhura* — of the sweet; *adhara* — lips; *sīdhuḥ* — the wine; *tat* — her; *vacaḥ* — speech; *manu* — of mantras; *varaḥ* — the best; *kuca* — of the breasts; *kumbhau* — the jars; *tau* — those; *maṇī* — the two gems; *vraja* — of Vraja; *vadhūḥ* — the young woman; *iha* — here; *kṛṣṇam* — Krishna; *kim* — why; *na* — not; *mohayatu* — should enchant; *jīvayatāt* — should bring to life; *vā* — or.

**73.** Her [healing] herb is that wine of her sweet lips; her speech is the best of mantras; the jars of her bosom are the two gems. Why then should the young woman of Vraja not enchant Krishna here, or bring Him to life?

*Note.* The three classical means of enchantment and healing: the herb (*oṣadhi*), the mantra and the gem (*maṇi*).

### Verse 74

अशिथिलपरिरम्भैश्चुम्बनैर्दन्तपातै-
रजनि रजनिमध्ये कान्तयोर्याथ तृप्तिः ।
नवनिधुवनलक्ष्मीलक्ष्मभाजोस्तथासौ
समधितपदमङ्गे सापराधा व्यरंसीत् ॥७४॥

*aśithila-parirambhaiś cumbanair danta-pātair*
*ajani rajani-madhye kāntayor yātha tṛptiḥ |*
*nava-nidhuvana-lakṣmī-lakṣma-bhājos tathāsau*
*samadhita-padam aṅge sāparādhā vyaraṁsīt ||74||*

*Word for word:* *aśithila* — close; *parirambhaiḥ* — by embraces; *cumbanaiḥ* — by kisses; *danta* — of the teeth; *pātaiḥ* — by the nips; *ajani* — arose; *rajani* — of the night; *madhye* — in the middle; *kāntayoḥ* — in the two lovers; *yā* — which; *atha* — then; *tṛptiḥ* — satiety; *nava* — of new; *nidhuvana* — love's play; *lakṣmī* — of the splendour; *lakṣma* — the marks; *bhājoḥ* — bearing; *tathā* — so; *asau* — it; *samadhita* — firmly set; *padam* — [its] foot; *aṅge* — in the body; *sa* — with; *aparādhā* — guilt; *vyaraṁsīt* — ceased.

**74.** The satiety that arose in the middle of the night in the two lovers, bearing the marks of the splendour of new love's play, through close embraces, kisses and the nips of teeth — it, though it had firmly set its foot in their bodies, ceased, guilty [as it was].

*Note.* The metre of verses 74–80 is *mālinī*. The sense of the second half is unclear (?): either satiety, having firmly settled in their bodies, brought the play to an end and is "guilty" of this, or satiety itself, as an offender against love, withdrew. The Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *rajani rajani-madhye*.

### Verse 75

स्मरसमरसमाप्तौ वीतभङ्गीभवद्भ्रूः
किमपि किमपि मन्दं मन्दमामीलिताक्षी ।
धनुरिव चिरसज्यं ज्याविहीनं विधत्ते
शरमिव चिरमुक्तं तूणमध्ये करोति ॥७५॥

*smara-samara-samāptau vīta-bhaṅgī-bhavad-bhrūḥ*
*kim api kim api mandaṁ mandam āmīlitākṣī |*
*dhanur iva cira-sajyaṁ jyā-vihīnaṁ vidhatte*
*śaram iva cira-muktaṁ tūṇa-madhye karoti ||75||*

*Word for word:* *smara* — of Smara; *samara* — of the battle; *samāptau* — at the close; *vīta* — lost; *bhaṅgī* — curve; *bhavat* — having; *bhrūḥ* — [whose] brows; *kim api kim api* — a little, a little; *mandam mandam* — very slowly; *āmīlita* — half-closed; *akṣī* — [whose] eyes; *dhanuḥ* — a bow; *iva* — as it were; *cira* — long; *sajyam* — strung; *jyā* — of the string; *vihīnam* — bereft; *vidhatte* — makes; *śaram* — an arrow; *iva* — as it were; *cira* — long since; *muktam* — loosed; *tūṇa* — of the quiver; *madhye* — within; *karoti* — puts.

**75.** At the close of Smara's battle, her brows having lost their curve, her eyes very slowly, little by little, closing, she, as it were, unstrings a bow long strung and puts back into the quiver an arrow long since loosed.

*Note.* The brows are the bow, the glance is the arrow.

### Verse 76

मदनरणविरामे कान्तयोः श्रान्तिभाजो-
रलसभरविभुग्नं सुप्तयो रात्रिशेषे ।
नहि नहि नहि कुत्राप्येवमस्तीति हर्षा-
दिव विधुरति शीर्षं वातधूतः प्रदीपः ॥७६॥

*madana-raṇa-virāme kāntayoḥ śrānti-bhājor*
*alasa-bhara-vibhugnaṁ suptayo rātri-śeṣe |*
*nahi nahi nahi kutrāpy evam astīti harṣād*
*iva vidhurati [vidhuvati?] śīrṣaṁ vāta-dhūtaḥ pradīpaḥ ||76||*

*Word for word:* *madana* — of Madana; *raṇa* — of the battle; *virāme* — at the cessation; *kāntayoḥ* — when the two lovers; *śrānti* — weariness; *bhājoḥ* — feeling; *alasa* — of drowsiness; *bhara* — under the weight; *vibhugnam* — bowed; *suptayoḥ* — had fallen asleep; *rātri* — of the night; *śeṣe* — at the end; *nahi nahi nahi* — no, no, no; *kutra api* — anywhere; *evam* — such; *asti* — is; *iti* — thus; *harṣāt* — from delight; *iva* — as if; *vidhurati* [*vidhuvati?*] — shakes; *śīrṣam* — the head; *vāta* — by the breeze; *dhūtaḥ* — stirred; *pradīpaḥ* — the lamp.

**76.** When Madana's battle had ceased and the two weary lovers had fallen asleep at the end of the night, the lamp, stirred by the breeze, as if from delight shakes its head, bowed under the weight of drowsiness: "No, no, no — nowhere is there anything like this!"

*Note.* The edition prints *विधुरति* (there is no such form); the metre (⏑⏑⏑⏑) suits *vidhuvati*, "shakes" (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text. *Alasa-bhara-vibhugnam* (neuter) is taken with *śīrṣam*: the flame, the lamp's "head", is bowed as if with drowsiness.

### Verse 77

अयमयमुदितोऽहं वर्तसे किं न्विदानी-
मिति परिणतकोपा लोहितस्तिग्मभानुः ।
अथ रजनिविरामे प्रेरयन् जालरन्ध्रे
करमिव किमु नैशं नाशयामास दीपम् ॥७७॥

*ayam ayam udito 'haṁ vartase kiṁ nv idānīm*
*iti pariṇata-kopā lohitas tigma-bhānuḥ |*
*atha rajani-virāme prerayan jāla-randhre*
*karam iva kim u naiśaṁ nāśayāmāsa dīpam ||77||*

*Word for word:* *ayam ayam* — here, here; *uditaḥ* — risen; *aham* — I [am]; *vartase* — do you remain; *kim nu* — why then; *idānīm* — now; *iti* — thus; *pariṇata* — ripened; *kopāt* — from anger; *lohitaḥ* — red; *tigma* — hot; *bhānuḥ* — [whose] rays [are] (the sun); *atha* — then; *rajani* — of the night; *virāme* — at the end; *prerayan* — thrusting; *jāla* — of the window lattice; *randhre* — into the opening; *karam* — the hand (ray); *iva* — as it were; *kim u* — whether; *naiśam* — the night; *nāśayāmāsa* — put out; *dīpam* — lamp.

**77.** "Here, here I am, risen! Why then do you remain now?" — so [saying], the hot-rayed sun, red with ripened anger, at the end of the night thrust, as it were, its hand through the opening of the window lattice: did it not put out the night-lamp?

*Note.* The edition prints *परिणतकोपा*; by the sense — *pariṇata-kopāl lohitaḥ*, "red from ripened anger". The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text. *Kara* means both "hand" and "ray".

### Verse 78

विकलकुवलयश्रीर्धूसरा संविमृष्टा
मृदुलतरमृणाली धर्षितं कोकयुग्मम् ।
ललितपुलिनवीथी पाणिजैरङ्किता त-
द्वद सरसि भवत्यां पुण्यवान् को ममज्ज ॥७८॥

*vikala-kuvalaya-śrīr dhūsarā saṁvimṛṣṭā*
*mṛdulatara-mṛṇālī dharṣitaṁ koka-yugmam |*
*lalita-pulina-vīthī pāṇijair aṅkitā tad*
*vada sarasi bhavatyāṁ puṇyavān ko mamajja ||78||*

*Word for word:* *vikala* — faded; *kuvalaya* — of the blue lotuses; *śrīḥ* — the beauty; *dhūsarā* — greyed; *saṁvimṛṣṭā* — crumpled; *mṛdulatara* — most tender; *mṛṇālī* — the lotus stalk; *dharṣitam* — disturbed; *koka* — of chakravakas; *yugmam* — the pair; *lalita* — lovely; *pulina* — of the sandbank; *vīthī* — the strip; *pāṇijaiḥ* — with nails; *aṅkitā* — marked; *tat* — so; *vada* — tell; *sarasi* — O lake; *bhavatyām* — into You; *puṇyavān* — fortunate one; *kaḥ* — what; *mamajja* — plunged.

**78.** "The beauty of the blue lotuses has faded; the most tender lotus stalk is greyed and crumpled; the pair of chakravakas is disturbed; the lovely strip of the sandbank is marked with nails. So tell [us], O lake, what fortunate one has plunged into You?"

*Note.* An allegory: a friend teases the beloved — evidently Radha (cf. 79, where She is the "lotus") — calling Her a "lake". The lotuses are Her eyes, the stalk Her arms, the chakravakas Her bosom, the sandbank Her hips.

### Verse 79

वपुरतुलपरागैर्धूसरं नास्ति शक्ति-
र्लवमपि निजपक्षक्षेपणे घूर्णसीव ।
परिकलितमिदं तत् कोऽपि ते नास्ति दोषो
मधुकर कमलिन्या एव कोऽपि प्रभावः ॥७९॥

*vapur atula-parāgair dhūsaraṁ nāsti śaktir*
*lavam api nija-pakṣa-kṣepaṇe ghūrṇasīva |*
*parikalitam idaṁ tat ko 'pi te nāsti doṣo*
*madhukara kamalinyā eva ko 'pi prabhāvaḥ ||79||*

*Word for word:* *vapuḥ* — the body; *atula* — with incomparable; *parāgaiḥ* — pollen; *dhūsaram* — grey; *na asti* — there is not; *śaktiḥ* — strength; *lavam api* — even a particle; *nija* — Your own; *pakṣa* — the wings; *kṣepaṇe* — for beating; *ghūrṇasi* — You reel; *iva* — as it were; *parikalitam* — understood; *idam* — this [is]; *tat* — so; *kaḥ api* — any; *te* — Your; *na asti* — there is not; *doṣaḥ* — fault; *madhukara* — O bee; *kamalinyāḥ* — of the lotus; *eva* — only; *kaḥ api* — some; *prabhāvaḥ* — power.

**79.** "Your body is grey with incomparable pollen; You have not a particle of strength to beat Your wings; You seem to reel… This is understood: there is no fault of Yours at all, O bee — it is only some power of the lotus."

*Note.* The friends tease Krishna (the "bee") and Radha (the "lotus").

### Verse 80

इति रहसि दिनादौ सानुतर्षं समन्ता-
न्मसृणवचनलक्ष्मीलक्ष्यहासोपहासा ।
निभृतनिभृतलीलालोलमन्योन्यमासी-
दभिसहचरि भूयः कान्तयोः कापि चेष्टा ॥८०॥

*iti rahasi dinādau sānutarṣaṁ samantān*
*masṛṇa-vacana-lakṣmī-lakṣya-hāsopahāsā |*
*nibhṛta-nibhṛta-līlā-lolam anyonyam āsīd*
*abhi-sahacari bhūyaḥ kāntayoḥ kāpi ceṣṭā ||80||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *rahasi* — in seclusion; *dina* — of the day; *ādau* — at the beginning; *sa* — with; *anutarṣam* — longing; *samantāt* — on all sides; *masṛṇa* — of soft; *vacana* — words; *lakṣmī* — by the beauty; *lakṣya* — marked; *hāsa* — [with] laughter; *upahāsā* — [and] jests; *nibhṛta-nibhṛta* — most secret; *līlā* — for play; *lolam* — eager; *anyonyam* — for each other; *āsīt* — there was; *abhi* — in the presence of; *sahacari* — the companions; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *kāntayoḥ* — of the two lovers; *kā api* — a certain [indescribable]; *ceṣṭā* — conduct.

**80.** Thus, in seclusion, at the beginning of the day, in the presence of their companions, there was again between the two lovers a certain indescribable conduct: full of longing, with laughter and jests on all sides marked by the beauty of soft words, eager for each other in most secret play.

**Colophon:** *iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahākāvye daśamaḥ sargaḥ* — "Thus [ends] the tenth sarga in the mahakavya 'Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita'." (The colophon gives no title for the sarga.)

---

## Sarga Eleven — verses 1–89

**Title of the sarga:** none — the colophon of the edition gives no title for this sarga.
**Metre:** *śikhariṇī* (17 syllables per pada: ⏑————— ⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑—— ⏑⏑⏑—); verse 66 — *upajāti* (a quotation from the Bhagavatam); verses 87–89 — *mandākrāntā*.
**Total verses:** 89 (verse 20 has six padas).

**Contents of the passage:** the night-time play in the house of the Acharya; the sannyasa at Katwa; the journey to Puri.
- 1–6 — Gaura arranges a night-time play in the house of the Acharya (cf. Chaitanya-bhagavata, Madhya 18): the roles are assigned; the wives of the brahmanas watch in secret together with Shachi; a guard stands at the door.
- 7–18 — the entrances: Srivasa as Narada, Shuklambara as his disciple, Gadadhara in a woman's role (the bathing in the month of Magha); Narada on the power of the Name (Ajamila); Srivasa's *nāndī*; Haridasa, staff in hand, rouses the three worlds and proclaims the command of Vaikuntha.
- 19–23 — Advaita in the costume of Krishna (with the Lord's flute and peacock feather); Nityananda as an old woman; Gadadhara in a woman's attire.
- 24–34 — a *kulaka* of eleven verses: the Lord Himself, in the guise of the Beloved (Lakshmi, then Girija), enters the shrine room.
- 35–37 — the Lord on the couch, Haridasa on His lap; seven days of dancing.
- 38–39 — Srivasa's question about the fruit of the Name; the answer about the four yugas.
- 40–48 — the intention to leave; the dream of the "great saying" and Murari's interpretation (the "genitive *tatpuruṣa*": *tasya tvam asi*); Keshava Bharati; the Lord departs across the Ganga.
- 49–57 — the lament of the townspeople and the women; the initiation (the Lord whispers the mantra to the guru), the tonsure (the barber weeps; "Hare Krishna"), the saffron cloth and the staff; the departure into the Radha country.
- 58–68 — three days in ecstasy; boys crying "Hari!" save Him from the river; Nityananda summons everyone to Advaita's house; the meeting (a quotation of Bhagavatam 11.23.57).
- 69–77 — at Advaita's house; the farewell (Haridasa with a straw between his teeth); the journey to Puri with Nityananda, Gadadhara and Mukunda.
- 78–86 — Remuna (the crown of Gopinatha), Sakshi-gopala, the broken staff, Yajapura (Jajpur), Bhubaneshvara, Kamalapura; Jagannatha.
- 87–89 (*mandākrāntā*) — conclusion: the well-being of Navadvipa while the Lord was present there.

### Verse 1

इतीदं तत्सर्वं विलसितमनुस्मृत्य सुदृशां
ससन्तोषं वृन्दावनमदन एषोऽतिमधुरः ।
विहर्तुं तद्भावैरकृत पुरतः स्वाङ्घ्रिदयितैः
समन्तादारम्भं द्रुतकनकगौरोज्ज्वलतनुः ॥१॥

*itīdaṁ tat sarvaṁ vilasitam anusmṛtya sudṛśāṁ*
*sasantoṣaṁ vṛndāvana-madana eṣo 'timadhuraḥ |*
*vihartuṁ tad-bhāvair akṛta purataḥ svāṅghri-dayitaiḥ*
*samantād ārambhaṁ druta-kanaka-gaurojjvala-tanuḥ ||1||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *idam* — this; *tat* — that; *sarvam* — all; *vilasitam* — play; *anusmṛtya* — having recalled; *sudṛśām* — of the fair-eyed [maidens]; *sa* — with; *santoṣam* — joy; *vṛndāvana* — of Vrindavana; *madanaḥ* — the Madana; *eṣaḥ* — this; *ati* — exceedingly; *madhuraḥ* — sweet; *vihartum* — to sport; *tat* — in their; *bhāvaiḥ* — in the moods; *akṛta* — made; *purataḥ* — before [Him]; *sva* — to His own; *aṅghri* — feet; *dayitaiḥ* — with [those] dear; *samantāt* — on every side; *ārambham* — preparation; *druta* — of molten; *kanaka* — gold; *gaura* — fair; *ujjvala* — radiant; *tanuḥ* — [whose] body.

**1.** Thus, having joyfully recalled all that play of the fair-eyed [gopis], this exceedingly sweet Madana of Vrindavana, whose radiant body is fair as molten gold, made preparations on every side, with those to whom His feet are dear [gathered] before Him, to sport in those same moods.

*Note.* The sarga opens with the night-time play in the house of the Acharya; cf. Chaitanya-bhagavata, Madhya 18 (verses 28–31: the play is staged in the house of Chandrashekhara Acharya); so too Murari 2.15.7 ff. The "Acharya" here is evidently Chandrashekhara Acharya himself.

### Verse 2

क्रमादेतां रात्रिं प्रहरनियमेनैव विभजन्
दिदेश प्रायेण प्रियजनमसौ योग्यललितम् ।
विचिन्त्याथो नृत्यस्थलमनिशमाचार्यनिलये
मुदा रङ्गी चक्रे प्रसृमरतरं चत्वरमथ ॥२॥

*kramād etāṁ rātriṁ prahara-niyamenaiva vibhajan*
*dideśa prāyeṇa priya-janam asau yogya-lalitam |*
*vicintyātho nṛtya-sthalam aniśam ācārya-nilaye*
*mudā raṅgī cakre prasṛmarataraṁ catvaram atha ||2||*

*Word for word:* *kramāt* — in due order; *etām* — this; *rātrim* — night; *prahara* — of the watches; *niyamena* — by the rule; *eva* — indeed; *vibhajan* — dividing; *dideśa* — assigned; *prāyeṇa* — for the most part; *priya* — to [His] dear; *janam* — people; *asau* — He; *yogya* — suitable; *lalitam* — roles; *vicintya* — having considered; *atho* — then; *nṛtya* — for dancing; *sthalam* — a place; *aniśam* — unceasingly; *ācārya* — of the Acharya; *nilaye* — in the house; *mudā* — joyfully; *raṅgī* — the lover of spectacle; *cakre* — made; *prasṛmarataram* — very spacious; *catvaram* — the courtyard; *atha* — then.

**2.** Dividing this night in due order according to the watches, He assigned suitable roles, for the most part, to His dear ones. Then, having pondered [it] unceasingly, the lover of spectacle joyfully made the very spacious courtyard in the Acharya's house the place for the dancing.

### Verse 3

ततो रम्ये स्थाने परिनियमिते निर्वृतिकरे
गुरूत्कण्ठाभाजो द्विजवररमण्योऽतिनिभृताः ।
समं शच्या देव्या प्रभुमतमभिज्ञाय समयो-
चितं धैर्यारम्भं गृहमभिदधत्यः प्रविविशुः ॥३॥

*tato ramye sthāne pariniyamite nirvṛti-kare*
*gurūtkaṇṭhā-bhājo dvija-vara-ramaṇyo 'tinibhṛtāḥ |*
*samaṁ śacyā devyā prabhu-matam abhijñāya samayo-*
*citaṁ dhairyārambhaṁ gṛham abhidadhatyaḥ praviviśuḥ ||3||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *ramye* — when the charming; *sthāne* — place; *pariniyamite* — had been arranged; *nirvṛti* — delight; *kare* — giving; *guru* — great; *utkaṇṭhā* — eagerness; *bhājaḥ* — feeling; *dvija-vara* — of the best of brahmanas; *ramaṇyaḥ* — the wives; *ati* — very; *nibhṛtāḥ* — quiet; *samam* — together; *śacyā devyā* — with Shachi-devi; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *matam* — the wish; *abhijñāya* — having learned; *samaya* — to the occasion; *ucitam* — befitting; *dhairya* — of restraint; *ārambham* — a show; *gṛham* — the house; *abhidadhatyaḥ* — displaying; *praviviśuḥ* — entered.

**3.** When the charming, delightful place had been arranged, the wives of the best of brahmanas, full of great eagerness, learned the Lord's wish and, together with Shachi-devi, very quietly entered the house, showing a restraint befitting the occasion.

### Verse 4

अलिन्दे गेहस्य प्रभुनटनसन्दर्शनमहो-
त्सुका लीना आसन्निभृतमुपविष्टाः सभयैः ।
अमूश्चित्रोत्कीर्णा विनिमिषगतस्पन्दवपुषो
नवै रागैः कान्ताः फलकभुवि ता मूर्तय इव ॥४॥

*alinde gehasya prabhu-naṭana-sandarśana-mahot-*
*sukā līnā āsan nibhṛtam upaviṣṭāḥ sabhayaiḥ (?) |*
*amūś citrotkīrṇā vinimiṣa-gata-spanda-vapuṣo*
*navai rāgaiḥ kāntāḥ phalaka-bhuvi tā mūrtaya iva ||4||*

*Word for word:* *alinde* — on the veranda; *gehasya* — of the house; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *naṭana* — the dancing; *sandarśana* — to behold; *mahā* — greatly; *utsukāḥ* — eager; *līnāḥ* — hidden; *āsan* — were; *nibhṛtam* — secretly; *upaviṣṭāḥ* — seated; *sa-bhayaiḥ* (?) — with timidity; *amūḥ* — they; *citra* — in a painting; *utkīrṇāḥ* — depicted; *vinimiṣa* — unblinking; *gata* — having lost; *spanda* — movement; *vapuṣaḥ* — [with] bodies; *navaiḥ* — with fresh; *rāgaiḥ* — colours; *kāntāḥ* — lovely; *phalaka* — of a panel; *bhuvi* — on the surface; *tāḥ* — those; *mūrtayaḥ* — figures; *iva* — like.

**4.** Greatly eager to behold the Lord's dancing, they hid on the veranda of the house and sat there secretly and timidly. Unblinking, their bodies motionless, they were like lovely figures painted in fresh colours on the surface of a panel.

*Note.* The edition has *सहभयैः* (*saha-bhayaiḥ*); the form is unclear (?) and is taken here as "timidly". It is this reading of the edition that gives the second pada its seventeen syllables. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 5

नियम्यैकं द्वारे दृढललितशौटीर्यवलितं
यथैकोऽप्यायाति क्षणमपि न तत्रेति निरतः ।
जनानाप्तानाप्तान् पुरमभिनिवेश्यैवमसकौ
महत्या निर्वृत्या जयति सततं गौरशशभृत् ॥५॥

*niyamyaikaṁ dvāre dṛḍha-lalita-śauṭīrya-valitaṁ*
*yathaiko 'py āyāti kṣaṇam api na tatreti nirataḥ |*
*janān āptān āptān puram abhiniveśyaivam asakau*
*mahatyā nirvṛtyā jayati satataṁ gaura-śaśabhṛt ||5||*

*Word for word:* *niyamya* — having stationed; *ekam* — one [man]; *dvāre* — at the door; *dṛḍha* — steadfast; *lalita* — graceful; *śauṭīrya* — with valour; *valitam* — endowed; *yathā* — so that; *ekaḥ api* — even one; *āyāti* — comes; *kṣaṇam api* — even for a moment; *na* — not; *tatra* — there; *iti* — thus; *nirataḥ* — intent; *janān* — people; *āptān āptān* — only the very closest; *puram* — into the house; *abhiniveśya* — having admitted; *evam* — thus; *asakau* — this; *mahatyā* — in great; *nirvṛtyā* — bliss; *jayati* — is victorious; *satatam* — ever; *gaura* — Gaura; *śaśabhṛt* — the moon.

**5.** Having stationed at the door one [man] — steadfast, graceful and full of valour — intent that not a single [outsider] should come in there even for a moment, and having thus admitted into the house only those closest [to Him], this moon Gaura is ever victorious in great bliss.

*Note.* The guard at the door is not named in the text. In the Chaitanya-bhagavata (Madhya 18.40–45) Haridasa, staff in hand, is the "constable of Vaikuntha" (*vaikuṇṭha-koṭāla*), who warns everyone.

### Verse 6

गृहैकं नेपथ्यस्थलमथ विधायाविशदसौ
प्रभुर्वेशं कर्तुं नटनकुतुकी प्रेमललितः ।
जनेनात्मीयेन स्वपदपरमप्रेमवहता
समारेजे श्रीमानतिशयकृपापूरसुभगः ॥६॥

*gṛhaikaṁ nepathya-sthalam atha vidhāyāviśad asau*
*prabhur veśaṁ kartuṁ naṭana-kutukī prema-lalitaḥ |*
*janenātmīyena sva-pada-parama-prema-vahatā*
*samāreje śrīmān atiśaya-kṛpā-pūra-subhagaḥ ||6||*

*Word for word:* *gṛha* — a room; *ekam* — one; *nepathya* — for dressing; *sthalam* — the place; *atha* — then; *vidhāya* — having made; *āviśat* — entered; *asau* — He; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *veśam* — costume; *kartum* — to put on; *naṭana* — for dancing; *kutukī* — eager; *prema* — with love; *lalitaḥ* — charming; *janena* — with the people; *ātmīyena* — His own; *sva* — for His own; *pada* — feet; *parama* — supreme; *prema* — love; *vahatā* — bearing; *samāreje* — shone; *śrīmān* — the beautiful [Lord]; *atiśaya* — of boundless; *kṛpā* — mercy; *pūra* — with a flood; *subhagaḥ* — lovely.

**6.** Then, having made one room the dressing-place, the Lord, eager for the dance and charming in His love, entered it to put on His costume. The beautiful [Lord], lovely with a flood of boundless mercy, shone among His own people, who bore supreme love for His feet.

*Note.* *Nepathya* is the backstage, the place where actors put on their costumes.

### Verse 7

गृहीत्वासौ वेशं पुरत ऋषिवर्यस्य परमं
निशादौ श्रीवासः प्रभुचरणपद्मप्रियतमः ।
जटाभिः पिङ्गाभिः स्फटिकमणिमालां कलयता
करेणोर्वीदेवप्रवर इव तत्राविशदथ ॥७॥

*gṛhītvāsau veśaṁ purata ṛṣi-varyasya paramaṁ*
*niśādau śrīvāsaḥ prabhu-caraṇa-padma-priyatamaḥ |*
*jaṭābhiḥ piṅgābhiḥ sphaṭika-maṇi-mālāṁ kalayatā*
*kareṇorvī-deva-pravara iva tatrāviśad atha ||7||*

*Word for word:* *gṛhītvā* — having assumed; *asau* — he; *veśam* — the guise; *purataḥ* — first; *ṛṣi-varyasya* — of the best of sages; *paramam* — splendid; *niśā* — of the night; *ādau* — at the beginning; *śrīvāsaḥ* — Srivasa; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *padma* — to the lotuses; *priyatamaḥ* — most dear; *jaṭābhiḥ* — with matted locks; *piṅgābhiḥ* — tawny; *sphaṭika* — of crystal; *maṇi* — beads; *mālām* — a rosary; *kalayatā* — telling; *kareṇa* — with a hand; *urvī* — of the earth; *deva* — of the gods (brahmanas); *pravaraḥ* — the foremost; *iva* — like; *tatra* — there; *āviśat* — entered; *atha* — then.

**7.** At the beginning of the night Srivasa, most dear to the lotus feet of the Lord, came in there first, having assumed the splendid guise of the best of sages: with tawny matted locks, telling a rosary of crystal beads with his hand, he entered like the foremost of brahmanas.

*Note.* The best of sages is Narada (cf. *devarṣi*, verses 9 and 11). *Urvī-deva*, "a god of the earth", is a brahmana.

### Verse 8

अथास्यैको दासो धृतकरकदर्भासनवरो
द्युवापीमृच्छुक्लो वपुषि भुवि शुक्लाम्बर इति ।
स देवेनाविष्टस्तमृषिवरमानम्य सहसा
गदाभृन्नामानं प्रभुदयितमूचे सुमधुरम् ॥८॥

*athāsyaiko dāso dhṛta-karaka-darbhāsana-varo*
*dyu-vāpī-mṛc-chuklo vapuṣi bhuvi śuklāmbara iti |*
*sa devenāviṣṭas tam ṛṣi-varam ānamya sahasā*
*gadābhṛn-nāmānaṁ prabhu-dayitam ūce sumadhuram ||8||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *asya* — his; *ekaḥ* — one; *dāsaḥ* — servant; *dhṛta* — holding; *karaka* — a water-pot; *darbha* — of *darbha* grass; *āsana* — a seat; *varaḥ* — excellent; *dyu* — of the heavenly; *vāpī* — stream (the Ganga); *mṛt* — with the clay; *śuklaḥ* — white; *vapuṣi* — on the body; *bhuvi* — on earth; *śuklāmbaraḥ* — Shuklambara; *iti* — [so called]; *saḥ* — he; *devena* — by the divinity; *āviṣṭaḥ* — possessed; *tam* — to that; *ṛṣi* — of sages; *varam* — best; *ānamya* — having bowed; *sahasā* — at once; *gadābhṛt* — Gadadhara; *nāmānam* — by name; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *dayitam* — to the beloved; *ūce* — spoke; *su-madhuram* — most sweetly.

**8.** Then came one of his servants, holding a water-pot and an excellent seat of *darbha* grass, his body white with the clay of the heavenly river — on earth he was called Shuklambara. Possessed by the divinity, he at once bowed to the best of sages and spoke most sweetly to the Lord's beloved one named Gadadhara.

*Note.* *Dyu-vāpī*, "the heavenly pool", is the Ganga. With the clay of the Ganga Vaishnavas draw the marks of *tilaka* on the body.

### Verse 9

अये त्वं देवर्षिश्चरणमवनम्यावद इदं
कलौ भूयां श्रीमत्प्रभुचरणसेवासु निरता ।
इतीदं श्रुत्वासौ मुनिरवददेतत् सुवदने
सुरस्रोतःस्वत्यां स्नपनमधिमाघं कुरु सदा ॥९॥

*aye tvaṁ devarṣiś caraṇam avanamyāvada idaṁ*
*kalau bhūyāṁ śrīmat-prabhu-caraṇa-sevāsu niratā |*
*itīdaṁ śrutvāsau munir avadad etat su-vadane*
*sura-srotaḥsvatyāṁ snapanam adhimāghaṁ kuru sadā ||9||*

*Word for word:* *aye* — O; *tvam* — you; *devarṣiḥ* — [of] the divine sage; *caraṇam* — to the feet; *avanamya* — having bowed; *āvada* — say; *idam* — this; *kalau* — in Kali; *bhūyām* — may I be; *śrīmat* — of the beautiful; *prabhu* — Lord; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *sevāsu* — to the service; *niratā* — devoted; *iti* — thus; *idam* — this; *śrutvā* — having heard; *asau* — this; *muniḥ* — sage; *avadat* — said; *etat* — this; *su-vadane* — O fair-faced one; *sura* — of the gods; *srotaḥsvatyām* — in the river; *snapanam* — bathing; *adhimāgham* — in the month of Magha; *kuru* — perform; *sadā* — always.

**9.** "O you, bow down to the feet of the divine sage and say this: 'May I in [the age of] Kali be devoted to the service of the feet of the beautiful Lord.'" Hearing this, the sage said: "O fair-faced one, always bathe in the river of the gods in the month of Magha."

*Note.* Gadadhara is playing a woman's role; hence *niratā* (feminine) and the address "fair-faced one". Magha (January–February) is the month of auspicious bathing in the Ganga. The edition has *अवनम्या वद इदं*; by the metre we read *avanamyāvada idam* (*ā-vada*, "say"), with hiatus before *idam*. *Devarṣiś* is formally a nominative; by the sense it is "[the feet] of the divine sage".

### Verse 10

तदा तत्पुण्येन प्रभुचरणपाथोजमिलनं
भविष्यत्येवं ते तदनु भवतीभिः कृतमिदम् ।
इदानीं तेन त्वं मुनिवरवरेण प्रभुपद-
प्रियो भूत्वा यातः किमु न विदितं तत् सुवदने ॥१०॥

*tadā tat-puṇyena prabhu-caraṇa-pāthoja-milanaṁ*
*bhaviṣyaty evaṁ te tad anu bhavatībhiḥ kṛtam idam |*
*idānīṁ tena tvaṁ muni-vara-vareṇa prabhu-pada-*
*priyo bhūtvā yātaḥ kim u na viditaṁ tat su-vadane ||10||*

*Word for word:* *tadā* — then; *tat* — of that; *puṇyena* — by the merit; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *pāthoja* — of the lotuses; *milanam* — meeting; *bhaviṣyati* — will be; *evam* — thus; *te* — for you; *tat anu* — after that; *bhavatībhiḥ* — by you [ladies]; *kṛtam* — done; *idam* — this; *idānīm* — now; *tena* — by that; *tvam* — you; *muni* — of sages; *vara* — of the best; *vareṇa* — by the blessing; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *pada* — to the feet; *priyaḥ* — dear; *bhūtvā* — having become; *yātaḥ* — have come; *kim u* — is it; *na* — not; *viditam* — known; *tat* — that; *su-vadane* — O fair-faced one.

**10.** "Then, by that merit, you will thus meet the lotus feet of the Lord. And afterwards this was done by you [ladies]. Now, by the blessing of that best of sages, you have become dear to the Lord's feet and have come [here] — is that not known [to you], O fair-faced one?"

*Note.* Who is speaking (the sage or Shuklambara) and how *tad anu bhavatībhiḥ kṛtam idam* should be understood are unclear (?). *Yātaḥ* is masculine despite the address "fair-faced one" — a play on the fact that the woman's role is played by Gadadhara. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 11

ततोऽसौ देवर्षिः स्वयमवददुच्चैः सुललितं
महत्त्वं तद्भक्तेरविदितगुरुत्वं पुलकितः ।
वदामः किं नाम्नः परममहिमानं यदघकृ-
द्द्विजाभासो दासीपतिरपि च मुक्तोऽघनिवहात् ॥११॥

*tato 'sau devarṣiḥ svayam avadad uccaiḥ sulalitaṁ*
*mahattvaṁ tad-bhakter avidita-gurutvaṁ pulakitaḥ |*
*vadāmaḥ kiṁ nāmnaḥ parama-mahimānaṁ yad agha-kṛd*
*dvijābhāso dāsī-patir api ca mukto 'gha-nivahāt ||11||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *asau* — this; *devarṣiḥ* — divine sage; *svayam* — himself; *avadat* — proclaimed; *uccaiḥ* — loudly; *sulalitam* — gracefully; *mahattvam* — the greatness; *tat* — to Him; *bhakteḥ* — of devotion; *avidita* — unknown; *gurutvam* — [whose] weight; *pulakitaḥ* — thrilling with rapture; *vadāmaḥ* — shall we say; *kim* — what; *nāmnaḥ* — of the Name; *parama* — supreme; *mahimānam* — about the glory; *yat* — since; *agha* — sins; *kṛt* — committing; *dvija* — of a brahmana; *ābhāsaḥ* — a semblance; *dāsī* — of a maidservant; *patiḥ* — the husband; *api ca* — even; *muktaḥ* — was freed; *agha* — of sins; *nivahāt* — from a heap.

**11.** Then the divine sage himself, thrilling with rapture, loudly and gracefully proclaimed the greatness of devotion to Him, whose weight is unknown: "What shall we say of the supreme glory of the Name? For even a sinner, a brahmana in semblance only, the husband of a maidservant, was freed [by it] from a heap of sins!"

*Note.* An allusion to Ajamila (Bhagavatam 6.1–2): a fallen brahmana who lived with a maidservant was saved by uttering the name of Narayana at his last hour.

### Verse 12

इतीवोक्ते तस्मिन् परममुदिताः सर्वमनुजा
हरेर्नाम्नामुच्चैः किमपि विदधुः कीर्तनमथ ।
सहर्षं श्रीवासः पुलकिततनुस्तत्र कुतुका-
त्पुरो नृत्यं चक्रे प्रथममिव नान्दीं विरचयन् ॥१२॥

*itīvokte tasmin parama-muditāḥ sarva-manujā*
*harer nāmnām uccaiḥ kim api vidadhuḥ kīrtanam atha |*
*saharṣaṁ śrīvāsaḥ pulakita-tanus tatra kutukāt*
*puro nṛtyaṁ cakre prathamam iva nāndīṁ viracayan ||12||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *iva* — as it were; *ukte* — when it had been said; *tasmin* — by him; *parama* — supremely; *muditāḥ* — delighted; *sarva* — all; *manujāḥ* — the people; *hareḥ* — of Hari; *nāmnām* — of the names; *uccaiḥ* — loudly; *kim api* — a wondrous; *vidadhuḥ* — performed; *kīrtanam* — kirtana; *atha* — then; *sa* — with; *harṣam* — joy; *śrīvāsaḥ* — Srivasa; *pulakita* — thrilling; *tanuḥ* — [whose] body; *tatra* — there; *kutukāt* — eagerly; *puraḥ* — in front; *nṛtyam* — a dance; *cakre* — performed; *prathamam* — first; *iva* — as if; *nāndīm* — the *nāndī*; *viracayan* — performing.

**12.** When he had spoken thus, all the people, supremely delighted, loudly performed a wondrous kirtana of the names of Hari. And Srivasa, his body thrilling, joyfully and eagerly danced there in front, as if first performing the *nāndī*.

*Note.* The *nāndī* is the benedictory prelude with which a Sanskrit drama opens.

### Verse 13

ततोऽस्मिन्निष्क्रान्ते कृतनटनसङ्कीर्तनरसे
विवेशासौ श्रीमान् धृतपरमवेशः सुमधुरः ।
प्रविष्टोऽसौ रेजे हिमकरसमूहप्रतिकृति-
र्गृहीत्वा सद्वेत्रं सपदि हरिदासोऽङ्गनभुवि ॥१३॥

*tato 'smin niṣkrānte kṛta-naṭana-saṅkīrtana-rase*
*viveśāsau śrīmān dhṛta-parama-veśaḥ sumadhuraḥ |*
*praviṣṭo 'sau reje hima-kara-samūha-pratikṛtir*
*gṛhītvā sad-vetraṁ sapadi haridāso 'ṅgana-bhuvi ||13||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *asmin* — when he; *niṣkrānte* — had gone out; *kṛta* — having tasted; *naṭana* — of dancing; *saṅkīrtana* — [and] of sankirtana; *rase* — the rasa; *viveśa* — entered; *asau* — this; *śrīmān* — beautiful; *dhṛta* — wearing; *parama* — a splendid; *veśaḥ* — costume; *su-madhuraḥ* — most sweet; *praviṣṭaḥ* — having entered; *asau* — he; *reje* — shone; *hima-kara* — of moons; *samūha* — of a host; *pratikṛtiḥ* — the likeness; *gṛhītvā* — having taken; *sat* — a fine; *vetram* — staff; *sapadi* — at once; *haridāsaḥ* — Haridasa; *aṅgana* — of the courtyard; *bhuvi* — on the ground.

**13.** When he, having tasted the rasa of dancing and sankirtana, had gone out, the beautiful, most sweet Haridasa entered, wearing a splendid costume. Having entered, he at once took up a fine staff and shone in the courtyard like a host of moons.

*Note.* *Vetra* — the staff of a doorkeeper or watchman. Cf. Chaitanya-bhagavata, Madhya 18.40–45, 100, where Haridasa plays the role of the watchman (*koṭāla*): staff in hand, he goes round everyone and rouses them with the cry "Wake up!"

### Verse 14

वदन्तूच्चैरुच्चैर्वद हरिमिति प्रेमविकलाः
कुरुध्वं तद्गाथामिति सरभसं चन्द्रललितः ।
दिशन् वेत्राग्रेण प्रतिपदवलद्धर्षविवश-
स्त्रिलोकीं संसुप्तामिव स यतते जागरयितुम् ॥१४॥

*vadantūccair uccair vada harim iti prema-vikalāḥ*
*kurudhvaṁ tad-gāthām iti sarabhasaṁ candra-lalitaḥ |*
*diśan vetrāgreṇa pratipada-valad-dharṣa-vivaśas*
*trilokīṁ saṁsuptām iva sa yatate jāgarayitum ||14||*

*Word for word:* *vadantu* — let them say; *uccaiḥ uccaiḥ* — loudly, loudly; *vada* — say; *harim* — "Hari"; *iti* — thus; *prema* — by love; *vikalāḥ* — overwhelmed; *kurudhvam* — make; *tat* — His; *gāthām* — song; *iti* — thus; *sa* — with; *rabhasam* — ardour; *candra* — [like] the moon; *lalitaḥ* — charming; *diśan* — pointing; *vetra* — of the staff; *agreṇa* — with the tip; *pratipada* — at every step; *valat* — surging; *harṣa* — by joy; *vivaśaḥ* — overcome; *trilokīm* — the three worlds; *saṁsuptām* — fast asleep; *iva* — as if; *saḥ* — he; *yatate* — strives; *jāgarayitum* — to awaken.

**14.** "Let them say it loudly, loudly! Say 'Hari!' Overwhelmed by love, sing His song!" — so he cried ardently, charming as the moon, pointing with the tip of his staff; overcome by a joy that surged at every step, he strove, as it were, to awaken the three worlds fast asleep.

### Verse 15

अकुण्ठाद्वैकुण्ठात् प्रभुचरणपाथोजनिकटा-
त्तदाज्ञातो भूमौ प्रथममवतीर्णोऽहमधुना ।
तदाज्ञावाचस्ताः शृणुत परमाः सीधुमधुराः
कलिव्यालग्रस्तप्रकटतरसञ्जीवनकरीः ॥१५॥

*akuṇṭhād vaikuṇṭhāt prabhu-caraṇa-pāthoja-nikaṭāt*
*tad-ājñāto bhūmau prathamam avatīrṇo 'ham adhunā |*
*tad-ājñā-vācas tāḥ śṛṇuta paramāḥ sīdhu-madhurāḥ*
*kali-vyāla-grasta-prakaṭatara-sañjīvana-karīḥ ||15||*

*Word for word:* *akuṇṭhāt* — from the unbounded; *vaikuṇṭhāt* — from Vaikuntha; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *pāthoja* — of the lotuses; *nikaṭāt* — from the vicinity; *tat* — His; *ājñātaḥ* — by command; *bhūmau* — to the earth; *prathamam* — first; *avatīrṇaḥ* — have descended; *aham* — I; *adhunā* — now; *tat* — His; *ājñā* — of command; *vācaḥ* — the words; *tāḥ* — those; *śṛṇuta* — hear; *paramāḥ* — supreme; *sīdhu* — [as] nectar; *madhurāḥ* — sweet; *kali* — of Kali; *vyāla* — by the serpent; *grasta* — of [those] swallowed; *prakaṭatara* — manifestly; *sañjīvana* — revival; *karīḥ* — effecting.

**15.** "From unbounded Vaikuntha, from beside the lotus feet of the Lord, I have now descended to earth first, by His command. Hear those supreme words of His command, sweet as nectar, which manifestly revive those swallowed by the serpent of Kali!

*Note.* A play on *akuṇṭha* ("unblunted, unbounded") and *vaikuṇṭha*.

### Verse 16

विना नाम्नां गाथामृतरसधुनीस्रोतसि सदा
कृतस्नानाँल्लोकानिति तदधुना वाञ्छितमिह ।
तदेतद्विश्वस्मिन्निह स विकिरन्नाजिगमिषु-
र्भवद्भिः कीर्त्यन्तां गुणसमुदयाः श्रीभगवतः ॥१६॥

*vinā nāmnāṁ gāthāmṛta-rasa-dhunī-srotasi sadā*
*kṛta-snānāl̐ lokān iti tad adhunā vāñchitam iha |*
*tad etad viśvasminn iha sa vikirann ājigamiṣur*
*bhavadbhiḥ kīrtyantāṁ guṇa-samudayāḥ śrī-bhagavataḥ ||16||*

*Word for word:* *vinā* — without; *nāmnām* — of the names; *gāthā* — of the songs; *amṛta* — of nectar; *rasa* — of the juice; *dhunī* — of the river; *srotasi* — in the stream; *sadā* — always; *kṛta* — having made; *snānān* — ablutions; *lokān* — people; *iti* — thus; *tat* — that; *adhunā* — now; *vāñchitam* — [is] desired; *iha* — here; *tat* — therefore; *etat* — this; *viśvasmin* — throughout the whole world; *iha* — here; *saḥ* — He; *vikiran* — scattering; *ājigamiṣuḥ* — wishing to come; *bhavadbhiḥ* — by you; *kīrtyantām* — let be glorified; *guṇa* — of qualities; *samudayāḥ* — the multitudes; *śrī-bhagavataḥ* — of the beautiful Bhagavan.

**16.** "[He has no need of] people unless they always bathe in the stream of the river of the nectarean rasa of the songs of the names — this is what He now desires here. He wishes to come here and scatter this throughout the whole world; therefore let the multitudes of the qualities of the beautiful Bhagavan be glorified by you!

*Note.* The syntax of the first half (*vinā … lokān iti*) is rendered according to the sense (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 17

इदानीं तस्याज्ञां श्रवसि परिपीय प्रतिपदं

इति श्रुत्वा तस्याननशशिसमुद्भूतवचसो
विलासं ते सर्वे विपुलपुलकाङ्गाः सुललितम् ॥१७॥

*idānīṁ tasyājñāṁ śravasi paripīya pratipadaṁ*
*bhavanto nṛtyantu prativihita-saṅkīrtana-rasāḥ |*
*iti śrutvā tasyānana-śaśi-samudbhūta-vacaso*
*vilāsaṁ te sarve vipula-pulakāṅgāḥ sulalitam ||17||*

*Word for word:* *idānīm* — now; *tasya* — His; *ājñām* — command; *śravasi* — with the ear; *paripīya* — having drunk in; *pratipadam* — at every step; *bhavantaḥ* — you; *nṛtyantu* — dance; *prativihita* — performed; *saṅkīrtana* — of sankirtana; *rasāḥ* — [relishing] the rasa; *iti* — thus; *śrutvā* — having heard; *tasya* — his; *ānana* — of the face; *śaśi* — from the moon; *samudbhūta* — arisen; *vacasaḥ* — of the speech; *vilāsam* — the play; *te* — they; *sarve* — all; *vipula* — with abundant; *pulaka* — thrill; *aṅgāḥ* — [with] limbs; *sulalitam* — charming.

**17.** Now, having drunk in His command with your ears, dance at every step, relishing the rasa of the sankirtana you perform!" Having heard this charming play of speech arisen from the moon of his face, all of them, their limbs thrilling abundantly…

*Note.* Verses 17–18 form one sentence.

### Verse 18

जगुर्गीतं रम्यं कलितकरतालध्वनिबल-
न्मृदङ्गालीभङ्ग्या स्वयमपि ननर्तैष परमः ।
असौ भूयोभूयः कृतनटनसङ्कीर्तनरसो
विनिष्क्रान्तो भूत्वा तदनु विरराम प्रमुदितः ॥१८॥

*jagur gītaṁ ramyaṁ kalita-kara-tāla-dhvani-balan-*
*mṛdaṅgālī-bhaṅgyā svayam api nanartaiṣa paramaḥ |*
*asau bhūyo bhūyaḥ kṛta-naṭana-saṅkīrtana-raso*
*viniṣkrānto bhūtvā tad anu virarāma pramuditaḥ ||18||*

*Word for word:* *jaguḥ* — sang; *gītam* — a song; *ramyam* — charming; *kalita* — struck; *kara-tāla* — of hand-claps; *dhvani* — with the sound; *balat* — mighty; *mṛdaṅga* — of mridangas; *ālī* — of a row; *bhaṅgyā* — in time with; *svayam* — himself; *api* — also; *nanarta* — danced; *eṣaḥ* — he; *paramaḥ* — excellent; *asau* — he; *bhūyaḥ bhūyaḥ* — again and again; *kṛta* — having tasted; *naṭana* — of dancing; *saṅkīrtana* — [and] of sankirtana; *rasaḥ* — the rasa; *viniṣkrāntaḥ* — gone out; *bhūtvā* — having; *tat anu* — after that; *virarāma* — rested; *pramuditaḥ* — joyful.

**18.** …sang a charming song to the sound of ringing hand-claps and in time with a row of mighty mridangas, and the excellent [Haridasa] himself danced too. Having tasted again and again the rasa of dancing and sankirtana, he went out and afterwards rested, joyful.

### Verse 19

ततोऽद्वैतस्तत्रानुकृतभगवद्वेशचरितः
कराभ्यां सानन्दं कलितमुरलीकः समविशत् ।
प्रभुः स्वं स्वं वेशं निजमुरलिकां बर्हिणशिखा-
वतंसं स्वं पीतं वसनमपि लावण्यमपि च ॥१९॥

*tato 'dvaitas tatrānukṛta-bhagavad-veśa-caritaḥ*
*karābhyāṁ sānandaṁ kalita-muralīkaḥ samaviśat |*
*prabhuḥ svaṁ svaṁ veśaṁ nija-muralikāṁ barhiṇa-śikhā-*
*vataṁsaṁ svaṁ pītaṁ vasanam api lāvaṇyam api ca ||19||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *advaitaḥ* — Advaita; *tatra* — there; *anukṛta* — imitating; *bhagavat* — of Bhagavan; *veśa* — the dress; *caritaḥ* — [and] deeds; *karābhyām* — with both hands; *sa* — with; *ānandam* — joy; *kalita* — holding; *muralīkaḥ* — a flute; *samaviśat* — entered; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *svam svam* — His very own; *veśam* — dress; *nija* — His own; *muralikām* — flute; *barhiṇa* — of a peacock; *śikhā* — of the plume; *avataṁsam* — the crest; *svam* — His own; *pītam* — yellow; *vasanam* — garment; *api* — and; *lāvaṇyam* — beauty; *api ca* — even.

**19.** Then Advaita entered there, imitating the dress and deeds of Bhagavan, joyfully holding a flute in both hands. The Lord — His very own dress, His own flute, the crest of peacock plume, His own yellow garment, and even His beauty…

*Note.* Verses 19–20 form one sentence.

### Verse 20

प्रदायामुं चक्रे कलितकलधौतोज्ज्वलतनु-
र्यथेच्छं नृत्येऽस्मिन् धृतपरमसन्नायकरुचिः ।
ततस्तैस्तैः सर्वैः परममधुराकारकमनः
प्रविष्टो भूत्वासौ किमपि कमलाक्षः परिषदि ।
लघूद्यन्मार्दङ्गध्वनिसुमधुरं नृत्यमकरो-
ल्लयैस्तालैर्मानैर्मलयजरसैश्चर्चिततनुः ॥२०॥

*pradāyāmuṁ cakre kalita-kaladhautojjvala-tanur*
*yathecchaṁ nṛtye 'smin dhṛta-parama-san-nāyaka-ruciḥ |*
*tatas taiḥ taiḥ sarvaiḥ parama-madhurākāra-kamanaḥ*
*praviṣṭo bhūtvāsau kim api kamalākṣaḥ pariṣadi |*
*laghūdyan-mārdaṅga-dhvani-sumadhuraṁ nṛtyam akarol*
*layais tālair mānair malayaja-rasaiś carcita-tanuḥ ||20||*

*Word for word:* *pradāya* — having given; *amum* — Him (Advaita); *cakre* — made [act]; *kalita* — having acquired; *kaladhauta* — [like] pure gold; *ujjvala* — radiant; *tanuḥ* — [whose] body; *yathā-iccham* — at will; *nṛtye* — in the dance; *asmin* — this; *dhṛta* — having assumed; *parama* — of the supreme; *sat* — noble; *nāyaka* — hero; *ruciḥ* — [whose] splendour; *tataḥ* — then; *taiḥ taiḥ sarvaiḥ* — with all these; *parama* — supremely; *madhura* — sweet; *ākāra* — in form; *kamanaḥ* — enchanting; *praviṣṭaḥ bhūtvā* — having entered; *asau* — He; *kim api* — indescribably; *kamala* — lotus-; *akṣaḥ* — eyed; *pariṣadi* — into the assembly; *laghu* — swiftly; *udyat* — rising; *mārdaṅga* — of mridangas; *dhvani* — with the sound; *su-madhuram* — most sweet; *nṛtyam* — a dance; *akarot* — performed; *layaiḥ* — with tempos; *tālaiḥ* — rhythms; *mānaiḥ* — [and] measures; *malayaja* — of sandalwood; *rasaiḥ* — with the pulp; *carcita* — anointed; *tanuḥ* — [whose] body.

**20.** …having given [all this] to Him, the Lord — His body radiant as pure gold, bearing the splendour of the supreme and noble hero — let Him act at will in this dance. Then the lotus-eyed one, indescribably enchanting with all these [adornments] in His supremely sweet form, entered the assembly and, His body anointed with sandal-paste, performed a most sweet dance to the sound of swiftly rising mridangas, keeping tempo, rhythm and measure.

*Note.* A verse of six padas. The nominatives of the first half (*kalita-kaladhautojjvala-tanuḥ*, *dhṛta-parama-san-nāyaka-ruciḥ*) agree grammatically with *prabhuḥ* (verse 19), the subject of *cakre*; by the sense they may also be referred to Advaita as the hero of the dance (?). By the grammar (*pradāya amuṁ cakre*; "with all these", *taiḥ taiḥ sarvaiḥ*) the dancer of the second half is evidently Advaita in the role of Krishna. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 21

तथा नृत्यत्यस्मिंस्तदनु जरतीवेशरसिको-
ऽवधूतो धूताङ्गः पलितललिताकीर्णचिकुरः ।
प्रविष्टस्त्वाविष्टः परमपरमोन्मादविवश-
स्तदा छित्त्वा भित्त्वा नटति जरतीभूमिकरुचिम् ॥२१॥

*tathā nṛtyaty asmiṁs tad anu jaratī-veśa-rasiko*
*'vadhūto dhūtāṅgaḥ palita-lalitākīrṇa-cikuraḥ |*
*praviṣṭas tv āviṣṭaḥ parama-paramonmāda-vivaśas*
*tadā chittvā bhittvā naṭati jaratī-bhūmika-rucim ||21||*

*Word for word:* *tathā* — thus; *nṛtyati* — while [He] was dancing; *asmin* — He; *tat anu* — after that; *jaratī* — of an old woman; *veśa* — the costume; *rasikaḥ* — relishing; *avadhūtaḥ* — the Avadhuta; *dhūta* — shaking; *aṅgaḥ* — [whose] body; *palita* — grey; *lalita* — charmingly; *ākīrṇa* — dishevelled; *cikuraḥ* — [whose] hair; *praviṣṭaḥ* — having entered; *tu* — and; *āviṣṭaḥ* — possessed; *parama-parama* — by the very greatest; *unmāda* — madness; *vivaśaḥ* — overpowered; *tadā* — then; *chittvā* — tearing; *bhittvā* — breaking; *naṭati* — dances; *jaratī* — of the old woman; *bhūmika* — of the role; *rucim* — the appearance.

**21.** While He was dancing thus, there entered after Him the Avadhuta, relishing the costume of an old woman, His body shaking, His grey hair charmingly dishevelled. Having entered, possessed, overpowered by the very greatest madness, He then danced, tearing and breaking the appearance of the old woman whose role He played.

*Note.* The Avadhuta is Nityananda.

### Verse 22

निवृत्तेऽस्मिंस्तैस्तैः कलितललनाभूमिकरुचि-
र्गदाधृक्संज्ञोऽसौ धृतवलयशङ्खोज्ज्वलकरः ।
प्रविष्टो गायद्भिर्लघु लघु मृदङ्गेऽतिमुखरे
तथा तालैर्मानैर्नटनकलया तत्र विबभौ ॥२२॥

*nivṛtte 'smiṁs taiḥ taiḥ kalita-lalanā-bhūmika-rucir*
*gadādhṛk-saṁjño 'sau dhṛta-valaya-śaṅkhojjvala-karaḥ |*
*praviṣṭo gāyadbhir laghu laghu mṛdaṅge 'timukhare*
*tathā tālair mānair naṭana-kalayā tatra vibabhau ||22||*

*Word for word:* *nivṛtte* — when [He] had finished; *asmin* — He; *taiḥ taiḥ* — with all those [adornments]; *kalita* — having assumed; *lalanā* — of a woman; *bhūmika* — of the role; *ruciḥ* — the appearance; *gadādhṛk* — Gadadhara; *saṁjñaḥ* — named; *asau* — he; *dhṛta* — worn; *valaya* — with bangles; *śaṅkha* — of conch-shell; *ujjvala* — shining; *karaḥ* — [whose] hands; *praviṣṭaḥ* — entered; *gāyadbhiḥ* — with singers; *laghu laghu* — very swiftly; *mṛdaṅge* — when the mridanga; *ati* — very; *mukhare* — resounded; *tathā* — and; *tālaiḥ* — with rhythms; *mānaiḥ* — with measures; *naṭana* — of dancing; *kalayā* — with the art; *tatra* — there; *vibabhau* — shone.

**22.** When He had finished, the one named Gadadhara entered with the singers, having assumed the appearance of a woman's role with all its adornments, his hands shining with bangles of conch-shell. As the mridanga resounded very swiftly and loudly, he shone there with rhythm, measure and the art of dancing.

### Verse 23

तदा नृत्यत्यस्मिन् धृतमधुरवेशोज्ज्वलरुचौ
मृदङ्गालीभङ्गीशतमधुरसङ्गीतकलया ।
जनैर्भूयोभूयः सुखजलधिमग्नैर्निर्निमिषैः
समन्तादासेदे जडिमजडिताङ्गैः किममृतम् ॥२३॥

*tadā nṛtyaty asmin dhṛta-madhura-veśojjvala-rucau*
*mṛdaṅgālī-bhaṅgī-śata-madhura-saṅgīta-kalayā |*
*janair bhūyo bhūyaḥ sukha-jaladhi-magnair nirnimiṣaiḥ*
*samantād āsede jaḍima-jaḍitāṅgaiḥ kim amṛtam ||23||*

*Word for word:* *tadā* — then; *nṛtyati* — while [he] was dancing; *asmin* — he; *dhṛta* — worn; *madhura* — sweet; *veśa* — of the costume; *ujjvala* — shining; *rucau* — [with] the splendour; *mṛdaṅga* — of mridangas; *ālī* — of a row; *bhaṅgī* — of modulations; *śata* — with a hundred; *madhura* — sweet; *saṅgīta* — of music; *kalayā* — with the art; *janaiḥ* — by the people; *bhūyaḥ bhūyaḥ* — again and again; *sukha* — of bliss; *jaladhi* — in the ocean; *magnaiḥ* — immersed; *nirnimiṣaiḥ* — unblinking; *samantāt* — all around; *āsede* — was attained; *jaḍima* — by numbness; *jaḍita* — stiffened; *aṅgaiḥ* — [with] limbs; *kim* — was not …?; *amṛtam* — nectar.

**23.** As he danced then, shining with the splendour of his sweet costume, to the art of sweet music with a hundred modulations from a row of mridangas, was not nectar attained by the people all around — immersed again and again in an ocean of bliss, unblinking, their limbs stiffened with numbness?

### Verse 24

प्रियावेशावेशस्फुरितरुचिरुद्यत्स्मितरुचा
परिध्वस्तध्वान्ता निभृतरभसास्वादविवशा ।
घनस्निग्धाभुग्नोल्लसितकबरीभारविलसत् (विगलत्)
प्रसूनैरम्भोदोद्गतभगणशोभां विदधती ॥२४॥

*priyā-veśāveśa-sphurita-rucir udyat-smita-rucā*
*paridhvasta-dhvāntā nibhṛta-rabhasāsvāda-vivaśā |*
*ghana-snigdhābhugnollasita-kabarī-bhāra-vilasat (vigalat)*
*prasūnair ambhododgata-bhagaṇa-śobhāṁ vidadhatī ||24||*

*Word for word:* *priyā* — of the Beloved; *veśa* — into the guise; *āveśa* — from absorption; *sphurita* — flashing forth; *ruciḥ* — [whose] splendour; *udyat* — rising; *smita* — of a smile; *rucā* — by the radiance; *paridhvasta* — dispelled; *dhvāntā* — [by whom] darkness; *nibhṛta* — with secret; *rabhasa* — ardour; *āsvāda* — of relishing; *vivaśā* — overpowered; *ghana* — of thick; *snigdha* — glossy; *ābhugna* — curving; *ullasita* — luxuriant; *kabarī* — of braids; *bhāra* — from the mass; *vilasat* (*vigalat*) — shining (falling); *prasūnaiḥ* — with flowers; *ambhoda* — from a cloud; *udgata* — emerging; *bha* — of stars; *gaṇa* — of a host; *śobhām* — the beauty; *vidadhatī* — displaying.

**24.** [Then the Lord Himself entered.] His splendour flashed forth from His absorption in the guise of the Beloved; the radiance of His dawning smile dispelled the darkness; He was overpowered by the secret ardour of relishing. With the flowers shining in the mass of His thick, glossy, curving, luxuriant braids, He displayed the beauty of a host of stars emerging from a cloud.

*Note.* From this verse onwards Gaura is described in a woman's guise. The attributes stand in the feminine, since it is the role that is described. The edition gives a variant: *vilasat* or *vigalat* ("falling"). The subject and the verb of the long description come in verse 34, at the end of the *kulaka* (verses 24–34): "this form … manifested the mood of Lakshmi, and then of Girija — and entered the shrine room".

### Verse 25

विलोलभ्रूभङ्गी नटनजितभृङ्गीविलसिता
स्मितापाङ्गी राजत्कुवलयदला लोलनयना ।
वहन्ती सत्ताम्रस्फुरदधरवीथीविलुठितां
रदच्छायां ज्योत्स्नामिव नवदिनेशांशुमिलिताम् ॥२५॥

*vilola-bhrū-bhaṅgī naṭana-jita-bhṛṅgī-vilasitā*
*smitāpāṅgī rājat-kuvalaya-dalā lola-nayanā |*
*vahantī sat-tāmra-sphurad-adhara-vīthī-viluṭhitāṁ*
*rada-cchāyāṁ jyotsnām iva nava-dineśāṁśu-militām ||25||*

*Word for word:* *vilola* — playful; *bhrū* — of the brows; *bhaṅgī* — [with] arching; *naṭana* — by dancing; *jita* — surpassed; *bhṛṅgī* — of the bee; *vilasitā* — [whose] sportiveness; *smita* — smiling; *apāṅgī* — [with] the corners of the eyes; *rājat* — of shining; *kuvalaya* — blue lotuses; *dalā* — [like] the petals; *lola* — lively; *nayanā* — [with] eyes; *vahantī* — bearing; *sat* — pure; *tāmra* — [like] copper; *sphurat* — gleaming; *adhara* — of the lips; *vīthī* — along the path; *viluṭhitām* — gliding; *rada* — of the teeth; *chāyām* — the lustre; *jyotsnām* — moonlight; *iva* — like; *nava* — of the new; *dina-īśa* — sun; *aṁśu* — with the rays; *militām* — mingled.

**25.** [His was] the playful arching of the brows, whose dancing surpassed the sportiveness of a bee; the smiling corners of the lively eyes, like the petals of shining blue lotuses; and He bore the lustre of the teeth gliding along the path of the lips, gleaming like pure copper — like moonlight mingled with the rays of the rising sun.

### Verse 26

स्फुरत्कम्बुग्रीवापरिसरविलासप्रणयिना
गुरूरोजद्वन्द्वोपरि घनविलोलत्वमयता ।
गिरेरुच्चैःपाताहितभयनिवृत्तेन खधुनी-
प्रवाहेणेवाति श्रियममलहारेण दधती ॥२६॥

*sphurat-kambu-grīvā-parisara-vilāsa-praṇayinā*
*gurūroja-dvandvopari ghana-vilolatvam ayatā |*
*girer uccaiḥ-pātāhita-bhaya-nivṛttena kha-dhunī-*
*pravāheṇevāti śriyam amala-hāreṇa dadhatī ||26||*

*Word for word:* *sphurat* — gleaming; *kambu* — [like] a conch; *grīvā* — of the neck; *parisara* — about the vicinity; *vilāsa* — play; *praṇayinā* — loving; *guru* — full; *uroja* — of the bosom; *dvandva* — the pair; *upari* — above; *ghana* — strongly; *vilolatvam* — swaying; *ayatā* — taking on; *gireḥ* — from a mountain; *uccaiḥ* — high; *pāta* — by the fall; *āhita* — caused; *bhaya* — from the fear; *nivṛttena* — freed; *kha* — of the sky; *dhunī* — of the river; *pravāheṇa* — by the current; *iva* — like; *ati* — great; *śriyam* — beauty; *amala* — by a spotless; *hāreṇa* — necklace; *dadhatī* — bearing.

**26.** He bore great beauty by a spotless necklace: it loved to play about the gleaming, conch-like neck and swayed strongly over the full bosom, like the current of the river of the sky, freed from the fear of a fall from a high mountain.

*Note.* According to tradition the Ganga descends from heaven upon the head of Shiva, on Mount Kailasa. The necklace resting on the "hills" of the bosom is like the Ganga, no longer threatened by a fall.

### Verse 27

वहन्त्यूरुद्वन्द्वं कनककदलीकाण्डमसृणं
पदे रक्ताम्भोजप्रथमसदवस्थाप्रणयिनी ।
तनुक्षौमं वासः परिहितवती तत्र ललितं
प्रभोः श्रीमन्मूर्तिर्लघुपदमथैषा निविविशे ॥२७॥ (कुलकम्)

*vahanty ūru-dvandvaṁ kanaka-kadalī-kāṇḍa-masṛṇaṁ*
*pade raktāmbhoja-prathama-sad-avasthā-praṇayinī |*
*tanu-kṣaumaṁ vāsaḥ parihitavatī tatra lalitaṁ*
*prabhoḥ śrīman-mūrtir laghu-padam athaiṣā niviviśe ||27|| (kulakam)*

*Word for word:* *vahantī* — bearing; *ūru* — of thighs; *dvandvam* — a pair; *kanaka* — of a golden; *kadalī* — plantain; *kāṇḍa* — [like] the stems; *masṛṇam* — smooth; *pade* — the two feet; *rakta* — of a red; *ambhoja* — lotus; *prathama* — first; *sat* — fair; *avasthā* — [of] the stage; *praṇayinī* — fond [of]; *tanu* — fine; *kṣaumam* — linen; *vāsaḥ* — a garment; *parihitavatī* — having put on; *tatra* — there; *lalitam* — gracefully; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *śrīmat* — the beautiful; *mūrtiḥ* — form; *laghu* — with a light; *padam* — step; *atha* — then; *eṣā* — this; *niviviśe* — entered.

**27.** With thighs smooth as the stems of a golden plantain, with feet akin to a red lotus in the first fair stage [of its blossoming], gracefully clad in a fine linen garment — thus the beautiful form of the Lord then entered there with a light step.

*Note.* The edition marks a *kulaka* here (verses 24–27): the subject of the whole description is *prabhoḥ śrīman-mūrtiḥ* ("the beautiful form of the Lord", feminine), and therefore all the attributes stand in the feminine.

### Verse 28

तदा पीयूषांशुः परिणत इवैकादशकलो

तथा तत्क्षौमाञ्चलललितखेलां विरचयन्
ववौ मन्दं तत्तत्परिमलसखश्चन्दनमरुत् ॥२८॥

*tadā pīyūṣāṁśuḥ pariṇata ivaikādaśa-kalo*
*rarāja śrī-mūrtau rahasi vilasantyāṁ sukha-paraḥ |*
*tathā tat-kṣaumāñcala-lalita-khelāṁ viracayan*
*vavau mandaṁ tat-tat-parimala-sakhaś candana-marut ||28||*

*Word for word:* *tadā* — then; *pīyūṣa* — nectar-; *aṁśuḥ* — rayed (the moon); *pariṇataḥ* — having reached; *iva* — as if; *ekādaśa* — the eleventh; *kalaḥ* — [whose] digit; *rarāja* — shone; *śrī-mūrtau* — when the beautiful form; *rahasi* — in seclusion; *vilasantyām* — was sporting; *sukha* — to bliss; *paraḥ* — given; *tathā* — and; *tat* — of that; *kṣauma* — linen [garment]; *añcala* — with the hem; *lalita* — graceful; *khelām* — play; *viracayan* — making; *vavau* — blew; *mandam* — gently; *tat-tat* — of all those; *parimala* — fragrances; *sakhaḥ* — the friend; *candana* — sandal-scented; *marut* — breeze.

**28.** Then, while the beautiful form was sporting in seclusion, the nectar-rayed moon shone blissfully, as if it had reached its eleventh digit. And the sandal-scented breeze, the friend of all those fragrances, blew gently, playing gracefully with the hem of that linen garment.

*Note.* The moon is divided into sixteen digits (*kalā*). "The eleventh digit" may be a hint at the night of Ekadashi (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 29

ततस्तैर्गायद्भिर्लघु लघु मृदङ्गध्वनिपरं

तथा भज्यन्मध्या मधुरिमपरीपाकविलस-
त्पदन्यासैः शिञ्जन्मणिमयतुलाकोटिमधुरा ॥२९॥

*tatas tair gāyadbhir laghu laghu mṛdaṅga-dhvani-paraṁ*
*sahāvaṁ nṛtyantī laya-valita-tālādi-lalitam |*
*tathā bhajyan-madhyā madhurima-parīpāka-vilasat-*
*pada-nyāsaiḥ śiñjan-maṇimaya-tulākoṭi-madhurā ||29||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *taiḥ* — with those; *gāyadbhiḥ* — singers; *laghu laghu* — very swiftly; *mṛdaṅga* — of the mridanga; *dhvani* — the sound; *param* — following; *sa* — with; *hāvam* — charming gestures; *nṛtyantī* — dancing; *laya* — with tempo; *valita* — interwoven; *tāla* — rhythm; *ādi* — and the rest; *lalitam* — gracefully; *tathā* — and; *bhajyat* — bending; *madhyā* — [whose] waist; *madhurima* — of sweetness; *parīpāka* — with the ripeness; *vilasat* — shining; *pada* — of the feet; *nyāsaiḥ* — with the placings; *śiñjat* — tinkling; *maṇi-maya* — jewelled; *tulākoṭi* — with anklets; *madhurā* — sweet.

**29.** Then, with those singers, following the swift sound of the mridanga, [the form] danced gracefully, with charming gestures, interweaving rhythm and the rest with the tempo. The waist bent, and the steps, shining with the ripeness of sweetness, were sweet with the tinkling of jewelled anklets.

### Verse 30

तथा वक्त्राम्भोजं लघुसमुदयत्स्वेदकणिका-
विकाशं मुक्ताभिः खचितमिव चामीकरविधुम् ।
वहन्ती सिन्दूरं विलसदलिके रुच्यदलके
तमःस्पृष्टं सन्ध्यारुणितमिव रम्यार्ककिरणम् ॥३०॥

*tathā vaktrāmbhojaṁ laghu-samudayat-sveda-kaṇikā-*
*vikāśaṁ muktābhiḥ khacitam iva cāmīkara-vidhum |*
*vahantī sindūraṁ vilasad-alike rucyad-alake*
*tamaḥ-spṛṣṭaṁ sandhyāruṇitam iva ramyārka-kiraṇam ||30||*

*Word for word:* *tathā* — and; *vaktra* — of the face; *ambhojam* — the lotus; *laghu* — lightly; *samudayat* — rising; *sveda* — of perspiration; *kaṇikā* — with drops; *vikāśam* — open; *muktābhiḥ* — with pearls; *khacitam* — studded; *iva* — like; *cāmīkara* — a golden; *vidhum* — moon; *vahantī* — bearing; *sindūram* — vermilion; *vilasat* — on the shining; *alike* — forehead; *rucyat* — with charming; *alake* — [framed by] curls; *tamaḥ* — by darkness; *spṛṣṭam* — touched; *sandhyā* — by twilight; *aruṇitam* — reddened; *iva* — like; *ramya* — a lovely; *arka* — of the sun; *kiraṇam* — ray.

**30.** And He bore the lotus of His face, open, with drops of perspiration lightly rising on it, like a golden moon studded with pearls; and on the shining forehead, framed by charming curls, He bore vermilion, like a lovely ray of the sun reddened by twilight and touched by darkness.

*Note.* Vermilion (*sindūra*) on the forehead and in the parting of the hair is the mark of a married woman. The edition has *रुज्यदलके*; we read *rucyad-alake* (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 31

तथा पाणिन्यासैः कलितवलयध्वानमुखरै-
रलिश्रेणीमुच्चैरुपरि परिलोलां विदधती ।
उदञ्चद्भ्रूवल्लीं मनसिजधनुष्काण्डकुटिलां
मुहुः क्षिप्त्वा श्यामं किमपि विदधत्यम्बरतलम् ॥३१॥

*tathā pāṇi-nyāsaiḥ kalita-valaya-dhvāna-mukharair*
*ali-śreṇīm uccair upari parilolāṁ vidadhatī |*
*udañcad-bhrū-vallīṁ manasija-dhanuṣ-kāṇḍa-kuṭilāṁ*
*muhuḥ kṣiptvā śyāmaṁ kim api vidadhaty ambara-talam ||31||*

*Word for word:* *tathā* — and; *pāṇi* — of the hands; *nyāsaiḥ* — with the movements; *kalita* — produced; *valaya* — of bangles; *dhvāna* — with the jingling; *mukharaiḥ* — resonant; *ali* — of bees; *śreṇīm* — a line; *uccaiḥ* — high; *upari* — above; *parilolām* — circling; *vidadhatī* — making; *udañcat* — rising; *bhrū* — of the brows; *vallīm* — the creeper; *manasija* — of Manasija; *dhanuḥ* — of the bow; *kāṇḍa* — [like] the shaft; *kuṭilām* — curved; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *kṣiptvā* — having raised; *śyāmam* — dark; *kim api* — somehow; *vidadhatī* — making; *ambara* — of the sky; *talam* — the vault.

**31.** With movements of the hands, resonant with the jingling of bangles, He made a line of bees circle high above; and, raising again and again the creeper of the brows, curved like the bow of Manasija, He somehow darkened the vault of the sky.

*Note.* Manasija, "the mind-born", is Kama.

### Verse 32

स्खलद्वक्षःक्षौमाञ्चलहतिलसन्मध्यमलसं
वलीभङ्गैर्भङ्गीगरिम नटयन्ती करमितम् ।
श्लथन्नीवीबन्धच्छुरितविमलद्योतिकलया
नितम्बस्वेदार्द्रं घनजघनमन्यादृशमिव ॥३२॥

*skhalad-vakṣaḥ-kṣaumāñcala-hati-lasan-madhyam alasaṁ*
*valī-bhaṅgair bhaṅgī-garima naṭayantī kara-mitam |*
*ślathan-nīvī-bandha-cchurita-vimala-dyoti-kalayā*
*nitamba-svedārdraṁ ghana-jaghanam anyādṛśam iva ||32||*

*Word for word:* *skhalat* — slipping; *vakṣaḥ* — from the bosom; *kṣauma* — of the linen [garment]; *añcala* — of the hem; *hati* — by the strokes; *lasat* — gleaming; *madhyam* — the waist; *alasam* — languid; *valī* — of the folds; *bhaṅgaiḥ* — with the curves; *bhaṅgī* — of grace; *garima* — with weight; *naṭayantī* — making dance; *kara* — by the hand; *mitam* — measurable; *ślathat* — loosening; *nīvī* — of the sash; *bandha* — of the knot; *churita* — glinting; *vimala* — of pure; *dyoti* — radiance; *kalayā* — with a gleam; *nitamba* — of the hips; *sveda* — with perspiration; *ārdram* — moist; *ghana* — full; *jaghanam* — the hips; *anyādṛśam* — of another kind; *iva* — as if.

**32.** He made the languid waist dance — so slender that a hand could span it — gleaming under the strokes of the hem of the linen garment as it slipped from the bosom, and weighty in grace with the curves of its folds; and the full hips, moist with perspiration, in the gleam of pure radiance glinting from beneath the loosening knot of the sash, seemed as if of quite another kind.

*Note.* *Kara-mitam*, "measured by the hand", is taken here of the slender waist that a hand can span (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 33

मुहुश्चक्रप्रायभ्रमणविगलत्केशकुसुमै-
स्तथा भ्राम्यद्भृङ्गीललितपरभागैः प्रसृमरैः ।
स्वयं नृत्योल्लासादुपरि मुखचन्द्रस्य नु दधे
सितच्छत्रं चित्रं मरकतसुरेखाविलसितम् ॥३३॥

*muhuś cakra-prāya-bhramaṇa-vigalat-keśa-kusumais*
*tathā bhrāmyad-bhṛṅgī-lalita-parabhāgaiḥ prasṛmaraiḥ |*
*svayaṁ nṛtyollāsād upari mukha-candrasya nu dadhe*
*sitac-chatraṁ citraṁ marakata-surekhā-vilasitam ||33||*

*Word for word:* *muhuḥ* — again and again; *cakra* — a wheel; *prāya* — like; *bhramaṇa* — from whirling; *vigalat* — falling; *keśa* — from the hair; *kusumaiḥ* — with flowers; *tathā* — and; *bhrāmyat* — circling; *bhṛṅgī* — by bees; *lalita* — charmingly; *parabhāgaiḥ* — set off; *prasṛmaraiḥ* — scattering; *svayam* — Himself; *nṛtya* — of the dance; *ullāsāt* — out of the rapture; *upari* — above; *mukha* — of the face; *candrasya* — the moon; *nu* — did not …?; *dadhe* — hold; *sita* — white; *chatram* — a parasol; *citram* — wondrous; *marakata* — with emerald; *su-rekhā* — fine stripes; *vilasitam* — adorned.

**33.** Again and again, whirling like a wheel, He scattered the flowers falling from the hair, charmingly set off by the circling bees. Did He not Himself, in the rapture of the dance, hold above the moon of His face a wondrous white parasol adorned with fine emerald stripes?

*Note.* The white flowers circling above the head are the white parasol (an emblem of royalty); the dark bees are the emerald stripes upon it.

### Verse 34

तथा नृत्योन्मादप्रमदमधुरिम्णातिमहता
नताङ्गी सङ्गीतोज्ज्वलरुचिररोचिःपटलिका ।
ततो लक्ष्मीभावं तदनु गिरिजाभावमपि सा
क्रमादाविष्कृत्य प्रकटमविशद्देवभवनम् ॥३४॥
(एकादशभिः कुलकम्)

*tathā nṛtyonmāda-pramada-madhurimṇātimahatā*
*natāṅgī saṅgītojjvala-rucira-rociḥ-paṭalikā |*
*tato lakṣmī-bhāvaṁ tad-anu girijā-bhāvam api sā*
*kramād āviṣkṛtya prakaṭam aviśad deva-bhavanam ||34||*
*(ekādaśabhiḥ kulakam)*

*Word for word:* *tathā* — and; *nṛtya* — of the dance; *unmāda* — of the madness; *pramada* — of the rapture; *madhurimṇā* — by the sweetness; *ati-mahatā* — exceedingly great; *nata* — bowed; *aṅgī* — [whose] body; *saṅgīta* — by the music; *ujjvala* — illumined; *rucira* — lovely; *rociḥ* — of radiance; *paṭalikā* — [with] a veil; *tataḥ* — then; *lakṣmī* — of Lakshmi; *bhāvam* — the mood; *tat-anu* — after that; *girijā* — of Girija (Parvati); *bhāvam* — the mood; *api* — also; *sā* — that (form); *kramāt* — in turn; *āviṣkṛtya* — having manifested; *prakaṭam* — openly; *aviśat* — entered; *deva* — of the Deity; *bhavanam* — the chamber.

**34.** And, His body bowed by the exceedingly great sweetness of the rapture and madness of the dance, veiled in a lovely radiance illumined by the music, that form manifested in turn first the mood of Lakshmi and then that of Girija as well — and openly entered the shrine room. *(A kulaka of eleven verses.)*

*Note.* Verses 24–34 form one *kulaka*. Cf. Chaitanya-bhagavata, Madhya 18: the Lord in the mood of Rukmini (verses 70–98), then He enters in the form of the Original Shakti (Adya-shakti, verses 120–154) and sits as Mahalakshmi (verse 163). Girija, "the daughter of the mountain", is Parvati.

### Verse 35

ततस्तां ते नत्वा स्तुतिवचनभङ्गीविरचनै-
र्महत्याः खट्वाया उपरि सरसाङ्गीं स्थितवतीम् ।
विधेहि प्रेमाणं भगवति समन्तादिति जगु-
स्ततोऽङ्के सा चक्रे झटिति हरिदासं शिशुमिव ॥३५॥

*tatas tāṁ te natvā stuti-vacana-bhaṅgī-viracanair*
*mahatyāḥ khaṭvāyā upari sarasāṅgīṁ sthitavatīm |*
*vidhehi premāṇaṁ bhagavati samantād iti jagus*
*tato 'ṅke sā cakre jhaṭiti haridāsaṁ śiśum iva ||35||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *tām* — to Her; *te* — they; *natvā* — having bowed; *stuti* — of praise; *vacana* — of words; *bhaṅgī* — with artful; *viracanaiḥ* — compositions; *mahatyāḥ* — large; *khaṭvāyāḥ* — a couch; *upari* — upon; *sa-rasa* — full of rasa; *aṅgīm* — [whose] form; *sthitavatīm* — seated; *vidhehi* — bestow; *premāṇam* — love; *bhagavati* — O Goddess; *samantāt* — everywhere; *iti* — thus; *jaguḥ* — sang; *tataḥ* — then; *aṅke* — on the lap; *sā* — She; *cakre* — placed; *jhaṭiti* — at once; *haridāsam* — Haridasa; *śiśum* — a child; *iva* — like.

**35.** Then they bowed to Her, who was seated upon a large couch, Her form full of rasa, and with artful words of praise they sang: "O Goddess, bestow love everywhere!" Then She at once took Haridasa on Her lap like a child.

*Note.* The edition has *खट्टायाः*; the usual form is *khaṭvāyāḥ* ("couch"). Cf. the Chaitanya-bhagavata (Madhya 18.203–208): the Lord in the form of the Mother of the universe feeds the devotees at Her breast like Her children.

### Verse 36

इतीदं सा नानाविधकुतुकचेष्टाविलसितै-
र्निशां नीत्वा प्रातः स्वभवनमगाच्चित्रचरितः ।
तदा भूयस्तस्मिन्नकृत बहु नृत्यं सुमधुरं
महस्वान् सप्ताहं मलयजरसैश्चर्चिततनुः ॥३६॥

*itīdaṁ sā nānā-vidha-kutuka-ceṣṭā-vilasitair*
*niśāṁ nītvā prātaḥ sva-bhavanam agāc citra-caritaḥ |*
*tadā bhūyas tasminn akṛta bahu nṛtyaṁ sumadhuraṁ*
*mahasvān saptāhaṁ malayaja-rasaiś carcita-tanuḥ ||36||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *idam* — this; *sā* — She; *nānā-vidha* — various; *kutuka* — playful; *ceṣṭā* — with acts; *vilasitaiḥ* — [and] pastimes; *niśām* — the night; *nītvā* — having spent; *prātaḥ* — in the morning; *sva* — to His own; *bhavanam* — home; *agāt* — went; *citra* — wondrous; *caritaḥ* — [whose] deeds; *tadā* — then; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *tasmin* — there; *akṛta* — performed; *bahu* — many; *nṛtyam* — dances; *su-madhuram* — most sweet; *mahasvān* — the radiant [Lord]; *saptāham* — for seven days; *malayaja* — of sandalwood; *rasaiḥ* — with the pulp; *carcita* — anointed; *tanuḥ* — [whose] body.

**36.** Having thus spent the night in various playful acts and pastimes, She — He whose deeds are wondrous — went home in the morning. And then for seven days the radiant [Lord], His body anointed with sandal-paste, again performed many most sweet dances there.

*Note.* The change of gender (*sā*, "She" — *citra-caritaḥ*, "He") reflects the Lord's stepping out of the role.

### Verse 37

समन्तादुच्चैर्दिशि दिशि मृदङ्गादिनिनदा
मदोन्मत्ताः सर्वे कति कति रसाढ्यं न जगदुः ।
प्रसूनैः स्रग्गन्धैर्मलयजरसैः पूर्णमभव-
ज्जगत् सप्ताहं श्रीमति विलसति श्रीभगवति ॥३७॥

*samantād uccair diśi diśi mṛdaṅgādi-ninadā*
*madonmattāḥ sarve kati kati rasāḍhyaṁ na jagaduḥ |*
*prasūnaiḥ srag-gandhair malayaja-rasaiḥ pūrṇam abhavaj*
*jagat saptāhaṁ śrīmati vilasati śrī-bhagavati ||37||*

*Word for word:* *samantāt* — all around; *uccaiḥ* — loudly; *diśi diśi* — in every direction; *mṛdaṅga* — of mridangas; *ādi* — and other [instruments]; *ninadāḥ* — the sounds; *mada* — with rapture; *unmattāḥ* — intoxicated; *sarve* — all; *kati kati* — how much; *rasa-āḍhyam* — rich in rasa; *na* — not; *jagaduḥ* — uttered; *prasūnaiḥ* — with flowers; *srak* — with garlands; *gandhaiḥ* — with perfumes; *malayaja* — of sandalwood; *rasaiḥ* — with the pulp; *pūrṇam* — full; *abhavat* — became; *jagat* — the world; *saptāham* — for seven days; *śrīmati* — when the beautiful; *vilasati* — was sporting; *śrī-bhagavati* — Sri Bhagavan.

**37.** All around, loudly, in every direction [rang] the sounds of mridangas and other [instruments]. All were intoxicated with rapture — how much, rich in rasa, did they not utter! For seven days, while the beautiful Sri Bhagavan was sporting, the world was full of flowers, garlands, perfumes and sandal-paste.

### Verse 38

तथा सप्ताहान्ते दिनकरशतप्रायमहसा
स्फुरन्तं श्रीवासः सभयचकितोल्लासमवदत् ।
कलौ नाम्नां गाथा यदिह विहिता तत्र ननु किं
फलं नूनं शाठ्ये भवति किमु वा नेति वद तत् ॥३८॥

*tathā saptāhānte dinakara-śata-prāya-mahasā*
*sphurantaṁ śrīvāsaḥ sabhaya-cakitollāsam avadat |*
*kalau nāmnāṁ gāthā yad iha vihitā tatra nanu kiṁ*
*phalaṁ nūnaṁ śāṭhye bhavati kim u vā neti vada tat ||38||*

*Word for word:* *tathā* — then; *sapta-aha* — of the seven days; *ante* — at the end; *dinakara* — of suns; *śata* — a hundred; *prāya* — like; *mahasā* — with effulgence; *sphurantam* — to [Him] shining; *śrīvāsaḥ* — Srivasa; *sa* — with; *bhaya* — awe; *cakita* — wonder; *ullāsam* — [and] joy; *avadat* — said; *kalau* — in Kali; *nāmnām* — of the names; *gāthā* — the chanting; *yat* — which; *iha* — here; *vihitā* — has been ordained; *tatra* — in it; *nanu* — pray; *kim* — whether; *phalam* — fruit; *nūnam* — surely; *śāṭhye* — with guile; *bhavati* — comes; *kim u vā* — or; *na* — not; *iti* — thus; *vada* — tell; *tat* — that.

**38.** Then, at the end of the seven days, Srivasa, with awe, wonder and joy, said to Him who shone with the effulgence of a hundred suns: "The chanting of the names that has been ordained here in [the age of] Kali — pray, does it surely bear fruit when [performed] with guile, or not? Tell me that."

*Note.* *Śāṭhye*, "with guile", is taken as "when [the names are chanted] insincerely" (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 39

कृते त्रेतायां च द्विज तदनु द्वापरयुगे
समस्तं ध्यानाद्यैर्भवति नितरां साधिततमम् ।
कलौ तत्राशक्तिं स्वयमिह विलोक्य प्रकटितं
प्रभुर्नामाख्योऽभूत्तदिह किमिव न्यूनफलता ॥३९॥

*kṛte tretāyāṁ ca dvija tad-anu dvāpara-yuge*
*samastaṁ dhyānādyair bhavati nitarāṁ sādhitatamam |*
*kalau tatrāśaktiṁ svayam iha vilokya prakaṭitaṁ*
*prabhur nāmākhyo 'bhūt tad iha kim iva nyūna-phalatā ||39||*

*Word for word:* *kṛte* — in the Krita; *tretāyām* — in the Treta; *ca* — and; *dvija* — O brahmana; *tat-anu* — after that; *dvāpara-yuge* — in the Dvapara-yuga; *samastam* — everything; *dhyāna* — by meditation; *ādyaiḥ* — and the rest; *bhavati* — is; *nitarām* — fully; *sādhitatamam* — accomplished; *kalau* — in Kali; *tatra* — for that; *aśaktim* — the incapacity; *svayam* — Himself; *iha* — here; *vilokya* — having seen; *prakaṭitam* — manifestly; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *nāma* — the Name; *ākhyaḥ* — called; *abhūt* — became; *tat* — so; *iha* — here; *kim iva* — how then; *nyūna* — small; *phalatā* — fruitfulness.

**39.** "O brahmana, in the Krita, in the Treta, and after that in the Dvapara-yuga, everything is fully accomplished by meditation and the rest. Seeing [people's] incapacity for that in Kali, the Lord Himself manifestly became here that which is called the Name — how, then, could its fruit be small here?"

*Note.* Cf. Bhagavatam 12.3.52: "What was attained in the Krita by meditation on Vishnu, in the Treta by sacrifices, in the Dvapara by temple worship, is attained in Kali by the chanting of [the names of] Hari."

### Verse 40

वदन्नेवं गौरो नयनजलपूर्णोऽन्यदवद-
न्न शक्तोऽहं स्थातुं गृहमभि गमिष्यामि नियतम् ।
तदाकर्ण्य प्रोचे यदपि भगवन् कर्तुमुचितं
जनान् दृष्ट्वा नैवं मतमिति मुरारिः सचकितम् ॥४०॥

*vadann evaṁ gauro nayana-jala-pūrṇo 'nyad avadan*
*na śakto 'haṁ sthātuṁ gṛham abhi gamiṣyāmi niyatam |*
*tad ākarṇya proce yad api bhagavan kartum ucitaṁ*
*janān dṛṣṭvā naivaṁ matam iti murāriḥ sacakitam ||40||*

*Word for word:* *vadan* — speaking; *evam* — thus; *gauraḥ* — Gaura; *nayana* — of the eyes; *jala* — with tears; *pūrṇaḥ* — filled; *anyat* — something else; *avadat* — said; *na* — not; *śaktaḥ* — able; *aham* — I; *sthātum* — to stay; *gṛham abhi* — towards home; *gamiṣyāmi* — I shall go; *niyatam* — certainly; *tat* — that; *ākarṇya* — having heard; *proce* — said; *yat api* — although; *bhagavan* — O Lord; *kartum* — to do; *ucitam* — fitting; *janān* — at the people; *dṛṣṭvā* — looking; *na* — not; *evam* — so; *matam* — [is our] opinion; *iti* — thus; *murāriḥ* — Murari; *sa* — with; *cakitam* — alarm.

**40.** Having spoken thus, Gaura, His eyes filled with tears, said something else: "I am not able to stay. I shall certainly go home." Hearing that, Murari said in alarm: "O Lord, although it is fitting for You to do [so], looking at the people we do not think so."

*Note.* Evidently a hint at the intention to accept sannyasa. "Home" may also mean the Lord's true abode. *Gṛham abhi* may also be construed with *sthātum*: "I am not able to stay at home; I shall certainly go [away]" (?).

### Verse 41

ततोऽन्येद्युः श्रीमान्नयनजलधौतः समवद-
द्द्विजैकः स्वप्ने मे श्रुतिमभि महावाक्यमवदत् ।
अतो हेतोर्हित्वा प्रभुचरणमन्यत् किमुचितं
ममेति क्रन्दामि क्षणमपि न मे निर्वृतिरिह ॥४१॥

*tato 'nyedyuḥ śrīmān nayana-jala-dhautaḥ samavadad*
*dvijaikaḥ svapne me śrutim abhi mahā-vākyam avadat |*
*ato hetor hitvā prabhu-caraṇam anyat kim ucitaṁ*
*mameti krandāmi kṣaṇam api na me nirvṛtir iha ||41||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *anyedyuḥ* — on the next day; *śrīmān* — the beautiful [Lord]; *nayana* — of the eyes; *jala* — with the tears; *dhautaḥ* — bathed; *samavadat* — said; *dvija* — brahmana; *ekaḥ* — a certain; *svapne* — in a dream; *me* — to Me; *śrutim abhi* — into the ear; *mahā-vākyam* — the great saying; *avadat* — spoke; *ataḥ hetoḥ* — for this reason; *hitvā* — having left; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *caraṇam* — the feet; *anyat* — else; *kim* — what; *ucitam* — fitting; *mama* — for Me; *iti* — thus; *krandāmi* — I weep; *kṣaṇam api* — even for a moment; *na* — no; *me* — for Me; *nirvṛtiḥ* — peace; *iha* — here.

**41.** Then, on the next day, the beautiful [Lord], bathed in tears, said: "A certain brahmana spoke the great saying into My ear in a dream. For this reason I weep, [thinking]: 'Having left the feet of the Lord, what else is fitting for Me?' There is no peace for Me here even for a moment."

*Note.* *Mahā-vākya* — the Upanishadic "great saying" (*tat tvam asi*, "you are That"), imparted at initiation into sannyasa. Cf. the account of this dream in Murari Gupta (2.18.1–6).

### Verse 42

इति श्रुत्वा गुप्तः सपदि स मुरारिः समवद-
त्प्रभो तत् षष्ठीतत्पुरुषवचनं तत्र कुरु भोः ।
तथा श्रुत्वा नाथः समुदितमनाः साम्प्रतमभू-
त्तथा ते च श्रुत्वा व्यथितमनसो गाढमभवन् ॥४२॥

*iti śrutvā guptaḥ sapadi sa murāriḥ samavadat*
*prabho tat ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa-vacanaṁ tatra kuru bhoḥ |*
*tathā śrutvā nāthaḥ samudita-manāḥ sāmpratam abhūt*
*tathā te ca śrutvā vyathita-manaso gāḍham abhavan ||42||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *śrutvā* — having heard; *guptaḥ* — Gupta; *sapadi* — at once; *saḥ* — that; *murāriḥ* — Murari; *samavadat* — said; *prabho* — O Lord; *tat* — that; *ṣaṣṭhī* — a genitive; *tatpuruṣa* — *tatpuruṣa*; *vacanam* — word; *tatra* — there; *kuru* — make; *bhoḥ* — O [Lord]; *tathā* — thus; *śrutvā* — having heard; *nāthaḥ* — the Master; *samudita* — gladdened; *manāḥ* — [whose] heart; *sāmpratam* — then; *abhūt* — became; *tathā* — but; *te* — they; *ca* — and; *śrutvā* — having heard; *vyathita* — pained; *manasaḥ* — [whose] hearts; *gāḍham* — deeply; *abhavan* — became.

**42.** Hearing this, Murari Gupta at once said: "O Lord, take that word there as a genitive *tatpuruṣa*!" Hearing this, the Master was then gladdened at heart; but the others, hearing [it all], were deeply pained at heart.

*Note.* Murari proposes a Vaishnava reading of *tat tvam asi*: not "you are That", but, as a genitive *tatpuruṣa*, *tasya tvam asi*, "you are His", that is, you are the servant of the Lord. The devotees grieve, understanding that the Lord is thinking of sannyasa.

### Verse 43

ततः सन्न्यासी केशव इति स भारत्युपहितो
भुवि ख्यातः कश्चित् प्रभुपुरत आसीद्विधिवशात् ।
तथा दृष्ट्वा नाथं निरवधि रुदन्तं समवद-
च्छुको वा प्रह्लादस्त्वमिति बहुधा विस्मितमनाः ॥४३॥

*tataḥ sannyāsī keśava iti sa bhāraty-upahito*
*bhuvi khyātaḥ kaścit prabhu-purata āsīd vidhi-vaśāt |*
*tathā dṛṣṭvā nāthaṁ niravadhi rudantaṁ samavadac*
*chuko vā prahlādas tvam iti bahudhā vismita-manāḥ ||43||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *sannyāsī* — a sannyasi; *keśavaḥ* — Keshava; *iti* — [so named]; *saḥ* — he; *bhāratī* — "Bharati"; *upahitaḥ* — with the title; *bhuvi* — on earth; *khyātaḥ* — known; *kaścit* — a certain; *prabhu* — the Lord; *purataḥ* — before; *āsīt* — came to be; *vidhi* — of providence; *vaśāt* — by the will; *tathā* — thus; *dṛṣṭvā* — seeing; *nātham* — the Master; *niravadhi* — endlessly; *rudantam* — weeping; *samavadat* — said; *śukaḥ* — Shuka; *vā* — or; *prahlādaḥ* — Prahlada; *tvam* — You; *iti* — thus; *bahudhā* — many times; *vismita* — astonished; *manāḥ* — [whose] mind.

**43.** Then by the will of providence there came before the Lord a certain sannyasi, known on earth as Keshava, with the title Bharati. Seeing the Master weeping thus endlessly, he said again and again in astonishment: "You are Shuka or Prahlada!"

*Note.* Keshava Bharati is the sannyasi from whom the Lord accepted sannyasa at Katwa. Shuka and Prahlada are the models of great devotees.

### Verse 44

प्रशंसां स्वां श्रुत्वा द्विगुणविकलोऽसौ पुनरपि
प्रकामं चक्रन्दायमपि पुनराहातिचकितः ।
भवान् देवो विष्णुर्विदितमिदमेवं खलु मये-
त्युपाकर्ण्य श्रीमान्न्यसनमिह कर्तुं स चकमे ॥४४॥

*praśaṁsāṁ svāṁ śrutvā dviguṇa-vikalo 'sau punar api*
*prakāmaṁ cakrandāyam api punar āhāti-cakitaḥ |*
*bhavān devo viṣṇur viditam idam evaṁ khalu mayety*
*upākarṇya śrīmān nyasanam iha kartuṁ sa cakame ||44||*

*Word for word:* *praśaṁsām* — the praise; *svām* — of Himself; *śrutvā* — having heard; *dviguṇa* — doubly; *vikalaḥ* — distraught; *asau* — He; *punaḥ api* — again; *prakāmam* — bitterly; *cakranda* — wept; *ayam* — this [sannyasi]; *api* — and; *punaḥ* — again; *āha* — said; *ati* — greatly; *cakitaḥ* — astonished; *bhavān* — You; *devaḥ* — the Lord; *viṣṇuḥ* — Vishnu; *viditam* — understood; *idam* — this; *evam* — so; *khalu* — truly; *mayā* — by me; *iti* — thus; *upākarṇya* — having heard; *śrīmān* — the beautiful [Lord]; *nyasanam* — renunciation; *iha* — here; *kartum* — to make; *saḥ* — He; *cakame* — desired.

**44.** Hearing His own praise, He, doubly distraught, again wept bitterly. And this [sannyasi], greatly astonished, said again: "You are the Lord Vishnu — this I have truly understood!" Hearing this, the beautiful [Lord] desired to accept renunciation here.

*Note.* *Nyasana* (renunciation) is sannyasa.

### Verse 45

मुकुन्दोऽथ प्रोचे विनिमिषममुं पश्यत मुहुः
प्रभुर्यावद्गेहे वसति न हि यावत् प्रचलति ।
ततोऽसौ श्रीवासं प्रभुरवददेतन्नु भवता-
मितोऽहं प्रेमार्थं प्रतिदिशमटिष्यामि नितराम् ॥४५॥

*mukundo 'tha proce vinimiṣam amuṁ paśyata muhuḥ*
*prabhur yāvad gehe vasati na hi yāvat pracalati |*
*tato 'sau śrīvāsaṁ prabhur avadad etan nu bhavatām*
*ito 'haṁ premārthaṁ pratidiśam aṭiṣyāmi nitarām ||45||*
