*Word for word:* *mukundaḥ* — Mukunda; *atha* — then; *proce* — said; *vinimiṣam* — without blinking; *amum* — at Him; *paśyata* — look; *muhuḥ* — constantly; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *yāvat* — while; *gehe* — at home; *vasati* — dwells; *na hi* — not; *yāvat* — while; *pracalati* — departs; *tataḥ* — then; *asau* — this; *śrīvāsam* — to Srivasa; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *avadat* — said; *etat* — this; *nu* — now; *bhavatām* — to you; *itaḥ* — from here; *aham* — I; *prema* — of love; *artham* — for the sake; *pratidiśam* — in every direction; *aṭiṣyāmi* — shall wander; *nitarām* — ceaselessly.

**45.** Then Mukunda said: "Look at Him constantly, without blinking, while the Lord dwells at home and has not yet departed!" Then the Lord said to Srivasa: "Let Me tell you this: from here I shall wander ceaselessly in every direction for the sake of love."

### Verse 46

पुनः श्रीवासोऽयं सभयमवदत्त्वद्विरहितैः
कथं स्थातुं शक्यं निरवधि विभो धक्ष्यति मनः ।
भवद्गेहे स्थास्याम्यहमिति जगाद प्रभुरथो
तथेत्येष स्थैर्यं मनसि लभमानः क्षणमभूत् ॥४६॥

*punaḥ śrīvāso 'yaṁ sabhayam avadat tvad-virahitaiḥ*
*kathaṁ sthātuṁ śakyaṁ niravadhi vibho dhakṣyati manaḥ |*
*bhavad-gehe sthāsyāmy aham iti jagāda prabhur atho*
*tathety eṣa sthairyaṁ manasi labhamānaḥ kṣaṇam abhūt ||46||*

*Word for word:* *punaḥ* — again; *śrīvāsaḥ* — Srivasa; *ayam* — this; *sa* — with; *bhayam* — fear; *avadat* — said; *tvat* — from You; *virahitaiḥ* — by [us,] separated; *katham* — how; *sthātum* — to live; *śakyam* — is it possible; *niravadhi* — without end; *vibho* — O mighty one; *dhakṣyati* — will burn; *manaḥ* — the heart; *bhavat* — your; *gehe* — in the house; *sthāsyāmi* — shall stay; *aham* — I; *iti* — thus; *jagāda* — said; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *atho* — then; *tathā* — so be it; *iti* — thus [saying]; *eṣaḥ* — he; *sthairyam* — steadiness; *manasi* — in the mind; *labhamānaḥ* — gaining; *kṣaṇam* — for a moment; *abhūt* — became.

**46.** Again Srivasa said fearfully: "How is it possible [for us], separated from You, to live? O mighty one, the heart will burn without end!" Then the Lord said: "I shall stay in your house." "So be it," [said] he, and for a moment he gained steadiness of mind.

*Note.* Cf. the Lord's promise to abide in Srivasa's house — Murari 2.18.17–23.

### Verse 47

ततः सायं गत्वा गृहमभि मुरारेरुपदिश-
ञ्जगादाद्वैते संश्रयितुमभिधायास्य चरितम् ।
ततोऽन्येद्युः श्रीमान् क्व च जनपदे भूरिकरुणः
प्रभुः पारेगङ्गं स सपदि तितिक्षुश्चलितवान् ॥४७॥

*tataḥ sāyaṁ gatvā gṛham abhi murārer upadiśañ*
*jagādādvaite saṁśrayitum abhidhāyāsya caritam |*
*tato 'nyedyuḥ śrīmān kva ca janapade bhūri-karuṇaḥ*
*prabhuḥ pāre-gaṅgaṁ sa sapadi titikṣuś calitavān ||47||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *sāyam* — in the evening; *gatvā* — having gone; *gṛham abhi* — to the house; *murāreḥ* — of Murari; *upadiśan* — instructing [him]; *jagāda* — told [him]; *advaite* — in Advaita; *saṁśrayitum* — to take shelter; *abhidhāya* — having related; *asya* — His [Advaita's]; *caritam* — life; *tataḥ* — then; *anyedyuḥ* — on the next day; *śrīmān* — the beautiful; *kva ca* — to a certain; *janapade* — district; *bhūri* — immensely; *karuṇaḥ* — merciful; *prabhuḥ* — Lord; *pāre-gaṅgam* — beyond the Ganga; *saḥ* — He; *sapadi* — at once; *titikṣuḥ* — forbearing; *calitavān* — set out.

**47.** Then in the evening He went to Murari's house and, instructing him, related Advaita's life and told him to take shelter with Him. Then on the next day the beautiful, immensely merciful Lord, full of forbearance, at once set out for a certain district beyond the Ganga.

*Note.* The district beyond the Ganga is Katwa, where Keshava Bharati lived.

### Verse 48

ततस्ते ते सर्वे निरवधि बलद्दुःखदलिताः
समुद्विग्ना नाथ क्व गत इति तेपुः सकरुणम् ।
विचार्यैस्तैरेतैरहह दिनसप्तान्तरमसौ
व्यदर्शि न्यासेच्छाकुलितहृदयः श्रीमयतनुः ॥४८॥

*tatas te te sarve niravadhi balad-duḥkha-dalitāḥ*
*samudvignā nātha kva gata iti tepuḥ sakaruṇam |*
*vicāryais tair etair ahaha dina-saptāntaram asau*
*vyadarśi nyāsecchākulita-hṛdayaḥ śrīmaya-tanuḥ ||48||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *te te sarve* — all of them; *niravadhi* — without end; *balat* — by mounting; *duḥkha* — grief; *dalitāḥ* — crushed; *samudvignāḥ* — anxious; *nātha* — O Lord; *kva* — where; *gataḥ* — [have You] gone; *iti* — thus; *tepuḥ* — lamented; *sa* — with; *karuṇam* — piteousness; *vicāryaiḥ* — reflecting; *taiḥ etaiḥ* — by them; *ahaha* — alas; *dina* — days; *sapta* — seven; *antaram* — before; *asau* — He; *vyadarśi* — had been seen; *nyāsa* — for renunciation; *icchā* — by the desire; *ākulita* — agitated; *hṛdayaḥ* — [with] a heart; *śrī-maya* — splendid; *tanuḥ* — [with] a body.

**48.** Then all of them, crushed by ever-mounting grief, anxious, lamented piteously: "O Lord, where have You gone?" As they reflected, [they realised] — alas! — that seven days before He of splendid form had been seen with a heart agitated by the desire for renunciation.

### Verse 49

समन्तात्तत्रत्यास्तमथ परिलोक्यैवमसकृ-
द्विलापैः सन्तापैः किमपि परितेपुः प्रतिमुहुः ।
अहो धातः किं ते विलसितमयं कामसुभग-
श्चिकीर्षुः सन्न्यासं विलसति कठोरस्त्वमसि भोः ॥४९॥

*samantāt tatratyās tam atha parilokyaivam asakṛd*
*vilāpaiḥ santāpaiḥ kim api paritepuḥ pratimuhuḥ |*
*aho dhātaḥ kiṁ te vilasitam ayaṁ kāma-subhagaś*
*cikīrṣuḥ sannyāsaṁ vilasati kaṭhoras tvam asi bhoḥ ||49||*

*Word for word:* *samantāt* — on every side; *tatratyāḥ* — the people there; *tam* — Him; *atha* — then; *parilokya* — having seen; *evam* — thus; *asakṛt* — repeatedly; *vilāpaiḥ* — with wailing; *santāpaiḥ* — [and] anguish; *kim api* — indescribably; *paritepuḥ* — lamented; *pratimuhuḥ* — again and again; *aho* — ah; *dhātaḥ* — O Creator; *kim* — what; *te* — your; *vilasitam* — play; *ayam* — this [one]; *kāma* — [like] Kama; *subhagaḥ* — handsome; *cikīrṣuḥ* — wishing to undertake; *sannyāsam* — sannyasa; *vilasati* — goes about; *kaṭhoraḥ* — cruel; *tvam* — you; *asi* — are; *bhoḥ* — oh.

**49.** Then the people there, seeing Him thus on every side, lamented indescribably again and again with wailing and anguish: "Ah, O Creator, what is this play of yours? He, handsome as Kama, goes about wishing to take sannyasa! Oh, how cruel you are!"

### Verse 50

स्त्रियः प्रोचुर्हा हा बत शिव शिवात्यन्तकठिनो
विधातुर्वैचित्र्यं कथमशनिपातोऽयमसकृत् ।
अहो रूपं शीलं मधुरिमसुलावण्यमहह
क्व सन्न्यासो वा क्व प्रतिमुहुरिदं मुह्यति मनः ॥५०॥

*striyaḥ procur hā hā bata śiva śivātyanta-kaṭhino*
*vidhātur vaicitryaṁ katham aśani-pāto 'yam asakṛt |*
*aho rūpaṁ śīlaṁ madhurima-su-lāvaṇyam ahaha*
*kva sannyāso vā kva pratimuhur idaṁ muhyati manaḥ ||50||*

*Word for word:* *striyaḥ* — the women; *procuḥ* — said; *hā hā* — alas, alas; *bata* — ah; *śiva śiva* — Heaven forbid; *atyanta* — utterly; *kaṭhinaḥ* — hard-hearted [is he]; *vidhātuḥ* — of the Creator; *vaicitryam* — the caprice; *katham* — how; *aśani* — of a thunderbolt; *pātaḥ* — the stroke; *ayam* — this; *asakṛt* — again and again; *aho* — ah; *rūpam* — the beauty; *śīlam* — the character; *madhurima* — the sweetness; *su-lāvaṇyam* — the exquisite loveliness; *ahaha* — alas; *kva* — where; *sannyāsaḥ* — sannyasa; *vā* — and; *kva* — where; *pratimuhuḥ* — again and again; *idam* — this; *muhyati* — is bewildered; *manaḥ* — mind.

**50.** The women said: "Alas, alas! Ah, Heaven forbid! Utterly hard-hearted [is he]: [such is] the caprice of the Creator! How [can] this thunderbolt strike again and again? Ah, the beauty, the character, the sweetness and exquisite loveliness — alas! — where are they, and where is sannyasa? Again and again this mind [of ours] is bewildered!"

*Note.* The turn *kva … kva* ("where the one — and where the other") expresses incompatibility. *Kaṭhinaḥ* (masculine) does not agree with *vaicitryam* (neuter): it evidently refers to the Creator.

### Verse 51

रुदन्नेवं देवः प्रसृमरसुखाविष्कृतिरसौ
जनानूचे मातः पितरिति च सम्बोध्य रुदतः ।
यथा प्रेमा भूयात् प्रभुचरणपाथोरुहयुगे
तथाशीर्वादोऽसौ मयि खलु विधेयो मुहुरिति ॥५१॥

*rudann evaṁ devaḥ prasṛmara-sukhāviṣkṛtir asau*
*janān ūce mātaḥ pitar iti ca sambodhya rudataḥ |*
*yathā premā bhūyāt prabhu-caraṇa-pāthoruha-yuge*
*tathāśīrvādo 'sau mayi khalu vidheyo muhur iti ||51||*

*Word for word:* *rudan* — weeping; *evam* — thus; *devaḥ* — the Lord; *prasṛmara* — spreading; *sukha* — bliss; *āviṣkṛtiḥ* — manifesting; *asau* — He; *janān* — to the people; *ūce* — spoke; *mātaḥ* — O Mother; *pitaḥ* — O Father; *iti* — thus; *ca* — and; *sambodhya* — having addressed; *rudataḥ* — weeping; *yathā* — so that; *premā* — love; *bhūyāt* — may be; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *pāthoruha* — lotus; *yuge* — for the pair; *tathā* — so; *āśīrvādaḥ* — blessing; *asau* — this; *mayi* — on Me; *khalu* — indeed; *vidheyaḥ* — should be bestowed; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *iti* — thus.

**51.** Weeping thus, yet manifesting a spreading bliss, the Lord addressed the weeping people as "O Mother! O Father!" and said: "Indeed, bestow on Me again and again the blessing that there may be love [in Me] for the pair of the Lord's lotus feet."

### Verse 52

गुरोर्गेहं तैस्तैर्विनयनिरतोऽभ्येत्य बहुधा
प्रणामं चक्रेऽसौ प्रतिविहितशिष्योचितरुचिः ।
ततो वैध्यं कृत्वा स्वगुरुमभिवाद्यास्य निरतं
श्रुतौ स्वप्नप्राप्तं शिव शिव महावाक्यमवदत् ॥५२॥

*guror gehaṁ tais tair vinaya-nirato 'bhyetya bahudhā*
*praṇāmaṁ cakre 'sau prativihita-śiṣyocita-ruciḥ |*
*tato vaidhyaṁ kṛtvā sva-gurum [sva-puram?] abhivādyāsya nirataṁ*
*śrutau svapna-prāptaṁ śiva śiva mahā-vākyam avadat ||52||*

*Word for word:* *guroḥ* — of the guru; *geham* — to the house; *taiḥ taiḥ* — with them; *vinaya* — to humility; *nirataḥ* — devoted; *abhyetya* — having come; *bahudhā* — many times; *praṇāmam* — obeisance; *cakre* — made; *asau* — He; *prativihita* — who had assumed; *śiṣya* — for a disciple; *ucita* — befitting; *ruciḥ* — a manner; *tataḥ* — then; *vaidhyam* — what was prescribed; *kṛtvā* — having performed; *sva* — His own; *gurum* — guru; *abhivādya* — having greeted; *asya* — his; *niratam* — earnestly; *śrutau* — into the ear; *svapna* — in a dream; *prāptam* — received; *śiva śiva* — Heaven forbid; *mahā-vākyam* — the great saying; *avadat* — spoke.

**52.** Humbly coming with them to the guru's house, He, who had assumed the manner befitting a disciple, bowed down many times. Then, having performed what was prescribed and greeted His own guru, He — Heaven forbid! — earnestly spoke into his ear the great saying received in a dream.

*Note.* The edition has *स्वपुरम्* (*sva-puram*); by the sense we read *sva-gurum* (?). According to tradition, Chaitanya Himself whispered into Keshava Bharati's ear the mantra He had received in a dream: the disciple initiated the guru (cf. v. 56). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 53

समाहूयाथैकं क्षुरिणमतिधन्यातिसुभगं
दिदेशासौ श्रीमानहह निजकेशापहरणे ।
स तु प्रेमाविष्टो निरवधि रुदन् कम्पिततनु-
र्भयात् किञ्चित् कर्तुं शिव शिव शशाकाथ न खलु ॥५३॥

*samāhūyāthaikaṁ kṣuriṇam ati-dhanyāti-subhagaṁ*
*dideśāsau śrīmān ahaha nija-keśāpaharaṇe |*
*sa tu premāviṣṭo niravadhi rudan kampita-tanur*
*bhayāt kiñcit kartuṁ śiva śiva śaśākātha na khalu ||53||*

*Word for word:* *samāhūya* — having summoned; *atha* — then; *ekam* — a certain; *kṣuriṇam* — barber; *ati* — supremely; *dhanya* — blessed; *ati* — supremely; *subhagam* — fortunate; *dideśa* — ordered; *asau* — He; *śrīmān* — the beautiful; *ahaha* — alas; *nija* — His own; *keśa* — hair; *apaharaṇe* — to remove; *saḥ* — he; *tu* — but; *prema* — by love; *āviṣṭaḥ* — overwhelmed; *niravadhi* — without end; *rudan* — weeping; *kampita* — trembling; *tanuḥ* — [with] a body; *bhayāt* — out of fear; *kiñcit* — anything; *kartum* — to do; *śiva śiva* — Heaven forbid; *śaśāka* — was able; *atha* — then; *na khalu* — not at all.

**53.** Then the beautiful [Lord] summoned a certain barber, supremely blessed and supremely fortunate, and — alas! — ordered him to remove His hair. But he, overwhelmed by love, weeping without end, his body trembling, out of fear — Heaven forbid! — could not do anything at all.

### Verse 54

ततः श्रीगौराङ्गः समवददतीवप्रमुदितो
हरेकृष्णेत्युच्चैर्वद मुहुरिति श्रीमयतनुः ।
ततोऽसौ तत् प्रोच्य प्रतिवलितरोमाञ्चललितो
रुदंस्तत्तत्कर्मारभत बहुदुःखैर्विदलितः ॥५४॥

*tataḥ śrī-gaurāṅgaḥ samavadad atīva-pramudito*
*hare kṛṣṇety uccair vada muhur iti śrīmaya-tanuḥ |*
*tato 'sau tat procya prativalita-romāñca-lalito*
*rudaṁs tat-tat-karmārabhata bahu-duḥkhair vidalitaḥ ||54||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *śrī-gaurāṅgaḥ* — Sri Gauranga; *samavadat* — said; *atīva* — exceedingly; *pramuditaḥ* — joyful; *hare kṛṣṇa* — "Hare Krishna"; *iti* — thus; *uccaiḥ* — loudly; *vada* — say; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *iti* — thus; *śrī-maya* — splendid; *tanuḥ* — [with] a body; *tataḥ* — then; *asau* — he; *tat* — that; *procya* — having uttered; *prativalita* — bristling; *romāñca* — with hair standing on end; *lalitaḥ* — lovely; *rudan* — weeping; *tat-tat* — that; *karma* — work; *ārabhata* — began; *bahu* — by many; *duḥkhaiḥ* — sorrows; *vidalitaḥ* — crushed.

**54.** Then Sri Gauranga, splendid of form, said exceedingly joyfully: "Say 'Hare Krishna' loudly, again and again!" Then he, uttering it, lovely with his hair bristling on end, weeping, crushed by many sorrows, began that work.

*Note.* In the Chaitanya-bhagavata (Madhya 28.140–152) the barber is not named: he weeps and delays, and the Lord bids everyone sing the Name. The name "Madhu" (Madhava the barber) is a later tradition; it is not found in our sources.

### Verse 55

तदानीं ये तत्र क्षणमपि च तस्थुः शिव शिव
प्रकामं ते मातः पितरिति गदन्तोऽतिकरुणम् ।
करौ दत्त्वा मूर्ध्नि प्रतिमुहुरधिक्षेपनिरताः
स्वजीवं निन्दन्तः कति नहि विलापं व्यरचयन् ॥५५॥

*tadānīṁ ye tatra kṣaṇam api ca tasthuḥ śiva śiva*
*prakāmaṁ te mātaḥ pitar iti gadanto 'tikaruṇam |*
*karau dattvā mūrdhni pratimuhur adhikṣepa-niratāḥ*
*sva-jīvaṁ nindantaḥ kati nahi vilāpaṁ vyaracayan ||55||*

*Word for word:* *tadānīm* — then; *ye* — who; *tatra* — there; *kṣaṇam api* — even for a moment; *ca* — and; *tasthuḥ* — stood; *śiva śiva* — Heaven forbid; *prakāmam* — unrestrainedly; *te* — they; *mātaḥ* — O Mother; *pitaḥ* — O Father; *iti* — thus; *gadantaḥ* — crying; *ati* — most; *karuṇam* — piteously; *karau* — the hands; *dattvā* — having placed; *mūrdhni* — on the head; *pratimuhuḥ* — again and again; *adhikṣepa* — to reproach; *niratāḥ* — given; *sva* — their own; *jīvam* — life; *nindantaḥ* — cursing; *kati* — how many; *na hi* — not; *vilāpam* — laments; *vyaracayan* — composed.

**55.** Then those who stood there even for a moment — Heaven forbid! — crying unrestrainedly and most piteously "O Mother! O Father!", placing their hands on their heads, given again and again to reproach, cursing their own lives — how many laments did they not compose!

### Verse 56

गुरुर्भूत्वा व्याजात् स्वयमिव पुरा शिष्यविधिना
ततो मन्त्रं लेभे जगति करुणामेव विकिरन् ।
ततो रोमाञ्चाढ्यं जिगमिषुमवेक्ष्य प्रभुमसौ
गृहाणेत्यह्नायारुणवसनदण्डादिकमदात् ॥५६॥

*gurur bhūtvā vyājāt svayam iva purā śiṣya-vidhinā*
*tato mantraṁ lebhe jagati karuṇām eva vikiran |*
*tato romāñcāḍhyaṁ jigamiṣum avekṣya prabhum asau*
*gṛhāṇety ahnāyāruṇa-vasana-daṇḍādikam adāt ||56||*

*Word for word:* *guruḥ* — guru; *bhūtvā* — having become; *vyājāt* — under a pretext; *svayam* — Himself; *iva* — as it were; *purā* — first; *śiṣya* — of a disciple; *vidhinā* — in the manner; *tataḥ* — then; *mantram* — the mantra; *lebhe* — received; *jagati* — over the world; *karuṇām* — mercy; *eva* — only; *vikiran* — scattering; *tataḥ* — then; *romāñca* — with thrills of ecstasy; *āḍhyam* — filled; *jigamiṣum* — wishing to go; *avekṣya* — having seen; *prabhum* — the Lord; *asau* — he (Keshava Bharati); *gṛhāṇa* — take; *iti* — thus [saying]; *ahnāya* — at once; *aruṇa* — saffron; *vasana* — cloth; *daṇḍa* — staff; *ādikam* — and the rest; *adāt* — gave.

**56.** First He Himself, under a pretext, as it were became the guru; then He received the mantra in the manner of a disciple, scattering nothing but mercy over the world. Then, seeing the Lord filled with thrills of ecstasy and wishing to depart, he [Keshava Bharati] at once said "Take [these]!" and gave Him the saffron cloth, the staff and the rest.

*Note.* Cf. v. 52: the Lord first spoke the "great saying" into His guru's ear, and only then received the mantra from him.

### Verse 57

गृहीत्वा दण्डाद्यं गुरुवचनसंपालनवशा-
दनैषीद्गौराङ्गो दिवसमवशात्मातिचतुरः ।
अथानुज्ञाप्यैनं सुकृतशतगाढं जनपदं
ययौ राढं गूढोपमपरमलोकोत्तरकृतिः ॥५७॥

*gṛhītvā daṇḍādyaṁ guru-vacana-saṁpālana-vaśād*
*anaiṣīd gaurāṅgo divasam avaśātmāti-caturaḥ |*
*athānujñāpyainaṁ sukṛta-śata-gāḍhaṁ janapadaṁ*
*yayau rāḍhaṁ gūḍhopama-parama-lokottara-kṛtiḥ ||57||*

*Word for word:* *gṛhītvā* — having taken; *daṇḍa* — the staff; *ādyam* — and the rest; *guru* — of the guru; *vacana* — the word; *saṁpālana* — of keeping; *vaśāt* — for the sake; *anaiṣīt* — spent; *gaurāṅgaḥ* — Gauranga; *divasam* — the day; *avaśa* — not under control; *ātmā* — [with] Himself; *ati* — supremely; *caturaḥ* — wise; *atha* — then; *anujñāpya* — having taken leave; *enam* — of him; *sukṛta* — of pious deeds; *śata* — with hundreds; *gāḍham* — filled; *janapadam* — to the country; *yayau* — went; *rāḍham* — to Radha; *gūḍha* — hidden; *upama* — incomparable; *parama* — supreme; *lokottara* — beyond this world; *kṛtiḥ* — [whose] deeds.

**57.** Having taken the staff and the rest, Gauranga — supremely wise, though not master of Himself — spent the day [there] for the sake of keeping His guru's word. Then, having taken leave of him, He whose deeds are hidden, incomparable, supreme and beyond this world went to the Radha country, filled with hundreds of pious deeds.

*Note.* Radha (*rāḍha*; not to be confused with Sri Radha) is a region of western Bengal. The edition has *गूढोपम*: possibly *gūḍhopama-*, "like something hidden", or *gūḍha-anupama-*; we take it as the latter. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 58

पथि ध्यायं ध्यायं स्वचरितमसौ सौख्यविवशः
स्वनामप्रेमार्द्रः प्रतिपदमशक्तः स्खलति सः ।
क्वचिद्गायत्यार्तः क्वचिदपि नदत्यार्तनिनदं
क्वचिन्मन्दं याति क्वचिदपि मृगेन्द्रद्रुतगतिः ॥५८॥

*pathi dhyāyaṁ dhyāyaṁ sva-caritam asau saukhya-vivaśaḥ*
*sva-nāma-premārdraḥ pratipadam aśaktaḥ skhalati saḥ |*
*kvacid gāyaty ārtaḥ kvacid api nadaty ārta-ninadaṁ*
*kvacin mandaṁ yāti kvacid api mṛgendra-druta-gatiḥ ||58||*

*Word for word:* *pathi* — on the way; *dhyāyam dhyāyam* — meditating again and again; *sva* — on His own; *caritam* — deeds; *asau* — He; *saukhya* — by bliss; *vivaśaḥ* — overwhelmed; *sva* — for His own; *nāma* — name; *prema* — with love; *ārdraḥ* — melted; *pratipadam* — at every step; *aśaktaḥ* — powerless; *skhalati* — stumbles; *saḥ* — He; *kvacit* — now; *gāyati* — sings; *ārtaḥ* — in distress; *kvacit api* — now; *nadati* — cries out; *ārta* — of anguish; *ninadam* — a cry; *kvacit* — now; *mandam* — slowly; *yāti* — goes; *kvacit api* — now; *mṛga-indra* — of the king of beasts (the lion); *druta* — swift; *gatiḥ* — [with] a gait.

**58.** On the way, meditating again and again on His own deeds, overwhelmed by bliss, melted with love for His own name, powerless, He stumbled at every step. Now He sang in distress, now He cried out with a cry of anguish; now He walked slowly, now with the swift gait of the king of beasts.

### Verse 59

प्रभुस्तस्मिन् देशे क्षणमपि न संश्रुत्य विवशः
स्वनाम त्यक्ष्यामि स्वतनुमिति गत्वोपतटिनि ।
जले मज्जन् डिम्भैर्वद हरिमिति ध्वानमुखरै-
रदर्शि प्रेमार्द्रः प्रतिपदपतद्बाष्पजडितः ॥५९॥

*prabhus tasmin deśe kṣaṇam api na saṁśrutya vivaśaḥ*
*sva-nāma tyakṣyāmi sva-tanum iti gatvopataṭini |*
*jale majjan ḍimbhair vada harim iti dhvāna-mukharair*
*adarśi premārdraḥ pratipada-patad-bāṣpa-jaḍitaḥ ||59||*

*Word for word:* *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *tasmin* — in that; *deśe* — country; *kṣaṇam api* — even for a moment; *na* — not; *saṁśrutya* — having heard; *vivaśaḥ* — in despair; *sva* — His own; *nāma* — name; *tyakṣyāmi* — I shall give up; *sva* — My own; *tanum* — body; *iti* — thus [resolving]; *gatvā* — having gone; *upa-taṭini* — to the river; *jale* — in the water; *majjan* — sinking; *ḍimbhaiḥ* — by children; *vada* — say; *harim* — "Hari"; *iti* — thus; *dhvāna* — with cries; *mukharaiḥ* — noisy; *adarśi* — was seen; *prema* — with love; *ārdraḥ* — melted; *pratipada* — at every step; *patat* — falling; *bāṣpa* — by tears; *jaḍitaḥ* — numbed.

**59.** Not hearing His own name in that country even for a moment, the Lord in despair [resolved]: "I shall give up My body," and went to the river. As He was sinking into the water, He was seen by children noisily crying "Say 'Hari'!" — and the Lord, melted with love, became numb with the tears that fell at every step.

*Note.* "His own name" is the name of Hari. Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 3.13–18: in the Radha country the cowherd boys, seeing the Lord, cry "Hari! Hari!", and He rejoices (the same in Chaitanya-bhagavata, Antya 1).

### Verse 60

ततः श्रुत्वा तैस्तैर्गदितमिदमुच्चैर्हरिरिति
प्रभुः प्रेमोन्मत्तः क्षितिमभिपतन् गाढमरुदत् ।
कियद्दूरं गत्वा तदनु विदधे भैक्षमुचितं
हसन् नृत्यन् गायन् क्वचिदपि रुदंस्तत् समगमत् ॥६०॥

*tataḥ śrutvā tais tair gaditam idam uccair harir iti*
*prabhuḥ premonmattaḥ kṣitim abhipatan gāḍham arudat |*
*kiyad dūraṁ gatvā tad-anu vidadhe bhaikṣam ucitaṁ*
*hasan nṛtyan gāyan kvacid api rudaṁs tat samagamat ||60||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *śrutvā* — having heard; *taiḥ taiḥ* — by them; *gaditam* — spoken; *idam* — this; *uccaiḥ* — loudly; *hariḥ* — "Hari"; *iti* — thus; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *prema* — with love; *unmattaḥ* — maddened; *kṣitim abhi* — to the ground; *patan* — falling; *gāḍham* — bitterly; *arudat* — wept; *kiyat* — a little; *dūram* — farther; *gatvā* — having gone; *tat-anu* — after that; *vidadhe* — performed; *bhaikṣam* — the begging of alms; *ucitam* — proper; *hasan* — laughing; *nṛtyan* — dancing; *gāyan* — singing; *kvacit api* — at times; *rudan* — weeping; *tat* — thus; *samagamat* — went on.

**60.** Then, hearing them loudly say "Hari!", the Lord, maddened with love, fell to the ground and wept bitterly. Going a little farther, He then performed the proper begging of alms, and thus went on — laughing, dancing, singing, and at times weeping.

### Verse 61

क्षणं गोपीभावैः क्षणमपि च दास्यैः क्षणमथो
तथैश्वर्यैः श्रीमान्नटनकलया कौतुकपरः ।
असीमप्रेमार्द्रो निरवधि चलन् पश्चिमदिशं
न सस्मारात्मानं क्षणमपि दिनानां त्रयमभि ॥६१॥

*kṣaṇaṁ gopī-bhāvaiḥ kṣaṇam api ca dāsyaiḥ kṣaṇam atho*
*tathaiśvaryaiḥ śrīmān naṭana-kalayā kautuka-paraḥ |*
*asīma-premārdro niravadhi calan paścima-diśaṁ*
*na sasmārātmānaṁ kṣaṇam api dinānāṁ trayam abhi ||61||*

*Word for word:* *kṣaṇam* — now; *gopī* — of a gopi; *bhāvaiḥ* — in the moods; *kṣaṇam api ca* — now; *dāsyaiḥ* — in the moods of a servant; *kṣaṇam atho* — and now; *tathā* — likewise; *aiśvaryaiḥ* — in the moods of majesty; *śrīmān* — the beautiful; *naṭana* — of dancing; *kalayā* — through the art; *kautuka* — on delight; *paraḥ* — intent; *asīma* — boundless; *prema* — with love; *ārdraḥ* — melted; *niravadhi* — ceaselessly; *calan* — walking; *paścima* — the western; *diśam* — direction; *na* — not; *sasmāra* — remembered; *ātmānam* — Himself; *kṣaṇam api* — even for a moment; *dinānām* — of days; *trayam abhi* — throughout three.

**61.** Now in the moods of a gopi, now in the moods of a servant, and now likewise in the moods of majesty, the beautiful [Lord], intent on delight through the art of dancing, melted with boundless love, walked ceaselessly westward, and for three days did not remember Himself even for a moment.

### Verse 62

ततो दैवादेवं भवति गमने दक्षिणदिशि
प्रबुद्धोऽभूच्छ्रीमान् क्वचन ननु यामीति मनसि ।
विचार्याद्वैतस्यालयमभि स गन्तुं समकरो-
न्मनो नित्यानन्दप्रभुमपि जगादातिमधुरम् ॥६२॥

*tato daivād evaṁ bhavati gamane dakṣiṇa-diśi*
*prabuddho 'bhūc chrīmān kvacana nanu yāmīti manasi |*
*vicāryādvaitasyālayam abhi sa gantuṁ samakaron*
*mano nityānanda-prabhum api jagādāti-madhuram ||62||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *daivāt* — by providence; *evam* — thus; *bhavati* — when [it] came to be; *gamane* — the course; *dakṣiṇa* — the southern; *diśi* — in the direction; *prabuddhaḥ* — awakened; *abhūt* — became; *śrīmān* — the beautiful; *kvacana* — where; *nanu* — indeed; *yāmi* — am I going; *iti* — thus; *manasi* — in the mind; *vicārya* — having reflected; *advaitasya* — of Advaita; *ālayam abhi* — to the house; *saḥ* — He; *gantum* — to go; *samakarot manaḥ* — resolved; *nityānanda-prabhum* — to Nityananda Prabhu; *api* — and; *jagāda* — spoke; *ati* — very; *madhuram* — sweetly.

**62.** Then, when by providence His course thus turned to the south, the beautiful [Lord] came to Himself: "Where indeed am I going?" Having reflected thus in His mind, He resolved to go to Advaita's house, and spoke very sweetly to Nityananda Prabhu:

*Note.* Verses 62–63 form a single speech. Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 3.16–24 (and Chaitanya-bhagavata, Antya 1), where Nityananda, having instructed the cowherd boys, cunningly leads the Lord to the Ganga and to Advaita's house in Shantipura; Murari 3.4.2–10.

### Verse 63

प्रयाहि त्वं शीघ्रं विबुधतटिनीतीरमधुरे
नवद्वीपे तत्रस्थान् मम निगदितैर्ब्रूहि मधुरम् ।
भवन्तोऽद्वैतस्यालयमभि चलन्त्वेव चपलं
प्रयास्ये तत्राहं सपदि स तथेति प्रचलितः ॥६३॥

*prayāhi tvaṁ śīghraṁ vibudha-taṭinī-tīra-madhure*
*navadvīpe tatrasthān mama nigaditair brūhi madhuram |*
*bhavanto 'dvaitasyālayam abhi calantv eva capalaṁ*
*prayāsye tatrāhaṁ sapadi sa tatheti pracalitaḥ ||63||*

*Word for word:* *prayāhi* — go; *tvam* — You; *śīghram* — quickly; *vibudha* — of the gods; *taṭinī* — of the river; *tīra* — on the bank; *madhure* — lovely; *navadvīpe* — to Navadvipa; *tatra-sthān* — to those there; *mama* — in My; *nigaditaiḥ* — words; *brūhi* — tell; *madhuram* — sweetly; *bhavantaḥ* — you; *advaitasya* — of Advaita; *ālayam abhi* — to the house; *calantu* — go; *eva* — indeed; *capalam* — quickly; *prayāsye* — shall come; *tatra* — there; *aham* — I; *sapadi* — at once; *saḥ* — He; *tathā* — so be it; *iti* — thus [saying]; *pracalitaḥ* — set off.

**63.** "Go quickly to Navadvipa, lovely on the bank of the river of the gods, and sweetly tell those there in My words: 'Go quickly to Advaita's house; I shall come there.'" "So be it," [said] He, and set off at once.

### Verse 64

ततो गत्वा तत्र प्रमुदितमना नाथगदितं
निगद्य प्रत्येकं समनयदमुत्रैव सहसा ।
शची चातिव्यग्रा परममुदिता तत्र चलिता
किमन्यद्वक्तव्यं गतमिव नवद्वीपमभवत् ॥६४॥

*tato gatvā tatra pramudita-manā nātha-gaditaṁ*
*nigadya pratyekaṁ samanayad amutraiva sahasā |*
*śacī cātivyagrā parama-muditā tatra calitā*
*kim anyad vaktavyaṁ gatam iva navadvīpam abhavat ||64||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *gatvā* — having gone; *tatra* — there; *pramudita* — joyful; *manāḥ* — [with] a heart; *nātha* — of the Lord; *gaditam* — the words; *nigadya* — having told; *pratyekam* — to each one; *samanayat* — brought [them]; *amutra* — there; *eva* — indeed; *sahasā* — at once; *śacī* — Shachi; *ca* — and; *ati* — greatly; *vyagrā* — agitated; *parama* — supremely; *muditā* — glad; *tatra* — there; *calitā* — set out; *kim* — what; *anyat* — more; *vaktavyam* — is to be said; *gatam* — departed; *iva* — as if; *navadvīpam* — Navadvipa; *abhavat* — became.

**64.** Then, going there, He [Nityananda], joyful at heart, told each one the words of the Lord and at once brought [them all] there. And Shachi too, greatly agitated and supremely glad, set out there. What more is there to say? Navadvipa itself, as it were, had departed.

### Verse 65

ततोऽन्येद्युः श्रीमान् धृतकरकदण्डः सदरुणं
वहन् वासोद्वन्द्वं बहलतडिदर्चिःप्रतिकृतिः ।
अकस्मादेकस्मिन् पथि गुरुशिखो गैरिकमयो
व्यदर्शि स्वर्णाद्रिप्रवर इव तैर्गौरशशभृत् ॥६५॥

*tato 'nyedyuḥ śrīmān dhṛta-karaka-daṇḍaḥ sad-aruṇaṁ*
*vahan vāso-dvandvaṁ bahala-taḍid-arciḥ-pratikṛtiḥ |*
*akasmād ekasmin pathi guru-śikho gairikamayo*
*vyadarśi svarṇādri-pravara iva tair gaura-śaśabhṛt ||65||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *anyedyuḥ* — on the next day; *śrīmān* — the beautiful; *dhṛta* — holding; *karaka* — a water-pot; *daṇḍaḥ* — [and] a staff; *sat* — fine; *aruṇam* — saffron; *vahan* — wearing; *vāsaḥ* — of garments; *dvandvam* — a pair; *bahala* — of dense; *taḍit* — lightning; *arciḥ* — of the radiance; *pratikṛtiḥ* — the likeness; *akasmāt* — suddenly; *ekasmin* — on a certain; *pathi* — road; *guru* — lofty; *śikhaḥ* — [with] a peak (with a tuft); *gairika* — of red ochre; *mayaḥ* — consisting (clad in ochre); *vyadarśi* — was seen; *svarṇa* — golden; *adri* — of mountains; *pravaraḥ* — the best; *iva* — like; *taiḥ* — by them; *gaura* — Gaura; *śaśabhṛt* — the moon.

**65.** Then on the next day they suddenly saw on a certain road the beautiful moon, Gaura, holding a water-pot and staff, wearing a pair of fine saffron garments, the likeness of the dense radiance of lightning — like the best of golden mountains, lofty-peaked and clad in red ochre.

*Note.* A play on words: *guru-śikha* means "with a lofty peak" (of a mountain) and also "with a long tuft of hair"; *gairika* is the red ochre on a mountain's slopes and also the ochre (saffron) cloth of a sannyasi.

### Verse 66

एतां स आस्थाय परात्मनिष्ठा-
मुपासितां पूर्वतमैर्महर्षिभिः ।
अहं तरिष्यामि दुरन्तपारं
तमो मुकुन्दाङ्घ्रिनिषेवयैव ॥६६॥

*etāṁ sa āsthāya parātma-niṣṭhām*
*upāsitāṁ pūrvatamair maharṣibhiḥ |*
*ahaṁ tariṣyāmi duranta-pāraṁ*
*tamo mukundāṅghri-niṣevayaiva ||66||*

*Word for word:* *etām* — this; *saḥ* — he (here: I); *āsthāya* — having taken up; *para-ātma* — to the Supreme Self; *niṣṭhām* — devotion; *upāsitām* — practised; *pūrvatamaiḥ* — by the most ancient; *mahā-ṛṣibhiḥ* — great sages; *aham* — I; *tariṣyāmi* — shall cross; *duranta-pāram* — whose far shore is hard to reach; *tamaḥ* — the darkness; *mukunda* — of Mukunda; *aṅghri* — to the feet; *niṣevayā* — by service; *eva* — alone.

**66.** "Having taken up this devotion to the Supreme Self, practised by the most ancient great sages, I shall cross the darkness whose far shore is hard to reach, by service to the feet of Mukunda alone."

*Note.* A quotation: Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.23.57 (the song of the Avanti brahmana who accepted sannyasa). The metre is *upajāti*. In the edition the verse received a serial number. *Sa* — in the Bhagavata, "that [brahmana]"; in the Lord's mouth, "I".

### Verse 67

इति श्लोकं भूयः पथि पथि पठित्वातिरभसं
नटन्तं नेत्राम्भःसमुदयसमुद्भ्रान्तवपुषम् ।
विलोक्यैनं प्राणानिव चिरमृतास्ते प्रमुदिताः
प्रभुं हर्षोत्कर्षात् क्षितिषु निपतन्तः समनमन् ॥६७॥

*iti ślokaṁ bhūyaḥ pathi pathi paṭhitvātirabhasaṁ*
*naṭantaṁ netrāmbhaḥ-samudaya-samudbhrānta-vapuṣam |*
*vilokyainaṁ prāṇān iva ciramṛtās te pramuditāḥ*
*prabhuṁ harṣotkarṣāt kṣitiṣu nipatantaḥ samanaman ||67||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *ślokam* — the shloka; *bhūyaḥ* — again and again; *pathi pathi* — on every road; *paṭhitvā* — reciting; *ati* — most; *rabhasam* — ardently; *naṭantam* — dancing; *netra* — of the eyes; *ambhaḥ* — of the waters; *samudaya* — by the flood; *samudbhrānta* — shaken; *vapuṣam* — [with] a body; *vilokya* — having seen; *enam* — Him; *prāṇān* — the breath of life; *iva* — like; *cira* — long; *mṛtāḥ* — dead; *te* — they; *pramuditāḥ* — rejoicing; *prabhum* — to the Lord; *harṣa* — of joy; *utkarṣāt* — from the excess; *kṣitiṣu* — to the ground; *nipatantaḥ* — falling; *samanaman* — bowed down.

**67.** Reciting this shloka again and again on every road, He danced most ardently, His body shaken by the flood of tears from His eyes. Seeing Him, they rejoiced like those long dead [regaining] the breath of life, and in the excess of their joy they fell to the ground and bowed down to the Lord.

### Verse 68

प्रभुः कांश्चिद्वाचा हसितसुधया कांश्चन कृपा-
वलद्दृष्ट्या कांश्चित् ससुखमपरान् स्पर्शकलया ।
चकारातिप्रीतान्निजचरणपङ्केरुहरतां-
स्ततोऽगादद्वैतालयमतिसुखार्द्रातिकरुणः ॥६८॥

*prabhuḥ kāṁścid vācā hasita-sudhayā kāṁścana kṛpā-*
*valad-dṛṣṭyā kāṁścit sasukham aparān sparśa-kalayā |*
*cakārātiprītān nija-caraṇa-paṅkeruha-ratāṁs*
*tato 'gād advaitālayam atisukhārdrātikaruṇaḥ ||68||*

*Word for word:* *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *kāṁścit* — some; *vācā* — with words; *hasita* — of a smile; *sudhayā* — with the nectar; *kāṁścana* — others; *kṛpā* — with mercy; *valat* — moving; *dṛṣṭyā* — with a glance; *kāṁścit* — others; *sa* — with; *sukham* — joy; *aparān* — others; *sparśa* — of touch; *kalayā* — with the art; *cakāra* — made; *ati* — greatly; *prītān* — pleased; *nija* — His own; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *paṅkeruha* — to the lotus; *ratān* — devoted; *tataḥ* — then; *agāt* — went; *advaita* — of Advaita; *ālayam* — to the house; *ati* — with exceeding; *sukha* — bliss; *ārdraḥ* — melted; *ati* — exceedingly; *karuṇaḥ* — merciful.

**68.** Some with words, others with the nectar of His smile, others with a glance moved by mercy, and others joyfully with the art of His touch — thus the Lord greatly pleased those devoted to His lotus feet. Then, melted with exceeding bliss and exceedingly merciful, He went to Advaita's house.

### Verse 69

ततोऽसौ गौराङ्गः शुचि समविश्यासनवरं
परिष्वज्याद्वैतं नयनजलसंभिन्नवपुषम् ।
समं क्रन्दद्भिस्तैर्गुणगरिमगाम्भीर्यवलिताः
स्फुरन्नामोद्गाथाः समकथयदत्यन्तललिताः ॥६९॥

*tato 'sau gaurāṅgaḥ śuci samaviśyāsana-varaṁ*
*pariṣvajyādvaitaṁ nayana-jala-saṁbhinna-vapuṣam |*
*samaṁ krandadbhis tair guṇa-garima-gāmbhīrya-valitāḥ*
*sphuran-nāmodgāthāḥ samakathayad atyanta-lalitāḥ ||69||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *asau* — this; *gaurāṅgaḥ* — Gauranga; *śuci* — pure; *samaviśya* — having sat; *āsana* — on a seat; *varam* — excellent; *pariṣvajya* — having embraced; *advaitam* — Advaita; *nayana* — of the eyes; *jala* — with the water; *saṁbhinna* — bathed; *vapuṣam* — [with] a body; *samam* — together; *krandadbhiḥ* — weeping; *taiḥ* — with them; *guṇa* — of the qualities; *garima* — with the weight; *gāmbhīrya* — [and] the depth; *valitāḥ* — endowed; *sphurat* — shining; *nāma* — of the Name; *udgāthāḥ* — hymns; *samakathayat* — sang; *atyanta* — most; *lalitāḥ* — charming.

**69.** Then Gauranga, seated on an excellent, pure seat, having embraced Advaita, whose body was bathed in the tears of His eyes, sang together with them, as they wept, most charming hymns shining with the Name, endowed with the weight and depth of [His] qualities.

### Verse 70

ततोऽसावद्वैतार्पितसुमधुरान्नं समभज-
त्ततोऽन्येद्युः प्रातः प्रतिजनमुवाच प्रमुदितः ।
अहं यामि क्षेत्रं प्रभुचरणसन्दर्शनवशा-
द्भवद्भिः कर्तव्यं सततहरिसङ्कीर्तनमिह ॥७०॥

*tato 'sāv advaitārpita-sumadhurānnaṁ samabhajat*
*tato 'nyedyuḥ prātaḥ pratijanam uvāca pramuditaḥ |*
*ahaṁ yāmi kṣetraṁ prabhu-caraṇa-sandarśana-vaśād*
*bhavadbhiḥ kartavyaṁ satata-hari-saṅkīrtanam iha ||70||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *asau* — He; *advaita* — by Advaita; *arpita* — offered; *su-madhura* — most sweet; *annam* — food; *samabhajat* — partook of; *tataḥ* — then; *anyedyuḥ* — on the next day; *prātaḥ* — in the morning; *pratijanam* — to each person; *uvāca* — said; *pramuditaḥ* — joyfully; *aham* — I; *yāmi* — am going; *kṣetram* — to the Kshetra; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *caraṇa* — the feet; *sandarśana* — of beholding; *vaśāt* — for the sake; *bhavadbhiḥ* — by you; *kartavyam* — must be performed; *satata* — constant; *hari* — of Hari; *saṅkīrtanam* — sankirtana; *iha* — here.

**70.** Then He partook of the most sweet food offered by Advaita, and on the next day, in the morning, He joyfully said to each person: "I am going to the Kshetra to behold the feet of the Lord. You must perform constant sankirtana of Hari here."

*Note.* The Kshetra ("the sacred field") is Purushottama-kshetra, Puri, the abode of Jagannatha.

### Verse 71

विसृज्यैवं तांस्तान्नयनसलिलैराप्लुततमं
परिष्वज्याद्वैतं चलितुमकरोदुद्यममसौ ।
तृणं कृत्वा दन्तैः क्षितिषु हरिदासोऽथ निपतन्
प्रभोः पादाब्जाग्रे निरवधि समुत्कण्ठितमतिः ॥७१॥

*visṛjyaivaṁ tāṁs tān nayana-salilair āplutatamaṁ*
*pariṣvajyādvaitaṁ calitum akarod udyamam asau |*
*tṛṇaṁ kṛtvā dantaiḥ kṣitiṣu haridāso 'tha nipatan*
*prabhoḥ pādābjāgre niravadhi samutkaṇṭhita-matiḥ ||71||*

*Word for word:* *visṛjya* — having dismissed; *evam* — thus; *tān tān* — them all; *nayana* — of the eyes; *salilaiḥ* — with the water; *āplutatamam* — utterly flooded; *pariṣvajya* — having embraced; *advaitam* — Advaita; *calitum* — to depart; *akarot udyamam* — made ready; *asau* — He; *tṛṇam* — a blade of grass; *kṛtvā* — having placed; *dantaiḥ* — between the teeth; *kṣitiṣu* — to the ground; *haridāsaḥ* — Haridasa; *atha* — then; *nipatan* — falling; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *pāda* — of the feet; *abja* — lotus; *agre* — before; *niravadhi* — boundlessly; *samutkaṇṭhita* — longing; *matiḥ* — [with] a mind.

**71.** Having thus dismissed them all and embraced Advaita, who was utterly flooded with the tears of His eyes, the Lord made ready to depart. Then Haridasa, placing a blade of grass between his teeth, fell to the ground before the Lord's lotus feet, his mind boundlessly longing.

*Note.* A blade of grass between the teeth is a sign of utmost humility.

### Verse 72

अथैवं तं दृष्ट्वा प्रभुरवददेवं तव कृते
जगन्नाथस्याग्रे निरवधि वदिष्यामि विनमन् ।
तदुत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठाश्वसिहि परिरभ्येति तमिमं
विसृज्यैवं यान्तं तमवददथाद्वैततनुभृत् ॥७२॥

*athaivaṁ taṁ dṛṣṭvā prabhur avadad evaṁ tava kṛte*
*jagannāthasyāgre niravadhi vadiṣyāmi vinaman |*
*tad uttiṣṭhottiṣṭhāśvasihi parirabhyeti tam imaṁ*
*visṛjyaivaṁ yāntaṁ tam avadad athādvaita-tanubhṛt ||72||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *evam* — thus; *tam* — him; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *avadat* — said; *evam* — thus; *tava* — of you; *kṛte* — for the sake; *jagannāthasya* — of Jagannatha; *agre* — before; *niravadhi* — ceaselessly; *vadiṣyāmi* — I shall speak; *vinaman* — bowing down; *tat* — so; *uttiṣṭha uttiṣṭha* — rise, rise; *āśvasihi* — take comfort; *parirabhya* — having embraced; *iti* — thus [saying]; *tam imam* — him; *visṛjya* — having let go; *evam* — thus; *yāntam* — going; *tam* — to Him; *avadat* — said; *atha* — then; *advaita* — Advaita; *tanubhṛt* — embodied.

**72.** Seeing him thus, the Lord said: "For your sake I shall ceaselessly speak before Jagannatha, bowing down. So rise, rise, take comfort!" Having said this, He embraced him and let him go; and as He was thus going, the embodied Advaita then said to Him:

### Verse 73

तव प्रस्थानेऽस्मिन् किमिह भविता तद्वद विभो
कथं धास्ये प्राणान् कथमिव तरिष्यामि विरहम् ।
इति क्षोभाक्रान्तं प्रभुरवददेवं यदि कृतं
भवद्भिस्तत् किं मे गमनमिति सम्भाष्य चलितः ॥७३॥

*tava prasthāne 'smin kim iha bhavitā tad vada vibho*
*kathaṁ dhāsye prāṇān katham iva tariṣyāmi viraham |*
*iti kṣobhākrāntaṁ prabhur avadad evaṁ yadi kṛtaṁ*
*bhavadbhis tat kiṁ me gamanam iti sambhāṣya calitaḥ ||73||*

*Word for word:* *tava* — Your; *prasthāne* — at the departure; *asmin* — this; *kim* — what; *iha* — here; *bhavitā* — will be; *tat* — that; *vada* — tell; *vibho* — O mighty one; *katham* — how; *dhāsye* — shall I keep; *prāṇān* — life; *katham iva* — how; *tariṣyāmi* — shall I cross; *viraham* — separation; *iti* — thus; *kṣobha* — by agitation; *ākrāntam* — to Him overcome; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *avadat* — said; *evam* — thus; *yadi* — if; *kṛtam* — is done; *bhavadbhiḥ* — by You (honorific plural); *tat* — then; *kim* — what [use]; *me* — My; *gamanam* — going; *iti* — thus; *sambhāṣya* — having spoken; *calitaḥ* — moved.

**73.** "What will become [of us] here at this departure of Yours? Tell [me] that, O mighty one! How shall I keep my life? How shall I cross [the ocean of] separation?" To Him, overcome with agitation, the Lord said: "If You act thus, then what [use] is My going?" — and, having spoken so, He was moved.

*Note.* *Calitaḥ* can also mean "set off"; but according to v. 74 the Lord stays several more days, so we translate "moved, shaken" (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 74

ततोऽद्वैतप्रीत्या प्रणतहरिदासस्य च मुदा
जगन्नाथक्षेत्रं जिगमिषुरपि स्वप्रियवशः ।
शचीदेव्या तत्पाचितमतुलमन्नं निजजनैः
समं तैर्भुञ्जानः कति च गमयामास दिवसान् ॥७४॥

*tato 'dvaita-prītyā praṇata-haridāsasya ca mudā*
*jagannātha-kṣetraṁ jigamiṣur api sva-priya-vaśaḥ |*
*śacī-devyā tat-pācitam atulam annaṁ nija-janaiḥ*
*samaṁ tair bhuñjānaḥ kati ca gamayāmāsa divasān ||74||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *advaita* — for Advaita; *prītyā* — out of love; *praṇata* — who lay bowed down; *haridāsasya* — of Haridasa; *ca* — and; *mudā* — for the joy; *jagannātha* — of Jagannatha; *kṣetram* — to the Kshetra; *jigamiṣuḥ* — wishing to go; *api* — though; *sva* — to His own; *priya* — dear ones; *vaśaḥ* — yielding; *śacī-devyā* — by Shachi-devi; *tat* — by her; *pācitam* — cooked; *atulam* — incomparable; *annam* — food; *nija* — His own; *janaiḥ* — with the people; *samam* — together; *taiḥ* — with them; *bhuñjānaḥ* — eating; *kati* — several; *ca* — and; *gamayāmāsa* — spent; *divasān* — days.

**74.** Then, though He wished to go to the Kshetra of Jagannatha, [the Lord], yielding to His dear ones, out of love for Advaita and for the joy of Haridasa, who lay bowed down, spent several days eating together with His own people the incomparable food cooked by Shachi-devi.

### Verse 75

अथैवं गच्छन्तं प्रभुमहह कश्चिद्द्विजवरो-
ऽवदत् पश्याम्येतत् प्रभुवर वपुस्तेऽतिमधुरम् ।
स इत्थं गात्रेभ्यो वसनमपकृष्यैव करुणः
प्रभुर्मेघापाये शशभृदिव रेजेऽतिविमलः ॥७५॥

*athaivaṁ gacchantaṁ prabhum ahaha kaścid dvija-varo*
*'vadat paśyāmy etat prabhu-vara vapus te 'timadhuram |*
*sa itthaṁ gātrebhyo vasanam apakṛṣyaiva karuṇaḥ*
*prabhur meghāpāye śaśabhṛd iva reje 'tivimalaḥ ||75||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *evam* — thus; *gacchantam* — to [Him] going; *prabhum* — to the Lord; *ahaha* — ah; *kaścit* — a certain; *dvija-varaḥ* — excellent brahmana; *avadat* — said; *paśyāmi* — let me see; *etat* — this; *prabhu-vara* — O best of lords; *vapuḥ* — body; *te* — Your; *ati* — most; *madhuram* — sweet; *saḥ* — He; *ittham* — thus; *gātrebhyaḥ* — from the limbs; *vasanam* — the cloth; *apakṛṣya* — having drawn off; *eva* — indeed; *karuṇaḥ* — merciful; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *megha* — of the clouds; *apāye* — at the departure; *śaśabhṛt* — the moon; *iva* — like; *reje* — shone; *ati* — utterly; *vimalaḥ* — spotless.

**75.** Then, as the Lord was going thus — ah! — a certain excellent brahmana said [to Him]: "O best of lords, let me see this most sweet body of Yours." And the merciful Lord, drawing the cloth off His limbs, shone thus utterly spotless, like the moon when the clouds depart.

*Note.* Grammatically, it is the merciful Lord Himself who draws off the cloth (*sa … karuṇaḥ prabhuḥ*).

### Verse 76

पुरो नित्यानन्दं मुदितहृदयं भूरिकरुणो
विधायासौ गच्छन्निजचरणपङ्केरुहरतैः ।
गदाधृग्विप्राद्यैरहह समुकुन्दैः परिवृत-
स्तदा तैस्तैः सर्वैः कथमपि हि दुःखेन ददृशे ॥७६॥

*puro nityānandaṁ mudita-hṛdayaṁ bhūri-karuṇo*
*vidhāyāsau gacchan nija-caraṇa-paṅkeruha-rataiḥ |*
*gadādhṛg-viprādyair ahaha sa-mukundaiḥ parivṛtas*
*tadā tais taiḥ sarvaiḥ katham api hi duḥkhena dadṛśe ||76||*

*Word for word:* *puraḥ* — in front; *nityānandam* — Nityananda; *mudita* — joyful; *hṛdayam* — at heart; *bhūri* — immensely; *karuṇaḥ* — merciful; *vidhāya* — having placed; *asau* — He; *gacchan* — going; *nija* — His own; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *paṅkeruha* — to the lotus; *rataiḥ* — by those devoted; *gadādhṛk* — by Gadadhara; *vipra* — by the brahmanas; *ādyaiḥ* — and others; *ahaha* — ah; *sa* — with; *mukundaiḥ* — Mukunda; *parivṛtaḥ* — surrounded; *tadā* — then; *taiḥ taiḥ sarvaiḥ* — by all of them; *katham api* — with difficulty; *hi* — indeed; *duḥkhena* — through grief; *dadṛśe* — was seen.

**76.** Placing Nityananda, joyful at heart, in front, the immensely merciful Lord went on, surrounded by those devoted to His lotus feet — Gadadhara, the brahmanas and others, together with Mukunda. Ah, all of them could then see Him only with difficulty, through their grief!

*Note.* *Gadādhṛk* ("bearer of the mace") is a synonym of the name Gadadhara. The compound *gadādhṛg-viprādyaiḥ* may also be read "by the brahmana Gadadhara and others".

### Verse 77

स इत्थं गौराङ्गः पथि निजगुणं नाम च गृण-
न्प्रियैः सार्धं स्वाङ्घ्रेर्निरवधि रुदन्नेव रुरुचे ।
अमी दानादानोल्लसितहृदयैर्दानिनिवहै-
र्न कुत्रापि श्रीमत्परिदृढकृपाढ्या रुरुधिरे ॥७७॥

*sa itthaṁ gaurāṅgaḥ pathi nija-guṇaṁ nāma ca gṛṇan*
*priyaiḥ sārdhaṁ svāṅghrer niravadhi rudann eva ruruce |*
*amī dānādānollasita-hṛdayair dāni-nivahair*
*na kutrāpi śrīmat-paridṛḍha-kṛpāḍhyā rurudhire ||77||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — He; *ittham* — thus; *gaurāṅgaḥ* — Gauranga; *pathi* — on the way; *nija* — His own; *guṇam* — qualities; *nāma* — name; *ca* — and; *gṛṇan* — chanting; *priyaiḥ* — with those dear; *sārdham* — together; *sva* — to His; *aṅghreḥ* — feet; *niravadhi* — ceaselessly; *rudan* — weeping; *eva* — indeed; *ruruce* — shone; *amī* — they; *dāna* — of tolls; *ādāna* — in the taking; *ullasita* — rejoicing; *hṛdayaiḥ* — [with] hearts; *dāni* — of toll-collectors; *nivahaiḥ* — by the crowds; *na* — not; *kutra api* — anywhere; *śrīmat* — of the beautiful [Lord]; *paridṛḍha* — steadfast; *kṛpā* — in the mercy; *āḍhyāḥ* — rich; *rurudhire* — were stopped.

**77.** Thus on the way Gauranga, chanting His own qualities and name together with those to whom His feet are dear, shone, weeping ceaselessly. And nowhere were they, rich in the steadfast mercy of the beautiful [Lord], stopped by the crowds of toll-collectors whose hearts rejoiced in the taking of tolls.

*Note.* *Dānin* is a collector of tolls at ferries and checkpoints. Cf. the episodes of the journey to Puri: Murari 3.5.7–9, 3.7 (the toll-collectors, the detention of Mukunda); Chaitanya-bhagavata, Antya 2.

### Verse 78

ततो गोपीनाथं स्ववसतिलसद्रेमुणमति-
प्रभावं तं दृष्ट्वा क्षितिमिलितमौली प्रणमतः ।
प्रभोः शीर्षे शीर्षादपि भगवतस्तस्य चलिता
प्रसूनानां चूडापतदखिले पश्यति जने ॥७८॥

*tato gopīnāthaṁ sva-vasati-lasad-remuṇam ati-*
*prabhāvaṁ taṁ dṛṣṭvā kṣiti-milita-maulī praṇamataḥ |*
*prabhoḥ śīrṣe śīrṣād api bhagavatas tasya calitā*
*prasūnānāṁ cūḍāpatad akhile paśyati jane ||78||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *gopīnātham* — Gopinatha; *sva* — by His own; *vasati* — residence; *lasat* — making shine; *remuṇam* — Remuna; *ati* — great; *prabhāvam* — [of] power; *tam* — that; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *kṣiti* — the ground; *milita* — touching; *maulī* — [with] the head; *praṇamataḥ* — as [He] bowed down; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *śīrṣe* — on the head; *śīrṣāt* — from the head; *api* — indeed; *bhagavataḥ* — of Bhagavan; *tasya* — of that; *calitā* — slipping; *prasūnānām* — of flowers; *cūḍā* — a crown; *apatat* — fell; *akhile* — all; *paśyati* — as [they] looked on; *jane* — the people.

**78.** Then [the Lord] saw that Gopinatha of great power whose residence makes Remuna shine. As He bowed down, His head touching the ground, a crown of flowers slipped from the head of that Bhagavan and, as all the people looked on, fell on the Lord's head.

*Note.* Remuna (near Balasore in Orissa) is the site of the temple of Gopinatha Kshirachora.

### Verse 79

ततः श्रीगौराङ्गः कटक इति संज्ञे जनपदे
स साक्षी गोपीनाथ इति जगति ख्यातिमगमत् ।
उभौ गौरश्यामद्युतिकृतविभेदौ न तु महा-
प्रभावाद्यैर्भिन्नौ सपदि ददृशाते जनचयैः ॥७९॥

*tataḥ śrī-gaurāṅgaḥ kaṭaka iti saṁjñe janapade*
*sa sākṣī gopīnātha iti jagati khyātim agamat |*
*ubhau gaura-śyāma-dyuti-kṛta-vibhedau na tu mahā-*
*prabhāvādyair bhinnau sapadi dadṛśāte jana-cayaiḥ ||79||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *śrī-gaurāṅgaḥ* — Sri Gauranga; *kaṭakaḥ* — Kataka; *iti* — thus; *saṁjñe* — called; *janapade* — in the district; *saḥ* — He; *sākṣī* — "the Witness"; *gopīnāthaḥ* — Gopinatha; *iti* — thus; *jagati* — in the world; *khyātim* — fame; *agamat* — attained; *ubhau* — both; *gaura* — by fair; *śyāma* — [and] dark; *dyuti* — lustre; *kṛta* — made; *vibhedau* — [having] a distinction; *na tu* — but not; *mahā* — by great; *prabhāva* — power; *ādyaiḥ* — and the rest; *bhinnau* — different; *sapadi* — at once; *dadṛśāte* — were seen; *jana* — of people; *cayaiḥ* — by crowds.

**79.** Then Sri Gauranga [came] to the district called Kataka, [where] He who has attained fame in the world as Sakshi-gopinatha [dwells]. The crowds of people at once beheld the two of Them: They were distinguished [only] by fair and dark lustre, but were not different in great power and the rest.

*Note.* Sakshi-gopala ("Gopala the Witness") is the Deity near Kataka (Cuttack). The syntax of the first half is elliptical. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 80

करे दत्त्वा दण्डं पथि तमवधूतस्य पुरतः
स्वयं श्रीगौराङ्गः सुखविवशचित्तश्चलितवान् ।
असौ पश्चाद्गच्छन् मनसि परिचिन्त्य प्रतिमुहु-
र्बभञ्जैनं दण्डं कृतकुतुकचेष्टोऽतिमुदितः ॥८०॥

*kare dattvā daṇḍaṁ pathi tam avadhūtasya purataḥ*
*svayaṁ śrī-gaurāṅgaḥ sukha-vivaśa-cittaś calitavān |*
*asau paścād gacchan manasi paricintya pratimuhur*
*babhañjainaṁ daṇḍaṁ kṛta-kutuka-ceṣṭo 'timuditaḥ ||80||*

*Word for word:* *kare* — into the hand; *dattvā* — having given; *daṇḍam* — the staff; *pathi* — on the way; *tam* — that; *avadhūtasya* — of the avadhuta; *purataḥ* — ahead; *svayam* — Himself; *śrī-gaurāṅgaḥ* — Sri Gauranga; *sukha* — by bliss; *vivaśa* — overwhelmed; *cittaḥ* — [with] a mind; *calitavān* — went; *asau* — He; *paścāt* — behind; *gacchan* — walking; *manasi* — in the mind; *paricintya* — having pondered; *pratimuhuḥ* — again and again; *babhañja* — broke; *enam* — this; *daṇḍam* — staff; *kṛta* — having played; *kutuka* — playful; *ceṣṭaḥ* — a prank; *ati* — greatly; *muditaḥ* — pleased.

**80.** On the way Sri Gauranga gave His staff into the hand of the avadhuta and Himself went ahead, His mind overwhelmed with bliss. And He [the avadhuta], walking behind, having pondered it again and again in His mind, broke that staff, greatly pleased with His playful prank.

*Note.* A famous episode: Nityananda breaks Chaitanya's sannyasa staff.

### Verse 81

अथासौ नेदीयानहह जगदे तेन चकितं
क्व मे दण्डो ब्रूहि प्रतिवचनमेषोऽपि विदधे ।
क्षितौ दैवादङ्घ्रिस्खलनमभवत्तेन समभू-
दसौ भग्नस्तत् किं तदनु च स चुक्रोध बहुधा ॥८१॥

*athāsau nedīyān ahaha jagade tena cakitaṁ*
*kva me daṇḍo brūhi prativacanam eṣo 'pi vidadhe |*
*kṣitau daivād aṅghri-skhalanam abhavat tena samabhūd*
*asau bhagnas tat kiṁ tad anu ca sa cukrodha bahudhā ||81||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *asau* — He; *nedīyān* — having come nearer; *ahaha* — ah; *jagade* — was addressed; *tena* — by Him; *cakitam* — in alarm; *kva* — where; *me* — My; *daṇḍaḥ* — staff; *brūhi* — tell; *prativacanam* — a reply; *eṣaḥ* — He; *api* — in turn; *vidadhe* — gave; *kṣitau* — on the ground; *daivāt* — by chance; *aṅghri* — of the foot; *skhalanam* — a slip; *abhavat* — happened; *tena* — because of that; *samabhūt* — became; *asau* — it; *bhagnaḥ* — broken; *tat* — so; *kim* — what [is to be done]; *tat anu* — after that; *ca* — and; *saḥ* — He; *cukrodha* — grew angry; *bahudhā* — greatly.

**81.** Then, when [the avadhuta] had come nearer, the Lord — ah! — said to Him in alarm: "Where is My staff? Tell Me!" And He in turn replied: "By chance My foot slipped on the ground, and so it broke. What [can be done]?" And after that the Lord grew very angry.

*Note.* The edition has *जगदेतेन*: by the metre (⏑⏑) this is not *jagāda* but *jagade tena*, "it was said by Him".

### Verse 82

तथा क्षुब्धो भूत्वा मनसि बहु संचिन्त्य स ययौ
हरेर्नाम्नां गाथाकथनमधुरोल्लासिवदनः ।
पथस्थान् देवांस्तान्निरवधि विलोक्य प्रमुदितो
ययौ पुण्यां धन्यामतिसुललितां याजनगरीम् ॥८२॥

*tathā kṣubdho bhūtvā manasi bahu saṁcintya sa yayau*
*harer nāmnāṁ gāthā-kathana-madhurollāsi-vadanaḥ |*
*patha-sthān devāṁs tān niravadhi vilokya pramudito*
*yayau puṇyāṁ dhanyām atisulalitāṁ yāja-nagarīm ||82||*

*Word for word:* *tathā* — thus; *kṣubdhaḥ* — agitated; *bhūtvā* — having become; *manasi* — in the mind; *bahu* — much; *saṁcintya* — having pondered; *saḥ* — He; *yayau* — went on; *hareḥ* — of Hari; *nāmnām* — of the names; *gāthā* — of songs; *kathana* — by the singing; *madhura* — sweetly; *ullāsi* — shining; *vadanaḥ* — [with] a face; *patha* — on the way; *sthān* — standing; *devān* — the Deities; *tān* — those; *niravadhi* — ceaselessly; *vilokya* — beholding; *pramuditaḥ* — joyful; *yayau* — came; *puṇyām* — to the holy; *dhanyām* — blessed; *ati-sulalitām* — most lovely; *yāja-nagarīm* — city of Yaja.

**82.** Thus agitated, and having pondered much in His mind, He went on, His face shining sweetly with the singing of songs of Hari's names. Joyfully beholding all the Deities along the way, He came to the holy, blessed, most lovely city of Yaja.

*Note.* Yaja-nagari is Yajapura (Jajpur) on the Vaitarani.

### Verse 83

अथैकाम्रक्षेत्रे स्मरदमनमालोक्य शतधा
स्तवं कृत्वा भूमौ पतति सति नाथे प्रमुदितः ।
शिवो देवः सोऽयं मलयरुहगन्धागुरुरसैः
प्रसादैरन्यैश्चार्चयदिव तत्पूजनविधिम् ॥८३॥

*athaikāmra-kṣetre smara-damanam ālokya śatadhā*
*stavaṁ kṛtvā bhūmau patati sati nāthe pramuditaḥ |*
*śivo devaḥ so 'yaṁ malayaruha-gandhāguru-rasaiḥ*
*prasādair anyaiś cārcayad iva tat-pūjana-vidhim ||83||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *ekāmra* — of Ekamra; *kṣetre* — in the sacred field; *smara* — of Smara; *damanam* — the Subduer; *ālokya* — having seen; *śatadhā* — a hundredfold; *stavam* — praise; *kṛtvā* — having offered; *bhūmau* — to the ground; *patati sati* — when [He] fell; *nāthe* — the Lord; *pramuditaḥ* — delighted; *śivaḥ* — Shiva; *devaḥ* — the god; *saḥ ayam* — he; *malayaruha* — of sandal; *gandha* — fragrant; *aguru* — of aguru; *rasaiḥ* — with essences; *prasādaiḥ* — with prasada; *anyaiḥ* — other; *ca* — and; *arcayat* — performed; *iva* — as it were; *tat* — His; *pūjana* — of worship; *vidhim* — the rite.

**83.** Then, in the sacred field of Ekamra, the Lord saw the Subduer of Smara, offered him praise a hundredfold and fell to the ground; and the god Shiva, delighted, as it were performed the rite of worshipping Him with essences of sandal and fragrant aguru and with other prasada.

*Note.* Ekamra-kshetra is Bhubaneshvara, the temple of Shiva Lingaraja. Shiva burned Kama (Smara) with the fire of his third eye.

### Verse 84

अथैतस्माद्गच्छन् कमलपुरमासाद्य ललितं
कपालेशं नत्वा विधिवदिह भार्गीस्नपनकृत् ।
ततस्तं प्रासादं गुरुशिखरकैलासललितं
स्फुरच्चक्रं वातप्रचलितपताकं कलितवान् ॥८४॥

*athaitasmād gacchan kamala-puram āsādya lalitaṁ*
*kapāleśaṁ natvā vidhivad iha bhārgī-snapana-kṛt |*
*tatas taṁ prāsādaṁ guru-śikhara-kailāsa-lalitaṁ*
*sphurac-cakraṁ vāta-pracalita-patākaṁ kalitavān ||84||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *etasmāt* — from there; *gacchan* — going; *kamala-puram* — Kamalapura; *āsādya* — having reached; *lalitam* — lovely; *kapāla-īśam* — to Kapalesha; *natvā* — having bowed; *vidhivat* — according to rule; *iha* — here; *bhārgī* — in the Bhargi; *snapana* — bathing; *kṛt* — performing; *tataḥ* — then; *tam* — that; *prāsādam* — temple; *guru* — with a lofty; *śikhara* — spire; *kailāsa* — [like] Kailasa; *lalitam* — lovely; *sphurat* — gleaming; *cakram* — [with] a disc; *vāta* — by the wind; *pracalita* — set fluttering; *patākam* — [with] a banner; *kalitavān* — beheld.

**84.** Going on from there, He reached lovely Kamalapura, bowed to Kapalesha and here bathed according to rule in the Bhargi. Then He beheld that temple, lovely as Kailasa with its lofty spire, with its gleaming disc and its banner fluttering in the wind.

*Note.* The temple is not named. Grammatically it could be Kapalesha's; but the "gleaming disc" (the Nila-chakra) and the banner are the marks of Jagannatha's temple, visible from afar from Kamalapura (Atharanala). According to tradition, it was here that the Lord, seeing the banner of the temple, was overcome with ecstasy (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 85

पतित्वा स क्षौण्यां नयनकमलोद्गीर्णपयसा
समं तैस्तैः सर्वैः क्षितितलमलं स्नानमकरोत् ।
ततो गत्वा क्षेत्रं कृतपरमभक्तिः प्रभुवरं
विवेशासौ श्रीमानथ समवलोक्यानमदमुम् ॥८५॥

*patitvā sa kṣauṇyāṁ nayana-kamalodgīrṇa-payasā*
*samaṁ tais taiḥ sarvaiḥ kṣiti-talam alaṁ snānam akarot |*
*tato gatvā kṣetraṁ kṛta-parama-bhaktiḥ prabhu-varaṁ*
*viveśāsau śrīmān atha samavalokyānamad amum ||85||*

*Word for word:* *patitvā* — having fallen; *saḥ* — He; *kṣauṇyām* — to the ground; *nayana* — of the eyes; *kamala* — from the lotuses; *udgīrṇa* — poured out; *payasā* — with the water; *samam* — together; *taiḥ taiḥ sarvaiḥ* — with all of them; *kṣiti* — of the earth; *talam* — the surface; *alam* — thoroughly; *snānam* — a bath; *akarot* — gave; *tataḥ* — then; *gatvā* — having come; *kṣetram* — to the Kshetra; *kṛta* — showing; *parama* — supreme; *bhaktiḥ* — devotion; *prabhu* — of lords; *varam* — [to] the Best; *viveśa* — entered; *asau* — He; *śrīmān* — the beautiful; *atha* — then; *samavalokya* — having beheld; *anamat* — bowed down; *amum* — to Him.

**85.** Falling to the ground together with all of them, He thoroughly bathed the surface of the earth with the water poured from His lotus eyes. Then, having come to the Kshetra, the beautiful [Lord], showing supreme devotion, entered [the presence of] the Best of lords and, beholding Him, bowed down.

*Note.* The Best of lords is Jagannatha.

### Verse 86

मुहुर्दृष्ट्वा तस्याननशशिनमत्यन्तमधुरं
गलन्नेत्राम्भोभिः स्वतनुमभिषिक्तामरचयत् ।
जगन्नाथोऽप्येनं निमिषरहितैरक्षिकमलै-
र्विलोक्य प्रेमाब्धौ निरवधि निमग्नोऽभवदिव ॥८६॥

*muhur dṛṣṭvā tasyānana-śaśinam atyanta-madhuraṁ*
*galan-netrāmbhobhiḥ sva-tanum abhiṣiktām aracayat |*
*jagannātho 'py enaṁ nimiṣa-rahitair akṣi-kamalair*
*vilokya premābdhau niravadhi nimagno 'bhavad iva ||86||*

*Word for word:* *muhuḥ* — again and again; *dṛṣṭvā* — gazing; *tasya* — His; *ānana* — of the face; *śaśinam* — on the moon; *atyanta* — most; *madhuram* — sweet; *galat* — streaming; *netra* — of the eyes; *ambhobhiḥ* — with the waters; *sva* — His own; *tanum* — body; *abhiṣiktām* — bathed; *aracayat* — made; *jagannāthaḥ* — Jagannatha; *api* — too; *enam* — at Him; *nimiṣa* — blinking; *rahitaiḥ* — without; *akṣi* — of the eyes; *kamalaiḥ* — with the lotuses; *vilokya* — looking; *prema* — of love; *abdhau* — in the ocean; *niravadhi* — endlessly; *nimagnaḥ* — immersed; *abhavat* — became; *iva* — as if.

**86.** Gazing again and again on the most sweet moon of His [Jagannatha's] face, He bathed His own body with the streaming tears of His eyes. And Jagannatha too, looking at Him with unblinking lotus eyes, became as if endlessly immersed in an ocean of love.

*Note.* Unblinking eyes are a mark of the gods and of the very form of Jagannatha.

### Verse 87

इत्थं चक्रे परमरभसं श्रीनवद्वीपभूमौ
गन्धैर्माल्यैर्मलयजरसैर्भूरिकर्पूरपूरैः ।
श्रीमद्वेशोद्गतमधुरिमाप्लावितशेषदेशः
स्वैः स्वैर्लोकैर्नटनकलया स्वैरमेष प्रकामम् ॥८७॥

*itthaṁ cakre parama-rabhasaṁ śrī-navadvīpa-bhūmau*
*gandhair mālyair malayaja-rasair bhūri-karpūra-pūraiḥ |*
*śrīmad-veśodgata-madhurimāplāvitāśeṣa-deśaḥ*
*svaiḥ svair lokair naṭana-kalayā svairam eṣa prakāmam ||87||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *cakre* — performed; *parama* — with the greatest; *rabhasam* — ardour; *śrī-navadvīpa* — of Sri Navadvipa; *bhūmau* — in the land; *gandhaiḥ* — with perfumes; *mālyaiḥ* — with garlands; *malayaja* — of sandal; *rasaiḥ* — with the essences; *bhūri* — abundant; *karpūra* — of camphor; *pūraiḥ* — with streams; *śrīmat* — splendid; *veśa* — from the appearance; *udgata* — arising; *madhurimā* — with the sweetness; *āplāvita* — who flooded; *aśeṣa* — all; *deśaḥ* — regions; *svaiḥ svaiḥ* — with His own; *lokaiḥ* — people; *naṭana* — of dancing; *kalayā* — with the art; *svairam* — freely; *eṣaḥ* — He; *prakāmam* — to His heart's content.

**87.** Thus in the land of Sri Navadvipa He who flooded all regions with the sweetness arising from His splendid appearance performed, with the greatest ardour, freely and to His heart's content, the art of dancing together with His own people — with perfumes, garlands, essences of sandal and abundant streams of camphor.

*Note.* Verses 87–89 are in the *mandākrāntā* metre: a summary of the Navadvipa period.

### Verse 88

गेहे गेहे समजनि सदा मूर्तिमत्येव लक्ष्मीः
स्थाने स्थाने सुखसमुदयो मूर्तिमानेव भूतः ।
नित्यं नित्यं नवनवमभूत् प्रेम सर्वस्य नाथे
स्वैरं स्वैरं विलसति तदा श्रीनवद्वीपभूमौ ॥८८॥

*gehe gehe samajani sadā mūrtimaty eva lakṣmīḥ*
*sthāne sthāne sukha-samudayo mūrtimān eva bhūtaḥ |*
*nityaṁ nityaṁ nava-navam abhūt prema sarvasya nāthe*
*svairaṁ svairaṁ vilasati tadā śrī-navadvīpa-bhūmau ||88||*

*Word for word:* *gehe gehe* — in every house; *samajani* — appeared; *sadā* — always; *mūrtimatī* — embodied; *eva* — herself; *lakṣmīḥ* — Lakshmi; *sthāne sthāne* — in every place; *sukha* — of happiness; *samudayaḥ* — the abundance; *mūrtimān* — embodied; *eva* — as if; *bhūtaḥ* — became; *nityam nityam* — day after day; *nava-navam* — ever new; *abhūt* — was; *prema* — the love; *sarvasya* — of everyone; *nāthe* — for the Lord; *svairam svairam* — quite freely; *vilasati* — when [He] sported; *tadā* — then; *śrī-navadvīpa* — of Sri Navadvipa; *bhūmau* — in the land.

**88.** When He sported quite freely in the land of Sri Navadvipa, in every house Lakshmi herself, embodied, was always present; in every place the abundance of happiness became as if embodied; and day after day everyone's love for the Lord was ever new.

### Verse 89

नासीन्निद्रा न भयमभवन्नाभवत् क्षुत्पिपासा
न स्वैरत्वं न च यमगता कालदण्डादिभीतिः ।
एकस्यापि प्रभुकरुणया यस्य कस्यापि तस्मि-
न्नेवं क्रीडत्यतिसुललितं श्रीनवद्वीपभूमौ ॥८९॥

*nāsīn nidrā na bhayam abhavan nābhavat kṣut-pipāsā*
*na svairatvaṁ na ca yama-gatā kāla-daṇḍādi-bhītiḥ |*
*ekasyāpi prabhu-karuṇayā yasya kasyāpi tasminn*
*evaṁ krīḍaty atisulalitaṁ śrī-navadvīpa-bhūmau ||89||*

*Word for word:* *na āsīt* — there was not; *nidrā* — sleep; *na* — not; *bhayam* — fear; *abhavat* — was; *na abhavat* — there was not; *kṣut* — hunger; *pipāsā* — [and] thirst; *na* — not; *svairatvam* — self-will; *na ca* — nor; *yama* — from Yama; *gatā* — coming; *kāla* — of Time; *daṇḍa* — of the rod; *ādi* — and the like; *bhītiḥ* — fear; *ekasya api* — of anyone at all; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *karuṇayā* — by the mercy; *yasya kasya api* — whoever he might be; *tasmin* — while He; *evam* — thus; *krīḍati* — sported; *ati-sulalitam* — most charmingly; *śrī-navadvīpa* — of Sri Navadvipa; *bhūmau* — in the land.

**89.** By the mercy of the Lord no one at all, whoever he might be, had sleep, or fear, or hunger and thirst, or self-will, or fear of Yama's rod of Time and the like, while He thus sported most charmingly in the land of Sri Navadvipa.

*Note.* *Kāla-daṇḍa*, "the rod of Time", is the staff of Yama, the lord of the departed.

**Colophon:** *iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahākāvye ekādaśaḥ sargaḥ* — "Thus [ends] the eleventh sarga in the mahakavya 'Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita'." (The colophon gives no title for the sarga.)
