## Sarga Twelve — verses 1–134

**Title of the sarga:** none — the colophon of the edition gives no title for this sarga.
**Metre:** *upajāti* (a mixture of *indravajrā* ——⏑——⏑⏑—⏑—— and *upendravajrā* ⏑—⏑——⏑⏑—⏑——; 11 syllables per pada); verse 87 — *śālinī*; verses 133–134 — *mālinī*.
**Total verses:** 134 (verses 49 and 112 have six padas; 112 opens with a quotation of Bhagavatam 10.81.16 in the *anuṣṭubh* metre; 87 — *śālinī*; 120 — the chant "Rāma Rāghava…"; 133–134 — *mālinī*).

**Contents of the passage:** the Lord in Puri with Sarvabhauma; the departure for the south as far as the Godavari.
- 1–9 — the Lord in Puri with Sarvabhauma; the darshan of Jagannatha.
- 10–35 — Sarvabhauma's plan to instruct the Lord in Vedanta; the disputation; the Lord refutes the doctrine of non-duality; the four-armed form; hymns of praise.
- 36–58 — the manuscript in Gopinatha's hand with Sarvabhauma's verse containing the word "Krishna"; the Lord, in ecstasy, returns to Puri; Gopinatha on the mercy shown to Sarvabhauma.
- 59–77 — the mahaprasada: Sarvabhauma eats it without first washing; both are in ecstasy; Sarvabhauma is humbled.
- 78–93 — eighteen interpretations of two stanzas from the Eleventh Canto; the verses *vairāgya-vidyā…* and *kālān naṣṭaṁ…* (the Lord tears up the leaf; Mukunda had copied them onto the wall); "bhakti-pade" instead of "mukti-pade".
- 94–106 — eighteen days in Puri; the departure for the south; Sarvabhauma advises the Lord to meet Ramananda; Kurma-kshetra, the brahmana Kurma.
- 107–117 — the leper Vasudeva is healed by an embrace; Kurma's lament.
- 118–121 — Nrisimha-kshetra; the Lord's gait; the chant "Rāma Rāghava… Kṛṣṇa Keśava…".
- 122–129 — the forests by the Godavari: peacocks, deer, parrots, cicadas, fearsome thickets and torrents.
- 130–132 — hesitation: whether to speak with Ramananda; the Lord passes by and goes on south in ecstasy.
- 133–134 (*mālinī*) — the wonder of the southerners: "A golden elephant? Meru set in motion? Lightning that does not fade?"

### Verse 1

प्रविश्य सत्क्षेत्रमदभ्रलीलः
श्रीसार्वभौमालयमाययौ सः ।
आकस्मिकं वीक्ष्य जगन्मनोज्ञं
सन्न्यासिनं सोऽथ ननन्द विप्रः ॥१॥

*praviśya sat-kṣetram adabhra-līlaḥ*
*śrī-sārvabhaumālayam āyayau saḥ |*
*ākasmikaṁ vīkṣya jagan-manojñaṁ [jñāna-manojñaṁ]*
*sannyāsinaṁ so 'tha nananda vipraḥ ||1||*

*Word for word:* *praviśya* — having entered; *sat* — the holy; *kṣetram* — Kshetra; *adabhra* — abundant; *līlaḥ* — [He whose] pastimes [are]; *śrī-sārvabhauma* — of Sri Sarvabhauma; *ālayam* — to the house; *āyayau* — came; *saḥ* — He; *ākasmikam* — unexpected; *vīkṣya* — having seen; *jagat* — to the world; *manojñam* — charming; *sannyāsinam* — the sannyasi; *saḥ* — that; *atha* — then; *nananda* — rejoiced; *vipraḥ* — brahmana.

**1.** Having entered the holy Kshetra, He whose pastimes are boundless came to the house of Sri Sarvabhauma. And that brahmana, seeing the unexpected sannyasi who charms the world, rejoiced.

*Note.* The edition has *ज्ञानमनोज्ञं* ("charming by knowledge"), but the metre requires ⏑⏑ at the sixth and seventh syllables; we read *jagan-manojñam*. The Kshetra is Purushottama-kshetra (Puri). Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya was a celebrated Vedantist and logician at the court of Puri.

### Verse 2

उत्थाय पाद्यादि समर्प्य भक्त्या
पुरो निवेद्यासनमप्युदारम् ।
कृतप्रणामो नु सुधीरमङ्ग
पप्रच्छ सर्वं विनयेन विप्रः ॥२॥

*utthāya pādyādi samarpya bhaktyā*
*puro nivedyāsanam apy udāram |*
*kṛta-praṇāmo nu sudhīram aṅga*
*papraccha sarvaṁ vinayena vipraḥ ||2||*

*Word for word:* *utthāya* — having risen; *pādya* — water for [washing] the feet; *ādi* — and the rest; *samarpya* — having offered; *bhaktyā* — with devotion; *puraḥ* — before [Him]; *nivedya* — having presented; *āsanam* — a seat; *api* — also; *udāram* — excellent; *kṛta* — having made; *praṇāmaḥ* — obeisance; *nu* — indeed; *su-dhīram* — very composedly; *aṅga* — (a particle); *papraccha* — asked; *sarvam* — about everything; *vinayena* — with humility; *vipraḥ* — the brahmana.

**2.** Rising, the brahmana with devotion offered water for [washing] the feet and the rest, set an excellent seat before [Him] as well, and, having made obeisance, very composedly and humbly asked about everything.

### Verse 3

कुतः समेतोऽसि कुतो नु यासि
हृद्यो भवान्निर्भरशान्तदान्तः ।
इत्थं प्रभौ तेन यथार्थपृष्टे
तदेकनाथाः सकलं तदूचुः ॥३॥

*kutaḥ sameto 'si kuto nu yāsi*
*hṛdyo bhavān nirbhara-śānta-dāntaḥ |*
*itthaṁ prabhau tena yathārtha-pṛṣṭe*
*tad-eka-nāthāḥ sakalaṁ tad ūcuḥ ||3||*

*Word for word:* *kutaḥ* — from where; *sametaḥ asi* — have You come; *kutaḥ nu* — where then; *yāsi* — are You going; *hṛdyaḥ* — charming; *bhavān* — You [are]; *nirbhara* — wholly; *śānta* — peaceful; *dāntaḥ* — [and] self-controlled; *ittham* — thus; *prabhau* — when the Lord; *tena* — by him; *yathārtha* — in substance; *pṛṣṭe* — had been asked; *tat* — Him; *eka* — as their only; *nāthāḥ* — [those who had as] Master; *sakalam* — all; *tat* — that; *ūcuḥ* — related.

**3.** "From where have You come, and where are You going? You are charming, wholly peaceful and self-controlled." When the Lord had been asked thus by him in earnest, those whose only Master He was related all of it.

### Verse 4

यथा-तथा तत् सकलं विदित्वा
ज्ञातं तदाज्ञातमिति प्रहृष्टः ।
ननन्द वृन्दारकवृन्दवन्द्य-
पादारविन्दस्य पुरः स विप्रः ॥४॥

*yathā-tathā tat sakalaṁ viditvā*
*jñātaṁ tadā 'jñātam iti prahṛṣṭaḥ |*
*nananda vṛndāraka-vṛnda-vandya-*
*pādāravindasya puraḥ sa vipraḥ ||4||*

*Word for word:* *yathā-tathā* — just as it was; *tat* — that; *sakalam* — all; *viditvā* — having learned; *jñātam* — [is] known; *tadā* — now; *ajñātam* — the unknown; *iti* — thus [thinking]; *prahṛṣṭaḥ* — delighted; *nananda* — rejoiced; *vṛndāraka* — of the gods; *vṛnda* — by the host; *vandya* — worshipped; *pāda* — feet; *aravindasya* — of [Him whose] lotus; *puraḥ* — before; *saḥ* — that; *vipraḥ* — brahmana.

**4.** Having learned all that just as it was, and delighted [at the thought] "Now the unknown has become known", that brahmana rejoiced before Him whose lotus feet are worshipped by the host of the gods.

*Note.* The edition has *तदाज्ञातम्*; we read *tadā 'jñātam*, "now the unknown [has become] known" (the metre is not affected).

### Verse 5

ज्ञात्वाथ तस्याशयमेव सद्यः
स्वयं स्वपुत्रेण सदादरेण ।
प्रस्थापयामास सितेतराद्रौ
प्रभुं जगन्नाथदिदृक्षुमञ्जः ॥५॥

*jñātvātha tasyāśayam eva sadyaḥ*
*svayaṁ sva-putreṇa sadādareṇa |*
*prasthāpayāmāsa sitetarādrau*
*prabhuṁ jagannātha-didṛkṣum añjaḥ ||5||*

*Word for word:* *jñātvā* — having understood; *atha* — then; *tasya* — His; *āśayam* — intention; *eva* — indeed; *sadyaḥ* — at once; *svayam* — himself; *sva* — with his own; *putreṇa* — son; *sat* — with due; *ādareṇa* — respect; *prasthāpayāmāsa* — sent; *sita-itara* — other than white (blue); *adrau* — to the mountain; *prabhum* — the Lord; *jagannātha* — Jagannatha; *didṛkṣum* — wishing to see; *añjaḥ* — straight.

**5.** Then, having understood His intention, he at once, with due respect, himself sent the Lord, who wished to see Jagannatha, straight to the Blue Mountain together with his own son.

*Note.* *Sitetarādri* ("the mountain other than white") is Nilachala, the "Blue Mountain", the hill of Jagannatha's temple.

### Verse 6

स तेन सार्धं समुपेत्य तत्र
सुखं ततः स्वैरमपि प्रविश्य ।
ददर्श नीलाचलमौलिरत्नं
तदातिसौख्याम्बुधिमग्न आसीत् ॥६॥

*sa tena sārdhaṁ samupetya tatra*
*sukhaṁ tataḥ svairam api praviśya |*
*dadarśa nīlācala-mauli-ratnaṁ*
*tadāti-saukhyāmbudhi-magna āsīt ||6||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — He; *tena* — with him; *sārdham* — together; *samupetya* — having come; *tatra* — there; *sukham* — joyfully; *tataḥ* — then; *svairam* — freely; *api* — and; *praviśya* — having entered; *dadarśa* — beheld; *nīlācala* — of Nilachala; *mauli* — of the crown; *ratnam* — the jewel; *tadā* — then; *ati* — of the greatest; *saukhya* — bliss; *ambudhi* — in an ocean; *magnaḥ* — immersed; *āsīt* — was.

**6.** Having come there together with him, and then joyfully and freely entering, He beheld the crest-jewel of Nilachala, and was then immersed in an ocean of the greatest bliss.

### Verse 7

विलोक्य भूयो नतिभिः स्तवैश्च
नेत्राम्बुभिः स्वामभिषिच्य मूर्तिम् ।
प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य च पञ्चकृत्वः
कृच्छ्रेण तस्माद्बहिराययौ सः ॥७॥

*vilokya bhūyo natibhiḥ stavaiś ca*
*netrāmbubhiḥ svām abhiṣicya mūrtim |*
*pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ca pañca-kṛtvaḥ*
*kṛcchreṇa tasmād bahir āyayau saḥ ||7||*

*Word for word:* *vilokya* — beholding; *bhūyaḥ* — again and again; *natibhiḥ* — with obeisances; *stavaiḥ* — with hymns; *ca* — and; *netra* — of the eyes; *ambubhiḥ* — with the waters; *svām* — His own; *abhiṣicya* — having bathed; *mūrtim* — form; *pradakṣiṇīkṛtya* — having circumambulated; *ca* — and; *pañca-kṛtvaḥ* — five times; *kṛcchreṇa* — with difficulty; *tasmāt* — from there; *bahiḥ* — out; *āyayau* — came; *saḥ* — He.

**7.** Beholding [Him] again and again with obeisances and hymns, having bathed His own form with the waters of His eyes, and having circumambulated five times, He came out from there with difficulty.

*Note.* *Svām mūrtim*, "His own form", may mean His own body, drenched with tears, or Jagannatha, the Lord's own Deity form (?).

### Verse 8

इति प्रभुस्तत्र विलोक्य कान्तं
ननन्द नीलाचलमौलिरत्नम् ।
स्वनामरत्नेन विधाय हारं
कण्ठे वहन्नेव रराज नित्यम् ॥८॥

*iti prabhus tatra vilokya kāntaṁ*
*nananda nīlācala-mauli-ratnam |*
*sva-nāma-ratnena vidhāya hāraṁ*
*kaṇṭhe vahann eva rarāja nityam ||8||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *tatra* — there; *vilokya* — beholding; *kāntam* — lovely; *nananda* — rejoiced; *nīlācala* — of Nilachala; *mauli* — of the crown; *ratnam* — the jewel; *sva* — of His own; *nāma* — name; *ratnena* — from the jewel; *vidhāya* — having made; *hāram* — a necklace; *kaṇṭhe* — on the neck; *vahan* — wearing; *eva* — indeed; *rarāja* — shone; *nityam* — always.

**8.** Thus the Lord rejoiced, beholding there the lovely crest-jewel of Nilachala. Having made a necklace of the jewel of His own name, and ever wearing it on His neck, He shone.

*Note.* That is, He chanted the Name unceasingly.

### Verse 9

मुकुन्ददत्तादिभिरात्मलोकैः
स तत्र नाथः कतिचिद्दिनानि ।
विलोकयन्नीलगिरीन्द्ररत्नं
निनाय कौतूहलपूर्णचित्तः ॥९॥

*mukunda-dattādibhir ātma-lokaiḥ*
*sa tatra nāthaḥ katicid dināni |*
*vilokayan nīla-girīndra-ratnaṁ*
*nināya kautūhala-pūrṇa-cittaḥ ||9||*

*Word for word:* *mukunda-datta* — with Mukunda Datta; *ādibhiḥ* — and others; *ātma* — His own; *lokaiḥ* — with people; *saḥ* — He; *tatra* — there; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *katicit* — some; *dināni* — days; *vilokayan* — beholding; *nīla* — of the Blue; *giri-indra* — king of mountains; *ratnam* — the jewel; *nināya* — spent; *kautūhala* — with eagerness; *pūrṇa* — filled; *cittaḥ* — [with] heart.

**9.** With Mukunda Datta and others of His own, the Lord spent some days there beholding the jewel of the Blue King of mountains, His heart filled with eagerness.

### Verse 10

स एकदा चेतसि सार्वभौमो
महीसुराग्र्यः कलयांचकार ।
प्रभावमैश्वर्यमिदं समस्तं
मनुष्यभावादविदन् कृपालोः ॥१०॥

*sa ekadā cetasi sārvabhaumo*
*mahīsurāgryaḥ kalayāṁ cakāra |*
*prabhāvam aiśvaryam idaṁ samastaṁ*
*manuṣya-bhāvād avidan kṛpāloḥ ||10||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — that; *ekadā* — once; *cetasi* — in the mind; *sārvabhaumaḥ* — Sarvabhauma; *mahī-sura* — of the gods of the earth (brahmanas); *agryaḥ* — the foremost; *kalayāṁ cakāra* — considered; *prabhāvam* — the power; *aiśvaryam* — the majesty; *idam* — this; *samastam* — all; *manuṣya* — human; *bhāvāt* — because of the condition; *avidan* — not knowing; *kṛpāloḥ* — of the Merciful One.

**10.** Once Sarvabhauma, the foremost of the brahmanas, reflected in his mind, not knowing, because of [His] human condition, all this power and majesty of the Merciful One.

*Note.* Verses 10–16 are Sarvabhauma's reflections.

### Verse 11

अखण्डपाण्डित्यसमुद्रवीचि-
प्रवाहकल्लोलकुलैरमन्दै-
र्यस्य प्रकामं बधिरीकृतोऽभू-
द्बृहस्पतिर्जाड्यमयं समेतः ॥११॥

*akhaṇḍa-pāṇḍitya-samudra-vīci-*
*pravāha-kallola-kulair amandair*
*yasya prakāmaṁ badhirīkṛto 'bhūd*
*bṛhaspatir jāḍyamayaṁ sametaḥ ||11||*

*Word for word:* *akhaṇḍa* — of unbroken; *pāṇḍitya* — learning; *samudra* — of the ocean; *vīci* — of the waves; *pravāha* — of the streams; *kallola* — of the billows; *kulaiḥ* — by the masses; *amandaiḥ* — mighty; *yasya* — by whose; *prakāmam* — utterly; *badhirīkṛtaḥ* — deafened; *abhūt* — became; *bṛhaspatiḥ* — Brihaspati; *jāḍya* — stupor; *mayam* — consisting of; *sametaḥ* — having fallen into.

**11.** He by whose mighty masses of billows, by whose streams of waves from the ocean of unbroken learning, Brihaspati himself was utterly deafened and fell into a stupor —

*Note.* *Yasya* ("he by whose") is taken up by *sa eva* ("that very one") in verse 12, which points to Sarvabhauma (?). Brihaspati is the preceptor of the gods, the very model of learning. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 12

स एव सम्भावितदम्भराशि-
र्गभीरधीर्यत्प्रभुपादपद्मम् ।
न वेद तन्नो खलु चित्रमेत-
न्न वेत्ति पाण्डित्यकुलादिलेशम् ॥१२॥

*sa eva sambhāvita-dambha-rāśir*
*gabhīra-dhīr yat prabhu-pāda-padmam |*
*na veda tan no khalu citram etan*
*na vetti pāṇḍitya-kulādi-leśam ||12||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ eva* — that very one; *sambhāvita* — esteemed; *dambha* — of pride; *rāśiḥ* — a heap; *gabhīra* — deep; *dhīḥ* — [of] intellect; *yat* — that; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *pāda* — of the feet; *padmam* — the lotus; *na veda* — did not know; *tat* — that; *no khalu* — not at all; *citram* — a wonder; *etat* — this; *na vetti* — does not know; *pāṇḍitya* — of the learning; *kula* — of the lineage; *ādi* — and so on; *leśam* — a particle.

**12.** — he, that very one, a heap of esteemed pride, deep of intellect, did not know the lotus feet of the Lord. That is no wonder at all: he does not know even a particle of His learning, lineage and so on.

*Note.* The edition has *yan na … na veda*, a double negative; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *yat prabhu-pāda-padmaṁ na veda*, and so we read: "that he did not know the feet of the Lord is no wonder".

### Verse 13

असौ महात्मा पुरुषप्रधानो
वयस्थ एव न्यसनं चकार ।
यदीदृशं स्वान्तरलं तदालं
विचिन्तितैर्नस्त्वयि कष्टमेतत् ॥१३॥

*asau mahātmā puruṣa-pradhāno*
*vayastha eva nyasanaṁ cakāra |*
*yadīdṛśaṁ svāntaralaṁ tad ālaṁ (?)*
*vicintitair nas tvayi kaṣṭam etat ||13||*

*Word for word:* *asau* — this; *mahātmā* — great soul; *puruṣa* — among men; *pradhānaḥ* — the foremost; *vayasthaḥ* — while young; *eva* — indeed; *nyasanam* — renunciation; *cakāra* — has made; *yadi* — if; *īdṛśam* — such; *sva-antaram* — His heart; *alam* — enough; *tat* — then; *ālam* (?) — enough; *vicintitaiḥ* — with deliberations; *naḥ* — our; *tvayi* — for You; *kaṣṭam* — hard; *etat* — this.

**13.** "This great soul, the foremost among men, has embraced renunciation while still young. If such is His heart, then enough of our deliberations. But for You this is hard!

*Note.* The second half is obscure. The edition has *स्वान्तरलं तदालं*, perhaps corrupt (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *yad īdṛśaṁ svāntar alaṁ tadā laṁ / vicintitair na tvayi kaṣṭam etat*, with *na*: "this is not hard for You".

### Verse 14

अनेकधा पुरुषरत्नचिह्नै-
र्मनोरमः सर्वजगज्जनस्य ।
कथं नु कालं गमयिष्यतीमं
सन्न्यासधर्मप्रतिपालनेन ॥१४॥

*anekadhā puruṣa-ratna-cihnair*
*manoramaḥ sarva-jagaj-janasya |*
*kathaṁ nu kālaṁ gamayiṣyatīmaṁ*
*sannyāsa-dharma-pratipālanena ||14||*

*Word for word:* *anekadhā* — manifold; *puruṣa* — among men; *ratna* — of a jewel; *cihnaiḥ* — by the marks; *manoramaḥ* — charming; *sarva* — of the whole; *jagat* — world; *janasya* — to the people; *katham nu* — how indeed; *kālam* — time; *gamayiṣyati* — will He pass; *imam* — this; *sannyāsa* — of sannyasa; *dharma* — of the duties; *pratipālanena* — by the observance.

**14.** He who by the manifold marks of a jewel among men charms the people of the whole world — how indeed will He pass this time in observing the duties of sannyasa?

*Note.* In the first pada the fifth syllable (*pu-* of *puruṣa*) is light, where both *indravajrā* and *upendravajrā* require a heavy one; perhaps the poetic form *pūruṣa* was intended (?).

### Verse 15

असौ महावंशसमुद्भवश्च
महाशयश्चाल्पवयोविकाशः ।
कलौ तदर्हां यतितां सुदुर्गां
कथं तरिष्यत्यहहातिकष्टम् ॥१५॥

*asau mahā-vaṁśa-samudbhavaś ca*
*mahāśayaś cālpa-vayo-vikāśaḥ |*
*kalau tad-arhāṁ yatitāṁ sudurgāṁ*
*kathaṁ tariṣyaty ahahāti-kaṣṭam ||15||*

*Word for word:* *asau* — He; *mahā* — of a great; *vaṁśa* — family; *samudbhavaḥ* — born; *ca* — and; *mahā-āśayaḥ* — magnanimous; *ca* — and; *alpa* — scarcely; *vayaḥ* — of age; *vikāśaḥ* — [whose] blossoming; *kalau* — in Kali; *tat* — for it; *arhām* — befitting; *yatitām* — asceticism; *su-durgām* — most arduous; *katham* — how; *tariṣyati* — will He get through; *ahaha* — alas; *ati* — exceedingly; *kaṣṭam* — hard.

**15.** He is born of a great family, He is magnanimous, and His youth has scarcely blossomed. How will He get through, in [the age of] Kali, the most arduous asceticism befitting it? Alas, how exceedingly hard!

### Verse 16

तदेतमत्यन्तसुशान्तचित्तं
संश्राव्य वेदान्तमजस्रमेव ।
करोमि वैराग्यरसेन भास्व-
ज्ज्ञानैकतानेन च मोक्षपान्थम् ॥१६॥

*tad etam atyanta-suśānta-cittaṁ*
*saṁśrāvya vedāntam ajasram eva |*
*karomi vairāgya-rasena bhāsvaj-*
*jñānaika-tānena ca mokṣa-pāntham ||16||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — therefore; *etam* — Him; *atyanta* — wholly; *su-śānta* — very peaceful; *cittam* — [whose] heart; *saṁśrāvya* — having made to hear; *vedāntam* — the Vedanta; *ajasram* — unceasingly; *eva* — indeed; *karomi* — I shall make; *vairāgya* — of detachment; *rasena* — by the taste; *bhāsvat* — to radiant; *jñāna* — knowledge; *eka-tānena* — [and] by whole-hearted devotion; *ca* — and; *mokṣa* — to liberation; *pāntham* — a wayfarer.

**16.** Therefore, by making Him, whose heart is wholly at peace, hear the Vedanta unceasingly, I shall make Him a wayfarer on the road to liberation, through the taste of detachment and through whole-hearted devotion to radiant knowledge."

*Note.* Sarvabhauma means to instruct the Lord in Advaita Vedanta. Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 6: for seven days Sarvabhauma expounds the Brahma-sutras.

### Verse 17

इत्यस्य हृन्मन्त्रितमाकलय्य
प्रभुः प्रफुल्लाम्बुजमञ्जुलास्यः ।
व्याप्य त्रिलोकीं स्फुरितानुकम्पा-
विलोलचेता मनसा जहास ॥१७॥

*ity asya hṛn-mantritam ākalayya*
*prabhuḥ praphullāmbuja-mañjulāsyaḥ |*
*vyāpya trilokīṁ sphuritānukampā-*
*vilola-cetā manasā jahāsa ||17||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *asya* — his; *hṛt* — of the heart; *mantritam* — the design; *ākalayya* — having perceived; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *praphulla* — full-blown; *ambuja* — [like] a lotus; *mañjula* — charming; *āsyaḥ* — [with] face; *vyāpya* — pervading; *trilokīm* — the three worlds; *sphurita* — with flashing forth; *anukampā* — compassion; *vilola* — stirred; *cetāḥ* — [with] heart; *manasā* — in the mind; *jahāsa* — laughed.

**17.** Having perceived this design of his heart, the Lord, whose face was charming as a full-blown lotus, and whose heart was stirred by a compassion that flashed forth and pervaded the three worlds, laughed inwardly.

### Verse 18

अन्येद्युरुद्दामखरांशुराजि-
राजद्द्युतिः स्वैश्चरणानुरक्तैः ।
जगाम तस्यालयमात्तजोषो
दोषाकराकारमनोहरास्यः ॥१८॥

*anyedyur uddāma-kharāṁśu-rāji-*
*rājad-dyutiḥ svaiś caraṇānuraktaiḥ |*
*jagāma tasyālayam ātta-joṣo*
*doṣākarākāra-manoharāsyaḥ ||18||*

*Word for word:* *anyedyuḥ* — on the next day; *uddāma* — of the unrestrained; *khara* — hot; *aṁśu* — [sun's] rays; *rāji* — with the array; *rājat* — shining; *dyutiḥ* — [with] splendour; *svaiḥ* — with His own; *caraṇa* — to [His] feet; *anuraktaiḥ* — devoted; *jagāma* — went; *tasya* — his; *ālayam* — to the house; *ātta* — having taken; *joṣaḥ* — contentment; *doṣākara* — of the moon; *ākāra* — with the form; *manohara* — charming; *āsyaḥ* — [with] face.

**18.** On the next day, His splendour shining like the array of the rays of the fierce, unrestrained sun, His face charming with the form of the moon, the Lord, content, went to his house with His own [devotees], who were devoted to His feet.

*Note.* *Doṣākara* ("maker of the night") is the moon.

### Verse 19

विलोक्य नाथं सह शिष्यवृन्दैः
समुत्थितः स प्रणनाम शश्वत् ।
सदासनं चाथ निवेद्य तस्मिं-
स्तत्र स्थितोऽभूत् स्वयमासनस्थः ॥१९॥

*vilokya nāthaṁ saha śiṣya-vṛndaiḥ*
*samutthitaḥ sa praṇanāma śaśvat |*
*sad-āsanaṁ cātha nivedya tasmiṁs*
*tatra sthito 'bhūt svayam āsana-sthaḥ ||19||*

*Word for word:* *vilokya* — having seen; *nātham* — the Lord; *saha* — together; *śiṣya* — of disciples; *vṛndaiḥ* — with the crowds; *samutthitaḥ* — having risen; *saḥ* — he; *praṇanāma* — bowed; *śaśvat* — again and again; *sat* — a fine; *āsanam* — seat; *ca* — and; *atha* — then; *nivedya* — having offered; *tasmin* — to Him; *tatra* — there; *sthitaḥ abhūt* — settled; *svayam* — himself; *āsana* — on a seat; *sthaḥ* — seated.

**19.** Seeing the Lord, he rose together with the crowds of his disciples and bowed down again and again. Then, having offered Him a fine seat, he himself settled there on a seat.

### Verse 20

उवाच विप्रो विनयेन नाथं
वेदान्त एतैः परिपठ्यतेऽत्र ।
भवादृशा योग्यतमाः शृणुध्वं
मनःकषायो यत आशु याति ॥२०॥

*uvāca vipro vinayena nāthaṁ*
*vedānta etaiḥ paripaṭhyate 'tra |*
*bhavādṛśā yogyatamāḥ śṛṇudhvaṁ*
*manaḥ-kaṣāyo yata āśu yāti ||20||*

*Word for word:* *uvāca* — said; *vipraḥ* — the brahmana; *vinayena* — with humility; *nātham* — to the Lord; *vedāntaḥ* — the Vedanta; *etaiḥ* — by these; *paripaṭhyate* — is studied; *atra* — here; *bhavādṛśāḥ* — those like You; *yogyatamāḥ* — [are] most worthy; *śṛṇudhvam* — listen; *manaḥ* — of the mind; *kaṣāyaḥ* — the impurity; *yataḥ* — whereby; *āśu* — quickly; *yāti* — goes away.

**20.** The brahmana humbly said to the Lord: "Here the Vedanta is studied by these [disciples]. Such as You are the most worthy [of it]. Listen, then, for by it the impurity of the mind quickly goes away."

*Note.* *Kaṣāya*, literally "astringent, dark", is in Yoga and Vedanta the residual impurity of the mind.

### Verse 21

अधीतमध्यापितमेतदुच्चै-
रनेकशस्तत् पुनरप्यमुष्य ।
प्रभोः समीपे धरणीसुराग्र्यो
बभूव संपाठयितुं प्रमत्तः ॥२१॥

*adhītam adhyāpitam etad uccair*
*anekaśas tat punar apy amuṣya |*
*prabhoḥ samīpe dharaṇī-surāgryo*
*babhūva saṁpāṭhayituṁ pramattaḥ ||21||*

*Word for word:* *adhītam* — [has been] studied; *adhyāpitam* — taught; *etat* — this; *uccaiḥ* — thoroughly; *anekaśaḥ* — many times; *tat* — therefore; *punaḥ api* — once again; *amuṣya* — of this; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *samīpe* — in the presence; *dharaṇī-sura* — of the gods of the earth (brahmanas); *agryaḥ* — the foremost; *babhūva* — set about; *saṁpāṭhayitum* — to teach; *pramattaḥ* — heedlessly.

**21.** "This I have thoroughly studied and taught many times" — and so the foremost of the brahmanas heedlessly set about teaching it once again in the presence of this Lord.

*Note.* *Pramatta*, "intoxicated, heedless": Sarvabhauma does not know whom he is teaching.

### Verse 22

साक्षान्महीगीष्पतिरेष चञ्च-
त्प्रागल्भ्यसंयुक्तवचा यथाधि ।
निर्वक्ति तत्तत् स निशम्य नाथः
शनैस्तदोद्ग्राहविधिं चकार ॥२२॥

*sākṣān mahī-gīṣpatir eṣa cañcat-*
*prāgalbhya-saṁyukta-vacā yathādhi |*
*nirvakti tat tat sa niśamya nāthaḥ*
*śanais tadodgrāha-vidhiṁ cakāra ||22||*

*Word for word:* *sākṣāt* — in person; *mahī* — of the earth; *gīṣpatiḥ* — the Brihaspati; *eṣaḥ* — this; *cañcat* — flashing; *prāgalbhya* — with boldness; *saṁyukta* — filled; *vacāḥ* — [with] speech; *yathā-adhi* — as he understood; *nirvakti* — expounds; *tat tat* — this and that; *saḥ* — He; *niśamya* — having heard; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *śanaiḥ* — slowly; *tadā* — then; *udgrāha* — of objection; *vidhim* — the procedure; *cakāra* — began.

**22.** This Brihaspati of the earth in person expounded this and that as he understood it, with speech full of flashing boldness. Having heard him, the Lord then slowly began, in due order, to raise objections.

*Note.* *Udgrāha* in debate is the putting forward of a thesis or an objection. *Yathādhi* — "according to [his] understanding" (*yathā* + *adhi*) (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 23

किमुच्यते कः खलु पूर्वपक्षः
किं वास्य राद्धान्तितमातनोषि ।
वेदान्तशास्त्रस्य न चायमर्थ-
स्तच्छ्रूयतां यत्तु निरूपयामः ॥२३॥

*kim ucyate kaḥ khalu pūrva-pakṣaḥ*
*kiṁ vāsya rāddhāntitam ātanoṣi |*
*vedānta-śāstrasya na cāyam arthas*
*tac chrūyatāṁ yat tu nirūpayāmaḥ ||23||*

*Word for word:* *kim* — what; *ucyate* — is said; *kaḥ* — what; *khalu* — indeed; *pūrva-pakṣaḥ* — [is] the initial thesis; *kim* — what; *vā* — or; *asya* — its; *rāddhāntitam* — conclusion; *ātanoṣi* — do you set forth; *vedānta* — of the Vedanta; *śāstrasya* — of the scripture; *na* — not; *ca* — and; *ayam* — this; *arthaḥ* — [is] the meaning; *tat* — therefore; *śrūyatām* — let it be heard; *yat* — what; *tu* — however; *nirūpayāmaḥ* — I shall set forth.

**23.** "What is being asserted here? What indeed is the initial thesis? Or what do you set forth as its conclusion? This is not the meaning of the Vedanta scripture. So hear what I shall set forth."

*Note.* *Pūrva-pakṣa* is the opponent's thesis, *siddhānta* (*rāddhānta*) the final conclusion: terms of Sanskrit disputation. *Nirūpayāmaḥ* is plural ("We shall set forth").

### Verse 24

इत्यस्य पक्षप्रतिपक्षरूपं
स पक्षमेकं स तु सज्जयित्वा ।
अद्वैतवादं विनिरस्य भक्ति-
संस्थापकं स्वीयमतं जगाद ॥२४॥

*ity asya pakṣa-pratipakṣa-rūpaṁ*
*sa pakṣam ekaṁ sa tu sajjayitvā |*
*advaita-vādaṁ vinirasya bhakti-*
*saṁsthāpakaṁ svīya-mataṁ jagāda ||24||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus [having spoken]; *asya* — his; *pakṣa* — of the thesis; *pratipakṣa* — of the counter-thesis; *rūpam* — in the form; *saḥ* — He; *pakṣam* — a thesis; *ekam* — one; *saḥ tu* — He; *sajjayitvā* — having made ready; *advaita* — of non-duality; *vādam* — the doctrine; *vinirasya* — having refuted; *bhakti* — bhakti; *saṁsthāpakam* — establishing; *svīya* — His own; *matam* — view; *jagāda* — expounded.

**24.** Having spoken thus, He made ready a thesis of His own in the form of a counter-thesis to his thesis, refuted the doctrine of non-duality and expounded His own view, which establishes bhakti.

### Verse 25

इत्थं प्रमाणैरखिलैश्च शक्त्या
तात्पर्यतो लक्षणया च गौण्या ।
मुख्याजहत्स्वार्थतदन्यमिश्र-
स्वरूपया स्वं मतमाबभाषे ॥२५॥

*itthaṁ pramāṇair akhilaiś ca śaktyā*
*tātparyato lakṣaṇayā ca gauṇyā |*
*mukhyā-jahat-svārtha-tad-anya-miśra-*
*svarūpayā svaṁ matam ābabhāṣe ||25||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *pramāṇaiḥ* — by the means of valid knowledge; *akhilaiḥ* — all; *ca* — and; *śaktyā* — by the [denotative] power [of words]; *tātparyataḥ* — by intention; *lakṣaṇayā* — by indication; *ca* — and; *gauṇyā* — by the figurative [sense]; *mukhyā* — primary; *jahat-svārtha* — abandoning its own meaning; *tat-anya* — the other than that [not abandoning it]; *miśra* — mixed; *svarūpayā* — by [indication] of the kinds; *svam* — His own; *matam* — view; *ābabhāṣe* — expounded.

**25.** Thus, by all the means of valid knowledge and by the power of words — by intention (*tātparya*), by indication (*lakṣaṇā*) and by the figurative sense (*gauṇī*), by the primary sense (*mukhyā*), and by indication that abandons its own meaning, that does not abandon it, and that is mixed — He expounded His own view.

*Note.* The categories of Sanskrit semantics are listed here: *mukhyā vṛtti*, the primary sense; *gauṇī*, the figurative sense based on similarity; *lakṣaṇā*, indication, of which there are three kinds: *jahat-svārthā* (the word's own meaning is abandoned), *ajahat-svārthā* (it is retained) and the mixed *jahad-ajahat-svārthā*; *tātparya*, the overall intention of a statement. *Śakti* is the denotative power of a word. The form *mukhyā* at the beginning of a compound is unusual (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 26

असौ वितण्डाच्छलनिग्रहाद्यै-
र्निरस्तधीरप्यथ पूर्वपक्षम् ।
चकार विप्रः प्रभुना स चाशु
स्वसिद्धसिद्धान्तवता निरस्तः ॥२६॥

*asau vitaṇḍā-cchala-nigrahādyair*
*nirasta-dhīr apy atha pūrva-pakṣam |*
*cakāra vipraḥ prabhunā sa cāśu*
*sva-siddha-siddhāntavatā nirastaḥ ||26||*

*Word for word:* *asau* — this; *vitaṇḍā* — by cavilling; *chala* — by quibbles; *nigraha* — by "points of defeat"; *ādyaiḥ* — and the like; *nirasta* — refuted; *dhīḥ* — [whose] intellect; *api* — though; *atha* — then; *pūrva-pakṣam* — a thesis; *cakāra* — put forward; *vipraḥ* — the brahmana; *prabhunā* — by the Lord; *saḥ* — he; *ca* — and; *āśu* — quickly; *sva* — by itself; *siddha* — established; *siddhānta* — conclusion; *vatā* — by [Him] possessing; *nirastaḥ* — was refuted.

**26.** Though his intellect had been refuted, the brahmana then put forward a thesis [again] by cavilling, quibbles, "points of defeat" and the like; and he was quickly refuted by the Lord, whose conclusion is self-established.

*Note.* *Vitaṇḍā* (cavilling: disputation without a thesis of one's own), *chala* (verbal quibble) and *nigraha-sthāna* (a ground for declaring the opponent defeated) are terms of Nyaya.

### Verse 27

अद्वैतवादी प्रथमः पदाब्ज-
वादी प्रभुश्च प्रतिभैकसिन्धुः ।
तौ भक्तसेव्यौ बहु दीर्घकालं
वदावदैर्निन्यतुरन्यथैव ॥२७॥

*advaita-vādī prathamaḥ padābja-*
*vādī prabhuś ca pratibhaika-sindhuḥ |*
*tau bhakta-sevyau bahu dīrgha-kālaṁ*
*vadāvadair ninyatur anyathaiva ||27||*

*Word for word:* *advaita* — of non-duality; *vādī* — a proponent; *prathamaḥ* — the first; *pada* — of the feet; *abja* — of the lotus; *vādī* — a proponent; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *ca* — and; *pratibhā* — of genius; *eka* — the one; *sindhuḥ* — ocean; *tau* — the two; *bhakta* — by adherents; *sevyau* — attended; *bahu* — very; *dīrgha* — long; *kālam* — time; *vadāvadaiḥ* — in disputations; *ninyatuḥ* — spent; *anyathā* — differently; *eva* — indeed.

**27.** The first was a proponent of non-duality, and the Lord, the one ocean of genius, a proponent of the lotus feet. Attended by their adherents, the two of them spent a very long time in disputations, each [arguing] in his own way.

*Note.* *Padābja-vādī* ("proponent of the lotus feet") — a defender of personal devotion to God.

### Verse 28

अथैष विस्मेरमना द्विजाग्र्यो
हृदा हृदि व्याकुलितो जगाद ।
क एष मत्प्रातिभखण्डनार्थ-
मिहावतीर्णः किमु गीष्पतिः स्यात् ॥२८॥

*athaiṣa vismera-manā dvijāgryo*
*hṛdā hṛdi vyākulito jagāda |*
*ka eṣa mat-prātibha-khaṇḍanārtham*
*ihāvatīrṇaḥ kim u gīṣpatiḥ syāt ||28||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *eṣaḥ* — this; *vismera* — astonished; *manāḥ* — [with] mind; *dvija* — of the brahmanas; *agryaḥ* — the foremost; *hṛdā hṛdi* — in the depth of his heart; *vyākulitaḥ* — troubled; *jagāda* — said; *kaḥ* — who; *eṣaḥ* — this; *mat* — my; *prātibha* — genius; *khaṇḍana* — of shattering; *artham* — for the sake; *iha* — here; *avatīrṇaḥ* — has descended; *kim u* — can it be that; *gīṣpatiḥ* — Brihaspati; *syāt* — He is.

**28.** Then the foremost of the brahmanas, his mind astonished, troubled in the depth of his heart, said [to himself]: "Who is He who has descended here to shatter my genius? Can He be Brihaspati?

### Verse 29

इतीह तर्को मम सर्वदासी-
द्बृहस्पतिर्मत्प्रतिभासमुद्रे ।
न पारमासादयिता कदापि
सदोद्यतः सन्नपि बुद्धिनावा ॥२९॥

*itīha tarko mama sarvadāsīd*
*bṛhaspatir mat-pratibhā-samudre |*
*na pāram āsādayitā kadāpi*
*sadodyataḥ sann api buddhi-nāvā ||29||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *iha* — here; *tarkaḥ* — reasoning; *mama* — my; *sarvadā* — always; *āsīt* — was; *bṛhaspatiḥ* — Brihaspati; *mat* — of my; *pratibhā* — genius; *samudre* — in the ocean; *na* — not; *pāram* — the farther shore; *āsādayitā* — will reach; *kadā api* — ever; *sadā* — always; *udyataḥ* — striving; *san api* — even though being; *buddhi* — of intellect; *nāvā* — in the boat.

**29.** My reasoning has always been this: Brihaspati, though ever striving in the boat of his intellect, will never reach the farther shore of the ocean of my genius.

### Verse 30

अयं तु कैशोरवयाः कियद्वा-
प्यधीतमास्ते वद पाठितं किम् ।
तथापि शक्तिर्मम नैव भूता
पराभवायास्य ममैव साभूत् ॥३०॥

*ayaṁ tu kaiśora-vayāḥ kiyad vāpy*
*adhītam āste vada pāṭhitaṁ kim |*
*tathāpi śaktir mama naiva bhūtā*
*parābhavāyāsya mamaiva sābhūt ||30||*

*Word for word:* *ayam* — He; *tu* — but; *kaiśora* — of boyhood; *vayāḥ* — [is of] age; *kiyat* — how much; *vā api* — indeed; *adhītam āste* — has [He] studied; *vada* — say; *pāṭhitam* — has [He] taught; *kim* — what; *tathā api* — even so; *śaktiḥ* — power; *mama* — my; *na eva* — not at all; *bhūtā* — served; *parābhavāya* — for the defeat; *asya* — His; *mama* — my; *eva* — only; *sā* — it; *abhūt* — served [for].

**30.** But He is only of the age of boyhood: how much can He have studied? Say, what has He taught? Even so, my power did not serve to defeat Him at all; it served only for my own [defeat].

*Note.* *Sā* (feminine) refers back to *śaktiḥ*: the power meant to overcome the Lord has served only to overcome Sarvabhauma himself. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 31

तदेष कृष्णः खलु नान्यथैव
चरित्रमेतद्गमकं हि तत्र ।
इत्थं विचिन्त्यैव हृदा हृदीशं
ननाम रोमाञ्चसमञ्चिताङ्गः ॥३१॥

*tad eṣa kṛṣṇaḥ khalu nānyathaiva*
*caritram etad gamakaṁ hi tatra |*
*itthaṁ vicintyaiva hṛdā hṛdīśaṁ*
*nanāma romāñca-samañcitāṅgaḥ ||31||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — so; *eṣaḥ* — He; *kṛṣṇaḥ* — [is] Krishna; *khalu* — surely; *na anyathā eva* — and not otherwise; *caritram* — conduct; *etat* — this; *gamakam* — the proof; *hi* — for; *tatra* — of that; *ittham* — thus; *vicintya* — having reflected; *eva* — indeed; *hṛdā* — in the heart; *hṛdi-īśam* — to the Lord of hearts; *nanāma* — bowed; *romāñca* — with horripilation; *samañcita* — covered; *aṅgaḥ* — [with] body.

**31.** So He is surely Krishna, and nothing else: this conduct is the proof of it." Having reflected thus in his heart, he, his body covered with horripilation, bowed down to the Lord of hearts.

### Verse 32

निर्यद्विलोलाक्षिसराः स रेमे
समुद्गमोऽसौ स्तुतिनत्युपेतः ।
प्रसादयामास विभुं स चापि
कृपैकसिन्धुः प्रससाद तत्र ॥३२॥

*niryad-vilolākṣi-sarāḥ sa reme*
*samudgamo 'sau stuti-naty-upetaḥ |*
*prasādayāmāsa vibhuṁ sa cāpi*
*kṛpaika-sindhuḥ prasasāda tatra ||32||*

*Word for word:* *niryat* — flowing; *vilola* — of the trembling; *akṣi* — eyes; *sarāḥ* — [with] streams; *saḥ* — he; *reme* — rejoiced; *samudgamaḥ* — with hair standing on end; *asau* — he; *stuti* — with praises; *nati* — [and] obeisances; *upetaḥ* — endowed; *prasādayāmāsa* — propitiated; *vibhum* — the Almighty; *saḥ* — He; *ca api* — and; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *eka* — the one; *sindhuḥ* — ocean; *prasasāda* — became gracious; *tatra* — then.

**32.** With streams flowing from his trembling eyes, he rejoiced; with his hair standing on end, he propitiated the Almighty with praises and obeisances. And He, the one ocean of mercy, then became gracious [to him].

*Note.* *Samudgama* (literally "rising") here probably means the bristling of the hair on the body. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 33

प्रदर्शयामास चतुर्भुजत्वं
दिवाकराणां शतकोटिभास्वत् ।
ततोऽधिकं सोऽपि ननन्द विप्र-
स्ततोऽधिकं च स्तवमप्यकार्षीत् ॥३३॥

*pradarśayāmāsa catur-bhujatvaṁ*
*divākarāṇāṁ śata-koṭi-bhāsvat |*
*tato 'dhikaṁ so 'pi nananda vipras*
*tato 'dhikaṁ ca stavam apy akārṣīt ||33||*

*Word for word:* *pradarśayāmāsa* — revealed; *catuḥ* — four-; *bhujatvam* — armed form; *divākarāṇām* — of suns; *śata-koṭi* — a thousand million; *bhāsvat* — shining [like]; *tataḥ* — thereupon; *adhikam* — still more; *saḥ api* — he too; *nananda* — rejoiced; *vipraḥ* — the brahmana; *tataḥ* — than that; *adhikam* — more exalted; *ca* — and; *stavam* — a hymn; *api* — also; *akārṣīt* — composed.

**33.** He revealed His four-armed form, shining like a thousand million suns. Thereupon the brahmana rejoiced still more, and composed a hymn more exalted still.

*Note.* In the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 6.202) the Lord shows Sarvabhauma first His four-armed form and then His own form, dark-complexioned and holding the flute; in the Chaitanya-bhagavata (Antya 3) He shows him a six-armed form. Karnapura speaks of the four-armed form.

### Verse 34

यद्यत् स भूमीसुरसङ्घमुख्य-
स्तुष्टाव तुष्टः सुमहाप्रगल्भः ।
तत्तन्न वाचस्पतिरप्यभीक्ष्णं
प्रयासतोऽपि प्रभवेद्भविष्णुः ॥३४॥

*yad yat sa bhūmīsura-saṅgha-mukhyas*
*tuṣṭāva tuṣṭaḥ sumahā-pragalbhaḥ |*
*tat tan na vācaspatir apy abhīkṣṇaṁ*
*prayāsato 'pi prabhaved bhaviṣṇuḥ ||34||*

*Word for word:* *yat yat* — whatever; *saḥ* — that; *bhūmī-sura* — of brahmanas; *saṅgha* — of the assembly; *mukhyaḥ* — chief; *tuṣṭāva* — praised; *tuṣṭaḥ* — delighted; *su-mahā* — most; *pragalbhaḥ* — eloquent; *tat tat* — that; *na* — not; *vācaspatiḥ* — Vachaspati (Brihaspati); *api* — even; *abhīkṣṇam* — again and again; *prayāsataḥ* — with effort; *api* — even; *prabhavet* — could master; *bhaviṣṇuḥ* — capable.

**34.** Whatever [hymns] that chief of the assembly of brahmanas, delighted and most eloquent, offered in praise, not even Vachaspati, capable though he is, could master, even striving again and again.

*Note.* The edition has *प्रभवेद्धविष्णुः*; perhaps a corruption of *prabhaviṣṇuḥ*, "capable" (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 35

अथैष नाथः कतिचिद्दिनानि
नीत्वा प्रयातुं दिशि दक्षिणस्याम् ।
चक्रे मनस्तं समनुव्रजन्तः
सर्वे च जग्मुर्हरिनामपूर्वम् ॥३५॥

*athaiṣa nāthaḥ katicid dināni*
*nītvā prayātuṁ diśi dakṣiṇasyām |*
*cakre manas taṁ samanuvrajantaḥ*
*sarve ca jagmur hari-nāma-pūrvam ||35||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *eṣaḥ* — this; *nāthaḥ* — Lord; *katicit* — some; *dināni* — days; *nītvā* — having spent; *prayātum* — to set out; *diśi* — in the direction; *dakṣiṇasyām* — southern; *cakre manaḥ* — resolved; *tam* — Him; *samanuvrajantaḥ* — following; *sarve* — all; *ca* — and; *jagmuḥ* — went; *hari* — of Hari; *nāma* — the name; *pūrvam* — [with … on their lips].

**35.** Then, having spent some days [there], the Lord resolved to set out to the south. And all went along, following Him, with the name of Hari [on their lips].

*Note.* In the edition the lines are wrongly divided (the first pada runs on to *nītvā*). By the metre, *nītvā* opens the second pada.

### Verse 36

गत्वा कियद्दूरमसौ कृपावान्
विसर्जयामास तदा समस्तान् ।
तत्रान्तरे वर्त्मनि सोऽपि गोपी-
नाथाह्वयो भूसुर आननाम ॥३६॥

*gatvā kiyad dūram asau kṛpāvān*
*visarjayāmāsa tadā samastān |*
*tatrāntare vartmani so 'pi gopī-*
*nāthāhvayo bhūsura ānanāma ||36||*

*Word for word:* *gatvā* — having gone; *kiyat* — some; *dūram* — distance; *asau* — He; *kṛpāvān* — merciful; *visarjayāmāsa* — dismissed; *tadā* — then; *samastān* — all; *tatra antare* — meanwhile; *vartmani* — on the road; *saḥ api* — he; *gopīnātha* — Gopinatha; *āhvayaḥ* — named; *bhūsuraḥ* — a brahmana; *ānanāma* — bowed down.

**36.** Having gone some distance, the merciful One then dismissed them all. Meanwhile, on the road, a brahmana named Gopinatha bowed down [to Him].

*Note.* In the edition the lines are again wrongly divided (*so 'pi / gopīnātha…*). Gopinatha Acharya, Sarvabhauma's brother-in-law, was a devotee of the Lord.

### Verse 37

प्रभुः करे तस्य विलोक्य पुस्ती-
मेकां स्तवानां प्रणयाद्विकृष्य ।
जग्राह गच्छन्नथ सर्व एव
समागतास्तं समनुव्रजन्तः ॥३७॥

*prabhuḥ kare tasya vilokya pustīm*
*ekāṁ stavānāṁ praṇayād vikṛṣya |*
*jagrāha gacchann atha sarva eva*
*samāgatās taṁ samanuvrajantaḥ ||37||*

*Word for word:* *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *kare* — in the hand; *tasya* — his; *vilokya* — having seen; *pustīm* — a manuscript; *ekām* — one; *stavānām* — of hymns; *praṇayāt* — affectionately; *vikṛṣya* — having snatched; *jagrāha* — took; *gacchan* — going on; *atha* — then; *sarve eva* — all; *samāgatāḥ* — came up; *tam* — Him; *samanuvrajantaḥ* — following.

**37.** Seeing a manuscript of hymns in his hand, the Lord affectionately snatched it and took it. Then, as He went on, all [the others] came up, following Him.

### Verse 38

गतेषु सर्वेषु स एक एव
प्रभुर्व्रजन् कुत्र च वृक्षमूले ।
सुखोपविष्टः परिमुच्य पुस्ती-
मालोकयामास चिराय हर्षात् ॥३८॥

*gateṣu sarveṣu sa eka eva*
*prabhur vrajan kutra ca vṛkṣa-mūle |*
*sukhopaviṣṭaḥ parimucya pustīm*
*ālokayāmāsa cirāya harṣāt ||38||*

*Word for word:* *gateṣu* — when [they] had gone; *sarveṣu* — all; *saḥ* — He; *ekaḥ eva* — alone; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *vrajan* — walking; *kutra ca* — at some; *vṛkṣa* — of a tree; *mūle* — at the foot; *sukha* — comfortably; *upaviṣṭaḥ* — seated; *parimucya* — having untied; *pustīm* — the manuscript; *ālokayāmāsa* — looked [at it]; *cirāya* — for a long time; *harṣāt* — with delight.

**38.** When all had gone, the Lord, walking alone, sat down comfortably at the foot of some tree, untied the manuscript and looked at it for a long time with delight.

### Verse 39

स तत्र नाथः परितो विचार्य
श्रीसार्वभौमस्य कवित्वमेकम् ।
विलोकयामास तदा पदानां
मध्ये पदं कृष्ण इति व्यपश्यत् ॥३९॥

*sa tatra nāthaḥ parito vicārya*
*śrī-sārvabhaumasya kavitvam ekam |*
*vilokayāmāsa tadā padānāṁ*
*madhye padaṁ kṛṣṇa iti vyapaśyat ||39||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — He; *tatra* — there; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *paritaḥ* — all round; *vicārya* — having examined; *śrī-sārvabhaumasya* — of Sri Sarvabhauma; *kavitvam* — a poem; *ekam* — one; *vilokayāmāsa* — saw; *tadā* — then; *padānām* — of the words; *madhye* — among; *padam* — the word; *kṛṣṇaḥ* — "Krishna"; *iti* — thus; *vyapaśyat* — noticed.

**39.** Examining it all round, the Lord saw there a poem of Sri Sarvabhauma, and then among its words He noticed the word "Krishna".

*Note.* Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 6.252–255: Sarvabhauma's verses glorifying Chaitanya as Krishna (*vairāgya-vidyā-nija-bhakti-yoga…*); Mukunda copied them onto a wall, and the Lord, having read them, tore up the leaf.

### Verse 40

विलोक्य तं कृष्णपदं तदैव
प्रेमातिरेकेण स विह्वलात्मा ।
पपात भूमौ नयनाश्रुधारा-
समूहधौताङ्गलतो विचेष्टः ॥४०॥

*vilokya taṁ kṛṣṇa-padaṁ tadaiva*
*premātirekeṇa sa vihvalātmā |*
*papāta bhūmau nayanāśru-dhārā-*
*samūha-dhautāṅga-lato viceṣṭaḥ ||40||*

*Word for word:* *vilokya* — having seen; *tam* — that; *kṛṣṇa* — "Krishna"; *padam* — word; *tadā eva* — at once; *prema* — of love; *atirekeṇa* — from the excess; *saḥ* — He; *vihvala* — overwhelmed; *ātmā* — [with] soul; *papāta* — fell; *bhūmau* — to the ground; *nayana* — of the eyes; *aśru* — of tears; *dhārā* — of the streams; *samūha* — by the flood; *dhauta* — washed; *aṅga* — of the body; *lataḥ* — [with] the creeper; *viceṣṭaḥ* — motionless.

**40.** Seeing that word "Krishna", He at once, His soul overwhelmed by an excess of love, fell motionless to the ground, the creeper of His body washed by a flood of streams of tears from His eyes.

### Verse 41

तथैव भूमौ पतितः स वृक्ष-
मूलेऽवशेषं दिवसस्य यच्च ।
निशां च सर्वामनयत् कृपालुः
श्रीसार्वभौमे करुणां विधित्सुः ॥४१॥

*tathaiva bhūmau patitaḥ sa vṛkṣa-*
*mūle 'vaśeṣaṁ divasasya yac [yaś] ca |*
*niśāṁ ca sarvām anayat kṛpāluḥ*
*śrī-sārvabhaume karuṇāṁ vidhitsuḥ ||41||*

*Word for word:* *tathā eva* — just so; *bhūmau* — on the ground; *patitaḥ* — lying; *saḥ* — He; *vṛkṣa* — of the tree; *mūle* — at the foot; *avaśeṣam* — the remainder; *divasasya* — of the day; *yat* — which; *ca* — and; *niśām* — the night; *ca* — and; *sarvām* — whole; *anayat* — spent; *kṛpāluḥ* — the Merciful One; *śrī-sārvabhaume* — to Sri Sarvabhauma; *karuṇām* — mercy; *vidhitsuḥ* — wishing to show.

**41.** Lying just so on the ground at the foot of the tree, the Merciful One spent what remained of the day and the whole night, wishing to show mercy to Sri Sarvabhauma.

*Note.* The edition has *यश्च*; by the sense, *yac ca*.

### Verse 42

प्रातः प्रबुद्धोऽतिसुविह्वलात्मा
जगाम वाग्गद्गदरुद्धकण्ठः ।
अहो ममाभूद्बहुलापराधो
महानुभावात्मनि सार्वभौमे ॥४२॥

*prātaḥ prabuddho 'tisuvihvalātmā*
*jagāma vāg-gadgada-ruddha-kaṇṭhaḥ |*
*aho mamābhūd bahulāparādho*
*mahānubhāvātmani sārvabhaume ||42||*

*Word for word:* *prātaḥ* — in the morning; *prabuddhaḥ* — having awoken; *ati-su-vihvala* — deeply overwhelmed; *ātmā* — [with] soul; *jagāma* — went; *vāk* — with speech; *gadgada* — faltering; *ruddha* — choked; *kaṇṭhaḥ* — [with] throat; *aho* — ah; *mama* — by Me; *abhūt* — has been [committed]; *bahula* — great; *aparādhaḥ* — an offence; *mahā-anubhāva* — great; *ātmani* — [whose] soul [is]; *sārvabhaume* — against Sarvabhauma.

**42.** Awaking in the morning, His soul deeply overwhelmed, He went on, His throat choked and His voice faltering: "Ah, I have committed a great offence against the great-souled Sarvabhauma!

*Note.* The Gosvami edition (GGM) also reads *jagāma*, "went"; the words of verses 42–44 are spoken as He goes.

### Verse 43

कथं नु वा तं परिहाय मोहा-
द्गच्छामि दम्भैकवशेन तीर्थम् ।
क्षेत्रं पुनर्यामि तदस्य सेवां
करोमि स त्वेव महानुभावः ॥४३॥

*kathaṁ nu vā taṁ parihāya mohād*
*gacchāmi dambhaika-vaśena tīrtham |*
*kṣetraṁ punar yāmi tad asya sevāṁ*
*karomi sa tv eva mahānubhāvaḥ ||43||*

*Word for word:* *katham nu vā* — how indeed; *tam* — him; *parihāya* — having abandoned; *mohāt* — out of delusion; *gacchāmi* — shall I go; *dambha* — of pride; *eka* — alone; *vaśena* — under the sway; *tīrtham* — on pilgrimage; *kṣetram* — to the Kshetra; *punaḥ* — again; *yāmi* — I shall go; *tat* — therefore; *asya* — his; *sevām* — service; *karomi* — I shall do; *saḥ* — he; *tu eva* — indeed; *mahā-anubhāvaḥ* — [is] a great soul.

**43.** How indeed can I abandon him out of delusion and go on pilgrimage under the sway of pride alone? I shall go back to the Kshetra and serve him, for he is indeed a great soul.

### Verse 44

अमुष्य सेवाविधिमन्तरेण
न किञ्चनापि प्रयतः करिष्ये ।
इत्येव भूयः करुणापयोधिः
क्षेत्रं समायात् प्रहरैकमध्ये ॥४४॥

*amuṣya sevā-vidhim antareṇa*
*na kiñcanāpi prayataḥ kariṣye |*
*ity eva bhūyaḥ karuṇā-payodhiḥ*
*kṣetraṁ samāyāt praharaika-madhye ||44||*

*Word for word:* *amuṣya* — his; *sevā* — of service; *vidhim* — the rite; *antareṇa* — apart from; *na kiñcana api* — nothing whatever; *prayataḥ* — diligently; *kariṣye* — shall I do; *iti* — thus [resolving]; *eva* — indeed; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *karuṇā* — of mercy; *payodhiḥ* — the ocean; *kṣetram* — to the Kshetra; *samāyāt* — came back; *prahara* — of a watch; *eka* — of one; *madhye* — within.

**44.** Apart from the rite of serving him, I shall diligently do nothing whatever." Resolving thus, the ocean of mercy came back again to the Kshetra within a single watch.

*Note.* A watch (*prahara*) is about three hours.

### Verse 45

आचार्यवर्यानयनाय कञ्चि-
त्संप्रेषयामास झटित्यथापि ।
स तु त्वरावान् समुपेत्य गोपी-
नाथं तमाचार्यवरं जगाद ॥४५॥

*ācārya-varyānayanāya kañcit*
*saṁpreṣayāmāsa jhaṭity athāpi |*
*sa tu tvarāvān samupetya gopī-*
*nāthaṁ tam ācārya-varaṁ jagāda ||45||*

*Word for word:* *ācārya* — of acharyas; *varya* — the best; *ānayanāya* — to fetch; *kañcit* — someone; *saṁpreṣayāmāsa* — [He] sent; *jhaṭiti* — at once; *atha api* — then; *saḥ* — he; *tu* — and; *tvarāvān* — hastening; *samupetya* — having come up; *gopīnātham* — to Gopinatha; *tam* — to that; *ācārya* — of acharyas; *varam* — the best; *jagāda* — said.

**45.** Then He at once sent someone to fetch the best of acharyas. And that [man], hastening, came up to Gopinatha, that best of acharyas, and said:

*Note.* The subject is not named in the text. By the context it is the Lord, who has just returned to the Kshetra (44): the messenger announces that "Krishna-Chaitanya has come here" (46), and Gopinatha hastens "to Him" (48), while Sarvabhauma does not yet know of the Lord's return.

### Verse 46

आचार्य शीघ्रं समुपेहि कृष्ण-
चैतन्यदेवोऽयमिहागतोऽस्ति ।
किमात्थ रे किं वितथं समस्तं
गतः सहर्षो दिशि दक्षिणस्याम् ॥४६॥

*ācārya śīghraṁ samupehi kṛṣṇa-*
*caitanya-devo 'yam ihāgato 'sti |*
*kim āttha re kiṁ vitathaṁ samastaṁ*
*gataḥ saharṣo diśi dakṣiṇasyām ||46||*

*Word for word:* *ācārya* — O Acharya; *śīghram* — quickly; *samupehi* — come; *kṛṣṇa-caitanya* — Krishna-Chaitanya; *devaḥ* — the divine; *ayam* — this; *iha* — here; *āgataḥ asti* — has come; *kim* — what; *āttha* — are you saying; *re* — hey; *kim* — can it be; *vitatham* — false; *samastam* — all; *gataḥ* — [He] went; *sa* — with; *harṣaḥ* — joy; *diśi* — in the direction; *dakṣiṇasyām* — southern.

**46.** "O Acharya, come quickly: the divine Krishna-Chaitanya has come here!" — "What are you saying, fellow? Can it all be false? [Why,] He joyfully went off to the south!

*Note.* The Lord's sannyasa name, Krishna-Chaitanya, is mentioned for the first time in this sarga.

### Verse 47

अस्माभिरेवायमनुव्रजद्भि-
र्विदूरतस्त्यक्त इतः कथं स्यात् ।
इत्युक्तवानेष पुनश्च तेन
सत्यं ब्रवीमीत्यसकृत् स उक्तः ॥४७॥

*asmābhir evāyam anuvrajadbhir*
*vidūratas tyakta itaḥ kathaṁ syāt |*
*ity uktavān eṣa punaś ca tena*
*satyaṁ bravīmīty asakṛt sa uktaḥ ||47||*

*Word for word:* *asmābhiḥ* — by us; *eva* — ourselves; *ayam* — He; *anuvrajadbhiḥ* — accompanying [Him]; *vidūrataḥ* — far away; *tyaktaḥ* — was left; *itaḥ* — from here; *katham* — how; *syāt* — could [He] be [here]; *iti* — thus; *uktavān* — spoke; *eṣaḥ* — he; *punaḥ* — again; *ca* — and; *tena* — by that [man]; *satyam* — the truth; *bravīmi* — I speak; *iti* — thus; *asakṛt* — repeatedly; *saḥ* — he; *uktaḥ* — was told.

**47.** We ourselves accompanied Him and took leave of Him far from here — how could He be here?" Thus [Gopinatha] spoke, and the other told him again and again: "I am speaking the truth!"

### Verse 48

त्वरान्वितस्तन्निकटं स गोपी-
नाथः सदाचार्यवरो जगाम ।
अवेक्ष्य तं हृष्टमना महात्मा
सविस्मयं सप्रियमाजगाद ॥४८॥

*tvarānvitas tan-nikaṭaṁ sa gopī-*
*nāthaḥ sad-ācārya-varo jagāma |*
*avekṣya taṁ hṛṣṭa-manā mahātmā*
*savismayaṁ sapriyam ājagāda ||48||*

*Word for word:* *tvarā* — with haste; *anvitaḥ* — filled; *tat* — to Him; *nikaṭam* — near; *saḥ* — that; *gopīnāthaḥ* — Gopinatha; *sat* — of worthy; *ācārya* — acharyas; *varaḥ* — the best; *jagāma* — went; *avekṣya* — having seen; *tam* — Him; *hṛṣṭa* — delighted; *manāḥ* — [with] a heart; *mahātmā* — the great soul; *sa* — with; *vismayam* — wonder; *sa* — with; *priyam* — affection; *ājagāda* — said.

**48.** Gopinatha, the best of worthy acharyas, hastened to Him. Seeing Him, the great soul rejoiced at heart and said with wonder and affection:

### Verse 49

किमेतदाश्चर्यमतीव देव
कथं गतो वा कथमागतो वा ।
ततः प्रभुर्दन्तविसूनरोचि-
श्छटासमापृक्तविलोहितौष्ठः ।
उवाच माध्वीकरसाप्लुतेन
वचोविलासेन विलासवान् सः ॥४९॥

*kim etad āścaryam atīva deva*
*kathaṁ gato vā katham āgato vā |*
*tataḥ prabhur danta-visūna-roci-*
*cchaṭā-samāpṛkta-vilohitauṣṭhaḥ |*
*uvāca mādhvīka-rasāplutena*
*vaco-vilāsena vilāsavān saḥ ||49||*

*Word for word:* *kim* — what; *etat* — this; *āścaryam* — wonder; *atīva* — very great; *deva* — O Lord; *katham* — how; *gataḥ* — [did You] go; *vā* — indeed; *katham* — how; *āgataḥ* — [have You] come back; *vā* — indeed; *tataḥ* — then; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *danta* — of [His] teeth; *visūna* — [like] blossomed [flowers]; *roci* — of the radiance; *chaṭā* — with the lustre; *samāpṛkta* — mingled; *vilohita* — crimson; *oṣṭhaḥ* — [with] lips; *uvāca* — spoke; *mādhvīka* — of honey-wine; *rasa* — with the juice; *āplutena* — steeped; *vacaḥ* — of speech; *vilāsena* — with the play; *vilāsavān* — graceful; *saḥ* — He.

**49.** "What is this very great wonder, O Lord? How did You go, and how have You come back?" Then the graceful Lord, His crimson lips mingled with the lustre of the radiance of His teeth, which were like blossomed flowers, spoke with a play of words steeped in the juice of honey-wine:

*Note.* A verse of six padas. *Visūna*, "blossomed": the usual *prasūna* ("flower") would break the metre.

### Verse 50

आचार्य भूयानपराधराशि-
र्ममाभवत् संप्रति सार्वभौमे ।
यतोऽहमेतं परिहाय दम्भा-
त्तीर्थाटनं कर्तुमना बभूव ॥५०॥

*ācārya bhūyān aparādha-rāśir*
*mamābhavat samprati sārvabhaume |*
*yato 'ham etaṁ parihāya dambhāt*
*tīrthāṭanaṁ kartu-manā babhūva ||50||*

*Word for word:* *ācārya* — O Acharya; *bhūyān* — great; *aparādha* — of offences; *rāśiḥ* — a heap; *mama* — of Mine; *abhavat* — has come about; *samprati* — now; *sārvabhaume* — against Sarvabhauma; *yataḥ* — because; *aham* — I; *etam* — him; *parihāya* — having abandoned; *dambhāt* — out of pride; *tīrtha* — to holy places; *aṭanam* — wandering; *kartu-manāḥ* — wishing to undertake; *babhūva* — became.

**50.** "O Acharya, I have now committed a great heap of offences against Sarvabhauma: for out of pride I abandoned him and wished to wander to the holy places.

### Verse 51

असौ महात्मा भगवत्स्वरूपो
जगत्त्रयीत्राणपरः सदीहः ।
यदस्य वक्त्रादुदभूत् स कृष्ण-
नामानवद्यं ललितैकपद्यम् ॥५१॥

*asau mahātmā bhagavat-svarūpo*
*jagat-trayī-trāṇa-paraḥ sad-īhaḥ |*
*yad asya vaktrād udabhūt sa kṛṣṇa-*
*nāmānavadyaṁ lalitaika-padyam ||51||*

*Word for word:* *asau* — he; *mahātmā* — the great soul; *bhagavat* — of Bhagavan; *svarūpaḥ* — [is] of the very nature; *jagat-trayī* — of the three worlds; *trāṇa* — to the deliverance; *paraḥ* — devoted; *sat* — good; *īhaḥ* — [with] aspirations; *yat* — for; *asya* — his; *vaktrāt* — from the mouth; *udabhūt* — came forth; *saḥ* — that; *kṛṣṇa* — of Krishna; *nāma* — [with] the name; *anavadyam* — faultless; *lalita* — charming; *eka* — one; *padyam* — verse.

**51.** That great soul is of the very nature of Bhagavan; he is devoted to the deliverance of the three worlds, and his aspirations are good: for from his mouth came forth that one faultless, charming verse with the name of Krishna.

### Verse 52

तदस्य सेवैव मया विधेया
मम त्वियं केवलमीशसेवा ।
इत्थं विचिन्त्यार्थमहं गतोऽपि
तीर्थप्रयाणे पुनरागतश्च ॥५२॥

*tad asya sevaiva mayā vidheyā*
*mama tv iyaṁ kevalam īśa-sevā |*
*itthaṁ vicintyārtham ahaṁ gato 'pi*
*tīrtha-prayāṇe punar āgataś ca ||52||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — therefore; *asya* — to him; *sevā* — service; *eva* — only; *mayā* — by Me; *vidheyā* — is to be rendered; *mama* — for Me; *tu* — indeed; *iyam* — this; *kevalam* — the only; *īśa* — to the Lord; *sevā* — service; *ittham* — thus; *vicintya* — having considered; *artham* — the matter; *aham* — I; *gataḥ api* — though having gone; *tīrtha* — to the holy places; *prayāṇe* — on the journey; *punaḥ* — again; *āgataḥ* — have come back; *ca* — and.

**52.** Therefore I must render service only to him: for Me this is the only service to the Lord. Having considered the matter thus, I have come back again, though I had set out on the journey to the holy places."

### Verse 53

इत्यस्य वाचं परमां दुरूहां
श्रुतिस्मृतीनामपि सारभूताम् ।
अथैव मृग्यां परिमृग्य विप्रः
क्षिप्रं जहास स्फुटदन्तपङ्क्तिः ॥५३॥

*ity asya vācaṁ paramāṁ durūhāṁ*
*śruti-smṛtīnām api sāra-bhūtām |*
*athaiva mṛgyāṁ parimṛgya vipraḥ*
*kṣipraṁ jahāsa sphuṭa-danta-paṅktiḥ ||53||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *asya* — His; *vācam* — speech; *paramām* — supreme; *durūhām* — inconceivable; *śruti* — of the shruti; *smṛtīnām* — [and] of the smriti; *api* — even; *sāra* — the essence; *bhūtām* — being; *atha* — then; *eva* — indeed; *mṛgyām* — worthy of inquiry; *parimṛgya* — having pondered; *vipraḥ* — the brahmana; *kṣipram* — at once; *jahāsa* — laughed; *sphuṭa* — displaying; *danta* — of teeth; *paṅktiḥ* — [with] a row.

**53.** Having pondered this supreme, inconceivable speech of His, worthy of inquiry and the very essence of the shruti and smriti, the brahmana at once laughed, displaying a row of teeth.

### Verse 54

अहो महाकारुणिकस्य चेष्टां
पश्य प्रभोर्दीनजने कृपालोः ।
को वास्य जानातु महादुरापं
माहात्म्यमेते खलु कीटकल्पाः ॥५४॥

*aho mahākāruṇikasya ceṣṭāṁ*
*paśya prabhor dīna-jane kṛpāloḥ |*
*ko vāsya jānātu mahā-durāpaṁ*
*māhātmyam ete khalu kīṭa-kalpāḥ ||54||*

*Word for word:* *aho* — ah; *mahā-kāruṇikasya* — of the supremely compassionate; *ceṣṭām* — the conduct; *paśya* — see; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *dīna* — to the wretched; *jane* — people; *kṛpāloḥ* — merciful; *kaḥ vā* — who indeed; *asya* — His; *jānātu* — can know; *mahā* — very; *durāpam* — hard to attain; *māhātmyam* — greatness; *ete* — these [people]; *khalu* — indeed; *kīṭa* — to worms; *kalpāḥ* — similar.

**54.** "Ah, see the conduct of the supremely compassionate Lord, merciful to wretched people! Who can know His greatness, so very hard to attain? These people are indeed like worms.

### Verse 55

अहो महाकारुणिकस्य पश्य
जगत्कृपापूरभृतं चिकीर्षोः ।
अनुग्रहं सम्प्रति सार्वभौमे
देवेशकल्पैरपि यो दुरापः ॥५५॥

*aho mahākāruṇikasya paśya*
*jagat kṛpā-pūra-bhṛtaṁ cikīrṣoḥ |*
*anugrahaṁ samprati sārvabhaume*
*deveśa-kalpair api yo durāpaḥ ||55||*

*Word for word:* *aho* — ah; *mahā-kāruṇikasya* — of the supremely compassionate [Lord]; *paśya* — see; *jagat* — the world; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *pūra* — with a flood; *bhṛtam* — filled; *cikīrṣoḥ* — wishing to make; *anugraham* — the favour; *samprati* — now; *sārvabhaume* — to Sarvabhauma; *deva-īśa* — the lord of the gods; *kalpaiḥ* — by those like; *api* — even; *yaḥ* — which; *durāpaḥ* — [is] hard to attain.

**55.** Ah, see the favour now [shown] to Sarvabhauma by the supremely compassionate [Lord], who wishes to fill the world with a flood of mercy — [a favour] hard to attain even for those like the lord of the gods!

### Verse 56

वेदान्तिनां मण्डलसार्वभौमः
स सार्वभौमो गतभक्तिगन्धः ।
दैवेन पद्योद्गतकृष्णनामा
बभूव युष्मत्करुणाधिपात्रम् ॥५६॥

*vedāntināṁ maṇḍala-sārvabhaumaḥ*
*sa sārvabhaumo gata-bhakti-gandhaḥ |*
*daivena padyodgata-kṛṣṇa-nāmā*
*babhūva yuṣmat-karuṇādhipātram ||56||*

*Word for word:* *vedāntinām* — of the Vedantists; *maṇḍala* — of the circle; *sārvabhaumaḥ* — the emperor; *saḥ* — that; *sārvabhaumaḥ* — Sarvabhauma; *gata* — devoid; *bhakti* — of devotion; *gandhaḥ* — [even of] the scent; *daivena* — by destiny; *padya* — in a verse; *udgata* — having appeared; *kṛṣṇa* — of Krishna; *nāmā* — [with] the name; *babhūva* — became; *yuṣmat* — Your; *karuṇā* — of mercy; *adhipātram* — the supreme vessel.

**56.** That Sarvabhauma, the emperor in the circle of Vedantists, in whom there was not even the scent of devotion, has become the supreme vessel of Your mercy [merely] because by destiny the name of Krishna appeared in his verse!

*Note.* A play on words: *sārvabhauma* means "emperor, sovereign of the whole earth", and it is also the name (an honorific title) of Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya.

### Verse 57

अहो महाकारुणिकं तमेनं
को मूढधीर्नानुभजेत लोकः ।
दोषान् बहून् प्रोज्झ्य लवं गुणस्य
गृह्णाति भूयः कुरुतेऽनुकम्पाम् ॥५७॥

*aho mahākāruṇikaṁ tam enaṁ*
*ko mūḍha-dhīr nānubhajeta lokaḥ |*
*doṣān bahūn projjhya lavaṁ guṇasya*
*gṛhṇāti bhūyaḥ kurute 'nukampām ||57||*

*Word for word:* *aho* — ah; *mahā-kāruṇikam* — the supremely compassionate; *tam enam* — Him; *kaḥ* — what; *mūḍha* — foolish; *dhīḥ* — [with] a mind; *na anubhajeta* — would not serve; *lokaḥ* — person; *doṣān* — faults; *bahūn* — many; *projjhya* — disregarding; *lavam* — a particle; *guṇasya* — of virtue; *gṛhṇāti* — He accepts; *bhūyaḥ* — again and again; *kurute* — shows; *anukampām* — compassion.

**57.** Ah, what foolish person would not serve Him, the supremely compassionate? Disregarding many faults, He accepts a particle of virtue and shows compassion again and again.

### Verse 58

न कस्य वक्त्रात् खलु कृष्णनाम
बहिः प्रयात्यस्य ततः किमासीत् ।
ज्ञातं तदा सम्प्रति सार्वभौमे
करिष्यसे भूरितरानुकम्पाम् ॥५८॥

*na kasya vaktrāt khalu kṛṣṇa-nāma*
*bahiḥ prayāty asya tataḥ kim āsīt |*
*jñātaṁ tadā samprati sārvabhaume*
*kariṣyase bhūritarānukampām ||58||*

*Word for word:* *na* — not; *kasya* — from whose; *vaktrāt* — mouth; *khalu* — indeed; *kṛṣṇa* — of Krishna; *nāma* — the name; *bahiḥ* — out; *prayāti* — comes; *asya* — in him; *tataḥ* — beyond that; *kim* — what; *āsīt* — was there; *jñātam* — [it was] understood; *tadā* — then; *samprati* — now; *sārvabhaume* — to Sarvabhauma; *kariṣyase* — You will show; *bhūritara* — very great; *anukampām* — compassion.

**58.** From whose mouth does the name of Krishna not come forth? What more than that was there in him? Then I understood: now You will show very great compassion to Sarvabhauma."

### Verse 59

इत्यस्य वाचं स निशम्य नाथः
सविस्मयोत्साहरसप्रफुल्लाम् ।
जगाद मैवं वद भो महात्मन्
सेवैव तस्येह मया विधेया ॥५९॥

*ity asya vācaṁ sa niśamya nāthaḥ*
*savismayotsāha-rasa-praphullām |*
*jagāda maivaṁ vada bho mahātman*
*sevaiva tasyeha mayā vidheyā ||59||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *asya* — his; *vācam* — speech; *saḥ* — He; *niśamya* — having heard; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *sa* — with; *vismaya* — wonder; *utsāha* — [and] enthusiasm; *rasa* — with the rasa; *praphullām* — blossoming; *jagāda* — said; *mā* — do not; *evam* — so; *vada* — speak; *bhoḥ* — O; *mahātman* — great soul; *sevā* — service; *eva* — only; *tasya* — to him; *iha* — here; *mayā* — by Me; *vidheyā* — is to be rendered.

**59.** Having heard his speech, blossoming with the rasa of wonder and enthusiasm, the Lord said: "Do not speak so, O great soul! Here I must only render service to him."

### Verse 60

इत्युक्तवांस्तं दिवसं निनीय
शेषे रजन्याः प्रथमावकाशम् ।
विलोकितुं तल्पतलादुदासी-
त्ततो जनैर्नित्यकृतिं चकार ॥६०॥

*ity uktavāṁs taṁ divasaṁ ninīya*
*śeṣe rajanyāḥ prathamāvakāśam |*
*vilokituṁ talpa-talād udāsīt*
*tato janair nitya-kṛtiṁ cakāra ||60||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *uktavān* — having spoken; *tam* — that; *divasam* — day; *ninīya* — having spent; *śeṣe* — at the end; *rajanyāḥ* — of the night; *prathama* — the first; *avakāśam* — opening [of the temple]; *vilokitum* — to see; *talpa* — of the bed; *talāt* — from the surface; *udāsīt* — rose; *tataḥ* — then; *janaiḥ* — with [His] people; *nitya* — daily; *kṛtim* — observances; *cakāra* — performed.

**60.** Having spoken thus, He spent that day; at the end of the night He rose from His bed to see the first opening [of the temple], and then, together with His people, performed the daily observances.

*Note.* *Prathamāvakāśa* is the first opening of the temple at dawn (*maṅgala-ārati*).

### Verse 61

ततो बहिश्चेलकटीरसूत्रे
प्रगृह्य नामग्रहणोत्ककण्ठः ।
प्रासादमध्ये प्रविवेश नाथो
यथोदयाद्रिं शरदिन्दुरेषः ॥६१॥

*tato bahiś-cela-kaṭīra-sūtre*
*pragṛhya nāma-grahaṇotka-kaṇṭhaḥ |*
*prāsāda-madhye praviveśa nātho*
*yathodayādriṁ śarad-indur eṣaḥ ||61||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *bahiḥ* — outer; *cela* — cloth; *kaṭīra* — of the waist; *sūtre* — [and] the cord; *pragṛhya* — having put on; *nāma* — of the name; *grahaṇa* — for the repeating; *utka* — eager; *kaṇṭhaḥ* — [with] a throat; *prāsāda* — of the temple; *madhye* — into the interior; *praviveśa* — entered; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *yathā* — as; *udaya* — of rising; *adrim* — the mountain; *śarat* — autumnal; *induḥ* — moon; *eṣaḥ* — this.

**61.** Then, having put on the outer cloth and the waist-cord, His throat eager to repeat the name, the Lord entered the temple, as the autumn moon [ascends] the Mountain of Rising.

*Note.* The *bahirvāsa* (outer cloth) and the *kaṭi-sūtra* (waist-cord with loincloth) are the garb of a sannyasi.

### Verse 62

खगाधिपस्तम्भवरस्य पश्चा-
च्चामीकरस्तम्भवदास्थितोऽसौ ।
ददर्श नीलाचलमौलिरत्नं
विलोचनाम्भोभरधौतदेहः ॥६२॥

*khagādhipa-stambha-varasya paścāc*
*cāmīkara-stambhavad āsthito 'sau |*
*dadarśa nīlācala-mauli-ratnaṁ*
*vilocanāmbho-bhara-dhauta-dehaḥ ||62||*

*Word for word:* *khaga* — of birds; *adhipa* — of the king; *stambha* — the pillar; *varasya* — splendid; *paścāt* — behind; *cāmīkara* — golden; *stambhavat* — like a pillar; *āsthitaḥ* — standing; *asau* — He; *dadarśa* — beheld; *nīlācala* — of Nilachala; *mauli* — of the crown; *ratnam* — the jewel; *vilocana* — of the eyes; *ambhaḥ* — of the waters; *bhara* — by the flood; *dhauta* — washed; *dehaḥ* — [with] a body.

**62.** Standing like a golden pillar behind the splendid pillar of the King of birds, He beheld the crest-jewel of Nilachala, His body washed by a flood of tears.

*Note.* The Garuda pillar (*garuḍa-stambha*) is the pillar bearing the image of Garuda in the temple of Jagannatha. Chaitanya usually stood behind it during darshan.

### Verse 63

ततः स धूपावधि सुस्थितोऽसौ
प्रत्यूषकृत्यानि विलोक्य तस्य ।
महाप्रसादान्नमतीवरम्यं
प्रगृह्य किञ्चिद्बहिराजगाम ॥६३॥

*tataḥ sa dhūpāvadhi susthito 'sau*
*pratyūṣa-kṛtyāni vilokya tasya |*
*mahā-prasādānnam atīva-ramyaṁ*
*pragṛhya kiñcid bahir ājagāma ||63||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *saḥ asau* — He; *dhūpa* — the incense [offering]; *avadhi* — until; *susthitaḥ* — having remained; *pratyūṣa* — morning; *kṛtyāni* — rites; *vilokya* — having watched; *tasya* — His [Jagannatha's]; *mahā-prasāda* — of mahaprasada; *annam* — food; *atīva* — most; *ramyam* — delightful; *pragṛhya* — having taken; *kiñcit* — a little; *bahiḥ* — outside; *ājagāma* — came.

**63.** Then, having remained there until the incense [offering] and watched His [Jagannatha's] morning rites, He took a little most delightful mahaprasada food and came outside.

### Verse 64

तथैव देवः स तु सार्वभौमं
विलोकितुं तस्य गृहं जगाम ।
स तु प्रभाते खलु तल्पमध्या-
द्दैवेन नैवोद्गतवांस्तथासीत् ॥६४॥

*tathaiva devaḥ sa tu sārvabhaumaṁ*
*vilokituṁ tasya gṛhaṁ jagāma |*
*sa tu prabhāte khalu talpa-madhyād*
*daivena naivodgatavāṁs tathāsīt ||64||*

*Word for word:* *tathā eva* — just so; *devaḥ* — the Lord; *saḥ* — He; *tu* — then; *sārvabhaumam* — Sarvabhauma; *vilokitum* — to see; *tasya* — his; *gṛham* — to the house; *jagāma* — went; *saḥ* — he; *tu* — however; *prabhāte* — at dawn; *khalu* — indeed; *talpa* — the bed; *madhyāt* — from; *daivena* — as it happened; *na eva* — not yet; *udgatavān* — had risen; *tathā* — so; *āsīt* — remained.

**64.** Just so, the Lord went to his house to see Sarvabhauma. He, however, as it happened, had not yet risen from his bed at dawn and was still lying there.

### Verse 65

ततोऽस्य केनाप्यनुगेन नाथं
विलोक्य तं बोधयितुं जगन्ते ।
निवारयामास ततः प्रभुस्तं
तत्स्वापगेहान्तविलीन एव ॥६५॥

*tato 'sya kenāpy anugena nāthaṁ*
*vilokya taṁ bodhayituṁ jagante (?) |*
*nivārayāmāsa tataḥ prabhus taṁ*
*tat-svāpa-gehānta-vilīna eva ||65||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *asya* — his; *kena api* — by a certain; *anugena* — servant; *nātham* — the Lord; *vilokya* — having seen; *tam* — him; *bodhayitum* — to wake; *jagante* (?) — when [he] was about to [go]; *nivārayāmāsa* — stopped; *tataḥ* — then; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *tam* — him; *tat* — his; *svāpa* — sleeping; *geha* — of the room; *anta* — inside; *vilīnaḥ* — hidden; *eva* — indeed.

**65.** Then, when one of his servants, having seen the Lord, was about to [go and] wake him, the Lord stopped him and hid Himself right inside the bedroom.

*Note.* The form *jagante* is unclear (?); the sense "was about to [go and] wake him" is taken from the context.

### Verse 66

ततोऽस्य पार्श्वस्य विवृत्तिकाले
श्रीकृष्ण कृष्णेति निशम्य नाथः ।
अर्धप्रबुद्धार्धनिमग्नवाणीं
जगाम निर्व्याजमनेकसौख्यम् ॥६६॥

*tato 'sya pārśvasya vivṛtti-kāle*
*śrī-kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇeti niśamya nāthaḥ |*
*ardha-prabuddhārdha-nimagna-vāṇīṁ*
*jagāma nirvyājam aneka-saukhyam ||66||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *asya* — his; *pārśvasya* — of the side; *vivṛtti* — of turning; *kāle* — at the time; *śrī-kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa* — "Sri Krishna, Krishna"; *iti* — thus; *niśamya* — having heard; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *ardha* — half; *prabuddha* — awake; *ardha* — half; *nimagna* — submerged [in sleep]; *vāṇīm* — speech; *jagāma* — attained; *nirvyājam* — unfeigned; *aneka* — manifold; *saukhyam* — bliss.

**66.** Then, as [Sarvabhauma] turned from one side [to the other], the Lord heard "Sri Krishna, Krishna!" — words half awake, half submerged [in sleep] — and attained unfeigned, manifold bliss.

*Note.* In the edition the lines are divided wrongly (*…vāṇīṁ jagāma / nirvyājam…*); by the metre *jagāma* opens the fourth pada.

### Verse 67

ततः प्रबुद्धोऽभवदेव भूमी-
गीर्वाणसिंहः स तु सार्वभौमः ।
ददर्श चाथो यतिमण्डलीनां
चूडामणिं श्रीयुतगौरचन्द्रम् ॥६७॥

*tataḥ prabuddho 'bhavad eva bhūmī-*
*gīrvāṇa-siṁhaḥ sa tu sārvabhaumaḥ |*
*dadarśa cātho yati-maṇḍalīnāṁ*
*cūḍāmaṇiṁ śrīyuta-gauracandram ||67||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *prabuddhaḥ* — awake; *abhavat* — became; *eva* — indeed; *bhūmī* — of the earth; *gīrvāṇa* — of the gods (the brahmanas); *siṁhaḥ* — the lion; *saḥ* — that; *tu* — then; *sārvabhaumaḥ* — Sarvabhauma; *dadarśa* — saw; *ca* — and; *atho* — then; *yati* — of ascetics; *maṇḍalīnām* — of the circles; *cūḍāmaṇim* — the crest-jewel; *śrīyuta* — beautiful; *gauracandram* — Gaurachandra.

**67.** Then Sarvabhauma, the lion among the gods of the earth, awoke and saw beautiful Gaurachandra, the crest-jewel of the circles of ascetics.

### Verse 68

ततोऽतिसंभ्रान्तमतिस्त्वरावां-
स्तल्पात् समुत्थाय ननाम हृष्टः ।
ततस्तु नानाकथया स काल-
स्तयोर्महाकौतुकपूर्ण आसीत् ॥६८॥

*tato 'tisaṁbhrānta-matis tvarāvāṁs*
*talpāt samutthāya nanāma hṛṣṭaḥ |*
*tatas tu nānā-kathayā sa kālas*
*tayor mahā-kautuka-pūrṇa āsīt ||68||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *ati* — greatly; *saṁbhrānta* — flustered; *matiḥ* — [with] a mind; *tvarāvān* — hastily; *talpāt* — from the bed; *samutthāya* — springing up; *nanāma* — bowed down; *hṛṣṭaḥ* — delighted; *tataḥ tu* — and then; *nānā* — varied; *kathayā* — with conversation; *saḥ* — that; *kālaḥ* — time; *tayoḥ* — of the two; *mahā* — great; *kautuka* — of joy; *pūrṇaḥ* — full; *āsīt* — was.

**68.** Greatly flustered, he hastily sprang up from his bed and joyfully bowed down. And then, in varied conversation, that time of the two of them was full of great joy.

### Verse 69

ततः प्रभुः कारुणिकोऽनुवेलं
समस्तलोकेषु महारसाब्धिः ।
आकृष्य वासोऽञ्चलतः प्रसाद-
मन्नं स जग्राह करारविन्दे ॥६९॥

*tataḥ prabhuḥ kāruṇiko 'nuvelaṁ*
*samasta-lokeṣu mahā-rasābdhiḥ |*
*ākṛṣya vāso-'ñcalataḥ prasādam*
*annaṁ sa jagrāha karāravinde ||69||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *kāruṇikaḥ* — compassionate; *anuvelam* — at every moment; *samasta* — to all; *lokeṣu* — people; *mahā* — great; *rasa* — of rasa; *abdhiḥ* — the ocean; *ākṛṣya* — having drawn out; *vāsaḥ* — of [His] garment; *añcalataḥ* — from the end; *prasādam* — sanctified; *annam* — food; *saḥ* — He; *jagrāha* — took; *kara* — of [His] hand; *aravinde* — in the lotus.

**69.** Then the Lord, compassionate at every moment to all people, the great ocean of rasa, drew the sanctified food out from the end of His garment and took it in His lotus hand.

### Verse 70

उद्यम्य बाहुं स महाप्रसाद-
सिद्धौषधिव्यावृतकल्पवृक्षम् ।
उवाच काले कृतनित्यकृत्यो
भवानिदं भोक्ष्यत इत्यदाच्च ॥७०॥

*udyamya bāhuṁ sa mahā-prasāda-*
*siddhauṣadhi-vyāvṛta-kalpa-vṛkṣam |*
*uvāca kāle kṛta-nitya-kṛtyo*
*bhavān idaṁ bhokṣyata ity adāc ca ||70||*

*Word for word:* *udyamya* — having raised; *bāhum* — [His] arm; *saḥ* — He; *mahā-prasāda* — of mahaprasada; *siddha* — with a miraculous; *oṣadhi* — herb; *vyāvṛta* — covered; *kalpa-vṛkṣam* — a wish-fulfilling tree; *uvāca* — said; *kāle* — in due time; *kṛta* — having performed; *nitya* — daily; *kṛtyaḥ* — [with] rites; *bhavān* — you; *idam* — this; *bhokṣyate* — will partake of; *iti* — thus [saying]; *adāt* — gave; *ca* — and.

**70.** Raising His arm — a wish-fulfilling tree covered with the miraculous herb of mahaprasada — He said: "When you have performed your daily rites, you will partake of this in due time," and gave [it to him].

### Verse 71

उत्थाय सोऽतिस्पृहया त्वरावा-
नादाय पाणौ सुमहाप्रसादम् ।
प्रसादलब्धौ यदि चेद्विलम्बः
कृतं कृतं तत् खलु विज्ञताभिः ॥७१॥

*utthāya so 'tispṛhayā tvarāvān*
*ādāya pāṇau sumahā-prasādam |*
*prasāda-labdhau yadi ced vilambaḥ*
*kṛtaṁ kṛtaṁ tat khalu vijñatābhiḥ ||71||*

*Word for word:* *utthāya* — having risen; *saḥ* — he; *ati* — great; *spṛhayā* — with longing; *tvarāvān* — hastily; *ādāya* — having taken; *pāṇau* — in [his] hand; *su-mahā-prasādam* — the precious mahaprasada; *prasāda* — of prasada; *labdhau* — upon receiving; *yadi cet* — if; *vilambaḥ* — delay; *kṛtam kṛtam* — enough, enough; *tat* — then; *khalu* — indeed; *vijñatābhiḥ* — with learned niceties.

**71.** He rose and with great longing hastily took the precious mahaprasada in his hand: "If there is delay upon receiving prasada, then enough, enough indeed of learned niceties!"

*Note.* Sarvabhauma eats the prasada at once, before he has washed, breaking the rules of morning purity. Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 6.

### Verse 72

इत्येष सद्यः पुलकालियुक्तो
महाप्रसादं वदने ददौ तम् ।
प्रभुर्महामोदसुमेदुरात्मा
प्रगृह्य दोर्भ्यां तमथो ननन्द ॥७२॥

*ity eṣa sadyaḥ pulakāli-yukto*
*mahā-prasādaṁ vadane dadau tam |*
*prabhur mahāmoda-sumedurātmā*
*pragṛhya dorbhyāṁ tam atho nananda ||72||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus [resolving]; *eṣaḥ* — he; *sadyaḥ* — at once; *pulaka* — of hairs standing on end; *āli* — with waves; *yuktaḥ* — filled; *mahā-prasādam* — the mahaprasada; *vadane* — into [his] mouth; *dadau* — put; *tam* — that; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *mahā* — with great; *āmoda* — joy; *su-medura* — brimming; *ātmā* — [with] a soul; *pragṛhya* — embracing; *dorbhyām* — with [His] arms; *tam* — him; *atho* — then; *nananda* — rejoiced.

**72.** Thus [resolving], he at once, covered with waves of hairs standing on end, put that mahaprasada into his mouth. Then the Lord, His soul brimming with great joy, embraced him with both arms and rejoiced.

### Verse 73

अन्योन्यदीर्घश्वसिताक्षिणीव
रोमाञ्चघर्माम्बुविभूषिताङ्गौ ।
आनन्दसिन्धुप्लवतृप्तचित्तौ
बभूवतुस्तौ प्रभुसार्वभौमौ ॥७३॥

*anyonya-dīrgha-śvasitākṣiṇīva (?)*
*romāñca-gharmāmbu-vibhūṣitāṅgau |*
*ānanda-sindhu-plava-tṛpta-cittau*
*babhūvatus tau prabhu-sārvabhaumau ||73||*

*Word for word:* *anyonya* — at each other; *dīrgha* — with long; *śvasita* — sighs; *akṣiṇī iva* (?) — as if [with] eyes; *romāñca* — with hairs standing on end; *gharma* — of sweat; *ambu* — [and] with the water; *vibhūṣita* — adorned; *aṅgau* — [with] bodies; *ānanda* — of bliss; *sindhu* — in the ocean; *plava* — by swimming; *tṛpta* — sated; *cittau* — [with] hearts; *babhūvatuḥ* — became; *tau* — the two; *prabhu* — the Lord; *sārvabhaumau* — and Sarvabhauma.

**73.** The Lord and Sarvabhauma sighed long, gazing at each other (?); their bodies were adorned with hairs standing on end and drops of sweat, and their hearts were sated by swimming in the ocean of bliss.

*Note.* The beginning of the verse (*°śvasitākṣiṇīva*) is corrupt or obscure and is translated by the sense (?). *Akṣiṇī* may also hint at tears: "adorned with long sighs for each other, [tears of] the eyes, hairs standing on end and sweat".

### Verse 74

दृशौ गलद्वारिविलुप्ततारे
देहश्च रोमाञ्चसमूहलुप्तः ।
तयोस्तदा प्रेमनदीकृतेन
स्नानेन जाड्यं परमं बभूव ॥७४॥

*dṛśau galad-vāri-vilupta-tāre*
*dehaś ca romāñca-samūha-luptaḥ |*
*tayos tadā prema-nadī-kṛtena*
*snānena jāḍyaṁ paramaṁ babhūva ||74||*

*Word for word:* *dṛśau* — the two eyes; *galat* — by flowing; *vāri* — water; *vilupta* — hidden; *tāre* — [with] pupils; *dehaḥ* — the body; *ca* — and; *romāñca* — of hairs standing on end; *samūha* — by a mass; *luptaḥ* — hidden; *tayoḥ* — of both; *tadā* — then; *prema* — of love; *nadī* — in the river; *kṛtena* — taken; *snānena* — by the bath; *jāḍyam* — numbness; *paramam* — utmost; *babhūva* — came about.

**74.** The pupils of their eyes were hidden by flowing water, and their bodies by masses of hairs standing on end. Then, from the bath they had taken in the river of love, utmost numbness came over them both.

*Note.* A play of images: after bathing in a cold river the body grows numb (*jāḍya*). Stupor (*stambha*) is one of the *sāttvika* symptoms of ecstasy.

### Verse 75

इत्थं प्रभुर्विप्रघटाग्रगण्यं

चित्तं ततस्तत् करुणारसेन
संक्रान्ततां निर्भरमाजगाम ॥७५॥

*itthaṁ prabhur vipra-ghaṭāgra-gaṇyaṁ*

*cittaṁ tatas tat karuṇā-rasena*
*saṁkrāntatāṁ nirbharam ājagāma ||75||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *vipra* — of brahmanas; *ghaṭā* — of the assembly; *agra-gaṇyam* — the foremost; *vaśe cakāra* — brought under His sway; *ati* — of great; *kṛpā* — mercy; *rasena* — by the rasa; *cittam* — the heart; *tataḥ* — then; *tat* — that; *karuṇā* — of compassion; *rasena* — with the rasa; *saṁkrāntatām* — permeation; *nirbharam* — fully; *ājagāma* — attained.

**75.** Thus by the rasa of great mercy the Lord brought under His sway the foremost of the assembly of brahmanas. And then that heart [of his] became fully permeated with the rasa of compassion.

### Verse 76

ततः प्रभृत्येष महाकृपालो-

कायेन वाचा मनसानुरक्तो
भवन्निरस्ताखिलगर्वभारः ॥७६॥

*tataḥ prabhṛty eṣa mahā-kṛpālor*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ prabhṛti* — from then on; *eṣaḥ* — he; *mahā-kṛpāloḥ* — of the supremely merciful; *gaurāṅga-candrasya* — of Gaurangachandra; *pada* — of the feet; *aravinde* — to the lotuses; *kāyena* — with body; *vācā* — speech; *manasā* — [and] mind; *anuraktaḥ* — attached; *bhavan* — becoming; *nirasta* — cast off; *akhila* — the whole; *garva* — of pride; *bhāraḥ* — [with] the burden.

**76.** From then on, having become attached with body, speech and mind to the lotus feet of supremely merciful Gaurangachandra, he cast off the whole burden of pride.

### Verse 77

इत्थं स चान्येद्युरसौ द्विजाग्र्यो
धूपावसाने प्रभुगौरचन्द्रम् ।
द्रष्टुं जगामाथ महाकृपालुं
विमुक्तविद्यामदभावशान्तः ॥७७॥

*itthaṁ sa cānyedyur asau dvijāgryo*
*dhūpāvasāne prabhu-gauracandram |*
*draṣṭuṁ jagāmātha mahā-kṛpāluṁ*
*vimukta-vidyā-mada-bhāva-śāntaḥ ||77||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *saḥ* — he; *ca* — and; *anyedyuḥ* — on the next day; *asau* — this; *dvija-agryaḥ* — foremost of the twice-born; *dhūpa* — of the incense [offering]; *avasāne* — at the end; *prabhu-gauracandram* — Lord Gaurachandra; *draṣṭum* — to see; *jagāma* — went; *atha* — then; *mahā-kṛpālum* — the supremely merciful; *vimukta* — freed; *vidyā* — of learning; *mada* — from the intoxication; *bhāva* — in disposition; *śāntaḥ* — humble.

**77.** And so, on the next day, at the end of the incense [offering], this foremost of the twice-born, freed from the intoxication of learning and humble in disposition, went to see the supremely merciful Lord Gaurachandra.

### Verse 78

दृष्ट्वा ननामावनिमूलराज-
न्मौलिर्महात्मा स्तवमप्यकार्षीत् ।
अथो जगादाशु च भीतभीतो
बद्धाञ्जलिः पाणिपुटेन विप्रः ॥७८॥

*dṛṣṭvā nanāmāvani-mūla-rājan-*
*maulir mahātmā stavam apy akārṣīt |*
*atho jagādāśu ca bhīta-bhīto*
*baddhāñjaliḥ pāṇi-puṭena vipraḥ ||78||*

*Word for word:* *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen [Him]; *nanāma* — bowed down; *avani* — of the earth; *mūla* — at the base; *rājat* — shining; *mauliḥ* — [with] a head; *mahātmā* — the great soul; *stavam* — a hymn of praise; *api* — also; *akārṣīt* — offered; *atho* — then; *jagāda* — said; *āśu* — at once; *ca* — and; *bhīta-bhītaḥ* — very timid; *baddha* — joined; *añjaliḥ* — [with] palms; *pāṇi* — of the hands; *puṭena* — in a cup; *vipraḥ* — the brahmana.

**78.** Seeing Him, the great soul bowed down, his head shining at the very ground, and also offered a hymn of praise. Then the brahmana, very timidly, his palms joined in the form of a cup, at once said:

### Verse 79

व्याख्याहि भो मय्यनुकम्पयेश
पद्यैकमेतद्गदितुं बिभेमि ।
व्याख्यायतेऽस्माभिरिदं न चात्र
हृत्प्रत्ययः कोऽपि च संप्रति स्यात् ॥७९॥

*vyākhyāhi bho mayy anukampayeśa*
*padyaikam etad gaditum bibhemi |*
*vyākhyāyate 'smābhir idaṁ na cātra*
*hṛt-pratyayaḥ ko 'pi ca samprati syāt ||79||*

*Word for word:* *vyākhyāhi* — explain; *bhoḥ* — O; *mayi* — to me; *anukampayā* — out of compassion; *īśa* — O Lord; *padya* — verse; *ekam* — one; *etat* — this; *gaditum* — to expound; *bibhemi* — I fear; *vyākhyāyate* — is explained; *asmābhiḥ* — by us; *idam* — this; *na* — not; *ca* — but; *atra* — in it; *hṛt* — of the heart; *pratyayaḥ* — conviction; *kaḥ api* — any; *ca* — and; *samprati* — now; *syāt* — there is.

**79.** "O Lord, out of compassion for me, explain this one verse: I am afraid to expound it. We do explain it, but now there is no conviction at all in [my] heart about it."

### Verse 80
