व्याख्यां चकारातिसुदुर्गमार्थाम् ॥८०॥

*ity ūcivān padya-yugaṁ pramodād*
*ekādaśa-skandha-bhavaṁ papāṭha |*
*niśamya tat kāruṇikāgra-gaṇyo*
*vyākhyāṁ cakārātisudurgamārthām ||80||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *ūcivān* — having spoken; *padya* — of verses; *yugam* — a pair; *pramodāt* — joyfully; *ekādaśa* — eleventh; *skandha* — canto; *bhavam* — from; *papāṭha* — recited; *niśamya* — having heard; *tat* — that; *kāruṇika* — of the compassionate; *agra-gaṇyaḥ* — the foremost; *vyākhyām* — an explanation; *cakāra* — gave; *ati-su-durgama* — most profound; *arthām* — [of] meaning.

**80.** Having spoken thus, he joyfully recited a pair of verses from the Eleventh Canto. Having heard it, the foremost of the compassionate gave an explanation of most profound meaning.

*Note.* In Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 6.186–193) the Lord explains the *ātmārāma* verse (Srimad-Bhagavatam 1.7.10); in Karnapura it is a pair of verses from the Eleventh Canto, and which ones is said neither here, nor by Murari, nor in the *Chaitanya-chandrodaya* (Act 6).

*Word for word:* *pṛthak pṛthaktvāt* — each separately; *navadhā* — in nine ways; *cakāra* — gave; *vyākhyām* — an explanation; *saḥ* — He; *padya* — of verses; *dvitayasya* — of the pair; *śaśvat* — in succession; *aṣṭādaśa* — eighteen; *arthān* — meanings; *ubhayoḥ* — of both; *niśamya* — having heard; *mahā* — utterly; *vimugdhaḥ* — amazed; *abhavat* — became; *eṣaḥ* — this; *vipraḥ* — brahmana.

**81.** He explained each of the two verses separately, one after the other, in nine ways. Hearing the eighteen meanings of both, the brahmana was utterly amazed.

**82.** Exceedingly amazed, the great soul praised [Him], censuring himself all the more: "Ah, O Lord, a fool like me — a beast in human form — did not understand Your greatness!"

दन्यच्च जन्मान्यदिवाप्यदृष्टम् ॥८९॥

*śrī-gauracandrasya kṛpā tu saiṣā*

*anyac ca janmānyad ivāpy adṛṣṭam ||89||*

*Word for word:* *śrī-gauracandrasya* — of Sri Gaurachandra; *kṛpā* — the mercy; *tu* — indeed; *sā eṣā* — such [is]; *vācā* — in words; *katham* — how [to describe it]; *tat* — with Him; *pratisaṅga* — of contact; *leśāt* — from a trace; *anyā eva* — quite different; *rītiḥ* — the cast; *khalu* — truly; *cetasaḥ* — of the mind; *syāt* — becomes; *anyat* — another; *ca* — and; *janma* — birth; *anyat* — another; *iva* — as if; *api* — also; *adṛṣṭam* — unseen destiny.

### Verse 91

कदाचिदेष प्रभुपूर्वतस्तु

*ity atra bhaktīti paṭhan nananda ||91||*

*Word for word:* *kadācit* — once; *eṣaḥ* — he; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *pūrvataḥ* — in the presence; *tu* — indeed; *prastāvataḥ* — as the occasion arose; *bhāgavatīya* — from the Bhagavata; *padyam* — a verse; *nipaṭhya* — having recited; *tat* — that; *mukti-pade sa dāya-bhāk* — "he is an heir in the abode of liberation"; *iti* — thus; *atra* — here; *bhakti* — "bhakti"; *iti* — thus; *paṭhan* — reading; *nananda* — rejoiced.

**91.** Once, as the occasion arose, he recited in the Lord's presence a verse from the Bhagavata, and in the words *mukti-pade sa dāya-bhāk* ("he is an heir in the abode of liberation") he read "bhakti" [in place of "mukti"] — and rejoiced.

*Note.* Srimad-Bhagavatam 10.14.8: "…one who lives thus is an heir in the abode of liberation (*mukti-pade*)." Sarvabhauma replaced *mukti* with *bhakti*. The episode is also found in the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 6.260–266).

**92.** Hearing this, the Lord — God Himself — at once put another meaning into the word "mukti" and upheld [the original reading]. Even so, he, anointed with His lordship, said:

### Verse 93

तथाप्यसभ्यस्मृतिहेतुकत्वा-
दश्लीलदोषोऽयमिति ब्रवीमि ।
इत्यादि यस्योक्तिर्मधु प्रसिद्धं
स सार्वभौमः कथया न कथ्यः ॥९३॥

*tathāpy asabhya-smṛti-hetukatvād*
*aślīla-doṣo 'yam iti bravīmi |*
*ity ādi yasyoktir madhu prasiddhaṁ*
*sa sārvabhaumaḥ kathayā na kathyaḥ ||93||*

*Word for word:* *tathā api* — even so; *asabhya* — of something indecent; *smṛti* — the recollection; *hetukatvāt* — because of causing; *aślīla* — of indecorum; *doṣaḥ* — the fault; *ayam* — this [is]; *iti* — thus; *bravīmi* — I say; *iti ādi* — such and the like; *yasya* — whose; *uktiḥ* — sayings; *madhu* — sweet; *prasiddham* — [are] well known; *saḥ* — that; *sārvabhaumaḥ* — Sarvabhauma; *kathayā* — by an account; *na* — not; *kathyaḥ* — describable.

**93.** "Even so, because it calls something indecent to mind, I say: this [word has] the fault of indecorum." That Sarvabhauma, whose sweet sayings such as this are well known, cannot be described by any account.

*Note.* *Aślīla-doṣa* is, in poetics, the fault of a word that evokes shameful, repulsive or inauspicious associations. For a devotee "mukti" (merging into Brahman) is such a word. Cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 6.266–268.

महाप्रभुर्गौरसुधामयूखः ।
आदाय तस्यैव निदेशमादौ
ययौ प्रमोदाद्दिशि दक्षिणस्याम् ॥९५॥

*dṛṣṭvā jagannātha-mahāprabhuṁ taṁ*
*mahāprabhur gaura-sudhā-mayūkhaḥ |*
*ādāya tasyaiva nideśam ādau*
*yayau pramodād diśi dakṣiṇasyām ||95||*

*Word for word:* *dṛṣṭvā* — having beheld; *jagannātha* — Jagannatha; *mahā-prabhum* — Mahaprabhu; *tam* — that; *mahā-prabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *gaura* — the fair; *sudhā* — of nectar; *mayūkhaḥ* — [whose] rays [are] (the moon); *ādāya* — having received; *tasya* — His; *eva* — indeed; *nideśam* — permission; *ādau* — first; *yayau* — went; *pramodāt* — joyfully; *diśi* — in the direction; *dakṣiṇasyām* — southern.

**95.** Having beheld that Mahaprabhu Jagannatha and having first received His permission, Mahaprabhu — the fair moon whose rays are nectar — joyfully set off to the south.

*Note.* The title *Mahāprabhu* ("the Great Lord") is applied here both to Jagannatha and to Chaitanya.

### Verse 96

गच्छन्तमित्थं स तु सार्वभौमः
शोकाकुलात्मा करुणं बभाषे ।
कथं प्रभो मां बहुदुःखदग्धं
कृत्वा कुतो वा प्रसभं प्रयासि ॥९६॥

*gacchantam itthaṁ sa tu sārvabhaumaḥ*
*śokākulātmā karuṇaṁ babhāṣe |*
*kathaṁ prabho māṁ bahu-duḥkha-dagdhaṁ*
*kṛtvā kuto vā prasabhaṁ prayāsi ||96||*

*Word for word:* *gacchantam* — to [Him who was] leaving; *ittham* — thus; *saḥ* — that; *tu* — but; *sārvabhaumaḥ* — Sarvabhauma; *śoka* — by grief; *ākula* — distraught; *ātmā* — [whose] heart [was]; *karuṇam* — piteously; *babhāṣe* — said; *katham* — how; *prabho* — O Lord; *mām* — me; *bahu* — by great; *duḥkha* — sorrow; *dagdham* — scorched; *kṛtvā* — having made; *kutaḥ vā* — where then; *prasabham* — so resolutely; *prayāsi* — are You going.

**96.** But Sarvabhauma, his heart distraught with grief, piteously said to Him as He was thus leaving: "How [can this be], O Lord? Having scorched me with great sorrow, where are You going so resolutely?

### Verse 97

कथं ममाभून्नहि पुत्रशोकः
कथं ममाभून्नहि देहपातः ।
विलोक्य युष्मत्पदपद्मयुग्मं
सोढुं न शक्तोऽस्मि भवद्वियोगम् ॥९७॥

*kathaṁ mamābhūn nahi putra-śokaḥ*
*kathaṁ mamābhūn nahi deha-pātaḥ |*
*vilokya yuṣmat-pada-padma-yugmaṁ*
*soḍhuṁ na śakto 'smi bhavad-viyogam ||97||*

*Word for word:* *katham* — why; *mama* — to me; *abhūt* — came; *na hi* — not; *putra* — for a son; *śokaḥ* — grief; *katham* — why; *mama* — to me; *abhūt* — came; *na hi* — not; *deha* — of the body; *pātaḥ* — the fall; *vilokya* — having seen; *yuṣmat* — Your; *pada* — of the feet; *padma* — of the lotuses; *yugmam* — the pair; *soḍhum* — to bear; *na* — not; *śaktaḥ asmi* — I am able; *bhavat* — from You; *viyogam* — separation.

**97.** Better that I had suffered grief for a son, better that my body had fallen! Having seen the pair of Your lotus feet, I am unable to bear separation from You.

*Note.* Literally, "Why did grief for a son not come to me? Why did the fall of my body not come to me?" — that is, any other sorrow would have been easier.

### Verse 98

बत क्व गन्तासि पथा नु केन
कथं पथः क्लेशसहोऽथ भावी ।
यद्येव गन्तासि तदा कृपालो
गोदावरीतीरभुवं समीयाः ॥९८॥

*bata kva gantāsi pathā nu kena*
*kathaṁ pathaḥ kleśa-saho 'tha bhāvī |*
*yady eva gantāsi tadā kṛpālo*
*godāvarī-tīra-bhuvaṁ samīyāḥ ||98||*

*Word for word:* *bata* — alas; *kva* — where; *gantā asi* — will You go; *pathā* — by road; *nu* — then; *kena* — by what; *katham* — how; *pathaḥ* — of the road; *kleśa* — the hardships; *sahaḥ* — bearing; *atha* — then; *bhāvī* — will You be; *yadi eva* — if indeed; *gantā asi* — You will go; *tadā* — then; *kṛpālo* — O Merciful One; *godāvarī* — of the Godavari; *tīra* — of the banks; *bhuvam* — to the land; *samīyāḥ* — please come.

**98.** Alas, where will You go, and by what road? How then will You bear the hardships of the way? If You must go, then, O Merciful One, come to the land on the banks of the Godavari.

### Verse 99

तत्रास्ति कश्चित् परमो महात्मा
श्रीकृष्णपादाम्बुजमत्तभृङ्गः ।
नोपाजिहीथा विषयीति रामा-
नन्दं भवानन्दतनूजरत्नम् ॥९९॥

*tatrāsti kaścit paramo mahātmā*
*śrī-kṛṣṇa-pādāmbuja-matta-bhṛṅgaḥ |*
*nopājihīthā viṣayīti rāmā-*
*nandaṁ bhavānanda-tanūja-ratnam ||99||*

*Word for word:* *tatra* — there; *asti* — is; *kaścit* — a certain; *paramaḥ* — supreme; *mahātmā* — great soul; *śrī-kṛṣṇa* — of Sri Krishna; *pāda* — of the feet; *ambuja* — at the lotus; *matta* — intoxicated; *bhṛṅgaḥ* — a bee; *na upājihīthāḥ* — do not disregard; *viṣayī* — a worldly man; *iti* — thus [thinking]; *rāmānandam* — Ramananda; *bhavānanda* — of Bhavananda; *tanūja* — of the sons; *ratnam* — the jewel.

**99.** There lives a certain supreme great soul, a bee intoxicated at the lotus feet of Sri Krishna. Do not disregard him, thinking him a worldly man — Ramananda, the jewel among the sons of Bhavananda."

*Note.* Ramananda Raya was the governor on the Godavari (the viceroy of King Prataparudra), later one of Chaitanya's closest associates. Hence the warning: "do not take him for a worldly man".

### Verse 100

तथेतिकृत्वा भगवान् कृपालुः

प्रकाशयंस्तत् करुणैव सैषा ॥१००॥

*namaś cakārātha nijāṁ sa bhaktiṁ*

*Word for word:* *tathā* — so be it; *itikṛtvā* — having said; *bhagavān* — Bhagavan; *kṛpāluḥ* — merciful; *kaurmam* — to Kaurma; *jagāma* — went; *prathamam* — first; *pramodāt* — joyfully; *namaḥ cakāra* — bowed down; *atha* — then; *nijām* — His own; *saḥ* — He; *bhaktim* — devotion; *prakāśayan* — revealing; *tat* — that; *karuṇā* — mercy; *eva* — indeed; *sā eṣā* — this [was].

**100.** Saying "So be it", the merciful Bhagavan joyfully went first to Kaurma, and there He bowed down [to Kurma], revealing His own devotion — and that indeed was His mercy.

*Note.* Kaurma is Kurma-kshetra (Shrikurmam, Andhra Pradesh), the temple of Vishnu in the form of the Tortoise.

### Verse 101

दृष्ट्वा चिरं तं स निजावतारं

चकार शिक्षागुरुतामुपेतः ॥१०१॥

*dṛṣṭvā ciraṁ taṁ sa nijāvatāraṁ*

*tat karma mādhyandinam asya mānaṁ*

**101.** Having long beheld that avatara of His own and bowed down again, the skilful and grateful [Lord], assuming the role of a teacher who instructs [by example], performed the midday rite of honouring Him [Kurma].

क्षेत्रे च तत्रातिसुधीर्महात्मा

**102.** In that holy place there was a very wise great soul named Kurma, born in a brahmana family. Seeing Him and bowing down again and again, he said sweetly and very timidly:

**108.** Having arrived, the steadfast [Vasudeva] approached the one named Kurma and asked about that Mahaprabhu; and he told that magnanimous man all this about the Abode of mercy:

### Verse 110

### Verse 111

*sacetanāṁ cārutarāṁ tanuṁ ca*
*prāpyānamat taṁ dhṛta-harṣa-śokaḥ ||111||*

*Word for word:* *āgatya* — having come; *dorbhyām* — with both arms; *parirabhya* — having embraced; *vipram* — the brahmana; *kuṣṭhaiḥ* — the leprosy; *samam* — together with; *moham* — the swoon; *apācakāra* — dispelled; *sa-cetanām* — conscious; *cārutarām* — far more beautiful; *tanum* — a body; *ca* — and; *prāpya* — having obtained; *anamat* — bowed down; *tam* — to Him; *dhṛta* — filled with; *harṣa* — joy; *śokaḥ* — [and] sorrow.

**111.** Coming [back], He embraced the brahmana with both arms and dispelled his swoon together with the leprosy. Having obtained a body restored to consciousness and far more beautiful, he, filled with joy and sorrow, bowed down to Him.

### Verse 112

क्वाहं दरिद्रः पापीयान्
क्व कृष्णः श्रीनिकेतनः ।
इत्यादि पद्यं परिपठ्य चोचे
नानुग्रहोऽयं बत निग्रहो मे ।
दैन्यं कृथा मा निरहङ्कृतः स-
न्मामेष्यतीत्यन्तरधाच्च देवः ॥११२॥

*kvāhaṁ daridraḥ pāpīyān*
*kva kṛṣṇaḥ śrī-niketanaḥ |*
*ity ādi padyaṁ paripaṭhya cocye [cūce]*
*nānugraho 'yaṁ bata nigraho me |*
*dainyaṁ kṛthā mā nirahaṅkṛtaḥ san*
*mām eṣyatīty antaradhāc ca devaḥ ||112||*

*Word for word:* *kva* — where [am]; *aham* — I; *daridraḥ* — poor; *pāpīyān* — most sinful; *kva* — and where [is]; *kṛṣṇaḥ* — Krishna; *śrī* — of Sri; *niketanaḥ* — the abode; *iti ādi* — beginning thus; *padyam* — the verse; *paripaṭhya* — having recited; *ca* — and; *ūce* — said; *na* — not; *anugrahaḥ* — mercy; *ayam* — this [is]; *bata* — alas; *nigrahaḥ* — punishment; *me* — for me; *dainyam* — to dejection; *kṛthāḥ mā* — do not give way; *nirahaṅkṛtaḥ* — free from egoism; *san* — being; *mām* — to Me; *eṣyati* — will come; *iti* — thus [saying]; *antaradhāt* — vanished; *ca* — and; *devaḥ* — the Lord.

**112.** He recited the verse beginning "Where am I, a poor sinner, and where is Krishna, the abode of Sri?" and said: "Alas, this is not mercy — this is punishment for me!" "Do not give way to dejection: free from egoism, [you] will come to Me," said the Lord, and vanished.

*Note.* The verse has six padas: the first two are the opening of Srimad-Bhagavatam 10.81.16 (the words of Sudama, in the *anuṣṭubh* metre), the rest are *upajāti*. The same quotation appears in Sarga Seven. Vasudeva fears that his new beauty will breed pride in him. *Eṣyati* ("will come", third person) may be taken with an implied respectful "you" (*bhavān*) or generically: "one who is free from egoism will come to Me". Cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 7.143–146. The edition has *चोचे*; the sense requires *cūce* (*ca ūce*).

### Verse 113

विलोक्य सोऽप्यत्र तथाविधं तं
मुमोह कूर्मः स्थितमर्मदुःखः ।
उत्थाय भूयः करुणं चकार
विलापमालामपि वैष्णवाग्र्यः ॥११३॥

*vilokya so 'py atra tathāvidhaṁ taṁ*
*mumoha kūrmaḥ sthita-marma-duḥkhaḥ |*
*utthāya bhūyaḥ karuṇaṁ cakāra*
*vilāpa-mālām api vaiṣṇavāgryaḥ ||113||*

*Word for word:* *vilokya* — having seen; *saḥ api* — he too; *atra* — here; *tathā-vidham* — in such a state; *tam* — him; *mumoha* — fainted; *kūrmaḥ* — Kurma; *sthita* — lodged; *marma* — in the heart; *duḥkhaḥ* — [whose] pain [was]; *utthāya* — having risen; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *karuṇam* — piteous; *cakāra* — made; *vilāpa* — of laments; *mālām* — a garland; *api* — and; *vaiṣṇava* — of Vaishnavas; *agryaḥ* — the foremost.

**113.** Seeing him in such a state, Kurma too fainted, pain lodged in his heart. Rising again, that foremost of Vaishnavas wove a piteous garland of laments:

### Verse 114

अत्रैव भाग्योदय ईदृशोऽभू-
न्महाप्रभुः सर्वजगत्प्रभुः सः ।
स्थितः समागत्य तथेशबुद्ध्या
न ज्ञात एष क्षणमात्रमेव ॥११४॥

*atraiva bhāgyodaya īdṛśo 'bhūn*
*mahāprabhuḥ sarva-jagat-prabhuḥ saḥ |*
*sthitaḥ samāgatya tatheśa-buddhyā*
*na jñāta eṣa kṣaṇa-mātram eva ||114||*

*Word for word:* *atra eva* — right here; *bhāgya* — of fortune; *udayaḥ* — a dawning; *īdṛśaḥ* — such; *abhūt* — there was; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *sarva* — of the whole; *jagat* — world; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *saḥ* — He; *sthitaḥ* — stayed; *samāgatya* — having come; *tathā* — and yet; *īśa* — as God; *buddhyā* — with the understanding; *na* — not; *jñātaḥ* — known; *eṣaḥ* — He; *kṣaṇa-mātram* — for a single moment; *eva* — even.

**114.** "Right here such a dawning of fortune took place: that Mahaprabhu, the Lord of the whole world, came and stayed — and yet not even for a single moment was He known [by me] as God!

### Verse 115

अहो महामूढमतिर्मनुष्यः
क्षुद्रो नृशंसः परमाघकारी ।
अमूल्यरत्ने स्वकरोपलब्धे
न रक्षितं तद्बत हेलयैव ॥११५॥

*aho mahā-mūḍha-matir manuṣyaḥ*
*kṣudro nṛśaṁsaḥ paramāgha-kārī |*
*amūlya-ratne sva-karopalabdhe*
*na rakṣitaṁ tad bata helayaiva ||115||*

*Word for word:* *aho* — ah; *mahā* — utterly; *mūḍha* — foolish; *matiḥ* — [whose] mind [is]; *manuṣyaḥ* — man; *kṣudraḥ* — petty; *nṛśaṁsaḥ* — cruel; *parama* — great; *agha* — sin; *kārī* — doing; *amūlya* — priceless; *ratne* — when a gem; *sva* — into his own; *kara* — hand; *upalabdhe* — had come; *na* — not; *rakṣitam* — kept; *tat* — it; *bata* — alas; *helayā* — through carelessness; *eva* — mere.

**115.** Ah, man is utterly foolish-minded, petty, cruel, a doer of great sin! When a priceless gem had come into his very hand, he did not keep it, alas, through mere carelessness.

### Verse 116

स्वभावमूढस्तृणमात्रभोक्ता
पशुः सुधास्वादरसं न वेत्ति ।
स्पृष्टेऽपि च स्पर्शमणौ न वेत्ति
मणिर्महानित्यसकृद्विमुग्धः ॥११६॥

*svabhāva-mūḍhas tṛṇa-mātra-bhoktā*
*paśuḥ sudhāsvāda-rasaṁ na vetti |*
*spṛṣṭe 'pi ca sparśa-maṇau na vetti*
*maṇir mahān ity asakṛd vimugdhaḥ ||116||*

*Word for word:* *svabhāva* — by nature; *mūḍhaḥ* — dull; *tṛṇa* — grass; *mātra* — only; *bhoktā* — eating; *paśuḥ* — a beast; *sudhā* — of nectar; *āsvāda* — of the tasting; *rasam* — the relish; *na* — not; *vetti* — knows; *spṛṣṭe* — when [it] has been touched; *api ca* — and even; *sparśa-maṇau* — the touchstone; *na* — not; *vetti* — knows; *maṇiḥ* — a gem; *mahān* — great; *iti* — that [it is]; *asakṛt* — many times; *vimugdhaḥ* — bewildered.

**116.** A beast, dull by nature and eating nothing but grass, does not know the relish of tasting nectar; and the bewildered one, even when he has touched the touchstone many times, does not know that it is a great gem."

*Note.* *Sparśa-maṇi*, "the touchstone", is the stone that turns iron into gold.

### Verse 117

अहो महाकारुणिकस्य तस्य
जगत्पतेरेष वियोगदुःखम् ।
असह्यमेतन्न शशाक सोढु-
मतिप्रमुग्धो बहुधा मुमोह ॥११७॥

*aho mahā-kāruṇikasya tasya*
*jagat-pater eṣa viyoga-duḥkham |*
*asahyam etan na śaśāka soḍhum*
*ati-pramugdho bahudhā mumoha ||117||*

*Word for word:* *aho* — alas; *mahā* — greatly; *kāruṇikasya* — compassionate; *tasya* — from that; *jagat* — of the world; *pateḥ* — from the Lord; *eṣaḥ* — he (Kurma); *viyoga* — of separation; *duḥkham* — the grief; *asahyam* — unbearable; *etat* — this; *na* — not; *śaśāka* — was able; *soḍhum* — to bear; *ati* — utterly; *pramugdhaḥ* — bewildered; *bahudhā* — many times; *mumoha* — fainted.

**117.** Alas! He could not bear this unbearable grief of separation from that greatly compassionate Lord of the world; utterly bewildered, he fainted again and again.

### Verse 118

अथैष तस्मात् परमः कृपालु-
र्व्रजन्नृसिंहः स तु नारसिंहे ।
क्षेत्रे समागत्य नृसिंहदेवं
नमश्चकार स्तवमप्यकार्षीत् ॥११८॥

*athaiṣa tasmāt paramaḥ kṛpālur*
*vrajan nṛsiṁhaḥ sa tu nārasiṁhe |*
*kṣetre samāgatya nṛsiṁha-devaṁ*
*namaś cakāra stavam apy akārṣīt ||118||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *eṣaḥ* — He; *tasmāt* — from there; *paramaḥ* — supremely; *kṛpāluḥ* — merciful; *vrajan* — going on; *nṛ-siṁhaḥ* — a lion among men; *saḥ tu* — He; *nārasiṁhe* — of Nrisimha; *kṣetre* — at the holy place; *samāgatya* — having arrived; *nṛsiṁha-devam* — to Lord Nrisimha; *namaḥ cakāra* — bowed down; *stavam* — a hymn of praise; *api* — also; *akārṣīt* — offered.

**118.** Then He, the supremely merciful, a lion among men, went on from there; arriving at the holy place of Nrisimha, He bowed down to Lord Nrisimha and also offered Him a hymn of praise.

*Note.* A play on words: *nṛsiṁhaḥ*, "a lion among men" (that is, Chaitanya), comes to *Nṛsiṁha-deva*. Evidently Jiyada-Nrisimha (Simhachalam) is meant; cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 8.3–5 (the Lord comes to Jiyada-Nrisimha and glorifies Nrisimha).

### Verse 119

सदा मदोन्मादकरीन्द्रगामी
महाविलासी वरपीनबाहुः ।
नखेन्दुपीयूषनदीप्रवाह-
धाराभिराप्लाव्य रसां जगाम ॥११९॥

*sadā madonmāda-karīndra-gāmī*
*mahā-vilāsī vara-pīna-bāhuḥ |*
*nakhendu-pīyūṣa-nadī-pravāha-*
*dhārābhir āplāvya rasāṁ jagāma ||119||*

*Word for word:* *sadā* — always; *mada* — by musth; *unmāda* — maddened; *kari-indra* — [like] a lordly elephant; *gāmī* — moving; *mahā* — the great; *vilāsī* — Sportive One; *vara* — beautiful; *pīna* — mighty; *bāhuḥ* — [whose] arms [are]; *nakha* — of the nails; *indu* — of the moons; *pīyūṣa* — of nectar; *nadī* — of the river; *pravāha* — of the current; *dhārābhiḥ* — with the streams; *āplāvya* — flooding; *rasām* — the earth; *jagāma* — went.

**119.** Always moving like a lordly elephant maddened by musth, the great Sportive One with beautiful, mighty arms went on, flooding the earth with the streams of a river of nectar flowing from the moons of His toenails.

*Note.* In the edition the lines are divided wrongly: *नखेन्दुपीयूषनदीप्रवाहधारा- / भिराप्लाव्य रसां जगाम*. By the metre, the pada boundary falls after *pravāha-*. *Rasā* — "the earth".

### Verse 120

राम राघव राम राघव
राम राघव पाहि माम् ।
कृष्ण केशव कृष्ण केशव
कृष्ण केशव रक्ष माम् ॥१२०॥

*rāma rāghava rāma rāghava*
*rāma rāghava pāhi mām |*
*kṛṣṇa keśava kṛṣṇa keśava*
*kṛṣṇa keśava rakṣa mām ||120||*

*Word for word:* *rāma* — O Rama; *rāghava* — O descendant of Raghu; *pāhi* — protect; *mām* — me; *kṛṣṇa* — O Krishna; *keśava* — O Keshava; *rakṣa* — save; *mām* — me.

**120.** "O Rama, O Raghava, O Rama, O Raghava, O Rama, O Raghava, protect me! O Krishna, O Keshava, O Krishna, O Keshava, O Krishna, O Keshava, save me!"

*Note.* This is a chant, not an *upajāti* stanza: its padas have 10 and 8 syllables. It is close to the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 7.96 (where *rakṣa* and *pāhi* stand in the reverse order); according to the Chaitanya-charitamrita, the Lord sings this chant on His way from Kurma-kshetra to the south.

### Verse 121

संकीर्तयन्नित्थममन्दमुच्चैः
पथि प्रकामं पुलकाचिताङ्गः ।
आर्तस्वरं कुत्र च वीक्ष्य भीमं
वनं परेशः परिरोदिति स्म ॥१२१॥

*saṅkīrtayann ittham amandam uccaiḥ*
*pathi prakāmaṁ pulakācitāṅgaḥ |*
*ārta-svaraṁ kutra ca vīkṣya bhīmaṁ*
*vanaṁ pareśaḥ parirodati sma ||121||*

*Word for word:* *saṅkīrtayan* — chanting; *ittham* — thus; *amandam* — unceasingly; *uccaiḥ* — loudly; *pathi* — on the way; *prakāmam* — to His heart's content; *pulaka* — with hairs standing on end; *ācita* — covered; *aṅgaḥ* — [whose] body [was]; *ārta* — plaintive; *svaram* — in a voice; *kutra ca* — and somewhere; *vīkṣya* — having seen; *bhīmam* — a fearsome; *vanam* — forest; *para-īśaḥ* — the Supreme Lord; *parirodati sma* — wept bitterly.

**121.** Thus He chanted on the way, loudly, unceasingly and to His heart's content, His body covered with hairs standing on end; and somewhere, seeing a fearsome forest, the Supreme Lord wept bitterly in a plaintive voice.

*Note.* The correct form is *pariroditi* (root *rud*, second class; cf. *roditi* in v. 132), as in the Devanagari; the IAST line has *parirodati*. The metre is the same either way.

### Verse 122

गोदावरीतुङ्गतरङ्गशीतै-
र्मरुद्भिराश्लिष्टलतासमूहैः ।
इतस्ततो भूरि समेतमन्त-
र्वनं विलोक्यैष ननन्द नाथः ॥१२२॥

*godāvarī-tuṅga-taraṅga-śītair*
*marudbhir āśliṣṭa-latā-samūhaiḥ |*
*itas tato bhūri sametam antar-*
*vanaṁ vilokyaiṣa nananda nāthaḥ ||122||*

*Word for word:* *godāvarī* — of the Godavari; *tuṅga* — by the high; *taraṅga* — waves; *śītaiḥ* — cooled; *marudbhiḥ* — with breezes; *āśliṣṭa* — embraced; *latā* — of creepers; *samūhaiḥ* — [by which] the clusters [were]; *itas tataḥ* — here and there; *bhūri* — abundantly; *sametam* — filled; *antar-vanam* — the depths of the forest; *vilokya* — having seen; *eṣaḥ* — He; *nananda* — rejoiced; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord.

**122.** Seeing the depths of the forest, filled here and there in abundance with breezes that were cooled by the high waves of the Godavari and embraced the clusters of creepers, the Lord rejoiced.

### Verse 123

कदम्बवीथीषु नदन्मृदङ्गैः
समुल्लसत्ताण्डवसत्कलापैः ।
विश्रब्धमुन्नेत्रयुगैः कृपालु-
र्ननन्द भूयो हरिणैः सकान्तैः ॥१२३॥

*kadamba-vīthīṣu nadan-mṛdaṅgaiḥ*
*samullasat-tāṇḍava-sat-kalāpaiḥ |*
*viśrabdham unnetra-yugaiḥ kṛpālur*
*nananda bhūyo hariṇaiḥ sa-kāntaiḥ ||123||*

*Word for word:* *kadamba* — of kadamba trees; *vīthīṣu* — in the avenues; *nadat* — resounding; *mṛdaṅgaiḥ* — [by those whose] mridangas [were]; *samullasat* — joyously; *tāṇḍava* — in the tandava dance; *sat* — with beautiful; *kalāpaiḥ* — [by those with] tails (by peacocks); *viśrabdham* — trustingly; *unnetra* — raised; *yugaiḥ* — [whose] pairs of eyes [were]; *kṛpāluḥ* — the Merciful One; *nananda* — rejoiced; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *hariṇaiḥ* — in the deer; *sa-kāntaiḥ* — with their mates.

**123.** In the avenues of kadamba trees [the peacocks], their mridangas resounding, joyously danced the tandava with their beautiful tails [spread], and the deer with their mates trustingly raised their eyes [to Him]; and the Merciful One rejoiced again.

*Note.* The text does not name the peacocks: they are indicated by *kalāpa* ("a peacock's tail"). Peacocks dance at the rumble of rain clouds; the "mridangas" are perhaps that rumble.

### Verse 124

निष्कूजशान्ताः क्वच चण्डशब्द-
प्रतिध्वनिग्रस्तदिशः क्वचापि ।
क्वच प्रसुप्तोरुकरालसत्त्व-
श्वासाग्निदीप्ता वनभूमिभागाः ॥१२४॥

*niṣkūja-śāntāḥ kva ca caṇḍa-śabda-*
*pratidhvani-grasta-diśaḥ kvacāpi |*
*kva ca prasuptoru-karāla-sattva-*
*śvāsāgni-dīptā vana-bhūmi-bhāgāḥ ||124||*

*Word for word:* *niṣkūja* — without the chirping [of birds]; *śāntāḥ* — silent; *kva ca* — somewhere; *caṇḍa* — of fierce; *śabda* — sounds; *pratidhvani* — by the echo; *grasta* — seized; *diśaḥ* — [whose] quarters [were]; *kva api* — somewhere; *kva ca* — somewhere; *prasupta* — sleeping; *uru* — of huge; *karāla* — fearsome; *sattva* — beasts; *śvāsa* — by the breath; *agni* — fiery; *dīptāḥ* — heated; *vana* — of the forest; *bhūmi* — of the land; *bhāgāḥ* — the stretches.

**124.** In some places the stretches of forest land were silent, without the chirping of birds; in others all their quarters were seized by the echo of fierce cries; and in others they were heated by the fiery breath of huge, fearsome beasts lying asleep there…

*Note.* *क्वच* (twice in the edition) is evidently *kva ca* ("and somewhere"), a variant of *kvacit*; the metre allows this reading. The verse is linked syntactically with the next (*yugmaka*).

### Verse 125

गोदावरीवेगमहानिनादा
भीमा गिरिप्रस्रवणा रवेण ।
श्रीगौरचन्द्रस्य वितेनुरुच्चैः
सुकोमलं चित्तमनाप्तधैर्यम् ॥१२५॥

*godāvarī-vega-mahā-ninādā*
*bhīmā giri-prasravaṇā raveṇa |*
*śrī-gauracandrasya vitenur uccaiḥ*
*sukomalaṁ cittam anāpta-dhairyam ||125||*

*Word for word:* *godāvarī* — of the Godavari; *vega* — of the rapids; *mahā* — great; *ninādāḥ* — [having] the roar; *bhīmāḥ* — fearsome; *giri* — mountain; *prasravaṇāḥ* — [having] torrents; *raveṇa* — with [their] din; *śrī-gauracandrasya* — of Sri Gaurachandra; *vitenuḥ* — made; *uccaiḥ* — greatly; *su-komalam* — most tender; *cittam* — the heart; *anāpta* — not retaining; *dhairyam* — composure.

**125.** …[stretches] full of the great roar of the Godavari's rapids, [full of] mountain torrents, fearsome with their din — [these] utterly robbed the most tender heart of Sri Gaurachandra of its composure.

*Note.* The subject of *vitenuḥ* is the stretches of forest land of v. 124. The plural forms in *-āḥ* can be taken as qualifying them ("[having] the great roar of the Godavari's rapids", "[having] mountain torrents"), or as further subjects: the great roar of the Godavari's rapids and the mountain torrents.

### Verse 126

क्षणात् स्खलत्पादविकम्प्रपक्षै-
श्चञ्चूपतद्बीजचयैः प्रपूर्णैः ।
शुकैर्दलद्दाडिमचुम्बवद्भि-
र्गोदावरीतीरवने स रेमे ॥१२६॥

*kṣaṇāt skhalat-pāda-vikampra-pakṣaiś*
*cañcū-patad-bīja-cayaiḥ prapūrṇaiḥ |*
*śukair dalad-dāḍima-cumbavadbhir*
*godāvarī-tīra-vane sa reme ||126||*

*Word for word:* *kṣaṇāt* — every moment; *skhalat* — slipping; *pāda* — [whose] feet [were]; *vikampra* — fluttering; *pakṣaiḥ* — [whose] wings [were]; *cañcū* — from the beaks; *patat* — falling; *bīja* — of seeds; *cayaiḥ* — [with] heaps; *prapūrṇaiḥ* — sated; *śukaiḥ* — in the parrots; *dalat* — split; *dāḍima* — pomegranates; *cumbavadbhiḥ* — kissing; *godāvarī* — of the Godavari; *tīra* — on the bank; *vane* — in the forest; *saḥ* — He; *reme* — took delight.

**126.** In the forest on the bank of the Godavari He took delight in the parrots "kissing" split pomegranates — sated, heaps of seeds tumbling from their beaks, their feet slipping every moment and their wings fluttering.

*Note.* Verses 126–129 form one description: the qualifiers in the locative case in vv. 127–129 refer to the "forest" (*vane*). *Skhalat-pāda* ("with slipping feet") is taken as referring to the birds.

### Verse 127

ताम्बूलवल्लीदलवृन्दमुच्चै-
र्भिन्दद्भिरुग्रैः क्रकचै रसद्भिः ।
अजस्रदीर्घेण विमुग्धझिल्ली-
झङ्काररावेण निकामरम्ये ॥१२७॥

*tāmbūla-vallī-dala-vṛndam uccair*
*bhindadbhir ugraiḥ krakacai rasadbhiḥ |*
*ajasra-dīrgheṇa vimugdha-jhillī-*
*jhaṅkāra-rāveṇa nikāma-ramye ||127||*

*Word for word:* *tāmbūla* — of betel; *vallī* — of the vines; *dala* — of leaves; *vṛndam* — the clusters; *uccaiḥ* — loudly; *bhindadbhiḥ* — tearing; *ugraiḥ* — by fierce; *krakacaiḥ* — "saws"; *rasadbhiḥ* — screeching; *ajasra* — ceaseless; *dīrgheṇa* — long-drawn; *vimugdha* — enchanting; *jhillī* — of cicadas; *jhaṅkāra* — of the chirring; *rāveṇa* — with the sound; *nikāma* — exceedingly; *ramye* — in [the forest] delightful.

**127.** [That forest was] exceedingly delightful: fierce, screeching "saws" loudly tore through the clusters of betel-vine leaves, and the ceaseless, long-drawn, enchanting chirring of cicadas [filled it].

*Note.* The edition has *क्रकचैरसद्भिः* (*krakacair asadbhiḥ*, "non-existent"?). We read *krakacai rasadbhiḥ* ("screeching"), cf. the same word in v. 128; the script allows this division as it stands. *Krakaca* means "a saw"; evidently parrots are meant, their beaks likened to a saw.

### Verse 128

ज्योतिर्गणाचुम्बिभिरम्बुदाभै-
स्तमालमालार्जुनकोविदारैः ।
नानाविधैः पत्ररथै रसद्भि-
श्चमूरुवृन्दैश्चमरैश्च जुष्टे ॥१२८॥

*jyotir-gaṇā-cumbibhir ambudābhais*
*tamāla-mālārjuna-kovidāraiḥ |*
*nānā-vidhaiḥ patra-rathai rasadbhiś*
*camūru-vṛndaiś camaraiś ca juṣṭe ||128||*

*Word for word:* *jyotiḥ* — of the stars; *gaṇa* — the hosts; *ā-cumbibhiḥ* — touching; *ambuda* — clouds; *ābhaiḥ* — resembling; *tamāla* — of tamalas; *mālā* — by rows; *arjuna* — by arjunas; *kovidāraiḥ* — by kovidaras; *nānā-vidhaiḥ* — of many kinds; *patra-rathaiḥ* — by birds; *rasadbhiḥ* — crying; *camūru* — of chamuru deer; *vṛndaiḥ* — by herds; *camaraiḥ* — by yaks; *ca* — and; *juṣṭe* — in [the forest] frequented.

**128.** [It was] frequented by rows of tamalas, by arjunas and kovidaras that touched the hosts of stars and resembled clouds, by crying birds of many kinds, by herds of chamuru deer and by yaks.

*Note.* The edition has *जुष्टैः*; we read *juṣṭe*, a locative agreeing with "forest" (v. 126), like *nikāma-ramye* in v. 127. *Patra-ratha* ("whose chariot is wings") is a bird.

### Verse 129

अर्कप्रभापक्वविहीनसान्द्र-
स्निग्धातिसच्छीतलचारुभूमौ ।
अकृत्रिमालेपनिपीतमूले
वापीतडागादिनिरन्तराले ॥१२९॥

*arka-prabhā-pakva-vihīna-sāndra-*
*snigdhāti-sac-chītala-cāru-bhūmau |*
*akṛtrimālepa-nipīta-mūle*
*vāpī-taḍāgādi-nirantarāle ||129||*

*Word for word:* *arka* — of the sun; *prabhā* — by the rays; *pakva* — scorching; *vihīna* — free from; *sāndra* — dense; *snigdha* — moist; *ati* — very; *sat* — pleasantly; *śītala* — cool; *cāru* — lovely; *bhūmau* — [whose] ground [was]; *akṛtrima* — with natural; *ālepa* — unguent; *nipīta* — saturated; *mūle* — [whose] roots [were]; *vāpī* — by step-wells; *taḍāga* — by ponds; *ādi* — and the like; *nirantarāle* — [whose] intervals [were] filled without a break.

**129.** Its ground, free from the scorching of the sun's rays, was dense [with growth], moist, very pleasantly cool and lovely; the roots [of its trees] were saturated with a natural unguent; and step-wells, ponds and the like filled it without a break.

*Note.* *Pakva* ("ripened, baked") here means "scorched" by the sun.

### Verse 130

ततः स गोदावरिकामुपेत्य
मनस्यथान्दोलिततां जगाम ।
संभाषितव्यः किमसौ नवेति
श्रीमद्भवानन्दसुतो महात्मा ॥१३०॥

*tataḥ sa godāvarikām upetya*
*manasy athāndolitatāṁ jagāma |*
*saṁbhāṣitavyaḥ kim asau na veti*
*śrīmad-bhavānanda-suto mahātmā ||130||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *saḥ* — He; *godāvarikām* — to the Godavari; *upetya* — having come; *manasi* — in mind; *atha* — then; *āndolitatām* — a wavering; *jagāma* — came to; *saṁbhāṣitavyaḥ* — is to be spoken with; *kim* — whether; *asau* — he; *na vā* — or not; *iti* — thus; *śrīmat* — of the illustrious; *bhavānanda* — of Bhavananda; *sutaḥ* — the son; *mahātmā* — great-souled.

**130.** Then, having come to the Godavari, He began to waver in His mind: should He speak with the great-souled son of the illustrious Bhavananda, or not?

*Note.* The edition has *संभाषिव्यः* — a misprint; the metre requires *saṁbhāṣitavyaḥ*. The son of Bhavananda is Ramananda Raya (see v. 99).

### Verse 131

तथाप्यभिव्यज्य विभुर्विरागं
न तं विलोक्यैव ययाववाचीम् ।
नानावनालोकनकोमलात्मा
क्वचित् प्रविश्यातिशयं रुरोद ॥१३१॥

*tathāpy abhivyajya vibhur virāgaṁ*
*na taṁ vilokyaiva yayāv avācīm |*
*nānā-vanālokana-komalātmā*
*kvacit praviśyātiśayaṁ ruroda ||131||*

*Word for word:* *tathā api* — and yet; *abhivyajya* — displaying; *vibhuḥ* — the Almighty; *virāgam* — detachment; *na* — not; *tam* — him; *vilokya* — having seen; *eva* — even; *yayau* — went; *avācīm* — to the south; *nānā* — various; *vana* — of forests; *ālokana* — by the sight; *komala* — softened; *ātmā* — [whose] heart [was]; *kvacit* — at times; *praviśya* — having entered [a thicket]; *atiśayam* — beyond measure; *ruroda* — wept.

**131.** And yet the Almighty, displaying detachment, went on to the south without even seeing him. His heart softened by the sight of the various forests, at times He would enter [a thicket] and weep beyond measure.

*Note.* In Krishnadasa Kaviraja (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 8) the conversation with Ramananda on the Godavari takes place on the way south. Karnapura in the Mahakavya transfers it to the return journey: 13.34–49 (Ramananda recites verses, the Lord answers "this is external" (*bāhya*), then the Bengali song *pahilahi rāga nayana-bhaṅga bhela* is sung — the same as in the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 8.192–193, in the numbering of the project's edition). Cf. Karnapura's own drama *Chaitanya-chandrodaya*, Act 7: there, as in the Chaitanya-charitamrita, the meeting with Ramananda takes place on the way south (with the same answer "this is external"), so the Mahakavya diverges even from Karnapura's own drama.

### Verse 132

क्वचित्क्वचिद्गायति मुक्तकण्ठं
क्वचित् क्वचिन्नृत्यति च स्वयं सः ।
क्वचित् क्वचिद्रोदिति हृष्टरोमा
रात्रिन्दिवं नैव विवेद गच्छन् ॥१३२॥

*kvacit kvacid gāyati mukta-kaṇṭhaṁ*
*kvacit kvacin nṛtyati ca svayaṁ saḥ |*
*kvacit kvacid roditi hṛṣṭa-romā*
*rātrin-divaṁ naiva viveda gacchan ||132||*

*Word for word:* *kvacit kvacit* — here and there; *gāyati* — sings; *mukta* — with open; *kaṇṭham* — throat; *nṛtyati* — dances; *ca* — and; *svayam* — Himself; *saḥ* — He; *roditi* — weeps; *hṛṣṭa* — standing on end; *romā* — [whose] hairs [were]; *rātrim-divam* — night and day; *na eva* — not at all; *viveda* — distinguished; *gacchan* — going.

**132.** Here and there He sang full-throated, here and there He Himself danced, here and there He wept, the hairs of His body standing on end; and as He went on He did not distinguish night from day at all.

### Verse 133

कनककरिवरोऽयं किं चिरोन्मुक्तबन्धः
किमु झटिति चरिष्णुर्मेरुरेषः प्रभाति ।
अथ किमु चिररोचिःपुञ्ज एष प्रकामं
स्फुरति चिरविलासः को नु वायं प्रपञ्चः ॥१३३॥

*kanaka-kari-varo 'yaṁ kiṁ cironmukta-bandhaḥ*
*kim u jhaṭiti cariṣṇur merur eṣaḥ prabhāti |*
*atha kim u cira-rociḥ-puñja eṣa prakāmaṁ*
*sphurati cira-vilāsaḥ ko nu vāyaṁ prapañcaḥ ||133||*

*Word for word:* *kanaka* — golden; *kari-varaḥ* — the best of elephants; *ayam* — this; *kim* — is it; *cira* — from long; *unmukta* — freed; *bandhaḥ* — [whose] bonds [are]; *kim u* — or; *jhaṭiti* — suddenly; *cariṣṇuḥ* — moving; *meruḥ* — Meru; *eṣaḥ* — this; *prabhāti* — shines; *atha kim u* — or else; *cira* — lasting; *rociḥ* — of light; *puñjaḥ* — a mass; *eṣaḥ* — this; *prakāmam* — freely; *sphurati* — flashes; *cira* — lasting; *vilāsaḥ* — play; *kaḥ nu vā* — or what indeed; *ayam* — this; *prapañcaḥ* — marvel.

**133.** "Is this a golden king of elephants, freed from long bondage? Or is this Meru, suddenly set in motion, that shines [here]? Or else is this a mass of lasting light that flashes so freely — a play [of lightning] that lasts? Or what indeed is this marvel?"

*Note.* The metre is *mālinī* (⏑⏑⏑ ⏑⏑⏑ ——— ⏑—— ⏑——). A play on words: lightning is *acira-ruc*, "light of a brief moment", whereas here we have *cira-rociḥ*, "lasting light" — lightning that does not fade.

### Verse 134

इति सकलनृलोको दाक्षिणात्यः सतोषं
विनिमिषमनुवेलं लोचनाभ्यां पिबन् सः ।
जडिमजडितचेता दूरमप्यत्र देवे
गतवति यतिचन्द्रे स्थाणुवत्तत्र तस्थौ ॥१३४॥

*iti sakala-nṛ-loko dākṣiṇātyaḥ satoṣaṁ*
*vinimiṣam anuvelaṁ locanābhyāṁ piban saḥ |*
*jaḍima-jaḍita-cetā dūram apy atra deve*
*gatavati yati-candre sthāṇuvat tatra tasthau ||134||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus [thinking]; *sakala* — all; *nṛ* — of people; *lokaḥ* — the folk; *dākṣiṇātyaḥ* — southern; *sa-toṣam* — with delight; *vinimiṣam* — without blinking; *anuvelam* — constantly; *locanābhyām* — with the eyes; *piban* — drinking; *saḥ* — they; *jaḍima* — by stupor; *jaḍita* — numbed; *cetāḥ* — [whose] minds [were]; *dūram* — far; *api* — even; *atra* — here; *deve* — when the Lord; *gatavati* — had gone; *yati* — of ascetics; *candre* — the moon; *sthāṇu-vat* — like posts; *tatra* — there; *tasthau* — stood.

**134.** Thus [thinking], all the southern folk drank Him in with their eyes, with delight, constantly and without blinking; their minds numbed with stupor, even when the Lord, the moon among ascetics, had gone far from there, they stood there like posts.

*Note.* *Mālinī*. The edition has *सन्तोषं*, but the metre requires a short syllable here (⏑—— at the end of the pada): *satoṣam*. *Vinimiṣam* means "without blinking"; one would expect *animiṣam*, and the edition's form may be a corruption (?).

**Colophon:** इति श्रीकृष्णचैतन्यचरितामृते महाकाव्ये द्वादशः सर्गः । (*iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahākāvye dvādaśaḥ sargaḥ*) — "Thus [ends] the twelfth sarga in the mahakavya 'Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita'." (The colophon gives no title for the sarga.)

---

## Sarga Thirteen — verses 1–148

**Title of the sarga:** none — the colophon of the edition gives no title for this sarga.
**Metre:**
- 1–63 — *upajāti* (a mixture of *indravajrā* ——⏑——⏑⏑—⏑—— and *upendravajrā* ⏑—⏑——⏑⏑—⏑——; 11 syllables per pada); 12–13 — *anuṣṭubh* (8 syllables per pada; a quotation from the Kurma Purana); 39 — *mandākrāntā* (————⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑——⏑——⏑——; 17 syllables); 42 — *vasantatilakā* (——⏑—⏑⏑⏑—⏑⏑—⏑——; 14 syllables); 46 — Ramananda's Bengali song (*rāga bhairavī*).
- 64–114 — *svāgatā* (—⏑—⏑⏑⏑—⏑⏑——) intermixed with *rathoddhatā* (—⏑—⏑⏑⏑—⏑—⏑—); 11 syllables per pada.
- 115–125, 128–134, 138–144 — *viyoginī* (odd padas ⏑⏑—⏑⏑—⏑—⏑—, 10 syllables; even padas ⏑⏑——⏑⏑—⏑—⏑—, 11 syllables); 119, 126–127, 135–137, 147 — *upajāti*.
- 145, 148 — *śārdūla-vikrīḍita* (———⏑⏑—⏑—⏑⏑⏑——⏑——⏑—; 19 syllables); 146 — *vasantatilakā*.

**Total verses:** 148.

**Contents of the passage:** the southern pilgrimage; the conversation with Ramananda; the return to Puri; the gathering of the devotees.
- 1–8 — the way south; Shrirangam: the chaturmasya in the house of Trimalla Bhatta; autumn.
- 9–13 — a brahmana devoted to Rama grieves over the abduction of Sita; the Lord shows him the verses of the Kurma Purana about the shadow Sita.
- 14–16 — the meeting with Paramananda Puri; he goes to Puri, the Lord to the Setu.
- 17–19 — seven palmyra palms are embraced and go to heaven.
- 20–30 — heretics try to allure the servant Krishnadasa; the Lord wins him back.
- 31–33 — Rameshvara at the Setu; the Lord turns back.
- **34–49 — the conversation with Ramananda on the way back, on the Godavari.** The verse on renunciation — "this is external"; the verse *nānopacāra…* — "external"; the song *pahilahi rāga…* on the highest oneness of the Two; the embrace; several days of conversation "on the path of realisation".
- 50–59 — Puri: the Snana-yatra; the anavasara; the Lord goes away to Alalanatha, and the devotees search for Him.
- 60–61 — **again on the Godavari**: four more months with Ramananda; at the onset of winter the Lord returns to Puri together with him.
- 62–71 — Kashi Mishra (he sees the Lord four-armed), Vishnudasa, Pradyumna Mishra.
- 72–77 — a grove reminiscent of Vrindavana: the creepers as dancers; the Lord's dance.
- 78–88 — Prataparudra in the grove: he glorifies the rasa dance; the embrace; "Who are you?" — "Your servant."
- 89–109 — Shikhi Mahiti, his brother Murari and his sister Madhava-devi (Madhavi-devi); Shikhi's dream; the meeting in the Jaganmohana; the embrace.
- 110–126 — the arrival of the Bengalis. The line of Madhavendra Puri and Ishvara Puri; Paramananda Puri in Navadvipa with Shachi and Acharyaratna; Kamalananda; the journey to Puri with Gadadhara and Jagadananda; the Lord bows to Paramananda; Vidyanidhi, Acharyaratna.
- 127–136 — Shivananda with Murari Gupta; Raghava; Govinda becomes [the Lord's] servant; Bhavananda ("you are like Pandu") and his five sons; Vaninatha.
- 137–144 — Purushottama Acharya becomes Svarupa Damodara.
- 145–148 — Vakreshvara, Vasudeva Datta, Bhagavan Acharya; the Lord's fame spreads; Satyaraja, Raghunandana, Narahari and Mukunda arrive.

### Verse 1

एवं स तीर्थाटनकौतुकेन
दीनैकबन्धुः करुणैकसिन्धुः ।
ततो ययौ भाग्यवतीमवाचीं
स्वनामरत्नग्रहणोत्सवोत्कः ॥१॥

*evaṁ sa tīrthāṭana-kautukena*
*dīnaika-bandhuḥ karuṇaika-sindhuḥ |*
*tato yayau bhāgyavatīm avācīṁ*
*sva-nāma-ratna-grahaṇotsavotkaḥ ||1||*

*Word for word:* *evam* — thus; *saḥ* — He; *tīrtha* — to the holy places; *aṭana* — for wandering; *kautukena* — with eagerness; *dīna* — of the wretched; *eka* — the only; *bandhuḥ* — friend; *karuṇā* — of compassion; *eka* — the one; *sindhuḥ* — ocean; *tataḥ* — from there; *yayau* — went; *bhāgyavatīm* — to the fortunate; *avācīm* — south; *sva* — of His own; *nāma* — name; *ratna* — of the jewel; *grahaṇa* — of the acceptance; *utsava* — for the festival; *utkaḥ* — eager.

**1.** Thus, eager to wander to the holy places, He — the only friend of the wretched, the one ocean of compassion — went from there to the fortunate south, longing for the festival of [people's] accepting the jewel of His own name.

### Verse 2

विलोक्य तं वर्त्मनि कृष्णसारा-
स्तृष्णावताक्ष्णोर्युगलेन भूयः ।
रूपामृतं पातुमिवाप्तधैर्याः
समं समन्तात् सविधं समीयुः ॥२॥

*vilokya taṁ vartmani kṛṣṇa-sārās*
*tṛṣṇāvatākṣṇor yugalena bhūyaḥ |*
*rūpāmṛtaṁ pātum ivāpta-dhairyāḥ*
*samaṁ samantāt savidhaṁ samīyuḥ ||2||*

*Word for word:* *vilokya* — having seen; *tam* — Him; *vartmani* — on the road; *kṛṣṇa-sārāḥ* — the black antelopes; *tṛṣṇāvatā* — with the thirsting; *akṣṇoḥ* — of eyes; *yugalena* — with the pair; *bhūyaḥ* — again [and again]; *rūpa* — of [His] form; *amṛtam* — the nectar; *pātum* — to drink; *iva* — as if; *āpta* — having gained; *dhairyāḥ* — courage; *samam* — all together; *samantāt* — from all sides; *savidham* — close [to Him]; *samīyuḥ* — came.

**2.** Seeing Him on the road, the black antelopes took courage, as if to drink again and again the nectar of His form with their thirsting pairs of eyes, and all together came close to Him from every side.

### Verse 3

श्रीरङ्गक्षेत्रमसौ दयालुः
कावेरिकावेष्टितमुच्चदेशम् ।
आसाद्य तत्रत्यमवेक्ष्य देवं
प्रियाकरोऽसौ मुदमाप तुङ्गाम् ॥३॥

*śrī-raṅga-kṣetram asau dayāluḥ*
*kāverikā-veṣṭitam ucca-deśam |*
*āsādya tatratyam avekṣya devaṁ*
*priyākaro 'sau mudam āpa tuṅgām ||3||*

*Word for word:* *śrī-raṅga-kṣetram* — Sri Ranga-kshetra; *asau* — He; *dayāluḥ* — the Merciful One; *kāverikā* — by the Kaveri; *veṣṭitam* — encircled; *ucca* — elevated; *deśam* — a place; *āsādya* — having reached; *tatratyam* — present there; *avekṣya* — having beheld; *devam* — the Deity; *priya* — of love (?); *ākaraḥ* — the mine; *asau* — He; *mudam* — joy; *āpa* — attained; *tuṅgām* — lofty.

**3.** The Merciful One reached Sri Ranga-kshetra, an elevated place encircled by the Kaveri. Beholding the Deity there, He, the mine of love, attained lofty joy.

*Note.* *Priyākara*, literally "a mine of what is dear", that is, a treasury of love; or perhaps "one who does what is pleasing" (?). Shrirangam stands on an island between the arms of the Kaveri. The first pada has only ten syllables (*śrī-raṅga-kṣetram asau dayāluḥ*: ————⏑⏑—⏑——) instead of the eleven of the *upajāti*; a syllable seems to have dropped out (?).

### Verse 4

त्रिमल्लभट्टस्य महाशयस्य
गृहे कृतावासविधिः कृपालुः ।
कुतूहलेनैव निनाय चातु-
र्मास्यं स आवश्यककर्म कुर्वन् ॥४॥

*trimalla-bhaṭṭasya mahāśayasya*
*gṛhe kṛtāvāsa-vidhiḥ kṛpāluḥ |*
*kutūhalenaiva nināya cātur-*
*māsyaṁ sa āvaśyaka-karma kurvan ||4||*

*Word for word:* *trimalla-bhaṭṭasya* — of Trimalla Bhatta; *mahāśayasya* — the noble-minded; *gṛhe* — in the house; *kṛta* — having made; *āvāsa* — of residence; *vidhiḥ* — the arrangement (having settled); *kṛpāluḥ* — the Merciful One; *kutūhalena* — with eager delight; *eva* — indeed; *nināya* — spent; *cāturmāsyam* — the chaturmasya; *saḥ* — He; *āvaśyaka* — obligatory; *karma* — duties; *kurvan* — performing.

**4.** Settling in the house of the noble-minded Trimalla Bhatta, the Merciful One spent the chaturmasya there with eager delight, performing the obligatory duties.

*Note.* In the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 9.82–86) the host is Venkata Bhatta, but in the brief summary (Madhya 1.108–109) the Lord spends the chaturmasya with Trimalla Bhatta, as in Karnapura; according to Gaudiya tradition, Trimalla and Venkata were brothers (the third being Prabodhananda Sarasvati). The chaturmasya is the four months of the rainy season, during which sannyasis do not travel.

### Verse 5

कावेरिकायां विहिताप्लवोऽयं
चकार तस्या बहुपावनत्वम् ।
श्रीरङ्गसङ्गं प्रविलोक्य देवं
निनाय मासांश्चतुरः कृपालुः ॥५॥

*kāverikāyāṁ vihitāplavo 'yaṁ*
*cakāra tasyā bahu-pāvanatvam |*
*śrī-raṅga-saṅgaṁ [-saṁjñaṁ?] pravilokya devaṁ*
*nināya māsāṁś caturaḥ kṛpāluḥ ||5||*

*Word for word:* *kāverikāyām* — in the Kaveri; *vihita* — having performed; *āplavaḥ* — bathing; *ayam* — He; *cakāra* — made; *tasyāḥ* — its; *bahu* — manifold; *pāvanatvam* — purifying power; *śrī-raṅga* — Sri Ranga; *saṅgam* (*saṁjñam*?) — named (?); *pravilokya* — beholding; *devam* — the Deity; *nināya* — spent; *māsān* — months; *caturaḥ* — four; *kṛpāluḥ* — the Merciful One.

**5.** Bathing in the Kaveri, He multiplied its purifying power. Beholding the Deity named Sri Ranga, the Merciful One spent four months [there].

*Note.* *श्रीरङ्गसङ्गं* in the edition is unintelligible. We conjecture *śrī-raṅga-saṁjñam*, "called Sri Ranga" (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 6

वर्षाशरन्मध्यगतः स कालः
परिष्वजन्तीं शरदं चुचुम्बे ।
कान्ताद्वयान्तःशयितो विलासी
पार्श्वाविवृत्ताविव वीतनिद्रः ॥६॥

*varṣā-śaran-madhya-gataḥ sa kālaḥ*
*pariṣvajantīṁ śaradaṁ cucumbe |*
*kāntā-dvayāntaḥ-śayito vilāsī*
*pārśvāvivṛttāv iva vīta-nidraḥ ||6||*

*Word for word:* *varṣā* — of the rains; *śarat* — and of autumn; *madhya* — in the middle; *gataḥ* — situated; *saḥ* — that; *kālaḥ* — season; *pariṣvajantīm* — embracing [it]; *śaradam* — autumn; *cucumbe* — kissed; *kāntā* — of beloveds; *dvaya* — two; *antaḥ* — between; *śayitaḥ* — lying; *vilāsī* — a lover; *pārśva* — onto [his] side; *āvivṛttau* — on turning; *iva* — like; *vīta* — rid of; *nidraḥ* — sleep.

**6.** That season lying between the rains and autumn kissed Autumn as she embraced him — like a lover lying between two beloveds who, waking and turning onto his side, [kisses the one who embraces him].

*Note.* That is, autumn set in. The edition has *स काल* without the visarga.

### Verse 7

ततो नवोत्फुल्लसरोरुहास्या
नवोत्पलाक्षी गतपङ्कजाला ।
सुजीवना तत्करुणाप्तिकामा
दासीव भेजे शरदीश्वरं तत् ॥७॥

*tato navotphulla-saroruhāsyā*
*navotpalākṣī gata-paṅka-jālā |*
*sujīvanā tat-karuṇāpti-kāmā*
*dāsīva bheje śarad īśvaraṁ tat ||7||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *nava* — freshly; *utphulla* — blossomed; *saroruha* — a lotus; *āsyā* — [whose] face [is]; *nava* — fresh; *utpala* — blue lotuses; *akṣī* — [whose] eyes [are]; *gata* — gone; *paṅka* — of mud (of sin); *jālā* — [whose] film [is]; *su-jīvanā* — [having] pure water (a good life); *tat* — His; *karuṇā* — mercy; *āpti* — to attain; *kāmā* — desiring; *dāsī* — a maidservant; *iva* — like; *bheje* — served; *śarat* — autumn; *īśvaram* — the Lord; *tat* — then (?).

**7.** Then Autumn — her face a freshly blossomed lotus, her eyes fresh blue lotuses, the film of mud gone from her, her waters pure — served the Lord like a maidservant who desires to attain His mercy.

*Note.* A double meaning (*śleṣa*): *paṅka* is both "mud" and "sin", *jīvana* both "water" and "life". The maidservant is free of sin, lives righteously and serves her master for the sake of his favour. The final *tat* is unclear; one would expect *tam* (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 8

अथात आनन्दसमूहमग्नो
ययौ प्रहृष्टो दिशि दक्षिणस्याम् ।
महाप्रभुः स्वीयगुणानुगाथा-
निरन्तरोत्कीर्तनमुग्धवक्त्रः ॥८॥

*athāta ānanda-samūha-magno*
*yayau prahṛṣṭo diśi dakṣiṇasyām |*
*mahāprabhuḥ svīya-guṇānugāthā-*
*nirantarotkīrtana-mugdha-vaktraḥ ||8||*

*Word for word:* *atha ataḥ* — then from here; *ānanda* — of bliss; *samūha* — in the mass; *magnaḥ* — immersed; *yayau* — went; *prahṛṣṭaḥ* — rejoicing; *diśi dakṣiṇasyām* — in the southern direction; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *svīya* — of His own; *guṇa* — qualities; *anugāthā* — of songs; *nirantara* — by unceasing; *utkīrtana* — loud chanting; *mugdha* — charming; *vaktraḥ* — [whose] face [was].

**8.** Then Mahaprabhu, immersed in a mass of bliss, went on from here, rejoicing, in the southern direction, His face charming with the unceasing loud chanting of songs about His own qualities.

*Note.* "His own qualities", that is, the qualities of Krishna.

### Verse 9

तत्र क्वचित् श्रीरघुनाथभक्तं
प्रशान्तचित्तं द्विजपुङ्गवं सः ।
सीता दशास्यापहृतेति शोका-
द्बहिर्व्रजत्प्राणमिवालुलोके ॥९॥

*tatra kvacit śrī-raghunātha-bhaktaṁ*
*praśānta-cittaṁ dvija-puṅgavaṁ saḥ |*
*sītā daśāsyāpahṛteti śokād*
*bahir-vrajat-prāṇam ivāluloke ||9||*

*Word for word:* *tatra kvacit* — somewhere there; *śrī-raghunātha* — of Sri Raghunatha; *bhaktam* — a devotee; *praśānta* — peaceful; *cittam* — [whose] mind [was]; *dvija-puṅgavam* — a best of brahmanas; *saḥ* — He; *sītā* — Sita; *daśa-āsya* — by the Ten-faced one; *apahṛtā* — has been abducted; *iti* — that; *śokāt* — from grief; *bahiḥ* — out; *vrajat* — going; *prāṇam* — [whose] life [was]; *iva* — as if; *āluloke* — saw.

**9.** Somewhere there He saw a best of brahmanas, a devotee of Sri Raghunatha, peaceful in mind, whose life, from grief that Sita had been abducted by the Ten-faced one, seemed to be departing.

*Note.* Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 9.179–215: in Southern Mathura a brahmana worshipper of Rama (Ramadasa) grieves over the abduction of Sita; later the Lord brings him the leaves of the Kurma Purana. The Ten-faced one is Ravana.

### Verse 10

लक्ष्मीरियं राक्षसहस्तयाता
किमेतदित्यस्य मनो विदित्वा ।
आश्वासयन्नेव तमब्रवीद्भो
मैवं स्वरूपं शृणु यद्ब्रवीमि ॥१०॥

*lakṣmīr iyaṁ rākṣasa-hasta-yātā*
*kim etad ity asya mano viditvā |*
*āśvāsayann eva tam abravīd bho*
*maivaṁ svarūpaṁ śṛṇu yad bravīmi ||10||*

*Word for word:* *lakṣmīḥ* — Lakshmi; *iyam* — she; *rākṣasa* — of a Rakshasa; *hasta* — into the hands; *yātā* — fallen; *kim* — what; *etat* — is this; *iti* — thus; *asya* — his; *manaḥ* — mind; *viditvā* — having understood; *āśvāsayan* — comforting; *eva* — indeed; *tam* — to him; *abravīt* — said; *bho* — O [brahmana]; *mā evam* — not so; *svarūpam* — the truth; *śṛṇu* — hear; *yat* — which; *bravīmi* — I tell.

**10.** Understanding his mind — "She is Lakshmi, and she has fallen into the hands of a Rakshasa? What is this?" — He comforted him and said: "O [brahmana], not so! Hear the truth, which I shall tell you.

### Verse 11

यद्वा मदीये वचसि प्रतीति-
र्न ते भवित्री तदिदं नु पश्य ।
पुराणपद्यद्वयमित्यकस्मा-
ददर्शयत् स्वाञ्चलतो विकृष्य ॥११॥

*yadvā madīye vacasi pratītir*
*na te bhavitrī tad idaṁ nu paśya |*
*purāṇa-padya-dvayam ity akasmād*
*adarśayat svāñcalato vikṛṣya ||11||*

*Word for word:* *yadvā* — or if; *madīye* — in My; *vacasi* — word; *pratītiḥ* — faith; *na* — not; *te* — of you; *bhavitrī* — will be; *tat* — then; *idam* — this; *nu* — now; *paśya* — look at; *purāṇa* — from a Purana; *padya* — of verses; *dvayam* — a pair; *iti* — thus [saying]; *akasmāt* — suddenly; *adarśayat* — showed; *sva* — of His own; *añcalataḥ* — from the hem of the cloth; *vikṛṣya* — having drawn out.

**11.** Or if you will not have faith in My word, then look at this now." So saying, He suddenly drew out from the hem of His cloth two verses from a Purana and showed [them to him].

*Note.* In the Chaitanya-charitamrita the order is different: the Lord hears the Kurma Purana in Rameshvaram, takes the old leaves with these verses and, returning to Southern Mathura, gives them to the brahmana Ramadasa (Madhya 9.200–215). In Karnapura the leaf is already with the Lord.

### Verse 12

सीतयाराधितो वह्नि-
श्छायासीतामजीजनत् ।
तां जहार दशग्रीवः
सीता वह्निपुरं गता ॥१२॥

*sītayārādhito vahniś*
*chāyā-sītām ajījanat |*
*tāṁ jahāra daśa-grīvaḥ*
*sītā vahni-puraṁ gatā ||12||*

*Word for word:* *sītayā* — by Sita; *ārādhitaḥ* — propitiated; *vahniḥ* — Agni; *chāyā* — a shadow; *sītām* — Sita; *ajījanat* — produced; *tām* — her; *jahāra* — carried off; *daśa-grīvaḥ* — the Ten-necked one; *sītā* — Sita; *vahni* — of Agni; *puram* — to the abode; *gatā* — went.

**12.** "Agni, propitiated by Sita, produced a shadow Sita. Her the Ten-necked one carried off, while [the real] Sita went to the abode of Agni.

*Note.* Metre *anuṣṭubh*. This is a quotation: verses 12–13 are cited in the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 9.211–212) as verses of the Kurma Purana (confirmed; the last pada of 13 there is different — see the note on 13).

### Verse 13

परीक्षासमये वह्निं
छायासीता विवेश सा ।
वह्निः सीतां समानीय
स्वपुरादुदनीनमत् ॥१३॥

*parīkṣā-samaye vahniṁ*
*chāyā-sītā viveśa sā |*
*vahniḥ sītāṁ samānīya*
*sva-purād udanīnamat ||13||*

*Word for word:* *parīkṣā* — of the ordeal; *samaye* — at the time; *vahnim* — into the fire; *chāyā-sītā* — the shadow Sita; *viveśa* — entered; *sā* — she; *vahniḥ* — Agni; *sītām* — Sita; *samānīya* — having brought; *sva* — from his own; *purāt* — abode; *udanīnamat* (read *udanīnayat*) — led out.

**13.** At the time of the ordeal the shadow Sita entered the fire, and Agni, bringing [the real] Sita from his own abode, led her forth [to Rama]."

*Note.* The edition has *उदनीनमत्*; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *sva-purād udanīnayat*, "led out from his abode" (the aorist of the causative of *nī*), and so we read. In the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 9.212) the last pada is different: *tat-purastād anīnayat*, "brought [her] before him", that is, before Rama.

### Verse 14

अथात्र कथञ्चिद्यतिनां वरिष्ठं
ददर्श नाथो बहुहृष्टचित्तम् ।
महानुभावं परमं पुरस्ता-
दानन्दमध्यं च पुरीं तदन्तम् ॥१४॥

*athātra kathañcid yatināṁ variṣṭhaṁ*
*dadarśa nātho bahu-hṛṣṭa-cittam |*
*mahānubhāvaṁ paramaṁ purastād*
*ānanda-madhyaṁ ca purīṁ tad-antam ||14||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *atra* — here; *kathañcit* (read *kañcit*, as GGM) — a certain; *yatinām* — of ascetics; *variṣṭham* — the best; *dadarśa* — saw; *nāthaḥ* — the Master; *bahu* — very; *hṛṣṭa* — joyful; *cittam* — [whose] heart [was]; *mahā-anubhāvam* — magnanimous; *paramam* — "Parama"; *purastāt* — at the beginning; *ānanda* — "ananda"; *madhyam* — [having] in the middle; *ca* — and; *purīm* — "Puri"; *tat-antam* — [having] at its end.

**14.** Then here the Master saw a certain best of ascetics, magnanimous and very joyful at heart, [whose name had] "Parama" at the beginning, "ananda" in the middle and "Puri" at its end.

*Note.* A riddle-name: Paramananda Puri, a disciple of Madhavendra Puri. Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 9.168–174: the Lord meets Paramananda Puri at Rishabha hill; he goes on to Puri, and the Lord to the Setu. In our edition the first pada has twelve syllables (*athātra kathañcid*); the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *athātra kañcid*, "a certain [best of ascetics]", which is metrically correct, and so we read.

### Verse 15

विलोक्य संभाष्य सुजातहर्षौ
बभूवतुस्तौ परमप्रभावौ ।
अन्योन्यसंप्रीतिवशौ कृपालू
तस्मात् प्रयातुं दधतुश्च चेतः ॥१५॥

*vilokya saṁbhāṣya sujāta-harṣau*
*babhūvatus tau parama-prabhāvau |*
*anyonya-saṁprīti-vaśau kṛpālū*
*tasmāt prayātuṁ dadhatuś ca cetaḥ ||15||*

*Word for word:* *vilokya* — having seen [each other]; *saṁbhāṣya* — having conversed; *sujāta* — arisen; *harṣau* — [in whom] joy [had]; *babhūvatuḥ* — became; *tau* — the two; *parama* — supreme; *prabhāvau* — [possessing] power; *anyonya* — of mutual; *saṁprīti* — love; *vaśau* — under the sway; *kṛpālū* — the two merciful ones; *tasmāt* — from there; *prayātum* — to depart; *dadhatuḥ* — set; *ca* — and; *cetaḥ* — [their] minds.

**15.** Having seen each other and conversed, the two, endowed with supreme power, were filled with joy. Under the sway of mutual love, both merciful, they resolved to depart from there.

*Note.* The edition has *कृपालु*; the dual *kṛpālū* is required.

### Verse 16

एको गतो गौरशशी त्ववाची-
मन्यः समागात् पुरुषोत्तमं च ।
सेतुं समुद्दिश्य चलन्नथासौ
रराज राजीवदलायताक्षः ॥१६॥

*eko gato gaura-śaśī tv avācīm*
*anyaḥ samāgāt puruṣottamaṁ ca |*
*setuṁ samuddiśya calann athāsau*
*rarāja rājīva-dalāyatākṣaḥ ||16||*

*Word for word:* *ekaḥ* — the one; *gataḥ* — went; *gaura* — the golden; *śaśī* — moon; *tu* — but; *avācīm* — to the south; *anyaḥ* — the other; *samāgāt* — set out; *puruṣottamam* — for Purushottama; *ca* — and; *setum* — the Setu; *samuddiśya* — heading for; *calan* — walking; *atha* — then; *asau* — He; *rarāja* — shone; *rājīva* — of a lotus; *dala* — [like] the petals; *āyata* — long; *akṣaḥ* — [whose] eyes [are].

**16.** The one, the golden moon, went south, and the other set out for Purushottama. And He whose eyes are long like lotus petals shone as He walked on, heading for the Setu.

*Note.* In the edition, as in the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Paramananda Puri goes to Puri. The Setu (Setubandha) is Rama's "bridge" in the south, near Rameshvaram.

### Verse 17

गच्छन् पथि प्रेमविभिन्नचेता
हसत्यलं रोदिति निर्भरार्तः ।
विभिन्नधैर्यश्चलितस्ततोऽसौ
ददर्श सप्तोच्छ्रिततालवृक्षान् ॥१७॥

*gacchan pathi prema-vibhinna-cetā*
*hasaty alaṁ roditi nirbharārtaḥ |*
*vibhinna-dhairyaś calitas tato 'sau*
*dadarśa saptocchrita-tāla-vṛkṣān ||17||*

*Word for word:* *gacchan* — going; *pathi* — along the road; *prema* — by love; *vibhinna* — broken; *cetāḥ* — [whose] heart [was]; *hasati* — laughs; *alam* — abundantly; *roditi* — weeps; *nirbhara* — utterly; *ārtaḥ* — afflicted; *vibhinna* — shattered; *dhairyaḥ* — [whose] composure [was]; *calitaḥ* — moving on; *tataḥ* — then; *asau* — He; *dadarśa* — saw; *sapta* — seven; *ucchrita* — tall; *tāla* — palmyra; *vṛkṣān* — trees.

**17.** Going along the road, His heart broken by love, He laughed abundantly and wept, utterly afflicted. His composure shattered, He moved on and then saw seven tall palmyra trees.

*Note.* The "Sapta-tala" are the seven palms connected with the story of Rama and Sugriva. Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 9.312–315 (the Lord embraces the seven palms and they vanish, "sent to Vaikuntha"); there this episode takes place on the way back.

### Verse 18

विलोक्य तांस्तालतरून् कृपालुः
प्रत्येकमेवाश्लिषदात्तहर्षः ।
अत्रान्तरे ते दिवमीयिवांसः
शून्या स्थली सा सहसैव याता ॥१८॥

*vilokya tāṁs tāla-tarūn kṛpāluḥ*
*pratyekam evāśliṣad ātta-harṣaḥ |*
*atrāntare te divam īyivāṁsaḥ*
*śūnyā sthalī sā sahasaiva yātā ||18||*

*Word for word:* *vilokya* — having seen; *tān* — those; *tāla-tarūn* — palm trees; *kṛpāluḥ* — the Merciful One; *pratyekam* — each one; *eva* — indeed; *āśliṣat* — embraced; *ātta* — seized; *harṣaḥ* — [by] joy; *atra antare* — at that very moment; *te* — they; *divam* — to heaven; *īyivāṁsaḥ* — went; *śūnyā* — empty; *sthalī* — ground; *sā* — that; *sahasā* — suddenly; *eva* — indeed; *yātā* — became.

**18.** Seeing those palm trees, the Merciful One, seized with joy, embraced each one of them. At that very moment they went to heaven, and that ground suddenly became empty.

### Verse 19

क एष गौराङ्गमहाप्रभोस्तत्
विचित्रनानानुभवस्य लोके ।
अतर्कनीयो महिमा कृपालो-
श्चित्रं कृपायाः किमशक्यमास्ते ॥१९॥

*ka eṣa gaurāṅga-mahāprabhos tat*
*vicitra-nānānubhavasya loke |*
*atarkanīyo mahimā kṛpāloś*
*citraṁ kṛpāyāḥ kim aśakyam āste ||19||*

*Word for word:* *kaḥ* — what [wonder]; *eṣaḥ* — is this; *gaurāṅga-mahāprabhoḥ* — for Gauranga Mahaprabhu; *tat* — then; *vicitra* — wondrous; *nānā* — manifold; *anubhavasya* — [whose] manifestations [are]; *loke* — in the world; *atarkanīyaḥ* — inconceivable; *mahimā* — the greatness; *kṛpāloḥ* — of the Merciful One; *citram* — a wonder; *kṛpāyāḥ* — for mercy; *kim* — what; *aśakyam* — impossible; *āste* — is there.

**19.** What wonder is this, then, for Gauranga Mahaprabhu, whose manifestations in the world are wondrous and manifold? The greatness of the Merciful One is inconceivable. A wonder [indeed] — yet what is impossible for mercy?

*Note.* *Tat* at the end of the pada, before a vowel, stands in the edition without sandhi.

### Verse 20

अथ व्रजन् दक्षिणदिग्विभागे
विलोकयन् कौतुकचेष्टितानि ।
अखण्डपाषण्डपथप्रविष्टा-
न्ददर्श नानाविधलिङ्गसंघान् ॥२०॥

*atha vrajan dakṣiṇa-dig-vibhāge*
*vilokayan kautuka-ceṣṭitāni |*
*akhaṇḍa-pāṣaṇḍa-patha-praviṣṭān*
*dadarśa nānā-vidha-liṅga-saṅghān ||20||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *vrajan* — going; *dakṣiṇa* — of the southern; *dik* — direction; *vibhāge* — in the region; *vilokayan* — observing; *kautuka* — curious; *ceṣṭitāni* — doings; *akhaṇḍa* — utter; *pāṣaṇḍa* — of heresy; *patha* — upon the path; *praviṣṭān* — who had entered; *dadarśa* — saw; *nānā-vidha* — of various kinds; *liṅga* — [with] marks; *saṅghān* — crowds.

**20.** Then, going on through the southern region and observing curious customs, He saw crowds bearing sectarian marks of various kinds, who had entered upon the path of utter heresy.

*Note.* *Liṅga* — the outward marks of a sect: dress, tilaka, staff and so on.

### Verse 21

निकामवामे पथि वर्तमानाः
पाषण्डिनस्ते परिलोक्य नाथम् ।
नानाविधेन स्वमतेन शश्व-
द्विलोभयाञ्चक्रुरदभ्रपापाः ॥२१॥

*nikāma-vāme pathi vartamānāḥ*
*pāṣaṇḍinas te parilokya nātham |*
*nānā-vidhena sva-matena śaśvad*
*vilobhayāñcakrur adabhra-pāpāḥ ||21||*

*Word for word:* *nikāma* — utterly; *vāme* — on a perverse; *pathi* — path; *vartamānāḥ* — abiding; *pāṣaṇḍinaḥ* — heretics; *te* — those; *parilokya* — having seen; *nātham* — the Master; *nānā-vidhena* — of various kinds; *sva* — with their own; *matena* — doctrine; *śaśvat* — constantly; *vilobhayāñcakruḥ* — tried to allure; *adabhra* — not slight; *pāpāḥ* — [whose] sins [were].

**21.** Those heretics, great sinners abiding on an utterly perverse path, saw the Master and constantly tried to allure Him with their own doctrines of various kinds.

### Verse 22

यदीयमायैकविजृम्भितेन
स्वं चातिपाषण्डपथप्रवृत्तम् ।
पश्यन्ति नैते तमिमं कथं वा
कुर्वन्तु नानाकुहकैर्विमुग्धम् ॥२२॥

*yadīya-māyaika-vijṛmbhitena*
*svaṁ cāti-pāṣaṇḍa-patha-pravṛttam |*
*paśyanti naite tam imaṁ kathaṁ vā*
*kurvantu nānā-kuhakair vimugdham ||22||*

*Word for word:* *yadīya* — whose; *māyā* — of the maya; *eka* — by the mere; *vijṛmbhitena* — unfolding; *svam* — themselves; *ca* — and; *ati* — of extreme; *pāṣaṇḍa* — heresy; *patha* — on the path; *pravṛttam* — set out; *paśyanti* — see; *na* — not; *ete* — they; *tam imam* — Him, this very one; *katham* — how; *vā* — then; *kurvantu* — could they make; *nānā* — various; *kuhakaiḥ* — by tricks; *vimugdham* — bewildered.

**22.** By the mere unfolding of His maya they do not see that they themselves have set out on the path of extreme heresy; how then could they bewilder Him with their various tricks?

### Verse 23

अथास्य सङ्गे जगदीश्वरस्य
व्रजन्तमेकं परिलोलचित्तम् ।
तं कृष्णदासाख्यममी विलोक्य
विलोभयाञ्चक्रुरतीवमन्दाः ॥२३॥

*athāsya saṅge jagad-īśvarasya*
*vrajantam ekaṁ parilola-cittam |*
*taṁ kṛṣṇadāsākhyam amī vilokya*
*vilobhayāñcakrur atīva-mandāḥ ||23||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *asya* — this; *saṅge* — in the company; *jagat* — of the world; *īśvarasya* — of the Lord; *vrajantam* — walking; *ekam* — one [man]; *parilola* — unsteady; *cittam* — [whose] mind [was]; *tam* — him; *kṛṣṇadāsa* — Krishnadasa; *ākhyam* — named; *amī* — they; *vilokya* — having seen; *vilobhayāñcakruḥ* — began to allure; *atīva* — extremely; *mandāḥ* — dull-witted.

**23.** Then those extremely dull-witted people saw a man of unsteady mind named Krishnadasa, who was walking in the company of the Lord of the world, and began to allure him.

*Note.* This is Kala Krishnadasa, the Lord's servant on the southern pilgrimage. In the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 9.226–231) he is lured away by the women of the Bhattatharis in Malara-desha, and the Lord rescues him.

### Verse 24

अरे कुतो गच्छसि दुःखमात्र-
साध्यं तदस्मासु कुरुष्व मैत्रीम् ।
ततस्त्वनेनैव शरीरकेण
स्वर्गं गमिष्यस्यथ नो विचारः ॥२४॥

*are kuto gacchasi duḥkha-mātra-*
*sādhyaṁ tad asmāsu kuruṣva maitrīm |*
*tatas tv anenaiva śarīrakeṇa*
*svargaṁ gamiṣyasy atha no vicāraḥ ||24||*

*Word for word:* *are* — hey; *kutaḥ* — where; *gacchasi* — are you going; *duḥkha* — suffering; *mātram* (ed. *mātra-*) — mere; *sādhyam* — to be gained; *tat* — therefore; *asmāsu* — with us; *kuruṣva* — make; *maitrīm* — friendship; *tataḥ* — then; *tu* — indeed; *anena eva* — in this very; *śarīrakeṇa* — little body; *svargam* — to heaven; *gamiṣyasi* — you will go; *atha* — and; *no* — no; *vicāraḥ* — doubt.

**24.** "Hey, where are you going? [There] only suffering is to be gained. So make friends with us, and then you will go to heaven in this very little body of yours — there is no doubt about it.

*Note.* In the edition *duḥkha-mātra-sādhyam* agrees with nothing; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *duḥkha-mātraṁ sādhyam*, "[there] only suffering is to be gained", and so we read.

### Verse 25

अस्त्येक एवात्र स कोऽपि पन्थाः
कियद्विदूरेऽखिललोकदुर्गः ।
तदेहि तेनैव पथा भवन्तं
संप्रापयिष्याम इतः खलु स्वः ॥२५॥

*asty eka evātra sa ko 'pi panthāḥ*
*kiyad-vidūre 'khila-loka-durgaḥ |*
*tad ehi tenaiva pathā bhavantaṁ*
*samprāpayiṣyāma itaḥ khalu svaḥ ||25||*

*Word for word:* *asti* — there is; *ekaḥ* — one; *eva* — indeed; *atra* — here; *saḥ kaḥ api* — a certain; *panthāḥ* — path; *kiyat* — a little; *vidūre* — at a distance; *akhila* — to all; *loka* — people; *durgaḥ* — inaccessible; *tat* — so; *ehi* — come; *tena eva* — by that very; *pathā* — path; *bhavantam* — you; *samprāpayiṣyāmaḥ* — we shall bring; *itaḥ* — from here; *khalu* — surely; *svaḥ* — to heaven.

**25.** There is a certain path here, a little way off, inaccessible to all people. So come: by that very path we shall surely bring you from here to heaven."

### Verse 26

इत्येष पाषण्डपथप्रविष्टै-
स्तैर्मोहितो दोलितचित्तवृत्तिः ।
शैथिल्यमीशस्य पथि प्रयाते
चकार किञ्चित् क्रमतो विमुग्धः ॥२६॥

*ity eṣa pāṣaṇḍa-patha-praviṣṭais*
*tair mohito dolita-citta-vṛttiḥ |*
*śaithilyam īśasya pathi prayāte*
*cakāra kiñcit kramato vimugdhaḥ ||26||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *eṣaḥ* — he; *pāṣaṇḍa* — of heresy; *patha* — upon the path; *praviṣṭaiḥ* — by those who had entered; *taiḥ* — by them; *mohitaḥ* — beguiled; *dolita* — swaying; *citta* — of mind; *vṛttiḥ* — [whose] disposition [was]; *śaithilyam* — slackness; *īśasya* — while the Lord; *pathi* — along the road; *prayāte* — went; *cakāra* — showed; *kiñcit* — somewhat; *kramataḥ* — gradually; *vimugdhaḥ* — bewildered.

**26.** Thus beguiled by those who had entered upon the path of heresy, his mind wavering, he grew bewildered and, as the Lord went along the road, gradually began to lag somewhat behind.

### Verse 27

प्रभुस्तदाज्ञाय दुरात्मभाजां
विचेष्टितं तस्य च लोलतां च ।
कृपैकसिन्धुर्जगदेकबन्धु-
र्दुराशयैस्तैरकरोद्विवादम् ॥२७॥

*prabhus tad ājñāya durātma-bhājāṁ*
*viceṣṭitaṁ tasya ca lolatāṁ ca |*
*kṛpaika-sindhur jagad-eka-bandhur*
*durāśayais tair akarod vivādam ||27||*

*Word for word:* *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *tat* — that; *ājñāya* — having perceived; *durātma* — wickedness; *bhājām* — of those possessing; *viceṣṭitam* — the machinations; *tasya* — his; *ca* — and; *lolatām* — fickleness; *ca* — and; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *eka* — the one; *sindhuḥ* — ocean; *jagat* — of the world; *eka* — the one; *bandhuḥ* — friend; *durāśayaiḥ* — with the evil-minded; *taiḥ* — with those; *akarot* — entered into; *vivādam* — a dispute.

**27.** Perceiving the machinations of those wicked people and his fickleness, the Lord — the one ocean of mercy, the one friend of the world — entered into a dispute with those evil-minded men.

### Verse 28

भो न्यासिनः किं मम दास एष
प्रलोभ्य बालः खलु नीयते क्व ।
नैतच्छिवं वो न च साधुचेष्टा
तत्त्यज्यतामेष विदूरमाध्वम् ॥२८॥

*bho nyāsinaḥ kiṁ mama dāsa eṣa*
*pralobhya bālaḥ khalu nīyate kva |*
*naitac chivaṁ vo na ca sādhu-ceṣṭā*
*tat tyajyatām eṣa vidūram ādhvam ||28||*

*Word for word:* *bho* — hey; *nyāsinaḥ* — O renunciants; *kim* — what [is this]; *mama* — My; *dāsaḥ* — servant; *eṣaḥ* — he; *pralobhya* — having enticed; *bālaḥ* — a boy; *khalu* — indeed; *nīyate* — is being led; *kva* — where; *na* — not; *etat* — this; *śivam* — good; *vaḥ* — for you; *na ca* — nor; *sādhu* — of the virtuous; *ceṣṭā* — the conduct; *tat* — so; *tyajyatām* — let [him] be left; *eṣaḥ* — he; *vidūram* — far away; *ādhvam* — stay.

**28.** "Hey, renunciants, what is this? He is My servant, a mere boy — where are you leading him, having enticed him? This bodes no good for you, nor is it the conduct of the virtuous. So leave him and keep far away!"

*Note.* *Ādhvam* is the imperative, second person plural, of *ās*, "to sit, to stay".

### Verse 29

इत्थं विवादी न चिरं कृतेन
कथं कथञ्चिद्विमुखीचकार ।
निजप्रभावेन कृपामयाब्धि-
स्तं सुप्रसन्ने हि विधौ तथा स्यात् ॥२९॥

*itthaṁ vivādī na ciraṁ kṛtena*
*kathaṁ kathañcid vimukhīcakāra |*
*nija-prabhāvena kṛpāmayābdhis*
*taṁ suprasanne hi vidhau tathā syāt ||29||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *vivādī* — disputing; *na ciram* — not long; *kṛtena* — by what was done (?); *katham kathañcit* — somehow or other; *vimukhīcakāra* — turned away; *nija* — by His own; *prabhāvena* — power; *kṛpā-maya* — of mercy; *abdhiḥ* — the ocean; *tam* — him; *su-prasanne* — when well pleased; *hi* — for; *vidhau* — destiny; *tathā* — so; *syāt* — it happens.

**29.** Thus, after disputing for no long time, the ocean of mercy by His own power somehow or other turned him away [from them]; for so it happens when destiny is well pleased.

*Note.* *Tam* is singular, so Krishnadasa is meant, not the heretics (?). The syntax of *na ciraṁ kṛtena* is unclear. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 30

इत्थं विलोक्यापथवर्तिनस्तत्
कुचेष्टितं किञ्चिदसौ विहस्य ।
न किञ्चिदूचे खलु कृष्णदासं
सेतुं समुद्दिश्य ततो जगाम ॥३०॥

*itthaṁ vilokyāpatha-vartinas tat*
*kuceṣṭitaṁ kiñcid asau vihasya |*
*na kiñcid ūce khalu kṛṣṇadāsaṁ*
*setuṁ samuddiśya tato jagāma ||30||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *vilokya* — having seen; *apatha* — on the wrong road; *vartinaḥ* — of the one standing; *tat* — that; *kuceṣṭitam* — misconduct; *kiñcit* — slightly; *asau* — He; *vihasya* — smiling; *na* — not; *kiñcit* — anything; *ūce* — said; *khalu* — at all; *kṛṣṇadāsam* — to Krishnadasa; *setum* — the Setu; *samuddiśya* — heading for; *tataḥ* — from there; *jagāma* — went.

**30.** Seeing such misconduct on the part of the one who had strayed from the road, He only smiled slightly, said nothing at all to Krishnadasa, and went on from there, heading for the Setu.

### Verse 31

पथि प्रभुः स्वैर्गुणनामधेयै-
र्निरन्तरं कीर्तनमेव कृत्वा ।
प्रेमाश्रुभिर्धौतसमस्तदेह-
श्चकार पूतामटवीं समस्ताम् ॥३१॥

*pathi prabhuḥ svair guṇa-nāmadheyair*
*nirantaraṁ kīrtanam eva kṛtvā |*
*premāśrubhir dhauta-samasta-dehaś*
*cakāra pūtām aṭavīṁ samastām ||31||*

*Word for word:* *pathi* — on the way; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *svaiḥ* — of His own; *guṇa* — qualities; *nāmadheyaiḥ* — [and] names; *nirantaram* — unceasingly; *kīrtanam* — kirtana; *eva* — indeed; *kṛtvā* — performing; *prema* — of love; *aśrubhiḥ* — by tears; *dhauta* — washed; *samasta* — whole; *dehaḥ* — [whose] body [was]; *cakāra* — made; *pūtām* — purified; *aṭavīm* — the forest; *samastām* — whole.

**31.** On the way the Lord unceasingly performed kirtana of His own qualities and names; His whole body washed by tears of love, He purified the whole forest.

### Verse 32

एवं स सेतुं प्रययौ कृपालुः
कृपापरिप्लावितसर्वदेशः ।
रामेश्वरं रामसमर्हितं तं
दृष्ट्वा ननाम स्तवमप्यकार्षीत् ॥३२॥

*evaṁ sa setuṁ prayayau kṛpāluḥ*
*kṛpā-pariplāvita-sarva-deśaḥ |*
*rāmeśvaraṁ rāma-samarhitaṁ taṁ*
*dṛṣṭvā nanāma stavam apy akārṣīt ||32||*

*Word for word:* *evam* — thus; *saḥ* — He; *setum* — to the Setu; *prayayau* — came; *kṛpāluḥ* — the Merciful One; *kṛpā* — with mercy; *pariplāvita* — flooded; *sarva* — all; *deśaḥ* — [by whom] the lands [were]; *rāmeśvaram* — Rameshvara; *rāma* — by Rama; *samarhitam* — worshipped; *tam* — that; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *nanāma* — bowed down; *stavam* — a hymn; *api* — also; *akārṣīt* — offered.

**32.** Thus the Merciful One, who had flooded all the lands with mercy, came to the Setu. Seeing that Rameshvara worshipped by Rama, He bowed down and offered a hymn as well.

*Note.* Rameshvara is the Shiva-linga that, according to tradition, Rama worshipped before His campaign against Lanka.

### Verse 33

विलोक्य सेतुं रघुनाथकीर्तिं
सेतोस्ततः श्रीमयगौरचन्द्रः ।
निवर्तितुं तत्र कृपासमुद्र-
श्चकार चित्तं परमप्रभावः ॥३३॥

*vilokya setuṁ raghunātha-kīrtiṁ*
*setos tataḥ śrīmaya-gauracandraḥ |*
*nivartituṁ tatra kṛpā-samudraś*
*cakāra cittaṁ parama-prabhāvaḥ ||33||*

*Word for word:* *vilokya* — having seen; *setum* — the Setu; *raghunātha* — of Raghunatha; *kīrtim* — the glory; *setoḥ* — from the Setu; *tataḥ* — then; *śrī-maya* — full of beauty; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra; *nivartitum* — to turn back; *tatra* — there; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *samudraḥ* — the ocean; *cakāra cittam* — resolved; *parama* — supreme; *prabhāvaḥ* — [whose] power [is].

**33.** Having seen the Setu, the glory of Raghunatha, the beautiful Gaurachandra, the ocean of mercy, whose power is supreme, then resolved there to turn back from the Setu.

### Verse 34

स तेन तेनैव पथा विलोक्य
श्रीरङ्गदेवं पुनरार्द्रचित्तः ।
गोदावरीमेत्य तथैव रामा-
नन्दस्य सन्दर्शनमेष चक्रे ॥३४॥

*sa tena tenaiva pathā vilokya*
*śrī-raṅga-devaṁ punar ārdra-cittaḥ |*
*godāvarīm etya tathaiva rāmā-*
*nandasya sandarśanam eṣa cakre ||34||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — He; *tena tena eva* — by that very same; *pathā* — road; *vilokya* — having seen; *śrī-raṅga-devam* — the Deity Sri Ranga; *punaḥ* — again; *ārdra* — melted; *cittaḥ* — [whose] heart [was]; *godāvarīm* — to the Godavari; *etya* — having come; *tathā eva* — likewise; *rāmānandasya* — of Ramananda; *sandarśanam* — a meeting; *eṣaḥ* — He; *cakre* — had.

**34.** [Returning] by that very same road, He saw the Deity Sri Ranga again, His heart melting; and, having come to the Godavari, He likewise had a meeting with Ramananda.

*Note.* Whether *tathaiva*, "likewise", implies that a meeting had already taken place on the way south (contrary to 12.131: *na taṁ vilokyaiva*) is not clear from the text (?). More probably *tathaiva* simply means "likewise [as He had seen Sri Ranga]". The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 35

उपेत्य गोदावरिकां स नाथः
प्रमोदतस्तत्परिलोचनाय ।
जगाम तद्वेश्मनि शीतरश्मि-
रिवोदयाद्रिं जलदागमान्ते ॥३५॥

*upetya godāvarikāṁ sa nāthaḥ*
*pramodatas tat-parilocanāya |*
*jagāma tad-veśmani śīta-raśmir*
*ivodayādriṁ jaladāgamānte ||35||*

*Word for word:* *upetya* — having approached; *godāvarikām* — the Godavari; *saḥ* — He; *nāthaḥ* — the Master; *pramodataḥ* — joyfully; *tat* — him; *parilocanāya* — in order to see; *jagāma* — went; *tat* — his; *veśmani* — to the house; *śīta-raśmiḥ* — the moon; *iva* — like; *udaya-adrim* — to the Mountain of Rising; *jalada* — of the clouds; *āgama* — of the coming; *ante* — at the end.

**35.** Having come to the Godavari, the Master joyfully went to [Ramananda's] house to see him — like the moon [going] to the Mountain of Rising at the end of the season of clouds.

### Verse 36

विलोक्य नाथं स तु कृष्णचित्तो
ननाम हर्षाद्भुवि संनिपत्य ।
अनन्तरे कोटिगुणप्रवृद्धा-
माह्लादलक्ष्मीमुदितां बभार ॥३६॥

*vilokya nāthaṁ sa tu kṛṣṇa-citto*
*nanāma harṣād bhuvi saṁnipatya |*
*anantare koṭi-guṇa-pravṛddhām*
*āhlāda-lakṣmīm uditāṁ babhāra ||36||*

*Word for word:* *vilokya* — having seen; *nātham* — the Master; *saḥ tu* — he, for his part; *kṛṣṇa* — [absorbed] in Krishna; *cittaḥ* — [whose] mind [was]; *nanāma* — bowed down; *harṣāt* — out of joy; *bhuvi* — to the ground; *saṁnipatya* — having fallen; *anantare* — thereupon; *koṭi-guṇa* — ten-millionfold; *pravṛddhām* — increased; *āhlāda* — of delight; *lakṣmīm* — the wealth; *uditām* — arisen; *babhāra* — bore.

**36.** And he, whose mind was [absorbed] in Krishna, seeing the Master, fell to the ground out of joy and bowed down. Thereupon he bore a wealth of delight that had arisen [in him], increased ten-millionfold.

*Note.* In the edition the verse number lacks the second danda: *॥३६*.

### Verse 37

ईशस्तु तद्दर्शनमात्रतोऽसौ
द्रुतोऽभवच्चेतसि हर्षभारैः ।
अथोपरिष्टाज्जगदेककान्ति-
र्बभ्राज कन्दर्पसमूहकम्रः ॥३७॥

*īśas tu tad-darśana-mātrato 'sau*
*druto 'bhavac cetasi harṣa-bhāraiḥ |*
*athopariṣṭāj jagad-eka-kāntir*
*babhrāja kandarpa-samūha-kamraḥ ||37||*

*Word for word:* *īśaḥ* — the Lord; *tu* — and; *tat* — of him; *darśana* — by the sight; *mātrataḥ* — merely; *asau* — He; *drutaḥ* — melted; *abhavat* — became; *cetasi* — in heart; *harṣa* — of joy; *bhāraiḥ* — by the weight; *atha* — then; *upariṣṭāt* — above (on a raised [seat]); *jagat* — of the world; *eka* — the sole; *kāntiḥ* — beauty; *babhrāja* — shone; *kandarpa* — of Kandarpas; *samūha* — [like] a host; *kamraḥ* — lovely.

**37.** And the Lord, at the mere sight of him, melted in heart under the weight of joy. Then He, the sole beauty of the world, lovely as a host of Kandarpas, shone forth on a raised [seat].

### Verse 38

उवाच किञ्चित् स्तनयित्नुधीरं
सकैतवं भोः कवितां पठेति ।
तदा तदाकर्ण्य महारसज्ञः
पपाठ वैराग्यरसाढ्यपद्यम् ॥३८॥

*uvāca kiñcit stanayitnu-dhīraṁ*
*sakaitavaṁ bhoḥ kavitāṁ paṭheti |*
*tadā tad ākarṇya mahā-rasajñaḥ*
*papāṭha vairāgya-rasāḍhya-padyam ||38||*

*Word for word:* *uvāca* — said; *kiñcit* — a little; *stanayitnu* — like thunder; *dhīram* — deep; *sa-kaitavam* — with guile; *bhoḥ* — O [friend]; *kavitām* — poetry; *paṭha* — recite; *iti* — thus; *tadā* — then; *tat* — that; *ākarṇya* — having heard; *mahā* — the great; *rasa-jñaḥ* — knower of rasa; *papāṭha* — recited; *vairāgya* — of renunciation; *rasa* — in the flavour; *āḍhya* — rich; *padyam* — a verse.

**38.** In a voice deep as thunder, and with guile, He said a few words: "O [friend], recite some poetry!" Hearing that, the great knower of rasa recited a verse rich in the flavour of renunciation.

*Note.* The edition clearly has *सकैतवं*, "with guile", that is, to test him. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 39

वैराग्यं चेज्जनयतितरां पापमेवास्तु यस्मात्
सान्द्रं रागं जनयति न चेत् पुण्यमस्मासु भूयात् ।
वैराग्येण प्रमुदितमनोवृत्तिरभ्येति रागं
रागेण स्त्रीजठरकुहरे ताम्यति ब्राह्मणोऽपि ॥३९॥

*vairāgyaṁ cej janayatitarāṁ pāpam evāstu yasmāt*
*sāndraṁ rāgaṁ janayati na cet puṇyam asmāsu bhūyāt |*
*vairāgyeṇa pramudita-mano-vṛttir abhyeti rāgaṁ*
*rāgeṇa strī-jaṭhara-kuhare tāmyati brāhmaṇo 'pi ||39||*
