*Word for word:* *vairāgyam* — renunciation; *cet* — if; *janayatitarām* — produces abundantly; *pāpam* — sin; *eva* — even; *astu* — let it be; *yasmāt* — from which; *sāndram* — dense; *rāgam* — attachment; *janayati* — produces; *na cet* — if not; *puṇyam* — merit; *asmāsu* — in us; *bhūyāt* — may there be; *vairāgyeṇa* — by renunciation; *pramudita* — gladdened; *manaḥ* — of the mind; *vṛttiḥ* — [one whose] disposition [is]; *abhyeti* — comes; *rāgam* — to attachment; *rāgeṇa* — through attachment; *strī* — of a woman; *jaṭhara* — of the womb; *kuhare* — in the hollow; *tāmyati* — languishes; *brāhmaṇaḥ* — a brahmana; *api* — even.

**39.** "If [a thing] abundantly produces renunciation, let it be even sin; may merit be ours [only] if dense attachment does not arise from it. Through renunciation the mind is gladdened; [but if one] comes to attachment, then through attachment even a brahmana languishes in the hollow of a woman's womb."

*Note.* Metre *mandākrāntā*. The rendering of the syntax is conjectural (?); the second half might also be construed "one whose mind is gladdened by renunciation comes to *rāga*", with *rāga* in the third pada understood as love [for the Lord], in contrast to the worldly *rāga* of the fourth (?). The sense: better a sin that leads to renunciation than a merit that breeds attachment, for attachment leads to a new birth. This is the first, "external" stage of the conversation; cf. the stages in the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 8.57–67): varnashrama, offering the fruits of action, giving up one's own dharma, devotion mixed with knowledge — each of which the Lord calls "external". The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 40

इतीदमाकर्ण्य स गौरचन्द्रो
बाह्यातिबाह्यं बत बाह्यमेतत् ।
इति स्फुरद्वाग्विभवोत्थतापोद्-
गमान्तकृन्नातिमुदं प्रपेदे ॥४०॥

*itīdam ākarṇya sa gauracandro*
*bāhyāti-bāhyaṁ bata bāhyam etat |*
*iti sphurad-vāg-vibhavottha-tāpod-*
*gamānta-kṛn nāti-mudaṁ prapede ||40||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *idam* — this; *ākarṇya* — having heard; *saḥ* — He; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra; *bāhya* — external; *ati-bāhyam* — exceedingly external; *bata* — alas; *bāhyam* — external; *etat* — this [is]; *iti* — thus [saying]; *sphurat* — flashing; *vāk* — of eloquence; *vibhava* — from the wealth; *uttha* — arisen; *tāpa* — of heat; *udgama* — to the rising; *anta* — an end; *kṛt* — making; *na* — not; *ati* — great; *mudam* — joy; *prapede* — attained.

**40.** Hearing this, Gaurachandra [said]: "This is external — external, exceedingly external, alas, external!" And He who puts an end to the rising of the heat born of the wealth of flashing eloquence did not attain great joy.

*Note.* The compound in the third and fourth padas is unclear (?). Cf. the famous *eho bāhya, āge kaha āra* ("this is external; speak further"), Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 8.59–66, where the Lord repeats this after each of Ramananda's answers. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 41

ततश्च संशुद्धमतिः स रामा-
नन्दो महानन्दपरिप्लुताङ्गः ।
पपाठ भक्तेः प्रतिपादयित्री-
मेकान्तकान्तां कवितां स्वकीयाम् ॥४१॥

*tataś ca saṁśuddha-matiḥ sa rāmā-*
*nando mahānanda-pariplutāṅgaḥ |*
*papāṭha bhakteḥ pratipādayitrīm*
*ekānta-kāntāṁ kavitāṁ svakīyām ||41||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ ca* — and then; *saṁśuddha* — purified; *matiḥ* — [whose] mind [was]; *saḥ* — that; *rāmānandaḥ* — Ramananda; *mahā* — by great; *ānanda* — bliss; *paripluta* — flooded; *aṅgaḥ* — [whose] body [was]; *papāṭha* — recited; *bhakteḥ* — bhakti; *pratipādayitrīm* — setting forth; *ekānta* — wholly; *kāntām* — lovely; *kavitām* — a poem; *svakīyām* — his own.

**41.** And then Ramananda, his mind purified, his body flooded with great bliss, recited a wholly lovely poem of his own that sets forth bhakti.

### Verse 42

नानोपचारकृतपूजनमार्तबन्धोः
प्रेम्णैव भक्तहृदयं सुखविद्रुतं स्यात् ।
यावत् क्षुदस्ति जठरे जरठा पिपासा
तावत् सुखाय भवतो ननु भक्ष्यपेये ॥४२॥

*nānopacāra-kṛta-pūjanam ārta-bandhoḥ*
*premṇaiva bhakta-hṛdayaṁ sukha-vidrutaṁ syāt |*
*yāvat kṣud asti jaṭhare jaraṭhā pipāsā*
*tāvat sukhāya bhavato nanu bhakṣya-peye ||42||*

*Word for word:* *nānā* — with various; *upacāra* — offerings; *kṛta* — performed; *pūjanam* — the worship; *ārta* — of the afflicted; *bandhoḥ* — of the Friend; *premṇā* — by love; *eva* — only; *bhakta* — of the devotee; *hṛdayam* — the heart; *sukha* — with happiness; *vidrutam* — melted; *syāt* — becomes; *yāvat* — as long as; *kṣut* — hunger; *asti* — there is; *jaṭhare* — in the stomach; *jaraṭhā* — keen; *pipāsā* — thirst; *tāvat* — so long; *sukhāya* — for pleasure; *bhavataḥ* — are; *nanu* — indeed; *bhakṣya* — food; *peye* — and drink.

**42.** "Worship of the Friend of the afflicted performed with various offerings — [in it] the devotee's heart melts with happiness only through love. For as long as there is hunger in the stomach and keen thirst, just so long do food and drink give pleasure."

*Note.* Metre *vasantatilakā*. In the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 8.70) this stanza is quoted by Ramananda; it is also found in Rupa Gosvami's *Padyavali* (13). Karnapura calls it Ramananda's own stanza (*svakīyām*, v. 41).

### Verse 43

इत्थं च संश्रुत्य तथैव बाह्यं
बाह्यं तदेतच्च परं पठेति ।
जगाद नाथोऽथ कचैः सुदीर्घैः
संवेष्ट्य नाथस्य पदौ पपात ॥४३॥

*itthaṁ ca saṁśrutya tathaiva bāhyaṁ*
*bāhyaṁ tad etac ca paraṁ paṭheti |*
*jagāda nātho 'tha kacaiḥ sudīrghaiḥ*
*saṁveṣṭya nāthasya padau papāta ||43||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — this; *ca* — and; *saṁśrutya* — having heard; *tathā eva* — likewise; *bāhyam* — external; *bāhyam* — external; *tat etat* — this here; *ca* — too; *param* — further; *paṭha* — recite; *iti* — thus; *jagāda* — said; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *atha* — then; *kacaiḥ* — with [his] hair; *sudīrghaiḥ* — very long; *saṁveṣṭya* — having entwined; *nāthasya* — of the Lord; *padau* — the feet; *papāta* — fell.

**43.** Having heard this too, the Lord said likewise: "External — this too is external! Recite further." Then [Ramananda] fell [at His feet], entwining the Lord's feet with his very long hair.

### Verse 44

निकामसम्मोहभरालसाङ्गो
गाङ्गेयगौरं तमनङ्गरम्यम् ।
प्रभुं प्रणम्याथ पदाब्जमूले
निपत्य संप्रोत्थित आननन्द ॥४४॥

*nikāma-sammoha-bharālasāṅgo*
*gāṅgeya-gauraṁ tam anaṅga-ramyam |*
*prabhuṁ praṇamyātha padābja-mūle*
*nipatya samprotthita ānananda ||44||*

*Word for word:* *nikāma* — of intense; *sammoha* — bewilderment; *bhara* — under the weight; *alasa* — languid; *aṅgaḥ* — [whose] body [was]; *gāṅgeya* — like gold; *gauram* — golden; *tam* — to Him; *anaṅga* — like Ananga; *ramyam* — charming; *prabhum* — to the Lord; *praṇamya* — having bowed; *atha* — then; *pada* — of the feet; *abja* — of the lotuses; *mūle* — at the base; *nipatya* — having fallen; *samprotthitaḥ* — having risen; *ānananda* — rejoiced.

**44.** His body languid under the weight of deep bewilderment, he bowed to the Lord — golden as gold, charming as Ananga — then fell at the base of His lotus feet, rose, and rejoiced.

*Note.* *Gāṅgeya* ("born of the Ganga") is gold.

### Verse 45

ततः स गीतं सरसालिपीतं
विदग्धयोर्नागरयोः परस्य ।
प्रेम्णोऽतिकाष्ठाप्रतिपादनेन
द्वयोः परैक्यप्रतिपाद्यवादीत् ॥४५॥

*tataḥ sa gītaṁ sarasāli-pītaṁ*
*vidagdhayor nāgarayoḥ parasya |*
*premṇo 'tikāṣṭhā-pratipādanena*
*dvayoḥ paraikya-pratipādy avādīt ||45||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *saḥ* — he; *gītam* — a song; *sa-rasa* — who relish rasa; *āli* — by the [female] friends; *pītam* — drunk in; *vidagdhayoḥ* — of the two clever; *nāgarayoḥ* — lovers; *parasya* — of the supreme; *premṇaḥ* — of love; *ati-kāṣṭhā* — the utmost limit; *pratipādanena* — by setting forth; *dvayoḥ* — of the Two; *para* — the supreme; *aikya* — oneness; *pratipādi* — setting forth; *avādīt* — sang.

**45.** Then he sang a song which the sakhis who relish rasa drink in. By setting forth the utmost limit of the supreme love of the two clever lovers, it sets forth the supreme oneness of the Two.

*Note.* "The oneness of the Two" — cf. *prema-vilāsa-vivarta* in the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 8.192–194; 8.190–193 in the numbering of the project's edition), the summit of the conversation with Ramananda.

### Verse 46

॥ भैरवी रागः ॥
पहिलहि राग नयनभङ्ग भेल ।
अनुदिन बाढ़ल अवधि ना गेल ॥
ना सो रमण ना हाम रमणी ।
दुँहु मन मनोभव पेशल जानि ॥
ए सखि सो सब प्रेमकाहिनी ।
कानुठामे कहवि विछुरल जानि ॥
ना खोजलुँ दूती ना खोजलुँ आन ।
दुँहुकेरि मिलने मधत पाँचबाण ॥
अब सोइ विराग तुँहु भेलि दूती ।
सुपुरुखप्रेमक ऐछन रीति ॥
वर्द्धनरुद्र नराधिपमान ।
रामानन्दराय कवि भाण ॥४६॥

*|| bhairavī rāgaḥ ||*
*pahilahi rāga nayana-bhaṅga bhela |*
*anudina bāḍhala avadhi nā gela ||*
*nā so ramaṇa nā hāma ramaṇī |*
*duṅhu mana manobhava peśala jāni ||*
*e sakhi so saba prema-kāhinī |*
*kānu-ṭhāme kahavi vichurala jāni ||*
*nā khojaluṅ dūtī nā khojaluṅ āna |*
*duṅhu-keri milane madhata pāṅca-bāṇa ||*
*aba soi virāga tuṅhu bheli dūtī |*
*supurukha-premaka aichana rīti ||*
*vardhana-rudra narādhipa-māna |*
*rāmānanda-rāya kavi bhāṇa ||46||*

*Word for word:* (Brajabuli, the poetic language of Bengal): *pahilahi* — at first; *rāga* — attraction; *nayana* — of the eyes; *bhaṅga* — from the play; *bhela* — arose; *anudina* — day by day; *bāḍhala* — grew; *avadhi* — a limit; *nā gela* — did not reach; *nā* — not; *so* — he; *ramaṇa* — the lover; *nā* — not; *hāma* — I; *ramaṇī* — the beloved; *duṅhu* — of both; *mana* — the minds; *manobhava* — Manobhava (the god of love); *peśala* (*peṣala*) — ground [into one]; *jāni* — I know; *e sakhi* — O friend; *so saba* — all this; *prema* — of love; *kāhinī* — tale; *kānu-ṭhāme* — to Kanu (Krishna); *kahavi* — tell; *vichurala* — one who has forgotten; *jāni* — as; *nā khojaluṅ* — I did not seek; *dūtī* — a messenger; *nā khojaluṅ* — I did not seek; *āna* — anyone else; *duṅhu-keri* — of us two; *milane* — in the meeting; *madhata* (*madhya ta*) — the go-between indeed; *pāṅca-bāṇa* — the Five-Arrowed one; *aba* — now; *soi* — that very; *virāga* — estrangement; *tuṅhu* — you; *bheli* — have become; *dūtī* — the messenger; *supurukha* — for a worthy man; *premaka* — of love; *aichana* — such; *rīti* — the way; *vardhana* — may [it] increase; *rudra* — of Rudra; *narādhipa* — of the king; *māna* — the honour (?); *rāmānanda-rāya* — Ramananda Raya; *kavi* — the poet; *bhāṇa* — says.

**46.** (Raga *bhairavī*.)
At first attraction arose from the play of glances;
day by day it grew and knew no limit.
He is not the lover, nor am I the beloved:
the god of love ground our two minds into one — this I know.
O friend, all this tale of love
tell to Kanu, as to one who has forgotten.
I sought no messenger, I sought no one else:
the go-between at our meeting was the Five-Arrowed one.
And now, with that estrangement, you have become the messenger —
such is the way of love for a worthy man.
May the honour of King Rudra increase! —
so says the poet Ramananda Raya.

*Note.* This song is quoted in the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 8.194; 8.193 in the numbering of the project's edition), but without the last couplet, the poet's signature (*bhaṇitā*): there it ends with the line about the messenger. Readings of the edition: *पेशल* (the Chaitanya-charitamrita has *peṣala*, "ground"), *मधत* (= *madhya ta*). The signature line is understood tentatively. "King Rudra" is apparently Prataparudra, the king of Orissa, under whom Ramananda served as governor.

### Verse 47

ततस्तदाकर्ण्य परात्परं स
प्रभुः प्रफुल्लेक्षणपद्मयुग्मः ।
प्रेमप्रभावप्रचलान्तरात्मा
गाढप्रमोदात्तमथालिलिङ्ग ॥४७॥

*tatas tad ākarṇya parāt-paraṁ sa*
*prabhuḥ praphullekṣaṇa-padma-yugmaḥ |*
*prema-prabhāva-pracalāntar-ātmā*
*gāḍha-pramodāt tam athāliliṅga ||47||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *tat* — that; *ākarṇya* — having heard; *parāt-param* — higher than the highest; *saḥ* — He; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *praphulla* — opened wide; *īkṣaṇa* — of the eyes; *padma* — of the lotuses; *yugmaḥ* — [whose] pair [was]; *prema* — of love; *prabhāva* — by the power; *pracala* — stirred; *antaḥ-ātmā* — [whose] inmost self [was]; *gāḍha* — deep; *pramodāt* — out of joy; *tam* — him; *atha* — then; *āliliṅga* — embraced.

**47.** Then, having heard that [song], higher than the highest, the Lord — the pair of His lotus eyes opened wide, His inmost self stirred by the power of love — embraced him in deep joy.

### Verse 48

इत्थं दृढाश्लेषकलाकलाप-
कल्लोललोलान्तरयोः स कोऽपि ।
कालस्तदासीत् सुखसागरोर्मि-
कदम्बकैः पर्वतया परीतः ॥४८॥

*itthaṁ dṛḍhāśleṣa-kalā-kalāpa-*
*kallola-lolāntarayoḥ sa ko 'pi |*
*kālas tadāsīt sukha-sāgarormi-*
*kadambakaiḥ parvatayā parītaḥ ||48||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *dṛḍha* — of firm; *āśleṣa* — embrace; *kalā* — of the arts; *kalāpa* — of the multitude; *kallola* — by the billows; *lola* — tossed; *antarayoḥ* — for the two whose hearts [were]; *saḥ kaḥ api* — some indescribable; *kālaḥ* — time; *tadā* — then; *āsīt* — was; *sukha* — of happiness; *sāgara* — of the ocean; *ūrmi* — of waves; *kadambakaiḥ* — with masses; *parvatayā* — with festivity; *parītaḥ* — pervaded.

**48.** Thus, for the two whose hearts were tossed by the billows of the manifold arts of firm embrace, that time became something indescribable — pervaded with festivity, with masses of waves of the ocean of happiness.

*Note.* The edition has *दृढाश्लेषकला कलाप-*; the space is erroneous. *Parvatā* — "festivity" (from *parvan*, "festival").

### Verse 49

इति स्वभावप्रणयामृतेन
चिराद्गतेनानुभवस्य वर्त्म ।
संभाष्य तं कत्यपि वासरान् स
नीत्वा जगन्नाथदिदृक्षुरासीत् ॥४९॥

*iti svabhāva-praṇayāmṛtena*
*cirād gatenānubhavasya vartma |*
*saṁbhāṣya taṁ katy api vāsarān sa*
*nītvā jagannātha-didṛkṣur āsīt ||49||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *svabhāva* — natural; *praṇaya* — of love; *amṛtena* — with the nectar; *cirāt* — long since; *gatena* — come; *anubhavasya* — of realisation; *vartma* — the path; *saṁbhāṣya* — having discussed; *tam* — with him; *kati api* — some; *vāsarān* — days; *saḥ* — He; *nītvā* — having spent; *jagannātha* — Jagannatha; *didṛkṣuḥ* — eager to see; *āsīt* — became.

**49.** Thus, with the nectar of a natural love that had come down from long ago, He discussed with him the path of realisation; and having spent some days [there], He became eager to see Jagannatha.

*Note.* In the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 8) the conversation lasts ten days and takes place on the way south. On the return journey (Madhya 9.328–335) the Lord again spends a night in conversation with Ramananda, and Ramananda, having written to the king asking to be relieved of his post, prepares to follow Him to Puri.

### Verse 50

अथाययौ क्षेत्रमदभ्रभूषं
श्रमापहं गौरसुधामयूखः ।
पूर्वं ततः स्नानमहोत्सवस्य
ददर्श नीलाचलमौलिरत्नम् ॥५०॥

*athāyayau kṣetram adabhra-bhūṣaṁ*
*śramāpahaṁ gaura-sudhā-mayūkhaḥ |*
*pūrvaṁ tataḥ snāna-mahotsavasya*
*dadarśa nīlācala-mauli-ratnam ||50||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *āyayau* — came; *kṣetram* — to the Kshetra; *adabhra* — richly; *bhūṣam* — adorned; *śrama* — weariness; *apaham* — removing; *gaura* — the golden; *sudhā-mayūkhaḥ* — nectar-rayed [moon]; *pūrvam* — before; *tataḥ* — then; *snāna* — of the bathing; *mahā-utsavasya* — the great festival; *dadarśa* — saw; *nīlācala* — of Nilachala; *mauli* — of the crown; *ratnam* — the jewel.

**50.** Then the golden nectar-rayed moon came to the Kshetra, richly adorned and removing [all] weariness; and then, before the great bathing festival, He beheld the jewel in the crown of Nilachala.

*Note.* The bathing festival is the Snana-yatra of Jagannatha. "The jewel in the crown of Nilachala" is Jagannatha.

### Verse 51

नीलाचले प्रोद्यति गौरचन्द्रे
पयोनिधिः पूरमुवाह तुङ्गम् ।
जनाश्च विध्वस्तशुगन्धकारा
बभूवुरुत्फुल्लदृगुत्पलान्ताः ॥५१॥

*nīlācale prodyati gauracandre*
*payonidhiḥ pūram uvāha tuṅgam |*
*janāś ca vidhvasta-śug-andhakārā*
*babhūvur utphulla-dṛg-utpalāntāḥ ||51||*

*Word for word:* *nīlācale* — over Nilachala; *prodyati* — when rising; *gauracandre* — Gaurachandra; *payaḥ-nidhiḥ* — the ocean; *pūram* — a tide; *uvāha* — raised; *tuṅgam* — high; *janāḥ* — the people; *ca* — and; *vidhvasta* — dispelled; *śuk* — of grief; *andhakārāḥ* — [whose] darkness [was]; *babhūvuḥ* — became; *utphulla* — blossomed; *dṛk* — of the eyes; *utpala* — of the lotuses; *antāḥ* — [whose] corners [were].

**51.** When Gaurachandra rose over Nilachala, the ocean raised a high tide; and the people, the darkness of their grief dispelled, had the lotuses of their eyes blossoming to their corners.

*Note.* The image rests on poetic conventions about the moon: its rising swells the tide of the ocean, dispels darkness and opens the night-blooming lotuses (*utpala*).

### Verse 52

केचिज्जगन्नाथविलोकनाच्च
केचित् प्रणामादथ पूजनाच्च ।
प्रदक्षिणात् केचन सेवनाच्च
सर्वे समं तत्सविधं समीयुः ॥५२॥

*kecij jagannātha-vilokanāc ca*
*kecit praṇāmād atha pūjanāc ca |*
*pradakṣiṇāt kecana sevanāc ca*
*sarve samaṁ tat-savidhaṁ samīyuḥ ||52||*

*Word for word:* *kecit* — some; *jagannātha* — of Jagannatha; *vilokanāt* — from beholding; *ca* — and; *kecit* — some; *praṇāmāt* — from bowing down; *atha* — and; *pūjanāt* — from worship; *ca* — and; *pradakṣiṇāt* — from circumambulation; *kecana* — others; *sevanāt* — from service; *ca* — and; *sarve* — all; *samam* — together; *tat* — Him; *savidham* — close to; *samīyuḥ* — gathered.

**52.** Some from beholding Jagannatha, some from bowing down and worship, others from circumambulation and service — all together gathered close around Him.

### Verse 53

प्रभुश्च कांश्चिद्धसितेन कांश्चित्
विलोकनेन स्मितसादरेण ।
कांश्चित् समाश्लेषरसेन सर्वान्
मनोरथैः फुल्लहृदश्चकार ॥५३॥

*prabhuś ca kāṁścid dhasitena kāṁścit*
*vilokanena smita-sādareṇa |*
*kāṁścit samāśleṣa-rasena sarvān*
*manorathaiḥ phulla-hṛdaś cakāra ||53||*

*Word for word:* *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *ca* — and; *kāṁścit* — some; *hasitena* — with laughter; *kāṁścit* — some; *vilokanena* — with a glance; *smita* — with a smile; *sādareṇa* — affectionate; *kāṁścit* — others; *samāśleṣa* — of embrace; *rasena* — with the sweetness; *sarvān* — all; *manorathaiḥ* — by [the fulfilment of their] desires; *phulla* — blossoming; *hṛdaḥ* — [having] hearts; *cakāra* — made.

**53.** And the Lord — some with laughter, some with an affectionate, smiling glance, others with the sweetness of His embrace — made the hearts of all blossom with [the fulfilment of their] desires.

*Note.* The edition has no sandhi before *vilokanena* (*kāṁścit vilokanena*).

### Verse 54

अथैष नाथः पुरतो ह्यमीषां
साक्षित्वमाधाय च कृष्णदासम् ।
तत् क्षेत्रमानीतमतिप्रयत्ना-
द्गच्छेति सम्यग्विससर्ज तत्र ॥५४॥

*athaiṣa nāthaḥ purato hy amīṣāṁ*
*sākṣitvam ādhāya ca kṛṣṇadāsam |*
*tat kṣetram ānītam ati-prayatnād*
*gaccheti samyag visasarja tatra ||54||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *eṣaḥ* — He; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *purataḥ* — in front; *hi* — indeed; *amīṣām* — of them; *sākṣitvam* — the role of witnesses; *ādhāya* — having assigned; *ca* — and; *kṛṣṇadāsam* — to Krishnadasa; *tat* — to that; *kṣetram* — Kshetra; *ānītam* — brought; *ati-prayatnāt* — with great effort; *gaccha* — go; *iti* — thus [saying]; *samyak* — for good; *visasarja* — dismissed; *tatra* — there.

**54.** Then the Lord, in front of them, having made [them] witnesses, said "Go!" to Krishnadasa, whom He had brought to that Kshetra with great effort, and there dismissed him for good.

*Note.* "With great effort" recalls vv. 20–30, where the Lord wins Krishnadasa back from the heretics. Cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 10.62–70: the Lord sends away Kala Krishnadasa, and the devotees send him to Bengal with the news of the Lord's return.

### Verse 55

पश्यन् स नीलाचलमौलिरत्नं

स्वकीयनेत्राम्बुझरेण भूयो
निजां तनुमेव सिषेच हृष्टः ॥५५॥

*paśyan sa nīlācala-mauli-ratnaṁ*
*gaurāṅga-candraḥ śata-ratna-ramyam |*

*Word for word:* *paśyan* — gazing at; *saḥ* — He; *nīlācala* — of Nilachala; *mauli* — of the crown; *ratnam* — the jewel; *gaurāṅga-candraḥ* — Gaurangachandra; *śata* — with a hundred; *ratna* — jewels; *ramyam* — lovely; *svakīya* — of His own; *netra* — eyes; *ambu* — of water; *jhareṇa* — with the stream; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *nijām* — His own; *tanum* — body; *eva* — indeed; *siṣeca* — bathed; *hṛṣṭaḥ* — overjoyed.

**55.** Gazing at the jewel in the crown of Nilachala, lovely with a hundred jewels, Gaurangachandra, overjoyed, again bathed His own body with the stream of water from His own eyes.

### Verse 56

अथासकौ स्नानमहोत्सवं स
ददर्श रम्यं विबुधैर्दुरापम् ।
आनन्दसन्दोहसमुद्रमुच्चैः
समुद्रतीरेऽन्यमिवेक्ष्यमाणः ॥५६॥

*athāsakau snāna-mahotsavaṁ sa*
*dadarśa ramyaṁ vibudhair durāpam |*
*ānanda-sandoha-samudram uccaiḥ*
*samudra-tīre 'nyam ivekṣyamāṇaḥ ||56||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *asakau* — He; *snāna* — of the bathing; *mahā-utsavam* — the great festival; *saḥ* — He; *dadarśa* — saw; *ramyam* — beautiful; *vibudhaiḥ* — by the gods; *durāpam* — hard to attain; *ānanda* — of bliss; *sandoha* — of the abundance; *samudram* — an ocean; *uccaiḥ* — lofty; *samudra* — of the ocean; *tīre* — on the shore; *anyam* — another; *iva* — as if; *īkṣyamāṇaḥ* — beholding.

**56.** Then He beheld the beautiful great bathing festival, hard for even the gods to attain, as though He were beholding on the ocean shore another, lofty ocean — of abounding bliss.

*Note.* *Īkṣyamāṇaḥ* is passive in form, but with the accusative *samudram* it must be taken actively ("beholding").

### Verse 57

अथ प्रभातावसरे तथैव
विलोकितुं तं गतवान् कृपालुः ।
गूढं तथा तत्र विलोक्य नासौ
बभूव दुःखी कृतबाष्पमोक्षः ॥५७॥

*atha prabhātāvasare tathaiva*
*vilokituṁ taṁ gatavān kṛpāluḥ |*
*gūḍhaṁ tathā tatra vilokya nāsau*
*babhūva duḥkhī kṛta-bāṣpa-mokṣaḥ ||57||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *prabhāta* — of daybreak; *avasare* — at the time; *tathā eva* — as before; *vilokitum* — to see; *tam* — Him; *gatavān* — went; *kṛpāluḥ* — the Merciful One; *gūḍham* — hidden; *tathā* — thus; *tatra* — there; *vilokya na* — not seeing; *asau* — He; *babhūva* — became; *duḥkhī* — sorrowful; *kṛta* — having made; *bāṣpa* — of tears; *mokṣaḥ* — a release.

**57.** Then, at daybreak, the Merciful One went as before to see Him; but not seeing Him there, hidden as He was, He became sorrowful and shed tears.

*Note.* After the Snana-yatra Jagannatha is hidden from view for two weeks (the *anavasara*). Cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 1.122 (in separation from Jagannatha during the anavasara the Lord goes to Alalanatha); 11.61–63. The word order *vilokya nāsau* stands for *na vilokya asau*.

### Verse 58

बहिः प्रयाय त्वरितं महोत्को
विचित्रचेष्टो मदसिंहरम्यः ।
आलालनाथं प्रययौ तथामी
ययुस्तदान्वेषणकातराङ्गाः ॥५८॥

*bahiḥ prayāya tvaritaṁ mahotko*
*vicitra-ceṣṭo mada-siṁha-ramyaḥ |*
*ālālanāthaṁ prayayau tathāmī*
*yayus tad-anveṣaṇa-kātarāṅgāḥ ||58||*

*Word for word:* *bahiḥ* — outside; *prayāya* — having gone; *tvaritam* — in haste; *mahā-utkaḥ* — in great longing; *vicitra* — wondrous; *ceṣṭaḥ* — [whose] behaviour [was]; *mada* — exhilarated; *siṁha* — like a lion; *ramyaḥ* — beautiful; *ālālanātham* — to Alalanatha; *prayayau* — went; *tathā* — likewise; *amī* — they; *yayuḥ* — went; *tat* — for Him; *anveṣaṇa* — in search; *kātara* — distressed; *aṅgāḥ* — [whose] bodies [were].

**58.** Going out in haste, in great longing, wondrous in His behaviour, beautiful as an exhilarated lion, He went off to Alalanatha; and they likewise went in search of Him, distressed in body.

*Note.* Alalanatha is a temple of Vishnu at Brahmagiri, south of Puri, to which the Lord would withdraw during the anavasara.

### Verse 59

विचार्य तस्मिन्नवलोक्य नैव
प्रतेपुरुच्चैरथ तेऽतिखिन्नाः ।
अथाययुः क्षेत्रमतीवदुःखैः
क्षणं च कल्पानिव मेनिरे स्म ॥५९॥

*vicārya tasminn avalokya naiva*
*pratepur uccair atha te 'tikhinnāḥ |*
*athāyayuḥ kṣetram atīva-duḥkhaiḥ*
*kṣaṇaṁ ca kalpān iva menire sma ||59||*

*Word for word:* *vicārya* — having searched; *tasmin* — there; *avalokya* — finding; *na eva* — not at all; *pratepuḥ* — were tormented; *uccaiḥ* — sorely; *atha* — then; *te* — they; *ati-khinnāḥ* — utterly dejected; *atha* — then; *āyayuḥ* — came; *kṣetram* — to the Kshetra; *atīva* — in exceeding; *duḥkhaiḥ* — sorrow; *kṣaṇam* — a moment; *ca* — and; *kalpān* — kalpas; *iva* — as; *menire sma* — they deemed.

**59.** Having searched there and not finding Him at all, they, utterly dejected, were sorely tormented. Then they came [back] to the Kshetra in exceeding sorrow, and a single moment seemed to them like kalpas.

*Note.* A *kalpa* is a "day of Brahma", an immense span of time.

### Verse 60

प्रभुस्तथा तेन पथैव गोदा-
वरीं वरीयान् प्रययौ कृपालुः ।
तेनैव सार्धं प्रियभाषणेन
निनाय मासांश्चतुरोऽपरांश्च ॥६०॥

*prabhus tathā tena pathaiva godā-*
*varīṁ varīyān prayayau kṛpāluḥ |*
*tenaiva sārdhaṁ priya-bhāṣaṇena*
*nināya māsāṁś caturo 'parāṁś ca ||60||*

*Word for word:* *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *tathā* — thus; *tena eva* — by that same; *pathā* — road; *godāvarīm* — to the Godavari; *varīyān* — the most excellent; *prayayau* — went; *kṛpāluḥ* — the Merciful; *tena eva* — that same [Ramananda]; *sārdham* — together with; *priya* — in dear; *bhāṣaṇena* — conversation; *nināya* — spent; *māsān* — months; *caturaḥ* — four; *aparān* — further; *ca* — and.

**60.** And the Lord, most excellent and merciful, went thus by that same road to the Godavari, and together with that same [Ramananda], in dear conversation, spent another four months.

*Note.* An important divergence from the Chaitanya-charitamrita (checked against Madhya 1.122–123 and 11). In Karnapura the Lord goes from Alalanatha (or from Puri after the anavasara) once more to the Godavari and spends another chaturmasya with Ramananda. In the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 11) Ramananda himself comes to Puri, and the Lord remains there.

### Verse 61

हेमन्तकालेऽथ तथैव तेन

ञ्जानातु कस्तच्चरितं विचित्रम् ॥६१॥

*hemanta-kāle 'tha tathaiva tena*
*samaṁ samantāt karuṇāṁ vitanvan |*
*samāyayau kṣetra-varaṁ varīyāñ*
*jānātu kas tac-caritaṁ vicitram ||61||*

*Word for word:* *hemanta* — of early winter; *kāle* — in the season; *atha* — then; *tathā eva* — likewise; *tena* — him; *samam* — together with; *samantāt* — all around; *karuṇām* — mercy; *vitanvan* — spreading; *samāyayau* — came; *kṣetra* — to the Kshetra; *varam* — best; *varīyān* — the Most Excellent; *jānātu* — can know; *kaḥ* — who; *tat* — His; *caritam* — deeds; *vicitram* — wondrous.

**61.** Then, in the season of early winter, the Most Excellent, likewise together with him, spreading mercy all around, came to the best of Kshetras. Who can know His wondrous deeds?

*Note.* *Hemanta* is the season after autumn (November–December).

### Verse 62

समेत्य नीलाचलमुत्सुकोऽसौ

विलोक्य हर्षेण निनाय कालम् ॥६२॥

*sametya nīlācalam utsuko 'sau*
*hemācalābhaḥ kamanīya-dehaḥ |*
*śaśvaj jagannātha-mahāprabhuṁ taṁ*

*Word for word:* *sametya* — having arrived; *nīlācalam* — at Nilachala; *utsukaḥ* — eager; *asau* — He; *hema* — golden; *acala* — a mountain; *ābhaḥ* — resembling; *kamanīya* — lovely; *dehaḥ* — [whose] body [was]; *śaśvat* — constantly; *jagannātha-mahāprabhum* — Jagannatha Mahaprabhu; *tam* — that; *vilokya* — beholding; *harṣeṇa* — in joy; *nināya* — passed; *kālam* — the time.

**62.** Having arrived at Nilachala, He — like a golden mountain, His body lovely — eagerly and constantly beheld that Mahaprabhu Jagannatha and passed the time in joy.

### Verse 63

समागतं तं परिकर्ण्य काशी-
मिश्रः क्षतागःपटलीतमिस्रः ।
विलोक्य नत्वा मुमुदे प्रकाम-
मभीप्सितं बाहुचतुष्टयाढ्यम् ॥६३॥

*samāgataṁ taṁ parikarṇya kāśī-*
*miśraḥ kṣatāgaḥ-paṭalī-tamisraḥ |*
*vilokya natvā mumude prakāmam*
*abhīpsitaṁ bāhu-catuṣṭayāḍhyam ||63||*

*Word for word:* *samāgatam* — arrived; *tam* — Him; *parikarṇya* — having heard; *kāśī-miśraḥ* — Kashi Mishra; *kṣata* — destroyed; *āgaḥ* — of sins; *paṭalī* — of the veil; *tamisraḥ* — [whose] darkness [was]; *vilokya* — having seen; *natvā* — having bowed; *mumude* — rejoiced; *prakāmam* — to his heart's content; *abhīpsitam* — the longed-for; *bāhu* — of arms; *catuṣṭaya* — with a set of four; *āḍhyam* — endowed.

**63.** Hearing that He had arrived, Kashi Mishra, whose darkness — the veil of his sins — had been destroyed, saw [Him], the longed-for [Lord], endowed with four arms, bowed down, and rejoiced to his heart's content.

*Note.* Kashi Mishra was a priest and superintendent of the Jagannatha temple; in his house (the Gambhira) the Lord lived in Puri.

### Verse 64

तत्कृपाभिरभिचुम्बित एष
श्रीमदङ्घ्रिकमलस्य रजोभिः ।
रञ्जितः पुलककण्टकिताङ्गः
सान्द्रसौख्यविवशः स रराज ॥६४॥

*tat-kṛpābhir abhicumbita eṣa*
*śrīmad-aṅghri-kamalasya rajobhiḥ |*
*rañjitaḥ pulaka-kaṇṭakitāṅgaḥ*
*sāndra-saukhya-vivaśaḥ sa rarāja ||64||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — His; *kṛpābhiḥ* — by the mercies; *abhicumbitaḥ* — kissed; *eṣaḥ* — he; *śrīmat* — of the beautiful; *aṅghri* — feet; *kamalasya* — of the lotus; *rajobhiḥ* — with the dust; *rañjitaḥ* — coloured; *pulaka* — with thrills of rapture; *kaṇṭakita* — bristling [as with thorns]; *aṅgaḥ* — [whose] body [was]; *sāndra* — by dense; *saukhya* — happiness; *vivaśaḥ* — overpowered; *saḥ* — he; *rarāja* — shone.

**64.** Kissed by His mercies, coloured by the dust of His beautiful lotus feet, his body bristling with thrills of rapture, overpowered by dense happiness, he shone.

*Note.* Here the metre changes: vv. 64–114 are in *svāgatā* (—⏑— ⏑⏑⏑ —⏑⏑ ——) alternating with *rathoddhatā* (—⏑— ⏑⏑⏑ —⏑— ⏑—).

### Verse 65

यो यदीयकृपया सुमहत्या
नीलशैलतिलकालयलक्ष्मीम् ।
स्वे वशे प्रकुरुते स्म गरीयां-
स्तस्य केन महिमा परिमेयः ॥६५॥

*yo yadīya-kṛpayā su-mahatyā*
*nīla-śaila-tilakālaya-lakṣmīm |*
*sve vaśe prakurute sma garīyāṁs*
*tasya kena mahimā parimeyaḥ ||65||*

*Word for word:* *yaḥ* — who; *yadīya* — by whose; *kṛpayā* — mercy; *su-mahatyā* — very great; *nīla-śaila* — of the Blue Mountain; *tilaka* — of the tilaka; *ālaya* — of the house; *lakṣmīm* — the Lakshmi (wealth); *sve* — in his own; *vaśe* — control; *prakurute sma* — held; *garīyān* — most worthy; *tasya* — his; *kena* — by whom; *mahimā* — greatness; *parimeyaḥ* — can be measured.

**65.** By whom can the greatness of that most worthy man be measured, who by His very great mercy held in his own control the Lakshmi of the house of [Him who is] the tilaka of the Blue Mountain?

*Note.* "The tilaka of the Blue Mountain" is Jagannatha. *Ālaya-lakṣmī* — "the Lakshmi (wealth) of the house", that is, the temple's estate.

गौरचन्द्रचरणद्वितयस्या-

*gauracandra-caraṇa-dvitayasyā-*
*jñāpanaṁ sakalam ātanute yaḥ |*
*īpsitaṁ parikalayya sa kāśī-*
*miśra eṣa kathayā kim u vedyaḥ ||66||*

*Word for word:* *gauracandra* — of Gaurachandra; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *dvitayasya* — of the pair; *ājñāpanam* — command; *sakalam* — every; *ātanute* — carries out; *yaḥ* — who; *īpsitam* — the wish; *parikalayya* — having discerned; *saḥ* — that; *kāśī-miśraḥ* — Kashi Mishra; *eṣaḥ* — this; *kathayā* — by an account; *kim u* — can it be that; *vedyaḥ* — [he is] knowable.

**66.** He carries out every command of Gaurachandra's two feet, discerning [His] wish: can this Kashi Mishra be known through any account?

### Verse 67

यो महोत्सवविधौ विविधानि

निर्मितानि विदधे प्रभुचित्तं
प्राकलय्य किमयं जनवेद्यः ॥६७॥

*yo mahotsava-vidhau vividhāni*
*prāyaśo nija-matāni viśeṣāt |*
*nirmitāni vidadhe prabhu-cittaṁ*
*prākalayya kim ayaṁ jana-vedyaḥ ||67||*

*Word for word:* *yaḥ* — who; *mahā-utsava* — of great festivals; *vidhau* — in arranging; *vividhāni* — various; *prāyaśaḥ* — mostly; *nija* — by himself; *matāni* — conceived; *viśeṣāt* — especially; *nirmitāni* — arrangements; *vidadhe* — carried out; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *cittam* — the mind; *prākalayya* — having discerned; *kim* — can; *ayam* — he; *jana* — by [ordinary] people; *vedyaḥ* — be understood.

**67.** In arranging the great festivals he, having discerned the Lord's mind, carried out various special arrangements, mostly of his own conception: can he be understood by ordinary people?

*Note.* The edition marks the verse number with a dash: *॥६७–*.

### Verse 68

कश्चनैष परमोऽथ महात्मा
विष्णुदास इति निर्मलबुद्धिः ।
सर्वमेव परिहाय ददर्श
श्रीशचीसुतपदाम्बुजयुग्मम् ॥६८॥

*kaścanaiṣa paramo 'tha mahātmā*
*viṣṇudāsa iti nirmala-buddhiḥ |*
*sarvam eva parihāya dadarśa*
*śrī-śacī-suta-padāmbuja-yugmam ||68||*

*Word for word:* *kaścana* — a certain; *eṣaḥ* — this; *paramaḥ* — exalted; *atha* — also; *mahātmā* — great soul; *viṣṇudāsaḥ* — Vishnudasa; *iti* — named; *nirmala* — pure; *buddhiḥ* — [whose] intelligence [was]; *sarvam* — everything; *eva* — indeed; *parihāya* — abandoning; *dadarśa* — beheld; *śrī-śacī-suta* — of the son of Sri Shachi; *pada* — of the feet; *ambuja* — of the lotuses; *yugmam* — the pair.

**68.** Also, a certain exalted great soul of pure intelligence, named Vishnudasa, abandoning everything, beheld the pair of lotus feet of the son of Sri Shachi.

*Note.* Cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 10.151 (Vishnudasa is among the Lord's associates who lived in Puri).

*sadya eva sa tadīya-kṛpābhir*
*vyānaśe sukṛta-sañcaya-dhanyaḥ |*
*locana-dvaya-galaj-jala-dhārā-*
*dhauta-sarva-tanur eva tadāsīt ||69||*

*Word for word:* *sadyaḥ eva* — at once; *saḥ* — he; *tadīya* — by His; *kṛpābhiḥ* — mercies; *vyānaśe* — was pervaded; *sukṛta* — of pious deeds; *sañcaya* — through the store; *dhanyaḥ* — blessed; *locana* — of eyes; *dvaya* — from the pair; *galat* — pouring; *jala* — of water; *dhārā* — by the streams; *dhauta* — washed; *sarva* — whole; *tanuḥ* — [whose] body [was]; *eva* — indeed; *tadā* — then; *āsīt* — became.

**69.** At once he, blessed through his store of pious deeds, was pervaded by His mercies, and then his whole body was washed by the streams of water pouring from his two eyes.

### Verse 70

कोऽपि भूरिसुकृतः सुभगः प्र-
द्युम्नमिश्र इति भाग्यमयाब्धिः ।
गौरचन्द्रचरणाम्बुजयुग्मं
लोचनातिथि सुखेन चकार ॥७०॥

*ko 'pi bhūri-sukṛtaḥ subhagaḥ pra-*
*dyumna-miśra iti bhāgya-mayābdhiḥ |*
*gauracandra-caraṇāmbuja-yugmaṁ*
*locanātithi sukhena cakāra ||70||*

*Word for word:* *kaḥ api* — a certain; *bhūri* — abundant; *sukṛtaḥ* — [whose] merits [were]; *subhagaḥ* — fortunate man; *pradyumna-miśraḥ* — Pradyumna Mishra; *iti* — named; *bhāgya-maya* — of good fortune; *abdhiḥ* — an ocean; *gauracandra* — of Gaurachandra; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *ambuja* — of the lotuses; *yugmam* — the pair; *locana* — of the eyes; *atithi* — the guest; *sukhena* — joyfully; *cakāra* — made.

**70.** A certain fortunate man of abundant merit, an ocean of good fortune, named Pradyumna Mishra, joyfully made the pair of Gaurachandra's lotus feet the guest of his eyes.

*Note.* The edition divides the first two padas wrongly (10 and 12 syllables); in the Gosvami edition (GGM) the boundary falls within the name — *subhagaḥ pra- / dyumna-miśra* — and both padas are correct (11 syllables each); the edition's *सुभयः* is apparently a misprint for *subhagaḥ*. Cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Antya 5.4–8: Pradyumna Mishra asks the Lord to speak about Krishna, and He sends him to hear Ramananda.

### Verse 71

लोचनातिथितयैव तदस्मि-

यद्विलोचनगता जलधारा
श्रावणाम्बुदपयोधर एव ॥७१॥

*locanātithitayaiva tad asminn*
*asya kāruṇikatā kalitāsīt |*
*yad-vilocana-gatā jala-dhārā*
*śrāvaṇāmbuda-payodhara eva ||71||*

*Word for word:* *locana* — of the eyes; *atithitayā* — by being the guest; *eva* — merely; *tat* — thus; *asmin* — on him; *asya* — His; *kāruṇikatā* — compassion; *kalitā āsīt* — was manifested; *yat* — for; *vilocana* — in [his] eyes; *gatā* — appearing; *jala* — of water; *dhārā* — the stream; *śrāvaṇa* — of [the month of] Shravana; *ambuda* — a cloud; *payodharaḥ* — rain-laden; *eva* — truly.

**71.** Thus, merely by being the guest of his eyes, His compassion was manifested upon him: for the stream of water that came to his eyes was truly a rain-laden cloud of the month of Shravana.

*Note.* *Shravana* is July–August, the season of the heaviest rains.

*raṇya-saṁsmṛti-kareṣu jagāma ||72||*

*Word for word:* *ekadā* — once; *nija* — His own; *vihāra* — pastimes; *viśeṣam* — particular; *saṁsmaran* — remembering; *upavaneṣu* — into the gardens; *saḥ* — He; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *mañjuleṣu* — charming; *rabhasena* — impetuously; *saḥ* — He; *vṛndā-araṇya* — of Vrindavana; *saṁsmṛti* — remembrance; *kareṣu* — awakening; *jagāma* — went.

**72.** Once the Lord, remembering His own particular pastimes, went impetuously into charming gardens that awaken remembrance of Vrindavana.

### Verse 73

तत् प्रविश्य वनमुत्तमशोभा-

आत्मना सह सनाथमतीव
प्रेमपूर्णहृदयो व्यजनिष्ट ॥७३॥

*tat praviśya vanam uttama-śobhā-*

*Word for word:* *tat* — that; *praviśya* — having entered; *vanam* — grove; *uttama* — of supreme; *śobhā* — splendour; *rāmaṇīyakam* — the charm; *avekṣya* — having beheld; *saḥ* — He; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *ātmanā saha* — in Himself; *sa-nātham* — possessed of a lord; *atīva* — exceedingly; *prema* — with love; *pūrṇa* — filled; *hṛdayaḥ* — [whose] heart [was]; *vyajaniṣṭa* — became.

**73.** Entering that grove — which in Him had found its lord — and beholding the charm of its supreme splendour, the Lord became exceedingly full-hearted with love.

*Note.* A play on words: the *nāthaḥ* ("Lord") enters the grove, and it becomes *sanātham* — "possessed of a lord".

### Verse 74

भृङ्गधर्षितप्रसूनसञ्चयां
वेपमाननवपल्लवावलीम् ।
ओष्ठदंशनरतं प्रियं प्रियां
पाणिपल्लवमिवावधुन्वतीम् ॥७४॥

*bhṛṅga-dharṣita-prasūna-sañcayāṁ*
*vepamāna-nava-pallavāvalīm |*
*oṣṭha-daṁśana-rataṁ priyaṁ priyāṁ*
*pāṇi-pallavam ivāvadhunvatīm ||74||*

*Word for word:* *bhṛṅga* — by bees; *dharṣita* — assailed; *prasūna* — of flowers; *sañcayām* — [whose] clusters [were]; *vepamāna* — trembling; *nava* — of young; *pallava* — shoots; *āvalīm* — [whose] rows [were]; *oṣṭha* — the lip; *daṁśana* — biting; *ratam* — delighting in; *priyam* — at the darling; *priyām* — a beloved; *pāṇi* — of the hand; *pallavam* — the shoot; *iva* — as if; *avadhunvatīm* — shaking.

**74.** [He beheld that row of creepers,] its clusters of flowers assailed by bees, its rows of young shoots trembling — as if it were a beloved shaking the tender shoot of her hand at her darling who delights in biting her lip…

*Note.* Verses 74–75 form a pair (*yugmaka*; so marked in the edition too). Metre *rathoddhatā*; in the first pada *-ta pra-* is long by position — a licence. The accusative *priyām* can stand: it is in apposition to *āvalīm* (v. 75), the row of creepers being itself the "beloved"; one could also read *priyā* (nominative) (?).

*Word for word:* *tām* — that; *dadarśa* — He beheld; *kamanīya* — lovely; *kṛśa* — slender; *aṅgīm* — [whose] limbs [were]; *āvalīm* — row; *lalita* — charming; *bhṛṅgavatīnām* — having bees (gallants); *tāla* — rhythm (palm trees); *māna* — measure; *laya* — tempo; *hāva* — expressive gestures; *vatīnām* — possessed of; *nartakī* — of dancing girls; *pariṣadam* — a company; *va* — like; *latānām* — of creepers.

**75.** …He beheld that row of creepers, lovely and slender-limbed, with their charming bees — like a company of dancing girls possessed of rhythm, measure, tempo and expressive gestures.

*Note.* *Va* = *iva* ("like"). Double meanings: *bhṛṅga* — "bee" and "gallant"; *tāla* — "rhythm" and "palm tree".

**76.** Thus for a long time, setting down the pair of His lotus feet here in a light dance, and here and there forgetting His own movements as He remembered the dance of the playful [gopis],

*Note.* The verse has no finite verb: the sentence closes with *vireje*, "He shone", in v. 77.

### Verse 77

अश्रुसंश्रवणसंभृतहार-
श्रीविराजितमनोहरवक्षाः ।

*aśru-saṁśravaṇa-saṁbhṛta-hāra-*

*Word for word:* *aśru* — of tears; *saṁśravaṇa* — by the streaming; *saṁbhṛta* — formed; *hāra* — of a necklace; *śrī* — with the beauty; *virājita* — resplendent; *manohara* — captivating; *vakṣāḥ* — [whose] chest [was]; *bibhrat* — bearing; *utpulakam* — bristling with rapture; *aṅga* — of the body; *latā* — the creeper; *antam* — to the tips; *pūrṇimā* — of the full; *indu* — moon; *vadanaḥ* — [whose] face [was like that]; *saḥ* — He; *vireje* — shone.

**77.** …His captivating chest resplendent with the beauty of a necklace formed by His streaming tears, the creeper of His body bristling with rapture to its very tips, His face like the full moon — He shone.

### Verse 78

एवमत्र विलसत्यनन्तरं
सार्वभौमकथितैः प्रलोभितः ।
उत्सुकस्तमभितो गजाधिपः
साहसादिह समाययौ द्रुतम् ॥७८॥

*evam atra vilasaty anantaraṁ*
*sārvabhauma-kathitaiḥ pralobhitaḥ |*
*utsukas tam abhito gajādhipaḥ*
*sāhasād iha samāyayau drutam ||78||*

*Word for word:* *evam* — thus; *atra* — here; *vilasati* — while [He] was sporting; *anantaram* — thereupon; *sārvabhauma* — of Sarvabhauma; *kathitaiḥ* — by the accounts; *pralobhitaḥ* — drawn; *utsukaḥ* — eager; *tam abhitaḥ* — into His presence; *gaja-adhipaḥ* — the Gajapati; *sāhasāt* — daringly; *iha* — here; *samāyayau* — came; *drutam* — quickly.

**78.** While He was thus sporting here, the Gajapati, drawn by Sarvabhauma's accounts, eagerly and daringly came here quickly into His presence.

*Note.* Gajapati ("lord of elephants") is the title of the kings of Orissa; here it is Prataparudra. In the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 14.4–16) this scene follows the Ratha-yatra: on Sarvabhauma's advice the king, dressed as a Vaishnava, enters the garden where the Lord is resting and recites to Him verses about the rasa-lila; at the stanza *tava kathāmṛtam* the Lord rises and embraces him.

### Verse 79

श्रेयसि प्रथममेव भूयते
वाञ्छितेन सफलैर्मनोरथैः ।
साहसेन यदकारि भूभुजा
तत्तु कोटिगुणसौख्यमादधे ॥७९॥

*śreyasi prathamam eva bhūyate*
*vāñchitena saphalair manorathaiḥ |*
*sāhasena yad akāri bhūbhujā*
*tat tu koṭi-guṇa-saukhyam ādadhe ||79||*

*Word for word:* *śreyasi* — when good fortune [comes]; *prathamam* — first of all; *eva* — indeed; *bhūyate* — one becomes [possessed]; *vāñchitena* — of what is desired; *saphalaiḥ* — fulfilled; *manorathaiḥ* — with wishes; *sāhasena* — daringly; *yat* — what; *akāri* — was done; *bhūbhujā* — by the king; *tat* — that; *tu* — but; *koṭi-guṇa* — ten-million-fold; *saukhyam* — happiness; *ādadhe* — brought.

**79.** When good fortune comes, first of all one gains what one longed for, one's wishes bearing fruit; but what the king did daringly brought him happiness ten million times over.

### Verse 80

केन तस्य महितात्मना लस-
त्पुण्यराशिमहितस्य निर्भरम् ।
भागधेयजलधेर्विधीयतां
भूयसी परिणतिर्महीपतेः ॥८०॥

*kena tasya mahitātmanā lasat-*
*puṇya-rāśi-mahitasya nirbharam |*
*bhāgadheya-jaladher vidhīyatāṁ*
*bhūyasī pariṇatir mahīpateḥ ||80||*

*Word for word:* *kena* — by whom; *tasya* — of that; *mahita* — exalted; *ātmanā* — [even] in spirit; *lasat* — shining; *puṇya* — of merits; *rāśi* — by the heap; *mahitasya* — glorified; *nirbharam* — exceedingly; *bhāgadheya* — of good fortune; *jaladheḥ* — of the ocean; *vidhīyatām* — could be made; *bhūyasī* — full; *pariṇatiḥ* — measurement; *mahīpateḥ* — of the king.

**80.** By whom, however exalted in spirit, could a full measure be taken of the ocean of good fortune of that king, exceedingly glorified by his shining heap of merits?

*Note.* *Pariṇati* is taken here as "measuring, reckoning"; the translation is tentative.

### Verse 81

स प्रविश्य वनमुत्तमं ततो
भूरिभाग्यमहितो महीपतिः ।
तप्तकाञ्चनमहीधरप्रभं
तं ददर्श करुणापयोनिधिम् ॥८१॥

*sa praviśya vanam uttamaṁ tato*
*bhūri-bhāgya-mahito mahīpatiḥ |*
*tapta-kāñcana-mahīdhara-prabhaṁ*
*taṁ dadarśa karuṇā-payonidhim ||81||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — he; *praviśya* — having entered; *vanam* — the grove; *uttamam* — excellent; *tataḥ* — then; *bhūri* — by great; *bhāgya* — fortune; *mahitaḥ* — glorified; *mahīpatiḥ* — the king; *tapta* — of molten; *kāñcana* — gold; *mahīdhara* — like a mountain; *prabham* — shining; *tam* — Him; *dadarśa* — saw; *karuṇā* — of compassion; *payonidhim* — the ocean.

**81.** Then the king, glorified by great fortune, entered that excellent grove and saw Him, the ocean of compassion, shining like a mountain of molten gold.

### Verse 82

दण्डवद् भुवि निपत्य च धृत्वा
पादपद्मयुगलं गलदश्रुः ।
अस्तुवत् सहजमेव महात्मा
रासलास्यमनुवर्ण्य विशेषम् ॥८२॥

*daṇḍavad bhuvi nipatya ca dhṛtvā*
*pāda-padma-yugalaṁ galad-aśruḥ |*
*astuvat sahajam eva mahātmā*
*rāsa-lāsyam anuvarṇya viśeṣam ||82||*

*Word for word:* *daṇḍa-vat* — like a rod; *bhuvi* — on the ground; *nipatya* — having fallen; *ca* — and; *dhṛtvā* — having clasped; *pāda* — of feet; *padma* — of the lotuses; *yugalam* — the pair; *galat* — streaming; *aśruḥ* — [with] tears; *astuvat* — praised; *sahajam* — artlessly; *eva* — indeed; *mahātmā* — the great soul; *rāsa* — of the rasa; *lāsyam* — the dance; *anuvarṇya* — describing; *viśeṣam* — in particular.

**82.** Falling to the ground like a rod and clasping the pair of [His] lotus feet, the great-souled [king], his tears streaming, artlessly praised [Him], describing in particular the rasa dance.

*Note.* Cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 14.8–13, where the king recites the Gopi-gita (Srimad-Bhagavatam 10.31, from *jayati te 'dhikam* to *tava kathāmṛtam*). In Karnapura he describes the rasa dance.

### Verse 83

स स्तुवन्निति तदा समुदासे
दोर्द्वयेन दृढमेव निबध्य ।
मत्तवारणकरप्रतिमेन
श्रीमता परमकारुणिकेन ॥८३॥

*sa stuvann iti tadā samudāse*
*dor-dvayena dṛḍham eva nibadhya |*
*matta-vāraṇa-kara-pratimena*
*śrīmatā parama-kāruṇikena ||83||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — he; *stuvan* — praising; *iti* — thus; *tadā* — then; *samudāse* — was lifted up (?); *doḥ* — of arms; *dvayena* — with the pair; *dṛḍham* — tightly; *eva* — indeed; *nibadhya* — having clasped; *matta* — of a maddened; *vāraṇa* — elephant; *kara* — the trunk; *pratimena* — resembling; *śrīmatā* — by the beautiful; *parama* — supremely; *kāruṇikena* — by the Merciful One.

**83.** As he was thus praising, he was then lifted up by the beautiful, supremely Merciful One, who clasped him tightly with His two arms, like the trunk of a maddened elephant.

*Note.* *Samudāse* is unclear: perhaps the perfect middle of *sam-ud-as* ("to toss up, to raise"), here with passive sense and the instrumental of the agent (*śrīmatā parama-kāruṇikena*) (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 84

अश्रुणा विगलता पुलकेन
प्रोद्यता विलसितः स गजेशः ।
मल्लराजबलवानपि राजा
तस्य बाहुदलितः क इवाभूत् ॥८४॥

*aśruṇā vigalatā pulakena*
*prodyatā vilasitaḥ sa gajeśaḥ |*
*malla-rāja-balavān api rājā*
*tasya bāhu-dalitaḥ ka ivābhūt ||84||*

*Word for word:* *aśruṇā* — with tears; *vigalatā* — streaming; *pulakena* — with thrill [of the hairs standing on end]; *prodyatā* — risen; *vilasitaḥ* — adorned; *saḥ* — that; *gaja-īśaḥ* — lord of elephants (the Gajapati); *malla* — of wrestlers; *rāja* — like the king; *balavān* — strong; *api* — though; *rājā* — the king; *tasya* — by His; *bāhu* — arms; *dalitaḥ* — crushed; *kaḥ iva* — as [a mere] nothing; *abhūt* — became.

**84.** Adorned with streaming tears and with the thrill of his hairs standing on end, that lord of elephants — the king, though as strong as a king of wrestlers — crushed in His arms, became as [a mere] nothing.

*Note.* *Gajeśa*, "lord of elephants", renders the title Gajapati borne by the kings of Orissa.

### Verse 85

तं विहाय निजगाद स भूयः
कस्त्वमित्यतिशयार्द्रतनूकः ।
दास एष जन एव तवैत-
द्देहि दास्यमिति सोऽपि जगाद ॥८५॥

*taṁ vihāya nijagāda sa bhūyaḥ*
*kas tvam ity atiśayārdra-tanūkaḥ |*
*dāsa eṣa jana eva tavaitad*
*dehi dāsyam iti so 'pi jagāda ||85||*

*Word for word:* *tam* — him; *vihāya* — having released; *nijagāda* — said; *saḥ* — He; *bhūyaḥ* — then; *kaḥ* — who; *tvam* — you; *iti* — thus; *atiśaya* — exceedingly; *ārdra* — moist; *tanūkaḥ* — [whose] body [was]; *dāsaḥ* — the servant; *eṣaḥ* — this; *janaḥ* — person; *eva* — indeed; *tava* — Your; *etat* — this; *dehi* — grant; *dāsyam* — service; *iti* — thus; *saḥ api* — he too; *jagāda* — said.

**85.** Releasing him, the Lord, His body all moist [with tears], then asked: "Who are you?" And he answered: "This person is indeed Your servant. Grant [him] this — service!"

### Verse 86

क्वापि नाहमभिधेय एव भो-
स्त्वादृशेति निजगाद स प्रभुः ।
निर्भरं प्रमुदितो भृशं तथा
रुद्रदेव उदवोचदुत्सुकः ॥८६॥

*kvāpi nāham abhidheya eva bhos*
*tvādṛśeti nijagāda sa prabhuḥ |*
*nirbharaṁ pramudito bhṛśaṁ tathā*
*rudradeva udavocad utsukaḥ ||86||*

*Word for word:* *kva api* — in any way; *na* — not; *aham* — I; *abhidheyaḥ* — to be named; *eva* — at all; *bhoḥ* — O [sir]; *tvādṛśā* — by one such as you; *iti* — thus; *nijagāda* — said; *saḥ* — He; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *nirbharam* — beyond measure; *pramuditaḥ* — delighted; *bhṛśam* — greatly; *tathā* — in turn; *rudradevaḥ* — Rudradeva; *udavocat* — spoke out; *utsukaḥ* — eagerly.

**86.** The Lord said: "O sir, by one such as you I ought not to be named at all!" And Rudradeva, greatly delighted beyond measure, eagerly spoke in turn.

*Note.* The sense of the Lord's words is unclear (?). It is not fitting for a sannyasi to associate with a king; cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 11.6–8: for a renounced sannyasi, meeting a king is like willingly drinking poison. Rudradeva is Prataparudra. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 87

सत्वरं तत इतो मुदितात्मा

र्दक्षिणे सति विधौ किमलभ्यम् ॥८७॥

*bhāgyavadbhir ati-bhūri-suceṣṭair*

*Word for word:* *satvaram* — quickly; *tataḥ itaḥ* — from there; *mudita* — joyful; *ātmā* — [whose] heart [was]; *niryayau* — went out; *bahala* — of abundant; *harṣa* — joy; *bhara* — with the weight; *āḍhyaḥ* — rich; *bhāgyavadbhiḥ* — by the fortunate; *ati-bhūri* — very abundant; *su-ceṣṭaiḥ* — [whose] good deeds [are]; *dakṣiṇe* — favourable; *sati* — being; *vidhau* — destiny; *kim* — what; *alabhyam* — [is] unattainable.

**87.** His heart joyful, rich with the weight of abundant joy, [the king] quickly went out from there. When destiny is favourable, what is unattainable for the fortunate, whose good deeds are very abundant?

### Verse 88

यत् प्रभुः प्रतिजनं परां कृपा-
माततान करुणैकसागरः ।
तत्तु किं कथयितुं भवेदहो
गीष्पतिः प्रभुरमी कुतोऽपरे ॥८८॥

*yat prabhuḥ pratijanaṁ parāṁ kṛpām*
*ātatāna karuṇaika-sāgaraḥ |*
*tat tu kiṁ kathayituṁ bhaved aho*
*gīṣpatiḥ prabhur amī kuto 'pare ||88||*

*Word for word:* *yat* — which; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *pratijanam* — to every person; *parām* — supreme; *kṛpām* — mercy; *ātatāna* — extended; *karuṇā* — of compassion; *eka* — the one; *sāgaraḥ* — ocean; *tat* — that; *tu* — indeed; *kim* — could; *kathayitum* — to tell; *bhavet* — be; *aho* — ah; *gīṣpatiḥ* — the lord of speech (Brihaspati); *prabhuḥ* — able; *amī* — these; *kutaḥ* — how then; *apare* — others.

**88.** The supreme mercy that the Lord, the one ocean of compassion, extended to every person — ah, could [even] the lord of speech be able to tell of it? How then these others?

*Note.* *Gīṣpati*, "the lord of speech", is Brihaspati, the preceptor of the gods.

### Verse 89

अस्ति तत्र विमलः शिखिनामा
माहितीति पुरुषोत्तमभूमौ ।
नीलशैलतिलकस्य महात्मा
दासवत् करुणतां समुपेतः ॥८९॥

*asti tatra vimalaḥ śikhi-nāmā*
*māhitīti puruṣottama-bhūmau |*
*nīla-śaila-tilakasya mahātmā*
*dāsavat karuṇatāṁ samupetaḥ ||89||*

*Word for word:* *asti* — there is; *tatra* — there; *vimalaḥ* — a pure [man]; *śikhi* — Shikhi; *nāmā* — by name; *māhitī* — Mahiti; *iti* — thus [called]; *puruṣottama* — of Purushottama; *bhūmau* — in the land; *nīla-śaila* — of the Blue Mountain; *tilakasya* — of the tilaka; *mahātmā* — a great soul; *dāsa-vat* — as a servant; *karuṇatām* — mercy; *samupetaḥ* — having obtained.

**89.** There, in the land of Purushottama, lives a pure man named Shikhi Mahiti — a great soul who, as His servant, has obtained the mercy of the tilaka of the Blue Mountain.

*Note.* "The tilaka of the Blue Mountain" — Jagannatha, the ornament of Nilachala. Shikhi Mahiti was a scribe of the Jagannatha temple; cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 10.135–136 (Shikhi Mahiti and his brother Murari Mahiti are constant companions of the Lord in Puri) and Antya 2.104–106. The rendering of *dāsavat karuṇatāṁ samupetaḥ* is conjectural (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 90

अस्य कोऽप्यवरजोऽस्ति मुरारि-
र्नाम तस्य च तथानु कनिष्ठा ।
शुद्धबुद्धिरथ माधवदेवी
भ्रातरस्त इति तत्र समासन् ॥९०॥

*asya ko 'py avarajo 'sti murārir*
*nāma tasya ca tathānu kaniṣṭhā |*
*śuddha-buddhir atha mādhava-devī*
*bhrātaras ta iti tatra samāsan ||90||*

*Word for word:* *asya* — of him; *kaḥ api* — a certain; *avarajaḥ* — younger brother; *asti* — there is; *murāriḥ* — Murari; *nāma* — by name; *tasya* — of him; *ca* — and; *tathā* — likewise; *anu* — after; *kaniṣṭhā* — the youngest [sister]; *śuddha* — pure; *buddhiḥ* — [whose] intelligence [is]; *atha* — and; *mādhava-devī* — Madhava-devi; *bhrātaraḥ* — siblings; *te* — these; *iti* — thus; *tatra* — there; *samāsan* — lived.

**90.** He has a younger brother named Murari, and after him, likewise, the youngest, a sister of pure intelligence, Madhava-devi. Thus these siblings lived there.

*Note.* The brother is Murari Mahiti, not Murari Gupta. In the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Antya 2.104–106) the sister is Madhavi-devi, an aged ascetic, whom the Lord counted among the associates of Radharani; the "three and a half" intimate associates [of the Lord in Puri] are Svarupa Damodara, Ramananda, Shikhi Mahiti and, as the "half", Madhavi.

### Verse 91

*Word for word:* *bhrātarau* — brother and sister; *punaḥ* — however; *imau* — these; *priya* — dear; *anujau* — younger; *gauracandra* — to Gaurachandra; *niratau* — devoted; *babhūvatuḥ* — became; *niścalā* — steadfast; *hi* — for; *sahajā* — innate; *matiḥ* — inclination; *śubhā* — auspicious; *vismṛtim* — forgetfulness; *na hi* — never at all; *dadhāti* — admits; *karhicit* — ever.

**91.** These two, however, the dear younger brother and sister, became devoted to Gaurachandra; for a steadfast, auspicious, innate inclination never admits of forgetfulness.

श्रीशचीजठरसिन्धुचन्द्रमाः ॥९२॥

*Word for word:* *nāthaḥ* — the Master; *eṣaḥ* — this; *paramaḥ* — the supreme; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *nidhiḥ* — treasury; *prema* — of love; *saṁprakaṭana* — the manifestation; *artham* — for the sake of; *udyataḥ* — has come forth; *kāntaḥ* — the Beloved; *eṣaḥ* — this; *kamanīyatā-mayaḥ* — made of loveliness; *śrī-śacī* — of Sri Shachi; *jaṭhara* — of the womb; *sindhu* — of the ocean; *candramāḥ* — the moon.

**92.** "This Master, the supreme treasury of mercy, has come forth to manifest love. This Beloved, made of loveliness, is the moon [risen] from the ocean of Sri Shachi's womb.

*Note.* The edition numbers this verse *॥८२॥*, a misprint for 92. Verses 92–93 give the thought of the brother and sister.

### Verse 93

गौरचन्द्र इह संप्रति वृन्दा-

एतयोरिति शुभा मतिरासीत्
सन्ततं विदधतो रतिराशिम् ॥९३॥

*santataṁ vidadhato rati-rāśim ||93||*

*Word for word:* *gauracandraḥ* — as Gaurachandra; *iha* — here; *samprati* — now; *vṛndāraṇya* — of Vrindavana; *candraḥ* — the Moon; *udiyāya* — has risen; *dharaṇyām* — on the earth; *etayoḥ* — of these two; *iti* — such; *śubhā* — auspicious; *matiḥ* — conviction; *āsīt* — was; *santatam* — constantly; *vidadhatoḥ* — of [those two] who cherished; *rati* — of love; *rāśim* — an abundance.

**93.** The Moon of Vrindavana has now risen here on the earth as Gaurachandra." Such was the auspicious conviction of these two, who constantly cherished an abundance of love.

*Word for word:* *agrajam prati* — toward the elder brother; *ca* — and; *nīla-giri-indra* — of the Lord of the Blue Mountain; *prema* — in love; *bhṛtyam* — the servant; *anayoḥ* — of these two; *ati* — great; *yatnaḥ* — effort; *gauracandra* — of Gaurachandra; *bhajana* — worship; *artham* — for the sake of; *atha* — then; *āsīt* — there was; *na* — not; *eṣaḥ* — he; *tatra* — to that; *nirataḥ* — inclined; *ca* — and; *babhūva* — became.

**94.** And these two made great efforts that their elder brother, the loving servant of the Lord of the Blue Mountain, should worship Gaurachandra; but he did not become inclined to it.

### Verse 95

सोऽपरेद्युरनुजोपदेशतः

यामिनीचरमकाल आगते
स्वप्नदर्शनसमाकुलोऽभवत् ॥९५॥

*so 'pare-dyur anujopadeśataḥ*
*santataṁ bahu-manaḥ-kathā-cyutaḥ |*
*yāminī-carama-kāla āgate*
*svapna-darśana-samākulo 'bhavat ||95||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — he; *apare-dyuḥ* — the next day; *anuja* — of the younger brother; *upadeśataḥ* — by the instruction; *santatam* — constantly; *bahu* — by many; *manaḥ* — of the mind; *kathā* — discourses; *cyutaḥ* — shaken (?); *yāminī* — of the night; *carama* — the last; *kāle* — when the time; *āgate* — had come; *svapna* — in a dream; *darśana* — by a vision; *samākulaḥ* — overwhelmed; *abhavat* — became.

**95.** The next day, at his younger brother's instruction, he was constantly [turning over] many thoughts in his mind; and when the last part of the night had come, he was overwhelmed by a vision in a dream.

*Note.* *Bahu-manaḥ-kathā-cyutaḥ* is unclear: perhaps read *-yutaḥ* ("occupied with many reflections") (?); or *cyutaḥ* may mean "lapsed [into sleep]" amid many reflections (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 96

भ्रातरौ पुनरनेन कनिष्ठौ
गौरचन्द्रपदपङ्कजहृष्टौ ।
तत्क्षणे स्वमपि जागरयन्तौ
स्वप्नदृष्टिचकितं ददृशाते ॥९६॥

*bhrātarau punar anena kaniṣṭhau*
*gauracandra-pada-paṅkaja-hṛṣṭau |*
*tat-kṣaṇe svam api jāgarayantau*
*svapna-dṛṣṭi-cakitaṁ dadṛśāte ||96||*

*Word for word:* *bhrātarau* — brother and sister; *punaḥ* — and; *anena* — his; *kaniṣṭhau* — younger; *gauracandra* — of Gaurachandra; *pada* — of the feet; *paṅkaja* — in the lotuses; *hṛṣṭau* — delighting; *tat-kṣaṇe* — at that moment; *svam* — their own [brother]; *api* — also; *jāgarayantau* — waking; *svapna* — in the dream; *dṛṣṭi* — by what was seen; *cakitam* — startled; *dadṛśāte* — saw.

**96.** And his younger brother and sister, who delighted in the lotus feet of Gaurachandra, were waking their brother at that very moment, and they saw him startled by what he had seen in the dream.

### Verse 97

चित्रदर्शनभवत्पुलकौघै-
र्हर्षतो द्विगुण एव बभूव ।
उन्मिमील शनकैर्जलपूर्णे
लोचने तदनु तौ च ददर्श ॥९७॥

*citra-darśana-bhavat-pulakaughair*
*harṣato dvi-guṇa eva babhūva |*
*unmimīla śanakair jala-pūrṇe*
*locane tad-anu tau ca dadarśa ||97||*

*Word for word:* *citra* — wondrous; *darśana* — from the vision; *bhavat* — arising; *pulaka* — of thrill [of the hairs standing on end]; *oghaiḥ* — by the floods; *harṣataḥ* — from joy; *dvi-guṇaḥ* — twofold; *eva* — indeed; *babhūva* — became; *unmimīla* — opened; *śanakaiḥ* — slowly; *jala* — with water; *pūrṇe* — filled; *locane* — the eyes; *tat-anu* — then; *tau* — the two; *ca* — and; *dadarśa* — saw.

**97.** With floods of thrill arising from the wondrous vision, his hairs standing on end, he became twice [his size] for joy. Slowly he opened his eyes, filled with tears, and then saw the two of them.

### Verse 98

तौ विलोक्य निजजागरणार्थ-
मागतौ सविधमेव महान्तौ ।
आलिलिङ्ग स दृढं परिहृष्टो
विस्मितावभवतां च तदा तौ ॥९८॥

*tau vilokya nija-jāgaraṇārtham*
*āgatau savidham eva mahāntau |*
*āliliṅga sa dṛḍhaṁ parihṛṣṭo*
*vismitāv abhavatāṁ ca tadā tau ||98||*

*Word for word:* *tau* — the two; *vilokya* — having seen; *nija* — his; *jāgaraṇa* — waking; *artham* — for the sake of; *āgatau* — come; *savidham* — close by; *eva* — indeed; *mahāntau* — great-hearted; *āliliṅga* — embraced; *saḥ* — he; *dṛḍham* — tightly; *parihṛṣṭaḥ* — overjoyed; *vismitau* — astonished; *abhavatām* — became; *ca* — and; *tadā* — then; *tau* — the two.

**98.** Seeing close beside him the two great-hearted ones, who had come to wake him, he, overjoyed, embraced them tightly; and then the two were astonished.

### Verse 99

भ्रातरौ शृणुत मे तदीक्षितं
स्वप्नतो यदिति चित्रमेव तत् ।
अप्रमेयमहिमा शचीसुतः
प्रत्ययोऽद्य खलु केवलमासीत् ॥९९॥

*bhrātarau śṛṇuta me tad īkṣitaṁ*
*svapnato yad iti citram eva tat |*
*aprameya-mahimā śacī-sutaḥ*
*pratyayo 'dya khalu kevalam āsīt ||99||*

*Word for word:* *bhrātarau* — O brother and sister; *śṛṇuta* — hear; *me* — my; *tat* — that; *īkṣitam* — [which was] seen; *svapnataḥ* — in a dream; *yat* — which; *iti* — thus; *citram* — a wonder; *eva* — indeed; *tat* — that [is]; *aprameya* — immeasurable; *mahimā* — [whose] greatness [is]; *śacī-sutaḥ* — the son of Shachi; *pratyayaḥ* — conviction; *adya* — today; *khalu* — indeed; *kevalam* — complete; *āsīt* — has come.

**99.** "O brother and sister, hear what I saw in a dream: it is a wonder indeed! The son of Shachi is of immeasurable greatness — of this I have today become fully convinced.

### Verse 100

नीलशैलतिलकं विलोकयं-
स्तत्र स प्रविशति प्रतिक्षणम् ।
भूय एव बहिरेत्य पश्यति
प्रायशो व्यतनुतैवमेव सः ॥१००॥

*nīla-śaila-tilakaṁ vilokayaṁs*
*tatra sa praviśati pratikṣaṇam |*
*bhūya eva bahir etya paśyati*
*prāyaśo vyatanutaivam eva saḥ ||100||*

*Word for word:* *nīla-śaila* — of the Blue Mountain; *tilakam* — the tilaka; *vilokayan* — gazing at; *tatra* — there [into Him]; *saḥ* — He; *praviśati* — enters; *pratikṣaṇam* — at every moment; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *eva* — indeed; *bahiḥ* — outside; *etya* — having come; *paśyati* — looks; *prāyaśaḥ* — again and again; *vyatanuta* — did; *evam* — thus; *eva* — just; *saḥ* — He.

**100.** Gazing at the tilaka of the Blue Mountain, He enters there [into Him] at every moment; then, coming outside again, He looks [at Him]. Just so He did again and again.

*Note.* That is, the Lord enters into Jagannatha and comes out of Him again. The dream of Shikhi Mahiti is not in the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Antya 2.104–106 merely names him and his sister among the intimate associates); it is apparently known only from Karnapura.

### Verse 101

चित्रमेव बहुचित्रमेव तत्
सोऽधुनापि तदवस्थ ईक्ष्यते ।
ईश्वरः परमविभ्रमेक्षण-
भ्रान्तिभागिव विलोचनद्वयम् ॥१०१॥

*citram eva bahu-citram eva tat*
*so 'dhunāpi tad-avastha īkṣyate |*
*īśvaraḥ parama-vibhramekṣaṇa-*
*bhrānti-bhāg iva vilocana-dvayam ||101||*

*Word for word:* *citram* — a wonder; *eva* — indeed; *bahu-citram* — a great wonder; *eva* — indeed; *tat* — this [is]; *saḥ* — He; *adhunā* — now; *api* — even; *tat* — in that; *avasthaḥ* — state; *īkṣyate* — is seen; *īśvaraḥ* — the Lord; *parama* — supreme; *vibhrama* — of the play; *īkṣaṇa* — from beholding; *bhrānti* — in bewilderment; *bhāk* — sharing; *iva* — as if; *vilocana* — of eyes; *dvayam* — the pair.

**101.** A wonder, a great wonder indeed! Even now I see the Lord in that state. My two eyes seem bewildered from beholding [His] supreme play.

*Note.* The syntax of the second half is unclear (?). Perhaps the pair of eyes is the Lord's own: "[His] two eyes as if bewildered from beholding the supreme grace [of Jagannatha]" (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 102

मां च तन्निकटगं खलु नाम-
ग्राहमाश्लिषदसीमकृपाब्धिः ।
दीर्घपीवरभुजाद्वितयेन
श्रीमता ललितजानुगतेन ॥१०२॥

*māṁ ca tan-nikaṭagaṁ khalu nāma-*
*grāham āśliṣad asīma-kṛpābdhiḥ |*
*dīrgha-pīvara-bhujā-dvitayena*
*śrīmatā lalita-jānu-gatena ||102||*

*Word for word:* *mām* — me; *ca* — and; *tat* — to Him; *nikaṭa-gam* — come near; *khalu* — indeed; *nāma-grāham* — calling by name; *āśliṣat* — embraced; *asīma* — of boundless; *kṛpā* — mercy; *abdhiḥ* — the ocean; *dīrgha* — long; *pīvara* — mighty; *bhujā* — of arms; *dvitayena* — with the pair; *śrīmatā* — beautiful; *lalita* — gracefully; *jānu* — to the knees; *gatena* — reaching.

**102.** And when I came near Him, the ocean of boundless mercy called me by name and embraced me with His pair of beautiful arms — long, mighty, gracefully reaching to the knees."

### Verse 103

इत्थमुत्पुलकमङ्गमावह-
न्प्रेमगद्गदवचा महोत्सुकः ।
निर्यदम्बुनयनद्वयं वह-
न्निर्ववार निगदन्निदं न सः ॥१०३॥

*ittham utpulakam aṅgam āvahan*
*prema-gadgada-vacā mahotsukaḥ |*
*niryad-ambu-nayana-dvayaṁ vahan*
*nirvavāra nigadann idaṁ na saḥ ||103||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *utpulakam* — with hairs standing on end; *aṅgam* — body; *āvahan* — bearing; *prema* — from love; *gadgada* — faltering; *vacāḥ* — [whose] speech [was]; *mahā-utsukaḥ* — in great agitation; *niryat* — streaming; *ambu* — [with] water; *nayana* — of eyes; *dvayam* — the pair; *vahan* — having; *nirvavāra na* — did not cease; *nigadan* — repeating; *idam* — this; *saḥ* — he.

**103.** Thus, his body thrilling with hairs on end, his voice faltering with love, in great agitation, his two eyes streaming with tears, he did not cease repeating this.

### Verse 104

तन्निशम्य सुखमापतुरेतौ
तत्र गन्तुमवलोकितुमेनम् ।
नाथमादिदिशतुर्गतवन्तं
नीलशैलपतिमीक्षितुमेव ॥१०४॥

*tan niśamya sukham āpatur etau*
*tatra gantum avalokitum enam |*
*nātham ādidiśatur gatavantaṁ*
*nīla-śaila-patim īkṣitum eva ||104||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — this; *niśamya* — having heard; *sukham* — happiness; *āpatuḥ* — attained; *etau* — these two; *tatra* — there; *gantum* — to go; *avalokitum* — to see; *enam* — this; *nātham* — Master; *ādidiśatuḥ* — bade [him]; *gatavantam* — who had gone; *nīla-śaila* — of the Blue Mountain; *patim* — the Lord; *īkṣitum* — to behold; *eva* — indeed.

**104.** Hearing this, the two were filled with happiness and bade [him] go there to see the Master, who had gone to behold the Lord of the Blue Mountain.

### Verse 105

तत्तथेति चपलं त्रय एव

जग्मुरीक्षितुमतीव महान्तो
गौरचन्द्रचरणे कृतवाञ्छाः ॥१०५॥

*tat tatheti capalaṁ traya eva*
*bhrātaro 'sita-mahīdhara-nātham |*

*Word for word:* *tat tathā* — so be it; *iti* — thus [saying]; *capalam* — quickly; *trayaḥ* — the three; *eva* — indeed; *bhrātaraḥ* — siblings; *asita* — of the Dark; *mahīdhara* — Mountain; *nātham* — the Lord; *jagmuḥ* — went; *īkṣitum* — to behold; *atīva* — exceedingly; *mahāntaḥ* — great-hearted; *gauracandra* — of Gaurachandra; *caraṇe* — on the feet; *kṛta* — having set; *vāñchāḥ* — [their] longing.

**105.** Saying "So be it," the three siblings, exceedingly great-hearted, who had set their longing on the feet of Gaurachandra, quickly went to behold the Lord of the Dark Mountain.

### Verse 106

तत्र तौ मुदितमानसौ जग-
न्मोहने प्रथमतः शचीसुतम् ।
तं विलोक्य विगलद्विलोचन-
द्वन्द्ववारिझरमापतुर्मुदम् ॥१०६॥

*tatra tau mudita-mānasau jagan-*
*mohane prathamataḥ śacī-sutam |*
*taṁ vilokya vigalad-vilocana-*
*dvandva-vāri-jharam āpatur mudam ||106||*

*Word for word:* *tatra* — there; *tau* — the two; *mudita* — joyful; *mānasau* — [whose] hearts [were]; *jagan-mohane* — in the Jaganmohana; *prathamataḥ* — first of all; *śacī-sutam* — the son of Shachi; *tam* — Him; *vilokya* — having seen; *vigalat* — flowing; *vilocana* — of eyes; *dvandva* — of the pair; *vāri* — of water; *jharam* — [with] a stream; *āpatuḥ* — attained; *mudam* — joy.

**106.** There the two, their hearts joyful, first of all saw the son of Shachi in the Jaganmohana; and seeing Him, with streams of tears flowing from their eyes, they attained joy.

*Note.* The Jaganmohana is the hall in front of the sanctuary of the temple. In the edition the lines are wrongly divided: *तत्र तौ मुदितमानसौ– / जगन्मोहने…*; by the metre the boundary falls after *jagan-*.

### Verse 107

अग्रजः पुनरयं शिखिनामा

प्रेमहृष्टहृदयो व्यजनिष्ट ॥१०७॥

*agrajaḥ punar ayaṁ śikhi-nāmā*

*prema-hṛṣṭa-hṛdayo vyajaniṣṭa ||107||*

*Word for word:* *agrajaḥ* — the elder brother; *punaḥ* — and; *ayam* — this; *śikhi-nāmā* — named Shikhi; *svapnataḥ* — in the dream; *khalu* — indeed; *dadarśa* — had seen; *yathā* — as; *enam* — Him; *tam* — Him; *tathā eva* — just so; *parilokya* — having seen; *samantāt* — in every respect; *prema* — with love; *hṛṣṭa* — thrilled; *hṛdayaḥ* — [whose] heart [was]; *vyajaniṣṭa* — became.

**107.** And the elder brother, Shikhi by name, seeing Him in every respect just as he had seen Him in the dream, became thrilled at heart with love.

### Verse 108

सोऽपि भूरिकरुणोऽथ मुरारे-
रग्रजस्त्वमिति दोर्द्वितयेन ।
आलिलिङ्ग स च तन्मतिरासी-
न्मूर्तिमान् समुदयः सुखराशेः ॥१०८॥

*so 'pi bhūri-karuṇo 'tha murārer*
*agrajas tvam iti dor-dvitayena |*
*āliliṅga sa ca tan-matir āsīn*
*mūrtimān samudayaḥ sukha-rāśeḥ ||108||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ api* — He too; *bhūri* — abundantly; *karuṇaḥ* — merciful; *atha* — then; *murāreḥ* — of Murari; *agrajaḥ* — the elder brother; *tvam* — you [are]; *iti* — thus [saying]; *doḥ* — of arms; *dvitayena* — with the pair; *āliliṅga* — embraced; *saḥ* — he; *ca* — and; *tat* — on Him; *matiḥ* — [whose] mind [was fixed]; *āsīt* — became; *mūrtimān* — embodied; *samudayaḥ* — the gathering; *sukha* — of happiness; *rāśeḥ* — of a mass.

**108.** And He, the abundantly merciful, then said, "You are Murari's elder brother," and embraced him with both arms; and he, his mind fixed on Him, became [as it were] the embodied gathering of a mass of happiness.

### Verse 109

तत्प्रभृत्ययममुष्य पदाब्ज-

सर्वदैव निजदैवतमेनं
सेवते प्रतिदिनं गुरुभाग्यः ॥१०९॥

*tat-prabhṛty ayam amuṣya padābja-*

*sarvadaiva nija-daivatam enaṁ*

*Word for word:* *tat-prabhṛti* — from that time on; *ayam* — he; *amuṣya* — His; *pada* — of feet; *abja* — of the lotuses; *dvandva* — of the pair; *gandha* — of the fragrance; *lava* — by a particle; *vismṛta* — having forgotten; *sarvaḥ* — everything; *sarvadā* — always; *eva* — indeed; *nija* — as his own; *daivatam* — Deity; *enam* — Him; *sevate* — serves; *pratidinam* — every day; *guru* — great; *bhāgyaḥ* — [whose] fortune [is].

**109.** From that time on, having forgotten everything through a particle of the fragrance of His pair of lotus feet, he always, every day, serves Him as his own Deity — so great is his fortune.

*Note.* The edition gives the number without the second stroke: *॥१०९*.

### Verse 110

एवमेव पुरुषोत्तमभूमा-
वाचकर्ष सहसा सुरनद्याः ।
तीरभूमिवसतीन्निजलोका-

*Word for word:* *evam eva* — just so; *puruṣottama* — of Purushottama; *bhūmau* — to the land; *ācakarṣa* — drew; *sahasā* — suddenly; *sura-nadyāḥ* — of the river of the gods; *tīra* — of the banks; *bhūmi* — on the land; *vasatīn* — dwelling; *nija* — His own; *lokān* — people; *sneha* — by affection; *kṛṣṭa* — drawn; *hṛdayaḥ* — [whose] heart [was]; *karuṇā* — of compassion; *abdhiḥ* — the ocean.

**110.** Just so the ocean of compassion, His heart drawn by affection, suddenly drew to the land of Purushottama His own people who dwelt on the banks of the river of the gods.

*Note.* "The river of the gods" is the Ganga; that is, [He drew His devotees from] Bengal.

### Verse 111

अस्ति माधवपुरीति स कोऽपि

विष्णुभक्तिरस एव शरीरी

*Note.* Madhava Puri is Madhavendra Puri, the guru of Ishvara Puri. The form *-vatāraṇa-* (for *avatāraṇa*) is for the sake of the metre.

### Verse 112

शिष्यतामधिगतोऽस्य महात्मा

*Word for word:* *śiṣyatām* — discipleship; *adhigataḥ* — attained; *asya* — his; *mahātmā* — a great soul; *sūrya* — of suns; *koṭiḥ* — a myriad; *iva* — like; *nirmala* — spotless; *tejāḥ* — [whose] splendour [was]; *satya* — truthful; *vāk* — [whose] speech [was]; *śucitamaḥ* — most pure; *sa-rasa* — full of rasa; *ātmā* — [whose] heart [was]; *sāgarāt* — than the ocean; *duravagāha* — unfathomable; *gabhīraḥ* — deeper.

**112.** A great soul became his disciple — of spotless splendour like a myriad suns, truthful in speech, most pure, with a heart full of rasa, unfathomable, deeper than the ocean…

### Verse 113

ईश्वरः फणिपतेरवतारो
मूर्तिमानिव स भक्तिरसोऽभूत् ।

भूमिषु न्यसनमप्यतनिष्ट ॥११३॥

*īśvaraḥ phaṇi-pater avatāro*
*mūrtimān iva sa bhakti-raso 'bhūt |*
*pūjakaḥ samajaniṣṭa sa pūrvaṁ*
*bhūmiṣu nyasanam apy atanīṣṭa ||113||*

*Word for word:* *īśvaraḥ* — Ishvara; *phaṇi-pateḥ* — of the lord of serpents; *avatāraḥ* — an avatara; *mūrtimān* — embodied; *iva* — as if; *saḥ* — he; *bhakti* — of bhakti; *rasaḥ* — the rasa; *abhūt* — was; *pūjakaḥ* — a worshipper; *samajaniṣṭa* — became; *saḥ* — he; *pūrvam* — before; *bhūmiṣu* — across the lands; *nyasanam* — renunciation; *api* — also; *atanīṣṭa* — spread.

**113.** …Ishvara [Puri], an avatara of the lord of serpents; he was as if the rasa of bhakti embodied. He became a worshipper [of the Lord], and before [Him] he also spread renunciation across the lands.

*Note.* Ishvara Puri is the guru of Sri Chaitanya. "An avatara of the lord of serpents" (Shesha, Ananta): we have not found such an identification in the other sources available to us. The Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *sa pūrvaṁ bhūmiṣu* (*pūrvam* as a separate word, not "in the eastern lands"); we accept *pūrvam* — "before", "first". Verses 111–114 form one connected group.

### Verse 114

येन सार्धमभवत् समागमो
दक्षिणे प्रभुवरस्य निर्भरः ।
शीतलः स्थिरमतिः सहिष्णुता-
राशिरेव किमु मूर्तिमानभूत् ॥११४॥

*yena sārdham abhavat samāgamo*
*dakṣiṇe prabhu-varasya nirbharaḥ |*
*śītalaḥ sthira-matiḥ sahiṣṇutā-*
*rāśir eva kim u mūrtimān abhūt ||114||*

*Word for word:* *yena* — whom; *sārdham* — with; *abhavat* — there was; *samāgamaḥ* — a meeting; *dakṣiṇe* — in the south; *prabhu-varasya* — of the best of Lords; *nirbharaḥ* — full; *śītalaḥ* — cool; *sthira* — steady; *matiḥ* — [whose] mind [was]; *sahiṣṇutā* — of forbearance; *rāśiḥ* — the mass; *eva* — itself; *kim u* — was [he] not; *mūrtimān* — embodied; *abhūt* — was.

**114.** With him the best of Lords had in the south a meeting full [of joy]. Cool [of temper], steady of mind — was he not the very mass of forbearance embodied?

*Note.* Grammatically the verse might continue the description of Ishvara Puri. But the meeting in the south (13.14–16) was with Paramananda Puri. Perhaps verses 111–114 speak of the line of Madhavendra Puri, and "he" here is already Paramananda, who is named in verse 115. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 115

जगतां परमः प्रियः प्रभुः
परमानन्दपुरीति शब्दितः ।
अथ सोऽभिययावटाट्यया
तदकस्मात् सुरदीर्घिकातटम् ॥११५॥

*jagatāṁ paramaḥ priyaḥ prabhuḥ*
*paramānanda-purīti śabditaḥ |*
*atha so 'bhiyayāv aṭāṭyayā*
*tad akasmāt sura-dīrghikā-taṭam ||115||*

*Word for word:* *jagatām* — of the worlds; *paramaḥ* — the supreme; *priyaḥ* — beloved; *prabhuḥ* — master; *paramānanda-purī* — Paramananda Puri; *iti* — thus; *śabditaḥ* — called; *atha* — then; *saḥ* — he; *abhiyayau* — came; *aṭāṭyayā* — in [his] wandering; *tat* — at that time; *akasmāt* — by chance; *sura-dīrghikā* — of the river of the gods; *taṭam* — to the bank.

**115.** Then the master called Paramananda Puri, the supreme beloved of the worlds, in [the course of his] wandering came at that time by chance to the bank of the river of the gods.

*Note.* From here to v. 125, except v. 119, the metre is *viyoginī* (⏑⏑—⏑⏑—⏑—⏑— / ⏑⏑——⏑⏑—⏑—⏑—). "The river of the gods" (*sura-dīrghikā*) is the Ganga.

### Verse 116

अथ नाथविहारभूषितं
स नवद्वीपमुपेत्य सस्पृहः ।
कुतुकात् परमप्रभोरयं
निलये विश्रमणं चकार च ॥११६॥

*atha nātha-vihāra-bhūṣitaṁ*
*sa navadvīpam upetya saspṛhaḥ |*
*kutukāt parama-prabhor ayaṁ*
*nilaye viśramaṇaṁ cakāra ca ||116||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *nātha* — of the Master; *vihāra* — with the pastimes; *bhūṣitam* — adorned; *saḥ* — he; *navadvīpam* — Navadvipa; *upetya* — having reached; *sa-spṛhaḥ* — full of longing; *kutukāt* — eagerly; *parama-prabhoḥ* — of the Supreme Lord; *ayam* — he; *nilaye* — in the house; *viśramaṇam* — rest; *cakāra* — took; *ca* — and.

**116.** Then, full of longing, he reached Navadvipa, adorned with the pastimes of the Master, and eagerly took his rest in the house of the Supreme Lord.

### Verse 117

जननी जगतीत्रयस्य या
पृथिवीकोटिसहिष्णुरञ्जसा ।
सुरनद्यधिकातिपावनी
सततस्नेहमयी महाशया ॥११७॥

*jananī jagatī-trayasya yā*
*pṛthivī-koṭi-sahiṣṇur añjasā |*
*sura-nady-adhikāti-pāvanī*
*satata-sneha-mayī mahāśayā ||117||*

*Word for word:* *jananī* — the mother; *jagatī* — of the worlds; *trayasya* — of the three; *yā* — who; *pṛthivī* — of earths; *koṭi* — [like] myriads; *sahiṣṇuḥ* — forbearing; *añjasā* — truly; *sura-nadī* — the river of the gods; *adhika* — surpassing; *ati-pāvanī* — exceedingly purifying; *satata* — constant; *sneha* — of affection; *mayī* — full; *mahā-āśayā* — great-hearted.

**117.** She who is the mother of the three worlds, truly as forbearing as myriads of earths, purifying beyond the river of the gods, full of constant affection, great-hearted —

*Note.* Verses 117–118 form a pair (*yugmaka*; so marked in the edition). They speak of Shachi.

### Verse 118

ननु भक्तिसुधा तनूमयी किं
प्रियता किं ननु माधुरीमयी ।
तमवेक्ष्य तदैव भिक्षया सा
सुतभावादवृणोन्महामतिम् ॥११८॥ (युग्मकम्)

*nanu bhakti-sudhā tanū-mayī kiṁ*
*priyatā kiṁ nanu mādhurī-mayī |*
*tam avekṣya tadaiva bhikṣayā sā*
*suta-bhāvād avṛṇon mahā-matim ||118|| (yugmakam)*

*Word for word:* *nanu* — is not; *bhakti* — of bhakti; *sudhā* — the nectar; *tanū-mayī* — embodied; *kim* — [is she]; *priyatā* — love [itself]; *kim* — [is she]; *nanu* — or not; *mādhurī-mayī* — made of sweetness; *tam* — him; *avekṣya* — seeing; *tadā eva* — at once; *bhikṣayā* — with alms; *sā* — she; *suta* — of a son; *bhāvāt* — with the feeling; *avṛṇot* — honoured; *mahā-matim* — the great-minded one.

**118.** — is she not the nectar of bhakti embodied? Is she love itself? Is she not made of sweetness? Seeing him, the great-minded one, she at once honoured him with alms, feeling for him as for [her own] son.

*Note.* The first pada has 11 syllables instead of 10: *kiṁ* is superfluous or corrupt (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 119

अन्येद्युरेषोऽतिमहानुभावः
प्रभोः प्रियस्यालय एव हृष्टः ।
आचार्यरत्नस्य चकार भिक्षां
वसन् सुखं तस्य मुहुर्वितन्वन् ॥११९॥

*anyedyur eṣo 'ti-mahānubhāvaḥ*
*prabhoḥ priyasyālaya eva hṛṣṭaḥ |*
*ācārya-ratnasya cakāra bhikṣāṁ*
*vasan sukhaṁ tasya muhur vitanvan ||119||*

*Word for word:* *anyedyuḥ* — on another day; *eṣaḥ* — he; *ati* — exceedingly; *mahā-anubhāvaḥ* — magnanimous; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *priyasya* — of the beloved; *ālaye* — in the house; *eva* — indeed; *hṛṣṭaḥ* — joyful; *ācārya-ratnasya* — of Acharyaratna; *cakāra* — took; *bhikṣām* — alms; *vasan* — dwelling; *sukham* — joy; *tasya* — to him; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *vitanvan* — bestowing.

**119.** On another day this most magnanimous one, joyful, took alms from Acharyaratna, dwelling in the very house of that beloved of the Lord and again and again bestowing joy on him.

*Note.* Acharyaratna is Chandrashekhara Acharya, the Lord's maternal uncle. Metre *upajāti*.

### Verse 120

अथ कश्चन गौरचन्द्रम-
श्चरणप्रेमसुधासरस्वती ।
नितरां बहुधावगाहना-
न्मुहुरन्तर्बहिरेव तन्मयः ॥१२०॥

*atha kaścana gauracandramaś-*
*caraṇa-prema-sudhā-sarasvatī |*
*nitarāṁ bahudhāvagāhanān*
*muhur antar-bahir eva tan-mayaḥ ||120||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *kaścana* — a certain one; *gauracandramasaḥ* — of Gaurachandra; *caraṇa* — for the feet; *prema* — of love; *sudhā* — of the nectar; *sarasvatī* — the Sarasvati (the river); *nitarām* — deeply; *bahudhā* — many times; *avagāhanāt* — from bathing; *muhuḥ* — constantly; *antaḥ* — within; *bahiḥ* — without; *eva* — indeed; *tat-mayaḥ* — filled with it.

**120.** Then a certain one — who, from bathing deeply and many times in the Sarasvati, the river of the nectar of love for the feet of Gaurachandra, was constantly filled with it within and without —

### Verse 121

दयितोऽस्य महान्महामतिः
कमलानन्द इति प्रकीर्तितः ।
निजगाम च तत्र सत्वरं
जननीं तामवलोकितुं मुदा ॥१२१॥

*dayito 'sya mahān mahā-matiḥ*
*kamalānanda iti prakīrtitaḥ |*
*nijagāma ca tatra satvaraṁ*
*jananīṁ tām avalokituṁ mudā ||121||*

*Word for word:* *dayitaḥ* — dear; *asya* — to Him; *mahān* — great; *mahā-matiḥ* — great-minded; *kamalānandaḥ* — Kamalananda; *iti* — thus; *prakīrtitaḥ* — named; *nijagāma* — came; *ca* — and; *tatra* — there; *satvaram* — in haste; *jananīm* — the Mother; *tām* — that; *avalokitum* — to see; *mudā* — joyfully.

**121.** — dear to Him, great and great-minded, named Kamalananda, came there in haste, joyfully, to see that Mother.

*Note.* Kamalananda is named in the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Adi 10.149) among the Bengali servants of the Lord who later settled with Him in Puri (together with Singabhatta, Kamabhatta and Shivananda); nothing more is known of him.

### Verse 122

जननीं परिलोक्य तं पुनः
परमानन्दपुरीं प्रभुं ततः ।
स ददर्श तथास्य दर्शना-
त्परमस्निग्धमतिर्बभूव सः ॥१२२॥

*jananīṁ parilokya taṁ punaḥ*
*paramānanda-purīṁ prabhuṁ tataḥ |*
*sa dadarśa tathāsya darśanāt*
*parama-snigdha-matir babhūva saḥ ||122||*
