*Word for word:* *jananīm* — the Mother; *parilokya* — having seen; *tam* — that; *punaḥ* — in turn; *paramānanda-purīm* — Paramananda Puri; *prabhum* — the master; *tataḥ* — then; *saḥ* — he; *dadarśa* — saw; *tathā* — and; *asya* — of him; *darśanāt* — from the sight; *parama* — supremely; *snigdha* — tender; *matiḥ* — [whose] heart [was]; *babhūva* — became; *saḥ* — he.

**122.** Having seen the Mother, he then in turn saw that master, Paramananda Puri, and from the sight of him he became supremely tender-hearted.

### Verse 123

कतिचिच्च दिनानि तत्र ते
गमयित्वा युगपत्तथा ययुः ।
स गदाधरपण्डितोऽप्ययं
जगदानन्दमहाशयोऽपि च ॥१२३॥

*katicic ca dināni tatra te*
*gamayitvā yugapat tathā yayuḥ |*
*sa gadādhara-paṇḍito 'py ayaṁ*
*jagadānanda-mahāśayo 'pi ca ||123||*

*Word for word:* *katicit* — some; *ca* — and; *dināni* — days; *tatra* — there; *te* — they; *gamayitvā* — having spent; *yugapat* — together; *tathā* — so; *yayuḥ* — set out; *saḥ* — that; *gadādhara-paṇḍitaḥ* — Gadadhara Pandita; *api* — also; *ayam* — this; *jagadānanda* — Jagadananda; *mahāśayaḥ* — the noble; *api ca* — and also.

**123.** Having spent some days there, they set out together — and with them that Gadadhara Pandita, and also this noble Jagadananda.

*Note.* In the Chaitanya-charitamrita the Lord's companions on the way to Puri are Nityananda, Jagadananda, Damodara and Mukunda (Madhya 3.209); Gadadhara is named among the Bengali devotees who came for the first Ratha-yatra (Madhya 11.84), and afterwards he stays with the Lord in Puri (15.183). The Mahakavya itself, in 11.76, already names Gadadhara among the Lord's companions on the way to Puri, and here he comes again — with Paramananda Puri.

### Verse 124

यतिराट् स तु गौरसुन्दर-
प्रभुसन्दर्शनभाग्यसोत्सुकः ।
पुरुषोत्तममुत्तमं ययुः
समुपेत्याददृशुः प्रभुं ततः ॥१२४॥

*yati-rāṭ sa tu gaura-sundara-*
*prabhu-sandarśana-bhāgya-sotsukaḥ |*
*puruṣottamam uttamaṁ yayuḥ*
*samupetyādadṛśuḥ prabhuṁ tataḥ ||124||*

*Word for word:* *yati-rāṭ* — the king of ascetics; *saḥ tu* — he; *gaura-sundara* — Gaurasundara; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *sandarśana* — of the sight; *bhāgya* — for the good fortune; *sa-utsukaḥ* — full of eagerness; *puruṣottamam* — to Purushottama; *uttamam* — the supreme; *yayuḥ* — [they] went; *samupetya* — having arrived; *adadṛśuḥ* — [they] saw; *prabhum* — the Lord; *tataḥ* — then.

**124.** That king of ascetics was full of eagerness for the good fortune of seeing the Lord Gaurasundara; [they all] went to the supreme Purushottama and, having arrived, then saw the Lord.

*Note.* The subject is singular, but the verbs are plural: *yayuḥ*, *adadṛśuḥ*.

### Verse 125

अथ गौरमहाप्रभोः पद-
द्वयपद्मं यतिराड् व्यलोकयत् ।
अनमत् स्वयमीश्वरोऽपि तं
स्थविरत्वेन कृतादरोदयः ॥१२५॥

*atha gaura-mahāprabhoḥ pada-*
*dvaya-padmaṁ yati-rāḍ vyalokayat |*
*anamat svayam īśvaro 'pi taṁ*
*sthaviratvena kṛtādarodayaḥ ||125||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *gaura-mahāprabhoḥ* — of Gaura Mahaprabhu; *pada* — of feet; *dvaya* — the pair; *padmam* — lotus; *yati-rāṭ* — the king of ascetics; *vyalokayat* — beheld; *anamat* — bowed down; *svayam* — Himself; *īśvaraḥ* — the Lord; *api* — even; *tam* — to him; *sthaviratvena* — as to an elder; *kṛta* — showing; *ādara* — of respect; *udayaḥ* — an abundance.

**125.** Then the king of ascetics beheld the pair of lotus feet of Gaura Mahaprabhu. And the Lord Himself even bowed down to him, showing him abundant respect as an elder.

*Note.* In the edition there is a superfluous danda at the end of the verse: *। ॥१२५॥*.

### Verse 126

आचार्यविद्यानिधिरप्यसीम-
गुणाम्बुधिः प्रेममयः सुखात्मा ।
आचार्यरत्नं महितो महात्मा
महानुभावोऽपि ययौ तथैव ॥१२६॥

*ācārya-vidyānidhir apy asīma-*
*guṇāmbudhiḥ prema-mayaḥ sukhātmā |*
*ācārya-ratnaṁ [-ratno?] mahito mahātmā*
*mahānubhāvo 'pi yayau tathaiva ||126||*

*Word for word:* *ācārya-vidyānidhiḥ* — Acharya Vidyanidhi; *api* — also; *asīma* — boundless; *guṇa* — of virtues; *ambudhiḥ* — an ocean; *prema-mayaḥ* — full of love; *sukha* — blissful; *ātmā* — [whose] soul [was]; *ācārya-ratnam* (*-ratnaḥ*?) — Acharyaratna; *mahitaḥ* — honoured; *mahātmā* — the great soul; *mahā-anubhāvaḥ* — magnanimous; *api* — also; *yayau* — came; *tathā eva* — likewise.

**126.** Acharya Vidyanidhi too came likewise — a boundless ocean of virtues, full of love, blissful of soul — and also the honoured, magnanimous Acharyaratna, the great soul.

*Note.* Vidyanidhi is Pundarika Vidyanidhi. The edition reads *आचार्यरत्नं* (accusative) — apparently a misprint for *ācāryaratnaḥ*. The metre of vv. 126–127 is *upajāti*. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 127

मुरारिगुप्तेन समं प्रयातः
श्रीमान् शिवानन्द इति प्रसिद्धः ।
व्यलोकयत्तत् प्रथमं तमीशं
स्वसौभगस्तोममिवाथ मूर्तम् ॥१२७॥

*murāri-guptena samaṁ prayātaḥ*
*śrīmān śivānanda iti prasiddhaḥ |*
*vyalokayat tat prathamaṁ tam īśaṁ*
*sva-saubhaga-stomam ivātha mūrtam ||127||*

*Word for word:* *murāri-guptena* — with Murari Gupta; *samam* — together; *prayātaḥ* — having come; *śrīmān* — the glorious; *śivānandaḥ* — Shivananda; *iti* — thus; *prasiddhaḥ* — known; *vyalokayat* — saw; *tat* — then; *prathamam* — for the first time; *tam* — that; *īśam* — Lord; *sva* — of his own; *saubhaga* — of good fortune; *stomam* — the heap; *iva* — as if; *atha* — and; *mūrtam* — embodied.

**127.** The glorious one known as Shivananda, having come together with Murari Gupta, then saw that Lord for the first time — as if the heap of his own good fortune embodied.

*Note.* Shivananda Sena is the father of Kavi Karnapura.

### Verse 128

स तु दीनदयार्द्रमानस-
श्चरणाङ्गुष्ठदलेन तच्छिरः ।
मुहुरस्पृशदूचिवानिदं
ननु जानामि भवन्तमित्यपि ॥१२८॥

*sa tu dīna-dayārdra-mānasaś*
*caraṇāṅguṣṭha-dalena tac-chiraḥ |*
*muhur aspṛśad ūcivān idaṁ*
*nanu jānāmi bhavantam ity api ||128||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ tu* — and He; *dīna* — for the wretched; *dayā* — with compassion; *ārdra* — softened; *mānasaḥ* — [whose] heart [was]; *caraṇa* — of the foot; *aṅguṣṭha* — of the big toe; *dalena* — with the petal; *tat* — his; *śiraḥ* — head; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *aspṛśat* — touched; *ūcivān* — said; *idam* — this; *nanu* — surely; *jānāmi* — I know; *bhavantam* — you; *iti* — thus; *api* — also.

**128.** And He, His heart softened with compassion for the wretched, again and again touched his head with the petal of His big toe, and also said this: "Surely I know you."

*Note.* Here *viyoginī* resumes. Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Antya 1.15–32: every year Shivananda Sena leads the Bengali devotees to Puri and takes care of everyone on the way, even of a stray dog.

### Verse 129

सुकृती कृतपुण्यसञ्चय-
स्तदनु प्रेममयः स राघवः ।
रभसेन ददर्श तं क्षणात्
करुणार्द्रः करुणां चकार सः ॥१२९॥

*sukṛtī kṛta-puṇya-sañcayas*
*tad-anu prema-mayaḥ sa rāghavaḥ |*
*rabhasena dadarśa taṁ kṣaṇāt*
*karuṇārdraḥ karuṇāṁ cakāra saḥ ||129||*

*Word for word:* *sukṛtī* — the righteous; *kṛta* — who had gathered; *puṇya* — of merits; *sañcayaḥ* — a store; *tat-anu* — after that; *prema-mayaḥ* — full of love; *saḥ* — that; *rāghavaḥ* — Raghava; *rabhasena* — impetuously; *dadarśa* — saw; *tam* — Him; *kṣaṇāt* — at once; *karuṇā* — with mercy; *ārdraḥ* — softened; *karuṇām* — mercy; *cakāra* — showed; *saḥ* — He.

**129.** After that the righteous Raghava, who had gathered a store of merits, full of love, impetuously [came and] saw Him; and He, softened with mercy, at once showed him mercy.

*Note.* Raghava Pandita of Panihati.

### Verse 130

अथ शुद्धमतिर्महाशयः स
तु गोविन्द इति प्रकीर्तितः ।
बहुतीर्थपरिभ्रमाद्बहिः
सुमहान् पुण्यपयोनिधिर्ययौ ॥१३०॥

*atha śuddha-matir mahāśayaḥ sa*
*tu govinda iti prakīrtitaḥ |*
*bahu-tīrtha-paribhramād bahiḥ*
*sumahān puṇya-payonidhir yayau ||130||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *śuddha* — pure; *matiḥ* — [whose] mind [was]; *mahāśayaḥ* — noble; *saḥ tu* — he; *govindaḥ* — Govinda; *iti* — thus; *prakīrtitaḥ* — named; *bahu* — many; *tīrtha* — through holy places; *paribhramāt* — after wandering; *bahiḥ* — abroad; *sumahān* — very great; *puṇya* — of merit; *payonidhiḥ* — an ocean; *yayau* — came.

**130.** Then a noble one of pure mind named Govinda, a very great ocean of merit, after wandering abroad through many holy places, came —

*Note.* Verses 130–131 form a pair (*yugmaka*). Govinda is the Lord's personal servant. In the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 10.131–148) he comes at the order of his guru Ishvara Puri. The first pada has 11 syllables: metrically *sa* belongs to the beginning of the second.

### Verse 131

पुरुषोत्तममेव तत्र तं
दयितं गौरकृपामहानिधिम् ।
स ददर्श च पादपद्मयोः
परिचर्यासु रतोऽभवन्मुहुः ॥१३१॥ (युग्मकम्)

*puruṣottamam eva tatra taṁ*
*dayitaṁ gaura-kṛpā-mahā-nidhim |*
*sa dadarśa ca pāda-padmayoḥ*
*paricaryāsu rato 'bhavan muhuḥ ||131|| (yugmakam)*

*Word for word:* *puruṣottamam* — to Purushottama; *eva* — indeed; *tatra* — there; *tam* — that; *dayitam* — Beloved; *gaura* — Gaura; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *mahā* — the great; *nidhim* — treasure-house; *saḥ* — he; *dadarśa* — saw; *ca* — and; *pāda* — of the feet; *padmayoḥ* — of the lotus; *paricaryāsu* — to the services; *rataḥ* — devoted; *abhavat* — became; *muhuḥ* — constantly.

**131.** — to Purushottama. There he saw that Beloved, Gaura, the great treasure-house of mercy, and became constantly devoted to the service of His lotus feet.

### Verse 132

अयमप्यतिभाग्यवांस्ततः
प्रभृति श्रीप्रभुपादपद्मयोः ।
निकटस्थ इतो दिवानिशं
परिचर्यामकरोद्गतक्रियः ॥१३२॥

*ayam apy ati-bhāgyavāṁs tataḥ*
*prabhṛti śrī-prabhu-pāda-padmayoḥ |*
*nikaṭa-stha ito divā-niśaṁ*
*paricaryām akarod gata-kriyaḥ ||132||*

*Word for word:* *ayam* — he; *api* — too; *ati* — very; *bhāgyavān* — fortunate; *tataḥ prabhṛti* — from then on; *śrī-prabhu* — of the Lord; *pāda* — of the feet; *padmayoḥ* — of the lotus; *nikaṭa-sthaḥ* — staying near; *itaḥ* — here; *divā-niśam* — day and night; *paricaryām* — service; *akarot* — rendered; *gata* — given up; *kriyaḥ* — [whose other] activities [were].

**132.** And this very fortunate one too, from then on staying here near the lotus feet of the Lord and having given up [all other] activities, rendered [Him] service day and night.

### Verse 133

अथ शुद्धमतिर्महाशयो
गुणवान् सच्चरितस्तदा प्रभुम् ।
प्रददर्श सुखौघभूषितः
स भवानन्द इति प्रकीर्तितः ॥१३३॥

*atha śuddha-matir mahāśayo*
*guṇavān sac-caritas tadā prabhum |*
*pradadarśa sukhaugha-bhūṣitaḥ*
*sa bhavānanda iti prakīrtitaḥ ||133||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *śuddha* — pure; *matiḥ* — [whose] mind [was]; *mahāśayaḥ* — noble; *guṇavān* — virtuous; *sat* — righteous; *caritaḥ* — [whose] conduct [was]; *tadā* — then; *prabhum* — the Lord; *pradadarśa* — beheld; *sukha* — of happiness; *ogha* — with floods; *bhūṣitaḥ* — adorned; *saḥ* — that; *bhavānandaḥ* — Bhavananda; *iti* — thus; *prakīrtitaḥ* — named.

**133.** Then a noble one of pure mind, virtuous and of righteous conduct, named Bhavananda, adorned with floods of happiness, beheld the Lord.

*Note.* Bhavananda Raya is the father of Ramananda.

### Verse 134

प्रभुरप्यतिशुद्धमानसं
भुजयुग्मेन दृढं समाश्लिषत् ।
अयि पाण्डुसमोऽसि भाग्यवा-
निति वाचं मधुरां जगाद च ॥१३४॥

*prabhur apy ati-śuddha-mānasaṁ*
*bhuja-yugmena dṛḍhaṁ samāśliṣat |*
*ayi pāṇḍu-samo 'si bhāgyavān*
*iti vācaṁ madhurāṁ jagāda ca ||134||*

*Word for word:* *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *api* — too; *ati* — very; *śuddha* — pure; *mānasam* — [him whose] heart [was]; *bhuja* — of arms; *yugmena* — with the pair; *dṛḍham* — firmly; *samāśliṣat* — embraced; *ayi* — O; *pāṇḍu* — to Pandu; *samaḥ* — equal; *asi* — you are; *bhāgyavān* — fortunate; *iti* — thus; *vācam* — words; *madhurām* — sweet; *jagāda* — spoke; *ca* — and.

**134.** And the Lord firmly embraced with both arms [him] whose heart was very pure, and spoke sweet words: "O, you are as fortunate as Pandu!"

*Note.* Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 10.51–53: the Lord calls Bhavananda Pandu, his wife Kunti, and his five sons the Pandavas.

### Verse 135

अथास्य पुत्रा अपि पञ्च रामा-
नन्दादयोऽस्यैव महाकृपालोः ।
अतिप्रिया एव बभूवुरञ्जः
पार्श्वस्थिताः सेवनमेव कृत्वा ॥१३५॥

*athāsya putrā api pañca rāmā-*
*nandādayo 'syaiva mahā-kṛpāloḥ |*
*ati-priyā eva babhūvur añjaḥ*
*pārśva-sthitāḥ sevanam eva kṛtvā ||135||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — and; *asya* — his; *putrāḥ* — sons; *api* — also; *pañca* — five; *rāmānanda-ādayaḥ* — Ramananda and the others; *asya* — to Him; *eva* — indeed; *mahā* — great; *kṛpāloḥ* — to the Merciful One; *ati* — very; *priyāḥ* — dear; *eva* — indeed; *babhūvuḥ* — became; *añjaḥ* — truly; *pārśva* — at the side; *sthitāḥ* — staying; *sevanam* — service; *eva* — just; *kṛtvā* — rendering.

**135.** And his five sons too, Ramananda and the others, staying at the side of that greatly Merciful One and rendering [Him] service, truly became very dear to Him.

*Note.* The metre of vv. 135–137 is *upajāti*.

### Verse 136

मृदुर्महात्मा परमप्रियोऽसौ
शान्तः सुहृत् सर्वजनस्य शश्वत् ।
चैतन्यचन्द्राङ्घ्रिरतश्च वाणी-
नाथस्तमेव प्रतिसेवमानः ॥१३६॥

*mṛdur mahātmā parama-priyo 'sau*
*śāntaḥ suhṛt sarva-janasya śaśvat |*
*caitanya-candrāṅghri-rataś ca vāṇī-*
*nāthas tam eva pratisevamānaḥ ||136||*

*Word for word:* *mṛduḥ* — gentle; *mahātmā* — a great soul; *parama* — supremely; *priyaḥ* — dear; *asau* — he; *śāntaḥ* — peaceful; *suhṛt* — the friend; *sarva* — of all; *janasya* — people; *śaśvat* — ever; *caitanya-candra* — of Chaitanya-chandra; *aṅghri* — to the feet; *rataḥ* — devoted; *ca* — and; *vāṇīnāthaḥ* — Vaninatha; *tam* — Him; *eva* — indeed; *pratisevamānaḥ* — serving.

**136.** Gentle, a great soul, supremely dear, peaceful, ever the friend of all people, devoted to the feet of Chaitanya-chandra — [such was] Vaninatha, who served Him.

*Note.* Vaninatha Pattanayaka is one of Bhavananda's sons.

### Verse 137

आचार्ययुक्तः पुरुषोत्तमाख्यो
महामतिः कश्चन चारुशीलः ।
श्रुत्वा तदीयं चरितं प्रयत्ना-
द्ययौ तमेवेक्षितुमुत्सुकात्मा ॥१३७॥

*ācārya-yuktaḥ puruṣottamākhyo*
*mahā-matiḥ kaścana cāru-śīlaḥ |*
*śrutvā tadīyaṁ caritaṁ prayatnād*
*yayau tam evekṣitum utsukātmā ||137||*

*Word for word:* *ācārya* — [the title] "acharya"; *yuktaḥ* — bearing; *puruṣottama* — Purushottama; *ākhyaḥ* — named; *mahā-matiḥ* — great-minded; *kaścana* — a certain; *cāru* — lovely; *śīlaḥ* — [whose] character [was]; *śrutvā* — having heard; *tadīyam* — His; *caritam* — deeds; *prayatnāt* — with effort; *yayau* — came; *tam* — Him; *eva* — indeed; *īkṣitum* — to see; *utsuka* — eager; *ātmā* — [whose] heart [was].

**137.** A certain great-minded one of lovely character, named Purushottama and bearing the title of Acharya, having heard of His deeds, came with effort, eager at heart, to see Him.

*Note.* The future Svarupa Damodara (see v. 143). Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 10.102–125.

### Verse 138

पुरुषोत्तममेत्य विह्वलः
प्रददर्शाथ कृपानिधेः पदम् ।
स तु दर्शनमात्रकौतुका-
दभवत् कीदृश एव सम्मतः ॥१३८॥

*puruṣottamam etya vihvalaḥ*
*pradadarśātha kṛpā-nidheḥ padam |*
*sa tu darśana-mātra-kautukād*
*abhavat kīdṛśa eva sammataḥ ||138||*

*Word for word:* *puruṣottamam* — to Purushottama; *etya* — having come; *vihvalaḥ* — overwhelmed; *pradadarśa* — beheld; *atha* — then; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *nidheḥ* — of the treasure-house; *padam* — the feet; *saḥ tu* — and he; *darśana* — of the sight; *mātra* — mere; *kautukāt* — from the delight; *abhavat* — became; *kīdṛśaḥ eva* — of what kind [one cannot say]; *sammataḥ* — esteemed (?).

**138.** Having come to Purushottama, he then, overwhelmed, beheld the feet of the treasure-house of mercy. And from the mere delight of seeing [them] he became — who can say what?

*Note.* *Sammataḥ* at the end is unclear (?). Perhaps: "he became esteemed [by the Lord] in a way beyond words" (?). The metre of vv. 138–144 is *viyoginī*. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 139

तनुरप्यहहैव विस्मृता
रसमात्रं सुखमात्रमीक्षितम् ।
अपि जीवितनाथदर्शना-
ज्जडता तेन सदैव संश्रिता ॥१३९॥

*tanur apy ahahaiva vismṛtā*
*rasa-mātraṁ sukha-mātram īkṣitam |*
*api jīvita-nātha-darśanāj*
*jaḍatā tena sadaiva saṁśritā ||139||*

*Word for word:* *tanuḥ* — the body; *api* — even; *ahaha* — ah; *eva* — indeed; *vismṛtā* — was forgotten; *rasa* — rasa; *mātram* — only; *sukha* — happiness; *mātram* — only; *īkṣitam* — was seen; *api* — and; *jīvita* — of [his] life; *nātha* — of the Lord; *darśanāt* — from the sight; *jaḍatā* — stupor; *tena* — by him; *sadā* — always; *eva* — indeed; *saṁśritā* — was entered into.

**139.** Ah, even [his] body was forgotten! Only rasa, only happiness was seen [by him]. And from the sight of the Lord of his life he was always overcome by stupor.

### Verse 140

अथ नयने जलनिर्झराकुले
वपुरुद्यत्पुलकैकभूषितम् ।
पृथुवेपथुभङ्गभङ्गुरं
गुरुमूरुद्वितयं तदादधे ॥१४०॥

*atha nayane jala-nirjharākule*
*vapur udyat-pulakaika-bhūṣitam |*
*pṛthu-vepathu-bhaṅga-bhaṅguraṁ*
*gurum ūru-dvitayaṁ tadā dadhe ||140||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *nayane* — two eyes; *jala* — of water; *nirjhara* — with cascades; *ākule* — filled; *vapuḥ* — a body; *udyat* — rising; *pulaka* — with hairs standing on end; *eka* — solely; *bhūṣitam* — adorned; *pṛthu* — with violent; *vepathu* — trembling; *bhaṅga* — breaking; *bhaṅguram* — giving way; *guru* — heavy; *ūru* — of thighs; *dvitayam* — a pair; *tadā* — then; *dadhe* — he bore.

**140.** Then he bore eyes filled with cascades of tears, a body adorned solely with hairs rising on end, and a heavy pair of thighs breaking and giving way under violent trembling.

*Note.* The first pada has 12 syllables instead of 10. Without *atha* the metre is correct: *nayane jala-nirjharākule* (?). The end of the verse (*गुरुमूरुद्वितयं*) is *gurum ūru-dvitayam*; so too in the Gosvami edition (GGM).

### Verse 141

दयितेक्षणभावभाविता
दयितैवाभवदेष भावितः ।
अयमप्यतिकोमलोऽभवत्
प्रियताभिः प्रियतैकसागरः ॥१४१॥

*dayitekṣaṇa-bhāva-bhāvitā*
*dayitaivābhavad eṣa bhāvitaḥ |*
*ayam apy ati-komalo 'bhavat*
*priyatābhiḥ priyataika-sāgaraḥ ||141||*

*Word for word:* *dayita* — of the beloved; *īkṣaṇa* — by the glance; *bhāva* — with emotion; *bhāvitā* — filled; *dayitā* — the beloved [maiden]; *eva* — very; *abhavat* — became; *eṣaḥ* — he; *bhāvitaḥ* — filled [with emotion]; *ayam* — He; *api* — too; *ati* — very; *komalaḥ* — tender; *abhavat* — became; *priyatābhiḥ* — by [these] displays of love; *priyatā* — of love; *eka* — the sole; *sāgaraḥ* — ocean.

**141.** Filled with emotion, he became the very beloved [maiden] filled with emotion by her lover's glance. And He too, the sole ocean of love, became very tender through [these] displays of love.

### Verse 142

बहुधा मधुरां श्रियं प्रभुः
परिलोच्याशु बभूव कोमलः ।
नितरामकरोदमुत्र च
प्रथितं प्रेम महारसाम्बुधिः ॥१४२॥

*bahudhā madhurāṁ śriyaṁ prabhuḥ*
*parilocyāśu babhūva komalaḥ |*
*nitarām akarod amutra ca*
*prathitaṁ prema mahā-rasāmbudhiḥ ||142||*

*Word for word:* *bahudhā* — in manifold ways; *madhurām* — sweet; *śriyam* — beauty; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *parilocya* — beholding; *āśu* — at once; *babhūva* — became; *komalaḥ* — tender; *nitarām* — deeply; *akarot* — showed; *amutra* — toward him; *ca* — and; *prathitam* — renowned; *prema* — love; *mahā* — of great; *rasa* — rasa; *ambudhiḥ* — the ocean.

**142.** Beholding [in him] such sweet beauty [of emotion], manifold, the Lord at once became tender; and He, the ocean of great rasa, showed him a deep and renowned love.

### Verse 143

अभजिष्ट तदा सदाशयः
स तु सन्न्यासमदभ्रभाग्यवान् ।
अगमत्तु रसस्वरूपता-
मिह दामोदर इत्युदीरितः ॥१४३॥

*abhajiṣṭa tadā sadāśayaḥ*
*sa tu sannyāsam adabhra-bhāgyavān |*
*agamat tu rasa-svarūpatām*
*iha dāmodara ity udīritaḥ ||143||*

*Word for word:* *abhajiṣṭa* — accepted; *tadā* — then; *sat* — good; *āśayaḥ* — [whose] disposition [was]; *saḥ tu* — and he; *sannyāsam* — sannyasa; *adabhra* — no small; *bhāgyavān* — possessing fortune; *agamat* — attained; *tu* — and; *rasa* — of rasa; *svarūpatām* — the very nature (*svarūpa*); *iha* — here; *dāmodaraḥ* — Damodara; *iti* — thus; *udīritaḥ* — called.

**143.** Then he, of good disposition and of no small fortune, accepted sannyasa and attained the very nature (*svarūpa*) of rasa; here he is called Damodara.

*Note.* A play on words: *rasa-svarūpatā* ("the very nature of rasa") hints at the name Svarupa Damodara. According to the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 10.103–109), Purushottama Acharya took sannyasa in Varanasi from Chaitanyananda Bharati without putting on saffron cloth, changing only his name (to Svarupa), and then, with his guru's permission, came to Puri.

### Verse 144

इति तेन निरन्तरं प्रभोः
पदपाथोजसमीपसङ्गतः ।
निमिषं सहते स्म नो दृशोः
परिपश्यन्निव तृष्णया पिबन् ॥१४४॥

*iti tena nirantaraṁ prabhoḥ*
*pada-pāthoja-samīpa-saṅgataḥ |*
*nimiṣaṁ sahate sma no dṛśoḥ*
*paripaśyann iva tṛṣṇayā piban ||144||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *tena* — by him (?); *nirantaram* — constantly; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *pada* — of the feet; *pāthoja* — of the lotuses; *samīpa* — near; *saṅgataḥ* — staying; *nimiṣam* — the blinking; *sahate sma* — tolerated; *no* — not; *dṛśoḥ* — of the eyes; *paripaśyan* — gazing; *iva* — as if; *tṛṣṇayā* — with thirst; *piban* — drinking.

**144.** Thus, staying constantly near the lotus feet of the Lord, he could not bear even the blinking of his eyes, gazing [at Him] as if drinking [Him] in with thirst.

*Note.* *Tena* is syntactically superfluous; perhaps a corruption (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 145

श्रीवक्रेश्वरपण्डितोऽतिमधुरः कश्चिन्महात्मा सदा
सान्द्रानन्दरसामृतोदधिरिति प्रेमास्पदं श्रीप्रभोः ।
आगत्याथ विलोक्य चाभवदयं यस्यास्य नृत्योद्गमे
सोऽयं गौरमहाप्रभुः प्रवणतां यातः स्वयं सर्वदा ॥१४५॥

*śrī-vakreśvara-paṇḍito 'ti-madhuraḥ kaścin mahātmā sadā*
*sāndrānanda-rasāmṛtodadhir iti premāspadaṁ śrī-prabhoḥ |*
*āgatyātha vilokya cābhavad ayaṁ yasyāsya nṛtyodgame*
*so 'yaṁ gaura-mahāprabhuḥ pravaṇatāṁ yātaḥ svayaṁ sarvadā ||145||*

*Word for word:* *śrī-vakreśvara-paṇḍitaḥ* — Sri Vakreshvara Pandita; *ati-madhuraḥ* — most sweet; *kaścit* — a certain; *mahātmā* — great soul; *sadā* — ever; *sāndra* — of dense; *ānanda* — bliss; *rasa* — of the rasa; *amṛta* — of the nectar; *udadhiḥ* — an ocean; *iti* — thus [being]; *prema* — of the love; *āspadam* — the abode; *śrī-prabhoḥ* — of Sri Prabhu; *āgatya* — having come; *atha* — then; *vilokya* — having beheld [Him]; *ca* — and; *abhavat* — became; *ayam* — he; *yasya asya* — at whose; *nṛtya* — of the dance; *udgame* — at the outset; *saḥ ayam* — this very; *gaura-mahāprabhuḥ* — Gaura Mahaprabhu; *pravaṇatām* — tender inclination; *yātaḥ* — attained; *svayam* — Himself; *sarvadā* — always.

**145.** Sri Vakreshvara Pandita — a certain most sweet great soul, ever an ocean of the nectar of the rasa of dense bliss, and so the abode of the love of Sri Prabhu — came, beheld [Him], and became one at the very outset of whose dancing Gaura Mahaprabhu Himself would always be tenderly inclined [toward him].

*Note.* Metre *śārdūla-vikrīḍita*. Vakreshvara was renowned for his dancing at kirtanas; cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 10.17: he could dance in unbroken ecstasy for seventy-two hours.

### Verse 146

श्रीवासुदेव इति दत्तकुलैकरत्नं
गौराङ्गचन्द्रमवलोक्य झटित्यमन्दम् ।
शश्वद्बभूव खलु जीवननिर्विशेषो
निःशेषतत्प्रणयसिन्धुनिमग्न एषः ॥१४६॥

*śrī-vāsudeva iti datta-kulaika-ratnaṁ*
*gaurāṅga-candram avalokya jhaṭity amandam |*
*śaśvad babhūva khalu jīvana-nirviśeṣo*
*niḥśeṣa-tat-praṇaya-sindhu-nimagna eṣaḥ ||146||*

*Word for word:* *śrī-vāsudevaḥ* — Sri Vasudeva; *iti* — by name; *datta* — of the Dattas; *kula* — of the family; *eka* — the one; *ratnam* — jewel; *gaurāṅga-candram* — Gauranga-chandra; *avalokya* — having seen; *jhaṭiti* — at once; *amandam* — wholly; *śaśvat* — for ever; *babhūva* — became; *khalu* — truly; *jīvana* — from [His] life; *nirviśeṣaḥ* — not different; *niḥśeṣa* — entirely; *tat* — in His; *praṇaya* — of love; *sindhu* — the ocean; *nimagnaḥ* — immersed; *eṣaḥ* — he.

**146.** Sri Vasudeva by name, the one jewel of the Datta family, having seen Gauranga-chandra, at once became wholly immersed in the ocean of love for Him and truly became for ever no different from [His] very life.

*Note.* Metre *vasantatilakā*. *Jīvana-nirviśeṣaḥ* is understood tentatively: "equal to [His] life", that is, as dear as life. *Ratnaṁ* is a neuter nominative in apposition to the subject (in the neuter the nominative and accusative coincide). Vasudeva Datta is famed for having asked the Lord to let him take upon himself the sins of all living beings (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 15.159–180). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 147

अथान्य एको भगवानितीह
ख्यातः सदाचार्यवरो महात्मा ।
श्रीगौरचन्द्रे प्रणतोऽनुवेलं
श्रीमज्जगन्नाथप्रभुं सिषेवे ॥१४७॥

*athānya eko bhagavān itīha*
*khyātaḥ sad-ācārya-varo mahātmā |*
*śrī-gauracandre praṇato 'nuvelaṁ*
*śrīmaj-jagannātha-prabhuṁ siṣeve ||147||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — and; *anyaḥ* — another; *ekaḥ* — a certain; *bhagavān* — Bhagavan; *iti* — thus; *iha* — here; *khyātaḥ* — known; *sat* — of true; *ācārya* — acharyas; *varaḥ* — the best; *mahātmā* — a great soul; *śrī-gauracandre* — to Sri Gaurachandra; *praṇataḥ* — bowed in devotion; *anuvelam* — constantly; *śrīmat* — the glorious; *jagannātha* — Jagannatha; *prabhum* — the Lord; *siṣeve* — served.

**147.** And another, a certain great soul known here as Bhagavan, the best of true acharyas, constantly bowed in devotion to Sri Gaurachandra, served the glorious Lord Jagannatha.

*Note.* Bhagavan Acharya; cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Antya 2.84–100 (a learned man and great devotee who lived with the Lord in Puri; his brother was Gopala Bhattacharya). Metre *upajāti*.

### Verse 148

इत्थं श्रीपुरुषोत्तमे स्थितवति प्रत्याशमासीद्ध्वनिः
सर्वासां विदिशां दिशाश्च जनता सोत्कण्ठमेवागता ।
ये चान्ये खलु सत्यराजसुमतिस्तद्भ्रातृपुत्रादयो
ये चान्ये रघुनन्दनो नरहरिः श्रीमन्मुकुन्दादिकः ॥१४८॥

*itthaṁ śrī-puruṣottame sthitavati pratyāśam [pratyāsam] āsīd dhvaniḥ*
*sarvāsāṁ vidiśāṁ diśāś ca janatā sotkaṇṭham evāgatā |*
*ye cānye khalu satyarāja-sumatis tad-bhrātṛ-putrādayo*
*ye cānye raghunandano narahariḥ śrīman-mukundādikaḥ ||148||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *śrī-puruṣottame* — Sri Purushottama; *sthitavati* — while abiding; *pratyāśam* — in every direction; *āsīt* — spread; *dhvaniḥ* — the report; *sarvāsām* — of all; *vidiśām* — of the intermediate quarters; *diśaḥ* — of the quarters; *ca* — and; *janatā* — the people; *sa-utkaṇṭham* — with longing; *eva* — indeed; *āgatā* — came; *ye* — who; *ca* — and; *anye* — others; *khalu* — also; *satyarāja* — Satyaraja; *sumatiḥ* — good-minded; *tat* — his; *bhrātṛ* — brothers; *putra* — sons; *ādayaḥ* — and the others; *ye* — who; *ca* — and; *anye* — others; *raghunandanaḥ* — Raghunandana; *narahariḥ* — Narahari; *śrīmat* — the glorious; *mukunda* — Mukunda; *ādikaḥ* — and the rest.

**148.** Thus, while Sri Purushottama abode [there], the report [of Him] spread in every direction, and the people of all the quarters and intermediate quarters came with longing. And others came too — the good-minded Satyaraja, his brothers, sons and others; and others again — Raghunandana, Narahari, the glorious Mukunda and the rest.

*Note.* Metre *śārdūla-vikrīḍita*. *Śrī-puruṣottame sthitavati* (locative absolute) can be understood both as "while [the Lord] abode in Sri Purushottama" and as "while Sri Purushottama — the Supreme Person, the Lord — abode [there]". The edition has *प्रत्यासम्*; we read *pratyāśam* ("in every direction") (?). *Tad-bhrātṛ-putrādayaḥ* may also be read as "his brother's sons and others". Satyaraja Khan is from Kulinagrama. Mukunda, his son Raghunandana and his brother Narahari Sarakara are from Shrikhanda. Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 10.89–90 (the residents of Kulinagrama and Mukunda, Narahari and Raghunandana of Khanda join Advaita) and 11.91–92. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

**Colophon:** इति श्रीकृष्णचैतन्यचरितामृते महाकाव्ये त्रयोदशः सर्गः । (*iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahākāvye trayodaśaḥ sargaḥ*) — "Thus [ends] the thirteenth sarga in the mahakavya 'Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita'." (The colophon gives no title for the sarga.)

---

## Sarga Fourteen — verses 1–135

**Title of the sarga:** none — the colophon of the edition gives no title for this sarga.
**Metre:**
- 1–129 — *anuṣṭubh* (*śloka*; 8 syllables per pada: odd padas ××××⏑——×, even padas ××××⏑—⏑×; the odd padas also admit the usual *vipulā* variants). Verses of six or more padas: 5, 37, 77, 81, 87, 102, 108, 109, 117; verses of two padas: 69, 82, 99. In the printed text the first line of 50 and the second line of 93 are one syllable short (in 93 the reading of the Gosvami edition, *stavana-*, restores the metre).
- 130–132, 134–135 — *śārdūla-vikrīḍita* (———⏑⏑—⏑—⏑⏑⏑———⏑——⏑—; 19 syllables per pada).
- 133 — *upajāti* (a mixture of *indravajrā* ——⏑——⏑⏑—⏑—— and *upendravajrā* ⏑—⏑——⏑⏑—⏑——; 11 syllables per pada).

**Total verses:** 135. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has 141: there the long stanzas of this edition (e.g. 37, 87, 108–109, 117) are divided into couplets, and number 71 is skipped; the text is the same, and nothing is missing.

**Contents of the passage:** the first coming of the Bengali devotees for the festival of the chariots; the Snana-yatra.
- 1–10 — the Lord calls Advaita and Srivasa to come every year for the chariot festival.
- 11–35 — the preparations. Srivasa, Vasudeva and Shivananda fix the day; with Shachi in Navadvipa; Advaita, Haridasa, Rama Pandita, Mukunda, Murari; the journey with kirtana as far as Remuna.
- 36–41 — Gopinatha in Remuna; the stream of devotees — "an ocean without shores" (*kulaka*).
- 42–56 — **Sarvabhauma in Jayapura.** He is going to Kashi to preach bhakti against the Lord's prohibition; he glorifies Advaita and Haridasa.
- 57–66 — Jajpur and the Vaitarani. After a dream Prataparudra summons Advaita to Cuttack (Advaita fears the Lord's displeasure); the others go by way of Hamseshvara; all are together again at Kamalapura.
- 67–82 — the temple of Jagannatha in the distance; garlands from the Lord; at the Narendra a message: a fast, and the meeting in Mishra's house; Murari, in his humility, stays behind by the tank.
- 83–114 — the darshan of Jagannatha and the meeting with the Lord. The description of His form (*kulaka*, 85–92); the mutual obeisances with Advaita (Bhagavatam 10.14.1); Srivasa, Rama Pandita, Vasudeva; two vessels of Ganga water; Murari comes with a blade of grass between his teeth.
- 115–135 — the wedding festival on the Ekadashi; the Snana-yatra on the full moon: the platform; the procession of Baladeva, Subhadra and Jagannatha; the bathing; the hyperbole of "the hero's march".

### Verse 1

एकदा प्राह नाथोऽयं निजपादपयोरुहम् ।
द्रष्टुं तत्रागतान् स्वीयानद्वैतप्रमुखान् जनान् ॥१॥

*ekadā prāha nātho 'yaṁ nija-pāda-payoruham |*
*draṣṭuṁ tatrāgatān svīyān advaita-pramukhān janān ||1||*

*Word for word:* *ekadā* — once; *prāha* — said; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *ayam* — this; *nija* — His own; *pāda* — of the feet; *payoruham* — the lotus; *draṣṭum* — to see; *tatra* — there; *āgatān* — to [those] who had come; *svīyān* — to His own; *advaita* — by Advaita; *pramukhān* — headed; *janān* — to the people.

**1.** Once the Lord said to His own people, headed by Advaita, who had come there to see His lotus feet:

### Verse 2

आचार्य हे महाबुद्धे हे पण्डित महाशय ।
यद्वदामि शृणु श्रीमज्जगन्नाथविचेष्टितम् ॥२॥

*ācārya he mahā-buddhe he paṇḍita mahāśaya |*
*yad vadāmi śṛṇu śrīmaj-jagannātha-viceṣṭitam ||2||*

*Word for word:* *ācārya* — O Acharya; *he* — O; *mahā-buddhe* — great in intellect; *he* — O; *paṇḍita* — Pandita; *mahāśaya* — noble-hearted; *yat* — what; *vadāmi* — I [shall] say; *śṛṇu* — hear; *śrīmat* — of the glorious; *jagannātha* — of Jagannatha; *viceṣṭitam* — about the doings.

**2.** "O Acharya, great in intellect! O noble-hearted Pandita! Hear what I shall say about the doings of the glorious Jagannatha.

*Note.* The Acharya is Advaita, the Pandita is Srivasa (cf. verses 11, 24).

### Verse 3

श्रीजगन्नाथदेवोऽसौ सदा सर्वरसाश्रयः ।
करोति गुण्डिचायात्रां विलासपरया धिया ॥३॥

*śrī-jagannātha-devo 'sau sadā sarva-rasāśrayaḥ |*
*karoti guṇḍicā-yātrāṁ vilāsa-parayā dhiyā ||3||*

*Word for word:* *śrī-jagannātha-devaḥ* — Lord Sri Jagannatha; *asau* — this; *sadā* — always; *sarva* — of all; *rasa* — the rasas; *āśrayaḥ* — the shelter; *karoti* — performs; *guṇḍicā* — to the Gundicha; *yātrām* — the journey; *vilāsa* — on play; *parayā* — intent; *dhiyā* — with a mind.

**3.** This Lord Sri Jagannatha, ever the shelter of all rasas, makes the journey to the Gundicha with a mind intent on play.

### Verse 4

गुण्डिचागारगमने वर्त्मनः पार्श्वयोर्द्वयोः ।
य एष पुष्पितारामो रामणीयकवानिह ॥४॥

*guṇḍicāgāra-gamane vartmanaḥ pārśvayor dvayoḥ |*
*ya eṣa puṣpitārāmo rāmaṇīyakavān iha ||4||*

*Word for word:* *guṇḍicā* — of Gundicha; *āgāra* — to the house; *gamane* — on the way; *vartmanaḥ* — of the road; *pārśvayoḥ* — on the sides; *dvayoḥ* — on both; *yaḥ* — which; *eṣaḥ* — this; *puṣpita* — blossoming; *ārāmaḥ* — garden; *rāmaṇīyakavān* — full of loveliness; *iha* — here.

**4.** This blossoming garden, full of loveliness, which [lies] here on both sides of the road on the way to the Gundicha temple —

*Note.* The relative clause (*ya eṣa…*) is taken up by *enam*, "it", in verse 5.

### Verse 5

वृन्दारण्यस्मृतिकरमेनं विद्धि विशेषतः ।
तत्र गत्वा जगन्नाथो गुण्डिचामण्डपे प्रभुः ।
एकाधिकाष्टदिवसं विहरंस्तत्र तिष्ठति ॥५॥

*vṛndāraṇya-smṛti-karam enaṁ viddhi viśeṣataḥ |*
*tatra gatvā jagannātho guṇḍicā-maṇḍape prabhuḥ |*
*ekādhikāṣṭa-divasaṁ viharaṁs tatra tiṣṭhati ||5||*

*Word for word:* *vṛndāraṇya* — of Vrindavana; *smṛti* — remembrance; *karam* — causing; *enam* — it; *viddhi* — know; *viśeṣataḥ* — especially; *tatra* — there; *gatvā* — having gone; *jagannāthaḥ* — Jagannatha; *guṇḍicā* — of Gundicha; *maṇḍape* — in the pavilion; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *eka* — by one; *adhika* — exceeding; *aṣṭa* — eight; *divasam* — days; *viharan* — sporting; *tatra* — there; *tiṣṭhati* — stays.

**5.** — know that it especially awakens the remembrance of Vrindavana. Going there, Lord Jagannatha stays in the pavilion of the Gundicha for eight days and one more, sporting there.

*Note.* A verse of six padas. "Eight days and one more" means nine days.

### Verse 6

तदिमां परमां यात्रां देवाद्यैरपि दुर्लभाम् ।
द्रष्टुं प्रत्यब्दमेवात्रागन्तव्यं हि भवादृशैः ॥६॥

*tad imāṁ paramāṁ yātrāṁ devādyair api durlabhām |*
*draṣṭuṁ pratyabdam evātrāgantavyaṁ hi bhavādṛśaiḥ ||6||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — therefore; *imām* — this; *paramām* — supreme; *yātrām* — procession; *deva-ādyaiḥ* — for the gods and others; *api* — even; *durlabhām* — hard to attain; *draṣṭum* — to see; *prati-abdam* — every year; *eva* — indeed; *atra* — here; *āgantavyam* — [it is] to be come; *hi* — surely; *bhavādṛśaiḥ* — by such as you.

**6.** Therefore people such as you should surely come here every year to see this supreme procession, hard to attain even for the gods and others."

### Verse 7

इति स्वीयविलासानां दर्शनाय महाप्रभुः ।
तानुवाच कृपाम्भोधी रथयात्राच्छलेन सः ॥७॥

*iti svīya-vilāsānāṁ darśanāya mahāprabhuḥ |*
*tān uvāca kṛpāmbhodhī ratha-yātrā-cchalena saḥ ||7||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *svīya* — of His own; *vilāsānām* — of the pastimes; *darśanāya* — for the seeing; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *tān* — to them; *uvāca* — spoke; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *ambhodhiḥ* — the ocean; *ratha-yātrā* — of the Ratha-yatra; *chalena* — on the pretext; *saḥ* — He.

**7.** Thus Mahaprabhu, the ocean of mercy, spoke to them on the pretext of the Ratha-yatra, [so that they might come] to see His own pastimes.

*Note.* The edition's *कृपाम्भोधी* is the regular sandhi form of *kṛpāmbhodhiḥ* before *r*.

### Verse 8

ततः प्रभृत्येवमेते रथस्य समये प्रभुम् ।
श्रीगौरचन्द्रं द्रष्टुं तं प्रत्यब्दं यान्ति सस्पृहम् ॥८॥

*tataḥ prabhṛty evam ete rathasya samaye prabhum |*
*śrī-gauracandraṁ draṣṭuṁ taṁ pratyabdaṁ yānti saspṛham ||8||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ prabhṛti* — from then on; *evam* — thus; *ete* — they; *rathasya* — of the chariot; *samaye* — at the time; *prabhum* — the Lord; *śrī-gauracandram* — Sri Gaurachandra; *draṣṭum* — to see; *tam* — Him; *prati-abdam* — every year; *yānti* — go; *sa-spṛham* — with longing.

**8.** From then on they have gone thus every year at the time of the chariot, longing to see Him, the Lord Sri Gaurachandra.

### Verse 9

यत् प्रत्यब्दं प्रयान्त्येते द्रष्टुं गौराङ्गसुन्दरम् ।
तत्कथां किं सुरगुरोः शतं कथयितुं भवेत् ॥९॥

*yat pratyabdaṁ prayānty ete draṣṭuṁ gaurāṅga-sundaram |*
*tat-kathāṁ kiṁ sura-guroḥ śataṁ kathayituṁ bhavet ||9||*

*Word for word:* *yat* — that; *prati-abdam* — every year; *prayānti* — go forth; *ete* — they; *draṣṭum* — to see; *gaurāṅga-sundaram* — the beautiful Gauranga; *tat* — of that; *kathām* — the story; *kim* — whether; *sura-guroḥ* — of the preceptor of the gods; *śatam* — a hundred; *kathayitum* — to tell; *bhavet* — could be [able].

**9.** The story of how they go forth every year to see the beautiful Gauranga — could even a hundred Brihaspatis, preceptors of the gods, tell it?

*Note.* The preceptor of the gods is Brihaspati, the type of eloquence.

### Verse 10

तथाप्युत्कण्ठया शश्वत् प्रथयन्नविशेषतः ।
एकवारस्य गमनं समन्ताद्वर्णयामहे ॥१०॥

*tathāpy utkaṇṭhayā śaśvat prathayann aviśeṣataḥ |*
*eka-vārasya gamanaṁ samantād varṇayāmahe ||10||*

*Word for word:* *tathā api* — nevertheless; *utkaṇṭhayā* — out of longing; *śaśvat* — constant; *prathayan* — setting forth; *aviśeṣataḥ* — without distinction (in general); *eka* — of one; *vārasya* — time; *gamanam* — the journey; *samantāt* — in full; *varṇayāmahe* — we shall describe.

**10.** Nevertheless, out of constant longing, setting it forth in a general way, we shall describe one such journey in full.

*Note.* *Aviśeṣataḥ*, "without distinction", i.e. in general: a single journey is described as representative of all of them, while *samantāt* means "in full", from beginning to end. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 11

अद्वैताचार्यदेवोऽसौ श्रीमच्छ्रीवासपण्डितः ।
गृहीत्वानेकशो लोकानन्याब्दे गमनोत्सुकः ॥११॥

*advaitācārya-devo 'sau śrīmac-chrīvāsa-paṇḍitaḥ |*
*gṛhītvānekaśo lokān anyābde gamanotsukaḥ ||11||*

*Word for word:* *advaitācārya-devaḥ* — the divine Advaita Acharya; *asau* — this; *śrīmat* — the glorious; *śrīvāsa-paṇḍitaḥ* — Srivasa Pandita; *gṛhītvā* — having taken; *anekaśaḥ* — many; *lokān* — people; *anya* — in the next; *abde* — in the year; *gamana* — for the journey; *utsukaḥ* — eager.

**11.** The next year the divine Advaita Acharya and the glorious Srivasa Pandita, taking many people with them, became eager to set out.

### Verse 12

प्रवृत्ते माधवे मासि वहन्मलयमारुते ।
रुते कोकिलभृङ्गाद्यैश्चारु ते गन्तुमुद्यताः ॥१२॥

*pravṛtte mādhave māsi vahan-malaya-mārute |*
*rute kokila-bhṛṅgādyaiś cāru te gantum udyatāḥ ||12||*

*Word for word:* *pravṛtte* — when [it] had begun; *mādhave* — Madhava; *māsi* — the month; *vahat* — blowing; *malaya* — from Malaya; *mārute* — when the breeze; *rute* — when [the air] resounded; *kokila* — with cuckoos; *bhṛṅga* — with bees; *ādyaiḥ* — and others; *cāru* — charmingly; *te* — they; *gantum* — to go; *udyatāḥ* — made ready.

**12.** When the month of Madhava had begun, when the Malaya breeze was blowing and [the air] resounded charmingly with cuckoos, bees and the rest, they made ready to go.

*Note.* Madhava is the month of Vaishakha (April–May). The Malaya breeze is the spring wind from the Malaya mountains in the south. Note the sound-play *-mārute | rute … cāru te*.

### Verse 13

प्रथमं हृष्टहृदयः श्रीमान् श्रीवासपण्डितः ।
श्रीगौरचन्द्रप्रेमातिनिर्भरस्निग्धमानसः ॥१३॥

*prathamaṁ hṛṣṭa-hṛdayaḥ śrīmān śrīvāsa-paṇḍitaḥ |*
*śrī-gauracandra-premāti-nirbhara-snigdha-mānasaḥ ||13||*

*Word for word:* *prathamam* — first; *hṛṣṭa* — joyful; *hṛdayaḥ* — [with] heart; *śrīmān* — the glorious; *śrīvāsa-paṇḍitaḥ* — Srivasa Pandita; *śrī-gauracandra* — for Sri Gaurachandra; *prema* — with love; *ati-nirbhara* — overflowing; *snigdha* — tender; *mānasaḥ* — [with] mind.

**13.** First the glorious Srivasa Pandita, joyful at heart, his mind tender and overflowing with love for Sri Gaurachandra…

*Note.* Verses 13–15 form one sentence.

### Verse 14

श्रीवासुदेवदत्तं तं श्रीशिवानन्दसेनकम् ।
हृष्ट ऊचे स्वहृदयं मोदयन्ननयोरपि ॥१४॥

*śrī-vāsudeva-dattaṁ taṁ śrī-śivānanda-senakam |*
*hṛṣṭa ūce sva-hṛdayaṁ modayann anayor api ||14||*

*Word for word:* *śrī-vāsudeva-dattam* — to Sri Vasudeva Datta; *tam* — to him; *śrī-śivānanda-senakam* — to Sri Shivananda Sena; *hṛṣṭaḥ* — joyful; *ūce* — spoke; *sva* — his own; *hṛdayam* — heart; *modayan* — gladdening; *anayoḥ* — of the two; *api* — also.

**14.** …joyfully spoke to Sri Vasudeva Datta and Sri Shivananda Sena, gladdening his own heart and theirs too:

### Verse 15

आगतोऽयं स समयो रथस्य तद्दिनं कुरु ।
प्रशस्तमस्मद्गमने युवयोरपि साम्प्रतम् ॥१५॥

*āgato 'yaṁ sa samayo rathasya tad dinaṁ kuru |*
*praśastam asmad-gamane yuvayor api sāmpratam ||15||*

*Word for word:* *āgataḥ* — has come; *ayam* — this; *saḥ* — that; *samayaḥ* — time; *rathasya* — of the chariot; *tat* — therefore; *dinam* — a day; *kuru* — fix; *praśastam* — auspicious; *asmat* — of us; *gamane* — for the going; *yuvayoḥ* — of you two; *api* — also; *sāmpratam* — now.

**15.** "That time of the chariot has come. So fix now an auspicious day for our setting out, and for yours too."

### Verse 16

ततो यात्रादिनं कृत्वा सर्वे परमसस्पृहाः ।
श्रीनवद्वीपगमने बभूवुरतिसोत्सुकाः ॥१६॥

*tato yātrā-dinaṁ kṛtvā sarve parama-saspṛhāḥ |*
*śrī-navadvīpa-gamane babhūvur ati-sotsukāḥ ||16||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *yātrā* — of departure; *dinam* — the day; *kṛtvā* — having fixed; *sarve* — all; *parama* — supremely; *sa-spṛhāḥ* — longing; *śrī-navadvīpa* — to Sri Navadvipa; *gamane* — for the going; *babhūvuḥ* — became; *ati* — very; *sa-utsukāḥ* — eager.

**16.** Then, having fixed the day of departure, all of them, full of the greatest longing, became very eager to go to Sri Navadvipa.

### Verse 17

श्रीशचीं तां भगवतीं विष्णुभक्तिस्वरूपिणीम् ।
मातरं सर्वजगतो ददृशुः परमाशयाः ॥१७॥

*śrī-śacīṁ tāṁ bhagavatīṁ viṣṇu-bhakti-svarūpiṇīm |*
*mātaraṁ sarva-jagato dadṛśuḥ paramāśayāḥ ||17||*

*Word for word:* *śrī-śacīm* — Sri Shachi; *tām* — that; *bhagavatīm* — holy; *viṣṇu* — for Vishnu; *bhakti* — of bhakti; *svarūpiṇīm* — the embodiment; *mātaram* — the mother; *sarva* — of the whole; *jagataḥ* — world; *dadṛśuḥ* — saw; *parama* — lofty; *āśayāḥ* — [of] disposition.

**17.** Those noble-minded ones saw the holy Sri Shachi, bhakti for Vishnu embodied, the mother of the whole world.

### Verse 18

स्थिता दिनद्वयं तत्र तत्स्नेहभरनिर्वृताः ।
श्रीमदद्वैतदेवं तं ददृशुर्बहुधोत्सुकम् ॥१८॥

*sthitā dina-dvayaṁ tatra tat-sneha-bhara-nirvṛtāḥ |*
*śrīmad-advaita-devaṁ taṁ dadṛśur bahudhotsukam ||18||*

*Word for word:* *sthitāḥ* — having stayed; *dina* — days; *dvayam* — two; *tatra* — there; *tat* — her; *sneha* — of affection; *bhara* — by the fullness; *nirvṛtāḥ* — made happy; *śrīmat* — the glorious; *advaita-devam* — Lord Advaita; *tam* — Him; *dadṛśuḥ* — saw; *bahudhā* — greatly; *utsukam* — eager.

**18.** Having stayed there two days, made happy by the fullness of her affection, they saw the glorious Lord Advaita, greatly eager [for the journey].

### Verse 19

ततो जगाद मधुरमद्वैताचार्य ईश्वरः ।
यात्रादिनं यद्युष्माकं प्रशस्तं तन्ममापि च ॥१९॥

*tato jagāda madhuram advaitācārya īśvaraḥ |*
*yātrā-dinaṁ yad yuṣmākaṁ praśastaṁ tan mamāpi ca ||19||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *jagāda* — said; *madhuram* — sweetly; *advaitācāryaḥ* — Advaita Acharya; *īśvaraḥ* — the Lord; *yātrā* — of departure; *dinam* — the day; *yat* — which; *yuṣmākam* — for you; *praśastam* — auspicious; *tat* — that; *mama* — for me; *api ca* — also.

**19.** Then the Lord Advaita Acharya said sweetly: "The day of departure that is auspicious for you is auspicious for me as well."

### Verse 20

ततः प्रमुदिताः सर्वे नृत्यकीर्तनतत्पराः ।
बभूवुस्तत्र गौराङ्गचरणस्नेहनिर्वृताः ॥२०॥

*tataḥ pramuditāḥ sarve nṛtya-kīrtana-tat-parāḥ |*
*babhūvus tatra gaurāṅga-caraṇa-sneha-nirvṛtāḥ ||20||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *pramuditāḥ* — delighted; *sarve* — all; *nṛtya* — to dancing; *kīrtana* — and to kirtana; *tat-parāḥ* — given; *babhūvuḥ* — became; *tatra* — there; *gaurāṅga* — of Gauranga; *caraṇa* — for the feet; *sneha* — by love; *nirvṛtāḥ* — made blissful.

**20.** Then all of them, delighted, gave themselves there to dancing and kirtana, made blissful by their love for the feet of Gauranga.

### Verse 21

श्रीमदद्वैत ईशोऽपि चलितः परमोत्सुकः ।
भक्तिलीलारसस्येव मर्यादापर्वतो महान् ॥२१॥

*śrīmad-advaita īśo 'pi calitaḥ paramotsukaḥ |*
*bhakti-līlā-rasasyeva maryādā-parvato mahān ||21||*

*Word for word:* *śrīmat* — the glorious; *advaitaḥ* — Advaita; *īśaḥ* — the Lord; *api* — too; *calitaḥ* — set out; *parama* — supremely; *utsukaḥ* — eager; *bhakti* — of bhakti; *līlā* — of the pastimes; *rasasya* — of the rasa; *iva* — as if; *maryādā* — boundary; *parvataḥ* — mountain; *mahān* — great.

**21.** The glorious Lord Advaita too set out, supremely eager — as if the great boundary mountain of the rasa of the pastimes of bhakti.

*Note.* In the edition the verse number lacks the second danda: *॥२१*.

### Verse 22

ततः श्रीहरिदासोऽसौ भक्तिलीलामहाम्बुधौ ।
मग्नो महापर्वतवन्मैनाक इव वारिधौ ॥२२॥

*tataḥ śrī-haridāso 'sau bhakti-līlā-mahāmbudhau |*
*magno mahā-parvatavan maināka iva vāridhau ||22||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *śrī-haridāsaḥ* — Sri Haridasa; *asau* — this; *bhakti* — of bhakti; *līlā* — of the pastimes; *mahā* — in the great; *ambudhau* — in the ocean; *magnaḥ* — immersed; *mahā* — great; *parvata-vat* — like a mountain; *mainākaḥ* — Mainaka; *iva* — like; *vāridhau* — in the ocean.

**22.** Then Sri Haridasa, immersed in the great ocean of the pastimes of bhakti like the great mountain Mainaka in the ocean…

*Note.* Mainaka is the mountain that hid in the ocean from Indra when he was cutting off the wings of the mountains. Verses 22–23 form one sentence.

### Verse 23

गुणकीर्तनमेवास्य सन्ततं महिमार्णवात् ।
आहृत्य सस्पृहं चक्रे यः सोऽप्यत्रैव सम्मतः ॥२३॥

*guṇa-kīrtanam evāsya santataṁ mahimārṇavāt |*
*āhṛtya saspṛhaṁ cakre yaḥ so 'py atraiva sammataḥ ||23||*

*Word for word:* *guṇa* — of the qualities; *kīrtanam* — the glorification; *eva* — indeed; *asya* — His; *santatam* — incessantly; *mahima* — of greatness; *arṇavāt* — from the ocean; *āhṛtya* — drawing; *sa-spṛham* — with longing; *cakre* — performed; *yaḥ* — who; *saḥ* — he; *api* — also; *atra eva* — to this very [journey]; *sammataḥ* — agreed.

**23.** …he who incessantly and longingly sang His qualities, drawing them from the ocean of His greatness — he too agreed to this very [journey].

*Note.* In the edition the verse number lacks the second danda: *॥२३*.

### Verse 24

तत एते महात्मानो हरिदासादयो जनाः ।
आचार्यपण्डितावादौ पुरस्कृत्य ययुः सुखम् ॥२४॥

*tata ete mahātmāno haridāsādayo janāḥ |*
*ācārya-paṇḍitāv ādau puraskṛtya yayuḥ sukham ||24||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *ete* — these; *mahātmānaḥ* — great souls; *haridāsa-ādayaḥ* — Haridasa and the others; *janāḥ* — people; *ācārya* — the Acharya; *paṇḍitau* — and the Pandita; *ādau* — in front; *puraskṛtya* — having placed; *yayuḥ* — went; *sukham* — happily.

**24.** Then these great souls, Haridasa and the others, placing the Acharya and the Pandita at their head, went on their way happily.

### Verse 25

श्रीवासुदेवदत्तोऽपि श्रीशिवानन्दसेनकः ।
अन्योन्यं परमप्रीतौ तत्सङ्गे ययतुर्मुदा ॥२५॥

*śrī-vāsudeva-datto 'pi śrī-śivānanda-senakaḥ |*
*anyonyaṁ parama-prītau tat-saṅge yayatur mudā ||25||*

*Word for word:* *śrī-vāsudeva-dattaḥ* — Sri Vasudeva Datta; *api* — also; *śrī-śivānanda-senakaḥ* — Sri Shivananda Sena; *anyonyam* — to each other; *parama* — supremely; *prītau* — attached; *tat* — their; *saṅge* — in the company; *yayatuḥ* — the two went; *mudā* — joyfully.

**25.** Sri Vasudeva Datta too and Sri Shivananda Sena, deeply attached to each other, went joyfully in their company.

### Verse 26

श्रीवासपण्डितस्यायादनुजो रामपण्डितः ।
यस्य गानेन गौराङ्गः सततं तद्वशोऽभवत् ॥२६॥

*śrīvāsa-paṇḍitasyāyād anujo rāma-paṇḍitaḥ |*
*yasya gānena gaurāṅgaḥ satataṁ tad-vaśo 'bhavat ||26||*

*Word for word:* *śrīvāsa-paṇḍitasya* — of Srivasa Pandita; *āyāt* — came; *anujaḥ* — the younger brother; *rāma-paṇḍitaḥ* — Rama Pandita; *yasya* — whose; *gānena* — by the singing; *gaurāṅgaḥ* — Gauranga; *satatam* — always; *tat* — his; *vaśaḥ* — under the sway; *abhavat* — was.

**26.** There came Srivasa Pandita's younger brother Rama Pandita, by whose singing Gauranga was always brought under his sway.

### Verse 27

शुचिः स्निग्धमतिः श्रीमान् मुकुन्दः परमः प्रियः ।
मधुरः शान्तिमान् सान्त्ववचाः परमकोमलः ॥२७॥

*śuciḥ snigdha-matiḥ śrīmān mukundaḥ paramaḥ priyaḥ |*
*madhuraḥ śāntimān sāntva-vacāḥ parama-komalaḥ ||27||*

*Word for word:* *śuciḥ* — pure; *snigdha* — gentle; *matiḥ* — [with] mind; *śrīmān* — the glorious; *mukundaḥ* — Mukunda; *paramaḥ* — supremely; *priyaḥ* — dear; *madhuraḥ* — sweet; *śāntimān* — peaceful; *sāntva* — consoling; *vacāḥ* — [with] speech; *parama* — supremely; *komalaḥ* — tender.

**27.** The pure, gentle-minded, glorious Mukunda, supremely dear, sweet, peaceful, consoling in speech, exceedingly tender…

*Note.* Verses 27–28 form a pair (*yugmaka*, so marked in the edition). Mukunda (Datta) is a singer, the Lord's friend from His youth.

### Verse 28

ततो मुरारिगुप्तश्च प्रेमभक्तिरसार्णवः ।
द्वितीय इव तत्सङ्गे द्वितीयः सन्मुदं ययौ ॥२८॥ (युग्मकम्)

*tato murāri-guptaś ca prema-bhakti-rasārṇavaḥ |*
*dvitīya iva tat-saṅge dvitīyaḥ san mudaṁ yayau ||28|| (yugmakam)*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *murāri-guptaḥ* — Murari Gupta; *ca* — and; *prema* — of loving; *bhakti* — of bhakti; *rasa* — of the rasa; *arṇavaḥ* — an ocean; *dvitīyaḥ* — a second [self]; *iva* — as if; *tat* — his; *saṅge* — in the company; *dvitīyaḥ* — a companion; *san* — being; *mudam* — to joy; *yayau* — went.

**28.** …and then Murari Gupta, an ocean of the rasa of loving bhakti, as if [Mukunda's] second self, went along in joy as a companion in his company.

*Note.* A play on *dvitīya*, "second" and "companion".

### Verse 29

अथ ते श्रीलगौराङ्गचरणप्रेमविह्वलाः ।
तस्यैव गुणनामादि कीर्तयन्तो मुदं ययुः ॥२९॥

*atha te śrīla-gaurāṅga-caraṇa-prema-vihvalāḥ |*
*tasyaiva guṇa-nāmādi kīrtayanto mudaṁ yayuḥ ||29||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *te* — they; *śrīla-gaurāṅga* — of Srila Gauranga; *caraṇa* — for the feet; *prema* — by love; *vihvalāḥ* — overwhelmed; *tasya* — His; *eva* — alone; *guṇa* — qualities; *nāma* — names; *ādi* — and so on; *kīrtayantaḥ* — chanting; *mudam* — to joy; *yayuḥ* — went.

**29.** Then, overwhelmed by love for the feet of Srila Gauranga, they went on in joy, chanting His qualities, names and so on — His alone.

### Verse 30

कीर्तनं प्रातरारभ्य सन्ध्यायामथवा निशि ।
कुर्वन्ति तेऽथ विश्रामं पथिकृत्यं तथा ततः ॥३०॥

*kīrtanaṁ prātar ārabhya sandhyāyām athavā niśi |*
*kurvanti te 'tha viśrāmaṁ pathi-kṛtyaṁ tathā tataḥ ||30||*

*Word for word:* *kīrtanam* — kirtana; *prātaḥ* — in the morning; *ārabhya* — having begun; *sandhyāyām* — at dusk; *athavā* — or; *niśi* — at night; *kurvanti* — make; *te* — they; *atha* — then; *viśrāmam* — rest; *pathi* — on the road; *kṛtyam* — what is to be done; *tathā* — and; *tataḥ* — after that.

**30.** Beginning the kirtana in the morning, they would rest [only] at dusk or at night, and after that [attend to] what had to be done on the road.

### Verse 31

एवं दिनं कीर्तनेन नृत्येन च महाशयाः ।
विनीय वर्त्मनि ययुः परमोत्सुकचेतसः ॥३१॥

*evaṁ dinaṁ kīrtanena nṛtyena ca mahāśayāḥ |*
*vinīya vartmani yayuḥ paramotsuka-cetasaḥ ||31||*

*Word for word:* *evam* — thus; *dinam* — the day; *kīrtanena* — in kirtana; *nṛtyena* — in dancing; *ca* — and; *mahāśayāḥ* — the noble-hearted; *vinīya* — spending; *vartmani* — on the road; *yayuḥ* — went; *parama* — supremely; *utsuka* — eager; *cetasaḥ* — [with] hearts.

**31.** Thus, spending the day in kirtana and dancing, the noble-hearted ones went along the road, their hearts supremely eager.

### Verse 32

तेषां तेषां वासराणां वर्णनीयं न किञ्चन ।
सुखसागर एवासीत् सर्वा विप्लावयन् दिशः ॥३२॥

*teṣāṁ teṣāṁ vāsarāṇāṁ varṇanīyaṁ na kiñcana |*
*sukha-sāgara evāsīt sarvā viplāvayan diśaḥ ||32||*

*Word for word:* *teṣām teṣām* — of each of those; *vāsarāṇām* — of the days; *varṇanīyam* — describable; *na kiñcana* — nothing; *sukha* — of happiness; *sāgaraḥ* — an ocean; *eva* — simply; *āsīt* — there was; *sarvāḥ* — all; *viplāvayan* — flooding; *diśaḥ* — the quarters.

**32.** Of each of those days nothing can be described: there was simply an ocean of happiness, flooding all the quarters.

### Verse 33

एवं ते हर्षपाथोधिकल्लोलाकुलमानसाः ।
लालसा गौरचरणे रेमुणायां ययुर्मुदा ॥३३॥

*evaṁ te harṣa-pāthodhi-kallolākula-mānasāḥ |*
*lālasā gaura-caraṇe remuṇāyāṁ yayur mudā ||33||*

*Word for word:* *evam* — thus; *te* — they; *harṣa* — of joy; *pāthodhi* — of the ocean; *kallola* — by the billows; *ākula* — tossed; *mānasāḥ* — [with] hearts; *lālasāḥ* — longing; *gaura* — of Gaura; *caraṇe* — for the feet; *remuṇāyām* — to Remuna; *yayuḥ* — came; *mudā* — joyfully.

**33.** Thus, their hearts tossed by the billows of the ocean of joy, longing for the feet of Gaura, they joyfully came to Remuna.

*Note.* Remuna is a town near Balasore, where the temple of Gopinatha Kshirachora stands.

### Verse 34

अस्ताद्रिमस्तके न्यस्य समस्तकरमेव सः ।
अर्को विषीदति मुहुस्तेषां दृष्टिमनाप्नुवन् ॥३४॥

*astādri-mastake nyasya samasta-karam eva saḥ |*
*arko viṣīdati muhus teṣāṁ dṛṣṭim anāpnuvan ||34||*

*Word for word:* *asta* — of setting; *adri* — of the mountain; *mastake* — on the crest; *nyasya* — having laid; *samasta* — all; *karam* — rays (hand); *eva* — indeed; *saḥ* — it; *arkaḥ* — the sun; *viṣīdati* — grieves; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *teṣām* — their; *dṛṣṭim* — glance; *anāpnuvan* — not obtaining.

**34.** The sun, laying all its rays upon the crest of the mountain of sunset, grieved again and again at not obtaining their glance.

*Note.* A play on *kara*, "ray" and "hand": the sun in despair "props its head on its hand" — and sets.

### Verse 35

तत्र ते नगरे श्रीमद्गोपीनाथं समीक्षितुम् ।
विविशुस्तत्पुरीं रम्यां पुलकाक्ताङ्गयष्टयः ॥३५॥

*tatra te nagare śrīmad-gopīnāthaṁ samīkṣitum |*
*viviśus tat-purīṁ ramyāṁ pulakāktāṅga-yaṣṭayaḥ ||35||*

*Word for word:* *tatra* — there; *te* — they; *nagare* — in the town; *śrīmat* — the glorious; *gopīnātham* — Gopinatha; *samīkṣitum* — to behold; *viviśuḥ* — entered; *tat* — that; *purīm* — city; *ramyām* — lovely; *pulaka* — with thrills of rapture; *akta* — anointed; *aṅga* — of the bodies; *yaṣṭayaḥ* — [with] the slender stems.

**35.** There, in that town, to behold the glorious Gopinatha, they entered the lovely city, their slender bodies covered with thrills of rapture.

### Verse 36

दृष्ट्वा तन्मुखचन्द्रं ते परमां प्रीतिमाययुः ।
नमस्कृत्य महात्मानः कृच्छ्रान्निववृतुर्बहिः ॥३६॥

*dṛṣṭvā tan-mukha-candraṁ te paramāṁ prītim āyayuḥ |*
*namaskṛtya mahātmānaḥ kṛcchrān nivavṛtur bahiḥ ||36||*

*Word for word:* *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *tat* — His; *mukha* — of the face; *candram* — the moon; *te* — they; *paramām* — the highest; *prītim* — to joy; *āyayuḥ* — came; *namaskṛtya* — having bowed down; *mahātmānaḥ* — the great souls; *kṛcchrāt* — with difficulty; *nivavṛtuḥ* — turned back; *bahiḥ* — outside.

**36.** Seeing the moon of His face, they attained the highest joy; and, having bowed down, the great souls came out [again] only with difficulty.

### Verse 37

प्रातः प्रतस्थिरे सर्वे सर्वदोत्सुकचेतसः ।
श्रीगौरचन्द्रचरणदर्शनार्ता महाशयाः ।
तेषामोघः स परमः सततं सुखतन्मयः ।
पारावार इवारेजे पारावारविवर्जितः ॥३७॥

*prātaḥ pratasthire sarve sarvadotsuka-cetasaḥ |*
*śrī-gauracandra-caraṇa-darśanārtā mahāśayāḥ |*
*teṣām oghaḥ sa paramaḥ satataṁ sukha-tan-mayaḥ |*
*pārāvāra ivāreje pārāvāra-vivarjitaḥ ||37||*

*Word for word:* *prātaḥ* — in the morning; *pratasthire* — set out; *sarve* — all; *sarvadā* — ever; *utsuka* — eager; *cetasaḥ* — [with] hearts; *śrī-gauracandra* — of Sri Gaurachandra; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *darśana* — for the sight; *ārtāḥ* — pining; *mahāśayāḥ* — the noble-hearted; *teṣām* — their; *oghaḥ* — stream; *saḥ* — that; *paramaḥ* — great; *satatam* — constantly; *sukha* — with happiness; *tat-mayaḥ* — filled; *pārāvāraḥ* — the ocean; *iva* — like; *āreje* — shone; *pāra-avāra* — of the further and nearer shores; *vivarjitaḥ* — devoid.

**37.** In the morning they all set out, the noble-hearted ones, their hearts ever eager, pining for the sight of the feet of Sri Gaurachandra. That great stream of theirs, constantly filled with happiness, shone like the ocean (*pārāvāra*) — but an ocean without either shore.

*Note.* A verse of six padas. A play on words: *pārāvāra*, "the ocean", literally "[that which has] a further and a nearer shore", while *pārāvāra-vivarjitaḥ* means "devoid of a further and a nearer shore". Verses 38–41 develop the comparison (*kulaka*, so marked in the edition after verse 41).

### Verse 38

अद्वैतोऽयं निधिरभूत् श्रीवासो भक्तिपर्वतः ।
अमृतं कीर्तनमभूत् हरिदासो महामणिः ॥३८॥

*advaito 'yaṁ nidhir abhūt śrīvāso bhakti-parvataḥ |*
*amṛtaṁ kīrtanam abhūt haridāso mahā-maṇiḥ ||38||*

*Word for word:* *advaitaḥ* — Advaita; *ayam* — this; *nidhiḥ* — the treasure; *abhūt* — was; *śrīvāsaḥ* — Srivasa; *bhakti* — of bhakti; *parvataḥ* — the mountain; *amṛtam* — the nectar; *kīrtanam* — the kirtana; *abhūt* — was; *haridāsaḥ* — Haridasa; *mahā* — the great; *maṇiḥ* — jewel.

**38.** Advaita was its treasure, Srivasa the mountain of bhakti, the kirtana its nectar, Haridasa its great jewel.

*Note.* The images come from the churning of the ocean: the treasures, Mount Mandara, the nectar, the Kaustubha jewel.

### Verse 39

तेषामन्योन्यसंप्रीतिर्लक्ष्मीरभवदुत्तमा ।
हिण्डीरो यशसां राशिस्तेजश्च बडवानलः ॥३९॥

*teṣām anyonya-saṁprītir lakṣmīr abhavad uttamā |*
*hiṇḍīro yaśasāṁ rāśis tejaś ca baḍavānalaḥ ||39||*

*Word for word:* *teṣām* — their; *anyonya* — mutual; *saṁprītiḥ* — love; *lakṣmīḥ* — Lakshmi; *abhavat* — was; *uttamā* — the supreme; *hiṇḍīraḥ* — the foam; *yaśasām* — of glories; *rāśiḥ* — the heap; *tejaḥ* — splendour; *ca* — and; *baḍavā-analaḥ* — the submarine fire.

**39.** Their mutual love was the supreme Lakshmi; the heap of their glories, the foam; and their splendour, the submarine fire.

*Note.* Lakshmi too rose from the churned ocean; glory is white in poetic convention, hence the foam. *Baḍavānala*, "the mare's fire", is the fire at the bottom of the ocean.

### Verse 40

कल्लोलो जयनिस्वानस्तरङ्गो निर्भराप्लुतिः ।
मीनाश्च पादाङ्गुलयो मुक्तास्तन्नखपङ्क्तयः ॥४०॥

*kallolo jaya-nisvānas taraṅgo nirbharāplutiḥ |*
*mīnāś ca pādāṅgulayo muktās tan-nakha-paṅktayaḥ ||40||*

*Word for word:* *kallolaḥ* — the billows; *jaya* — of "Jaya!"; *nisvānaḥ* — the cry; *taraṅgaḥ* — the waves; *nirbhara* — unrestrained; *āplutiḥ* — leaping; *mīnāḥ* — the fish; *ca* — and; *pāda* — of the feet; *aṅgulayaḥ* — the toes; *muktāḥ* — the pearls; *tat* — of them; *nakha* — of the nails; *paṅktayaḥ* — the rows.

**40.** The cries of "Jaya!" were its billows, their unrestrained leaping [in the dance] its waves, their toes its fish, and the rows of their toenails its pearls.

*Note.* *Āpluti* is taken as "leaping" (from *ā-plu*, "to leap; to plunge"); it may also be understood as "overflowing, flood" [of rapture].

### Verse 41

सर्पा अपि भुजा आसन् वक्षांसि द्वीपसञ्चयाः ।
आश्चर्यकमलान्यासन् वदनानि विभान्त्यपि ॥४१॥ (कुलकम्)

*sarpā api bhujā āsan vakṣāṁsi dvīpa-sañcayāḥ |*
*āścarya-kamalāny āsan vadanāni vibhānty api ||41|| (kulakam)*

*Word for word:* *sarpāḥ* — serpents; *api* — also; *bhujāḥ* — the arms; *āsan* — were; *vakṣāṁsi* — the chests; *dvīpa* — of islands; *sañcayāḥ* — clusters; *āścarya* — wondrous; *kamalāni* — lotuses; *āsan* — were; *vadanāni* — the faces; *vibhānti* — shining; *api* — and.

**41.** Their arms were serpents, their chests clusters of islands, and their shining faces wondrous lotuses.

*Note.* The edition apparently reads *वक्षांसि*, "chests".

### Verse 42

ततो जयपुरे ग्रामे सार्वभौमो महामतिः ।
समागमेन तत्रैव परमोत्सुक आगतः ॥४२॥

*tato jayapure grāme sārvabhaumo mahā-matiḥ |*
*samāgamena tatraiva paramotsuka āgataḥ ||42||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *jayapure* — in Jayapura; *grāme* — in the village; *sārvabhaumaḥ* — Sarvabhauma; *mahā-matiḥ* — great-minded; *samāgamena* — for a meeting; *tatra eva* — to that very place; *parama* — supremely; *utsukaḥ* — eager; *āgataḥ* — came.

**42.** Then to that very place, the village of Jayapura, came the great-minded Sarvabhauma, supremely eager to meet [them].

*Note.* The episode of Sarvabhauma on his way to Kashi (verses 42–56) is not in the Chaitanya-charitamrita. Sarvabhauma's departure for Varanasi to preach bhakti is found in Karnapura's own drama (Chaitanya-chandrodaya, Act 10), but there it comes later.

### Verse 43

मुञ्चन्नयनयोर्वारि तान् प्रति स्नेहमेव तत् ।
बिभ्रत्पुलकसङ्घेन समन्तादाकुलां तनुम् ॥४३॥

*muñcan nayanayor vāri tān prati sneham eva tat |*
*bibhrat pulaka-saṅghena samantād ākulāṁ tanum ||43||*

*Word for word:* *muñcan* — shedding; *nayanayoḥ* — from the eyes; *vāri* — water; *tān prati* — towards them; *sneham* — love; *eva* — itself; *tat* — that; *bibhrat* — bearing; *pulaka* — of thrills of rapture; *saṅghena* — with a host; *samantāt* — all over; *ākulām* — overwhelmed; *tanum* — a body.

**43.** Shedding water from his eyes — that was his very love for them — his body overwhelmed all over by a host of thrills of rapture…

### Verse 44

अद्वैतं तत्र दृष्ट्वासौ महात्मानं महाशयः ।
अस्तुवच्छ्लोकबन्धेन स्वकवित्वेन सत्कविः ॥४४॥

*advaitaṁ tatra dṛṣṭvāsau mahātmānaṁ mahāśayaḥ |*
*astuvac chloka-bandhena sva-kavitvena sat-kaviḥ ||44||*

*Word for word:* *advaitam* — Advaita; *tatra* — there; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *asau* — he; *mahātmānam* — the great soul; *mahāśayaḥ* — the noble-hearted; *astuvat* — praised; *śloka* — of a verse; *bandhena* — with the composition; *sva* — his own; *kavitvena* — by poetic gift; *sat-kaviḥ* — a true poet.

**44.** …seeing Advaita, the great soul, there, he — noble-hearted, a true poet — praised Him with a verse composed by his own poetic gift:

### Verse 45

अद्वैताय नमस्तेऽस्तु महेशाय महात्मने ।
यत्प्रसादेन गौराङ्गचरणे जायते रतिः ॥४५॥

*advaitāya namas te 'stu maheśāya mahātmane |*
*yat-prasādena gaurāṅga-caraṇe jāyate ratiḥ ||45||*

*Word for word:* *advaitāya* — to Advaita; *namaḥ* — obeisance; *te* — to You; *astu* — let there be; *mahā-īśāya* — to Mahesha; *mahātmane* — to the great soul; *yat* — by whose; *prasādena* — by the grace; *gaurāṅga* — of Gauranga; *caraṇe* — for the feet; *jāyate* — is born; *ratiḥ* — love.

**45.** "Obeisance to You, Advaita, Mahesha, the great soul, by whose grace love for the feet of Gauranga is born!"

*Note.* Advaita is honoured as an incarnation of Maha-Vishnu and of Sadashiva (Mahesha, "the great Lord").

### Verse 46

एवमुक्त्वा पपातासौ दण्डवद्धरणीतले ।
पुलकप्रेमजडितो महात्मा भाग्यतोयधिः ॥४६॥

*evam uktvā papātāsau daṇḍavad dharaṇī-tale |*
*pulaka-prema-jaḍito mahātmā bhāgya-toyadhiḥ ||46||*

*Word for word:* *evam* — thus; *uktvā* — having spoken; *papāta* — fell; *asau* — he; *daṇḍa-vat* — like a rod; *dharaṇī* — of the earth; *tale* — on the surface; *pulaka* — with hairs standing on end; *prema* — and with love; *jaḍitaḥ* — numbed; *mahātmā* — the great soul; *bhāgya* — of good fortune; *toyadhiḥ* — an ocean.

**46.** Having spoken thus, he — a great soul, an ocean of good fortune — numbed by love, his hairs standing on end, fell to the ground like a rod.

### Verse 47

हरिदासं समालोच्य भक्तिमानभवन्महान् ।
दण्डवद्भुवि हृष्टोऽसौ पतित्वा पुलकान्वितः ॥४७॥

*haridāsaṁ samālocya bhaktimān abhavan mahān |*
*daṇḍavad bhuvi hṛṣṭo 'sau patitvā pulakānvitaḥ ||47||*

*Word for word:* *haridāsam* — Haridasa; *samālocya* — having seen; *bhaktimān* — full of reverence; *abhavat* — became; *mahān* — the great [man]; *daṇḍa-vat* — like a rod; *bhuvi* — on the ground; *hṛṣṭaḥ* — joyful; *asau* — he; *patitvā* — having fallen; *pulaka-anvitaḥ* — with hairs standing on end.

**47.** Seeing Haridasa, the great man was filled with reverence and, joyful, his hairs standing on end, fell to the ground like a rod.

### Verse 48

चकार भूयशः श्रीमान् प्रणामान्नतकन्धरः ।
कुलजात्यनपेक्षाय हरिदासाय ते नमः ॥४८॥

*cakāra bhūyaśaḥ śrīmān praṇāmān nata-kandharaḥ |*
*kula-jāty-anapekṣāya haridāsāya te namaḥ ||48||*

*Word for word:* *cakāra* — made; *bhūyaśaḥ* — again and again; *śrīmān* — the illustrious [one]; *praṇāmān* — obeisances; *nata* — bowed; *kandharaḥ* — [with] neck; *kula* — on family; *jāti* — and on caste; *anapekṣāya* — to [him who is] not dependent; *haridāsāya* — to Haridasa; *te* — to you; *namaḥ* — obeisance.

**48.** With bowed neck the illustrious one made obeisances again and again: "Obeisance to you, Haridasa, [whose greatness] does not depend on family or caste!"

*Note.* Haridasa was born in a Muslim family; Sarvabhauma, a brahmana, bows down to him.

### Verse 49

ततः सगद्गदां वाचमुवाच द्विजपुङ्गवः ।
पुलकैः कण्टकीभूतं वपुर्बिभ्रत् गलत्क्लमः ॥४९॥

*tataḥ sa-gadgadāṁ vācam uvāca dvija-puṅgavaḥ |*
*pulakaiḥ kaṇṭakī-bhūtaṁ vapur bibhrat galat-klamaḥ ||49||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *sa-gadgadām* — faltering; *vācam* — speech; *uvāca* — spoke; *dvija-puṅgavaḥ* — the best of brahmanas; *pulakaiḥ* — with hairs standing on end; *kaṇṭakī-bhūtam* — become bristling; *vapuḥ* — a body; *bibhrat* — bearing; *galat* — gone; *klamaḥ* — [whose] weariness [was].

**49.** Then the best of brahmanas, his weariness gone, his body bristling with hairs standing on end, spoke in a faltering voice:

### Verse 50

श्रीगौरचन्द्रचरणकमलस्याप्यज्ञया ।
वेदान्तान्यार्थकृतये तज्ज्ञानां तारणाय च ॥५०॥

*śrī-gauracandra-caraṇa-kamalasyāpy ajñayā |*
*vedāntānyārtha-kṛtaye taj-jñānāṁ tāraṇāya ca ||50||*

*Word for word:* *śrī-gauracandra* — of Sri Gaurachandra; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *kamalasya* — of the lotus; *api* — even; *ajñayā* — without the leave [read *anājñayā*]; *vedānta* — to Vedanta; *anya* — another; *artha* — meaning; *kṛtaye* — for giving; *tat* — of it; *jñānām* — of the knowers; *tāraṇāya* — for the deliverance; *ca* — and.

**50.** "Even without the leave of the lotus feet of Sri Gaurachandra — to give Vedanta another meaning and to deliver its knowers…

*Note.* Verses 50–51 form one period. In the printed text the second pada has only seven syllables (the first line has fifteen); probably *kamalasyāpy anājñayā* ("without the leave") should be read: this restores the metre and agrees with v. 52–54, where the Lord forbids the journey. The text is left as printed.

### Verse 51

चिरादध्यात्मयोगस्य भावनाशुष्ककण्ठिनः ।
एतया भक्तिसुधया जीवयामीति गम्यते ॥५१॥

*cirād adhyātma-yogasya bhāvanā-śuṣka-kaṇṭhinaḥ |*
*etayā bhakti-sudhayā jīvayāmīti gamyate ||51||*

*Word for word:* *cirāt* — for long; *adhyātma* — of the Self; *yogasya* — of the yoga; *bhāvanā* — by meditation; *śuṣka* — parched; *kaṇṭhinaḥ* — [people with] throats; *etayā* — with this; *bhakti* — of bhakti; *sudhayā* — with the nectar; *jīvayāmi* — I shall revive; *iti* — with this [aim]; *gamyate* — [I] am going.

**51.** …and to revive with this nectar of bhakti those whose throats have long been parched by meditation on the yoga of the Self — with this [aim] I am going.

### Verse 52

अत्र प्रभो मत्प्रतिज्ञाश्रवणानन्तरं यथा ।
वाचोविलासं माकार्षीर्वृथाश्रममतिस्फुटम् ॥५२॥

*atra prabho mat-pratijñā-śravaṇānantaraṁ yathā |*
*vāco-vilāsaṁ mākārṣīr vṛthā-śramam ati-sphuṭam ||52||*

*Word for word:* *atra* — here; *prabho* — O Master; *mat* — my; *pratijñā* — of the vow; *śravaṇa* — the hearing; *anantaram* — after; *yathā* — thus; *vācaḥ-vilāsam* — a play of words; *mā akārṣīḥ* — do not engage in; *vṛthā* — vain; *śramam* — labour; *ati-sphuṭam* — very plainly.

**52.** Here, O Master, after hearing my vow, He [said] thus, very plainly: 'Do not engage in a play of words and vain labour.'

*Note.* Sarvabhauma addresses Advaita (*prabho*). The syntax is compressed: after *yathā* "said" is understood.

### Verse 53

अथाप्युत्कण्ठया गन्तुकामं मां करुणानिधिः ।
प्रत्युवाच न ते शक्तिर्भविष्यति कथञ्चन ॥५३॥

*athāpy utkaṇṭhayā gantu-kāmaṁ māṁ karuṇā-nidhiḥ |*
*pratyuvāca na te śaktir bhaviṣyati kathañcana ||53||*

*Word for word:* *atha api* — and yet; *utkaṇṭhayā* — out of eager longing; *gantu* — to go; *kāmam* — wishing; *mām* — to me; *karuṇā* — of mercy; *nidhiḥ* — the treasury; *pratyuvāca* — replied; *na* — not; *te* — of you; *śaktiḥ* — strength; *bhaviṣyati* — will be; *kathañcana* — in any way.

**53.** And when, out of eager longing, I still wished to go, the Treasury of Mercy replied to me: 'In no way will you have the strength [for it].

### Verse 54

मास्म गा मा कृथा व्यर्थं परिश्रममिमं द्विज ।
यस्य नो वर्तते भाग्यं किं तु त्वं कारयिष्यसि ॥५४॥

*mā sma gā mā kṛthā vyarthaṁ pariśramam imaṁ dvija |*
*yasya no vartate bhāgyaṁ kiṁ tu tvaṁ kārayiṣyasi ||54||*

*Word for word:* *mā sma gāḥ* — do not go; *mā kṛthāḥ* — do not undertake; *vyartham* — useless; *pariśramam* — labour; *imam* — this; *dvija* — O brahmana; *yasya* — of whom; *no* — not; *vartate* — there is; *bhāgyam* — good fortune; *kim* — what; *tu* — then; *tvam* — you; *kārayiṣyasi* — will make [him] do.

**54.** Do not go; do not undertake this useless labour, O brahmana. What can you make a man do who has no good fortune?'

### Verse 55

तथाप्युत्कण्ठया यामि काशीं परमनिस्त्रपः ।
मनोरथो मे सफलो यथा स्यात्तत्कृपां कुरु ॥५५॥

*tathāpy utkaṇṭhayā yāmi kāśīṁ parama-nistrapaḥ |*
*manoratho me saphalo yathā syāt tat kṛpāṁ kuru ||55||*

*Word for word:* *tathā api* — even so; *utkaṇṭhayā* — out of eager longing; *yāmi* — I go; *kāśīm* — to Kashi; *parama* — utterly; *nistrapaḥ* — shameless; *manorathaḥ* — desire; *me* — my; *sa-phalaḥ* — fruitful; *yathā* — so that; *syāt* — may be; *tat* — therefore; *kṛpām* — mercy; *kuru* — show.

**55.** Even so, utterly shameless, out of eager longing I am going to Kashi. Therefore show [me] mercy, so that my desire may bear fruit."

*Note.* Kashi (Varanasi) was the stronghold of the Mayavadi sannyasis; cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 7 and Madhya 25, where the Lord Himself converts the Mayavadis of Kashi headed by Prakashananda.

### Verse 56

इत्युक्तवान् सार्वभौमो भूमिगीर्वाणपण्डितः ।
नमस्कृत्वा महाभागो जगाम सुखतन्मयः ॥५६॥

*ity uktavān sārvabhaumo bhūmi-gīrvāṇa-paṇḍitaḥ |*
*namaskṛtvā mahā-bhāgo jagāma sukha-tan-mayaḥ ||56||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *uktavān* — having spoken; *sārvabhaumaḥ* — Sarvabhauma; *bhūmi* — of the earth; *gīrvāṇa* — among the gods; *paṇḍitaḥ* — the learned [one]; *namaskṛtvā* — having bowed down; *mahā-bhāgaḥ* — the most fortunate; *jagāma* — went away; *sukha* — with happiness; *tat-mayaḥ* — filled.

**56.** Having spoken thus, Sarvabhauma, the learned one among the gods of the earth, most fortunate, bowed down and went away, filled with happiness.

*Note.* "The gods of the earth" are the brahmanas.

### Verse 57

ततः एते महात्मानो रम्यां याजपुरीं ययुः ।
कृत्वा वैतरणीस्नानं जग्मुर्नगरमध्यतः ॥५७॥

*tataḥ ete mahātmāno ramyāṁ yājapurīṁ yayuḥ |*
*kṛtvā vaitaraṇī-snānaṁ jagmur nagara-madhyataḥ ||57||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *ete* — these; *mahātmānaḥ* — great souls; *ramyām* — to charming; *yājapurīm* — Yajapura; *yayuḥ* — went; *kṛtvā* — having made; *vaitaraṇī* — in the Vaitarani; *snānam* — a bath; *jagmuḥ* — went; *nagara* — of the town; *madhyataḥ* — through the middle.

**57.** Then these great souls came to charming Yajapura (Jajpur) and, having bathed in the Vaitarani, went through the middle of the town.

*Note.* In the edition *ततः एते* stands without sandhi.

### Verse 58

अथ प्रतापरुद्रेण स्वप्नं दृष्ट्वा महात्मना ।
प्रेषितो यानमुत्थाप्य तदीयोऽद्वैतमानयत् ॥५८॥

*atha pratāparudreṇa svapnaṁ dṛṣṭvā mahātmanā |*
*preṣito yānam utthāpya tadīyo 'dvaitam ānayat ||58||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *pratāparudreṇa* — by Prataparudra; *svapnam* — a dream; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *mahātmanā* — by the great-souled; *preṣitaḥ* — sent; *yānam* — a palanquin; *utthāpya* — having raised; *tadīyaḥ* — his man; *advaitam* — Advaita; *ānayat* — brought.

**58.** Then the great-souled Prataparudra, having seen a dream, sent his man; that man had a palanquin raised and brought Advaita.

### Verse 59

राजसम्भाषणं कर्तुं गन्तुं मामिति संविदन् ।
किं वदिष्यति नाथोऽसाविति चिन्ताकुलोऽभवत् ॥५९॥

*rāja-sambhāṣaṇaṁ kartuṁ gantuṁ mām iti saṁvidan |*
*kiṁ vadiṣyati nātho 'sāv iti cintākulo 'bhavat ||59||*

*Word for word:* *rāja* — with the king; *sambhāṣaṇam* — conversation; *kartum* — to hold; *gantum* — to go; *mām* — I; *iti* — that; *saṁvidan* — realizing; *kim* — what; *vadiṣyati* — will say; *nāthaḥ* — the Master; *asau* — He; *iti* — thus; *cintā* — by anxiety; *ākulaḥ* — troubled; *abhavat* — became.

**59.** Realizing, "I am to go and converse with the king," He became troubled with anxiety: "What will the Master say?"

*Note.* Verses 59–60 form a pair (*yugmaka*). It does not befit a sannyasi or a Vaishnava to seek the company of a king; cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 11.6–8: for a renounced sannyasi meeting a king is like drinking poison of one's own accord.

### Verse 60

ईश्वरोऽप्येष गौराङ्गचन्द्रभीत्याशु वेपितः ।
श्रीवासुदेवदत्तं तं निनाय निजसङ्गतः ॥६०॥ (युग्मकम्)

*īśvaro 'py eṣa gaurāṅga-candra-bhītyāśu vepitaḥ |*
*śrī-vāsudeva-dattaṁ taṁ nināya nija-saṅgataḥ ||60|| (yugmakam)*

*Word for word:* *īśvaraḥ* — the Lord (Ishvara); *api* — though; *eṣaḥ* — He; *gaurāṅga-candra* — of Gauranga-chandra; *bhītyā* — from fear; *āśu* — at once; *vepitaḥ* — trembling; *śrī-vāsudeva-dattam* — Sri Vasudeva Datta; *tam* — him; *nināya* — took; *nija* — as His own; *saṅgataḥ* — companion.

**60.** Though He is Himself Ishvara, He trembled with fear of Gauranga-chandra and at once took Sri Vasudeva Datta with Him as His companion.

*Note.* The edition has *भीताशु* — apparently for *bhītyāśu*. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 61

केचित् तत्सङ्गतो जग्मुरद्वैतानुगता जनाः ।
कटकस्य पथा ते च श्रीगौरचरणाश्रयाः ॥६१॥

*kecit tat-saṅgato jagmur advaitānugatā janāḥ |*
*kaṭakasya pathā te ca śrī-gaura-caraṇāśrayāḥ ||61||*

*Word for word:* *kecit* — some; *tat* — with Him; *saṅgataḥ* — together; *jagmuḥ* — went; *advaita* — of Advaita; *anugatāḥ* — followers; *janāḥ* — people; *kaṭakasya* — of Kataka; *pathā* — by the road; *te* — they; *ca* — and; *śrī-gaura* — of Sri Gaura; *caraṇa* — at the feet; *āśrayāḥ* — having taken shelter.

**61.** Some people, followers of Advaita who had taken shelter at the feet of Sri Gaura, went together with Him by the road through Kataka (Cuttack).

*Note.* Kataka (Cuttack) was the capital of Prataparudra.

### Verse 62

अन्ये तु हरिदासाद्या महात्मानो महाशयाः ।
श्रीवासं पुरतः कृत्वा हंसेश्वरपथैर्ययुः ॥६२॥

*anye tu haridāsādyā mahātmāno mahāśayāḥ |*
*śrīvāsaṁ purataḥ kṛtvā haṁseśvara-pathair yayuḥ ||62||*

*Word for word:* *anye* — others; *tu* — but; *haridāsa-ādyāḥ* — Haridasa and the rest; *mahātmānaḥ* — great souls; *mahāśayāḥ* — noble; *śrīvāsam* — Srivasa; *purataḥ* — in front; *kṛtvā* — having placed; *haṁseśvara* — of Hamseshvara; *pathaiḥ* — by the roads; *yayuḥ* — went.

**62.** But the others, noble great souls — Haridasa and the rest — placing Srivasa in front, went by the roads through Hamseshvara.

### Verse 63

तद्दिनं तत्र संनीय दृष्ट्वा च तमुमापतिम् ।
प्रातरुत्थाय सुखिताः परितस्ते मुदा ययुः ॥६३॥

*tad-dinaṁ tatra saṁnīya dṛṣṭvā ca tam umāpatim |*
*prātar utthāya sukhitāḥ paritas te mudā yayuḥ ||63||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — that; *dinam* — day; *tatra* — there; *saṁnīya* — having spent; *dṛṣṭvā* — having beheld; *ca* — and; *tam* — that; *umā-patim* — Lord of Uma; *prātaḥ* — in the morning; *utthāya* — having risen; *sukhitāḥ* — happy; *paritaḥ* — onward; *te* — they; *mudā* — with joy; *yayuḥ* — went.

**63.** Having spent that day there and beheld that Lord of Uma, they rose in the morning and, happy, joyfully went on.

*Note.* "The Lord of Uma" is Shiva, here Hamseshvara. The edition has *सुखिता* for *sukhitāḥ*.

### Verse 64

कियद्दूरे हि ते तिष्ठन् श्रीवासप्रमुखा जनाः ।
निकटं गच्छतां तेषामुत्कण्ठा द्विगुणाभवत् ॥६४॥

*kiyad-dūre hi te tiṣṭhan śrīvāsa-pramukhā janāḥ |*
*nikaṭaṁ gacchatāṁ teṣām utkaṇṭhā dvi-guṇābhavat ||64||*

*Word for word:* *kiyat* — some; *dūre* — at a distance; *hi* — indeed; *te* — they; *tiṣṭhan* — waited; *śrīvāsa* — by Srivasa; *pramukhāḥ* — headed; *janāḥ* — the people; *nikaṭam* — near; *gacchatām* — going; *teṣām* — of them; *utkaṇṭhā* — the longing; *dvi-guṇā* — twofold; *abhavat* — became.

**64.** The people headed by Srivasa waited some distance away; and as they drew near, their longing doubled.

*Note.* *Tiṣṭhan* is apparently for *atiṣṭhan* (imperfect plural). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 65

विलोकितव्या गौराङ्गनखचन्द्रच्छटा इति ।
अद्वैतोऽपि ततस्तत्र मिलितोऽभून्महामतिः ॥६५॥

*vilokitavyā gaurāṅga-nakha-candra-cchaṭā iti |*
*advaito 'pi tatas tatra milito 'bhūn mahā-matiḥ ||65||*

*Word for word:* *vilokitavyāḥ* — are to be seen; *gaurāṅga* — of Gauranga; *nakha* — of the toenails; *candra* — of the moons; *chaṭāḥ* — the splendours; *iti* — thus [thinking]; *advaitaḥ* — Advaita; *api* — too; *tataḥ* — then; *tatra* — there; *militaḥ* — joined; *abhūt* — became; *mahā-matiḥ* — the great-minded.

**65.** "The splendour of the moons of Gauranga's toenails is soon to be seen!" — thinking thus, the great-minded Advaita too then joined them there.

### Verse 66

एकत्रैव मिलित्वा ते ययुः कमलके पुरे ।
मुदा परमया युक्ताः कीर्तयन्तोऽभितोऽभितः ॥६६॥

*ekatraiva militvā te yayuḥ kamalake pure |*
*mudā paramayā yuktāḥ kīrtayanto 'bhito 'bhitaḥ ||66||*

*Word for word:* *ekatra eva* — in one place; *militvā* — having joined together; *te* — they; *yayuḥ* — went; *kamalake* — to Kamalaka; *pure* — to the town; *mudā* — with joy; *paramayā* — with supreme; *yuktāḥ* — filled; *kīrtayantaḥ* — chanting; *abhitaḥ abhitaḥ* — everywhere around.

**66.** Having joined together in one place, they went to the town of Kamalaka, filled with supreme joy and chanting [the Name] everywhere around.

*Note.* In the edition the last pada has seven syllables; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *kīrtayanto 'bhito 'bhitaḥ*, and so we read. Kamalaka is Kamalapura (cf. 11.85).

### Verse 67

नदीमासाद्य सुस्नाताः प्रासादं ददृशुर्मुहुः ।
औत्तुङ्गेन विवस्वन्तं नभस्थं पातयन्निव ॥६७॥

*nadīm āsādya susnātāḥ prāsādaṁ dadṛśur muhuḥ |*
*auttuṅgena vivasvantaṁ nabhasthaṁ pātayann iva ||67||*

*Word for word:* *nadīm* — the river; *āsādya* — having reached; *su-snātāḥ* — well bathed; *prāsādam* — the temple; *dadṛśuḥ* — beheld; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *auttuṅgena* — by [its] height; *vivasvantam* — the sun; *nabha-stham* — standing in the sky; *pātayan* — knocking down; *iva* — as if.

**67.** Having reached the river and bathed well, they beheld again and again the temple, which by its height seemed to knock the sun down from the sky —

*Note.* Verses 67–69 form one period. The edition has *प्रसादं* for *prāsādam* (so in v. 68).

### Verse 68

तेजसा कोटिसूर्याभः सुधया च समन्वितः ।
स नीलपर्वतपतेः प्रासादः सुखदर्शनः ॥६८॥

*tejasā koṭi-sūryābhaḥ sudhayā ca samanvitaḥ |*
*sa nīla-parvata-pateḥ prāsādaḥ sukha-darśanaḥ ||68||*

*Word for word:* *tejasā* — in splendour; *koṭi* — of myriads; *sūrya* — of suns; *ābhaḥ* — having the likeness; *sudhayā* — with nectar (with plaster); *ca* — and; *samanvitaḥ* — endowed; *saḥ* — that; *nīla* — of the Blue; *parvata* — Mountain; *pateḥ* — of the Lord; *prāsādaḥ* — the temple; *sukha* — joyful; *darśanaḥ* — to behold.

**68.** — in splendour like myriads of suns and endowed with nectar: that temple of the Lord of the Blue Mountain, a joy to behold,

*Note.* A play on words: *sudhā* means both "nectar" and "lime plaster" (whitewash).

### Verse 69

सुखदः सर्वभूतानां तैरदर्शि महाशयैः ॥६९॥

*sukhadaḥ sarva-bhūtānāṁ tair adarśi mahāśayaiḥ ||69||*

*Word for word:* *sukha-daḥ* — giving joy; *sarva* — to all; *bhūtānām* — beings; *taiḥ* — by them; *adarśi* — was seen; *mahāśayaiḥ* — by the noble.

**69.** giving joy to all beings, was seen by those noble ones.
