*Note.* A verse of two padas; verses 67–69 together make six padas.

### Verse 70

दृष्ट्वा प्रासादमुत्तुङ्गं तुङ्गरोमाञ्चसञ्चयैः ।
हर्षस्तेषां समजनि तत्समो भृशमुच्छ्रितः ॥७०॥

*dṛṣṭvā prāsādam uttuṅgaṁ tuṅga-romāñca-sañcayaiḥ |*
*harṣas teṣāṁ samajani tat-samo bhṛśam ucchritaḥ ||70||*

*Word for word:* *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *prāsādam* — the temple; *uttuṅgam* — lofty; *tuṅga* — high-standing; *romāñca* — of bristling hairs; *sañcayaiḥ* — with masses; *harṣaḥ* — joy; *teṣām* — in them; *samajani* — arose; *tat* — to it; *samaḥ* — equal; *bhṛśam* — greatly; *ucchritaḥ* — lofty.

**70.** When they saw the lofty temple, their hairs stood high on end in masses, and a joy arose in them as greatly lofty as the temple itself.

### Verse 71

विलोक्य हर्षसन्दोहनिर्भराः स्फूर्तिविह्वलाः ।
नमश्चक्रुर्महात्मानो हरिकीर्तनतत्पराः ॥७१॥

*vilokya harṣa-sandoha-nirbharāḥ sphūrti-vihvalāḥ |*
*namaś cakrur mahātmāno hari-kīrtana-tat-parāḥ ||71||*

*Word for word:* *vilokya* — beholding; *harṣa* — of joy; *sandoha* — with an abundance; *nirbharāḥ* — overflowing; *sphūrti* — by the [inner] vision; *vihvalāḥ* — overwhelmed; *namaḥ cakruḥ* — bowed down; *mahātmānaḥ* — the great souls; *hari* — of Hari; *kīrtana* — to the kirtana; *tat-parāḥ* — devoted.

**71.** Beholding it, the great souls, devoted to the kirtana of Hari, overflowing with an abundance of joy and overwhelmed by the [inner] vision, bowed down.

### Verse 72

अथ प्राप्य महात्मासौ मालां परमपावनीम् ।
श्रीगौरचन्द्रप्रहितां मुमुदेऽद्वैत ईश्वरः ॥७२॥

*atha prāpya mahātmāsau mālāṁ parama-pāvanīm |*
*śrī-gauracandra-prahitāṁ mumude 'dvaita īśvaraḥ ||72||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *prāpya* — having received; *mahātmā* — the great soul; *asau* — He; *mālām* — a garland; *parama* — supremely; *pāvanīm* — purifying; *śrī-gauracandra* — by Sri Gaurachandra; *prahitām* — sent; *mumude* — rejoiced; *advaitaḥ* — Advaita; *īśvaraḥ* — the lord.

**72.** Then the great soul, Lord Advaita, receiving a supremely purifying garland sent by Sri Gaurachandra, rejoiced.

*Note.* Cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 11.74–78: the Lord sends Svarupa and Govinda to meet the Bengalis with prasada and garlands; Svarupa first places a garland on Advaita.

### Verse 73

कीर्तयद्भिर्निरवधि प्रेमहृष्टैर्महात्मभिः ।
अद्वैतोऽपि सुखाविष्टो नटनायोपचक्रमे ॥७३॥

*kīrtayadbhir niravadhi prema-hṛṣṭair mahātmabhiḥ |*
*advaito 'pi sukhāviṣṭo naṭanāyopacakrame ||73||*

*Word for word:* *kīrtayadbhiḥ* — [with] chanting; *niravadhi* — without end; *prema* — from love; *hṛṣṭaiḥ* — exulting; *mahātmabhiḥ* — with the great souls; *advaitaḥ* — Advaita; *api* — too; *sukha* — by happiness; *āviṣṭaḥ* — possessed; *naṭanāya* — to dance; *upacakrame* — began.

**73.** As the great souls, exulting in love, chanted without end, Advaita too, possessed by happiness, began to dance.

### Verse 74

नृत्यन्नसौ कीर्तयन्तस्तेऽपि गौराङ्गलालसाः ।
नरेन्द्राख्यसरस्तीरमासाद्य सुखमाययुः ॥७४॥

*nṛtyann asau kīrtayantas te 'pi gaurāṅga-lālasāḥ |*
*narendrākhya-saras-tīram āsādya sukham āyayuḥ ||74||*

*Word for word:* *nṛtyan* — dancing; *asau* — He; *kīrtayantaḥ* — chanting; *te* — they; *api* — and; *gaurāṅga* — for Gauranga; *lālasāḥ* — longing; *narendra* — Narendra; *ākhya* — called; *saraḥ* — of the lake; *tīram* — the shore; *āsādya* — having reached; *sukham* — happiness; *āyayuḥ* — attained.

**74.** So — He dancing and they chanting, longing for Gauranga — they reached the shore of the lake called Narendra and were happy.

*Note.* Narendra-sarovara is a sacred pond in Puri (cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 11.68: the Bengali devotees halt at Narendra Lake; Madhya 14: the water pastimes there).

### Verse 75

अथ भूयोऽपि गोविन्दान्मालामासाद्य पावनीम् ।
अद्वैतस्तन्निगदितं शुश्राव भृशमुत्सुकः ॥७५॥

*atha bhūyo 'pi govindān mālām āsādya pāvanīm |*
*advaitas tan-nigaditaṁ śuśrāva bhṛśam utsukaḥ ||75||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *bhūyaḥ api* — once more; *govindāt* — from Govinda; *mālām* — a garland; *āsādya* — having received; *pāvanīm* — purifying; *advaitaḥ* — Advaita; *tat* — His; *nigaditam* — message; *śuśrāva* — heard; *bhṛśam* — intensely; *utsukaḥ* — eager.

**75.** Then, receiving once more a purifying garland, from Govinda, Advaita, intensely eager, heard His message:

*Note.* Govinda is the Lord's servant in Puri.

### Verse 76

समुद्रतटसंस्थस्य निदेशोऽयं महाप्रभोः ।
उपवासोऽस्ति विहितो नात्र युष्माकमागमः ॥७६॥

*samudra-taṭa-saṁsthasya nideśo 'yaṁ mahāprabhoḥ |*
*upavāso 'sti vihito nātra yuṣmākam āgamaḥ ||76||*

*Word for word:* *samudra* — of the ocean; *taṭa* — on the shore; *saṁsthasya* — staying; *nideśaḥ* — instruction; *ayam* — this [is]; *mahāprabhoḥ* — of Mahaprabhu; *upavāsaḥ* — a fast; *asti* — is; *vihitaḥ* — enjoined; *na* — not; *atra* — here; *yuṣmākam* — your; *āgamaḥ* — coming.

**76.** "This is the instruction of Mahaprabhu, who is staying on the shore of the ocean: a fast is enjoined, and you are not to come here.

*Note.* Verses 76–77 form one speech.

### Verse 77

भविष्यति हि तत्रैव पुण्डरीकाक्ष ईक्ष्यताम् ।
अहं तत्रैव यास्यामि विलम्बेन सुनिश्चितम् ।
भविष्यति समालापस्तत्र मिश्रालयान्तरे ॥७७॥

*bhaviṣyati hi tatraiva puṇḍarīkākṣa īkṣyatām |*
*ahaṁ tatraiva yāsyāmi vilambena suniścitam |*
*bhaviṣyati samālāpas tatra miśrālayāntare ||77||*

*Word for word:* *bhaviṣyati* — will be; *hi* — for; *tatra eva* — right there; *puṇḍarīka-akṣaḥ* — the Lotus-eyed One; *īkṣyatām* — let be seen; *aham* — I; *tatra eva* — to that very place; *yāsyāmi* — shall come; *vilambena* — after a while; *suniścitam* — certainly; *bhaviṣyati* — will be; *samālāpaḥ* — conversation; *tatra* — there; *miśra* — of Mishra; *ālaya* — of the house; *antare* — inside.

**77.** For [the darshan] will be right there: behold the Lotus-eyed One. I shall certainly come to that very place after a while, and we shall converse there, in Mishra's house."

*Note.* A verse of six padas. The Lotus-eyed One is Jagannatha. Mishra's house is the house of Kashi Mishra (cf. 13.63). The first pada is syntactically incomplete.

### Verse 78

इति श्रुत्वाद्वैत ईशो मायैषेति वितर्कयन् ।
तथैवानुमतिं चक्रे तद्वशोऽसौ यतः स्वयम् ॥७८॥

*iti śrutvādvaita īśo māyaiṣeti vitarkayan |*
*tathaivānumatiṁ cakre tad-vaśo 'sau yataḥ svayam ||78||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *śrutvā* — having heard; *advaitaḥ* — Advaita; *īśaḥ* — the lord; *māyā* — a stratagem; *eṣā* — this [is]; *iti* — thus; *vitarkayan* — surmising; *tathā eva* — just so; *anumatim* — consent; *cakre* — gave; *tat* — of Him; *vaśaḥ* — under the control; *asau* — He; *yataḥ* — since; *svayam* — Himself.

**78.** Hearing this, Lord Advaita surmised, "This is a stratagem," yet He gave His consent just so, since He Himself is under [the Lord's] control.

*Note.* *Tad-vaśo 'sau* can also be taken the other way: "since He [the Lord] Himself is under [Advaita's] control" (?). Grammatically both readings are possible; we keep ours. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 79

मुरारिगुप्तोऽथ महानिर्वेदपरया धिया ।
पतित्वा दण्डवद्भूमौ रुदन्निदमभाषत ॥७९॥

*murāri-gupto 'tha mahā-nirveda-parayā dhiyā |*
*patitvā daṇḍavad bhūmau rudann idam abhāṣata ||79||*

*Word for word:* *murāri-guptaḥ* — Murari Gupta; *atha* — then; *mahā* — of great; *nirveda* — despondency; *parayā* — full; *dhiyā* — with a mind; *patitvā* — having fallen; *daṇḍa-vat* — like a rod; *bhūmau* — on the ground; *rudan* — weeping; *idam* — this; *abhāṣata* — said.

**79.** Then Murari Gupta, his mind full of great despondency, fell to the ground like a rod and, weeping, said this:

### Verse 80

दीनोऽयं दुःखिततमो जीवलोकः सुपामरः ।
एतावद्दूरमानीतो भवद्भिर्महिताशयैः ॥८०॥

*dīno 'yaṁ duḥkhitatamo jīva-lokaḥ su-pāmaraḥ |*
*etāvad dūram ānīto bhavadbhir mahitāśayaiḥ ||80||*

*Word for word:* *dīnaḥ* — wretched; *ayam* — this; *duḥkhitatamaḥ* — most miserable; *jīva-lokaḥ* — creature; *su-pāmaraḥ* — utterly vile; *etāvat* — so; *dūram* — far; *ānītaḥ* — has been brought; *bhavadbhiḥ* — by you; *mahita* — worthy; *āśayaiḥ* — [with] souls.

**80.** "This wretched, most miserable, utterly vile creature has been brought so far by you, worthy souls.

*Note.* Verses 80–82 form one speech.

### Verse 81

न पारयेऽहं व्रजितुं न शक्तिर्मम वर्तते ।
न साहसं मेऽस्ति तावद्द्रष्टुं जगदधीश्वरम् ।
भवद्भिर्ज्ञापिते पश्चाद्गन्तुं शक्तिर्भविष्यति ॥८१॥

*na pāraye 'haṁ vrajituṁ na śaktir mama vartate |*
*na sāhasaṁ me 'sti tāvad draṣṭuṁ jagad-adhīśvaram |*
*bhavadbhir jñāpite paścād gantuṁ śaktir bhaviṣyati ||81||*

*Word for word:* *na pāraye* — am not able; *aham* — I; *vrajitum* — to go; *na* — not; *śaktiḥ* — strength; *mama* — of me; *vartate* — there is; *na* — not; *sāhasam* — courage; *me* — of me; *asti* — there is; *tāvat* — as yet; *draṣṭum* — to see; *jagat* — of the world; *adhīśvaram* — the Supreme Lord; *bhavadbhiḥ* — by you; *jñāpite* — when it has been made known; *paścāt* — afterwards; *gantum* — to go; *śaktiḥ* — strength; *bhaviṣyati* — will be.

**81.** I am not able to go; I have no strength; nor have I as yet the courage to see the Supreme Lord of the world. Afterwards, when you have made [me] known [to Him], I shall have the strength to go."

*Note.* A verse of six padas.

### Verse 82

इत्युक्त्वा बहुनिर्विण्णो दुःखी तत्रैव सुस्थिरः ॥८२॥

*ity uktvā bahu-nirviṇṇo duḥkhī tatraiva susthiraḥ ||82||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *uktvā* — having spoken; *bahu* — greatly; *nirviṇṇaḥ* — dejected; *duḥkhī* — sorrowful; *tatra eva* — right there; *susthiraḥ* — [remained] motionless.

**82.** Having spoken thus, greatly dejected and sorrowful, he remained motionless right there.

*Note.* A verse of two padas. Cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 11.152–157: Murari does not go to the Lord at once but bows down from afar, in the street; later he comes with two bunches of grass between his teeth and draws back: "Do not touch me."

### Verse 83

तदनन्तरमद्वैतप्रमुखास्ते महाशयाः ।
पुण्डरीकाक्षयुगलमीक्षां चक्रुर्जगत्पतेः ॥८३॥

*tad-anantaram advaita-pramukhās te mahāśayāḥ |*
*puṇḍarīkākṣa-yugalam īkṣāṁ cakrur jagat-pateḥ ||83||*

*Word for word:* *tat-anantaram* — after that; *advaita* — by Advaita; *pramukhāḥ* — headed; *te* — those; *mahāśayāḥ* — noble ones; *puṇḍarīka* — lotus; *akṣa* — of eyes; *yugalam* — the pair; *īkṣām cakruḥ* — beheld; *jagat-pateḥ* — of the Lord of the world.

**83.** After that, those noble ones headed by Advaita beheld the pair of lotus eyes of the Lord of the world.

### Verse 84

महोरस्कं महाबाहुं विशालायतलोचनम् ।
तं विलोक्य जगन्नाथं मुदमापुर्महत्तराम् ॥८४॥

*mahoraskaṁ mahā-bāhuṁ viśālāyata-locanam |*
*taṁ vilokya jagannāthaṁ mudam āpur mahattarām ||84||*

*Word for word:* *mahā-uraskam* — broad-chested; *mahā-bāhum* — mighty-armed; *viśāla* — wide; *āyata* — long; *locanam* — [with] eyes; *tam* — that; *vilokya* — beholding; *jagannātham* — Jagannatha; *mudam* — joy; *āpuḥ* — attained; *mahattarām* — the greatest.

**84.** Beholding that Jagannatha — broad-chested, mighty-armed, with wide, long eyes — they attained the greatest joy.

### Verse 85

अथ श्रीश्रीगौरचन्द्रश्चन्द्रकोटिमहोज्ज्वलः ।

*atha śrī-śrī-gauracandraś candra-koṭi-mahojjvalaḥ |*
*udiyāya sukhāviṣṭaḥ sravad-aśru-bhara-plutaḥ ||85||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *śrī-śrī-gauracandraḥ* — Sri Sri Gaurachandra; *candra* — of moons; *koṭi* — [like] myriads; *mahā-ujjvalaḥ* — brilliantly shining; *udiyāya* — rose; *sukha* — by happiness; *āviṣṭaḥ* — possessed; *sravat* — of streaming; *aśru* — of tears; *bhara* — in a flood; *plutaḥ* — bathed.

**85.** Then Sri Sri Gaurachandra rose [before them], shining brilliantly like myriads of moons, possessed by happiness, bathed in a flood of streaming tears.

*Note.* Verses 86–92 form one descriptive period (*kulaka*); its subject is the Lord.

### Verse 86

पादन्यासैर्दलन् भूमिं मत्तपद्मीन्द्रविक्रमः ।
मत्तसिंहमहोल्लासो लसदाजानुदोर्द्वयः ॥८६॥

*pāda-nyāsair dalan bhūmiṁ matta-padmīndra-vikramaḥ |*
*matta-siṁha-mahollāso lasad-ājānu-dor-dvayaḥ ||86||*

*Word for word:* *pāda* — of the feet; *nyāsaiḥ* — with the placings; *dalan* — crushing; *bhūmim* — the earth; *matta* — of a maddened; *padmī-indra* — king of elephants; *vikramaḥ* — [with] the gait; *matta* — of a maddened; *siṁha* — lion; *mahā* — with the great; *ullāsaḥ* — exultation; *lasat* — shining; *ājānu* — reaching to the knees; *doḥ* — of arms; *dvayaḥ* — [with] a pair.

**86.** Crushing the earth with His footfalls, with the gait of a maddened king of elephants, with the great exultation of a maddened lion, His two shining arms reaching to His knees;

*Note.* The edition has *पञ्चीन्द्र* — a corruption; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *padmīndra*: *padmin* is an "elephant" (with lotus-like spots on its skin), *padmīndra* — "the king of elephants".

*jaṅgamaḥ kāñcana-giriḥ sākṣād iva sudhākaraḥ |*
*galad-aśru-jharāsāra-jhara-nirjhara-sañcayaḥ |*
*sudhāṁśu-koṭir yugapad ekībhūya samudgataḥ |*
*vikiran satatāsārāṁ pīyūṣa-drava-dīrghikām ||87||*

*Word for word:* *jaṅgamaḥ* — moving; *kāñcana* — golden; *giriḥ* — a mountain; *sākṣāt* — in person; *iva* — as if; *sudhākaraḥ* — the moon; *galat* — of flowing; *aśru* — of tears; *jhara* — of streams; *āsāra* — from downpours; *jhara-nirjhara* — of cascades and waterfalls; *sañcayaḥ* — [with] a mass; *sudhāṁśu* — of moons; *koṭiḥ* — myriads; *yugapat* — at once; *ekībhūya* — having become one; *samudgataḥ* — risen; *vikiran* — pouring forth; *satata* — with unceasing; *āsārām* — downpours; *pīyūṣa* — of nectar; *drava* — liquid; *dīrghikām* — a lake.

*Note.* A verse of eight padas.

### Verse 93

अद्वैतोऽपि सुखाविष्टो हृष्टरोमा ननाम तम् ।

### Verse 95

### Verse 96

### Verse 97

ततोऽस्यावरजो रामपण्डितोऽतिमहाशयः ।
श्रीवासुदेवदत्तोऽपि नेमतुर्युगपत् प्रभुम् ॥९७॥

*tato 'syāvarajo rāma-paṇḍito 'ti-mahāśayaḥ |*
*śrī-vāsudeva-datto 'pi nematur yugapat prabhum ||97||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *asya* — his; *avarajaḥ* — younger brother; *rāma-paṇḍitaḥ* — Rama Pandita; *ati* — very; *mahāśayaḥ* — noble-hearted; *śrī-vāsudeva-dattaḥ* — Sri Vasudeva Datta; *api* — and; *nematuḥ* — the two bowed down; *yugapat* — together; *prabhum* — to the Lord.

**97.** Then his younger brother, the very noble-hearted Rama Pandita, and Sri Vasudeva Datta bowed down to the Lord together.

### Verse 98

तौ जग्राह भुजस्तम्भयुगलेन महाप्रभुः ।
श्रीशिवानन्दसेनोऽपि तत्पश्चादनमन्मुदा ॥९८॥

*tau jagrāha bhuja-stambha-yugalena mahāprabhuḥ |*
*śrī-śivānanda-seno 'pi tat-paścād anaman mudā ||98||*

*Word for word:* *tau* — the two; *jagrāha* — clasped; *bhuja* — of arms; *stambha* — of pillars; *yugalena* — with the pair; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *śrī-śivānanda-senaḥ* — Sri Shivananda Sena; *api* — too; *tat-paścāt* — after them; *anamat* — bowed down; *mudā* — joyfully.

**98.** Mahaprabhu clasped the two with the pair of pillars that were His arms. After them Sri Shivananda Sena too joyfully bowed down…

### Verse 99

गङ्गाजलस्य च पुरो भाण्डद्वयमथानयत् ॥९९॥

*gaṅgā-jalasya ca puro bhāṇḍa-dvayam athānayat ||99||*

*Word for word:* *gaṅgā* — of the Ganga; *jalasya* — of water; *ca* — and; *puraḥ* — before [Him]; *bhāṇḍa* — of vessels; *dvayam* — a pair; *atha* — then; *ānayat* — set down.

**99.** …and then set before Him two vessels of Ganga water.

*Note.* A verse of two padas.

### Verse 100

तत्तु दृष्ट्वा कृपाम्भोधिर्गङ्गामाहात्म्यमुज्जगौ ।
उवाच मधुरं चानु दन्तद्योतोज्ज्वलाधरः ॥१००॥

*tat tu dṛṣṭvā kṛpāmbhodhir gaṅgā-māhātmyam ujjagau |*
*uvāca madhuraṁ cānu danta-dyotojjvalādharaḥ ||100||*

*Word for word:* *tat* — that; *tu* — and; *dṛṣṭvā* — seeing; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *ambhodhiḥ* — the ocean; *gaṅgā* — of the Ganga; *māhātmyam* — the glory; *ujjagau* — sang aloud; *uvāca* — spoke; *madhuram* — sweetly; *ca anu* — and then; *danta* — of the teeth; *dyota* — by the gleam; *ujjvala* — lit up; *adharaḥ* — [with] lips.

**100.** Seeing this, the ocean of mercy sang aloud the glory of the Ganga, and then, His lips lit up by the gleam of His teeth, He spoke sweetly:

### Verse 101

स्नानोत्सवायैकमिदं मह्यमेकं च दीयताम् ।
तद्द्वयं श्रीवासुदेवश्रीशिवानन्दयोः पृथक् ॥१०१॥

*snānotsavāyaikam idaṁ mahyam ekaṁ ca dīyatām |*
*tad-dvayaṁ śrī-vāsudeva-śrī-śivānandayoḥ pṛthak ||101||*

*Word for word:* *snāna* — of the bathing; *utsavāya* — for the festival; *ekam* — one; *idam* — this; *mahyam* — to Me; *ekam* — one; *ca* — and; *dīyatām* — let be given; *tat* — those; *dvayam* — two; *śrī-vāsudeva* — of Sri Vasudeva; *śrī-śivānandayoḥ* — and of Sri Shivananda; *pṛthak* — separately.

**101.** "Let this one be given for the bathing festival, and one to Me." Those two [vessels] belonged separately to Sri Vasudeva and Sri Shivananda, [one to each].

*Note.* The second half is understood tentatively (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text. In the next verse the Lord divides the water, knowing the wish of both; so the vessels belonged to the two of them, one each.

### Verse 102

उभयोरेव विज्ञाय वासनां पुनरुक्तवान् ।
तयोरर्धं विभज्यादौ जगन्नाथाय दीयताम् ।
अन्यदर्धं ततोऽत्रैव स्थाप्यतामिति स प्रभुः ॥१०२॥

*ubhayor eva vijñāya vāsanāṁ punar uktavān |*
*tayor ardhaṁ vibhajyādau jagannāthāya dīyatām |*
*anyad ardhaṁ tato 'traiva sthāpyatām iti sa prabhuḥ ||102||*

*Word for word:* *ubhayoḥ* — of both; *eva* — indeed; *vijñāya* — knowing; *vāsanām* — the wish; *punaḥ* — again; *uktavān* — spoke; *tayoḥ* — of them; *ardham* — half; *vibhajya* — dividing; *ādau* — first; *jagannāthāya* — to Jagannatha; *dīyatām* — let be given; *anyat* — the other; *ardham* — half; *tataḥ* — then; *atra eva* — right here; *sthāpyatām* — let be kept; *iti* — thus; *saḥ* — He; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord.

**102.** Knowing the wish of both, the Lord spoke again: "Divide them: first let half be given to Jagannatha, and then let the other half be kept right here."

*Note.* A verse of six padas.

### Verse 103

अथ श्रीमान् कृपाम्भोधिः प्रपच्छ विस्मयान्वितः ।
मुरारिः क्व मुरारिः क्व क्वासौ सत्वरमानय ॥१०३॥

*atha śrīmān kṛpāmbhodhiḥ papraccha vismayānvitaḥ |*
*murāriḥ kva murāriḥ kva kvāsau satvaram ānaya ||103||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *śrīmān* — the glorious; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *ambhodhiḥ* — the ocean; *papraccha* — asked; *vismaya* — with wonder; *anvitaḥ* — filled; *murāriḥ* — Murari; *kva* — where; *murāriḥ* — Murari; *kva* — where; *kva* — where; *asau* — he; *satvaram* — quickly; *ānaya* — bring.

**103.** Then the glorious ocean of mercy, filled with wonder, asked: "Where is Murari? Where is Murari? Where is he? Bring him quickly!"

*Note.* The edition has *प्रपच्छ* for *papraccha*; the number lacks the second danda: *॥१०३*.

### Verse 104

इति श्रुत्वा प्रधावन्तः शतशो भृशमुत्सुकाः ।
सत्वरं तत्र गत्वा च नरेन्द्रसरसस्तटे ॥१०४॥

*iti śrutvā pradhāvantaḥ śataśo bhṛśam utsukāḥ |*
*satvaraṁ tatra gatvā ca narendra-sarasas taṭe ||104||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — this; *śrutvā* — hearing; *pradhāvantaḥ* — running off; *śataśaḥ* — by hundreds; *bhṛśam* — extremely; *utsukāḥ* — eager; *satvaram* — quickly; *tatra* — there; *gatvā* — going; *ca* — and; *narendra* — of the Narendra; *sarasaḥ* — of the lake; *taṭe* — on the shore.

**104.** Hearing this, [people] by the hundred, extremely eager, ran off and, quickly going there, on the shore of Narendra Lake…

*Note.* Verses 104–107 form one period (in the edition 106–107 are marked as a *yugmaka*).

### Verse 105

विह्वलं पतितं भूमौ रुदन्तं दीनचेतसम् ।
ददृशुस्ते तथैवोचुः शीघ्रमागम्यतामिति ॥१०५॥

*vihvalaṁ patitaṁ bhūmau rudantaṁ dīna-cetasam |*
*dadṛśus te tathaivocuḥ śīghram āgamyatām iti ||105||*

*Word for word:* *vihvalam* — overwhelmed; *patitam* — lying; *bhūmau* — on the ground; *rudantam* — weeping; *dīna* — downcast; *cetasam* — [with] a heart; *dadṛśuḥ* — saw; *te* — they; *tathā eva* — and so; *ūcuḥ* — said; *śīghram* — quickly; *āgamyatām* — come; *iti* — thus.

**105.** …saw him, overwhelmed, lying on the ground, weeping, his heart downcast; and so they said: "Come quickly!"

### Verse 106

तथा निशम्य तद्वाक्यं मुरारिः परमोत्सुकः ।
विह्वलोऽश्रुजलैः शश्वदाप्लुतो धूलिधूसरः ॥१०६॥

*tathā niśamya tad-vākyaṁ murāriḥ paramotsukaḥ |*
*vihvalo 'śru-jalaiḥ śaśvad āpluto dhūli-dhūsaraḥ ||106||*

*Word for word:* *tathā* — thus; *niśamya* — hearing; *tat* — their; *vākyam* — words; *murāriḥ* — Murari; *parama* — extremely; *utsukaḥ* — eager; *vihvalaḥ* — overwhelmed; *aśru* — of tears; *jalaiḥ* — by the waters; *śaśvat* — ceaselessly; *āplutaḥ* — drenched; *dhūli* — with dust; *dhūsaraḥ* — grey.

**106.** Hearing their words thus, Murari, extremely eager, overwhelmed, ceaselessly drenched with tears, grey with dust…

### Verse 107

तथैव विरुदन् भूरिकाकुप्रोक्तैर्महाशयः ।
ययौ परमनिर्विण्णः प्राणप्रभुमवेक्षितुम् ॥१०७॥ (युग्मकम्)

*tathaiva virudan bhūri-kāku-proktair mahāśayaḥ |*
*yayau parama-nirviṇṇaḥ prāṇa-prabhum avekṣitum ||107|| (yugmakam)*

*Word for word:* *tathā eva* — just so; *virudan* — sobbing; *bhūri* — with many; *kāku* — plaintive; *proktaiḥ* — utterances; *mahāśayaḥ* — the noble-hearted one; *yayau* — went; *parama* — utterly; *nirviṇṇaḥ* — despondent; *prāṇa* — of [his] life; *prabhum* — the Lord; *avekṣitum* — to see.

**107.** …sobbing just so, with many plaintive utterances, the noble-hearted one, utterly despondent, went to see the Lord of his life.

### Verse 108

स्तम्भघर्माम्बुभिः शश्वत् स्खलत्पदयुगः पतन् ।
संवीतस्यैव चेलस्य गले बद्धार्धमञ्चलम् ।
दन्ते निधाय बहुधा तृणानि तृणवद्व्रजन् ।
गलदश्रुपयोयुक्तवक्षोमौक्तिकहारधृक् ।
प्रेमान्ध इव तत्रैव चिरं प्रभुमलोकयत् ॥१०८॥

*stambha-gharmāmbubhiḥ śaśvat skhalat-pada-yugaḥ patan |*
*saṁvītasyaiva celasya gale baddhārdham añcalam |*
*dante nidhāya bahudhā tṛṇāni tṛṇavad vrajan |*
*galad-aśru-payo-yukta-vakṣo-mauktika-hāra-dhṛk |*
*premāndha iva tatraiva ciraṁ prabhum alokayat ||108||*

*Word for word:* *stambha* — from stupor; *gharma-ambubhiḥ* — and from sweat; *śaśvat* — constantly; *skhalat* — stumbling; *pada* — of feet; *yugaḥ* — [with] the pair; *patan* — falling; *saṁvītasya* — worn; *eva* — indeed; *celasya* — of the cloth; *gale* — on the neck; *baddha* — tied; *ardham* — half; *añcalam* — [with] the edge; *dante* — in the teeth; *nidhāya* — placing; *bahudhā* — many; *tṛṇāni* — blades of grass; *tṛṇa-vat* — like a blade of grass; *vrajan* — going; *galat* — flowing; *aśru* — of tears; *payaḥ* — with the water; *yukta* — made; *vakṣaḥ* — on the chest; *mauktika* — of pearls; *hāra* — a necklace; *dhṛk* — wearing; *prema* — by love; *andhaḥ* — blinded; *iva* — as if; *tatra eva* — right there; *ciram* — for a long time; *prabhum* — at the Lord; *alokayat* — gazed.

**108.** From stupor and sweat his feet kept stumbling, and he kept falling. The edge of the cloth he was wearing he had half tied round his neck; he had put many blades of grass between his teeth and went along [humble] as a blade of grass; on his chest he wore a necklace of pearls made of the water of his flowing tears. As if blinded by love, he gazed right there at the Lord for a long time.

*Note.* A verse of ten padas. A cloth round the neck and grass between the teeth are signs of complete submission. Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 11.152–157 (Murari with two bunches of grass between his teeth).

### Verse 109

सबाष्पकण्ठं किमपि वक्तुं शक्तो न च क्षणम् ।
तथापि गद्गदोद्गारलक्षकाकूक्तिवानसौ ।
दधार चरणाम्भोजे प्रभोः परमदीनधीः ।
तत्पादाम्बुजयुग्मं तत् सिषेच खलु भूयशः ।
लोचनद्वयनिर्गच्छदश्रुधारासमुच्चयैः ॥१०९॥

*sa-bāṣpa-kaṇṭhaṁ kim api vaktuṁ śakto na ca kṣaṇam |*
*tathāpi gadgadodgāra-lakṣa-kākūktivān asau |*
*dadhāra caraṇāmbhoje prabhoḥ parama-dīna-dhīḥ |*
*tat-pādāmbuja-yugmaṁ tat siṣeca khalu bhūyaśaḥ |*
*locana-dvaya-nirgacchad-aśru-dhārā-samuccayaiḥ ||109||*

*Word for word:* *sa-bāṣpa* — choked with tears; *kaṇṭham* — [with] the throat; *kim api* — anything; *vaktum* — to say; *śaktaḥ* — able; *na* — not; *ca* — and; *kṣaṇam* — even for a moment; *tathā api* — yet; *gadgada* — faltering; *udgāra* — in cries; *lakṣa* — a hundred thousand; *kāku* — plaintive; *uktivān* — uttering words; *asau* — he; *dadhāra* — clasped; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *ambhoje* — the lotuses; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *parama* — utterly; *dīna* — humble; *dhīḥ* — [with] a mind; *tat* — His; *pāda* — of feet; *ambuja* — of lotuses; *yugmam* — the pair; *tat* — that; *siṣeca* — bathed; *khalu* — indeed; *bhūyaśaḥ* — again and again; *locana* — of eyes; *dvaya* — from the pair; *nirgacchat* — issuing; *aśru* — of tears; *dhārā* — of streams; *samuccayaiḥ* — with masses.

**109.** His throat choked with tears, he could not say anything even for a moment. Yet, uttering a hundred thousand plaintive words in faltering cries, utterly humble in mind, he clasped the lotus feet of the Lord, and again and again he bathed that pair of His lotus feet with masses of streams of tears issuing from his two eyes.

*Note.* A verse of ten padas. The edition has *-samuccaye*; we read *-samuccayaiḥ* (instrumental) (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text as the edition.

### Verse 110

सोऽपि प्रभुस्तस्य पृष्ठं सिषेच नयनोद्भवैः ।
अम्भोभिरायतारक्तलोचनाम्बुरुहद्वयः ॥११०॥

*so 'pi prabhus tasya pṛṣṭhaṁ siṣeca nayanodbhavaiḥ |*
*ambhobhir āyatārakta-locanāmburuha-dvayaḥ ||110||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ api* — He too; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *tasya* — his; *pṛṣṭham* — back; *siṣeca* — bathed; *nayana* — from the eyes; *udbhavaiḥ* — springing; *ambhobhiḥ* — with waters; *āyata* — long; *ārakta* — reddened; *locana* — of eyes; *amburuha* — of lotuses; *dvayaḥ* — [with] the pair.

**110.** And the Lord, the pair of His long lotus eyes reddened, bathed his back with the waters that sprang from His eyes.

### Verse 111

तत्रस्थः सकलो लोकस्तस्य रोदनकाकुभिः ।
अरुदत् तत्सम इव तन्मयः समयोऽभवत् ॥१११॥

*tatra-sthaḥ sakalo lokas tasya rodana-kākubhiḥ |*
*arudat tat-sama iva tan-mayaḥ samayo 'bhavat ||111||*

*Word for word:* *tatra-sthaḥ* — present there; *sakalaḥ* — all; *lokaḥ* — the people; *tasya* — his; *rodana* — by the weeping; *kākubhiḥ* — and by the plaints; *arudat* — wept; *tat* — to him; *samaḥ* — like; *iva* — as if; *tat-mayaḥ* — full of him; *samayaḥ* — the time; *abhavat* — became.

### Verse 112

प्रभुश्च तत् काकुवादं रोदनं च महत्तरम् ।
दृष्ट्वा श्रुत्वा क्षणमपि न सेहे विकलोऽभवत् ॥११२॥

*prabhuś ca tat kāku-vādaṁ rodanaṁ ca mahattaram |*
*dṛṣṭvā śrutvā kṣaṇam api na sehe vikalo 'bhavat ||112||*

*Word for word:* *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *ca* — and; *tat* — those; *kāku* — plaintive; *vādam* — words; *rodanam* — weeping; *ca* — and; *mahattaram* — most intense; *dṛṣṭvā* — seeing; *śrutvā* — hearing; *kṣaṇam api* — even for a moment; *na sehe* — did not bear; *vikalaḥ* — shaken; *abhavat* — became.

**112.** And the Lord, seeing that most intense weeping and hearing those plaintive words, could not bear it even for a moment and was shaken.

### Verse 113

ततो बभौ तत्र नाथोऽद्वैतादिकसमन्वितः ।
स्निग्धो राकानिशानाथ इव नक्षत्रमण्डितः ॥११३॥

*tato babhau tatra nātho 'dvaitādika-samanvitaḥ |*
*snigdho rākā-niśānātha iva nakṣatra-maṇḍitaḥ ||113||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *babhau* — shone; *tatra* — there; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *advaita* — by Advaita; *ādika* — and the others; *samanvitaḥ* — accompanied; *snigdhaḥ* — gentle; *rākā* — of the full-moon night; *niśānāthaḥ* — the moon; *iva* — like; *nakṣatra* — with stars; *maṇḍitaḥ* — adorned.

**113.** Then the Lord shone there, accompanied by Advaita and the others, gentle, like the moon of the full-moon night adorned with stars…

### Verse 114

उद्यद्विद्रुमशोणास्यहास्यरञ्जितचन्द्रिकः ।
स्वाङ्गज्योत्स्नाच्छटाशश्वत्स्नापिताशावधूमुखः ॥११४॥

*udyad-vidruma-śoṇāsya-hāsya-rañjita-candrikaḥ |*
*svāṅga-jyotsnā-cchaṭā-śaśvat-snāpitāśā-vadhū-mukhaḥ ||114||*

*Word for word:* *udyat* — gleaming; *vidruma* — like coral; *śoṇa* — red; *āsya* — of the mouth; *hāsya* — by the smile; *rañjita* — tinged; *candrikaḥ* — [whose] moonlight; *sva* — of His own; *aṅga* — body; *jyotsnā* — of the moonlight; *chaṭā* — by the radiance; *śaśvat* — ceaselessly; *snāpita* — bathed; *āśā* — of the quarters; *vadhū* — of the maidens; *mukhaḥ* — [by whom] the faces.

**114.** …His moonlight tinged by the smile of His mouth, red as gleaming coral; with the radiance of the moonlight of His own body He ceaselessly bathed the faces of the maidens of the quarters.

### Verse 115

अथ ते कृष्णचैतन्यचरणासवलम्पटाः ।
स्नानयात्रादर्शनाय बभूवुरनिशोत्सुकाः ॥११५॥

*atha te kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caraṇāsava-lampaṭāḥ |*
*snāna-yātrā-darśanāya babhūvur aniśotsukāḥ ||115||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *te* — they; *kṛṣṇa-caitanya* — of Krishna-Chaitanya; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *āsava* — for the intoxicating drink; *lampaṭāḥ* — greedy; *snāna-yātrā* — the Snana-yatra; *darśanāya* — for seeing; *babhūvuḥ* — became; *aniśa* — ceaselessly; *utsukāḥ* — eager.

**115.** Then they, greedy for the intoxicating drink of the feet of Krishna-Chaitanya, became ceaselessly eager to see the Snana-yatra.

### Verse 116

एकादश्यां च ददृशुर्विवाहोत्सवमुत्सुकाः ।
ततश्च पूर्णिमायां ते स्नानयात्रां च पावनीम् ॥११६॥

*ekādaśyāṁ ca dadṛśur vivāhotsavam utsukāḥ |*
*tataś ca pūrṇimāyāṁ te snāna-yātrāṁ ca pāvanīm ||116||*

*Word for word:* *ekādaśyām* — on the Ekadashi; *ca* — and; *dadṛśuḥ* — saw; *vivāha* — of the wedding; *utsavam* — the festival; *utsukāḥ* — eager; *tataḥ* — then; *ca* — and; *pūrṇimāyām* — on the full moon; *te* — they; *snāna-yātrām* — the Snana-yatra; *ca* — and; *pāvanīm* — purifying.

**116.** On the Ekadashi they eagerly watched the wedding festival, and then, on the full moon, the purifying Snana-yatra.

*Note.* The wedding is apparently the festival of Rukmini-harana, which in Puri is celebrated on the Ekadashi of the bright fortnight of Jyeshtha, four days before the Snana-yatra (on the full moon); not confirmed in our sources.

### Verse 117

तत्र नीलगिरौ रम्ये सौधाट्टालकगोपुरे ।
पुरे महितसौन्दर्ये रमणीये सुखावहे ।
शुभ्राभ्रंलिहसश्रीकप्रासादवति कश्चन ।
स्नानमञ्चः सञ्चरति सुधाभिरनुरञ्जितः ॥११७॥

*tatra nīla-girau ramye saudhāṭṭālaka-gopure |*
*pure mahita-saundarye ramaṇīye sukhāvahe |*
*śubhrābhraṁliha-saśrīka-prāsādavati kaścana |*
*snāna-mañcaḥ sañcarati sudhābhir anurañjitaḥ ||117||*

*Word for word:* *tatra* — there; *nīla-girau* — on the Blue Mountain; *ramye* — lovely; *saudha* — with mansions; *aṭṭālaka* — towers; *gopure* — [and] gateways; *pure* — in the city; *mahita* — exalted; *saundarye* — [with] beauty; *ramaṇīye* — delightful; *sukha-āvahe* — bringing happiness; *śubhra* — white; *abhraṁliha* — cloud-licking; *sa-śrīka* — splendid; *prāsāda-vati* — with temples; *kaścana* — a certain; *snāna* — of bathing; *mañcaḥ* — platform; *sañcarati* — moves along [as it were]; *sudhābhiḥ* — with whitewash (with nectar); *anurañjitaḥ* — adorned.

**117.** There, on the lovely Blue Mountain, in the delightful, joy-bringing city of exalted beauty, with its mansions, towers and gateways, with its splendid white temples that lick the clouds, a certain bathing platform, adorned with whitewash (and as if steeped in nectar), moves along, as it were.

*Note.* A verse of eight padas. *Sañcarati* ("moves") is understood thus: the platform is stationary, but it seems to move. *Sudhā* means both "whitewash" and "nectar". The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 118

ततः पूर्वेद्युरस्ताद्रिं द्युमणौ याति सुन्दरम् ।
तं मञ्चं मण्डितं कर्तुमारेभे तत्परो जनः ॥११८॥

*tataḥ pūrve-dyur astādriṁ dyumaṇau yāti sundaram |*
*taṁ mañcaṁ maṇḍitaṁ kartum ārebhe tat-paro janaḥ ||118||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *pūrve-dyuḥ* — on the day before; *asta* — of setting; *adrim* — to the mountain; *dyumaṇau* — when the sun; *yāti* — was going; *sundaram* — beautifully; *tam* — that; *mañcam* — platform; *maṇḍitam* — adorned; *kartum* — to make; *ārebhe* — began; *tat-paraḥ* — zealous; *janaḥ* — the people.

**118.** Then, on the day before, when the sun was going to the mountain of its setting, the zealous people began to adorn that platform beautifully.

### Verse 119

तथैव तत्र कलया हीनः पूर्णवदुद्गतः ।
रराज रजनीकान्तः कान्तयंस्तत् पुरं महत् ॥११९॥

*tathaiva tatra kalayā hīnaḥ pūrṇavad udgataḥ |*
*rarāja rajanī-kāntaḥ kāntayaṁs tat puraṁ mahat ||119||*

*Word for word:* *tathā eva* — likewise; *tatra* — there; *kalayā* — by one digit; *hīnaḥ* — lacking; *pūrṇa-vat* — as if full; *udgataḥ* — risen; *rarāja* — shone; *rajanī* — of the night; *kāntaḥ* — the beloved (the moon); *kāntayan* — beautifying; *tat* — that; *puram* — city; *mahat* — great.

**119.** Likewise there the beloved of the night — the moon — rose, lacking one digit yet as if full, and shone, beautifying that great city.

*Note.* The evening of the fourteenth day, the eve of the full moon.

### Verse 120

स्नानमञ्चमपि श्रीमान् सुधांशुः सुधयान्वितः ।
करैः संमार्जयामास सेवापर इव प्रभोः ॥१२०॥

*snāna-mañcam api śrīmān sudhāṁśuḥ sudhayānvitaḥ |*
*karaiḥ saṁmārjayāmāsa sevā-para iva prabhoḥ ||120||*

*Word for word:* *snāna* — of bathing; *mañcam* — the platform; *api* — too; *śrīmān* — the lovely; *sudhāṁśuḥ* — moon; *sudhayā* — with nectar; *anvitaḥ* — filled; *karaiḥ* — with rays (with hands); *saṁmārjayāmāsa* — swept clean; *sevā* — on service; *paraḥ* — intent; *iva* — as if; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord.

**120.** And the lovely moon, full of nectar, swept the bathing platform clean with its rays — its hands — as if intent on the Lord's service.

*Note.* The edition has *करौ* (dual). We read *karaiḥ* (?). A play on words: *kara* is both "ray" and "hand"; *sudhā* — "nectar" and "whitewash". The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text as the edition.

### Verse 121

जालेन महता राजत्क्षुद्रघण्टासुघर्घरैः ।
सतोरणेन दिव्येन पुष्पमाल्यैरनेकधा ॥१२१॥

*jālena mahatā rājat-kṣudra-ghaṇṭā-sughargharaiḥ |*
*satoraṇena divyena puṣpa-mālyair anekadhā ||121||*

*Word for word:* *jālena* — with a net; *mahatā* — great; *rājat* — glittering; *kṣudra* — small; *ghaṇṭā* — of bells; *su-ghargharaiḥ* — with the ringing jingle; *sa-toraṇena* — with arches; *divyena* — wondrous; *puṣpa* — of flowers; *mālyaiḥ* — with garlands; *anekadhā* — in many ways.

**121.** With a great, wondrous net with arches, with the ringing jingle of glittering little bells, with garlands of flowers of many kinds —

*Note.* Verses 121–122 form one period. The edition has *दीव्येन*, a misprint for *divyena*.

### Verse 122

मण्डिते स्नाननिलये तच्छोभानां समुद्गमे ।
अभूत् क इव निर्वाच्यो जगज्जनमनोरमः ॥१२२॥

*maṇḍite snāna-nilaye tac-chobhānāṁ samudgame |*
*abhūt ka iva nirvācyo jagaj-jana-manoramaḥ ||122||*

*Word for word:* *maṇḍite* — when adorned; *snāna* — of bathing; *nilaye* — the pavilion; *tat* — its; *śobhānām* — of the beauties; *samudgame* — at the full rising; *abhūt* — arose; *kaḥ iva* — what; *nirvācyaḥ* — to be described; *jagat* — of the world; *jana* — of the people; *manaḥ-ramaḥ* — delighting the minds.

**122.** — when the bathing pavilion had been [so] adorned, at the full rising of its beauties there arose something — how could it be described? — that delighted the minds of the people of the whole world.

### Verse 123

ततो गौराङ्गचन्द्रस्याज्ञापनेन महाशयाः ।
स्नानसंदर्शनोत्कण्ठाः प्राकारोपरि सुस्थिराः ॥१२३॥

*tato gaurāṅga-candrasyājñāpanena mahāśayāḥ |*
*snāna-saṁdarśanotkaṇṭhāḥ prākāropari susthirāḥ ||123||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *gaurāṅga-candrasya* — of Gauranga-chandra; *ājñāpanena* — by the command; *mahāśayāḥ* — the noble-hearted ones; *snāna* — the bathing; *saṁdarśana* — to see; *utkaṇṭhāḥ* — longing; *prākāra* — of the enclosure wall; *upari* — on top; *susthirāḥ* — firmly settled.

**123.** Then, at the command of Gauranga-chandra, the noble-hearted ones, longing to see the bathing, settled firmly on top of the enclosure wall…

*Note.* Verses 123–124 form one period.

### Verse 124

विरेजुरन्तरीक्षस्था देवा इव हरेः पुरः ।
श्रीगौराङ्गकरालिप्तचन्दनै राजितोरसः ॥१२४॥

*virejur antarīkṣa-sthā devā iva hareḥ puraḥ |*
*śrī-gaurāṅga-karālipta-candanai rājitorasaḥ ||124||*

*Word for word:* *virejuḥ* — shone; *antarīkṣa* — in the sky; *sthāḥ* — standing; *devāḥ* — the gods; *iva* — like; *hareḥ* — of Hari [Indra]; *puraḥ* — before; *śrī-gaurāṅga* — of Sri Gauranga; *kara* — by the hand; *ālipta* — applied; *candanaiḥ* — with sandal paste; *rājita* — adorned; *urasaḥ* — [with] chests.

**124.** …and shone like the gods standing in the sky before Hari, their chests adorned with sandal paste applied by the hand of Sri Gauranga.

*Note.* *Hari* here is probably Indra, the king of the gods.

### Verse 125

यामिन्याश्चरमे काले आगते दयितादयः ।
सन्नाहपट्टं विमलं श्रीमदङ्गे न्ययोजयन् ॥१२५॥

*yāminyāś carame kāle āgate dayitādayaḥ |*
*sannāha-paṭṭaṁ vimalaṁ śrīmad-aṅge nyayojayan ||125||*

*Word for word:* *yāminyāḥ* — of the night; *carame* — in the last; *kāle* — time; *āgate* — when [it] had come; *dayita* — the dayitas; *ādayaḥ* — and others; *sannāha* — of girding; *paṭṭam* — the silk band; *vimalam* — spotless; *śrīmat* — beautiful; *aṅge* — on the body; *nyayojayan* — fastened.

**125.** When the last part of the night had come, the dayitas and others fastened the spotless silk girding-band on the beautiful body [of Jagannatha].

*Note.* The dayitas (daitapatis) are the temple servitors who carry the Deities.

### Verse 126

ततः पूर्वं हलधरो विजयोद्यममावहन् ।
सिंहासनादवतरन् बभौ कोटीन्दुवद्विभुः ॥१२६॥

*tataḥ pūrvaṁ haladharo vijayodyamam āvahan |*
*siṁhāsanād avataran babhau koṭīnduvad vibhuḥ ||126||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *pūrvam* — first; *hala-dharaḥ* — the Plough-bearer; *vijaya* — for the triumphal march; *udyamam* — readiness; *āvahan* — showing; *siṁhāsanāt* — from the throne; *avataran* — descending; *babhau* — shone; *koṭi* — millions; *indu-vat* — like moons; *vibhuḥ* — the almighty Lord.

**126.** Then first the Plough-bearer, showing His readiness for the triumphal march, descended from the throne — the almighty Lord shone like millions of moons.

*Note.* The Plough-bearer is Balarama (Baladeva). The edition has a superfluous syllable: *बभौ क कोटीन्दुवद्*; the metre requires *क* to be omitted.

### Verse 127

ततो भगवती देवी सुभद्राथ जगत्पतिः ।
जगन्नाथोऽप्यवतरन् विचित्रां श्रियमाययौ ॥१२७॥

*tato bhagavatī devī subhadrātha jagat-patiḥ |*
*jagannātho 'py avataran vicitrāṁ śriyam āyayau ||127||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *bhagavatī* — holy; *devī* — the goddess; *subhadrā* — Subhadra; *atha* — then; *jagat-patiḥ* — the Lord of the world; *jagannāthaḥ* — Jagannatha; *api* — too; *avataran* — descending; *vicitrām* — wondrous; *śriyam* — splendour; *āyayau* — attained.

**127.** Then the holy goddess Subhadra, and then the Lord of the world, Jagannatha, too, descending [from the throne], attained a wondrous splendour.

### Verse 128

ततो गौरसुधारश्मिः पुरतः पुरतो व्रजन् ।
ददर्श वर्त्मविजयं क्रमशस्तं त्रयस्य च ॥१२८॥

*tato gaura-sudhā-raśmiḥ purataḥ purato vrajan |*
*dadarśa vartma-vijayaṁ kramaśas taṁ trayasya ca ||128||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *gaura* — the golden; *sudhā-raśmiḥ* — moon; *purataḥ purataḥ* — ever ahead; *vrajan* — going; *dadarśa* — watched; *vartma* — along the way; *vijayam* — the triumphal march; *kramaśaḥ* — one after another; *tam* — that; *trayasya* — of the three; *ca* — and.

**128.** And then the golden Moon, going ever ahead, watched that triumphal march of the Three along the way, one after another.

*Note.* *Vijaya* (Oriya *pahaṇḍi vijaya*) is the solemn procession of the Deities.

### Verse 129

पादन्यासैर्दलन् भूमिं कशिपोः कशिपूत्तमम् ।
व्रजन् बभौ जगन्नाथो यथा भाद्भान्तरं शशी ॥१२९॥

*pāda-nyāsair dalan bhūmiṁ kaśipoḥ kaśipūttamam |*
*vrajan babhau jagannātho yathā bhād bhāntaraṁ śaśī ||129||*

*Word for word:* *pāda* — of the feet; *nyāsaiḥ* — by the treading; *dalan* — shaking; *bhūmim* — the earth; *kaśipoḥ* — from a cushion; *kaśipu* — to a cushion; *uttamam* — finer; *vrajan* — passing; *babhau* — shone; *jagannāthaḥ* — Jagannatha; *yathā* — as; *bhāt* — from a star; *bha-antaram* — to another star; *śaśī* — the moon.

**129.** Shaking the earth with His steps, passing from cushion to finer cushion, Jagannatha shone like the moon passing from star to star.

*Note.* During the procession the Deities are carried along cotton cushions (*kaśipu*) laid out on the way.

### Verse 130

तं सोपानपरम्पराभिरमलं स्वच्छद्युतिं मण्डपं
चञ्चद्वीचिपरम्पराप्रविलसत्क्षीराब्धिशोभामुषम् ।
घण्टाघर्घरनादलक्षितजयध्वानैश्च जालोच्चयैः
सम्यग्भूषितमारुरोह भगवान् नीलाद्रिचूडामणिः ॥१३०॥

*taṁ sopāna-paramparābhir amalaṁ svaccha-dyutiṁ maṇḍapaṁ*
*cañcad-vīci-paramparā-pravilasat-kṣīrābdhi-śobhā-muṣam |*
*ghaṇṭā-ghargharanāda-lakṣita-jaya-dhvānaiś ca jāloccayaiḥ*
*samyag bhūṣitam āruroha bhagavān nīlādri-cūḍāmaṇiḥ ||130||*

*Word for word:* *tam* — onto that; *sopāna* — of steps; *paramparābhiḥ* — by the rows; *amalam* — spotless; *svaccha* — clear; *dyutim* — [of] radiance; *maṇḍapam* — pavilion; *cañcat* — dancing; *vīci* — of waves; *paramparā* — with a succession; *pravilasat* — sparkling; *kṣīra-abdhi* — of the ocean of milk; *śobhā* — the beauty; *muṣam* — stealing; *ghaṇṭā* — of bells; *ghargharanāda* — by the jingling; *lakṣita* — marked; *jaya* — of "jaya"; *dhvānaiḥ* — with the cries; *ca* — and; *jāla* — of nets; *uccayaiḥ* — with masses; *samyak* — fully; *bhūṣitam* — adorned; *āruroha* — ascended; *bhagavān* — the Lord; *nīla-adri* — of the Blue Mountain; *cūḍā-maṇiḥ* — the crest-jewel.

**130.** Onto that pavilion — spotless, clear in radiance with its rows of steps, stealing the beauty of the ocean of milk that sparkles with a succession of dancing waves, fully adorned with masses of nets and with cries of "Jaya!" marked by the jingling of bells — the Lord, the crest-jewel of the Blue Mountain, ascended.

*Note.* The metre of verses 130–132 and 134–135 is *śārdūla-vikrīḍita*.

### Verse 131

श्रीचैतन्यमहाप्रभुश्च पुरतो भक्तैर्जनैरावृतः
शश्वल्लोचनपङ्कजद्वयगलद्धारां वहन् वक्षसि ।
धाराभिर्विलसन्नसावपि जगन्नाथः स्वयं स्नापितो
रेजेऽन्योन्यसमानविभ्रमसमालोकेन हर्षाकुलः ॥१३१॥

*śrī-caitanya-mahāprabhuś ca purato bhaktair janair āvṛtaḥ*
*śaśval-locana-paṅkaja-dvaya-galad-dhārāṁ vahan vakṣasi |*
*dhārābhir vilasann asāv api jagannāthaḥ svayaṁ snāpito*
*reje 'nyonya-samāna-vibhrama-samālokena harṣākulaḥ ||131||*

*Word for word:* *śrī-caitanya-mahāprabhuḥ* — Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu; *ca* — and; *purataḥ* — in front; *bhaktaiḥ* — devotee; *janaiḥ* — by people; *āvṛtaḥ* — surrounded; *śaśvat* — ceaselessly; *locana* — of eyes; *paṅkaja* — of lotuses; *dvaya* — from the pair; *galat* — flowing; *dhārām* — the stream; *vahan* — bearing; *vakṣasi* — on the chest; *dhārābhiḥ* — with streams; *vilasan* — gleaming; *asau* — He; *api* — too; *jagannāthaḥ* — Jagannatha; *svayam* — Himself; *snāpitaḥ* — bathed; *reje* — shone; *anyonya* — mutual; *samāna* — equal; *vibhrama* — of the play; *samālokena* — by the beholding; *harṣa* — with joy; *ākulaḥ* — overwhelmed.

**131.** Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, surrounded by devotees, [stood] in front, bearing on His chest the stream that flowed ceaselessly from His two lotus eyes; and Jagannatha Himself too, being bathed, gleamed with streams [of water]. Beholding in each other the same play, [each] shone, overwhelmed with joy.

### Verse 132

उच्चैरुच्चवदुल्लसज्जयजयस्वानैः समानोत्थितैः
पुष्पस्तोमसमानवृष्टिभिरपि श्रीमान् महानुत्सवः ।
आसीत् सर्वजनस्य लोचनयुगानन्दामृताय स्फुटं
ब्रह्माद्यैरपि दुर्लभोऽसितगिरिश्रीमन्मणेः साम्प्रतम् ॥१३२॥

*uccair uccavad ullasaj-jaya-jaya-svānaiḥ samānotthitaiḥ*
*puṣpa-stoma-samāna-vṛṣṭibhir api śrīmān mahān utsavaḥ |*
*āsīt sarva-janasya locana-yugānandāmṛtāya sphuṭaṁ*
*brahmādyair api durlabho 'sita-giri-śrīman-maṇeḥ sāmpratam ||132||*

*Word for word:* *uccaiḥ* — loudly; *ucca-vat* — on high; *ullasat* — ringing out; *jaya-jaya* — of "jaya, jaya"; *svānaiḥ* — with the cries; *samāna* — all together; *utthitaiḥ* — risen; *puṣpa* — of flowers; *stoma* — of heaps; *samāna* — even; *vṛṣṭibhiḥ* — with showers; *api* — and; *śrīmān* — splendid; *mahān* — great; *utsavaḥ* — the festival; *āsīt* — became; *sarva* — of all; *janasya* — of the people; *locana* — of eyes; *yuga* — of the pairs; *ānanda* — of bliss; *amṛtāya* — for the nectar; *sphuṭam* — plainly; *brahma-ādyaiḥ* — for Brahma and the others; *api* — even; *durlabhaḥ* — hard to attain; *asita* — of the Dark; *giri* — of the Mountain; *śrīmat* — of the glorious; *maṇeḥ* — of the jewel; *sāmpratam* — now.

**132.** With loud cries of "Jaya, jaya!" ringing out on high, rising all together, and with even showers of heaps of flowers, the splendid great festival of the glorious jewel of the Dark Mountain — hard to attain even for Brahma and the others — now plainly became a nectar of bliss for the eyes of all the people.

*Note.* The edition has *दुर्लभो सितगिरि-*, without the avagraha. We read *durlabho 'sita-giri-* ("of the Dark Mountain", that is, of Nilachala).

### Verse 133

स्नानाम्बुधाराप्लुत एष नील-
गिरीश्वरो गौरसुधाकरस्य ।
विच्छेदभावेन रुदन् विरेजे
चिराय गुप्तो भवितेति देवः ॥१३३॥

*snānāmbu-dhārāpluta eṣa nīla-*
*girīśvaro gaura-sudhākarasya |*
*viccheda-bhāvena rudan vireje*
*cirāya gupto bhaviteti devaḥ ||133||*

*Word for word:* *snāna* — of the bathing; *ambu* — of water; *dhārā* — by the streams; *āplutaḥ* — drenched; *eṣaḥ* — this; *nīla-giri* — of the Blue Mountain; *īśvaraḥ* — the Lord; *gaura* — from the golden; *sudhākarasya* — moon; *viccheda* — of separation; *bhāvena* — in the mood; *rudan* — weeping; *vireje* — shone; *cirāya* — for a long time; *guptaḥ* — hidden; *bhavitā* — [I] shall be; *iti* — thus [thinking]; *devaḥ* — the Lord.

**133.** Drenched by the streams of bathing water, this Lord of the Blue Mountain shone, weeping in the mood of separation from the golden Moon, [as if thinking]: "For a long time I shall be hidden."

*Note.* The metre is *upajāti*. The streams of bathing water are fancied as tears. A hint at the anavasara (cf. 13.57). The edition numbers the verse *॥२३३॥*, a misprint for 133.

### Verse 134

एवं स्नानमहोत्सवामृतरसस्निग्धोरुवक्षःस्थलः
श्रीनीलाचलमौलिरम्यतिलकः स्थित्वा क्षणं सक्षणः ।
आरेभे पुनरप्यसौ कशिपुभिर्गच्छन् शुभं दक्षिणा-
वर्तं सेवकसञ्चयैर्वृतभुजस्तम्भद्वयः श्रीयुतः ॥१३४॥

*evaṁ snāna-mahotsavāmṛta-rasa-snigdhoru-vakṣaḥ-sthalaḥ*
*śrī-nīlācala-mauli-ramya-tilakaḥ sthitvā kṣaṇaṁ sakṣaṇaḥ |*
*ārebhe punar apy asau kaśipubhir gacchan śubhaṁ dakṣiṇā-*
*vartaṁ sevaka-sañcayair vṛta-bhuja-stambha-dvayaḥ śrīyutaḥ ||134||*

*Word for word:* *evam* — thus; *snāna* — of the bathing; *mahā-utsava* — of the great festival; *amṛta* — of the nectar; *rasa* — with the liquid; *snigdha* — anointed; *uru* — broad; *vakṣaḥ-sthalaḥ* — [whose] chest; *śrī-nīlācala* — of Sri Nilachala; *mauli* — of the crown; *ramya* — lovely; *tilakaḥ* — the tilaka; *sthitvā* — having stood; *kṣaṇam* — a moment; *sa-kṣaṇaḥ* — in festive joy; *ārebhe* — began; *punaḥ api* — again; *asau* — He; *kaśipubhiḥ* — over the cushions; *gacchan* — going; *śubham* — auspicious; *dakṣiṇa-āvartam* — a clockwise circuit; *sevaka* — of servants; *sañcayaiḥ* — by throngs; *vṛta* — held; *bhuja* — of arms; *stambha* — of pillars; *dvayaḥ* — [whose] pair; *śrī-yutaḥ* — splendid.

**134.** Thus He — the lovely tilaka on the crown of Sri Nilachala, His broad chest anointed with the nectar-liquid of the great bathing festival — stood [there] a moment in festive joy; then, splendid, He began again to move over the cushions in an auspicious clockwise circuit, the pair of pillars that were His arms held by throngs of servants.

### Verse 135

कूर्मः सीदति शेष एष चलितः सर्वैः फणामण्डलैः
क्षौणी क्षुभ्यति भूभृतो विदलिता ब्रह्माण्डमुत्खण्डितम् ।
मर्यादामपि सागरोऽप्यतिगतो दुद्राव भास्वानसौ
प्रस्थाने मुरवैरिणो विजयिनो नीलाद्रिचूडामणेः ॥१३५॥

*kūrmaḥ sīdati śeṣa eṣa calitaḥ sarvaiḥ phaṇā-maṇḍalaiḥ*
*kṣauṇī kṣubhyati bhūbhṛto vidalitā brahmāṇḍam utkhaṇḍitam |*
*maryādām api sāgaro 'py atigato dudrāva bhāsvān asau*
*prasthāne mura-vairiṇo vijayino nīlādri-cūḍāmaṇeḥ ||135||*

*Word for word:* *kūrmaḥ* — the Tortoise; *sīdati* — sinks; *śeṣaḥ* — Shesha; *eṣaḥ* — this; *calitaḥ* — shaken; *sarvaiḥ* — with all; *phaṇā* — of hoods; *maṇḍalaiḥ* — with the circles; *kṣauṇī* — the earth; *kṣubhyati* — quakes; *bhūbhṛtaḥ* — the mountains; *vidalitāḥ* — split; *brahmāṇḍam* — the egg of Brahma; *utkhaṇḍitam* — cracked; *maryādām* — the bounds; *api* — even; *sāgaraḥ* — the ocean; *api* — and; *atigataḥ* — has overstepped; *dudrāva* — has fled; *bhāsvān* — the sun; *asau* — yonder; *prasthāne* — at the setting out; *mura-vairiṇaḥ* — of the Enemy of Mura; *vijayinaḥ* — of the victorious; *nīla-adri* — of the Blue Mountain; *cūḍā-maṇeḥ* — of the crest-jewel.

**135.** At the setting out of the victorious Enemy of Mura, the crest-jewel of the Blue Mountain, the Tortoise sinks, this Shesha is shaken with all the circles of his hoods, the earth quakes, the mountains are split, the egg of Brahma is cracked, the ocean has overstepped even its bounds, and the sun yonder has taken to flight!

*Note.* The classical hyperbole of "the hero's march". The Tortoise and Shesha uphold the earth. The Enemy of Mura is Krishna.

**Colophon:** इति श्रीकृष्णचैतन्यचरितामृते महाकाव्ये चतुर्दशः सर्गः । (*iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahākāvye caturdaśaḥ sargaḥ*) — "Thus [ends] the fourteenth sarga in the mahakavya 'Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita'." (The colophon gives no title for the sarga.)

---

## Sarga Fifteen — verses 1–110

**Title of the sarga:** none — the colophon of the edition gives no title for this sarga.
**Metre:**
- 1–104 — *puṣpitāgrā* (odd padas ⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑—⏑—⏑——, 12 syllables; even padas ⏑⏑⏑⏑—⏑⏑—⏑—⏑——, 13 syllables).
- 105 — *sragdharā* (————⏑——⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑——⏑——⏑——; 21 syllables per pada).
- 106 and 108 — *śārdūla-vikrīḍita* (———⏑⏑—⏑—⏑⏑⏑———⏑——⏑—; 19 syllables per pada); 106 is a verse of six padas.
- 107 — *pṛthvī* (⏑—⏑⏑⏑—⏑—⏑⏑⏑—⏑——⏑—; 17 syllables per pada).
- 109 — *hariṇī* (⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑—————⏑—⏑⏑—⏑—; 17 syllables per pada), with rhyme at the ends of the padas.
- 110 — *mālinī* (⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑———⏑——⏑——; 15 syllables per pada).

**Total verses:** 110.

**Contents of the passage:** the anavasara; the cleansing of the Gundicha temple; the Netrotsava; Jagannatha mounts the chariot.
- 1–11 — the anavasara: Jagannatha remains hidden with Lakshmi; the Lord's longing (the separation of the gopis); His consolation — the Lord of the gopis on the swing, with the dancing of the devadasis (9–10, *yugmaka*).
- 12–23 — the preparations: the brooms, the bath before dawn, the crimson cloth; the Lord gives out a hundred brooms; the run to the Gundicha, like an elephant broken loose.
- 24–34 — the sweeping: the devotees forget themselves; "you — here, you — there"; blows with brooms for latecomers; the Lord cleans the throne and is covered with dust; "Krishna, Krishna, Krishna".
- 35–54 — the washing: water from the well passed along a chain, "a game of ball with pitchers"; the Lord washes the veranda; the drenched crimson cloth ("Meru in the evening clouds").
- 55–65 — gathering blades of grass and pebbles in the courtyard, a contest of who gathers more (57–58); kirtana and dancing.
- 66–70 — bathing in the tank; obeisance to Nrisimha.
- 71–77 — **the Netrotsava**: the first darshan after the anavasara; the Lord and Jagannatha are "alike": neither of them blinks; at the bhoga-mandapa.
- 78–90 — Jagannatha with Lakshmi; the journey to the Gundicha as "a journey to Vrindavana"; the descent from the throne over cushions.
- 91–99 — the procession: the "game of ball" of Jagannatha and Gaura; Prataparudra sweeps with a golden broom (95–96); Jagannatha mounts the chariot.
- 100–110 — the Lord bathes Advaita, Srivasa and the singers and anoints them with sandal paste (the list, 105–106); the setting out; He falls prostrate before the chariot of Baladeva.

### Verse 1

असितगिरिपतिस्ततोऽयमन्तः-
पुरपरिचारिकया श्रिया समेतः ।
अनवसरमुपेत्य गूढवेशो
वसति जनस्य विलोचनातिदूरः ॥१॥

*asita-giri-patis tato 'yam antaḥ-*
*pura-paricārikayā śriyā sametaḥ |*
*anavasaram upetya gūḍha-veśo*
*vasati janasya vilocanāti-dūraḥ ||1||*

*Word for word:* *asita* — of the Dark; *giri* — Mountain; *patiḥ* — the Lord; *tataḥ* — then; *ayam* — this; *antaḥ-pura* — of the inner apartments; *paricārikayā* — with the attendant; *śriyā* — with Lakshmi; *sametaḥ* — united; *anavasaram* — the anavasara; *upetya* — having reached; *gūḍha* — hidden; *veśaḥ* — [whose] guise [is]; *vasati* — dwells; *janasya* — of the people; *vilocana* — from the eyes; *ati-dūraḥ* — far away.

**1.** Then, when the anavasara has come, this Lord of the Dark Mountain, together with Lakshmi, the attendant of the inner apartments, dwells in hidden guise, far away from the eyes of the people.

*Note.* The *anavasara* is the fortnight after the Snana-yatra during which Jagannatha is not shown to the people. The Lord of the Dark Mountain is Jagannatha (the Dark Mountain is Nilachala).

### Verse 2

असितगिरिनिवासिभक्तलोका-
नतिशयितार्तिपरान् विधातुकामः ।
स निभृतमथवा श्रिया विहर्तुं
रहसि निलीय रराज देव एषः ॥२॥

*asita-giri-nivāsi-bhakta-lokān*
*atiśayitārti-parān vidhātu-kāmaḥ |*
*sa nibhṛtam athavā śriyā vihartuṁ*
*rahasi nilīya rarāja deva eṣaḥ ||2||*

*Word for word:* *asita-giri* — on the Dark Mountain; *nivāsi* — dwelling; *bhakta* — devoted; *lokān* — people; *atiśayita* — to boundless; *ārti* — anguish; *parān* — given over; *vidhātu* — to make; *kāmaḥ* — desiring; *saḥ* — He; *nibhṛtam* — in seclusion; *athavā* — or else; *śriyā* — with Lakshmi; *vihartum* — to sport; *rahasi* — in secret; *nilīya* — having hidden; *rarāja* — shone; *devaḥ* — God; *eṣaḥ* — this.

**2.** Whether desiring to give the devoted people who dwell on the Dark Mountain over to boundless anguish, or else to sport with Lakshmi in seclusion, this God hid Himself and shone in secret.

### Verse 3

अथ तदनवलोकनातिदुःख-
क्षुभिततमानि मनांसि बिभ्रतस्ते ।
असितगिरिनिवासिनो महान्तो
भृशमतपन् प्रभुदर्शनेन हीनाः ॥३॥

*atha tad-anavalokanāti-duḥkha-*
*kṣubhitatamāni manāṁsi bibhratas te |*
*asita-giri-nivāsino mahānto*
*bhṛśam atapan prabhu-darśanena hīnāḥ ||3||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *tat* — of Him; *anavalokana* — from not seeing; *ati-duḥkha* — by great sorrow; *kṣubhitatamāni* — utterly agitated; *manāṁsi* — hearts; *bibhrataḥ* — bearing; *te* — they; *asita-giri* — on the Dark Mountain; *nivāsinaḥ* — dwelling; *mahāntaḥ* — great souls; *bhṛśam* — intensely; *atapan* — were tormented; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *darśanena* — of the sight; *hīnāḥ* — deprived.

**3.** Then those great souls who dwelt on the Dark Mountain, bearing hearts utterly agitated by the great sorrow of not seeing Him, were intensely tormented, deprived of the sight of the Lord.

### Verse 4

प्रभुरपि स शचीसुतोऽथ दुःखी
भृशमभवद्विकलो न तं विलोक्य ।
प्रकटयति च तच्छलेन वृन्दा-
वनरमणीजनविप्रयोगदुःखम् ॥४॥

*prabhur api sa śacī-suto 'tha duḥkhī*
*bhṛśam abhavad vikalo na taṁ vilokya |*
*prakaṭayati ca tac-chalena vṛndā-*
*vana-ramaṇī-jana-viprayoga-duḥkham ||4||*

*Word for word:* *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *api* — also; *saḥ* — He; *śacī-sutaḥ* — the son of Shachi; *atha* — then; *duḥkhī* — sorrowful; *bhṛśam* — greatly; *abhavat* — became; *vikalaḥ* — distraught; *na* — not; *tam* — Him; *vilokya* — seeing; *prakaṭayati* — reveals; *ca* — and; *tat* — of this; *chalena* — under the pretext; *vṛndāvana* — of Vrindavana; *ramaṇī* — of the beautiful women; *jana* — of the folk; *viprayoga* — of separation; *duḥkham* — the sorrow.

**4.** And the Lord, the son of Shachi, not seeing Him, then became sorrowful and greatly distraught. And under this pretext He reveals the sorrow of separation of the beautiful women of Vrindavana.

### Verse 5

निरवधि हृदयस्थितानि वृन्दा-
वनरमणीविरहस्य दुःखितानि ।
अनुभवति स तच्छलेन लब्धा-
वसरमुदेति हि चेतसो विकारः ॥५॥

*niravadhi hṛdaya-sthitāni vṛndā-*
*vana-ramaṇī-virahasya duḥkhitāni |*
*anubhavati sa tac-chalena labdhā-*
*vasaram udeti hi cetaso vikāraḥ ||5||*

*Word for word:* *niravadhi* — unceasingly; *hṛdaya* — in the heart; *sthitāni* — abiding; *vṛndāvana* — of Vrindavana; *ramaṇī* — of the beautiful women; *virahasya* — of separation; *duḥkhitāni* — the pains; *anubhavati* — experiences; *saḥ* — He; *tat* — of this; *chalena* — under the pretext; *labdha* — having found; *avasaram* — an opportunity; *udeti* — rises; *hi* — for; *cetasaḥ* — of the heart; *vikāraḥ* — the agitation.

**5.** Under this pretext He experiences the pains of separation of the beautiful women of Vrindavana, which abide unceasingly in His heart; for the agitation of the heart rises up as soon as it has found an opportunity.

### Verse 6

निरवधिगलदश्रुणोऽवतारै-
रुरसि सुसंभृतहारविभ्रमाढ्यः ।
कृशिमभिरवशिष्टशिष्टनामा
चिरविरहाद्विषसाद गौरचन्द्रः ॥६॥

*niravadhi-galad-aśruṇo 'vatārair*
*urasi susaṁbhṛta-hāra-vibhramāḍhyaḥ |*
*kṛśimabhir avaśiṣṭa-śiṣṭa-nāmā*
*cira-virahād viṣasāda gauracandraḥ ||6||*

*Word for word:* *niravadhi* — unceasingly; *galat* — flowing; *aśruṇaḥ* — of tears; *avatāraiḥ* — by the descents; *urasi* — on the chest; *su-saṁbhṛta* — well formed; *hāra* — of a necklace; *vibhrama* — with the charm; *āḍhyaḥ* — rich; *kṛśimabhiḥ* — through emaciation; *avaśiṣṭa* — remaining; *śiṣṭa* — only; *nāmā* — [whose] name [was]; *cira* — long; *virahāt* — from separation; *viṣasāda* — languished; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra.

**6.** Rich with the charm of a necklace well formed on His chest by the streams of tears flowing unceasingly, so wasted that only His name was left, Gaurachandra languished from long separation.

### Verse 7

विकिरति बहुदीर्घमुष्णमुच्चैः
श्वसितसमीरणमम्बु लोचनाभ्याम् ।
सदरुणकमलद्वयारुणाभ्यां
कृशतनुरन्वहमेवमेव भूतः ॥७॥

*vikirati bahu-dīrgham uṣṇam uccaiḥ*
*śvasita-samīraṇam ambu locanābhyām |*
*sad-aruṇa-kamala-dvayāruṇābhyāṁ*
*kṛśa-tanur anvaham evam eva bhūtaḥ ||7||*

*Word for word:* *vikirati* — sends forth; *bahu-dīrgham* — very long; *uṣṇam* — hot; *uccaiḥ* — heavily; *śvasita* — of sighs; *samīraṇam* — the wind; *ambu* — water; *locanābhyām* — from the eyes; *sat-aruṇa* — beautiful red; *kamala* — of lotuses; *dvaya* — like a pair; *aruṇābhyām* — from red; *kṛśa* — emaciated; *tanuḥ* — [whose] body [is]; *anvaham* — day after day; *evam eva* — just so; *bhūtaḥ* — having become.

**7.** Heavily He sends forth the very long, hot wind of sighs, and water from His eyes, red as a pair of beautiful red lotuses. Thus, day after day, His body grew thin.

### Verse 8

असितगिरिपतेरदर्शनेन
द्विगुणितदुःखदवानलः कृपाब्धिः ।
कियदिव स जगाम तत्र गोपी-
पतिविजयं परिलोच्य चित्तधैर्यम् ॥८॥

*asita-giri-pater adarśanena*
*dvi-guṇita-duḥkha-davānalaḥ kṛpābdhiḥ |*
*kiyad iva sa jagāma tatra gopī-*
*pati-vijayaṁ parilocya citta-dhairyam ||8||*

*Word for word:* *asita-giri* — of the Dark Mountain; *pateḥ* — of the Lord; *adarśanena* — by not seeing; *dvi-guṇita* — doubled; *duḥkha* — of sorrow; *dava-analaḥ* — [whose] forest fire [was]; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *abdhiḥ* — the ocean; *kiyat iva* — somewhat; *saḥ* — He; *jagāma* — attained; *tatra* — there; *gopī-pati* — of the Lord of the gopis; *vijayam* — the procession; *parilocya* — beholding; *citta* — of heart; *dhairyam* — steadiness.

**8.** The ocean of mercy, whose forest fire of sorrow was doubled by not seeing the Lord of the Dark Mountain, attained some steadiness of heart on beholding there the procession of the Lord of the gopis.

*Note.* Evidently during the anavasara the Lord watched the festival of Jagannatha's representative — Krishna with the flute on the swing (verses 9–10). In the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 11.62–63) the Lord goes to Alalanatha during the anavasara; such a festival is not mentioned in our sources. *Vijaya* can also mean "triumph".

### Verse 9

सुललितमुरलीकरः स दोला-
मति मधुरामधिरुह्य राजमानः ।
निरवधि वरवारनागरीणां
नटनकलाकुतुकी त्रिसन्ध्यमेव ॥९॥

*sulalita-muralī-karaḥ sa dolām*
*ati madhurām adhiruhya rājamānaḥ |*
*niravadhi vara-vāra-nāgarīṇāṁ*
*naṭana-kalā-kutukī tri-sandhyam eva ||9||*

*Word for word:* *su-lalita* — very graceful; *muralī* — a flute; *karaḥ* — [in whose] hand [is]; *saḥ* — He; *dolām* — a swing; *ati* — very; *madhurām* — charming; *adhiruhya* — having mounted; *rājamānaḥ* — shining; *niravadhi* — unceasingly; *vara* — of the finest; *vāra-nāgarīṇām* — of the temple dancers; *naṭana* — of dance; *kalā* — in the art; *kutukī* — delighting; *tri-sandhyam* — at the three junctures of the day; *eva* — indeed.

**9.** With a very graceful flute in His hand, mounted on a most charming swing, He shines, and at the three junctures of the day He delights unceasingly in the art of dance of the finest temple dancers…

*Note.* Verses 9–10 form a pair (*yugmaka*). The dancers are the devadasis of Jagannatha's temple.

### Verse 10

विलसति पटहप्रकृष्टभेरी-
मधुरमृदङ्गविभङ्गरम्यगीतैः ।
निरवधि सुमनःसमूहवृष्ट्या
गुरुधवलीकृतवेश्ममध्यभूमौ ॥१०॥ (युग्मकम्)

*vilasati paṭaha-prakṛṣṭa-bherī-*
*madhura-mṛdaṅga-vibhaṅga-ramya-gītaiḥ |*
*niravadhi sumanaḥ-samūha-vṛṣṭyā*
*guru-dhavalī-kṛta-veśma-madhya-bhūmau ||10|| (yugmakam)*

*Word for word:* *vilasati* — sports; *paṭaha* — with drums; *prakṛṣṭa* — excellent; *bherī* — kettledrums; *madhura* — sweet; *mṛdaṅga* — of mridangas; *vibhaṅga* — with the rolls; *ramya* — charming; *gītaiḥ* — and with songs; *niravadhi* — unceasing; *sumanaḥ* — of flowers; *samūha* — of masses; *vṛṣṭyā* — by a shower; *guru* — thickly; *dhavalī-kṛta* — whitened; *veśma* — of the hall; *madhya* — in the middle; *bhūmau* — on the floor.

**10.** …and He sports to drums, excellent kettledrums, the rolls of sweet mridangas and charming songs, in the middle of a hall whose floor is thickly whitened by an unceasing shower of masses of flowers.

### Verse 11

इति विरहविषण्णचित्तवृत्ति-
र्निजजनवीक्षणकिञ्चिदात्तधैर्यः ।
निरवधि विरुदन् विमुक्तकण्ठं
कति दिवसानि निनाय गौरचन्द्रः ॥११॥

*iti viraha-viṣaṇṇa-citta-vṛttir*
*nija-jana-vīkṣaṇa-kiñcid-ātta-dhairyaḥ |*
*niravadhi virudan vimukta-kaṇṭhaṁ*
*kati divasāni nināya gauracandraḥ ||11||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *viraha* — by separation; *viṣaṇṇa* — dejected; *citta* — of mind; *vṛttiḥ* — [whose] state [was]; *nija* — of His own; *jana* — people; *vīkṣaṇa* — by the sight; *kiñcit* — a little; *ātta* — having gained; *dhairyaḥ* — steadiness; *niravadhi* — unceasingly; *virudan* — weeping; *vimukta* — opened; *kaṇṭham* — throat; *kati* — some; *divasāni* — days; *nināya* — passed; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra.

**11.** Thus, His mind dejected by separation, and gaining only a little steadiness from the sight of His own people, Gaurachandra passed some days weeping unceasingly and aloud, with open throat.

### Verse 12

अथ निजचरणाम्बुजैकभक्तैः
सह स तु गौरशशी समुद्यतोऽभूत् ।
रचयितुमभिमार्जनां समन्तात्
प्रथितवतो भवनस्य गुण्डिचेति ॥१२॥

*atha nija-caraṇāmbujaika-bhaktaiḥ*
*saha sa tu gaura-śaśī samudyato 'bhūt |*
*racayitum abhimārjanāṁ samantāt*
*prathitavato bhavanasya guṇḍiceti ||12||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *nija* — His own; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *ambuja* — to the lotuses; *eka* — exclusively; *bhaktaiḥ* — with devotees; *saha* — together; *saḥ tu* — He; *gaura* — golden; *śaśī* — moon; *samudyataḥ* — prepared; *abhūt* — became; *racayitum* — to perform; *abhimārjanām* — a cleansing; *samantāt* — complete; *prathitavataḥ* — of [that] known; *bhavanasya* — of the temple; *guṇḍicā* — Gundicha; *iti* — as.

**12.** Then the golden Moon, together with the devotees exclusively devoted to His own lotus feet, made ready to perform a complete cleansing of the temple known as the Gundicha.

*Note.* Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 12.79–151 — the famous scene of the cleansing of the Gundicha (the brooms — 12.80).

### Verse 13

अथ सकलजनैश्चकार पूर्वे-
ऽहनि शचितनुजो विधाय युक्तिम् ।
झटिति रुचिरमार्जनीसमूह-
मुदितमना भवनस्य मार्जनार्थम् ॥१३॥

*atha sakala-janaiś cakāra pūrve*
*'hani śaci-tanujo vidhāya yuktim |*
*jhaṭiti rucira-mārjanī-samūham*
*udita-manā bhavanasya mārjanārtham ||13||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — and; *sakala* — with all; *janaiḥ* — with the people; *cakāra* — prepared; *pūrve* — on the previous; *ahani* — on the day; *śaci* — of Shachi; *tanujaḥ* — the son; *vidhāya* — having made; *yuktim* — a plan; *jhaṭiti* — quickly; *rucira* — of beautiful; *mārjanī* — brooms; *samūham* — a multitude; *udita* — elated; *manāḥ* — [whose] heart [was]; *bhavanasya* — of the temple; *mārjana* — of the cleansing; *artham* — for the sake.

**13.** And on the previous day the son of Shachi, having made a plan with all the people, quickly prepared, with an elated heart, a multitude of beautiful brooms for the cleansing of the temple.

*Note.* The even pada as printed has 12 syllables instead of 13, and with the short *śaci-* it does not scan in any case. It becomes regular if the *a* of *ahani*, elided across the pada boundary (*pūrve 'hani*), is counted and *śacī-* is read with a long *ī*: *ahani śacī-tanujo vidhāya yuktim* (⏑⏑⏑⏑—⏑⏑—⏑—⏑——). The edition writes *-समूहमुदितमना* continuously; we divide *samūham udita-manā(ḥ)* (the visarga is dropped by sandhi before *bh-*); *mudita-manāḥ*, "joyful at heart", is also possible, with the same sense. The text is the same in the Gosvami edition (GGM).

### Verse 14

अथ रजनीविरामकालपूर्वं
रभसवशादुदियाय तल्पमध्यात् ।
विमलसलिलसञ्चयैर्विधातुं
स्नपनमथो भगवान् समुद्यतोऽभूत् ॥१४॥

*atha rajanī-virāma-kāla-pūrvaṁ*
*rabhasa-vaśād udiyāya talpa-madhyāt |*
*vimala-salila-sañcayair vidhātuṁ*
*snapanam atho bhagavān samudyato 'bhūt ||14||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *rajanī* — of the night; *virāma* — of the end; *kāla* — the time; *pūrvam* — before; *rabhasa* — of eagerness; *vaśāt* — under the sway; *udiyāya* — rose; *talpa* — the bed; *madhyāt* — from; *vimala* — of pure; *salila* — water; *sañcayaiḥ* — with abundance; *vidhātum* — to perform; *snapanam* — bathing; *atho* — and; *bhagavān* — the Lord; *samudyataḥ* — prepared; *abhūt* — became.

**14.** Then, before the time of the night's end, the Lord, under the sway of eagerness, rose from His bed and made ready to bathe with an abundance of pure water.

*Note.* In the first pada the fifth syllable (*-nī-*) is long, whereas the metre requires a short one; with the stem *rajani-* (an equally correct form) the pada would be regular.

### Verse 15

विमलसुरभिशीतलवारिवृन्दैः
स्नपनमथैष विधाय चेलमन्यत् ।
सदरुणमभजद्यथा सुमेरु-
र्निबिडमुपाश्लिषदुत्सुकेन सन्ध्याम् ॥१५॥

*vimala-surabhi-śītala-vāri-vṛndaiḥ*
*snapanam athaiṣa vidhāya celam anyat |*
*sad-aruṇam abhajad yathā sumerur*
*nibiḍam upāśliṣad utsukena sandhyām ||15||*

*Word for word:* *vimala* — pure; *surabhi* — fragrant; *śītala* — cool; *vāri* — of water; *vṛndaiḥ* — with masses; *snapanam* — bathing; *atha* — then; *eṣaḥ* — He; *vidhāya* — having performed; *celam* — a cloth; *anyat* — another; *sat-aruṇam* — bright crimson; *abhajat* — put on; *yathā* — as; *sumeruḥ* — Sumeru; *nibiḍam* — tightly; *upāśliṣat* — embraced; *utsukena* — eagerly; *sandhyām* — the evening glow.

**15.** Having bathed with abundant pure, fragrant, cool water, He then put on another cloth, of bright crimson — as if Sumeru had eagerly and tightly embraced the evening glow.

*Note.* In the edition *सुरभी-*; the metre requires *surabhi-*. Even so the first pada has 13 syllables instead of 12; with *śīta-* for *śītala-* it would be regular (?). The golden Lord in crimson cloth is compared to the golden mountain Sumeru embracing the red glow of evening.

### Verse 16

सुरुचिरकटिसूत्रकेण बद्ध्वा
वसनमतीव दृढं महाकृपाब्धिः ।
मलयरुहविशेषकं विधाय
श्रियमतिनिर्भरसुन्दरीमवाप ॥१६॥

*surucira-kaṭi-sūtrakeṇa baddhvā*
*vasanam atīva dṛḍhaṁ mahā-kṛpābdhiḥ |*
*malaya-ruha-viśeṣakaṁ vidhāya*
*śriyam ati-nirbhara-sundarīm avāpa ||16||*

*Word for word:* *su-rucira* — with a very beautiful; *kaṭi-sūtrakeṇa* — with a waist-cord; *baddhvā* — having tied; *vasanam* — the garment; *atīva* — very; *dṛḍham* — firmly; *mahā* — great; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *abdhiḥ* — the ocean; *malaya-ruha* — of Malaya sandalwood; *viśeṣakam* — a tilaka; *vidhāya* — having applied; *śriyam* — beauty; *ati-nirbhara* — overflowing; *sundarīm* — lovely; *avāpa* — attained.

**16.** Having tied His garment very firmly with a very beautiful waist-cord and applied a tilaka of Malaya sandalwood, the great ocean of mercy attained an overflowing, lovely beauty.

### Verse 17

अथ बहिरुपगत्य सर्वलोका-
नरुणकटाक्षतरङ्गितेन दृष्ट्वा ।
निजपुर उपनीय मार्जनीनां
शतमददात् क्रमतः पृथक् पृथक् सः ॥१७॥

*atha bahir upagatya sarva-lokān*
*aruṇa-kaṭākṣa-taraṅgitena dṛṣṭvā |*
*nija-pura upanīya mārjanīnāṁ*
*śatam adadāt kramataḥ pṛthak pṛthak saḥ ||17||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *bahiḥ* — outside; *upagatya* — having come; *sarva* — at all; *lokān* — the people; *aruṇa* — reddish; *kaṭākṣa* — of glances; *taraṅgitena* — with the waves; *dṛṣṭvā* — having looked; *nija* — Himself; *puraḥ* — before; *upanīya* — having had brought; *mārjanīnām* — of brooms; *śatam* — a hundred; *adadāt* — gave; *kramataḥ* — in turn; *pṛthak pṛthak* — to each separately; *saḥ* — He.

**17.** Then, coming outside and looking at all the people with waves of reddish glances, He had a hundred brooms brought before Him and gave them out in turn, to each one separately.

### Verse 18

प्रभुचरणपयोजभक्तवर्गः
स च सुखभूरुहमञ्जरीमिवैताम् ।
प्रभुकरकमलादवाप्य चार्वीं
सपदि रहोऽतिमार्जनीं ननन्द ॥१८॥

*prabhu-caraṇa-payoja-bhakta-vargaḥ*
*sa ca sukha-bhūruha-mañjarīm ivaitām |*
*prabhu-kara-kamalād avāpya cārvīṁ*
*sapadi raho 'ti mārjanīṁ nananda ||18||*

*Word for word:* *prabhu* — of the Lord; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *payoja* — of the lotuses; *bhakta* — of devotees; *vargaḥ* — the host; *saḥ* — that; *ca* — and; *sukha* — of happiness; *bhūruha* — of the tree; *mañjarīm* — a cluster of blossoms; *iva* — like; *etām* — this; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *kara* — of the hand; *kamalāt* — from the lotus; *avāpya* — having received; *cārvīm* — beautiful; *sapadi* — at once; *rahaḥ* — in secret; *ati* — exceedingly; *mārjanīm* — broom; *nananda* — rejoiced.

**18.** And that host of devotees of the Lord's lotus feet, receiving from the lotus hand of the Lord this beautiful broom, like a cluster of blossoms of the tree of happiness, at once rejoiced exceedingly in secret.

*Note.* *Raho 'ti* is understood as "in secret, exceedingly" (?). The text is the same in the Gosvami edition (GGM). As printed, the fourth pada is a syllable short (12 instead of 13); the reading *rahasy ati* ("in secret, exceedingly") would make it regular — a conjecture (?).

### Verse 19

अथ मदकरिराजराजिगामी
कनकमहीध्र इवातिजङ्गमोऽसौ ।
परमरभसलोलचित्तखेल-
स्त्वरितमधावत माधुरीधुरीणः ॥१९॥

*atha mada-kari-rāja-rāji-gāmī*
*kanaka-mahīdhra ivāti-jaṅgamo 'sau |*
*parama-rabhasa-lola-citta-khelas*
*tvaritam adhāvata mādhurī-dhurīṇaḥ ||19||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *mada* — maddened; *kari-rāja* — of kings of elephants; *rāji* — like a line; *gāmī* — moving; *kanaka* — golden; *mahīdhraḥ* — mountain; *iva* — like; *ati* — very; *jaṅgamaḥ* — moving; *asau* — He; *parama* — by supreme; *rabhasa* — impetuosity; *lola* — stirred; *citta* — of the heart; *khelaḥ* — [whose] play [was]; *tvaritam* — swiftly; *adhāvata* — ran; *mādhurī* — in sweetness; *dhurīṇaḥ* — the foremost.

**19.** Then He — moving like a line of maddened kings of elephants, like a golden mountain that had begun to move, the play of His heart stirred by supreme impetuosity, the foremost in sweetness — ran swiftly.

*Note.* Verses 19–20 form a single period.

### Verse 20

चिरसमयनिरुद्धशीघ्रमुक्तः
प्रमदकरीव निरङ्कुशोऽभिधावन् ।
पदकमलविहारभूरिभारै-
रवनितलं तरलीचकार शश्वत् ॥२०॥

*cira-samaya-niruddha-śīghra-muktaḥ*
*pramada-karīva niraṅkuśo 'bhidhāvan |*
*pada-kamala-vihāra-bhūri-bhārair*
*avani-talaṁ taralīcakāra śaśvat ||20||*

*Word for word:* *cira* — for a long; *samaya* — time; *niruddha* — held back; *śīghra* — suddenly; *muktaḥ* — released; *pramada* — maddened; *karī* — an elephant; *iva* — like; *niraṅkuśaḥ* — free of the goad; *abhidhāvan* — running; *pada* — of the feet; *kamala* — of the lotuses; *vihāra* — of the play; *bhūri* — with great; *bhāraiḥ* — weights; *avani* — of the earth; *talam* — the surface; *taralīcakāra* — made tremble; *śaśvat* — continually.

**20.** Running like a maddened elephant long held back and suddenly set free, unchecked by the goad, He made the surface of the earth tremble continually with the great weight of the play of His lotus feet.

*Note.* The *aṅkuśa* is the elephant-driver's goad.

### Verse 21

द्रुतगतिरथ गुण्डिचालयस्य
प्रभुवरगम्यसमीपमुत्कचित्तः ।
सुखजलधिमिवाविशत् पुरं त-
च्चिरसमयेन तु ते समीपमीयुः ॥२१॥

*druta-gatir atha guṇḍicālayasya*
*prabhu-vara-gamya-samīpam utka-cittaḥ |*
*sukha-jaladhim ivāviśat puraṁ tac*
*cira-samayena tu te samīpam īyuḥ ||21||*

*Word for word:* *druta* — swift; *gatiḥ* — [whose] going [was]; *atha* — then; *guṇḍicā* — of Gundicha; *ālayasya* — of the temple; *prabhu-vara* — by the supreme Lord; *gamya* (?) — to be gone to (?); *samīpam* — to the vicinity; *utka* — eager; *cittaḥ* — [whose] heart [was]; *sukha* — of happiness; *jaladhim* — into the ocean; *iva* — as if; *āviśat* — entered; *puram* — the enclosure; *tat* — that; *cira-samayena* — after a long time; *tu* — but; *te* — they; *samīpam* — near; *īyuḥ* — came.

**21.** Then, going swiftly, His heart eager, [He came] to the vicinity of the Gundicha temple, the goal of the supreme Lord's journey, and entered that enclosure as if [plunging] into an ocean of happiness. But they came near only long after.

*Note.* *-gamya-* in the second pada is obscure (?). We take *prabhu-vara-gamya-* as "to be gone to by the supreme Lord", that is, the Gundicha temple as the destination of Jagannatha's journey (cf. 14.3–5); it may also be understood of Gaura Himself: "the best of lords [reached] the vicinity…". The verse is metrically complete: all four padas scan as regular *puṣpitāgrā*. The text is the same in the Gosvami edition (GGM).

### Verse 22

प्रथममयमतीवहर्षपूर्णः
पुरमभिविश्य निजैर्जनैस्तदैव ।
इत इत उपगृह्य मार्जनीं तां
सपदि ममार्ज पृथक् पृथक् क्रमेण ॥२२॥

*prathamam ayam atīva-harṣa-pūrṇaḥ*
*puram abhiviśya nijair janais tadaiva |*
*ita ita upagṛhya mārjanīṁ tāṁ*
*sapadi mamārja pṛthak pṛthak krameṇa ||22||*

*Word for word:* *prathamam* — first; *ayam* — He; *atīva* — exceedingly; *harṣa* — with joy; *pūrṇaḥ* — filled; *puram* — the enclosure; *abhiviśya* — having entered; *nijaiḥ* — with His own; *janaiḥ* — with people; *tadā eva* — then and there; *itaḥ itaḥ* — here and there; *upagṛhya* — having taken up; *mārjanīm* — broom; *tām* — that; *sapadi* — at once; *mamārja* — swept; *pṛthak pṛthak* — each [place] separately; *krameṇa* — in order.

**22.** Filled with exceeding joy, He entered the enclosure first, and then and there, with His own people, took up that broom and at once swept here and there, each place separately, in due order.

### Verse 23

अथ युगपदयं प्रमार्जनोत्को
जननिचयः प्रभुकीर्तनातिमुग्धः ।
अनुगृहमनुभित्ति चान्वलिन्दं
त्वनुवलभि प्रममार्ज मार्जनीभिः ॥२३॥

*atha yugapad ayaṁ pramārjanotko*
*jana-nicayaḥ prabhu-kīrtanāti-mugdhaḥ |*
*anugṛham anubhitti cānvalindaṁ*
*tv anuvalabhi pramamārja mārjanībhiḥ ||23||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *yugapat* — all at once; *ayam* — this; *pramārjana* — for the cleansing; *utkaḥ* — eager; *jana* — of people; *nicayaḥ* — the crowd; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *kīrtana* — by the kirtana; *ati-mugdhaḥ* — utterly enchanted; *anugṛham* — every room; *anubhitti* — every wall; *ca* — and; *anvalindam* — every veranda; *tu* — and; *anuvalabhi* — every roof; *pramamārja* — swept; *mārjanībhiḥ* — with brooms.

**23.** Then this crowd of people, eager for the cleansing and utterly enchanted by the Lord's kirtana, all at once swept with brooms every room, every wall, every veranda and every roof.

### Verse 24

प्रभुवदननिरीक्षणेन मुग्धा
रहसि च केचन मार्जनीं गृहीत्वा ।
नयनजलझरेण धौतदेहा-
श्चिरमिव विस्मृतमार्जनक्रियाः स्युः ॥२४॥

*prabhu-vadana-nirīkṣaṇena mugdhā*
*rahasi ca kecana mārjanīṁ gṛhītvā |*
*nayana-jala-jhareṇa dhauta-dehāś*
*ciram iva vismṛta-mārjana-kriyāḥ syuḥ ||24||*

*Word for word:* *prabhu* — of the Lord; *vadana* — of the face; *nirīkṣaṇena* — by beholding; *mugdhāḥ* — enchanted; *rahasi* — apart; *ca* — and; *kecana* — some; *mārjanīm* — a broom; *gṛhītvā* — having taken; *nayana* — of the eyes; *jala* — of the water; *jhareṇa* — by a torrent; *dhauta* — washed; *dehāḥ* — [whose] bodies [were]; *ciram* — for a long time; *iva* — as if; *vismṛta* — having forgotten; *mārjana* — of sweeping; *kriyāḥ* — the work; *syuḥ* — would be.

**24.** And some, enchanted by beholding the face of the Lord, would stand apart, broom in hand, their bodies washed by a torrent of tears, and for a long while seemed to have forgotten the work of sweeping.

### Verse 25

सुपुलकमपि केचिदीशसूक्ति-
श्रवणपरेण हृदा विनिद्रिताङ्गाः ।
गृहमपि च तथैव मार्जयन्तः
कृतमपि कर्म न चाविदन् विमुग्धाः ॥२५॥

*supulakam api kecid īśa-sūkti-*
*śravaṇa-pareṇa hṛdā vinidritāṅgāḥ |*
*gṛham api ca tathaiva mārjayantaḥ*
*kṛtam api karma na cāvidan vimugdhāḥ ||25||*

*Word for word:* *su-pulakam* — with intense thrill; *api* — also; *kecit* — some; *īśa* — of the Lord; *sūkti* — of the fine words; *śravaṇa* — on the hearing; *pareṇa* — intent; *hṛdā* — with a heart; *vinidrita* — awakened (bristling); *aṅgāḥ* — [whose] limbs [were]; *gṛham* — the room; *api* — also; *ca* — and; *tathā eva* — in the same way; *mārjayantaḥ* — sweeping; *kṛtam* — done; *api* — even; *karma* — the work; *na* — not; *ca* — and; *avidan* — knew; *vimugdhāḥ* — lost in bewilderment.

**25.** And some, with hearts intent on hearing the Lord's fine words, their limbs bristling with intense thrill, also swept the room in the same way, but, lost in bewilderment, did not notice even the work already done.

### Verse 26

प्रभुरपि परमप्रहर्षमुग्ध-
स्त्वमित इतस्ततस्ततस्त्वम् ।
सुललितमिति मार्जयेति लोका-
नदिशदलं सुखितान्मुहुः प्रकुर्वन् ॥२६॥

*prabhur api parama-praharṣa-mugdhas*
*tvam ita itas tatas tatas tvam |*
*sulalitam iti mārjayeti lokān*
*adiśad alaṁ sukhitān muhuḥ prakurvan ||26||*

*Word for word:* *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *api* — and; *parama* — by supreme; *praharṣa* — joy; *mugdhaḥ* — enraptured; *tvam* — you; *itaḥ* — here; *itaḥ* — here; *tataḥ tataḥ* — there, there; *tvam* — you; *su-lalitam* — nicely; *iti* — thus; *mārjaya* — sweep; *iti* — thus; *lokān* — to the people; *adiśat* — gave directions; *alam* — abundantly; *sukhitān* — happy; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *prakurvan* — making.

**26.** And the Lord, enraptured by supreme joy, gave abundant directions to the people, making them happy again and again: "You — here, here! There, there — you! Sweep nicely!"

*Note.* The second pada has 10 syllables instead of 13 — the text is corrupt (?). The text is the same in the Gosvami edition (GGM).

### Verse 27

प्रभुवचनविलासतो यदेते
विदधति कर्म ततस्ततो निकामम् ।
द्विगुणितमलभन्त सौख्यभारं
न च परितृप्तिसमाप्तिराबभूव ॥२७॥

*prabhu-vacana-vilāsato yad ete*
*vidadhati karma tatas tato nikāmam |*
*dvi-guṇitam alabhanta saukhya-bhāraṁ*
*na ca paritṛpti-samāptir ābabhūva ||27||*

*Word for word:* *prabhu* — of the Lord; *vacana* — of the words; *vilāsataḥ* — through the play; *yat* — since; *ete* — they; *vidadhati* — perform; *karma* — the work; *tatas tataḥ* — here and there; *nikāmam* — to their heart's content; *dvi-guṇitam* — doubled; *alabhanta* — obtained; *saukhya* — of happiness; *bhāram* — a load; *na* — not; *ca* — and; *paritṛpti* — of satiety; *samāptiḥ* — completion; *ābabhūva* — came about.

**27.** Since, through the play of the Lord's words, they did the work here and there to their heart's content, they obtained a doubled load of happiness, and yet their satiety never came to completion.

*Note.* In the edition *विलासते* — a misprint for *vilāsato*.

### Verse 28

प्रभुरपि च विलम्बितेन यो यः
पुरत उपैति स तस्य तस्य पृष्ठे ।
प्रणयरसभरेण मार्जनीभि-
र्बहुतरगाढमतिक्रुधा जघान ॥२८॥

*prabhur api ca vilambitena yo yaḥ*
*purata upaiti sa tasya tasya pṛṣṭhe |*
*praṇaya-rasa-bhareṇa mārjanībhir*
*bahutara-gāḍham ati-krudhā jaghāna ||28||*

*Word for word:* *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *api ca* — and; *vilambitena* — with delay; *yaḥ yaḥ* — whoever; *purataḥ* — before [Him]; *upaiti* — comes; *saḥ* — He; *tasya tasya* — of each such [one]; *pṛṣṭhe* — on the back; *praṇaya* — of love; *rasa* — of the rasa; *bhareṇa* — out of the fullness; *mārjanībhiḥ* — with brooms; *bahutara* — very; *gāḍham* — hard; *ati-krudhā* — with great anger; *jaghāna* — struck.

**28.** And whoever came before Him late, the Lord, out of the fullness of the rasa of love, struck him very hard on the back with brooms, in great anger.

### Verse 29

स तु जननिचयश्च मार्जनीनां
दृढतरघातरुजापि सौख्यमायात् ।
