परिणतिरियमेव हार्दराशे-
र्यदलघु दुःखमपि प्रियं तनोति ॥२९॥

*sa tu jana-nicayaś ca mārjanīnāṁ*
*dṛḍhatara-ghāta-rujāpi saukhyam āyāt |*
*pariṇatir iyam eva hārda-rāśer*
*yad alaghu duḥkham api priyaṁ tanoti ||29||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ tu* — that; *jana* — of people; *nicayaḥ* — the crowd; *ca* — and; *mārjanīnām* — of the brooms; *dṛḍhatara* — very hard; *ghāta* — of the blows; *rujā* — from the pain; *api* — even; *saukhyam* — happiness; *āyāt* — attained; *pariṇatiḥ* — the fruit; *iyam* — this; *eva* — indeed; *hārda* — of heartfelt love; *rāśeḥ* — of an abundance; *yat* — that; *alaghu* — no small; *duḥkham* — pain; *api* — even; *priyam* — dear; *tanoti* — makes.

**29.** But that crowd of people attained happiness even from the pain of the very hard blows of the brooms. Such indeed is the fruit of an abundance of heartfelt love: it makes even no small pain dear.

### Verse 30

क्षणमपि भगवान् स्वयं विधत्ते
सुललितमार्जनमूर्जितप्रहर्षः ।
क्षणमपि च विलोकतेऽन्यकर्म
क्षणमपि च कारयति प्रियैर्निदेशैः ॥३०॥

*kṣaṇam api bhagavān svayaṁ vidhatte*
*sulalita-mārjanam ūrjita-praharṣaḥ |*
*kṣaṇam api ca vilokate 'nya-karma*
*kṣaṇam api ca kārayati priyair nideśaiḥ ||30||*

*Word for word:* *kṣaṇam api* — now; *bhagavān* — the Lord; *svayam* — Himself; *vidhatte* — performs; *su-lalita* — graceful; *mārjanam* — sweeping; *ūrjita* — mighty; *praharṣaḥ* — [whose] joy [is]; *kṣaṇam api* — now; *ca* — and; *vilokate* — watches; *anya* — of others; *karma* — the work; *kṣaṇam api* — now; *ca* — and; *kārayati* — has [them] work; *priyaiḥ* — with affectionate; *nideśaiḥ* — with instructions.

**30.** In mighty joy the Lord now Himself sweeps gracefully, now watches the work of others, now has them work with affectionate instructions.

*Note.* As printed, the fourth pada has 14 syllables instead of 13; without the *ca* (perhaps repeated from the third pada) it would be regular (?).

### Verse 31

सकलजनसमीपमेव गच्छ-
न्नतिशयहर्षभरं चकार तेषाम् ।
स्मितवचननिरीक्षणाभिमर्शैः
शमितसमस्तशुगोघदत्तहर्षः ॥३१॥

*sakala-jana-samīpam eva gacchann*
*atiśaya-harṣa-bharaṁ cakāra teṣām |*
*smita-vacana-nirīkṣaṇābhimarśaiḥ*
*śamita-samasta-śug-ogha-datta-harṣaḥ ||31||*

*Word for word:* *sakala* — to all; *jana* — the people; *samīpam* — near; *eva* — indeed; *gacchan* — going; *atiśaya* — extreme; *harṣa* — of joy; *bharam* — a load; *cakāra* — produced; *teṣām* — in them; *smita* — with smiles; *vacana* — words; *nirīkṣaṇa* — glances; *abhimarśaiḥ* — and touches; *śamita* — having calmed; *samasta* — of all; *śuk* — griefs; *ogha* — the floods; *datta* — having given; *harṣaḥ* — joy.

**31.** Going up close to each and every one, He produced in them a load of extreme joy. With smiles, words, glances and touches He calmed the floods of all their griefs and gave them joy.

*Note.* *Abhimarśa* here means "touch".

### Verse 32

स्वयमपि कतिभिर्जनैः स सिंहा-
सनमभितोऽभित एकदत्तचित्तः ।
परमसुखभरेण मार्जयित्वा
सपदि च सेक्तुमथोद्यतो बभूव ॥३२॥

*svayam api katibhir janaiḥ sa siṁhā-*
*sanam abhito 'bhita eka-datta-cittaḥ |*
*parama-sukha-bhareṇa mārjayitvā*
*sapadi ca sektum athodyato babhūva ||32||*

*Word for word:* *svayam* — Himself; *api* — also; *katibhiḥ* — with a few; *janaiḥ* — people; *saḥ* — He; *siṁhāsanam* — the throne; *abhitaḥ abhitaḥ* — all around; *eka* — wholly; *datta* — given; *cittaḥ* — [whose] heart [was]; *parama* — of supreme; *sukha* — of happiness; *bhareṇa* — in the fullness; *mārjayitvā* — having cleaned; *sapadi* — at once; *ca* — and; *sektum* — to sprinkle; *atha* — then; *udyataḥ* — prepared; *babhūva* — became.

**32.** And He Himself, with a few people, His heart wholly given [to the task], cleaned the throne all around in the fullness of supreme happiness, and then at once made ready to sprinkle [it with water].

*Note.* The throne (*siṁhāsana*) is the platform for the Deities in the Gundicha temple.

### Verse 33

असकृदसकृदापतद्भिरेभि-
र्निरवधिवर्धितमार्जनीरजोभिः ।
अभिवृतकनकाचलेन्द्रदेहः
क इव बभूव शचीसुतस्तदानीम् ॥३३॥

*asakṛd asakṛd āpatadbhir ebhir*
*niravadhi-vardhita-mārjanī-rajobhiḥ |*
*abhivṛta-kanakācalendra-dehaḥ*
*ka iva babhūva śacī-sutas tadānīm ||33||*

*Word for word:* *asakṛt asakṛt* — again and again; *āpatadbhiḥ* — settling; *ebhiḥ* — by this; *niravadhi* — unceasingly; *vardhita* — raised; *mārjanī* — by the brooms; *rajobhiḥ* — by the dust; *abhivṛta* — covered; *kanaka* — golden; *acala-indra* — [like] the king of mountains; *dehaḥ* — [whose] body [was]; *kaḥ iva* — like whom; *babhūva* — became; *śacī-sutaḥ* — the son of Shachi; *tadānīm* — then.

**33.** His body, like a golden king of mountains, covered by this dust that the brooms raised unceasingly and that settled again and again — whom did the son of Shachi then resemble?

*Note.* *Ka iva babhūva*, literally "like whom did He become?": He seemed someone else altogether, beyond any comparison.

### Verse 34

अपि निरवधि कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्णे-
त्यनुपमधीरगभीरचारु जल्पन् ।
स्मितमधुरसुमेदुरास्यचन्द्रः
पुरपरिमार्जनमाततान नाथः ॥३४॥

*api niravadhi kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇety*
*anupama-dhīra-gabhīra-cāru jalpan |*
*smita-madhura-sumedurāsya-candraḥ*
*pura-parimārjanam ātatāna nāthaḥ ||34||*

*Word for word:* *api* — and; *niravadhi* — unceasingly; *kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa* — "Krishna, Krishna, Krishna"; *iti* — thus; *anupama* — incomparably; *dhīra* — steadily; *gabhīra* — deeply; *cāru* — beautifully; *jalpan* — repeating; *smita* — with a smile; *madhura* — sweet; *su-medura* — full; *āsya* — of the face; *candraḥ* — [whose] moon [was]; *pura* — of the enclosure; *parimārjanam* — the cleansing; *ātatāna* — carried on; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord.

**34.** And, unceasingly repeating "Krishna, Krishna, Krishna" in an incomparably steady, deep and beautiful [voice], the moon of His face full of sweet smiles, the Lord carried on the cleansing of the enclosure.

### Verse 35

अथ सकलजनैर्घटीघटाभि-
र्घटयितुमस्य पुरस्य धौतमुच्चैः ।
अतिशयदृढरज्जुसज्जिताभि-
र्जलहरणार्थमभावि तत्र कूपात् ॥३५॥

*atha sakala-janair ghaṭī-ghaṭābhir*
*ghaṭayitum asya purasya dhautam uccaiḥ |*
*atiśaya-dṛḍha-rajju-sajjitābhir*
*jala-haraṇārtham abhāvi tatra kūpāt ||35||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *sakala* — by all; *janaiḥ* — the people; *ghaṭī* — of pitchers; *ghaṭābhiḥ* — with multitudes; *ghaṭayitum* — to accomplish; *asya* — of this; *purasya* — of the enclosure; *dhautam* — the washing; *uccaiḥ* — thoroughly; *atiśaya* — very; *dṛḍha* — strong; *rajju* — with ropes; *sajjitābhiḥ* — fitted; *jala* — of water; *haraṇa* — of drawing; *artham* — for the sake; *abhāvi* — it was set about; *tatra* — there; *kūpāt* — from the well.

**35.** Then, to accomplish a thorough washing of this enclosure, all the people set about drawing water there from the well with multitudes of pitchers fitted with very strong ropes.

*Note.* A play of sounds: *ghaṭī-ghaṭābhir ghaṭayitum*.

### Verse 36

क्वचिदथ गृहीतरज्जुकुम्भाः
कटितटपरिनद्धतरोत्तरीयवस्त्राः ।
कतिचिदपि तदन्तिके सुसज्जाः
कति च तथैव तदन्तिकेऽथ तस्थुः ॥३६॥

*kvacid atha gṛhīta-rajju-kumbhāḥ*
*kaṭi-taṭa-parinaddhatarottarīya-vastrāḥ |*
*katicid api tad-antike susajjāḥ*
*kati ca tathaiva tad-antike 'tha tasthuḥ ||36||*

*Word for word:* *kvacit* — in one place; *atha* — then; *gṛhīta* — having taken; *rajju* — ropes; *kumbhāḥ* — [and] pots; *kaṭi* — of the hips; *taṭa* — on the slope; *parinaddhatara* — tied very firmly; *uttarīya* — upper; *vastrāḥ* — [whose] garments [were]; *katicit* — some; *api* — also; *tat* — to them; *antike* — near; *su-sajjāḥ* — fully ready; *kati* — some; *ca* — and; *tathā eva* — likewise; *tat* — to those; *antike* — near; *atha* — then; *tasthuḥ* — stood.

**36.** In one place people, their upper garments tied very firmly about their hips, took up ropes and pots; some stood fully ready near them, and others likewise near those.

*Note.* The first pada has 11 syllables instead of 12 (?); the same in verse 41. The second pada, for its part, has 15 syllables instead of 13. The text is the same in the Gosvami edition (GGM).

### Verse 37

अथ जननिचयः स कोऽपि रज्ज्वा
घटघटया हरति स्म वारिपूरम् ।
अथ कथमपि कस्यचिच्च कोऽपि
व्यदददथ क्रमतश्च कोऽपि निन्ये ॥३७॥

*atha jana-nicayaḥ sa ko 'pi rajjvā*
*ghaṭa-ghaṭayā harati sma vāri-pūram |*
*atha katham api kasyacic ca ko 'pi*
*vyadadad atha kramataś ca ko 'pi ninye ||37||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *jana* — of people; *nicayaḥ* — the crowd; *saḥ* — that; *kaḥ api* — someone; *rajjvā* — with a rope; *ghaṭa* — of pitchers; *ghaṭayā* — with a multitude; *harati sma* — drew; *vāri* — of water; *pūram* — a flood; *atha* — and; *katham api* — somehow; *kasyacit* — to someone; *ca* — and; *kaḥ api* — someone; *vyadadat* — handed; *atha* — and; *kramataḥ* — in succession; *ca* — and; *kaḥ api* — someone; *ninye* — carried on.

**37.** Then, in that crowd of people, someone drew up a flood of water with a rope and a multitude of pitchers; someone somehow handed it to someone else, and someone carried it on in succession.

*Note.* In the edition the third pada reads *कथमभि … कस्यचिन्न*; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *kasyacic ca*, and the superfluous *na* disappears; *katham api* is our correction of *कथमभि*. The threefold *ko 'pi*, "someone", describes the chain of people passing the water along.

### Verse 38

कतिचिदथ समुन्नयन्ति पूर्णा-
न्कतिचिदधश्च घटान्नयन्त्यपूर्णान् ।
परिणतिरुभयोरियं हि रम्या
न खलु विपर्ययमेति हि स्वभावः ॥३८॥

*katicid atha samunnayanti pūrṇān*
*katicid adhaś ca ghaṭān nayanty apūrṇān |*
*pariṇatir ubhayor iyaṁ hi ramyā*
*na khalu viparyayam eti hi svabhāvaḥ ||38||*

*Word for word:* *katicit* — some; *atha* — and; *samunnayanti* — raise up; *pūrṇān* — full; *katicit* — some; *adhaḥ* — down; *ca* — and; *ghaṭān* — pitchers; *nayanti* — carry; *apūrṇān* — empty; *pariṇatiḥ* — the outcome; *ubhayoḥ* — of both; *iyam* — this; *hi* — indeed; *ramyā* — delightful; *na* — not; *khalu* — surely; *viparyayam* — reversal; *eti* — goes to; *hi* — for; *svabhāvaḥ* — nature.

**38.** Some raised up the full pitchers, and some carried the empty ones down. Delightful indeed is this outcome for both: for nature surely does not turn into its opposite.

*Note.* A play on words: what is full rises, what is empty goes down.

### Verse 39

सुखभरपरमोल्लसद्भिरेभि-
र्मुहुरितरेतररिक्तिपूर्तिभाजाम् ।
घटनविघटनैर्घटीघटानां
घटमयकन्दुककेलिरन्वघाटि ॥३९॥

*sukha-bhara-paramollasadbhir ebhir*
*muhur itaretara-rikti-pūrti-bhājām |*
*ghaṭana-vighaṭanair ghaṭī-ghaṭānāṁ*
*ghaṭamaya-kanduka-kelir anvaghāṭi ||39||*

*Word for word:* *sukha* — of happiness; *bhara* — from the fullness; *parama* — supremely; *ullasadbhiḥ* — rejoicing; *ebhiḥ* — by them; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *itara-itara* — by turns; *rikti* — emptiness; *pūrti* — and fullness; *bhājām* — of [those] having; *ghaṭana* — by passing on; *vighaṭanaiḥ* — and handing back; *ghaṭī* — of pitchers; *ghaṭānām* — of multitudes; *ghaṭa-maya* — made of pitchers; *kanduka* — of ball; *keliḥ* — a game; *anvaghāṭi* — was set going.

**39.** By them, supremely rejoicing from the fullness of happiness, through the passing to and fro of multitudes of pitchers, again and again now empty, now full by turns, a game of ball played with pitchers was set going.

*Note.* Again a play of sounds on *ghaṭ-*: *ghaṭana-vighaṭanair ghaṭī-ghaṭānāṁ ghaṭamaya… anvaghāṭi*.

### Verse 40

इत इत इत आनयानयेति
ध्वनिरसकौ रसकौतुकात् समुत्थः ।
सपुलकमुदितोच्चहुंकृताढ्यो
घटभरणस्वनचुम्बितो जगल्भे ॥४०॥

*ita ita ita ānayānayeti*
*dhvanir asakau rasa-kautukāt samutthaḥ |*
*sapulaka-muditocca-huṅkṛtāḍhyo*
*ghaṭa-bharaṇa-svana-cumbito jagalbhe ||40||*

*Word for word:* *itaḥ itaḥ itaḥ* — here, here, here; *ānaya ānaya* — bring, bring; *iti* — thus; *dhvaniḥ* — the cry; *asakau* — this; *rasa* — from relish; *kautukāt* — [and] from merriment; *samutthaḥ* — arisen; *sa-pulaka* — thrilled; *mudita* — joyful; *ucca* — loud; *huṅkṛta* — with shouts of "hum"; *āḍhyaḥ* — rich; *ghaṭa* — of the pitchers; *bharaṇa* — of the filling; *svana* — by the gurgling; *cumbitaḥ* — kissed; *jagalbhe* — boldly rang out.

**40.** "Here, here, here! Bring it, bring it!" — this cry, arisen from relish and merriment, rich with thrilled, joyful, loud shouts of "hum" and kissed by the gurgling of the filling pitchers, boldly rang out [all around].

### Verse 41

क्वचिदथ पयो घटानलिन्दे
मुहुरकिरन् क्वचिच्च भित्तिवृन्दे ।
कतिचन वलभौ कति च्छदिःषु
प्रभुवचनेन सुखैकमग्नचित्ताः ॥४१॥

*kvacid atha payo ghaṭān alinde*
*muhur akiran kvacic ca bhitti-vṛnde |*
*katicana valabhau kati cchadiḥṣu*
*prabhu-vacanena sukhaika-magna-cittāḥ ||41||*

*Word for word:* *kvacit* — in some places; *atha* — and; *payaḥ* — water; *ghaṭān* — [from] pots; *alinde* — on the veranda; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *akiran* — poured; *kvacit* — in some places; *ca* — and; *bhitti* — of walls; *vṛnde* — on the multitude; *katicana* — some; *valabhau* — on the roof; *kati* — some; *chadiḥṣu* — on the awnings; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *vacanena* — by the word; *sukha* — in happiness; *eka* — wholly; *magna* — immersed; *cittāḥ* — [with] hearts.

**41.** In some places they poured water from pots again and again on the veranda, in others on the many walls; some on the roof, some on the awnings. At the Lord's word their hearts were wholly immersed in happiness.

*Note.* The first pada has eleven syllables instead of twelve, as in v. 36 (?); the second pada, too, has twelve instead of thirteen (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text. *Payo ghaṭān* may perhaps be taken as one compound, *payo-ghaṭān*, "pots of water".

### Verse 42

त्वमित इत इतस्त्वमत्र च त्वं
त्वमित इति प्रतिलोकमुक्तिमाध्व्या ।
प्रभुरपि परिशोधयाञ्चकार
प्रतिभवनं सकलप्रदेशवृन्दम् ॥४२॥

*tvam ita ita itas tvam atra ca tvaṁ*
*tvam ita iti pratilokam ukti-mādhvyā |*
*prabhur api pariśodhayāñcakāra*
*pratibhavanaṁ sakala-pradeśa-vṛndam ||42||*

*Word for word:* *tvam* — you; *itaḥ itaḥ itaḥ* — this way, this way, this way; *tvam* — you; *atra* — here; *ca* — and; *tvam* — you; *tvam* — you; *itaḥ* — this way; *iti* — thus; *pratilokam* — to each person; *ukti* — of speech; *mādhvyā* — with sweetness; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *api* — too; *pariśodhayāñcakāra* — had cleaned; *pratibhavanam* — in every chamber; *sakala* — all; *pradeśa* — of corners; *vṛndam* — the multitude.

**42.** "You — this way, this way, this way! You — here! And you, you — this way!" — thus, with sweetness of speech to each person, the Lord too had all the corners in every chamber cleaned.

### Verse 43

कतिचिदथ जना घटान् सुपूर्णान्
प्रभुकरपद्मयुगे ददत्यभीक्ष्णम् ।
कतिचिदपि च तस्य पादभूमौ
परिसरतः सिषिचुः पयःप्रपूरम् ॥४३॥

*katicid atha janā ghaṭān supūrṇān*
*prabhu-kara-padma-yuge dadaty abhīkṣṇam |*
*katicid api ca tasya pāda-bhūmau*
*parisarataḥ siṣicuḥ payaḥ-prapūram ||43||*

*Word for word:* *katicit* — some; *atha* — then; *janāḥ* — people; *ghaṭān* — pots; *su-pūrṇān* — brimming; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *kara* — of the hands; *padma* — of the lotuses; *yuge* — into the pair; *dadati* — place; *abhīkṣṇam* — continually; *katicit* — some; *api ca* — and also; *tasya* — His; *pāda* — of the feet; *bhūmau* — on the ground; *parisarataḥ* — all around; *siṣicuḥ* — poured; *payaḥ* — of water; *prapūram* — floods.

**43.** Some people continually placed brimming pots into the pair of the Lord's lotus hands, while others poured floods of water on the ground all around His feet.

### Verse 44

प्रभुरपि च दधाति तत्र पूर्णं
घटमपरं विजहाति हृष्टचित्तः ।
अवसरमधि पूर्तिशून्यताभ्या-
मभवदुदाहरणं द्वयोर्द्वयं तत् ॥४४॥

*prabhur api ca dadhāti tatra pūrṇaṁ*
*ghaṭam aparaṁ vijahāti hṛṣṭa-cittaḥ |*
*avasaram adhi pūrti-śūnyatābhyām*
*abhavad udāharaṇaṁ dvayor dvayaṁ tat ||44||*

*Word for word:* *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *api ca* — and; *dadhāti* — takes; *tatra* — there; *pūrṇam* — a full; *ghaṭam* — pot; *aparam* — another; *vijahāti* — gives up; *hṛṣṭa* — joyful; *cittaḥ* — [with] heart; *avasaram adhi* — in turn; *pūrti* — by fullness; *śūnyatābhyām* — and by emptiness; *abhavat* — became; *udāharaṇam* — an illustration; *dvayoḥ* — for the two; *dvayam* — twofold; *tat* — that.

**44.** And the Lord, with a joyful heart, took a full pot there and gave up another, [empty one]. By fullness and emptiness in turn, that twofold [exchange] became an illustration for the two.

*Note.* That is, as the pots passed between them, now the devotees, now the Lord were in turn "full" and "empty".

### Verse 45

पुलकपटलपूरिताखिलाङ्गाः
सुखभरतः पृथुवेपथूत्थभङ्गाः ।
प्रभुकरकमले घटप्रदाना-
त्कतिचन निर्वृतिमेव तत्र नापुः ॥४५॥

*pulaka-paṭala-pūritākhilāṅgāḥ*
*sukha-bharataḥ pṛthu-vepathūttha-bhaṅgāḥ |*
*prabhu-kara-kamale ghaṭa-pradānāt*
*katicana nirvṛtim eva tatra nāpuḥ ||45||*

*Word for word:* *pulaka* — of hairs standing on end; *paṭala* — with masses; *pūrita* — filled; *akhila* — all; *aṅgāḥ* — [with] limbs; *sukha* — of happiness; *bharataḥ* — from the fullness; *pṛthu* — violent; *vepathu* — by trembling; *uttha* — caused; *bhaṅgāḥ* — [with] swayings; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *kara* — of the hand; *kamale* — into the lotus; *ghaṭa* — of pots; *pradānāt* — from the giving; *katicana* — some; *nirvṛtim* — satiety; *eva* — at all; *tatra* — there; *na āpuḥ* — did not attain.

**45.** Some — all their limbs covered with masses of hairs standing on end, their bodies swaying with the violent trembling caused by the fullness of happiness — could find no satiety at all in giving pots into the lotus hand of the Lord.

### Verse 46

कतिचन दयितस्य पादपद्म-
द्वयमभि निर्भरमुत्सुका जलानि ।
रहसि परिकिरन्ति केवलं स्म
क्व च गृहधौतविधिः स्थितस्तदेषाम् ॥४६॥

*katicana dayitasya pāda-padma-*
*dvayam abhi nirbharam utsukā jalāni |*
*rahasi parikiranti kevalaṁ sma*
*kva ca gṛha-dhauta-vidhiḥ sthitas tad eṣām ||46||*

*Word for word:* *katicana* — some; *dayitasya* — of the Beloved; *pāda* — of the feet; *padma* — of the lotuses; *dvayam abhi* — upon the pair; *nirbharam* — copiously; *utsukāḥ* — eager; *jalāni* — water; *rahasi* — in secret; *parikiranti sma* — poured; *kevalam* — only; *kva* — where; *ca* — then; *gṛha* — of the chambers; *dhauta* — of the washing; *vidhiḥ* — the business; *sthitaḥ* — remained; *tat* — then; *eṣām* — for them.

**46.** Some, eager [for Him], secretly poured water copiously on the pair of the Beloved's lotus feet alone. Where, then, did the business of washing the chambers remain for them?

*Note.* The rhetorical question means that they quite forgot about washing the chambers. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 47

अवकिरति मुहुः स्वलोकवृन्दे
पदसविधे शतधा घटैर्जलानि ।
प्रभुरयमथ जानुदघ्नतिम्यत्-
सदरुणचेलवरो रराज भूयः ॥४७॥

*avakirati muhuḥ sva-loka-vṛnde*
*pada-savidhe śatadhā ghaṭair jalāni |*
*prabhur ayam atha jānu-daghna-timyat-*
*sad-aruṇa-cela-varo rarāja bhūyaḥ ||47||*

*Word for word:* *avakirati* — [when] pouring; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *sva* — His own; *loka* — of people; *vṛnde* — the host; *pada* — the feet; *savidhe* — near; *śatadhā* — a hundred times over; *ghaṭaiḥ* — with pots; *jalāni* — water; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *ayam* — this; *atha* — then; *jānu-daghna* — up to the knees; *timyat* — wet; *sat-aruṇa* — bright red; *cela* — [with] cloth; *varaḥ* — splendid; *rarāja* — shone; *bhūyaḥ* — still more.

**47.** As the host of His own people poured water from pots near His feet again and again, a hundred times over, the Lord shone still more splendidly in His bright red cloth, wet up to the knees.

### Verse 48

श्रमजलकणिकाविकाशभास्व-
द्वदनविधुस्तिमितारुणांशुकान्तः ।
इत इत इत उक्षिताम्बुसार्द्रः
स्नपनकलोत्थितवत् प्रभू रराज ॥४८॥

*śrama-jala-kaṇikā-vikāśa-bhāsvad-*
*vadana-vidhus timitāruṇāṁśukāntaḥ |*
*ita ita ita ukṣitāmbu-sārdraḥ*
*snapana-kalotthitavat prabhū rarāja ||48||*

*Word for word:* *śrama* — of exertion; *jala* — of water (sweat); *kaṇikā* — of the droplets; *vikāśa* — with the glistening; *bhāsvat* — shining; *vadana* — of the face; *vidhuḥ* — [whose] moon; *timita* — wet; *aruṇa* — of the red; *aṁśuka* — garment; *antaḥ* — [whose] border; *itaḥ itaḥ itaḥ* — from every side; *ukṣita* — splashed; *ambu* — by water; *sa-ārdraḥ* — drenched; *snapana* — of bathing; *kalā* — from the sport; *utthita-vat* — like one risen; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *rarāja* — shone.

**48.** The moon of His face shining with the glistening of droplets of sweat, the border of His red garment wet, drenched by the water splashed from every side, the Lord shone as though He had just come out of a sport of bathing.

### Verse 49

स्वयमपि निजभक्तपाणिपद्मा-
द्घटमपि गृह्य जलेन पूर्णपूर्णम् ।
सरभसमवकीर्य चावकीर्य
प्रघणमपूरि घनं घनो यथा सः ॥४९॥

*svayam api nija-bhakta-pāṇi-padmād*
*ghaṭam api gṛhya jalena pūrṇa-pūrṇam |*
*sarabhasam avakīrya cāvakīrya*
*praghaṇam apūri ghanaṁ ghano yathā saḥ ||49||*

*Word for word:* *svayam* — Himself; *api* — too; *nija* — of His own; *bhakta* — devotee; *pāṇi* — of the hand; *padmāt* — from the lotus; *ghaṭam* — a pot; *api* — and; *gṛhya* — taking; *jalena* — with water; *pūrṇa-pūrṇam* — full to the brim; *sa-rabhasam* — impetuously; *avakīrya ca avakīrya* — pouring and pouring; *praghaṇam* — the veranda; *apūri* — flooded; *ghanam* — densely; *ghanaḥ* — a raincloud; *yathā* — like; *saḥ* — He.

**49.** And He Himself, taking from the lotus hand of His devotee a pot full to the brim with water, impetuously poured and poured, and flooded the veranda densely, like a raincloud.

*Note.* *Praghaṇa* is a covered veranda before the entrance.

### Verse 50

क्वचन जलकणाभिचुम्बिताङ्गः
क्वचन च कर्दमखेलया विमुग्धः ।
अभिनवसरसीविलोडनोत्थः
स तु जलकुञ्जरवत्तदा रराज ॥५०॥

*kvacana jala-kaṇābhicumbitāṅgaḥ*
*kvacana ca kardama-khelayā vimugdhaḥ |*
*abhinava-sarasī-viloḍanotthaḥ*
*sa tu jala-kuñjaravat tadā rarāja ||50||*

*Word for word:* *kvacana* — here; *jala* — of water; *kaṇa* — by drops; *abhicumbita* — kissed; *aṅgaḥ* — [whose] body; *kvacana* — there; *ca* — and; *kardama* — with mud; *khelayā* — by play; *vimugdhaḥ* — enraptured; *abhinava* — fresh; *sarasī* — a pond; *viloḍana* — after churning up; *utthaḥ* — emerged; *saḥ tu* — He; *jala* — in the water; *kuñjara-vat* — like an elephant; *tadā* — then; *rarāja* — shone.

**50.** Here His body kissed by drops of water, there enraptured by play with the mud, He shone then like an elephant in the water that has come out after churning up a fresh pond.

### Verse 51

सलिलपटलसेकतोऽभितिम्यत्-
सदरुणचेललसन्नितम्बशोभः ।
दिनकरभयमग्नसान्ध्यमेघा-
वृत इव मेरुरयं तदा रराज ॥५१॥

*salila-paṭala-sekato 'bhitimyat-*
*sad-aruṇa-cela-lasan-nitamba-śobhaḥ |*
*dinakara-bhaya-magna-sāndhya-meghā-*
*vṛta iva merur ayaṁ tadā rarāja ||51||*

*Word for word:* *salila* — of water; *paṭala* — by the masses; *sekataḥ* — from the drenching; *abhitimyat* — wet through; *sat-aruṇa* — bright red; *cela* — through the cloth; *lasat* — shining; *nitamba* — of the hips; *śobhaḥ* — [whose] beauty; *dinakara* — of the sun; *bhaya* — out of fear; *magna* — sheltering; *sāndhya* — by evening; *megha* — clouds; *āvṛtaḥ* — enveloped; *iva* — like; *meruḥ* — Meru; *ayam* — He; *tadā* — then; *rarāja* — shone.

**51.** The beauty of His hips shining through the bright red cloth, wet through from the drenching with masses of water, He shone then like Mount Meru enveloped in evening clouds that have taken shelter [on it] out of fear of the sun.

*Note.* The edition has *सेकतोऽभिताम्यत्*. By sense we read *-'bhitimyat*, "wet through"; cf. v. 47 (?). Metrically the two readings are equivalent. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text as the edition.

### Verse 52

कति कति न घटास्तदा बभञ्जुः
कति कति नो पुनराययुश्च तत्र ।
कति कति न जलानि चाहृतानी-
त इत इतः कति वाभवन्न नद्यः ॥५२॥

*kati kati na ghaṭās tadā babhañjuḥ*
*kati kati no punar āyayuś ca tatra |*
*kati kati na jalāni cāhṛtānī-*
*ta ita itaḥ kati vābhavan na nadyaḥ ||52||*

*Word for word:* *kati kati* — how many; *na* — not [i.e. how very many]; *ghaṭāḥ* — pots; *tadā* — then; *babhañjuḥ* — broke; *kati kati* — how many; *no* — not; *punaḥ* — again; *āyayuḥ* — came back; *ca* — and; *tatra* — there; *kati kati* — how much; *na* — not [i.e. how very much]; *jalāni* — water; *ca* — and; *āhṛtāni* — was brought; *ita itaḥ* — here and there; *kati* — how many; *vā* — and; *abhavan* — arose; *na* — not [i.e. how very many]; *nadyaḥ* — rivers.

**52.** How many pots broke then, how many never came back there again, how much water was brought — and how many rivers sprang up here and there!

*Note.* *चाहृतानीत* = *cāhṛtāni + ita* (sandhi across the pada boundary).

### Verse 53

निरवधि कलसैश्च लोचनैश्च
प्रसृमरहर्षभरैः किरन्त आपः ।
बभुरतिरहसान्तरान्तरा च
स्फुटजयनादजुषो घना इवैते ॥५३॥

*niravadhi kalasaiś ca locanaiś ca*
*prasṛmara-harṣa-bharaiḥ kiranta āpaḥ |*
*babhur atirahasāntarāntarā ca*
*sphuṭa-jaya-nāda-juṣo ghanā ivaite ||53||*

*Word for word:* *niravadhi* — ceaselessly; *kalasaiḥ* — with pitchers; *ca* — and; *locanaiḥ* — with eyes; *ca* — and; *prasṛmara* — overflowing; *harṣa* — of joy; *bharaiḥ* — from the fullness; *kirantaḥ* — pouring; *āpaḥ* — water; *babhuḥ* — shone; *ati-rahasā* — impetuously; *antarā antarā* — now and again; *ca* — and; *sphuṭa* — loud; *jaya* — of "jaya"; *nāda* — cries; *juṣaḥ* — giving forth; *ghanāḥ* — clouds; *iva* — like; *ete* — they.

**53.** Ceaselessly pouring water from pitchers and from their eyes out of the fullness of overflowing joy, and now and again impetuously raising loud cries of "Jaya!", they shone like [thundering] clouds.

### Verse 54

निरवधिसलिलाभिषेकतिम्यत्-
करनिकरा वरवारणा इवैते ।
उपपुरि विबभुः प्रभोः समीपे
न सुखचयस्तु ममौ जगत्यमीषाम् ॥५४॥

*niravadhi-salilābhiṣeka-timyat-*
*kara-nikarā vara-vāraṇā ivaite |*
*upapuri vibabhuḥ prabhoḥ samīpe*
*na sukha-cayas tu mamau jagaty amīṣām ||54||*

*Word for word:* *niravadhi* — ceaseless; *salila* — with water; *abhiṣeka* — by the drenching; *timyat* — wet; *kara* — of hands (trunks); *nikarāḥ* — [with] multitudes; *vara* — noble; *vāraṇāḥ* — elephants; *iva* — like; *ete* — they; *upapuri* — by the enclosure; *vibabhuḥ* — shone; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *samīpe* — near; *na* — not; *sukha* — of happiness; *cayaḥ* — the mass; *tu* — but; *mamau* — was contained; *jagati* — in the world; *amīṣām* — of theirs.

**54.** Their many hands wet from the ceaseless drenching with water, they shone by the enclosure near the Lord like noble elephants with their trunks; and the mass of their happiness could not be contained in the world.

*Note.* A play on words: *kara* means both "hand" and "trunk".

### Verse 55

अथ सकलपुरं विशोध्य सिंहा-
सनमपि निर्भरधौतमाविधाय ।
बहिरगमदयं स चत्वरान्तः
प्रभुरसकौ रसकौतुकी सदैव ॥५५॥

*atha sakala-puraṁ viśodhya siṁhā-*
*sanam api nirbhara-dhautam āvidhāya |*
*bahir agamad ayaṁ sa catvarāntaḥ*
*prabhur asakau rasa-kautukī sadaiva ||55||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *sakala* — the whole; *puram* — enclosure; *viśodhya* — having cleaned; *siṁhāsanam* — the throne; *api* — and; *nirbhara* — thoroughly; *dhautam* — washed; *āvidhāya* — having made; *bahiḥ* — outside; *agamat* — went; *ayam* — this; *saḥ* — He; *catvara* — of the courtyard; *antaḥ* — into; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *asakau* — He; *rasa* — in rasa; *kautukī* — delighting; *sadā eva* — ever.

**55.** Then, having cleaned the whole enclosure and washed the throne thoroughly, the Lord — He who ever delights in rasa — went outside, into the courtyard.

### Verse 56

अथ सुविहितपङ्क्तिषूपविश्य
प्रभुरधिचत्वरमेकतः क्रमेण ।
अतिशयमृदुलाङ्गुलीभिरङ्गैः
स इत इतस्तृणशर्करा निरास ॥५६॥

*atha suvihita-paṅktiṣūpaviśya*
*prabhur adhi-catvaram ekataḥ krameṇa |*
*atiśaya-mṛdulāṅgulībhir aṅgaiḥ*
*sa ita itas tṛṇa-śarkarā nirāsa ||56||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *su-vihita* — well arranged; *paṅktiṣu* — in rows; *upaviśya* — sitting down; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *adhi-catvaram* — in the courtyard; *ekataḥ* — from one side; *krameṇa* — in order; *atiśaya* — very; *mṛdula* — with tender; *aṅgulībhiḥ* — fingers; *aṅgaiḥ* — [and] with hands; *saḥ* — He; *ita itaḥ* — here and there; *tṛṇa* — blades of grass; *śarkarāḥ* — [and] pebbles; *nirāsa* — removed.

**56.** Then the Lord sat down in the courtyard among [the devotees] seated in well-arranged rows and, starting from one side, in order, removed blades of grass and pebbles here and there with His very tender fingers and hands.

### Verse 57

अधिधरणि निपात्य भूरिलीलो
ललितबहिर्वसनं त्वरायुतः सः ।
विहितपणफलं बलाज्जिगीषु-
र्न कति तृणानि शर्कराश्च जह्रे ॥५७॥

*adhi-dharaṇi nipātya bhūri-līlo*
*lalita-bahir-vasanaṁ tvarāyutaḥ saḥ |*
*vihita-paṇa-phalaṁ balāj jigīṣur*
*na kati tṛṇāni śarkarāś ca jahre ||57||*

*Word for word:* *adhi-dharaṇi* — on the ground; *nipātya* — spreading; *bhūri* — rich; *līlaḥ* — [in] pastimes; *lalita* — graceful; *bahiḥ-vasanam* — outer garment; *tvarā-yutaḥ* — in haste; *saḥ* — He; *vihita* — fixed; *paṇa* — of the wager; *phalam* — the prize; *balāt* — at all costs; *jigīṣuḥ* — wishing to win; *na kati* — how many … not [i.e. how very many]; *tṛṇāni* — blades of grass; *śarkarāḥ* — pebbles; *ca* — and; *jahre* — gathered.

**57.** Rich in pastimes, He hastily spread His graceful outer garment on the ground and, wishing to win the prize of the fixed wager at all costs — how many blades of grass and pebbles did He not gather!

*Note.* The edition has *नैकति*; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *na kati* ("how many … not"), and so we read. The second pada is metrically correct; it is the fourth pada that is one syllable short (twelve instead of thirteen), with either reading (?). Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 12.89–91: the devotees gather the dust and rubbish into their cloths, and the Lord, looking at the heaps, judges who has worked best.

### Verse 58

क्रमत इत इतः समस्तलोका-
हृततृणलोष्टचयं विलोक्य नाथः ।
इयदियदियदेव यद्भवद्भि-
स्तदिह पराजितमित्यखेलयत् सः ॥५८॥

*kramata ita itaḥ samasta-lokā-*

*iyad iyad iyad eva yad bhavadbhis*
*tad iha parājitam ity akhelayat saḥ ||58||*

*Word for word:* *kramataḥ* — in turn; *ita itaḥ* — here and there; *samasta* — by all; *loka* — the people; *āhṛta* — gathered; *tṛṇa* — of grass; *loṣṭa* — [and] of clods; *cayam* — the heap; *vilokya* — inspecting; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *iyat iyat iyat* — so much, so much, so much; *eva* — only; *yat* — since; *bhavadbhiḥ* — by you; *tat* — therefore; *iha* — here; *parājitam* — [it is] lost; *iti* — thus; *akhelayat* — sported; *saḥ* — He.

**58.** Inspecting in turn the heaps of grass and clods gathered here and there by all the people, the Lord sported [with them]: "Since you have [gathered] only so much, so much, so much — you have lost here!"

### Verse 59

इति सकलगृहस्य चत्वरान्तः-

अतिरभसभरालसान्तरात्मा
स निजजनैर्निजकीर्तनं ततान ॥५९॥

*iti sakala-gṛhasya catvarāntaḥ-*
*prati-pura-gopura-rathyam asau viśodhya |*
*ati-rabhasa-bharālasāntar-ātmā*
*sa nija-janair nija-kīrtanaṁ tatāna ||59||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *sakala* — of the whole; *gṛhasya* — temple; *catvara* — the courtyard; *antaḥ* — inner; *prati* — every; *pura* — of the enclosure; *gopura* — gate; *rathyam* — [and] the road; *asau* — He; *viśodhya* — having cleaned; *ati* — of great; *rabhasa* — eagerness; *bhara* — from the fullness; *alasa* — wearied; *antaḥ-ātmā* — [whose] inner self; *saḥ* — He; *nija* — with His own; *janaiḥ* — people; *nija* — His own; *kīrtanam* — kirtana; *tatāna* — began.

**59.** Having thus cleaned the inner courtyard of the whole temple, every gate of the enclosure and the road, He — His inner self wearied by the fullness of His great eagerness — began His own kirtana with His own people.

*Note.* The second pada has fourteen syllables instead of thirteen (?).

### Verse 60

सहजपरमसुस्वरास्त एते

तदिह जनः परिवर्णयेदहो कः ॥६०॥

*sahaja-parama-susvarās ta ete*
*prabhu-purataḥ prabhu-nartane tathaite |*
*yad atha jagur udāra-cāru-dhīraṁ*
*tad iha janaḥ parivarṇayed aho kaḥ ||60||*

*Word for word:* *sahaja* — by nature; *parama* — supremely; *su-svarāḥ* — sweet-voiced; *te ete* — these very ones; *prabhu* — the Lord; *purataḥ* — before; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *nartane* — during the dancing; *tathā* — so; *ete* — they; *yat* — how; *atha* — then; *jaguḥ* — sang; *udāra* — nobly; *cāru* — beautifully; *dhīram* — majestically; *tat* — that; *iha* — here; *janaḥ* — person; *parivarṇayet* — could describe; *aho* — ah; *kaḥ* — what.

**60.** How these [singers], by nature supremely sweet-voiced, sang then before the Lord as He danced — nobly, beautifully, majestically — ah, what person here could describe it?

*Note.* The edition has *प्रभुनर्त्तने*.

अतिशयललितातिदीर्घदीर्घ-

*Word for word:* *atiśaya* — exceedingly; *lalita* — graceful; *ati-dīrgha-dīrgha* — long, very long; *svara* — with notes; *paripūrita* — filling; *kinnara* — of the kinnaras; *ogha* — of the hosts; *karṇāḥ* — the ears; *pulaka* — by hairs standing on end; *vikalitāḥ* — overcome; *sukha* — with happiness; *eka* — wholly; *pūrṇāḥ* — filled; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *naṭane* — during the dancing; *jaguḥ* — sang; *ete* — they; *eka* — [with] one; *cittāḥ* — [with] mind.

**61.** Filling the ears of the hosts of kinnaras with exceedingly graceful, long, very long notes, overcome by rapture, their hairs standing on end, wholly filled with happiness, they sang with one mind during the Lord's dance.

*Note.* The kinnaras are celestial musicians.

*Word for word:* *ati* — of great; *rabhasa* — eagerness; *bhareṇa* — by the fullness; *jānu* — of the knees; *hṛt* — [and] of the chest; *kṣepaṇa* — from the flinging up; *parijṛmbhita* — spreading; *dīrgha* — long; *roma-harṣaḥ* — [whose] thrill of the hairs; *niravadhi* — ceaselessly; *galat* — flowing; *aśru* — of tears; *vṛnda* — by streams; *dhauta* — washed; *akhila* — whole; *tanuḥ* — [whose] body; *ullasitaḥ* — exulting; *nanarta* — danced; *gauraḥ* — Gaura.

**62.** In the fullness of His great eagerness He flung up His knees and His chest, and a long thrill of the hairs spread over His body; His whole body washed by streams of ceaselessly flowing tears, Gaura danced, exulting.

**63.** In the fullness of great joy He beautifully uttered hundreds of graceful, soft and deep cries of "Hum!", and danced, whirling now lightly, now swiftly, now slowly.

**64.** Now He made the people, no different from His own body, dance with unceasing rasa; [now] He sang in a deep voice, making the quarters resound with the sweetness of the soft sound of His clapping palms.

**65.** Now, delighted, He looks on; now He sings, now He dances. Having gained splendour from the mingling of sweat, of tears from His eyes and of mire [caused] by the heat, the Lord shone.

### Verse 66

इति पुरपरिमार्जनावसाने

**66.** Thus, at the end of the cleaning of the enclosure, having also displayed the art of dancing, Gaurachandra then wished to sport in the pond; the slender stem of His body was exhausted under the burden of weariness.

**67.** Then, to dispel His weariness, Gaurachandra eagerly sat down for a while with the company of His own people in a soft, cool spot and, His face sweet, delighted in good talks.

सुखमतनोत् परिपश्यतां दृशोः सः ॥६८॥

*jala-viharaṇa-vāñchayā tato 'sau*

*laghu laghu vicalan śramālasāṅgaḥ*
*sukham atanot paripaśyatāṁ dṛśoḥ saḥ ||68||*

*Word for word:* *jala* — in the water; *viharaṇa* — of sporting; *vāñchayā* — with the desire; *tataḥ* — then; *asau* — He; *saha* — together; *nija* — of His own; *bhakta* — devotees; *cayaiḥ* — with the throngs; *puraḥ* — first (?); *sarasyām* — to the pond; *laghu laghu* — slowly, slowly; *vicalan* — walking; *śrama* — from weariness; *alasa* — languid; *aṅgaḥ* — [whose] body; *sukham* — happiness; *atanot* — gave; *paripaśyatām* — of the onlookers; *dṛśoḥ* — to the eyes; *saḥ* — He.

**68.** Then, with the desire to sport in the water, He walked slowly, slowly to the pond together with the throngs of His devotees, His body languid with weariness, and gave happiness to the eyes of the onlookers.

*Note.* *Puraḥ sarasyām* is unclear (?): *puraḥ* may mean "first" or "in front". Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 12.151–153: after the cleaning and the kirtana the Lord goes with the devotees to the pond, sports in the water, and then bows down to Nrisimhadeva. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

**69.** Then, after a long, playful sport in the water, the slender stem of His body thoroughly cooled, He came with delight to the bank together with the crowd of His own people and put on two fine garments.

### Verse 70

तदनु च नरसिंहदेवमेत्य

तदनु चलितुमुद्यतस्तथैव
प्रतिपदमुल्लसिताङ्घ्रिपद्म आसीत् ॥७०॥

*tad-anu ca narasiṁha-devam etya*

*pratipadam ullasitāṅghri-padma āsīt ||70||*

*Word for word:* *tat-anu* — after that; *ca* — and; *narasiṁha-devam* — to Lord Nrisimha; *etya* — coming; *pramuditaḥ* — delighted; *eva* — indeed; *nanāma* — bowed down; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra; *tat-anu* — after that; *calitum* — to go; *udyataḥ* — ready; *tathā eva* — just so; *pratipadam* — at every step; *ullasita* — exultant; *aṅghri* — of the feet; *padmaḥ* — [whose] lotuses; *āsīt* — was.

**70.** After that Gaurachandra came to Lord Nrisimha and, delighted, bowed down [to Him]. Then He made ready to go on, and at every step His lotus feet were just as exultant.

*Note.* The temple of Nrisimha is near the Gundicha; cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 12.136 (the Lord cleans the temple of Nrisimha too) and 12.152 (having changed His clothes on the bank of the pond, He bows down to Nrisimhadeva, whose temple is close by).

### Verse 71

अथ सकलजगज्जनस्य नेत्रो-

न्तरितमदर्शि समं जनैश्च तेन ॥७१॥

*atha sakala-jagaj-janasya netrot-*
*sava-karam ānana-padmam īśvarasya |*
*asita-giri-viśeṣakasya pakṣān-*
*taritam adarśi samaṁ janaiś ca tena ||71||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *sakala* — of the whole; *jagat* — world; *janasya* — of the people; *netra* — for the eyes; *utsava* — a festival; *karam* — making; *ānana* — of the face; *padmam* — the lotus; *īśvarasya* — of the Lord; *asita-giri* — of the Dark Mountain; *viśeṣakasya* — of the tilaka; *pakṣa* — by a fortnight; *antaritam* — hidden; *adarśi* — was seen; *samam* — together; *janaiḥ* — with the people; *ca* — and; *tena* — by Him.

**71.** Then, together with the people, He beheld the lotus face of the Lord who is the tilaka of the Dark Mountain — the face that makes a festival for the eyes of the people of the whole world, which had been hidden [from Him] for a fortnight.

*Note.* A play on words: *netrotsava*, "a festival for the eyes", is also the name of the festival of the first darshana after the anavasara — the Netrotsava. Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 12.204–211 (the Netrotsava falls on the day after the cleaning; the Lord's eyes, like bees, drink the honey of Jagannatha's lotus face).

चिरविरहकृतोपवासतृष्णा-

*Word for word:* *cira* — long; *viraha* — by separation; *kṛta* — caused; *upavāsa* — of the fast; *tṛṣṇā* — by the thirst; *ākulitatamena* — utterly tormented; *vilocanena* — with eyes; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *gata* — gone; *nimiṣam* — blinking; *api* — although; *pralocya* — gazing; *na* — not; *āsīt* — was; *sapadi* — at once; *tat* — His; *ānana* — of the face; *candra* — with the moon; *mātra* — merely; *tṛptiḥ* — [whose] satisfaction.

**72.** With eyes utterly tormented by the thirst of the fast caused by long separation, the Lord gazed without blinking; yet the mere moon of His [Jagannatha's] face could not satisfy Him at once.

### Verse 73

अभिनवघनरागरम्यमूर्ती
विगतनिमेषसतृष्णलोचनाब्जौ ।

रहसि तदा सदृशौ बभूवतुः स्म ॥७३॥

*abhinava-ghana-rāga-ramya-mūrtī*
*vigata-nimeṣa-satṛṣṇa-locanābjau |*
*asita-śikhara-ratna-gauracandrau*

*Word for word:* *abhinava* — fresh; *ghana* — thick; *rāga* — with colour (with love); *ramya* — lovely; *mūrtī* — [whose] forms; *vigata* — without; *nimeṣa* — blinking; *sa-tṛṣṇa* — thirsting; *locana* — of the eyes; *abjau* — [whose] lotuses; *asita* — of the Dark; *śikhara* — Peak; *ratna* — the Jewel; *gauracandrau* — and Gaurachandra; *rahasi* — secretly; *tadā* — then; *sadṛśau* — alike; *babhūvatuḥ sma* — became.

**73.** The Jewel of the Dark Peak and Gaurachandra secretly became alike then: the forms of both were lovely with fresh, thick colour — with love — and the lotuses of the eyes of both were thirsting and unblinking.

*Note.* A double meaning: *rāga* is both "colour" and "love". For the Netrotsava Jagannatha is freshly painted, and His eyes never blink.

### Verse 74

अखिलजनमुखोद्गतैः समन्ता-
ज्जय जय देव जयेति रम्यशब्दैः ।
मुहुरुदयितहस्तवीचिपूरै-
रपर इवाजनि तत्र वारिराशिः ॥७४॥

*akhila-jana-mukhodgataiḥ samantāj*
*jaya jaya deva jayeti ramya-śabdaiḥ |*
*muhur udayita-hasta-vīci-pūrair*
*apara ivājani tatra vāri-rāśiḥ ||74||*

*Word for word:* *akhila* — of all; *jana* — the people; *mukha* — from the mouths; *udgataiḥ* — issuing; *samantāt* — on all sides; *jaya jaya deva jaya* — "Jaya, jaya, O Lord, jaya!"; *iti* — thus; *ramya* — lovely; *śabdaiḥ* — with sounds; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *udayita* — raised; *hasta* — of hands; *vīci* — of waves; *pūraiḥ* — with the swell; *aparaḥ* — another; *iva* — as it were; *ajani* — arose; *tatra* — there; *vāri-rāśiḥ* — ocean.

**74.** With the lovely sounds "Jaya, jaya, O Lord, jaya!" issuing on all sides from the mouths of all the people, and with the swell of the waves of hands raised again and again, another ocean, as it were, arose there.

### Verse 75

सकलजनसमूहमेव जित्वा
मुहुरतुलोच्छ्रितकाययष्टिशोभः ।
विमलदृषदि भोगमण्डपान्ते
परिकलयन्नुपतस्थिवान् परेशम् ॥७५॥

*sakala-jana-samūham eva jitvā*
*muhur atulocchrita-kāya-yaṣṭi-śobhaḥ |*
*vimala-dṛṣadi bhoga-maṇḍapānte*
*parikalayann upatasthivān pareśam ||75||*

*Word for word:* *sakala* — the whole; *jana* — of people; *samūham* — crowd; *eva* — indeed; *jitvā* — surpassing; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *atula* — incomparably; *ucchrita* — tall; *kāya* — of the body; *yaṣṭi* — of the stem; *śobhaḥ* — [with] the beauty; *vimala* — on a clean; *dṛṣadi* — stone; *bhoga-maṇḍapa* — of the hall of offerings; *ante* — at the edge; *parikalayan* — beholding; *upatasthivān* — stood before; *para-īśam* — the Supreme Lord.

**75.** Surpassing again and again the whole crowd of people with the beauty of the incomparably tall stem of His body, He stood on a clean stone at the edge of the hall of offerings before the Supreme Lord, beholding Him.

*Note.* The edition has *विमलदृशदिभोग-*; we read *vimala-dṛṣadi bhoga-*. The bhoga-mandapa is the hall of food offerings in the Jagannatha temple.

### Verse 76

नयनजलझरैः पदारविन्द-
द्वयनखचन्द्रमसः पवित्रयन् सः ।
न हि जगति दुरापमेतदन्य-
त्किमिति तदाभिसिषेच सोऽङ्घ्रिपद्मम् ॥७६॥

*nayana-jala-jharaiḥ padāravinda-*
*dvaya-nakha-candramasaḥ pavitrayan saḥ |*
*na hi jagati durāpam etad anyat*
*kim iti tadābhisiṣeca so 'ṅghri-padmam ||76||*

*Word for word:* *nayana* — of the eyes; *jala* — of water; *jharaiḥ* — with torrents; *pada* — of the feet; *aravinda* — of the lotuses; *dvaya* — of the pair; *nakha* — of the nails; *candramasaḥ* — the moons; *pavitrayan* — purifying; *saḥ* — He; *na hi* — for there is not; *jagati* — in the world; *durāpam* — hard to attain; *etat* — than this; *anyat* — anything else; *kim* — whether; *iti* — [thinking] thus; *tadā* — then; *abhisiṣeca* — bathed; *saḥ* — He; *aṅghri* — of the feet; *padmam* — the lotus.

**76.** With torrents of tears He purified the moons of the nails of the pair of lotus feet. Was it [with the thought] "For in the world there is nothing else so hard to attain as this" that He then bathed the lotus feet?

*Note.* Whose feet are meant — His own or Jagannatha's — is unclear (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 77

नयनयुगमुवाह शोणपद्म-

असितगिरिसुधांशुवक्त्रचन्द्रं
रहसि विलोकयतोऽस्य निस्पृहस्य ॥७७॥

*nayana-yugam uvāha śoṇa-padma-*
*śriyam ati kuḍmalatāṁ tataḥ śarīram |*
*asita-giri-sudhāṁśu-vaktra-candraṁ*
*rahasi vilokayato 'sya nispṛhasya ||77||*

*Word for word:* *nayana* — of eyes; *yugam* — the pair; *uvāha* — took on; *śoṇa* — of a red; *padma* — lotus; *śriyam* — the beauty; *ati* — very much; *kuḍmalatām* — the state of a bud; *tataḥ* — then; *śarīram* — the body; *asita-giri* — of the Dark Mountain; *sudhāṁśu* — of the Moon; *vaktra* — of the face; *candram* — the moon; *rahasi* — in secret; *vilokayataḥ* — beholding; *asya* — of Him; *nispṛhasya* — desiring nothing [else].

**77.** As He, desiring nothing else, secretly beheld the moon of the face of the Moon of the Dark Mountain, the pair of His eyes took on the beauty of red lotuses, and then His body became very much like a bud.

*Note.* "Like a bud": the body contracted.

### Verse 78

इति स तु जगदीश्वरोऽसिताद्रौ

अवसरमवगम्य वासरैकं
सह रमया रमणेच्छया निनाय ॥७८॥

*iti sa tu jagad-īśvaro 'sitādrau*
*madhura-tanur daśa-pañca-vāsarānte |*
*avasaram avagamya vāsaraikaṁ*
*saha ramayā ramaṇecchayā nināya ||78||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *saḥ tu* — He; *jagat-īśvaraḥ* — the Lord of the world; *asita-adrau* — on the Dark Mountain; *madhura* — charming; *tanuḥ* — [whose] form; *daśa-pañca* — of fifteen; *vāsara* — days; *ante* — at the end; *avasaram* — the opportunity; *avagamya* — perceiving; *vāsara* — day; *ekam* — one; *saha* — with; *ramayā* — Rama; *ramaṇa* — to sport; *icchayā* — with the wish; *nināya* — spent.

**78.** Thus the Lord of the world, of charming form, at the end of fifteen days on the Dark Mountain, perceiving the opportunity, spent one day with Rama, wishing to sport [with her].

*Note.* Rama is Lakshmi.

### Verse 79

अपरदिवस एष नीलचन्द्रो

परमरुचिमनोहरोऽभविष्य-
द्रथविजयोत्सवकौतुकी रराज ॥७९॥

*apara-divasa eṣa nīla-candro*
*dvi-guṇita-bhojana-hṛṣṭa-puṣṭa-dehaḥ |*
*parama-ruci-manoharo 'bhaviṣyad-*
*ratha-vijayotsava-kautukī rarāja ||79||*

*Word for word:* *apara* — on the next; *divase* — day; *eṣaḥ* — this; *nīla* — blue; *candraḥ* — moon; *dvi-guṇita* — doubled; *bhojana* — by meals; *hṛṣṭa* — gladdened; *puṣṭa* — nourished; *dehaḥ* — [whose] body; *parama* — supreme; *ruci* — by splendour; *manoharaḥ* — captivating; *abhaviṣyat* — impending; *ratha* — of the chariot; *vijaya* — of the procession; *utsava* — for the festival; *kautukī* — eager; *rarāja* — shone.

**79.** On the next day this Blue Moon — His body gladdened and nourished by doubled meals, captivating with supreme splendour — shone, eager for the coming festival of the chariot procession.

### Verse 80

अयमसितमहीध्रनीलरत्नं

*ayam asita-mahīdhra-nīla-ratnaṁ*
*sakala-rasāsvādito mahā-vilāsī |*
*anukṛta-sakalāvatāra-līlaḥ*
*satatam anugrahavān svakīya-loke ||80||*

*Word for word:* *ayam* — this; *asita* — of the Dark; *mahīdhra* — Mountain; *nīla* — blue; *ratnam* — jewel; *sakala* — all; *rasa* — the rasas; *āsvāditaḥ* — who has tasted; *mahā* — great; *vilāsī* — sportive one; *anukṛta* — re-enacted; *sakala* — of all; *avatāra* — the incarnations; *līlaḥ* — [by whom] the pastimes; *satatam* — always; *anugrahavān* — gracious; *svakīya* — toward His own; *loke* — people.

**80.** This blue jewel of the Dark Mountain — the great sportive Lord who has tasted all the rasas, who re-enacts the pastimes of all the incarnations, ever gracious toward His own people…

*Note.* Verses 80–81 form one period. In the second pada the sixth syllable (*svā* in *rasāsvādito*) is heavy where the metre requires a light one (?).

### Verse 81

निजजनमभि सत्कृपाभिरार्द्रः
स्वयमनुवत्सरमेव गुण्डिचायाम् ।
व्रजति समनुनीय तत्र लक्ष्मीं
रहसि मिथो दशपञ्चवासरेण ॥८१॥

*nija-janam abhi sat-kṛpābhir ārdraḥ*
*svayam anuvatsaram eva guṇḍicāyām |*
*vrajati samanunīya tatra lakṣmīṁ*
*rahasi mitho daśa-pañca-vāsareṇa ||81||*

*Word for word:* *nija* — toward His own; *janam abhi* — people; *sat* — with good; *kṛpābhiḥ* — with mercies; *ārdraḥ* — softened; *svayam* — Himself; *anuvatsaram* — every year; *eva* — indeed; *guṇḍicāyām* — to the Gundicha; *vrajati* — goes; *samanunīya* — having propitiated; *tatra* — there; *lakṣmīm* — Lakshmi; *rahasi* — in secret; *mithaḥ* — alone together; *daśa-pañca* — of fifteen; *vāsareṇa* — after the passing of days.

**81.** …softened by good mercies toward His own people, Himself goes every year to the Gundicha, having propitiated Lakshmi there, in secret, alone together [with her], after the passing of fifteen days.

*Note.* The syntax of the second half is unclear. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text. The sense seems to be that the Lord spends the fifteen days of the anavasara alone with Lakshmi and, having won her over, sets out for the Gundicha; cf. v. 78.

*pathi mṛdu-sikatā-samūha-ramye*

*vana-parama-smṛti-kṛj jagan-manojñaḥ ||82||*

*Word for word:* *pathi* — along the path; *mṛdu* — of soft; *sikatā* — sand; *samūha* — with heaps; *ramye* — lovely; *yat* — which; *ubhayataḥ* — on both sides; *vividha* — with various; *druma* — trees; *ādi* — and so on; *ramyaḥ* — lovely; *upavana* — of groves; *nicayaḥ* — the cluster; *saḥ eṣaḥ* — that very; *vṛndāvana* — of Vrindavana; *parama* — the highest; *smṛti* — remembrance; *kṛt* — awakening; *jagat* — the world; *manojñaḥ* — enchanting.

**82.** On both sides of the path, lovely with heaps of soft sand, [stretches] that very cluster of groves, lovely with trees of many kinds and so on, which enchants the world and awakens the highest remembrance of Vrindavana.

*Note.* Verses 82–83 form one period; cf. 14.4–5.

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *ratha* — of the chariot; *vijaya* — of the procession; *chalena* — under the pretext; *vṛndāvana* — to Vrindavana; *calita* — of the journey; *anuvidhāna* — on the re-enactment; *datta* — set; *cittaḥ* — [whose] mind; *upavana* — of groves; *nicaye* — in the cluster; *vihāra* — to sport; *vāñchā* — by the desire; *ākulitaḥ* — seized; *uvāca* — said; *purā* — before; *yat* — which; *eṣaḥ* — this; *gauraḥ* — Gaura.

**83.** Thus, under the pretext of the chariot procession, [Jagannatha] sets His mind on re-enacting the journey to Vrindavana and is seized by the desire to sport in the cluster of groves — as this Gaura had said before.

### Verse 84

**84.** The Supreme Lord sports by the Ratha-yatra; and Gaurachandra, having experienced that happiness, then displays here and there in the groves the countless delights of Vrindavana.

*Word for word:* *sthitavati sati* — while staying; *nīla-śaila* — of the Blue Mountain; *ratne* — the Jewel; *nava* — nine; *divasena* — by days; *hi* — indeed; *guṇḍicā* — of the Gundicha; *gṛha* — the temple; *antaḥ* — within; *upavana* — of the groves; *pavana* — of the breeze; *anupāta* — by the wafting; *pūtaḥ* — refreshed; *vilasati* — sports; *gaura* — the golden; *śaśī* — Moon; *rasa* — of rasa; *amburāśiḥ* — the ocean.

**85.** While the Jewel of the Blue Mountain stays for nine days within the Gundicha temple, the golden Moon, an ocean of rasa, refreshed by the wafting of the breeze in the groves, sports [there].

**86.** Then at the close of night the Blue Moon, eager for the joy of the procession, clad in [His] array, with fitting splendour, [came down], under the guise of a descent, from His lovely great throne, like the moon [setting] from a mountain.

### Verse 87

विरचितरुचिरावतारमध्ये

*Note.* *क्षितिक्षिद्* is apparently a corruption of *kṣitibhṛd* ("earth-bearer", i.e. mountain). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 88

अथ धरणिषु क्रमादुपेतः

द्युतिसमुदायविदूरितान्धकारः ॥८८॥

*atha dharaṇiṣu kramād upetaḥ*
*kaśipu-cayair vihitāplutiḥ samantāt |*
*pratibham iva śaśī vrajan vireje*
*dyuti-samudāya-vidūritāndhakāraḥ ||88||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *dharaṇiṣu* — to the ground; *kramāt* — gradually; *upetaḥ* — having come down; *kaśipu* — of cushions; *cayaiḥ* — over the heaps; *vihita* — making; *āplutiḥ* — leaps; *samantāt* — all around; *pratibham* — from star to star; *iva* — like; *śaśī* — the moon; *vrajan* — going; *vireje* — shone; *dyuti* — of radiance; *samudāya* — by the abundance; *vidūrita* — dispelled; *andhakāraḥ* — [by whom] the darkness.

*Note.* Cf. 14.129. The first pada has 11 syllables instead of 12 (?): instead of the six light syllables with which the pada opens, there are only five (*a-tha-dha-ra-ṇi-*), while the rest of the pada (*-ṣu kramād upetaḥ*, —⏑—⏑——) is regular.

### Verse 89

क्रमत इत इतः पदानि जिष्णुः

द्रुतसुरपतिरत्नसागरोर्मि-
प्रचयरुचिं विजिगाय तत् प्रकामम् ॥८९॥

*kramata ita itaḥ padāni jiṣṇuḥ*

*druta-surapati-ratna-sāgarormi-*
*pracaya-ruciṁ vijigāya tat prakāmam ||89||*

*Word for word:* *kramataḥ* — gradually; *ita itaḥ* — here and there; *padāni* — steps; *jiṣṇuḥ* — the Victorious One; *kaśipuṣu* — on the cushions; *nikṣipati* — sets; *kṣaṇāt* — at once; *atha* — and; *eṣaḥ* — He; *druta* — of molten; *surapati-ratna* — sapphire; *sāgara* — of the ocean; *ūrmi* — of waves; *pracaya* — of a mass; *rucim* — the beauty; *vijigāya* — surpassed; *tat* — thereby; *prakāmam* — fully.

**89.** As the Victorious One gradually set His steps here and there on the cushions, He at once fully surpassed thereby the beauty of a mass of waves on an ocean of molten sapphire.

*Note.* *Surapati-ratna* ("the jewel of Indra") is the sapphire (*indranīla*).

### Verse 90

कटितटपरिबद्धपट्टडोर-
द्वितयविजृम्भितसेवकावहृष्टः ।
स जयति किमु नाभिपद्मनाल-
द्वयजविधातृसभा रहः समन्तात् ॥९०॥

*kaṭi-taṭa-paribaddha-paṭṭa-ḍora-*
*dvitaya-vijṛmbhita-sevakāvahṛṣṭaḥ |*
*sa jayati kim u nābhi-padma-nāla-*
*dvaya-ja-vidhātṛ-sabhā rahaḥ samantāt ||90||*

*Word for word:* *kaṭi* — of the waist; *taṭa* — on the slope; *paribaddha* — tied; *paṭṭa* — of silk; *ḍora* — of ropes; *dvitaya* — the pair; *vijṛmbhita* — [who] stretched; *sevaka* — by servants; *avahṛṣṭaḥ* — drawn (?); *saḥ* — He; *jayati* — is victorious; *kim u* — is it perhaps; *nābhi* — of the navel; *padma* — of the lotus; *nāla* — of stalks; *dvaya* — from a pair; *ja* — born; *vidhātṛ* — of creators; *sabhā* — the assembly; *rahaḥ* — in private; *samantāt* — all around.

**90.** Victorious is He, drawn by the servants who stretched taut the pair of silk ropes tied about the slope of His waist: is this perhaps the assembly of creators, born from a pair of lotus-stalks of His navel, [gathered] all around [Him] in private?

*Note.* The image is understood tentatively. The ropes by which the Deity is drawn are compared to the stalks of the lotus from Vishnu's navel, and the servants to the Brahmas born from it. *Avahṛṣṭaḥ* is understood as "drawn" (perhaps for *avakṛṣṭaḥ*) (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 91

उपरि परिधृतातपत्रवृन्दै-
र्मुखशशिसेवनतत्परेन्दुरूपैः ।
निरवधि सुमनःसमूहवृष्ट्या
सितरणभूरपि नीलशैलनाथः ॥९१॥

*upari paridhṛtātapatra-vṛndair*
*mukha-śaśi-sevana-tat-parendu-rūpaiḥ |*
*niravadhi sumanaḥ-samūha-vṛṣṭyā*
*sita-raṇa-bhūr api nīla-śaila-nāthaḥ ||91||*

*Word for word:* *upari* — above [Him]; *paridhṛta* — held up; *ātapatra* — of parasols; *vṛndaiḥ* — by the multitude; *mukha* — of the face; *śaśi* — the moon; *sevana* — to serving; *tat-para* — devoted; *indu* — of moons; *rūpaiḥ* — in the form; *niravadhi* — unceasing; *sumanaḥ* — of flowers; *samūha* — of masses; *vṛṣṭyā* — by the rain; *sita* — white; *raṇa* — of battle; *bhūḥ* — a field; *api* — even; *nīla-śaila* — of the Blue Mountain; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord.

**91.** By the multitude of parasols held up above [Him] — moons, as it were, devoted to serving the moon of His face — and by the unceasing rain of masses of flowers, even the Lord of the Blue Mountain [became] a white field of battle.

*Note.* The meaning is unclear (?). The play is on colours: the blue Lord, covered by white parasols and white flowers, becomes white; the procession is the victor's "march" (*vijaya*), hence the "field of battle". The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 92

अनुसरति पुरो यथासितेन्दुः
किमपि तथापसरत्यसौ शचीजः ।
अभिमुखमभिगच्छतोस्तयोस्त-
त्सुललितकन्दुकविभ्रमं बभार ॥९२॥

*anusarati puro yathāsitenduḥ*
*kim api tathāpasaraty asau śacījaḥ |*
*abhimukham abhigacchatos tayos tat*
*sulalita-kanduka-vibhramaṁ babhāra ||92||*

*Word for word:* *anusarati* — moves; *puraḥ* — forward; *yathā* — as; *asita* — the Dark; *induḥ* — Moon; *kim api* — a little; *tathā* — so; *apasarati* — draws back; *asau* — He; *śacī-jaḥ* — the son of Shachi; *abhimukham* — face to face; *abhigacchatoḥ* — of the [two] approaching; *tayoḥ* — of those two; *tat* — that; *su-lalita* — of a graceful; *kanduka* — game of ball; *vibhramam* — the semblance; *babhāra* — bore.

**92.** As the Dark Moon moves forward, so the son of Shachi draws back a little. That [movement] of the two, approaching face to face, bore the semblance of a graceful game of ball.

### Verse 93

असितगिरिपतिर्यथा स्वभृत्यैः
परिकलितः स तथैव गौरचन्द्रः ।
सुरपतिमणिहेमरत्नभासौ
जनचयलक्ष्यतनू बभूवतुस्तौ ॥९३॥

*asita-giri-patir yathā sva-bhṛtyaiḥ*
*parikalitaḥ sa tathaiva gauracandraḥ |*
*surapati-maṇi-hema-ratna-bhāsau*
*jana-caya-lakṣya-tanū babhūvatus tau ||93||*

*Word for word:* *asita-giri* — of the Dark Mountain; *patiḥ* — the Lord; *yathā* — as; *sva* — by His own; *bhṛtyaiḥ* — servants; *parikalitaḥ* — surrounded; *saḥ* — He; *tathā eva* — just so; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra; *surapati-maṇi* — of a sapphire; *hema* — golden; *ratna* — of a jewel; *bhāsau* — [with] the lustre; *jana* — of people; *caya* — to the throngs; *lakṣya* — visible; *tanū* — [whose] bodies; *babhūvatuḥ* — became; *tau* — the two.

**93.** As the Lord of the Dark Mountain was surrounded by His servants, just so was Gaurachandra. The two of them, with the lustre of a sapphire and of a golden jewel, were visible to the throngs of people.

### Verse 94

क्वचिदयमपि गौरचन्द्रभासा
भवति सुवर्णरुचिस्तथैव सोऽपि ।
जगति तदुभयोः सितेतराद्रेः
परिवृढता परितः प्रकाशितासीत् ॥९४॥

*kvacid ayam api gauracandra-bhāsā*
*bhavati suvarṇa-rucis tathaiva so 'pi |*
*jagati tad-ubhayoḥ sitetarādreḥ*
*parivṛḍhatā paritaḥ prakāśitāsīt ||94||*

*Word for word:* *kvacit* — at times; *ayam* — He (Jagannatha); *api* — too; *gauracandra* — of Gaurachandra; *bhāsā* — by the radiance; *bhavati* — becomes; *suvarṇa* — golden; *ruciḥ* — [whose] lustre; *tathā eva* — likewise; *saḥ api* — that One too; *jagati* — in the world; *tat* — thus; *ubhayoḥ* — of both; *sita-itara* — not white; *adreḥ* — over the mountain; *parivṛḍhatā* — the lordship; *paritaḥ* — all around; *prakāśitā* — manifested; *āsīt* — was.

**94.** At times He too, [Jagannatha], becomes golden-hued by the radiance of Gaurachandra, and likewise that One too [becomes blue]. Thus the lordship of both over the not-white Mountain was manifested to the world all around.

*Note.* The "not-white Mountain" is Nilachala. The first sentence is compressed: [Gaurachandra becomes blue from the radiance of Jagannatha].

### Verse 95

गजपतिकरदण्डखण्डखण्डी-
कृतसकलारिरशेषविघ्नहर्ता ।
नृपतिगणपतिः प्रतापरुद्रो
रविरिव यः प्रतपत्यसौ सदैव ॥९५॥

*gaja-pati-kara-daṇḍa-khaṇḍa-khaṇḍī-*
*kṛta-sakalārir aśeṣa-vighna-hartā |*
*nṛpati-gaṇa-patiḥ pratāparudro*
*ravir iva yaḥ pratapaty asau sadaiva ||95||*

*Word for word:* *gaja-pati* — of the king of elephants; *kara* — of the trunk; *daṇḍa* — with the staff; *khaṇḍa-khaṇḍī-kṛta* — hacked to pieces; *sakala* — all; *ariḥ* — [by whom] the foes; *aśeṣa* — of all; *vighna* — obstacles; *hartā* — the remover; *nṛpati* — of kings; *gaṇa* — of the host; *patiḥ* — the lord; *pratāparudraḥ* — Prataparudra; *raviḥ* — the sun; *iva* — like; *yaḥ* — who; *pratapati* — blazes (shines with might); *asau* — he; *sadā eva* — ever.

**95.** Prataparudra — who with the staff of the trunk of the king of elephants hacked all his foes to pieces, the remover of all obstacles, the lord of the host of kings, who, like the sun, ever blazes with might —

*Note.* Verses 95–96 form a pair (*yugmaka*). A play on words: *gaja-pati*, "king of elephants", is also the title of the kings of Orissa, the Gajapatis. The epithets "remover of all obstacles" and "lord of the host" (*gaṇa-pati*), together with the elephant's trunk, also suggest Ganesha.

### Verse 96

स तु लघुतरसेवकायमानः
करकलितामलहैममार्जनीकः ।
किमपि तदुभयोर्विहारलीलां
परिकलयन् गतसर्वचेष्ट आसीत् ॥९६॥ (युग्मकम्)

*sa tu laghutara-sevakāyamānaḥ*
*kara-kalitāmala-haima-mārjanīkaḥ |*
*kim api tad-ubhayor vihāra-līlāṁ*
*parikalayan gata-sarva-ceṣṭa āsīt ||96|| (yugmakam)*

*Word for word:* *saḥ tu* — he; *laghutara* — the humblest; *sevakāyamānaḥ* — behaving like a servant; *kara* — in the hand; *kalita* — holding; *amala* — a spotless; *haima* — golden; *mārjanīkaḥ* — broom; *kim api* — indescribable; *tat* — of those; *ubhayoḥ* — of the two; *vihāra* — of sport; *līlām* — the pastime; *parikalayan* — beholding; *gata* — gone; *sarva* — all; *ceṣṭaḥ* — [whose] movements; *āsīt* — was.

**96.** …he, behaving like the humblest servant, a spotless golden broom in his hand, beholding the indescribable sporting pastime of those two, stood motionless, all his movements gone.

*Note.* Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 13.15–16: the king sweeps the road with a broom with a golden handle; for this humility the Lord later shows him mercy (13.184).

### Verse 97

सततमुभयतो ज्वलन्महोल्का-
विविधमहातपविस्मृतक्षपान्तः ।
पटहपटलमण्डुडिण्डिमाद्यै-
रतिमहिमा समयोऽयमेवमासीत् ॥९७॥

*satatam ubhayato jvalan-maholkā-*
*vividha-mahātapa-vismṛta-kṣapāntaḥ |*
*paṭaha-paṭala-maṇḍu-ḍiṇḍimādyair*
*ati-mahimā samayo 'yam evam āsīt ||97||*

*Word for word:* *satatam* — constantly; *ubhayataḥ* — on both sides; *jvalat* — blazing; *mahā-ulkā* — of great torches; *vividha* — by the manifold; *mahā-ātapa* — great glare; *vismṛta* — forgotten; *kṣapā* — of the night; *antaḥ* — [in which] the end; *paṭaha* — of drums; *paṭala* — by the multitude; *maṇḍu* — by mandus; *ḍiṇḍima* — by dindimas; *ādyaiḥ* — and so on; *ati* — surpassing; *mahimā* — [whose] grandeur; *samayaḥ* — the time; *ayam* — this; *evam* — thus; *āsīt* — was.

**97.** By the manifold great glare of the great torches blazing constantly on both sides, the end of the night was forgotten; and by the multitude of drums, mandus, dindimas and the rest, that time was thus one of surpassing grandeur.

*Note.* The edition has *मरातप*, a corruption; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *mahātapa* ("great glare, heat"), and so we read. The *maṇḍu* and *ḍiṇḍima* are kinds of drums.

### Verse 98

इति रथनिकटं व्रजन् विरेजे
परिकलयन् पुरतः स गौरचन्द्रः ।
इत इत इत एतदेतदेतत्
परिकलनीयमितः स्वभृत्यनादैः ॥९८॥

*iti ratha-nikaṭaṁ vrajan vireje*
*parikalayan purataḥ sa gauracandraḥ |*
*ita ita ita etad etad etat*
*parikalanīyam itaḥ sva-bhṛtya-nādaiḥ ||98||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *ratha* — to the chariot; *nikaṭam* — near; *vrajan* — going; *vireje* — shone; *parikalayan* — gazing; *purataḥ* — in front; *saḥ* — He; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra; *itaḥ itaḥ itaḥ* — from here, from here, from here; *etat etat etat* — this, this, this; *parikalanīyam* — must be seen; *itaḥ* — from here; *sva* — of His own; *bhṛtya* — servants; *nādaiḥ* — amid the cries.

**98.** Thus, going near the chariot and gazing at [Jagannatha] in front, Gaurachandra shone, amid the cries of His servants: "From here, from here, from here! This, this, this! It must be seen from here!"

### Verse 99

अथ रथमधिरुह्य नीलशैल-
प्रभुरसकौ रसकौतुकी रराज ।
परिणत इव पूर्वपर्वतान्ते
मधुमधुरो जलदात्यये हिमांशुः ॥९९॥

*atha ratham adhiruhya nīla-śaila-*
*prabhur asakau rasa-kautukī rarāja |*
*pariṇata iva pūrva-parvatānte*
*madhu-madhuro jaladātyaye himāṁśuḥ ||99||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *ratham* — the chariot; *adhiruhya* — having mounted; *nīla-śaila* — of the Blue Mountain; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *asakau* — He; *rasa* — in rasa; *kautukī* — delighting; *rarāja* — shone; *pariṇataḥ* — full; *iva* — like; *pūrva* — of the eastern; *parvata* — mountain; *ante* — on the edge; *madhu-madhuraḥ* — honey-sweet; *jalada* — of the clouds; *atyaye* — at the passing; *hima-aṁśuḥ* — the moon.

**99.** Then the Lord of the Blue Mountain, delighting in rasa, mounted the chariot and shone like the honey-sweet full moon on the edge of the eastern mountain when the clouds have passed.

*Note.* In the edition the number *॥९९॥* lacks the first danda.

### Verse 100

इति पथि विहितेऽपि सद्विहारे
