निजजननिचयैः स गौरचन्द्रः
स्नपनविहारचिकीर्षया जगाम ॥१००॥

*iti pathi vihite 'pi sad-vihāre*
*ratham adhirohati nīla-śaila-nāthe |*
*nija-jana-nicayaiḥ sa gauracandraḥ*
*snapana-vihāra-cikīrṣayā jagāma ||100||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *pathi* — on the way; *vihite* — when performed; *api* — and; *sat* — fine; *vihāre* — the sport; *ratham* — the chariot; *adhirohati* — when mounting; *nīla-śaila* — of the Blue Mountain; *nāthe* — the Lord; *nija* — of His own; *jana* — people; *nicayaiḥ* — with the throngs; *saḥ* — He; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra; *snapana* — of bathing; *vihāra* — the sport; *cikīrṣayā* — with the wish to do; *jagāma* — went.

**100.** Thus, when the fine sport on the way had been performed and the Lord of the Blue Mountain was mounting the chariot, Gaurachandra went with the throngs of His own people, wishing to sport in bathing.

### Verse 101

अथ लघुविहितावगाहरम्याः
प्रभुपुरतो मिलिता बभूवुरेते ।
स्वयमपि विहिताप्लवः प्रकामं
मलयजपङ्कचयैर्लिलेप तांस्तान् ॥१०१॥

*atha laghu-vihitāvagāha-ramyāḥ*
*prabhu-purato militā babhūvur ete |*
*svayam api vihitāplavaḥ prakāmaṁ*
*malayaja-paṅka-cayair lilepa tāṁs tān ||101||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *laghu* — quickly; *vihita* — made; *avagāha* — by a plunge; *ramyāḥ* — refreshed; *prabhu* — the Lord; *purataḥ* — before; *militāḥ* — gathered; *babhūvuḥ* — became; *ete* — they; *svayam* — Himself; *api* — and; *vihita* — having made; *āplavaḥ* — [whose] bath; *prakāmam* — abundantly; *malayaja* — of sandal; *paṅka* — of paste; *cayaiḥ* — with heaps; *lilepa* — anointed; *tān tān* — each of them.

**101.** Then they, refreshed by a quick plunge, gathered before the Lord; and He, having bathed Himself, abundantly anointed each of them with heaps of sandal paste.

### Verse 102

प्रथममसकृदद्वितीयभावो-
रसि रसिकः करपल्लवेन हृष्टः ।
मलयरुहरसैर्लिलेप तस्य
द्विगुणितमुत्सुकयन् सरोमवृन्दम् ॥१०२॥

*prathamam asakṛd advitīya-bhāvo-*
*rasi rasikaḥ kara-pallavena hṛṣṭaḥ |*
*malaya-ruha-rasair lilepa tasya*
*dvi-guṇitam utsukayan saroma-vṛndam ||102||*

*Word for word:* *prathamam* — first; *asakṛt* — repeatedly; *advitīya* — of non-duality; *bhāva* — [of Him whose] nature; *urasi* — on the chest; *rasikaḥ* — the relisher of rasa; *kara* — of the hand; *pallavena* — with the tender shoot; *hṛṣṭaḥ* — joyful; *malaya-ruha* — of sandal; *rasaiḥ* — with the juice; *lilepa* — anointed; *tasya* — His; *dvi-guṇitam* — doubly; *utsukayan* — thrilling; *sa-roma-vṛndam* — with the mass of His hairs.

**102.** First the joyful relisher of rasa repeatedly anointed with sandal juice, with the tender shoot of His hand, the chest of Him whose nature is non-duality, thrilling Him doubly, to the very hairs [of His body].

*Note.* "Whose nature is non-duality" (*advitīya-bhāva*) is a hint at the name Advaita.

### Verse 103

तदनु च भुवि नारदस्वरूपं
द्विजकुलचन्द्रमसं महानुभावम् ।
तदनु तदनुजं ततस्तथान्या-
न्क्रमत इतो मलयोद्भवैर्लिलेप ॥१०३॥

*tad-anu ca bhuvi nārada-svarūpaṁ*
*dvija-kula-candramasaṁ mahānubhāvam |*
*tad-anu tad-anujaṁ tatas tathānyān*
*kramata ito malayodbhavair lilepa ||103||*

*Word for word:* *tat-anu* — then; *ca* — and; *bhuvi* — on earth; *nārada* — of Narada; *svarūpam* — the very self; *dvija* — of brahmanas; *kula* — of the race; *candramasam* — the moon; *mahā-anubhāvam* — the magnanimous; *tat-anu* — then; *tat* — his; *anujam* — younger brother; *tataḥ* — then; *tathā* — likewise; *anyān* — others; *kramataḥ* — in order; *itaḥ* — from here on; *malaya-udbhavaiḥ* — with sandal; *lilepa* — anointed.

**103.** Then [He anointed] the magnanimous one, the moon of the brahmana race, Narada's very self on earth; then his younger brother; and then likewise, in order, others from here on He anointed with sandal.

*Note.* Narada's very self on earth is Srivasa; his younger brother is Rama Pandita.

### Verse 104

तदनु सकलगायनान् विशेषं
प्रतिजनमेवमुरःस्थले कृपालुः ।
प्रमदभरभरालसाङ्गयष्टि-
र्नटनकलाकुलितो लिलेप तैस्तैः ॥१०४॥

*tad-anu sakala-gāyanān viśeṣaṁ*
*prati-janam evam uraḥ-sthale kṛpāluḥ |*
*pramada-bhara-bharālasāṅga-yaṣṭir*
*naṭana-kalākulito lilepa tais taiḥ ||104||*

*Word for word:* *tat-anu* — then; *sakala* — all; *gāyanān* — the singers; *viśeṣam* — specially; *prati-janam* — each one; *evam* — thus; *uraḥ-sthale* — on the chest; *kṛpāluḥ* — the Merciful One; *pramada* — of joy; *bhara-bhara* — by the full weight; *alasa* — languid; *aṅga* — of the body; *yaṣṭiḥ* — [whose] stem; *naṭana* — of dancing; *kalā* — by the art; *ākulitaḥ* — stirred; *lilepa* — anointed; *taiḥ taiḥ* — with that [sandal].

**104.** Then the Merciful One — the slender stem of His body languid under the full weight of joy, stirred by the art of dancing — thus specially anointed with that [sandal] the chest of each and every one of the singers.

*Note.* This is the last verse in *puṣpitāgrā*.

### Verse 105

ये ते श्रीवासरामौ स्वरविजितपिकौ वासुदेवो मुकुन्दः
श्रीमद्दामोदराख्यो यतिरिति जगति ख्यातवान् प्रेमपुञ्जः ।
श्रीमद्वक्रेश्वरश्च प्रथितगुणगणः श्रीलदामोदरोऽसौ
भूमीगीर्वाणमुख्यस्तदनु सुमधुरः कोऽपि नारायणाख्यः ॥१०५॥

*ye te śrīvāsa-rāmau svara-vijita-pikau vāsudevo mukundaḥ*
*śrīmad-dāmodarākhyo yatir iti jagati khyātavān prema-puñjaḥ |*
*śrīmad-vakreśvaraś ca prathita-guṇa-gaṇaḥ śrīla-dāmodaro 'sau*
*bhūmī-gīrvāṇa-mukhyas tad-anu sumadhuraḥ ko 'pi nārāyaṇākhyaḥ ||105||*

*Word for word:* *ye te* — those who [are]; *śrīvāsa-rāmau* — Srivasa and Rama; *svara* — by voice; *vijita* — [by whom] surpassed; *pikau* — the cuckoos; *vāsudevaḥ* — Vasudeva; *mukundaḥ* — Mukunda; *śrīmat* — the illustrious; *dāmodara* — Damodara; *ākhyaḥ* — named; *yatiḥ* — an ascetic; *iti* — as; *jagati* — in the world; *khyātavān* — renowned; *prema* — of love; *puñjaḥ* — a mass; *śrīmat* — the illustrious; *vakreśvaraḥ* — Vakreshvara; *ca* — and; *prathita* — celebrated; *guṇa* — of virtues; *gaṇaḥ* — [whose] host; *śrīla-dāmodaraḥ* — Srila Damodara; *asau* — that; *bhūmī-gīrvāṇa* — of the gods on earth (brahmanas); *mukhyaḥ* — the foremost; *tat-anu* — then; *su-madhuraḥ* — most sweet; *kaḥ api* — a certain; *nārāyaṇa* — Narayana; *ākhyaḥ* — named.

**105.** Namely: Srivasa and Rama, who surpassed the cuckoos with their voices; Vasudeva; Mukunda; the illustrious one named Damodara, renowned in the world as an ascetic, a mass of love; the illustrious Vakreshvara, with his celebrated host of virtues; that Srila Damodara, foremost of the brahmanas; then a certain most sweet one named Narayana…

*Note.* The metre is *sragdharā*. Verses 105–106 form one period. The ascetic Damodara is Svarupa Damodara (13.143); Srila Damodara is Damodara Pandita. Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 13.32–47: the seven kirtana parties of the Ratha-yatra (the first led by Svarupa Damodara).

### Verse 106

श्रीकान्तो मकरध्वजः सुमधुरः शुद्धः शुभानन्दकः
काशीनाथकवल्लभौ च हरिदासाख्यो रघुः शुद्धधीः ।
एतांस्तान् सहसैव चन्दनरसैर्लिप्त्वा स स्वयं श्रीमता
गौराङ्गेन दृढं निबध्य वसनं श्रीमत्कटीरोधसि ।
आजानुद्वयलम्बिपीवरभुजद्वन्द्वेन मन्दोल्लस-
द्रोमाञ्चाञ्चितविग्रहेण परमाविष्टेन तैर्निर्यये ॥१०६॥

*śrīkānto makaradhvajaḥ sumadhuraḥ śuddhaḥ śubhānandakaḥ*
*kāśīnāthaka-vallabhau ca haridāsākhyo raghuḥ śuddha-dhīḥ |*
*etāṁs tān sahasaiva candana-rasair liptvā sa svayaṁ śrīmatā*
*gaurāṅgena dṛḍhaṁ nibadhya vasanaṁ śrīmat-kaṭī-rodhasi |*
*ājānu-dvaya-lambi-pīvara-bhuja-dvandvena mandollasad-*
*romāñcāñcita-vigraheṇa paramāviṣṭena tair niryaye ||106||*

*Word for word:* *śrīkāntaḥ* — Shrikanta; *makaradhvajaḥ* — Makaradhvaja; *su-madhuraḥ* — most sweet; *śuddhaḥ* — pure; *śubhānandakaḥ* — Shubhananda; *kāśīnāthaka* — Kashinatha; *vallabhau* — and Vallabha; *ca* — and; *haridāsa* — Haridasa; *ākhyaḥ* — named; *raghuḥ* — Raghu; *śuddha* — pure; *dhīḥ* — [whose] mind; *etān tān* — all these; *sahasā eva* — at once; *candana* — of sandal; *rasaiḥ* — with the juice; *liptvā* — having anointed; *saḥ* — He; *svayam* — Himself; *śrīmatā* — by the beautiful; *gaurāṅgena* — by Gauranga; *dṛḍham* — firmly; *nibadhya* — having tied; *vasanam* — the cloth; *śrīmat* — beautiful; *kaṭī* — of the waist; *rodhasi* — on the slope; *ājānu* — to the knees; *dvaya* — both; *lambi* — reaching; *pīvara* — stout; *bhuja* — of arms; *dvandvena* — [with] the pair; *manda* — gently; *ullasat* — thrilling; *romāñca* — with hairs standing on end; *añcita* — adorned; *vigraheṇa* — [with] a body; *parama* — wholly; *āviṣṭena* — absorbed; *taiḥ* — with them; *niryaye* — there was a setting out.

**106.** …Shrikanta, Makaradhvaja, the most sweet and pure Shubhananda, Kashinatha and Vallabha, the one named Haridasa, Raghu of pure mind — all these He Himself at once anointed with sandal juice. And then the beautiful Gauranga, having firmly tied His cloth on the slope of His beautiful waist — with His pair of stout arms reaching to both knees, His body adorned with gently thrilling hairs standing on end, wholly absorbed [in ecstasy] — set out with them.

*Note.* A verse of six padas; the metre is *śārdūla-vikrīḍita*. Note the passive *niryaye* (literally "there was a setting out [by Gauranga]"). The third pada has 20 syllables instead of 19 (?): without *sa* (*…liptvā svayaṁ śrīmatā*) it would be regular, and *sa* is awkward in any case beside the instrumental *gaurāṅgena* of the passive *niryaye*.

### Verse 107

अमन्दकरतालकप्रकररम्यसन्मन्दिरा-
स्वलङ्कृतकराम्बुजाः पुलकवृन्दसान्द्राङ्गकाः ।
अमी तदनु सत्वरं प्रतिपदं पदं निर्भरं
स्खलत्पदसरोरुहाः सुखसमुद्रमग्ना ययुः ॥१०७॥

*amanda-kara-tālaka-prakara-ramya-san-mandirā-*
*svalaṅkṛta-karāmbujāḥ pulaka-vṛnda-sāndrāṅgakāḥ |*
*amī tad-anu satvaraṁ pratipadaṁ padaṁ nirbharaṁ*
*skhalat-pada-saroruhāḥ sukha-samudra-magnā yayuḥ ||107||*

*Word for word:* *amanda* — loud; *kara-tālaka* — of karatalas; *prakara* — with a multitude; *ramya* — lovely; *sat* — fine; *mandirā* — with mandiras; *su-alaṅkṛta* — well adorned; *kara* — of hands; *ambujāḥ* — [whose] lotuses; *pulaka* — of thrills of rapture; *vṛnda* — with masses; *sāndra* — thickly [covered]; *aṅgakāḥ* — [whose] bodies; *amī* — they; *tat-anu* — after [Him]; *satvaram* — quickly; *pratipadam* — at every step; *padam* — step; *nirbharam* — helplessly; *skhalat* — stumbling; *pada* — of feet; *saroruhāḥ* — [whose] lotuses; *sukha* — of happiness; *samudra* — in the ocean; *magnāḥ* — sunk; *yayuḥ* — went.

**107.** Their lotus hands well adorned with a multitude of loud karatalas and fine, lovely mandiras, their bodies thickly covered with the thrills of rapture, they went quickly after [Him]; at every step their lotus feet stumbled helplessly, and they were sunk in an ocean of happiness.

*Note.* The metre is *pṛthvī*. Karatalas and mandiras are hand cymbals.

### Verse 108

गोविन्दस्त्वरितं समेत्य नितरां नैकट्यमासादितः
पार्श्वस्थः सुखसागरेषु सततं मज्जन् प्रतस्थे ततः ।
एते ये च समागताः प्रतिपदोल्लासाकुलाः श्रीयुजो
नैषां हर्षसुधाम्बुधिर्निरवधिर्ब्रह्माण्डमध्येऽञ्चितुम् ॥१०८॥

*govindas tvaritaṁ sametya nitarāṁ naikaṭyam āsāditaḥ*
*pārśvasthaḥ sukha-sāgareṣu satataṁ majjan pratasthe tataḥ |*
*ete ye ca samāgatāḥ pratipadollāsākulāḥ śrīyujo*
*naiṣāṁ harṣa-sudhāmbudhir niravadhir brahmāṇḍa-madhye 'ñcitum ||108||*

*Word for word:* *govindaḥ* — Govinda; *tvaritam* — quickly; *sametya* — having come up; *nitarām* — very; *naikaṭyam* — nearness; *āsāditaḥ* — having attained; *pārśva-sthaḥ* — standing at [His] side; *sukha* — of happiness; *sāgareṣu* — in the oceans; *satatam* — constantly; *majjan* — immersed; *pratasthe* — set out; *tataḥ* — then; *ete ye* — those who; *ca* — and; *samāgatāḥ* — had come; *pratipada* — at every step; *ullāsa* — by exultation; *ākulāḥ* — agitated; *śrī-yujaḥ* — splendid; *na* — not; *eṣām* — their; *harṣa* — of joy; *sudhā* — of nectar; *ambudhiḥ* — the ocean; *niravadhiḥ* — boundless; *brahmāṇḍa* — of the universe; *madhye* — within; *añcitum* (?) — to be contained (?).

**108.** Govinda quickly came up and, having drawn very near, standing at [His] side and constantly immersed in oceans of happiness, then set out [with the Lord]. And as for those splendid ones who had come, agitated by exultation at every step — the boundless ocean of the nectar of their joy [could] not be contained within the universe.

*Note.* The metre is *śārdūla-vikrīḍita*. Govinda is the Lord's servant. The ending (*'ñcitum*) is read tentatively. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 109

अथ मदमृगेन्द्रालीलीलाविलासिपदक्रमः
प्रमदविगलद्घर्मस्नानप्रचायकपदक्रमः ।
अनुपमसुखारोहाद्रोमोद्गमाञ्चितविग्रहः
पथि लघु ययौ गौरस्तेजोनिरस्तरविग्रहः ॥१०९॥

*atha mada-mṛgendrālī-līlā-vilāsi-pada-kramaḥ*
*pramada-vigalad-gharma-snāna-pracāyaka-pada-kramaḥ |*
*anupama-sukhārohād romodgamāñcita-vigrahaḥ*
*pathi laghu yayau gauras tejo-nirasta-ravi-grahaḥ ||109||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *mada* — maddened; *mṛga-indra* — of lions; *ālī* — of a troop; *līlā* — playful; *vilāsi* — graceful; *pada* — of steps; *kramaḥ* — [whose] gait; *pramada* — from joy; *vigalat* — streaming; *gharma* — of sweat; *snāna* — a bath; *pracāyaka* — scattering; *pada-kramaḥ* — [whose] gait; *anupama* — of incomparable; *sukha* — happiness; *ārohāt* — from the surge; *roma-udgama* — with hairs standing on end; *añcita* — adorned; *vigrahaḥ* — [whose] body; *pathi* — along the road; *laghu* — swiftly; *yayau* — went; *gauraḥ* — Gaura; *tejaḥ* — by [His] effulgence; *nirasta* — outshone; *ravi* — of the sun; *grahaḥ* — [by whom] the orb.

**109.** Then Gaura — His gait playful and graceful [like that] of a troop of maddened lions, His steps scattering a bath of sweat that streamed from joy, His body adorned with hairs standing on end from the surge of incomparable happiness — went swiftly along the road, outshining with His effulgence the orb of the sun.

*Note.* The metre is *hariṇī*, with rhyme at the ends of the padas (*pāda-anta-yamaka*: *pada-kramaḥ / pada-kramaḥ; vigrahaḥ / ravi-grahaḥ*). The second pada is read according to the Gosvami edition (GGM): *…pracāyaka-pada-kramaḥ* (our edition has *-mada-kramaḥ*). In either reading the second pada has 18 syllables instead of 17 (?): at its end *-yaka-pada-kramaḥ* gives ⏑⏑⏑—⏑— where the metre requires ⏑⏑—⏑—, i.e. one light syllable is superfluous.

### Verse 110

रथमभि बलदेवस्याग्रतो गौरचन्द्रः
प्रमदमदमनोज्ञः श्रीविराजत्तनूकः ।
द्रुतकनकमहीध्रो दण्डवद्भूमिपृष्ठं
सह नयनजलेन प्रेमतः प्राप भूयः ॥११०॥

*ratham abhi baladevasyāgrato gauracandraḥ*
*pramada-mada-manojñaḥ śrī-virājat-tanūkaḥ |*
*druta-kanaka-mahīdhro daṇḍavad bhūmi-pṛṣṭhaṁ*
*saha nayana-jalena premataḥ prāpa bhūyaḥ ||110||*

*Word for word:* *ratham abhi* — toward the chariot; *baladevasya* — of Baladeva; *agrataḥ* — in front; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra; *pramada* — of joy; *mada* — by the intoxication; *manojñaḥ* — charming; *śrī* — with beauty; *virājat* — shining; *tanūkaḥ* — [whose] body; *druta* — molten; *kanaka* — of gold; *mahīdhraḥ* — a mountain; *daṇḍa-vat* — like a rod; *bhūmi* — of the earth; *pṛṣṭham* — the surface; *saha* — together; *nayana* — of the eyes; *jalena* — with the water; *premataḥ* — out of love; *prāpa* — reached; *bhūyaḥ* — again.

**110.** In front of the chariot of Baladeva, Gaurachandra — charming in the intoxication of joy, His body shining with beauty, [like] a mountain of molten gold — out of love again fell to the surface of the earth like a rod, together with [a flood of] tears.

*Note.* The metre is *mālinī*.

**Colophon:** इति श्रीकृष्णचैतन्यचरितामृते महाकाव्ये पञ्चदशः सर्गः । (*iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahākāvye pañcadaśaḥ sargaḥ*) — "Thus [ends] the fifteenth sarga in the mahakavya 'Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita'." (The colophon gives no title for the sarga.)

---

## Sarga Sixteen — verses 1–49

**Title of the sarga:** *Guṇḍicā-nṛtyādi-varṇana*, "The Description of the Dance [on the Way] to the Gundicha and Other [Events]" (from the colophon).
**Metre:**
- 1–3, 5 — *mālinī* (⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑———⏑——⏑——; 15 syllables per pada). In 5 the first pada is one syllable short.
- 4, 48 — *mandākrāntā* (————⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑——⏑——⏑——; 17 syllables per pada).
- 6–8, 33–36 — *vasanta-tilakā* (——⏑—⏑⏑⏑—⏑⏑—⏑——; 14 syllables per pada); 6–8 form a *viśeṣaka* (three verses, one sentence). In 34 the fourth pada has fifteen syllables (*mūrdhani*, where the metre requires *mūrdhni*).
- 9–11, 22–23, 26–27, 32, 49 — *śārdūla-vikrīḍita* (———⏑⏑—⏑—⏑⏑⏑———⏑——⏑—; 19 syllables per pada). In 9 the second pada has only seventeen syllables; in 10 the first pada has a light syllable (*saha*) in the sixteenth place.
- 12–16, 24, 28–30 — *sragdharā* (————⏑——⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑——⏑——⏑——; 21 syllables per pada). In 28 the printed first pada has nineteen syllables (restored from the Gosvami edition); in 30 the fourth pada has a light syllable (*pu-* of *-purī*) in the seventeenth place.
- 17–19, 31 — *pṛthvī* (⏑—⏑⏑⏑—⏑—⏑⏑⏑—⏑——⏑—; 17 syllables per pada).
- 20–21 — *hariṇī* (⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑—————⏑—⏑⏑—⏑—; 17 syllables per pada). In 20 the fourth pada has a light syllable (*-la* of *lola-*) in the eighth place.
- 25 — *praharṣiṇī* (———⏑⏑⏑⏑—⏑—⏑——; 13 syllables per pada).
- 37–47 — *bhujaṅga-prayāta* (⏑——⏑——⏑——⏑——; 12 syllables per pada); 37–46 form a *kulaka*.

**Total verses:** 49.

**Contents of the passage:** the Ratha-yatra — the Lord's dancing before the chariot of Jagannatha on the way to the Gundicha.
- 1–5 — raising His arm, the Lord recites three verses: Mukunda-mala 2, Srimad-Bhagavatam 10.90.48 and Padyavali 63 (*nāhaṁ vipro…*); cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 13.
- 6–8 — a portrait of Gaura dancing (a *viśeṣaka*).
- 9–16 — the chariot: its height; "a new king of mountains"; the festival of the people of Puri; the earth beneath the wheels; the rivalry of the chariots; the dust up to the heavens; the sufferings of Kurma and Shesha; "but the dancing Gauranga has captured the hearts of all".
- 17–23 — the dance: the sound of the kirtana pierces the shell of the universe; whirling like a wheel, the tears form a ring like a halo; foam at the mouth; tears like a breaking string of pearls.
- 24 — three circles: the singers; the devotees headed by Kashi Mishra, holding one another's hands; Prataparudra outside.
- 25–29 — no one blinks; the Lord in a swoon, the chariot stands still; the devotees carry Him aside; He leans on Advaita; Prataparudra serves His feet (28).
- 30–33 — Paramananda Puri; a play on the name of Svarupa Damodara (31); Damodara embraces the Lord's feet; Kashishvara, Kashi Mishra, Govinda.
- 34–36 — the Lord places His foot on the heads of the devotees, presses His own foot to His heart and "tastes" it.
- 37–47 — the *kulaka* (37–46): an extended portrait of the Lord dancing; Jagannatha cannot blink.
- 48–49 — the miracle of the garland; immersion in the ocean of bliss.

### Verse 1

अथ पुलकसमूहभ्राजमानं प्ररोह-
न्मुकुलकुलविराजत्काञ्चनद्रुप्रकाशम् ।
मधुरमपठदुच्चैः पीनमुन्नीय बाहुं
कनकगिरिरिवासौ शृङ्गलग्नान्तरीक्षः ॥१॥

*atha pulaka-samūha-bhrājamānaṁ prarohan-*
*mukula-kula-virājat-kāñcana-dru-prakāśam |*
*madhuram apaṭhad uccaiḥ pīnam unnīya bāhuṁ*
*kanaka-girir ivāsau śṛṅga-lagnāntarīkṣaḥ ||1||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *pulaka* — of hairs standing on end; *samūha* — with the mass; *bhrājamānam* — shining; *prarohat* — of opening; *mukula* — of buds; *kula* — with clusters; *virājat* — resplendent; *kāñcana* — a golden; *dru* — tree; *prakāśam* — resembling; *madhuram* — sweetly; *apaṭhat* — recited; *uccaiḥ* — loudly; *pīnam* — mighty; *unnīya* — having raised; *bāhum* — [His] arm; *kanaka* — golden; *giriḥ* — a mountain; *iva* — like; *asau* — He; *śṛṅga* — to [whose] peak; *lagna* — clinging; *antarīkṣaḥ* — [with] the sky.

**1.** Then, raising His mighty arm — which shone with a mass of hairs standing on end and resembled a golden tree resplendent with clusters of opening buds — He, like a golden mountain with the sky clinging to its peak, loudly and sweetly recited [these verses]:

*Note.* Metre — *mālinī*; verses 1–5 are in *mālinī*, except 4 (*mandākrāntā*). Before the chariot the Lord now recites three verses; cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 13.78–80, where the same verses are cited before His dance at the chariot (2 — from the Mukunda-mala, 3 — Srimad-Bhagavatam 10.90.48, 4 — Padyavali 63).

### Verse 2

जयति जयति देवो देवकीनन्दनोऽसौ
जयति जयति कृष्णो वृष्णिवंशप्रदीपः ।
जयति जयति मेघश्यामलः कोमलाङ्गो
जयति जयति पृथ्वीभारनाशो मुकुन्दः ॥२॥

*jayati jayati devo devakī-nandano 'sau*
*jayati jayati kṛṣṇo vṛṣṇi-vaṁśa-pradīpaḥ |*
*jayati jayati megha-śyāmalaḥ komalāṅgo*
*jayati jayati pṛthvī-bhāra-nāśo mukundaḥ ||2||*

*Word for word:* *jayati jayati* — glory, glory [to]; *devaḥ* — God; *devakī* — of Devaki; *nandanaḥ* — the son; *asau* — this; *kṛṣṇaḥ* — Krishna; *vṛṣṇi* — of the Vrishnis; *vaṁśa* — of the dynasty; *pradīpaḥ* — the lamp; *megha* — like a cloud; *śyāmalaḥ* — dark; *komala* — tender; *aṅgaḥ* — [whose] body [is]; *pṛthvī* — of the earth; *bhāra* — of the burden; *nāśaḥ* — the remover; *mukundaḥ* — Mukunda.

**2.** Glory, glory to this God, the son of Devaki! Glory, glory to Krishna, the lamp of the Vrishni dynasty! Glory, glory to Him who is dark as a cloud, whose body is tender! Glory, glory to Mukunda, the remover of the burden of the earth!

*Note.* A verse of Kulashekhara from the Mukunda-mala (v. 2); there the reading is *jayatu jayatu* ("may He be glorious"), here *jayati* ("He is glorious").

### Verse 3

जयति जननिवासो देवकीजन्मवादो
यदुवरपरिषत् स्वैर्दोर्भिरस्यन्नधर्मम् ।
स्थिरचरवृजिनघ्नः सुस्मितश्रीमुखेन
व्रजपुरवनितानां वर्द्धयन् कामदेवम् ॥३॥

*jayati jana-nivāso devakī-janma-vādo*
*yadu-vara-pariṣat svair dorbhir asyann adharmam |*
*sthira-cara-vṛjina-ghnaḥ susmita-śrī-mukhena*
*vraja-pura-vanitānāṁ vardhayan kāma-devam ||3||*

*Word for word:* *jayati* — glorious is; *jana* — of [all] beings; *nivāsaḥ* — the abode; *devakī* — from Devaki; *janma* — about [whose] birth; *vādaḥ* — [there is only] a manner of speaking; *yadu* — of the Yadus; *vara* — the best; *pariṣat* — [whose] retinue [are]; *svaiḥ* — with His own; *dorbhiḥ* — arms; *asyan* — casting away; *adharmam* — irreligion; *sthira* — of the unmoving; *cara* — [and] the moving; *vṛjina* — of the sin; *ghnaḥ* — the destroyer; *su-smita* — beautifully smiling; *śrī* — with the beautiful; *mukhena* — face; *vraja* — of Vraja; *pura* — and of the city (Mathura); *vanitānām* — of the women; *vardhayan* — increasing; *kāma-devam* — the god of love.

**3.** Glorious is He, the abode of all beings, whose birth from Devaki is only a manner of speaking; whose retinue are the best of the Yadus; who with His own arms casts away irreligion; the destroyer of the sin of all that moves and does not move; who with His beautiful smiling face increases the god of love in the women of Vraja and of the city!

*Note.* Srimad-Bhagavatam 10.90.48; the text is identical. *Yadu-vara-pariṣat* — "whose retinue are the best of the Yadus", or "surrounded by the best of the Yadus". We take *vraja-pura-vanitā* as "the women of Vraja and of Mathura and Dvaraka", following the widespread interpretation. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 4

नाहं विप्रो न च नरपतिर्नापि वैश्यो न शूद्रो
नाहं वर्णी न च गृहपतिर्नो वनस्थो यतिर्वा ।
किन्तु प्रोद्यन्निखिलपरमानन्दपूर्णामृताब्धे-
र्गोपीभर्तुः पदकमलयोर्दासदासानुदासः ॥४॥

*nāhaṁ vipro na ca nara-patir nāpi vaiśyo na śūdro*
*nāhaṁ varṇī na ca gṛha-patir no vana-stho yatir vā |*
*kintu prodyan-nikhila-paramānanda-pūrṇāmṛtābdher*
*gopī-bhartuḥ pada-kamalayor dāsa-dāsānudāsaḥ ||4||*

*Word for word:* *na aham* — I [am] not; *vipraḥ* — a brahmana; *na ca* — nor; *nara-patiḥ* — a king (a kshatriya); *na api* — nor; *vaiśyaḥ* — a vaishya; *na śūdraḥ* — nor a shudra; *varṇī* — a brahmachari; *gṛha-patiḥ* — a householder; *no* — not; *vana-sthaḥ* — a forest-dweller (a vanaprastha); *yatiḥ* — an ascetic (a sannyasi); *vā* — or; *kintu* — but; *prodyat* — surging; *nikhila* — of complete; *parama* — supreme; *ānanda* — bliss; *pūrṇa* — full; *amṛta* — of nectar; *abdheḥ* — of the ocean; *gopī* — of the gopis; *bhartuḥ* — of the Lord; *pada* — of the feet; *kamalayoḥ* — of the lotuses; *dāsa* — of the servant; *dāsa* — of the servant; *anudāsaḥ* — the servant.

**4.** I am not a brahmana, nor a king, nor a vaishya, nor a shudra; I am not a brahmachari, nor a householder, nor a forest-dweller, nor an ascetic. But I am the servant of the servant of the servant of the lotus feet of the Lord of the gopis, the ocean of nectar full of surging, complete, supreme bliss.

*Note.* Metre — *mandākrāntā*. Padyavali 63, where it is ascribed to Sri Chaitanya Himself; in the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 13.80, the Lord recites this verse at the chariot.

### Verse 5

इति नटनकलादौ श्रीवृन्दावनेन्दोः
परममहिमवत्त्वं निर्भरार्त्तो निरूप्य ।
अतिशयकरुणार्द्रः प्रेमभक्तिं वितन्व-
न्नयमतिमधुराङ्गो हर्षपूर्णो बभूव ॥५॥

*iti naṭana-kalādau śrī-vṛndāvanendoḥ*
*parama-mahimavattvaṁ nirbharārtto nirūpya |*
*atiśaya-karuṇārdraḥ prema-bhaktiṁ vitanvann*
*ayam ati-madhurāṅgo harṣa-pūrṇo babhūva ||5||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *naṭana* — of the dance; *kalā* — of the art; *ādau* — at the beginning; *śrī-vṛndāvana* — of Sri Vrindavana; *indoḥ* — of the moon; *parama* — the supreme; *mahimavattvam* — greatness; *nirbhara* — deeply; *ārttaḥ* — stirred; *nirūpya* — having set forth; *atiśaya* — by boundless; *karuṇā* — compassion; *ārdraḥ* — softened; *prema* — loving; *bhaktim* — devotion; *vitanvan* — spreading; *ayam* — He; *ati* — exceedingly; *madhura* — charming; *aṅgaḥ* — [whose] body [is]; *harṣa* — with joy; *pūrṇaḥ* — filled; *babhūva* — became.

**5.** Thus at the beginning of His artful dance, having set forth, deeply stirred, the supreme greatness of the Moon of Sri Vrindavana, He — whose body is exceedingly charming — softened by boundless compassion and spreading loving devotion, became filled with joy.

*Note.* The first pada has fourteen syllables instead of fifteen: after *śrī-* (the ninth syllable) a light syllable is missing, so that the heavy *vṛn-* falls in the tenth place, which requires a light one (?). The Sanskrit is given as printed.

### Verse 6–8

आस्फोट्य वामकरकक्षतटीं करेण
रज्यद्वपुर्मधुरकोमलतातिरम्यः ।
लीलाविलोलमुखचन्द्रमयूखरोचिः-
श्रीमच्छटाझलमलायितदिक्समूहः ॥६॥

उच्चैर्मुहुर्जयजयेति विमुक्तकण्ठ-
मुच्चारयन् सह तनूरुहवृन्दहर्षैः ।
मुष्टिप्रमेयतनुमध्यविलासबद्ध-
रक्ताम्बरद्युतिविडम्बितबन्धुजीवः ॥७॥

श्रीमद्विलोचनजलाप्लुतगौरदेहः
प्रत्यग्रघर्मकणिकाखचितास्यचन्द्रः ।
उद्दामताण्डवकलाकुलिताङ्गभङ्गः
श्रीमानथ स्वजनमध्यमलंचकार ॥८॥
(विशेषकम्)

*āsphoṭya vāma-kara-kakṣa-taṭīṁ kareṇa*
*rajyad-vapur madhura-komalatāti-ramyaḥ |*
*līlā-vilola-mukha-candra-mayūkha-rociḥ-*
*śrīmac-chaṭā-jhalamalāyita-dik-samūhaḥ ||6||*

*uccair muhur jaya-jayeti vimukta-kaṇṭham*
*uccārayan saha tanūruha-vṛnda-harṣaiḥ |*
*muṣṭi-prameya-tanu-madhya-vilāsa-baddha-*
*raktāmbara-dyuti-viḍambita-bandhujīvaḥ ||7||*

*śrīmad-vilocana-jalāpluta-gaura-dehaḥ*
*pratyagra-gharma-kaṇikā-khacitāsya-candraḥ |*
*uddāma-tāṇḍava-kalākulitāṅga-bhaṅgaḥ*
*śrīmān atha svajana-madhyam alaṁcakāra ||8||*
*(viśeṣakam)*

*Word for word:* *āsphoṭya* — having slapped; *vāma* — of the left; *kara* — arm; *kakṣa* — of the armpit; *taṭīm* — the side; *kareṇa* — with [His] hand; *rajyat* — reddening; *vapuḥ* — [whose] body [is]; *madhura* — by sweetness; *komalatā* — [and] tenderness; *ati-ramyaḥ* — most lovely; *līlā* — in play; *vilola* — moving; *mukha* — of the face; *candra* — of the moon; *mayūkha* — of the rays; *rociḥ* — of the radiance; *śrīmat* — with the beautiful; *chaṭā* — streams; *jhalamalāyita* — made to glitter; *dik* — of the directions; *samūhaḥ* — [by whom] the whole host.

*Word for word:* *uccaiḥ* — loudly; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *jaya-jaya* — "Glory, glory!"; *iti* — thus; *vimukta* — released (i.e. at the top of His voice); *kaṇṭham* — [with] throat; *uccārayan* — crying out; *saha* — together with; *tanūruha* — of hairs; *vṛnda* — of the multitude; *harṣaiḥ* — with the bristling; *muṣṭi* — by a fist; *prameya* — measurable; *tanu* — slender; *madhya* — on the waist; *vilāsa* — gracefully; *baddha* — tied; *rakta* — of the crimson; *ambara* — of the cloth; *dyuti* — by the lustre; *viḍambita* — [by whom] mocked; *bandhujīvaḥ* — the bandhujiva flower.

*Word for word:* *śrīmat* — of the beautiful; *vilocana* — of the eyes; *jala* — with the water; *āpluta* — bathed; *gaura* — golden; *dehaḥ* — [whose] body [is]; *pratyagra* — with fresh; *gharma* — of perspiration; *kaṇikā* — with drops; *khacita* — studded; *āsya* — of the face; *candraḥ* — [whose] moon [is]; *uddāma* — of the unrestrained; *tāṇḍava* — of the tandava; *kalā* — by the art; *ākulita* — agitated; *aṅga-bhaṅgaḥ* — [whose] bendings of the body [are]; *śrīmān* — the beautiful one; *atha* — then; *svajana* — of His own people; *madhyam* — the midst; *alaṁcakāra* — adorned.

**6–8.** Slapping the side of His left armpit with His hand; His body reddening; most lovely in His sweetness and tenderness; making the whole host of the directions glitter with the beautiful streams of radiance from the rays of the moon of His face, moving in play; again and again loudly crying out "Glory, glory!" at the top of His voice, together with the bristling of the multitude of hairs on His body; mocking the bandhujiva flower with the lustre of the crimson cloth gracefully tied about His slender waist, which a fist could measure; His golden body bathed in the water of His beautiful eyes; the moon of His face studded with fresh drops of perspiration; the bendings of His body agitated by the art of the unrestrained tandava — the beautiful [Gaura] then adorned the midst of His own people.

*Note.* Metre — *vasanta-tilakā*; the three verses form a *viśeṣaka* (so marked in the edition). Slapping the armpit (*āsphoṭana*) is a wrestler's gesture, a challenge before a bout; here it is a sign of exultation before the dance. *Jhalamalāyita* is a denominative from the onomatopoeic *jhalamala*, "glitter, twinkling". The *bandhujīva* is a crimson flower (*Pentapetes phoenicea*).

### Verse 9

औत्तुङ्ग्येन नभस्थलं तरलयन्मार्त्तण्डबिम्बं मुहु-
श्चुम्बन् देवसभाजनविधिं संपादयन्निर्भरम् ।
ब्रह्माण्डान्तरसंस्थितस्य नयनानन्दोत्सवोत्साहकः
साटोपं मुरवैरिणो विजयते लक्ष्मीमयः स्यन्दनः ॥९॥

*auttuṅgyena nabhas-thalaṁ taralayan mārttaṇḍa-bimbaṁ muhuś*
*cumban deva-sabhājana-vidhiṁ saṁpādayan nirbharam |*
*brahmāṇḍāntara-saṁsthitasya nayanānandotsavotsāhakaḥ*
*sāṭopaṁ mura-vairiṇo vijayate lakṣmī-mayaḥ syandanaḥ ||9||*

*Word for word:* *auttuṅgyena* — by [its] loftiness; *nabhaḥ-sthalam* — the expanse of the sky; *taralayan* — making tremble; *mārttaṇḍa* — of the sun; *bimbam* — the disc; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *cumban* — kissing; *deva* — of the gods; *sabhājana* — of honouring; *vidhim* — the rite; *saṁpādayan* — performing; *nirbharam* — fully; *brahmāṇḍa* — the universe; *antara* — within; *saṁsthitasya* — of [all that] abides; *nayana* — for the eyes; *ānanda* — of joy; *utsava* — of the festival; *utsāhakaḥ* — the inspirer; *sāṭopam* — majestically; *mura-vairiṇaḥ* — of the Enemy of Mura; *vijayate* — triumphs; *lakṣmī* — splendour; *mayaḥ* — full of; *syandanaḥ* — the chariot.

**9.** Majestically triumphs the chariot of the Enemy of Mura, full of splendour: by its loftiness it makes the expanse of the sky tremble; again and again it kisses the disc of the sun; it fully performs the rite of honouring the gods; and it inspires a festival of joy for the eyes of all that abides within the universe.

*Note.* Metre — *śārdūla-vikrīḍita*; verses 9–11 are in *śārdūla*. The edition prints औत्तुङ्गेन (*auttuṅgena*, which is not a word); we read *auttuṅgyena*, "by its loftiness" (the metre is the same). *Deva-sabhājana* may also be understood through *deva-sabhā*, "the assembly of the gods": "it brings full joy to the assembly of the gods". The second pada has only seventeen syllables instead of nineteen and does not scan from the ninth syllable on (*-na* of *-sabhājana-* stands where a heavy syllable is required): some two syllables seem to have dropped out (?).

### Verse 10

कैलासं नमयन्नशेषविधिना मेरुं सहनिर्भरं
सोत्कण्ठं किल विन्ध्यकं विकलयन् गौरीगुरुं ग्लापयन् ।
अन्यः कोऽप्यधुनावनौ शिखरिणां राजेव किं निर्मितो
धात्रा स्यन्दन इत्यसौ मुररिपुश्रीमूर्त्तिपीयूषभृत् ॥१०॥

*kailāsaṁ namayann aśeṣa-vidhinā meruṁ saha-nirbharaṁ*
*sotkaṇṭhaṁ kila vindhyakaṁ vikalayan gaurī-guruṁ glāpayan |*
*anyaḥ ko 'py adhunāvanau śikhariṇāṁ rājeva kiṁ nirmito*
*dhātrā syandana ity asau mura-ripu-śrī-mūrtti-pīyūṣa-bhṛt ||10||*

*Word for word:* *kailāsam* — Kailasa; *namayan* — bowing down; *aśeṣa* — in every; *vidhinā* — way; *merum* — Meru; *saha* — together with; *nirbharam* — [its] excess [of pride] (?); *sa-utkaṇṭham* — with longing; *kila* — indeed; *vindhyakam* — the paltry Vindhya; *vikalayan* — distressing; *gaurī* — of Gauri; *gurum* — the father (the Himalaya); *glāpayan* — dejecting; *anyaḥ* — another; *kaḥ api* — some; *adhunā* — now; *avanau* — on the earth; *śikhariṇām* — of mountains; *rājā iva* — a king, as it were; *kim* — whether; *nirmitaḥ* — has been made; *dhātrā* — by the Creator; *syandanaḥ* — the chariot; *iti* — thus; *asau* — this; *mura-ripu* — of the Enemy of Mura; *śrī* — of the beautiful; *mūrtti* — form; *pīyūṣa* — the nectar; *bhṛt* — bearing.

**10.** Bowing Kailasa down in every way, [humbling] Meru together with all its pride, indeed throwing the paltry Vindhya into longing distress and dejecting the father of Gauri — "Has the Creator now made on earth some other king, as it were, of the mountains?" — [so people thought of] this chariot, which bore the nectar of the beautiful form of the Enemy of Mura.

*Note.* The edition prints राजेक (*rājeka*), which makes no sense; we read *rājeva* (= *rājā iva*), as does the Gosvami edition (GGM). *Meruṁ saha-nirbharaṁ* is obscure, and the sense given is conjectural; moreover, *saha* puts a light syllable in the sixteenth place, where the *śārdūla-vikrīḍita* requires a heavy one. The variant *meruṁ hasan nirbharaṁ*, "laughing heartily at Meru", scans correctly and gives a clear sense (?). The diminutive *vindhyaka* is contemptuous ("some Vindhya or other"). The father of Gauri (Parvati) is Himavan, the Himalaya.

### Verse 11

उत्पक्ष्माक्षिसरोरुहाञ्जलिपुटैर्नीलाद्रिचूडामणेः
श्रीमूर्त्तिच्छुरितामृतानि पिबतामुल्लासधन्यात्मनाम् ।
निष्पन्दं पुलकावलीविलसतामानन्दमन्दाकिनी-
कल्लोलैः किल तत्र तत्र भवतामासीन्महानुत्सवः ॥११॥

*utpakṣmākṣi-saroruhāñjali-puṭair nīlādri-cūḍāmaṇeḥ*
*śrī-mūrtti-cchuritāmṛtāni pibatām ullāsa-dhanyātmanām |*
*niṣpandaṁ pulakāvalī-vilasatām ānanda-mandākinī-*
*kallolaiḥ kila tatra tatra bhavatām āsīn mahān utsavaḥ ||11||*

*Word for word:* *utpakṣma* — with lashes raised; *akṣi* — of the eyes; *saroruha* — of the lotuses; *añjali-puṭaiḥ* — with the cupped hands; *nīla-adri* — of the Blue Mountain; *cūḍā-maṇeḥ* — of the crest-jewel; *śrī* — from the beautiful; *mūrtti* — form; *churita* — radiating; *amṛtāni* — the nectars; *pibatām* — of [those] drinking; *ullāsa* — by exultation; *dhanya* — blessed; *ātmanām* — [whose] souls [were]; *niṣpandam* — motionless; *pulaka* — of hairs standing on end; *āvalī* — with rows; *vilasatām* — of [those] shining; *ānanda* — of bliss; *mandākinī* — of the Mandakini; *kallolaiḥ* — with the waves; *kila* — indeed; *tatra tatra* — everywhere there; *bhavatām* — among the worthy [people]; *āsīt* — there was; *mahān* — a great; *utsavaḥ* — festival.

**11.** Among the worthy [people of Puri] — whose souls were blessed by exultation, who with the cupped hands of their lotus eyes, their lashes raised, drank the nectars radiating from the beautiful form of the Crest-Jewel of the Blue Mountain, and who shone motionless with rows of hairs standing on end — there was indeed everywhere a great festival, with waves of the Mandakini of bliss.

*Note.* The Mandakini is the heavenly Ganga. *Utpakṣma*, "with lashes raised", i.e. without blinking.

### Verse 12

भूयो भूयः समन्तात् सरभसमनसामागतानां विशेषं
तत्तत्सीमन्तिनीनामलिकविकलितैः कम्रसिन्दूरपूरैः ।
सैन्दूरीकर्त्तुमासीद्रथपरिसरभूश्चक्रनिष्पीडनेन
क्षुब्धापि प्रायशः सा प्रमुदितमनसात्मानमुत्कण्ठितेव ॥१२॥

*bhūyo bhūyaḥ samantāt sarabhasa-manasām āgatānāṁ viśeṣaṁ*
*tat-tat-sīmantinīnām alika-vikalitaiḥ kamra-sindūra-pūraiḥ |*
*saindūrī-karttum āsīd ratha-parisara-bhūś cakra-niṣpīḍanena*
*kṣubdhāpi prāyaśaḥ sā pramudita-manasātmānam utkaṇṭhiteva ||12||*

*Word for word:* *bhūyaḥ bhūyaḥ* — again and again; *samantāt* — from all sides; *sa-rabhasa* — eager; *manasām* — [with] hearts; *āgatānām* — of [those] who had come; *viśeṣam* — especially; *tat-tat* — of these and those; *sīmantinīnām* — of the women; *alika* — from the foreheads; *vikalitaiḥ* — fallen; *kamra* — of lovely; *sindūra* — vermilion; *pūraiḥ* — with the streams; *saindūrī-karttum* — to colour with vermilion; *āsīt* — was; *ratha* — of the chariot; *parisara* — surrounding; *bhūḥ* — the ground; *cakra* — of the wheels; *niṣpīḍanena* — by the pressure; *kṣubdhā* — tormented; *api* — although; *prāyaśaḥ* — almost [all]; *sā* — it; *pramudita* — with a gladdened; *manasā* — heart; *ātmānam* — itself; *utkaṇṭhitā* — longing; *iva* — as if.

**12.** The ground around the chariot, though almost all of it was tormented by the pressure of the wheels, with a gladdened heart seemed to long to colour itself with vermilion — with the lovely streams of sindura fallen especially from the foreheads of the many women who came again and again from all sides with eager hearts.

*Note.* Metre — *sragdharā*; verses 12–16 are in *sragdharā*. The edition has *saindūrī-* (the *vṛddhi* derivative of *sindūra*), which is admissible. Sindura on the forehead (in the parting of the hair) is the mark of a married woman.

### Verse 13

नृत्यन्तं गौरचन्द्रं चरणसरसिजद्वन्द्वविन्यासरम्यं
दृष्ट्वा दृष्ट्वा प्रकामं सरभसमनसो भ्रातरस्ते रथस्थाः ।
भूयोऽहंपूर्विकाभिः प्रसृमरगतयः कौतुकेनाग्रतोऽमी
जङ्घालास्तत्र तत्र प्रमदमदभरान्नर्त्तनं कुर्वतेव ॥१३॥

*nṛtyantaṁ gauracandraṁ caraṇa-sarasija-dvandva-vinyāsa-ramyaṁ*
*dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭvā prakāmaṁ sarabhasa-manaso bhrātaras te ratha-sthāḥ |*
*bhūyo 'haṁ-pūrvikābhiḥ prasṛmara-gatayaḥ kautukenāgrato 'mī*
*jaṅghālās tatra tatra pramada-mada-bharān narttanaṁ kurvateva ||13||*

*Word for word:* *nṛtyantam* — dancing; *gauracandram* — Gaurachandra; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *sarasija* — of the lotuses; *dvandva* — of the pair; *vinyāsa* — by the placing; *ramyam* — charming; *dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭvā* — looking and looking; *prakāmam* — to their hearts' content; *sa-rabhasa* — eager; *manasaḥ* — [with] hearts; *bhrātaraḥ* — the brothers; *te* — those; *ratha-sthāḥ* — standing on the chariots; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *ahaṁ-pūrvikābhiḥ* — with rivalry ("I first!"); *prasṛmara* — swift; *gatayaḥ* — [whose] going [was]; *kautukena* — with eagerness; *agrataḥ* — forward; *amī* — these; *jaṅghālāḥ* — swift-footed ones; *tatra tatra* — here and there; *pramada* — of joy; *mada* — of the intoxication; *bharāt* — from the excess; *narttanam* — a dance; *kurvata* — performed; *iva* — as if.

**13.** Looking and looking to their hearts' content at Gaurachandra as He danced, charming in the placing of His pair of lotus feet, those brothers standing on the chariots grew eager at heart; and again, vying with one another — "I first!" — moving swiftly and eagerly forward, these swift-footed ones here and there, as it were, danced from the excess of their joyful intoxication.

*Note.* The "brothers" are Jagannatha, Balarama and Subhadra (the brothers and their sister). Grammatically the subject of the whole verse is one — *bhrātaraḥ … amī jaṅghālāḥ* — that is, the chariots themselves, overtaking one another (?); the second half may also be referred to the people running before the chariots, vying to go first. *Kurvata* is an epic form without the augment (= *akurvata*). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 14

आरुन्धन् दिक्करीन्द्रोत्करकरविवरं साम्बु चक्षुःसहस्रं
कुर्वन्नैरावणेशं पलितविलसिता देवतास्तत्र कुर्वन् ।
सेतुभ्रान्तिं पयोधे पुनरपि रचयन्नेवमुज्जृम्भतेऽसौ
प्रोन्मीलच्चक्रचक्रोद्दलनविसृमरोद्धूतधूलीप्रवाहः ॥१४॥

*ārundhan dik-karīndrotkara-kara-vivaraṁ sāmbu cakṣuḥ-sahasraṁ*
*kurvann airāvaṇeśaṁ palita-vilasitā devatās tatra kurvan |*
*setu-bhrāntiṁ payodhe(ḥ) punar api racayann evam ujjṛmbhate 'sau*
*pronmīlac-cakra-cakroddalana-visṛmaroddhūta-dhūlī-pravāhaḥ ||14||*

*Word for word:* *ārundhan* — blocking; *dik* — of the directions; *karī-indra* — of the lordly elephants; *utkara* — of the host; *kara* — of the trunks; *vivaram* — the openings; *sa-ambu* — tearful (literally "with water"); *cakṣuḥ* — of eyes; *sahasram* — [whose] thousand [are]; *kurvan* — making; *airāvaṇa* — of Airavana; *īśam* — the lord (Indra); *palita* — with grey hair; *vilasitāḥ* — shining; *devatāḥ* — the gods; *tatra* — there; *kurvan* — making; *setu* — of a bridge; *bhrāntim* — the illusion; *payodheḥ* — over the ocean; *punaḥ api* — once again; *racayan* — creating; *evam* — thus; *ujjṛmbhate* — spreads; *asau* — this; *pronmīlat* — rolling (literally "opening"); *cakra* — of the wheels; *cakra* — by the circles; *uddalana* — from the crushing; *visṛmara* — spreading; *uddhūta* — raised; *dhūlī* — of dust; *pravāhaḥ* — the stream.

**14.** The stream of dust, raised and spreading from the crushing [of the ground] by the circles of the rolling wheels, spreads so that it blocks the openings of the trunks of the host of lordly elephants of the directions, makes the Lord of Airavana tearful in all His thousand eyes, makes the gods there shine with grey hair, and once again creates the illusion of a bridge over the ocean.

*Note.* The bridge over the ocean is the one built by Rama's army (the Setu). The edition has *payodhe* without the visarga; we read *payodheḥ*. Airavana (= Airavata) is Indra's elephant.

### Verse 15

कूर्मो मर्मव्यथोऽभूत् फणिपतिरसकौ शीर्षतः शीर्षमध्यं
भूयोभूयो धरित्रीं नयति नतशिरा जीर्णमण्डं बभूव ।
वेलालोलैः पयोभिश्चिरमिव जलधिः क्षीणमर्याद आसी-
त्तत्रौत्सुक्येन नीलक्षितिधरतिलके प्रस्थिते गुण्डिचायाम् ॥१५॥

*kūrmo marma-vyatho 'bhūt phaṇi-patir asakau śīrṣataḥ śīrṣa-madhyaṁ*
*bhūyo-bhūyo dharitrīṁ nayati nata-śirā jīrṇa-maṇḍaṁ babhūva |*
*velā-lolaiḥ payobhiś ciram iva jaladhiḥ kṣīṇa-maryāda āsīt*
*tatrautsukyena nīla-kṣitidhara-tilake prasthite guṇḍicāyām ||15||*

*Word for word:* *kūrmaḥ* — the Tortoise; *marma* — in [his] vital parts; *vyathaḥ* — [feeling] pain; *abhūt* — became; *phaṇi* — of the serpents; *patiḥ* — the lord; *asakau* — this; *śīrṣataḥ* — from head; *śīrṣa* — of head; *madhyam* — to the middle; *bhūyaḥ-bhūyaḥ* — again and again; *dharitrīm* — the earth; *nayati* — moves; *nata* — bowed; *śirāḥ* — [with] heads; *jīrṇa* — worn out; *maṇḍam* — ornament (?); *babhūva* — became; *velā* — at the shore; *lolaiḥ* — tossing; *payobhiḥ* — with waters; *ciram* — for long; *iva* — as if; *jaladhiḥ* — the ocean; *kṣīṇa* — lost; *maryādaḥ* — [whose] bounds [had]; *āsīt* — was; *tatra* — then; *autsukyena* — eagerly; *nīla* — of the Blue; *kṣitidhara* — Mountain; *tilake* — [when] the ornament; *prasthite* — had set out; *guṇḍicāyām* — for the Gundicha.

**15.** When the Ornament of the Blue Mountain eagerly set out for the Gundicha, the Tortoise felt pain in his vital parts; this lord of the serpents, his heads bowed, again and again moved the earth from head to head — [and each head] became worn; and the ocean, its waters tossing at the shore, seemed for a long time to have lost its bounds.

*Note.* The Tortoise (Kurma) and Shesha are the supports of the earth. *Jīrṇa-maṇḍam babhūva* is obscure (?): perhaps "[each head] became worn" (as if *jīrṇa-maṇḍala*), or "he grew exhausted". The metre confirms *-maṇḍaṁ*. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 16

राजन्तां तत्र तास्ताः सुरपतिपरिषत्कम्रलक्ष्मीरधोऽधः
कृत्वा कृत्वा मुरारेरथ रथविजये भूतयो रत्नभाजः ।
तत्तादृग्भूषणाढ्यः स्वयमपि भगवान् सम्यगुज्जृम्भतां सः
श्रीमान् किन्त्वेष नृत्यन्नखिलजनमनोरुद्धगौराङ्गचन्द्रः ॥१६॥

*rājantāṁ tatra tās tāḥ surapati-pariṣat-kamra-lakṣmīr adho 'dhaḥ*
*kṛtvā kṛtvā murārer atha ratha-vijaye bhūtayo ratna-bhājaḥ |*
*tat-tādṛg-bhūṣaṇāḍhyaḥ svayam api bhagavān samyag ujjṛmbhatāṁ saḥ*
*śrīmān kintv eṣa nṛtyann akhila-jana-mano-ruddha-gaurāṅga-candraḥ ||16||*

*Word for word:* *rājantām* — let shine; *tatra* — there; *tāḥ tāḥ* — all those; *surapati* — of the lord of the gods (Indra); *pariṣat* — of the assembly; *kamra* — the lovely; *lakṣmīḥ* — splendour; *adhaḥ adhaḥ kṛtvā kṛtvā* — again and again putting below (surpassing); *murāreḥ* — of Murari; *atha* — now; *ratha* — of the chariot; *vijaye* — at the triumphal setting out; *bhūtayaḥ* — riches; *ratna* — jewels; *bhājaḥ* — bearing; *tat* — those; *tādṛk* — such; *bhūṣaṇa* — in ornaments; *āḍhyaḥ* — rich; *svayam api* — Himself too; *bhagavān* — the Lord; *samyak* — fully; *ujjṛmbhatām* — let display [His] splendour; *saḥ* — He; *śrīmān* — beautiful; *kintu* — but; *eṣaḥ* — this; *nṛtyan* — dancing; *akhila* — of all; *jana* — the people; *manaḥ* — the hearts; *ruddha* — [who has] captured; *gaurāṅga* — Gauranga; *candraḥ* — the moon.

**16.** Let all the jewelled riches shine there at the triumphal setting out of Murari's chariot, again and again surpassing the lovely splendour of the assembly of the lord of the gods; let the beautiful Lord Himself, rich in such ornaments, display His splendour to the full — but it is this dancing Moon, Gauranga, who has captured the hearts of all the people!

*Note.* *Ratha-vijaya*, "the triumphal setting out", is the procession of the chariot.

### Verse 17

शचीसुतकलानिधिः किमपि साङ्गभङ्गं मुहु-
र्विलासचरणक्रमोन्मथितरम्यपङ्केरुहः ।
निरन्तरदिगन्तरच्छुरितमच्छकान्तिच्छटा-
मलज्झलमलायितं मनसि वः समुज्जृम्भताम् ॥१७॥

*śacī-suta-kalānidhiḥ (-nidheḥ?) kim api sāṅga-bhaṅgaṁ muhur*
*vilāsa-caraṇa-kramonmathita-ramya-paṅkeruhaḥ |*
*nirantara-digantara-cchuritam accha-kānti-cchaṭā-*
*malaj-jhalamalāyitaṁ manasi vaḥ samujjṛmbhatām ||17||*

*Word for word:* *śacī* — of Shachi; *suta* — of the son; *kalā-nidhiḥ* — the moon (literally "the treasury of digits"); *kim api* — indescribable; *sa-aṅga-bhaṅgam* — with bendings of the body; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *vilāsa* — playful; *caraṇa* — of the feet; *krama* — by the step; *unmathita* — [by whom] outdone; *ramya* — the lovely; *paṅkeruhaḥ* — lotuses; *nirantara* — unceasingly; *digantara* — through the directions; *churitam* — spreading; *accha* — of pure; *kānti* — radiance; *chaṭā* — of the streams; *malat* (?) — [obscure]; *jhalamalāyitam* — the glittering; *manasi* — in the heart; *vaḥ* — your; *samujjṛmbhatām* — may expand.

**17.** May that indescribable glittering of the streams of pure radiance of the Moon, the son of Shachi, which spreads unceasingly through the directions, expand in your hearts — [the glittering] of Him who, again and again bending His body, has outdone the lovely lotuses by the playful steps of His feet.

*Note.* Metre — *pṛthvī* (⏑—⏑⏑⏑—⏑—⏑⏑⏑—⏑——⏑—); verses 17–19 are in *pṛthvī*. The edition has the nominative *kalānidhiḥ*, but the sense requires the genitive *kalānidheḥ* (the metre is the same); *-paṅkeruhaḥ* is then genitive too. *-Malaj-* is obscure (?); the conjecture *-mālā-*, "a garland of streams of radiance", would fit the sense but not the metre, which requires a light syllable followed by a heavy one here. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 18

अमन्दतरमन्दिरानिनदसङ्गिसङ्गीतक-
ध्वनिर्ध्वनितदिग्वधूवदनपङ्कजैः पूजितः ।
विभिद्य मुहुरुच्चवच्चरमखण्डखण्डान्तरं
प्रयाति कति दूरतः स खलु मीयतां कैः पुनः ॥१८॥

*amanda-tara-mandirā-ninada-saṅgi-saṅgītaka-*
*dhvanir dhvanita-dig-vadhū-vadana-paṅkajaiḥ pūjitaḥ |*
*vibhidya muhur uccavac carama-khaṇḍa-khaṇḍāntaraṁ*
*prayāti kati dūrataḥ sa khalu mīyatāṁ kaiḥ punaḥ ||18||*

*Word for word:* *amanda-tara* — of the loudest; *mandirā* — of hand-cymbals; *ninada* — with the ringing; *saṅgi* — blending; *saṅgītaka* — of the singing; *dhvaniḥ* — the sound; *dhvanita* — echoing; *dik* — of the directions; *vadhū* — of the maidens; *vadana* — of the faces; *paṅkajaiḥ* — by the lotuses; *pūjitaḥ* — worshipped; *vibhidya* — having pierced; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *uccavat* — loud; *carama* — of the last; *khaṇḍa* — layer; *khaṇḍa-antaram* — the partition; *prayāti* — goes; *kati* — how; *dūrataḥ* — far; *saḥ* — it; *khalu* — indeed; *mīyatām* — may be measured; *kaiḥ* — by whom; *punaḥ* — then.

**18.** The sound of the singing, blending with the ringing of the loudest hand-cymbals and worshipped by the lotus faces of the maidens of the directions, who echo it, loudly and again and again pierces the partition of the last layer [of the universe] — and how far it goes, by whom then can that be measured?

*Note.* *Mandirā* (Bengali *mandira*) are small hand-cymbals (karatalas). *Uccavaccaram* in the edition is obscure. The Gosvami edition (GGM) divides the same letters as *uccavac carama-khaṇḍa-khaṇḍāntaram*, "the loud [sound, piercing] the partition of the last layer"; we accept this division. The metre confirms the syllables of the printed text.

### Verse 19

मुहुर्मधुरचक्रवद्भ्रमिविलोलयाश्लेषणः
परिस्फुरितधारया परिधिभूषितश्चन्द्रवत् ।
विलोचनपयोभरैर्वलयितैः समन्ताद्दिशां
मुखानि परिमार्जयन् जयति सोऽत्र नृत्योद्यमे ॥१९॥

*muhur madhura-cakravad-bhrami-vilolayāśleṣaṇaḥ (?)*
*parisphurita-dhārayā paridhi-bhūṣitaś candravat |*
*vilocana-payo-bharair valayitaiḥ samantād diśāṁ*
*mukhāni parimārjayan jayati so 'tra nṛtyodyame ||19||*

*Word for word:* *muhuḥ* — again and again; *madhura* — by the sweet; *cakra-vat* — wheel-like; *bhrami* — whirling; *vilolayā* — set swaying; *āśleṣaṇaḥ* (?) — encircled; *parisphurita* — glittering; *dhārayā* — by a stream; *paridhi* — with a halo; *bhūṣitaḥ* — adorned; *candra-vat* — like the moon; *vilocana* — of the eyes; *payaḥ* — of water; *bharaiḥ* — with the floods; *valayitaiḥ* — formed into a ring; *samantāt* — all around; *diśām* — of the directions; *mukhāni* — the faces; *parimārjayan* — washing; *jayati* — triumphs; *saḥ* — He; *atra* — here; *nṛtya* — of the dance; *udyame* — in the exertion.

**19.** Again and again encircled by a glittering stream [of tears] set swaying by His sweet whirling like a wheel — like the moon adorned with a halo — He triumphs here in the exertion of the dance, washing the faces of the directions all around with the floods of water from His eyes, formed into a ring.

*Note.* The image: as the Lord whirls, His tears fly out in a ring, like a halo around the moon. *-Vilolayāśleṣaṇaḥ* is obscure (?): we read *vilolayā* (agreeing with *dhārayā*) + *āśleṣaṇaḥ*, "embraced, encircled". The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 20

जय जय जयत्वित्यत्युच्चैर्निनादपरःशतै-
र्मुखरमुखरीभूताः सर्वा दिशः किमकुर्वत ।
निरवधि दृशौ तासु क्षिप्त्वा यदेष विलोहिते
नटनकलया लोलशोणीचकार जगत्तलम् ॥२०॥

*jaya jaya jayatv ity atyuccair nināda-paraḥśatair*
*mukhara-mukharībhūtāḥ sarvā diśaḥ kim akurvata |*
*niravadhi dṛśau tāsu kṣiptvā yad eṣa vilohite*
*naṭana-kalayā lola-śoṇī-cakāra jagat-talam ||20||*

*Word for word:* *jaya jaya jayatu* — "Glory, glory, may He be glorious!"; *iti* — thus; *ati-uccaiḥ* — very loud; *nināda* — of cries; *paraḥ-śataiḥ* — by hundreds upon hundreds; *mukhara-mukharī-bhūtāḥ* — made to resound deafeningly; *sarvāḥ* — all; *diśaḥ* — the directions; *kim* — what; *akurvata* — did [they] do; *niravadhi* — unceasingly; *dṛśau* — the eyes; *tāsu* — on them; *kṣiptvā* — having cast; *yat* — since; *eṣaḥ* — He; *vilohite* — reddened; *naṭana* — of the dance; *kalayā* — by the art; *lola* — trembling; *śoṇī-cakāra* — made crimson; *jagat* — of the world; *talam* — the surface.

**20.** What could all the directions do, made to resound deafeningly by hundreds upon hundreds of very loud cries of "Glory, glory, may He be glorious!"? For He, unceasingly casting His reddened eyes on them, by the art of His dance made the surface of the world trembling and crimson.

*Note.* Metre — *hariṇī* (⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑—————⏑—⏑⏑—⏑—); verses 20–21 are in *hariṇī*. The edition prints *ninādaparaḥ śatair*; we read *paraḥśataiḥ* as one word, "more than a hundred, hundreds upon hundreds". In the fourth pada the light *-la* of *lola-* stands in the eighth place, where the metre requires a heavy syllable (?).

### Verse 21

मुखशशिसमुद्गीर्णैः फेनैर्हसन्निव शारदं
सततविजितं लक्ष्म्या लक्ष्माकुलं हिमदीधितिम् ।
पुलकपटलैरत्युद्भिन्नैः सुमेरुमिवोद्गता-
ङ्कुरशतपरिच्छेदातीतः स एष विराजते ॥२१॥

*mukha-śaśi-samudgīrṇaiḥ phenair hasann iva śāradaṁ*
*satata-vijitaṁ lakṣmyā lakṣmākulaṁ hima-dīdhitim |*
*pulaka-paṭalair atyudbhinnaiḥ sumerum ivodgatā-*
*ṅkura-śata-paricchedātītaḥ sa eṣa virājate ||21||*

*Word for word:* *mukha* — of the face; *śaśi* — from the moon; *samudgīrṇaiḥ* — poured forth; *phenaiḥ* — with the foam; *hasan* — laughing; *iva* — as if; *śāradam* — [at] the autumn; *satata* — ever; *vijitam* — defeated; *lakṣmyā* — by [His] beauty; *lakṣma* — with spots; *ākulam* — filled; *hima-dīdhitim* — the cool-rayed (moon); *pulaka* — of hairs standing on end; *paṭalaiḥ* — with the masses; *ati-udbhinnaiḥ* — thickly sprouted; *sumerum* — Sumeru; *iva* — like; *udgata* — sprouted; *aṅkura* — of shoots; *śata* — of hundreds; *pariccheda* — the counting; *atītaḥ* — beyond; *saḥ eṣaḥ* — He; *virājate* — shines.

**21.** With the foam poured forth from the moon of His face He seems to laugh at the cool-rayed autumn moon, full of spots and ever defeated by [His] beauty; with the thickly sprouted masses of hairs standing on end He is like Sumeru, with sprouted shoots in hundreds beyond all counting: so He shines.

*Note.* Foam at the mouth is one of the signs of ecstatic love. The golden Lord with His hairs standing on end is compared to the golden mountain Sumeru covered with sprouting shoots.

### Verse 22

उन्मील्य प्रथमं परिप्लवयता पक्ष्माणि भूयः क्षणा-
च्छ्रीमद्गण्डतटीषु दीर्घमयता धाराभिरुच्चैस्ततः ।
प्राप्योरःपदवीं त्रिधा प्रसरता भूमौ त्रुटन्मौक्तिक-
श्रेणीवत् क्रियतां सदैव जगतां हर्षः प्रभोरश्रुणा ॥२२॥

*unmīlya prathamaṁ pariplavayatā pakṣmāṇi bhūyaḥ kṣaṇāc*
*chrīmad-gaṇḍa-taṭīṣu dīrgham ayatā dhārābhir uccais tataḥ |*
*prāpyoraḥ-padavīṁ tridhā prasaratā bhūmau truṭan-mauktika-*
*śreṇīvat kriyatāṁ sadaiva jagatāṁ harṣaḥ prabhor aśruṇā ||22||*

*Word for word:* *unmīlya* — having opened; *prathamam* — first; *pariplavayatā* — flooding; *pakṣmāṇi* — the eyelashes; *bhūyaḥ* — then; *kṣaṇāt* — at once; *śrīmat* — beautiful; *gaṇḍa* — of the cheeks; *taṭīṣu* — down the slopes; *dīrgham* — long; *ayatā* — flowing; *dhārābhiḥ* — in streams; *uccaiḥ* — abundantly; *tataḥ* — then; *prāpya* — having reached; *uraḥ* — of the chest; *padavīm* — the path; *tridhā* — in three; *prasaratā* — spreading; *bhūmau* — on the ground; *truṭat* — breaking; *mauktika* — of pearls; *śreṇī-vat* — like a string; *kriyatām* — may be brought about; *sadā eva* — ever; *jagatām* — of the worlds; *harṣaḥ* — the joy; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *aśruṇā* — by the tear.

**22.** May the joy of the worlds ever be brought about by the tear of the Lord, which first opens the eyelashes and floods them, then at once flows long in abundant streams down the slopes of His beautiful cheeks, then, reaching the path of His chest, spreads in three [streams and falls] on the ground like a breaking string of pearls.

*Note.* Metre: *śārdūla-vikrīḍita* (22–23).

### Verse 23

विश्वं प्लावयतेव तत्र लुठता भूमीषु वक्षःस्थले
गर्भोद्यत्कनकाश्मरम्यतटिनीशोभां तिरस्कुर्वता ।
अक्ष्णोर्मग्नसरोजसुन्दरसरःशोभेन गौरप्रभो-
रानन्दाश्रुभरेण तेन जगतामानन्द आधीयताम् ॥२३॥

*viśvaṁ plāvayateva tatra luṭhatā bhūmīṣu vakṣaḥ-sthale*
*garbhodyat-kanakāśma-ramya-taṭinī-śobhāṁ tiraskurvatā |*
*akṣṇor magna-saroja-sundara-saraḥ-śobhena gaura-prabhor*
*ānandāśru-bhareṇa tena jagatām ānanda ādhīyatām ||23||*

*Word for word:* *viśvam* — the universe; *plāvayatā* — flooding; *iva* — as if; *tatra* — there; *luṭhatā* — rolling; *bhūmīṣu* — over the ground; *vakṣaḥ-sthale* — on the chest; *garbha* — from the depths; *udyat* — emerging; *kanaka* — golden; *aśma* — with stones; *ramya* — lovely; *taṭinī* — of a river; *śobhām* — the beauty; *tiraskurvatā* — eclipsing; *akṣṇoḥ* — in the eyes; *magna* — submerged; *saroja* — with lotuses; *sundara* — beautiful; *saraḥ* — of a lake; *śobhena* — having the beauty; *gaura-prabhoḥ* — of Lord Gaura; *ānanda* — of bliss; *aśru* — of tears; *bhareṇa* — by the flood; *tena* — by that; *jagatām* — on the worlds; *ānandaḥ* — bliss; *ādhīyatām* — may be bestowed.

**23.** May bliss be bestowed on the worlds by that flood of Lord Gaura's tears of bliss which, rolling there over the ground, as it were floods the universe; which on His chest eclipses the beauty of a lovely river through whose depths golden stones show; and which in His eyes has the beauty of a lovely lake with submerged lotuses.

*Note.* Gaura's chest is the golden stones on the bed of the river of tears; His eyes are the lotuses under the water.

### Verse 24

गायद्भिर्गायनैस्तैः प्रमथवलयिते मण्डले तद्बहिश्च
श्रीकाशीमिश्रमुख्यैः परमसुमतिभिस्तत्पदाब्जप्रपन्नैः ।
हस्तग्राहं प्रमोदात् सततवलयिते तद्बहिश्च प्रताप-
प्राक् श्रीश्रीरुद्रदेवे निभृतमित इतो वेष्टिते भाति नाथः ॥२४॥

*gāyadbhir gāyanais taiḥ pramatha- (prathama-) valayite maṇḍale tad-bahiś ca*
*śrī-kāśīmiśra-mukhyaiḥ parama-sumatibhis tat-padābja-prapannaiḥ |*
*hasta-grāhaṁ pramodāt satata-valayite tad-bahiś ca pratāpa-*
*prāk śrī-śrī-rudradeve nibhṛtam ita ito veṣṭite bhāti nāthaḥ ||24||*

*Word for word:* *gāyadbhiḥ* — singing; *gāyanaiḥ* — by the singers; *taiḥ* — by those; *prathama* — first [the edition has *pramatha*]; *valayite* — formed into a ring; *maṇḍale* — [when] the circle; *tat* — of that; *bahiḥ* — outside; *ca* — and; *śrī-kāśīmiśra* — by Sri Kashi Mishra; *mukhyaiḥ* — headed; *parama* — supremely; *sumatibhiḥ* — by the right-minded; *tat* — His; *pada* — of the feet; *abja* — at the lotuses; *prapannaiḥ* — who had taken refuge; *hasta-grāham* — holding hands; *pramodāt* — out of joy; *satata* — unbroken; *valayite* — ringed; *tat-bahiḥ ca* — and outside that; *pratāpa-prāk* — with "Pratapa" before [his name]; *śrī-śrī-rudradeve* — [when] Sri Sri Rudradeva; *nibhṛtam* — unobtrusively; *itaḥ itaḥ* — here and there; *veṣṭite* — encircled [it]; *bhāti* — shines; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord.

**24.** When the first circle had been formed by those singing singers, and outside it [a second] had been ringed unbroken by the supremely right-minded [devotees] headed by Sri Kashi Mishra, who had taken refuge at His lotus feet and joyfully held one another's hands, and when outside that Sri Sri Rudradeva, with "Pratapa" before [his name], unobtrusively went round [them] here and there — the Lord shines.

*Note.* The edition has प्रमथ- (*pramatha-*), a misprint for *prathama-*, "first" (the metre is the same). The name of Prataparudra is split up for the sake of the metre: "Sri Sri Rudradeva, before whom [stands] 'Pratapa'". Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 13.88–90: three circles around the dancing Lord — the first led by Nityananda, the second formed by the devotees headed by Mukunda and Kashishvara, holding one another's hands, and the third, outside, by Prataparudra with his retinue.

### Verse 25

इन्द्रः किं किमथ विधि(ः) किमीशदेवो
नैवेषां भवति तदा ह्यपेक्षणीयः ।
श्रीगौरे नटनविलासवेशरम्ये
नैवासीत् क्षणमपि पक्ष्मणो निवृत्तिः ॥२५॥

*indraḥ kiṁ kim atha vidhiḥ kim īśa-devo*
*naivaiṣāṁ bhavati tadā hy apekṣaṇīyaḥ |*
*śrī-gaure naṭana-vilāsa-veśa-ramye*
*naivāsīt kṣaṇam api pakṣmaṇo nivṛttiḥ ||25||*

*Word for word:* *indraḥ* — Indra; *kim* — whether; *kim atha* — or else; *vidhiḥ* — the Creator; *kim* — or; *īśa-devaḥ* — the god Isha (Shiva); *na eva* — not at all; *eṣām* — of them; *bhavati* — is; *tadā* — then; *hi* — indeed; *apekṣaṇīyaḥ* — worth regarding; *śrī-gaure* — [while] Sri Gaura; *naṭana* — of dance; *vilāsa* — of the play; *veśa* — in the attire; *ramye* — [was] lovely; *na eva āsīt* — there was not at all; *kṣaṇam api* — even for a moment; *pakṣmaṇaḥ* — of the eyelashes; *nivṛttiḥ* — closing.

**25.** Whether Indra, or the Creator, or the god Isha — none of them was then worth regarding: while Sri Gaura was lovely in the attire of the play of dance, there was not even for a moment any closing of the eyelashes.

*Note.* Metre: *praharṣiṇī* (———⏑⏑⏑⏑—⏑—⏑——). The edition has विधि without the visarga; the metre requires *vidhiḥ*.

### Verse 26

आनन्देन जडीकृते भुवि चिरं स्तब्धे तथा स्यन्दने
श्रीनीलाद्रिपतेरुपैति च सति व्यग्रीभवद्भिर्भृशम् ।
तैरेतैः करपल्लवैर्निजनिजक्रोडेषु कृत्वा किय-
द्दूरे स्वैरमुपार्पितो विजयते श्रीगौरचन्द्रः प्रभुः ॥२६॥

*ānandena jaḍīkṛte bhuvi ciraṁ stabdhe tathā syandane*
*śrī-nīlādri-pater upaiti ca sati vyagrībhavadbhir bhṛśam |*
*tair etaiḥ kara-pallavair nija-nija-kroḍeṣu kṛtvā kiyad-*
*dūre svairam upārpito vijayate śrī-gauracandraḥ prabhuḥ ||26||*

*Word for word:* *ānandena* — by bliss; *jaḍīkṛte* — [when He had been] made motionless; *bhuvi* — on the ground; *ciram* — for long; *stabdhe* — [when] had stopped; *tathā* — likewise; *syandane* — the chariot; *śrī-nīlādri* — of the Blue Mountain; *pateḥ* — of the Lord; *upaiti* — approaches; *ca* — and; *sati* — [when] it; *vyagrībhavadbhiḥ* — growing anxious; *bhṛśam* — greatly; *taiḥ etaiḥ* — by these [devotees]; *kara* — of the hands; *pallavaiḥ* — with the shoots; *nija-nija* — each into his own; *kroḍeṣu* — arms (lit. "bosoms"); *kṛtvā* — having taken; *kiyat* — some way; *dūre* — off; *svairam* — gently; *upārpitaḥ* — carried; *vijayate* — is victorious; *śrī-gauracandraḥ* — Sri Gaurachandra; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord.

**26.** When He, made motionless by bliss, [lay] long on the ground, the chariot of the Lord of the Blue Mountain likewise stood still; and when it [again] began to approach, these [devotees], growing greatly anxious, took Him each into his own arms with their tender, shoot-like hands and gently carried Him some way off. Victorious is Lord Sri Gaurachandra!

*Note.* Metre: *śārdūla-vikrīḍita* (26–27). The chariot does not move while the Lord lies unconscious — cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 13.99 (the chariot stops, and Jagannatha gazes without blinking at the Lord's dance) and 14.48–55 (the chariot will not move, however it is pulled, until the Lord pushes it with His head).

### Verse 27

आनन्देन जडीभवन्ननुपदं हुङ्कारकोलाहलै-
रद्वैतार्पितपाणिपल्लवरसस्निग्धोरुवक्षःस्थलः ।
दण्डाकारमितस्ततो विनिपतद्दोर्दण्डपादद्वयो
नृत्योल्लासमनोहरो विजयते श्रीगौरचन्द्रः प्रभुः ॥२७॥

*ānandena jaḍībhavann anupadaṁ huṅkāra-kolāhalair*
*advaitārpita-pāṇi-pallava-rasa-snigdhoru-vakṣaḥ-sthalaḥ |*
*daṇḍākāram itas tato vinipatad-dor-daṇḍa-pāda-dvayo*
*nṛtyollāsa-manoharo vijayate śrī-gauracandraḥ prabhuḥ ||27||*

*Word for word:* *ānandena* — from bliss; *jaḍībhavan* — becoming motionless; *anupadam* — at every step; *huṅkāra* — of roars of "hum"; *kolāhalaiḥ* — with the clamour; *advaita* — by Advaita; *arpita* — offered; *pāṇi* — of the hand; *pallava* — of the shoot; *rasa* — by the touch (lit. "sap"); *snigdha* — moistened; *uru* — broad; *vakṣaḥ-sthalaḥ* — [whose] chest; *daṇḍa-ākāram* — like a staff; *itaḥ tataḥ* — this way and that; *vinipatat* — falling; *doḥ* — of arms; *daṇḍa* — with the staffs; *pāda* — of feet; *dvayaḥ* — [whose] pair; *nṛtya* — of the dance; *ullāsa* — by the exuberance; *manoharaḥ* — captivating; *vijayate* — is victorious; *śrī-gauracandraḥ* — Sri Gaurachandra; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord.

**27.** Victorious is Lord Sri Gaurachandra, captivating with the exuberance of His dance: at every step He grows motionless from bliss, amid a clamour of roars of "hum"; His broad chest is moistened by the touch of the tender hand that Advaita offers [Him]; His staff-like arms and both His feet fall this way and that like a staff.

*Note.* *Advaitārpita-pāṇi-pallava* is either "the tender hand which Advaita offered [for support]" or "the tender hand which [the Lord] laid on Advaita"; *uru* may also be taken as *ūru*, "thighs" ("His thighs and chest").

### Verse 28

आनन्दोत्साहमूर्च्छागत इव भवति स्पन्दनिश्वासमन्दे
रोहद्रोमाञ्चपूरैर्विकलितवपुषानन्दमन्दीकृतेन ।
स्यन्दन्नेत्रारविन्दद्वयसलिलजुषा रुद्रदेवेन भूयः
सानन्दं सेविताङ्घ्रिद्वयसरसिरुहो राजते गौरचन्द्रः ॥२८॥

*ānandotsāha-mūrcchāgata iva bhavati spanda-niśvāsa-mande*
*rohad-romāñca-pūrair vikalita-vapuṣānanda-mandīkṛtena |*
*syandan-netrāravinda-dvaya-salila-juṣā rudradevena bhūyaḥ*
*sānandaṁ sevitāṅghri-dvaya-sarasiruho rājate gauracandraḥ ||28||*

*Word for word:* *ānanda* — of bliss; *utsāha* — from the surge; *mūrcchā* — into a swoon; *āgate* — fallen; *iva* — as if; *bhavati* — [when He] was; *spanda* — in movement; *niśvāsa* — [and] breathing; *mande* — slowed; *rohat* — rising; *romāñca* — of hairs standing on end; *pūraiḥ* — by the floods; *vikalita* — shaken; *vapuṣā* — [whose] body; *ānanda* — by bliss; *mandīkṛtena* — made slow; *syandat* — streaming; *netra* — of eyes; *aravinda* — of lotuses; *dvaya* — of the pair; *salila* — the water; *juṣā* — having; *rudradevena* — by Rudradeva; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *sa-ānandam* — with bliss; *sevita* — served; *aṅghri* — of feet; *dvaya* — of the pair; *sarasiruhaḥ* — [whose] lotuses; *rājate* — shines; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra.

**28.** When He, as if fallen into a swoon from the surge of bliss, was slow in movement and breath, Gaurachandra shines, the pair of His lotus feet served again with bliss by Rudradeva — whose body was shaken by floods of rising hairs standing on end, who was slowed by bliss, and whose pair of lotus eyes streamed with water.

*Note.* Metre: *sragdharā* (28–30). In the edition the first pada has nineteen syllables instead of twenty-one; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *mūrcchāgata iva bhavati* (*-gate iva* with sandhi), and the gap is filled from it. Rudradeva is King Prataparudra; cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 14.4–18 (the king, dressed as a Vaishnava and with the devotees' permission, serves the feet of the Lord, who lies in the garden with closed eyes — 14.6–7).

### Verse 29

उन्मीलन्नेत्रपद्मे पुलकपटलिकालोलसर्वाङ्गयष्टौ
निष्ठीवत्फेनपूरोल्लसितमुखशशिद्योतनिर्धूतचन्द्रे ।
सान्द्रानन्दालिमन्दे मधुरिमलहरीसिन्धुसौभाग्यचन्द्रे
नृत्यत्यस्मिन्न केषां प्रभवति जडिमा श्रीलगौराङ्गचन्द्रे ॥२९॥

*unmīlan-netra-padme pulaka-paṭalikā-lola-sarvāṅga-yaṣṭau*
*niṣṭhīvat-phena-pūrollasita-mukha-śaśi-dyota-nirdhūta-candre |*
*sāndrānandāli-mande madhurima-laharī-sindhu-saubhāgya-candre*
*nṛtyaty asmin na keṣāṁ prabhavati jaḍimā śrīla-gaurāṅga-candre ||29||*

*Word for word:* *unmīlat* — opening; *netra* — of eyes; *padme* — [whose] lotuses; *pulaka* — of hairs standing on end; *paṭalikā* — with the covering; *lola* — trembling; *sarva* — of the whole; *aṅga* — body; *yaṣṭau* — [whose] stem; *niṣṭhīvat* — spat forth; *phena* — of foam; *pūra* — by the flood; *ullasita* — gleaming; *mukha* — of the face; *śaśi* — of the moon; *dyota* — by the radiance; *nirdhūta* — who has cast off; *candre* — the moon; *sāndra* — of dense; *ānanda* — bliss; *āli* — by the succession; *mande* — slowed; *madhurima* — of sweetness; *laharī* — of waves; *sindhu* — of the ocean; *saubhāgya* — of the good fortune; *candre* — the moon; *nṛtyati* — [when] dances; *asmin* — this; *na keṣām* — in whom not; *prabhavati* — arises; *jaḍimā* — stupor; *śrīla* — beautiful; *gaurāṅga* — Gauranga; *candre* — the Moon.

**29.** When this beautiful Moon, Gauranga, dances — His lotus eyes opening, the stem of His whole body trembling under a covering of hairs standing on end, outshining the moon with the radiance of His moonlike face that gleams with the flood of foam He spits forth, slowed by a succession of dense bliss, the moon [that brings] good fortune to the ocean of waves of sweetness — in whom does stupor not arise?

### Verse 30

आनन्दं नेत्ररन्ध्रैर्निरवधिपरमानन्दसन्दोहधारा-
धौतप्रत्यङ्गलक्ष्मीमधुरिमविभवो रामणीयोत्कचित्तः ।
पीत्वा पीत्वा यदायं नटनरसधुनीपूरमुल्लासलोलो
निस्पन्दो बोभवीति प्रथयति परमानन्दपुरी सहर्षम् ॥३०॥

*ānandaṁ netra-randhrair niravadhi-paramānanda-sandoha-dhārā-*
*dhauta-pratyaṅga-lakṣmī-madhurima-vibhavo rāmaṇīyotka-cittaḥ |*
*pītvā pītvā yadāyaṁ naṭana-rasa-dhunī-pūram ullāsa-lolo*
*nispando bobhavīti prathayati paramānanda-purī saharṣam ||30||*

*Word for word:* *ānandam* — bliss; *netra* — of the eyes; *randhraiḥ* — through the openings; *niravadhi* — boundless; *parama-ānanda* — of supreme bliss; *sandoha* — of the abundance; *dhārā* — by the streams; *dhauta* — washed; *pratyaṅga* — of every limb; *lakṣmī* — of the beauty; *madhurima* — the sweetness; *vibhavaḥ* — [whose] wealth; *rāmaṇīya* — for loveliness; *utka* — yearning; *cittaḥ* — [whose] heart; *pītvā pītvā* — having drunk and drunk; *yadā* — when; *ayam* — he; *naṭana* — of the dance; *rasa* — of the rasa; *dhunī* — of the river; *pūram* — the flood; *ullāsa* — with exultation; *lolaḥ* — trembling; *nispandaḥ* — motionless; *bobhavīti* — becomes again and again; *prathayati* — spreads; *paramānanda-purī* — Paramananda Puri; *sa-harṣam* — joyfully.

**30.** Paramananda Puri — whose wealth is the sweetness of the beauty of every limb washed by streams of an abundance of boundless supreme bliss, and whose heart yearns for loveliness — when, having drunk again and again the flood of the river of the rasa of the dance, he trembles with exultation and again and again becomes motionless, joyfully spreads bliss through the openings of his eyes.

*Note.* *Bobhavīti* is an intensive of *bhū*. Bliss "through the openings of the eyes" means tears streaming from the eyes. *Paramānanda-sandoha*, "an abundance of supreme bliss", echoes the name Paramananda. Paramananda Puri is a senior companion of the Lord, a disciple of Madhavendra Puri. In the fourth pada the seventeenth syllable (*pu-* of *-purī*) is light where the *sragdharā* requires a heavy one: the name does not fit the metre (?).

### Verse 31

दधार कटिसूत्रकं प्रभुरितीह दामोदरः
स्वरूप इव तस्य किं यतिवरोऽयमुद्घुष्यते ।
य एष नटनोत्सवे हृदयकायवाग्वृत्तिभिः
शचीसुतकलानिधौ प्रविशतीव सान्द्रोत्सुकः ॥३१॥

*dadhāra kaṭi-sūtrakaṁ prabhur itīha dāmodaraḥ*
*svarūpa iva tasya kiṁ yati-varo 'yam udghuṣyate |*
*ya eṣa naṭanotsave hṛdaya-kāya-vāg-vṛttibhiḥ*
*śacī-suta-kalānidhau praviśatīva sāndrotsukaḥ ||31||*

*Word for word:* *dadhāra* — wore; *kaṭi* — waist; *sūtrakam* — cord; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *iti* — because; *iha* — here; *dāmodaraḥ* — Damodara; *svarūpaḥ* — Svarupa ("His own form"); *iva* — as it were; *tasya* — His; *kim* — is it [that]; *yati* — of renunciants; *varaḥ* — the best; *ayam* — this; *udghuṣyate* — is proclaimed; *yaḥ eṣaḥ* — he who; *naṭana* — of the dance; *utsave* — at the festival; *hṛdaya* — of heart; *kāya* — body; *vāk* — [and] speech; *vṛttibhiḥ* — with the workings; *śacī-suta* — the son of Shachi; *kalānidhau* — into the moon; *praviśati* — enters; *iva* — as if; *sāndra* — intensely; *utsukaḥ* — longing.

**31.** Is it because the Lord wore a waist-cord that this best of renunciants is proclaimed here "Damodara", as though he were His "Svarupa", His own form? — he who at the festival of the dance, intensely longing, with all the workings of heart, body and speech, as it were enters into the Moon that is the son of Shachi.

*Note.* Metre: *pṛthvī*. A play on words: *dāmodara*, "[he who has] a cord (*dāman*) round the belly (*udara*)", is a name of Krishna, who was bound by Yashoda; the Lord wears a waist-cord, and so His companion is called Damodara, as if he were His *svarūpa*, His "own form". Svarupa Damodara is meant.

### Verse 32

उन्मीलन्मकरन्दसुन्दरपदद्वन्द्वारविन्दोल्लस-
द्विन्यासः क्षितिषु प्रकाममनुना दामोदरेण प्रभुः ।
आमुग्धैः करकुट्नलैरित इतो हर्षादधोऽधो गुरु-
स्नेहार्द्रेण दृढोपगूहितपदो नृत्यन्नसौ दृश्यताम् ॥३२॥

*unmīlan-makaranda-sundara-pada-dvandvāravindollasad-*
*vinyāsaḥ kṣitiṣu prakāmam anunā (amunā) dāmodareṇa prabhuḥ |*
*āmugdhaiḥ kara-kuṭnalair ita ito harṣād adho 'dho guru-*
*snehārdreṇa dṛḍhopagūhita-pado nṛtyann asau dṛśyatām ||32||*

*Word for word:* *unmīlat* — appearing; *makaranda* — with nectar (sweat); *sundara* — beautiful; *pada* — of feet; *dvandva* — of the pair; *aravinda* — of lotuses; *ullasat* — gleaming; *vinyāsaḥ* — [whose] placing; *kṣitiṣu* — on the ground; *prakāmam* — freely; *amunā* — by this; *dāmodareṇa* — by Damodara; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *āmugdhaiḥ* — with tender; *kara* — of the hands; *kuṭnalaiḥ* — with the buds; *itaḥ itaḥ* — here and there; *harṣāt* — out of joy; *adhaḥ adhaḥ* — low down, low down; *guru* — by great; *sneha* — love; *ārdreṇa* — melted; *dṛḍha* — firmly; *upagūhita* — embraced; *padaḥ* — [whose] feet; *nṛtyan* — dancing; *asau* — this; *dṛśyatām* — let be seen.

**32.** Behold this Lord dancing: He freely sets on the ground, gleaming, the pair of His beautiful lotus feet, on which [sweat] appears like nectar, while this Damodara, melted by great love, out of joy, here and there, low down, firmly embraces His feet with the tender buds of his hands.

*Note.* Metre: *śārdūla-vikrīḍita*. The edition has *anunā*, a misprint for *amunā*, "by this"; the correction is made by sense, since metrically the two readings are equivalent. *Kuṭnala* = *kuḍmala*, "bud".

### Verse 33

काशीश्वरप्रभृतयो रभसेन काशी-
मिश्रश्च हर्षभरविश्रमणैकपात्रम् ।
गोविन्द एष च परस्परमुत्कचित्ता
दृग्भिस्तदीयनटनामृतमाधयन्ति ॥३३॥

*kāśīśvara-prabhṛtayo rabhasena kāśī-*
*miśraś ca harṣa-bhara-viśramaṇaika-pātram |*
*govinda eṣa ca parasparam utka-cittā*
*dṛgbhis tadīya-naṭanāmṛtam ādhayanti ||33||*

*Word for word:* *kāśīśvara* — Kashishvara; *prabhṛtayaḥ* — and the others; *rabhasena* — eagerly; *kāśī-miśraḥ* — Kashi Mishra; *ca* — and; *harṣa* — of joy; *bhara* — of the fullness; *viśramaṇa* — of resting; *eka* — the sole; *pātram* — vessel; *govindaḥ* — Govinda; *eṣaḥ* — this; *ca* — and; *parasparam* — [vying] with one another; *utka* — eager; *cittāḥ* — [whose] hearts; *dṛgbhiḥ* — with their eyes; *tadīya* — His; *naṭana* — of the dance; *amṛtam* — the nectar; *ādhayanti* — drink.

**33.** Kashishvara and the others, and Kashi Mishra — the sole vessel in which the fullness of joy rests — and this Govinda, their hearts eager, vying with one another, eagerly drink with their eyes the nectar of His dance.

*Note.* Metre: *vasanta-tilakā* (33–36). Kashishvara and Govinda are servants of the Lord (disciples of Ishvara Puri).

### Verse 34

नृत्यन् क्षितौ समुपदिश्य निजाङ्घ्रिपद्मं
दोर्भ्यां सुखेन परिरभ्य विलोलमौलिः ।
चुम्बन् जनं जनमभिप्रकटानुरागो
मूर्द्धनि क्षिपन् विजयते कनकाद्रिगौरः ॥३४॥

*nṛtyan kṣitau samupadiśya nijāṅghri-padmaṁ*
*dorbhyāṁ sukhena parirabhya vilola-mauliḥ |*
*cumban janaṁ janam abhiprakaṭānurāgo*
*mūrdhani kṣipan vijayate kanakādri-gauraḥ ||34||*

*Word for word:* *nṛtyan* — dancing; *kṣitau* — on the ground; *samupadiśya* — having set (?); *nija* — His own; *aṅghri* — foot; *padmam* — lotus; *dorbhyām* — with both arms; *sukhena* — happily; *parirabhya* — embracing; *vilola* — swaying; *mauliḥ* — [whose] head; *cumban* — kissing; *janam janam* — person after person; *abhiprakaṭa* — manifest; *anurāgaḥ* — [whose] love; *mūrdhani* — on the head; *kṣipan* — placing; *vijayate* — is victorious; *kanaka* — of gold; *adri* — [like] a mountain; *gauraḥ* — fair.

**34.** Victorious is He who is fair as a mountain of gold: dancing, He sets His lotus foot on the ground; with swaying head He happily embraces person after person with His arms, kisses them and, His love made manifest, places [His foot] on their heads.

*Note.* *Samupadiśya* ("having pointed out", "having directed") is strange in this context (?); the sense seems to be that, setting His feet on the ground in the dance, He places His foot on the heads of the devotees. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text. In the fourth pada *mūrdhani* gives fifteen syllables instead of fourteen; the metre requires the equally correct locative *mūrdhni* (?).

### Verse 35

एतद्विना जगति नान्यदिहास्ति रम्यं

इत्याकलय्य नटने निजपादपद्मं
हृद्यर्पयन् विजयते सततं च चुम्बन् ॥३५॥

*etad vinā jagati nānyad ihāsti ramyaṁ*
*śrīmat sugandhi guru-kāruṇikaṁ durāpam |*
*ity ākalayya naṭane nija-pāda-padmaṁ*
*hṛdy arpayan vijayate satataṁ ca cumban ||35||*

*Word for word:* *etat vinā* — apart from this; *jagati* — in the world; *na anyat* — nothing else; *iha* — here; *asti* — is; *ramyam* — lovely; *śrīmat* — beautiful; *sugandhi* — fragrant; *guru* — of great; *kāruṇikam* — full of mercy; *durāpam* — hard to attain; *iti* — thus; *ākalayya* — having considered; *naṭane* — in the dance; *nija* — His own; *pāda* — foot; *padmam* — lotus; *hṛdi* — to the heart; *arpayan* — pressing; *vijayate* — is victorious; *satatam* — constantly; *ca* — and; *cumban* — kissing.

**35.** "Apart from this there is nothing else here in the world so lovely, beautiful, fragrant, full of great mercy and hard to attain" — having considered thus, He presses His own lotus foot to His heart in the dance and constantly kisses it. Victorious is He!

*Note.* Cf. v. 36: Gaura, like Krishna, relishes the sweetness of His own feet (the motif of the infant Krishna sucking His toe). Another understanding: in the dance He places His feet in the hearts [of the devotees].

*Word for word:* *snihyan* — loving; *iva* — as if; *pratipadam* — at every step; *hṛdaya* — of the heart; *antareṣu* — into the depths; *kurvan* — placing; *iva* — as if; *akṣi* — of eyes; *yugalena* — with the pair; *piban* — drinking; *iva* — as if; *asau* — He; *āsvādayan* — tasting; *iva* — as if; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *nija* — His own; *pāda* — foot; *padmam* — lotus; *nṛtye* — in the dance; *jayati* — is victorious; *aviratam* — unceasingly; *kamanīya* — charming; *gauraḥ* — Gaura.

**36.** As if loving His own lotus foot at every step, as if placing it in the depths of His heart, as if drinking it with His pair of eyes, and as if again and again tasting it, the charming Gaura is unceasingly victorious in the dance.

*Word for word:* *tat* — of that; *ānanda* — bliss; *dhārām* — the stream; *vahan* — carrying; *kṣīra* — of milk; *vārāṁnidheḥ* — the ocean; *sa-anukārām* — resembling; *vikāri* — transforming; *pracārām* — [whose] course; *vilola* — darting; *ali* — of bees; *khelā* — [like] the play; *vilāsa* — with grace; *akṣi* — of the eyes; *līlā* — of the play; *rasaiḥ* — with the relishes; *sādhu* — wonderfully; *kurvan* — making; *janasya* — for the people; *abja* — of a lotus; *garbham* — the heart (?).

*Word for word:* *alaṁkurvat* — adorning; *ānanda* — of bliss; *mūrcchā* — of swoon; *prakāśa* — by the manifestation; *śrita* — accompanied; *stambha* — of stupor; *romāñca* — of hairs standing on end; *kampa* — of trembling; *prakāśaḥ* — [whose] manifestation; *anirvārya* — irresistible; *bhāva* — of feeling; *prakāśa* — of manifestation; *atireka* — from the excess; *sphurat* — flashing; *deha* — of the body; *kānti* — of the radiance; *chaṭā* — with the streams; *channa* — who has covered; *lokaḥ* — the world.

*Word for word:* *trilokī* — over the three worlds; *sphurat* — spreading; *kīrtti* — of fame; *pīyūṣa* — of nectar; *dhāraḥ* — [whose] stream; *prakāśīkṛta* — who has made manifest; *prema-bhakti* — of loving devotion; *pracāraḥ* — the propagation; *lasat* — shining; *tapta* — molten; *kārttasvara* — [like] gold; *śrīmat* — beautiful; *aṅga* — of the body; *chaṭā* — by the streams; *channa* — covered; *lāvaṇya* — of loveliness; *tāruṇya* — of youth; *bhaṅgaḥ* — [whose] waves.

*Word for word:* *nadat* — ringing; *mandirā* — of cymbals; *vṛnda* — with a host; *riṅgat* — rumbling; *mṛdaṅgaiḥ* — with mridangas; *samudyat* — surging; *mahā* — of great; *ullāsa* — exultation; *pāthodhi* — of the ocean; *bhaṅgaiḥ* — with the waves; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *gāyanaiḥ* — with singers; *mugdha* — of charming; *saṅgīta* — melodies; *bhaṅgī* — in the modulations; *samutkaṇṭha* — ardent; *kaṇṭhaiḥ* — [whose] voices; *sadā* — always; *ānanda* — with bliss; *saṅgī* — accompanied.

*Word for word:* *jagannātha-devam* — Lord Jagannatha; *vimugdham* — enchanted; *sva* — by His own; *lāsyaiḥ* — dances; *vilokya* — having seen; *ati* — excessive; *harṣa* — of joy; *aśru* — with tears; *gharma-ambu* — with sweat; *hāsaiḥ* — [and] with laughter; *rasa* — of rasa; *utkarṣataḥ* — from the excess; *niḥsaha* — exhausted; *śrīmat* — beautiful; *aṅgaḥ* — [whose] body; *sadā* — always; *rajyat* — reddening; *ākuñcita* — narrowed; *apāṅga* — of the corners of the eyes; *bhaṅgaiḥ* — with the curves.
