*Note.* The metre of the sarga is *anuṣṭubh* (except where otherwise stated).

### Verse 2–3

{ प्रयातुं यमुनातीरं गङ्गातीरे मनो दधे ।
यत्तटे सोऽवतीर्णोऽस्ति तस्यां प्रीतिर्महीयसी ॥२॥
दक्षिणादागतो यावत्तावत्तत्र महाप्रभुः ।
मथुरायां चलत्येव रामानन्दोऽत्र बाधते ॥३॥ }**

*prayātuṁ yamunā-tīraṁ gaṅgā-tīre mano dadhe |*
*yat-taṭe so 'vatīrṇo 'sti tasyāṁ prītir mahīyasī ||2||*
*dakṣiṇād āgato yāvat tāvat tatra mahāprabhuḥ |*
*mathurāyāṁ calaty eva rāmānando 'tra bādhate ||3||*

*Word for word:* *prayātum* — to set out; *yamunā* — of the Yamuna; *tīram* — for the bank; *gaṅgā* — of the Ganga; *tīre* — on the bank; *manaḥ* — [His] mind; *dadhe* — He set; *yat* — on whose; *taṭe* — bank; *saḥ* — He; *avatīrṇaḥ asti* — has descended; *tasyām* — for her; *prītiḥ* — love; *mahīyasī* — very great.

*Word for word:* *dakṣiṇāt* — from the south; *āgataḥ* — returned; *yāvat … tāvat* — no sooner … than; *tatra* — then; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *mathurāyām* — for Mathura; *calati eva* — is already setting off; *rāmānandaḥ* — Ramananda; *atra* — at this; *bādhate* — hinders (holds [Him] back).

**2–3.** Wishing to set out for the bank of the Yamuna, He set His mind [first] on the bank of the Ganga: for it is on her bank that He has descended, and His love for her is very great. No sooner had Mahaprabhu returned from the south than He was already setting off for Mathura — but at this Ramananda holds Him back.

*Note.* The edition's footnote (in Sanskrit): "In this book two verses were illegible because of a printing defect; therefore, after consulting another book, they were typeset by computer." Verses 2–3 are enclosed in braces; that is, we have a later reprint with an insertion. *Bādhate* means rather "holds back"; cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 16.4–8, 85–92: for years Sarvabhauma and Ramananda dissuade the Lord from going to Vrindavana, until He reproaches them.

### Verse 4

चातुर्मास्यान्तरे नाथं कर्हिचिद्गमनोद्यतम् ।
उवाच बहुदुःखेन श्रीरामानन्दरायकः ॥४॥

*cāturmāsyāntare nāthaṁ karhicid gamanodyatam |*
*uvāca bahu-duḥkhena śrī-rāmānanda-rāyakaḥ ||4||*

*Word for word:* *cāturmāsya* — of the Chaturmasya; *antare* — at the end; *nātham* — to the Master; *karhicit* — once; *gamana* — to depart; *udyatam* — ready; *uvāca* — said; *bahu* — with great; *duḥkhena* — sorrow; *śrī-rāmānanda-rāyakaḥ* — Sri Ramananda Raya.

**4.** Once, at the end of the Chaturmasya, when the Master was ready to depart, Sri Ramananda Raya said with great sorrow:

### Verse 5

दशम्यां विजयायां तु गमनं भविता प्रभोः ।
दशम्यां विजयायां तु दशायामहमग्रतः ॥५॥

*daśamyāṁ vijayāyāṁ tu gamanaṁ bhavitā prabhoḥ |*
*daśamyāṁ vijayāyāṁ tu daśāyām aham agrataḥ ||5||*

*Word for word:* *daśamyām* — on the tenth [day]; *vijayāyām* — of Vijaya; *tu* — indeed; *gamanam* — the departure; *bhavitā* — will take place; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *daśamyām* — in the tenth; *vijayāyām* — all-conquering; *tu* — but; *daśāyām* — in the state; *aham* — I [shall be]; *agrataḥ* — before [that].

**5.** "On Vijaya-dashami the Lord's departure will take place — but I shall be in the tenth, all-conquering state before [that]."

*Note.* A play on words (*yamaka*: the first half of each line is the same), explained in the edition's Sanskrit commentary: *vijayā daśamī* is the festival of Vijaya-dashami (in autumn); in the second line *vijayā* is "she who conquers especially" (*viśeṣeṇa jayatīti*), and *daśamī daśā* is the tenth of the ten states of one in love, that is, the end of life. The commentary gives the list: "attraction of the eyes, attachment of the mind, constant thought, sleeplessness, emaciation, aversion to [other] objects, loss of shame, madness, swooning, dying — these are the states in order." The sense: "The Lord will depart on the day of Vijaya, but I shall die even before."

### Verse 6

गोविन्दो जगदानन्दः श्रीदामोदरपण्डितः ।
परमानन्दपुरी च तत्सङ्गे मिलिता ययुः ॥६॥

*govindo jagadānandaḥ śrī-dāmodara-paṇḍitaḥ |*
*paramānanda-purī ca tat-saṅge militā yayuḥ ||6||*

*Word for word:* *govindaḥ* — Govinda; *jagadānandaḥ* — Jagadananda; *śrī-dāmodara-paṇḍitaḥ* — Sri Damodara Pandita; *paramānanda-purī* — Paramananda Puri; *ca* — and; *tat-saṅge* — in His company; *militāḥ* — together; *yayuḥ* — went.

**6.** Govinda, Jagadananda, Sri Damodara Pandita and Paramananda Puri went together in His company.

*Note.* In the third pada (*paramānanda-purī ca*: ⏑⏑——⏑⏑—⏑) the fifth to seventh syllables are ⏑⏑—, which is neither the normal form of the odd pada of the *anuṣṭubh* (⏑——) nor one of its permitted variants (*vipulā*); a licence with a proper name.

### Verse 7

गङ्गातीरे समागत्य वैष्णवेभ्यो विसर्जितुम् ।
महाप्रसादान् विविधान्नेतुं तत्रादिशत् प्रभुः ॥७॥

*gaṅgā-tīre samāgatya vaiṣṇavebhyo visarjitum |*
*mahāprasādān vividhān netuṁ tatrādiśat prabhuḥ ||7||*

*Word for word:* *gaṅgā* — of the Ganga; *tīre* — on the bank; *samāgatya* — having arrived; *vaiṣṇavebhyaḥ* — to the Vaishnavas; *visarjitum* — to distribute; *mahā-prasādān* — mahaprasada; *vividhān* — of various kinds; *netum* — to take along; *tatra* — then; *ādiśat* — ordered; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord.

**7.** Then the Lord ordered that mahaprasada of various kinds be taken along, to distribute it to the Vaishnavas on arriving at the bank of the Ganga.

### Verse 8

एते नाथनिदेशेन मुदिता भूय आददुः ।
महाप्रसादान् विपुलान् डोरचन्दनमुख्यकान् ॥८॥

*ete nātha-nideśena muditā bhūya ādaduḥ |*
*mahāprasādān vipulān ḍora-candana-mukhyakān ||8||*

*Word for word:* *ete* — they; *nātha* — of the Master; *nideśena* — by the order; *muditāḥ* — joyful; *bhūyaḥ* — much; *ādaduḥ* — took; *mahā-prasādān* — mahaprasada; *vipulān* — abundant; *ḍora* — cords; *candana* — sandalwood paste; *mukhyakān* — and so on (lit. headed by).

**8.** At the Master's order they joyfully took much abundant mahaprasada — cords, sandalwood paste and so on.

*Note.* *Ḍora* — the sanctified silk cords of Jagannatha (*paṭṭa-ḍorī*).

### Verse 9

मात्रे निर्म्माल्यवसनमात्मेच्छाभिर्महाप्रभुः ।
परमानन्दपुर्यूढां परमां युक्तिमादधे ॥९॥

*mātre nirmālya-vasanam ātmecchābhir mahāprabhuḥ |*
*paramānanda-puryūḍhāṁ paramāṁ yuktim ādadhe ||9||*

*Word for word:* *mātre* — for [His] mother; *nirmālya* — sanctified; *vasanam* — a garment; *ātma* — by [His] own; *icchābhiḥ* — wishes; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *paramānanda-purī* — by Paramananda Puri; *ūḍhām* — put forward; *paramām* — excellent; *yuktim* — counsel; *ādadhe* — adopted.

**9.** [Wishing to give] His mother, of His own accord, a sanctified garment, Mahaprabhu adopted the excellent counsel put forward by Paramananda Puri.

*Note.* The counsel itself is given in 12.

### Verse 10

इदं श्रीमज्जगन्नाथनिर्म्माल्यं परमांशुकम् ।
प्रतापरुद्रेण च मे दत्तं परमदुर्लभम् ॥१०॥

*idaṁ śrīmaj-jagannātha-nirmālyaṁ paramāṁśukam |*
*pratāparudreṇa ca me dattaṁ parama-durlabham ||10||*

*Word for word:* *idam* — this; *śrīmat-jagannātha* — of Sriman Jagannatha; *nirmālyam* — the sanctified [remnant]; *parama* — excellent; *aṁśukam* — cloth; *pratāparudreṇa* — by Prataparudra; *ca* — and; *me* — to Me; *dattam* — given; *parama* — extremely; *durlabham* — rare.

**10.** "This excellent cloth, the sanctified [remnant] of Sriman Jagannatha, extremely rare, was given to Me by Prataparudra.

### Verse 11

कस्मै दास्यामि तन्नूनं गदितुं त्वमिहार्हसि ।
मया सन्दिग्धमनसा स्थीयते साम्प्रतं खलु ॥११॥

*kasmai dāsyāmi tan nūnaṁ gadituṁ tvam ihārhasi |*
*mayā sandigdha-manasā sthīyate sāmprataṁ khalu ||11||*

*Word for word:* *kasmai* — to whom; *dāsyāmi* — shall I give; *tat* — it; *nūnam* — then; *gaditum* — to say; *tvam* — you; *iha* — here; *arhasi* — ought; *mayā* — by Me; *sandigdha* — doubting; *manasā* — with a mind; *sthīyate* — it is remained (I remain); *sāmpratam* — now; *khalu* — indeed.

**11.** To whom shall I give it? You ought to tell Me this here, for I am now indeed in doubt."

### Verse 12

इत्युक्तोऽसौ पुरीस्वामी बभाषेऽथ महाप्रभुम् ।
जनन्यै देयमेतत्तु ममैतन्मतमुत्तमम् ॥१२॥

*ity ukto 'sau purī-svāmī babhāṣe 'tha mahāprabhum |*
*jananyai deyam etat tu mamaitan matam uttamam ||12||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *uktaḥ* — addressed; *asau* — this; *purī-svāmī* — Puri Svami; *babhāṣe* — said; *atha* — then; *mahāprabhum* — to Mahaprabhu; *jananyai* — to [Your] mother; *deyam* — should be given; *etat tu* — this; *mama* — my; *etat* — this [is]; *matam* — opinion; *uttamam* — firm (lit. highest).

**12.** Thus addressed, Puri Svami then said to Mahaprabhu: "This should be given to [Your] mother — that is my firm opinion."

*Note.* Puri Svami is Paramananda Puri (cf. 9).

### Verse 13

ऊचे पूर्वेद्युरसकौ रसकौतुकविभ्रमः ।
विभ्रमच्छेदकृद्दृष्टिर्हृद्दृष्टिसुखदः प्रभुः ॥१३॥

*ūce pūrvedyur asakau rasa-kautuka-vibhramaḥ |*
*vibhrama-ccheda-kṛd-dṛṣṭir hṛd-dṛṣṭi-sukhadaḥ prabhuḥ ||13||*

*Word for word:* *ūce* — said; *pūrvedyuḥ* — on the day before; *asakau* — this; *rasa* — in rasa; *kautuka* — of delight; *vibhramaḥ* — [whose] charm [is]; *vibhrama* — of delusion; *cheda* — the cutting; *kṛt* — effecting; *dṛṣṭiḥ* — [whose] glance [is]; *hṛt* — to the heart; *dṛṣṭi* — [and] to the eyes; *sukha-daḥ* — giving joy; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord.

**13.** On the day before [the departure] this Lord — full of the charm of delight in rasa, whose glance cuts away delusion, who gives joy to the heart and the eyes — said:

*Note.* A chain of repetitions at the junctions (*rasakau / rasa-kautuka*, *vibhramaḥ / vibhrama-*, *dṛṣṭiḥ / hṛd-dṛṣṭi-*). *Asakau* is a by-form of *asau* with the suffix *-ak-*, chosen here for the sound-play.

### Verse 14

गायं गायं गमिष्यामि जगन्नाथं विलोकितुम् ।
दामोदरोऽसौ मत्सङ्गे गायन् स्थास्यति निश्चितम् ॥१४॥

*gāyaṁ gāyaṁ gamiṣyāmi jagannāthaṁ vilokitum |*
*dāmodaro 'sau mat-saṅge gāyan sthāsyati niścitam ||14||*

*Word for word:* *gāyam gāyam* — singing and singing; *gamiṣyāmi* — I shall go; *jagannātham* — Jagannatha; *vilokitum* — to see; *dāmodaraḥ* — Damodara; *asau* — this; *mat-saṅge* — with Me; *gāyan* — singing; *sthāsyati* — will be; *niścitam* — certainly.

**14.** "I shall go to see Jagannatha, singing all the way, and this Damodara will certainly be [there] with Me, singing."

*Note.* In verses 6 and 24 the Lord's companion in this episode is expressly called Damodara Pandita, so presumably it is he here too, although the one who usually sings for the Lord is Svarupa Damodara. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 15

इत्यसौ रजनीशेषे प्रथमावसरं विभोः ।
निजकीर्त्तनसंहर्षैर्गच्छन् पथि बभौ प्रभुः ॥१५॥

*ity asau rajanī-śeṣe prathamāvasaraṁ vibhoḥ |*
*nija-kīrttana-saṁharṣair gacchan pathi babhau prabhuḥ ||15||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus [having spoken]; *asau* — He; *rajanī* — of the night; *śeṣe* — at the end; *prathama* — to the first; *avasaram* — service; *vibhoḥ* — of the All-pervading Lord; *nija* — of His own; *kīrttana* — kirtana; *saṁharṣaiḥ* — with the raptures; *gacchan* — going; *pathi* — on the road; *babhau* — shone; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord.

**15.** Having spoken thus, at the end of the night the Lord, going along the road to the first service (*avasara*) of the All-pervading Lord [Jagannatha], shone with the raptures of His own kirtana.

### Verse 16

दैवाद्दामोदरः सोऽयं मिलितो नाभवत्तदा ।
सिंहद्वारे क्षणं तस्थौ तमपेक्ष्य स्वयं प्रभुः ॥१६॥

*daivād dāmodaraḥ so 'yaṁ milito nābhavat tadā |*
*siṁha-dvāre kṣaṇaṁ tasthau tam apekṣya svayaṁ prabhuḥ ||16||*

*Word for word:* *daivāt* — as fate would have it; *dāmodaraḥ* — Damodara; *saḥ ayam* — that very; *militaḥ* — joined; *na abhavat* — had not; *tadā* — then; *siṁha-dvāre* — at the Lion Gate; *kṣaṇam* — for a while; *tasthau* — stood; *tam* — for him; *apekṣya* — waiting; *svayam* — Himself; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord.

**16.** As fate would have it, that Damodara had not joined [them] then, and the Lord Himself stood for a while at the Lion Gate, waiting for him.

### Verse 17

भावाभावाभिभावाभिभवभावे बभौ भवः ।
विभावेवम्भावभावे बभूव भुवि वैभवम् ॥१७॥
(द्व्यक्षरः)

*bhāvābhāvābhibhāvābhibhava-bhāve babhau bhavaḥ |*
*vibhāv evam-bhāva-bhāve babhūva bhuvi vaibhavam ||17||*
*(dvyakṣaraḥ)*

*Word for word:* (following the word division of the edition's commentary: *bhāva abhāva abhibhāva abhibhava bhāve babhau bhavaḥ | vibhau evambhāva bhāve babhūva bhuvi vaibhavam*): *bhāva* — of the presence; *abhāva* — from the absence; *abhibhāva* — [by] the all-pervading state [of separation]; *abhibhava* — of being overcome; *bhāve* — [when there was] the state; *babhau* — shone forth; *bhavaḥ* — the birth [of Damodara]; *vibhau* — [when] the Master [was]; *evam-bhāva* — such; *bhāve* — in a state; *babhūva* — there arose; *bhuvi* — on earth; *vaibhavam* — glory.

**17.** When [the Lord] was in the state of being overcome by the all-pervading state [of separation] arising from the absence [of Damodara], the birth [of Damodara] shone forth; when the Master was in such a state, [his] glory arose on earth.

*Note.* *Dvyakṣara*, a "two-consonant" verse: the whole verse uses only the consonants *bh* and *v* (a kind of *citra-kāvya*). The translation follows the edition's Sanskrit commentary: "*bhāva* is existence; its *abhāva* is the absence of Sri Damodara; *abhi-bhāva* is the state of separation on all sides; *abhibhava* is being overcome by it; in this state *bhavaḥ*, the birth [of Damodara], shone forth, and on earth there was *vaibhavam*, honour. The sense: he in separation from whom the Lord becomes agitated — his birth is fruitful, and honour is his." The commentary adds: "From here on there follows one verse each on one, two, three and more consonants."

### Verse 18

ततः किञ्चिद्विलम्बेन मिलितोऽभूत् स भूसुरः ।
प्रभुराविष्टचित्तोऽसौ तं दृष्ट्वा कुपितोऽभवत् ॥१८॥

*tataḥ kiñcid vilambena milito 'bhūt sa bhūsuraḥ |*
*prabhur āviṣṭa-citto 'sau taṁ dṛṣṭvā kupito 'bhavat ||18||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *kiñcit* — with a slight; *vilambena* — delay; *militaḥ abhūt* — joined [them]; *saḥ* — that; *bhūsuraḥ* — brahmana (lit. god on earth); *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *āviṣṭa* — absorbed [in feeling]; *cittaḥ* — [whose] heart [was]; *asau* — He; *tam* — him; *dṛṣṭvā* — seeing; *kupitaḥ* — angry; *abhavat* — became.

**18.** Then, after a slight delay, that brahmana joined [them]; the Lord, His heart absorbed [in feeling], became angry on seeing him.

*Note.* The Lord's "anger" (*kupita*) here is a play of love with His eternal associate, not a worldly emotion: the Lord is not subject to anger, and Karnapura himself names the cause in verse 19 — "out of love" (*praṇayāt*).

### Verse 19

तं तु गीतापुस्तिकया पृष्ठे भूयो जघान सः ।
निष्पिपेष पदाघातैः प्रणयात् प्रणयाम्बुधिः ॥१९॥

*taṁ tu gītā-pustikayā pṛṣṭhe bhūyo jaghāna saḥ |*
*niṣpipeṣa padāghātaiḥ praṇayāt praṇayāmbudhiḥ ||19||*

*Word for word:* *tam tu* — him; *gītā* — of songs (?); *pustikayā* — with a little book; *pṛṣṭhe* — on the back; *bhūyaḥ* — many times; *jaghāna* — struck; *saḥ* — He; *niṣpipeṣa* — pummelled; *pada* — of the feet; *āghātaiḥ* — with blows; *praṇayāt* — out of love; *praṇaya* — of love; *ambudhiḥ* — the Ocean.

**19.** And He, the Ocean of love, out of love struck him many times on the back with a little book of songs and pummelled him with kicks.

*Note.* *Gītā-pustikā* is either "a little book of the Gita" or "a little book of songs". There is no such episode in the Chaitanya-charitamrita. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 20

इत्थं प्रविश्य प्रासादं दृष्ट्वा श्रीपुरुषोत्तमम् ।
नत्वा स्तुत्वा च चलितुं मनश्चक्रे कृपानिधिः ॥२०॥

*itthaṁ praviśya prāsādaṁ dṛṣṭvā śrī-puruṣottamam |*
*natvā stutvā ca calituṁ manaś cakre kṛpā-nidhiḥ ||20||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *praviśya* — having entered; *prāsādam* — the temple; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *śrī-puruṣottamam* — Sri Purushottama; *natvā* — having bowed down; *stutvā* — having praised; *ca* — and; *calitum* — to set out; *manaḥ cakre* — resolved; *kṛpā-nidhiḥ* — the Treasure-house of Mercy.

**20.** Having thus entered the temple, seen Sri Purushottama, bowed down and offered praise [to Him], the Treasure-house of Mercy resolved to set out.

### Verse 21

की र्त्त नं च क्रि रे के च स मु त्सु क म नो ल याः ।
× × × × × × × × × × × × × × × ×
न र्त्त नं च क्रि रे के च स मु त्सु क म नो ल याः ॥२१॥
(गोमूत्रिका बन्धः)

*kīrttanaṁ cakrire ke ca samutsuka-mano-layāḥ |*
*narttanaṁ cakrire ke ca samutsuka-mano-layāḥ ||21||*
*(gomūtrikā-bandhaḥ)*

*Word for word:* *kīrttanam* — kirtana; *cakrire* — performed; *ke ca* — some; *samutsuka* — in longing; *manaḥ* — of the hearts; *layāḥ* — [whose] absorption [was]; *narttanam* — dancing; *cakrire* — performed; *ke ca* — others; *samutsuka-mano-layāḥ* — their hearts absorbed in longing.

**21.** Some, their hearts absorbed in longing, sang kirtana; others, their hearts absorbed in longing, danced.

*Note.* *Gomūtrikā-bandha*, "the pattern of a cow's urine trail": the verse is written out in two lines, syllable by syllable, and read in a zigzag, alternating between the upper and the lower syllable (the crosses in the edition mark the turns of the zigzag). Here the two lines differ only in their first syllable (*kī-* / *na-*), so the zigzag reading yields the same text. The explanation follows the edition's Sanskrit commentary. The edition prints *samūt* for *samut*.

### Verse 22

काशीमिश्रमुखाः सर्वे पश्चात्पश्चात् समाययुः ।
समनुव्रजतस्तांस्तान् विससर्ज कृपानिधिः ॥२२॥

*kāśīmiśra-mukhāḥ sarve paścāt paścāt samāyayuḥ |*
*samanuvrajatas tāṁs tān visasarja kṛpā-nidhiḥ ||22||*

*Word for word:* *kāśīmiśra* — by Kashi Mishra; *mukhāḥ* — headed; *sarve* — all; *paścāt paścāt* — behind, behind; *samāyayuḥ* — came along; *samanuvrajataḥ* — following [Him]; *tān tān* — all of them (lit. them, them); *visasarja* — sent back; *kṛpā-nidhiḥ* — the Treasure-house of Mercy.

**22.** All, headed by Kashi Mishra, came along behind [Him]; the Treasure-house of Mercy sent back all those who were following [Him].

*Note.* In the edition the second and third padas are each one syllable short; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *paścāt paścāt samāyayuḥ / samanuvrajatas tāṁs tān*, and this reading is adopted.

### Verse 23

निशावसाने तैरेतैः कीर्त्तयद्भिर्मुहुर्मुहुः ।
प्रतस्थे गानकलया लोलः श्रीगौरसुन्दरः ॥२३॥

*niśāvasāne tair etaiḥ kīrttayadbhir muhur muhuḥ |*
*pratasthe gāna-kalayā lolaḥ śrī-gaurasundaraḥ ||23||*

*Word for word:* *niśā* — of the night; *avasāne* — at the end; *taiḥ etaiḥ* — with those; *kīrttayadbhiḥ* — singing kirtana; *muhuḥ muhuḥ* — again and again; *pratasthe* — set out; *gāna* — of singing; *kalayā* — by the art; *lolaḥ* — stirred; *śrī-gaurasundaraḥ* — Sri Gaurasundara.

**23.** At the end of the night Sri Gaurasundara, stirred by the art of singing, set out [on the journey] with those who were singing kirtana again and again.

### Verse 24

गोविन्दो जगदानन्दः श्रीदामोदरपण्डितः ।
यतिश्रेष्ठपुरीस्वामी कीर्त्तयन्तः समाययुः ॥२४॥

*govindo jagadānandaḥ śrī-dāmodara-paṇḍitaḥ |*
*yati-śreṣṭha-purī-svāmī kīrttayantaḥ samāyayuḥ ||24||*

*Word for word:* *govindaḥ* — Govinda; *jagadānandaḥ* — Jagadananda; *śrī-dāmodara-paṇḍitaḥ* — Sri Damodara Pandita; *yati-śreṣṭha* — the best of ascetics; *purī-svāmī* — Puri Svami; *kīrttayantaḥ* — singing kirtana; *samāyayuḥ* — went along.

**24.** Govinda, Jagadananda, Sri Damodara Pandita and Puri Svami, the best of ascetics, went along [with Him], singing kirtana.

### Verse 25

ललल्लीलो ललल्लीलो लोलो लोलो ललल्ललः ।
लीलालोलोऽलिलीलालीं लीलालीं लोललां ललुः ॥२५॥
(एकाक्षरः)

*lalal-līlo lalal-līlo lolo lolo lalal-lalaḥ |*
*līlā-lolo 'li-līlālīṁ līlālīṁ lolalāṁ laluḥ ||25||*
*(ekākṣaraḥ)*

*Word for word:* (following the edition's commentary): *lalat* — shining; *līlaḥ* — [whose] pastime [of going to Vraja is]; *lalat* (= *laḍat*) — cast aside; *līlaḥ* — [whose] pastime [of living at Nilachala is]; *lolaḥ* — restless; *lolaḥ* — eager [to go to Vraja]; *lalat* — wishing; *lalaḥ* (= *laḍaḥ*) — [to send all the people away]; *līlā* — in play; *lolaḥ* — unsettled; *ali* — of bees; *līlā-ālīm* — [like] a series of sports; *lola* — the restless one; *lām* — holding back; *[ceṣṭā-]ālīm* — a series of [efforts] (?); *laluḥ* — [the devotees] made.

**25.** [The Lord], whose pastime [of going to Vraja] shone forth, who had cast aside the pastime [of living at Nilachala], restless, eager, wishing to send [everyone] away, was unsettled in His play; [and the devotees], like bees at their sport, made a series of efforts to hold back the restless One.

*Note.* *Ekākṣara*, a "one-consonant" verse: the whole verse uses only the consonant *l* (*ḍ* and *l* being treated as identical). The sense follows the edition's Sanskrit commentary: as bees do not abandon a flower swaying in the wind but try to settle on it, so Govinda, Damodara and the others did not leave the departing Shachinandana but tried to hold Him back. *Laluḥ* is the perfect of *lā*, "to take, to hold". The second *līlālīm* is taken as "a series of [efforts]" (the commentary's *ceṣṭā-ālīm*, "a series of actions") (?). In the edition the second line has 13 syllables instead of 16; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *līlālolo 'li-līlālīṁ līlālīṁ lolalāṁ laluḥ*, and the repeated *līlālīṁ* is restored accordingly.

### Verse 26

ततोऽनु दोलामारुह्य श्रीरामानन्दरायकः ।
एतदीयाश्च ये चान्ये समेतास्ते त आययुः ॥२६॥

*tato 'nu dolām āruhya śrī-rāmānanda-rāyakaḥ |*
*etadīyāś ca ye cānye sametās te ta āyayuḥ ||26||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ anu* — after that; *dolām* — a palanquin; *āruhya* — having mounted; *śrī-rāmānanda-rāyakaḥ* — Sri Ramananda Raya; *etadīyāḥ* — his [people]; *ca* — and; *ye* — who; *ca anye* — and others; *sametāḥ* — assembled; *te te* — all of them (lit. they, they); *āyayuḥ* — came.

**26.** After that Sri Ramananda Raya [came], having mounted a palanquin; and his people, and all the others who had assembled, came as well.

*Note.* *Te ta āyayuḥ* stands for *te te āyayuḥ* (by sandhi the final *e* before a vowel becomes *a*).

### Verse 27

श्रुत्वा सर्वे जनास्तत्र स्त्रीपुमांसः समन्ततः ।
हरिं वदेति सोत्कण्ठं वदन्तो भूय आययुः ॥२७॥

*śrutvā sarve janās tatra strī-pumāṁsaḥ samantataḥ |*
*hariṁ vadeti sotkaṇṭhaṁ vadanto bhūya āyayuḥ ||27||*

*Word for word:* *śrutvā* — having heard; *sarve* — all; *janāḥ* — the people; *tatra* — there; *strī-pumāṁsaḥ* — women and men; *samantataḥ* — from all sides; *harim vada* — "say 'Hari'"; *iti* — thus; *sa-utkaṇṭham* — with longing; *vadantaḥ* — saying; *bhūyaḥ* — in great numbers; *āyayuḥ* — came.

**27.** Having heard [of this], all the people there, women and men, came from all sides in great numbers, saying with longing, "Say 'Hari'!"

*Note.* *Hariṁ vada* is a Sanskrit rendering of the Bengali "Hari bol!".

### Verse 28

ततः समुदिते भानौ भानुकोटिसमप्रभः ।
प्रातःकृत्यं चकारासौ तैरेतैर्निजभक्तकैः ॥२८॥

*tataḥ samudite bhānau bhānu-koṭi-sama-prabhaḥ |*
*prātaḥ-kṛtyaṁ cakārāsau tair etair nija-bhaktakaiḥ ||28||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *samudite* — [when] had risen; *bhānau* — the sun; *bhānu* — of suns; *koṭi* — to millions; *sama* — equal; *prabhaḥ* — [whose] effulgence [is]; *prātaḥ* — morning; *kṛtyam* — duties; *cakāra* — performed; *asau* — He; *taiḥ etaiḥ* — with those; *nija* — His own; *bhaktakaiḥ* — devotees.

**28.** Then, when the sun had risen, He whose effulgence equals that of millions of suns performed His morning duties together with those devotees of His own.

### Verse 29

स तत्र गमनारम्भे नतत्रात्रा न नाबबौ ।
पवित्राङ्घ्रिजनानन्दं भवित्रागमनाननम् ॥२९॥
(मुरजबन्धः)

*sa tatra gamanārambhe natatrātrā(ḥ) na nābabau |*
*pavitrāṅghri-janānandaṁ bhavitrāgamanānanam ||29||*
*(muraja-bandhaḥ)*

*Word for word:* (following the edition's commentary): *saḥ* — He; *tatra* — then; *gamana* — of the journey; *ārambhe* — at the beginning; *nata* — of the humble; *trātṛ* — of the protectors; *trāḥ* — the protector; *na na ābabau* — did not not go (= did go); *pavitra* — pure; *aṅghri-jana* — to the servants of [His] feet; *ānandam* — joy [giving]; *bhavitra* — auspicious; *āgamana* — return; *ānanam* — [whose] face [promised].

**29.** At the beginning of the journey He, the protector [even] of the protectors of the humble, could not but set out — [and He set out] giving pure joy to the servants of His feet, His face [promising] an auspicious return.

*Note.* *Muraja-bandha*: a verse whose syllables, written out in a grid, form the pattern of a *muraja* drum. The hardest part is analysed by the edition's Sanskrit commentary: *natatrātrāḥ na na ābabau*; *aṅghri-janāḥ* — "the servants of the feet" (a *karmadhāraya* with the middle member elided); *na ābabau na* — "it is not that He did not go: He went indeed". The sense: at the very start of His departure He gave the devotees joy, strengthened their hope of His return, and went quickly. The edition has *natatrātrā* without the visarga.

### Verse 30

प्रभाते पृष्ठतो दृष्ट्वा प्रहारस्य च लक्षणम् ।
दामोदरस्य पिदधे वस्त्रेणैव पुरीप्रभुः ॥३०॥

*prabhāte pṛṣṭhato dṛṣṭvā prahārasya ca lakṣaṇam |*
*dāmodarasya pidadhe vastreṇaiva purī-prabhuḥ ||30||*

*Word for word:* *prabhāte* — at dawn; *pṛṣṭhataḥ* — on the back; *dṛṣṭvā* — seeing; *prahārasya* — of the blow; *ca* — and; *lakṣaṇam* — the mark; *dāmodarasya* — of Damodara; *pidadhe* — covered; *vastreṇa eva* — with cloth; *purī-prabhuḥ* — Puri Prabhu.

**30.** At dawn, seeing the mark of the blow on Damodara's back, Puri Prabhu covered it with cloth.

*Note.* Puri Prabhu is presumably Paramananda Puri (cf. 12, 24).

### Verse 31

कियद्दूरं ततो गत्वा विरराम महाप्रभुः ।
श्रीरामानन्दरायेण प्रणयद्वन्द्ववान्मिथः ॥३१॥

*kiyad dūraṁ tato gatvā virarāma mahāprabhuḥ |*
*śrī-rāmānanda-rāyeṇa praṇaya-dvandvavān mithaḥ ||31||*

*Word for word:* *kiyat* — some; *dūram* — distance; *tataḥ* — then; *gatvā* — having gone; *virarāma* — stopped; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu; *śrī-rāmānanda-rāyeṇa* — with Sri Ramananda Raya; *praṇaya* — of love; *dvandvavān* — engaged in a dispute; *mithaḥ* — with each other.

**31.** Having then gone some distance, Mahaprabhu stopped, engaging with Sri Ramananda Raya in a dispute of love with each other.

### Verse 32

स त्यक्ता गच्छता तेन प्रभुनानुनयैर्बहु ।
तर्पितोऽपि न वै तृप्तिं जगाम क्षणमप्युत ॥३२॥

*sa tyakto (tyaktā?) gacchatā tena prabhuṇānunayair bahu |*
*tarpito 'pi na vai tṛptiṁ jagāma kṣaṇam apy uta ||32||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ* — he; *tyaktaḥ* — left behind; *gacchatā* — departing; *tena* — by that; *prabhuṇā* — by the Lord; *anunayaiḥ* — with conciliatory words; *bahu* — many; *tarpitaḥ* — consoled; *api* — although; *na vai* — not at all; *tṛptim* — consolation; *jagāma* — found; *kṣaṇam api* — even for a moment; *uta* — indeed.

**32.** Left behind by the departing Lord, he, though consoled with many conciliatory words, found no consolation even for a moment.

*Note.* The edition has *tyaktā*; read *tyaktaḥ* (the metre is the same). The Devanagari also has प्रभुना (*prabhunā*) for *prabhuṇā*.

### Verse 33

मनोज्ञदृङ्नामनोज्ञविभ्रमभ्रमणाकुलः ।
मनोज्ञदृङ्नामनोज्ञविभ्रमभ्रमणाकुलः ॥३३॥

*manojña-dṛṅ-nāmanojña-vibhrama-bhramaṇākulaḥ |*
*manojña-dṛṅ nāma no jña-vibhrama-bhramaṇākulaḥ ||33||*

*Word for word:* (following the edition's commentary). First line: *manojña* — on the Charming One; *dṛk* — [whose] gaze [was fixed]; *na-amanojña* — by no means uncharming; *vibhrama* — of grace; *bhramaṇa* — by the wandering; *ākulaḥ* — agitated. Second line: *manojña* — intimate; *dṛk* — [whose] gaze [is]; *nāma* — evidently; *no* — not; *jña* — of the knowing; *vibhrama* — the special delusion [causing]; *bhramaṇa* — by [such] wandering; *ākulaḥ* — bewildered.

**33.** He whose gaze was fixed on the Charming One was agitated by His wandering, full of captivating grace; [yet] he, whose gaze was intimate, was evidently not bewildered by that wandering which causes delusion [even] in those who know.

*Note.* The two lines sound identical (*yamaka*) and differ only in the division into words. The subject is Ramananda (continuing from verse 32). The commentary: "Ramananda, following the Lord, did not cause the wise sorrow."

### Verse 34

स तु प्रेमास्पदस्यास्य रामानन्दो महानिधिः ।
तदलोकनदुःखेन कथङ्कारं भविष्यति ॥३४॥
('करिष्यति' पाठान्तरं)

*sa tu premāspadasyāsya rāmānando mahānidhiḥ |*
*tad-alokana-duḥkhena kathaṅkāraṁ bhaviṣyati ('kariṣyati') ||34||*

*Word for word:* *saḥ tu* — and he; *prema* — of love; *āspadasya* — of the object; *asya* — of this; *rāmānandaḥ* — Ramananda; *mahā-nidhiḥ* — a great treasure-house; *tat* — Him; *alokana* — from not seeing; *duḥkhena* — with sorrow; *kathaṅkāram* — how; *bhaviṣyati* — will [live].

**34.** And Ramananda, a great treasure-house [of love] — how will he [live] in sorrow at not seeing this object of his love?

*Note.* A variant reading given in the edition: *kariṣyati*, "how will he act".

### Verse 35

ततो महाप्रसादौघः सद्यस्तत्र चतुर्विधः ।
वाणीनाथेन प्रहितो मिलितोऽभूदनेकशः ॥३५॥

*tato mahāprasādaughaḥ sadyas tatra catur-vidhaḥ |*
*vāṇīnāthena prahito milito 'bhūd anekaśaḥ ||35||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *mahā-prasāda* — of mahaprasada; *oghaḥ* — an abundance; *sadyaḥ* — at once; *tatra* — there; *catuḥ-vidhaḥ* — of four kinds; *vāṇīnāthena* — by Vaninatha; *prahitaḥ* — sent; *militaḥ abhūt* — arrived; *anekaśaḥ* — in great quantity.

**35.** Then an abundance of mahaprasada of four kinds, sent by Vaninatha, at once arrived there in great quantity.

*Note.* The four kinds of food are those that are chewed, swallowed, licked and drunk. Vaninatha (Pattanayaka) is the brother of Ramananda Raya.

### Verse 36

नीलाचलात् समायान्तं सद्यः श्रीमदनूत्तमम् ।
महाप्रसादं दृष्ट्वासौ मुमुदे परमप्रभुः ॥३६॥

*nīlācalāt samāyāntaṁ sadyaḥ śrīmad-anūttamam |*
*mahāprasādaṁ dṛṣṭvāsau mumude parama-prabhuḥ ||36||*

*Word for word:* *nīlācalāt* — from Nilachala; *samāyāntam* — arriving; *sadyaḥ* — just now; *śrīmat* — splendid; *anūttamam* — unsurpassed; *mahā-prasādam* — the mahaprasada; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *asau* — He; *mumude* — rejoiced; *parama-prabhuḥ* — the supreme Lord.

**36.** Seeing the splendid, unsurpassed mahaprasada that had just arrived from Nilachala, the supreme Lord rejoiced.

### Verse 37

नानाना नुनि नानेने नाना नूननू ननु ।
नाना नूने नाननान्नोने नो नान ननुन्ननु ॥३७॥
(पुनरेकाक्षरः)

*nānānā nuni nānene nānā nūnanū nanu |*
*nānā nūne nānanānnone no nāna nanunnanu ||37||*
*(punar ekākṣaraḥ)*

*Word for word:* (following the commentary): *nanu* — oh!; *nānānā* — a certain man among many; *nuni* — humbly (?); *ā-aṇūn* — quite small [offerings]; *nānā* — manifold; *ina* — to the Lord; *inān* — equal (= the Lord's prasada); *anaṇūn anu* — considering [them] abundant; *nānā-anūne* — in regard to variety and abundance; *ānana* — of the mouth; *anna* — of the food (= the nectar of the lips); *ūne* — in a [supposed] deficiency; *no* — not; *nānā* — "[it is] little"; *nut* — saying; *na* — was not.

**37.** Oh! A certain man among many, seeing the manifold [gifts of prasada], equal to the Lord, considered them abundant, though they were quite small: neither as to their variety and quantity, nor on the ground that they fell short of the nectar of His lips, did he say, "[It is] little."

*Note.* Again an *ekākṣara*: the whole verse uses only the consonant *n* (*ṇ* being treated as equal to *n*). The sense follows the edition's Sanskrit commentary: the Lord's prasada is equal to the Lord Himself, and so even a small quantity of it was honoured by all as abundant. The commentary quotes the Brihad-bhagavatamrita: "What is offered to the Lord of the world — food, drink and the rest — is unchanging like Brahman: as Vishnu is, so is it." *Ina* — "lord, master"; *inena tulyaḥ inaḥ* — "[the prasada,] equal to the Lord". The translation is tentative (?). Metre: the second pada (*nānā nūnanū nanu*) has only seven syllables (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

**The edition's word division and prose order:** *nanu nānānā nuni ā-aṇūn nānā-inenān anaṇūn anu | nānānūne na ānana-anna-ūne no nānā nut na nanu.*

### Verse 38

महाप्रसादोपयोगं कृत्वा तत्र कृपानिधिः ।
विश्रम्य च क्षणं हर्षात् प्रतस्थे तैः समं पुनः ॥३८॥

*mahāprasādopayogaṁ kṛtvā tatra kṛpā-nidhiḥ |*
*viśramya ca kṣaṇaṁ harṣāt pratasthe taiḥ samaṁ punaḥ ||38||*

*Word for word:* *mahā-prasāda* — of the mahaprasada; *upayogam* — partaking; *kṛtvā* — having done; *tatra* — there; *kṛpā-nidhiḥ* — the Treasure-house of Mercy; *viśramya* — having rested; *ca* — and; *kṣaṇam* — for a moment; *harṣāt* — joyfully; *pratasthe* — set out; *taiḥ samam* — with them; *punaḥ* — again.

**38.** Having partaken of the mahaprasada there and rested for a moment, the Treasure-house of Mercy joyfully set out again together with them.

### Verse 39

कञ्चिद्देशं समासाद्य स्थितं तं सर्व एव हि ।
द्रष्टुं समन्तादौत्सुक्यादाययौ चित्रमेव तत् ॥३९॥

*kañcid deśaṁ samāsādya sthitaṁ taṁ sarva eva hi |*
*draṣṭuṁ samantād autsukyād āyayau citram eva tat ||39||*

*Word for word:* *kañcit* — some; *deśam* — place; *samāsādya* — having reached; *sthitam* — staying; *tam* — Him; *sarvaḥ eva* — everyone; *hi* — indeed; *draṣṭum* — to see; *samantāt* — from all around; *autsukyāt* — out of eagerness; *āyayau* — came; *citram* — a wonder; *eva* — indeed; *tat* — that.

**39.** Whenever He reached some place and stopped there, everyone came from all around, eager to see Him — that was a wonder indeed!

### Verse 40

विरमत्येव ये वास्मिन् कृष्टा आसन् समन्ततः ।
तत्रत्या वायुना सार्द्धं धैर्यसौहित्यसौरभैः ॥४०॥

*viramaty eva ye vāsmin kṛṣṭā āsan samantataḥ |*
*tatratyā vāyunā sārdhaṁ dhairya-sauhitya-saurabhaiḥ ||40||*

*Word for word:* *viramati* — stopping; *eva* — just; *ye* — who; *vā* — indeed; *asmin* — [when] He; *kṛṣṭāḥ* — drawn; *āsan* — were; *samantataḥ* — from all around; *tatratyāḥ* — the local [people]; *vāyunā sārdham* — together with the wind; *dhairya* — of steadfastness; *sauhitya* — [and] kindliness; *saurabhaiḥ* — by the fragrances.

**40.** As soon as He stopped, the local people [living] all around were drawn, together with the wind, by the fragrances of His steadfastness and kindliness.

### Verse 41

लीलालोलालिललना ललन्नलिनलालनैः ।
नलाल ललनालीनां लीलां लाननिलो ललन् ॥४१॥
(द्व्यक्षरः)

*līlā-lolāli-lalanā lalan nalina-lālanaiḥ |*
*nalāla (? calāla) lalanālīnāṁ līlāṁ lān anilo lalan ||41||*
*(dvyakṣaraḥ)*

*Word for word:* (following the edition's commentary): *līlā* — in play; *lola* — restless; *ali* — of the bees; *lalanāḥ* — the female companions; *lalan* — desiring; *nalina* — of the lotuses; *lālanaiḥ* — by the swaying; *lalanā-ālīnām* — of those clinging to [their] companions; *līlām* — the play; *lān* — taking; *anilaḥ* — the wind; *lalan* — desiring [= well pleased]; *nalāla* (?) — moved.

**41.** The wind, swaying the lotuses, desiring the female companions of the bees, restless in their play, and taking on the play proper to those who cling to their companions, moved along, well pleased (?).

*Note.* A *dvyakṣara*: the verse uses only two consonants, *l* and *n*. The commentary: "*anilaḥ* — the wind; *nalina-lālanaiḥ* — by swaying the lotuses: as a husband beckons his playful wife with his hand, so the wind, desiring the bees' companions, moved, swaying the lotuses, [its] hands." The commentary explains the verb *nalāla* as *cacāla*, "moved", by the rule that *ḍa* and *la* are identical (from the root *laḍ*); the passage is obscure (?). The conjecture *calāla* recorded in the IAST line would break the two-consonant scheme. Metre: both lines are regular (the first pada is a *na-vipulā*). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 42

पथि प्रेमाविष्कृतिभिः कृतिभिस्तैः समं व्रजन् ।
मज्जति स्मैष परमामानन्दामृतदीर्घिकाम् ॥४२॥

*pathi premāviṣkṛtibhiḥ kṛtibhis taiḥ samaṁ vrajan |*
*majjati smaiṣa paramām ānandāmṛta-dīrghikām ||42||*

*Word for word:* *pathi* — on the road; *prema* — of love; *āviṣkṛtibhiḥ* — with manifestations; *kṛtibhiḥ* — accomplished; *taiḥ* — with those; *samam* — together; *vrajan* — going; *majjati sma* — plunged; *eṣaḥ* — He; *paramām* — into the supreme; *ānanda* — of bliss; *amṛta* — of the nectar; *dīrghikām* — long pond.

**42.** Going along the road together with those accomplished [companions], amid manifestations of love, He plunged into the supreme long pond of the nectar of bliss.

*Note.* A chime of sounds: *premāviṣkṛtibhiḥ kṛtibhiḥ*.

### Verse 43

अथ वीक्ष्य द्रुमं श्रेष्ठं धावन्नारादवारितः ।
स्कन्धमुत्प्लुत्य धृत्वा च लम्बमानः श्रियं दधे ॥४३॥

*atha vīkṣya drumaṁ śreṣṭhaṁ dhāvann ārād avāritaḥ |*
*skandham utplutya dhṛtvā ca lambamānaḥ śriyaṁ dadhe ||43||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *vīkṣya* — having seen; *drumam* — a tree; *śreṣṭham* — splendid; *dhāvan* — running; *ārāt* — from afar; *avāritaḥ* — unrestrained; *skandham* — a bough; *utplutya* — having leapt up; *dhṛtvā* — having caught hold of; *ca* — and; *lambamānaḥ* — hanging; *śriyam* — beauty; *dadhe* — displayed.

**43.** Then, seeing a splendid tree, He ran to it from afar, unrestrained, leapt up, caught hold of a bough and, hanging from it, displayed [great] beauty.

### Verse 44

आलिलिङ्ग तरुं भूयो लोचनाम्बुभिराप्लुतः ।
कं वा केन प्रकारेण नोद्दधार महाप्रभुः ॥४४॥

*ālilinga taruṁ bhūyo locanāmbubhir āplutaḥ |*
*kaṁ vā kena prakāreṇa noddadhāra mahāprabhuḥ ||44||*

*Word for word:* *ālilinga* — embraced; *tarum* — the tree; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *locana* — of the eyes; *ambubhiḥ* — with the waters; *āplutaḥ* — bathed; *kam* — whom; *vā* — indeed; *kena* — by what; *prakāreṇa* — means; *na uddadhāra* — did not deliver; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu.

**44.** Bathed in the waters of His eyes, He embraced the tree again. Whom indeed, and by what means, did Mahaprabhu not deliver?

### Verse 45

का के ने व व ने के का
ला व के न न के व ला ।
शु द्धा सा र र सा द्धा शु
नु ति र सु सु रा ति नु ॥४५॥
(प्रतिलोमानुलोमपादः)

*kā kene va vane kekā*
*lāvakena na kevalā |*
*śuddhāsāra-rasāddhāśu-*
*nuti-rā su-surātinu ||45||*
*(pratilomānuloma-pādaḥ)*

*Word for word:* *kākena iva* — as by a crow; *vane* — in the forest; *kekā* — the peacock's cry; *lāvakena* — by the lāvaka bird; *na kevalā* — not alone (= accompanied); *śuddha* — pure; *āsāra* — of the showers (of the rainy season); *rasā* — fond; *addhā* — truly; *āśu* — at once; *nuti* — praise; *rā* — giving; *su-surā* — sweet intoxication; *atinu* — surpassing in praise.

**45.** In the forest the peacock's cry — not alone, but [joined] by [the call of] the lāvaka bird, as if by a crow — fond of the pure showers, truly and at once giving praise, surpassed in praise [even] sweet intoxication (?).

*Note.* A *pratilomānuloma-pāda*: each pada reads the same from left to right and from right to left (a palindrome): *kā ke ne va va ne ke kā*, and so on. The printed syllables *kā kene va* are taken as *kākena iva*. The translation follows the edition's Sanskrit commentary; the sense is tentative (?). The lāvaka is a kind of quail. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

**The commentary's word division of the second half:** *śuddha-āsāra-rasā addhā āśu nuti-rā su-surā-atinu.*

### Verse 46

वृन्दावनद्रुमानित्थमालिङ्गयति विह्वलः ।
तथालिलिङ्ग स तरुं यथा चूर्णायते मुहुः ॥४६॥

*vṛndāvana-drumān ittham āliṅgayati vihvalaḥ |*
*tathālilinga sa taruṁ yathā cūrṇāyate muhuḥ ||46||*

*Word for word:* *vṛndāvana* — of Vrindavana; *drumān* — the trees; *ittham* — thus; *āliṅgayati* — embraces; *vihvalaḥ* — overwhelmed; *tathā* — so; *ālilinga* — embraced; *saḥ* — He; *tarum* — the tree; *yathā* — that; *cūrṇāyate* — is crumbling to powder; *muhuḥ* — again and again.

**46.** Thus, overwhelmed, He embraces [these trees as] the trees of Vrindavana; and He embraced the tree so [hard] that it seemed again and again about to crumble to powder.

### Verse 47

अधः कण्टकसंकीर्णे निपतिष्यन्तमञ्जसा ।
भिया पुरिप्रभृतयो जगृहुर्वरबाहुभिः ॥४७॥

*adhaḥ kaṇṭaka-saṅkīrṇe nipatiṣyantam añjasā |*
*bhiyā puri-prabhṛtayo jagṛhur vara-bāhubhiḥ ||47||*

*Word for word:* *adhaḥ* — down; *kaṇṭaka* — with thorns; *saṅkīrṇe* — onto [a place] strewn; *nipatiṣyantam* — about to fall; *añjasā* — at once; *bhiyā* — in alarm; *puri* — Puri; *prabhṛtayaḥ* — and the others; *jagṛhuḥ* — caught [Him]; *vara* — strong; *bāhubhiḥ* — with arms.

**47.** When He was about to fall down onto [ground] strewn with thorns, [Paramananda] Puri and the others, in alarm, at once caught Him with their strong arms.

### Verse 48

ऊचेऽथ पश्य पश्यायं कृष्णचन्द्रोऽभितोऽभितः ।
प्रतिद्रुमं विलसति जगत्येतन्मयीक्ष्यते ॥४८॥

*ūce 'tha paśya paśyāyaṁ kṛṣṇacandro 'bhito 'bhitaḥ |*
*pratidrumaṁ vilasati jagaty etan mayīkṣyate ||48||*

*Word for word:* *ūce* — said; *atha* — then; *paśya paśya* — look, look; *ayam* — here [is]; *kṛṣṇacandraḥ* — Krishnachandra; *abhitaḥ abhitaḥ* — everywhere around; *pratidrumam* — in every tree; *vilasati* — sports; *jagatī* — the world; *etat-mayī* — consisting of Him; *īkṣyate* — is seen.

**48.** Then He said: "Look, look! Here is Krishnachandra all around, sporting in every tree! The world is seen to consist of Him."

*Note.* *Jagaty etan mayīkṣyate* is divided *jagatī etan-mayī īkṣyate*, "the world is seen as consisting of Him": *mayā* + *īkṣyate* would give *mayekṣyate*, so *mayī* must be the feminine of the suffix *-maya*, agreeing with *jagatī*. *Paśyāyam* = *paśya ayam* (regular sandhi).

### Verse 49

अवपयोऽतिविमलमनन्तमसकृद्बभौ ।
निष्पङ्कं भूतलं चाथ चित्रचित्रा प्रभोर्गतिः ॥४९॥
(श्लोकावृत्तिः)

*avapayo 'tivimalam anantam asakṛd babhau |*
*niṣpaṅkaṁ bhūtalaṁ cātha citra-citrā prabhor gatiḥ ||49||*
*(ślokāvṛttiḥ)*

*Word for word:* *avapayaḥ* (?) — the water (?); *ati-vimalam* — exceedingly clear; *anantam* — boundless; *asakṛt* — constantly; *babhau* — shone; *niṣpaṅkam* — free of mud; *bhū-talam* — the surface of the earth; *ca* — and; *atha* — then; *citra-citrā* — most wonderful; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *gatiḥ* — the journey.

**49.** The water (?), exceedingly clear and boundless, shone constantly, and the surface of the earth [was] free of mud; and most wonderful then was the Lord's journey.

*Note.* The label *ślokāvṛtti* ("repetition of the verse") apparently means that the verse admits a second reading with a different word division (?); how it is meant is not explained. *Avapayaḥ* is unclear (?): the neuter adjectives *ativimalam anantam* seem to agree with *payaḥ*, "water", but *ava-* remains unexplained; the first line may also be referred to the sky or to the earth (?). Clear water and dry earth mark autumn, the season after the rains (cf. 4–5). Metre: the first pada is irregular — its second and third syllables (*-va-pa-*) are both light. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 50

अधिकं शुशुभे तत्र विजयेन प्रभोरसौ ।
विकसत्काशकुसुमसुस्मिता सुरसा शरत् ॥५०॥

*adhikaṁ śuśubhe tatra vijayena prabhor asau |*
*vikasat-kāśa-kusuma-susmitā surasā śarat ||50||*

*Word for word:* *adhikam* — still more; *śuśubhe* — shone; *tatra* — then; *vijayena* — by the [triumphal] journey; *prabhoḥ* — of the Lord; *asau* — this; *vikasat* — blossoming; *kāśa* — of kasha grass; *kusuma* — with the flowers; *su-smitā* — sweetly smiling; *su-rasā* — rich in sap; *śarat* — autumn.

**50.** Through the Lord's triumphal journey this autumn — rich in sap, sweetly smiling with the blossoming flowers of the kasha grass — then shone still more beautifully.

*Note.* Kasha grass (*Saccharum spontaneum*) bears white plumes in autumn; in poetics whiteness is a "smile".

### Verse 51

भुवनेश्वर आगत्य ददर्श भुवनेश्वरम् ।
महाप्रसादं प्रोपास्य तत्रैव विरराम सः ॥५१॥

*bhuvaneśvara āgatya dadarśa bhuvaneśvaram |*
*mahāprasādaṁ propāsya tatraiva virarāma saḥ ||51||*

*Word for word:* *bhuvaneśvare* — at Bhubaneshvara; *āgatya* — having arrived; *dadarśa* — saw; *bhuvaneśvaram* — Bhuvaneshvara (Shiva); *mahā-prasādam* — the mahaprasada; *propāsya* — having honoured; *tatra eva* — right there; *virarāma* — stopped; *saḥ* — He.

**51.** Arriving at Bhubaneshvara, He saw Bhuvaneshvara [Shiva], honoured the mahaprasada and stopped right there [for the night].

*Note.* Bhubaneshvara is both the town and its deity of the same name — Shiva as Lingaraja, the "Lord of the Worlds". Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 16.98–99: Ramananda follows the Lord in a palanquin, Vaninatha sends prasada, and next morning the Lord comes to Bhubaneshvara.

### Verse 52

अन्येद्यू रजनीशेषे प्रतस्थे तैः समं प्रभुः ।
हरिदासं पुरः प्राप्याविशद्ग्रामं महाप्रभुः ॥५२॥

*anyedyū rajanī-śeṣe pratasthe taiḥ samaṁ prabhuḥ |*
*haridāsaṁ puraḥ prāpyāviśad grāmaṁ mahāprabhuḥ ||52||*

*Word for word:* *anyedyuḥ* — on the next day; *rajanī* — of the night; *śeṣe* — at the end; *pratasthe* — set out; *taiḥ samam* — with them; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *haridāsam* — Haridasa; *puraḥ* — ahead; *prāpya* — having met; *aviśat* — entered; *grāmam* — a village; *mahāprabhuḥ* — Mahaprabhu.

**52.** The next day, at the end of the night, the Lord set out with them; and meeting Haridasa ahead [of Him], Mahaprabhu entered a village.

*Note.* Which Haridasa and which village are meant is unclear; the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 16) does not mention this meeting. According to 54, Ramananda had prepared lodgings here in advance — apparently on his own land.

### Verse 53

सा र सा स र सा रं
र सा नू त न नू त ना ।
ना त नू त त नू सा र
रं सा सा र स सा र सा ॥५३॥
(प्रतिलोमानुलोमश्लोकः)

*sārasā sarasā (?) raṁ*
*rasā nūtana-nūtanā |*
*nātanūtatanū-sāra-*
*raṁsā sā rasa-sārasā ||53||*
*(pratilomānuloma-ślokaḥ)*

*Word for word:* *sārasā* — full of sarasa cranes; *sa-rasā* — full of water; *ram* (?) — (?); *rasā* — the earth; *nūtana-nūtanā* — new and ever new; *na-atanū-atanū* — of [things] embodied and unembodied (?); *sāra* — the essence; *raṁsā* (?) — bestowing; *sā* — she (autumn); *rasa* — with juices; *sārasā* — filled.

**53.** That [autumn] — a fresh, ever-fresh earth, full of water and of sarasa cranes, bestowing the essence on all things embodied and unembodied, filled with juices — [shone] (?).

*Note.* A *pratilomānuloma-śloka*: the whole verse, written out syllable by syllable, reads the same from the beginning and from the end. The word division is partly conjectural (?). As printed, the palindrome is imperfect: the first pada has only seven syllables (सा र सा स र सा रं), whereas the mirror image of the fourth (रं सा सा र स सा र सा) requires eight — सा र सा स र सा सा रं; and the fifth syllable of the second pada (*na* in *nūtana*) does not mirror the fourth syllable of the third (*ta*). Metre: apart from the short first pada, the verse is regular. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 54

तत्र नूतनगेहादि कारयित्वा निदेशतः ।
पुरा रामानन्दरायो निनाय प्रभुमञ्जसा ॥५४॥

*tatra nūtana-gehādi kārayitvā nideśataḥ |*
*purā rāmānanda-rāyo nināya prabhum añjasā ||54||*

*Word for word:* *tatra* — there; *nūtana* — a new; *geha* — house; *ādi* — and so on; *kārayitvā* — having had built; *nideśataḥ* — by [his] orders; *purā* — beforehand; *rāmānanda-rāyaḥ* — Ramananda Raya; *nināya* — led; *prabhum* — the Lord; *añjasā* — at once.

**54.** Ramananda Raya, who beforehand had by his orders had a new house and other [buildings] put up there, at once led the Lord [to it].

### Verse 55

लेपितं शुद्धमालोक्य गृहं तत्र कृपानिधिः ।
उवास परमप्रीत्या परमानन्दपूरिणा ॥५५॥

*lepitaṁ śuddham ālokya gṛhaṁ tatra kṛpā-nidhiḥ |*
*uvāsa parama-prītyā paramānanda-pūriṇā ||55||*

*Word for word:* *lepitam* — plastered; *śuddham* — clean; *ālokya* — having seen; *gṛham* — the house; *tatra* — there; *kṛpā-nidhiḥ* — the Treasure-house of Mercy; *uvāsa* — stayed; *parama* — with the greatest; *prītyā* — delight; *paramānanda-pūriṇā* — with Paramananda Puri.

**55.** Seeing the clean, freshly plastered house there, the Treasure-house of Mercy stayed in it with the greatest delight, together with Paramananda Puri.

*Note.* *Lepita* — [walls and floor] plastered with clay and cow dung, a purification of a dwelling. A possible play: *paramānanda-pūriṇā* also suggests "filled with supreme bliss".

### Verse 56

ततो नीलाचलादाशु समायातोऽभवन्मुहुः ।
महाप्रसादनिचयः स्वन्नपानकपिष्टकः ॥५६॥

*tato nīlācalād āśu samāyāto 'bhavan muhuḥ |*
*mahāprasāda-nicayaḥ sv-anna-pānaka-piṣṭakaḥ ||56||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *nīlācalāt* — from Nilachala; *āśu* — swiftly; *samāyātaḥ abhavat* — arrived; *muhuḥ* — again and again; *mahā-prasāda* — of mahaprasada; *nicayaḥ* — an abundance; *su-anna* — [with] fine rice; *pānaka* — drinks; *piṣṭakaḥ* — [and] cakes.

**56.** Then from Nilachala an abundance of mahaprasada — fine rice, drinks and cakes — arrived swiftly, again and again.

*Note.* The first syllables of the second half are damaged in the printed text; the reading given is a reconstruction (?). *Piṣṭaka* — rice cakes (Bengali *pitha*).

### Verse 57

यदाज्ञा ब्रह्मरुद्राद्यैराधाय शिरसीड्यते ।
किं तस्य विभवो लोकैर्ज्ञायते विभवो नु कैः ॥५७॥

*yad-ājñā brahma-rudrādyair ādhāya śirasīḍyate |*
*kiṁ tasya vibhavo lokair jñāyate vibhavo nu kaiḥ ||57||*

*Word for word:* *yat* — whose; *ājñā* — command; *brahma* — by Brahma; *rudra* — Rudra; *ādyaiḥ* — and the others; *ādhāya* — having placed; *śirasi* — on the head; *īḍyate* — is praised; *kim* — whether; *tasya* — His; *vibhavaḥ* — majesty; *lokaiḥ* — by people; *jñāyate* — is known; *vibhavaḥ* — majesty; *nu* — indeed; *kaiḥ* — by whom.

**57.** He whose command Brahma, Rudra and the others praise, placing it on their heads — can His majesty be known by people? By whom indeed [is His] majesty [known]?

### Verse 58

तं दृष्ट्वा परमप्रीतः प्रेम्णोपास्य च तैः समम् ।
श्रीरामानन्दरायेण कथया रजनीं ययौ ॥५८॥

*taṁ dṛṣṭvā parama-prītaḥ premṇopāsya ca taiḥ samam |*
*śrī-rāmānanda-rāyeṇa kathayā rajanīṁ yayau ||58||*

*Word for word:* *tam* — it (the prasada); *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *parama* — supremely; *prītaḥ* — pleased; *premṇā* — with love; *upāsya* — having honoured; *ca* — and; *taiḥ samam* — together with them; *śrī-rāmānanda-rāyeṇa* — with Sri Ramananda Raya; *kathayā* — in conversation; *rajanīm* — the night; *yayau* — spent.

**58.** Seeing it, He was supremely pleased; He honoured it with love together with them, and spent the night in conversation with Sri Ramananda Raya.

### Verse 59

एतेनैव समं नानाकथाकथनतत्परः ।
निनाय रजनीं नाथो रजनीनाथसुन्दरः ॥५९॥

*etenaiva samaṁ nānā-kathā-kathana-tat-paraḥ |*
*nināya rajanīṁ nātho rajanī-nātha-sundaraḥ ||59||*

*Word for word:* *etena eva samam* — together with him; *nānā* — of various; *kathā* — stories; *kathana* — to the telling; *tat-paraḥ* — wholly given; *nināya* — passed; *rajanīm* — the night; *nāthaḥ* — the Lord; *rajanī-nātha* — [as] the lord of the night (the moon); *sundaraḥ* — beautiful.

**59.** Wholly given to telling various stories together with him, the Lord, beautiful as the lord of the night, passed the night.

*Note.* A play on words: *rajanīṁ nātho rajanī-nātha-*, "the night … the Lord … the lord of the night".

### Verse 60

प्रभुश्च परमानन्दपुरी चापि पुरो ययौ ।
रामानन्दस्तु मतिमान् पश्चात् पश्चात् समाययौ ॥६०॥

*prabhuś ca paramānanda-purī cāpi puro yayau |*
*rāmānandas tu matimān paścāt paścāt samāyayau ||60||*

*Word for word:* *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *ca* — and; *paramānanda-purī* — Paramananda Puri; *ca api* — also; *puraḥ* — ahead; *yayau* — went; *rāmānandaḥ tu* — but Ramananda; *matimān* — wise; *paścāt paścāt* — behind, behind; *samāyayau* — followed.

**60.** The Lord and Paramananda Puri too went on ahead, while the wise Ramananda followed along behind [them].

### Verse 61

एवमेवं पथि चलन्मधुराधररोचिषा ।
जजाप निजनामानि करुणारससागरः ॥६१॥ (असंयोगः)

*evam evaṁ pathi calan madhurādhara-rociṣā |*
*jajāpa nija-nāmāni karuṇā-rasa-sāgaraḥ ||61|| (asaṁyogaḥ)*

*Word for word:* *evam evam* — thus, thus; *pathi* — on the road; *calan* — going; *madhura* — sweet; *adhara* — of the lips; *rociṣā* — with the radiance; *jajāpa* — chanted; *nija* — His own; *nāmāni* — names; *karuṇā* — of compassion; *rasa* — of the rasa; *sāgaraḥ* — the Ocean.

**61.** Thus, going along the road, the Ocean of the rasa of compassion chanted His own names, His sweet lips shining.

*Note.* An *asaṁyoga*: a verse without consonant clusters. Only at the word junction *calan madhura-* do *n* and *m* meet (written in the Devanagari as the ligature न्म).

### Verse 62

एवं व्रजन्नुपनदि वीक्ष्यावासं मनोरमम् ।
ऊचेऽनुगायन्मधुरं मधुराधरसुन्दरः ॥६२॥

*evaṁ vrajann upanadi vīkṣyāvāsaṁ manoramam |*
*ūce 'nugāyan madhuraṁ madhurādhara-sundaraḥ ||62||*

*Word for word:* *evam* — thus; *vrajan* — going; *upanadi* — by the river; *vīkṣya* — having seen; *āvāsam* — a lodging; *manoramam* — charming; *ūce* — said; *anugāyan* — singing; *madhuram* — sweetly; *madhura* — sweet; *adhara* — with lips; *sundaraḥ* — beautiful.

**62.** Going along thus and seeing a charming lodging by the river, He who is beautiful with sweet lips said, singing sweetly:

### Verse 63

अग्रे गच्छत यूयं तु कटके तत्र नीवृति ।
दर्शनं मम गोपीशप्रासादेषु भविष्यति ॥६३॥

*agre gacchata yūyaṁ tu kaṭake tatra nīvṛti |*
*darśanaṁ mama gopīśa-prāsādeṣu bhaviṣyati ||63||*

*Word for word:* *agre* — ahead; *gacchata* — go; *yūyam tu* — you; *kaṭake* — in Kataka; *tatra* — there; *nīvṛti* — in the country; *darśanam* — the sight; *mama* — of Me; *gopīśa* — of the Lord of the gopis; *prāsādeṣu* — in the temple; *bhaviṣyati* — will be.

**63.** "You go on ahead. There, in the country of Kataka, you will see Me [again] in the temple of the Lord of the gopis."

*Note.* Kataka (Cuttack) was then the capital of Orissa; the Lord of the gopis is Gopinatha, that is, Sakshi-gopala (cf. 11.79). In the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 16.100) the Lord at Kataka visits the temple of Gopala, and the brahmana Svapneshvara invites Him for a meal.

### Verse 64

इत्युक्तास्ते महात्मानः पुरीप्रभृतयस्तदा ।
प्रययुस्तत्र गौराङ्गो विशश्रामाथ केनचित् ॥६४॥

*ity uktās te mahātmānaḥ purī-prabhṛtayas tadā |*
*prayayus tatra gaurāṅgo viśaśrāmātha kenacit ||64||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *uktāḥ* — told; *te* — those; *mahā-ātmānaḥ* — great souls; *purī* — Puri; *prabhṛtayaḥ* — and the others; *tadā* — then; *prayayuḥ* — went off; *tatra* — there; *gaurāṅgaḥ* — Gauranga; *viśaśrāma* — rested; *atha* — and; *kenacit* — with someone.

**64.** Thus instructed, those great souls — Puri and the others — then went off, while Gauranga rested there with someone [of His companions].

*Note.* *Kenacit* may also mean "for a while" (?).

### Verse 65

आयाति करुणासिन्धुरिति श्रुत्वा गजेश्वरः ।
आज्ञया सकलं तीर्थं चकार करलालितम् ॥६५॥
(निरोष्ठ्यः)

*āyāti karuṇā-sindhur iti śrutvā gajeśvaraḥ |*
*ājñayā sakalaṁ tīrthaṁ cakāra kara-lālitam ||65||*
*(niroṣṭhyaḥ)*

*Word for word:* *āyāti* — is coming; *karuṇā* — of mercy; *sindhuḥ* — the Ocean; *iti* — thus; *śrutvā* — having heard; *gaja-īśvaraḥ* — the lord of elephants (the Gajapati); *ājñayā* — by [his] command; *sakalam* — every; *tīrtham* — landing-place; *cakāra* — made; *kara* — by hands; *lālitam* — tended.

**65.** Hearing, "The Ocean of Mercy is coming," the lord of elephants by his command had every landing-place tended by [his people's] hands.

*Note.* A *niroṣṭhya*: a verse without labial consonants (*p, ph, b, bh, m*; the anusvara is not counted). The semivowel *v* (in *śrutvā*, *gajeśvaraḥ*), being dento-labial, is evidently not reckoned as labial, nor is the vowel *u* (in *karuṇā*, *sindhuḥ*). The "lord of elephants" is the Gajapati, the title of the kings of Orissa — here Prataparudra. *Tīrtha* — a landing-place or ford for crossing a river. Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 16.112–116: the king orders houses and new boats to be made ready for the Lord at the crossings, and memorial pillars to be set up.

### Verse 66

सर्वाङ्गीनैरलङ्कारैर्माधुर्य्यौजःप्रसादवान् ।
गोपीनाथो रराजासौ वाग्विलासः कवेरिव ॥६६॥

*sarvāṅgīnair alaṅkārair mādhuryaujaḥ-prasādavān |*
*gopīnātho rarājāsau vāg-vilāsaḥ kaver iva ||66||*

*Word for word:* *sarva-aṅgīnaiḥ* — covering all the limbs; *alaṅkāraiḥ* — with ornaments; *mādhurya* — sweetness; *ojaḥ* — vigour; *prasāda* — [and] clarity; *vān* — possessing; *gopīnāthaḥ* — Gopinatha; *rarāja* — shone; *asau* — He; *vāk* — of words; *vilāsaḥ* — the play; *kaveḥ* — of a poet; *iva* — like.

**66.** Gopinatha, with ornaments covering all His limbs, possessing sweetness, vigour and clarity, shone like a poet's play of words.

*Note.* A double meaning: *alaṅkāra* is both "ornament" and "figure of speech", and *mādhurya*, *ojas* and *prasāda* are the three excellences (*guṇa*) of poetic diction. The edition's Sanskrit commentary explains: *mādhurya* is the delight that melts the heart; *ojas* is the brilliance that expands the heart (in the heroic, the loathsome and the furious rasas); *prasāda* is that which pervades the heart at once, as fire seizes dry wood.

### Verse 67

उत्कण्ठां तरुणीं प्राप्य निरन्तरनवां नवाम् ।
रराज राजा मधुरः सश्रीक इव चैत्रिकः ॥६७॥

*utkaṇṭhāṁ taruṇīṁ prāpya nirantara-navāṁ navām |*
*rarāja rājā madhuraḥ saśrīka iva caitrikaḥ ||67||*

*Word for word:* *utkaṇṭhām* — longing; *taruṇīm* — youthful (also: a young woman); *prāpya* — having attained; *nirantara* — continually; *navām navām* — new and ever new; *rarāja* — shone; *rājā* — the king; *madhuraḥ* — charming (also: vernal); *sa-śrīkaḥ* — with Shri (beauty); *iva* — like; *caitrikaḥ* — the [month of] Chaitra.

**67.** Having attained a youthful longing, continually new and ever new, the charming king shone like [the month of] Chaitra accompanied by beauty.

*Note.* A double meaning: *taruṇī* is also "a young woman", and *madhura* also "vernal" (*madhu* — spring; Madhu is another name of the month of Chaitra): like spring united with beauty, the king was united with a fresh longing as with a young bride. The king is not named; probably Prataparudra is meant (cf. 65 and 81 ff.) (?).

### Verse 68

तत एते महात्मानो गोपीनाथमहाप्रभोः ।
प्रासादं विविशुर्हृष्टाः प्रसादोल्लसिताननाः ॥६८॥

*tata ete mahātmāno gopīnātha-mahāprabhoḥ |*
*prāsādaṁ viviśur hṛṣṭāḥ prasādollasitānanāḥ ||68||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *ete* — these; *mahā-ātmānaḥ* — great souls; *gopīnātha* — Gopinatha; *mahāprabhoḥ* — of the great Lord; *prāsādam* — the temple; *viviśuḥ* — entered; *hṛṣṭāḥ* — joyful; *prasāda* — with contentment; *ullasita* — beaming; *ānanāḥ* — [with] faces.

**68.** Then these great souls, joyful, their faces beaming with contentment, entered the temple of the great Lord Gopinatha.

*Note.* A play on *prāsāda* (temple) and *prasāda* (contentment, grace).

### Verse 69

तत्र तान् परया प्रीत्या वेत्रवेल्लितपाणयः ।
अनयन्नन्तरं वेश्म विस्मृतान्यमनोरथान् ॥६९॥

*tatra tān parayā prītyā vetra-vellita-pāṇayaḥ |*
*anayann antaraṁ veśma vismṛtānya-manorathān ||69||*

*Word for word:* *tatra* — there; *tān* — them; *parayā* — with great; *prītyā* — joy; *vetra* — canes; *vellita* — swinging; *pāṇayaḥ* — [whose] hands; *anayan* — led; *antaram* — inner; *veśma* — into the chamber; *vismṛta* — who had forgotten; *anya* — other; *manorathān* — desires.

**69.** There [the doorkeepers], canes swinging in their hands, with great joy led them — who had forgotten all other desires — into the inner chamber.

### Verse 70

ते विलोक्याथ तं प्रेम्णा प्रीतिमापुर्महत्तराम् ।
अथ कश्चित् समागत्य तत्रत्यः पृथिवीसुरः ।
भिक्षार्थमवृणोत्तत्र परमानन्दपूरिणम् ॥७०॥

*te vilokyātha taṁ premṇā prītim āpur mahattarām |*
*atha kaścit samāgatya tatratyaḥ pṛthivī-suraḥ |*
*bhikṣārtham avṛṇot tatra paramānanda-pūriṇam ||70||*

*Word for word:* *te* — they; *vilokya* — having seen; *atha* — then; *tam* — Him; *premṇā* — with love; *prītim* — joy; *āpuḥ* — attained; *mahattarām* — the very greatest; *atha* — then; *kaścit* — a certain; *samāgatya* — having come; *tatratyaḥ* — local; *pṛthivī-suraḥ* — god on earth (brahmana); *bhikṣā-artham* — for a meal; *avṛṇot* — invited; *tatra* — there; *paramānanda-pūriṇam* — Paramananda Puri.

**70.** Seeing Him with love, they attained the very greatest joy. Then a certain local brahmana came and invited Paramananda Puri there for a meal.

*Note.* The verse has three lines (six padas) — perhaps a half-verse of a neighbouring verse merged with it in typesetting (?); all six padas are metrically regular. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 71

अत्रान्तरे गौरचन्द्रश्चन्द्रकोटिसमुज्ज्वलः ।
ज्वलत्काञ्चनशैलाभो लाभोदय इवागमत् ॥७१॥

*atrāntare gauracandraś candra-koṭi-samujjvalaḥ |*
*jvalat-kāñcana-śailābho lābhodaya ivāgamat ||71||*

*Word for word:* *atra antare* — meanwhile; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra; *candra* — of moons; *koṭi* — [like] millions; *samujjvalaḥ* — shining brightly; *jvalat* — of a blazing; *kāñcana* — golden; *śaila* — mountain; *ābhaḥ* — [having] the appearance; *lābha* — of good fortune; *udayaḥ* — the rising; *iva* — like; *āgamat* — came.

**71.** Meanwhile Gaurachandra came, shining like millions of moons, resembling a blazing golden mountain — like the rising of good fortune.

*Note.* A chain of repetitions at the junctions of words: each word picks up the sound of the end of the preceding one (*-candraś candra-*, *-ujjvalaḥ jvalat-*, *-ābho lābho-*).

### Verse 72

दृष्ट्वा चिरं कृपासिन्धुर्गोपीनाथं मनोरमम् ।
मनोरथं मूर्त्तिमन्तमिव तत्र मुदं ययौ ॥७२॥

*dṛṣṭvā ciraṁ kṛpā-sindhur gopīnāthaṁ manoramam |*
*manorathaṁ mūrttimantam iva tatra mudaṁ yayau ||72||*

*Word for word:* *dṛṣṭvā* — having beheld; *ciram* — for a long time; *kṛpā* — of mercy; *sindhuḥ* — the Ocean; *gopīnātham* — Gopinatha; *manoramam* — charming; *manoratham* — a heart's desire; *mūrttimantam* — embodied; *iva* — like; *tatra* — there; *mudam* — joy; *yayau* — attained.

**72.** Having long beheld charming Gopinatha, who was like a heart's desire embodied, the Ocean of Mercy was filled with joy there.

*Note.* *Manoramam / manoratham* — a play on similar sounds.

### Verse 73

अथ स्वप्नेश्वरो नाम सोऽयं धरणिदैवतम् ।
भिक्षार्थमवृणोत्तत्र गृहेऽपि च समानयत् ॥७३॥

*atha svapneśvaro nāma so 'yaṁ dharaṇi-daivatam |*
*bhikṣārtham avṛṇot tatra gṛhe 'pi ca samānayat ||73||*

*Word for word:* *atha* — then; *svapneśvaraḥ nāma* — named Svapneshvara; *saḥ ayam* — this same; *dharaṇi* — of the earth; *daivatam* — god (a brahmana); *bhikṣā-artham* — for a meal; *avṛṇot* — invited; *tatra* — there; *gṛhe* — to [his] house; *api ca* — and also; *samānayat* — brought.

**73.** Then this same god on earth, the brahmana named Svapneshvara, invited [the Lord] there for a meal and also brought [Him] to his house.

*Note.* *So 'yam*, "this same", presumably points to the brahmana of verse 70. In the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 16.100) the brahmana Svapneshvara invites the Lord to a meal at Kataka, and afterwards the Lord rests beneath a bakula tree (16.102).

### Verse 74

अन्यांस्तु जगदानन्दमुख्यान् सुखपरायणान् ।
श्रीरामानन्दरायोऽसौ निनाय निजमन्दिरम् ॥७४॥

*anyāṁs tu jagadānanda-mukhyān sukha-parāyaṇān |*
*śrī-rāmānanda-rāyo 'sau nināya nija-mandiram ||74||*

*Word for word:* *anyān tu* — but the others; *jagadānanda-mukhyān* — headed by Jagadananda; *sukha* — to bliss; *parāyaṇān* — devoted; *śrī-rāmānanda-rāyaḥ* — Sri Ramananda Raya; *asau* — he; *nināya* — led; *nija* — to his own; *mandiram* — house.

**74.** But the others, headed by Jagadananda, devoted to bliss, Sri Ramananda Raya led to his own house.

### Verse 75

आगाराहित्यसुखदे मनोरामे स तानथ ।
आगाराहित्यसुखदे सदारामे तदानयत् ॥७५॥

*āgārāhitya-sukhade manorāme sa tān atha |*
*āgārāhitya-sukhade sadārāme tadānayat ||75||*

*Word for word:* (following the edition's commentary). First line: *āgāra* — for the house; *āhitya* — [of] being beneficial; *sukha-de* — giving the pleasure; *manorāme* — charming. Second line: *āga* (= *aga*, "mountain") — of the mountains; *arāhitya* — inseparable [pleasure], i.e. the pleasure of hill country (*pārvatya-sukha*); *sukha-de* — giving; *sadā-ārāme* — to a fine garden; *tadā* — then; *ānayat* — brought; *saḥ* — he; *tān* — them; *atha* — then.

**75.** Then he brought them at that time to a fine garden — charming, giving the pleasure of being beneficial to the household, and giving the unfailing pleasure of hill country (?).

*Note.* *Yamaka*: the two lines open with the same sequence of syllables (*āgārāhitya-sukhade*), which is divided and understood differently in each. The analysis of the edition's Sanskrit commentary: *hitaṁ karotīti hityam* ("that which does good", with the suffix *yat*); *na gacchantīti agāḥ*, "those that do not move", i.e. mountains, with the suffix *aṇ* giving *āgāḥ*; *sadārāma* is an excellent garden near a house. The translation is tentative (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 76

आरामारामललितान् कृत्वा तानथ सत्वरम् ।
रामानन्दो जनानन्दोल्लासकृद्भूपमासदत् ॥७६॥

*ārāmārāma-lalitān kṛtvā tān atha satvaram |*
*rāmānando janānandollāsa-kṛd bhūpam āsadat ||76||*

*Word for word:* *ārāma* — of the garden; *ārāma* — with the delight; *lalitān* — gladdened; *kṛtvā* — having made; *tān* — them; *atha* — then; *satvaram* — quickly; *rāmānandaḥ* — Ramananda; *jana* — of people; *ānanda* — of the joy; *ullāsa* — the exultation; *kṛt* — causing; *bhūpam* — to the king; *āsadat* — went.

**76.** Having made them glad with the delights of the garden, Ramananda, who causes people to exult with joy, then quickly went to the king.

*Note.* A play on sounds: *ārāmārāma-*, *rāmānando janānando-*.

### Verse 77

ते तत्र रन्धनोद्योगं चक्रुर्विश्रमणान्तरम् ।
कृतभिक्षः पुरीस्वामी प्रभुना तत्र चागमत् ॥७७॥

*te tatra randhanodyogaṁ cakrur viśramaṇāntaram |*
*kṛta-bhikṣaḥ purī-svāmī prabhuṇā tatra cāgamat ||77||*

*Word for word:* *te* — they; *tatra* — there; *randhana* — for cooking; *udyogam* — preparations; *cakruḥ* — made; *viśramaṇa* — rest; *antaram* — after; *kṛta* — having taken; *bhikṣaḥ* — [his] meal; *purī-svāmī* — Puri Svami; *prabhuṇā* — with the Lord; *tatra* — there; *ca* — and; *āgamat* — came.

**77.** After resting, they set about cooking there; and Puri Svami, having taken his meal, came there with the Lord.

*Note.* The edition misprints *randhona-*; read *randhana-*, "cooking" (so the text above). Puri Svami is Paramananda Puri, who was invited to a meal in verse 70.

### Verse 78

तत्रोपवनमध्येऽस्ति सूच्छ्रितो वकुलद्रुमः ।
विसारी निबिडच्छायः कुलानां वकुलद्रुमः ॥७८॥

*tatropavana-madhye 'sti sūcchrito vakula-drumaḥ |*
*visārī nibiḍa-cchāyaḥ kulānāṁ vakula-drumaḥ (? bakula = ba-kula / kubera) ||78||*

*Word for word:* *tatra* — there; *upavana* — of the garden; *madhye* — in the middle; *asti* — there is; *su-ucchritaḥ* — tall; *vakula-drumaḥ* — a bakula tree; *visārī* — spreading; *nibiḍa* — dense; *chāyaḥ* — [whose] shade [is]; *kulānām* — among the families [of trees]; *vakula-drumaḥ* — (?) (see the note).

**78.** There, in the middle of the garden, is a tall bakula tree — spreading, with dense shade, a *vakula-druma* among the families [of trees] (?).

*Note.* The second *vakula-drumaḥ* repeats the first (*yamaka*) with a different, unclear sense (?). One interpretation, noted in the IAST line, connects it with Kubera: "among the trees of its kind this bakula was rich as Kubera", i.e. like a wish-fulfilling tree. Since *va* is listed in the lexicons as a particle equal to *iva*, "like", the words can perhaps also be divided *kulānāṁ va kula-drumaḥ*, "like the head tree (*kula-druma*) of the families [of trees]" (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 79

परमानेन ललिता परमानेन सर्वतः ।
राजीवनस्य साजीवराजीवयुगथाभवत् ॥७९॥

*paramānena lalitā paramānena (pavamānena?) sarvataḥ |*
*rājī vanasya sājīva-rājīva-yug athābhavat ||79||*

*Word for word:* *para-mānena* — by [its] excellent measure; *lalitā* — lovely; *paramānena* (variant *pavamānena*) — by the breeze; *sarvataḥ* — on all sides; *rājī* — the line; *vanasya* — of the grove; *sa-jīva* — living; *rājīva* — with lotuses; *yuk* — joined; *atha* — then; *abhavat* — became.

**79.** The line of the grove, lovely with its excellent measure [and fanned] on all sides by the breeze, then became joined with living lotuses (?).

*Note.* *Yamaka*: *paramānena* is repeated, and *rājī vanasya* is echoed in *rājīva*. The edition notes a variant: instead of *paramānena lalitā paramānena sarvataḥ* — *pavamānena lalitā pavamānena sarvataḥ*, "charming by the breeze, the breeze [blowing gently] from all sides". The sense of the verse is unclear (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 80

वकुलद्रुममूलेऽसौ वसन् भाति स्म सुस्मितः ।
अनेन हेमरूपेण जम्बुवृक्षं जिगाय सः ॥८०॥

*vakula-druma-mūle 'sau vasan bhāti sma susmitaḥ |*
*anena hema-rūpeṇa jambu-vṛkṣaṁ jigāya saḥ ||80||*

*Word for word:* *vakula* — of the bakula; *druma* — tree; *mūle* — at the foot; *asau* — He; *vasan* — staying; *bhāti sma* — shone; *su-smitaḥ* — smiling beautifully; *anena* — by this; *hema* — golden; *rūpeṇa* — form; *jambu-vṛkṣam* — the jambu tree; *jigāya* — conquered; *saḥ* — He.

**80.** Staying at the foot of the bakula tree, He shone with a beautiful smile, and with this golden form of His He conquered the jambu tree.

*Note.* The cosmic Jambu tree on Meru yields the juice from which *jāmbūnada* gold is born; the golden Gaura beneath the tree surpassed it.

### Verse 81

अत्रान्तरे गुरुश्रीको भूपचक्रशिरोमणिः ।
विजयं गौरचन्द्राङ्घ्रिदृष्टये तत्र चकार सः ॥८१॥

*atrāntare guru-śrīko bhūpa-cakra-śiromaṇiḥ |*
*vijayaṁ gauracandrāṅghri-dṛṣṭaye tatra cakāra saḥ ||81||*

*Word for word:* *atra antare* — meanwhile; *guru* — of great; *śrīkaḥ* — [possessed] of splendour; *bhūpa* — of kings; *cakra* — of the circle; *śiraḥ-maṇiḥ* — the crest-jewel; *vijayam* — a royal progress; *gauracandra* — of Gaurachandra; *aṅghri* — the feet; *dṛṣṭaye* — in order to see; *tatra* — there; *cakāra* — made; *saḥ* — he.

**81.** Meanwhile the crest-jewel of the circle of kings, possessed of great splendour, made a royal progress there in order to see the feet of Gaurachandra.

*Note.* The king is Prataparudra. Metre: the fourth pada has nine syllables instead of eight (*dṛṣṭaye tatra cakāra saḥ*: —⏑——⏑⏑—⏑—); the text is not emended.

### Verse 82

रामानन्दसहायः स सवसन्त इव स्मरः ।
चतुरङ्गबलैर्युक्तः समयात् समयात्ततः ॥८२॥

*rāmānanda-sahāyaḥ sa savasanta iva smaraḥ |*
*catur-aṅga-balair yuktaḥ samayāt samayāt tataḥ ||82||*

*Word for word:* *rāmānanda* — Ramananda; *sahāyaḥ* — [having as his] companion; *saḥ* — he; *sa-vasantaḥ* — with Spring; *iva* — like; *smaraḥ* — Smara (Kama); *catuḥ-aṅga* — of four divisions; *balaiḥ* — with forces; *yuktaḥ* — accompanied; *samayāt* — at the proper time; *samayāt* — arrived; *tataḥ* — then.

**82.** With Ramananda as his companion — like Smara with Spring — accompanied by forces of four divisions, he then arrived at the proper time.

*Note.* *Yamaka*: *samayāt samayāt* — first the ablative of *samaya*, "at the [proper] time", then the imperfect *sam-ayāt*, "arrived". The four divisions of an army are elephants, horses, chariots and infantry.

### Verse 83

अवतीर्य गजस्कन्धात् गजस्कन्धातिसुन्दरः ।
तदारामं प्रति प्रीत्या भूमौ गच्छन् बभौ भृशम् ॥८३॥

*avatīrya gaja-skandhāt gaja-skandhāti-sundaraḥ |*
*tad-ārāmaṁ prati prītyā bhūmau gacchan babhau bhṛśam ||83||*

*Word for word:* *avatīrya* — having descended; *gaja* — of the elephant; *skandhāt* — from the back; *gaja* — [like] an elephant's; *skandha* — [whose] shoulders [were]; *ati-sundaraḥ* — most handsome; *tat* — to that; *ārāmam prati* — towards the garden; *prītyā* — joyfully; *bhūmau* — on the ground (on foot); *gacchan* — going; *babhau* — shone; *bhṛśam* — greatly.

**83.** Descending from the back of his elephant, the most handsome [king], whose shoulders were like an elephant's, joyfully went on foot towards that garden and shone greatly.

*Note.* *Yamaka*: *gaja-skandhāt* (from the elephant's back) / *gaja-skandhāti-sundaraḥ* (most handsome, with shoulders like an elephant's).

### Verse 84

सदा सदानैर्गुरुभिर्नागैर्नागैर्हयैर्वृतः ।
पत्तिसंपत्तिसञ्चार्यैर्भूयो भूयो रराज सः ॥८४॥

*sadā sadānair gurubhir nāgair nāgair hayair vṛtaḥ |*
*patti-saṁpatti-sañcāryair bhūyo bhūyo rarāja saḥ ||84||*

*Word for word:* *sadā* — always; *sa-dānaiḥ* — with ichor [flowing]; *gurubhiḥ* — huge; *nāgaiḥ* — by elephants; *nāgaiḥ* (= *na-agaiḥ*) — moving (lit. "not immobile"); *hayaiḥ* — by horses; *vṛtaḥ* — surrounded; *patti* — of infantry; *saṁpatti* — by the wealth; *sañcāryaiḥ* — moving; *bhūyaḥ bhūyaḥ* — more and more; *rarāja* — shone; *saḥ* — he.

**84.** Surrounded by huge elephants, ever flowing with ichor, [like mountains yet] not immobile, by horses and by the moving wealth of infantry, he shone more and more.

*Note.* *Yamaka*: *sadā sadānaiḥ*, *nāgair nāgair*, *patti-saṁpatti-*, *bhūyo bhūyo*. In *nāgair nāgair* the first word means "elephants"; the second is divided *na-agaiḥ*, "not immobile" (*aga*, "that which does not move", is a mountain or a tree) (?). *Dāna* is the ichor that flows from an elephant's temples in rut.

### Verse 85

नास्त्येवास्य समो राजा किं स्वर्गे किं महीतले ।
इतीव तत्र तत्रोच्चैः क्षुरैरक्षोभि घोटकैः ॥८५॥

*nāsty evāsya samo rājā kiṁ svarge kiṁ mahī-tale |*
*itīva tatra tatroccaiḥ kṣurair akṣobhi ghoṭakaiḥ ||85||*

*Word for word:* *na asti eva* — there is not at all; *asya* — to him; *samaḥ* — equal; *rājā* — a king; *kim svarge* — whether in heaven; *kim mahī-tale* — or on the surface of the earth; *iti iva* — as if [proclaiming] thus; *tatra tatra* — here and there; *uccaiḥ* — loudly (or: tall, with *ghoṭakaiḥ*); *kṣuraiḥ* — with hooves; *akṣobhi* — [the ground] was churned; *ghoṭakaiḥ* — by the horses.

**85.** As if loudly proclaiming here and there, "There is no king equal to him, either in heaven or on earth!", the horses churned [the ground] with their hooves.

*Note.* *Uccaiḥ* may be the adverb "loudly" (with the implied proclamation) or the instrumental plural of *ucca*, "tall", agreeing with *ghoṭakaiḥ*: "the tall horses".

### Verse 86

रामानन्दभुजं धृत्वा नियोज्यामात्यसञ्चयम् ।
अभितोऽभिययौ राजा पूर्णचन्द्रोऽर्कयुग्यथा ॥८६॥

*rāmānanda-bhujaṁ dhṛtvā niyojyāmātya-sañcayam |*
*abhito 'bhiyayau rājā pūrṇa-candro 'rka-yug yathā ||86||*

*Word for word:* *rāmānanda* — of Ramananda; *bhujam* — the arm; *dhṛtvā* — having taken; *niyojya* — having stationed; *amātya* — of ministers; *sañcayam* — the host; *abhitaḥ* — all around; *abhiyayau* — approached; *rājā* — the king; *pūrṇa-candraḥ* — the full moon; *arka* — with the sun; *yuk* — joined; *yathā* — like.

**86.** Taking Ramananda by the arm and stationing the host of ministers all around, the king approached, like the full moon joined with the sun.

### Verse 87

अमात्यैरमरप्रायैरन्तर्बलनिवेशिभिः ।
प्रथमं वलयीभूतो भूप्रदेशो रराज सः ॥८७॥

*amātyair amara-prāyair antar-bala-niveśibhiḥ |*
*prathamaṁ valayībhūto bhū-pradeśo rarāja saḥ ||87||*

*Word for word:* *amātyaiḥ* — by the ministers; *amara* — the immortals; *prāyaiḥ* — resembling; *antaḥ* — within; *bala* — the army; *niveśibhiḥ* — stationed; *prathamam* — first; *valayībhūtaḥ* — encircled; *bhū-pradeśaḥ* — tract of ground; *rarāja* — shone; *saḥ* — that.

**87.** First [came] that tract of ground, encircled by the ministers, who were like the immortals, stationed within the army; it shone.

*Note.* The edition gives the variant *antar-vana-nivāsibhiḥ* ("dwelling in the forest") and rejects it: "this reading is not good".

### Verse 88

तद्बहिः पत्तयोऽतिष्ठंस्तद्बहिर्हयसञ्चयः ।
तद्बहिश्च गजाः सर्वे व्यूह एवाभवत्तदा ॥८८॥

*tad-bahiḥ pattayo 'tiṣṭhaṁs tad-bahir haya-sañcayaḥ |*
*tad-bahiś ca gajāḥ sarve vyūha evābhavat tadā ||88||*

*Word for word:* *tat-bahiḥ* — outside that; *pattayaḥ* — the foot-soldiers; *atiṣṭhan* — stood; *tat-bahiḥ* — outside that; *haya* — of horses; *sañcayaḥ* — a host; *tat-bahiḥ ca* — and outside that; *gajāḥ* — the elephants; *sarve* — all; *vyūhaḥ eva* — a veritable battle array; *abhavat* — was formed; *tadā* — then.

**88.** Outside that stood the foot-soldiers; outside them a host of horses; and outside them all the elephants: a veritable battle array was formed then.

*Note.* Cf. the three rings around the dancing Lord in 16.24.

### Verse 89

पादारविन्दयुगलं वीक्ष्य तत्र द्रवन्मनाः ।
भूपतिर्भूतलं भूयः प्राप हर्षाश्रुणा सह ॥८९॥
(असन्ध्यक्षरः)

*pādāravinda-yugalaṁ vīkṣya tatra dravan-manāḥ |*
*bhūpatir bhū-talaṁ bhūyaḥ prāpa harṣāśruṇā saha ||89||*
*(asandhy-akṣaraḥ)*

*Word for word:* *pāda* — of feet; *aravinda* — lotus; *yugalam* — the pair; *vīkṣya* — having seen; *tatra* — there; *dravat* — melting; *manāḥ* — [whose] heart [was]; *bhū-patiḥ* — the king; *bhū-talam* — the surface of the earth; *bhūyaḥ* — again and again; *prāpa* — reached (fell to); *harṣa* — of joy; *aśruṇā* — tears; *saha* — together with.

**89.** Seeing the pair of lotus feet there, the king, his heart melting, fell to the ground again and again together with tears of joy.

*Note.* *Asandhy-akṣara*: a verse without diphthongs (*e, ai, o, au*), as the edition's subscript indicates; note also the alliteration *bhūpatir bhū-talaṁ bhūyaḥ*. Cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 16.102–107: while the Lord rests beneath the bakula tree, Ramananda brings the king, who falls at His feet and offers prayers.

### Verse 90

प्रणम्य बहुधा दृग्भ्यामपिबद्वदनाम्बुजम् ।
न च तृप्तिमगाद्भूपश्चित्रं गौराङ्गचेष्टितम् ॥९०॥

*praṇamya bahudhā dṛgbhyām apibad vadanāmbujam |*
*na ca tṛptim agād bhūpaś citraṁ gaurāṅga-ceṣṭitam ||90||*

*Word for word:* *praṇamya* — having bowed down; *bahudhā* — many times; *dṛgbhyām* — with [his] two eyes; *apibat* — drank; *vadana* — of the face; *ambujam* — the lotus; *na ca* — and not; *tṛptim* — satiety; *agāt* — attained; *bhūpaḥ* — the king; *citram* — wonderful; *gaurāṅga* — of Gauranga; *ceṣṭitam* — the doing.

**90.** Having bowed down many times, the king drank with his eyes the lotus of [the Lord's] face and could not be sated. Wonderful are the doings of Gauranga!

*Note.* The edition notes the variant *na tṛptim agamad bhūpaḥ*.

### Verse 91

बहुधा गौरचन्द्रोऽपि प्रेम्णाभाष्य वचोऽमृतैः ।
सिषेच तस्य सर्वाङ्गं सर्वाङ्गीनमिवाश्लिषन् ॥९१॥

*bahudhā gauracandro 'pi premṇābhāṣya vaco-'mṛtaiḥ |*
*siṣeca tasya sarvāṅgaṁ sarvāṅgīnam ivāśliṣan ||91||*

*Word for word:* *bahudhā* — in many ways; *gauracandraḥ api* — Gaurachandra too; *premṇā* — with love; *ābhāṣya* — having spoken; *vacaḥ* — of words; *amṛtaiḥ* — with the nectar; *siṣeca* — sprinkled; *tasya* — his; *sarva-aṅgam* — whole body; *sarva-aṅgīnam* — [with an embrace] covering the whole body; *iva* — as if; *āśliṣan* — embracing.

**91.** Gaurachandra too, speaking to him lovingly in many ways, sprinkled his whole body with the nectar of His words, as if embracing him from head to foot.

### Verse 92

आज्ञायाज्ञां प्रसादं च कृतकृत्यः स निर्ययौ ।
अमात्यनिचयाः सर्वे ततो द्रष्टुं ययुर्द्रुतम् ॥९२॥

*ājñāyājñāṁ prasādaṁ ca kṛta-kṛtyaḥ sa niryayau |*
*amātya-nicayāḥ sarve tato draṣṭuṁ yayur drutam ||92||*

*Word for word:* *ājñāya* — having received; *ājñām* — the command; *prasādam* — the favour; *ca* — and; *kṛta-kṛtyaḥ* — having accomplished [his] purpose; *saḥ* — he; *niryayau* — departed; *amātya* — of ministers; *nicayāḥ* — the throngs; *sarve* — all; *tataḥ* — then; *draṣṭum* — to see [the Lord]; *yayuḥ* — went; *drutam* — quickly.

**92.** Having received [the Lord's] command and favour, his purpose accomplished, he departed; then all the throngs of ministers quickly went to see [the Lord].

*Note.* A play on sounds: *ājñāyājñām*.

### Verse 93

पारेचित्रोत्पलं सोऽकूपारे चित्रोत्पलं यथा ।
यियासोः स्वमतं ज्ञात्वा भूपः सत्पात्रमब्रवीत् ॥९३॥
(पद्मभेदः)

*pāre-citrotpalaṁ so 'kūpāre citrotpalaṁ yathā |*
*yiyāsoḥ svamataṁ jñātvā bhūpaḥ sat-pātram abravīt ||93||*
*(padma-bhedaḥ)*

*Word for word:* *pāre-citrotpalam* — beyond the Chitrotpala; *saḥ* — he; *akūpāre* — in the ocean; *citra-utpalam yathā* — as [one would go] for many-coloured lotuses; *yiyāsoḥ* — of [the Lord], who wished to go; *svamatam* — the intention; *jñātvā* — having learnt; *bhūpaḥ* — the king; *sat-pātram* — to a worthy person; *abravīt* — said.

**93.** Having learnt the intention of [the Lord], who wished to go beyond the Chitrotpala — as [one would go] into the ocean for many-coloured lotuses (?) — he, the king, said to a worthy [servant]:

*Note.* *Padma-bandha* (the edition's subscript: *padma-bhedaḥ*), "the lotus pattern": a figured verse whose syllables, written out in a diagram, form the shape of a lotus (the arrangement itself is not explained (?)). The first line also contains the near-repetition *pāre-citrotpalam / akūpāre citrotpalam* (*yamaka*). The Chitrotpala is a river (a branch of the Mahanadi; cf. 94).
