The edition's Sanskrit commentary: *pāre-citrotpalam* is an *avyayībhāva* compound under the rule "*pāre* and *madhye* [are compounded] with a genitive"; *akūpāra* means "ocean" (according to the Amarakosha). The point of the simile is not clear (?).

### Verse 94

मङ्गराज भवानेव हरिचन्दनसंगतः ।
पारेमहानदि महाप्रभुमन्वेतु सत्वरम् ॥९४॥

*maṅgarāja bhavān eva haricandana-saṁgataḥ |*
*pāre-mahānadi mahāprabhum anvetu satvaram ||94||*

*Word for word:* *maṅgarāja* — O Mangaraja; *bhavān* — your honour; *eva* — indeed; *haricandana* — Harichandana; *saṁgataḥ* — together with; *pāre-mahānadi* — beyond the Mahanadi; *mahāprabhum* — Mahaprabhu; *anvetu* — should escort; *satvaram* — quickly.

**94.** "O Mangaraja, you yourself, together with Harichandana, should quickly escort Mahaprabhu beyond the Mahanadi."

*Note.* The edition has *bhavānena*; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *bhavān eva*, and this reading is adopted. Mangaraja and Harichandana are officers of the king; cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 16.113, 126: the king entrusts Harichandana and Mangaraja with the service of the Lord, and they follow Him together with Ramananda.

### Verse 95

तदाज्ञयाथ ते सोऽपि श्रीरामानन्दरायकः ।
नौकाः सुमहतीश्चक्रे प्रभुं चाथ समानयन् ॥९५॥

*tad-ājñayātha te so 'pi śrī-rāmānanda-rāyakaḥ |*
*naukāḥ sumahatīś cakre prabhuṁ cātha samānayan ||95||*

*Word for word:* *tat-ājñayā* — by his command; *atha* — then; *te* — they; *saḥ api* — he too; *śrī-rāmānanda-rāyakaḥ* — Sri Ramananda Raya; *naukāḥ* — boats; *su-mahatīḥ* — very large; *cakre* — prepared; *prabhum* — the Lord; *ca* — and; *atha* — then; *samānayan* — brought across.

**95.** By his command they — and Sri Ramananda Raya too — made ready very large boats and then brought the Lord across.

*Note.* *Cakre*, "prepared", is singular (with Ramananda), while *samānayan*, "brought", is plural.

### Verse 96

उदियाय तदा पूर्णो भगवान् मृगलाञ्छनः ।
करैः सम्मार्जयामास पन्थानमखिलं ततः ॥९६॥

*udiyāya tadā pūrṇo bhagavān mṛga-lāñchanaḥ |*
*karaiḥ sammārjayāmāsa panthānam akhilaṁ tataḥ ||96||*

*Word for word:* *udiyāya* — rose; *tadā* — then; *pūrṇaḥ* — full; *bhagavān* — the divine; *mṛga* — with a deer; *lāñchanaḥ* — marked (the moon); *karaiḥ* — with [his] rays (= hands); *sammārjayāmāsa* — swept clean; *panthānam* — the road; *akhilam* — the whole; *tataḥ* — then.

**96.** Then the divine full moon, marked with a deer, rose, and with his rays — his hands — swept the whole road clean.

*Note.* *Kara* means both "ray" and "hand".

### Verse 97

ततो गच्छति गौराङ्गे राजकीयस्तदागतः ।
तत्रत्यांस्तत्र निर्णीय तदाज्ञां निजगाद सः ॥९७॥

*tato gacchati gaurāṅge rājakīyas tadāgataḥ |*
*tatratyāṁs tatra nirṇīya tad-ājñāṁ nijagāda saḥ ||97||*

*Word for word:* *tataḥ* — then; *gacchati* — as [He] was going; *gaurāṅge* — Gauranga; *rājakīyaḥ* — a royal [officer]; *tadā* — then; *āgataḥ* — having come; *tatratyān* — to the local [people]; *tatra* — there; *nirṇīya* — having determined [the place] (?); *tat* — his (the king's); *ājñām* — command; *nijagāda* — announced; *saḥ* — he.

**97.** Then, as Gauranga was going on, a royal officer who had come at that time determined [the place] there (?) and announced the king's command to the local people:

### Verse 98

आज्ञापयति देवो यच्छ्रूयतां तन्महोत्तमाः ।
आरोप्योऽत्र स्तम्भ एको येन तीर्थं भवेदिदम् ॥९८॥

*ājñāpayati devo yac chrūyatāṁ tan mahottamāḥ |*
*āropyo 'tra stambha eko yena tīrthaṁ bhaved idam ||98||*

*Word for word:* *ājñāpayati* — commands; *devaḥ* — His Majesty; *yat* — what; *śrūyatām* — let it be heard; *tat* — that; *mahā-uttamāḥ* — O most excellent ones; *āropyaḥ* — is to be erected; *atra* — here; *stambhaḥ* — a pillar; *ekaḥ* — one; *yena* — by which; *tīrtham* — a holy place; *bhavet* — may become; *idam* — this.

**98.** "Hear, O most excellent ones, what His Majesty commands: a pillar is to be erected here, so that this [place] may become a holy place."

*Note.* Cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 16.115: Prataparudra orders a memorial column to be set up at every place where the Lord bathes or crosses a river.

### Verse 99

इति श्रुत्वा नृपाज्ञां ते स्तम्भमारोप्य तत्र च ।
नौकामारोप्यो मुदिताः प्रभुं हर्षादुपासत ॥९९॥

*iti śrutvā nṛpājñāṁ te stambham āropya tatra ca |*
*naukām āropyo (āropya) muditāḥ prabhuṁ harṣād upāsata ||99||*

*Word for word:* *iti* — thus; *śrutvā* — having heard; *nṛpa* — of the king; *ājñām* — the command; *te* — they; *stambham* — a pillar; *āropya* — having erected; *tatra* — there; *ca* — and; *naukām* — onto a boat; *āropyo* (read *āropya*) — having placed [Him]; *muditāḥ* — glad; *prabhum* — the Lord; *harṣāt* — with joy; *upāsata* — served.

**99.** Hearing the king's command thus, they erected a pillar there and, placing [the Lord] in a boat, gladly served the Lord with joy.

*Note.* The edition has *āropyo*, a misprint for *āropya*. The play *āropya* — "having erected" (the pillar) / "having placed" (the Lord in the boat).

### Verse 100

इत्थं पारेनदि स तु चतुर्द्वारमागत्य तैस्तै-
रात्रौ चन्द्रातपमधुरिमव्यावृतायां समन्तात् ।
स्वापं चक्रे प्रभुरथ जगन्नाथसन्मण्डपान्त-
र्लोकैर्लक्षावधिभिरपि तु स्थानमेवात्र नापे ॥१००॥

*itthaṁ pāre-nadi sa tu catur-dvāram āgatya tais tai*
*rātrau candrātapa-madhurima-vyāvṛtāyāṁ samantāt |*
*svāpaṁ cakre prabhur atha jagannātha-san-maṇḍapāntar*
*lokair lakṣāvadhibhir api tu sthānam evātra nāpe ||100||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *pāre-nadi* — beyond the river; *saḥ tu* — He; *catur-dvāram* — to Chaturdvara; *āgatya* — having come; *taiḥ taiḥ* — with all those [companions]; *rātrau* — in the night; *candra* — of the moon; *ātapa* — of the light; *madhurima* — by the sweetness; *vyāvṛtāyām* — enveloped; *samantāt* — on all sides; *svāpam* — sleep; *cakre* — took; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *atha* — then; *jagannātha* — of Jagannatha; *sat* — of the fine; *maṇḍapa* — pavilion; *antaḥ* — inside; *lokaiḥ* — by the people; *lakṣa* — a hundred thousand; *avadhibhiḥ* — numbering up to; *api tu* — but; *sthānam eva* — even a place; *atra* — there; *na āpe* — was not found.

**100.** Thus, having crossed the river and come to Chaturdvara with all those [companions], the Lord then slept, in a night enveloped on all sides by the sweetness of the moonlight, inside the fine pavilion of Jagannatha; but the people, up to a hundred thousand [in number], could not find even a place there.

*Note.* Metre — *mandākrāntā* (————⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑——⏑——⏑——; 17 syllables per pada); the verse scans correctly. Chaturdvara is a village on the northern bank of the Mahanadi opposite Kataka (cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 16.116, 122: the king has new houses built there, and on the night of the full moon the Lord crosses to Chaturdvara in a new boat).

**Colophon:** इति श्रीकृष्णचैतन्यचरितामृते महाकाव्ये श्रीवृन्दावनयात्रायामूनविंशः सर्गः ॥ (*iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahākāvye śrī-vṛndāvana-yātrāyām ūnaviṁśaḥ sargaḥ*) — "Thus [ends] the nineteenth sarga, 'The Journey to Sri Vrindavana', in the mahakavya 'Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita'."

---

## Sarga Twenty — verses 1–49

**Title of the sarga:** none — the colophon of the edition gives no title for this sarga (*iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahākāvye śrīla-karṇapūra-kṛtau viṁśatitamaḥ sargaḥ*, "Thus [ends] the twentieth sarga in the great poem Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita, the work of Srila Karnapura"; it goes on: "This great poem Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita is complete. Number of verses: 1911").
**Metre:**
- 1–36 and 41 — *śālinī* (*ma-ta-ta-ga-ga*: — — — — | — ⏑ — — ⏑ — —; 11 syllables per pada, caesura after the fourth). The edition says: "up to verse 36 — *śālinī*".
- 37 and 47 — *śārdūla-vikrīḍita* (*ma-sa-ja-sa-ta-ta-ga*: ———⏑⏑—⏑—⏑⏑⏑———⏑——⏑—; 19 syllables per pada).
- 38–39 and 48 — *mandākrāntā* (*ma-bha-na-ta-ta-ga-ga*: ————⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑——⏑——⏑——; 17 syllables per pada).
- 40 — *śikhariṇī* (*ya-ma-na-sa-bha-la-ga*: ⏑—————⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑——⏑⏑⏑—; 17 syllables per pada).
- 42–45 and 49 — *vasantatilakā* (*ta-bha-ja-ja-ga-ga*: ——⏑—⏑⏑⏑—⏑⏑—⏑——; 14 syllables per pada).
- 46 — *mālinī* (*na-na-ma-ya-ya*: ⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑———⏑——⏑——; 15 syllables per pada, caesura after the eighth).

**Total verses:** 49. The publisher gives the total number of verses of the poem as 1911 (in the colophon and in his note after verse 49). The printed numbering of the twenty sargas runs without gaps or repetitions and adds up to 1912 (29 + 122 + 144 + 77 + 129 + 123 + 107 + 63 + 95 + 80 + 89 + 134 + 148 + 135 + 110 + 49 + 66 + 63 + 100 + 49); the difference of one is not explained by the numbering itself and is presumably a slip in the publisher's count (his other figures in the same note are also inexact; see the note on 49). The unnumbered quotations in Sargas 6 and 7 are not included in either figure.

**Contents of the passage:** the journey through Bengal, the return, the Lord's departure; the author's conclusion.
- 1–10 — the Lord dismisses the ministers; by Prataparudra's order houses are built for Him everywhere; crowds of people; the Lord and Puri point each other out (7); Ramananda turns back from Bhadra (9).
- 11–19 — Gauda: the abode of Raghava (12); the house of Srivasa and the crowds; the secret departure by boat at night; Srivasa and the others search for Him.
- 20–25 — Shantipura: the meeting with Advaita; **Mother Shachi** (23); six days; Advaita regales the people.
- 26–30 — a place across the Ganga, west of Navadvipa (Kuliya?); crowds; the Lord hides Himself.
- 31–36 — an obscure place, "Gopinatha" (31); the way towards the Yamuna, the return to the Ganga, then to Puri (32–34); the second departure for the Yamuna (35); Ramananda gives up his life in separation (36 — at variance with the Chaitanya-charitamrita).
- 37–41 — summary: twenty years of festivals in Puri; the Lord's departure to His own abode; chronology: sannyasa in His twenty-fourth year, three years of wandering, twenty years in Puri, forty-seven years in all (40–41).
- 42–49 — the author's conclusion:
  - the source — the records of **Murari** (Gupta), which "the child saw" (42–43);
  - a blessing on the poem; the author's humility (44–45, 48);
  - the signature: the youngest son of Shivananda Sena (46);
  - the hero of the poem is *dhīrodātta* (47);
  - the date of completion: Shaka 1464 (1542 CE), the month of Ashadha, a Monday, the second tithi of the dark fortnight (49).

### Verse 1

रात्रिर्याता नाथ तल्पं जहीही-
त्याकर्ण्य पक्षिणां कूजितानि ।
नेत्रे निद्रामुद्रिते जागृहीति
द्रागाक्षिप्यन् पाणिनाथोदियाय ॥१॥

*rātrir yātā nātha talpaṁ jahīhīty*
*ākarṇya pakṣiṇāṁ kūjitāni |*
*netre nidrā-mudrite jāgṛhīti*
*drāg ākṣipyan pāṇinā thodiyāya (pāṇinātha udiyāya) ||1||*

*Word for word:* *rātriḥ* — the night; *yātā* — has gone; *nātha* — O Master; *talpam* — the bed; *jahīhi* — leave; *iti* — thus; *ākarṇya* — having heard; *pakṣiṇām* — of the birds; *kūjitāni* — the warbling; *netre* — [His] two eyes; *nidrā* — by sleep; *mudrite* — sealed; *jāgṛhi* — wake up; *iti* — [saying] thus; *drāk* — quickly; *ākṣipyan* — rubbing; *pāṇinā* — with [His] hand; *atha* — then; *udiyāya* — rose.

**1.** Hearing the warbling of the birds — "The night has gone, O Master; leave Your bed!" — He quickly rubbed with His hand His eyes, sealed by sleep, [saying to them,] "Wake up!", and then rose.

*Note.* The metre is *śālinī* (so the edition: "up to verse 36 — *śālinī*"). As printed, the second pada has only ten syllables (*ākarṇya pakṣiṇāṁ kūjitāni*: — — ⏑ — ⏑ — — ⏑ — ⏑): of the four heavy syllables of the opening only three are present, and *-ṇya* is light; something has dropped out. The printed run *pāṇināthodiyāya* is to be divided *pāṇinā atha udiyāya*, "with the hand; then [He] rose"; the division *pāṇinā thodiyāya* in the transliteration line is merely mechanical.

### Verse 2

निर्माल्यान्नं तत्र सद्यः समेतं
दृष्ट्वा हर्षादाह्निकान्यारभेत ।
अन्नं पानं पिष्टकादि प्रकामं
तैस्तैर्भुक्त्वा प्रीतिमांश्च प्रतस्थे ॥२॥

*nirmālyānnaṁ tatra sadyaḥ sametaṁ*
*dṛṣṭvā harṣād āhnikāny ārabheta |*
*annaṁ pānaṁ piṣṭakādi prakāmaṁ*
*tais tair bhuktvā prītimāṁś ca pratasthe ||2||*

*Word for word:* *nirmālya* — sanctified; *annam* — food; *tatra* — there; *sadyaḥ* — just; *sametam* — arrived; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *harṣāt* — joyfully; *āhnikāni* — the daily rites; *ārabheta* — began; *annam* — rice; *pānam* — drink; *piṣṭaka-ādi* — cakes and the rest; *prakāmam* — to [His] heart's content; *taiḥ taiḥ* — with all of them; *bhuktvā* — having eaten; *prītimān* — pleased; *ca* — and; *pratasthe* — set out.

**2.** Seeing the sanctified food that had just arrived there, He joyfully began His daily rites; and having eaten to His heart's content, with all of them, rice, drink, cakes and the rest, He set out, pleased.

*Note.* The optative *ārabheta* is used in the sense of the past (for the metre).

### Verse 3

तत्रामात्यौ तेन सम्यग्विसृष्टौ
ताभ्यां भूयो नेत्रपाथोजपाथः ।
तेने क्षामे तत्तनू हन्त ताभ्या-
मुत्साहोऽयं कः प्रकारो विधातुः ॥३॥

*tatrāmātyau tena samyag visṛṣṭau*
*tābhyāṁ bhūyo netra-pāthoja-pāthaḥ |*
*tene kṣāme tat-tanū hanta tābhyām*
*utsāho 'yaṁ kaḥ prakāro vidhātuḥ ||3||*

*Word for word:* *tatra* — there; *amātyau* — the two ministers; *tena* — by Him; *samyak* — duly; *visṛṣṭau* — [were] dismissed; *tābhyām* — by the two; *bhūyaḥ* — abundantly; *netra* — of the eyes; *pāthoja* — of the lotuses; *pāthaḥ* — the water; *tene* — was shed; *kṣāme* — [became] wasted; *tat* — their; *tanū* — two bodies; *hanta* — alas; *tābhyām* — by the two [had been shown]; *utsāhaḥ* — zeal; *ayam* — this; *kaḥ* — what; *prakāraḥ* — [is] the way; *vidhātuḥ* — of the Creator.

**3.** There the two ministers were duly dismissed by Him. They shed abundant water from the lotuses of their eyes, and their bodies — alas! — wasted away; and such zeal [had been shown] by them! What a way the Creator has!

*Note.* The ministers are Mangaraja and Harichandana (19.94).

### Verse 4

देशं देशं प्रत्युपेयुः समन्ता-
दाज्ञा राज्ञो लेखपूर्वाः समस्ताः ।
स्थाने स्थाने नव्यनव्यं निशान्तं
सामग्रीभिः कर्त्तुमग्रे पवित्रम् ॥४॥

*deśaṁ deśaṁ pratyupeyuḥ samantād*
*ājñā rājño lekha-pūrvāḥ samastāḥ |*
*sthāne sthāne navya-navyaṁ niśāntaṁ*
*sāmagrībhiḥ karttum agre pavitram ||4||*

*Word for word:* *deśam deśam* — to land after land; *pratyupeyuḥ* — came; *samantāt* — on every side; *ājñāḥ* — the orders; *rājñaḥ* — of the king; *lekha-pūrvāḥ* — written; *samastāḥ* — all; *sthāne sthāne* — at every place; *navya-navyam* — brand-new; *niśāntam* — a dwelling; *sāmagrībhiḥ* — with provisions; *karttum* — to make; *agre* — in advance; *pavitram* — clean.

**4.** To land after land, on every side, came all the king's written orders: at every place a brand-new, clean dwelling was to be made ready in advance, with provisions.

### Verse 5

उद्यन्नासीद्यत्र तैरेष नाथो
हर्षोत्कर्षाल्लक्षसंख्यैर्मनुष्यैः ।
निष्प्रत्यूहं तत्र तत्रेक्षणाब्जैः
काकुप्रोक्तैः पूजितः संस्तुतश्च ॥५॥

*udyann āsīd yatra tair eṣa nātho*
*harṣotkarṣāl lakṣa-saṅkhyair manuṣyaiḥ |*
*niṣpratyūhaṁ tatra tatrekṣaṇābjaiḥ*
*kāku-proktaiḥ pūjitaḥ saṁstutaś ca ||5||*

*Word for word:* *udyan* — appearing; *āsīt* — was; *yatra* — wherever; *taiḥ* — by those; *eṣaḥ* — this; *nāthaḥ* — Master; *harṣa* — of joy; *utkarṣāt* — from the excess; *lakṣa* — in hundreds of thousands; *saṅkhyaiḥ* — numbering; *manuṣyaiḥ* — by people; *niṣpratyūham* — without hindrance; *tatra tatra* — there; *īkṣaṇa* — of the eyes; *abjaiḥ* — with the lotuses; *kāku* — plaintive; *proktaiḥ* — with words; *pūjitaḥ* — [was] worshipped; *saṁstutaḥ* — praised; *ca* — and.

**5.** Wherever this Master appeared, there, out of the excess of their joy, people numbering hundreds of thousands worshipped Him without hindrance with the lotuses of their eyes and praised Him with plaintive words.

### Verse 6

अद्य श्वो वा नूनमत्रैष्यतीति
प्रोच्चैरासीदग्रतो हर्षनादः ।
पश्चादायातीति तस्मादुपेतो
भो भोः पश्चादेव सर्वत्र भूयः ॥६॥

*adya śvo vā nūnam atraiṣyatīti*
*proccair āsīd agrato harṣa-nādaḥ |*
*paścād āyātīti tasmād upeto*
*bho bhoḥ paścād eva sarvatra bhūyaḥ ||6||*

*Word for word:* *adya* — today; *śvaḥ* — tomorrow; *vā* — or; *nūnam* — surely; *atra* — here; *eṣyati* — He will come; *iti* — thus; *pra-uccaiḥ* — very loudly; *āsīt* — there was; *agrataḥ* — ahead; *harṣa* — of joy; *nādaḥ* — a cry; *paścāt* — afterwards; *āyāti* — He is coming; *iti* — thus; *tasmāt* — then; *upetaḥ* — He has come; *bho bhoḥ* — ho, ho!; *paścāt eva* — afterwards; *sarvatra* — everywhere; *bhūyaḥ* — again.

**6.** "Today or tomorrow He will surely come here!" — such was the cry of joy that rang out very loudly ahead [of Him]; afterwards, "He is coming!"; then, "Ho, ho! He has come!" — and so again everywhere afterwards.

### Verse 7

केचित् केचित्तत्र पप्रच्छुरार्य्याः
क्वासौ क्वासौ कृष्णचैतन्यचन्द्रः ।
इत्थं नाथं पूरिणं तं प्रभुं तं
तावन्योन्यं दर्शयामासतुस्तान् ॥७॥

*kecit kecit tatra papracchur āryāḥ*
*kvāsau kvāsau kṛṣṇa-caitanya-candraḥ |*
*itthaṁ nāthaṁ pūriṇaṁ taṁ prabhuṁ taṁ*
*tāv anyonyaṁ darśayāmāsatus tān ||7||*

*Word for word:* *kecit kecit* — some; *tatra* — there; *papracchuḥ* — asked; *āryāḥ* — worthy [people]; *kva asau* — where is He; *kṛṣṇa-caitanya-candraḥ* — Krishna-Chaitanya-chandra; *ittham* — thus; *nātham* — the Master; *pūriṇam* — Puri; *tam* — that; *prabhum* — Lord; *tam* — that; *tau* — the two; *anyonyam* — each other; *darśayāmāsatuḥ* — pointed out; *tān* — to them.

**7.** Some worthy people there asked: "Where is He, where is He — Krishna-Chaitanya-chandra?" Thereupon those two pointed each other out to them: [Puri showed them] the Master, that Lord, [and the Lord showed them] that Puri.

*Note.* A playful scene: each of the two points to the other. Puri is presumably Paramananda Puri, the Lord's companion on this journey (19.6, 12). There is no such scene in the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 16).

### Verse 8

वासं वासं प्रत्युपेते प्रभाते
राज्ञामाज्ञायन्त्रिताः सर्व एव ।
देशे देशे शुद्धगेहानि कृत्वा
सामग्रीश्च प्रोन्मदा आनयन्ति ॥८॥

*vāsaṁ vāsaṁ pratyupete prabhāte*
*rājñām ājñā-yantritāḥ sarva eva |*
*deśe deśe śuddha-gehāni kṛtvā*
*sāmagrīś ca pronmadā ānayanti ||8||*

*Word for word:* *vāsam vāsam* — at halting place after halting place; *pratyupete* — when [He] had arrived; *prabhāte* — at dawn; *rājñām* — of the kings; *ājñā* — by the order; *yantritāḥ* — constrained; *sarve eva* — all; *deśe deśe* — in every land; *śuddha* — clean; *gehāni* — houses; *kṛtvā* — having built; *sāmagrīḥ* — provisions; *ca* — and; *pronmadāḥ* — in rapture; *ānayanti* — bring.

**8.** Whenever He arrived at dawn at one halting place after another, all [the people] in every land, bound by the order of the kings, built clean houses and in rapture brought provisions.

*Note.* *Rājñām* is plural, "of the kings"; perhaps it stands for *rājño*, "of the king".

### Verse 9

रामानन्दो भद्रपर्यन्तमेत्य
प्रत्यावृत्तस्तेन सम्यग्विसृष्टः ।
विच्छेदार्त्तः क्षेत्रमेव प्रतस्थे
गौराङ्गोऽयं सोऽप्युपेयादुदीचीम् ॥९॥

*rāmānando bhadra-paryantam etya*
*pratyāvṛttas tena samyag visṛṣṭaḥ |*
*vicchedārttaḥ kṣetram eva pratasthe*
*gaurāṅgo 'yaṁ so 'py upeyād udīcīm ||9||*

*Word for word:* *rāmānandaḥ* — Ramananda; *bhadra-paryantam* — as far as Bhadra; *etya* — having come; *pratyāvṛttaḥ* — turned back; *tena* — by Him; *samyak* — duly; *visṛṣṭaḥ* — dismissed; *viccheda* — by separation; *ārttaḥ* — afflicted; *kṣetram eva* — to [Sri] Kshetra; *pratasthe* — set out; *gaurāṅgaḥ ayam* — and this Gauranga; *saḥ api* — He for His part; *upeyāt* — went; *udīcīm* — to the north.

**9.** Ramananda, having come as far as Bhadra and been duly dismissed by Him, turned back and, afflicted by separation, set out for [Sri] Kshetra; and Gauranga for His part went on to the north.

*Note.* Bhadra is Bhadraka. According to the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 16.151–155), Ramananda accompanies the Lord as far as Remuna, and there, taking leave, falls unconscious.

### Verse 10

ओड्रं यावद्भूपतेर्लेखयुक्ता
आसंस्तावत्तावदेवं धुरीणैः ।
प्रातर्धूपान्तर्गतं राजयोग्यं
निर्माल्यं चानीतमेव प्रकामम् ॥१०॥

*oḍraṁ yāvad bhūpater lekha-yuktā*
*āsaṁs tāvat tāvad evaṁ dhurīṇaiḥ |*
*prātar-dhūpāntargataṁ rāja-yogyaṁ*
*nirmālyaṁ cānītam eva prakāmam ||10||*

*Word for word:* *oḍram yāvat* — as far as Odra [extended]; *bhūpateḥ* — of the king; *lekha* — with the letters; *yuktāḥ* — provided; *āsan* — [the places] were; *tāvat tāvat* — so far, all the way; *evam* — thus; *dhurīṇaiḥ* — by the officials in charge; *prātaḥ* — of the morning; *dhūpa* — *dhupa* [offering]; *antargatam* — forming part; *rāja-yogyam* — fit for a king; *nirmālyam* — the sanctified remnants; *ca* — and; *ānītam eva* — were brought; *prakāmam* — in abundance.

**10.** As far as Odra [extended], [the places] were provided with the king's letters; and all that way the officials in charge thus brought in abundance the sanctified remnants of the morning *dhupa* offering, fit for a king.

*Note.* Odra is Orissa.

### Verse 11

श्रीमान् गौडं देशमासाद्य गङ्गा
द्रष्टव्येति प्रेमवैह्वल्यनुन्नः ।
तत्संसृष्टिस्निग्धमुग्धान्तरात्मा
तत्तत्स्थानाप्यायिताङ्गः स रेजे ॥११॥

*śrīmān gauḍaṁ deśam āsādya gaṅgā*
*draṣṭavyeti prema-vaihvalya-nunnaḥ |*
*tat-saṁsṛṣṭi-snigdha-mugdhāntarātmā*
*tat-tat-sthānāpyāyitāṅgaḥ sa reje ||11||*

*Word for word:* *śrīmān* — the beautiful [Lord]; *gauḍam* — of Gauda; *deśam* — the land; *āsādya* — having reached; *gaṅgā* — the Ganga; *draṣṭavyā* — must be seen; *iti* — thus; *prema* — of love; *vaihvalya* — by the agitation; *nunnaḥ* — impelled; *tat* — with her; *saṁsṛṣṭi* — by contact; *snigdha* — softened; *mugdha* — [and] charmed; *antara-ātmā* — [whose] inner self [was]; *tat-tat* — of those various; *sthāna* — places; *āpyāyita* — refreshed; *aṅgaḥ* — [whose] limbs [were]; *saḥ* — He; *reje* — shone.

**11.** Having reached the land of Gauda, the beautiful [Lord], impelled by the agitation of love — "The Ganga must be seen!" — shone, His inner self softened and charmed by contact with her, His limbs refreshed by those various places.

*Note.* Gauda is Bengal. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 12

आगत्य श्रीराघवस्याश्रमान्तः
श्रीगौरश्चन्द्रवत् पूर्वशैलम् ।
गन्धैर्माल्यैः पुष्पधूपोपहारैः
प्रेमाविष्टः कौतुकी संममाद ॥१२॥

*āgatya śrī-rāghavasyāśramāntaḥ*
*śrī-gauraś candravat pūrva-śailam |*
*gandhair mālyaiḥ puṣpa-dhūpopahāraiḥ*
*premāviṣṭaḥ kautukī saṁmamāda ||12||*

*Word for word:* *āgatya* — having come; *śrī-rāghavasya* — of Sri Raghava; *āśrama* — the abode; *antaḥ* — into; *śrī-gauraḥ* — Sri Gaura; *candra-vat* — like the moon; *pūrva-śailam* — [to] the Eastern Mountain; *gandhaiḥ* — with fragrances; *mālyaiḥ* — with garlands; *puṣpa* — flowers; *dhūpa* — incense; *upahāraiḥ* — [and] offerings; *prema* — by love; *āviṣṭaḥ* — possessed; *kautukī* — delighted; *saṁmamāda* — rejoiced.

**12.** Having come into the abode of Sri Raghava, as the moon [comes] to the Eastern Mountain, Sri Gaura, possessed by love and delighted, rejoiced amid fragrances, garlands, flowers, incense and offerings.

*Note.* Raghava Pandita of Panihati (cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 16.202–205: the Lord arrives at Panihati by boat, and Raghava Pandita leads Him with difficulty through the crowd to his house). As printed, the second pada has only ten syllables (*śrī-gauraś candravat pūrva-śailam*: — — — — ⏑ — — ⏑ — ⏑): of the five heavy syllables of the opening only four are present.

### Verse 13

तत्र स्थित्वा राघवस्याश्रमेऽसौ
नीत्वा नाथः पञ्चषान् वासरान् सः ।
ज्येष्ठं तावच्छ्रीनवद्वीपभूमा-
वग्रे प्रीत्या प्रेषयामास हृष्टः ॥१३॥

*tatra sthitvā rāghavasyāśrame 'sau*
*nītvā nāthaḥ pañcaṣān vāsarān saḥ |*
*jyeṣṭhaṁ tāvac chrī-navadvīpa-bhūmāv*
*agre prītyā preṣayāmāsa hṛṣṭaḥ ||13||*

*Word for word:* *tatra* — there; *sthitvā* — having stayed; *rāghavasya* — of Raghava; *āśrame* — in the abode; *asau* — He; *nītvā* — having spent; *nāthaḥ* — the Master; *pañcaṣān* — five or six; *vāsarān* — days; *saḥ* — He; *jyeṣṭham* — the senior [companion]; *tāvat* — meanwhile; *śrī-navadvīpa* — of Sri Navadvipa; *bhūmau* — to the land; *agre* — ahead; *prītyā* — lovingly; *preṣayāmāsa* — sent; *hṛṣṭaḥ* — joyful.

**13.** Having stayed there in Raghava's abode and spent five or six days, the Master, joyful, meanwhile lovingly sent the senior [companion] ahead to the land of Sri Navadvipa.

*Note.* "The senior" is apparently Paramananda Puri. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 14

तस्मिन् याते गौरचन्द्रः समेतः
श्रीवासस्य प्रेमपात्रस्य गेहम् ।
स्थित्वा तत्र प्राणिमात्रे दयालुः
सर्वत्रासौ संव्यधत्तानुकम्पाम् ॥१४॥

*tasmin yāte gauracandraḥ sametaḥ*
*śrīvāsasya prema-pātrasya geham |*
*sthitvā tatra prāṇi-mātre dayāluḥ*
*sarvatrāsau saṁvyadhattānukampām ||14||*

*Word for word:* *tasmin yāte* — when he had gone; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra; *sametaḥ* — arrived [with His companions]; *śrīvāsasya* — of Srivasa; *prema* — of love; *pātrasya* — the vessel; *geham* — at the house; *sthitvā* — staying; *tatra* — there; *prāṇi-mātre* — to every living being; *dayāluḥ* — compassionate; *sarvatra* — everywhere; *asau* — He; *saṁvyadhatta* — showed; *anukampām* — mercy.

**14.** When he had gone, Gaurachandra arrived [with His companions] at the house of Srivasa, the vessel of love; and staying there, compassionate to every living being, He showed mercy everywhere.

*Note.* According to the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 16.205–206), on this visit the Lord stays at Kumarahatta with Srivasa, and then visits Shivananda Sena and Vasudeva Datta.

### Verse 15

द्वित्रैरस्मिन् वासरैर्लक्षसंख्या
भूयो भूयो हर्षपाथोधिमग्नाः ।
यातायातं सर्वतश्चक्रुरत्र
च्छिद्रं नासीच्चैवमस्यानुभावः ॥१५॥

*dvitrair asmin vāsarair lakṣa-saṅkhyā*
*bhūyo bhūyo harṣa-pāthodhi-magnāḥ |*
*yātāyātaṁ sarvataś cakrur atra*
*cchidraṁ nāsīc caivam asyānubhāvaḥ ||15||*

*Word for word:* *dvi-traiḥ* — in two or three; *asmin* — here; *vāsaraiḥ* — days; *lakṣa-saṅkhyāḥ* — hundreds of thousands; *bhūyaḥ bhūyaḥ* — again and again; *harṣa* — of joy; *pāthodhi* — in the ocean; *magnāḥ* — immersed; *yāta-āyātam* — going and coming; *sarvataḥ* — from all sides; *cakruḥ* — made; *atra* — here; *chidram* — a gap; *na āsīt* — there was not; *ca* — and; *evam* — such [is]; *asya* — His; *anubhāvaḥ* — power.

**15.** In two or three days here hundreds of thousands [of people], immersed again and again in an ocean of joy, came and went from all sides, and there was not [even] a gap here. Such is His power!

### Verse 16

रथ्यास्वोकःद्वारि केचिद्द्रुमेषु
प्राचीरेषु प्रायशोऽन्ये मनुष्याः ।
आसन् लीलाभित्तिचित्रप्रतीका
नोत्कण्ठानां पारमीयुः कदाचित् ॥१६॥

*rathyāsv okaḥ-dvāri kecid drumeṣu*
*prācīreṣu prāyaśo 'nye manuṣyāḥ |*
*āsan līlā-bhitti-citra-pratīkā*
*notkaṇṭhānāṁ pāram īyuḥ kadācit ||16||*

*Word for word:* *rathyāsu* — in the streets; *okaḥ* — of houses; *dvāri* — at the doors; *kecit* — some; *drumeṣu* — in the trees; *prācīreṣu* — on the walls; *prāyaśaḥ* — mostly; *anye* — others; *manuṣyāḥ* — people; *āsan* — were; *līlā* — of a pleasure-[house]; *bhitti* — on the wall; *citra* — pictures; *pratīkāḥ* — like; *na* — not; *utkaṇṭhānām* — of [their] longing; *pāram* — the end; *īyuḥ* — reached; *kadācit* — ever.

**16.** Some people were in the streets, at the doors of houses, in the trees; others, for the most part, on the walls — [standing] like pictures on the wall of a pleasure-house; and they never reached the end of their longing.

*Note.* *Okaḥ-dvāri* keeps the visarga before *d* against the rules of sandhi (regularly *oko-dvāri*); the metre does not require it, since *-ko-* would be heavy as well.

### Verse 17

रात्रावेकोऽपह्नुतो नौकयासौ
तत्तद्ग्रामस्योत्तरेणान्यदेशम् ।
आयातः श्रीवासुदेवस्य गेहं
गत्वा पायात् श्रीशिवानन्दगेहम् ॥१७॥

*rātrāv eko 'pahnuto naukayāsau*
*tat-tad-grāmasyottareṇānya-deśam |*
*āyātaḥ śrī-vāsudevasya gehaṁ*
*gatvā pāyāt (prāyāt?) śrī-śivānanda-geham ||17||*

*Word for word:* *rātrau* — at night; *ekaḥ* — alone; *apahnutaḥ* — concealed; *naukayā* — by boat; *asau* — He; *tat-tat* — that; *grāmasya* — of the village; *uttareṇa* — to the north; *anya* — another; *deśam* — to a place; *āyātaḥ* — having come; *śrī-vāsudevasya* — of Sri Vasudeva; *geham* — to the house; *gatvā* — having gone; *prāyāt* (?) — set out; *śrī-śivānanda* — of Sri Shivananda; *geham* — for the house.

**17.** At night, alone and concealed, He came by boat to another place, north of that village; having gone to the house of Sri Vasudeva, He [then] set out for the house of Sri Shivananda.

*Note.* *Pāyāt* is probably a misprint for *prāyāt*, "set out"; one could also divide *gatvā 'pāyāt* (*apāyāt*, "went away"). From the context (18–19: Srivasa and the others search for Him and cannot find Him) the subject is the Lord Himself, who has secretly left the crowd. Shivananda Sena was of Kumarahatta (Kanchanapalli); Vasudeva is Vasudeva Datta: the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 16.206) names the two together. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 18

अस्मिन् गेहे रात्रिमेकां तु नीत्वा
भिक्षां चक्रे देश एवोत्तरे सः ।
तत्तल्लोकैर्लक्षसंख्यैः समेतो
नौकारूढः शान्तिपुर्यां जगाम ॥१८॥

*asmin gehe rātrim ekāṁ tu nītvā*
*bhikṣāṁ cakre deśa evottare saḥ |*
*tat-tal-lokair lakṣa-saṅkhyaiḥ sameto*
*naukārūḍhaḥ śāntipuryāṁ jagāma ||18||*

*Word for word:* *asmin* — in this; *gehe* — house; *rātrim* — night; *ekām* — one; *tu* — and; *nītvā* — having spent; *bhikṣām* — [His] meal; *cakre* — took; *deśe eva uttare* — in that same northern quarter; *saḥ* — He; *tat-tat* — of those parts; *lokaiḥ* — by the people; *lakṣa-saṅkhyaiḥ* — numbering hundreds of thousands; *sametaḥ* — accompanied; *nauka-ārūḍhaḥ* — having boarded a boat; *śāntipuryām* — to Shantipura; *jagāma* — went.

**18.** Having spent one night in this house, He took His meal in that same northern quarter; and, accompanied by hundreds of thousands of the people of those parts, He boarded a boat and went to Shantipura.

### Verse 19

श्रीवासाद्यैस्तैरथालोक्य नैनं
प्रत्युद्विग्नैः सर्वतोऽन्विष्य भूयः ।
यावन्नैषोऽदर्शि तावत् सुदुःखै-
र्गाढं गाढमर्द्यमानैरभावि ॥१९॥

*śrīvāsādyais tair athālokya nainaṁ*
*pratyudvignaiḥ sarvato 'nviṣya bhūyaḥ |*
*yāvan naiṣo 'darśi tāvat suduḥkhair*
*gāḍhaṁ gāḍham ardyamānair abhāvi ||19||*

*Word for word:* *śrīvāsa-ādyaiḥ* — by Srivasa and the others; *taiḥ* — by those; *atha* — then; *ālokya* — seeing; *na* — not; *enam* — Him; *pratyudvignaiḥ* — alarmed; *sarvataḥ* — everywhere; *anviṣya* — having searched; *bhūyaḥ* — at length; *yāvat* — as long as; *na* — not; *eṣaḥ* — He; *adarśi* — was found; *tāvat* — so long; *su-duḥkhaiḥ* — in great grief; *gāḍham gāḍham* — sorely, sorely; *ardyamānaiḥ* — tormented; *abhāvi* — [they] remained.

**19.** Then Srivasa and the others, not seeing Him, were alarmed and searched everywhere at length; and as long as He was not found, they remained in great grief, sorely, sorely tormented.

*Note.* *Abhāvi* is an impersonal passive ("it was [so] with them"). As printed, the fourth syllable of the fourth pada is light (*gāḍhaṁ gāḍham ardya-*: — — — ⏑ — ⏑ …), where the *śālinī* requires a heavy one.

### Verse 20

नावा गच्छन् स्वर्धुनीमध्यभूमौ
नाम्नां गाथां लोलचित्तः प्रकाश्य ।
अद्वैतस्य ग्राममासाद्य नाथः
प्रेम्नोत्तस्थौ गन्तुमत्यन्तमुत्कः ॥२०॥

*nāvā gacchan svardhunī-madhya-bhūmau*
*nāmnāṁ gāthāṁ lola-cittaḥ prakāśya |*
*advaitasya grāmam āsādya nāthaḥ*
*premnottasthau gantum atyantam utkaḥ ||20||*

*Word for word:* *nāvā* — by boat; *gacchan* — going; *svardhunī* — of the Heavenly River (the Ganga); *madhya-bhūmau* — in the midst; *nāmnām* — of the Names; *gāthām* — the song; *lola* — tremulous; *cittaḥ* — [whose] heart [was]; *prakāśya* — having sung out; *advaitasya* — of Advaita; *grāmam* — the village; *āsādya* — having reached; *nāthaḥ* — the Master; *premnā* — out of love; *uttasthau* — rose; *gantum* — to go; *atyantam* — extremely; *utkaḥ* — eager.

**20.** Going by boat in the midst of the Heavenly River and, His heart tremulous, singing out the song of the Names, the Master reached Advaita's village and rose out of love, extremely eager to go [to Him].

### Verse 21

मध्येद्वारं तेन सार्द्धं महार्हः
सङ्गस्तस्याश्लेषकोलाहलेन ।
आसीन्नैषां प्राणिनां भाग्यभाजां
चक्षुःश्रोत्रद्वन्द्वतृप्त्यै बभूव ॥२१॥

*madhye-dvāraṁ tena sārdhaṁ mahārhaḥ*
*saṅgas tasyāśleṣa-kolāhalena |*
*āsīn naiṣāṁ (āsīd eṣāṁ?) prāṇināṁ bhāgya-bhājāṁ*
*cakṣuḥ-śrotra-dvandva-tṛptyai babhūva ||21||*

*Word for word:* *madhye-dvāram* — in the doorway; *tena sārdham* — with Him [Advaita]; *mahā-arhaḥ* — most precious; *saṅgaḥ* — the meeting; *tasya* — His; *āśleṣa* — of embraces; *kolāhalena* — with the clamour; *āsīt* — there was; *na* — not; *eṣām* — of these; *prāṇinām* — living beings; *bhāgya-bhājām* — fortunate; *cakṣuḥ* — of eyes; *śrotra* — [and] ears; *dvandva* — of the pairs; *tṛptyai* — for the satisfaction; *babhūva* — was.

**21.** In the doorway there took place His most precious meeting with Him, amid the clamour of embraces; [yet] it was not enough to satisfy the eyes and ears of these fortunate beings.

*Note.* The printed *āsīn naiṣāṁ* is to be divided *āsīt* | *na eṣām*: *āsīt* completes the first sentence ("there was the meeting"), and *na … tṛptyai babhūva* says that what they saw and heard did not sate the eyes and ears of the fortunate onlookers — they could not have enough of it. So the printed text gives good sense, and an emendation to *āsīd eṣām* ("it became the satisfaction of the eyes and ears of these fortunate beings") is not necessary. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 22

भूयो भूयो गाढमाश्लेषपीडौ
प्रेमाविष्टौ स्तस्तथाद्वैतगौरौ ।
तत्रान्तेऽसौ तं तथा योगमेनं
पूजाचर्यावाग्विलासैरुपासीत् ॥२२॥

*bhūyo bhūyo gāḍham āśleṣa-pīḍau*
*premāviṣṭau stas tathādvaita-gaurau |*
*tatrānte 'sau taṁ tathā yogam enaṁ*
*pūjā-caryā-vāg-vilāsair upāsīt ||22||*

*Word for word:* *bhūyaḥ bhūyaḥ* — again and again; *gāḍham* — tightly; *āśleṣa* — in embraces; *pīḍau* — pressing [each other]; *prema* — by love; *āviṣṭau* — overwhelmed; *staḥ* — were; *tathā* — thus; *advaita-gaurau* — Advaita and Gaura; *tatra ante* — at the end of that; *asau* — He (Advaita); *tam* — Him; *tathā* — thus; *yogam* (?) — [fittingly?]; *enam* — this [guest]; *pūjā* — with worship; *caryā* — service; *vāk* — of words; *vilāsaiḥ* — [and] the play; *upāsīt* — honoured.

**22.** Again and again Advaita and Gaura, overwhelmed by love, pressed each other tightly in embraces. At the end of that He [Advaita] honoured Him, this [guest], thus ⟨fittingly?⟩, with worship, service and the play of words.

*Note.* *Yogam* is unclear (?); perhaps a misprint for *yogyam*, "fittingly" (*tathā yogyam*, "as was fitting"), which would scan equally. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 23

आगत्याथो श्रीशचीनाम देवी
त्रैलोक्यनामेव माता तमेनम् ।
दृष्ट्वा मेने हर्षपाथोधिमग्नं
तत्रात्मानं सप्रमोदार्त्तिलज्जम् ॥२३॥

*āgatyātho śrī-śacī-nāma devī*
*trailokyānām eva mātā tam enam |*
*dṛṣṭvā mene harṣa-pāthodhi-magnaṁ*
*tatrātmānaṁ sapramodārtti-lajjam ||23||*

*Word for word:* *āgatya* — having come; *atho* — then; *śrī-śacī-nāma* — named Sri Shachi; *devī* — the goddess; *trailokyānām* — of the three worlds; *eva* — truly; *mātā* — the mother; *tam enam* — Him; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *mene* — felt; *harṣa* — of joy; *pāthodhi* — in the ocean; *magnam* — immersed; *tatra* — then; *ātmānam* — herself; *sa-pramoda* — with delight; *ārtti* — pain; *lajjam* — [and] bashfulness.

**23.** Then came the goddess named Sri Shachi, truly the mother of the three worlds; seeing Him, she felt herself immersed in an ocean of joy, with delight, pain and bashfulness.

*Note.* The edition prints *trailokya-nām* (त्रैलोक्यनामेव), a slip for *trailokyānām* (or *trailokyasya*); the metre requires a heavy third syllable, that is, *trailokyānām*, as in the transliteration. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 24

तत्रैवासीत् षड्दिनानि क्रमेण
श्रीगौराङ्गो मातृदत्तान्नतृप्तः ।
आचार्येण प्रीत्युपानीतचर्यो
नेत्रानन्दं प्राणिनामेव कुर्वन् ॥२४॥

*tatraivāsīt ṣaḍ-dināni krameṇa*
*śrī-gaurāṅgo mātṛ-dattānna-tṛptaḥ |*
*ācāryeṇa prīty-upānīta-caryo*
*netrānandaṁ prāṇinām eva kurvan ||24||*

*Word for word:* *tatra eva* — right there; *āsīt* — stayed; *ṣaṭ* — six; *dināni* — days; *krameṇa* — in succession; *śrī-gaurāṅgaḥ* — Sri Gauranga; *mātṛ* — by [His] mother; *datta* — given; *anna* — with the food; *tṛptaḥ* — satisfied; *ācāryeṇa* — by the Acharya; *prīti* — lovingly; *upānīta* — offered; *caryaḥ* — [accepting] the service; *netra* — of the eyes; *ānandam* — joy; *prāṇinām* — to living beings; *eva* — indeed; *kurvan* — giving.

**24.** Right there Sri Gauranga stayed six days in succession, satisfied with the food His mother gave Him, accepting the service lovingly offered by the Acharya, and giving joy to the eyes of [all] living beings.

*Note.* The Acharya is Advaita.

### Verse 25

तेषां तेषां वासराणां समूहे
यामो लोका लक्षकोट्यः समीयुः ।
आचार्योऽसौ प्रत्यहं तांस्तथैव
द्रव्यैर्भूयः प्रीणयामास हर्षात् ॥२५॥

*teṣāṁ teṣāṁ vāsarāṇāṁ samūhe*
*yāmo (?) lokā lakṣa-koṭyaḥ samīyuḥ |*
*ācāryo 'sau pratyahaṁ tāṁs tathaiva*
*dravyair bhūyaḥ prīṇayāmāsa harṣāt ||25||*

*Word for word:* *teṣām teṣām* — of those; *vāsarāṇām* — days; *samūhe* — in the course; *yāmaḥ* (?) — [unclear]; *lokāḥ* — people; *lakṣa-koṭyaḥ* — hundreds of thousands and millions; *samīyuḥ* — assembled; *ācāryaḥ asau* — that Acharya; *prati-aham* — every day; *tān* — them; *tathā eva* — likewise; *dravyaiḥ* — with provisions; *bhūyaḥ* — abundantly; *prīṇayāmāsa* — regaled; *harṣāt* — joyfully.

**25.** In the course of those days people assembled ⟨*yāmo*?⟩ in hundreds of thousands and millions, and every day that Acharya likewise joyfully regaled them abundantly with provisions.

*Note.* *Yāmo* is unclear (?) (perhaps *yāvat* or *yāmyāḥ*, "southerners"); in the printed form it does not agree with the rest of the sentence. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 26

अन्येद्युः स श्रीनवद्वीपभूमेः
पारेगङ्गं पश्चिमे क्वापि देशे ।
श्रीमान् सर्वप्राणिनां तत्तदङ्गै-
र्नेत्रानन्दं सम्यगागत्य तेने ॥२६॥

*anyedyuḥ sa śrī-navadvīpa-bhūmeḥ*
*pāre-gaṅgaṁ paścime kvāpi deśe |*
*śrīmān sarva-prāṇināṁ tat-tad-aṅgair*
*netrānandaṁ samyag āgatya tene ||26||*

*Word for word:* *anyedyuḥ* — on another day; *saḥ* — He; *śrī-navadvīpa-bhūmeḥ* — of the land of Sri Navadvipa; *pāre-gaṅgam* — beyond the Ganga; *paścime* — in the west; *kva api* — in some; *deśe* — place; *śrīmān* — the beautiful [Lord]; *sarva* — of all; *prāṇinām* — living beings; *tat-tat* — by each of His; *aṅgaiḥ* — limbs; *netra* — for the eyes; *ānandam* — joy; *samyak* — fully; *āgatya* — having come; *tene* — spread.

**26.** On another day the beautiful [Lord], having come to a certain place beyond the Ganga, to the west of the land of Sri Navadvipa, fully spread joy for the eyes of all living beings by each of His limbs.

*Note.* According to the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 16.207–209), [He stayed] at the house of Vidya-Vachaspati, and then for a week at the house of Madhava Dasa, where hundreds of thousands of people flocked (by tradition, in Kuliya).

### Verse 27

किम्वा मूकः किन्नु पङ्गुः किमन्धः
किम्वा वृद्धः किं शिशुः किं स्त्रियो वा ।
ये ये सर्वे श्रीनवद्वीपभूस्था-
प्रीत्युद्रेकात्ते त एवाथ जग्मुः ॥२७॥

*kiṁvā mūkaḥ kiṁ nu paṅguḥ kim andhaḥ*
*kiṁvā vṛddhaḥ kiṁ śiśuḥ kiṁ striyo vā |*
*ye ye sarve śrī-navadvīpa-bhū-sthāḥ*
*prīty-udrekāt te ta evātha jagmuḥ ||27||*

*Word for word:* *kiṁvā* — whether; *mūkaḥ* — mute; *kim nu* — or; *paṅguḥ* — lame; *kim* — or; *andhaḥ* — blind; *kiṁvā* — or; *vṛddhaḥ* — old; *kim* — or; *śiśuḥ* — a child; *kim* — or; *striyaḥ* — women; *vā* — or; *ye ye* — whoever; *sarve* — all; *śrī-navadvīpa* — of Sri Navadvipa; *bhū* — in the land; *sthāḥ* — dwelling; *prīti* — of love; *udrekāt* — from an excess; *te te* — every one of them; *eva* — indeed; *atha* — then; *jagmuḥ* — went.

**27.** Whether mute, or lame, or blind, or old, or a child, or women — all those, whoever they were, who dwelt in the land of Sri Navadvipa, every one of them then went [to Him] out of an excess of love.

### Verse 28

यावत्तस्थौ तत्र गौराङ्गचन्द्र-
स्तावत् सर्वे सर्वतो लक्षकोट्यः ।
गाढोत्कण्ठानिर्भरार्त्ताः समीयु-
र्द्रष्टुं तं ते किं स्त्रियः किं पुमांसः ॥२८॥

*yāvat tasthau tatra gaurāṅga-candras*
*tāvat sarve sarvato lakṣa-koṭyaḥ |*
*gāḍhotkaṇṭhā-nirbharārttāḥ samīyur*
*draṣṭuṁ taṁ te kiṁ striyaḥ kiṁ pumāṁsaḥ ||28||*

*Word for word:* *yāvat* — as long as; *tasthau* — stayed; *tatra* — there; *gaurāṅga-candraḥ* — Gaurangachandra; *tāvat* — so long; *sarve* — all; *sarvataḥ* — from everywhere; *lakṣa-koṭyaḥ* — hundreds of thousands and millions; *gāḍha* — by deep; *utkaṇṭhā* — longing; *nirbhara* — utterly; *ārttāḥ* — afflicted; *samīyuḥ* — gathered; *draṣṭum* — to see; *tam* — Him; *te* — they; *kim* — whether; *striyaḥ* — women; *kim* — or; *pumāṁsaḥ* — men.

**28.** As long as Gaurangachandra stayed there, so long did all of them — hundreds of thousands and millions, women and men alike, utterly afflicted by deep longing — gather from everywhere to see Him.

### Verse 29

मध्ये मध्ये तत्र लोकप्रचारै-
रत्युद्विग्नो भूयसोऽन्तर्दधाति ।
किन्तूत्कण्ठा वर्द्धते गाढगाढं
तेषां तेषां क्रन्दतां मुक्तकण्ठम् ॥२९॥

*madhye madhye tatra loka-pracārair*
*atyudvigno bhūyaso 'ntardadhāti |*
*kintūtkaṇṭhā vardhate gāḍha-gāḍhaṁ*
*teṣāṁ teṣāṁ krandatāṁ mukta-kaṇṭham ||29||*

*Word for word:* *madhye madhye* — from time to time; *tatra* — there; *loka* — of people; *pracāraiḥ* — by the throngs; *ati-udvignaḥ* — greatly troubled; *bhūyasaḥ* — many times; *antardadhāti* — hides Himself; *kintu* — but; *utkaṇṭhā* — the longing; *vardhate* — grows; *gāḍha-gāḍham* — ever more intensely; *teṣām teṣām* — of all those; *krandatām* — crying; *mukta-kaṇṭham* — at the top of their voices.

**29.** From time to time, greatly troubled by the throngs of people there, He hid Himself, many times over; but the longing of all those who cried at the top of their voices grew ever more intense.

### Verse 30

एवं नीत्वा तत्र नाथो दिनानि
प्रीत्युद्रेकात् पञ्चषाणि क्रमेण ।
नेत्रानन्दं सर्वलोकस्य तन्वं-
स्तैस्तैर्दिव्यं देशमेव प्रतस्थे ॥३०॥

*evaṁ nītvā tatra nātho dināni*
*prīty-udrekāt pañcaṣāṇi krameṇa |*
*netrānandaṁ sarva-lokasya tanvaṁs*
*tais tair divyaṁ deśam eva pratasthe ||30||*

*Word for word:* *evam* — thus; *nītvā* — having spent; *tatra* — there; *nāthaḥ* — the Master; *dināni* — days; *prīti* — of love; *udrekāt* — from an excess; *pañcaṣāṇi* — five or six; *krameṇa* — in succession; *netra* — for the eyes; *ānandam* — joy; *sarva-lokasya* — of all people; *tanvan* — spreading; *taiḥ taiḥ* — with all of them; *divyam* — to the divine; *deśam* — land; *eva* — indeed; *pratasthe* — set out.

**30.** Having thus spent five or six days there in succession out of an excess of love, spreading joy for the eyes of all people, the Master set out, together with all of them, for the divine land.

*Note.* "The divine land" is unclear (?); according to verse 32 He goes westwards, towards the Yamuna. *Tais taiḥ* may also be understood as instrumental of means, as in verse 26 (*tat-tad-aṅgaiḥ … netrānandaṁ tene*): "spreading joy for the eyes of all people by those various [charms]". The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 31

कश्चिद्गोपीनाथशीतिप्रसिद्धं
गोपीनाथे शेत इत्यन्वयेन ।
तस्मिन् देशे क्वापि गौराङ्गचन्द्रः
प्रेमाविष्टो वीक्ष्य शश्वन्ननन्द ॥३१॥

*kaścid gopīnātha-śīti-prasiddhaṁ*
*gopīnāthe śeta ity anvayena |*
*tasmin deśe kvāpi gaurāṅga-candraḥ*
*premāviṣṭo vīkṣya śaśvan nananda ||31||*

*Word for word:* *kaścit* — a certain [one]; *gopīnātha-śīti* (= *gopīnātha-śī iti*? (?)) — as "Gopinatha-shi"; *prasiddham* — renowned; *gopīnāthe* — at Gopinatha; *śete* — lies (sleeps); *iti* — thus; *anvayena* — by the derivation; *tasmin* — in that; *deśe* — region; *kva api* — somewhere; *gaurāṅga-candraḥ* — Gaurangachandra; *prema* — by love; *āviṣṭaḥ* — overcome; *vīkṣya* — having seen; *śaśvat* — continually; *nananda* — rejoiced.

**31.** Somewhere in that region — renowned as "Gopinatha[-shi]" (?) by the derivation "he lies at Gopinatha" — Gaurangachandra, having seen a certain [person], was overcome by love and rejoiced continually.

*Note.* An obscure verse (?). The syntax does not resolve cleanly: *kaścit* is nominative, *prasiddham* accusative or neuter. The translation takes *prasiddham* with the region and *kaścit* as the person the Lord saw. *-śīti* is probably *śī iti*: the name "Gopinatha-shi" (*śī*, "lying") explained by the derivation *gopīnāthe śete*, "he lies at Gopinatha". If *kaścit* is a misprint for *kañcit* (accusative), the sense would be "having seen a certain [one] renowned as 'Gopinatha-shi'". Perhaps a place where Gopinatha "sleeps" is meant (cf. Remuna with Kshirachora Gopinatha?); it cannot be identified from our sources. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 32

कालिन्दीये तीर एव प्रयातुं
गाढोत्कण्ठः पश्चिमे क्वापि गत्वा ।
प्रत्यावृत्तो भूय एष स्वचित्ते
किम्वालोक्य स्वर्धुनीतीरमायात् ॥३२॥

*kālindīye tīra eva prayātuṁ*
*gāḍhotkaṇṭhaḥ paścime kvāpi gatvā |*
*pratyāvṛtto bhūya eṣa sva-citte*
*kiṁvālokya svardhunī-tīram āyāt ||32||*

*Word for word:* *kālindīye* — of the Kalindi; *tīre eva* — to the very bank; *prayātum* — to go; *gāḍha* — deeply; *utkaṇṭhaḥ* — longing; *paścime* — to the west; *kva api* — somewhere; *gatvā* — having gone; *pratyāvṛttaḥ* — turned back; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *eṣaḥ* — He; *sva-citte* — in His own heart; *kiṁvā* — something; *ālokya* — having considered; *svardhunī* — of the Heavenly River; *tīram* — to the bank; *āyāt* — came.

**32.** Deeply longing to go to the very bank of the Kalindi, He went somewhere to the west; but, having considered something in His own heart, He turned back and came again to the bank of the Heavenly River.

*Note.* The Kalindi is the Yamuna; the Heavenly River (*svardhunī*) is the Ganga. According to the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 16.211, 265–274), the Lord, having reached Kanai Natashala, turns back, remembering Sanatana's words that one does not go to Vrindavana with a crowd.

### Verse 33

तत्तद्देशे भूय एव प्रकामं
स्थित्वा कृत्वा दीर्घदीर्घानुकम्पाम् ।
श्रीनीलाद्रौ भूय एव प्रतस्थे
चित्रं चित्रं तस्य तत्तच्चरित्रम् ॥३३॥

*tat-tad-deśe bhūya eva prakāmaṁ*
*sthitvā kṛtvā dīrgha-dīrghānukampām |*
*śrī-nīlādrau bhūya eva pratasthe*
*citraṁ citraṁ tasya tat-tac-caritram ||33||*

*Word for word:* *tat-tat* — in those various; *deśe* — places; *bhūyaḥ eva* — again; *prakāmam* — to His heart's content; *sthitvā* — having stayed; *kṛtvā* — having shown; *dīrgha-dīrgha* — long, long; *anukampām* — compassion; *śrī-nīlādrau* — for Sri Niladri; *bhūyaḥ eva* — again; *pratasthe* — set out; *citram citram* — wonderful, wonderful; *tasya* — His; *tat-tat* — every; *caritram* — deed.

**33.** Having again stayed to His heart's content in those various places and shown long, long compassion, He again set out for Sri Niladri. Wonderful, wonderful is His every deed!

### Verse 34

तत्तद्व्याजात् स्वर्धुनीतीरमायात्
यत्र श्रीमांश्चित्रमेवावतीर्णः ।
नेत्रानन्दं सर्वलोकस्य कृत्वा
नीलाद्रिस्थप्रीतये भूय आसीत् ॥३४॥

*tat-tad-vyājāt svardhunī-tīram āyāt*
*yatra śrīmāṁś citram evāvatīrṇaḥ |*
*netrānandaṁ sarva-lokasya kṛtvā*
*nīlādri-stha-prītaye bhūya āsīt ||34||*

*Word for word:* *tat-tat* — by this or that; *vyājāt* — pretext; *svardhunī* — of the Heavenly River; *tīram* — to the bank; *āyāt* — came; *yatra* — where; *śrīmān* — the beautiful [Lord]; *citram eva* — wondrously; *avatīrṇaḥ* — had descended; *netra* — for the eyes; *ānandam* — joy; *sarva-lokasya* — of all people; *kṛtvā* — having given; *nīlādri* — on Niladri; *stha* — of Him who dwells; *prītaye* — for the delight; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *āsīt* — was [there].

**34.** On this or that pretext He came to the bank of the Heavenly River, where the beautiful [Lord] had wondrously descended [into the world]; having given joy to the eyes of all people, He was again [in Puri], for the delight of Him who dwells on Niladri.

*Note.* *Nīlādri-stha*, "He who dwells on Niladri", is Jagannatha.

### Verse 35

स्थित्वा तत्र श्रीमयो गौरचन्द्रः
कञ्चित् कालं भूयोऽध्वनैव ।
कालिन्दीयं तीरमेव प्रतस्थे
विच्छेदार्त्तांस्तत्र तांस्तान् विधाय ॥३५॥

*sthitvā tatra śrīmayo gauracandraḥ*
*kañcit kālaṁ bhūyo 'dhvanaiva (tenaiva?) |*
*kālindīyaṁ tīram eva pratasthe*
*vicchedārttāṁs tatra tāṁs tān vidhāya ||35||*

*Word for word:* *sthitvā* — having stayed; *tatra* — there; *śrī-mayaḥ* — full of splendour; *gauracandraḥ* — Gaurachandra; *kañcit kālam* — for some time; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *adhvanā eva* — by the road itself; *kālindīyam* — of the Kalindi; *tīram eva* — to the very bank; *pratasthe* — set out; *viccheda* — by separation; *ārttān* — afflicted; *tatra* — there; *tān tān* — all of them; *vidhāya* — having left.

**35.** Having stayed there for some time, Gaurachandra, full of splendour, again set out by the road (?) for the very bank of the Kalindi, leaving all of them there afflicted by separation.

*Note.* Metre: the second pada (*kañcit kālaṁ bhūyo 'dhvanaiva*) has only nine syllables (——————⏑—⏑), where *śālinī* requires eleven (—————⏑——⏑——): two syllables are missing, not one. A reading *bhūya evādhvanaiva* (*bhūyaḥ eva adhvanā eva*, cf. *bhūya eva* in verse 33) would scan correctly (?); the text is not emended. According to the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 17), the second journey to Vrindavana goes through the forest of Jharikhanda, not through Bengal; Karnapura compresses the events. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

### Verse 36

रामानन्दस्तद्वियोगाधिपीडा-
क्षीणक्षीणस्तत्यजेऽसून् महात्मा ।
विच्छेदे स्याद्योग्यमेतच्चरित्रं
प्रेम्णस्तावत्तादृशस्यास्य नूनम् ॥३६॥

*rāmānandas tad-viyogādhi-pīḍā-*
*kṣīṇa-kṣīṇas tatyaje 'sūn mahātmā |*
*vicchede syād yogyam etac caritraṁ*
*premṇas tāvat tādṛśasyāsya nūnam ||36||*

*Word for word:* *rāmānandaḥ* — Ramananda; *tat* — from Him; *viyoga* — of separation; *ādhi* — of mental anguish; *pīḍā* — by the torment; *kṣīṇa-kṣīṇaḥ* — utterly wasted away; *tatyaje* — gave up; *asūn* — [his] life-breaths; *mahā-ātmā* — the great soul; *vicchede* — in separation; *syāt* — must be; *yogyam* — fitting; *etat* — this; *caritram* — conduct; *premṇaḥ* — of love; *tāvat* — indeed; *tādṛśasya* — of such; *asya* — of this; *nūnam* — surely.

**36.** Ramananda, the great soul, utterly wasted away by the torment of the anguish of separation from Him, gave up his life-breaths. Surely, in separation, this is the conduct fitting for such a love as this.

*Note.* The last verse of the run in *śālinī* (26–36; verse 41 is again in *śālinī*). The statement that Ramananda gave up his life from separation diverges from the Chaitanya-charitamrita, where Ramananda remains with the Lord in Puri to the end and hears verses with Him in the Gambhira (Antya 20).

### Verse 37

स्थित्वा तत्र दिनानि हन्त कतिचिद्भूयोऽसिताद्रौ प्रभुः
श्रीमानेत्य ननन्द नन्दयति च स्मैतानजस्रं जनान् ।
एवं विंशतिहायनान्तरभवां यात्रां विलोक्याखिलां
स्वं धामाथ जगाम कैश्चिदपि तैः सार्द्धं कृपासागरः ॥३७॥

*sthitvā tatra dināni hanta katicid bhūyo 'sitādrau prabhuḥ*
*śrīmān etya nananda nandayati ca smaitān ajasraṁ janān |*
*evaṁ viṁśati-hāyanāntara-bhavāṁ yātrāṁ vilokyākhilāṁ*
*svaṁ dhāmātha jagāma kaiścid api taiḥ sārdhaṁ kṛpā-sāgaraḥ ||37||*

*Word for word:* *sthitvā* — having stayed; *tatra* — there; *dināni* — days; *hanta* — alas; *katicit* — some; *bhūyaḥ* — again; *asita-adrau* — to the Dark Mountain; *prabhuḥ* — the Lord; *śrīmān* — beautiful; *etya* — having come; *nananda* — rejoiced; *nandayati sma* — gladdened; *ca* — and; *etān* — these; *ajasram* — unceasingly; *janān* — people; *evam* — thus; *viṁśati* — of twenty; *hāyana* — years; *antara* — in the course; *bhavām* — taking place; *yātrām* — the festivals; *vilokya* — having beheld; *akhilām* — all; *svam* — to His own; *dhāma* — abode; *atha* — then; *jagāma* — went; *kaiścit api* — with some; *taiḥ sārdham* — together with them; *kṛpā-sāgaraḥ* — the Ocean of Mercy.

**37.** Having stayed there for some days, the beautiful Lord came again to the Dark Mountain, rejoiced, and unceasingly gladdened these people. Thus, having beheld all the festivals that took place in the course of twenty years, the Ocean of Mercy then — alas! — went to His own abode, together with some of them.

*Note.* Metre — *śārdūla-vikrīḍita* (———⏑⏑—⏑—⏑⏑⏑———⏑——⏑—; 19 syllables per pada); the verse scans correctly. The Dark Mountain (*asitādri*) is Nilachala (Puri). "Went to His own abode" — the disappearance of the Lord from the world. "With some of them" — together with those associates who departed after Him.

### Verse 38

प्रेमाम्भोधौ जगदतिशये मज्जयित्वा स भूयो
विच्छेदाग्नावपि च विदधे मग्नमत्यन्तदुर्गे ।
चित्रं चित्रं तदपि सततं प्रेमसिन्धुर्बलीया-
नासीत् कोऽयं शिवशिव महान् गौरचन्द्रानुभावः ॥३८॥

*premāmbhodhau jagad atiśaye majjayitvā sa bhūyo*
*vicchedāgnāv api ca vidadhe magnam atyanta-durge |*
*citraṁ citraṁ tad api satataṁ prema-sindhur balīyān*
*āsīt ko 'yaṁ śiva śiva mahān gauracandrānubhāvaḥ ||38||*

*Word for word:* *prema* — of love; *ambhodhau* — in the ocean; *jagat* — the world; *atiśaye* — boundless; *majjayitvā* — having immersed; *saḥ* — He; *bhūyaḥ* — then; *viccheda* — of separation; *agnau* — in the fire; *api ca* — also; *vidadhe* — made; *magnam* — sunk; *atyanta-durge* — utterly impassable; *citram citram* — wonderful, wonderful; *tat api* — even so; *satatam* — always; *prema* — of love; *sindhuḥ* — the ocean; *balīyān* — stronger; *āsīt* — was; *kaḥ ayam* — what is this; *śiva śiva* — Heaven forbid; *mahān* — great; *gauracandra* — of Gaurachandra; *anubhāvaḥ* — power.

**38.** Having immersed the world in the boundless ocean of love, He then made it sink also in the utterly impassable fire of separation. Wonderful, wonderful! Even so, the ocean of love was always the stronger. What is this — Heaven forbid! — great power of Gaurachandra?

*Note.* Metre — *mandākrāntā* (————⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑——⏑——⏑——; 17 syllables per pada); the verse scans correctly. *Śiva śiva* — an exclamation, here of awe mingled with dismay.

### Verse 39

नानादेशान्निजनिजजनानेवमेकत्र कृत्वा
तानन्योन्यं प्रणयनिबिडान् कारयित्वा प्रकामम् ।
तैस्तैः सार्द्धं बत विलसितो हन्त गौडोत्कलेषु
स्वं धामास्मिन् गतवति गता भूर्वियोगाग्निसिन्धौ ॥३९॥

*nānā-deśān nija-nija-janān evam ekatra kṛtvā*
*tān anyonyaṁ praṇaya-nibiḍān kārayitvā prakāmam |*
*tais taiḥ sārdhaṁ bata vilasito hanta gauḍotkaleṣu*
*svaṁ dhāmāsmin gatavati gatā bhūr viyogāgni-sindhau ||39||*

*Word for word:* *nānā* — from various; *deśāt* — lands; *nija-nija* — His own; *janān* — people; *evam* — thus; *ekatra* — in one place; *kṛtvā* — having gathered; *tān* — them; *anyonyam* — to one another; *praṇaya* — by love; *nibiḍān* — closely bound; *kārayitvā* — having made; *prakāmam* — fully; *taiḥ taiḥ sārdham* — together with all of them; *bata* — ah; *vilasitaḥ* — having sported; *hanta* — alas; *gauḍa* — in Gauda; *utkaleṣu* — [and] in Utkala; *svam* — to His own; *dhāma* — abode; *asmin* — He; *gatavati* — when [He] had gone; *gatā* — went (sank); *bhūḥ* — the earth; *viyoga* — of separation; *agni* — of fire; *sindhau* — into the ocean.

**39.** Having thus gathered His own people from various lands in one place and made them fully bound to one another by close love, He — ah! — sported with all of them in Gauda and Utkala; [and] when He — alas! — had gone to His own abode, the earth sank into an ocean of the fire of separation.

*Note.* Metre — *mandākrāntā*; the verse scans correctly. Utkala is Orissa.

### Verse 40

चतुर्विंशे तावत् प्रकटितनिजप्रेमविवशः
प्रकामं सन्न्यासं समकृत नवद्वीपतलतः ।
त्रिवर्षश्च क्षेत्रादपि तत इतो यन्नगमय-
त्तथा दृष्ट्वा यात्रा व्यनयदखिला विंशतिसमाः ॥४०॥

*caturviṁśe tāvat prakaṭita-nija-prema-vivaśaḥ*
*prakāmaṁ sannyāsaṁ samakṛta navadvīpa-talataḥ |*
*tri-varṣaś ca kṣetrād api tata ito yann agamayat*
*tathā dṛṣṭvā yātrā vyanayad akhilā viṁśati-samāḥ ||40||*

*Word for word:* *caturviṁśe* — in the twenty-fourth [year]; *tāvat* — first; *prakaṭita* — made manifest; *nija* — by His own; *prema* — love; *vivaśaḥ* — overpowered; *prakāmam* — fully; *sannyāsam* — sannyasa; *samakṛta* — accepted; *navadvīpa-talataḥ* — from Navadvipa; *tri-varṣaḥ* — three years; *ca* — and; *kṣetrāt* — from the Kshetra; *api* — even; *tataḥ itaḥ* — hither and thither; *yan* — going; *agamayat* — spent; *tathā* — thus; *dṛṣṭvā* — beholding; *yātrāḥ* — the festivals; *vyanayat* — passed; *akhilāḥ* — all; *viṁśati* — twenty; *samāḥ* — years.

**40.** In the twenty-fourth [year], overpowered by His own love, which He had made manifest, He first fully accepted sannyasa, [leaving] from Navadvipa; three years He spent going hither and thither, [setting out] even from the Kshetra; and thus, beholding the festivals, He passed all of twenty years.

*Note.* Metre — *śikhariṇī* (⏑—————⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑——⏑⏑⏑—; 17 syllables per pada); the verse scans correctly. *Tri-varṣaḥ* is nominative; the sense requires "three years" as the object of *agamayat* (?). Karnapura's chronology: sannyasa at twenty-four, three years of wandering, twenty years in Puri — forty-seven years of life in all (cf. verse 41). In the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 1.15–21): twenty-four years in Navadvipa and twenty-four years after sannyasa — six years of travel and eighteen years in Puri.

### Verse 41

इत्थं चत्वारिंशता सप्तभाजा
श्रीगौराङ्गो हायनानां क्रमेण ।
नानालीलालास्यमासाद्य भूमौ
क्रीडन् धाम स्वं ततोऽसौ जगाम ॥४१॥

*itthaṁ catvāriṁśatā sapta-bhājā*
*śrī-gaurāṅgo hāyanānāṁ krameṇa |*
*nānā-līlā-lāsyam āsādya bhūmau*
*krīḍan dhāma svaṁ tato 'sau jagāma ||41||*

*Word for word:* *ittham* — thus; *catvāriṁśatā* — by forty; *sapta* — seven; *bhājā* — including; *śrī-gaurāṅgaḥ* — Sri Gauranga; *hāyanānām* — of years; *krameṇa* — in succession; *nānā* — of various; *līlā* — pastimes; *lāsyam* — the dance; *āsādya* — having displayed; *bhūmau* — on earth; *krīḍan* — sporting; *dhāma* — to [His] abode; *svam* — own; *tataḥ* — then; *asau* — He; *jagāma* — went.

**41.** Thus Sri Gauranga, sporting on earth through a succession of forty years and seven, and displaying the dance of various pastimes, then went to His own abode.

*Note.* Metre — *śālinī* (—————⏑——⏑——; 11 syllables per pada). The edition has a superfluous syllable in the fourth pada (*svaṁ svaṁ*); the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads *dhāma svaṁ*, which is adopted here and scans correctly.

### Verse 42

आशैशवं प्रभुचरित्रविलासविज्ञैः
केश्चिन्मुरारिरितिमङ्गलनामधेयैः ।
यद्यद्विलासललितं समलेखि तज्ज्ञै-
स्तत्तद्विलोक्य विलिलेख शिशुः स एषः ॥४२॥

*āśaiśavaṁ prabhu-caritra-vilāsa-vijñaiḥ*
*keścin (kaiścin) murārir iti maṅgala-nāmadheyaiḥ |*
*yad yad vilāsa-lalitaṁ samalekhi taj-jñais*
*tat tad vilokya vililekha śiśuḥ sa eṣaḥ ||42||*

*Word for word:* *ā-śaiśavam* — from childhood; *prabhu* — of the Lord; *caritra* — of the deeds; *vilāsa* — [and] pastimes; *vijñaiḥ* — by [one] who knew; *kaiścit* — by a certain [person]; *murāriḥ iti* — "Murari"; *maṅgala* — auspicious; *nāmadheyaiḥ* — bearing the name; *yat yat* — whatever; *vilāsa* — of the pastimes; *lalitam* — charm; *samalekhi* — was written down; *tat-jñaiḥ* — by [one] who knew it; *tat tat* — all that; *vilokya* — having seen; *vililekha* — wrote; *śiśuḥ* — child; *saḥ eṣaḥ* — this very.

**42.** Whatever charm of the pastimes was written down by a certain [person] bearing the auspicious name "Murari" — one who from childhood knew the deeds and pastimes of the Lord, who knew these things — having seen all that, this very child wrote [it].

*Note.* Metre — *vasantatilakā* (——⏑—⏑⏑⏑—⏑⏑—⏑——; 14 syllables per pada), verses 42–45. Karnapura names the records of Murari Gupta (Murari's *kaḍacā*) as the source of the poem; a comparison of the two texts is a matter for separate study. "The child" is the author himself. *Ā-śaiśavam* may also mean "from [the Lord's] childhood on". The plural instrumentals (*kaiścit … vijñaiḥ … nāmadheyaiḥ … taj-jñaiḥ*) are honorific. In the edition *keścin* is a misprint for *kaiścin*.

### Verse 43

बद्धाञ्जलिः शिरसि निर्भरकाकुवादै-
र्भूयो नमाम्यहमसौ स मुरारिसंज्ञम् ।
तं मुग्धकोमलधियं ननु यत्प्रसादा-
च्चैतन्यचन्द्रचरितामृतमक्षिपीतम् ॥४३॥

*baddhāñjaliḥ śirasi nirbhara-kāku-vādair*
*bhūyo namāmy aham asau sa murāri-saṁjñam |*
*taṁ mugdha-komala-dhiyaṁ nanu yat-prasādāc*
*caitanya-candra-caritāmṛtam akṣi-pītam ||43||*

*Word for word:* *baddha* — joined; *añjaliḥ* — [with] palms; *śirasi* — on the head; *nirbhara* — full; *kāku* — of humble entreaty; *vādaiḥ* — with words; *bhūyaḥ* — again and again; *namāmi* — bow down; *aham* — I; *asau* — this one; *saḥ* — he; *murāri* — Murari; *saṁjñam* — named; *tam* — to him; *mugdha* — simple; *komala* — [and] tender; *dhiyam* — [whose] mind; *nanu* — for indeed; *yat* — whose; *prasādāt* — by the grace; *caitanya-candra* — of Chaitanya-chandra; *carita* — of the deeds; *amṛtam* — the nectar; *akṣi* — with the eyes; *pītam* — drunk.

**43.** With palms joined upon my head, with words full of humble entreaty, I bow down again and again to him who is named Murari, of simple and tender mind — for indeed by his grace the nectar of the deeds of Chaitanya-chandra has been drunk [by me] with the eyes.

*Note.* *Asau sa* — pronouns that fill out the metre: *asau* can go with *aham* ("I, this one"), while *sa* (nominative) does not agree with the accusative *murāri-saṁjñam* (?).

### Verse 44

चैतन्यचन्द्रचरितामृतमत्युदारं
सर्वे दृशा च मनसा मुदा वहन्तु ।
यद्दृष्टमात्रमपहन्ति दुरापपारं
संसारसागरमजस्रमुदग्रहिंस्रम् ॥४४॥

*caitanya-candra-caritāmṛtam atyudāraṁ*
*sarve dṛśā ca manasā (ca) mudā vahantu |*
*yad dṛṣṭa-mātram apahanti durāpa-pāraṁ*
*saṁsāra-sāgaram ajasram udagra-hiṁsram ||44||*

*Word for word:* *caitanya-candra-carita-amṛtam* — the "Chaitanya-chandra-charitamrita"; *ati-udāram* — most generous; *sarve* — all; *dṛśā* — in the gaze; *ca* — and; *manasā* — in the mind; *mudā* — with joy; *vahantu* — may carry; *yat* — which; *dṛṣṭa-mātram* — merely seen; *apahanti* — destroys; *durāpa* — hard to reach; *pāram* — [whose] far shore; *saṁsāra* — of samsara; *sāgaram* — the ocean; *ajasram* — unceasingly; *udagra* — fierce; *hiṁsram* — [full of] predators.

**44.** May all, with joy, carry in their gaze and in their mind the most generous "Chaitanya-chandra-charitamrita", which, merely seen, unceasingly destroys the ocean of samsara, whose far shore is hard to reach and which is full of fierce predators.

*Note.* Metre: the second pada is one syllable short (*sarve dṛśā ca manasā mudā vahantu*: ——⏑—⏑⏑⏑—⏑—⏑—⏑, 13 syllables instead of 14); with *ca* after *manasā* (as the bracket in the transliteration suggests) it scans correctly (——⏑—⏑⏑⏑—⏑⏑—⏑——) (?). *Ajasram* may also be taken with *udagra-hiṁsram*: "ceaselessly [full of] fierce predators". The title of the poem is played upon. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text (without *ca*).

### Verse 45

नाहं स्तुतौ बत नतौ विनतौ च शक्तो
यत्तैश्च तैर्जनचयं स्ववशे करिष्ये ।
आश्रित्य किन्तु निजकारुणिकत्वमेव
यद्योग्यमत्र तदहो रचयन्तु धीराः ॥४५॥

*nāhaṁ stutau bata natau vinatau ca śakto*
*yat taiś ca tair jana-cayaṁ sva-vaśe kariṣye |*
*āśritya kintu nija-kāruṇikatvam eva*
*yad yogyam atra tad aho racayantu dhīrāḥ ||45||*

*Word for word:* *na aham* — I am not; *stutau* — in praise; *bata* — alas; *natau* — in bowing; *vinatau* — in humble entreaty; *ca* — and; *śaktaḥ* — capable; *yat* — so that; *taiḥ taiḥ* — by these; *ca* — and; *jana* — of people; *cayam* — a multitude; *sva-vaśe* — under my sway; *kariṣye* — I might bring; *āśritya* — resorting; *kintu* — but; *nija* — to their own; *kāruṇikatvam* — compassion; *eva* — indeed; *yat* — what; *yogyam* — fitting; *atra* — here; *tat* — that; *aho* — oh; *racayantu* — may [they] do; *dhīrāḥ* — the wise.

**45.** Alas, I am not capable of praise, of bowing, or of humble entreaty, so that by these I might bring a multitude of people under my sway. But may the wise, resorting to their own compassion, do here — oh! — whatever is fitting.

### Verse 46

इह परमकृपालोर्गौरचन्द्रस्य कोऽपि
प्रणयरसशरीरः श्रीशिवानन्दसेनः ।
भुवि निवसति तस्यापत्यमेकं कनीय-
स्त्वकृत परममोग्ध्याच्चित्रमेतं प्रबन्धम् ॥४६॥

*iha parama-kṛpālor gauracandrasya ko 'pi*
*praṇaya-rasa-śarīraḥ śrī-śivānanda-senaḥ |*
*bhuvi nivasati tasyāpatyam ekaṁ kanīyas*
*tv akṛta parama-maugdhyāc citram etaṁ prabandham ||46||*

*Word for word:* *iha* — here; *parama* — supremely; *kṛpāloḥ* — merciful; *gauracandrasya* — of Gaurachandra; *kaḥ api* — a certain; *praṇaya* — of love; *rasa* — of the rasa; *śarīraḥ* — the embodiment; *śrī-śivānanda-senaḥ* — Sri Shivananda Sena; *bhuvi* — on earth; *nivasati* — lives; *tasya* — his; *apatyam* — child; *ekam* — one; *kanīyaḥ* — younger; *tu* — indeed; *akṛta* — made; *parama* — utter; *maugdhyāt* — out of simplicity; *citram* — wonderful; *etam* — this; *prabandham* — composition.

**46.** Here on earth there lives a certain Sri Shivananda Sena, an embodiment of the rasa of love for the supremely merciful Gaurachandra; one younger child of his, out of utter simplicity, made this wonderful composition.

*Note.* Metre — *mālinī* (⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑———⏑——⏑——; 15 syllables per pada); the verse scans correctly. The author's signature: Kavi Karnapura (Paramananda) is the youngest son of Shivananda Sena.

### Verse 47

धीरोदात्तमहत्तमो गुणनिधिर्यस्मिन्नसौ नायको
यत्रामूर्लिपयो निरन्तरबलत्प्रेमप्रकाशाक्षराः ।
यत्रानेकमहामहोत्तमधियां चारित्रमन्तर्गतं
तच्चैतन्यचरित्रवर्णनमिदं जीयादजस्रं भुवि ॥४७॥

*dhīrodātta-mahattamo guṇa-nidhir yasminn asau nāyako*
*yatrāmūr lipayo nirantara-balat-prema-prakāśākṣarāḥ |*
*yatrāneka-mahā-mahottama-dhiyāṁ cāritram antargataṁ*
*tac caitanya-caritra-varṇanam idaṁ jīyād ajasraṁ bhuvi ||47||*

*Word for word:* *dhīra-udātta* — "steadfast and exalted" (*dhīrodātta*); *mahattamaḥ* — supremely great; *guṇa* — of virtues; *nidhiḥ* — a treasury; *yasmin* — in which; *asau* — this one; *nāyakaḥ* — the hero; *yatra* — in which; *amūḥ* — these; *lipayaḥ* — writings; *nirantara* — unceasingly; *balat* — growing strong; *prema* — love; *prakāśa* — manifesting; *akṣarāḥ* — [whose] syllables; *yatra* — in which; *aneka* — of many; *mahā-mahā-uttama* — the very greatest; *dhiyām* — of minds; *cāritram* — the conduct; *antargatam* — is contained; *tat* — that; *caitanya* — of Chaitanya; *caritra* — of the deeds; *varṇanam* — description; *idam* — this; *jīyāt* — may triumph; *ajasram* — forever; *bhuvi* — on earth.

**47.** That [poem] in which the hero is He — *dhīrodātta*, supremely great, a treasury of virtues; in which these writings have syllables that manifest an unceasingly growing love; in which is contained the conduct of many of the very greatest minds — may this description of the deeds of Chaitanya triumph forever on earth!

*Note.* Metre — *śārdūla-vikrīḍita*; the verse scans correctly. *Dhīrodātta*, "steadfast and exalted", is the type of hero that the canon of poetics (the Sahitya-darpana) requires of a mahakavya; Karnapura shows that his poem meets the requirements of the genre.

### Verse 48

एतत्तापत्रयनिरसनं प्रेममात्रैकबीजं
श्रीगौराङ्गप्रणयवलितोत्कीर्त्तिमात्रस्वरूपम् ।
दृष्ट्वा स्वान्तःकरणपदवीं मामनालोच्य धीराः
शश्वत् कण्ठे दधतु मुदिता रम्यमेनं प्रबन्धम् ॥४८॥

*etat tāpa-traya-nirasanaṁ prema-mātraika-bījaṁ*
*śrī-gaurāṅga-praṇaya-valitotkīrtti-mātra-svarūpam |*
*dṛṣṭvā svāntaḥ-karaṇa-padavīṁ mām anālocya dhīrāḥ*
*śaśvat kaṇṭhe dadhatu muditā ramyam enaṁ prabandham ||48||*

*Word for word:* *etat* — this; *tāpa* — miseries; *traya* — threefold; *nirasanam* — removing; *prema* — love; *mātra* — alone; *eka* — sole; *bījam* — [whose] seed; *śrī-gaurāṅga* — of Sri Gauranga; *praṇaya* — with love; *valita* — imbued; *utkīrtti* — exalted glory; *mātra* — nothing but; *svarūpam* — [whose] very nature; *dṛṣṭvā* — having seen; *sva* — of their own; *antaḥ-karaṇa* — inner sense (heart); *padavīm* — the path; *mām* — me; *anālocya* — not considering; *dhīrāḥ* — the wise; *śaśvat* — forever; *kaṇṭhe* — on the neck; *dadhatu* — may wear; *muditāḥ* — delighted; *ramyam* — charming; *enam* — this; *prabandham* — composition.

**48.** This [poem] removes the threefold miseries; its sole seed is love alone; its very nature is nothing but the exalted glory of Sri Gauranga, imbued with love. Seeing [in it] the path of their own hearts, and not considering me, may the wise, delighted, wear this charming composition upon their necks forever!

*Note.* Metre — *mandākrāntā*; the verse scans correctly. "Wear on the neck" — as a necklace or garland.

### Verse 49

वेदा रसाः श्रुतय इन्दुरिति प्रसिद्धे
शाके तथा खलु शुचौ शुभगे च मासि ।
वारे सुधाकिरणनाम्न्यसितद्वितीया-
तिथ्यन्तरे परिसमाप्तिरभूदमुष्य ॥४९॥

*vedā rasāḥ śrutaya indur iti prasiddhe*
*śāke tathā khalu śucau śubhage ca māsi |*
*vāre sudhā-kiraṇa-nāmny asita-dvitīyā-*
*tithy-antare parisamāptir abhūd amuṣya ||49||*

*Word for word:* *vedāḥ* — the Vedas (4); *rasāḥ* — the rasas (6); *śrutayaḥ* — the shrutis (4); *induḥ* — the moon (1); *iti* — thus; *prasiddhe* — known; *śāke* — in the Shaka year; *tathā* — and; *khalu* — indeed; *śucau* — in Shuchi (Ashadha); *śubhage* — auspicious; *ca* — and; *māsi* — in the month; *vāre* — on the day; *sudhā-kiraṇa* — of the Nectar-rayed (the moon); *nāmni* — bearing the name; *asita* — of the dark [fortnight]; *dvitīyā* — second; *tithi* — lunar day; *antare* — within; *parisamāptiḥ* — the completion; *abhūt* — took place; *amuṣya* — of this [work].

**49.** In the Shaka year known [as] "the Vedas, the rasas, the shrutis, the moon", and indeed in the auspicious month of Shuchi, on the day bearing the name of the Nectar-rayed [moon], within the second lunar day of the dark [fortnight], the completion of this [work] took place.

*Note.* Metre — *vasantatilakā*; the verse scans correctly. A chronogram (*bhūta-saṅkhyā*): the Vedas = 4, the rasas = 6, the shrutis = 4, the moon = 1; the digits are read from right to left — Shaka 1464, i.e. 1542 CE; the month of Ashadha (June–July), a Monday, the second tithi of the dark fortnight. The publisher adds: the Lord appeared in Shaka 1407 and lived forty-seven years; the poem was written nine years after His disappearance; "it is now Shaka 1905, that is, the poem is 498 years old; it has 1911 verses". The publisher's reckoning is inexact: 1407 + 47 = 1454, and from 1454 to 1464 is ten years (according to the Chaitanya-charitamrita, the Lord's disappearance was in Shaka 1455, 1533 CE); 498 = 1905 − 1407, the years since the Lord's appearance, whereas from Shaka 1464 to 1905 is 441 years (?). On the total of 1911 (the printed numbering of the twenty sargas adds up to 1912), see **Total verses** in the header of the sarga.

**Colophon:** इति श्रीकृष्णचैतन्यचरितामृते महाकाव्ये श्रीलकर्णपूरकृतौ विंशतितमः सर्गः ॥ समाप्तमिदं श्रीकृष्णचैतन्यचरितामृतं महाकाव्यम् । श्लोकसंख्या १९११ । (*iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahākāvye śrīla-karṇapūra-kṛtau viṁśatitamaḥ sargaḥ || samāptam idaṁ śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛtaṁ mahākāvyam | śloka-saṅkhyā 1911 |*) — "Thus [ends] the twentieth sarga in the mahakavya 'Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita', the work of Srila Karnapura. Completed is this mahakavya 'Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita'. Number of verses: 1911."
